reviews.comment: Not a helpful professor. There was a lot of work and little to no feedback during office hours. He just read from slides that were not even his own. I am just glad this class is over.

He will NOT drop ANYTHING. Every week pre lab + lab(which takes 1-3 hours to finish) + lab quiz every week + sometimes class quiz + heavy homework every week(which takes 3-5 hours to finish). He will not drop anything. There is no curve. Professor just reads from lecture notes. His exams will be only 40-45 minutes but you will need to solve a lot.

This class is very easy to get a good grade in due to the amount of things you are assigned and the lack of care in how they are graded. As an EE who has to take this class and will not go into a computer related field the amount of just stuff that there is to do is mind numbing. Every assignment is super tedious.
nope, nope, nope! teacher is not helpful at all

I liked Maruf's teaching style, he has a short explanation, hands-on style. If that's not for you, Maruf isn't your guy. There is a lot of homework and labs, but they are easy grades and they are great prep for exams. Also, your exam score is curved up 30% (up to 100). Easy A if you do the work; would recommend him if you like hands-on teaching.

Avoid this instructor. Classes mainly consist of reading slides (not his own), offering little clarification, and students must learn on their own. Attendance declines quickly due to the lack of value in the lectures. The TAs are helpful and knowledgeable, though, but you won't gain much from the professor. Choose a different section.

This professor is terrible — he reads slides he didn't make, explains nothing, and expects students to teach themselves. The class quickly empties out because the lectures are useless. The only good part is the TAs, who actually know the material and make the tedious labs manageable. You won't learn anything from him — avoid at all costs.

Overall, I really enjoyed Maruf's teaching style. He makes participation apart of the class to see if you are learning properly. He is really friendly in office hours and you can tell he enjoys working with students. Exams are not difficult and he posts past exams which are pretty helpful. Lectures are all accessible online too.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty chill guy, really wants you to understand the content. He can be a little difficult to understand when you start off, but it gets much better throughout the semester. The labs take 1-3 hours to complete, getting worse throughout the semester. Exams aren't bad at all, and he gives out a generous amount of extra credit.

Maruf is probably one of my favorite teachers. His lectures are alright; they are sort of based on the book, so you don't really need to read it to do well. He is very passionate about hardware design, and you can tell that while talking to him. Super fun class. Exams are also graded easily, you only need to get 100 out of 130 points to get an A.

Dr. Maruf is a great professor; very straight to the point and informative, but grading takes some time and lectures are packed full of course material.

Besides that, he is a good professor IF you have good learning habits, show up to class, focus, and take notes.

If this isn't your style of learning, I would recommend Dr. Stoytchev.

Maruf is a nice guy and I think he explains things well, but he is not very accessible outside of class. I've asked him questions in class and he just asks to send an email that he usually just forwards to his TAs. I had a quiz take over a month to get graded after emailing him. Content-wise, the class isn't very hard if you go to lecture everyday
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The tags didn't have many negative things that embody this guy. He is lazy, reads the slides of the previous professors that he didn't create, can't explain, can't grade homework, can't create homework and certainly can't create and grade tests. Those are all done by the TAs.

Hard class! But it will REALLY prepare you for future courses. The TAs (spring of 2022) were fantastic. The lectures were not my style, but I really appreciate the quizzes. The exams reflected the course material (for once). Maruf cares about his students learning, you just have to make the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: While I agree that he does just kind of read off slides and has a bit of an accent, Prof. Ahamed is an increadibly fair grader and will even add points that TAs take off if he thinks they were too harsh (which happened often.) The labs could be a pain but this generally wasn't his fault and was more of a course problem. Overall very happy with him.

Professor Maruf embodies fairness and integrity in teaching, accommodating student needs and maintaining transparent grading. With clear communication, he fosters a supportive learning environment, prioritizing student success and academic standards. Highly recommended.

Has a semi-heavy accent. He was overall just a pretty meh professor. His help hours were never too helpful to me and his lectures felt pointless because we were required to read ahead of time. The class had a lot of work and was mostly about the labs.

Definitely a weed-out class, but even if you have never coded before (like me) you can still do fine. Prof just read off of slides but he is super nice and knowledgeable if you get to talk with him 1 on 1. Labs are the worst and would always take me extra time to complete. Also Notepad++ and cygwin is a baptisms by fire way of learning to code.

Took him for SE 185. He mostly read the slides, but he is a decent lecturer. His assignments could have been organized more. Instructions for labs and quizzes was sometimes unclear. Always curves the exam, even though I never did terribly on them. If you try you'll probably pass.

Just read from the slides. The only reason I got a good grade is due to former knowledge, other students in my class were not as lucky. Labs were horrible, and TAs had no idea what was happening. I would recommend against this professor, if worst comes to worst; get your information on youtube.

He read off slideshows for every lecture but knew his stuff about C. I personally never had experience in C before this class and did just fine. Make sure you do all the homework and really focus on the Labs. The Labs were the hardest part of the class and required more effort than everything else. TAs are your best resource for those.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He isn't too bad with lectures but if I just read from zybook I'm fine. I personally have a background in coding so this course is pretty easy, but I can see it being more difficult for someone with no experience. Keep in mind this course teaches C which isn't the most beginner friendly, but the exams were straightforward and most people did well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ahmed is not exactly a good teacher. This is supposed to be a "beginner" course but it is not at all. I have an A in the class only because I have had experience. All my friends haven't and they are struggling to pass. Do not take this class if you have no experience. You will most likely fail. The lectures teach you nothing.
Can be a bit dull in lectures but is very helpful and responsive when questions arise
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
I would not recommend Maruf for CPR E 281. He just reads off of the slides and is sometimes hard to understand because of his accent. The graduate TAs in this class grade extremely hard, averaging around 60% on homework and quizzes.

While his teaching may not be the best, he records all his lectures and gives a lot of resources to study for exams.
If you can read the slides you too can teach just like this professor

The class is not easy and exams move very quickly so make sure you work fast. However Maruf is always willing to help and homework will prepare you for the exams. Labs can be challenging towards the end of the class and the project is difficult so start early if possible. Very kind professor as well.

I really enjoyed his CPRE 281 course. The lectures were good and he was really good at answering questions. The TAs were knowledgeable and were good at answering questions/troubleshooting. I highly suggest going to every lecture as they go over a lot of material in 50 minutes and it's really helpful for labs/homeworks/quizzes. Overall a great prof

Overall, he is a good professor. I found his lectures to be informative, and he was always willing to answer any questions students had. Participation is important to him. 281 specific: Lots of homework, but the lectures prep you for it nicely. Same goes for the exams. Be quick on the exams, time runs out fast.

He is a mediocre professor at best. He doesn't teach; he relies on the students to teach themselves prior to lectures and he then goes over the material that we just learned using the textbook. I would avoid him at all costs for more advanced coding classes.

Maruf is a great teacher his lectures are good and informative truly cares about the students understanding. Really nice and most importantly even though there is a lot of homework this is one of the few classes where they teach you for your test through all of the assignments, labs and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly, he does not do anything. Does not explain well, slides are not his. Granted you will get an A in his class if you just show up as he throws As at anyone who will come to his class, probably to get better ratings. Some of the reviews here seem like to be done by bots or himself. You will not learn anything from his class & regret later
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Best professor
He's a good professor, took the time to explain small details that most professors expect you to know, and was laid back in class while making exams doable if one does the homework.
Very much willing to help his students and cares about you understanding the material to the best of your capabilities.
Final project is hard, course is easy. Easy A if you work hard on your final project.

Lectures are SO LONG. She goes into depth about each subject, which is nice but sometimes it is hard to pick out what she would find important for exams and quizzes. Her exam reviews are very helpful, but there are some mystery artworks on the quizzes, so you really need to pay attention to details on slide IDs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The course was very well organized, and the lectures were clear and engaging. I also loved that the lectures had captions so I could read what was being said. The weekly modules were broken down into images, handouts, and review lectures before each exam, which made the content easier to learn and study. I really enjoyed this course!

Great lectures! I didn't know if Id like art history, but she made the material interesting. It was a lot of work but the handouts helped and she gave tips on how to do well. I didn't do great on the first exam but met with her online and did much better on the others. She was also really nice.

For each exam, you were required to memorize around 100 photos of art; the name, the artist, and the date it was made. No notes were allowed. 90% of the questions were about the photos, not about actual history. I could tell you why each artwork was made, how, or with what material, but I could NOT memorize each and every one of them.

Had actual reasons to not take tests during her 2 days of time, she did not allow me to make accommodations and failed each test for me. Was told to plan my medical appointments that were planned months in advance around her class because quote "I had the test dates from the start". Taking it again as she is the only option. Tests are 80% of grades

April Eisman was rude to me and others in E-mail's asking for help or accomodations. She allowed no notes during the exams. Exams were primarily memorizing names of artwork. Study guides are practically useless. Unclear about expectations for extra credit, causing me to waste hours working on it for no credit.

I really enjoyed her class and learned a lot! I liked how the class was organized. She has a few lectures each week and provides handouts with images of important art and their info, as well as important vocabulary. The 4 exams were somewhat difficult, but as long as you study what is on the handouts and review the lectures, you'll do fine!

I wouldn't recommend, as this has the most challenging course taken. Must complete every task per module. Grades are consistently muted, and there is no feedback/rubric provided. Communication through emails tends to have little empathy for students. Be prepared to rely heavily on memorization for everything. Lockdown browser with no notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is the nicest professor I've had so far. She actually seems to care how you do in the class and helps you figure out how you can do better. The exams are hard and I hate exams but as long as you take good notes on the lectures then you'll do fine.

Dr. Eisman is a fantastic professor. She was easily the most accessible and kind professor I have ever had at Iowa State. The course is easy to do well in as long as you watch the lectures and take good notes.

Professor Eisman was one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures were super interesting and her passion for the subject really transferred. I took the course online and her tests were all open note. She also organized study guides with the images for each test. The class was really great, and I would highly recommend taking Art History.

While she does expect you to learn a lot of content, it's nice that you are able to for the most part work on it at your own pace. Sometimes it's frustrating with her exams because you do have a small timeframe and lockdown browser, but overall it's not the worse class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have the option of any other teacher then her then please take that option. Absolutely the worst teacher I have ever had here. You have 3 days per week to get through a few hours of online lectures, needing to memorize dozens of pictures per section and her exams are ridiculously long. Half the subjects on the exams aren't in study guides.

There is no feedback given for any of the written assignments, and there is no rubric provided ahead of time, so the grading is arbitrary. I asked Eisman about the grading of one of my assignments and received a rude, passive-aggressive response. You only get 3.5 days to do the whole module every week with all the lectures and assignments.

Eisman was my favorite professor last semester! She was so clear in her lectures, had open-book tests, and made the class generally enjoyable. I would take her again in a heartbeat and really enjoyed the other elements of the class too! Take her, please!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was an online class. The lectures were interesting and it was well organized. There were images posted online and study guides for every lecture. I had no problem meeting with her when I had questions and found her helpful and encouraging. There is a lot covered, but after the first exam, I knew exactly what to study. Great class!

She does not care about your grades and blames you that you don't understand the tough material. Making the test cumulative is not fair to memorize over 160 imges (name, time period, date, place, and artist), plus vocab and history. She is not helpful if you want to meet outside of class because she will only meet at a certain time.

The best way to describe this professor is that she made me get an account for this site because I had such a bad experience. It felt as if the professor cared little for students, refusing all emails directly from students and only communicating through ta's. Never had office hours for students either. I did well only because of constant studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was an online class so never really met her but her tests are absurd, her videos contain so much information that could easily be deemed as important but not even 2/3 of the video material ends up on the actual exam so it's very difficult to know exactly what to study. memorize dates and the names of the work for her art hist tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far the best class I've ever taken in my college career! There was no 'textbook' but a few smaller books we read throughout the semester. The class focused theory and how it relates to art and visual culture. The course was intense but extremely rewarding and definitely opened my eyes to a lot of issues in society.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Magnificent class! Definitely one of my favorite professors at ISU. Her course was centered around lectures and a final group project.

Professor Eisman is really great! This course is a standard art history survey and so there is memorization involved in the tests. The class is quite large and so every class was a lecture, but you can tell she is very passionate about what she is teaching which made each class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff but her teaching style is very old school. She will make you memorize dates and who wrote the book when, which in my opinion is useless. No one wants to hire a robot. She will make you do the exam like its 1940. Questions with answers that will test your memory and not your understanding of the topics. Wont recommend

She is very knowledgable. Don't get the text books, you won't need them. Everything on the tests comes from notes you take in lecture so go to class. Do as she says and make flash cards to study for exams, it really helps. She doesn't want you to fail, she even dropped our lowest test score at the end of the semester.

This is one of the most difficult classes i have taken in my life. What boils my blood is that ISU MFA GD program does not enable you to create an amazing portfolio. Its extremely dependent on literature and very less on practical work. This course is one of the 5 others history classes that you have to take and its not worth all the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: April is my favorite teacher at Iowa State! Her class for both ArtH280 and ArtH395 are amazing. ArtH280 is all about the tests and that's it. Just go to class, read the book, and study the slide IDs and you'll do just fine. I love all of her lectures and actually want to go to class. So interesting!
Ok, not great.
Fairly easy course if you pay attention. I never touched the book, just went to class and filled out and studied the handouts and got good grades. Interesting class.
Fantastic course, fantastic teacher! Dr. Eisman's courses are challenging but fair. Put the time and effort in and you'll do fine. Very interesting course.
always knew what to expect on a test, prof made subject easy to understand...
Memorize EVERYTHING she says.  Everything is fair game.  Also, make sure to study.  All of her projects should be over-the-top in terms of quality in order to achieve maximum "excellence points."

Dr. Eisman is very good teacher, knowledgable and wanting students to succeed. Her lectures are engaging, well planed. My only complaint is that for class projects she is not always clear about her expectations. Her tests are also difficult at first. You have to understand her teaching style before you can do well in the class. that takes some time

She was really into the class and made it more interesting.  I felt she was very open minded realizing that not everyone is an art history major and tried to make things a little more fun.  I kind of wish she would place less emphasis on the architectural aspect of the course as no one taking it was an architecture major.

Really passionate teacher.I often fell asleep,but if you don't, she tells you the answers for the handout, just memorize and pay attention to her and you should be able to get a good grade. if you don't study or pay attention- this class can be quite difficult. but she is a good teacher.

She makes lectures very interesting with GOOD powerpoints and handouts. She really likes class participation, which in a lecture of 200+ I found more distracting from the material. The tests were very straight forward and clear, with no surprises. She stated very clearly what was going to be on each test.

I am usually terrible at art history due to teaching styles. April doesn't just talk about a work of art but goes into detail, talkes about the time period and what was going on. I really enjoyed her class. She is extremely nice and knows what she is teaching. I would recomend a class with her!

I had her for Art H 495. Very effective teaching style. Class attendence is not required, but I recommend it. It's not hard to get an A if you can make it to every class, pay attention, and memorize a decent number of slide IDs.

New this year. Lots of 'in class' and 'in group' work. Lots of slide ID and in class material coverage. Tests aren't horribly hard, but very random in the way information is reguested. You'll be asked to recall facts that were mentioned only once and did not particularly relate to the artist.

Angela Koppes was not a great instructor for this course. She was unfamiliar of the course schedule as well as the project deliverables multiple times throughout the course of the semester. She would also go on lengthy tangents about her personal life, intending to relate them back to coursework, but she failed every time, and instead wasted class.
I have PTSD from Angela Koppes. Traumatizing class and person.

Honestly not as bad as people put her out to be. At times very passive-aggressive, but when Jamie's section is full, do not worry about having angela. Class was very homework-heavy, with 1-2 assignments a week.

I had a very disappointing experience with this professor. She often came across as rude and condescending when students asked questions. She acts like they care about students' success, but it feels very performative, more for appearances than genuine support. Feedback was dismissive or sarcastic toned; choose a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Students are expected to make little to no mistakes, regardless of the teacher's self-proclaimed forgiveness. Work given is confusing and directionless, with the expectation of flawless results. Whether on the professor's or the TA's behalf, the commentary was unhelpful and had no corrective description. Expect frustration and an affected GPA
She could care less about you or your situation if you have the choice of another professor do it. Many rude remarks and demeaning over email.

Very nitpicky grader! Class was an introductory graphics course but was graded as if everyone was familiar with the programs. Angela often provided feedback that wasn't helpful in any regard, such as telling students to "refer back to the assignment's instructions" when it was clearly apparent that what was provided was hard to interrupt.

It is not helpful when looking for feedback or what we need to change. Very little answer is received when asking about the assignments, and she just says to look on Canvas. She is looking for a very specific design for each assignment, yet she encourages students to be creative and think outside of the box. I would not recommend her.

I would not recommend taking Angela's class. She knows a lot about design, but does not know how to effectively teach her knowledge. She is a tough grader and gives little feedback to help students revise their work. She also has a very specific design eye and loves it when students can design in her style but not when students find their own.

Angela is very disrespectful and our entire class is having problems with her. There is almost 100 of us. She is rude and unprofessional and makes me want to pull my hair out. I love design, but I am losing my passion for it with the constant criticism. All of the other professors are great and I get along easily with them, so this is just her.

Angela is knowledgeable in everything interior design, especially when it is code related, but is very unprofessional to students. She can be very unorganized, and the negative impacts of this affect students directly. Grading is tough but it seems we are set up for failure as assignments are explained poorly.
Would highly recommend taking Angela for any class at Iowa State. She gives great feedback and you can tell she cares about her students. As long as you work hard and try your best, you'll be fine.
Angela has been one of the sweetest professors I have ever had. Her love for Design and her students make them want to do better. Very good with software. Very kind and gives good feedback
Very helpful when it comes to answering questions. Knowledgeable about the material and provides good real-life in the workplace details about her own experience in the design world!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Most down to earth professor I have ever had. Extremely understanding of difficult situations and willing to make adjustments to work around your situation. She is one of the professors that will inspire you to be more like her. She respects her students like her own family. Truly an amazing professor to work with and learn from!!

I took this course in the fall 2025 semester, and all the bad reviews are true. In the final month, he went off the deep end. Prof A turned into Professor Alexander, and he also changed his appearance. The reason was that he accused everyone in all sections of using AI on open-note quizzes and exams. Genuinely, please don't take this course!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Accused everyone of cheating with no evidence whatsoever and fearmongered everyone into "confessing" their academic misconduct. I advise not taking this class (at least with Professor Alexander).

His lecture slides are complex and he constantly contradicts himself. He claimed his entire class was cheating with no backing and required students to fess up if they were cheating. He also was extremely rude to a friend of mine and cussed in emails to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class moves at a very fast paced. Bi-weekly exams. For it being an introductory class it was harder than usual. He tried to get his students to fall in love with philosophy, but I just hate it now. The topics were confusing, talking about some AI having moral personhood? What? The exam questions weren't hard just confusingly written.

When asking questions, I'd get more confused than before. Lots of quizzes and exams and literally nothing on them was ever taught in class or in readings. He also lost it near the end and accused everyone in every section of cheating and threatened to turn you in unless you wrote a detailed email on how you cheated even if you were innocent...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice and funny professor, but classes move quick so make sure to stay on top of your work. Attendance is mandatory but only worth a little bit amount of points. The tests used to be open notes, but due to people cheating, the professor (obviously) made us take the tests in class. These are pretty easy though, as long as you study.

Don't listen to any ratings from before 2025. Attendance is now mandatory, quizzes are not worth points, and tests are in-class, on lockdown browser, and closed-note. A good chunk of the readings are written by him and hard to understand. He accused every student of using AI with no evidence and fear mongered to get confessions so he could report.

Avoid this class after fall 2025; the syllabus is being completely revised to make it much harder for an introductory course. Exams used to be at home open note, but Exams/quizzes will now be in-class, no aids, and monitored with a lockdown browser. Attendance is mandatory, and there will be no extra credit options. Consider taking another course.

Don't listen to any of the reviews made before November 2025. He found out people in the class were using AI to cheat and kind of flipped. All the exams and quizzes except for midterm and final used to be open note, but not anymore. Attendance is now mandatory and tests are locked down. He shaved his head and changes his name. Not the same prof.

This class was tough, and Dr. Alexander moves at a VERY quick pace. We had exams every 2-3 weeks. Essay questions were on the midterm and finals. He was kinda boring (but the subject was kinda boring too) and I struggled to focus in this class. I did well overall so I can't complain too much. Just be prepared for long and muddled readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is awful and the most boring class I have ever been too. He is a nice prof who really cares about philosophy but all the material makes zero sense whatsoever. He grades super hard even if you think you know what you are doing and feel good about it he will still give u a 5/20 on a test.

In a 1:1 meeting with this professor, I was cussed and yelled at, held my grades hostage, and had my intelligence berated and insulted for 30 minutes. The pleasant  attitude and good class material hides a deeply emotional, condescending, and unprepared professor. I sincerely hope that no one has the misfortune of disagreeing with this professor.

Professor Alexander is super funny and really nice!! The class isn't too difficult as long as you keep up with the readings and stay on top of the material to make sure you're understanding the concepts. I loved this class, and it definitely made me want to take more philosophy courses in the future. Also lots of opportunities for extra credit.

Prof. Alexander is great and cares about philosophy, but I wouldn't recommend this class as a Gen Ed. He writes most of the material himself, and the quizzes and exams are very tough, even being open-note. Preparing for the written midterm and final is stressful. He offered up to 10% EC for TopHat questions, which bumped me from an A- to an A.
Great Person and a great teacher

Fun guy but I absolutely hated his class. The questions on exams and quizzes are open ended and subjective from person to person. For an intro class, the material and lectures were difficult. I think his goal was to get the class to fall in love with philosophy but it did the exact opposite for me. This class is the reason I now hate philosophy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Alexander was a great professor; be prepared for some corny jokes. When I took the class, after each module, we had to write an essay to show our understanding of the unit. There were also quizzes that were open-note. He would write the papers that we were to read, I thought that was pretty cool. Pretty easy class if you pay attention in lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved Alexander as a person, but I did not enjoy the class. All tests were open-note but still difficult. Be sure you know what the test covers before taking it. The readings are "required" but you can get by without reading them, it may help for the tests though.

has an infectious attitude about the content he teaches. is willing to work with students if they need to miss assignments due to extenuating circumstances, and overall just a fun person to be around.

I absolutely despised taking this course. This course was way harder than needed, considering it was an introductory class. He gives multiple quizzes every module, only three to four points. Missing one question automatically means getting a 70%. His questions are either difficult to understand or could be interpreted differently. Do not recommend.

He is a good guy with a fun personality, but the class is extremely difficult. you can understand all the concepts and still do terrible on quizzes and exams. all the questions on them are very misleading and open ended. A better way to do the class would be writing papers because then you would be able to show your understanding better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had quizzes and an exam per module. His lectures, at times, can be funny and entertaining. He genuinely cares about his students and listens to the feedback that he receives. This class was harder than it needed to be, but if you work hard enough to succeed, you can do it.

I loved this class and Professor Alexander. The course material was a little tricky at times, but his lectures are super helpful (and entertaining!) and he's glad to answer any questions and encourages discussion. There is a lot of assigned readings but they are not always necessary. I hope to have Prof Alexander again in the future!

I enjoyed this class. He is a smart and caring guy. The material can get complicated. Be prepared to go to class and take thorough notes. You will not do well if you don't pay attention. It is particularly difficult for an intro class but very entertaining, and I learned a lot. You have to be able to understand abstract ideas and think critically.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very kind and interesting to listen to. Attendance really can help your grade if you struggle on quizzes or tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor. The class was a bit tougher than it needed to be. A lot of the questions were open-ended but were multiple-choice. A lot of reading. The curve is helpful. A very interesting class that I think back to, but if you're not interested in philosophy and just looking for genfor ed, I would recommend against this class. Lectures are

Taking 201 with Prof. Alexander was so fun! He's passionate about philosophy and loves engaging students in discussions about the material. He even gave us a week off in the middle of the semester to recharge! Overall a fantastic prof, the class material isn't easy but he does a good job explaining it in lectures and answering questions.

Professor Alexander is a great teacher but does not know how to use Canvas properly. I cannot express the number of points I lost because he either did not publish the assignment or put assignment due dates later or earlier than expected. It is extremely frustrating that he does not fix this even when it has been clearly communicated.

Kind professor for the most part, however, the exam questions were very confusing. I often found that they could be interpreted in multiple different ways. Additionally, do not ask the professor to round your grade for this class, he will say no!

Overall really cool prof. About four quizzes, 1 one page paper, and 1 test every 2 weeks (all online). Everything is open notes. Pretty easy tests if you do the tophat and quizzes. Attendance counts so go to class and you'll be good.
Great teacher but exam questions are hard to understand.

If you want to do well in this class, you need to read and participate. This class is a weed-out class and is definitely difficult. This professor is amazing and I have a lot of respect for him. Is very understanding and accommodating. If you have a question he gives a detailed answer. Overall I would love to take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very nice guy and wants everyone to be successful but goes way to in-depth and makes his lectures confusing. Tests are very hard! even with notes, tophat, quizzes, slides, and a tutor still failed almost every test. When asking him questions and saying you are confused he says you would have to be a genius to understand philosophy.

He is extremely knowledgeable in philosophy but for it being an intro class and someone who knows nothing about the subject, the class was difficult.  The professor overall made me uncomfortable, lecture slides are confusing to understand if you don't attend class.  You can try asking him for help if you are lost but be prepared to be ridiculed.

He's a really chill professor. If you don't go to lecture then you won't understand anything that is going on. He makes slideshows that don't make sense unless you go to the class. Most of the readings are pointless and hard to understand. You have to buy tophat so you can get points for attendance which really helps your grade. No extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Alexander is by far the best professor Ive had at ISU. His lectures are very fun and engaging, and he really cares for his students. Attendance is taken through tophat, theres multiple quizzes online every werk, and exams are online after every module. Fun class, and not too challenging so long as you attend class regularly.
One of the best teachers i have ever had. Fun lectures, challenging material, and hes a really nice guy.

He created an environment in class where he made me feel bad + stupid for asking clarification questions about complicated philosophical ideas (ideas that are more difficult to understand than some of my engineering classes, might I add). I did not feel comfortable coming to class. He's very smart, but the environment in class was toxic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, top hat is taken for attendance, not accuracy but it affects your grade. Lectures are put online after class. Quizzes before every class. If struggling, ask for help! He is caring and wants his students to succeed. He is super passionate about the subject matter but this is not an easy elective at all. Not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rock solid philosophy professor

Lets his belief get in the way of grading. He very hard headed, if its not his way then he wont pay attention to it. When someone stumps him, he moves on instead of looking for an answer or giving one. Is very annoying and laughs at his own jokes in lecture, which usually arent that funny. Very tough grader with everything you do in the course
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Alexander has a great personality which makes the class enjoyable. Does not require a textbook but there our weekly quizzes that can either help or hurt your grade. The exams are very hard and cover all the quizzes and power point notes he presents and they are on canvas. This class is not an easy elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Alexander is a good professor and tries to be as interactive as he can. However, if you are taking this class as an elective, I would not recommend taking his class. Lecture notes are not always helpful. Exams require you to study everything in depth and put in more effort than some of my engineering classes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Alexander is really good at teaching Philosphy because he makes the class interactive and fun. Many of the discussions in class are engaging and he encourages students to speak out if there is a topic that doesn't make sense. Overall, he is a motivated professor that make your tuition money worth it.

Prof. Alexander is a funny guy who very clearly loves philosophy and teaching it. This class took some effort though. Especially on tests. Not so much effort that passing should be a concern, but if you want an A you'll have to put in some time. Attendance is very important. Do not skip class unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: A pleasure to have in class. Joking aside, Alexander uses powerpoints and TopHat for his lectures. Attendance is graded and is taken through TopHat as well. There is a quiz every class that tends to be about 5-10 questions over the reading that you have to do on blackboard the night before. Makes lectures fun and interesting, you wont fall asleep!

Excellent professor in a good class. The notes are a little hard to follow but if you write down what he is saying more than what he has on the slides, you should be fine. Witty, funny, interesting to talk to outside of class. 10/10 would recommend for this or other classes.

The readings are really dense, but he doesn't require a textbook which is nice. The power points are put online and are very helpful when taking the biweekly online quizzes, which are difficult if you haven't reviewed the material beforehand but not bad if you have. It is clear what will be on test, strongly recommend studying the power points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures are very good for preparing students for tests. He did not require a textbook because he wanted to save students money which is considerate. He assigns nightly reading quizzes. I find philosophy to be very interesting other people may not but he does try to make it interesting for the majority of students.

Prof. Alexander is unexpectedly hilarious and really interesting to talk to. His lectures do a great job of explaining some of the harder concepts from the book, which you will need to buy & use for pre-class quizzes. His exams are very straightforward and there are no surprises - the study guides tells you exactly what'll be on them. Great prof.

I took three classes with Dr. Alexander and can't say enough good things about him. Yes, you will work your butt off if you want a good grade, but he will help every step of the way if you ask and are willing to do that work.  If you love philosophy you will not regret having him!

His beliefs usually got in the way of grading. As he put it "Learning philosophy is a skill" If you had an opposing view, he would come back at it with his knowledge. It was his way or the highway. Tests were also too hard for an intro class.

Took this class to fulfill a Gen Ed and thought it would be much harder than it really is. Dr. Alexander is a great professor to have, especially with an intro course. It isn't required to go to class but is almost imperative to go because it is tricky info and Dr. Alexander is able to explain it very well. Also, he doesn't post notes online.

I just took this class to fill a humanities requirement, and it was the class I enjoyed most this semester. The concepts can be challenging at times, but he was happy to help me during his office hours. I only opened the book to get ideas for the final paper, and averaged a B+ on his tests. He gives out study guides with all the test questions.

Friendly, kind, empathetic, and very knowledgeable. The class was discussion-based, assigned a meaningful presentation/paper project. Tests were standard essay-based tests. The class was incredibly fun and useful and I would prefer him over any other philosophy teacher I have had so far.

Very challenging. The book is useless for the class because his lectures tell you everything. That is if you understand them. He does not help really when you ask question. And if you ask about something you guys just went over just to clarify but get the concept wrong he comes off as very mean. Test are hard class avg. was usually D , D- range.

Very enthusiastic and engaging in class. I would hate to have to get into a debate with him. I would echo what others said about his exams: they are very challenging. Don't expect comments in your blue book. You receive a score on the front, and that is all.
Pretty Good!
I learned a ton in this class. You'll definitely want to do the readings, though.  He does a great job of addressing the topics and questions.
Brilliant. clear, systematic, very helpful. He puts a lot of effort into making the lectures useful. There were a couple of papers and a couple of essay-based tests.
Tests are way too hard for an intro class

his scalar intensities course is an htc course i'd highly recommend to everyone for an easy A, and all you do is sit through 2.5 hr lectures and sometimes do a 1 or 2 short write-ups, and a final physical model/3000 word essay/drawing worth 75% of your grade.

Very solid class and professor. Hybrid with attendance only mandatory for the 4 discussions. Responses are easy to write, and lectures are fun to watch and interesting! Highly recommend, especially for the HAC requirement for Architecture.
For ARCH 3210, you don't have to attend every class; there are no quizzes and no exams. As long as you complete the assignments and show up for your discussions, you'll earn 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Highly recommend! The class is set up into 5 modules, completed on your own time by a due date. He is very understanding and tries his best to make the class manageable. For each module, you watch lectures, write a 300-word summary for 4, and show up to a 30-minute discussion. There is one essay at the end of the year, but that is your final.
Easy class and very interesting at that

Prof. Gleeson's ARCH321 is a hybrid course, with attendance only mandatory for four in-person discussion sessions. The course allowed work to be completed on students' time, with modules open for about 2 weeks each. Overall, the course was laid back and interesting. Gleeson's teaching style made me want to complete my work.

Hybrid course. Watch lectures and write one page summary for assignments. 4 discussions during the semester only time you need to show up, don't need to participate though. One final paper at the end 1000 words. Easy extra credit also. Super interesting and fun professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have ever taken, and it was because Dr. Mullis was the professor. I retook it with another professor and got an A.

Hands down the worst professor I have ever had, heavy workload for a 0-credit class. The tests are ridiculous and have content we have never looked at before. He does not teach and just talk for a minute at the start of class, and the rest is "free time", which means we just did the class work by ourselves. Please do not take a class with him.

Tough professor, but he is understanding and very helpful, if you struggle to understand a topic he can break it down extremely easily. I wish there were more clarity on exams so we could succeed, thats my only complaint.

He does not take constructive criticism from the mandatory semester review surveys seriously. This is a PASS/FAIL course, and I don't see the point in him going out of his way to make it more difficult than it has to be. Told me that while taking past exams will improve my exam scores, it doesn't 'improve understanding'.
Says practice exams hinder learning ability and problem solving as an engineer

Not good professor. Straight up does not know how to teach, just works through problems on the screen in bad handwriting and he can't even explain why he's doing the things he does. And he takes forever to get the test back, which are way harder than anything he goes over in class.
He takes a long time to grade, and has a harsh criteria that honestly doesn't make sense.

Homeworks were easy to get 100% on as they were graded on completion... However, the final group project, worth like 50% of our grade, was graded unreasonably hard. After a full semester of ridiculously easy grading, no one was prepared for how harsh he would be, and most people failed it. He graded it late, too, so there was nothing we could do.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough exams, but he is very relaxed on grading. His office hours have been amazing. He is new so he is still learning how to structure the courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mullis is a knowledgeable and awesome person. But, you can't expect everyone to remember every topic from all the Calcs and Chems. A big reason people struggle in this course is because there are no lectures reintroducing previous topics, and for some reason differential equations is not a pre req, even though most of the course is that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mullis seems like a nice person, which is the only reason I rate him a 2/5 instead of 1/5. I would recommend avoiding his section because he does not adequately prepare students for the extremely difficult exams he writes. In CHE 2100, he also did not seem to explain the material clearly enough for students to fully understand it.

He is not a good teacher, the class filled out the anonymous surveys rating him and his class, at the start of one class he took the responses and had the things he could improve on the board. THIS GUY then went through and proceeded to explain why he wasn't going to improve on any of those things. THIS WAS FOR A 0 CREDIT CLASS.
A 3 credit intro level course with 6 exams, extremely difficult. Averages in 40s, highs in 70s. Dr. Mullis is a really chill awesome guy, but I would never take another course with him.

Every other week was an exam, and on top of this, professionalism essays and a multi-phase project. He changed due dates constantly. There were multiple times where he changed the prompt for the essay a few days before it was due and I had to rewrite all of it. DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE A CHOICE

CHE 2100 by itself is not a hard class, but somehow he made it difficult. It's flipped, and I understand why it is. However, Dr. Mullis was not able to handle the flipped format. He's a decent guy but a bad professor. He did not use class time effectively to go over problems. Lectures were a waste of time. I did most of my learning independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Mullis is a nice guy, to be honest. The class is the 5 exams in the 4-phase project that stress you out in the sophomore year. He didn't know what he taught (I have to explain what I did in the exam about my solution), so he can regrade it. The class basically, he copied the answer from his previous note, and I'm kinda sure everyone can do that.

Adam is extremely hard to learn from. I needed one single point more to pass his class and he did not allow this. He doesn't teach during class, but it's still mandatory. Even with one absence to attend the career fair that was communicated in advance, my professionalism score was 0.5/8. His "flipped classroom" teaching is not effective. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Adam Mullis is a teacher that doesn't teach. He just talks at you and does problems in front of the class and expects learning from that. He uses a flipped classroom (You do the learning by yourself and just come to class for "practice") which makes no sense in an entry level course. He doesn't offer any form of retakes and is overly strict.

Dr. Mullis is a nice person, but I did not find his teaching style very effective. The course structure felt disorganized, with six exams including the final, a heavy project, and many homework assignments. The material often did not align with the exams, leaving me feeling unprepared.

Professor Mullis was a new addition to a faculty, but his class was extra difficult for no reason at all. The classroom format is “flipped”, so in essence you basically teach yourself the material. 5 Exams which were super difficult especially at the start of the semester, and a huge group project that is way too much work for a 2000 level course.

Mullis was brand new this semester, so he has a long way to go. He's very nice and tries his best to be helpful. Lectures weren't very useful since most time was used writing out problems, not explaining. There was an exam every 2 weeks-ish, and he had to shorten them for people to finish. Read the book and go to TA office hours and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The way he writes questions baffles me.
This class is pretty much all reading and discussions. So. Much. Reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was so weird. The lectures were split up into 6 different sub lectures and was impossible to find what you needed. The quizzes are due at 12 in the afternoon on Friday. It was such a weird time for me that I couldn't keep track. Probably is a good guy but I was not a fan of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you have a lot of notes heavy courses. Every week he assigns around 3-7 lectures that you have to watch/take notes on which are sometimes 100 or more slides and information heavy. There are also weekly discussion posts which are due at 9 pm and quizzes which are due at noon. Do not recommend unless you have a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took SOC220 freshman year and have been working for Dr. Hallam as a TA for 3 years. Genuinely the sweetest man and cares a lot about his students, reach out and he will respond within minutes. He may not be the most tech-savvy, but he is a WEALTH of knowledge and is very passionate about sustainability. Easy and interesting course.

Worst Gen Ed to take at Iowa State. You're better off taking some random history class than taking this class. The quizzes and final are annoying af to take. Grading is weird and no specifications for answers. After the 4th week, there are constant Econ and engineering questions and it makes you question whether this is a sociology class.

Tech illiterate turbo-boomer. Have an online quiz? Good luck. Lectures? Prerecorded and over an hour long, but in separate videos because of course. Video meeting? good luck getting in because he doesn't know how to use zoom, WebEx, etc. I have literally taken calc courses that are less tedious than this.

He was an okay professor but he gets sidetracked during class. There are 100+ lecture slides per class because they include the bullet point by bullet point animations so it is impossible to print out and take notes on during lecture. The math part was very tedious and he sped through it during lecture when it was a major topic of the first exam.

Don't listen to these low ratings for SOC 220. Hallam is a good teacher and this class is joke level easy. Quizzes and exams are almost verbatim the practice quizzes and exams, yet kids endlessly moan and complain because they have to do basic multiplication (middle school level) and have study for once in their life. Show up, listen, study. Easy A

Took class online. I was .04 off, one decimal point off from getting the answer correct and he would not accept it. This was due to his lack of specifications as he did not specify how many decimal points to round too. He is unprofessional, inconsiderate, and very strict. Rude professor and would never take again.

Literally worst class I have ever taken. so boring and non of the lectures were truly applicable to the homework. Definitely wasted my tuition signing up for this course. His jokes are annoying and seem dialogued. Easy class tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Arne is a good professor. He tends to get distracted often, but with good reason (usually discussion of a student's question). He teaches the first 5 weeks of the class. There's some tedious math, but it's pretty repetitive. The portion as a whole seemed very repetitive and hardly applies to the remainder of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought it would be an interesting class, but in reality, 90% of it was a math class. Quizzes did not give enough time to do all of the calculations. Professor was not very understanding.

Global Sustainability, more like finance and engineering. This class has taught me little, and takes up a ton of time and effort. If you are taking this online for your international perspectives class, don't. There is an in depth discussion board every week, and 2 hour quizzes every 2 weeks. Not much online help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Online, this class is a breeze. You needn't even read the material or watch the lectures he posts to pass with flying colors. He grades based on group discussion posts and quizzes you can take from home. Just use the study guides to search the answers during the quizzes (which can be lengthy) and you'll be golden.

Signed up for anthropology 211, got Social Change 2-something. They said all you'd need was high school algebra, but they had us solving econ-level and engineering problems by week 5. Would not recommend.
A bit unorthodox in his syllabus (long division by hand?) but a great teacher and every engaging.  You might catch him riding his bike to campus in a suit if he still does that.
Very good teacher, I learned a lot in the class.  Demands a lot from you in homework.  Wonder if he needs a grad student?
very knowledgable and makes it fun. would recommend
Great prof.  Makes hard material seem easy, and it's never hard to pay attention in class.  Great handouts (don't even need the book), and homework prepares you well for the tests.
Energetic and made class fun.  Exceptional handouts help understanding the material easier.
very good teacher, this class has alot of homework. Mr. Hallam has an effective teaching style, he makes difficult material easy. You MUST attend lecture and do your homework. Don't by the $150 book.
Very helpful, but econ is just boring by nature.

If you can avoid her, do it. She teaches this like a 300 level course and it's a 100 by the way. She teaches this like we already have a couple years of experience in this field. Is she nice? Yes she is. She is knowledgeable as well but it is very difficult to understand the material she teaches. Exams somewhat difficult. Hard to study.

Her guidelines on the final project weren't very clear in Canvas, so going to the TAs' office hours was helpful. Also, make sure to read the textbook because I learned more from that than her lectures. Be prepared for lots of short-answer questions on the exam too.
Likes to swear at students
Class is heavy in memorization and vocab. Not the best at explaining topics in full depth.

Dr. Anderson is very nice and cares about students, but she isn't a strong lecturer. The class is hard to follow sometimes, but it is still easy to do well. The test review sessions were very helpful. Dr. Anderson and the TAs are easily accessible for questions and help.

The final project was so disorganized, the content and directions were very vague. She is very passionate about soil but is not great at explaining the content and expects everyone to know what she is talking about. She is also very hard to get ahold of.

Terrible professor, do not take this class if you don't have to. She is terrible at teaching, tends to ramble and the slides are not helpful at all. I received a 60/140 on the final project which is unfairly low in my opinion, her criteria for it was vague and unclear. She is sweet but don't let it fool you, this class is taught like a 300 level.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course felt disorganized, with everything being very vague. The slideshows are not super helpful, as you need to be in the lecture to understand them. The lectures feel like a long tangent, making it hard to know what material is necessary to know. Dr. Anderson was nice and passionate about the subject, but not a strong lecturer or instructor.

I did not enjoy taking Amber's class. I found her tests to be ridiculous and it felt like she did not focus enough on material that would be on tests. Every time I took an exam, I felt surprised by what was on it and ill prepared. Get ready to feverishly review the material. The only good thing she did for me was round up my grade.

Was probably the worst professor I've ever had. Didn't teach me anything and was very disorganized. I didn't try very hard but did try very hard on the final project and still got a terrible grade because I left a couple graphs off. Would never take any class with her ever again.

Professor Anderson was very kind and willing to assist with exam questions.  Plenty of discussions and assignments to increase grade percentage.  Be ready for plenty of short answer questions and a lot of projects.  Everything was very beneficial and I really enjoyed the material she had in store for students.

Probably the most difficult professor to work with I've ever had.  Extremely disorganized, lectures are hard to understand and goes on a lot of tangents during the lecture.  She is very hard to get a hold of, especially during the last month of classes.  I do not recommend this professor's classes.

Took this class intending to use it as an easy gen ed. Professor is very nice, but the course was unnecessarily difficult and required a lot of work outside of class. Wound up dropping the class as my grades were slipping in my core courses trying to keep up with all of the work required for this. Would hazard against taking AGRON342 with her.
My first and only C in agronomy; I don't understand how she can make a 100 level class harder than a 300+ level class. Do not take this class with her if you do not have to.

One of my favorite professors to have ever taken a class with at Iowa State. There was always an abundance of resources available for concepts I may have needed some extra help on. The teaching style of this class definitely helped me learn the most and also have it stick for use in future semesters. Definitely recommend taking classes with her.

Take this class online; being in person was pointless except for getting participation points. Amber is extremely helpful in-person but not so much in an email. It takes a while for her to get back to you. She also adds way too much to the class that is not needed.

Amber is extremely knowledgeable about her field, and it was obvious she wanted every one of her students to succeed. However, I would not take World food issues with her again. Compared to other sections, we had a ton of additional and unnecessary work. She could also be impatient, and rude to students or TAs who asked a simple question.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Agronomy 342 is a class about world food issues, but we talked about food issues maybe 1/3 of the time. The majority of the lectures are unrelated to the matter. However, if you need to take this class, you need to show up for attendance points, just do homework. It's not like you learn anything in this class that's relevant anyways.
I took the online version of this class. Was not run well and didn't really enjoy the class. Not really any textbook but you're supposed to have a ton memorized.

In this class, you will have no clue what is going on the entire semester. you pretty much talk to your peers the whole time about topics that are completely irrelevant. She doesn't know how to teach which is why there is nothing learned in this class. don't take the class if it's not required.
Does not teach you anything relevant to exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Attendance is crucial but so is learning almost everything outside class. I have never studied so much to end up feeling so unprepared. Try to get another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Slides of presentations are posted but they usually just have a heading or minimal information. You need to go to class. I started off on the wrong foot because the book was labeled as required but was told on the first day that it wasn't required. Had trouble returning it. Lectures lean too heavy on participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For this class, she doesnt require a book and it is a project based class. It is quite easy especially if you participate in class. Shes not strict at all and you get to choose what your projects are based on so its something you are interested in.

Most points are in class participation points, discussion based, so if you don't enjoy that, you won't like the class (I didn't). No real lectures or notes, group project and individual project you research on your own related to food issues. I did not feel like I learned anything I didn't already know, and discussions weren't engaging to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: No actual lecture material to take notes over. I don't feel like I gained anything from this class. No tests. Papers, in class group assignments, outside lectures, food service activity, and a couple projects. Fair grader. Was really hoping to learn more in this class... was really let down. Wouldn't recommend ESPECIALLY if its not required.

She's a good professor and clearly knows what she's talking about. But she likes to go off on tangents and her notes really stop being helpful after the first exam. Gives little to no extra credit so the few exams and homework really matter for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amber is a great person and is very knowledgeable about soils, however, is incredibly difficult to follow in class. She goes off on tangents, her slides have no information actually on them and quizzes are terribly unfair. As an out-of-state student, I really struggled following all the "basic" material that she expects you to walk in knowing.

Amber is a decent person, but her lectures are horrible and she often gets off topic easily or goes from presenting power point slides to scribbling illegibly on some piece of paper that nobody can read. She also is not always very friendly when someone asks a question during class.

Amber's lectures can sometimes get confusing, but she is always happy to clarify by explaining the topic a different way. She posts old tests or has review sessions that give you a good idea of what will be on the upcoming test. If you show up to lecture and pay attention, it is pretty easy to get an A or B in the class.
100 level class, she can increase difficulty to 300 level. Confusing lecturing with Confusing lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amber is very disorganized and the class is full of in-class assignments and discussion-based work. Dont take this course with her if you dont have to.

The teacher gives very disorganized lectures that makes it harder to learn. The tests are pretty challenging and although not a very hard class in terms of content it is a lot harder then it needs to be.

Best thing I can say is go to the study sessions because they will save your test score. The lectures are not clear as to what should be important for you to remember. She knows what she's talking about but the class is too confusing. Got to clas though because every once in a while there's an attendance question, and those add up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Always open to help you but she expects you to put in the work. World Food Issues is an excellent class that makes you think about the food system in new ways. Amber wants you to express your opinion and then broaden your mind. If you do not like participating in class then this class might be difficult for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures, but the grading scale and its weight are kind of ridiculously disproportionate. A decent chunk of your grade will be from in-class participation activities. This class is all group-based, FYI.

Anderson is an excellent lecturer. I enjoyed learning from her in Agron 154. She has encouraged me personally to "dig deep" into the understandings of soil. I plan to work as many of her classes into my schedule for the remainder of my time here at ISU.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you go to class then the material in the notes will be on the exams.  She will even point out material in class that she wants you to know for the test.  She will answer questions late at night if you email her and she will help if you have problems with her homework. Easy points for attendance given.

She doesn't really help you and during her "lecture" she just asks a bunch of questions without really telling you anything. She just stands there.  I hardly learned a thing from her.  She's horrible. Very confusing.  Doesn't explain anything very well.   Avoiding taking her class if possible.

Her thought process is all over the place and she is very unorganized. If you want a more structured class or for your questions to be answered concisely, I would not recommend taking a class with her. The classes can be easy if you attend and do the work.

This class was horrible because of the professor. She assumes everyone is a farmer and she doesn't even teach anything. Her TA's do all the work and they're not easy graders. I thought this would be an interesting and fun class to take, but instead it destroyed my GPA and caused so much frustration. Don't take this with her.
Great T/A who loves to help her students and knows how to teach.

Be willing to have a little fun and whimsy, it makes this class so much more enjoyable. There are three major assignments that you'll have to do, so the workload isn't too intensive. Overall, this class was one of my favorites this semester! (Took this class last semester, edited the wording recently)

(My review is for ENGL-3050, but it doesn't show up as an option.)

Achilles is incredibly informative, thoughtful, and intelligent. The class discussions he hosted were very fun, lively, and helpful. He does a great job at balancing humor and moments of fun with important and well-thought-out teaching moments. Absolutely worth taking his courses!
Extremely kind and funny teacher while also teaching us valuable English skills!!
Achilles, for lack of better words, is a pretty awesome professor!

He was a great teacher who provided valuable feedback on essays. There were only 3 papers in total, and he was very clear about the guidelines and what he was looking for in the essay. There is reading that needs to be done before class, but it is not much, and he just wants people to discuss the chapters in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Achilles is an amazing professor! He is always willing to help out in class, or respond to emails on his own time. Not many assignments, but just make sure to participate in class.
Laid back in the best way, gives great feedback, and has lots of good insight/advice!

Really great teacher! He is really helpful when it comes to asking questions in class and is really willing to work with your schedule if you have things going on and need extensions. Would recommend taking ENGL 2500 with him!
Achilles was great: 10/10 would recommend. He is super engaging and encourages classroom discussion. Fun, helpful, and patient.
Good professor
WOW! I hate words, and English is an L language, but I would take any class with this professor, even like a stem class (gross)

Very kind and honest professor. Makes learning enjoyable and overall a fun experience. He has been the most dedicated and has provided me tons of feedback to improve my writing.

By far one of the best English professors
N/a ooga booga ooga booga

Nice person...but…All of his critiques on student works felt abrupt and unhelpful. Would often shift class discussion to make a point in workshops and try to stir up unnecessary discourse. The sarcastic comments about students and their work creates a negative environment during workshops even if the professor thinks it lightens the mood.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Achilles is a great TA! I found his feedback incredibly helpful. There were not too many assignments in the class and he gives enough extra credit to make the class easy to finish at an A. Definitely recommend. He is also a very fun and understanding guy.
Great class, and because his experience in law enforcement it was interesting to hear him discuss how criminal investigations work.

Great professor, responds to email in a timely manner so I don't have to worry about if he'll respond before the due date. Very direct and clear of what he wants to be done each week and how to get a good grade in his class. Very stress free course, I would definitely recommend as a course for CJ majors!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This course was a lot of fun and very manageable! Brinkley is very kind and a great professor! If you are looking for a fun, easy, and interesting course that gives you a good background in investigation then this is perfect for you. Even though the class was online, Brinkley included some interesting projects and labs to change things up a bit.

Highly recommend taking this course. There is one field day that gains perspective of law enforcement. This course will also help you make connections in the workforce. The homework assignments are easy. However there are some readings that get heavy but it is manageable if you plan ahead. There is one book to read but it was effortless.

This class is one of the easiest classes I have taken so far. Chief Brinkley is super helpful when asking questions/wanting to know more about the crim j field. There is roughly one assignment every week and as long as you include what he asks you to it is an easy A. I learned a decent amount from this class and it didn't make me feel overwhelmed.

This class is perfect. Jeff is a good professor and the class is entertaining. The assignments are simple and you will get a good grade if you do them and try.  He does take attendance for participation but is caring and understands that life happens sometimes.

Jeff Brinkley is an amazing instructor. His 351 class is one of my favorite classes that i have taken so far here at ISU. The class is not very challenging. The topics are very interesting and up to date. There are 2 journals, 2 online discussions, 1 paper, 2 exams (take online wherever, open note/book). I would HIGHLY HIGHLY recommend this class!!

If you have an option, take your class with anyone else. Quiz questions aren't clear and will tank your grade. Lectures are confusing and constantly changing the meaning of things. Takes more time out of your week than organic chemistry or anatomy and physiology combined.

Truly thinks her class is the most important thing in your life and is not understanding of external events. Have had her for two courses and both were awful. I'm a good student and do well in school; I didn't think KIN 372 or KIN 473 were hard (unpopular opinion though). Attendance policy is terrible and strict. Don't recommend her.

Professor is uninterested in actually teaching the material in class. Instead she just reads questions off a powerpoint. None of the material is taught in class as it is 'reverse format.' There are unclear expectations for assignments and projects. Content on exams is written unprofessionally with typos.

Content-wise, this course is the toughest I have completed here at ISU. It is extremely dense and hard to follow at times. Take-home exams are extremely difficult and time-consuming. Extremely long semester project. But, if you attend class, READ, and take the time to understand the content it is doable. Do not miss class and submit quality work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very straightforward class. I was satisfied with this prof. early on but when classes went online (COVID-19) I was very disappointed by her lack of effort to help students succeed. IS NOT understanding of extenuating circumstances of students. Alright at lecturing but does not exhibit the characteristics of a prof that cares about student learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Exams are stupid hard. Lectures don't don't go into depth. No easy way to study for exams, she just says "this might be on the exam" during lecture. You're expected to know everything about anything if you want to do well in this class. She seems like she wants students to succeed but doesn't do anything to make sure that happens.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty basic lecture class with tophat and reading assignments. Tests are pretty hard and there's no clear way to study for them. Content seems understandable until small detailed questions are asked. Both her and the TA's are heavily involved in their research and see that as a priority.

Teacher and class like none other that I've ever taken! It stretched and grew me in so many ways and really helped to prepare me for grad school. Assigments were heavy but served as great tools in testing my knowledge on the content. If you are crazy about the brain and body connection, then this class will cover all your questions! Integrating
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVE Dr. S. If you don't get to know her personally, you may be intimidated by her classes.
