She does not let you skim through her classes easily, but if you put in the effort and go see her for help, you will get an easy A. She is a wonderful and fun professor. Pay close attention on tests and they are so easy!
She is sassy as heck and doesn't make sense when she's explaining things in class. Her tests were stupid-hard, with abc and then extra options mix and matching the answers.
Tough grader and likes to be detailed in classes. Needs to work on having study guides and better ways to study for tests.

Dr. Steg was a lot better of an instructor in this class than in 372. Never skip class; ALWAYS take notes because she likes to put specific things on exams. 2 take home (mind-blowingly difficult and time consuming) exams, and final projects are all individual. This class kicked my ass, but I got an A and am ready for medical school because of it.

She had a tough time teaching in 372 with over a hundred students but was way better with 11 in Kin 472.  Easy going and enjoyed a laugh once in a while. Seemed to really connect with us students. Was always receptive to questions and clarifications. Very knowledgeable but makes it easy to understand. Definitely take Kin 472 with her if need be.

She had 3 TA's that all told me 3 different things, the book said something different, and so did she. She's really nice and wants her students to succeed which is why it's hard  to blame her, but she's a new professor & a very hard grader. Tests are really REALLY detailed. Read the book before class, and don't skip.

Lee Burras is a great professor. He makes his lectures very engaging and is a fun guy to be around. 2820 has very few assignments and only 2/3 tests so it won't take a lot of your time. Theres frequent office hours and tests from previous years are given so you can know what to study.Getting a good grade is very easy if you do any amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing guy!

Dr. Burras is easily one of the best professors i've had during my time at Iowa State. I am not an agronomy major, but found the content of AGRON 182 super interesting. This class is graded off of very few things. There were three exams (only two were graded), a report, and a field trip, so doing good on those is important.
Outstanding lectures. Inspirational, and enthusiastic about ensci. Great opportunity to learn about soils.

I wish all my professors were like Dr. Burras. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and has fun teaching. Always makes time for questions and is very knowledgeable. So far the classes seem easy, but I'm still learning more with him than I have other professors. He understands that you can learn more when you aren't set up to fail.

Best professor. Very easy courses but conveys important information that makes you want to care. Really a sweet, funny guy with a funny laugh. None of his assignments have real due dates, only suggestions. He is very lenient with grading and time lines, and he is very understanding.

Such a great professor! I'm really glad this was one of my few in-person classes this semester. He cares so much about teaching students and is so passionate about what he does. He's always willing to answer questions and meet with you outside of class. 10/10 would take this class again

Dr. Burras is energetic and highly engaging! I loved having him as a professor because he provides a lot of insight into topics not normally discussed, and it's clear he loves teaching. Dr. Burras is super sarcastic, but he's always upbeat and easy to listen to!

Dr. Burras was probably one of the favorite professors at ISU. This class was easy and I enjoyed going to his lectures because he was always engaging and enthusiastic. No textbook or canvas, so you don't know what your grade is until the last day. Super easy if you go to class.

Lee is a great professor and he truly wants everyone to succeed not only in his class, but after graduation as well. Very little homework and it can be turned in whenever. Only two exams and if you are happy with your grade you don't have to take the final. He is one of the best professors I've had and the class is enjoyable too. I recommend.

He gives you a syllabus at the start of the class but he does not grade off of it. You get to turn in the homework whenever. He gives you study guides for the exams. As long as you turn in all the homework you will pass. Highly recommended doing the optional land use report, as long you do it you get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had Dr. Burras for a few classes, honestly my favorite professor. You learn a lot, science and in life, and he's an amazing lecturer. Take his classes whenever possible, you will NOT regret it!!
Never better professor you will meet in the ISU.
Take his classes. The end.
Dr. Burras is a riveting lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Professor always keeps you interested

This professor is amazing. He really cares about his students and makes going to lectures enjoyable, even if the topic is not your favorite. However, participation is a very big part of your overall grade and if you don't come to class you will miss out on a lot of really simple credit points.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've taken a few classes with Dr. Burras and hes a wonderful man. You can tell he loves teaching and inspiring students. Hands down my favorite professor I have ever had!! Word of advise: take his classes even when they aren't required, you will thank me later!

Dr. Lee is the BEST. Super easy class, didn't require a textbook. He keeps things updated and interesting and while he may come off as arrogant at times, he genuinely cares about people and his students. 10/10 would take him again, I only wish he taught more classes in my major.

Dr. Burras is an AMAZING professor! Genuinely enjoys his classes, will remember your name if you see him outside of class, and will answer questions you have about anything class/professional related. I asked him for some tips for a job interview once and he spent an hour talking to me about do's and don'ts. Would take again in a heart beat!

Burras is a great professor for any course. He specializes in soil science but I have had him for En Sci and Agron and he is great either way. Assignments are short and grading is set up for student success!
Burras made EnSci a great start to the school day. He doesn't have a book and is always willing to help. Also you can make up test up to two weeks later!
Easy one credit class. He is very easy to listen to keeps the lecture engaging.  Easily the best professor I've had here at Iowa State.
One of the BEST professors at ISU. He's an amazing person, mentor, and educator. Class isn't mandatory, but go to class. You learn so much more than just science. So much more.

Incredible person, extremely knowledgeable, practical, and wise. While class attendance isn't required, you should really go to class to get the full substance and his life lessons. He's an absolute joy.

Very laid back and clearly loves his job and loves teaching. Class wasn't mandatory but he had random quizzes about every other week and if you caught 7/10 of them you got full credit for all. Relaxed atmosphere and very open to questions and stories. Uses current situations to teach. Will remember you even if you're quiet in a class of 150+!
Top three best professors I've ever had in 4 years of college.  He's a great guy and extremely easy to listen to during lecture.

Dr. Burras is incredibly knowledgable, and loves what he does. He makes the class interesting by using the future to talk about current problems. No book, chalkboard notes, several trips off campus. Best ISU professor!
Best teacher on campus. Loves his job and does anything to better his students.
Hearing his laugh makes the class worthwhile. Great guy, very friendly, and he clearly loves his job and teaching
Best Professor at ISU by far
Great Professor.  Class is relatively easy and solely based on his chalkboard notes.  He actually cares about students and gives many professional tips.
Very helpful and incredibly knowledgeable.

Lee is a very cool professor.  He makes things easy to understand, offers several grading options so you can get the best grade possible, and doesn't really give out much homework.  The only problem I had was all the disrespectful talking students did during his lectures.

Easy one credit class.  Show up one day each week to sit and listen to some of his old grad students talk about their jobs and experience in Agronomy.  Only one thing that we had to hand in all semester was a Full Resume and Cover letter.  He is entertaining to listen to
Very excited about what he teaches. Gotta love his laugh!
Very Fun to listen to!
Awesome teacher, you'll really enjoy the class, actually worth the ISU tuition money spent for the class :)

Excellent professor- teaches well, knows what he is talking about, gives little outside work, nice and funny.  Don't hesitate to take one of his classes you will enjoy it even if you have little interest in the area and you wont have to buy a book.
He is absolutely amazing.  He knows what he talks about.
Easy

One of nicest, friendliest, and most honest professors that I've had at ISU.  He doesnt use a textbook...only a chalkboard, so his lectures are very personable...he is excited about his teaching, and presents information so that you can form your own opinions...welcomes criticism and oposing arguments...oh, and his laugh is awesome :)
easiest A of my life..
He was flexible and discussed the subjects in a way he wanted to instead of following a textbook.  He's definitely interested in what he's teaching.  Some of his test questions could be tough though.
No Comments
No Comments
great professor. great to work with, very helpful, lectures enjoyable. I highly recomend
Great teacher.  One of my favorites.  Kept the subject ver interesting and easy to understand.  Overall great guy.  Easy to talk to and willing to help with anything.
Makes somewhat unenjoyable subjects enjoyable. Keeps everyone interested.  Doesn't ask too much of students.
He's a goodfella easy to understand and does not demand too much of his students
No Comments
Katherine Bangert is a terrific Children's Literature Prof, and I hereby grant her authority to teach all children henceforth. Seriously, she's great!

You can tell she loves what she does and cares about the content and students. Take notes and engage. Provides a lot of real life information which is helpful and encourages discussions with some activities. Attendance is taken but there is flexibility.
Easy online class, would recommend for elective requirements

This professor made the class seem like it was a 4000+ level class. Smartbooks had over 100 concepts, practicum hours, observations hours, numerous writing assignments that were graded so harshly, and the lectures were dreadful. I would avoid this professor because even in other classes it's literally the same thing. No guided notes either.

This class and this professor made me hate HDFS. She gave us so much homework that I was spending at least 10-15 hours a week on her class alone. Compared to the other classes she teaches, she overloaded us with work. I can't say how she is in person, but as an online professor I think she hated her students because I was in the trenches every week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was beyond boring. The lectures were not helpful and did not provide any information that couldn't have been shared in a 5 minute video on Canvas. Attendance is required even though the content during lectures is useless as its all in the smartbook readings. Wouldn't recommend unless its required for your major like me unfortunately.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is incredibly nice but the lectures get boring pretty quickly as it just repeats the same thing that is already in the textbook. This course also has A LOT of work and a good chunk of it feels redundant and like doing busy work. She was also very accessible for questions and responded to messages well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She does take attendance. It was an okay class, however every week you are to do a Connect assignment on McGraw Hill, sometimes takes upwards of a couple hours. Other then that, the weekly assignments and quizzes are relatively easy. Notes were very helpful while taking the midterm and final.
She was super helpful and understanding. super approachable and always checks in with groups during in class projects!

She is very nice, but the class is mostly just busy work. Set aside time to do your smart books because they have a lot of topics. Lectures are late in the day and slightly boring if you do not plan to go into education.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was large but you get to pick your own groups for all the book days. Utilized this class as a study hall sometimes as there is not a lot of teaching happening. Smartbooks from McGraw Hill Connect and busy work made up a majority of the points in this class. Going to class felt like a waste of time sometimes.

She assigns a lot of busy work and calls it not busy work. She uses McGraw Hill Connect for the textbook and heavily relies on McGraw Hill Connect to do the actual teaching. Smartbooks will seem never ending as they tend to be 20+ concepts. Her lectures were kind of boring, but the entire semester most of the work was with a group of your choosing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is very strict about attendance, and tends to not be very understanding if you ever have to miss class. Way too much busy work, be prepared to spend a lot of time doing busy work that will not matter for tests/ quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very Easy class.  Lots of attendance points, but can be used as a study hall essentially.  Katie is very passionate and makes the class fun and lighthearted.
Katie is such a kind woman. She wants us to succeed and is willing to help us get there.

Large class and you get to pick a group. She reads books and it's a nice class to have at the end of the day. Wish it wasn't as late. Provided activities to keep interest and had some good real life experience to share. Overall, a good class and she provided reminders and set the work into doable chunks.

This class is easy if you go to class and attend all of the book days. If you don't like talking or are shy, this is a great class to take. She was not very responsive to emails, and I rarely talked to her. All presentations are in small groups, so it is not bad. The TAs grade everything, though I have not met them. Instructions can be confusing.

She is a great professor and is very nice. There is a decent amount of homework. Attendance is taken but she tries to end class early. There are many days off throughout the semester. She does give some extra credit opportunities. Overall, I would take one of her classes again.

Katie Bangert is an engaging educator. It's clear she's passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter. The practicum aspect of this course can sometimes feel repetitive, but it's not hard at all. She gives out the exam terms and short-answer questions ahead of time so you can prepare. The only downside is that the exams are handwritten.

Her TA grades tough, but she is willing to meet and go over grades and will most likely bump up your grade if you put in the effort. She is so kind, personable and one of the only professors here I have felt a true connection to in her class. Her smaller classes are better than hdfs 240. She is very understanding about not turning stuff in on time.
Enjoyed the class. Professor Bangert shows passion for the subject.
Her lectures were long and unorganized. She did not give clear directions for assignments and she did a poor job of answering questions.

I do not like Katherine Bangert as a professor. I have a medical problem, and once a month, I need to go to a hospital and get medication for it, and I cannot miss it. When I told Mrs. Bangert about this through email. She sent me a very mean email saying I shouldn't have picked this class if I knew I would miss so many of her classes.
Big class size, but uses small groups for discussions. End of day, but not a terrible class to have late. She reads books and provides snacks. Go to her student hours! That helps.
This class is super easy but time-consuming. Kate is really nice and brought us food and read us books all the time.

Professor Bangert was nice, but her lectures were unorganized. I didn't learn much that I didn't already know about children's literature. Instructions for assignments were too broad, and I felt like I was guessing all the time. TA grades everything. Very easy course, but as an EL ED major, I was disappointed by the lack of educational content.

Lectures are terribly boring but the class is overall easy. She did change requirements from the previous semester though. Attendance is taken and can effect your grade, and there's assignments in lecture worth points now. I don't think she's great at explaining rubrics vs. what she expects. Can be fun, can be snappy.

I loved this course and the professor! She is extremely relatable and friendly. Wants to make class fun but still learn something. This course gave me the opportunity to destress and deep-dive into children's stories. She will read to the class different stories which were really fun! If possible, would definitely take another one of her courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Lectures are mostly entertaining. Bring children's books to class for a lot of points. Easy class and a good way to meet people while getting an A.

Overall she was good. The projects were a little difficult, but otherwise the class was an easy A. Lectures were kinda boring, but she was pretty well organized. Sent out reminders when things were due. No final either which was nice. The application project was a bit tough, but very doable.

She was my teacher before Covid-19. She seemed to have good intentions but the busy work was immense. As well has her telling our class once a week that we werent trying hard enough or that we didnt do a good enough job, when she had 3+ assignments all due on the same day. She quite often yelled at our class for little things.

Love her!! I have not reached out to her personally, but she is lovely. Her recorded lectures are wonderful; as long as you pay attention, you will do great! 10/10 would recommend this class with her! :)

Professor Bangert genuinely cares about her students. She is very passionate about children's literature and that bleeds through her teaching. This made me excited to learn and overall just enjoy being in her class. She is always willing to help and just wants the best for her students. Go to her office hours! I highly recommend taking this class.

This entire class was just so odd. Conceptually not too difficult to understand if you pay attention in class, but some of the exam questions were just so far off of what we learned or what was on any of the practice exams. This professors teaching style was okay, mostly reading definitions off slides and attempting examples.

One of the worst math teachers I have ever had in the math department at ISU.Does not know how to communicate effectively with students. She acts like a high school English teacher and makes jokes that never hit. If you need help from her, don't email her; she will NEVER see your message. Also, she is very misleading about what will be on the exams

Lectures were fine however, the exams were like reading the enchantment table from Minecraft. Don't trust the practice exams either. Anything on the practice exam will not be on the real exam. She'll put something on the real exam that she barely went over in a lecture.
I had her for a few weeks at the beginning of the semester and she was great. She disappeared and I would like to know what happened.

She had a lot of bad jokes that made me laugh then dipped about 3 weeks into lecture and I'm not sure where she went. Now we have a guy who doesn't have funny jokes but he's ight no complaints from me other than I have no clue what's going on really banking on the curve this semester I hope it's steeper than Steven Hawkins back. Anyways good luck.

she teaches very well and she is accessible to answer questions. she will re-explain anything you ask multiple times till you understand it. she was fun! her tests were easy just homework and homework quiz every week.

Her lectures are useful, but not required. Nice person but I get second hand embarrassment from her jokes or weird comments. Clearly states how she does not care if you come or not she only cares about the money. That being said she teaches the class well and if you enjoy listening to a who openly embarrasses herself and has no humility she ur prof

Victoria is OK. She might be the most sarcastic person I've ever met, and that style of humor really started to annoy me as the semester went on.  She definitely understands the content well and will always answer questions, though sometimes not in the most easy-to-understand way. Her quizzes weren't too bad with a lot of gimme points.

Spends way too much time trying to be "hip" and funny in lectures. Her lectures and study guide are nothing like exams. My TAs were even confused about how the material matched up with our quizzes. Blames students for low average on exams.

Blumen is hilarious, very nice, and I really enjoyed the lectures themselves. I was disappointed in the material change from HW to quiz to exam and on whether we got EC. Wildly different in some cases. Also terrible about responding to emails and sent out incorrect announcements several times. A good grade is possible, but you'll work for it.

Goodluck getting an email back. In class reviews don't go into depth. Practice exams cover completely different topics than what's on the exam. Save yourself time and trouble and take this class online.

She was good at teaching the material but wasn't a good teacher in other aspects. She doesn't respond to emails, sends out incorrect announcements, and says she'll post extra exam practice on Pearson, doesn't, and then says a coordinator controls that, not her. Exams aren't fully consistent with past exams, but sometimes that's all we get to study.

She is terrible at responding to emails and proofreading her own. Doesn't know what she's doing with the website we use to do our homework. She says there is extra credit for exams, but it doesn't show up on the site, then when she figures it out, she takes forever to put it in the grade book.

Great professor. Material isn't hard as long as you pay attention in the lecture, which Victoria makes extremely engaging, so it's hard not to do well. She loves to tell stories while doing example problems, which gives everyone a good laugh.

Victoria always makes an effort to ensure that students understand the material. She makes lectures enjoyable while still being able to get through all of the material without rushing. It seems like the only people giving her bad ratings are people in MATH143 and MATH151, but for higher level math classes she is great

Had her for calc 2 during the Spring 23 semester. Extremely good professor, using lots of examples and engaging with any questions students had. Gave really good advice for solving difficult problems and used humor during lectures to keep students engaged with the topic. Really friendly outside of lectures and helpful during office hours as well.

Vicky is by far the best professor I have had in college so far. She teaches well, does a good job of answering questions that students have, and makes lectures enjoyable overall. To address all of the comments saying that there are lots of exams and homework, that is something that the course coordinator decides, it is not the professor's fault.

She is lucky that her TA's actually care about making her look good. They are a whole lot better at teaching than she is. The only reason that I am passing is because my TA actually cares about how I do in the class.

To start, this person acts like a child sometimes throughout her lectures, making the class respond or she will sit there without progressing throughout her lecture.
