reviews.comment: Igor is undoubtedly the worst professor I've ever had at Iowa State. His lectures are an absolute snoozefest, and they throw a tremendous amount of content at you. The quizzes and exams pull the most obscure information from the lectures; it's baffling. If you have to take this class, find some good Quizlet sets to study for the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst class I have ever taken at ISU. He sets his students up to fail it is ridiculous. It is all multiple choice but the questions he picks are so niche. He is the only professor. He talks in the most boring tone of all time, and the content is so naptime. Good luck, and I hope you can pass and not annihilate your GPA too badly.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture slides are bloated with words to an obscene degree. Grade distribution is disproportionate in favor of in-class quizzes. That is just memorization, not genuine understanding.

reviews.comment: Igor on the first day of class said we need a way to select certain people to be eliminated to help reduce climate impact. I think this is a terrible thing to say. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Igor wasnt a bad professor in the sense that he is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the content in GEOL201, but he will give 8 quizzes about niche areas of the course content that make up a heavy portion of your grade. Because you cant avoid him, Id recommend just taking very specific notes and studying hard for quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Entire teaching model is lectures and memorization. The entire class was based off listening and memorizing everything he said, which was impossible because of how boring he is. All of the exams and quizzes had nonsense questions about the silliest things, or material that wasn't even touched on or was a tiny corner of 1 slide of a 50 slide lecture

The quizzes are very difficult because the questions are always over minor details. The lectures are very boring, you are just as well off only reading through the powerpoint. The lab was kind of fun however, it wasn't tied together with the lectures so it felt like a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does not curve at all even though the average of the class is very low. Hard to understand his lecture due to his speech. Quizzes and exams are very specific details which would surprise you every time. Lab is a joke because you learn nothing and it's about self studying to do the homework.

Igor is knowledgeable but very abrasive, and likes calling people out in class. If you skip lecture and read the PowerPoints, you won't miss anything. Labs are mostly busywork. Tests are over very specific details - this is a surprisingly difficult class for a lot of people. One silver lining: post-midterm, material gets a lot more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is kinda dry, but hey, you chose civil engineering. Lectures can be interesting at times. Very knowledgeable professor. Quizzes are extremely specific and make up a significant chunk of final grade, so spend time studying hard for them.
Igor has really fascinating lectures with really unique pictures. Beware of the quizzes and tests, these ask super specific questions.
Boring class and boring lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Igor takes the best pictures. Relates real life to lectures using the pictures.

Very knowledgeable professor, however, he makes this class difficult. His quizzes are extremely detailed and cover minor topics rather than the general idea. This class was useless, the lab is a waste of time. This course should be an elective, it is ridiculous that this is required rather than a subject like linear algebra.

You have 2 books, a lab book and a textbook. Don't buy the textbook, I didn't open it all semester. The lab is a breeze but you need the book. He had a cool Russian accent and shows pictures of all the places he's been! Lecture is boring and you can skip often, just don't miss the quizzes (generally on Thursday). Look at the Powerpoint slides.

Igor is not interesting and does not appeal to the non-geology major. He tests over insignificant details so don't bother going to class except for quizzes and tests. Your best bet is to find old tests and quizzes to study answers from. LAB COMPONENT IS A JOKE. Good thing the grading is lenient because everyone struggles.

He's a good guy with a Russian accent which is not terrible. The quizzes are extremely specific making it difficult to study for the them. Go through his study questions they do help a little. The lab you pretty much teach yourself, which is frustrating at times.
Does not give extra credit and is VERY VERY specific in his quizzes. Tests the most minor of details.

He's terrible. For our course, he provided multiple choice practice exams in the same format as the actual exams, but made the actual tests inordinately difficult filled with completely obscure questions. For example, on the 40 question practice exams I would generally only miss a couple of questions (95%), then go into the final and get a D.

While Geology 201 is a pretty dry subject, he does his best to add in photos that he or others have taken.  Sometimes he moves through the slides too fast, but the powerpoints are uploaded to blackboard.  Don't expect to be lazy for this class.  The quizzes literally come from the lectures, but they are somewhat difficult concepts.

He reads off of slides during lecture and posts the lectures online so you don't have to show up. Gives a quiz once every four lectures. Quizzes are 5% of grade with only ten questions so each question is worth 0.5% of your grade which is stressful as hell. Lab is easy A but mandatory. Buy the lab manual not the textbook. It's required.

He is an okay sorta guy. will teach you everything but his speech generally not so clear, talks into the microphone weird idk whats it.  Lectures are long but tests are completely based on lectures no twisted questions. He is meh. not bad or good. just average

Igor was easy to understand with his accent. The hardest part of this class was the quizzes. Every quiz you take counts for 5% of the grade, so try to prepare for those. I copied his lecture slides onto flash cards and they were very effective for exam prep. Everything is multiple choice. The lab is extremely easy.

I am biased, because I was excited for this class before it even started because I like geology. Overall, Professor Beresnev is passionate about what he teaches and wants respect from his students. DON'T FALL ASLEEP IN LECTURE! I enjoyed his personal stories and pictures in class, and he was one of my favorite teachers this semester.

This was a surprisingly difficult class.  Only a few grades go into what determines your final grade, and everything is multiple choice.  So if you miss just a couple questions it will have a big impact on your grade.  Lab is super easy though.  Lecture was usually not the full class length.  Cool accent.

Everything you need to know is in the lecture slides which he posts. Quizzes and tests are moderately difficult. Labs are pretty easy. He likes to call people out in class, Russian accent but very manageable.

Didn't have any problems in 201. He gave us study guides for all of the quizes and tests, posted slides that was all of the material on them, and potentially curves the class. Just study for the quizes and tests and you'll be fine.
His lectures are straight from book. Just do your studying before hand and you will be fine. It's sort of a boring class but he is nice.

Professor Spears is a relatable professor who is good at his job. This course had multiple large projects followed by a team project at the end of the semester. The class itself isn't too hard, just a lot of work at points. Professor Spears has a clear grading criteria and is helpful for getting feedback

The class was ENGL314 Tech Communication. (Not 310) I enjoyed the class. Lectures informative. He is approachable and wants you to succeed. A couple individual papers and group paper/presentation. Mutual respect if you try and complete the work.

He is a real one.
Very fun and enjoying professor.

Very talkative and fun to be around. Several extra books needed for readings. Material can get boring and long, but he made it entertaining to be in class. Several assignments, but he is okay with an extra day to turn things in with approval the day before. If you miss too many days of class it is an automatic fail, based on how much information yo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He was cool

Prof. Spears clearly cares about the subject he is teaching, which made me want to attend the class even though I found the material boring. It did take him a while to grade the major speeches, but when you consider that he had to take over for another professor after the course had already started, I was willing to forgive this.

She is by far my favorite professor. You can tell she cares about how well her students do. She does offer extra credit. This course is very power point heavy and you defiantly will need to read them and study almost everything on the power points. The most important things are bolded or underlined.

Most is a very engaging lecturer, she's funny and gives information in an easy to understand way. She is receptive to student feedback and is always willing to work with you to understand the content. She also offers a substantial amount of extra credit and comprehensive study guides. The accompanying lab is quite difficult tho.

Decided to take her over winter break instead of Biederman based on what I've heard. The class was online and consisted of interactive readings, quizzes, and a weekly discussion post, all open book. Would definitely recommend taking her, she responds quickly and is super kind and helps u. Definitely don't regret taking her as a winter break course.
Fun class. You should do fine if you go to class and do the textbook readings.

Great professor! Her research is remarkable, and she has a very engaging teaching style.  She also has a sense of humor which makes class go faster. Some of the test questions however are very challenging and almost trying to trick you.  I got a lot from the class and if you take it be sure to take quality notes!

I loved Dr. Most because her lectures were actually interesting and she makes class enjoyable. She asks questions throughout her lectures to make sure everyone is understanding the material and she shares lots of cool stories from her research on wild baboons in Kenya. Overall she's a great professor and a cool person. Lots of extra credit too!

The workload every week: read the chapter every week, take a quiz over it, attend lecture, post in the discussion, and compelete the lab; however it didn't feel unmanageable. Everything is super organized, and there are tons of opportunities for extra credit. Dr. Most responds really fast and is also a really fast grader. I'd take this class again.
She's really smart and kind, she is honestly an inspiring person, and I'm so glad to be in her class
She made this challenging class fun and enjoyable. Very personable and kind.

Dr. Most is one of the most caring professors I've had. If she finds something unfair, she makes a point to talk about it and correct it the best she can (she offered lots of extra credit when some of us were struggling). She's really fun and engaging, and very approachable. If you have the chance, take one of her classes!

Great class. The assignments are tough, but there is plenty of TA help. It's a new way for me to think about math work. There are multiple correct answers, clarity and writing out assumptions is really important.

All aspects of this class are very difficult due to lack of directions and little to no help from the TAs. Homework problems are math based with no equations provided and values that you have to look help with no site listed. Exams are based on lecture material but the questions have multiple correct answers with only one being accepted as correct.

reviews.comment: Large class, lots of lecture, but material is very useful. New understanding and appreciation for nutrients and water.
Great class. Useful information for career. Kind of tough that there aren't always right answers, but get the hang of it.

Great course if you like thinking about plants and soils. Castellano says it is where all the energy is, so that's the focus. The first half was all fundamentals. The second half was all applied ag systems corn, soybeans, grazing, forests.

Super helpful professor. The assignments are difficult, but they now have a TA to help and Castellano is happy to provide help too. Online exams are difficult, but they are open book and curved. Extra credit makes up for - do the extra credit, and you will be prepapred for the exam.

He teaches an agronomy course disguised as and environmental science class. He is an ag professor and teaches about corn and soybeans and nothing else. There are very few assignments and very boring lectures.
ENSCI 318 is not an ecosystems class. It is fully an agronomy course so be ready to learn about corn and soybeans.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Introduction to Ecosystems no longer has group work, and assignments are done individually. While the lectures can sometimes feel long, they are full of great information, and Professor Castellano's ability to lecture from his vast knowledge is remarkable. Very attentive to students needing help, but the assignment instructions can be quite tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class. I took a notebook full of material to refer to for the rest of my life. Application to current events a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Solid professor with strong knowledge of the material. Doesn't require attendance; but certainly easier if you attend. Great course.
Castellano was a great lecturer. Assignments were difficult. I am sure they annoy some people, but you learn.

This professor somehow made Introduction to Ecosystems to one of the hardest courses I have ever taken. Homeworks (done in groups) were incredibly unclear and difficult, exams had to be curved due to how hard they were, and the material was basically all about corn and soybeans and not about the course. One of the worst professors I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer and really struggles with getting assignments out on time, communicating due dates, responding to emails and just- with tech in general. Not recommended.

Castellano is very knowledgeable about this topic and goes into depth about environmental and soil science. However, he is very slow at getting to the point and his class overall is boring, monotone, and hard to pay attention in. Additionally, it was an hour and 10 minute class, most of the students check out after the first 30 minutes.

I learned so much from Dr. Castellano and his perspectives. If you don't go to class or don't listen in class you won't do well. I'm surprised by his ratings because I enjoyed his lectures and examples given. Quizzes/exams were moderately difficult but nothing horrible. Also, he is chill.

It is sink or swim, but plenty of opportunities for feedback and discussion. You have to go to class because the exams are heavy on the material covered in class rather than the book. You cannot make up exams or assignments instead low scores drop. Yes, ag heavy, but also examples from forests and grasslands.
Course was really good. Thoughtful discussion about how ecosystems function and can be managed to balance needs for food and conservation.

-Assignments were poorly written and lacked direct connections to lecture material
-Tests asked about a lot of random information that may have only been mentioned once in previous lectures
-Slides uploaded to Canvas lacked sufficient information to study later- there were pictures with no text to explain the content or significance

The exams were very hard and had random stuff that was not gone over in lecture. You could tell the professor is really passionate about his knowledge in soil and farming. I would not say this class was really an intro to environment, most of the modules have to do with dirt. I took this as a hybrid class and he stopped uploading videos early on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hybrid due to COVID. Students had the option to attend in person or over zoom. It became clear that Castellano didn't care too much about the students taking the online option. He stopped uploading lecture recordings to canvas b/c "nobody was watching them" and "they are time consuming to upload". Assignments did not cover lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very enjoyable workshops where I got to make diagrams, write poetry, and think about what architecture means to me. We also got to learn from our future professors in a series of talks about their own design and research practices. I look forward to taking their studios in the future, they look fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very refreshing class with lots of material to pick from to focus on. I particularly loved some of the faculty presentations and our design of postcards about our field trip and about architecture in general. The class helped me reflect on what it is that I would like to do once I am a professional in the field of architecture.

I got to work on diagrams, drawings, and poems that reflected on the presentations of the many speakers we had in class. A pair of designers would present their work and we would ask them questions. The first presentation was by the professors, where they showed their own books, some of which have been very helpful in studio. Recommended!

The professors organized a lecture series with many of the professors that teach in the department of architecture. It was very helpful to see the varied approaches to design and to learn about what our teachers are interested about and how they have pursued their interests in many different ways. I enjoyed the presentations and discussions.
I've taken several classes with Prof. Garcia and enjoyed them all. 220 was fun and the booklet I designed for the class got me an internship in a design magazine.
I appreciate their feedback and advise. They're very approachable outside of class time.
Enjoy his feedback and recommendations. Gave me valuable career advice. They are very approachable and helpful whenever I have tried to pick their brain for ideas and advise.
best teacher I had

Makes you check your ego. Will sound disappointed in you and make you redo your entire building design multiple times, but has the best intentions. As long as you show up, do your work, and take his advice, you'll be fine.

Had Cruz as a professor & on reviews, this class is a series of empty buzz words & virtue signaling. He shows up late, often not at all to his own classes, & will just bail on studio final reviews. Genuinely will show up to reviews only to eat the snacks and offer no relevant feedback. Complete pseudo intellectual, far better professors at isu.

also took his arch5280 class and learned so much. very inspiring and part of the reason iowa state's arch program is worthwhile. if you're interested in learning about theory him and nathalie are amazing
What got me the most excited were the many zines we could produce in class. That, and all the pop-culture references. Can't wait to take studio with them.
favorite class and made me think about issues that are important to me and I was afraid were not part of design education.
if a class would be a pizza, this would have pepperoni, mushrooms, olives, onions, chicken, ground beef, bbq, hot sauce, honey... you get the eclectic deal
he's whatever
No other professor in the department has more than a handful of reviews. This is not a coincidence, read the 1/5s to get the real picture.
2200 will fundamentally change how you think about architecture and its role in the world.
if you come to class and pay attention to the references, you're free to make a book with any interesting thing you may find. i loved making special hand-made books with maps and diagrams.

The lectures in this class were some of the most insightful I've ever attended. The artist book projects were a great way to engage with the material. I highly recommend this course to anyone looking to expand their understanding of architecture.
It's a challenging but incredibly rewarding class that will change how you think about architecture.

If you're looking for a class that will push you to think critically and creatively, this is it. The lectures are intense but incredibly enriching, and the focus on creating publications was a unique way to engage with the material. I came away with a much more holistic understanding of architecture and its connections to broader societal issues.

This course is not just about buildings; it's about understanding architecture as a dynamic, interdisciplinary practice. The lectures were incredibly engaging, and the publication projects helped me develop a voice. I feel like I've gained a much deeper appreciation for the field.
The publication assignments were a highlight—they forced me to synthesize complex ideas and present them in a creative way.

This class completely changed how I see architecture. The lectures were incredibly insightful in ways I never considered. The focus on creating publications pushed me to think critically and articulate my ideas clearly. It's a challenging but deeply rewarding course that broadens your perspective on architecture as a holistic discipline.

Before class starts you can read the syllabus (or lack thereof) to get an idea of what this course is. The syllabus and lectures cover zero relevant content and are too abstract, nothing is actually being taught. Cruz and the course alike are very good at talking a lot without ever saying anything, beyond vague concepts and leftist politics.

The class content helped me connect the dots between architecture, design, policy, environmental and social issues. I wanted to be a designer because of the public good we can do with design, and this class assured me that I'm on the correct track.
I discovered that I like designing books in this class. Up to now, it has been the only course where I have designed books.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite was the combination of popular culture elements with design content.
I'm not a design student, but these lectures were very comprehensive and informative.
very resourceful for critical thinkers who understand that architecture touches many facets of life and many environments
Liberal propaganda disguised as academia
great people. will take again. many times.
Very very very very complex topics. I read tons of philosophy on my free time and that helps understand the subjects presented in class. A+
few times I have felt a class challenged my understanding of a subject. I hope to take more classes with the professor again in the future.
Fantastic. Fantastic. Fantastic.

I wholeheartedly recommend this class to any student seeking a challenging yet rewarding learning experience. They are an exceptional educator who goes above and beyond to inspire and support their students.

very creative class that showed me how architecture is in almost everything we do and every space we live in. it was the first time I designed a book. Would recommend even for non-architecture students.

very thoughtful and creative lecture class. so many references and many ideas to pick from. I designed a couple of publications that I am proud of and helped me put my ideas together. truly enjoyed the class.
Really fun and informative class.

The variety of sources used in this course was incredible. We explored everything from videos of buildings, got to write a manifesto, designed and wrote a couple of small books, and drew some diagrams. Class was quite interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love not having to take quizzes and tests and instead making zines. They provide so many references that you should be able to download from canvas.

They answered questions when I needed at the start of the semester. If you make the three publications assignments with content that relates to class, you should have a good grade. 
It's a big lecture but sometimes we can discuss during the class. There's one group project at the beginning of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I made a couple of cool publications for this class. The lectures were fun and sometimes included music or movies. It def made me think of architecture differently.

If you come to the lectures you should get all you need for the book making assignments. There's so many topics that give you freedom to chose the angle you want to focus on. This was one of my favorite classes.
This class was cool. I recommend writing names down from the lectures, because it helped me when making my publications and diagrams. Cruz and Nathalie are very approachable out of class.
The assignments let me think critically and creatively about how I connect different issues to architecture. Loved the lectures.

Nathalie and Cruz did a great job of connecting seemingly disparate ideas and showing how they relate to the bigger picture of architecture. All you have to do for class is to make three publications or books designed by you, and come to the lectures, which are always surprising and fun.
I gained a much deeper appreciation for the historical and theoretical context behind contemporary architecture and also, I love making the books for class.
Cruz and Nathalie were incredibly passionate and knowledgeable. Each class was stimulating and thought-provoking. This was my favorite class at ISU.

Professors Garcia and Frankowski emphasized that contemporary architectural issues extend far beyond just building design, encompassing social, environmental, and political dimensions. If done on time, the publications for each of the topics, was a fun project that is now going in my portfolio. They provide so many references.

This course challenged me to look beyond my preconceived notions of what architecture is and consider its broader impact on society. Both professors are very accessible and also provide awesome feedback to my publications and studio projects.

Having the opportunity to design our own publications was a fantastic way to apply what we learned and explore our own architectural ideas. I love making books and having projects that allow me to design how do I present information that I care about.

I really appreciated the multimedia approach to learning in this class. The documentaries, films, and animations brought the concepts to life and made them much more engaging. Many of my classmates wouldn't come to class, so they missed an opportunity.

The variety of sources used in this course was incredible. We explored everything from academic texts and critical essays to manifestos and built works, giving us a well-rounded understanding of architectural theory.

Professor Garcia and Frankowski showed us an incredible amount of works for ARCH 2200, exposing us to a diverse range of architectural, urban, social, and interdisciplinary approaches, philosophies and styles.
My favorite class in college. Taught me that architecture is everywhere, and that we have to be aware of its influence if we want to make positive change.

I love their classes. Very knowledgeable, makes the class appealing by brining many references from different sources. Clearly cares about us learning something outside of “conventional” architecture.

can't teach, period. goes on insanely unintelligible rants, doesn't even show up to his own class, does not give warnings to his students about his absence, and basically makes his TA's do all the work for him while he goes on self-important tangents.
Most of this class revolves around reading mid-wit commie essays about seemingly everything BUT architecture. If you are looking for a class that teaches architectural theory this is not it.
Bro doesn't even go to his own classes 💀💀💀

while i do think that the ethical concepts in class are important, Cruz Garcia is undeniably the worst professor i've ever had. despite stating that attendance was not mandatory on his first day of class, he decided to take a random roll call and make attendance worth more points than all assignments combined, failing more than 50% of his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although it is called architecture 2200 this class has little to no relevance to actual architectural theory or design and instead is a platform for Cruz to inject his far left political ideology into, and rant about oppression etc.  Understanding Cruz is difficult as he likes to rant about abstract political issues in a very pseudo intellectual.

This is the most pointless and annoying class I've ever taken. all they do is ramble about the most random things that they wanted to "teach" about that day. They're super into books and there's lots of reading for no reason. The worst hour and fifteen minutes of my life.

Extremely knowledgeable and passionate professor! Him and Nathalie put together some thought-provoking and informative lectures. The content is theory-heavy and is sometimes hard to follow, but the work they are doing is incredible. No exams, just have to make 3 "publications" and attend lecture.

There is no real material he goes over, it's all abstract and some form of hogwash activism mixed with constant complaining about the west/ the U.S. He even goes as far as to say some pretty offensive things without citing a source to his argument. Garcia will lecture on the same thing every day, if there wasn't attendance, I'd say to never go.
Such a pointless class, no one knew what was going on ever

ARCH 220, garbage lecture and class was one of the biggest wastes of time.Realize that & just turn in your monthly assignment and stop showing up because theres no rubric or instructions for any of it.The syllabus is next to non existent. Care about diversity and thats the entire class. No theory if thats what you wanted from him.
Not a hard class, good resources to study for exams, lectures are good, but I didn't really feel the need to go to them after a certain point.

Dr. Bonaccorsi is amazing! She covers material in a digestable way and does examples and experiments in class to help students understand the concepts she teaches. Exams are fairly easy and on-par with the practice problems given in class, and generally easier than the homework. She is very caring and compassionate and open to answering questions.

Dr. Bonaccorsi is a great professor who truly cares about her students' success. You can expect weekly homework and recitation worksheets. She does 5 drops out of 15 recitations, so if you're sick or struggling, you can catch up. She truly cares a lot and even has a small snack bin for students. Small accent. Practice exams similar to real exams.

Make sure to attend lectures, she does a lot of extra practice problems. She records the lectures too as well if you can not attend. She truly cares about her students and isn't afraid to postpone homework so you have extra time to complete it. Always has office hours to come to her for help with problems. Overall I would recommend her!

She was a very nice professor! She always asked if we had any questions, and the day of exams, we had a Q&A day/review day, which you rarely find with other professors. She also did very well with not just using her slides to teach, she worked through every problem in class and had some fun demonstrations.

Lectures go over a lot of content, but she does her best to explain it all. She records her lectures as well in case you are sick or whatnot. She genuinely cares for her students, and she makes it clear. She wants everyone to succeed as well.

Honestly an amazing professor, you can tell she actually cares for her students as well as they way people see her. Her lectures are very heavy with material but she thoroughly goes through what she's trying to teach. While lecture is not mandatory it is easier to learn when you attend. I would take every chem class I have with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Christina's lectures were very information-packed and dense. This made it very hard for her to explain every subject properly in the course. However, explaining group theory and crystal structures in a 2-credit class is extremely difficult, so I will give her the benefit of the doubt. She breaks down topics the best she possibly can.

Absolutely magnificent to put it into simplest terms. She speaks clearly and explains clearly. When she introduces a hard topic she gives it to us in the hardest form then slowly dissects it and feeds us the material extremely well. She gives the class questions and goes over them afterward, telling us why each choice was right or wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
A great professor who made learning Chemistry all the more bearable. Her lectures are not mandatory to attend, but I felt like they were worth going to, since she does a good job explaining, and we do some in-class exercises as well. She is also happy to help you after the lectures.

But beware, the TAs for this class are awful, aside from a few.
She was a great professor who was always there for you in office hours and gave amazing lectures. She was super nice and helpful. The same cannot be said for the TA.
Amazing professor, she really cares about students, she's very flexible in everything and she offers amazing lectures.
Great professor that makes the class enjoyable with demonstrations and real-life applications. Show up to class and take notes and you should be fine on the exams.

Dr. Bonaccorsi is very kind and always excited to teach what she does. She does read through the PowerPoint quickly, so I would recommend having the PowerPoint open on a computer or tablet so you can take notes. Overall her class is pretty straightforward and not too difficult since she does drop a few bad scores to help your grade.
Fantastic lecturer for a class that's mostly conceptual. Nothing like a long week of classes and hearing that Italian accent say that we're going to light something on fire in lecture.

Excellent professor. Class content isnt too fast paced and is generally easy for most to understand. Exams are doable and extra credit is possible. Your final exam can replace one of your three lowest midterm exams. A great person overall.

This professor is so great! Made theories easier to understand and made class fun with experiments every so often. She made the class welcoming and always gave us constant reminders on due dates and overall, such a great time in this class.

She as very nice and her accent does not affect comprehension at all. Her lectures were a little bit fast but as long as you attend them regularly you should do pretty well. I would definitely take a class taught by her again. Make sure to complete all the homework assignments so you have more room to breathe on exams.

She seems to be a nice person who cares about her students' success. However, she flies through the lectures at breakneck speed, so it's really hard to take notes without losing your bearings. I found it was much easier to watch the recorded lectures.

Incredible lecturer. She makes the lecture more entertaining with little one liners and jokes here and there, but as long as you take halfway decent notes and pay attention to objectively, borderline entertaining lectures, you'll be fine in this class. Excellent professor and personality!

She did a really good job at making lectures interesting, there were lots of experiments or demos! The tests were in general easy if you studied the practice exams. She is very understanding and there are lots of drops which help your grade!
Just a class you need to get through. Decently easy class due to the periodic table you can write notes on. Boring lectures

Dr. Bonaccorsi was amazing! I had taken this course in the past with a different professor and I hated how he taught Chemistry but Dr. B made the tough material easy to understand. Would highly recommend going to the SI sessions because that helped me a ton with any material I didn't quite understand. Overall, loved how she taught 177.
She very kind and genuine. Would retake her classes. You get a periodic table that you can write on for exams and quizzes. And quizzes are group quizzes. She is a very kind professor.

Bonaccorsi is an excellent teacher! She may be a little fast-paced at times, but if you say something she will go over it again to make sure everyone understands everything. I wouldn't have wanted any other professor.
I liked her personality but I strongly disliked her teaching style. She went way too fast and I had no idea what was going on the entire time to be honest.

Top Hat counts as a grade, so lectures do have some importance. She tends to over-explain unimportant things, which can be confusing. I recommend previewing the lecture slides beforehand. If you dislike large lectures, make sure to ask questions during recitation. She's very knowledgeable and enthusiastic.

Pacing is too fast to accurately take notes on paper during lectures. If you want to understand everything in a lecture, take notes from slides beforehand on your own time. Very enthusiastic to teach, but her accent is so thick that it's hard to understand everything. Due to this, lectures are only helpful for clarification and Tophat points.

She uses Top Hat quizzes in class sometimes, so attendance is mandatory. Sometimes, she goes a bit too fast through her slides. Other than that, she is an amazing professor. Her lectures are precise, and her slides are the only thing you need for exams. Great for CHEM 167.

This course with Bonaccorsi is pretty much made for engineering majors to pass. You only have to go to 75% of the classes to get a 100% Top Hat Score, she posts both her powerpoint and a recorded lecture on Canvas, so you can follow along during class and take better notes, or just skip and go through the video. She goes over practice problems too!

What made this class difficult was the during lectures. I swear I was falling asleep every single time. I hated going to this class and I really hated that in a lecture of 400 people she was taking attendance :l
She tests on stuff she doesnt lecture about
She is a really nice person except sadly she is a bad professor. Nothing against her personally it's just she doesn't teach well.
Does a good job, but way over explains some things.

Great professor. Straightforward class if you go to class, do the homework, and make a good note sheet for the exams. Always available for help before and after class. Enjoy the class, because in the engineering program, professors like her are few in number.

Very nice and understanding. She would frequently go over exam/quiz example questions in lectures. The section size was fairly large (400+), so it was much easier to receive individual help in the recitations. I did not use the textbook, but a code was needed to use the online homework portal.

Dr. Bona was one of the best chemistry professors I've ever had. During my semester we were able to use a periodic table with notes written on it for all of our exams, including the final. Our final exam grade could replace our worst score (if it was higher than exams). She explains topics well, and makes chemistry somewhat fun. 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS PROF! She really is AMAZING. She explained things clearly and when they were unclear she took the time to sit down and explain it until it made sense. She is the best professor in the chemistry department in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy to understand with an accent. kinda boring, will make you want to skip every once in a while.

Dr. Bonaccorsi is knowledgeable about the Chemistry she is lecturing on, but her explanations aren't always well received by the class, in fact, I would say my recitation leader did a better job at explaining some topics. Furthermore, her accent may be an acquired taste for some, but give it a week and you will get used to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a very good professor. Very passionate about the subject. Her lectures go very in depth because she fully explains every formula, theory, etc. Even when the students only need to know how to plug the numbers into the formula. HW can be frusturating because the website looks and runs like an early 2000s site.

Dr. Bonaccorsi is a great chemistry teacher and knows what shes talking about, shes there to teach students and answer any questions after class, quizzes/exams can be difficult and there is no curve. Top Hat questions during class strongly suggested you should show up.

Weekly homework takes a while. Lectures are pretty straightforward, the Italian accent was not an issue. She had a tendency to rush a few topics towards the end. I highly recommend reading the txtbk ch. before class. Most important thing is to stay on top of the topics, the last thing you want to do in this class is be confused/behind on topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: In a lecture hall of almost 400 students, Christina did a fantastic job of keeping the lectures fun and engaging. Almost all of the content covered could be prior knowledge if you had a good chem teacher in high school. She has Top Hat every class and is VERY generous in the assignments and homework that is dropped. I would strongly recommend her.

Helpful and detailed lectures, but they can sometimes be very confusing and the graded Top Hat questions can be somewhat vague. The homework she assigns also frequently does not line up with what was learned in class that week. For example, we've had several concepts on homework that we didn't learn until the week after the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Just Had my first class. I didn't listen anything she was saying cause she is insanely pretty. She also has a cute accent. Or maybe, I found her accent cute b/c she is pretty.
Dr. Bonaccorsci is very clear in her expectations, and is a good lecturer. Her lectures were very reflective of what was going to be on the homework/tests.

Lectures are the best way to learn for her. She is a very good lecturer, but her material is almost straight out of the book which meant that I didn't read it that much. Attendance is mandatory, but lectures are fairly interesting.

Great teacher for Chem 167. Lectures where clear and went over all the material that was covered on exams. Take Recitation assignments seriously sense that is the material that will show up again on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Christina has, by far, has the best lectures. You likely won't be bored, plus she does some really cool demos throughout the semester. The class itself is really straight forward; go to lecture, read, do the homework, and you'll definitely pass. The concepts get a little complicated, but put in the effort and you'll succeed no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Bonaccorsi is very gifted when it comes to chemistry. She explains everything in a way that someone who is just beginning will be able to grasp it. One thing is she is not great at keeping her lectures in check sometimes and it gets kind of loud so I would recommend sitting near the front. She also follows her syllabus exactly as written.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her course was like taking a course with your mom as a teacher.
Her accent is a little tough. Grading is clear. Compared to other professors, her class is better to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Bonaccorsi was a great professor. I came into the class thinking it would be awful, but she made the class much better. She has great PowerPoints and breaks up the class with TopHat questions. You can tell that she loves chemistry and knows what she is doing. Also, she is Italian and has a great accent (but still understandable).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you're taking Chem167 it doesn't matter which professor you are taking it with besides for lectures. All of the professors use the same blackboard page and will have the same exams and quizzes. Expect a fair amount of homework, quizzes, and TopHat questions. If you read the book ahead of time nothing said during the lecture will be new to you.
Christina is a great professor. Be very sure to do the homework right as you get them as they are long and sometimes hard. But if you pay attention, take notes, you will do fine in the class.
Not a bad experience with her for me.
Good personality that comes through making lectures more easy to follow, even in a lecture hall of a couple hundred. Clear with what you need to know to pass.
We watched Toy Story for the first ten mins of every class. She is awesome but the class tough. You definitely want her, she does a lot of cool demonstrations in class too which kept it interesting.

Bonaccorsi's lectures are interesting (and she's got a cool accent), and she often does demos and Top Hat questions to break up the lecture and keep everyone engaged. The tests and homework aren't very hard. If you go to class and study for tests, you shouldn't have much trouble with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bonaccorsi was great. She made it clear what was expected to get an A so if you worked for it, it was possible. All of the slides were uploaded, and past tests, which were SUPER similar to the tests from this year. If you did the homework and did the practice tests, you probably got a good grade and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bonacorsi made Chemistry actually interesting. She makes class interesting and loves to do demonstrations. She also gives plenty of opportunity for extra credit.  The tests were hard, but the final exam had questions that were previously on the unit tests.
One of the best professors that I've had so far. Gives a lot of opportunities to get points and extra credit. Her tests were also straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy if you went to lecture each day. She did a good job explaining how each concept works and takes her time to explain the content. The quizzes were easy pts. She also gave points for answering tophat questions. She gave 0.5 points for trying and 0.5 points for the answer. If you got 75% of the points, she gave 100% of pts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Italian accent, kinda hot. Easy to understand and breaks material down well. Doesnt go too fast and cares about students. A+

Dr. Bonaccorsi explains the material very well as long as you pay attention in lecture. She also wants to make sure her students understand the material. She utilizes top hat for attendance and participation points so skipping class is not a good idea.

Tough first college class. Learn to study for this class because the first test was 3 weeks in. She's an ok teacher. She covers very general concepts compared to whats on the quizzes. Always expect to see something on the tests that you know nothing about and you're expected to use your "applied knowledge".
Clear, concise, and easy of draw information from.

If chemistry isn't your strongest subject, be prepared to do a TON of work for this class. She makes a few concepts hard and confusing to understand. She makes so many little mistakes during lectures when doing example problems. I found my tutor and TA more helpful than her. Otherwise, if you put in the work you should be able to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The grading criteria is very clear. Homework and tests are fair. She does a really good job explaining and keeping the class engaging, even with 400 student. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's Italian, has a cool accent, is goofy, and likes to blow stuff up.  Her lectures are easy to follow, she makes sure people get what she is talking about, it can get pretty boring especially in a 400 person lecture, but she tries to keep you engaged and it works for the most part.  Use the past exams online. almost the same thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is an awesome teacher, one of my favorites that I've had so far. cares about students and is engaging in class as best she can be in a lecture hall environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. Clear on the subject matter. She is kind of a goof and messes up demos often, but its all in good fun. Offer plenty of extra credit and makes it extremely easy to get an A in the course. 75% of the finals questions were straight off the first three exams.
She has a slight Italian accent but is very understandable. She makes class enjoyable and she is really nice. Great professor.

Bonaccorsi is a great professor. Very straightforward. Explains every topic very thoroughly. You get extra credit for each online homework assignment you score above 90% on. Tests are very easy and she takes questions directly off the practice tests she posts online. If you can get in her section for any chem class, I would recommend it.

Christina is an decent teacher. The lectures are boring enough. Clickers every day. The material is moved through very slowly. Go through her slides to study for tests. There is a small amount of material to master for each test.

Solid class overall. Like mentioned, very straight forward. Show up, do the homework, take the tests. Nothing overtaxing, nothing extra. If you got through 177 you'll be fine in 178 with her. She's a pretty good lecturer, keeps our interest and tells you what you need to know. Old exams really help. Fairly easy but not really any curve.

Bonaccorsi's class was relatively straightforward - go to lecture for clickers, do assigned homework and quizzes and answer 70% conceptual questions on the tests. I found the tests easy and straightforward. The final was hyped up but most of us finished with half the time to spare as it was mostly concepts. Relatively easy class.
If you understood 176 decently then 177 is going to be a breeze. She over explains everything. Tests can be a little hard at times because she over explains the easy stuff.

She would show Disney movies 10 minutes before lecture.  She was a good teacher and easier to understand than the other 167 professor.  Makes jokes and does a lot of in class experiments. Great course, though the lab sucks.  I enjoyed this class.  Easy A if you do the work.  Exams are all multiple choice.

Her accent is great, could listen to her talk all day, but it's still very clear to understand her. She keeps everything very organized and has tons of resources posted on blackboard. Just go to lectures and pay attention and you'll be fine.

Her accent is great, could listen to her talk all day, but it;s still very clear to understand her. She keeps everything very organized and has tons of resources posted on blackboard. Just go to lectures and pay attention and you'll be fine.
She really cares,  almost always has a demo

She makes chemistry interesting. Jokes around with the full 400 student lecture. Does as many demos as possible, including blowing up balloons every other week. Overall great class and I highly suggest taking this class with her.

Dr. Bonaccorsi is a really good teacher and she is really good at explaining if you have any doubts. She goes over a lot of examples, to make sure everyone is understanding what we are doing. Here tests are not bad, as long as you study previews tests, which are somewhat similar. She is not amazing, but she is definitely a decent teacher.
Kinda hard to understand her

Professor Bonaccorsi is a very intelligent person and really wants students to do well. If you reach out and ask her for help, she is more than willing to help you. She does a good job of explaining concepts and gives lots of example problems in class. Overall, great professor!

It's not an easy class, but she really does her best to give you relevant information, and takes time to go through the tougher math problems. Typically offers some sort of make up exam or way to make up for a bad grade or two. Of the three 178 lecturers, this is the one you want.
Great professor, knows her stuff, and the class is fairly easy as long as you pay attention. The material is covered thoroughly and she will answer any question you have.

Lectures were often boring, but she did show Disney movies before each lecture which gave me motivation to show up. She is knowledgeable on the subject and knows how to explain the material in a way that students understand.

Professor Bonaccorsi is a very nice woman and very intelligent, but I found her lectures to be very boring. Homework is only once a week, but you have to go to class to get clicker points. Overall not a difficult class but you still have to try and go to class.

Yes, her Italian accent is hard to understand, but you get used to it. Don't pack up early or else she'll get upset and not lecture about the last thing in her plan that might be a big topic that's on the test. There's a clicker quiz each day. Lots of fun demos. You watch Disney movies before each lecture. READ THE BOOK.
She's OK.

I took accel chem in high school so this class was pretty easy. She is pretty "easy" teacher/grader, in terms of in class questions and tests. Downside, she really bored me. This is her only class, and she is at the university to do research, so teaching is not her best skill.

Easy to understand her Italian Accent. Made me laugh couple times in class. Good Professor, although I would recommend you taking this class with the Head Professor Dr. Greenbowe because he tells his students what is going to be in the tests
She told some good jokes to try to make class better.
Her powerpoints are kind of worthless but if you pay attention to what she is saying the concepts are easy to grasp. Her accent is hard to understand sometimes but she tries hard to be understood.
Go to class because of clicker question. overall, not a hard class. Make sure to stay on top of whats going on, its easy to fall behind. First two tests are easy.
Basically gives you the answers to in class questions. Explains contents well and answers any questions you have. Go to class and you'll be fine. Even if you don't the tests are pretty easy.
All around not a bad professor at all and even easy on the eyes.

I thought her class was completely fair.  You have to pay attention and do the practice problems she gives you, but if you do, you'll be fine.  She was always willing to talk about questions that the class had.  I didn't have much trouble with her accent either.  I thought she was a good teacher and I enjoyed the class.
The worst chemistry professor by far. Not clear, and not helpful.  Don't take chem 163 with her or you'll do really bad.

Horrible! Unlike other good teachers who curve, she won't.  The final is hard and it's even harder because she doesn't teach well at all so good luck if she's your teacher.  I'm very angry about my final exam test because all of my other tests are A's while this is a B so my final grade will be like 89% and she won't curve up so it will be a B.

We just had a test, and let me tell you she crammed chapter 8 in with a few slides the lecture before the test. Also she put up a study guide unless than 24 hours. She is the worst professor by far and I feel sorry for anyone who has to have her. She also always messes up teaching and has to reteach it to us. Yeah awesome teacher.. not! :(

She is horrible, and expects you to know this stuff already. Also she will go through things very fast when a test is coming up and doesn't thoroughly teach it right. Also she has messed up on problems quite a bit. Her accent is hard to understand. Overall she is a horrible teacher and I would not recommend her to anyone!!!

She really does want to help her students learn, but this class is a real pain. All the homework is online and she usually had them due before she teaches the material which is frustrating. The in-class clicker quizzes are annoying too. The tests generally arn't too hard if you do the practice exams.
She uses the blackboard to explain almost every equation. I do like her. The exam is much easier than homework. It's not hard to get a good grade.
She is so horrible and teaching. she really does try and wants to help, but the book is so much better than her. the clicker quizzes are some dumb and not really helpful.
Very nice Prof. She is very helpfull and alwys there to help.
No Comments

Honestly, she is the worst professor I have had throughout my entire college career. She goes through the slides so fast, and expects us to do so much work at the end of class from our textbooks. When we don't understand she gets upset and is no help at all. She's always rushing through things and doesn't take time to stop and actually teach.

Dr. Xiang is a great professor. This is a tough course, but she is very knowledgeable about the topic. The lecture has a lot of people in it which can make it harder to understand things. I recommend talking to her after class or scheduling a meeting with her if you need help. The textbook is your best friend!

Dr. Xiang was a super nice and understanding professor. The course itself is pretty difficult but as long as you show up consistently and put effort into the class you should end up with a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

he's really nice and lectures are pretty interesting, but an exam every other week gets to be a lot. practice problems arent very helpful for preparing for exams, so it can be a lot of guesswork. dont get to see what you get wrong on exams. for final paper he basically said its impossible to get an A. way too hard for an intro class

Ranpal is a really fun professor but can be a picky grader when it comes to exams. However, he is always willing to help and encourages students to go to office hours for extra support. There is a LOT of participation credit, so be sure to attend lectures. There are 7 short exams and one final paper, along with participation points.

The class was overall ok. Active participation is discouraged as the philosophical arguments are always poorly constructed and setup for failure. The test are also unreasonably hard. The instructor also seems to follow the idea that test need to be secret and not based on class.

Hardest class Ive ever taken. Not a bad teacher,bad class. Gives you 20 min at the beginning of class to go over problems,10 min quiz,and then teaches the new material for 15 min. Available for help,really difficult material. Mix between math, linguistics, and computer science. Ive also heard from ling and com sci majors that its advanced for them.

This proffessor is one of the best in the philosophy department. He knows the material well and can explain it in easy to understand ways. He also is very good about keeping the dense information light with pop culture references whenever he can. 10/10 would reccomend Ranpal!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are necessary to pass this class, but he makes it very fun and engaging. One of the only classes I loved going to this year. Personally love the teaching he gives. Exams are pretty tough but if you study right and get the right stuff on the cheat sheet you're allowed to have then you'll be fine.

This is the most challenging class Im taking, and Im in 400 level courses. The class has 2 tests which are next to impossible to get a decent grade on, and we got to use a cheat sheet for both. The class is curved, so a 70 is a B, but its hard to get anything better than a 75. There is simply too much lecture material to be crammed into the exams.

Ranpal is amazing. Go to class, he discusses all of the content that will show up on exams, not to mention his lectures are really entertaining. RIP orange chalk, you will be missed. This class was always a bright spot in my day, I highly recommend taking it with Ranpal. PS: he's meme literate
tough grader. impossible class. wish I would have taken another instructor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Dosanjh gives very good, clear lectures and made the class understandable. While this class was challenging, that is the nature of the material. He uses good examples to clearly explain what he intends to teach, and makes every effort for the student to succeed. He was even very forgiving when I slept through an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. He clearly knows the material and creates awesome discussions. As long as you do the readings and pay attention, you should do fine.

Professor Ranpal gives some of the best lectures I've received at ISU. They really pull you in, so if you have any interest in Philosophy you will do great. He's very approachable and is happy to talk with you after class or in office hours about whatever concepts you want. If you're just looking to fill a gen ed you'll probably have a harder time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Dosanjh was a phenomenal professor! I was so scared of the class because of how little you're graded on, but right from the beginning he explains how to do well and gives you all the tools. Every class there's an activity you get a point for just for being there so even though class isn't mandatory, you'll lose easy points if you skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The grading & material in this course is inappropriate for an entry-level philosophy course. The grading rubric is not specified, therefore, leaving too much room for grading bias. He seems to enjoy demonstrating his grasp of the material with less interest in creating an approachable & engaging learning environment for a diverse student body.

Professor Dosanjh is one of the most intelligent professors I've had. His lectures are packed with information, and his tests really evaluate your knowledge on the subject. However, he is available during his office hours and answers questions in an understandable way. You will have to put in the effort, but you will learn a lot.

It's a very lecture heavy class, and some days keeping your eyes open will be the real challenge, but Ranpal does a great job explaining every topic covered in the course, even though some are rather difficult for many to grasp. Overall he was genuinely one of the most obviously intelligent professors I've ever had.
Great teacher, inspiring in what he says and energetic so as to keep you engaged for the whole time. Open for conversations outside the classroom too.
Ranpal is very intimidating and intense at first but if you show an interest and put the work in, you'll be okay. Go to class (and pay attention), do the readings, and study for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ranpal is a fantastic professor and is generally really fun to talk about Philosophy with. He is extremely smart and while it can be hard to get him to speak at your level sometimes, you always leave the conversation feeling like you have learned something. 10/10 would recommend.
Class is very easy granted you show up and pay attention in class. Very nice guy and has some funny moments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory. Overall easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice and enthusiastic professor. I took this class hoping it would be similar to my Phil 230 class. It is nothing like Phil 230! Very hard grader. Gives long winded lectures that can become hard to listen to and even harder to understand. The notes are just long essays that can be hard to decipher. Prepare to put a lot of work into this class.

Great at explaining concepts and answering questions. Knowledgeable and cares about his subject. Does not let personal biases affect the way he presents the material. Difficult concepts and material but I loved the class anyway!

He is a great professor. All of the other reviews are from his 201 class. As a philosopher major that took 207 pretty late in the game, I can say that most people who aren't a philosopher major think that their 201 professor (no matter who it is) is bad. As for 207, he is an amazing professor. I would definitely take a class with him again.

Professor Dosanjh is extremely knowledgeable on the material, however, the lectures get long and are often difficult to follow due to the nature of the material. He will clarify anything you have problems with if you ask! His tests are very difficult, but you get a "cheat sheet" to make and use. Toughest class I've taken.

He is a very nice man and really gets to know each student. Every week you read a passage and write a one page essay. 20% of your grade is attendance and those essays. If you get an 80% in the course you have an A-. The class is fun, but the tests are very difficult. The average midterm and final test grade was a 60%. Study a lot for the tests!

Ranpal Dosanjh is a very nice professor, character wise. But, he is a very difficult professor, and his class is even more difficult. I went into Philosophy interested about it, and went out of it not knowing anything and more confused than when I first started the course.
This guy is soooo nice and friendly.  Very smart and interesting, not easy.

He is a super nice and helpful guy. I did not do too well at the midterm, because I used all 6 of my skips right away (whoops..) However, I made an effort to email him with any questions and went to his office hours quite a bit. I ended up bringing my grade up to a B with a lot of dedication. The best advice I  can say  is DON'T EVER GIVE UP!

He is a very hard grader.  This was his first semester at ISU. He wasn't very specific on what was going to be on the test. Test were short answer questions while other professors that taught the class had multiple choice.  He didn't seem willing to add a grading curve even though the average grade of the class was a D.

He's very nice and helps whenever you have a question. His lectures are long and boring, though. He isn't great at explaining concepts and ideas in his lectures. He is very vague on what is on the tests, hence why many people received poor grades. Doesn't give out study guides. Readings aren't too hard to do, some were a bit long.

20% of your grade is just from showing up in class. Everyday there is a group activity each worth 1% so you can miss a few classes. 50% of grade is based on final and midterm. Our midterm average test grade was a D. the content to learn about is awful and none of us get it at all. Final is cumulative but he makes his grading scale easier.

Professor Wohlgemuth, Is very nice and understanding but didn't respond to one of my emails the entire semester, his class is confusing and if you dont know math like calc you will not like him. Do the homework and get the material in the beginning or you will be very lost at the end
would not recommend

Literally nothing this guy says makes any sense whatsoever. The TA could not even understand what this man was trying to teach. If you have the option to take this class online do it because this class will tank your GPA. This class is a gen ed but has the difficulty of 4000 level class. If you have the option take the class online!

I really enjoyed having him as my professor. He's super nice, caring, understanding, and always willing to help. He has a good sense of humor and I felt very comfortable talking to him and going to his office hours.
Doesn't cover information that is on exams.

He seems like a nice guy. I wish nothing but the best for him. He is the epitome of a midwestern dad, it just sneaks into his lectures often. ECON 101 was pretty straightforward, just make sure you stay on top of the homework.
This man deserves a fancam.
Great structure, good lecturer, the best Econ professor I have had at ISU. It can be challenging, but if you just do the homework and study for exams, you will be fine.

I took this guy in econ 101 and econ 207, I had no choice for econ 207. Exams are 69% of your grade, if you dont need this class DO NOT TAKE IT. if you could avoid him, please do.I'm not even joking.He explains to you answers in a rude way. I do not RECOMMEND!

I personally thought Darin was a great professor. He explained things thoroughly and well. The only thing I did not like was at times, he over-explained which made me confused about the topic. He genuinely wants his students to do well. The practice exams he provides are extremely similar to the real exams. I recommend taking economics with Darin!
Made this class so much more difficult than it needed to be. Lots of homework for an introductory class. Please avoid if possible, even if the time fits well into your schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Darin's class was extremely difficult and was sometimes made more complicated than it needed to be, get ready for lots of homework that will take hours to complete. This class took me to the brink of insanity

Lectures were great! Just go to them and take good notes so you are ready for exams. Do all the homework's and assignments on time and do all the extra credit you can do. And be sure you know all your formulas and equations for the exams.
just go to lectures and you will be fine. He makes it clear what is most important to know on the exams and the difficulty is on par with high school econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor, always go to the lecture all quizzes and exams are from the lecture, and ignore all the slides and the textbook its useless. FOCUS ON LECTURES!
Would not recommend this professor for Econ 101. This class was made harder not by the material, but by the professor. 100/100 please get a different professor.

For Econ 101, this class should not have been has hard has it it currently. Would recommend taking this class with a different professor. Darin has heavy lectures and the recommended practice does not help with the exam. 1/5 do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend this econ professor, hard exams and heavy lectures. Please sign up for a different Econ 101 professor. A 101 class should not be this content heavy and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very heavy lectures that make little sense. The exam material is not what he tells you to study for; he often just expects you to know things. It should be easy for a 101 course. Class average on exams is usually very low; he offers extra credit, but it tends to be just as hard as the exam.
Does not know how to teach, expects you to understand without even explaining. Exams have nothing that we were taught in the lecture. He spends more time graphing than explaining anything.

There are 3 tests before the final and all 3 have practice exams that are very similar. Watch the videos from the textbook and do the questions that go along with them. They were SO helpful. Dr. Darin was interactive with the class, which made it fun, and I think he is the easiest ECON101 professor.
75% of final grade is based off test. Test are very difficult too, overall good Professor though
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Actually took ECON501 (not a form option). The class was hard - not because the content was overly difficult, but the pace was intense. If you miss one class or concept it is hard to catch up with how quickly the content builds upon previous lectures. Dr. Darin is friendly and willing to help, especially if he knew you were trying. Weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Darin as a guy but didn't love his lectures. He moves pretty fast and used the slides from the textbook rather than his own, which I think just didn't translate great with his teaching. Exams are tough but he usually offers up to 5 points of extra credit for everyone. He also offers TopHat classes for most lectures.

A professor that is actually pretty good at teaching. He didn't cover material fast enough to keep up with the homework and labs, but what he did teach you understood. He goes over some easy things multiple time when time would be spent better elsewhere. Overall he was a good professor for the class and I got what I needed to out of it.

Dr. Darin was a very kind professor who cares about his students. There is not very much work outside of class except a weekly online assignment. Tophat was 10% of the grade so I recommend going to class.  Overall a pretty good class, and a nice professor.
Do I understand Econ? no. Darin was really nice and seems like he really cares about his students. His lectures are boring but he gave us opportunity for extra credit on the exams.

Darin did a good job with his first semester teaching ECON 492. A simple course for graduating seniors. He was very responsive to any emails and questions. I couldn't be in class because of a conflicting class, but he always allowed me to make up missed points. Great professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The class is easy as long as you pay attention to lectures and do the TopHat homework questions. The extra credit helps and is easy if you watch the videos he posts with them. Be ready for dad jokes
Im not sure why everyone is saying hes a bad teacher. I think hes one of the best lecturers Ive had, and he does a great job explaining concepts. The class is also super easy (Econ101).

He went through things so quickly, and did not explain things well enough in class. He gave us nothing to prepare for the exams, and expected us to simply just study/know everything. Very hard, would not take this class with him again. Avoid at all costs!

Darin is a great guy. Microeconomics was made into a really simple concept with his lectures. Don't know what people are talking about on here badmouthing him. The lectures were good, and he repeats important concepts to really instill the topics into you. Gives extra credit after exams. Exams weren't that difficult if you went to class. What a guy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If Darin Wohlgemuth was an animal, he would be a lion because he is king of the economics world. The man's silky voice improves the day of anyone who hears it. 10 / 10 would frick with Darin's class again.

Well if you ask me this site is full of some salty slackers. Darin Wohlgemuth is an absolute gem in the economics world. So long as you go to his class and absorb his wisdom, you will not only succeed in this class, but become a much better person for it. I haven't even begun to mention his comical genius as well. All in all, a great professor.

Relatively easy class. He's a good lecturer and explains the stuff decently well. The class is easy as long as you read the notes before exams. The exams are somewhat easy and he gives decent extra credit as well, but you'll have to be present in class to get it. Not much else to say: just show up, take notes, and you'll be fine.

The class shouldn't be difficult, but it is because he's terrible at lecturing. I think he gives out extra credit because people don't tend to do well on the exams. I guess you have to give him the benefit of the doubt because I think it's his first time lecturing, but just cause he's knowledgeable and a professor, doesn't mean he can teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Really good at lecturing and if you have questions answers them very easily. Not that much homework and it is easy.

Punctuality & preparedness  BAD Lecture slides contain mistakes. Doesn't know how to use basic technology. Doesn't explain enough & repeats things already stated multiple times. After midterms, draws graphs every day in class, so you better understand what the graphs mean. Lots of work outside of class to understands the basics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is so kind, caring, and loves what he teaches. If you pay attention and put in the effort you will succeed. Remember to keep an open mind to what he teaches as he takes into account all angles (this is philosophy) and don't be closed off to what he asks you to think about.

If you attend class (which participation is not required), you will get a great hold of the material. There are a lot of readings but they aren't that difficult to understand. He grades very graciously.
