While I didn't interact with the professor at all, the class was quite easy. One quiz a week with a fairly simple final project. As long as you set time to do the quizes and skim through the lecture, you'll make a good grade.
Homework takes a very long time. He does not believe in giving As and purposely makes tests too hard. He swears excessively. He is disorganized and seems unprepared for lectures.

Fleming is an okay professor. He's not great, he's not awful, he's just okay. His lectures don't corelate to the homework material, and his exams tend to be rough. He is known for making the exams hard just to see what you will do. You're stuck taking his class so your best bet is to buckle down and pretend you like him more than you do.

He's a funny guy, with lots of cool stories and is good at teaching the material. He's a professor you like to talk to. However, be prepared for unclear criteria combined with harsh grading. Check your canvas A LOT and you'll do good enough.
Would be helpful if lectures for homework correlated better. Review sessions are a saving grace.
Tests are hard, and lectures do not help prepare for the tests. He prides himself for how hard he makes it.

Currently taking him right now for ABE 378 and he is certainly something, that's for sure. He spends 40 of the 50 minutes in class yapping about some equation and how you derive it (which isn't even useful to the class), and rarely does example problems like the ones in the homework or exam. Be prepared for a rough ride

Will spend the whole class deriving an equation and ranting about something. Rarely has time for examples in class. Tries to make jokes in class, but they are actually just rude remarks. Makes homework difficult and is proud of the difficulty. Gives 5 in class quizzes and lowest is dropped.

He's not the worst lecturer I have had but the content isn't too bad. Go to the exam review TA sessions and you'll do good. If you play into his jokes, he'll like you. Also, make sure to ask about submarines in lecture!

Took the summer ABE3780 course and struggled. There were three exams; they did not match the content from the practice exams; homework was very hard. The average class exam score of the first two exams was 55%, meaning more than half of the class was failing. There was no curve at the end of the course, so lots of people had failed without reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had to withdraw due to the horror of his summer class. Took the content of Dr. Biddle word for word, example for example and amde it worse by the way he teaches. The summer 2025 first exam was 100000x harder than the spring 2025, I mean no one took a good grade on it at all. Overall a mediocre person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fleming is a great teacher. He gives you all the necessary information to succeed, and I love his tangents. Nuclear Submarine life is interesting!
Great lectures and very inspiring. I love submarines.

I see so many people rating this class and Professor Fleming terribly. It is not a hard class, and AP Physics in High School was 100 times harder compared to this. Fleming is always available to help and give more than enough information from the slides, and they are POSTED too. There is extra credit, and I got 104%. Just study.
Not gonna lie, if it is a super difficult course I may not recommend. However, if you are a decent student, the class should be free and he makes lectures entertaining.
Some People didnt like him, he definelty will go on tangets that have nothing to do with physics but they are hilarious and he is one of the best professors I have ever had.

Reads off the slides super quickly and expects the students to know how to apply equations to problems without showing examples. Our class had an all time low average on an exam; the next class he told us he made the exam harder but still doesn't know how we did worse than the average last semester.

Terrible professor. Nothing more to say than that. Hope he isn't the only professor for the required course. Stay away if possible. Watch Prof Bittle on YouTube; way more helpful than when he tries to explain a topic since he always goes on some unnecessary tangent on unrelated topics from his past.

He is such a terrible professor. He derives an equation for the entirety of the lecture off of his Ipad explaining nothing. He talks down to you when you try and ask questions. He puts things on the homework's that he did not cover in lecture and expects you to just know these things. Considering he is the only professor just hope he gets fired.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a bit disorganized but great teacher and hilarious. I had him for ENGR 1600 which wasn't difficult, but he made the class fun.

4 or 5 exams in the semester. Lots of HW. HW is awful. Needed an LLM to do it and we did nothing comparable in difficulty on quizzes or exams. He is decently funny, but got old quick because of how bad he is at giving lectures. TopHat and help room for extra credit. I didn't read the textbook b/c the class was easy for me. Others think otherwise.

Course content is relatively straight-forward, but somehow this man teaches it so horribly. Watch Dr. Biddle's lectures on youtube instead. Fleming uses Biddle's content sentence-for-sentence, example-for-example, yet only one of them actually teaches the content...

Worst professor I have ever had. Does little to no teaching that is beneficial to you or your work. Homework becomes practically impossible without looking up videos actually teaching you the concepts or attending office hours/review sessions. Incompetent in teaching. Almost feels like he does not WANT you to do well. Avoid at all costs.
Flemming was an overall great teacher who kept the lectures interesting and engaging.
Great professor, you either love him or you hate him but he was great. The only time I wanted to show up for a class.

I'm a 3rd yr engineering student who has never considered withdrawing from a class before, but I am withdrawing from his. He is rude & patronizing under the guise of "dry humor", literally calling an auditorium of over 100 students idiots regularly. He does very little actual teaching and has no study materials for exams. Good luck if you have him.

Avoid this guy if you're taking physics in the future. He is unqualified as he does not even have a physics degree. Also goes on unnecessary side tangents about random topics and barely teaches the content. Horrible idea of the physics department to have engineering professors as "physics instructors".

I hate the way that he talks, the way that he walks, and the way that he dresses. Fleming was possibly the worst professor I have had during my time at Iowa State so far. His lectures taught me nothing, he would go off on side tangents instead of teaching, and provided no good resources to study to prepare for exams.

Fleming is an overall good professor who strives to make lectures interesting. Unfortunately, as this was his first semester teaching 231, he was inexperienced. He would sometimes spend too much time going off on tangents about unrelated material and thus didn't fully cover the examples he began in class. Middle of the road pick in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Fleming may have had good intentions, but their inexperience with the content and preference for tangents over clear explanations made this course challenging for students.
Goes on frequent side tangents on unrelated material. No good testing helps. Rude, inconsiderate, and difficult to talk to after class and during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
AVOID AT ALL COST IN PHYSICS COURSES!!!!!

He goes on unnecessary side tangents that distract from the main material. Unqualified to teach physics courses. Does not upload lecture or activity notes online until the day of or after the exam. Gives minimal studying resources for exams. Is condescending to students who ask for help or are tardy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fleming definitely has the ability to be a good teacher, but I felt like he did not try very hard. He would even make comments saying "if I was a better teacher then..." He will mostly read off powerpoint slides to teach the class and moved extremely fast through them. Most of the grading points come later in the semester so don't freak out early.

Professor Fleming is a great guy, when he is in a good mood. It is vital to attend class or he will be reluctant to help you. Schedule office hours with him it is the most helpful resource. Engr 160 is a extremely pointless class, we learned outdated VBA. This class basically prepares you for mechanical engineering.

Professor Fleming made mechanics of fluids into "try not to lose my mind" class. Unfortunately, I found him to be pessimistic, rude, and overall rather difficult. Go to his office hours if you want to succeed in the course. If you do not regularly attend lecture and ask for help, this will strain your relationship and make him reluctant to help you
Does love him a submarine or airplane problem.
He talks about submarines a lot. If you don't like dry humor and coffee, you'll probably hate this class.
He taught me all the dos and donts of having a great lawn and being on a military submarine, it was great!
Learned nothing about engineering, but I did learn how to have the best lawn in the game 10/10 would take again
This guys rocks and teaches at the same time! You can tell he loves his job. A blessing to have as an instructer!  Much Love!

Easiest class at Iowa State University next to ComSci 103. Kleptach freakin rules, if you think otherwise, you might as well cease to exist. When you play concerts you usually get the impression that symphonic and wind ensemble laugh at how mediocre the band sounds but the songs are fun and its an easy A. Take it.

Kick 'em in the Kleptach! (Yeah! The Kleptach!). The man has about the funniest last name possible and Emperor Kleppy lives up to it in person, he picks lots of great Sousa marches for concert band and makes that group really fun and a nice way to get an easy A and to stay with an instrument. Plus, he helps out with marching band and with pep band.
Obvious he loves his job.

I LOVE this man!!!! He's the best ever. I'll be in his band for my fifth semester next spring, and I can't wait. Not a strict conductor, just loves to have fun and enjoy the music. Recommendations: write down all the funny things he comes up with during class. It makes an awesome "Kleptach Quotes" keepsake. Say hi to the crazy oboist Nikki!
Words cannot describe the greatness of this director.  I've been through some crappy band experiences in my time and this was a sight for sore eyes.
awesome

He's willing to help you play the music; he wants you to succeed.  You could get through the class without learning anything new about music, though.  That's OK if you're looking for a fun, informal band.
Well.. Its a EASY A, but if you want to play something other than marches, don't take it.  Fill out the absence sheets if you're gone, but he usually doesn't have a problem with you not showing up.
Mr Kleptach is so sweet. He's like your grandpa or santa klaus. Yeah, maybe not the greatest conductor but its concert band-who cares? He doesnt have the greatest players to work with either.
Good guy, but he doesn't have the greatest choice in music pieces to play.  I would have rather not done so many marches.
OH YEAH
He's getting kinda old to do this, but he's really nice and can be kinda funny at times. He likes to do a lot of marches in concert band and really likes to push for excellence.
Very relaxed conductor.  Maybe not the best, but he is fun and doesn't take things too seriously.  If you just want to play without a lot of stress, take this class.

I felt that the way he conducted Concert Band was very unprofessional. I constently makes mistakes without knowing in and his choice of concert music isn't the greatest. Though he is a lot of fun and the  course is a breeze, he's a crappy conductor.

Do NOT take dsn1020 with him. He is impossible to reach when not in class and when in class is not helpful at all. He will barely explain projects and expect you to know what he wants. He has clear favorite students based on style and talent even though he is teaching an intro course, and obviously enjoys certain kinds of work more. Does not shower

Project criteria is often vague, he expects you to figure out what is necessary to convey your idea, he pushes for a lot of production mainly physical (models, drawings) but towards the end of the semester is more lenient on digital production, he likes weird designs and holds traditional viewpoints of architecture
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst professors, barely gives any feedback on your work. Doesn't have any criteria filled out on canvas so you don't even know what you are graded on. His projects are completely different from the ones of other professors and have extremely high expectations. You can never find him outside of class even through email.

For someone who is not very artsy, Pete was an amazing professor. Will tell you what is wrong and make YOU figure it out instead of just telling you. Very laid back and brings a good vibe with him to class every day. If you take his class seriously, he will make you enjoy the class.
Worst professor ever. Never available to talk, he doesn't teach anything in the class. No help from his side.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
He's a good teacher, but the instructions about projects and grading can be vague in class. If you were graded unfairly, argue for a better grade. The better you can explain your art, the better the grade. His class was WORK, but if you enjoy being creative, it'll be fun.
(PS, Don't get too intimidated by him. You'll have more fun arguing with him)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pete is an interesting guy, but just hear him out and give him due consideration. He has a preferred style, but for good reason. His goal is to use a specific studio style to make you do things that most would consider to be further into art than design to get you to think differently than your peers. Invest the time, swallow your pride, buckle up.

Pete is a studio instructor who believes certain aesthetics are universally better or worse than others, which is a somewhat outdated standpoint within our post-postmodern era of architecture. He also puts a huge emphasis on the conceptual aspect of design, for better or for worse.
God tier
This man is the real deal. I am 100x better because of his class. He is the greatest inspiration I have ever had.

Excellent professor.  Makes you work for your grade, so others might not review him different.  But the point of going to college is to learn and expand your horizon so you can be better in the real world so those who want an easy " A" really aren't learning what they should be learning.  Group projects are fun and challenging.

One of the best professors I have ever had.  He opens your mind up to things you may have never occurred to you.  If you want learn out of the box thinking then take as many classes as he offers.  ISU is lucky to have him.  His mind is literally amazing.

Awesome teacher. Very difficult class/projects, but Pete is a great resource and helps you think in ways you never thought possible. Really inspiring (sorry for sounding cheesy). Do the work, get an a.

We had some rough patches, but I believe he is honestly concerned with each student in his class, and he is willing to work with you to better your design skills. Mine certainly improved. This is not always true of studio professors.  I wish he was in class a bit more though...he goes to reviews a lot.

He has a very unique style of teaching this class considering he teaches a 400 level class as well, but if you chalenge the things he tells you to do or the rules of the asignment you will be in his good graces. Also make sure you turn in every asignment becuase they all effect your grade a lot

This was a required class and he did not give clear details on what needed to be done.  This ended up being great because I learned a lot and he taught a lot.  As long as you try he will help you.  I have learned so much from him.  He is one of the hardest but best professors I have had.
Mr. Goche was the most difficult teacher i have ever had, but you come out with sooooo much learned its rediculous.  I would recommend him if you want a challenge and if you want very good citiques.

I want to explain that he has the opposite of a clear grading scale. He will give an incomplete assignment the same grade as a completed assignment graded on the same rubric. If you like extremely moody grading and a teacher who can't email you when he won't show up to class, you'd love his class.

Dr. Griffiths was a super fun professor, I think he's one of those you either love him or hate him kind of professors, mainly because he likes to joke around a lot and gets off topic relatively frequently. His exam papers are pretty hefty, but there's only 2 you have to take along with 4 other smaller essays. Good professor if you like silly profs.
Love the professor, but he is a tough grader. The class is just papers, not tests, and requirements for papers were not given out 100% so you just had to know what to do.

Reasons why you should take his class (HIST 201):
- Final is worth 40% of your grade
- He reads from only the slides
- His syllabus makes no sense
- Refuses to create any kind of rubric on what he's expecting
- Misses key points for an essay that are important
- Has not set up an actual Canvas page
- Grading homework assignments is very unclear

Provides no grading rubric for the assignments. If you are planning on taking this class, remember: you CANNOT pass this class by only using the reading he provides. Despite it not saying it on the assignment, he expects you to research outside sources to help you get a full grasp of the assignment. He also doesn't believe in perfect grades.

Gives absolutely no rubric on how to write papers, and no feedback either. Says things in class about grading that don't line up at all with the grades actually given as well as assignment expectations. Lectures are not engaging at all so makes it very hard to want to go to class where attendance is mandatory. Wouldn't take another class from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great experience taking the class! He is highly knowledgeable about the subject material and makes lectures engaging with his funny commentary and banter. Attendance is very important, so prepare to show up to class every time. Grading on assignments/tests isn't super harsh, but expect to put in adequate effort for an A.

This class was primarily made up of writing essays. Expect three two pages papers along with two 8 page essays. There is no homework and class is mandatory. Professor is very fun and engages with his class. His grading is pretty harsh and attendance makes up a huge part of your grade. As long as you go to class you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Paul Griffiths was a very funny professor, and he made the lectures engaging and fun. This class was difficult for one main reason, the exams. You had two exams and a final. You were given a list of around six prompts and were given just one weekend to write two minimum four-page essays using the prompts given. Fun professor hard class.

The professor creates decent lectures and is pretty funny, however, his notes slides can lack in information and he often goes off on tangents. He assigns two 4 page essays that are expected to be done in about 3 days. His due dates aren't in favor of his students either. Expect to write these essays during parent weekend and Thanksgiving break.

Really knowledgeable, made lectures interesting, and is a guy you can just tell knows a ton about what he is talking about. The tests are papers, however, if you take good lecture notes then the papers are not to difficult, also working with him or the other teacher in the room goes a long way.

Nice guy, seems to really care about his students and want everyone to do well. He is very helpful and easy reach outside of class. His lectures are interesting, but super hard to follow. I had a really tough time taking notes because there is almost no words on the powerpoints and he kind of rambles on so it's tough to know what to write.

Dont take this class if you dont like or arent good at writing papers. Also dont take if you rely on notes a lot, his slides do absolutely nothing for you. His lectures are long and he goes off on tangents a lot. He is an easy grader too, but dont expect your grade to be in for about 3-4 weeks after you submit your assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To begin, the class itself isn't too bad if you like writing long papers. There are 3 papers that are at least 8 pages long with a short amount of time to do them. That part of the class may be stressful however, Dr. Griffiths has wonderful lectures that are funny and entertaining which makes the 75 mins fly by. Be ready to write but also have fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only thing this professor has going for him is his humor. Not a lot of points to be earned and gives unreasonable long essays for a short amount of time.

Dr. Griffiths truly does care about his students and lectures with him are fairly entertaining. He usually is a fairly easy grader but his exams are always long papers. Like 8 pages minimum for the first 2 exams and 9 for the final. If you clearly explain your thoughts, show up to recitation, and participate in lectures you'll easily pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very good guy- will work with you to help you succeed and has hilarious and very interesting lectures. One of my favorite lecturers in the history department.

thick accent! You don't really need to pay attention in class. There are three quizzes in the beginning-rather hard in my opinion, but I'd never taken a history class before so it was all new stuff to me. You're mainly graded on three large essays but he's an easy grader. I was expecting a D- in the class and finished with a B somehow. Very comical
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Keeps class fun and interesting. There is a lot of reading, but if you find the material interesting, that wont be a problem. Make use of him as well as TAs to fully understand how he wants essays formatted and the contents he wants in them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Griffiths is pretty funny while in lecture and will call out some people in class but not embarrassing them. He has an english accent and doesn't use a mic so sometimes its hard to hear. Overall, if you participate in section and write decent papers for the exams you will pass with an A. He also has a lot of chances in class for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fun class but the grading is somewhat tough. There are only 100 total points in the class. Your grade is mostly based on the three exams. He doesn't use a textbook and doesn't give out homework, which was nice until I did not know how to study for the final exam. attendance is mandatory to pass. Cool guy but I wish there were more points possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Just show up to lecture, take notes, it's really not that hard. Just writing the essay exams isn't fun (not very bad though). Really funny and laid-back professor.

He is an ok professor. I didn't do so well due to the fact I missed a lot of days. His lectures are very boring and the notes on the slideshows are short. You better understand thick British accents to pick up what he's saying. He is from Liverpool, (very welfare dependent city), so he is against republicans and jokes about them/Trump.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I enjoy it
It was a summer 4 week class. 2 hour lectures and i found it very interesting and actually fun. I enjoy history also but be prepared to write essays like your life depends on it
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Griffiths is one of my favourite professors, though he is arrogant and teases students. If you take what he says literally you won't like him. He genuinely cares  and will go out of his way to help you succeed.  His personality isn't for everyone but he teaches the material well, is very knowledgeable, and shares fun relevant stories and trivia.

He is British, and proudly so. His accent is thick, and is hard to understand sometimes. He is very passionate about this subject, and really knows what he is talking about, except the lectures are super boring. Regardless, he is super helpful, and is funny.

Very funny and informational instructor.  Doesn't use BlackBoard, so you need to email him or go to his office to see grades. Points are given for attendance so go to class. Uses power points with little information, so write down as many words he says as you can. English accent is tough to understand at first, but eventually you don't even notice.

Griffiths is one of the best and most knowledgable professors I've had at ISU.  He meanders a bit and is somewhat hard to follow, but if you do the readings, show up to class and take notes, all will be well.  He jokes around a lot, and it may seem like he is attacking you personally, but this is definitely not the case.  I recommend him highly.

He knows his stuff , but it can seem like he is not prepared until you realize that he really does not need a single note to talk for hour.  Do take notes, do the readings, and do not take his jabs at you seriously.  He will give you a hard time, but if you are struggling he will of out of his way to help you.

This is the second class I've taken with him. One of the best professors I've had at ISU. He really knows what he is talking about. He does pick on people sometimes, but it's always in good taste. He takes the time to get to know his students, which wasn't very difficult considering there were 10 people in the class

Paul is fantastic at his craft.  The most refreshing thing about his classes is they are not taught in a "normal" way.  If you slack off you will get a poor grade.  If you are at least making a valid attempt he is very helpful and you will get a respectable grade.  Quizes are rough but not impossible.

While I can definitely understand why some people don't like him, I thoroughly enjoyed this class with Paul. He's funny, keeps things interesting, and really knows his stuff. The way he lectures is actually pretty entertaining. That being said, he's a tough grader and can sometimes come off a bit intimidating. Definitely recommend him though.

Love his sense of humor, but it's definitely not for everyone.  He really knows his stuff, and does a good job of teaching it. Doesn't return quizzes or papers, so you really don't know what you missed or could stand to work on.  That being said, I've had him for two classes, and rec'd an A- in one, B+ in other, and I felt both marks were fair.

He's quite rude towards people and spends about 10-15 minutes of the lecture just joking around or pointing things out in the crowd such as people yawning. His class is very powerpoint heavy, but not boring. The way he opens your mind to western civilization is quite unique, but again, his time wasting/rudeness upset me a bit.

He was terrible, I hated this class. He joked at the students expense, made a student plug the meter for his car, was so disorganized I couldn't take notes, and was very unprepared for lectures. I would not recommend him to an enemy. I couldnt figure out what he wanted for his tests or quizzes even at the end of the semester. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Hes' a British guy and he's hiliarious. Lecture is not mandatory but recitation is. Over all he tests of themes and gives you a vary good idea of what they are going to be. His test were fairly easy consiting of just a couple essay questions. Would recommend him for any classes!.

An arrogant man, but he knows what he's talking about. An odd little British man, yet quite entertaining. He tells you what you need to know for test/quizzes SO STUDY IT! And do your research for the final essay.

He has an odd sense of humor but his stories are pretty funny. He loves to tease Americans because he is British but it is pretty funny. The class in general is difficult and you really have to study and do research on and take lots of time for homework and stuff especially before tests.

He covers a lot of material with wordy essays but he tries to make it as interesting as possible.  if you have a class that is willing to talk the discussions can be interesting.  He has an odd sense of humor, and class might seem easy, but come quiz/test/essay time, make sure you do your research.

Most of his lectures are off-topic. Quizzes are tough to get points. He teased his class a lot, but it ate most of our times. Take this class if you like a humorous type and like history. Don't take this class if you think most of his talking waste your time. He's strict on essays, but seems helpful to students who have problems with essays.
He seems arrogant at first but after a while his classes were fun. The stories he tells are hilarious and make the class interesting. Not an easy class if you're looking to get an A
Disorganized. Quizzes are WAY too hard. At one point, the highest quiz score in the class was 301/400.
Awesome professor. I love every class I've taken with him. Also it's great that he is intelligent, funny, and hot.

One of the best professors I've had at ISU. Definitely a very good representative of the history department. At first the course seemed overwhelming but he gave me all the sources I needed for my paper. I'd take another class from him in a heartbeat. Doesn't help that he's easy on the eyes in a European way.
Amazing professor. Loved both classes I took with him.
Bounces from one subject to another. Tests are essay and easy but is very strict on the term paper.

Very disorganized. Just talks and rambles and goes off on tangents. He's funny though, which makes it a little more bearable, and the accent is hot. I don't know how, but I got a B in the class and missed quite frequently. He's very, very smart, but maybe power point lectures would help as it was impossible to take any kind of notes.
disorganized. thinks he's great.
This guy was not very organized. His lectures were off-topic a lot, and our TAs corrected him during labs often. Tough to follow. However, he is hilarious and fun, so class wasn't too boring.
Very interesting class. Mostly becasue he goes of topic and never realy teaches anything. The test get easier as the course goes on and the TAs made up for his lack of teaching.

I enjoyed his class. He has a good back and forth banter with students and is willing to go out of his way to help you out. He knows which students are willing to work and which ones are going to screw off.
Like the other posts.  He is very funny, but I've heard other teachers are easier?!?!
Funny, makes class not so boring, sucks at teaching but doesnt matter because tests are really easy

Yes, he's sort of cute.  Yes, the accent is intriguing.  But wow, he was sooo confusing.  Lectures are completely useless and unorganized.  Make sure to go to recitation if you plan on learning anything.
Funny for a brit and smart.
Best teacher ever. He was funny and involved that into his teachings. He is always making fun of various pictures of looking up his cricket and futbol scores during our little streching breaks.
Great teacher!  Funny as hell, makes class a pleasure.  Sexy, too, in that older-and-intellectual kind of way.
Yum!  I would take any of his classes not only because he is a great professor (hilarious, helpful, interesting), but because I enjoy thinking dirty thoughts about him during and after class.

WORST CLASS!  He doesn't emphasize anything for the tests so you go in there with very poor notes and the book isn't relavent to the tests.  I really couldn't stand this class so I dropped it and I'm glad I did because everyone I talked to that stayed in the class got a C- or lower.

He has an English accent so it's like watching the history channel when you go to class. He is a good teacher but talks a little fast. All in all he is an effective teacher as long as you go to class.
Very confusing throughout his lecture, nots of notes that are unclear. Tests are essay format, so that can be difficult for some. Lots of terms to memorize.

Some would say that he isn't very effective in his lectures. I would disagree. He is very passionate about what he teaches, and is there for students who want to learn about the subject, not just for credit.
The worst prof in Hist dept. in my opinion. He always seemed to give girls (only the hot ones) better grades, more points for participation, etc. He was terrible
No Comments
No Comments

Off topic 75% of the time in lecture, tests are written in a challenging format and are very confusing. During our semester, we had a final project which was incredibly disorganized. Constantly late sending out announcements. Learned almost everything in the class by reading the slides on my own.

Very knowledgeable professor. Once told me the antichrist could possess AI. Brings up Subnautica at least once per semester. People say he "wants a lot of students to fail," which is true but misleading out of context. The only people he wants to fail are those trying to game the major, which unfortunately is a lot. This man is an oracle of truth.
Underrated professor. If you listen to him, the material will make sense. Does say questionable things sometimes, though jokingly.

Just a few highlights: On topic 30% of the time. Lectures are typed on a laptop running a bootleg version of windows 7 using a windows 98 asthetic. Often says something is "really quite simple", meaning you need to study it outside of class. Once talked about mass genocide. However, he does write exams, so understanding him is good for preperation.
do not take this professor. or even come close to him. he's incredibly disrespectful and loves to be in power and is just a menace.
shouldve never become a teacher, like wdym you dont want the students to succeed man wtf 😭

everybody says he's horrible but i lowkey can't keep pretending I don't like the guy. Granted, he's not that great at presenting things in a manner that people can understand, but he's pretty funny, and will catch you off guard with a zinger. I think he recycles the same couple jokes every semester as I've heard from others, but they are good ones

Tests and attendance are worth a lot. Make sure you attend lectures. They are not the most helpful but they will boost your grade. He talks about random things that aren't very relevant to exams. I learned the most from the ZyBooks.
228 is absolutely a weedout class but compared to the other professors Batinov geniunely makes an effort to fail as many students as he possibly can and is proud of that
does not want students to succeed.

Georgi is such a bad teacher. Lectures are mandatory, and you gain so little from going to them. The exams often cover material you won't cover in class. Georgi makes info up and arives late daily. Brags that 70% will fail. The homework assignments are graded heavily by the TAs. They run the tests and submit the grades without checking your code.

The lectures were required to complete a tophat form before the lecture finished. Georgi did NOT talk about anything useful during the 55-minute lectures. Most TAs were extremely harsh graders and often would run tests and grade your homework solely on the score it received. Prepare to teach this class to yourself.

Where to start with Batinov? I think everyone should have him at least once for the experience. He's not very good at explaining things in lectures which sucked because they were mandatory. He does make up for it somewhat in the funny out-of-pocket comments. The TA's exam reviews really carried the education part so make sure to attend those.

did alright in his data structures @ isu.
the TA's weren't the best, took a long time for them to grade our assignments and tests, only for the grades to not be very accurate, and be regraded but ONLY AFTER STUDENTS REQUESTED A REGRADE.

Lecture is mandatory with attendance, however he barely discusses topics and doesn't do it in detail. Lots of tangents, be ready to learn basically everything on your own. Although I will say homework is clear and exams are fair.
He is a great professor. The more effort you put into this  class, the more success you will achieve. However, this class requires a lot of self-study and dedication to truly understand the material.

One of my favorite classes so far. Georgi's lectures had clear and engaging explanations and examples. The first half of the class is almost completely a repetition of COMS 227, and if you don't rush through zyBooks exercises, they give a pretty good understanding of the new material. 
Also, I strongly recommend using Piazza for help with homework.

I like Georgi Batinov as a person, but as a teacher in com S 2280 not so much. Homeworks had bare minimum guidelines, so it felt like you were gambling with your submission because the graders were very strict. Exams lacked prep material. All you got was an out dated practice exam and a list of the material on the exam. Lectures weren't great.

I hated Georgi with a passion. He is knowledgeable, but he flies through content without offering much explanation (and then claims it's "really quite simple"). Went so fast I couldn't write down half of the code most times. He was also constantly late to class. Homework assignments are also typically a mess with little to no communication.

This class was horribly mismanaged. The material wasn't particularly difficult to understand, but exams were thrown together with random questions and no proper way to prepare. He would allow students to argue for points back, but this shouldn't be how you have to maintain a grade in my opinion. Not to mention the lectures were practically useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lacks clear grading criteria. Told us in class to do crack. Tests over random things not covered in class, and makes up his own answers. Exam reviews are really just yap sessions & don't provide useful information. He lets you argue points back, but won't make it easy. Always shows up to class & exams late. Lacks respect for students & their time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Batinov offloads almost all of his work to them and as a result not many want to work with him. This lowers the bar for being a TA so they do not fully understand the material or(in my case) the grading criteria on the syllabus. He gives thoughtful answers to questions, though. Overall very knowledgeable, just does not care about the class much.

Professor required students to stay 1 hour or more past lecture time to demo their projects. Some groups could not demo as someone needed to take the room. He said to stay after the next lecture to demo. Assignment documents are vague and confusing with requirements not clear. Blames the students for being "confused". Contradicts the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: “I don't respond to emails so don't bother emailing me”. Exams are terrible, never covering what is mentioned in class, and he also assigned me a completely different exam bc I had accommodations (which were topics he didn't go over). I aced the projects, I did think they were fun and pretty engaging.  Lectures were mandatory.

Is Georgi the best prof I've had at Iowa State? No. To be honest his lectures can be boring and you will probably spend a lot of time studying outside of class to catch up. You will have to put in more work to succeed. Even if Georgi isn't a very good prof he's funny though. Let us watch Starship troopers. 5 stars.

Claims to be one of the busiest professors in the department. Frequently late to class. Held online class for 7PM during march madness...? He clearly is knowledgeable in the field, but lectures off of slides that were passed down to him. Exam scores were low, and graded pretty harshly for some questions. I don't feel like I learned much from him

The only word to describe Batinov is lazy. He uses the same structure for the class every semester and still posts the homework assignments about a week after he said he would. Overall, he is VERY unorganized and has terrible communication outside his sections, making the other class professors look bad.

Walking contradiction of himself. Easy course understood all the concepts, however, I had to stop attending and trying because he made it clear that the students were not the priority. Unfortunately, he was either the only or one of the few professors that taught this course. Extremely boring, and uninspired to say the least.

His lectures can be pretty boring and hard to focus in mostly because he does all of his lectures just by typing in Notepad++. For Com S 228 specifically, just be aware of the difficulty of the tests. I was able to secure almost perfect scores on every single coding assignment while at the same time struggling to get passing grades on the exams.
doesn't even care enough to answer emails
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot judge his teaching style because I learned better from coding the concepts in class. I asked multiple questions that were upvoted by many other students just to not receive a response and have to go to a TA. Also, weirdly canceled lectures 10 and 50 minutes before for seemingly predictable reasons.

He's a decent enough lecturer to let me do decent enough on the tests. Homework in this class is a pain because the directions aren't always clear what exactly they want from you, and if you don't do it how they want you'll lose points.

This professor is so far one of my favorite at Iowa State. He's tough on his students but does it in his best effort to see them succeed. Will go over where you lost points on exams or homeworks and helps you know where you messed up. Lecture attendance was graded which I like because lectures in this class are pretty needed in order to succeed.

Georgi is a good professor, an old school one. He will help you achieve the knowledge you need but don't go there thinking you an do everything a day before the exams. Study on your own, try to understand the material. This class is the most important one in my opinion since it will help you pass an interview.
Professor Georgi Batinov is probably the best computer science teacher I have had so far. He is a really nice person and great a teaching.
This class goes through a lot of material so attending the lectures is very important.

Most of these reviews are coming from students who put minimal effort and blame it on the professor. He genuinely cares for your mental health, and very often says that it is ok to struggle in this and future classes. His teaching style isn't very good, I feel like there could be a massive improvement but he does upload his lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not care about the students at all. Just wants to have a job. Always cancel his office hours or even lectures. He finishes class too early. Overal, he's lazy. He also used racist and sexist jokes. Exams are very difficult and don't have enough time at all.

Just does a text to speech of his slides during lecture, and then a speech back to text taking notes on his notepad ++. Never uses an IDE to explain how codes work, just notepad++ in a very unorganized fashion. Extremely strict with homeworks all semester. Didn't actually learn a single thing from coming to classes, learnt it all from outside tutor
He is funny.  What else could you want.
Funny and very caring.

I am really surprised by how low people are rating him.  You may not like his style of lectures but you can't deny he cares about his students and wants them to do well.  He is also hilarious and really fun to talk to.

This professor had by far the most entertaining lectures I've ever had in a college course.  Attendance was not required but I never wanted to miss a lecture.  Really nice guy and genuinely funny.  Course itself was a little challenging at times but that's to be expected from this subject.

Been a few semesters but yall been doing Georgi dirty, the class is definitely tough but I thought Georgi was really fun, a good lecturer, and made learning about data structures and algorithms much more bearable. I would rather have him use Notepad++ than show slides with code blocks that take more time to understand. Put some respect on his name.
Be prepared to worked way to hard for a 200 level class, he does not care about you. He does not respond to emails. I wolf never take him again

Within a week we had already shelled out $100 so that the professor could take attendance... lectures were required and not generally helpful. The professor takes notes on Notepad++ with a green-black "hacker" theme on an old Windows 7 laptop without a genuine license. Lectures were interrupted every few minutes by a Windows popup: average at best.
A confusingly humorous professor who enjoys teaching, I was just not the biggest fan of the class as a whole

The lectures were literally all on notepad++. The lectures were mandatory participation for points. Overall the lectures almost dont help you with learning how to apply data structures. But overall the quality of teaching was horrible nor the lack of care of teaching. I do not recommend him as a professor

Dr. Batinov is a fun professor with interesting speeches every now and then during lecture, but I would have wished for a much better professor for this course. His teaching style is awful; he just types stuff from a powerpoint on to a text file. Extremely inaccessible outside of class too, he rarely responds to emails in a timely manner.

I really liked him as a person, but I didn't always go to class because I felt like I could learn better off Youtube. Some of the homework required very technical instructions but sometimes details wouldn't be communicated well, which resulted in frustration. Overall, I would be friends with Batinov but he wasn't my favorite teacher.

He genuinely cares about his students and wants all of them to do well. If you go to get help from him in his office hours he is genuinely helpful, he spends time after class answering questions from students. He is kind and encouraging, the kind of professor one should strive to be. The only downfall of this class is that the TAs are terrible.

Georgi is a great guy and cares about his students, but this class was very unorganized. The PDFs and slides were hard to follow in case you missed. He takes lecture notes onto a textfile and it's often explained poorly. He sidetracks a lot so it's hard to pull the important information. Going to office hours helped. Overall was frustrating all sem
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Batinov is a professor that genuinely cares. A lot of people dislike 228 because it requires work and repetition. If you don't understand concepts he's more than willing to answer questions in class and during his office hours. You can tell he wants us to succeed. He's been very flexible this semester and cares about our mental health/burning out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Won't answer emails. I have a job and the main way I communicate with profs is through email so it blocked it. Probably sexist, he got upset everytime I asked a question but if a guy in my class asked the same thing he would answer. Got upset when I had a class during an exam and asked for a make-up time. make ups are for "medical emergencies only"

Class overall is meh but communication with TA's sucks. Class is very lecture heavy, mainly just listen as he types onto a txt from slides. Project has a bonus for each day submitted early, rules weren't clear for a part of it and the docs were changed. Everyone had to resub and lost points, we were told we should have thought of it earlier.

Batinov is never on topic and frequently spends lectures going on random tangents about the real world or other irrelevant topics like capitalism and communism. Some of the test questions and projects were very poorly worded and even left TAs confused. Class is very poorly organized and it's rather unfortunate because it's such an important class.

I went to class only because he kept saying that he was going to do TopHat, but he never did. He cancelled class 3 times, but never gave us more than a 15 minute warning and once walked in 5 minutes late to cancel. Lectures were very boring. Go to the labs and turn everything in on time. Make a good cheat sheet for the test and you'll be fine.

A lot to say for this guy. Did not take class seriously -- several days where he cancelled, had a sub for the first day of class. Second day of class, told us we wouldn't enjoy the class because no one enjoys math. That attitude really brought stuff down. Said a lot of things that were not appropriate for the setting and made people uncomfortable.

Doesnt seem to care. Cancels or ends lectures early often. Things arent posted in time for labs or class. Either doesnt reply, or takes forever to reply to emails. Makes lecture awkward by forcing silence if someone doesnt volunteer to answer a question he asked.

He rambles a lot in his lectures and it usually doesnt make sense, nor is it relevant to the topic on hand. I often leave class learning absolutely nothing. Most of the people in my class are not computer science majors because it is an entry level course but he will go on and on about how a computer works instead teaching us the code/material.

Georgi is the type of teacher I respect. He made sure to teach a subject until you got bored with it rather than move on to a new one while you're still trying to understand. He would give 5 minutes breaks in the middle of class to "give your brain a rest." Even with the slower pace and breaks, we still got all the material covered.

He's actually not that bad. His exams come directly from his slides. He explains things fairly easily. The only thing that I didn't like is that his exams are easy in a sense, but they are graded way too harshly. You either get a 0 or you get full points. There's no partial credit for any questions you can't fully answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He seems inexperienced as a professor and seems to always be changing assignment requirements or adding readings the day before the exam. Lectures are dry and he doesnt post the slides and yet doesnt slow down enough for you to take notes. Be prepared for exam questions that are super specific. Would not take again with him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Absolutely adored Professor Gaffar. Every single person who rated him poorly is someone who failed his class. Was extremely nice and SUPER smart. You can tell he really loves what he teaches. As long as you actually show up to class and actually do the work you will without a doubt get an A+.
Literally the worst course I have taken at Iowa State. Do not waste your time and money. This guy is a total clown.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not recommend

This man will ramble and rant for the entire lecture and expect you to get an actual lessons-worth of understanding from it. You try to take notes every class but he'd end up completely off topic. The actually important or relevant parts are given in single sentences scattered throughout the lecture. The topics are easy to learn on your own though.

Lectures cover very basic concepts and rarely branch into new intriguing concepts. The entire grade is poorly defined labs which are time consuming but provide little learning opportunities along with a quiz which is easy but you are given a very short amount of time to barely complete it.
Generally unknowledgeable in his field. Did not write his slides. Homework is alternately tedious and nonsensical. I pity anyone and everyone who has to take this class.

This is easily the worst professor I have ever had in my life. He assigned 100 assignments in three weeks, all useless nonsense to waste our time. He assigned a midterm on Memorial Day, and we could only take it on Memorial Day. This teacher exists to waste students brainpower and time, you should not EVER consider taking a class of his.

I didn't like Gaffar. His lectures seemed very pointless, with lots of rambling about his time in silicon valley and other personal anecdotes that serve no purpose other than to talk about himself. His slides look like they're from before 2010 and feel very outdated content-wise. He has an air about him that seems like he thinks he's better than us

Lectures are absolutely pointless. Little to no communication outside of the lecture about the quizzes. Talks about his time in industry and about planes the whole time. Uses publicly available slides for his lecture material. I really feel like I learned nothing about software testing. If you want to learn about that topic, take 4170.
guys i think he worked at SAP and mayo clinic. I'm not sure tho :(
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going to lecture is a waste of time. Labs make up 80% of grade, are long and tedious work. Mostly consists of setting up a project and taking a ton of screenshots. The labs are also very vague and if you ask questions he will say to read it again. His mugshot is funny if you can find it online.

This professor literally talks about anything but the class. He talks about his time in the industry, and that is literally it. Avoid at all costs, but if you do take this class, I would skip every lecture.

The runaway favorite for the worst professor I've had at Iowa State. If you actually bother going to lecture, you're subjected to endless anecdotes about his time in industry. Homeworks were less about learning how to test software and more about building mini java projects just to test your code. Incredibly inefficient and I'd avoid at all costs.

To start, for 90% of the lectures you actually talk about nothing. This professor gives you nothing to actually learn, and mainly spends his time talking about things he's "worked on" in the past. Apparently he's worked at over 20 companies and been everywhere around the globe. The quizzes (exams) are straight up memorization from the slides.

Many people are saying that "Goofy" Gaffar should be awarded the Worst Professor on Iowa State. He is wholly incapable, perhaps because of his lack of IQ, of delivering a coherent lecture without rambling about his So-Called Accomplishments at Mayo Clinic and others. He really should be nowhere near a Lecture Hall. Really sad day for our school!

Class was extremely unorganized. Assignments wouldn't be posted to canvas until right before due date. TA's inaccessible and take forever to respond to emails. He rambles way too much in lectures and wonders why no one shows up.

He is the only professor who worries about people not paying attention to him. He is an attention seeker. He likes talking about himself and the work he did before coming to ISU. I also want to point out that he was ARRESTED I don't how ISU accepted this horrible professor. By far the worst professor ever

>Lecture is just him monotonously reading slides
>Posts slides on canvas
>Yet he complains that no one comes to class.
---
>Class is called software TESTING
>Spend 70% of your time building software before you test it (Not even TDD)

first 4 labs are easy, last 3 are the size of 227/228 assignments.
My 2nd most disliked prof and class at ISU.

Be careful if you choose to take 422. If you get assigned a terrible group like I did you are screwed. I explained to him countless of times how my group is lazy and incompetent and he doesn't seem to care, so my grade is severely penalized for it. Overall the class should be an easy A but its harder than it seems and depends on your group.

He is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He constantly calls people out for being on their laptops and gets upset when no one comes to class, and will bully anyone there. He is extremely contradictory and will only talk about himself and his work which does not apply to the class. Be ready to go over at most 5 useless slides per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 "quizzes" and 1 lab each worth 15% of your final grade, the other 55% is just labs. No rubric or clear grading criteria. Labs were vague, and if you ask for clarification, you are told to "read it again"; no further information will be given unless it is given on the day the lab is due. The professor blatantly lies to and yells at his students

He is, without a doubt, the worst professor I have had at Iowa State. It may be tempting to take his classes because they are easy but I promise it is not worth it. Lectures and assignments are completely useless and all he does is talk about nothing and cry that no one goes to class.

Likes to talk about himself and his work. Lab descriptions are extremely vague and change depending on his mood. He hasn't graded anything in months and changed the rubric of a lab after it was due. Decided since no one showed up to his lecture to change the format of the final quiz so people would start attending class, didn't work. 0/10

Overall going to Gaffar's lectures is an uncomfortable experience. In each lecture, he calls out students for not typing in class or paying attention. 

On top of that, the course is graded out of ~100 points so every assignment feels very high stakes. He gives multiple quizzes worth about ~40% of the grade and only have ~15 questions each.

Lectures are somewhat related to software testing but often times he decides ramble about his own accomplishments. The labs range from easy which occurs when he takes the labs from the lab book or ridiculously time consuming when he comes up with them. When asking for clarification he will not respond to your questions unless you are in person.

You literally cannot type anything in class or he will call you out in lecture and tell you to leave in a class where we are writing and learning about unit testing. Constantly talks of his work at Mayo Clinic that no one cares about and changes the course structure almost the day of an in class 30% total grade quiz that was suppose to be online.

He constantly tells students to leave lecture for just being on their laptops and he is always shocked when only 10 students show to lecture. He always talks about the work he did at Mayo Clinic or SAP every 10 minutes. He encourages for us to ask questions, yet when someone does he belittles them. Do yourself a favor and avoid him at all cost.

Continuation of my last review, The professor constantly talks down to students and then spends all class talking about his previous achievements that do not pertain to the course work. Takes weeks for grades to come out and then it is impossible to get in contact with the professor or TA. Avoid this Professor at ALL costs

One of the worst professors I have ever had, spends every class calling out students for being on their laptops in a class about coding Junit tests. Gets upset when students don't show up to class even though in the syllabus he gives no repercussions for not showing up. Lies to students about the class layout and changes quizzes and labs 12h before

This guy's assignments are very vague, and the in class content isn't taught very well. He is funny, but mostly unintentionally. He loves to talk about working at sap, and about cars. He wants his students to check Expedia every day.

AERE364 is a weird class, but I did not like Holland for it. Lectures felt arbitrary, and he would go rambling on about topics that were nearly irrelevant for the class, like how to derive inverse Laplace transforms. The project at the end was also really rushed and stressful. The class has interesting topics, but I would avoid unless doing CPS.

Holland may not be the most exciting lecturer, but he makes things very clear. Derivations are easy to follow if you understand physics and calculus. Take very good notes; the homework will often ask for very specific things. There is really not reason to not get an A in this class if you do all the homework and come to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Holland's lecture are messy and handwritten. Homework is self-graded and completion (full solutions posted after due date). Semester long group project will take all of your time. First test was easy (scored 99%); second one threw me for a loop (77%); but lecture quizzes buffer your grade (careful for trick questions on lecture quizzes).

Holland did a good job explaining the material but it always seemed like he never gave all the equations meaning I had to go look at the other professors lecture notes to get everything. Homework and project chunks were mostly graded on completion with little feedback. Exams were much tougher than anything learned in class.

Overall great professor. He does a great job on making sure you are well prepared for exams and future AERE classes. He is also a pretty funny guy, cracks some good joke during lecture. Overall, would recommend making sure you have him as your professor for this class.
There was no feedback on any assignments and projects. The tests were always so much harder than anything else.

Professor Holland is actually not too bad, his lecture was little messy and he does not require you to attend the class since it he pre record the lecture and put them on canvas, the Hw is on graded on completion but still try your best. Hw solution will be given which is extremely helpful during exam since it is open notes.

The class content is not challenging, but Holland is a terrible professor. My number one issue is that he provides zero feedback to any assignments. The grading is arbitrary at best, if not complete BS. He also will not respond to your emails.
Steve was an amazing professor. His lectures were clear, concise, and useful. He made concepts clear and was always willing to help.

Kind of quirky, but very well informed about aerospace engineering. Learned a lot. He has a tendancy to derive too much in my opinion, but perhaps thats just not my cup of tea. Easy grade bump for hw and group project, but tests are no cake walk. You will get a 1 page cheat sheet. Use it. Study. If you do that, you'll be fine. Fun class all around.

Dr. Holland is a nice guy, he knows the stuff and I'm sure he was a smart student.  the class is not that difficult but he's a tough grader. 2 tough exams and worse final. also the projects are kinda hard, you need to work hard to get A

He does a solid job of explaining things, and is very good about responding to his very helpful online discussion board. Did a good job of making lectures fairly interesting, but I wish he'd stop handwriting everything because his handwriting isn't that great.

He is a good professor and he knows his stuff pretty well. His handwriting can be messy at times, but you can read it fairly easily.  There are group projects that take a lot of time to do, but he is good at explaining it in lecture.

Prof. Holland is a real student's teacher. This semester in AerE 261 has been my best semester in Aerospace, thanks to his straightforward and understandable lectures, homework which follows word for word from lecture, and tests which you would have trouble failing if you'd payed some degree of attention in class and done your homework. Thanks man!

The projects are long and tedious and the class is full of derivations. Everything being taught however is building what is essential knowledge in AerE. He explains things clearly and will lead you on the right path. I thought he was great.

I thought he was a very good teacher and an interesting class. Yes, his handwriting isn't the best, but it was legible. The tests weren't hard at all. The hardest part of the course was the homework and projects. They were long and demanded a lot of time but there weren't very many of them and Holland was good about making clarifications in class.
Absolute worst teacher I've ever had. Extremely unorganized, has no motivation whatsoever.
Worst handwriting possible! Lectures did not help at all and  office hours are useless because he is not help. The TA was amazing wish she taught the class.
Worst prof. ever made me feel so dumb every time i talked to him and is useless in lecture on account of his horrible handwriting.
Great professor! He explains linear algebra concepts clearly, while adjusting the classes' pace based on the cohort and really cares about his students.

Scott seemed a bit disengaged with teaching some days. In my opinion he made this course too easy. There should've been more proofs for it being a proofs course. It felt like 207 with an extra lecture and slightly harder calculation problems. By week 14 we were still row reducing matrices. Overall, nice guy who could have made the course harder.
He was not able to convey any of the material in a way that students could understand. He never used a microphone so you could not hear anything he was saying. Poorly followed Butler's videos.
Mumbled and stuttered, poor handwriting, doesn't look up from slides. Not very nice to students. Made mistakes in lecture and had to constantly be corrected by students.

Went to his lectures the first few weeks and realized how pointless they were. He took the problems in Butler's videos and explained them even worse than how Butler did. He was scatterbrained and just hard to learn from. My tips to succeed are to go to EVERY SI, watch and take notes on every Butler video and do as many practice exams as you can
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures given by Scott Hansen are pointless to go to. Handwriting is almost illegible. No useful examples are given and content is not explained well. If taking this class use the online videos by professor butler instead as Scott Hansen will not teach you diff eq.

Do not take him, he skips so many steps when teaching new material. He also belittles students and calls their questions dumb. Handwriting is awful so you constantly have to ask him questions if you want to understand what he has written at all.

Took Diff Eq with Hansen in F2020, lectures were horrible. Mistakes were not corrected at all so when you went back to look at examples they were all wrong. Exams were crazy hard, final exam took about 20 hours of work, he changed the problems 18 hours into the 36 hour window and made everyone resubmit if they had already finished the exam, 0/10
Scott Hansen does not do a good job at nearly any of the lectures, doesn't explain steps, and is generally hard to follow along. I was often totally lost and confused during his lectures.

20% Exam 1 15% Exam 2 20% Exam 3 25% Final 10% Weekly HW 10% Weekly Quizzes Very average teacher. Extremely boring lectures but posts notes to his own class website (not canvas). The class itself is not too hard. The computations are easy, but remembering the processes can be tricky. Test averages around 75%. The course was curved about 4%.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Math 267 with Scott Hansen and his exams were way harder then all other professors teaching math 267. He was very vague and wrote with sharpie during lecture and when something was wrong he would scribble it all out. Overall hard to follow, curve was insane. IF you have to take him get a tutor I learned so much from mine.

Dr. Hansen is a good professor. Linear Algebra is not difficult as long as you are willing to put the time in. I wish there were more proofs in this class; we did so many application problems! Dr. Hansen is in his office after class if you need help. The exams are pretty straightforward. Linear Algebra is a beautiful class! It shows up everywhere!!

He knows the material well and does a good job going through examples in class. A few opportunities for extra credit is nice and he does a good job making clear deadlines and altering them to accommodate university events, like the career fairs. My only gripe lies in his teaching, the material's all good but he's very monotone.

Good professor all around. Sometimes doesn't really explain things in class. However, if you stay afterwards and ask him or go to his office hours you can tell he really knows what he's talking about and generally can clarify a question really well.

I think Dr. Hansen is a great professor. I for one do not believe that calculus or math in general can ever be learnt solely by lectures. Study somewhat beforehand and always pay attention. He's super caring about his students and only wants them to succeed. Also, PLEASE do the MyMathLab assignments. Its a lot, but you'll get so good after them.
Good teacher!
He mumbles and doesn't look up from the board his entire lecture. Had to teach myself everything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He seems very unorganized and is not great at explaining concepts.  I was fine at the beginning of the course, but about 1/3 of the way through I can't follow him in lecture.

Very intelligent and very helpful. He wants his students to succeed and likes to connect with the students. He is sometimes hard to follow but he is always willing to go back and explain things. I really enjoyed his class and thought he was a very fair teacher.

He's a super helpful guy when you go talk to him during office hours. He is THE MOST UNORGANIZED guy ever! He's scatter brained so he'll forget things quite often, his notes were hard for me to follow. If you follow the book you should be fine. Take his class if you can learn from the textbook and can take semi-hard tests. His grading is lenient.

Very intelligent teacher who did a great job explaining concepts to the class.  He was always very helpful and responsive to answering students questions.  I would definitely recommend this professor!

He's a smart man and he knows what he's talking about, but students can't follow him. He doesn't explain very well and he's all over the place with his lesson. It's almost impossible to follow him without reading the chapter and doing example problems BEFORE class.

Sometimes very difficult to understand. He definitely knows what he is talking about, but he teaches as if we all already do too. Make sure to follow along with notes and do examples out of the book because almost no homework is given. Tests will be much harder if you don't do any homework. It would have been nice to see more assigned homework.
very interesting class, I would recommend this professor
Dr. Hansen is a very intelligent, kind, caring professor.  If I ever had a question, he was happy to help me with a problem.  I enjoyed his class.  He also has a sense of humor, that helps.
hes seriously the boringest guy who has ever taught anything, hasnt been a class i havent fallen asleep
he doesn't explain very well
Tests and quizzes were pretty easy. Presents material clearly and isn't too boring. Overall he's a good teacher
This was the easiest math class at ISU.  He taught the material so well in class that there was hardly any time spent out of class doing homework.

Dr. Hansen is an okay prof.  He does talk a little monotone, but he does a very good job teaching the material.  He does give out about 3 homeworks and quizzes for the year, and that's it.  As long as you go to class, you'll be fine.  Most of the exams and quizzes are problems similar to those he went over in class.  I'd recommend him.

As someone commented before.. he is a pretty boring guy to be  teaching a class. He often confuses himself. But then he is very helpful and he had good knowledge of the sunject. Kept the tests and assignments reasonably hard. A good pick!
It was basacly imposible to not fall asleep when he talks

I really like this Teacher !  i used to study for his class less than 2 hours a week and I ended up with an A. His exams are quite easy & he explains pretty well the materials.  And as a personality he's very nicee cool/ weird. ( at the beginning of the semester everything is harder just after the first test the class became very easy

If you would like to take a class where you can sit and watch a professor do calculus problems himself on the board without teaching anyone anything, this class is definitely for you.  So if you don't understand the class you should go get help, from your TA, who can't teach either!

Explains too top level.  Skips over a lot of steps so you REALLY have to pay attention and go to EVERY class.  He also is very quiet and monotone.  Confuses himself and makes you rewrite lots of notes.  PICK SOMEONE ELSE
really enjoyed this class. as long as you do homework and go to class youll do well in this class because he explains things pretty well. answers questions good too.

He is very helpful and his tests are easy if you do the homework problems and his practice tests.  Otherwise, the class could be hard for you.  He wants to do what he can to help us do well.  Sometimes he skips some steps in problems and it can get confusing if you aren't paying close attention.
No Comments
Hard to follow him sometimes, but tests are not too bad...and makes the test curve great!
If you want the material you really need to go to class as he does not release the slides. Otherwise he is a pretty good teacher and helps explain anything if you need help.

Funny guy, however actually attending the class serves little to no purpose. In response to this, he makes tophats graded and not showing up to class really hurts your grade. That's a shame considering the class (assignments and exams) are entirely online and can be done by yourself as the software explains in great detail how to do everything.
Super chill guy, made the class extremely easy to do well in. There is lots of busy work but nothing difficult at all.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: When enough people do not show up, it becomes pretty attendance-based. Honestly the professor doesnt even matter for this course I would just recommend taking it online since it is mostly an online course.

Very funny guy, just show up to lectures if you take the in-person version. Most of the class is online, with very clear week-to-week work. Very quick to respond to emails, overall good dude would reccomend.

Nice and funny professor. Is caring and will do his best to help you. Lectures are 'mandatory' but I ended up going only once and still ended up with a good grade. Due Dates are annouced in the syllabus, and that's it, so you must stay on top of your work. Overall a good dude though.

Great guy! Most lectures just went over basic commands for excel and access which wasn't completely necessary but he also will give quiz answers during lectures. If you can't make class he posts tophat questions at the end of the week. Funny guy and you can tell he knows what he's doing.  Also very good at answering emails!
Light class just come to classes and your be straight. Only thing is Tophat is glitchy on not wanting to save answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attend lectures to complete the top hat questions.  Don't really need to pay super close attention because you learn through the homework and labs.  Chill dude.

For an introductory class, he teaches all the basics of Python so well. Btw, he gives the students, especially cs majors touch of reality about the tech world and teaches about past experiences that he had. If you attend the lectures, you will be okay. Exams as in every coms classes are on paper and even the slightest error of syntax is less points
This dude is boring and rude. Just AI this class, it's so free. I low k feel bad for bro because nobody comes to class (there is no reason too) and he gets butt hurt that his lectures are useless.

He's snarky, impatient, and acts like he'd rather be anywhere else than teaching. Assignments are due at 6pm Thursdays despite being auto-graded. He uses Top Hat with trick attendance questions and refuses extensions. He replies fast to emails, which is nice, but makes you feel bad for mistakes. Tbh, I would take a diff prof cause I hate attending.

He's gonna expect you to know everything before you come into class. He doesn't really teach; all he says is practice for hours a day, and you'll be good. Essentially, he's saying, ' Teach yourself. ' He's going to go through problems just by doing them and not explaining them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very passive aggressive and snarky when talking about people who don't come to class (every single assignment is online, lectures generally provide no value). Also, his assignments are due at 6pm instead of 11:59pm even though they are AUTO GRADED. Easy A but I really dislike the attitude.. in a 100 level class at that.
The lectures are not necessary to attend to get a good grade. He is very passive aggressive and doesn't give clear instruction. Tough class to want to attend.

His grading criteria is gibberish, and his instructions on assignments are ridiculously vague. You are then told "This is not what you were asked to do." This class is not properly directed toward beginner programmers. Do not even try asking questions, especially about exams, because everything is last minute and he will "not know yet."
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor talks way too quickly and he rarely goes into any kind of depth for the things he teaches. Also, he acts like he expects everyone to have prior knowledge of the ins and outs of python and programming as a whole.
