The exams have a lot of things that he either never talked about or briefly glossed over because it "wasn't important"

He is a funny guy, but I hated the way he taught this intro course. If you have experience with Python, it would be a breeze; if you don't, good luck. Notes were pen and paper, and he barely gave us time to write anything down because he would just read off the slide and move on to the next topic.

Disappointed with this professor. For an intro course, he unfairly flagged minimal code as AI. He was unresponsive, failed to provide updates, and ignored my concerns. The class itself was easy, but I would not recommend him due to his lack of professionalism and poor communication.

He changed the way he teaches this semester. Now the lectures are a mix of slides and coding examples as opposed to just coding examples. I find the lectures to be helpful. For 127, he assumes you have 0 experience and he will teach everything you need for the exams. The grading is very lenient. He is chill, has a sense of humor, and teaches well.

The lectures in this class can become quite boring and end up not feeling as important as the ZyBooks. The ZyBook assignments end up teaching you more than the lectures. Prof. Holman is very caring, and you can tell he wants you to succeed. He's very accommodating to your needs/requests.

The professor's lectures are not effective or engaging. He covers material that isn't helpful and rarely explains how to apply concepts to solve problems, which is crucial for success in this field. he's not strict/difficult. The lectures are dry, unhelpful, and largely unnecessary. TLDR skip class and focus on the Zybooks material instead.

It was an easy class but a terrible student experience. The instructor was okay, but his selection of TAs was awful. They were inexperienced in this subject and had a poor attitude towards struggling students and even those with a lot of experience.

If you have prior experience, this is an easy A. For everyone else, it is an awful class.

Having no programming experience, this class was surprisingly easy. I didn't find the lectures to be entertaining, and felt like I was just watching him code (little explanation). ZyBooks and especially assignments were more challenging than the exams. Lab was unnecessary; if you showed progress on that weeks homework you were able to leave.

Matthew Hollman is a great and very approachable guy. Lecture attendance wasn't graded like many other professors do, but I would recommend going anyway. A lot of people will complain about the zybooks and the written tests, but I thought they were a great part of the course. The complainers just don't understand or know what the purpose of it was.

Pretty laid back guy. For having no programming experience, this class was pretty easy and fun. Lectures are optional and posted in Canvas. I believe he mainly just does examples of stuff talked about in the ZyBook, which is where you are going to be learning basically everything. Labs are basically just to check if you are reading and taking notes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty cool guy

I took 227 with him and it was a poorly structured class. The class felt lazy, however that's beside the point. Matt was a very boring professor, and he will ramble off topic for a long time. He also never was much helped when I had questions. Overall, not horrible, but not good.

Mathew Hollman is a great first semester Professor. His class was very easy for me. There was a lot of emphasis on labs and assignments. Lecture was not graded for attendance and I'm glad so because I did not feel the need to attend. He would go over the same things as the textbook (which you had to read and take notes on anyways for lab).Good TA's
Just doesn't speaking talking. Mostly speak what's not a part of the class.
He is so cheap.
Very easy just very boring. Liked to ask questions to the class about what to name variables which made the class drag on. Didn't need to show up at least.

Approachable, funny, and friendly guy. However, I stopped attending lectures two weeks in, as it's mostly just covering the textbook you have to take notes on anyway. Usually easy class, don't procrastinate on the assignments, though. Good introductory Python course. But there's too much focus on writing code in paper-pencil tests, in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this professor for COMS 127, he was extremely nice and funny. Assignments and labs weren't too bad, and lectures are optional. Matthew is very willing to help and is easy to work with. Only complaint is that lectures move very very slow, which can be quite boring. I found myself taking the lecture times to do assignments instead.

Professor Holman is a good professor to have for an introductory programming class. Lectures are clear and always makes sure that all assignments/labs are going well. Assignments can be time consuming but you have a large time frame to do them. Labs are quite easy. I also liked the fact that he used Webex for his lectures so I could watch online.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very funny professor, but at the same time, his presenting voice is a little bit monotone, so if you don't digest the material well that way, he might not be great for you. Make sure to start assignments way ahead of time because they get long, and attend all of your labs.

Matthew Holman is a good lecturer.  He has a great understanding of computer science and explains concepts at a level of a beginner programmer.  Sometimes he can take his lectures a little too slow, and is also not very sociable and sometimes hard to approach. Learning the fundamentals of Python before taking this class will make it more manageable
Great guy

Hilliard is a very good professor. I thoroughly enjoyed the assignments and lectures she gave. Attendance is important, but it isn't the end of the world if you skip. Hilliard is very understanding and is more than willing to help if you fall behind or are struggling. I'd definitely take her class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kathleen is very passionate about history however my problem was that she often assumed that students had prior knowledge on many of the topics which if you are from the U.S. you might but if you are not prepare to be confused at times. As long as you do the work and attend class and pay attention you can pass the class with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, she gives interesting lectures that are easy to follow and to take notes with. She is helpful, easy to reach, genuinely cares about her students and their success.

Could not use more tags but she is awesome. Reading seems daunting but is doable. Participation is mandatory to getting what you want from course, but is engaging. Not done with class but love, she outlines what she expects out of us very clearly and simply. But I would recommend her for higher courses rather lower with her teaching style.

Dr. Hilliard is amazing. She's one of the best professors at ISU. Her classes aren't unreasonably difficult and if you ask her for help, she'll go out of her way to help you. She's also super funny and loves to talk to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures were interesting and fun. She puts her powerpoints up online, but they have basic points, so attend lecture to get all of the necessary info. During recitation you should talk and discuss, because part of your grade is discussion points. Once a week you read a passage and write 2 paragraphs on it. Pay attention, those are on the test.

Dr Hilliard  is a fine professor who is engaging, fun, and helpful. But she also demands wayyyyy too much of your focus. She requires a 5-6 credit focus for a 3 credit course. So while I would reccomend her for upper level courses, I would shy away from taking any entry level classes with her. unless you want to spend all your study time on geneds

Pretty standard history class. Pay attention and you should do well. TA grades everything, so it helps if you get an easy one. I dozed off in most lectures, but was able to pull a B without much studying and not much prep on tests. Essays are easy to get by on.

She's a great teacher and keeps history interesting for a survey class. This is the first time I've had her, but I made sure to have her next semester too. The only problem is her selection of TAs. You must read and TALK in the non-lecture classes to get a decent grade. Tests are easy. 20 multiple choice (2 pts each) and an essay question. (60 pts)

I liked her. Though her lectures were a bit redundant if you already read your textbook. But she really cares for her students and makes an attempt from the first day to learn everyone's names. Real nice and always there if you need help. She was pretty nice when it came to grading. Her husbands an awesome teacher too.

She is a really great teacher!  She truely cares about her students.  When some students said they loaded down with homework, she gave us an extra class to do a paper!  She is really nice and you learn a lot!  There is a good amount of reading, but hey!  You're a history major!  I would recommend this class!

I absolutely loved Dr. Hilliard. She seemed excited to teach every day and was passionate about the subject. Her lectures were interesting and loved going to them. I definitely hope I have her again someday.

I loved Prof. Hilliard's lectures. Especially the revolutionary/civil war lectures. She provided some awesome facts about America's founding/upbringing and really opened my eyes to how this country was truly built up. Her tests are fairly easy, same for the homework assignments. Show up to class because stuff from lecture shows up on the test!
Great Prof! Her lectures are like listening to stories. Grades pretty easy on tests and answers any questions you have.

One of the best professors at ISU! I also had her for History 222. She is extremely helpful and will do just about anything for you to succeed. She really cares about her students. Your grade will depend on you. Do your work and ask for help when you need it. There is no reason you should get a grade any lower than a "B."

Taking this class with her has been a blast.  She actually makes me want to go to class every time it meets, not many profs can do that.  Grades fair, but you will have to put in the effort to get a good grade. Go to class and keep up with the readings and you should be fine.
Skip the reading and just go to lecture. Lectures are pretty interesting and she explains everything you need to know. Do the readings for the recitation though, hard to pass without reading those.

Lectures are somewhat interesting and easy to understand. Take good notes b/c they are not posted online, and 1st 10 test questions are always directly from lectures. All homework is graded by recitation TAs, but it is easy, just requires a lot of reading. Don't buy the textbook, but "Contending Voices" and "Stono" are a MUST. Easy A.

Hilliard is a really great prof.  Gets very in depth with attitudes and ideas, but she's also pretty good at looking at the military and political aspects of things.  Tests and papers are graded fairly.  Lots of reading, but in the end you only need to do about half of it.  She's also very attractive, which certainly helped improve my attendance.

Frustrating experience. Questions rarely got clear answers, yet participation was graded, which felt inconsistent. Feedback on reports often came across as unnecessarily harsh, and grading seemed overly strict for the expectations.

She grades incredibly harshly, without even giving you clear grading criteria. Her attitude towards students is very inconsistent as well; one day she will act like a friend, and the next she will be stern and talk down to you like you don't know anything. This class is just a ton of busy work that is graded exceedingly hard. 0/10 would recommend

While Professor Hallmark seems tough and stuckup at the beginning of the semester, she is actually a pretty good professor. She gives good lectures and her grading, while strict, is clearly layed out. She teaches well. 1600 is a tough class no matter what, but she does a good job with the in class time explaining. I do recommend having her.

CHE 1600 is a difficult class in general, and would be with any professor. The class is flipped so you have to watch the lectures on your own, which makes it more difficult to grasp the concepts. There is a lot of work for this class: watching lectures, completing weekly homework and group assignments. Study and practice or you will not succeed.

This class is an intro to the major, and it reflects that difficulty. There are weekly group projects that take a few hours and the weekly homework takes even longer. You have very little time for them, so make sure that you can do the work fast. Check the rubrics because you get more points for knowing how to solve a problem than solving it.
She didn't even major in chemE in college so she doesn't really understand how to teach undergrad classes. She was a pretty tough grader without much partial credit or curve given...

Professor Hallmark may seem intimidating at first, but don't let that discourage you from seeking help! Her exams are more challenging than what many freshmen may expect, so consistent studying and effort are important to succeed. She is not an unreasonably harsh grader, just make sure to cover all parts of the exams to maximize points.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is relatively difficult, and you have to be ready to work outside of class. Make sure you watch the videos before class, because class time is used more like work time instead of learning. The tests are very difficult and there is no curve

She was a really nice teacher, and really helpful when I went to her with questions. Make sure you are ready to read and watch the lecture videos though, as the class is a flipped schedule so in-class there are worksheets and time for questions. Also, double check the time that assignments are due, as some of them are due at the start of class.

I really enjoyed his class, and he was good at explaining the more difficult topics. There are 6 total assignments, 4 essays, a midterm, and a final. He provides study guides for each and has review sessions. He is good at answering questions and made class engaging and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Holter was the professor I hated the most in all my time at Iowa State. The way he would have a weekly pop quiz, sometimes even twice a week, would send anyone to the point of making attendance required. And you would be reading 30+ pages every week, like I have other classes I need to do homework for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor has been one of the worst professors I've had here. He assigns so many readings. He asks a simple question with an easy answer, but in the most complex way so that no one understands. His grading is also tough because you may define something one way, and he may not agree even though it is explaining the same concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Holter's lectures are very sporadic and not well laid out, but despite this his class is interesting and he's able to help students make connections between the course concepts. I think the biggest way he could help students feel more prepared in the class is by posting reading guides and moving more calmly through lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Holter has a hard time effectively communicating ideas in his lectures, he doesn't think before he speaks. He does not use technology or aids in his lectures. The class is also very reading heavy and the readings are dense and lengthy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Holter is one of the smartest people I have ever met. I think he is so smart that he is unable to effectively teach and explain most topics. This makes the lectures hard to understand. He tries his best but most of the time you will probably have to teach yourself. This class is challenging, but a good challenge to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.Holter is a great professor if you love politics and want to learn more about the government. I've really enjoyed his class. He does assign a lot of readings which can be overwhelming. These readings are often confusing and hard to understand. You need to attend class to understand readings and do well on exams.

All lectures and going to class is important if you are not going to do all the readings. His lectures seem like he is boosted up on 10 cups of coffee. He truly tries his best to explain the content which is helpful. Exams are all either essay or short answer, in which it is all in class essays and exams.

Dr. Heinen is a very respectable and professional professor. She gives great feedback and explains how to approach problems with great detail. Her grading is strict but it is fair. She is very knowledgeable and understanding, if a circumstance comes up, she is willing to accommodate. I would recommend her as a professor.

Dr. Heinen is a very knowledgeable professor. She is known to be a tough one, but you will come out of her class knowing a lot more than if you were to take it with another professor. The class is graded heavily on exams that are graded harsh. This 3 credit class definitely should be 5.

Dr. Heinen is a good professor and is very knowledgeable about the information she teaches, but it requires a lot of work to be successful in this class. Since the homework answers are provided on Canvas, almost your entire grade rides on your 4 exam scores. There is no grading curve or extra credit, so study hard and go to office hours.

CHE 1600 is a tough course and so is the rest of the CHE curriculum. I feel as though Dr. Heinen puts the introductory course at this sort of difficulty to show students what kind of course difficulty you can expect from courses within CHE. If you are putting effort in the class she will recognize that and be helpful, if not she will not be as nice

The class gets easier as you move on, the first two exams are designed to weed you out. Heinen is a knowledgeable and great professor, however I did not enjoy the structure of this class, and a chunk of the grade was based on team challenges and my teammates did nothing which brought my grade down and forced me to spent countless nights

Test was hard, super tough grader. She will take a point from even little mistakes. Follow her steps from the homework or practice problems to earn the point. She tried to help students understand the problem, but she wanted the class to have the lowest grade possible. The pre-curve is 30%, and there was only a curve in the first exam.

Amazing professor, one of the best ive had at ISU. sets you up for success, her exams are EXTREMELY difficult and many people fail this class, but if you take advantage of all the resources and commit, you will pass.

Very good teacher and by taking this class with her you will come out of it KNOWING everything you will need to succeed in other courses, but her tests take the class up to 10. Do not expect to finish a test prepare for a steep curve, but don't slack every test is comprehensive so you must know last units material too.

Heinen will doc you points any chance she gets on the homework and for projects. She is harsh and unforgiving, if you are able to postpone taking this class until there is a new instructor, please consider doing so.

Dr. Heinen is an will always be my favorite professor. While her tests are notoriously tough, she gives you every resource you need in order to be successful in the class. I never learn as much as I do in her lectures. ATTEND HELP HOURS, she wants to help you and gives such good advice there. Use the homework to learn and ask questions often.

Awful, CH E 160 is the most difficult intro engineering class at ISU, and Heinen is not afraid to fail students. Class averages on exams were around 30% pre curve, and if you did below average, you did not even get a curve. You have 3 lab reports per semester, and she takes away points for minor details. Overall, good luck since you will need it.

Hardest class I've taken this semester and still my favorite. Dr. Heinen is willing to help you, highly recommend taking advantage of her help hours. The exams are pretty difficult, however, the rubrics for exams are given in advance so you can plan ahead (since you likely won't finish the exam). When you start to struggle, ask for help right away.

Tests are very difficult, and chances are you will never have time to finish them, but they are predictable. Go over all content from the unit and have a good understanding of all of it. She is a very nice person and will try to accommodate you if you communicate with her. Overall a caring person and easy to talk to, but not a good professor.

You definitely need to attend and pay attention during every lecture. Dr. Heinen moves pretty fast, but she will take the time to explain any concepts you hare having a hard time understanding. She gives plenty of examples in class, and even gives time to work on the homework in class to ensure she can answer any questions you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: You need to put in a next level of effort to pass this class, but that is not Professor Heinen's fault. She gives you the resources you need, but it is up to you to utilize them. She is extremely helpful during office hours... but this is only if you put in the effort to go there. Simply put, it is your responsibility to take initiative.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is an class for chemical engineering majors, so I don't know why people are shocked that it requires hard work. Dr Heinen is organized, prepared, fair, and very helpful inside and outside of class. If freshmen think that this work load is too heavy, they should probably do themselves a favor and switch majors. I highly recommend Dr. Heinen.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Group projects can only make your grade worse, the average grades were rarely above a 90%. She also only teaches by example. The exams are much worse than anything you are given to study from and the average final exam was a 40% so she was forced to curve it by 25 points or else only half the class would've passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Heinen is tough on her students by expecting highly of them. There's a lot of work to put into the course but its all worth it for later courses. She's very willing to help students succeed as long as they're willing to put in the effort. This isn't a course you want to go through on your own, make sure you have study buddies. Flipped learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Heinen expects a lot from her students, but is sure to make herself available to students as much as she can. The tests are very difficult and are hard to finish in the time allotted. The only way to do well in this class is to go to every class and practice VBA, MatLab, and material balance with a pencil and paper a lot before the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you're not used to studying A LOT and asking for help you're up for a rude awakening. There's practically no material to study from and the material that's available, like someone else mentioned, is pretty terrible. I honestly don't know how I survived. I broke down many times. It was absolutely terrible. good luck! You'll definitely need it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Be prepared to spend many frustrating hours doing homework. All the information is learned online via terrible 240p videos. The exams are much more difficult than any homework or in class problems. Be prepared to do a lot of programing. You will lose your will to live... This class will destroy you and your gpa. "The horror! The horror!" 0/5 rating
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Heinen is a very nice lady, but her tests are difficult and hard to study for. She rarely lectures over the material. Almost all of the material is learned through watching videos that are poorly explained. The homework is also very difficult. Go to her office hours!!! She's very helpful in office hours. Switching to industrial bc of this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Dr. Heinen was a very difficult grader, but you learn the material very well. She gives very good feedback during her office hours. You need to start studying for her exams about a week ahead of time, as they are incredibly difficult, but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Heinen tends to like anyone who kisses up to her, and is very clear about who her favorite students are. Watch her online videos or you will have no clue what is going on in class. Study A LOT for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: First off, I loved Dr. Heinen as a person. Super nice and easy to get along with. But she is not a good professor in my opinion. The course lectures are online with actual class being sort of a lab. If you can even get past her monotone voice in the lectures, it's hard to find useful content. Tough grader, even harder exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Nice lady but grades like an absolute savage. Tests were online, which is not ideal for an engineering course that focuses on programming.  Not only were the tests online, they were also very difficult.  Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Heinen was a very tough grader but always noted why she took points off. Nice woman and good professor, again, very tough grader. Dont put homework off, and put in work and you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I think if you are actually looking forward to excel in the upcoming classes. Dr Heinen is the professor you are actually looking for. She teaches the class very beautifully and takes care about her students a lot. Although, there is much of work in her class, but making the students do more work helps in being more eleoquent in the course.

reviews.comment: This class was a nightmare. I spent more time on this class than I did on any of my other classes combined. It couldn't be more obvious that the purpose of this class was to weed people out. Almost 1/2 of the class dropped by the end. Heinen's grading was ridonk. Almost cried during the final and it also destroyed my will to live. The worst.

reviews.comment: She is an absolute savage. Throws curve balls on exams that do not pertain to anything you have seen before. Avoid at all costs.

reviews.comment: Great teacher! So much so that I took her again for ChE 310.

reviews.comment: Surprised by all these reviews. Dr. Heinen is a great teacher and really cares about her students. Her class is hard but she is always willing to work with you outside of class.

The worst grader you will ever experience in college.  Period.  Class was taught through videos which explained at-times difficult topics very poorly.  Do everything you can to avoid Jen Heinen/O'Donnell.

Heinen is the best teacher I've ever had in my life. I received 2 D's and only failed 2 exams throughout the semester. Iowa State University doesn't deserve Heinen's teaching style. It is simply exemplary. Definitely would take the class 2-3 more times.

This is one of the easiest classes that i have attended in my life. TO FAIL. The hybrid course even make it much easier to fail because all what you learn in her videos online are completely unrelated to what her tests look like. O'Donnell will also make it better for you to fail. Because,Guess what, there are no other teachers for this course.

Atrocious class. Atrocious teaching. She talks to students in a condescending way all while assuming they know everything. She'll make you want to switch to Kinesiology. Won't stop talking about the Patriots who cheat anyway
She is a sweet little meanie.

Awful class. When asked about printer usage, she just replied "IT'S FINE" in an agitated voice. The group problems were stupid. When the entire class failed a test she just said "let's just forget about that". Told us she would curve but after poor teaching she still didn't. She was pregnant too, damn do I feel sorry for that kid.

Professor Heinen was the worst teacher I have ever had- and it isn't even close. The extraordinarily horrible teaching nearly took me to the point of taking my own life. If you are in this witch's hybrid class, and you value life, DO NOT take this class. Get someone else. Switch to biosystems. Whatever you do just don't take Heinen.

If you took/are taking the class in the hybrid format, leave NOW. After half of the class dropped, the average on the tests was still an F.  Good luck trying to get help from her because just about everyone in the class needs it.  Her grading was also bs.  There is no curve and I think its safe to say only 25% of my class passed.
Reads straight from the book. Doesnt teach so much as she just copies down problems without explaining why you do things. Assumes you know most things already. Tough course over all

Heinen is just awful. Extremely inconsistent in grading. I actually was one of the students she liked and graded easy but my goodness the bias was so easy to see it was ridiculous. Doesn't teach too clearly and gets frustrated when asked. Would not recommend, unless you know she loves you.

I had Dr. Heinen for ChE 160 in the "hybrid" class format so it was new for both students and professors. The 2 hours less of class a week is heavenly, and she did a good job of providing us videos and examples on materials for out of class. She is helpful when approached and wants you to succeed. Fairly easy class but takes some work.

It was obvious half way through the semester who was getting As, Bs, Cs, and who was failing. You could go in to talk to her and get "help" till your face turned blue. She had already made of her mind. If you're one of her As your set for life and should keep taking class with her.

She really wants everyone to do well. Spends lots of time on deriving and explaining concepts. She went around and talked to groups of students during the computer lab portion to make sure we all understood. One of my favorite professors in CH E!

Had Professor Heinen for 160 and she was amazing. Really does care about her students and them succeeding. Homework can me difficult at times and it is important to have a good group for group assignments. Overall exams are doable but you need to have a solid understanding of the material.
She Knows how to teach,and materials are fair to understand together with exams. Hard thing is quizzes and Team assessment, you'll never pass those without preparation and extra working.

She is very helpful outside of class and has all the necessary example problems on blackboard.  Exams are very fair and straightforward.  The hardest parts of the course are the team assessments and quizzes.  Great Class.

Jen is one of the most awesome professor I've ever had. She teaches in a really clear way, somehow makes so much sense. The class itself needs you to put adequate effort, but she makes this class so interesting.

Jen is so nice and helpful! The homework and project are really hard but the tests are very reasonable.  She clearly loves teaching and goes out of her way to make sure everyone understands the material!
O'Donnell really cares that you understand the material she covers. She moves at the perfect pace and encourages questions and class involvement. She is a great professor.

She was absolutely awful towards the end of the semester. She accused me and fellow classmates of using AI even when we didn't, and from there made me then re-do ones that she said had AI. She did this during DEAD WEEK, which added so much stress on top of my already due projects, moving out of my house, and just general things going on in my life.
Do not take this class with her. She does not know how to teach and is on a huge power trip.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Haughn might be the most caring person in the world. Absolutely amazing professor. She is knowledgeable, flexible, helpful, and overall an amazing human being. She also gives great feedback and knows how to connect with everyone well.

Dr Haughn was overall a very good professor. Grading was not difficult which is helpful as this class is typically just a university requirement and most students had other classes they needed to focus on. There were a few points were her political opinion influenced class lectures but overall it was not a problem.

Dr. Haughn gave good feedback, and if you showed up to class, did the work, and put any amount of effort in, you'd get an A.  Very easy grader.  My biggest complaint is that she was very vocal about her political opinion, which was annoying since it had nothing to do with the class.

I love Dr. Haughn. She is very understanding if you are struggling with the public speaking aspect of the class. She is kind, and gives decent feedback. She has a lot of children who get sick a lot so a couple of classes were cancelled due to that (not complaining). Overall great professor choice for this class.
N/A

Professor Haughn is willing to work with students to put their needs first and accommodate them however they need. She is straightforward about grading criteria and will give you clear feedback. She's a passionate and caring individual, and her enthusiasm for her classes makes it enjoyable.
Genuinely cares about her students and their progress in the class. Course is straightforward, and she guides you throughout the entire process.

She is a very passionate and caring person who is not afraid to give her perspective on deeper real-world issues. Her outlook on grading and lives outside the classroom was very refreshing as she values the wellbeing of her students. If you show you care and put in the effort, she will reward and respect you.

Professor Haughn is very caring towards the health and well-being of students, putting emphasis on taking care of yourself before stressing about the school work. She clearly explains the criteria for each paper and as long as you meet the criteria, will give you full credit. She's passionate about English and makes class as enjoyable as possible.

Geniunely one of the most personable professors I've had. Ilker is an awesome individual who is very understanding of the challenges students face. He does a great job of explaining concepts and makes it clear what will be on quizzes/exams. There is a good amount of work in this class, including a big group project, but he makes it manageable.

Professor Karaca has been one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He understands students have a life outside of class. He grades for attendance but he make lectures enjoyable to sit through. A lot of the class is active engagement through excel work and it really helps you learn new things. I would take him for every class if I could.

One of the best professors in finance at Iowa State. Go to class because he goes over a lot of the HW assignments with you in class. Tests are over the book and HWs that you will have the answers to prior to the test.

He is extremely caring and appreciative of his students. He genuinely wants to see everyone succeed and is more than willing to help when necessary. It can be confusing at times because he is very smart, however he is willing to post lecture videos to review after the class.

Would not recommend this class to anyone. Lectures are confusing. Homework will take you several hours. He doesn't explain things and expects you to know everything in the book. When students asked him to slow down during examples, he was rude and got annoyed. He's a tough professor and expects a lot out of his students. Basically a stats class.

Overall a very caring professor, but the class is basically stats. A lot of it was hard to understand, and the lectures were a bit confusing. The quizzes are open note and open book. Some of the quzzes were curved, and the professor was very helpful with any questions. We also got good feedback and went through harder problems in class.

This was a very good class and the professor is very caring. The grading was fair and all quizzes were open note/book. Attendance is taken, and lectures can be a bit boring, but the professor is very knowledgeable.

Cares about his students but the lecture is very dry and hard to follow. Relies heavily on excel work that can be hard to access at times. 462 was statistics-heavy and, in my opinion, is closer to an actuarial sci class than finance-related material.

Ilker Karaca is the best professor I've ever had. Attendance is mandatory, but if you miss class he is very accommodating. Quizzes are open note, and he curves them. Ilker is very responsive & helpful over email. 
Overall, he cares so much about his students and seems to genuinely enjoy our presence. 10/10 recommend taking this class with him!
Professor Karaca is a gem at the business school and has a vast knowledge of the investment field. I enjoyed the class and would recommend taking his courses.

Ilker is one of the most caring and intelligent professors at Iowa State. He is really smart so it can be hard to keep up with at times, but he wants everyone to do really well. The average in the class is a B and it is curved a little. Overall, I would take any of Ilkers classes at ISU.

Would take this class again if I could. Very informative look into corporate risk management and how insurance works. Professor Karaca seems to care a lot and wants the best for his students. Does not burden students with massive amounts of homework in 462. Would recommend this class to most students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely cares about his students. Goes over homework before they are due in lecture so that students understand. Gives great feedback on any assignment you turn in. I had this professor for two classes and would take any of his courses again if given the opportunity.

class is based off of case studies which you'll be assigned a random firm from the text to analyze and present one week. every other week you ask questions for other groups' firms. Excel homework & quizzes are based off lecture & practice problems and very easy to walk through. Beware, he gets sidetracked easily and can rant to himself for 20+ mins
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't suggest any students take this class as their final semester, it has a lot of work, you will have a quiz, a group assignment every week, and you will have a lot of excel homework, he is a very responsible professor but I definitely feel like I'm heavy-loaded in this class. As an international student, his class is kind of hard to swallow.

Karaca means very well and he truly cares about how you perform in his class. We had 5 quizzes and they are all similar to his practice problems. Plus, he takes the two lowest scores and drops them. The homework was a bit difficult, but he was willing to help in office hours. Midterms are not bad either, just make sure you go to class.

There are lots (4) excel based homeworks which are confusing and hard, he kinda expects you to be an excel whiz. His lectures are hard to get through and he does everything the long way. His quizzes are easy though and he's a really nice guy. He means well but you can tell he's new at teaching.

Karaca was decent. Lectures are a bit long and dry and may seam really difficult in the beginning. However, his tests aren't bad and he is a fairly easy grader. He tries really hard and is helpful during office hours. Gets a bad reputation but hes actually a pretty good professor if you give him a chance. One of my favorite finance classes
The professor is nice and if you have any questions I would email him. His lectures are pretty useless and the exams are like the homework.
This professor is a little underrate. He is very smart. Class was a little awkward.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Contrary to what many have said, I really enjoyed Ilker's class. He took the time to make sure we understood some very important equations. The group assignments were difficult, but he was accessible to ask questions, so they shouldn't have been that hard to finish. Also, the exams may have been hard, but the questions were from the sample-test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had in my life. If you can get another professor for this class change ASAP. He would be good in a corporate finance setting but should be nowhere near an academic setting. The case studies are useless, he's a terrible lecturer, and the exams are ridiculously hard. He has to give a crazy curve on all exams.

This guy is probably a genius but he does not relay the information that well to the class. He makes the class a whole lot more complicated than it needs to be. He will teach you the most difficult formula instead of showing the short cuts that make the most sense. The case studies are from a 400 level class.

He is knowledgeable in finance but has a hard time getting his point across, stutters and has long pauses trying to figure out what he needs to say. 7 case projects and 3 exams, power point slides from class are not very useful

Often publicly humiliated, shamed students, and made them cry. Her method of teaching is "don't ask questions." Not much time given for research part of the design process. You will spend a LOT of time outside of class. She clearly is a professor for the benefits of research, not at all to teach students. Only positive is the techniques learned.

I hoped printing would be fun and grow my love for it, but it wasn't. She is very harsh when giving feedback. She is very unclear on instructions and details on projects. The projects are so big, and you barely have time to do anything. Barely gives time in class, you must always be on task, or she will call you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this course because it was required and fell in love with the medium! But there's no way I could put up with her to ever take those classes again. She is condescending and unclear with expectations.

I would take this class again in a heartbeat. Raluca was very personable and interactive. Easy to talk to and gives useful feedback. She also gives help as much as you need. If you need extra help you can also schedule private time with her for it. I will be taking her classes in the future and will miss not having her in my next semester.

This had to be one of the most difficult classes I have ever taken. She was not very fair in her grading, picked favorites, and was overall inflexible unless you talked to her. Although, you did get to put a lot of your stuff on gallery displays. Unless it was trash. Oh and get ready to devote your whole life to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she is very knowledgeable and professional at what as he does, but she isn't a warm forgiving person. It was hard to learn because I was scared to ask for help, because whenever I did she would get visibly upset or talked down to me. During Covid times, professors should be understanding about absences but she required doctors notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If I had to describe her in one word, it'd be "uninspired". She frequently cancelled class (to "extend" our Spring break, due to non-existent bad weather, etc.) or offloaded classes to her TA. Lectures consist of her reading off the slides + 15 minutes for a group assignment. Several presentations you complete with your group, but content was easy.

She just reads the slides in lecture. Sometimes it seems like this is her first time reading them. Assignments are easy, but criteria is never clear. This class should be called intro to technical jargon because that is all we learn. Only saving grace was all assignments are group based. Also, she looks like Batman when she stares out the window.

Judith is an excellent professor who patiently clarifies doubts and ensures students understand the material. She is approachable, student-friendly, and has improved greatly in her teaching. A key strength is how she adapts the course structure daily, making changes based on what benefits students most.

Judith has improved a lot compared to her previous semesters. I collected some old lectures to prepare myself before starting F25, and found that almost nothing is similar to her previous semesters, except for the concept. This course is easy-going. Obviously, teaching style is different for each professor, so I will not compare with others.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her classes are incredibly easy just boring. People hate on her a lot but she's just as good or better than professors like Gaffar. Exams and quizzes are all easy you can learn the info the day of and get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is this what it's like to be a psychology major? The exams and quizzes are 100% memorization. Easy class, just boring asl.

Dr. Islam is a kind professor and her classes are easy. Many people complain about her lecture style but it is comparable to other professors in the department (e.g. Gaffar) but they receive less backlash. I think a lot of students need to examine their unconscious bias against women in academia and tech.

Honestly don't understand the bad reviews for this professor. Judith is a nice professor, and her classes are easy. If you attend the quiz/exam review sessions, you are basically guaranteed to get an A on the quizzes/exams. I took this class looking for an easy 400-level elective, and if you are looking for one too, take one with this professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I've been a student for 16 years. Kindergarten through Senior in college. This has got to be the most boring and maybe worst overall teacher I've ever had. All she does is read lecture slides every class. When she does deviate from the words on the slides, she just reorders the words and says obvious things to act like she's providing any value.
There is no learning in this course. You listen to lectures, then summarize them and repeat every class. The quizzes are also just copy and paste. I hope you like memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She isn't the best but she is brand new to teaching so I will cut her some slack. Her classes are also super easy just needs to get a little better at the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a complete waste of time. As a SE's only required security it is a joke you learn ZERO application and focus on memorization that is it nothing more. The lectures themselves are the exact same issues as other comments here, long boring, paragraphs on slides, and exams based around memorizing definitions. Total joke of a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tragically awful. Only reads the slides to you; talks in circles. Gave an assignment to "make three open source contributions" with no further context. This was 30/150 points on a project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The other posts weren't exaggerating. The ONLY thing she does is read the slides. Word. For. Word. No nuance or elaboration AT ALL. Exams and quizzes are literally the same weight so effectively you have an exam every two weeks. After every lecture, you need to write a 150-word summary and every two weeks you have to write a 1000-word summary.

Things I would rather than go to this class:
I tried to copy and paste all the things into this review but I hit the character limit

Current assignments include reading a conference paper and doing tasks such as combing through all of the paper's citations to find "factual errors" to critique the authors, it has become a complete waste of a class, and it is a disaster if you ever have an option to not take a class with this professor ALWAYS choose a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please, I'm begging someone who has authority at Iowa State reads this. Please do something about this professor. Enough has been said already just read the other 30 1-star reviews.

The worst professor I have had in my 4 years at Iowa State. She has no qualifications whatsoever to teach this class. Instead of learning about software vulnerability testing and analyzing code for vulnerabilities, all we have learned so far is the basics of cyber security (CIA triad, AAA gold standard, and cryptography) and its not taught well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class should be renamed "watching paint dry 101".  Get ready to sit in dead silence while she reads the slides to her self before reading them out loud to the class.  Remember daycare when they would read stories while you fell asleep for nap time?  This class is like that but you can't take a nap and she isn't reading Goodnight Moon.

I am disappointment with the way this class it taught. Mostly reads her slides.
The way Dr. Islam teaches it would be best to memorize all of her slides word for word. You don't need to really understand anything, but find ways to rephrase what she has said.

Driest lectures I've ever seen from a professor, literally read word for word from her slides for every. single. lecture. Had required attendance, in-class quizzes (the first of which was on lockdown browser?), and was generally dismissive of student concerns. Would not recommend.

I wanted to wait until the end of the semester, but Judith was nothing but dull, monotonous, and not a good lecturer. She read STRAIGHT from her slides (which came from the textbook, word for word) for 80 minutes. Mandatory Attendance. An unclear rubric and grading scale, and an overall lack of communication and even desire to teach. Thumbs Down.

The school should just save money by letting the students read the slides themselves rather than paying the professor to read them word for word (which are just copy-pasted from the textbook), because that's all she does.

Its honestly baffling that this is even a course that's offered at a university, let alone a required course.  We have talked about nothing important or applicable to the real world.  Its all memorization and the grading is far from generous.  I would say avoid this class, but it is required for all S E students, so have fun.

From talking to previous grads about this class, its usually rather easy and a forgettable experience, taking this with Islam is a completely different experience. Super boring and reading heavy lectures taken straight from the book, NO CONTEXT OR HINTS on important topics to study for quizzes/exams and a nitpicky grader on assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are few opportunities to receive credit and improve your grade. Attendance is mandatory, and you learn very little. Slides come directly from textbook, with very little to no elaboration. Quizzes cover hundreds of slides with far too much to memorize - with no indication of the most important concepts to try and effectively study. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring lectures and tough grading.  She doesn't cover any useful information but instead choosing to read vague information straight from a textbook.  One of, if not the, worst class I've ever taken.

Get ready to read and memorize lectures full of generic terms and vague definitions that don't actual mean anything.  Nothing you learn in this class is applicable to the real world, its entirely definitions and memorization.  Absolute joke of a class.

This professor is by far the worst I have ever had. She just reads off of her boring slides for an hour and a half without providing any insight. I still have not learned a thing in class. Everything is very theoretical and I have no idea how to implement any of the things she talks about. Overall, AVOID THIS CLASS LIKE THE PLAGUE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 416 is a class about software maintenance and evolution so the material is very dry. Dr. Islam does her best to keep us engaged. It's her first semester here at ISU and I think there are improvements she could make, such as making her classes more hands-on. However, I won't complain about a laidback class where I learn industry-oriented material.

This class is awful. We sit and listen to the professor read off of lecture slides that she copies word for word from the textbook. She also has 2 quizzes that are 10% of our grade and she will give you zero points for a question you answered saying your answer is too vague, when she gives no requirements to the question.

Unfortunately, Professor Islam's lectures are very boring as she simply reads from her slides. There's a lot of information to absorb only in a short amount of time. She emphasizes too much group discussion and makes quizzes unnecessarily strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I feel she doesn't know what she is speaking about. She only reads her slides without even making eye contact with the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Where to begin? Professor Islam is truly awful. Lectures are useless, but required. Get ready for some monotonous, word-for-word regurgitation for nearly an hour straight.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Quizzes are over two books, and her lecture slides have no clear idea of what it could be over, she does not seem to take any time in preparation as she only reads directly from the slides and never once gives any information that makes the lecture worth going to.

Lectures are just the professor reading paragraphs off of a powerpoint.  It comes across as if she's never even seen the slides before and is reading them for the first time.  Quizzes are way too difficult for what the class should be.

Boring, text-heavy lectures and unnecessary quizzes and exams. Mandatory attendance and discussions in each class. Might as well be an online course if I have to attend just to have slides read to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All she does is read word for word from the slides. These slides also have multiple paragraphs of text so it is hard to keep up with when taking notes. Still uses lockdown browser in 2023. Its early in the semester but I do not see this class getting much better.
The final is worth 40% of your grade. The lectures are just her reading (large) blocks of text off of slides, with a small writing activity about those large blocks of text. This is every lecture.

Why am I required to come to class when all you do is read from the lecture slides for an hour and 15 minutes straight? I can read through them literally 20x faster on my own. Why do I have to discuss what I just learned and type it into canvas? That's the type of stuff I did in seventh grade. I'm sorry, but it's just a waste of all our time.

The most boring lectures I've ever sat in, has powerpoint slides that she just reads off. Includes a discussion question each lecture that doesn't further your knowledge in any way shape or form. Doesn't care to answer the questions that students ask.

Ingrid is a great professor to work with. She is talented with what she does and it shows. She has expectations of students to pay attention and grow their skills in ceramics. Students need to show up and do the work in order to be better and I can see this would be a difficult class for those who don't. She sets clear guidelines and deadlines.

Ingrid is easily one of my top professors. She is highly skilled in her field and is clear in her instructions and expectations while also allowing her class the freedom to explore the art. She is professional and inspirational, she gives honest feedback to her students.

This professor is just a mean lady. If you're not good by her standards, she'll make fun of you and ridicule you. I would feel like crap most days after her class. I cried a few times afterwards and a couple other classmates told me they did the same. Instead of encouraging us, she belittled the efforts of those who didn't have a natural talent

The introductory ceramics class was very fun! Only half a semester, so only 2 projects, but they were fun and we were given plenty of time! There were 3 writing assignments but they weren't hard and were graded easy. The teacher is fun and understanding, helpful, and has great ideas for projects. Little strict with proper procedure. Great teacher!

Excellent professor, currently the Director of the ISA program, expects a lot from her students, and really makes you work, but VERY helpful and understands that everyone's skill level is different. I hand-built most all my projects and was pretty bad when I first started, my skills have dramatically increased thanks to Ingrid!

Hes an awesome guy but he tries to simplify things to a point where its a little sometimes confusing. Joey is good at organazing his work and wants to help us. He also doesn't allow phones in the lecture. Whenever I went to his office hours, as well help me with the question, he would help organize my work. Which is really good for calculus.

Joey was a great Calc 2 professor. He's a super fun professor, always keeping the class light and not changing his energy when he responds to students. He does write very fast, but he provides lecture notes you can print out that make keeping up with him very simple.
Had him for Math 166 and he was great

No phones allowed because he actually cares about if you are learning in the lecture. Explains everything very well and always takes questions after problems. Funny/witty and usually prepares you well for the quizzes.

I took Linear Algebra with him in Fall 2022. He did not let people use phones during lecture and would call you out if you did. Had in-class quizzes once a week, so that was how attendance was taken. He's hilarious and really nice and teaches clearly. There was one BS question on the final that screwed me out of a solid A but it is what it is.

Professor Iverson gives excellent lectures and was helpful in answering questions. For good or for worse, he strictly enforces a no-electronics policy during lecture. He definitely helped me suceed in Calc II, however, Calc II is a fairly challenging course no matter whose lectures you attend.

I had Prof. Iverson during the semester of Fall 2022. He was the best teacher out of all the instructors teaching the class, and he always stopped to ask if we were understanding the material. I'd say to succeed in this class, ATTEND LECTURES and go to help hours frequently!! I made the mistake of not attending help hours, and I regret it.

Joey truly cares and is great at teaching, math is clearly a passion of his. The homework is usually useless in learning the content, I would recommend focusing on the practice quizzes. If/when there's a time where you leave the lecture lost, watch Butler's videos - he will almost always cure your confusion. DO NOT go on your phone in class!!

Dr. Iverson always took the time to write out each problem on the chalkboard. He was very kind when it came to the students asking him questions in class and office hours. He treats you like an equal and tries to understand your question before giving out a generic answer.

Although Joey's life revolves around math, he is a very kind man who cares deeply about his students. He makes rigorous topics easier to understand through his teaching style and likes to see a student succeed. He also likes to light up the class with jokes every now and then. Very good man and teacher. 10/10

Joey is a legend the only entertaining professor in the whole math department, also makes calc 2 way easier to understand. Nobody who tried one of his lectures would ever go to a different lecture for this class.

Joey is the best math teacher I have ever had. He really cares about his job and is an amazing lecturer. He provides guided notes and puts himself in your shoes to make sure he is teaching in a clear and concise way. He has a very friendly demeanor and is pretty funny as well. 10/10.
Great lectures for Calc 2, prepares problems before class to demonstrate topics you're learning and walks through them with thorough explanations.
hes great

If you want to do well in calc 2, get Joey as your professor and follow along in class. He is really good at explaining concepts and his teaching style is very engaging. He does make a point of calling you out if you are on your phone, but you're in calc 2 - you should know how to participate in class and take notes at this point.

Doesn't actually teach linear algebra concepts, rather just writes proofs about these concepts and expects you to know all the background. Grades extrmely harshly, you can demonstrate you know the concept and still get full points off for small proving mistake. Very strict in every field from phones to grading to masks to accepting homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have to take him you will be fine, but try everything in your power to avoid. This is a high level math course, so the students are smart. However, the averages on the test were 60% and occasional would have to give extra credit on exams otherwise majority of the class would fail. One test a girl had a panic attack and ran out of the room.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Iverson was the best math professor I have had so far. Calc 2 is a difficult class, but he did a good job explaining concepts, and did so in memorable ways. His lectures were as entertaining as you can make calc, and he was nice and always willing to answer questions. He also did plenty of examples. Very strict about no phones though.

He was a very good professor! I really enjoyed his lectures and he was a nice guy. He would always answer our questions. Sometimes the concepts were hard to understand but he did multiple examples. Although, sometimes he would have to speed through examples to get everything done or he spent to much time showing how the equation was derived.

Out of all the calc professors in Fall 2019, he was the best. His class was hard so of course the lectures were heavy - he always asked people if they understood what was going on, but sometimes the concepts were so hard I didn't know what I didn't know. I watched online videos for the most difficult concepts. NO PHONES OR LAPTOPS IN HIS LECTURES
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: pretty chill, grades chill. good prof to have for ENGL 2500 if all you care about is grades
Made me very uncomfortable would never take again.
I did not care for this professor at all. He gave a weird vibe and was kinda rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took PHYS 422 Quantum Computing with Iadecola. He's very knowledgeable and friendly. The course involved a lot of heavy theoretical physics and linear algebra, and not as much practical application as I would have liked. I was hoping to make a kind of concrete project in this course to show off, but instead we created a research paper.

A decent professor overall, but he often had trouble explaining things in ways that made sense. He also spent a lot of time deriving formulas just to tell us at the end which ones are actually useful. Tophats are probably the best part of the lecture because of extra credit, but be prepared for trick questions or stuff you haven't learned yet.

Difficult class made much easier by a great prof. Attendance is extra credit, dropped assignments and makeup points for quizzes. Lectures can be confusing and move a little fast sometimes but online resources help make sense of everything. Attend lectures, take notes, and do practice problems and class is easy.

Tom is a great teacher, and he really tries to involve all of his students and learn about each of them individually. A lot of your grade depends on how much you show up to class and actually put in effort and I think that's a valuable quality. Very good professor and I would take again.

Loved Dr. Isenhart. Not only is he very well-versed, but he is also good at communicating that information. I am a shyer student who has a hard time applying myself. Despite that, he always tried to get me involved and make me feel seen.  I will always remember that, and it brings a smile to my face!

Dr. Isenhart is by far one of -if not the best- professors I have had at Iowa State. He is extremely personable, and strives to get to know each one of his students personally. He also makes a point to show that he is working for YOU the student, and tries to make sure you understand everything he teaches. He gives clear directions always.
By far one of my favorite classes. Cares about us as people AS WELL AS students, and puts more emphasis on making sure we understand the material we cover rather than covering a lot of material.

I usually wait until after the end of the semester to give my ratings on this site... but I feel so confident in Tom that I can rate him this highly only 4 weeks into the semester. I leave his class every day with new knowledge and a something to think about. He cares about his students and the content of the course, even likes to have fun. A+++!

Tom is great! You definitely won't go to sleep in his class as he keeps things incredibly interesting. He really cares about his students and gets to know them by name. Participation is huge in his class so definitely don't skip. If you need help outside of class, he is more than happy to help you and he keeps his office door open all the time.
He really knew what he was talking about and gave good lectures! Some group work but overall he was clear on his expectations.

Cares about the students and is more than willing to help if you just ask.  Makes it tough to sleep in lectures because he is so interesting.  Definitely take him if you have the option.  Will have to work for good grade but its not hard when you have a prof this good.
No Comments

Good instructor, the class was at 8 in the morning so it was very hard to stay awake. the class itself is pretty challenging in the aspects of tests and attendance activities. it takes a lot of hard work and time to do well in the lecture and lab. he is a very nice guy and will meet with you to talk about your grade.

Professor Remes is an incredible professor! His passion for film shines through his lectures. He's easy to reach out to for help and clear with his grading criteria. This class consists of seven quizzes (worst two are dropped) and two essays. His feedback is essential in essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took his version of 355, "Experimental Film." 2 essays & 4 quizzes, with the worst score of the quizzes dropped.  No final, no large projects, no group projects - just interesting readings & lectures. Helps if you are prepared to watch experimental films. He is very passionate about them & a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved taking this class, so far I've taken 3 of his classes and he is very passionate about film. He makes the class very interesting and you can tell he's just excited to share what he likes. It is a fairly easy class, just do the readings and pay attention to the discussion because that's what's on the quizzes.

I took this class completely online. One movie per week along with a lecture that was usually less than ten minutes and readings that were usually short. Quizzes are easy and papers are very open ended so you can write about whatever you want. Gave great feedback and was really passionate about film. I definitely enjoyed this class and Dr. Remes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Remes is very knowledgeable and his lectures are easy to understand. He always goes the extra mile in helping students understand symbols in films and has a very deep knowledge of each film he talks about. He is a tough grader, but he won't hesitate to let you do corrections and always backs up his grades. Highly recommend.

This class is supposed to be about learning how to analyze literature and the way this was taught expected you to already know how to do it going it. He's very arbitrary in that some times he'll say "I like this because it's different," and others he'll say like, "That's not how it's done." It's fairly easy if you don't mind your brain melting.
Loved his class. He is exceptionally well-spoken in lectures and is fascinating to listen to. He has high expectations for his essays but they challenge you to do good work. Quizzes are easy.

His passion for film pulls you into his lectures.  He expects the best out of everyone and challenges you to be creative in your writing, it's more about situating your argument than just the typical theme paper in an English class.  Iowa State is lucky to have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lectures were for extra credit points, so I didn't go most of the time. However, I loved her class structure. We had homework problems and a quiz every week, along with 3 exams and a final. She would drop your lowest exam, and there was infinite attempts of the homework and two attempts on the quiz. In the end not a difficult class.

Class was easy. Econ isn't hard? Just pay attention and use common sense. She lets you drop an exam + the final was more or less just all the practice exams. People are just kind of slow and have no common sense (which is all econ is).
Nice professor but just wasn't personally a big fan of her. Module exams are pretty tough, but the final is literally all the practice exams put together.

Honestly a really solid professor there is an Exam Drop and close to 5% in extra credit takes a decent amount of effort to learn but if you focus on the fundamentals of the concepts this class should basically be a breeze

had her for climate econ not micro and was super informative, she is passionate about the subject and cares about our learning, assignments may seem like they are graded hard but she wants us to learn, would recommend her as a professor especially for climate econ
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just go to class, take notes, get 100% on all homework and quizzes and you'll be fine. Exams are hard average is high 70's, as long as you do this you'll do fine. Idk why people rate her a 1 she's not that bad

Nothing great and nothing terrible either. I don't understand why the reviews are so harsh, as she isn't bad, just average. Econ is a hard class no matter what, so you need to put in effort regardless.

She was a very nice and understanding professor. She made her course very interactive, and it felt like she genuinely cared about how we were doing in the class. The course can be a bit overwhelming because there are many concepts that may feel foreign or differ from preconceptions. She genuinely cares. I highly recommend her.

She was a very nice and understanding professor. She made her course very interactive, and it felt like she genuinely cared about how we were doing in the class. The course can be a bit overwhelming because there are many concepts that may feel foreign or differ from preconceptions. She is very open to helping. I highly recommend her.
She goes through concepts relatively slow, which would be helpful if you don't understand things quickly. Concepts are easy, and all of the homework has unlimited attempts.
Nice Lady, taught concepts well and had lots of examples throughout the class. Concepts are hard though and you need to be vigilant about studying.

Prof. Jacqz herself is a good professor, I am unsure why the reviews are so negative. The content of Econ can be hard, so it is important to take notes and pay attention while doing the homework. As a person, she was one of my favorite professors. SI sessions are helpful if you get a good instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mid. Looks like Courtney Cox.

Professor Jacqz's taught by using slides. She's a tough grader whose homework's do not reflect what's on the exam. Unprepared TA's once tried giving a test review using a whiteboard no one could read. She makes a 101 class unnecessarily difficult. Avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard class but good teacher over all.

She could not make this class any more difficult even if she tried. I am usually a straight-A student and struggled a lot in this class. I had to teach myself the material because she did so poorly. Oh, and for the final... She reopens the previous tests and that's what you can use to study. Awesome, thanks so much!

Not too sure why there is so many negative reviews. Yes, the lectures can be long and exams are concept heavy. However, she provides several opportunities for her students to succeed and goes in depth with the material. If you attend lectures and go to the SI sessions, you'll do great.
She reads straight from the textbook with her slides. Does not go into depth when teaching, very self-taught. Get ready and I'm sorry.

If I could rate this class zero stars I would. The only way I was able to learn is the SI sessions. The professor didn't even really teach but just yap. Class averages on tests were at the highest a D+. It was basically just reading off the board as lectures as the professor did not do anything to make us successful.

Econ is a very hard class by itself, but Ms. Jacqz made it worse. You can tell she is passionate about the topic because she speaks at an almost impossible-to-understand pace. She is sweet and always willing to help, but the exams are very hard and concept-heavy. There aren't many pre-exam study resources. GO TO SI, it's the only reason I passed.
She did a good job presenting her lectures and giving students lots of resources over material in class.
She is pretty nice but talks a bit too fast. Good professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't understand all the negative reviews of this professor. Her lectures are great; you simply have to pay attention, take notes, and study a bit, just like any other college-level class. It's clear the other reviews are just lazy students who are still in high school mode. BEWARE, effort is required... great lectures, covers all material on exam.
She talks quite fast, but overall a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do. Not. Take. Irene's. Class. Extremely tough grader. She makes it so hard to learn and comprehend any material she presents. She has to willingness to help. Overall, do not take her class.

if you get her just drop out, she just be lying about the curve the whole semester and is hard to understand because of her lisp. You have to go to the lecture for the extra credit. I got Jury Duty and she basically told me to piss off and that I wont pass.

I had to work hard for my grade. You can tell she cares about improving herself & her students. She asks for feedback all the time, she rounds, & she offers extra credit. I definitely didn't like the class, not because she's a bad prof, but bc the material is TOUGH. Its obvious that people just blame her bc they were lazy and did poorly

Yeah, don't really get all the negative scores. Not an amazing professor or anything, but as long as you take down notes and do the homework, this really isn't a difficult class at all. Exams are all multiple-choice and as long as you learn the definitions, the rest of the class is fairly intuitive.

She is definitely not an easy professor and teaches straight out of the textbook. She goes through slides fast in class, and they are long. The biggest help for the course was ECON SI and her practice exams, although the actual exams are different. There is a curve at the end that helps your grade.

REQUEST PROFESSOR CHANGE! I wish I would've. With this course being required for my major, it was hard enough not being interested in the subject. I ended up having to teach myself most of the course because of Irene's difficult and confusing teaching with course scenarios that were extremely hard to follow/didn't relate to the subject whatsoever.

Request a section change if you get Irene! -- Her class is very lengthly and fast. Hard to pay attention, very boring and long lectures. Tons of definitions. Doesn't post lectures until after class.
