Her tests have averages of 50-60% on them. As a Mech E major, I struggled in the class and it was my hardest class. Attendance required for points

Irene was terrible to learn from. DON'T TAKE FROM HER!!!! I ended up teaching myself almost everything, and her lectures were a waste of time, coming from someone who attended every single one. Her exams were difficult and really required you to know every aspect of the material. Very little EC/curve. Rude and condescending to speak with also.

A deeply flawed subject taught half-heartedly. I attended the syllabus class, and promptly decided never to come back. I've scored okay on exams (upper 25%) with only the mandatory weekly homework and quizzes, and some textbook skimming. After this semester I despise economics and its verbose, useless definitions for market phenomena.
She puts way too many complicated things into something that could be so easy to understand. Also, we have asked questions and she does not help. There is no final review online either.

Slides are heavily worded and she moves very fast. The tests are nothing like what is learned in class. The questions on homework, quizzes, and exams are worded in confusing ways and very complex. She claims the questions you answer in class are for extra credit, but she grades them out of 10 so attendance is basically required.

Irene's Econ 101 class is unnecessarily hard for what an Econ 101 class should be. She is consistently at least 3-4 units ahead of the other Econ 101 professors. Her lectures are very fast paced and even harder to take notes from. Homework's and quizzes are usually poorly worded and harder then they should. Test heavy. She seems nice though.

Her tests are way harder than the homework or quizzes and she goes extremely fast with the material in class. Her lectures are helpful but very fast paced. She is not very accessible outside of class either. She is a nice lady though.

This professor rushes through course material, lacks accommodation for diverse learning needs, and refuses to post lecture notes despite technical issues. The lecture content is basic, but exams are exceedingly difficult. Practice exams are nothing like the test, you can only take them once because the questions repeat.

The class is an entry-level class but is taught at a 400-level. She is three units ahead of every other economics teacher and doesn't provide adequate study tools that would prepare you for the exams. The practice exams are nothing like the actual exams, so you are not prepared if you try to use them as a study tool.
She is very hard to learn from and the practice exams are nothing like the exams.

Lectures were straightforward and gave you all the information you needed. Exams were pretty easy, but most of the class seemed to fail them anyways. Just take notes, do the homework, and study a little bit and you will do well.
Goes wayyyyy too fast and is difficult to understand. Posts notes long after the lecture and zooms through slides.

She covers the most basic information in the lectures and makes the tests hard. I stopped wasting my time in lectures and my grade improved. The average on the tests were 60s. It's very hard to get an A in this section, so choose another professor if you can.

The average for all our exams was 60% and she was always saying how happy she was with that. She could explain things in a much simpler way but doesn't. Also, the exams are difficult since they don't really line up with the lecture. The best thing to do is read the textbook and learn it yourself. It is just too hard for a 101 intro class.

Overall, I thought Jacqz's class was more difficult than it needed to be. Though, I found that she explained things in an understandable way, and I found success through utilizing the textbook. Exams are lengthy and all multiple choice, though they can be difficult. Attendance is not mandatory, but I highly recommend it. No extra credit offered.

Very nice professor and puts lots of effort into teaching her students, but the exams are not similar to the homework/quizzes. The averages on the exams has been consistently below a 60% yet she is going to only curve the grades by 5%. Unnecessarily difficult, do not take this class.

You can tell that Irene is passionate about teaching her class and will help you whenever you reach out. The lecture slides are heavily filled with information and she quickly moves on to the other slides. The exams are NOT like the HW and Quizzes and are extremely confusing. We go over excess material other classes do not go over or test on.

Not a fan of this class. The prof moves very quickly through detailed material. The homework & quizzes pop up once a week which is not terrible and could be expected in your typical Econ course. Just when you think you are ahead the exam sneaks up on you. The exams are nothing like the homework and quizzes. The exam formatting is wordy & confusing.

She isnt terrible but the class is very challenging. I find it hard to keep up in lectures and the exams are nothing like the quizzes or homework. Shes a second year professor is what I was told (Idk if its true or not) but that would make sense if she was. If youre struggling early I suggest you get a tutor because she doesnt round grades up.
She's new so whatever but she makes everything waaaaaaay more complicated then it needs to be

She seemed like a very passionate teacher, however, the material, in her teaching ways was not understandable. I watched videos online that helped me understand more, even then when I asked for help from my TAs, none of them responded to my email. There were no SI sessions for this class or at least none that I was made aware of.

Her class is hard for no reason, the homework is unnecessarily long and time consuming and there is a weekly quiz (sometimes two). Many people in our lecture struggled with this class, the average grade for our final was a 52%. Attendance is not mandatory and she posts all lectures online.

While she is very passionate about econ and a nice lady, her class was terrible. I got a tutor and even he was confused. This class was very detailed for a 101 class and the homework was not like the test. The final average was a 49% and she still said the test was not difficult. Would not recommend this class unless you are an econ scholar.
The class average for our final exam was a 49%. Lets hope we get graded on a curve for once.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Homeworks and quizzes were easy enough, and even the first 3 exams, but the final was awful. While everything else was online (lol), the final was in person. She gave us no study guide and there was no real way to prepare for the exam, as the homework and quizzes never related very well to the exams. Hoping for a curve, but theclassavgforfinalwasaF
The quiz's and Homeworks are nothing like the exams, and she did not give a study guide for the final (which was comprehensive and cumulative) As well as the average final grade was an F.

Jacqz's Econ 101 was tough. But, I've heard 101 here with any professor is hard. She FLIES through her lecture slides, I would suggest you try and pay attention instead of take notes and take the notes later, BECAUSE SHE REFUSES TO POST THEM BEFORE CLASS? Also, the exams are online, but the final is in person. Jacqz is okay, just be ready is all.

As you can tell by everyone's responses, her exams are way too hard. They are never on a curve either, and after the first exam she told the class that the class average was "too high" and made the second exam more challenging than previously before. She is very nice, but still learning as a professor (Pretty sure this is her first class ever).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are hell and way to hard for what the class is. Information overload

During her lecture she goes way too fast and the concepts past the first 3 weeks are way too advanced. We have a homework and quiz once a week that I found myself spending hours on After the first test the average was an 80 and she said we did too well and the rest of the averages were in the 70s 101 class average grade should be higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Jacqz is nice and caring and you know she tries her best but its her first year teaching and you can tell. She relies on Pearson software to grade and create homework and quizzes but she writes her own test which throw you off. Her lectures are way to much information, very little student/teacher interaction during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Irene is certainly one of the nicer professors, but it is abundantly clear that she is new to the teaching scene. She does the best she can but her homework and quizzes are graded by canvas but she gives a ton of graphing problems, of which the tools are so picky that it is impossible to get a good grade on them sometimes.

This definitely wasn't my favorite class, it was really hard to follow the lectures because they were so fast. I opted for reading the book and using Khan Academy. Exams are tricky and there's no curve. Irene is kind and she really seems to care but her teaching style doesn't work for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself definitely wasn't my favorite as I just took it for the credits and now I regret it as there were much easier options out there. The lectures were long and boring and by the halfway mark I was lost because she goes so fast. There is a lot of mandatory homework and quizzes. they're not mandatory but GO TO THE LECTURES! It will help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is very obvious this is her first year. She moves too quickly through the lectures and material for you to take notes, and when asked she said you should go through the lectures she posts to take notes on those. But she refuses to post lectures before class for you to follow along with and take notes on, making class hard to follow and boring.

She does not do a good job of explaining topics. Everything we learn is too abstract and not realistic. Her lectures are not interactive at all. Very boring. Every exam had a different format, and she continued to amp up the difficulty.

Do not recommend her at all, the topics make little to no sense and she doesn't explain anything well. Supposed to be an easier intro class but that is definitely not the case. On the first exam we had "too high of an average" so she made the second exam much harder so we would lower the average and get worse grades. Switch professors ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Found her class very difficult. She walked back on information she posted on her slides multiple times. Went way too in depth for a 101 class. The class average for test #1 was an 80% and she said the grade was too high for her taste. I had to get a tutor for the class and it got to the point where even the tutor was lost. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The final exam is in-person with a lockdown browser. All other exams are online

Dr. Jacqz is great. She is very knowledgeable, especially on environmental economics. Very lecture heavy, so just attend those and you will do just fine. Homework, quizzes, and exams are online (except for the final exam) through MyLab. She really cares for students, so try to participate whenever possible!
Dr. Smith is a great professor; he's funny, caring and extremely knowledgeable. He also explains the content very clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just such a happy professor! He is always glad to teach. He always incorporates a fun analogy or back story to the subject that makes the lectures very engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This might be one of the most jolly people I have ever met. I have yet to finish this class, but I can already tell that John is an absolutely fantastic lecture conductor. He explains concepts great and answers questions about the homework in great detail without overcomplicating it. I hope everyone can experience a class with John at some point.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Smith made each lecture was engaging. My only complaint is that there are not that many assignments, only 100 points total, so one bad day can severely hurt your grade. Smith also only assigns full letter grades: A, B, C, D, F, so there are no plus or minuses awarded, which can hurt or help the student. He is very caring and approachable.

I found 201 to be pretty tough, but the professor was great. Lectures were really helpful, so make sure to go to class. If you put in the work, you'll be successful. The second half of the semester is a lot harder than the first half, so don't get lured into a false sense of confidence. Professor was engaging, knowledgeable, and helpful.

I found 201 as a course a little tough but Professor Smith's lectures were great. Very engaging professor, explained things well, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. HWs were a bit tough but quizzes and exams were not bad. The exams were also very similar to the practice exam so make sure you go to class when he goes over the practice.

Very knowledgeable in the material, and has a good way of explaining tough concepts. But those concepts start to get harder and harder as the class goes on, and if you're not interested in the subject or can't remember, a lot of what he says goes over your head. Also you can't afford to get behind at all, or it is hard to catch back up.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is super funny in his own way. His lectures are very enjoyable, even though the content can be exceptionally difficult. The assignments and tests are weighted heavily, so make sure you are prepared. He provides great resources--take notes and do the practice Exam.

Dr. Smith was a good professor overall. Everyday I went to class I was still shocked when he started speaking in his British accent, so that helps keep you entertained. He knows his stuff and is willing to look over anything you believe was graded unfairly. Practice exams are very similar to actual exams. The class is only 100 pts total, so beware!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the best math professors in the department. The class itself was extremely easy but the homework, quizzes, and tests are graded in a way that is not very forgiving if you make a minor mistake. I picked up on this the first couple weeks of class and after I did the class became a lot easier. I learned a lot in the process and would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tough grader, but exams are VERY similar to previous versions and practice exams. Doesn't post schedule or include it with the syllabus, so make sure you're clear on when the next quiz/exam/due date is. Class starts easy then gets hard FAST.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I didn't like him for a while because of the grading scale of the class (there's only 100 points total so if you make one small mistake that's a whole point off) but he curved the class so it's all good. Practice exams are almost the exact same as the real exams. He really understands what he's teaching and can explain really well.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hes a pretty cool guy and is very helpful. He teaches the material very well and its pretty easy to follow along for the most part. Just be careful on homework and tests because a couple minor mistakes can set you back a whole letter grade (since every point in the class is 1% of your grade). Practice tests are pretty similar to the actual test.
Smith knows what he is talking about. He reviews the material and goes over any homework questions you have in class. The practice exams are very similar to the actual ones!

Great! I usually have problems staying awake in lectures but Jonathan Smith changed that. Really clear and helpful. Watch out on small computational problems though, each point you lose is one percent of your overall grade you lose

I got a B in this class. I feel I deserved an A. The class is easy, but it's really easy to F-up by making Very small mistakes. This is advanced math, designed for math majors. Be prepared to study on your own if you don't understand something. The professor was good, but the class sucked. I may never take another math class ever again.

One of the best professors I have had. He really takes the time to make sure his students understand the material. He articulates the content clearly and understandably.  If you have any conflicts or problems with, he is extremely willing to help. Highly recommended.

I must admit--I didn't get very many things in this class.  Yet, I passed with a B.  Smith is a funny guy, makes class interesting, assigns homework that is doable and has very straight forward exams.  I felt that he made class hard for you if you didn't know the material because he wrote the book that you use in class! It's like insulting to him..
No Comments

I actually enjoyed this class.  He was always willing to help out and the tests were not extremely hard.  He wrote the text so during class I followed along the textbook while adding notes to it.  My suggestion for doing well: Go to class, take notes, and ask for help.

Julia is an amazing professor! She really cares about her students and makes sure you understand the material in office hours. Exams are very similar to homework assignments, and a lot of extra credit is given on them. Final exam score replaces the lowest midterm score.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zaikina is truly passionate about chemistry. She is harder to understand and would frequently lock your total grades so you are unable to view them. I also felt that the test content often was not taught thoroughly. Genuinely the hardest class I have ever taken.

Dr. Zaikina is nice, but if you don't have a pretty solid background in Chem, good luck. Lectures are fast paced, and it's unclear how the material being taught will be applied to actual practice problems. Majority of your grade is dependent on the exams. No extra credit. Also exam study guides are helpful, but not that similar to the actual exam.

While her accent can be difficult to understand at times and she tends to move quickly as long as you do work assigned you'll be fine. Do all the practice tests as they are almost always nearly identical to the tests except for the numbers used

The definition of “just fine”. She clearly knows her stuff but isn't the best at communicating her ideas. Her lectures move very quickly so taking notes is hard but she posts the slides on canvas beforehand. She does quite a few demos though which are always pretty cool

dr. zaikina seems very nice, but unfortunately i was not a fan of her class. her exams are confusing and almost seem to be setting you up for failure. her slides were also extremely overwhelming to look at and it was hard to take notes. i will say that the curve is pretty good. overall the class is manageable but another prof might be better.

The lectures in this class seemed to have no relevance at times and rarely helped with the homework and discussion quizzes. The slides were incredible overwhelming to look at, along with a very fast pace in the lecture, which made learning so hard. The only way I was able to learn was through my discussion each week.

This is the absolute worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life, and I mean it. She is impossible to understand, preps the wrong material, and her exam averages are literally 50-60% and all she has to say to that is "better luck next time." She doesn't help her students at all. The good is the curve, but tbh a good grade is a long shot w her.
She has a very strong accent. Exams are worth a lot and the averages are terrible.
Badbadbadbad

Dr. Zaikina does an incredible job of relating course content with real-world practical applications. She does chemistry demos in almost every lecture, which makes coming to class more exciting. Lectures are fast! Attendance is mandated by the TopHat questions she conducts (they can be quite tough). Overall, one of my favorite chemistry professors!

This professor has an extremely heavy accent. If you want to understand what you are learning... you cant. Want to go over the lecture slides before class? Can't do that either because she doesn't have filled out notes posted... ever. The class content would be much easier if I didn't have this professor. I recommend switching if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: goes through slides so fast, and just expects you to figure it out. be prepared to teach yourself all of the information! incredibly boring lectures and weirdly hard top-hats. she will blame you for not doing well even though the whole class is failing, test average was 60% and she blamed US! dont even get me started on the 15 min limit on quizzes.

Literally have no clue what she says half the time. She goes through her slides quickly, so hopefully you have an iPad otherwise, you will fail. She blames the class if they do badly on exams, even though we all don't understand. Even the SI leaders say she doesn't go over the right things. Go to SI and tutoring if you want to AT LEAST pass.

Julia was a good fair professor. Her homework was graded difficulty, but they were reasonable. She gives practice exams that perfectly represent the material on the exam. No textbook is required, which is helpful when trying to save money.

Yulia was kind of hard to understand in class with her accent at times and she would go through slides pretty fast. If you don't download the lecture pdf before class, it's hard to keep up with notes if you are a heavy note-taker. I would go to all the lectures because you will have TopHat questions in nearly every lecture.

Homeworks take forever to finish especially if you're having trouble understanding the material. Her tests are very hard, especially the final exam and her lectures are hard to follow. But she does give extra credit for each test to make up points you lost which is nice.

This woman is horrible and just blames her students for failing on the students even though the whole class is failing. it is so exhausting, and i hate going to her class because her lectures or long and boring and unhelpful

Julia is kind and caring. She gives fair grades to everyone and is always happy to help. I bought textbooks but found that just listening to her lecture and reviewing the ppt she gave is totally enough. Although quizzes may be too many, it's ok if you review the materials she gave in class. And she gave a booster quiz to improve the grade.

There are seven class quizzes, and the time is short, so don't be late because it's half the total and you don't have a chance to fix it. She will generally assign about ten questions for the take-home exam, but only two or three are graded.

Julia is nice, but there are few homework assignments and she only selects a few problems from each assignment to actually grade, so not all your work will count. The tests are worth a large majority of your grade

Zaikina is a good teacher overall. Her accent may be a bit hard to get around, and her lectures do drone on, but she does give you the content you need to succeed. My advice, copy down her lecture notes (from your laptop or phone) in your notebook in her lecture. You will get the content you need, at a pace that works for you, and still get Tophats

Zaikina has been one of my least favorite professors. Extremely tough grader. I had a 4.0 GPA before this class and I'm a junior. Very test heavy, prepare for the lowest exam scores you've ever received. Tests have some multiple choice and some short answer. Homework takes at least a few hours every week and recitation quizzes are terrible.

She's the first Chemistry teacher that I actually understand. The lecture slides are very clear, you don't need the book. It's better if you pay attention to what she says rather than write what's on the slides. Quizzes and homeworks every week. TopHat. Exams are hard if you have little chemistry knowledge.
Excellent lectures.  Would definitely recommend taking this class.
Some of the topics were covered fast but otherwise ok.

Mechanical Vibration wasn't even showing up in the schedule at first and I only added it last minute because I needed another class. The class was pretty small which honestly made it better. It ended up being the best class and professor I've had so far. If you don't know what a diffy q is going in, you definitely will by the time you're done.

This seminar was honestly my favorite class this semester.  You are mostly in the innovation labs not classroom.  The professor made everyone feel comfortable and low stress.  Recommend taking it if you get the chance.
He's very organized and wants everyone to enjoy the projects. You get to make stuff in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fun class with a professor who knows his stuff.  Would definitely take it again.

I took this as an honors seminar (Imagine, Design, Make). It was SO much fun, this class was a great way to relax. Grading is based on participation and effort, not success. Very much a "do your best and enjoy the experience" type of thing.

The one credit statics course is the worst class I have ever taken as a student. It was put together terribly. Rouse teaches like you are already extremely qualified in statics and his tests are 10 times harder than what he covers in class and the practice test.

This class made me feel like a worm being cooked in an easy bake oven, but Matt was very good at teaching the material and had very clear grading criteria, so I would 100% recommend him to other students
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: During lecture, a student asked when grades would be posted on Canvas. He responded that because of the large number of students who took the exam, entering all the scores into Canvas would be too much work, so students would need to do his job for him and calculate their own grades.

The content he taught in this class did not prepare us for the exam we took March with the average being roughly 60%. Jon not only intends on not adding a curve to the exam scores, but he also explicitly said that attendance points, top hat questions, and exam scores are all not going to be put into canvas so no one knows what their true grade is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 1 lecture and 1 recitation per week and 1 homework assignment per week that can take anywhere from 2-4 hours to complete. Homework is graded very harshly. Only 1 midterm, which is disproportionately difficult compared to material covered in class and in hw. Graphics and figures are difficult to understand. Final worth 50% of you grade.

Jon is a decent professor, however CE 2710 is a very poorly organized class. For one credit class, u do more homework than your other 3-4 credit classes. Also expect very low grades with not much reasoning as to why. not enough content in this class to make it an entire semester, every week in lecture it felt like we learned the exact same thing.

Doesn't know how to teach the course and spends his entire lecture talking about stuff that barely helps with the homework and exams. TAs are brutal graders and will give basically zero feedback for the errors. He somehow managed to make a course that's "supposedly" the easier version of statics have a much lower pass rate than the normal statics.

Jon spends the entire hour talking about the topic and leaves examples unfinished. The textbook wasn't finished on time, and homework assignments were all graded differently. The practice exams are nothing like the final and there are no step by step solutions for the exams. Overall, the class was poorly structured and could have been much easier.

I would not bother taking this course at isu if possible. Calling this a 1 credit course is genuinely insulting for how much genuin effort and time one has to sink in to do even remotely well. This is just another classic nightmare of a course that engineers like myself are expected to take. All I can say is good luck.

Extremely disorganized and difficult to follow. Lectures often devolve into long rambles about topics completely unrelated to the course material. While he is lenient regarding deadlines to compensate for the chaos, the lack of structure is very stressful. He also basically ignores Canvas, so it's hard to track your progress.

This class was unnecessarily difficult; things felt all over the place and very disorganized. The textbook wasn't complete, and it was being written while the class was in session, which made preparing for exams a nightmare. The exams were disproportionately more difficult than homework and lectures. He was also unhelpful if you were confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rouse is a great prof, but makes his exams difficult. Exams are given in class but not written for such a format, making it extremely hard to finish the exam with confidence. Only 2 midterms and a final, each worth ~25%. The first exam for this semester had a ~60% average and he refuses to curve. The TAs will grade the homework harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Im probably not going to pass the class due to the first two tests being impossibly hard along with not having enough time to finish them like the rest of the class. You basically have to go to the lectures because he posts nothing on Canvas. The only thing he posts on Canvas is past tests and then the one you take is nothing like it. Complete Joke
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His exams are nearly impossible to finish in 50 minutes. He should switch to night exams. He is a great teacher, but the exams are much more difficult than the homework. It's very difficult, but I think they should switch to having us take it at the business school. The exams are worth a lot and there aren't many grades in the gradebook.
206 is a pretty easy class. Tests can be a little difficult but are similar to the homework. Attending lectures is not mandatory, but it helps to ensure you learn the content.

Possibly one of the best professors and people have had the pleasure of knowing. Matt is so methodical in his teaching and goes over every single type of problem there is. There's a lot of H.W, so stay on top of that. Matt is caring and respectful and he makes you feel as though there are no wrong questions; he's extremely approachable.
The worst professor I've had so far at ISU. Class was painful, although maybe he is a decent guy. But it's just so boring and uneventful.

Matt is a patient, diligent professor and probably the top pick for EM 274. He goes above and beyond what he needs to for this course. Another review here knocked him for messing up problems -- that happens occasionally as is expected for complicated problems. You skipping class entirely is more indicative of being a bad student.

Took him last semester and I didn't enjoy his class at all. After a month going to class, I stopped going. His teaching was very slow and sometimes he made mistakes when solving problems. I passed the class by reading the textbook at home. So, save your time for other classes since you can just read the textbook yourself, and you may be better off.

A bunch of my friends took EM274 with different professors. They came to lecture with me one day and were blown away by how great of a teacher Matt is. If you put in the work and do the online problems for practice you will pass statics!

Matt is one of the best professors I've had at ISU. He cares so much about every student and makes the class easy (as possible) to understand. His office hours are extremely helpful and he often asks for suggestions in lecture on what else he could do to assist students prepare. He goes the extra mile-- definitely take statics with Rouse.
Rouse is a good guy and is always teaching relevant material to the class. He also brings a positive attitude to the room. If you are on the fence choose his class! Coming from someone with experi

Matt is a great EM professor. His lectures consist of practice problems from the material assigned during that week. Example problems are clear and he is always available outside class or after class if you have questions, even though I didn't go to his office hours often. As an added benefit, he's a really good guy and very likable.
Such a great Professor, I wish he would teach all EM courses. Nice guy and his teaching style helps you do better on exams.

Class is pretty tough but I don't think Rouse could have done a better job. He knows the material really well and does a lot of examples. Some students felt surprised by exam questions but if you always go to class and do HW you will realize he covers any material that shows up.
Fantastic lecturer and provides great feedback on work done. Always willing to help you out. However, if your handwriting is not perfect, you will lose 25% on each homework assignment

Rouse is exactly what I wanted in a professor. Clearly presents example problems which are representative of test questions. Emphasizes important material. Homework covers exactly what's on the tests. Most students that complain about this professor or the course likely just didn't put the work in. Great professor, still requires a lot of studying.

Rouse's class structure is pretty much all example problem based which is helpful for the homework and tests. He doesn't post anything online but does follow along with the textbook for the most part so you don't have to go to class. But I found it helpful. Finds ways to explain things concisely and as interesting as possible

Professor Rouse goes by Matt. I took Statics with him and it was his first time teaching it. This being said, the lectures got better as the semester progressed. He teaches things slowly, with many examples. He is prone to making small mistakes during examples, but will correct them when asked. He is very personable and knows everyone's names.

I think Professor Phares was strong in teaching the conceptual parts of the course similar to SCM 310, but the math-heavy sections were harder to follow. In my opinion, he didn't explain the equations clearly or provide enough examples to fully understand the material. Then would throw you in-class worksheets, assuming we understood it all.

3 exams 180 points each roughly 40 questions, Pack back discussion, with a final exam that is optional if your grade is high enough or good enough for you. It can be a drag at times especially when the entire course is mainly Phares lecturing about common sense stuff like transportation about how a truck moves cargo to a warehouse.
Professor Phares is a wholesome man who made going to supply chain management at 7:45 am 3 days a week less of a drag. He told cheesy jokes but they made the class more fun. Great man and professor.

One of the easiest classes I've ever taken. The final is not cumulative and is optional, so after the 2nd exam, if your grade is high enough, there is no incentive to go to lecture. Although, his lectures are pretty good, but leans on student participation a lot, and a morning class can be kind of rough for participation.

Interesting lectures with real world experience mixed in that is very helpful. Tests are a bit challenging and I wish he would post practice exams as my first exam went poorly due to not knowing what to study. Takes attendance randomly but is very understanding if you have a good reason to miss class. Had interesting guest speakers also.

Jonathan was an amazing professor. I have to hand it to him; he does a really great job teaching from experience. He did supply chain for Walmart, which was always interesting to hear about. I liked the way he related it to the course content. Keep in mind; he gives out in-class activities that have a huge toll on your grade, so don't skip class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Sturgill's class isn't hard if you pay attention during lecture and complete assignments. SI and office hours are very helpful before exams.

Mrs. Sturgill, Is a very nice professor in the classroom but emailing her, is a different story she is quite rude and mean. I will say her class isn't super difficult but you should go to the lectures! The notes are super helpful, and make sure you do the homework it counts for a lot at the end!

The class itself is not hard to understand at all. The tests are average and she does homework about every week. As far as the professor goes, she likes to talk and be the boss. If you are talking at the beginning of class that will set the mood for the lecture. It's interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very nice in lectures and if you attend the lectures you will be fine, but in emails she is not helpful and kinda mean, I liked her as a professor I don't have to actually speak with. Do the Homework!!!
One quiz every week, which was open-note (slides). One midterm, one final, and one presentation. She is very helpful and makes a boring class somewhat enjoyable.

Her lectures are sometimes all over the place and the group projects can be confusing. She is helpful but can be a little off putting. Exams are written and in class. McGraw Hill homework assignments, in class projects, and case studies outside of class. Grades the projects and case studies lightly, but looks for exact work shown on exams.

Really good professor. If you go to class and take the provided notes, you'll be just fine. She gives you plenty of heads up on the exams and what'll be on them and makes sure you're prepared. Make sure you plan ahead for lectures though. If you miss one, you'll miss a lot of material. Exams aren't too difficult, plus there's usually extra credit.
Very easy class due to her teaching.

Sturgill was very helpful and responsive; fairly manageable course load. All assignments opened at beginning of semester w/ weekly deadlines. 1 SmartBook, 1 HW, and sometimes 1 APPLY weekly. 1 Quizam at the end of the semester. Done 2 1/2 weeks before the end of the semester. Be very specific in your emails to get help. Completely online; no EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Sturgill makes the material approachable for students. Follow her recommended studying and homework plans and you'll be fine.

Professor Sturgill is a good lecturer who will gladly help students with any questions or difficulties in the course. Doing homework and attending lecture is crucial for understanding the concepts in this course. If you put in the effort, ACCT 284 will not be that difficult.

as long as you do all of the homework the exams really don't matter that much. Theres plenty of extra credit to put you at a C minimum without much effort. she's passionate about teaching and loves her classes.

You can get a C minimum in this class pretty easily. I wish I had done the extra credit earlier in the year so I would be in a better place, so learn from my mistake! do ALL the homework, it says it's "optional" but it'll add so many points at the end of the semester if you get at least 80% or more on most or all of them.

Definitely not the all-time best ACCT professor here, but she gets the job done and isn't a bad professor. I struggled with the concepts in her class, but she wasn't to blame. super nice lady, plenty of EC to get you by. Exams aren't super hard either.
go to lectures to be successful in the class

Professor Sturgill is helpful, I had her for multiple classes. If you can't meet during office hours, make an appointment. She wants students to succeed and goes out of her way to help. Exam reviews are very helpful, don't skip those.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ACCT 301 wasn't difficult, just overly time-consuming for 1 credit. Sturgill was acutely unhelpful when I addressed issues I was having with the ALEKS program. She also held a supposedly mandatory in-person meeting, causing me to cancel work and drive to Ames, only to find out it was recorded and was literally just going over the syllabus slowly.
had her for all my accounting courses and she is very helpful. The lectures can be long but are very beneficial and if u attend class you should get good grades on tests

Acct 301 is a fairly easy accounting course if you've had some accounting experience. The online course has a portion that's learning along with homework and a final. Must get an 80% or higher on the final to pass the course, but you get 2 attempts. Also a simulation and a project that you do at the end of the course. Due dates to keep on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sturgill helped during office hours, this class didn't come easy to me and after the first exam Sturgill really helped me study. Help lab was also a good way to work on the class project.

It was an alright class. Jenny was a nice woman and frequently plugged resources to get help outside of class. Lectures were a little boring and a few of her explanations of some concepts were pretty vague. However she still did a pretty good job with the things that she did explain in full detail. The weekly LearnSmarts were a bit unnecessary.

Very bad at explaining the content the further you get into the notes, seems like she gave up halfway through. Expects students to understand the content at the drop of a hat. Can't read her writing, and so much as if someone sneezes she'll take a 30 second break and just stare at them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sturgill was good! I didn't interact with her much because the course layout was set up in a way where I could pretty much do it myself online. She was available when I had questions and held in-person meetings when there were unclear assignments. Overall nice professor and a very good course!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Online 1 credit course with a fair amount of work. However she is extremely accessible and helpful during her office hours. She will sit with you and take time to make sure you succeed. Very clear expectations in the syllabus for a self-paced course and I found it extremely manageable to stay on track.

Jenny is by far one of my favorite acct professors here. She gives out a lot of extra credit on participation and the LearnSmarts, so don't overlook those. She is also very willing to work with you outside of office hours, just ensure you make efforts to try in the class. For as difficult as the class is, I think she is the best person to teach it.

Sturgill is the best professor I have ever had at Iowa State. If you put in the effort to attend her office hours or reach out to her, she will stop at nothing to help you understand the concepts and cares so deeply for her students. She wants her students to succeed and her experience as a CPA shows in her lectures as she has real experience

Had no trouble with the content, but she never responded to emails, and when she did was frankly disrespectful. She often got the due dates and times for office hours incorrect, and when I asked for clarification, she was rude in response. Very few opportunities for help, and she didn't take the responsibility of helping her students seriously.

This 1-credit course is entirely self-paced & online. I thought it was pretty easy if you felt confident about ACCT 284. It felt like a lot of work for only one credit, but if you work ahead, you can be done early. I didn't actually interact with the prof too much, but she sent a lot of reminder emails & was pretty accessible.

First class of the semester, we had to print off all of the lecture notes OR go and buy them because the notes were fill-in-the-blank style. Lectures were hard to follow, and weekly assignment setups were tedious.

I had Professor Sturgill for ACCT 383 over the summer. She was an amazing help when it came to understanding the information. She was also very understanding when I got covid at the beginning of the semester and had to miss quite a few classes. She was easy to ask for help to get caught up and she helped before and after class to finish assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really do not understand such harsh reviews on professor Sturgill. She is a fantastic professor who is able and willing to help you if you reach out and put in the work. Her lectures are not mandatory but she does not post the notes, so you need to come to class. To those who struggled, SI would gave been a good idea for you.

Expects very highly for students to understand the information right away. Her lectures were boring yet mandatory and very fast- and she was persistent on not recording lectures. Accounting did not come easily to me and she was not very helpful outside of class.

Good professor and helpful outside of class. Lectures are pretty easy to understand. You have to do your notes in a printed copy, which some people don't like, but it's not so bad. Good study materials given before tests.

You are required to buy a textbook, then go to class where she makes it  a "no-screen zone" where you have to buy a notes book and can only full in the blanks in class. If you skip, she doesn't post the notes online. She's nice, but she's not a professor staying modern with tech and learning.

Professor Sturgill is one of the most helpful professors I have had at Iowa State so far.  She emails back almost always within 30 minutes and is always open for you to come see her during office hours.  Even though ACCT 301 is so much work (which is not her fault), she is there to help and wants you to succeed.
Professor Sturgill helped me prepare for the Final Exam in ACCT 301 online. Attending office hours helps a lot to understand some of the concepts. I procrastinated and she still helped me study.

All rounded professor. However, I would request a little more leniency from her side in regards to the timings of the examination! Although there were several announcements made stating that it should be done before a certain time, which doesn't make sense and it could at least span out till the end of that day. Very accessible professor otherwise.

Jenny will stop talking for 30 seconds mid-lecture due to one person talking in the back, then rant about not getting material covered. She has inconvenient exam times and blows through too much material in one sitting. She brags about how hard her tests are and demands nobody use devices in her class. So far one of my worst college professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy class if you stay on top of it. Professor Sturgill is more than willing to help out, and I reached out to her during the large project which I procrastinated until right before the due date and she still responded quickly and helped me earn an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Surprised by the negative reviews on Professor Sturgill. She was very understanding with whatever situations came up and willing to work with you as long as you communicated in advance. Very helpful with the in-class group assignments if you ask. If you're willing to ask questions and communicate she is a great professor to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was graded based off of mainly exams and projects. In my opinion this is the hardest and longest accounting project I've ever had to do as an accounting major. A lot of the criteria we had to do was unclear and all over the place.
Tough class, but Professor Sturgill cares about her students. Accessible and helpful if you have questions, office hours help a lot. Study guides and practice tests are helpful for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The more I went to class the more confused I got from her lectures. Didn't get a single response from emailing her all semester.

It is great to have a teacher with this much real-world experience. It does take effort to keep up in the class but based on talking with friends other sections are similar. She is very approachable and has been very responsive. I would take her again.
pretty tough assignments but very responsive to emails from students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ashlock is a great professor and very nice. He clearly knows what he is talking about, and there is a reason he is well-respected in the geotechnical community. I would highly recommend taking one of his classes, especially for Geotechnical Engineering. His exams are easier than those of other geotechnical engineering professors, too.

The class was quite heavy on group projects. The design project is quite interesting, and a good group is vital. The homework is also done in groups. This class has a lot of lectures that move fast toward the end of the semester. The tests are quite straightforward and close related to in-class problems.

360 with Ashlock is a mixed bag experience. He is a great guy and wants everyone to be interested in his class and do well. However, the class is loaded with many different topics and can feel like a lot. Homework is done in the same team as your lab report, so it is important to get a good group. Tests are similar to examples in class.
Very responsible, kind and helpful.
Good explanation. Take notes of in-class problems. Make cheat sheet of all important material he's covered till the exam and you'll get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Difficult class, it's very DENSE. But luckily Ashlock knows what he's talking about and knows how to explain things to students. He definitely makes the class more do-able.

Dr. Ashlock is NOT a good teacher. He reads directly from his notes and doesn't clarify or go into depth on any topic. Once something gets complicated he just says to read the textbook and moves on. The project is long and complicated and he does not provide enough structure even though he grades by a rigid rubric.

kevin is a great guy, would always give direct feedback at desk crits with genuinely helpful feedback. he has high expectations for his students but as long as you try in class and have a conversation with him he's helpful.

out of all of the architecture professors at isu, i'd say i've learned the most from kevin. he is an extremely knowledgable person when it comes to ecology-conscious design, and he shows that through talking extensively about what he's passionate about. it can be repetitive, but trust in his vision and guidance and you'll learn lots.

Kevin is a wonderful guy and a great designer but is not great with teaching, especially this course. He continuously showed up late and would ramble a lot during studio. His abstract ideas were good but would hold our class back in comparison to others and did not have clear instruction. Very nice person but near impossible to understand sometimes

He is excellent as long as you show up and do your work. He's always there to help and tries to support and push you to do better. His goal is to be unstructured, so YOU decide what to do and how to design things through your own views. He is so chill. Great guy.

Very vague about expectations, lectures for hours about nonsense and talks around the point, made the site his own property, which is 1.5 hours from Ames, was constantly late but reprimanded us when we were, and sent us upwards of 125 emails in one semester. On the bright side, you will have no issues contacting him outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very smart guy but cannot effectively speak to students. Lectures during studio time & you have to drive over an hour to the site -you will have to spend hours & hours outside of class working on your projects because you wont be able you effectively use studio time. His course management is awful & his excessive emails are condescending. Avoid...

At first nothing was making sense but after you realize the genius behind his backwards metaphorical riddles, thats when it all makes sense. He spoke with such profoundness and apotheosis stature that challenged my every day thinking. Overall, he's a beaut but just has unorthodox ways of conveying ideas and messages.

Great guy, he's a little vague until you get to know him. You really gotta dig deep with Kev, once you stop trying to understand you start to relize the true genius of what he's telling you. Very profound. Helped develop me more than almost any professor ever has. If you're gonna run a marathon, you gotta do it.

He is a very nice guy, but I literally had no idea what he was talking about this entire semester. He never takes attendance but states that you're only allowed to miss two classes. He can be a veery inspirational guy but when he lectures or assigns homework, well Good luck Charlie.
He is extremely vague and does not teach or lecture but expects you to know what he's talking about and read his mind.
Most vague person I have ever met

Well he's a pretty nice guy at least. His assignments are very confusing and he doesn't give a lot of structure in terms of what he's looking for, however will tell you it is not what he is looking for. He is inspirational when you talk to him but is frustrating when you want to know something specific.
Kevin is terrible, late to class, not helpful and sometimes disrespectful, unclear, and likes to go on tangents about random things. I'd recommend another prof if you end up with Kevin...

Very smart man, but not a good professor.  He will talk for an hour without saying anything helpful.  He doesn't explain assignments, our class was always behind the others.  Switch to another professor if you can.
No Comments

I could see him being decent for 4th year students perhaps, but i just didnt get him.  Either way, he still did a poor job of adapting to a less advanced group of second year students.  His general teaching method is rather unstructured, no "real" due dates, but expects progress on a daily basis, which can be really bad if you tend to slack off.
I spent all semester trying to figure out what this guy was talking about.
Not a good teacher. Late to class and doesnt help much.
Avoid!
Karla is a good professor. Her grading is on the tougher side but she really cares about the students learning. You'll do better and learn more in person.
Worst professors I have had at iowa state

Karla is an extremely tough, selective grader. She often gives negative feedback on aspects of an assignment that she already approved, or read over prior to submission. She also admitted to grading student assignment in an inconsistent manner, sometimes depending on time of day or order of who is graded first. She gives rubric but doesn't grade it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course has two major individual assignments and one group project and presentation. The first assignment seemed to be graded somewhat subjectively and it strayed from the rubric, but it improved for later assignments. Professor Ruden is very thorough with announcements and communicating information online.

She's a tough grader, but I learned a ton about how to write professionally. If I didn't understand something, she explained it so I could. She's kind of funny, and she cares about students. Class discussions are usually interesting.

She is nice and cares about students. Her grading seemed harsh. Attendance for the english department is mandatory and your grade will drop if miss more than 3 classes. She extends the due dates for almost every assignment
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Karla Ruden is a wonderful English professor. This course has you write 5 papers which have clear guidelines but requires you to still work for an A. Additionally, you will have 2 presentations over the last two papers that you write. Professor Ruden explains everything very well and genuinely cares about her students. I cannot recommend her enough
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Knaplund has truly grown into an excellent instructor. He made class as interesting as possible for what it was (lecture-heavy and statistics) and did it with grace. He is kind and understanding and wants everyone to succeed (so long as they put in the effort). Great guy and surprisingly helpful class even for those not interested in research.

Great psych elective for any major. Lectures were fill in the blank notes - attendance was not mandatory. One quiz each week on Canvas, a unit exam every four weeks and a unit reflection paper afterwards (1-2 pages). He emphasizes getting the textbook but I personally only ever used it a few times. Pretty good class overall!

If you attend the lectures and pay attention, its the easiest class you can take, however if you don't attend the lectures you will struggle.  He was a very kind professor but pretty obviously new to the teaching world, his office hours were easily accessible and helpful.  The tests were almost entirely covered by the review lectures.

Knaplund is clearly new to the teaching world. He has the potential to be a good professor, but he is just not there yet. He is very passionate about the subject, though. I can see how some might enjoy his teaching style, but it just didn't do it for me. Practice exam lecture quizzes are tedious and annoying but extremely helpful.

Dr.Knaplund is a super genuine, sweet guy who loves teaching psychology. He cracks jokes in class which keeps it entertaining. Lecture quizzes after every class. I did just fine without reading the readings assigned. Tests are difficult; make sure to know everything on the study guide to do well. The material is super interesting, highly recommend.

Put more effort into this class than psych 440, organic chemistry, physics AND calc 1 and 2 yet still recieved a lower grade than those courses. Worst class I have ever taken its beyond difficult and exams are so specific you might want to write down and memorize every word that comes from his mouth and the textbook. Would avoid this class!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You need to attend lecture because there are fill in the blank notes for lecture that will not be posted afterwards. I would also suggest reading the textbook for weekly reading quizzes. Besides reading the textbook, there is no outside homework. Quizzes tend to be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took his 211 class and it was easy and informative. He is very understanding and willing to answer any questions you have. Very kind person who obviously enjoys teaching.

I loved psych 211 with Tyler! I think this class was very valuable in contemplating the future with a degree in psychology, but with zero pressure to pass. Just turn in the assignments on time and show up, and you will no doubt pass. Tyler is super caring and just wants to see us succeed as psych majors :)
He's super understanding and knows that people can make mistakes. Make sure you keep on the homework. It's super easy and the longest part is reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Knaplund is the best lab professor ever! He is very accessible and relatable. If you ever have a problem with the class, just talk to him and he'll do his best so that you don't get a bad grade. I would take this class a million times again with this same professor. He really is the best!

Tyler was a great teacher!! He makes the material fun and understandable. He is young and always very nice and relatable. He is always responds to emails quickly. He grades easily and if you show up you will do great. Definitely take Tyler's class!

He is lenient in grading. His lectures have problems similar to questions on homework and exams. Exams are based on questions from homework and lectures. There is a discussion most Fridays after going over the homework. He also posts notes and answers. He answers emails quickly when you have questions.

The class was quite interesting; however, lectures could be boring, and it is unnecessary to go. Tests are very close to his practice exams. He seems like a very nice guy and is quick to respond to emails or answer any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The first 4 homework are gonna make you cry in the moment. Extremely hard, but it gets better as you figure it out. Looking back, those first homeworks werent hard. Homework graded on effort. Theres a paper due at the end. Midterms had a massive curve. Great professor. Super smart. Its his second year so the lectures are very dry.

Kevin is such a chill professor, especially for a class like stats. The notes are great for following along in lecture and helpful when preparing for exams. You are allowed one page of front and back notes to use during the exams. Exams are mostly multiple choice.

This class is pretty simple and easy to do well in. However, the wording for some of the homework can get overly specific and not very clear on what it wants. Great professor overall, very chill and forgiving.
Kasper is so fun and makes a 9 am lecture feel worth it. He is very empathetic towards students and wants you to succeed. It's a lot of writing but the exams are mostly multiple choice.

Kevin has to be the best professor I have EVER had. He is so nice and explains the work very well, his lectures aren't boring and very useful. He makes his exams easy and we are allowed to have a cheat sheet!! 10/10

Kevin is an awesome instructor! Homework assignments can be time-consuming, but they're very helpful when preparing for exams. Kevin's straightforward about what will be on the tests and even includes extra credit. He's also entertaining and always willing to answer questions. He genuinely wants students to succeed.

Definitely attend his lectures. On top of being an overall chill and great guy, it's a lot easier to understand his notes through his lectures rather than going over them on your own. He for sure got me very motivated to learn more about Statistics.

Easily my favorite professor so far. Lectures had guided notes, and he would go over the concepts in great detail. They were worth attending, but the notes would be posted. Every friday there was homework due that took me no longer than 30 minutes each week. If you can understand the homework, you'll do fine on exams. Lab was essentially extra prac

On a weekly basis, we would normally have two assignments due on Friday at 5 pm. One of which was a "vocab" quiz and the other an "online hw" quiz. Both had two attempts, and you can come back whenever. Great teacher, and he made the class fun. He doesn't count attendance, but I'd recommend going. Labs were basically extra practice, which = easy

Kevin is awesome!! The lectures are not insanely interesting, but he makes them bearable and usually lets us out of class a few minutes early. Lectures are not mandatory, however, they helped my understanding of the material a lot. Lots of homework, but it was all helpful.

Love this professor. Lectures flowed well, he explained the concepts in great detail, and made learning the material very easy. Homeworks were very helpful for the exams, and he was very clear about what would be on exams. He is extremely kind and understanding as well. Great professor.

Kevin is a super chill dude.  He gives guided notes at the beginning of the week and after lectures he posts the annotated notes if you missed class. Majority of the grades are homework which you can complete off the notes online. Lectures are optional. Tests are easier than expected, as long as you understand the homework you're chillin.

Best professor I've ever had at ISU. The professor was really kind and helpful. I had to leave during the year due to a family emergency and the professor was understanding and helped me get back on track. His lectures are really helpful and the exams were similar to the exams. His homeworks do take a while to complete and some questions are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: class is hard, but he gives EC and makes lectures fun
If you do the work and attend lectures, you will succeed in the class.

Kevin is definitely a must-have professor for STAT 101. He is very chill and lenient, and his lectures are straightforward and easy to listen to. His exams are easy as you can have a page of notes front and back on them. The only downside of the class is there are online homework and vocab due every week. The lab is also very unnecessary.

Kevin Kasper did a great job introducing statistics. I had never taken a statistics course before so I was worried, but the way he has his lectures and notes set up makes it really easy to follow along in class. Be prepared to print off notes before each class. Attending lectures is the best way to succeed. Lots of homework, but it helped me learn!

I struggled so much in high school stats but taking stats 101 with Kevin made it so easy. I was able to understand stats in a semester where it took me a year in high school & I didn't learn anything there. He will answer your questions & is very chill with attendance. Go to labs, they are like participation points and help. Take stats with Kevin.

Class is very easy, exam averages were in the B range. Course content is very easy and intuitive in nature. Throughout the course, concepts were continually reemphasized, which became very boring to listen to. Labs are graded on participation. Homework is the hardest part, and Professor Kasper tends to assign homework with odd start and end times.
Kevin is a G. He's a great teacher and makes it really easy to learn. If you have questions, he'll answer them right away. Easy class with scheduled homework for every week.

For preface, I did not take stats in high school, but we touched on it in algebra. Easiest class I've taken. Yes, there's a lab but if you show up you get credit and it's helpful to learn how to do the written homework. Tests are 70% multiple choice and you get a cheat sheet to bring. Lots of homework, but very easy and so are the tests. No final!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kevin made learning the material of STAT 330 pretty straightforward. There were some topics I was confused about, but he was pretty accessible outside of class. You could probably not even show up to the lectures and pass. But, if you want a good grade, you're probably going to have to go to some lectures and walk through some examples.

Very well designed course. Dr. Kasper knows what he's talking about and gives plenty of examples in lectures. Homework, while heavy at the beginning, feels like a breeze and so do the tests. Most of everyone got A's in this class taking it with him and he was very proud. My only complaint was that there was little review content/problems for tests.
Best stat teacher I have had, prepared me for higher level stat classes. When choosing between professors, choose Kevin.
One of the better professors I've ever had
Class was a little dull, but that comes with the material. He did a good job of presenting the material and not making the class too difficult. It was a good introductory stats class.
honestly my favorite professor at Iowa State
Kevin made learning stats super easy. He does a good job at giving examples. Homework is very similar to the test.

Kevin is a great guy. This is the first professor I've given a 5 to because I feel like he deserves it. He makes you feel engaged in statistics and describes solutions to problems in a very approachable way. He drops an exam, which is very helpful for students and their grade.

Kevin did a wonderful job teaching! His lectures are packed (with a dash of humor), so make sure you attend and take notes. Homework was every week there wasn't a test, two midterms and a final (3 total), and a quiz in stat lab every week. The hw can take some time and you get a cheat sheet on each test. All (hw, 3 test, quiz) was weighed 20% each.
Great professor. Seems to care about students and material he teaches. Exams are very easy. Opportunity for extra credit if you come to class!

He is very energetic and is fine at lecturing. The only issue pops up when he switches to lecturing on powerpoints. He doesn't explain things very well when on powerpoints. I can't believe I'm actually saying this, but, the exams are a but too easy to cheese. You don't really need to understand the underlying concepts to do well.

Kevin Kasper is the best statistics professor I have had at Iowa State, and being a statistics major, I've had a lot of different stat profs. Professor Kasper is a very down to earth guy and you can tell he genuinely enjoys teaching. His exams were exactly what he covers in class. Lectures are very informative with a splash of dry humor.

Kevin is by far one of the best professors I've had at Iowa State. He really cares about the students and wants to make sure that they learn and understand the material. He also will throw in some dry humor during the lectures. On the exams, we got to bring a piece of paper with whatever we wanted to write on it.

IF YOU HAVE TO TAKE STATS 101, TAKE IT WITH KEVIN!!!!! He made this class so easy because you can tell he enjoys statistics and teaching so it's so easy to learn the material. He's a great person and very understanding if you miss a test, etc. Tests are mainly multiple choice with a couple short answer but it's easy as long as you do the homework.
Pretty nice, relaxed guy. Lectures can feel a bit long at times but he occasionally throws in some dry humor to make it not too bad.

Professor Kasper was a good professor and was clear on what was needed to pass the class and made it so students could do so if they put in effort.  Attendance wasn't mandatory for the lectures but every once in a while he'd pass around an attendance sheet (which overall still wasn't worth much). There is a good chunk of hw due every week.

I took Stat 301 with Kevin Kasper. He teaches by coming up with things off the top of his head and writing on the board rather than Powerpoint notes. He also teaches mostly based on the examples instead of in general. There was one weekly homework assignment that was sometimes substituted with a group assignment in the lab.
Gives clear instructions on due dates and whats to be expected on the exams.  Not necessarily the most energetic lecturer but he does what he can with the material.

He is quite unorganized in terms of the notes he presents. There are no Powerpoint slides or anything, he just comes up with stuff off the top of his head and writes it on the board during lectures. There is one homework assignment per week that is kind of long but he gives examples in class or in lab to help you complete it.

Kevin is easy to understand and is very clear in all his lectures. He sometimes gives examples for the homework and if you pay attention, you get 100%. He does random attendance checks and those are the "lecture quizzes" you get points for, but he lets you miss 2. Lots of homework, so don't try to do it the morning its due

Ashwin has the best lectures ive seen from any professors ive had as a junior. He clearly cares about his students and the examples he provides helps greatly for comprehension. If you go to lectures and ask good questions the class should be easy. Overall take it with Him!

Amazing professor! Really cares for his students. He checks in if you're behind. He's open during office hours and is very understanding if you communicate well. If you can get ashwin for 228 or 309, take it with him without thinking twice.

COMS 228 is a mess. Ashwin is the lone bright spot. He cares about his students, is a good teacher, and goes the extra mile to make sure we succeed. The lead professor and TA's make 228 almost impossible to navigate, but Ashwin does his best to make it manageable. Class averages for tests are 50% with no curve given, make sure to do EC on homework.

Good and helpful, but the best thing you can do during class is use the entire time to work on your project and quietly talk to your group members about it. Use most classes like a team meeting, and you will do great and make a great app. The app demonstrations are most of your grade, so focus on the project more than the class.

This guy is one of the best professors I've ever had. I took COMS 342 in the fall 2024 and forgot to write a review, his lectures were AWESOME. The guy answers any questions without mumbling and makes sure that students are on the same page as him. Just a great guy.
I took this class in Fall 2024, Ashwin cares about his students and if you pay attention you should be able to get a good grade.

COMS 2280 is not ran by Ashwin, so all of my gripes with the class itself fall on that professor. However, I respect no professor more than Ashwin. He busted his butt to make this mess of a class somewhat manageable for his students and did everything in his power to make up shortcomings (with mixed success, again not his fault.) Take 2280 with him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Difficult class, but he is very good about making sure people understand what's going on and will take the time during office hours to explain things. Definitely take this class with him. Lectures fell behind sometimes, so we crammed a lot in the last 2 weeks. Typically no class curve, and exam averages were around 50%. Extra credit for projects.

Had Ashwin as my lecturer for both 2280 and 2300. Would definitely recommend him for both of these classes. He takes time to make sure lectures are understood by the class and actually cares how well you do in the class. Definitely take his section if possible.

Ashwin is very good at explaining topics that were tough for me initially, like iterators and splay trees. He moves slowly so the whole class can understand, which occasionally made the class fall behind, but it was very useful to make sure we understood the topics. He's also funny and cares alot about the success of his students.

3420 is a challenging class, but the professor's teaching techniques made it easy to follow. He does use grammar more advanced than in other courses, but if you have enough idea about the terms, it will be reasonably straight forward. Would love to be his student again!

Ashwin is such a great professor, and if you're planning on taking 228 make sure you take it with him! He gives amazing feedback and is very accommodating, he wants to see you succeed. I would 100% recommend him to anyone. This is not an easy class, however, he makes it easier.

Ashwin lectured my 228 class and also was in my 230 class to help. He's a really good professor and I was able to understand his lectures easily. He also posted the markdown files he went over in class and this was a very easy and organized way for me to review content. He was very responsive to any questions and was super helpful.

Ashwin is an extremely down-to-earth instructor. He cares and wants you to pass. He will take the time to explain topics to you and will try other methods if it doesn't work. His lectures and notes are much better than the alternative because he puts effort into making them worthwhile. Overall, already an amazing instructor with lots of potential.

Some of the assignments took a decent amount of time to complete, but the rubrics are extremely clear, and if you follow the directions given, you will do very well. She also offered extra credit every week, which made it so I wasn't worried about my grade in the course dropping from one bad assignment.
She is a wonderful professor, clearly cared for students. Exams had a tendency to be a little difficult but would ask for feedback and curve the exam after.

Would not recommend for completing natural science credit, only take if actually interested in astronomy. Class average on our second midterm was a 63%, if that clears anything up. She is nice and there are extra credit opportunities, but not an easy class.

Dr. Leung is obviously extremely intelligent and educated and it shows. She clearly cares and wants students to do well. She offers so much extra credit, drops your worse exam score and her lectures are great. I'm a business major and I did great, she's a great teacher.
Actually cares about students' progression and learning. Deeply cares about the material too and enjoys her job, making her class very enjoyable too.

Dr. Leung is an amazing professor. Her lectures are super interesting and she try to keep the class engaged. The exams can be tougher, but if you read the online textbook you'll be set. She also gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit.

Worst instructor at ISU and I'm writing this as I'm graduating this semester so I reflected on the whole 4 years. She's technically a student, since her knowledge is shallow. Also can't teach. Ironically my dad took class from her dad, and had the same bad experience. Must be running in the blood. Avoid taking her class, do Engr 1600 instead.

She's really strict, when it comes to homeworks and grading. For the homeworks, you have to use same method that they used in lecture other wise, you will get way less grades, and her exams are hard.

I wished that there's other prof other than her.

Horribly structured class.
