Looking back as a recent graduate, her class did not prepare me for future classes as it was not an accurate representation of upper-level classes like she claimed-- the upper level classes were FAR better. Some definitely challenging, but profs actually posted material and helped. You will struggle in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor here easily. Murmurs during lecture so you can barely hear her and speaks way too fast making it even worse. Doesn't explain anything during lecture and just goes through problems by herself. On top of that, hard personality to work with; not a professor you can email if you have a situation

The homework and Group Projects at the end of the semester were the worst part of this class by far. Examples given in class did not help us with the Homework at all, and the projects had no rubric except for a few bullet points. Exams were not that bad as long as you went to the review session.

The homework was almost always 10x more complicated than the examples Lauren went over in class. The Excel Project was so complex that even the TA's didn't know how to do it. No rubrics given for either of the projects, and the final project came down to the last two weeks during finals and prep week, a demanding amount of work for the timing.

I absolutely adored CE1600 this Fall! Lauren created a welcoming environment and was easy to follow during lectures. Homework assignments were fairly challenging, but accurately prepared me for the exam, as former exam problems were used. I felt supported by the TA staff and Lauren throughout the semester.

Nice person usually, and often the homeworks really aren't that bad if you're willing to go to some help hours every now and again. The problem comes with the fact that the projects are graded harshly and you're given minimal direction. She often expects a lot out of students who are often either freshman or sophomores with minimal experience.

Schwab expects us to do homework that includes things barely taught in class, TA said her reasoning was "your employer will expect you to know these things without being taught." In-class quizzes make attendance basically mandatory for lectures that fail to prepare you for the course. Class ended up just being Excel anyways with bad group projects.

Lauren is a very nice person but this class was awful. You have to teach yourself how to do everything as the lectures don't teach you how to do much of anything. The projects in this class have components you never truly learn how to do in class. The homework was complicated and took hours.
She doesnt put grades in until a month later. We don't learn much from class and are expected to do hard homework.

She basically wants you to learn everything by yourself and the homework always takes at least 3 hours to complete. Once you finally finish the homework, most likely you get 75% or lower. Horrible teacher.
No course material
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm sure that Lauren was a great person, but no so much a great professor. The homework was very difficult and required lots of help hours which always sucked. The final project is ridiculous and requires a lot of time and effort, as well as knowledge only attained in upper level classes. Also the class had NOTHING to do with Env E, only civil.
Zero course material outside of lectures. Gives assignments over material you haven't learned yet.

Lauren will not provide any assistance or rubrics of any kind and grades harshly and without any reason. Your grade will be mostly up to chance. The chance that you remember some tiny thing she said once that may end up being the backbone of the final project. Who knows! Nothing is regulated. Everything is random.

Lauren quite literally throws her students to the wolves. There are not enough help hours, and when there are help hours, there are over 50 students in attendance. So, it's very difficult to get help. It's very hard to follow along with her and you are expected to know how to do everything on your own for the homework and projects.

This class is a joke and the instructor does not explain well. A lot of the assignments and exams are just busy work. This class does not add any value to my education and should be made optional. The instructor is the type of person who thinks that she is cool but actually she is not. Too bad there's no other instructor so you can't avoid her.

Lauren is a nice person but definitely does not provide enough resources when it comes to the exams. Good luck on the final project, as there are very few instructions and she grades very harshly when it comes time for the presentation. Overall, this class is a good introduction to engineering but just gone about in a very disastrous manner,

I believe Dr. Schwab is a nice person, but I would never willingly take a class she taught again. She is frequently disorganized and often feels like the course sets you up for failure. She relies heavily on lecture attendance, but time during lectures often feels wasted and like what she teaches is useless for the course.

Lauren is a funny, witty and sharp person and I enjoyed interacting with her during class. But that said, everything else about the class was a mess. Grades were not put in on time and were graded harshly without a lot of grading rubrics. There was also a general lack of resources, no notes, no lecture videos, and not a lot of feedback. Frustrating

Lauren may seem like a kind and caring professor on the outside, but after being in her class, she has proven she's just the opposite of that. She's unprofessional and unhelpful when you ask her for help. She throws projects at you with very few instructions and expects you to know how to solve them as if you've been doing them for years. Good luck

i heard lots of complaints about her but shes a pretty good professor if you take notes in class and go to the office hours. homeworks are kind of hard but she goes over similar questions in lecture and lab. on projects her and the TAs for the class help and answer questions which is nice.
Complete lack of resources and understanding. Very cold and strict on policiesgenuinely one of the worst professors I will ever have

Lauren is kind and caring, but this class was straight up MISERABLE. Very little guidance was given on projects and even when TAs helped they werent able to answer all questions. There needs to be lecture videos and MORE examples (with ANSWERS and steps) available for students. The lack of resources for this class is shocking. Struggle is real!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lauren is a good teacher in a tough-to-teach class. CE160 is meant to introduce both the concepts and, partially, the workload of higher-level CE courses and I think she did a good job of that. Homework, exams and projects were graded very harshly (Im a transfer, I knew all the content), and that is the only gripe I had with the course.
Forgettable course. Gives trick exams. First homework assignment was a question on a EM 274 homework.

I'm really bummed to see the negative reviews here. Lauren is a great teacher, and she's very understanding and kind. People don't like how she doesn't offer help on group projects, but she lets you struggle to learn more. The class is a great introductory class into CCEE, and you become fluent in Excel, which is a very good skill to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: It bummed me out to see the negative reviews on here for Lauren! I felt that the class was very manageable and she was always friendly and pretty willing to help. On the two main projects, there definitely were periods where there was very little guidance, which was irritating. But overall I felt that the class was run well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was sad to see bad reviews for this prof. She was really one of my favorites, she is pretty solid at explaining stuff, and didn't bat an when I was late/missed class. She is also pretty funny if you like dry humor, overall, I had a really great experience. Really fantastic teacher if you enjoy the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is a joke. The department really needs to evaluate this system. A waste of resources with tons of TAs that are not helpful and an instructor who doesn't know what she's doing. As a transfer student that can't transfer a similar class from another college, I am disappointed since I learned more there. This class is just tons of busy work.

If you want to take a class where you need to teach yourself, you've come to the right place. The ability to convey information was completely lacking, and if you want to get a good grade, you either need to ask several questions in help hours, or buy chegg.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Valery does not teach at all; he uses Oleg's lecture videos that you have to watch before class. Homework is difficult, with multiple individual assignments due at one time. In-class scores do more to your grade than exams. Not great at answering questions during in-class either.

The class isn't very difficult—just stay on top of lectures and start homework early. The professor is fine, but I'd recommend Oleg's class if possible. Oleg keeps things more interesting and makes it something you actually want to attend. Valery's can feel slower and less engaging. He isn't very tech-savvy and has a strong accent, but he's kind.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Levitas was awesome, cracking jokes and giving hints during Tophat. I wasn't the biggest fan of watching lectures outside class and using lecture time to do quiz-style Tophats. Sometimes, the homework was challenging and took some time, but it ultimately was the best practice, helping me succeed in the class and do well on exams and Tophat.

Cool guy, he knows the material very well and occasionally cracks a witty joke. For EM324 he used Oleg's lectures which meant the class was reversed (watch lectures outside of class then solve problems in class). He doesn't teach many undergrad courses but if you get the chance I'd take him.

Dr. Liu made frequent mistakes in lectures and in homework and is extremely harsh in grading exams. Did not explain concepts well and required group homework that were more work than they were helpful.

A professor who honestly seems like she is against her students. Is condescending and not approachable. Awards very little partial credit which led to a 48% average on an exam. Her "solutions" to the exam grades would only raise half a grade letter. Consistently makes mistakes every lecture, but is unnecessarily harsh with student's mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Dr. Lu's first time teaching the class, & I understand that can come with its difficulties. However, when the average grade of an exam was 48% & most of the feedback being "I didn't finish the test", I'm not comforted by "That's to be expected, this is a tough class". She makes a lot of errors on her ppts, and can't answer most questions.

Does a great job relating real world experience and ideas into the classroom lectures. Makes the learning environment conducive to thinking in a practical sense for relating concepts to what is seen in the field and actual project teams.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Scott is Incredible

I actually had him for our capstone ME415, but that wasn't an option. He is a super chill guy and pretty much let us handle the class by ourselves on our own schedule. He talks a lot about his experiences in the industry to help teach us. Even did a raffle for some old items he had, like a mini basketball hoop and some beat up table.

Scott Merkle is one of the best guys you'll ever meet. He treats students as equals to himself. He allows almost every deadline to be flexible in 4210 within reason. He knows and respects that we have lives outside of the class. He always has interesting facts and insight. His classes feel like you're learning in the real world and not restricted.

He is awesome for 415. He understands that you are a college student with deadlines and other classes, lets your group work independently and decide your own schedule, and understands that some company sponsors can be a bit difficult to work with. Super flexible and helpful with assignments (Deadlines and the actual assignment guidelines).

One of the few professors that treats us like peers/people instead of students. Very nice instructor with lots of experience in industry. Very helpful relating coursework to industry. Scott is probably the coolest professor I've had. Make sure you get Scott's Bulletproof Coffee if you get a chance to try it.

Very nice, easy and interesting to talk to, with plenty of industry experience. Lectures are scattered and not always the greatest, but he can clarify if you ask questions. Tests are simple and extremely similar to HW. He tries to relate the topics in the class to things he experienced in industry which can be interesting.
Super nice guy

He doesn't really teach, just talks about things that may or may not relate to the class at all. Extremely nice and you can learn a lot from him, kinda scattered though. The hw isn't great but the quizzes are exactly like it. You may not learn much unless you want to, but Scott will be an easy A. Awesome guy but not great at actually teaching

Scott is a nice guy but not a great teacher. The lectures were laid back and ended early almost every time. The class is run like a 100 level, but the exams were 400 level and very difficult. He did a good job trying to incorporate real world examples into class, but it came at the expense of learning the actual material. Didn't learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Scott has a lot of industry experience and always brings that information to class. However, if you are really wanting to learn machine design I'd take it with another professor. I took ME325 with him over the summer and it was the easiest ME class I took at ISU, it was a joke. He tries hard and really cares about his students, great to chat with.

I'm giving a low rating because Merkle isn't good if you want to learn (maybe he's good for senior design, but not a standard "book" class). He doesn't teach. Repeatedly ended class 15 minutes in. Not ONCE did he actually go through material or work through problems. Easy grader. Bad professor. You won't learn anything useful.

Very easy to get a good grade with him, tests are made easy if you understand the material enough to make your cheat sheet(s) and go to the review. Actual learning of the material was more difficult, but if you're looking for an easy grade you'll probably get it.
One of the coolest professors Ive had at Iowa State. He cares a lot about his students tries to connect with them through his experiences and stories he shares in class.
The class is easy as long as you're willing to seek help from the professor!

If you REALLY wanna learn, don't take him. If u just wanna get an easy "A", take him. I learn nothing, but still get an "A". Very easy going. This subject is known to be the hardest in ME, but with him, its even easier than 100 level courses. Bout the test, its almost spoon-feeding / at best you can call it "fill-in-the-blanks".

Had for a summer term in ME 325, one of the hardest classes in the core program. Very easy-going, wants you to actually learn important things and pass. Very good on material clarity, was always prepared and us students were generally happy. Just do the assignments and ask questions. Common sense professor!

Seems to have a poor grasp on modern-day design. Definitely someone who has an outdated view on the world and refuses to get with the times. If I followed her advice I'd be making half my salary at my post grad job. This is a consistent issue with ISU graphic design professors, but Miriam's classes are especially bad.

She is very passionate about design and provides blunt but helpful feedback. Take everything she says as a learning opportunity, even though sometimes it can get disheartening. Her attitude is wonderful and she's really funny. I suggest taking as many classes with her as possible.

Miriam's class was challenging, but I truly learned so much, and her assignments were amazing portfolio builders. She very much knows what she's doing and can be blunt sometimes, so it depends on what you want from your teacher. A lot is expected of you, but it makes you a better designer. I came out feeling more confident about design than ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Miriam holds you to a very high standard, and expects a lot out of you. She also goes over a lot in class so it is hard to miss class. If you miss, you might fall behind. She is very particular about the way you use different apps and the way you save files. Very structured classes and assignments.

A lot of filler work that, although is relevant to content, significantly takes away from project work time. Can be condescending and made classmates cry on multiple occasions. Overall feedback was helpful and I learned a lot, so would still recommend for skills/portfolio. Illustration heavy. If you're neurodivergent you're gonna have a hard time.

if you have the opportunity to pick another GD professor do it! she's way too harsh on students, students will cry during class due to how rude she is. i am warning you do not take her class. and if u have to good luck and don't take anything personally she is just a bitter woman
There are many other graphic design professors that don't put down students and constantly talk about themselves. Would recommend literally any other prof

I loved taking this class with Miriam. She is a tough grader with many small details that you always need to worry about. Her class moves quickly, but she is there to help you the entire time. The homework stressed me, but I learned more from this class than any other one-semester graphic design class.
She slays. Such a fun professor and is genuinely so helpful. Her classes are always super chill and students actually look forward to coming to class.

Miriam is an awesome person and a great instructor. She's so good at helping your work reach a professional standard and is super accommodating of all styles and approaches. Everyone says her workload is a lot, but I disagree, it's pretty average. She is super experienced at what she does, and she's such a nice person

Had Miriam for 4 courses my sophomore year. Workload is a lot, but if it wasn't for her teaching & willingness to help students succeed & understand, then I would've been lost as a junior & senior. Does demos and actually teaches how to use software, & she goes to great lengths to help. Best professor I've ever had, hands down.

While the work she assigns may seem a little overwhelming at first, she is an amazing professor who wants to see you succeed. When she is teaching, she makes sure everyone understands what's going on. She gives great feedback and conversations with her enthusiastic attitude make you excited for the next class.

Miriam will always give you feedback, whether you're ready or not. She just wants to push you and see you succeed. She's a sweet lady who does really enjoy her students and her projects are well thought out and build upon what you already know. Her projects are pretty heavy sometimes, but she knows what you're capable of and wants to help you.

Miriam is by far my favorite professor in graphic design. She is super kind, funny, and always helpful. She's willing to let you explore things you want to and always gives great constructive criticism. She praises you for your work as well. If you have stuff going on in your personal life and get behind she's understanding as long as you tell her.

This is the fourth class I've had with Miriam and I can hands down say she is the best Graphic Design professor I've had at Iowa State. She pushes you to become better and you always learn a lot in her classes if you're willing to work. She cares a lot about her students and has a funny personality. She knows her stuff and is willing to share.

Miriam is THE BEST professor I have ever had. She is the most caring, kind hearted soul and understands everyones story is different. She gave excellent feedback and truly helped me grow as a designer. Not to mention, she made sure all students had a say in the class and made sure we werent struggling! Take her every chance you get!

Miriam is one of the best GD teachers I have had. While her projects are intricate, each layer helps you to recognize different needs within design and requires meticulous attention to each phase. She focuses on analysis and research of audiences, good design, and textbook readings so that you can create effective systems, not just good designs.
Too much homework and lectures did not make sense at all. I did like how nice she was really nice though. Take the class at your own risk.
Peg is sooooo cool, however just too many assignments. Super great person to be around.

Very minimal in-class lectures, she assigns 5-10 assignments weekly. There is a lot of group and solo work; she is a tough grader. Attendance is regulated by a signature at the beginning of class, and there are harsh penalties for poor attendance. Class concepts are not difficult by any means, but the amount of busy work is insane.

Whomever left the feedback on Dec 17th, 2025 didn't totally get the class. The professor was fine and gave real world examples. Life is not going to hand you something on a silver platter and they gave some good advice in class.
Good person. Treats students with respect.
Learned alot.
Genuinely, the most pointless class I have ever taken at Iowa State. Did not learn anything except filling in blanks on sheets-long assignments. Get ready to show up to lecture for nothing.
I genuinely was so frustrated with how pointless this class was.

MKT361-I liked the class but was a ton of work. Attendance is mandatory but you can email her any excuse and she'll count it as excused absence. You have to pick a real and fake company at the beginning of the semester so make sure it's something interesting to you.For some reason she only comments on assignments when its 100%,otherwise no feedback
Good person. Approachable. Good teacher. Answers emails 24/7.

Extremely unorganized and doesn't ever seem prepared for class. You will have assignments she will never mention in class, and you have no clue if you are even doing them right. They are also just copied assignments and documents from online that she puts no time into making. Easy A, but not the best professor if you actually want to learn.

I took MKT 361 (SSM strategy) with her. She's soo nice and cares about her students, but the class itself is horrible. Outdated material, like 8 assignments per week that you fill in worksheets which all repeat the same thing, and they take FOREVER. But, the class is generally easy & you can email her if you're missing class & she will excuse you.

I have not learned a single thing in class. She will (mis)read off the lecture slides in 10 minutes, and then tell us to do an assignment with our group. The assignments are easy, and she grades really easy, too, but if you are in it to actually learn something, good luck.
Prof. Mattison is a great professor. Would definitely recommend taking any of her marketing classes. Very laid back, all homework/quizzes are on McGraw-Hill.

Great guy, the assignments can be kind of difficult but he offers plenty of replacement assignments if you do bad. He knows what he's doing and can answer any questions he is also lenient on late work as long as it is only a couple of times.

Definitely has flaws in grading structure but he would be a great fit for somebody actually interested in Solidworks and manufacturing. You get used to his speech in 5 minutes. He goes in great depth about how CADD relates to real world manufacturing and is happy to converse with students. Get a buddy to work with cuz you are going to suck at first

This professor is extremely hard to understand, his tongue is amputated and does not speak clearly. He refuses to release rubrics for any assignments because he believes it helps students focus more on modeling rather than checking off boxes which obscures grading. On top of that he is already a very hard grader. minor mistakes=half grade or less.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures lasted eons, professor was bad at explaining things. Time consuming homework that was much more difficult than other sections. Exams were 11 MCQ so missing one permanently hurt your grade.

Tests are easy but have no curve—your grade is the raw percentage from 12-question multiple-choice tests. Missing a question is a hefty penalty. The assignments are tough overall, and there is no safety net in the class. Missing a quiz will crack your grade. Morgan is chill though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures drag on forever with yapping. Nothing is learned and barely practiced before getting graded on it. Midterms were 12 questions no curve. Prof lowk had unfathomable knowledge though. Try to make him give into peer pressure.
Awesome guy. Has engaging lectures and is willing to work with you if you reach out for help.
Old school prof who's set in his ways but you can tell he cares about us students and knows what he's talking about
Nice guy, but he doesnt let you know your grade till the end of the semester, and his lectures are confusing and nobody pays attention.

Awesome chill prof. Uses a lot of real world analogies that makes difficult concepts easy to understand. Very kind and passionate about his teaching. If you ask him a question, he will take 10 minutes to explain it.

Best professor I've had at ISU by far. Super engaging and makes you think differently about the world. He sometimes lectures like it's an advanced econ class but the exams are fair. Very down to earth guy who wants everyone to succeed.

Great and funny guy! His lectures are very hard to follow and you will not take much away from them. He wants everyone to pass, he curves all the exams and has a ton of extra credit to offer. Many exam questions are exact homework questions.

Brent was a super nice guy and one of my favorite professors. His lectures were engaging and often used sports analogies that helped students better understand the material. If you complete the homework, attend the lecture, and review the in-class top hat questions, you'll do fine.
His lectures suck...

Great professor, lectures aren't mandatory, but I highly recommend going.  Offers extra credit opportunities for attending class.  The class is fairly test-heavy, and I found his exams to be difficult and challenging to study for.  The worst part of the class was not being able to see my grade, and I am still wondering what my final grade will be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super nice guy and is pretty funny, but dude just yaps. I'm no good at econ, and the tests are so hard. He's super nice, but overall difficult.
Awesome teacher, awesome man. Very caring for his students. Cares a ton about his work. Attend the lectures and do all the work and you will be fine.
Down to earth professor who cares about us students

I was nervous about taking econ, but the professor was an amazing teacher who made everything relatable. He was by far the best professor I've had at ISU. He does go off on tangents with stories but its always tied back to the rest of the material to make it more interesting. Definitely recommend.
He wasn't a bad professor. His class was just harder for me!
Worked with students whenever a problem would arise, had weekly assignments, and offers daily extra credit questions at the end of class.

Good class overall! A required reading with questions was assigned through TopHat (~once a week), but this helped with understanding- take your time! Lectures were a little unclear but do have extra credit TopHat- I personally did not attend. Tests were difficult, but curved HEAVY. Many questions were taken from TopHat questions.

Kreider is a really nice guy and wants you to succeed. However, his grading needs to be changed. He doesn't use canvas and uses top hat for everything, so you do not know what your grade is until the final grade is posted, and it's just a surprise to you. Your only grade in the class is tests and a small percent of top hat questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, this class was awful; Kreider is a great guy, though, as he always tries to relate his topics to the modern day. He is funny too. The lectures make no sense, and the tests are impossible to study for. His grade curve is a blessing.

Brent is a nice guy... who likes economics... but doesn't know how to teach. Going to class will not help you at all with the test so don't waste your time, spend it studying the textbook and tophat questions.

There is nothing wrong with Professor Kreider. The topics can seem complicated, and the readings are dense. However, he gives plenty of examples in each lecture. He doesn't grade anything besides the class exams, reading questions, and in-class Top Hat questions. On the contrary, no quizzes exist, and he drops the lowest score of the three exams.

This class was decently easy. He gives extra credit every day in class, and you get partial credit just for answering the question. The homework is a bit of a read, but he does drop 2 chapter assignments. Overall, he's a great professor and tries his best to give you the best grade possible in his class. He does ramble sometimes so beware of that.

His lectures don't make much sense but I love hearing about his college adventures during them. The material on the tests have nothing to do with what you learned so just be ready to show up and wing it. Gets 3 stars from me because he seems like a chill guy and the grading curve is a life savor.

Kreider makes econ engaging with real-world examples. While lectures can be a bit dense, the textbook and Unstuck ai's tools helped me stay on top of the material. Attendance is a must, but the extra credit makes it worth it.
Such a sweet and caring professor! Always ensures that you have the resources needed to be successful in Econ super caring and understanding!
Does not use the common portal (canvas) that all other teachers post upcoming assignments on. Attendance is therefore required to know what assignments are upcoming.

Great guy who tries to make lectures engaging to get people to show up and learn. Even with that though it's more than alright to miss class and receive a good grade. He tells lots of jokes and gives good real-world examples to help relate economics in a way students can understand.
Super great professor! Very passionate about what he does and is very caring. Lectures can be a little hard to follow but the content is explained well. If you want to pass going to class will hep.

I might be a little biased because I am an econ major, but I had a really good time taking 101 from Kreider. If you pay a little bit of attention during lectures and do the homework, you will do fine on the exams. Another incentive for showing up to class is the extra credit; my advice is to go as often as you can.

Brent is a real homie. He's a genuine dude who actually does care about his students' well being. His lectures can get a bit boring, but he'll sprinkle in humor or stories to keep it interesting. For Econ, just do the readings and the Top Hat questions and you should be good. He uses those questions on the exams which are pretty light. Great guy.

Kreider is very knowledgable about Econ, although his lectures are very difficult to follow along. There is weekly homework reading/assignments which consist of 30-50 questions and one chapter in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To start, you will need Top Hat to access the Homework and exams. There are only four things that go towards your grade. 2 out of 3 exams Drop the worse one, a required final, and homework. He's super nice after, I would say, three weeks, he starts to do extra credit every lecture that ends up adding up. He also curves the exams so just do average.

You could tell he was very passionate about econ. You do not need to attend lectures and can learn just as much doing the homework. All the exams you took online and don't have class that specific day.

Very easy with his new format. Everything you may do in lectures is all online and usually in lectures he will ramble on a slightly off topic rant where you cant tell if he's lecturing or telling a story, but when he is on topic he does well. I didn't go to the lectures for probably 3/4 of the semester and w everything online you can keep up well

Attendance is not mandatory!! Everything you complete is online and you don't need to go to a testing center. He didnt put any test grades in till the very end of the semester so you really had no idea what your grade would be. The exam questions do come from his in class lectures but he does tend to ramble on about other things/ hard to learn

Brent somehow makes econ 101 enjoyable with the interesting (but sometimes extremely off-topic) lectures, personal stories in economics, and applications for many different majors. I would highly recommend attending the lectures, even if they are sometimes boring, because he gives extra credit and teaches better than the textbook does.

Attendance is optional due to Covid, and I wouldn't recommend going every time because he tends to ramble a lot, and you can learn the material through the textbook on Top Hat. Do the readings and questions or you won't pass. Beware that he locks your grade on Canvas so you won't know your final grade until the end of the semester!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes cool, but hes got off track from time to time.

one of my favorite professors, I enjoy listening to his lectures bc you can tell hes passionate, he teaches life lessons along the way, makes some jokes, and gives extra credit opportunities when you come to class. Econ itself is difficult, so be prepared to study, class isnt mandatory but i recommend going bc a lot of examples are on the test
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is a breeze. Krieder is nice and does help when you ask. But you literally dont need to attend any lectures to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of notes but it is not that hard to get a good grade. He literally gives you a pool of the test questions before you take the test but even then the tests can be stressful sometimes. Overall, you do have to work for a good grade if Econ doesn't come naturally to you.

Lectures are very boring and hard to comprehend. Homework is easy enough you can figure out. Exams are quite difficult because of the similar answer choices. I did horrible on all 3 exams during the semester then did well on the final. He curved the class a lot but don't rely on it if you want a good grade. There's extra credit at end of lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's a little nutty but a good guy overall. Econ itself is hard, but he made it pretty easy to understand. Parts of the test were strictly about the lecture so I think attendance is mandatory, but a lot of people skipped.

While attendance is not mandatory there is Top Hat nearly every day and most of the topics that end up on the tests are covered in lectures. Sometimes the only time you will hear something on a test is from lecture so it is important to show up and take notes. Other than that he is a good lecturer and if you have questions he will always answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He uses tophat for textbooks, tests, pop quizzes, and homework. Although sometimes he is a bit long winded on topics, he explains things pretty well and uses lots of examples. Tests are pretty easy and graded on a curve. There is a lot of participation points from top hat questions and the notes have blanks in them so you have to go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, I would not take this professor. Hes not the worst, but his lectures are so boring! He also at the beginning would assign huge readings on Monday that needed to be completed in 5 days. Some of the questions dont make sense because of how vague they are as well. His tests are pretty good tho, as they are all multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Kreider gives really good lectures, and he makes learning the content enjoyable by using games over Top Hat. He grades fairly, the homework is not curved and the tests are slightly curved in the students' favor. I personally don't like Economics, and if you feel the same, I think taking it with him is your best shot at tolerating the class.

The professor knows what hes talking about its just hard to focus and I feel like I havent learned much in this class from the lectures. If you go to lecture and do all the readings youll be fine and the tests are usually curved. One complaint I have is that we have never had a total letter grade all semester so Im still unsure of my grade.

Amazing professor and teaches students life lessons along with the class content. Tests are mostly easy but there is a lot of online textbook reading each week. Would definitely recommend even as an elective.
while the lectures are often boring he seems genuinely passionate about the subject and attempts to bring enthusiasm to class, if econ is your dig I'd say go for it 100% (oh also the class was easy)

Super easy class, have barely paid attention aside from a little studying before the exams and am currently sitting with a B+. Brent is a genuine good guy and you wont have any problems passing this class.

It is week 12 in the semester right now, and we still don't have a letter grade. He barely uses Canvas for grading, and it takes a while to get your grade. I feel like I haven't learned anything in this class, and I find it very hard to pay attention to lectures. The homework questions don't make any sense. I would not recommend this teacher.
What a chill dude. The class isnt too hard. As long as you do a decent amount or the reading and show up to lectures you should get along fine. Warning though, his voice miiiiight put you to sleep.
He's known to be the best economics teacher in the department. Take his class if you can.
Knows his stuff. Lecturers at a high level that includes material from his graduate class, but exams are scaled down and fair. You'll be fine if you pay attention in class.

Kreider is an amazing professor. He sees it as his mission to teach everything about econ but also about current events and gives tips about life in general, like how to invest. That can get distracting when trying to figure out what's going to be graded, bit its still worth it. Its not hard to do well if you go to class and pay attention.

Kreider is the best teacher I've ever had. He goes over every topic starting with the general concept, why we should care, and then boils it down to real life examples. What I liked best is that his examples came from current events news of the day instead of just relying on old textbook examples. Made the graphs and equations easy to follow.

Tests are hard because there is no study guide for them. It's hard to determine what content will be on the tests. Some tests might be all from Top Hat questions and others might be all from the lectures. Homework is difficult and time consuming as well. I didn't know what my grade was until the end because he has a a weird grading scale.

His tests are basically TopHat questions and examples from lecture. Has a weird grading scale where you don't know you're grade till the end. Has very funny examples and applicable to life. Cares about his students. Tests are tricky and very hard to study for since he doesn't have a study guide.
Great prof and very down to earth. Dr. Kreider is passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about his students. He uses lots of every day life examples in his lectures and is very approachable.

You mostly have to learn on your own and you dont really know where you are for grades because he uses TopHat.  Tests are tough as he goes off on tangents and doesnt do study guides.  When he tells you what will be on the test then those things arent.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Brent is a great prof if ya go to most classes the tests will be easy. He often makes jokes in class they definitely fall in the dad joke category but I still think theyre funny. His class is mostly graded by tests but they are pretty easy I didnt study more than an hour for them. The other grades is top hat both in class and out, its curved

If you take to take Econ 101, try to take it with Dr. Kreider. Sure he is rather nerdy and tells some jokes few will find funny, but his lectures are entertaining because he uses lots of examples and stories. He goes on tangents at times, but there is usually a concept behind it. He does care about his students.

A living legend. This guy is like Patton Oswalt, but even better. You ever seen Patton Oswalt? Of course you have. Just like, go to class enough and study for quizzes and tests and you'll be fine. You'll get there.

Good prof. He gives lots of examples and makes complicated problems easy to understand. Half of the exam questions come from top hat questions in class but the other half seem more random. You should be fine if you come to class and do the assignments.

Kreider is an amazing professor. You can tell he really cares about all his students and wants us to succeed in life. He teaches the chapters in a way that emphasizes how the logic from class can used in other parts of our lives, like making good financial decisions. He does go off on some tangents, but there's usually a good point behind them.

Personally, economics is not my thing, so I struggled a lot in this class. Given that, Kreider did an okay job. He tangents a lot, so expect to learn most of the material on your own (because it won't get covered in class). There isn't a crazy amount of work, and if you do really well on the final exam, you should get a good grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff and does a great job translating difficult concepts into examples we can understand. My friends and I wish he was teaching every econ class.
Hands down the best professor I've had so far in two years at ISU. Knows his stuff and how to teach. Take him if you can.

One of my favorite professors at this university. He uses lots of real world examples that help make complicated concepts easy to understand. I'm not an econ person and I liked how he tied econ together with other fields like psychology and physics to show the bigger picture. Sometimes used calculus but didn't make us know it for the exams.

Amazing professor who makes you think differently about everyday life. The most interesting parts were about game theory and price discrimination. I liked that he changed up the lecture topics depending on current events, like when predicted what would happen with Iowa soybeans farmers when tariffs were added on steel and aluminum.

His lectures dont make any sense and uses too many examples that dont make sense. The grading criteria wasnt clear so no one knew what grade they had in the class the whole semester. He curves a lot. He does TopHat. You wont gain a lot from the lectures but he does give some examples that will be on the tests.

Brent was an amazing professor one of my favorite professor's I've had here at Iowa State. I took Econ 101 as an elective and coming into the class knew very little than the basic principles. Brent always came to class well prepared and in a good mood he has a unique lecture style and can be hilarious with his stories he ties to the material.
Brent Kreider is an impostor. So many people adore him but I don't get it.

Dr. Kreider really cares about the success of his students. He is more than willing to help the students understand the content and if you like nerdy jokes, youll like him. If you have to take Economics at ISU, take it with him.

Brent cares about econ a lot and will shamelessly try to convert you to an econ major. He loves econ so much he can get a little off the chapter topic, which can be interesting at times and off-putting at others. Overall good econ professor.
Puts me to sleep but is generally good at teaching the content.
Good guy, easy to have a personal connection with if you display interest

Gets off topic a lot in lectures and strays from the real point of the lecture. HOWEVER, he does genuinely enjoy teaching students about Micro Economics. For those who struggle understanding the basic concepts of ME, he does an incredible job of dumbing it down. He absolutely gives you the opportunity to thrive in that class, take it seriously!

Hands down the best professor I've had in my two years at ISU.  He wants you to succeed and helps you prepare for the real world after college.  It's hard to go wrong taking this class if you put the time in.

Pretty good professor. Lectures can be boring at times but Econ isn't my favorite. The class isn't too hard as long as you do the readings. There's weekly online homework assignments and 4 exams including the final, he drops your 2 lowest homework and lowest exam score

He's a good lecturer the topic is just very boring. He often times asks for students to come in to get help, and posts resources to help students; so don't be afraid to approach him. He also uses a lot of egg and cheese examples if you enjoy that at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor.  The class is pretty laid back and he gives good lectures.  He gives a lot of practical examples and has a lot of interesting examples of unintended consequences of government policies.  The tests can be difficult, but he telegraphs a lot of questions he's going to ask so just go to class if you want a good grade.

The lectures are confusing and I found myself falling asleep. He has a hard time staying on topic all of the time, but if you're dedicated and read the chapter - you'll be fine. Tests are mostly multiple choice & some short answer. There is some online homework. No powerpoints; he gives fill in the blank notes on blackboard.  SI helps a lot.
He's pretty hard, but Economics can be tough in general. His lectures are pretty clear, but he says "Um" a lot.

His classes isn't hard at all if you show up to classes and read the book. Then again you could probably do just as well without going to class. He is an interesting guy but the topic that he teaches put me to sleep; I had to get coffee every time before hand to stay awake.

Great Professor, he's the reason I'm considering double majoring now (to include Economics).  Economics is not the easiest class, so a lot of people struggle, but if you're willing to work, you'll get a good grade.
Very confusing to understand during class, class often gets really boring, homework and tests get really confusing and difficult.

Kreider realizes that not all students will learn econ at the same pace or in the same learning style. He makes it a point to use real life stories to back up his main lecture points.  He also really cares about his students and seeing them succeed.  He also offers extra credit and adjusts the grades with a small curve.

Kreider made me love econ. His lectures sometimes  go off on an unimportant tangent, but uses class discussions for test questions so pay attention. I attended all SI sessions and read the book and it was such an easy A. He is a great guy.
He's good.

Great professor, great class.  Every lecture I come out thinking about the world differently.  He gives you all the information you need to do well on the tests but uses a grading distribution that seems harsher than necessary for a 101 class.  Its easy to pass but hard to improve your gpa.  He is very helpful if you ask questions.

Professor Kreider is a more difficult instructor; however, if you go to class you will be in pretty good shape.   Classroom discussions often come up as questions in testing material, so going to class is critical.  He will work with you if you need help, he's got some good jokes too.  All in all, I would recommend him as a professor.

I recommend Dr. Kreider for an easy A. I read every chapter, and rarely paid much attention in class. Tests were not bad, but definitely take advantage of the extra credit. Weird sense of humor, but did crack some good jokes. Take Econ 101 with him for an easy grade.
If you study the book and pay attention in lecture, the exams are really easy. Even if you do poorly on the exams, he has an extremely flexible grading scale and plenty of extra credit.

The class can be very hard to follow if you aren't interested in the material (and because of his tone of voice). Kreider tries his best to make lecture somewhat fun, and the class isn't necessarily that difficult.
I can hardly understand what he's talking about in lectures

He's a nice guy, Econ is just a boring subject in my opinion. His lectures are a bit confusing, he jumps around a lot some days but other days the lecture super clear. Has 2 in class extra credit assignments, multiple aplia ones and a extra credit paper.

I dropped after failing my second test.  He tries to be helpful but not all of us get econ.  if you dont get the first few chapters its to late to catch up.  peeple either get it or they dont, alot end up dropping or getting stuck bringing down there gpa. The average grade on the curve is a c+ but easy for some and impossible for some of us

Class was very easy. Honestly, i hardly went and got A's on all the tests. He drops your lowest test score out of three. Lectures are extremely boring because you will focus on the same graph for the whole time, but he does make sure people understand.

Class act, always prepared and makes it a mission to get every student to learn the basics of econ.  The prof is a natural at relating real life to the concepts and gives good practical advice about a lot of things like how to buy a house or choose whether to buy an extended warranty.

Great teacher. Holds you accountable for yourself. No clicker attendance or otherwise. Just show up and he gives you everything you need to know. Very knowledgeable. He has his own sense of humor that lightens the mood and keeps you entertained. I would recommend him to anyone.

Great Teacher. He makes a usually boring topic very interesting, his lecture style is great for learning the material. Good examples, funny, and fill-in the blank notes are very helpful. Highly recommended!!

I think this has to be the best professor at Iowa State. It's amazing to see his passion for economics and his passion for helping students succeed. To get an A on the tests, its so simple. Go to class, skim the notes and you can even skim the book for extra clarity but not necessary. Great man I promise you will enjoy!
Great teacher.  He really knows what he is talking about.  As long as you pay attention in class and do the homework, you should be fine.

Fantastic analogies.  Easily one of the funniest professors I've ever had.  Loves to be called "Brent".  I would love to hang out with him some time just to hear the stories he has to share.  Overall great guy, great father, and great professor.

Seems like an easy-going laid back guy. Has notes online that you just print off and then fill in a couple blanks as he lectures. The lectures can get boring at times, but if you go to lectures and fill out the notes you won't have to read. You'll still have to buy a textbook for the online homework.
I really enjoy how he teaches. He is really helpful and straight forward with exams. Makes economics bearable

He's pretty decent, overall if you go to class and do the homework you will do ok.  He publishes his notes online and all you have to do is fill in the blank.   Does go off on tangents from time to time. But overall if you attend class you will be ok

Kreider is an excellent professor who does everything he can to make sure students get their money's worth taking his class. He packs in a lot of detail and often goes off on tangents, but he reviews his main points very clearly. As others have pointed out, he's stingy with giving A's but makes it easy to at least pass if you pay attention.
Great proffessor. He is interesting to listen to in lecture, and if you go to lecture you will have an easy a.

Nice guy who knows how to teach, and he'll always go the extra mile to help you understand the lecture.  Its an easy class to pass, but good luck trying to get an A unless you're an engineering student. Don't let him catch you on your phone if you dont want to get called out for five minutes in front of 200 students.

I have had experience with Econ before but was still nervous walking in. Brent is super helpful and explains things very clearly. He even tells his students not to worry before they take an exam. Great guy and super approachable. TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU CAN, much easier and more enjoyable than other sections of the same class.

Kreider is an okay professor. He talks a lot, and can get off topic in class. This made it sort of hard to determine what information was actually important out of his lectures. However, he gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and curves the test a lot. Much easier than other econ101 prof's that I have heard of. Clear on expectations.

Kreider uses a fill in the note packets to over in class. Best to read the suggested readings before class. He can go very fast over the material and expects students to know basic ideas. Lectures are boring except when he goes off topic which was not uncommon. Overall, willing to help students that go in for office hours.

Best professor I've had at ISU. He covers material very clearly and can make you change how you think about some things.  Talks alot about unintended consequences of policies.  It helps to go to class to do well on the tests because he often talks about things that arent in the book.

He is easy to understand and follow. He uses real-world examples in his lectures to help give students a better understanding of what he talks about. He also like to include a little bit of humor in his lectures which is always nice. He is by far my favorite professor

Excellent professor who covers material carefully and is always willing to help students after class or in office hours.  He sometimes talks too much over most students heads but he enjoys what he's teaching.  I liked how he brings in material from current events like health reform and can relate it to intro students.

Its a ridiculous grading scale for a 101 class thats supposed to be an introducory class.  It might be easy for people that already had  econ or or engineering but most of the class gets a C or below and lots of people drop so they dont fail. If your not good at econ it will ruin your freshman GPA

It seriously has to be impossible to fail his class, I slacked all semester and passed with an A. Granted, I had a lot of background knowledge in Economics, but the point is clear. He's definitely a prof you want for a class like this.

He gives lots of extra credit opportunities but don?t be fooled into thinking it makes it easy to get an A.  Its only worth a bump of a half grade if you end up on the bubble between grades.  His class page posts his final grades from previous years 15% A, 32% B, 27% C, 15% D, 10% F and you have to do well on exams to get an A or B
By far my favorite professor. Very helpful and wants all of his students to succeed. I've never received so much extra credit in one class in my entire life...
A little boring, but goes over material very well. As long as you read the book or attend class regularly, you'll do just fine. Plus he offers tons of extra credit.

This class sucked. You can study from his book to pass his tests. Also you dont need to purchase the testbook if you are enrolled in the Aplia for his section.His lectures were pointless and I only attended class when there was a test. His lectures did not help me with my aplia assignments at all either. I hated this class.
Great professor.  really cares about the students and wants us to succeed.  Uses lots of real life examples in class.  I wish he was teaching 102.

Very boring and hard to stay awake in class. Explains every little thing, and goes off topic frequently. Very nice and easy to communicate with, just dull. Maybe due to first time in such a big class?
He was a good teacher but his lectures were very boring.  Many kids were asleep and sometimes it was hard to grasp the concepts.
Outstanding prof. He presents both sides of the issues and if anything is too patient.
Impatient with any student who questions his voodoonomics assumptions. If you are going to teach half truths, you need to be prepared to defend them. He won't miss me.
Impatient with any student who questions his voodoonomics assumptions. If you are going to teach half truths, you need to be prepared to defend them. He won't miss me.
I was expecting this class to be dull, but it was interesting and I still use what I learned more than a year later. He makes class interesting.

He is a pretty good teacher that uses a lot of examples when trying to explain things about economics.  I generally had a good semester with him and would recommend him for an Econ professor.  His class was pretty easy.

Every lecture he has there is atleast 20 people sleeping. I have gone to every single lecture this year and the only thing I got from them is a few questions on the tests, what to study for on the tests, and updates on the homework. He is a boring speaker and too knowledgeable to teach a basic econ class.
funny to listen to, brings up current events into his lecture.
He is mildly funny and keeps things simple. Uses alot of examples and is easy to understand. Get this professor he is an O.G.
Best Prof ever !! take this class with him !!
Best professor at ISU.

I loved this class. Prof really cares about making sure we succeed.  If you go to his office hours or email him questions, he'll take the time to explain everything in perfect detail. Lectures stray from the book a lot but are great for getting into real world examples and seeing the big picture.

The prof was a relatively cool guy, he just got distracted a bit but was mostly down to earth about things.  He helped make the rather boring class more entertaining, but the class was still rather rough as far as material.  Would recommend.

Prof is very smart and down-to-earth, a rare combination. Is always prepared and can be pretty funny when he wants to be.  Very approachable, and you can tell he cares a lot about teaching.  Lectures are incredible some days, though can also be pretty mundane depending on the topic.  Gives mostly B?s and C?s with not that many A?s or F?s.
He's a bit of a fruit loop. Occasionally has difficulty completing thoughts. Easy homework. Boring class.

Great Professor, great class.  Highly recommended if you want to actually learn how to think economically about the world and not just memorize facts.  Tries hard to relate to all students and is very helpful in office hours.

Kreider definitely enjoys what he's teaching.  he wants his students to succeed in this course, and offers both extra credit in and out of class and will weight midterms/finals to each student's advantage.  Overall a really nice guy  who knows his stuff.  Also, he's very much aware student often take his course for non-major undergraduate credit.

Excellent prof, seems dedicated to making sure his students learn the material and succeed in the class.  Very clear examples, seamlessly ties topics together from different chapters and lectures.  Highly recommend class.

Kreider is very monatone and hard to follow. I did well in other economic courses but this course was next to impossible. He runs off topic frequently, jumps from subject to subject, many T.A.s don't speak very good english, has a T.A. run all grades and is clueless onn grades when you ask for help, never returns e-mails.

Probably the easiest econ 101 professor, easy A. Offers extra credit and his tests are straightforward,and easy. His lecture are boring, I fall asleep evertday, but the textbook is really easy to understand
Great Professor.. his lectures may get boring at times but he tries to make sure everyone understands and keep a dryer class somewhat interesting.
Lectures are impossible to stay awake for. I take naps before class and drink coffee and i still doze. It's easier to skip and read the chapter and do the online examples.
I find his lectures useless - I simply cannot stay awake in his class, it is so boring. I basically learned on my own through the book and homework.

Brent Kreider is one of the most uninteresting professors I've ever had. He has no personality, and doesn't really explain the material well. Basically I learned on my own through reading the book word for word. HEED MY WORDS-DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS, HE'LL BORE YOU TO DEATH!!

One of the best classes I've taken at ISU. Prof is amazing at relating concepts with examples and analogies from the real world. You don't have to do that much to get a decent grade, but he's stingy with the As. Comprehensive final exam. No pop quizes, but uses lots of examples from lectures to weed out people that don't show up for class.
Great Professor.  added economics as a second major because of Prof. Kreider and this class.

Kreider is a great economics professor! He's very good at relating the material to real life situations. I would definitely take another course with him if he taught mid level econ even though I'm a Finance major
Good Professor.

Very easy professor, especially when compared to other professors for econ 101.  We used aplia, an online homework thing you have to pay for, a lot.  That and the tests made up the grade.  He's pretty lenient on grading, too.  Lectures tend to be kinda dull, with him often getting stuck on a single story or point.
Outstanding Professor. Real nice guy. I Learned a lot in his class, and I highly recommend him.
Krieder is a great teacher! His lectures can be boring at times but he does his best to relate to students. His tests are not overly difficult if you attend lecture and keep up in the book.
He is a very good teacher.  I learned a lot in this class.

Excellent teacher. Funny and makes things easy to learn. Could not have had a better teacher for Econ101. He uses Aplia which can be tough but it helps you to learn and I like online homework. He offers some extra credit which is really nice and pretty easy (get extra points for going to class certain days). A++ Definitely take with him if you can.

The class was pretty easy and all but your doing it basically on your own. his lectures are useless. He will ramble on about one point for the whole hour. The aplia is useful and the tests are all multiple choice and he will drop one.
Kreider is very practical in his teaching.  The online problem sets help a lot too.  Tests are all multiple choice and aren't too difficult.

Very good prof. Taught material several different ways, good examples. Before class I did not care about economics, but am now considering taking further econ classes. Funny guy, very personable. If Econ 101 or 102 is a requirement, take 101 with Krieder, he's amazing.

Pretty cool guy. Easy class. He provides his lecture notes with some blanks in them and you fill them in when you go to the lectures. Tests are not to bad, sometimes worded weird. Overall, pretty easy.

I hated Econ but loved this professor. He made class interesting & was very helpful. There are lots of tests, so its easy to pass. Aplia is difficul toward the end but use your notes from class. He offers alot of extra credit.

He is a fairly good professor.  He jokes around in class a little, and tends to get off track sometimes.  Puts copies of the class notes online with a few blanks missing to make you go to class or you can get them from someone else.  Tests aren't too bad, but there are a lot of them.  The questions can be a little confusing, so read them carefully.
Good guy, keeps things clear. Aplia practice and assignments aren't always congruent, but that's not his fault. Study harder for the second exam.

This man is the Bruce Campbell of economics professors. He is the reason I am an econ-major, and much of what I learned from him has carried me in higher-level courses. He has an incredible way to break down tricky concepts with parables and makes the math so simple it almost dances. If you need Econ 101 and have a chance to take Kreider, do it.
THE MAN, THE MYTH, THE LEGEND.  Great way of conveying complex economics into common everyday examples.
Brent is the man.  No final very easy class.  Awesome teacher, best at ISU.
His class is not hard at all. Go to class look over the notes and do the aplia.
Great Guy. Great teacher. Makes Econ understandable, and simple.
this guy makes econ understandable if you've never experienced econ before, his tests are great too
very down to earth and understands our wants and needs, willing to make things easier to help convey the material. oh yeah, no final!

I don't know where these previous ratings are coming from. Maybe Dr. Kreider and my learning methods are different, but do to the fact that I can't understand anything he's talking about in lecture, I've spent this whole semester teaching myself from the book and the online sets.
No Comments
He's a pretty good teacher on some days, on other days you want to fall asleep. Try to do well on his problem sets, they help you understand concepts for the tests.

Extremely good professor. He knows his stuff very well, and craks good jokes. He goes over the material so that everyone understands what is being covered. I was not that excited about econ before this class, but i have taken more econ classes after this one.
He is an extremely nice guy and I went to three different econ classes just so I could find the best professor!  He beat them all!  I definately recommend him!
His lectures were really boring.  I fell asleep in class almost everyday.  But the class itself wasn't very hard.  Probably could've studied more.
Good teacher overall. HW is not really related to lectures, but a decent class because tests are decent
Quite a few questions on the tests are directly from lectures.  Overall a decent teacher but I didn't learn anything I didn't already know and still did bad in the class.

He did not give information or examples in class that were relevant to the homework or the tests. I spent more time just trying to figure out the homework that what should have been necessary. His lectures are extremely boring.
Good!!!
Amazing teacher, knows his information. Hard to stay awake in his class, but still can get and A or B

Very good teacher. knows his stuff and goes over the material several times. Is very reasonable when it comes to homework and tests. also a rather funny guy, he makes jokes that are actually funny, unlike alot of other professors.

I thought Econ would be hard for me, but Kreider is awesome at teaching! He goes over stuff slowly enough for everyone to understand and you can tell he wants all his students to succeed. His tests/assignments are very reasonable. I recommend Kreider!!
Very helpful teacher.He's a badass.teachers the basics of microeconomics very well.good examples.tests and hw are very fair.
Great instructor.. repeated information so that the entire class was sure to understand. Well educated. I have already recommended him to several other students. Office hours are helpful.
This professor is Great.  He is the best teacher for Economics.  I highly recommend this teacher if you ever decide to take Econ 101.
Very good teacher.  Has good examples in class and the course is very laid back.  The tests and homework are all very reasonable.
Way too smart to be teaching this class. Went over some people's heads.
Great professor and course! If you want to learn about real estate, she will provide you with the real information. The work is challenging but helpful and lasting!

100 points of HW. 80% exams. Awful lectures that were overly difficult to understand. Really not sure why this professor is teaching finance, nor an online class. She is not online savvy whatsoever, and seems to pride herself on not communicating with students throughout the semester. Grading scale not clear and was devoid of minuses. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nappi is not a bad professor, but she does little to show care for her students. She does not interact at all on canvas, her lectures are very fast paced, and as a student, you will have to learn how to study on your own for her exams in particular. Overall, she is a somewhat difficult professor, but could do better for students.

Difficult to understand during lectures, moves through notes way too fast, and is unreasonable with students level of comprehension. Had a very poor conversation regarding a makeup exam. Was inconsiderate and disrespectful during in-person conversation despite my attempt to be professional and respectful. Short and rude to students that struggled.

Worst finance professor at Iowa State. She got her masters in English literature and B.A. in business administration and clearly knows nothing about finance. She doesn't post anything to Canvas, never interacts with students during lectures. My recommendation is never to take a class with this professor.

This is a very independent class if you take it online. If you watch lectures and take notes, you'll be fine. Beware of test dates; she doesnt post reminders. Accessible and answers emails in a reasonable time. She is open to help with homework during her office hours. Overall, I had a good experience with this class and found it interesting.

Arguably the worst professor I've had ever since I came to Iowa State two years ago. Exams are 80% of your grade. She will have review sessions days before the exam, but the material she covers isn't on the exam. She will put terms on the exam that you haven't learned or talked about at all. If I could give her a 0 instead of a 1, I would.

Nappi wants her students to succeed. She curves most tests. My only complaint is that I wish we had more time to work on problems in class. Project guidelines are hard to understand. It's also hard to know what will be on the test, so its best to know everything learned from lecture and use the textbook to supplement.

This class with Nappi is very math focused, but do-able. Attendance isn't taken but it is highly encouraged to go to class, if you want to do good. There's grade in-class assignments (you can take home too) and will help your grade from exams. She is an extremely helpful and sweet professor that likes to see her students succeed. I would recommend

Exams are weighted 70%, so if you don't test well, you basically fail the class. She is VERY unclear with directions, so the group project worth 10% of your grade is very hard to complete. She makes it very hard to want to come to class. Bad professor. Don't take this class with this professor

She's nice but this class was awful. 80% of your grade was from exams. The lectures didn't make sense. She didn't respond to emails. No extra credit. Said she would curve and didn't. You couldn't see your grade the entire semester until the final grades were released at the end of the semester. Do yourself a favor and take it with someone else.

Very nice, but if you don't know much about Finance, I would advise you to choose a different professor. Very lecture-heavy. Doesn't wait for people to ask questions. Grinds through lecture, leave a little early and repeat that for a semester. Day in and day out. Does her job, and you can understand her decently well. STUDY

In all honesty, the professor is nice. However, the beginning of the semester starts with futures and options ( hardest concepts). Uses the white board and is allergic to expo markers. I don't know if anyone has made suggestions to utilize the projector? I ended up taking the same class with a different professor and saw a completely new grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she starts writing on the whiteboard and doesn't look back until the end of class. There is different information given across lectures, PowerPoints, and the book chapter so often there is 3 totally different definitions of something, so you don't know what to use.
All lecture based, pretty boring. Grades hard on assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have taken. She clearly, does not care for her students. Be ready to do most things outside the class hour. If you are not a master in finance do not take the class with her.

Nappi is a really good professor. Finance as a subject is hard, hence the 4-rating on difficulty, but she teaches it pretty well, however, if you don't understand the material, she is more than happy to explain it to you further. She's truly a caring professor and is willing to work with you if you show her that you're putting in the effort.

Class has very little structure or guidance. It's very hard to take notes because she just spills info on the board. The powerpoints on canvas only partially cover what she wants you to know. The only way you'll get a decent grade in this class is if you ask A TON of questions. That's the only way you'll get any good info out of her.

I do not understand why everyone is saying that she is a good professor. She does NOT reply to emails and does not care how you are doing in the class. She definitely plays favorites as well. Class is not mandatory, but there are random in class assignments that are a LOT of points. If you miss one, you grade will plummet and you cannot get it up.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her class has absolutely no structure. We only meet in Webex 6 times throughout the semester, the rest are recorded lectures. There is no course material schedule that best paces you for the exam. The prerecorded lectures start off well but gradually become rushed and full of errors. No in-person office hours. If you can, find another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've had Nappi for both 310 and 320. Her tests are really hard but if you study a lot and review all of the worksheets prior to the test it's not too bad. There is always a group project instead of a final which can be nice. She can be a bit tough but she really cares.

She's quick to judge you before you can even talk to her. She thought I was cheating and was quick to jump to the conclusion that I was before I could even defend myself. I then tried to defend myself but she already made up her mind that I cheated. I've lost all respect for her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you go every time, can keep up your notes with how fast she talks, and have a passion for finance you'll be fine, even though the class is a little hard. There is a big project at the end so either take the class with friends or chose a group that is smart or you'll get stuck with all the work/receive a poor grade on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was a great professor but the course was not easy. Took it in the summer so she had exams worth 85% of the grade. Overall liked the course but after taking the class didn't think she was great until the curve at the end. Curve was enough to take a class with her.

I took this class in the Summer, but she was really helpful with understanding the content in a short period of time. Lectures and Chapter Assignments were all in one day, so it is a lot of material. Since it was condensed down the Chapter questions on the Tests on Friday were not very intense. Nappi over all was pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Buy the book only to work through problems before the exams. Revisit all problems completed in class before taking the exams and use your notecard wisely! She's a really great teacher for 320, and I would definitely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nappinnai does one or two problem sets for each chapter, use the problems from in class to study for the exam and your notes/any slides on blackboard to study for the multiple choice section. Instructions for the group project are not well organized, make sure to read it all carefully and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nappi is a great professor and will help you out. If you are in class and show that you're trying she'll understand your struggles and try to help you. Genuinely cares about her students and is very kind. Take her if you're able to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nappi is my favourite professor in ISU. I took FIN310, FIN320, FIN371 with her. Attendance is mandatory, but her lecture helps a lot as she teach you the calculation step by step. See her if you have any confusion, she is patience and helpful. Definitely take her class again. I wish she teach 400 level class too. She has generous curve as well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Nappi was a very engaging professor. There is no textbook for this class, just a case study book, so class attendance is the key to success. Nappi would supplement lectures with PowerPoint slides. Most lectures consisted of writing terminology and example problems on the white board. Each lecture concept was supplemented with group worksheets.
