You have to go to class to pass this class not because the lectures will magically give you insight, but because she gives random 'in class assignments' that are worth a lot of points and you can't make up. The lectures are really dry and not very informative. You will definitely need to teach yourself everything by reading the book.
the ppt slides are useless, read the textbook

I have taken every class I could with Nappi. She doesn't teach a walk through class, but she is always there to help you. I was struggling in a few of her classes until I went and talked to her (thats all it takes). She allowed me to have extra time on her exams because I wanted to learn. SHE IS GREAT!!!!!!!!

Nappi, as she likes to be called, is a very clear teacher if you pay attention. Her accent is not very thick, but it is there. She pretty much tests out of the book, and gives lectures accordingly. I've had her for three classes, and she is extremely helpful when you ask for it. Put in some effort and you'll get a good grade.
Nappi is great! She is passionate about finance, very knowledgable, and willing to help.  One of my favorite professors at ISU.

Great professor! Really cares about her students, knows a lot about finance, and willing to help with whatever you need. She is challenging and at the same time clear. She is one my favorite professors I've had at this school!

Good teacher. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you don't go to class you won't pass the tests. The text book is also helpful at times. She is very clear. She grades on a curve as well. She will give you extra points on tests to raise the average. Also curves at the end. Average grade was about 75%

She is a very nice person and knows a lot about Real Estate. But it seems her tests reflect the notes but make sure you are prepared beyond that. Tests are hard so make sure you are prepared. Go to class and make sure you get all the in-class assignments. Will greatly buffer your grade.

Attending class is not mandatory and she gives reviews on what are on the test so as long as you study that you will at least pass.  She teaches a subject for a couple of days and then devotes an entire day to working out problems to help you better understand how to apply what you learned.  She grades on a curve at the end of the class.

It is amazing how much she knows about this subject! I have learnt so much from this class. She is a great teacher. Her tests are challenging and make you think. But, she prepares you well for them. She teahes a variety of courses. If you ever have an opportunity to take a class from her,you really should. You would be happy you did. I am.

One of the best Finance teachers I have ever had. I took three of her classes. She is very knowledable, teaches very clearly and  cares very much for her students. I not only learned a lot from her classes,but also enjoyed them immensely.
This class is extremely easy.  Don't buy the test book, but do come to class b/c she has in class assignments that are unannounced.  If you do this you will get an A.
This class is extremely easy.  Don't buy the test book, but do come to class b/c she has in class assignments that are unannounced.
No one can understand what she write on the board
Never take this class, she is the worst professor I have had in ISU
never take clearly notes

there are 2 choice at beginning semester, listen to class or take notes, because her notes is very very unclearly. after half semester, people give up to take notes, and i don't understand what she said
Very good teacher, go to class and complete in class assignments and you should do fine. I would suggest reading the book and doing the questions at the end of the chapter to help study for exams.
If it wasn't in the notes it wasn't on the test but it was easy if you showed up to class and received the points there plus a heavy curve place on it
I enjoyed her in class assignments a lot. 3 hour classes are a bit much. But, she did  a good job of keeping us focused. Good teacher. She seemed to really care for her students.
I enjoyed her in class assignments a lot. 3 hour classes are a bit much. But, she did  a good job of keeping us focused. Good teacher. She seemed to really care for her students.
Good lectures. She gave challenging exams, but her lectures were very relevant to her exams. Very helpful. Good class. I learned a lot
Brutal. Hard to understand in lecture, her notes aren't very clear.
No Comments
She confused us with material taught and what she tested over.  She is willing to compromise. good curve

Dr. Nguyen may come off as a bit aloof at first, but she's quite nice in fact. The second half of this course in particular is quite difficult, but Dr. Nguyen's generous curve and opportunity for bonus points make it doable with hard work. Contrary to what another wrote, she has an accent, but it's light, and her knowledge of English is excellent.

Was horrible for the online Math 1660 class. Was very unhelpful in emails and did not put any effort into the class. The canvas page was set up poorly and the class was very test heavy. They also decided to change the grading scale halfway through the semester because over 80% of the class was failing. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!
Avoid her, take any other professor if possible. A good human but awful grader doesn't even curve. I got my first C because of her.

She is not a good grader, when she teaches it seems like you understood but even if you make a small mistake she won't give you full or partial credit. I would suggest taking some other professor instead of her for Proofs class.
She has a way of just making things make sense. Shes a great drawer

Dr. Nguyen gave clear, well-prepared lectures (if you're wondering, she doesn't have an accent). The exams were brutally hard so doing well on homework and the frequent, but easy quizzes was critical. She cares about teaching & likes to try new methods over the semester. Dr. Nguyen isn't one of ISU's best professors, but she's a solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She makes her first test really hard to see who drops, which in my class was about 1/4 people. Overall she's probably an above average calc teacher. Next two tests were fair but you gotta really study if you want to do well. No departmental tests so you wont get railed by a question you couldn't prepare for.

As far as calculus professors at Iowa State go, she's definitely above average. As far as professors in general go, she's mediocre. I found it incredibly difficult to pay attention in lecture and her homework assignments ranged from fairly short to excruciatingly long. Tests are long and you only get an hour so make sure you practice for speed.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class is what you make it. Show up every day and take notes and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She records attendance for every class. But I really don't know why I need to go to the class, since her lecture is terrible. I can learn more if I study by myself. The exam is difficult, most proportion of the final grade is consists  of the exam score. If you want to pass Cal III, never take her class.

Pretty awful. Her lectures are hard to pay attention to with her monotone voice, yet attendance is part of the grade so you have to go. 80% of your grade is based on the 4 tests (3 midterms and a final) taken, so one bad test and it could drop your grade 15% right there; and they are not super easy tests either. Overall poor professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Explains the material very good but she makes you work for the grade you want. She takes attendance everyday and it goes towards your final grade. But honestly, if you are not showing up for class you shouldn't be taking calc 3.

Statics is a very daunting course, and Miner makes it digestible. He holds weekly office hours, which are great if you take advantage of them. His pre-lecture videos on topics are great if you want to review material, and he goes over meaningful examples in class to prepare you for exams. The exams and the course are hard, but it's to be expected.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Make sure to watch the pre-lecture videos, as they make learning in class much easier. It also helps to attend recitations and attend his office hours. He is really nice and wants to help. If you go to office hours, he is also willing to give you some credit back on exams if you explain yourself and he belives its valid.

Course is easy, instructor made the experience 10x harder. If you ask him question, he will make you 10x more confused, so he has this skill to make things worse. I stopped going to class and watched online videos, then improved in the exams.
Good teacher
Good professor who cares about his students. So far, enjoying having him for statics.

Professor Miner is a phenomenal teacher and makes Statics incredibly digestible, even though the course itself is hard as nails. The exams are graded extremely harshly, but you can typically meet with Miner himself to discuss grading and potentially earn points back.

Nathan was a great professor overall for how hard Statics is. He makes examples in class manageable and doesn't try to make the class a "sunshine and rainbows" experience like other professors. Homework and exams are absurdly hard in this class, but he will give you the resources you need to succeed. Just put in the time, and you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took him last semester. Poor teacher. It's like you asked him, and he asked AI, and he gave you the answer from AI, that kind of experience. He has a lot of small things in class that are not useful for learning. I ended up learning everything myself using Steve Hanson youtube videos and passed. Worst teacher I have had so far.
He is a graduate student who can't teach. Tries to be friendly with students, but has no knowledge of the contents. Exam time is difficult to catch up. Avoid him.
The best professor for Statics, he has very good lectures and is very accessible outside of class for help with the course material. He is a very understanding professor.

Make no mistake, statics is an exceptionally hard class. However, Miner does a fantastic job being accessible outside of class so there are very few days where you can't get a hold of him for help. If you want to pass this class, actually DO all the problems he gives. Don't shortcut or Chegg them, it'll bite you on the exams.

He can't explain well and is very mean to students, although he tries hard to pretend that he cares. Very inexperienced and has no engineering background. Worst part is he thinks he is smart, although it's the opposite. Avoid this teacher.
Not a good professor and hides it by giving extra credit that doesn't count or help with the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor and is always open to discuss the graded exam copies. TAs are tough graders. Be sure to complete extra credit problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Miner uses the flipped classroom to teach a class: outside of class, you watch short 7-10 min lectures, then in class, you answer short top hats about the lectures, and then he goes through a few example problems similar to exams/homework. I loved this method, but its not for everyone. Statics is tough no matter what, but I appreciate his method.

Nathan Miner does not know the material well. He always struggles when explaining the concepts and the examples. When he explains more, it gets more and more confusing. I don't think he is a good instructor at all. I gained more information from the textbook. If you go to his office hours, you will not get helped. Take a different instructor.
Made a very difficult course much easier

Nathan Miner created an amazing learning environment in which ALL questions were created with patience, and understanding. Sometimes, the lecture content would feel too heavy for anyone to digest, but Nathan was always willing to answer questions, work through examples, and check for student's understanding throughout. Overall, 10/10 amazing !!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Statics is hard. Do the HW, extra credit, and platoon meetings. Show up, lectures aren't posted. Try and do the HW yourself and try and understand it; solutions are all over online; use them to verify, not copy. Go to office hours; Miner knows it's hard and wants to help. Have him regrade exams; graders are bad, never didn't get points back.

Nathan has been a great professor. He cares about the content and everyone's understanding and provides lots of practice as well as walkthroughs of problems in lectures. Be sure to check your exam multiple times and bring any questions to his office hours because you will probably get points back as the TAs are bad graders.

Nathan is a professor with great intentions. The average on the first exam was a 45, but Nathan provided multiple extra credit quizzes throughout the semester to help everyone catch back up. Overall, go see Nathan during office hours and be sure to check your exam multiple times. (HORRIBLE GRADERS) Go to platoon meetings!!

I took his class during his first semester teaching this course, and he did a good job. He was clear about the content, and was going slow enough so that you had time to write down the diagrams. He stopped for questions often, and gave a lot of examples and explained the methods. He is also really happy to help anyone who comes to office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent professor, it is an absolute shame she doesn't teach more courses at ISU. She clears literally every professor I can think of in the AERE department.
Very cool love her
Great professor, she is super understanding you just have to communicate with her. Workload is definitely do-able just stay focused and go to class.

Overall a good and enjoyable class. Dr Altukhova seems to genuinely care about her students and is knowledgeable about Matlab. Lots of homework problems but they are manageable. Group projects can be tough depending on who you get but she does a good job with peer weighting to make sure your grade reflects how much effort you put in.

Dr. Altukhova's class is very manageable to get through. Not a heavy workload besides the projects being tedious. Definitely attend every class for tophat, watch the videos before class or learn the material by yourself, and learn a bit of Matlab beforehand. Labs are very easy. Grading takes a while and sometimes expectations aren't always clear.

Hope you enjoy wasting your time in class. Terrible professor. No guidelines for any project. No rubrics for the report that worth half your grade or the subsequent presentation. She overall a very mediocre professor brought down by incredibly stupid grading practices and lectures.

AMAZING professor! She really cares about her students. She is also really nice and helpful when it comes to explaining concepts. There's a top hat question at the beginning of every class, so make sure to watch videos/go through the lecture notes. I'm not the biggest fan of flipped classrooms, but she made it bearable. Definitely recommend!
Just a solid teacher all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A lot of required online lectures that you had to watch/read prior to class. There was a tophat quiz over these lectures every class. 1st half was over programming ( read the lecture notes and do HW), 2nd was numerical methods (work through hw several times). Two big projects. 1st individual programming, 2nd group solidworks. Pretty time heavy.
Great professor in general.

*DISCLAIMER* I took AER E 161 during COVID-19 when all classes were online. Dr. Altukhova teaches all of the material in a clear and concise manner. Her lecture videos were all edited and chopped up to waste as little of the student's time as possible. She was very kind and flexible... when the student did their part. Skim textbook before lecture!

Dr. Altuhkova does a great job explaining things in her lectures. Unfortunately, she is brutal with exams. Anything turned in late whether it be by a minute or longer is not counted. NO EXEPTIONS. I had a error with MATLAB on the one question worth over half the exam points and received no mercy from Dr. Altuhkova. Don't be late.

Dr. Altukhova's lectures were concise and to the point. She transitioned to an online format seamlessly. Even if the material could be somewhat dull, Dr. Altukhova made the content interesting. This was by far my favorite class I've taken so far.
Awesome professor. Doesn't try to trick you on exams like most professors. Is very clear of what will be on the exam. Does a great job of explaining the concepts.

Nataliya is by far the best AER E professor you will ever get. She is well versed in MATLAB and is great at explaining things. I didn't use the MATLAB text book at all because her lecture notes were good enough. She is helpful during office hours as well. Just don't cheat, she has zero tolerance for that. Overall great teacher!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nataliya is good at going through examples in lecture and she does lots of example problems, but her lectures can be a bit on the boring side. That's not really her fault, though; the topics themselves aren't very fun. She can explain topics fairly well though and unlike AerE 160, she actually taught us how to code instead of just telling us to.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She goes very quickly during class, it's fairly difficult to learn much during lecture, but luckily the lecture notes are online
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great!! Lectures are clear, she made learning MATLAB as easy as possible. Lectures are posted online to review later, and her notes are clear and easy to follow. Exams are not easy, but fair. My advice: Do all the homework and projects and don't fall behind with the material and you'll do fine. Also, cheating is not tolerated, so don't even try.
Do anything end everything you have to do with your schedule to be in her Mechanics class.

She is one of my best professor in ISU. She made sure that everyone understand her lectures and very easy going. Take with her and you won't regret it. Grades mostly based on exams, but she gives practice exam, which would be very similar to the actual exam. There is also in-class assignments so you have to go to lectures.

Very good professor. She explains everything very well, so that you understand it. There were very few, if any, things that I had trouble understanding just from lectures. I actually felt like I learned a new skill from this class (MATLAB), which is pretty rare for me.

I struggled BIG time with coding in high school, but Dr. Altukhova made it so easy to understand. She, in my opinion, is one of the best aero professors at Iowa State. If you're ever confused, she's very accessible and actually cares about your success in the class. She also gives opportunities for extra credit, which helped my grade a lot!

Nataliya is the best aero professor by far. Super nice, very helpful, and explains the material very well. Her classes are very organized as well, she posts all her notes on Canvas and everything is clear and easy to follow. Make sure to go to lecture, she makes MATLAB and numerical methods easy to understand!

Nataliya is the best Aerospace teacher I've had thus far. Her lectures are easy to understand, she's very knowledgeable about the subjects, and her lecture notes are even color-coded! She made MATLAB seem easy and fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Altukhova does an excellent job of explaining the content in a comprehensible way.  MATLAB has never seemed so easy!

Dr. Altukhova might be the best professor I have ever had. Crystal clear lectures, typically replies to emails very quickly, easily available outside of class, and offered bits of extra credit throughout. She has the magical ability to explain complex information in simple, easy to understand terms. I cannot recommend her enough!

Honestly one of the best professors in the engineering mechanics department. She actually explains how to do statics problems and does it in a way that people can understand. Be warned, however, tests will make up most of your grade and they can be challenging. But if you can, take statics with her and you will do great.

She is probably the most thorough teacher at Iowa State, of all the professors I have had she is easily the best one by a long shot. Take any course with her you can, because she cares about every single person in her class, is fair, and puts an insane amount of effort into being good at teaching. 10/10 would take again.

Attend Class and take attentive notes, there's your easy A! Nataliya genuinely wants to see you succeed and is very willing to work through examples and problems to help you understand. One of the best professors I have had at Iowa State!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Altukhova is hands down the BEST professor at Iowa State. Her lectures are so clear and easy to understand, and you can tell she really cares about her students and their grades. There's also random in-class assignments. She also mixes up about 10 extra credit assignments in class, so make sure to go everyday. She makes statics very, very easy.

I was lucky to get Nataliya for statics, she is pretty well known for being the best EM professor and for good reason.  Her lectures are very relevant as she goes over example problems.  She usually give examples just like those that will be on the test, too.
Great Professor, value her because no other aero e professor equates to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She knows what she teaches and is a great professor.
Best professor thus far. Really cares for her students and lectures are really comprehensive.

Dr. Altukhova is one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lecture notes are incredibly useful and she color-codes them which makes it very easy to understand what is going on. She made a very difficult class very easy to understand. Would definitely take again and highly recommend her to anyone.

Would strongly recommend Dr. Altukhova. She has great lectures, posts many relevant examples, and posts excellent lecture slides. Make sure you attend lectures because quizzes or extra credit occur nearly every lecture. Made a difficult class quite simple for  students due to her excellent teaching methods and passion for helping us learn.

We have 5-10 minute in-class assignments at the end of each lecture for attendance. She walks you through each step in the coding lectures and has very organized notes which she also uploads online for studying.

Fantastic Aerospace professor. You can understand her 90-95% of the time.. She cracks jokes often and always encourages people to ask questions. She is VERY helpful in her offer and is always nice. If you feel that an exam or project was graded unfairly and you take it to her she will hear your case and maybe give you points back if she agrees
Best professor I ever, helped me in statics although I wasn't in her statics class. Highly recommend her for any class.

She had great PowerPoints and was usually available to help with homework. She is super friendly and keeps her lectures interesting. I would definitely recommend taking this class with her if you can.

I highly recommend taking EM 324 with this instructor. Lectures were filled with examples which made the homework go much smoother. Exams were based off the review problems posted on Blackboard before each test. I strongly recommend doing all of the online homework. If you have any questions, she's very helpful!
Amazing
She is very clear and helpful in her classes and is incredibly nice!
I love her. She is kind, always reply my email even at the midnight. The way she explaining is very clear. I bet you will never regret if you take her class.

She was extremely helpful and willing to help student, she always did a good job of making sure she went over problems after she explained a new concept.Pay attention to her lecture notes and the problems she goes over before a test. Those problems she goes over with you are very similar to one on the exam. (hint hint)

Nataliya did a good job of making this class comprehensible and her class notes are very helpful when studying. She clearly preps well before class and her lecture notes are always posted on blackboard. Her tests cover exactly what is covered in class and there are never any surprises or cheep shots. Overall a great professor.

Lectures are hard to follow and boring. Questions on exams are sometimes grammatically very hard to follow. Exams taken in testing centers. Some things on exams are never discussed, so you have to at least skim the textbook for vocabulary and general concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy but not very helpful for understanding the material. Little to no feedback on homework, so you're mostly teaching yourself. Exams don't match lectures well, so you have to rely heavily on the textbook and outside studying to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is an okay professor. I would recommend sitting near the front for less distraction, and read some of textbook. A lot of things we learned were interesting but I didn't like how most of it was memorizing instead of thinking critically. There is a part near the beginning with confusing math that she doesn't explain well, but you'll get thru it!

Reading the textbook helps a lot. She also lets you have a note sheet for the exams, which are in the testing center. The questions seem a bit random, but they are pretty fair. Overall not the greatest, not bad either.

Dr. Valenzuela is clearly passionate about evolutionary biology, but her lectures and exams have zero correlation. Exam questions are not relevant to what is discussed in class because even she does not know what is on the exam. Attendance is mandatory because of TopHat. I would recommend taking this class with a different professor.

She has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology and she does not know how to simplify concepts for people new to evolutionary biology. You get no feedback from exams. The exams are so hard she gives extra credit after the exam if people do bad enough, instead of making them easier. This class is much more advanced than a general biology course should be.

Dr. Valenzuela really cares about the topics, but she is not helpful with questions when asked. The tests are worth most of the grade, but they are not about topics from lecture. The questions always took forever to figure out what it was actually asking. Reading the textbook is a MUST if you want to do well, but its around 150 pages per exam

This was the hardest class I have taken at ISU and I am a senior in Bio. Dr. Valenzuela is very passionate about the material but is sometimes hard to understand in class and her questions are worded complicatedly on the exams. Reading the book helped some, but certain questions just felt out of left field.

Dr. Valenzuela's evolution class was near impossible. I met with her multiple times and was interrupted whenever I asked a question. The tests were impossible and the class relied heavily on the textbook. Close-together tests (think 1 week apart with multiple chapters per test) with too much material to properly study. Lecture videos were 3 min lon

reviews.comment: Exam content is not very relevant to her "lectures" or homework. No clear instructions doesn't answer questions well, not very helpful in any way. Exams contain few questions worth many points. Read the book, but most exam questions I felt I learned in other classes.

reviews.comment: This class doesn't have a lot going for it, but Prof. Valenzuela is really sweet if you talk to her and she actually does care about your grades. reviews.comment: She's not a bad professor, but is hard to understand at times. She offers extra credit, but don't expect it to be easy or get a lot of points.

reviews.comment: The content is hard to make super interesting, but she gives good examples. Going to office hours helped me a ton and she is super nice and easy to talk to!! It is hard though, really study for the exams because lots of people struggle. No curve

Prof. Valenzuela is a good teacher but the main issue is that she is hard to understand sometimes and then her tests are worded poorly which makes them extremely difficult. There is some extra credit but it is difficult and doesn't correspond very well to class materials.

reviews.comment: She clearly cares about her students and is passionate, but writes difficult exams. Mostly I think the exams are difficult because of the wording.

reviews.comment: Professor Valenzuela is not a bad professor; she is very intelligent. The only thing that was annoying was her grading system. It was based on like 5 tests, and in class tophat questions. I had a hard time with the tophat questions and my grade suffered greatly from this. She does curve the entire grade, which is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Her class has great information. My 2 main problems with her class were that she was very difficult to understand, and her tests seemed very poorly written.

I loved her, I was going to ask he to mary me, but the semester ended, that was a joke. but in all honestly the class was pretty easy and she is really a nice person. hard to understand at times but just follow the quizes in the book and you will be just fine.
hated this class..super boring..hard to understand the prof..tests sucked
it's a pretty boring class, but the notes are online.  she is hard to understand at times, but a good teacher and will help you if asked.
No Comments

Art History II has a very clear structure where the lectures and handouts connect. The only issue I had was with the exams. Exam reviews and handouts had specific artworks and their details, but when it came test time there were multiple images that were only on the lecture slides. Also, do NOT buy the textbook: huge waste of money for little use.

Lectures were very clear and easy to understand; it is clear she is passionate about her class. Note allowances are very generous, making exams easy. There have been a few instances of her being very petty and passive aggressive in the middle of class when students upset her which has really dampened my opinion of an otherwise great professor.

Vianna is a great lecturer! Sure, the exams were difficult, but as long as you put the paintings that are starred on the lecture slides your cheat sheet (which can be typed and printed with pictures allowed!) you'll be okay! This class is MUCH easier than the other Art History class you will most likely take first semester.

While this professor is funny the exams are extremely hard. Biggest advice is to write EVERYTHING from lecture onto ur cheat sheet. No matter how much you study you will need it. She includes every photo from every lecture onto the quiz. Its embarrassing to say this is one of the hardest classes i am in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Vianna is fun and engaging during lectures, and she has interesting assignments to do like museum trips and such. She allows note sheets on exams - which is a lifesaver for tests about history. She does use top-hat so make sure you go to class to get credit as she does it randomly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory but I encourage it. Prof. Newman Dennis is a fantastic lecturer. The subject matter is super interesting, and there isn't much outside work for this class. Textbook readings aren't necessary. Very approachable outside of class.
horrible.

This professor does not even teach her own online class; rather, she posts video lectures taught by someone else. The length of all the video lectures per week is usually between 80-100 minutes (sometimes more). The amount of memorization required is ridiculous (nobody likes the memorize-and-forget method). Would not recommend.

This class material is hard to begin with and with almost no notes on the board, the amount terms and people that you're supposed to memorize is astronomical. When you gain the courage to ask for assistance you're told to review the textbook or the lecture slides that are published on Canvas. (yes, the same slides that don't have notes.) Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's funny and very helpful. Assignments and labs are all great for helping deepen your understanding of course material. All you have to do is go to lecture and pay attention.
Neihart is an amazing professor who always tells funny jokes and stories. His exams can be hard, and the homework can be tough, but his TAs are amazing.

Unaccommodating with rigid policies. Valid excuses for absences were rejected, and homework questions during office hours were refused. The course assumes you are already an expert in the subject. Avoid taking this class if you have a busy semester, as you will not get the support you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: nice guy with funny stories but seems to enjoy intentionally tripping up students and seeing them struggle. you'll need to invest way more time into this class than you should normally have to given the material is super easy and almost always involves basic algebra
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor like the plague, at least for EE 2300. Lectures at unreasonable times, exams cover material never mentioned in lecture. He is never understanding of student circumstances and won't allow late submissions. It's a weedout course, so he'll do everything he can to get you to drop and be miserable. Find another professor
gg to whoever gets this guy next
Honestly hes cool as a person and he has good advice. But hes a horrible professor if your not religious pick one and start praying.

By far, top 3 lecturer in the department. One of the most responsive people to talk to if you go and attend his office hours. His exams are incredibly easy if you actually have spend any time listening or reading on what he is talking about. 7:45 is brutal but besides that, I have found his classes to be a cut above the rest here.

I'm fine with being given hard exams, but at least give us some idea as to what we'll be tested on. Every other course at ISU does this. Reviews in this professor's class are virtually nonexistent. You have no idea what to actually prepare for..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but probably one of the worst professors I've had at Iowa State. The material is not hard, but he intentionally makes the class stressful if you're unable to attend lecture at the worst possible time. Only ones succeeding in this class are rich on campus students with no life outside of school. Openly calls students “dumb” and “weak”
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Huge disconnect between lectures, homework, and what is asked on exams. Class organization is very poor, TA's are rude and unresponsive. Exam times aren't discussed until the last minute. Intentionally made more difficult than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a professor who believes that showing up to lecture is a minimum. If you don't go to lectures or office hours you will likely do poorly. Lecture this semester was at 7:45 AM meaning it was hard to go to class often. Exams did not have practice exams but they were not unfair questions. Tough but fair professor at a gross lecture time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: EE230 is tough and Neihart doesn't hold your hand, but he is NOT unfair. Attendance matters, he won't post announcements on Canvas. I guarantee the 1 star reviews are from students who routinely skipped lecture and refused to take accountability for failing the exams. Don't let the bad reviews scare you, just make sure you understood EE201 well.

Disconnect between lecture slides and homework material. It's the naturally gifted students who can piece it together, or maybe they find other resources that are better or something. Doesn't seem to care about your success either. He does not like giving practice exams. He should have made exam details accessible on Canvas.

He's a great professor.
I audited the class, but he communicates quite effectively and teaches in a fun and engaging way.

Dr. Neihart is very knowledgeable and challenges students to think critically. If you take EE 2300 with him, be prepared to really work hard. Lectures are at 7AM, the TAs are often unresponsive and rude, and homeworks are very long. This class is absolutely a time commitment, so be prepared.

Exams can be challenging, but using office hours and practicing outside of class makes them very manageable. The TAs are flexible and are a great resource for understanding the material. While the homework can be difficult, spreading it out over several days helps a lot. I would recommend this professor to all EE majors for a deeper understanding.

Professor Neihart was always happy to help answer any questions I asked. I found his lectures informative, and if you regularly attend lectures and ensure you understand the concepts covered in the course, his tests and homework are not too difficult. So, if you put a reasonable amount of effort into this course, you should expect a good grade.

As a Junior in EE, Neihart is the best professor I've had in the department up to this point. His lectures are entertaining and he challenges his students to think about "why" something is true instead of memorizing a process. For anyone wanting to truly understand circuits, Neihart is the right professor. 11/10, I wish he taught all my courses.

This course provides limited effective instruction. Exams are difficult unless your cheat sheet covers nearly every problem type. Lectures often drift off-topic, so the textbook becomes the main source of learning. Reading it is essential to succeed.
He is a good professor, he just wants us to understand that there is a difference between what we will be doing in class to what the industry actually does

Neihart knows what he is teaching. He has real world experience, so it's not copy and paste reading from the lecture/textbook. However, if you don't ask for the help, he was not entitled to give the answers. Engineering is hard to study, but if you're looking for free handouts or a perfect grade, he is not the guy. If you want to understand, he is
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's just a lazy professor overall, you can spend hours upon hours reviewing every lecture and all of the homework and still get a bad grade on the exam. He says curves are for bad professors but his exams have failing averages. If you take this course with him get ready to find outside resources to study from, because his are garbage.

This course with Neihart was very challenging, the exams were significantly harder than anything covered in class, his lectures had consistent errors in them, he did not have any clear grading criteria of his exams (some were for partial credit, others were not), he doesn't curve exams if 2 or more students get very high scores on them.

He used to help those during his office hours and I don't mind his lectures, though in order to do the homework you will need outside help. However, instead of learning from criticism, he became angry- calling everyone stupid and worthless to their faces and that they won't pass. Unhelpful, unkind, and some empathy might help student succeed.

Good Professor, the material is very hard, and homework takes a long time. (Start it as soon as possible.) Lectures were some of the best I have had. Studying is huge if you want to pass; many don't. He is very good at answering questions. There are many complaints about the tests; If you study and actually do homework, it is fine.

Dr. Neihart is an amazing teacher, although you definitely need to pay attention in class and do work, but overall his class is fairly easy as long as you have a basic work ethic. I would 100% take his class again, he's amazing!
The homework takes so many hours and you only have about 55 min to do an exam and you have to learn the material all by your self. if you take him GOODLUCK.

He doesn't give you any feedback at all on the exams or homework. There's only one TA that's actually helpful. He doesn't care if you fail this class. If it was a different teacher that actually cared. There would be more people passing this class. The material is not bad whatsoever. It just this guy does not know how to teach or give back feedback

Get ready to study because you are going to have to spend 25 hours a week working on this class if you take it with Neihart. His homeworks are due at 8am on Tuesday. The feedback on the homework and exams are godawful - just "-1, -2, -1" on question. Tells you absolutely nothing you got wrong. Curves Nothing even the avg grade is failing. Awful.

I go to every lecture I can't keep up. I don't understand the few who can. His lectures are bad. He blazes through equations. 
The homework has awful feedback; doesn't even tell you what you did wrong. He refuses to curve exams despite how bad the grade is. He refuses to give out practice exams. Do NOT take EE230 with Neihart. He will tank your GPA
Try to get a different professor who will help and guide you.

I wish he could just be let go like before. He obviously doesn't know how to teach, but rather how to punish. Doesn't help students whatsoever so if you can avoid his class do it at all costs. Exams are the majority of your grade and if you think he would help you know the information you would be dead wrong. Idk how he's allowed to teach

Makes this course more difficult than it needs to be, trys to force students to attent lecture in the worst way possible rather than just doing a top hat attendance and have that as points. But the lectures are basically useless, you get more out of teaching yourself with youtube videos and other freinds who have taken it before.+

Worst professor I have ever seen. If I could give a rating lower I'd give him -1000. He shouldn't have a job. Never seen a more careless professor that likes to see his students fail. Passing this class is miracle work. I hope a board member reads these because he should be taken off of the staff, and his teaching license should be revoked.

Assignments and exams didn't always line up with what we went over in class, which made the whole course feel more stressful than it needed to be. It often felt like we were just left to figure things out on our own without much guidance or examples.
show up youll still not undertsnad anything hes been kickeed off this coursee before i wouldnt doubt itll happen again.

This guy makes EE 230 WAY more difficult than it needs to be on purpose. He seems like a nice person, but as a professor he likes seeing students struggle and stressed. Doesn't announce when exams are until the last minute. TAs are pretentious. 7am lectures. It's a weedout class, so be prepared and try and find a better professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: honestly has to be the worst prof in this department.
The exams are your whole grade in this class he wont curve it if 3 people get 100s and doesn't have a clear grading exams save ur self the time and dont take it with him
no partial credit and bad exams

He was kicked off of this course before and now I understand why. No curve, you can't really prepare well for the exam since you got no review. You spend hours on top of hours studying material that won't be on the exam and then you fail that's the cycle of his class. Don't take him if you care abt ur sanity

As a person Neiharts cool but as a professor nope. Save your self the time and stress and take it with someone else. If you do take it with Neihart be prepared by not knowing anything. He doesn't give any sort of review for exams since he doesn't believe in them at all. The first exam abg was a 50% no curve and second was a 60%. Goodluck

I wouldn't recommend Neihart for EE230. His first exam average was 50% and second exam was 60%. He doesn't post practice exams or do any curves on the exams. He's been removed from teaching this class before and I see why now
Exam average was 50%. He refuses to curve and post practice exams stating “only bad teachers use (curve, practice exams)”. The only redeeming part of this class were the TAs

Taking this course with Neihart is the absolute worst! He doesn't post a single thing about exam dates, and claims that practice exams are a way of resolving bad teaching, but students are doing very poorly in his class. The bold idea that the average is 50% on an exam but  he refuses to curve if anyone gets 100% is astonishing. Don't even bother!
Bad prof EE-2300

Nathan is a good guy and professor, loved the way he did the homework for this class splitting it up over the week I just wish it was posted earlier to allow more time to work on it. Very engaging lectures loves to joke around a lot and would definitely take a class with him again. Good office hours. Doesn't use canvas well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There's a lot of homework, and its very tough. However, this is offset by how amazing Neihart is at lectures. Very easy to understand concepts, very funny, and a very good professor to visit at office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Iowa State. His homework's were long and difficult, but they did help reinforce the material. His lectures were always entertaining and he does a good job at getting you involved in the lecture (and getting him off topic is fun). Very fair tests. I highly recommend office hours and attending lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a fantastic lecturer, does a great job of reinforcing what the material is. He started getting a little too theoretical at the end of the semester (more examples would have helped instead of proofs). His tests are very well done and tests actual knowledge of the subject. Funny guy, but leaves you with a sense that he likes to see you squirm.
EE230 Grading wise not as easy as other professors class that you find in the school but great teaching as with him, you actually learn stuff. Homework is due every week and mostly textbook stuffs.
Comes prepared to class with an amazing set of lecture slides; assigns a lot of homework, projects, lab work but is always available for help. Have learned a lot in his class.
Work hard on homework and labs, pay attention and ask questions. So much knowledge to be learned from neihart.
Awesome professor.  Makes you get involved in lectures. Definitely worth taking his classes.
Good class. Hard but if you stick with it very satisfying. Prof. Neihart is always willing to help out and very available.
Good class, good notes, and always available in office for extra help.
know nothing; randomly grade homework and exam; copy hw and project directly from other university without any citation;Verrrrrrrry poor!

Dr. Neihart was a wonderful professor! Very clear, concise lesson flow--great handwriting. Can be incredibly funny if so inspired, don't be afraid to answer questions in his class. Generous test grading, very fair. Tries to stay in touch with where students are in comprehension.
While the class was challenging Prof. Neihart was very helpful and well organized. Grading was fair and while the homework was challenging, the exams weren't too bad.

Out of touch with students.  Covers only basics of theory in class, but assigns very advanced problems for homework. Homework problems are not from the book. Textbook and lectures often don't explain what's needed to solve homework problems. Gives misleading help on homework.  Posted homework solutions are ambiguous and difficult to follow.

The class was very surface-level, and I had difficulty paying attention. Nesbit was okay, but she did say some questionably ignorant things, especially at the end when getting into multicultural and feminist perspectives. I didn't pay attention to most of the class and still got a decent grade.
this is my 4th time having this teacher. didn't even know who I was after I went to office hours the past 4 semesters and nt very clear on lecture notes and examples
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: class was so hard. the class made no sense and the notes were not clear at all. went to office hours and those didn't help. I had to get a tutor and still got the A but the class is very disorganized and not clear at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor and really cares about her students. The class exams weigh heavily on your grade. You will write many activity papers.

Dr. Nesbit is a very interesting professor, her lectures are very engaging, and she really knows what she is talking about. She asks very in-depth exam questions that can be difficult. Exams and quizzes are online, and two attempts so it's doable, and she gives extra credit. Her grading criteria is sometimes unclear though. Not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I find that Dr.Nesbit is a very caring individual, however, I had a really difficult time with this course. Nesbit tends to go on many tangents in her lectures, so I often had to use the textbook to take notes. The textbook is very dry and difficult to read. If you struggle with paying attention when you read, do not take this course!

Absolutely love her. If you can, come to class. You will get a lot out of it. Its easier to understand the content by going to in-person lectures. The online lectures are very short and vague. Tests are very easy. Papers arent bad as long as you actually understand the topic. Hated the group projects though...
Wonderful class. I learned a fair amount. The majority of this class malarial is covered in other classes at ISU, so pretty easy if youve taken lots of psych. Good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Nesbit is a great lecturer, but she has a lot going on in her life so she's often a little scatterbrained and hard to reach via email. Writing papers for this class was easy, and the tests were really easy as well as long as you come to class and read the book.
He is most immiserizing.  :-)

One of my favorite professors at ISU. He's incredibly smart (it's so cool to see how his brain works as he tries to answer challenging questions) and clearly has a passion for teaching. Orazem is energetic, funny, and keeps class very entertaining. Would definitely recommend this class

Orazem is a great professor. If you're interested in the material, you'll like his class. He is really funny and knowledgeable. He engages the class often. The tests are heavy, but if you show up to class and listen they aren't extremely difficult. There are a few group homework's and a group presentation but they are straightforward.

Peter is who is extremely smart. He throws in a little humor, but overall the content is just extremely dry and boring. The exams are decently difficult, so make sure you study. He does offer review sessions. There is group homework, individual homework, a group presentation for participation, and packback assignments. Not my favorite class.

He's the best Econ 301 teacher out of all of the professors here. Real genius from Yale, and explains concepts using funny real world examples (some jokes might fall flat on their face). Can get dry when talking about elasticity. A lot of extra credit on exams for going above and beyond, and has opportunities outside of class. Labs suck.
Ultimately this class is a weed out class for Ag business and people wanting to get a minor in Econ. This class is fairly difficult but offering some extra credit point helps a little.

Orazem is a decent teacher and knows the material, but sometimes doesn't present in a way that facilitates learning as much as it could. Additionally, he says many inappropriate things that make class somewhat unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Always had really funny comments that made lecture interesting. Only like an hour of homework each week and the labs didn't usually have out of class work but were difficult. The tests were harder than I would have expected from the rest of the work though.

Very good lectures, ties almost all of the topics into detailed, real-world examples. Paying attention to these will make the class much easier. This is the case in labs too, many of them are exactly like test questions so participating and understanding these is incredibly helpful. Prof Orazem is always making jokes too which is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at Iowa State. This class also uses an honestly interesting textbook. Orazem genuinely cares so much about his students. If you ask questions and make conversation with him outside of class, he is likely to be a friend and mentor to you for the remainder of your time at Iowa State. Plus, his comedy acts are on youtube.

Great guy who is very passionate about his work and really cares about his students. He has a quirky but endearing sense of humor that makes class a joy! However, he can be a tad confusing and his logic can be a bit tough to follow at times.

Ive known him for two years. Once he sees potential in you, he pushes yo to the best of your abilities. I took his class once and now I am working on two research projects with him, which gives me the ability to learn so much more than just coursework, but also everything in Economics. He's very smart - take his class if you get the chance!

Expectations for the tests are not clear, and little feedback is given after the few and far between homework assignments. After one of the two tests are the only time you can accurately asses where your grade is for the class.

Gave extra credit points for attending evening guest speaker lectures and donating blood. Tough professor because half of the stuff he says doesn't make sense. Tests are almost impossible but he curves them. Labs are very easy b/c he walks you through them all & they are graded on participation. You don't need the book but you need the access code.
Not a easy class.

This has by far been the most difficult class I have take here at ISU. The Labs are pretty simple and he basically walks you through them. The information is very hard to grasp and the tests are very difficult. He is a very funny professor though, so he keeps you interested. I definitely enjoyed this class although it was tough.
He's an awesome professor. If you can take a class with him - do it. My favorite in the whole department
He's awesome!

Orazem is a great econ professor! The material is hard (as it is economics). But unlike other professors in econ who are very dull and hard to listen to, Orazem makes the class exciting and the material more interesting. Would highly recommended him of the econ professors I've had.

Great professor. His lectures get pretty dry with graphs and statistics sometimes, but that is to be expected in an Econ class and he makes up for it with his funny/awkward personality and jokes (used to be a comedian). Interesting class too, definitely opened my perspective. Exams aren't too difficult either.
Dr. Orazem has been polled by CNN, GMA, and other news organizations for his input.  He KNOWS Econ.  He is probably pretty advanced for 101, but he is a great teacher at high levels.

Really interesting lectures, very funny, very helpful and engaging in class. He goes pretty quickly and expects back knowledge so I can see why he would be difficult for lower level class students. For upper level courses and those with econ background, he's fantastic.

This class moved very fast and it was VERY hard. He knows the subject so well that he teaches it in a way that is hard to understand if you have never seen it. I recommend another professor for beginners

Does move very fast through his material and can be hard to understand.  I just studied the book a week in advance from the test and looked online to comprehend more of the material. Read the book and DO THE EXTRA CREDIT and you will be fine.

Prepare to hurt. This class is extremely difficult and moves incredibly fast. Orazem is a funny guy and is really nice if you have a chance to talk to him. Offers a lot of extra credit but the course is so hard it almost doesn't matter. I like the guy but unfortunately would recommend another professor just because they might be a bit easier.

He is VERY funny, but Many of us found this class very difficult. He taught very quickly and his formulas and graphs were hard to understand. It's hard to keep up and overall, this class was just awful. Very hard. I hear other teachers are MUCH better, so GET OUT IF YOU CAN. If you can't, teach yourself and get a tutor!
Really liked him! He was funny and made econ more interesting than it normally is! He was pretty good at explaining and gives lots of extra credit options!

One of the most helpful professors I have ever had. Always makes time for students even outside of office hours. Great sense of humor, a lot of his jokes did go over a lot of the class's head. Made the course interesting enough I am taking more economics courses in the future, I really enjoyed it.
The homework is completely different from all the tests and he tends to contradict himself A LOT. If you can get a different teacher do so ASAP!

I usually just look at ratemyprofessor.com to get an idea of what my teachers will be like.  However, with this one.. take head of warnings and get out now.  I have never been so confused by a class, and I don't blame the content.  He is funny at times, but that doesn't make up for his lack of ability to explain, coordinate, or organize anything.

I found his lectures funny and he always tries to get the class laughing. He always emailed me promptly to answer all my questions. He went out of his way to make sure everyone could find time for extra credit, and the company work really boosted my grade. I really enjoyed class with him.

Did not improve my understanding of economics at all. He goes at a very fast pace and tells you to study things that are not on the test. It is difficult to pay attention in class, and while he makes jokes only he finds them funny. He is not reasonable with grading, so do not expect any breaks or rounding. I would not recommend this guy to anyone.
Probaly one of the worst classes I will ever take. Lectures were not understandable at all and them graphs just made it worse. Tests were hard! Definately do the extra credit.

Not a bad class, very funny teacher, keeps boring lectures moving with his jokes. Make sure you go to his test prep, and have questions ready. This is very helpful. Class is not mandatory but recomended.

Horrible teacher. I had no idea what he was talking about and I'm pretty sure he didn't even know what he was talking about. Lectures were not helpful at all and I was confused everytime I left the class. He is extremely energetic, which is not always a good thing. I wish I could have dropped this class. Good luck if you are taking it.

He does a horrible job teaching. All the things he covers in class are just random statistics and I have taken econ 101 before and if I hadnt taken the class before I would probably have dropped this class from the beginning!

Class is extremely boring..don't get anything out of it..tests 2 and 3 are hard.  I didn't have a big problem with him, just wasn't a great teacher..make sure to go to the SI sessions before a test..really helps!

Funny, but too fast. Never went to class because it was too hard to follow him. I was so confused everytime I left. Graphs don't make sense, and he makes you wear red every Friday for extra credit- I only have so much red shirts!! Definitely don't recommend if you want to actually understand Economics.

He goes fast. I did very well on the first test and thought for sure I could manage a B in the class but the other tests were very  difficult. I almost never went to class and read the book to learn the material. If you can put up with his very long and boring lectures and can take good notes then you'll probably do well but good luck with that.
really nice class

Nice guy, but he is a horrible teacher. He teaches all of his concepts through graphs that you would never understand. He goes so fast that you have no idea what he is talking about. You are more distracted by how much he spits and his pit stains to be able to concentrate on how fast he is talking. The tests are EXTREMELY hard, even if you do study

He can be funny at times, but honestly, he makes it pretty hard to do well. His grading scale stinks and he is not good at explaining the concepts. Lectures are boring so you won't want to attend class. There are 4 exams, each is 20% of your grade. I DO NOT recommend him as your professor, if you want to do well, get out of his class.

The guy really does try, but it is really boring.  I suggest going to class and catching up on other reading, that way you can pick up on some of the important concepts.  Missing class is not a big deal, and he offers a lot of extra credit.  Study for the 2nd and 3rd tests, thy can be hard.
He's a good guy.  I really enjoyed lectures, although not important to go to.  Gives a lot of extra credit.  Goes very fast in lecture and the tests are very difficult after the first one.

Funny at times, does a horrible job explaining economics. Talks like he is out of a book. Horrible supplemental instrution, I went once... that was all it took. Study hard for this class, it is a freshman drop-out class.
He is a really nice guy...the class can get boring sometimes...but going to class helps.  Use tests to study for the final, and re-do your aplia assignments to study too...it really helps.

Alright professor, nice guy. He can be fun at times and really does try, but it is still ridiculously boring. I tried to stay awake, but I found that sudoku and solitaire do the job much better. The book explains things much better than he does. Some in-class assignments. Wording on tests can be really bad at times, and study guides help little.

Really knows the material and can describe it really well, but it's incredibly boring. Missing class is not a huge deal. Tests are not too bad. Lots of ability to get help though which is awesome. He's kind of funny and awkward at the same time.
before each test he hosts his own review sessions... very helpful
Overall fairly good applies info to real world applications well

Knows his stuff, very smart professor.  Puts a lot of effort into getting people through his class (extra credit, practice assignments, supplimental instruction, review sessions, etc)  Moves a little quickly in lectures at times.  Go to class and do the homework and you should get out with at least a B.

Pretty good professor overall. Sometimes gets caught up in what he's teaching and will move much quicker than most of us are capable of following. Uses examples and metaphors while teaching, which makes difficult material much easier to understand.
No Comments

DO NOT take it with her. She is a nice person and wants to help, but it literally set you up for failure. Weekly assignments are fine.. its the exams. No matter how hard you study, you will practically fail the exam. She doesnt give you good materials to study, and she takes two questions from the 40 question practice exam for the exam.

Hard to understand. A decent bit of the info you need to learn is just on the slides. Near the end of the semester me and a buddy in the class just started studying during the class time in the library.
Tests are not similar to the class material. Makes TA do half the lectures and does not show up. Nothing about the class prepares for the exams.
She is pretty nice but she has a accent that is hard to understand and her class is impossible. THe tests are nothing on what you learn so your guaranteed to do bad. Do not take her I repeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are alright, but the exams were extremely difficult. Nobody finished the exams, and they don't even grade the exams correctly. Be prepared to do a ton of assignments come exam week. Pick another proffesor.

I would take her again for micro. Exams are tough but worst midterm gets dropped and notes are allowed on the final exam. She does give a lot of extra credit opportunities which are basically mandatory to pass the class.

Truly a nice person, but lectures are very hard to comprehend and most people only show up for the Tophats which are graded. Assignments were beyond difficult. I would recommend a different professor.

Go for the tophats, learn on your own time, read the slides, it is all she does. You go through the material very quickly, which makes it hard to gain a thorough understanding. Exams are tough, but she sometimes curves them when the class average is below a 60%. Overall, if there is an option for another professor, I would take them.

Lectures are very difficult to follow, and content is often skipped over, so you pretty much have to teach yourself or go to SI. Don't bother with the study guides as half the stuff on them won't be on the exams. The tophats in class are also graded seemingly at random, as even if you get them all correct, they will be graded as if they weren't

Miyoung is an awful professor. She never curves the exams even though the average is 60%. Her lectures don't teach you anything because you can't understand her. Top Hat questions are in class everytime. Go to the SI sessions to actually learn material. Do the homework and get at least 60 on tests and you will get a B at least.

Great person, horrible professor. Tests are unrelated to study guides completely and TA sessions give very little insight. Exams are barely curved and the extra credit opportunities are slim. Lectures are dense and hard to understand. Register this class with another professor.

Miyoung's teaching is poor, and her exams are unrelated to the study guides, with class averages around 50%. SI sessions were the only help. While she offers extra credit, it doesn't make up for her terrible teaching. Take someone else for this class.

She is a nice person but she is a horrible instructor. Her lectures are all over the place and make no ense. Can't even study for exams because her "study guides" have nothing to do with what's actually on the exams. Exam average is 60% or less. If you can, avoid her lectures for your own sanity. also no make-up policy, you just take the 0%.
A little bit hard to understand. One of the worst professors i've ever had she's not engaging at all the class is boring she just goes through the slides and that's about it.

Great and caring professor, lectures are kind of hard to follow and you really need to spend time outside to make sure you understand the information. Lowest exam score was dropped and multiple attempts so she was very forgiving. Her accent can be hard to understand and she was constantly asking for participation.
Lectures are hard to follow, but with Unstuckstudy and dedication, you can get through this class. The professor is nice, and the extra credit helps boost your grade.

Professor Oh has an accent which could affect learning for some, but she is a caring professor and wants you to succeed. Half of Tophats get dropped, one exam, and one HW. 4 pages of notes and 2 attempts allowed on all exams.

When I first read Prof. Oh's ratings I was dreading the class because her ratings are overwhelmingly bad, but she is honestly not bad at all. She has tons of extra credit opportunities, Homework where it's physically impossible to get anything other than 100, and 2 attempts on an exam with 2 sheets of notes. Her english isn't a problem, Its decent

I really like this teacher! She very obviously cares about her classes and she tries really hard to involve the students in learning. She's a fair teacher, and for the people that do study and turn up, this class is rewarding! I never found economics easy, but I've genuinely learned a lot from this teacher.

Worst professor ever. Never answers emails and will come up to you in lectures no matter where you sit. Also no phones allowed or talking. All info is shared in class so if you don't go you won't know a thing. Go to SI it's the only reason I passed. All in all DO NOT RECOMMEND

Econ 102 itself is not incredibly difficult. That being said get ready to learn it on your own because lectures are of no use. Its going to take a ton of work outside of class to get a good grade. However she did curve the tests and final and gave tons of extra credit, so it definitely is hard to fail with so many opportunities.

The unfortunate truth of the matter is that Prof. Oh's Korean accent makes learning incredibly difficult during her already haphazard lectures. There's a huge disconnect between lecture material, in-class activities, exam prep/study guide content, homework, and what's on the actual exams. Cryptic extra credit policies are frustrating too.
If you hate yourself I recommend this course. This professor does an incredible job at draining all of my joy and energy and still having a 50% average on the final.

BEWARE!!!. This class has been the bane of my existence, the average score on the final exam is a 50 with zero information about a curve. The extra credit is a joke, it barely boosts your grade and is not applied until the end so your ending grade is a complete mystery until its too late.
Nice professor, but lectures are hard to follow. She gives you a lot of extra credit that will help your grade. Test questions are questions you have seen if you study and can memorize answers.

Worst professor ever. Unorganized, doesn't know how to teach or use Canvas. Lectures are a jumbled mess that are impossible to follow. Tests are unnecessarily hard, and lectures don't help you in any way to prepare. It is baffling to me that Miyoung still has a job at Iowa State.

Lectures are not organized at all. Reviews are not held at the convenience of students and are not relevant to what is being tested. Exam averages for her sections are 60% or below, and most people leave lectures wondering why they came to class. Gives lots of easy extra credit to inflate grades and to negate her teaching neglect.

Professor Oh was the worst professor I have ever had in my 3 years of college. She needs to be considered for probation as the lectures were a disaster, and the exams contained information we did not touch on in class once. Please stay away from her if you can. I put a lot of work into studying, but I still get 70% and below on the exams.

Her exam average is a 60 or less every time so if that doesn't say enough idk what will. She doesn't prepare her students and just hopes for the best. nice woman but absolutely awful professor. Is not easy to communicate with either. Also puts surprise topics in her exams and causes people to fail cuz of it. honestly laughable at times
Idk if I am just dumb, or if this is just way too hard.

This entire course was genuinely one of the most frustrating experiences of my life. Her style of lecture was very strange and all over the place. Exams were extremely hard because most of it was never covered in class and the studying materials provided were extremely unhelpful.

Miyoung is nice enough but she is simply not good at actually teaching. Exams are super hard for no reason and it's super discouraging to anyone wanting to learn econ, especially because she is the only ECON102 professor and this is an entry level course.

She spends about a third of every lecture calling out like one or two people for talking, which just wastes all 300 other people's time. Nothing is actually learned because when she does teach, it's irrelevant information. Exams are extremely hard and the average is always low. Lots of extra credit tho.

Lectures often do not cover most of the material on exams or assignments, so you'll have to teach yourself a lot of the class. She does not stop to answer questions in class either and will talk about other unrelated topics. Exams are extremely difficult and the class average is consistently very low, which is indicative of her poor teaching.
no curve on test exam average is a D

Dr. Oh is very kind and wants all of her students to succeed. She is very accessible outside of class. She offers a lot of extra credit, which you should definitely do, because her tests are very hard. She sometimes struggles to communicate clearly, which can be frustrating, but she is very accommodating for the most part.

Her lectures were all over the place hard to follow as part of it were on computers doing LC and just listening or hearing her talk. Her test are not bad as long as you do the test run and the practice exams on each module as the questions are the same or similar. She offers 5% of extra credit on random things and 20% back on exam corrections.

She is pretty energetic and funny sometimes She does lots of extra credit questions during lectures and some of them are exam questions Her tests are very hard and the averages are low but because everyone does so bad in her class she offers a ton of extra credit and curves the grades a lot at the end of the sem
she cares but she just kind of sucks at teaching.

Miyoung tries to make the class engaging and fun, and she does offer a lot of extra credit. However, her exams are very difficult and it is solely based on memorization. The class consists of many graphs and memorizing answers.

Lectures were dry but she made the exam like the practice exam and that brought my grade from an F to an A.

Do the work and you will pass
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Oh definitely cares about her students but her lectures are awful. Her exams are extremally hard. I think that the reason her lectures are so hard to understand is because of the poor use of slides and jumping around.If I were to take econ again I would Avoid at all costs.

Miyoung Oh started the semester as my favorite teacher and after 4 weeks, was my least favorite. Her teaching style was next to awful. Many concepts on the exams are not even covered in class. I was extremely disappointed in Miyoung, along with the quality and quantity of information I took away from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Oh is such a sweet lady when you know her out of class. That being said, if you are not already experienced in Econ, be ready to teach yourself a lot of the material because her lectures don't do a great job of teaching the material. She offers a ton of extra credit to those willing to participate. Overall 4/5.

Miyoung is a great professor for Econ 301 if you were confident in 207. If that's the case you will have no problems in the class. Lectures got dry at times but they are important to go to. She is a caring and funny person. The exams are structured exactly like the practice exams and you get to use your notes on them.

Professor Oh was literally so confusing. The entire class was structured so bad and you never know what actual grade you're going to receive because she changes the "extra credit" and curve so much. The only good is she dropped an exam and then basically curved all my exams to A's because the class average was so bad on every single test.

Impossible to understand and tests are insanely difficult. Test averages 50-55%. Free response is impossible the tests as she does not teach anything worthwhile in class despite giving out attendance points...only good thing going for her is LOTS of extra credit given out to boost everyone's horrible grades. WORST PROFESSOR EVER NOT EVEN KWAN CHOI

Lots of extra credit so I ended up with 101.86% but I definitely didnt understand all the material. If you want a good grade, Miyoung is the way to go, but if you want to understand the material with minimal extra studying, pick someone else. She is a funny person and genuinely loves econ, but her teaching method is different from my learningmethod

Started out the semester rough but she really helped make sure everyone would succeed. She had exams boosters if the exam average was below 70% and tons of extra credit throughout the semester. The exams are tough, but it is easy to get a good grade if you put in the effort.

She gives SO MUCH extra credit it's honestly hard to fail the class. She is a decent lecturer does not read off slides the entire time, which is cool, and literally gives exam questions in class if you go. Just attend class pay a little bit of attention and you will be fine in the class.

Great instructor that cares about her students and listens to their feedback. Gives lots of extra credit opportunities. Lectures can be a bit overwhelming but they are in a large lecture hall so that's part of it.
Professor Oh is a great lecturer. Very interactive & cares about her students. Homework & exams can be tricky, but if you study the materials she gives you really closely, you should be good.
She honestly makes Iowa state look bad and is discouraging to anyone actually wanting to learn Econ.

She gives out questions multiple times per lecture that are worth participation and correctness and most of the time the questions dont make any sense.
