reviews.comment: Good teaching and course.
He really cares about his students. Bad handwriting and a thick accent, but if you put the time into the course, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can hardly understand Oliver or read his handwriting, so good luck, and I hope you like reading from the textbook. The grading scale was nasty and brutal to poor exam takers. The lectures were dry and dull. The TA's were just as confused, and I felt like I learned nothing.

Oliver usually confused me when he explained stuff. I could usually understand what he was saying if I revisited it enough times. Answers were leaked to an extra credit assignment (16.25% of grade) that likely led to a bunch of undeserved grades. I would not want to take a class with him again.
bad homeworks, worst handwriting, worst lecturer, learned nothing

He has the absolute worst handwriting I have ever seen and because this semester was taken online due to covid, handwriting is especially important. I could read maybe 30% of what was written. I would have to rewatch certain parts of the lecture multiple times to see if he said what was written beforehand so I could get the correct information.
The worst lecturer in Iowa State

Basically what he did during the class is taking something from his prepared paper to the whiteboard, while most of examples are directly taken from the textbook. Only one third of people attend his lectures, really confused and helpless.

DO NOT take this class if it is not required by your major. If you do, you will work very hard just to pass and the majority of what is taught and learned is not applicable to real life. If you are good at mathematical proofs you will do well, but you will still have to devote a lot of time to complete the homework.

It's more than possible to get an A on the first two exams, yet the average is 65. Teaches out of the textbook, but the textbook is really good so that sorta works. This course is the hardest in my major so it's gonna be difficult with both him and lutz. That being said, he might not curve. That would fail 70% of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Covers topics only at surface level. Homework is very advanced for the lessons he teaches during lecture. Course description says for students with little or no programming experience but coming from someone with none, the class was still very challenging.
Awful. Can't understand him. Can't read anything he writes.
Not too bad! Goes over the material a lot, and the test material is fairly predictable. Lecture is a little boring, but what did you expect?

Was supposed to be grad course, but felt like an easy undergrad course.  We didn't write code, just jumped from topic to topic, covering some with very little depth.  Eulenstein knows his material and is good a clarifying details, but is not good at organizing his lectures in general.  The "presentations" we made in class were useless.

Concepts covered in CS311 are very fundamental and interesting.  However, Prof. Eulenstein has made it very difficult and boring for students to learn.  As a senior with a 3.8 GPA, I had to watch lectures and supplemental materials found elsewhere to learn the materials.  Only 25-30 percent students attended classes after the first few weeks of 311

Eulenstein has a very thick accent, doesn't explain things clearly, erases what is on the board immediately after writing it, wears distractingly tight pants, covers topics too quickly, and doesn't explain things clearly.
The worst teacher I have ever had in Iowa State

Well, this class was required, but thanks to wonderful teaching our class size dropped from 120 to 15 students who apparently didn't realize attendance wasn't required.  Books could be written and papers have already been of how lousy this was.

This class is entirely asynchronous. With that in mind, there is an immense amount of readings, documentaries, and other class work that need to be finished, all of which are incredibly intriguing. I do recommend this class to anyone looking for a simple 3 credit hour half semester course. Dr. Mesropova is really good and incredibly accomodating!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of reading/watch material so be prepared of that. Pace yourself accordingly. Will add a charge to your account despite not having to purchase course materials and does not respond to emails. I personally wouldn't recommend since I feel there are better classes with professors who may actually communicate with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Just do your work, and you'll be fine. Really nice and accommodating lady with a super easy class. She allows it to be done at any point during the semester and works hard to make things work for students. Wonderful and reasonably interesting class!

I did this class during prep week, and it was not very hard. The readings were kind of long, but you could end up choosing two points from one reading and apply them to the modules, with some analysis, of course, and you would be OK. Very interesting documentaries. Easy quizzes and final. Dr. Mesropova is also really accessible through her email!
Pretty easy, but this class is very reading heavy and has weekly, so be prepared.

I took this course during the Winter. The 4 weeks was more than enough time to finish the course. This course was fun and engaging. You get to watch Russian movies, understand the culture, and see the point of view of Russian citizens amidst the Ukrainian war. Plus, I learned how to do a case study! It's worth taking this class. Hits many LAS reqs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, this is an easy A class for a GPA boost. Discussion posts and essays take a while, but the quizzes and final exam are very easy, and you can find most answers on Quizlet. I finished it all during finals week, which I don't recommend procrastinating, but it worked out fine for me, you just need to really lock in for like a day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course was extremely easy. I finished it in 2 days, after completing my finals. Just lock in, complete everything with a little bit of analysis on discussion posts and the final project and you'll get an A. Prof. Mesropova was really accessible through email and was quick in response. Don't hesitate to ask her questions!

Easy and interesting class. Put effort into the discussion posts, and you'll do well on those. The quizzes are untimed, and the information is easy to find in the material. The final paper and exam aren't that bad, either. Good class and worth 3 credits.

Way, way too easy of a course. You won't learn anything because you're not incentivized to. Everything is on quizlet and there is a lot of oversimplification or flat out wrong characterizations of events anyway, which is horrible for a history class. If you want a rubber stamp 3 credits, take it. If you want to learn about Russian history, don't.

The online RUS 375 is set up with discussion boards, quizzes and readings/videos weekly then a final and final paper due at the end. Super informative course and the professor is super great and supportive. She is quick to remind everyone about the deadlines and grades quickly. Overall, a great course!

No due dates, so it is easy to push things off and make the end of your semester stressful, but she grades fairly independent of when you submit assignments. The material was interesting and by the end of the semester, I felt like I learned a ton from the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Oh My God. An online professor that doesn't arbitrarily lock content behind date walls for no reason? Sign me up. You could knock RUS375 out in a weekend but I wouldn't, I actually found the content interesting and enjoyable. Discussion is more demanding than in most classes, but it does a good job of forcing you to learn.
Easy A, you can do it at any time too. Probably don't do it all during dead week like I did but you do you. Pretty easy grader.

Very well-designed & straightforward class. Just do the reading quizzes, come to class to watch the films, & submit the essay about the film afterwards. You need 10 quizzes & 10 essays to pass. She gives study guides that have all the questions for the midterm & final exams. Final project is a short paper. She's super nice, totally worth taking!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Mesropova is a very authentic person and shes always willing to help people come to their own conclusions about whether film we watched. The class is an easy A, so long as you attend class and do the minimum of 10 film responses/quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Olga is awesome! Entirely self-paced half semester online class that consists of lots of discussion posts, 9 tests (very fair), and a 5-7 pg. final research paper. Interesting movies/documentaries and readings for each module. I felt like I learned A LOT and was genuinely interested! I took this for fun and would highly recommend!

Extremely well-organized and stress-free class. She recommends submission dates as a guideline (which I wish I'd followed), but you can also work at your own pace. All work is basically due at the end of exam week. The grading turnaround is amazingly fast even though there are hundreds of students in the class. Interesting material, helpful prof.

One of my favorite professors at ISU. She really knows how to make learning Russian fun and easy. I came to RUS101 without any prior knowledge of the language and was able to hold half-way decent conversations by the end of the semester. Highly recommend taking 101 with her!

Olga is an amazing professor who wants to help you learn - prompt with email, etc. 8 modules (lots of reading and movies) each with 1 quiz and 1 discussion post + 2 classmate responses. The final is a 5-7 pg essay & test. Completely self paced course. Info on quizzes is completely fair and her grading on discussion posts is lax. I loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved everything about her Russian film class. Extremely intelligent and really interesting lectures. She is very passionate about cinema and Russian culture and this really pulls you into her lectures. Decent amount of written assignments and quizzes are easy if you do the readings. I would take a class from her again! ISU is lucky to have her.

She's fantastic, the best language professor I've had. Knows a ton and really wants you to learn. The classes are fun, amounts of homework are reasonable, feedback is super quick and helpful, plus loads of extra credit: tutoring, film nights, etc. I don't think she teaches RUS 101 very often, so sign up if you see that she's teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: We had like 9 journals and 9 quizzes. Just had to make sure to do it before the end of the semester. (Half semester class) Theres a final paper too, she gives you the topics/sources. Ended up with a 93%. Shes a bit tougher on the journal grading despite hundreds of students but if you have enough sources the paper is easy grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took this class just to stay full-time because I dropped another one. Ended up being more work than expected since I procrastinated assignments until the end but the amount of work was reasonable and the grading became more relaxed.

RUS378 was based on russian films as well as history, pretty dry topics especially for a 6-9PM class. Dr. Mesropova was very energetic and enthusiastic about the topic and made everything very interesting to learn! She is very clear about due dates and expectations, and the tests and weekly papers/quizzes are easy if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She gives great feedback, whether you get a good grade or not. Interesting class, good professor
Awesome professor. Learnt a lot about Russian geopolitical and social scenario and enjoyed learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class online and there was no due date which made it stressful. However, it's very manageable if you don't wait until the last minute. She's a really easy grader and offers a ton of extra credit. Although it may seen like a lot of reading, if you just skim through the readings you'll be fine! 10 discussions & quizzes, 3 novel, & a paper
Mrs. Mesropova is a wonderful professor. She's always quick to respond to emails and she's very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor.  A lot of reading and longer videos, but pretty interesting stuff. Quizzes and the final exam are pretty straightforward and the professor is a fairly easy grader on the discussions. Definitely recommend this professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Mesropova was one of the nicest and most caring professors I have ever had. She always gave really helpful feedback on any discussion posts and sent regular reminders to the class about deadlines. Her online Russ 375 class was a lot of work, but if you do it you will actually enjoy it. She is always rooting for her students to do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really caring professor, who is quick to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking her class. There are lots of readings, but not too bad for a literature class. No deadlines or required order of submissions, so you can work around your schedule. Quizzes are not that hard and there are extra credit points in each quiz. She is very knowledgeable, fair, and totally responds to any email within 10 minutes.

Ridiculous amounts of work required for a Humanities elective course. 3 huge novels, weekly quizzes (sometimes two a week). Grade consists almost entirely on a final paper, exam, and 3 novels you have to read.

She is one of my favorite proffesors at ISU. I went into this class interested in learning a 3rd language and right after declared a Russian minor. She is fantastic. Participate in class and don't save your workbook for the night before the tests, it takes awhile to do!
One of the best profs I've had at ISU.

Speaks very fast, doesn't write on board, ppts are mostly pictures, doesn't make power points available until a couple days before the exams. Readings aren't available very far in advance. Exams are pretty easy - mix of mult choice, short answer, and essay.

She is the best professor I have ever had. There are a lot of tests so you don't have to know too much information and she goes over what exactly is on each test the day before so it is very easy to get an A on all of the tests. I didn't get below a 91% on any of the tests and it is very easy to get 100% on the homework. She is seriously the best!
She is a great teacher.  She snowballs all of the information over and over.  If you do the homework, then you will learn it.  Overall, she is fantastic.
I enjoyed her straightforward teaching style and bluntness. She doesn't let you get away with wrong answers but she's still super nice about it. I enjoyed her class.
Professor Mesropova is a superb instructor- if you are interested in learning, take any of her classes.
Great teacher. If you want to take Russian make sure it's her class. It's a hard language to learn but she is very helpfull
Good at explaining
Very good teacher - highly organised, comprehensive understanding of the subject, approachable, makes understanding and progressing with the material easy, and hot as hell.
Quite nice, somewhat young prof, easy to approach. The "Troika: A communicative approach" textbook for 101 is terrible; it's a joke compared to other 101 language texts. And yes, she is kinda cute.
Great prof.  Made learning Russian very easy.  Definitely WILL take more classes with her and will recommend to anyone interested in Russian.

While I do enjoy the subject that she taught, Professor Mesropova has a few quirks that I can't help but notice. She constantly "shushes" people even if they're whispering, so it's hard to talk to other students in her class at all. But she is a somewhat fair grader, although I do question some grades I got from her.
Olga is a great professor!! Makes learning Russian super easy
the class has been very difficult for me, but I sought help and my grade is coming up.  She is fun and cares about her students.  Be sure to check the syllabus on webct for test dates.
Olga is awesome! One of my favorite professors at ISU.
Great professor. Speaks clearly and makes teh class both fun and simple.
No Comments
Awesome prof.
Real good teacher, gets you to learn the stuff and helps you understand the stuff clearly.  If you having any trouble you could ask her for help no problem. And like the other guy said she cute.
Awesome teacher!
Honors seminar on Russian film- so sit back, and write a one page movie analysis every other week.  Bonus: the prof is kinda cute.
No Comments

Lectures are super boring and pointless, all he does is derive equations. I stopped going to lectures early on or if I did it was for extra credit tophat. Easier/more efficient to learn content on your own via the homework or other resources.
He goes pretty quick in lecture, but it's just physics 1. The class overall is easy so his teaching style didn't hurt my learning, and it could've been much worse.

Overall, a good professor; lectures are in-depth and usually easy to follow, and he throws in little jokes or sarcastic jabs every once in a while that make the lectures more interesting. He can get a little confusing at times, but often stays behind for a bit after the lecture and is willing to answer questions.

I am currently taking this class for Physics 2310. I learn nothing in lecture. He reads off his slideshow, but he prints out every slide and then writes them word for word on the chalk board making everything go much slower than it needs to be. He also does not explain anything. He simply reads the slides and moves on.

Dr. Canfield was great. He gets excited to talk about what he does, and if you have questions after class, he is more than happy to help explain. Class is not too difficult, and he explains everything pretty well, though.

I found Proffessor Canfield's lectures to be very interesting and enjoyable. He moves very quickly, and sometimes doesn't really explain things too well, however, I could more or less piece things together well enough. Quizzes in this class are easy, exams are moderately difficult. The TAs I had for recitation and lab were amazing.
I learned all the material by doing practice exams
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Canfield is the worst professor that I've had in my three years at ISU and probably the most arrogant. For one thing, he runs his lectures as though you already know all of the material he is presenting, so he runs through confusing examples instead of teaching everything. I had to read the book to get any concrete material out of this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Canfield definitely knows the material, but his teaching wasn't very effective for me. He also tries to be enthusiastic about what he teaches, but it's only sometimes. He's more of a middle of the road professor, at least in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Paul Canfield proved himself to be a big "know-it-all" however lacks basic human empathy. I wouldn't recommend him to anyone.

His lectures are fantastic. He does everything on the chalkboard. The labs and lab reports are straightforward. The quizzes aren't really that bad. The tests are a little rough. The homework is only graded for completion. The hard part of this class is that it moves so fast. If you want to do well on the tests, then practice older tests quickly.

Phys221 is one of the hardest courses at ISU, but P Canfield is an AMAZING professor! He's so knowledgeable and always willing to explain things to you. Always read the book before class. It'll help you understand the lecture. If you're still confused, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! He is always delighted to answer questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Such an odd, old school man. He always comes prepared and knows 100% of what he's talking about. His lectures flow, are relevant, but not always beneficial. Funny guy. (P.S. my difficulty rating would probably be a 5 if I hadn't taken AP Physics in high school)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Paul Canfield is a great guy and he is extremely smart. Physics is definitely the hardest class I've ever taken, so it tended to be difficult for me to keep up in lecture, but that was not due to his lack of teaching ability. Lecture can be useful but a lot of it is deriving equations which is not something we're tested on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The hardest class I've ever taken. Good lecturer, however, read the book, that helped me the most. Stick it out. The class sucks but just do it. Good luck!

Quirky old guy that loves his comics. If you take his class be prepared to take notes during the entire time your in class. Going to lecture is helpful but finding outside resources such as a tutor or SI's will help out. Its a weed out class and it has been the hardest class i've taken at ISU.

PHYS 221 in general is a very hard course, especially at ISU (from what I've heard about other physics departments), so don't expect a cakewalk no matter what professor you take the class with. Dr. Canfield does a very thorough job of explaining all of the concepts, and is a very smart guy who will be able to answer any question you have for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Paul is a very smart professor which I feel hurts his lecturing ability. There are times in class when it seems like he just assumes we know what he is talking about. Another downfall to his lecturing style is he cares more about how equations and ideas are derived instead of showing us how to use these ideas.

Really great Physics professor. Very clear lectures with great examples. Class isn't easy, but if you just put a bit of effort into it, you'll do fine. Overall a funny guy who keeps lectures interesting while still staying on topic.

Honestly, if you do the reading beforehand and actually complete every homework assignment, without looking up answers, you should have NO problem getting an A.  Professor Canfield is also fairly clear, provides examples, makes goofy dad jokes, and is VERY helpful and friendly if you go to him during office hours!!!

Some people seem to be confusing a hard class and a bad prof.  Canfield is a great prof but the class is very difficult.  It covers a lot and he can't spend too much time on any one topic.  Attend class, look over the book, and do the homework.

Canfield is certainly one of the better professors for physics. The class is straight-up hard, but the guy's whimsical mannerisms makes it go a little better. He certainly knows what he's doing, but I'm not sure if he realizes most people just say "yup, looks good to me.....i guess.." once he finished a monstrous derivation.
Physics is tough, but he makes it interesting and definitely knows his stuff. Be prepared to feel lost if you don't read the textbook before class. He covers material very quickly.

Really awesome teacher, definitely is passionate about what he does and made you excited about physics. While the tests were difficult there were plenty of resources for those that need help. An amazing professor anybody would be lucky to have for physics. He also writes everything out on the blackboard so you can actually keep up with notes.

Very enthusiastic teacher. You will be pleased to have him if you have any intention of learning the material. Teaches on the blackboard (You'll be thankful), and teaches very purposefully ("This is why you want to know this"-kind of teaching). I went to two different lectures regularly; definitely preferred his.

Professor Canfield is a very smart and eccentric teacher. He really tries to get you excited about physics, but he has to cover a lot of material so the lectures are pretty bland. I barely used the textbook (although I probably should have) and did decent. What makes the class so hard is the homework and the department quizzes.
Excellent lecturer. He makes every lecture interesting and entertaining. It made me want to go to the 8 am lecture every day . Very knowledgable about the subject and very clear in his explanations.

I actually loved Phys 221. I got a very strong A and didn't find it near as time consuming as others say. go to class, pay attention, ask questions in recitation. Canfield is very clear and I find it very helpful that he writes on the board as he goes. Best professor I've had in my college career.
Very good looking, and very helpful when needed.  He has this odd chain coming out of his pocket though...

Canfield is a fun professor when he wants to be.  Later in the year we lecture after lecture on full derivations and my opinion dropped.  I rarely ever got much out of the later lectures because he just copied derivations from his notebook on the board.  As a side note, I got a very strong A in phys so I'm not whining because of a bad grade
the class itself is HARD.  But Canfield is a really fun and witty lecturer, plus he really knows his stuff

Talented speaker but spends too much of his lectures on derivation. His tests are pretty tough, so make sure you've looked a lot of examples from the book/old tests. Lots of material, so you'll have to put a lot of work in to get a good grade.

Seriously one of the hardest classes I have taken here. Tests are near impossible. I wish he gave more practical examples in class instead of just deriving everything. If you can take it with Craig Ogilvie, he was a sub once for our class and that was the most I'd learned during lecture all semester.

Funny, good demos, and easy to understand.  However, he doesn't cover application enough.  The difficult MC tests vary widely from the given old tests and the (easy) quizzes, and aren't even remotely as easy as the "test examples" he gives in class.  If you're not looking to study the book a ton, wait until the next semester - it should be easier.

I did not like him as a teacher.  I think too much emphasis was put on derivation and not enough on practical use of what we derived.  He was interesting in lecture but that doesn't go far in making up for his lack of teaching ability. One example per day is not sufficient in teaching a method of proper solving for each topic. Unhappy

Very intelligent, clearly knows what he's talking about.  When he's not proving formulas he can be interesting.  Believed to have split his soul into a number of horcruxes (what is on the end of that chain leading to his pocket?!) Left-handed.

If you take his class make sure you go to class. Even if you do I found him useless most of the time. I passed the class with the use of the book. He is not helpful at all. He expects everyone to be a genius. For the average students out there he is a bad choice as an professor.
He enjoys teaching very much and is very comprehensive in the material. The level of class may be difficult but the text book helped a lot.

Best physics professor you're probably ever going to get.  Spends a lot of time deriving formulas, but also offers some decent examples in class, and tells some funny jokes and does some interesting experiments to keep things lively.

His primary lecture technique is formula derivations.  He doesn't show many example problems, which I think would help a lot.  Entertaining lecturer, with a lot of demos.  Certainly better than other Physics professors that I have had.

Physics is not an easy class unless you had AP physics and your highschool teacher was really good. Canfield is extremely helpful with writing on the board compared to quickly going through slides. He might be hard to follow sometimes, but compared to other teachers he's a good choice.
Good professor, Makes physics more interesting than ever before. Likes to use Foxtrot cartoons for in class examples.
I really liked him. He seemed like he really was excited about physics. But the class was impossible. and the book was a waste of money....never opened it once
this guy was awesome.  he tried to keep the students interested, which is why i went.  he was an all around good guy.   the class was still very hard, but c'mon, it is physics.

Canfield is a good guy but lectures are almost meaningless.  Spends most of the time explaining equations that are already in the text.  Then he has some extremely straightforward examples that make you think this material is easy until you take the tests.  Crippling difficulty but he does a good job at doing the best he can to soften the blow.
Dr. Canfield is a great lecturer.  He has a lot of enthusiasm and is hilarious at times.  However, the exams are extremely hard.  I put a ton of effort into this class and still didn't do well.

Ok so he knows his Sh*t!! But he is also, I felt, a little cocky!! That seemed to get into the way during lecture!! He did have good notes if they all weren't about theory and such! Not a bad teacher just a VERY BAD CLASS!! GOOD LUCK TO ALL THAT TAKE IT! It can be very stressful!

Dr. Canfield clearly shows his enthusiasm for the material in every lecture and he even makes a wave motion when he erases the board.  Overall, the class is very demanding even for a 5-crd class.  However, Dr. Canfield's mastery of the english language serves to ilustrate challenging concepts rather clearly.  By far my best professor this semester.
Draws the best stick figures/objects i have ever seen in my life. I would advise going to the lectures just to see his stick figures.
Makes Physics interesting, and almost fun.
Funny guy!
He knows what he's talking about and he explains it all

Excellent lecturer.  Does fun demonstrations and has a good sense of humor.  Exams are relatively fair, but he likes to have lots of E) None of the above answers.  Course policies are fair and clear.  The coursework can be difficult because it is a rather broad physics course, but he covers it well.
Hard ass class, would have been nice if didn't chaulk talk it all of the time and show those f****ing Fox Trot comics
No Comments

Very Hard class, he is very affected by the material also; if he doesn't like the section that is going on he is very boring and very hard to listen to. But if he likes it the concepts are very easy to understand.
hard ass class but he was a decent teacher

He was a great teacher, understood everything he said in class, and made an attempt to help in any way possible. Dynamics is a hard class, but he made it very easy to understand and follow along in class. He was very accessible outside of class and would definitely take his class again.

He mostly worked through in class practice problems, but sometimes didn't finish them or didn't explain them well enough. There were 3 homework assignments every week as well as reading assignments. There are 4 night exams, but he posts a lot of study guides and examples for you to study. There were also in class activities due each week.

The course didn't seem well planned which left students in a reactive position. His lectures seemed to be rambling and it was difficult to determine which information was useful during lecture. I wasn't a fan of the teaching style, there was a heavy dose of equation derivation and little in the way of example problems. Interesting content though.

Great professor. Loved the structure of this class. No tests, 6 quizzes (largely dependent on your grade so do well), and 2 group projects. Fairly straightforward class. Learned a lot, would definitely take again.
Excellent professor

as a distance student, he was very difficult to get a hold of. difficult to follow lectures, he tends to ramble. it is tough to discern what is important information and he also makes many mistakes in lectures; makes it tough to learn material.  exams seem different than lecture material. however, does not grade homework too hard.
He is grades the exams fairly. The tests are entirely based on the lecture notes so you just need to pay attention in the class.

First of All this class is totally misleading.  It is a repeat of mechanics applied to gears and shafts.  As for Pranav, he is ok, talks too fast and his exams cover alot more of the concepts than math.
No Comments

He's really interested in students learning the material.  He's very helpful and friendly if you go to his office hours.  The class was basically everything you need to know to design a gearbox.  Think EM 324 only more indepth.

Barloon was a very good lecturer this semester. His lectures were very informative and went over the material. Sometimes he'd get a bit behind for the week, and we'd finish the topics a bit late, but overall, he made the material easy to understand. Calc 3 is a hard class, and he made it better to take. Make sure to do practice exams and quizzes.
I've had Barloon for Calc 1, 2, and 3. He's an amazing professor who teaches very well. His lectures are excellent, as he pauses to ask questions and takes his time to answer them.

Professor Barloon is a really solid professor.  He genuinely cares about his students and is more than willing to work 1 on 1 with you to improve your grade.  He has enthusiasm that makes his lectures very easy to sit through.  He does sometimes run off on tangents that can cause the class to be a bit behind schedule, but it is usually a non-issue.
Calc 3 is a lot harder than calc 1 but Barloon was pretty good. I did not like him in calc 1 but at least for this class he is really good at teaching.

I took every calculus class with him. Kept coming back because he helped me understand the material the best. He often works through examples and also derives equations so that you develop conceptual understanding; he cracks jokes too. There are many resources available in the calculus department. I'm gonna miss him as I take differential equations

Prof. Barloon is a great teacher for Calc 3. He explains the concepts really well and always pair each with a couple example. He's so lively and energetic for a 7:45 AM class and that alone makes it worth it to wake up early three times a week. I like the way he breaks down the equations into something digestible. Class could be a little slow.

For calc 1, he explained incredibly well and adequately prepared us for all of the exams. I highly recommend you go to class as he does a good job in actually teaching the material as well as giving tips that might help us on tests.

Barloon is a great Professor to have in Calculus, if you can't get Butler. Barloon has well-thought-out notes in classes, and the warm-up questions are always really helpful. My only gripe is that he gets very far behind the rest of the lectures, causing fewer review days and being behind for the Homework.

Every time I attended Prof. Barloon's calc lecture, I left feeling confused. Maybe it's just me, but Butler's videos ended up teaching me better than the lectures. However, Barloon does teach the topics well, he just uses different ways than Butler. His lectures are also very fast-paced, and he doesn't always give a full explanation. Nice guy tho.
Hes a really fast paced teacher and for me that was not an issue but for other that may be. Keep in mind that he is fast for an ALREADY fast course.
He's good at teaching. Attendance is not mandatory, but it helps a lot to go to lectures because he will give hints and things to remember.

Barloon is a great guy, and he's great during help hours in the morning before quizzes. However, it was difficult to keep up with his insanely fast-paced style during his lectures, and he mumbled a lot. Great dude, but butler was the one who taught me all the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Barloon's Calc 1 lectures are pretty good; he goes in-depth to explain essential topics and makes a point to show the derivation of certain equations if he feels necessary. Sometimes, classes can get slightly behind, but I doubt we lose much. Overall, he's a good prof and he makes the class enjoyable.

Barloon is a great professor and would make sure nobody was left behind. As a result, some concepts would be sped over to maintain pace. Lectures were helpful, but watching Steve Butlers videos online was just as good or better. Exams were challenging, but working over past exams was extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Moves fast, but overall a pretty good professor. He's nice and gets excited over being asked good questions. Not intimidating, but to be fully prepared for exams it's good to have outside sources like youtube.

Calc 1 is generally an exam-heavy course, but between Barloon and Butler, you have two great options. Barloon explains things well and makes concepts easy to understand. He also answers your questions clearly as long as you ask them. I only got a bad grade because I'm not good at math, but he's still a very good teacher
SOS this man is not here to cater to students he is on the move and you better keep up godspeed everyone
he explains everything really good and clear. straight to the point. his lectures cover the material fast but not too fast. is really good at answering questions too. would def take again.

Focuses heavily on examples during lecture, not spending too much time on conceptual stuff. Follow along with the examples, even if you don't understand it totally, and you'll do just fine in the class.
Very long lectures that often go over the time. Covers very few examples which often do not correlate to the homework at all and leave a lot to be answered. Nice guy but mumbles a lot.
Super great lectures that make calculus pretty easy to learn

He's a pretty chill guy, lectures are usually stretched time toward the end of class, and that causes some confusion. Otherwise he's always asking if students have questions and mentions everyday where students can get help. Also he links his slides which always contain problems that look awfully similar to test questions.
Lectures and explanations make no sense. When asking questions, he seems like he's forced to answer instead of just helping
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very open to learning and adapting his teaching style based on how comfortable his students are in the material which is demonstrated through his top hats throughout class. Focuses primarily on examples and an a borderline cheat code come exam time because his examples are so helpful and often pretty close to what's actually on the exam.

He sounds like he just mumbles to himself all lecture and moves way too fast. if you've never taken calc before this class is a nightmare. the test he writes are very different formatting and ways to ask a question compared to practice tests and what's covered in class.
Great lecturer!! Really simplifies the material and makes it digestible. He has a good idea of what students make mistakes on and forget, which makes his lecturers super helpful.

Seriously the best professor I've ever had! He is so helpful and ensures you know what's going on before moving on. The content was difficult but he made it easy to manage and made me feel like I COULD do hard things. 10/10 recommend!

Barloon is a cool guy who's approach to math is refreshing. He will treat all math backgrounds equally in the course and has a fun teaching style if you go to lectures. They are not mandatory and you can easily learn the material on your own. However, this tendency gets dangerous for the weekly recitation quizzes.
His lectures can be a little dry at times, but he is a very good guy.

What can I say About Prof. Barloon, the way he teaches makes you understand what's going on. He discourages memorization and goes into great detail on how a formula was formed. Although he is always rushed at the end since he is always behind schedule, he is an amazing professor.
Amazing professor that answerd all questions clearly. Very approachable and nice.

Professor Barloon gives fairly effective lectures, but often seems to fall behind and has to speed through some things to stay on track. Overall, he was a good professor and is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. He was often available in the help room, which was very helpful.

Barloon is a solid lecture teacher. Easy to understand and clear on what is being covered. The only complaint is that he teaches at a fast past and spacing out will cause you to miss out on most of the information for what he's teaching. Overall enjoyed the number of examples. Feel free to miss lectures, Butler videos still exist.
Absolutely great professor makes learning calc easy,

If you are taking MATH 165, I would 100% recommend taking it with Paul Barloon. He "simplifies" all of the math wordiness into something students can understand. His lecture notes are also straightforward, he introduces the topic, writes down how to solve problems based on the topic, and then goes through some examples in class. One of the best.

Maybe it was because calculus online sucks, but I had a very hard time following his lectures. His monotone voice does nothing to help. Homework wasn't bad, and there were always lots of example problems available.

There was no book for this class, but you had to buy a top hat to get attendance points. You could do the top hat from your room so you don't have to go to class, but if you miss them it will affect your grade. There are recitations once a week and are graded every other week. You work as a group in recitations. The tests are in person.

Did not enjoy his class. If you took pre-calc in high school, it's just about the same thing. However, I only felt more confused when I went to lectures. Of all the simple ways there are to solve a problem, he took the hardest route every time. He uses tophat for participation, did not enjoy that. I felt that I learned much more on canvas alone.

Math 140 is a decent class, most of the learning and homework is done on a site called ALEKS (very helpful in my opinion.) Attendance points are taken every class and each week there is generally a group project to work on. Showing up is important to succeed in this class.

This professor is super nice and explains very well. He will explain more than one problem of the same one if you don't get it. His exams aren't that hard, but you have to understand the problems he gives you and what to do with them. You'll do good if you just practice from Aleks most days.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Barloon was exceptional. He explains things really well. Lots of top hat. Tests are easy if you do the homework. Lots of hw on Aleks, but if you manage your time it isnt bad. My only complaint is that he would give tophat with 30 secs left of class (when i had a class 10 mins after this one that was a far walk) Other than that, great guy.

Honestly seems to care about students learning. Hard to show up because the majority of the class you can teach yourself with ALEKS. Lots of Homework, but given enough time to complete. Willing to explain things further if you have questions.

Barloon was organized and diligent. You always knew what to expect from his course and it made it easier for me to stay on top of studies. However, I could not keep up with his lecture notes. He crammed as much information in as possible often saving the hardest concept for the last 3 minutes of class. It was really frustrating.

Barloon's lectures are a bit dry and he can make the problems appear more difficult than they actually are. The only thing that scares me in this class is that the tests are show-your-work style and not multiple choice.

Paul has been my favorite professor by far at Iowa State. He is very good at explaining complicated equations into words that students can understand. He always treated students with respect and students treated him with respect as well. If you must take an advanced math class at Iowa State, I would definitely recommend taking that class with Paul.

He's a very solid lecturer. Sometimes can get boring but it is math lol. He's very prepared, speaks clearly, and always is responsive to questions in class. Once you get the math program format down, you'll be able to bust through these 3 calc classes. If you go to class, finish all your quiz sets, and study the math166 site info, you'll be good.
Calc I at iowa state in general is a nightmare, but it is worse when the professor does notes so fast that the class can't keep up, and skips examples that will be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Teaches Calc 2 very well and answers all questions. He tends to go slow through the majority of the lecture then rush through the last few minutes, but it's not too big of a deal. He tries to joke around sometimes to make the class less awful, so it takes a little bit of stress out of the lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The tags sort of suggest that the class sucks, but Paul Barloon is very skilled at explaining topics in a way that I can understand. He'll say things like "let's see, I don't know how to do this right away. Oh! let's try this" and continues to go through the example. Basically the entire class is examples but they're very helpful and study for exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer. Walks through all the steps of a derivation, and although it may seem pointless, the more experienced you are with calculus, the more you can see how related everything is. The better understanding you have of the relationship between all of the concepts in calculus, the better prepared you will be for the exams in Calc 3.

Barloon was a very good lecturer, but focused a lot more on derivation than example problems. This made it difficult to apply what we learned for the test without a lot of extra work. However, the class being departmental had very accessable resources and Barloon was easy to meet outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Have had Barloon for 3 semesters. Great instructor that has tons of in class examples and top hat. Great at answering questions and is willing to tell you if he doesnt know the answer and will her back to you. Accessible outside of lectures. Homework is out of his control, but not awful.

I really enjoyed Barloon's lectures. He really understands the material and articulates ideas well. Calc 3 lets you attend any lecture as top hat is not for credit, so if you don't like his lecture you can attend another professor's to figure out who you like best.

He has top hat in class. Best math teacher I've had at any school. Utilize his videos he posts about the lectures after class. He does a good job of "dumbing" down every subject in calculus which is helpful.

The Calculus department at Iowa State is coordinated, so lectures will all cover the same topics at the same time throughout the semester. He is easy to understand, and will gladly go into detail on something if it didn't make sense the first time. He can go a little fast, but he gets through the material, so it's a trade off that has to be made.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a very good lecturer. Walks through derivations of formulas and their applications. Best calc professor that I have had. Really helps you to understand the material better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Personally I loved Barloon because he would explain the derivation of equations really well which helped me understand everything behind each equation instead of just the equation itself. His class is no more difficult than any of the other calc 265 courses, but it is definitely a class that you need to show up to everyday if you want a good grad.

Great professor who truly cares about being an effective teacher. Tests and quizzes given by him are easier than what other profs give. This was my first math class in 2 years, but I was still able to get a decent grade because he doesn't give impossible exams. Lots of homework, but if you use Symbolab it won't take as long.

Calculus is hard as is and Barloon attempts to take it easy and fully explains how to find the equation but if you zone out your done for. Quizs every week. HARD AS HECK midterm. Tophat is used every day. Hes not awful by any means hes just not the greatest if you know what I mean.

Barloon is the man! He is a great teacher and he's not intimidating. I had to retake Calc 165 and he explains concepts much better. He has tons of material for students, including homework, online lessons, and weekly quizzes, but if you take advantage of your resources (Student Instruction, TA help desks), I guarantee you'll come out on top!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Awesome clear lectures, nice guy, good class structure with weekly quizzes and online hw. Tests are stuff that is expected, and he also provides tons of resources/video lectures online.
Really good professor for Calc 1, takes time to break down mathematical jargon
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 5/5. Cares about the material, teaches very clearly and at a decent pace. Tests are more than fair. Always prepared for class and wants everyone to do well. Take him for math, hes the best math teacher I've ever had. I failed Pre-Algebra in middle school and have gotten to this point, and going on to Calc II because of Barloon.

Uses online program ALEKS for homework. Theres no other assignments besides ALEKS. Youll do a worksheet on resitation days with a group. Easy class if you just do the homework modules on ALEKS and do the sample tests before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Really good at explaining topics in class, and does step by step processes that are easy to follow. It's really worth going to lecture because you'll get tips and advice from him that will make the homework so much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: Amazing guy. Uses in-class examples and top hat questions that go together perfectly. I personally wish he could have taught every one of my math classes. He does have a very tight grading scale, but if you show up to class and prepare yourself for the fairly easy tests, you'll do well.
Go to class and pay attention. If you made it through calc 1 without trouble and calc 2 parametric equations, you will be fine. Take Paul if you can
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Paul Barloon is an absolutely outstanding professor. I never have I had an instructor who comes to class more prepared, & more driven to ensuring an easy A & developed understanding of Math. Go to class, take notes, and do the homework. I had him for Calc 1, 2, & 3 by choice after calc 1 because of his straight forward/understandable teaching style.

If you show up to class and pay attention to what he says then you will do fine on quizzes. Also participation is graded. His tests are fair if you study whats on his practice tests. Final and midterm aren't made by him and will rail you if you don't study hard.

Weekly homework, weekly in class quizzes, and daily participation. You can skip lectures and be able to still get a score for the participation from home. You can't skip recitations without missing an in class quiz. No curve for the grades and it's a tough course if you don't pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Barloon gives great lectures and does a ton of examples. He explains how most formulas were derived which makes them much easier to understand and remember. He never uses a chalkboard because he writes everything on a tablet. His lecture slides with and without his writing on them are available online so it is very easy to review for tests.

Dr. Barloon is a great Prof. Calc 2 is a hard class, but if you are having trouble, he is fairly accessible outside of class. His lectures are very helpful, and the exams he writes are extremely fair. Take him if you have the option to for any class.

Mr. Barloon is awesome! He explains everything super clearly and explains where everything comes from. He was pretty quirky and funny during lectures too. He seemed to care a lot about the students and was a great lecturer.  He did give a lot of online homework, but it was beneficial in the end.

Dr. Barloon does an excellent job making mathematics easy to understand.  The book was completely useless; if you don't understand it how he explains it, the book will only confuse you more. He really seems to care about his students.

I had him for 165 and 166; he is that great. He makes math easy to understand. Just know that his quizzes/exams center around homework. As long as you understand and do every homework problem, you'll do good on his quizzes and exams.
Professor Barloon is one of the best math professors here at Iowa State because he explains his work so well and makes sure his students understand it as well.

Paul Barloon is great guy, and for sure knows his stuff when it comes to calculus.  I found that it was not necessary to attend daily lecture, as I could teach myself just as efficiently doing the online homework.  The weekly quizzes are not bad if you study and know the homework. The tests were challenging, and graded without much curve.
Great teacher. Knows what he's talking about. Fun teacher and doesn't care what you do.
Paul Barloon otherwise know the god of calculus.  He has great lecture and overall provides clear cut examples and made the class very easy to understand

Very good at explaining problems and going over how ideas work. If you have never done calc before he goes through how to do all the shortcuts and explains all the steps he is taking to get to the answers.

I didn't do too hot that first time I took Math 165 so I decided to take it again. This time I got Paul and he made everything so clear to me. Where I was confused last semester, I was an expert at this semester. He is very clear and has online videos of each lecture and examples. I hope to have him as a professor in Math 166.

This class was very easy and this professor helped to make it so by explaining each concept clearly so even if you had no prior knowledge about the subject you were going to be fine. A great class and professor.

Great professor. He truly cares about his students. He adds more test than needed during the semester but they are truly beneficial to the student because you are always studying making the midterm and final less stressul. His test are very easy!
Good professor but tough grader.

Paul was a good lecturer, since that is all he does. I definitely does help in the first weeks to look at the  book, since you can find the formulas used in blue boxes, and if you can memorize all 6 of them you should do well on the first exam. He had a tendency to push back assignments if he hadn't covered the section material fully.

Dr. Barloon is the best math professor I had so far. He is very clear at communicating the material during the lecture and make sure you understand them. The way that he organizes his class is very clear. His class was one of the most highest attendance I ever seen in college. I will def suggest him if you want to really learn the material!

Some may say that his courses are tough. I disagree with that, calculus isn't an easy subject for many, so don't blame the professors if you don't work hard enough. It's college people, not high school.
Lecture is long and boring and he uses clickers so be ready to go to class.
He's one of the best math professors I have encountered. I think I'm getting a B-, but that is my fault because I didn't prepare as I should have for my quizzes and exams.
Fantastic professor, hope to have him again soon.

Very, VERY easy to follow. Is really great during lecture although it may get boring. Homework is very easy, allows multiple attempts so you should always get 100. Quiz every week is easy and only 2 exams, Midterm and Final.

Take this class during the summer!(I took it in the fall) Getting help from SI and the TA is essential. The tests are the worst.  The practice exams help, but some tests will have one question worth 20% of the grade and it's a random homework problem the is re-worded. Our class averages on tests were in the low sixties and there is no curve.

The only tests are midterm and final but partial credit is given on everything. Weekly quizzes are given by TA's and partial credit is given them too. Online homework once a week and clicker questions in class for points. Lectures can get boring but the notes help on the homework. Notes are posted online and never used the textbook.

Professor Barloon always had a joke to every class period. He is quite a quirky type of guy, which adds a creativity to the class. He fixes his mistakes and listens to e-mails. The tests are pretty hard, so know the material. he will extend an assignment date if we didn't get to the material yet in class. He was realistic and understood students.

One of the most straightforward professors at school. He only tests on material he covers on homework, so there are no surprises. Gives detailed solutions to homework so studying is fairly straightforward.

Amazing professor because he always tries to breakdown complicated concepts into smaller digestible pieces. created his own website with class materials, diagrams, and simulations to help clarify the material from the book. Extremely helpful outside of class as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Davit clearly cares about the content and wants to help you learn.  With that being said, the homework assignments take hours to complete and are much harder than the content on the exams or taught in class.  The exams are not graded very harshly, and he offers up to 3% of your final grade in extra credit if you complete Python coding assignments.

DOES NOT CURVEEEEE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Feels for you with sympathy but will not do anything to help 
I would not recommend

Mumbles in class, and illegible notes on the board. He goes all over the place and doesn't explain where he gets variables or equations from. GOOD LUCK

-many dropped the class too soon because only one of the 4 exams had gone in by the time the drop date rolled around and this was devasting for many students and ruined their plans making them have to graduate later due to how prerequisites worked. 
-the website was almost useless due to packed content it was impossible to filter
-NOT CURVED

Davit is not that great of a teacher. When he works out problems in front of the class he talks as if he's taking an exam. Like mumbling under his breath and just very hard to understand. The exams are very difficult and most of the time and personally class feels like a waste of time because it is very hard to feel connected to the material or understand what is going on. Working though problems in class helps some, but steps are hard to follow most of the time.
Great guy all around. Homework heavy.

Not a bad teacher. some of the derivations he does are kinda useless and we wont use them but, he will teach you everything you need to know for the test. has a pretty strong curve on the tests to expect 10-20% better than what you got without it.

Lecture powerpoints can be a bit hard to follow at class speed.

The material was presented in a very understandable way. The videos in class were a very good representation of visualizing the difficult concepts to understand, so keep doing the videos. I have no complaints about the class or material, I learned a lot.

reviews.comment: It is tough but enjoyable if you have a decent math background, do your homework, ask questions and attend the class and you will be fine, this course inspired me and I think I have a good understanding of the subject matter

just s9 so so  bad

reviews.comment: Qi Li is my favorite professor in CS so far. Her lectures are engaging, and you can tell she puts in a lot of effort into making the material palatable. Highly recommend.
Qi Li is probably my favorite CS professor so far!! Her lectures are engaging, and she makes the material very palatable.

Dr. Li has made this my favorite CS course so far! She's a great lecturer and explains things in multiple ways + uses top hat questions to make sure everyone understands. She is very helpful teacher.

This professor is amazing. She was very accessible through office hours. You can tell she put in a lot of effort in her lectures. Kind and caring Professor.

This class is manageable especially if you actually put the work in. You're given pretty much everything you need to do well. The class was hard. The professor was pretty boring and I found it hard to stay awake. Going to help hours was the most helpful thing in the class. Lecture slides didn't apply to the homework and I always had to get help.

Strict professor, grades are pretty much determined by clicker points. Felt like things weren't well explained in the class.

Good teacher but in order to get a good grade you must be able to put in the work. Attending class everyday will make or break your grade.

Teacher seems like he doesn't really know what he's talking about sometimes and confuses me a lot when he says things that are wrong. He's never even sure of his own questions he asks us....
He is an alright teacher with multiple choice tests. But there was really no way for him to make econ 101 fun. There is also a lot of reading.
good

Dr. Qing is great. Very approachable so if you need help just ask. I enjoyed the class very much

Nice guy but horrible at lecturing. Speaks somewhat softly and very monotone, has poor command of the classroom. Extremely hard to pay attention, most students looking at phones or pc's.

He was a great teacher. He leaves no fluff in his lectures, so make sure to look at the lecture notes ahead of time and then use the lectures to refine your knowledge. Clearly passionate about his work.

Average professor, but extremely easy class to pass. There is no other choice but to take the class with him, so make sure to try to get an A so that it can average out with EE448, which is much harder to do good on.

Had a great time with Que. Even though he can be hard to understand, his slides are still very easy to follow and understand.  The way the class is set up, as long as you do the homework and show up to labs, it will be an easy class.

EE442 Fall 23

Dr. Que is an okay professor. The classes are extremely short (max 25 mins). Excellent teacher. Easy to understand and with great patience.

Incredibly tough to understand as he has an extremely thick accent.  Lectures were useless and consisted of him reading directly from Power Points.  Material was not very difficult and grading was fair.  One of my worst experiences here at Iowa State.
Excellent teacher

Great teacher!

Nice Professor with good sense of humor!

I would definitely retake his class. I love the professor's teaching style. It was a three-unit course and the work was not heavy. He always let everyone work in groups except for the final project. He is always clear on grading which makes it so much easier.
It's an excellent introduction class for polymers. I don't have any background before. Professor Wang is always ready to answer your questions. Pretty enjoy his lectures though.

reviews.comment: He was nice and was open to help and give feedback but wasn't good at explaining things. If you're really confused he's always available to you. Otherwise good professor.

Professor Wnag can be difficult to understand during his lectures but at the end of the day, he really cares about his students and is a great guy. He's also an extremely fair grader and gives lots of feedback.

Extremely difficult to understand. Sometimes he just wont understand what your question is either and so you wont get the answer youre looking for. Hes a really nice guy and is trying but his accent is just too thick. Grading is also very extreme and sometimes unexplainable, even when asking him why you lost that amount of points.

Professor Wang is always helpful. He will try his best to answer any questions you have on troubling topics. He's also a funny guy. Makes the class slightly less boring. But the working load is really high. Wang has strict requirements on work in order to make you make standard answer. Wish to have less assignments.

Professor Wang is dedicated to helping students in any way he can. If you are struggling with something you can email him or go to his office hours and he will always do his best to answer your questions. ENGR 160 is a very difficult class with a huge workload but professor Wang will extend due dates if needed for difficult assignments.
VERY difficult to understand and a pretty tough grader on homework and tests
Took 160 with him, pretty awful professor.

He is hard to understand and doesn't give the most helpful feedback in his grading and a lot of learning needs to be put in outside of class. However, the dude is a great guy and is always positive. He really cares for you on a person to person level, will answer questions via email after 11 pm, grades easily, and tries to get you good grades.

This has been the best class I ever taken in Iowa State. Dr. Wang has nothing but a great teacher. He always has a smile and he is always positive. He is ready and willing to help when I was in struggling. He is by far the best professor I ever had!

I took his ENGR160 Course in the fall. This was my first engineering specific course and I was worried. At the start, Dr. Wang comes in with an accent and a kinda awkward persona and the workload is hard for a while. But, get to know him. He's a wonderful guy and he cares about you. He is a great guy. Utilize his office hours, and work hard.
please do not take his class.

Dr. Wang taught me and helped me along the way in a difficult, and stressful class of Engineering 160. I truly appreciated it. This semester was tough. But he lessened the stress for being a good teacher and guided me to become a better student. Dr. Wang is more than a professor, but a guider, a good person, and a friend. Thanks for everything!

This is a very tough class so if I had to pick any of the professors for this course I would pick him. He is very hard to understand but grades very generously and allows you to fight back points on anything. This is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken, so if you find a good group to work on assignments with and attend SI's you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: Qun Wang does not speak english very well and talks super fast. This class is based off of Excel and Microsoft Word VBA and Qun Wang has no idea how to navigate through ether program. All of the homework and tests are preselected and graded by the head professor.
Dr. Wang is a nice person. He is easy to reach and very helpful. I learned a lot from this class.

The WORST professor i have ever had in ISU. DO yourself a favor and just don't register for his class!! He can't talk english for good nor teach for good. No idea who why he's in the faculty. Not helpful and grades horribly.
Did not explain things well. Very few in class examples and little to no exam prep. Spent lectures deriving instead of teaching.

Not accessible outside of class. Lectures were not very helpful. Wouldn't reply to most of my emails. Homework was hard and he usually couldn't help without just looking up the answer in his answer key.

Professor Zhong was an engaging teacher who made learning a breeze. The example problems he covered in class were super helpful, and I loved how he encouraged independent and collaborative problem-solving. It pushed me to think deeply instead of just passively receiving information. And his lecture slides were awesome!

I had Zhong in his first semester of teaching, and he did a great job! He seemed a little nervous at first, but by the end, the lectures were very clear, and the examples were very close to the exam content. He even would give little hints as to the exam content and was always willing to award points back on exams.

Default response is "I have a meeting" when asked for help
Send an email w/ questions & he more than likely won't respond
Lectures are fast-paced w/o deep explanation & just examples that have been solved in the book
I HIGHLY recommend switching to Dr. Schofbach's ME 345 when you know you have Qiang. Very obvious that Dr. Paul is the best teacher

Prof. McClain is a very good teacher and responds right away if I have any questions. It was an easy course if you stayed on top of your work and participated in the group projects. There is a lecture, assignment, and quiz every week, but pretty straightforwardly, they were not hard. Also case studies and discussions. Highly recommend this class!
Never had class on Friday!
I loved Professor McClain. She was very kind and very accessible. She posts the slides and you only go to class 2/3 days. Friday's are a work from home day to complete your assignment.
No class fridays

I was appreciative of the way Rita set up the class, only meeting face to face MW instead of MWF. Team activities are the only required day to show up, and weekly homework assignments are easy to get done too. She was a great professor and was easily accessible if there were any issues, and very understanding!

Fantastic professor. Just go to class and you will be completely fine. The homework is very easy and always due at the same time and date. Tests were online and easy to complete. She does a great job in her lectures and cares about what she is doing.

Rita is such a nice woman who really cares about her students. MGMT 371 was super easy, in my class we did a lecture on Mondays, group activity on Wednesdays, and had no class on Fridays! The group activities were super easy and its a very low-pressure class. There are exams but they are take-home and open note. Rita is new to MGMT, but is great!

Classes are mainly lectures and some group work. Can get a little dry at times, but I think this is because I have no interest in management. Most assignments are pretty easy - as long as you put a little effort into what you're writing you'll get full points. It's really nice to only have class MW for a MWF class.

Rita is a great professor who is clearly passionate about what she teaches and she does a great job keeping the class engaged and not wasting class time. As long as you do the assignments at the end of the week (which you can refer back to the lecture slides to do so) this class would be pretty hard to fail. Also loved that this class was only MW!

Her lectures and slides are pretty simple and informational. You'll have weekly worksheets/quizzes to do, and a few simple assignments. 1 final exam which is made from weekly quizzes. She's a great professor and made the class really manageable for being in-person then switching to online because of COVID. Super caring and passionate about her work
She seems like she hates students and is not well prepared. I'm sure she's a nice person but I dread doing anything in that class. She doesn't really teach, so the class is pointless.

Easy class. She does take attendance so if you want the points, show up. Her lectures are pretty boring and there are group projects every couple weeks. Don't by the textbook because you probably won't ever use it.
Her tone is boring. She seems like does not know the field very much
Rita is literally the nicest lecturer and easiest grader I've ever had.

I've had Julien as an instructor for a few different classes but I've been working with him for my undergraduate research for a couple of years. If you have an opportunity to take a course with him do so, he is an incredibly intelligent and thoughtful lecturer.

reviews.comment: Julien Roche is a great professor. He makes the material easy to understand and lectures are swift and to the point. My only gripe is that there is very few things graded in this class. My homework scores lowered my grade so make sure you get good scores on them.

reviews.comment: An amazing professor that actually teaches so the students understand. Tests on are all on canvas which makes planning out when to take them very easy. Some hard topics, but he explains them very well.

Teaches difficult concepts in ways that are very easy to understand. Willing to answer questions and go through any confusing points. Lectures are clear and tests are straightforward, does not include anything not discussed in class. Great professor, would recommend!

He is an amazing lecturer, and does a fantastic job explaining difficult topics. I am not all that good at chemistry, but he made everything understandable for me, especially hard sections like organic chemistry and biochemistry. He lectures Mondays and Wednesdays, then on Friday you do a worksheet. Get extra credit for less than 3 absences.

I took this class online so I would not have to do meetings. I tried telling her all her times don't work for me, and she said I had to join to get a good grade, she also schedules things to be due at 5 pm, very inconvenient.

reviews.comment: I just wouldn't take this class. All of the "meeting" times are in the middle of my class times (the reason I took an online class) and she will NOT schedule around those. I have had professors file complaints with this lady because I am missing classes, and still nothing has changed. She's not a bad person, just not a good professor.

Weekly assignments can be difficult at times but a lot of answers can be found in the class material. Exams are online but you have 4-5 meetings you have to attend throughout the semester and participate in that are ultimately pointless.
Required meetings that were kind of bothersome since I expected to complete the class on my own time, but overall still a very easy class if you're looking to fulfill a global perspectives credit.

Typically, people take an online class to do it on their own time and not feel restricted by scheduled meetings. This is not one of those online classes if that's what you need. You must join several REQUIRED meetings 1-2 times a month. The assignments seem unnecessarily hard and time-consuming.

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. If you are looking for a flexible and easy online course, this is not it. You must attend mandatory Zoom meetings, which are all scheduled at the most inconvenient times. Lots of unnecessary busy work. Not worth it.

Was enrolled in an online course that wasn't supposed to have set meeting times, but she required attendance of Webex meetings. Even when I provided proof that all of my in-person classes conflicted, I was offered no accommodations and my grade was docked points. Completely unprofessional and unreasonable.
Don't take unless you have previous musical background, or have knowledge about musical theory. Class, is way too hard for what is supposed to be an introductory level courses and graded strictly.

Music 102 is not difficult, just complete the work and you'll do well. Tin-Shi is passionate about the class, and is kind of funny. It's a good elective to take and it's not going to take up all that much of your time.

She is the worst professor I ever had and when you emailed about questions she never replied and send you back to the lectures. what is the point of going to office hours. she is worst and will never take her classes again

There are non-graded review quizzes at the end of the modules. If you do those you will pass the exams no problem. You do have to attend concerts but there are free options! Granted she is a little hard to understand obviously, But besides that she is a wonderful teacher at least when she teaches what she is really passionate about. She doesn't care about musical ability just that you try . One of the best teacher  I have ever had.

I took this class online pass/fail. Writings can be a little difficult if you don't know a lot about music theory. You have to attend 5 concerts and do a write up over them. Teacher was gracious enough to give me private lessons after some health issues with Dr. Zeigler arose. hahahah! Tin-Shi is an awesome teacher.  Although she can't communicate with everyone very well, I really enjoy this class and I think Tin-Shi is an awesome prof:)
I took the class online and it was easy. Just read the book and take the quizes right away. Writings were easy.

I have her for an online course, but she must think that all of her students should have some magic ingrained music ability. Its quite difficult to get a decent grade on her written assignments. Never interacted with her directly, though.
She is fairy, fairy hard to understand...I didn't like her too much, but I got a good grade only because I had previous music knowledge.
One of the worst teachers I have ever had. Could not clearly communicate with students.

Nice and can understand your absence and mistakes test are hard but you get to take your time

Lectures discuss lots a different material, most of which isn't related to exams. The tests are very long and almost impossible to complete before the class ends. Tim is a very engineering minded person, in TSM 115 he tried to make all of the AST/ITEC majors engineers. He knows what he is doing, but he goes very fast. A tough but fair professor who wants to see his students succeed but also expects you to put in work. Too many questions in the test with not enough time to finish them. No one I know was able to finish the entire test.
