Everything you read is true. She blames students for the bad grades, even though the study guides are nothing like the test and never does review days. Go to class half the stuff on the test is what she says + top hat points  and skim the readings. Not a fun easy class.

If you are thinking about taking this class because of your love for myth, I recommend just not.

I took this class as an anthro major interested in Greek myth. Meyers often refers to Greek stories and pulls Roman details out of nowhere or vice versa. Don't take this class just because you are interested in myth. It's incredibly difficult and will suck the motivation out of you. Only upside is she can be nice?

Do not take Greek Mythology if you want an easy Arts and Humanities credit. Tons of work and reading, while Prof. Meyers' lectures are really useless, yet attendance is required. reviews.comment: I enjoyed CL ST 273 with Dr. Meyers. She was very enjoyable to have as a professor and always brought her all to class and gave good lectures. If you don't want to do around 15 minutes of around 3 days a week, don't take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved her Greek Mythology course! Although, if you're looking for an easy Arts and Humanities, this isn't really what you want. She focuses on how mythology reflects on ancient Greek ideals, not just reading the mythology. If you're expecting Percy Jackson, take a step back and reevaluate. She has really creative assignments - love this course!

Meyers is a good professor. I enjoyed her class a lot. Most of her assignments are reasonable and fairly easy. Being involved in discussions is really important for this class, but they are structured and generally pretty simple. A few writing assignments are kind of weird and feel unnecessary, but they aren't a big deal when put in context.

I am a business major that needed a humanities credit and took this course because it sounded interesting. Turns out, you spend about three hours a week reading and you need to remember every small detail about the reading for the weekly in-class quizzes. Wayyyy too time consuming if you're looking for an easy A. Professor is mediocre at best.

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. Her tests mostly focus on the female aspects of the stories and not the entire thing. If you are looking for a class about the myths look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Never has such an interesting topic been so boring. This course is more the study of the study of greek mythology. We study people who studied and analyzed greek society. Very boring. Also she tests and quizzes on topics that were never discussed in class and expects you to know it. She focuses too much on greek society rather than the greek myths.

Overall great professor. Only assignments are short reading responses and one essay. There are only a couple of online quizzes each on 3 chapters, a midterm exam, and a final exam (both online). Quizzes and exams are very easy if you attend class and scan the textbook. She has a pleasant personality and good sense of humor!
Her classes are so entertaining and if you show up you'll get to know here really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Read all of the sections she gives you, because specific details from those readings will be on the test. You should attend lecture because she gives out pop quizzes (6 per semester). It was a really fun class overall, her jokes are really funny and she's very passionate about her job. She is always willing to talk about grades and tests with you.

Dr. Meyers presents her material in mostly lecture form-a few small group discussions 5 mins long-and some short clips. Overall this class is a bit difficult but very interesting. Read the readings and take good notes-you'll get an A, but get behind and you'll truly regret it. She is funny and clear in lecture, truly a fun class if try.

The material is extremely hard, the instructor is extremely helpful and clear. You have to study hard to pass but it is not rocket science. Meyers responds quickly to emails. The course is well organized.

She is tough but not unfair.  You have to work for the grade you want and you will get the grade you deserve.  There's a lot of reading but there's lots of pictures and most of the text is equivalent to reading little stories.  the class is appropreatly difficult.

I thought this was a very easy class. I took it my first semester as a freshman and it was my best grade (B) of the semester. If you take notes in class, you don't have to read the book. If you read the book, you don't have to show up to class. I thought the exams were on-topic and fair. She's a great and funny professor.

Great professor! She's very funny and helpful. There is a lot of reading for this class but I suggest you do it all, lectures highlight the important material and quizzes/tests are not bad if you've done the work. The first material covered in class is a bit boring, but stick with it, it'll pick up.

She is an outstanding professor who went out of her way to help me learn the course material.  If you do the readings, pay attention in class and follow directions, you'll be successful and learn with her.  She has a good sense of humor and is attractive.
Class is unnecessarily difficult. Professor is knowledgeable but cold. Quizzes and exams cover random material. Textbook reading is essential.Lecture is dry.
She's really monotone, so it's hard for me to stay interested in the class, and I feel like the tests are way too focused on the reading and not what we cover in class.

Took it online. She herself doesn't teach it-they have a one Madeline Henry and her pre-recorded lecture+slides. For the class itself, it's not especially difficult but, because it's Latin, worth booking it. Fun language to learn. Professor Meyers is more of in an advisory/monitoring role, so i can't comment on what she is like in the classroom.

Prof. Meyers was a really great teacher. Yes, she has high expectations, but it is not difficult to get a good grade if you attend class and review the nice study guides she gives. I agree that she seemed a little cold at first, but she definitely was more approachable as the class progressed. Great teacher overall.

Professor Meyers is a really good teacher.  She speaks clearly and explains things as completely as she can.  However, the class is not easy if you don't focus on the materials, and she clearly states what you SHOULD be reading too.  And almost everything on the tests are from past sentences/readings done in class.  Mrs. Meyers does her job well.

Overall a pretty good proffesor. She's very straight forward and puts a lot of emphasis on reading the book. Seriously READ IT. A lot of quizzes and tests are based on readings in the book. It also helps to have an interest in the class otherwise material would just be weird and unfamiliar.
Class is tested over the most random material. Each quiz and test is either an A or a bad grade depending on your luck of material studied. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

She's very young.  She's presumptuous and full of herself, and insists on being treated like some sort of speshul snowflaek.  Has an inordinate fondness for group work, despite how useless group work is.  Revels in power, and does not hesitate to exercise it to remind a student of his or her "place."

Prof Meyers is a very good teacher, if not super interesting. Like other rater noted, she does seem cold at first, but she warms up. Her class is structured but it moves really fast and you must work hard.

Definately a difficult class, and she seems frosty at first, but will warm up later on. Very patient and understanding with her students in this class, and the same with every other class I have had with her.

If you have no previous knowledge of Greek and Roman mythology, do NOT take this class. Her tests and quizzes are over the most random material and I swear you could study for a solid week and still not know the answers. Also, reading is unnecessary. I managed to get an A- without reading the book at all. But its a stupid class, don't take it.
No idea where she pulls her test questions from. I'm a freshman in Honors, and I had major struggles in this class. Don't take it if you care about grades!

Don't take it if you're a freshmen unless you're really good at keeping up with readings and really interested in mythology. her quizzes and tests are really hard. i wish i would've read these reviews before i took the class so i wouldn't have taken it in the first place. if grades are important to you, don't take this class !

The material in the class was pretty interesting, but the way she tested over it was impossible to understand. The tests were really hard, and the average scores were really low overall. There are few grades in the class, so really try to get good test grades! She seems like a nice lady but not a very nice or easy professor.

This woman was ridiculous, rude, and disrespectful to students.  Literally expects you to read her mind on exams and doesn't bother to check to make sure the answers she inputs are correct.  My favorite lecture was the guest lecture on soybeans--nothing to do with Cl St. Ridiculous.

Average exam scores hovering around 60%. Little correlation between topics covered in class and the topics on the multiple choice exams. Seems like half the class dropped. I probably should have, too.
sets high expectations.
No Comments

Latin 101 is not as easy as you may think. As is with any language class, there is a LOT of information to memorize. That being said, Professor Meyers is probably the sweetest woman in the world. Keep in mind, I took the class in the summer online, but she was EXTREMELY lax about switching due dates around for you if you ask ahead. Great teacher!

Professor Meyers is a fairly easy professor. Attendance is mandatory with her, especially with the fact that quizzes are given often and graded quickly. She teaches the subject well and explains the best she can. One of the best professors I've had at ISU.

This guy sucks. Why give us a formula sheet but not the correct formulas, or why not update it so that it is REVELANT. If I had to choose to either be stabbed 57 times or take this class with this sucky professor, I would choose to be hit a bus and then backed up over again. If you think I am being dramatic, take the class and you will understand.

teaching style is very fast an incompatible with majority of students. Prepare to teach yourself just about everything in this class using an outside resource. I pray this professor never reproduces or tries to pass on his teaching style as he is an incompetent inbred failure of a teacher.

Be careful about the exams. He does give a study guide, and the first two are great. However, after the second midterm, the study guides stop being relevant. TA's in the course, and in other courses, have said that the homework is difficult and not relevant. They also say that the exam questions are either too difficult or too easy. Good luck.

It was rare that anything taught in the class matched or helped with the exams or quizzes. The homework was extremely unhelpful.If you get one mistake on the homework your grade drops, and it makes a significant difference on your grade. The professor is sweet and has a heart for physics but his teaching makes it very hard for me to have one.

The professor is hard to understand. He does show and walk through many examples of material in class, but most of the time does not show any understanding of how to learn the concepts. He cares about the students, but he cannot explain how he got to the answer, to understand it in any way. Just ask your questions in recitation, and they will help.

I am a good student who tries hard, shows up for class, and uses outside resources and I still struggled so much with this class. The homework is harder than needed and you miss points for answering incorrect. Professor does not answer questions kindly. Lectures not helpful but there's TopHat. He obviously cares, but it terrible at teaching.

His lectures were not very helpful in understanding the material. I think I learned more from the recitation sessions. He does not do a good job at describing what is on the lectures and the lectures do not really flow well. I did not pay attention much but I did try to understand what everything on the formula sheet meant.

You can tell he is passionate about Physics but isn't the best at teaching it. Has an accent, so can be a little hard to understand at times and TopHat is either really difficult or really easy. I suggest getting a tutor or you won't be prepared for the exams. The homework is 100 times harder than it needs to be. The recitation quizzes are fine.

If you have to take this class, get a tutor. He does not go through anything in class and is mean when you ask questions. His example questions are very confusing. You will not get through the homework without going to help hours. I put in a lot of time into this class which is how I got a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: You can tell that he genuinely wants students to do well in the class. If you attend lectures and take good notes, you should do well in the class. There are TopHat questions and those can definitely boost your grade. The exams weren't too hard if you apply yourself and study well. He made physics easier to understand than most professors would.

I really love this professor. He does so many demonstrations and tries to get the class involved by allowing them to do parts of the demonstrations. He walks through a ton of examples in class and does a ton of practice problems. When he does practice problems, he will ask for answers people got and he encourages mistakes to help with growth.
His lectures are useless and you never know what to expect on the exams (which decides almost all of the grade). Avoid him unless you want your GPA to go down by a lot.

Not very good at explaining material. I basically stopped going to lectures because he posts the PowerPoints on canvas and I don't feel that attending lecture is helpful. Tests are only 7 questions and there's only 3 exams so it's difficult to know what to study. I'm basically teaching myself the material with the textbook.

Lectures are very hard to follow. He often talks about very difficult concepts, however, he does not make sure you understand everything.  Clickers are awful and confusing. Tests are relatively easy. Yet, you don't really learn a lot.
Horrible teacher. Doesn't know what hes talking about, and not helpful and the tests are hard.
This class sucks. I learned nothing from it and the professor only made it more difficult for me to learn anything.
Clicker questions are not clearly defined

Hey was a terrible teacher, i literally learned nothing from his class. He doesn't use the book at all just power point slides. My advise is to get a tutor if you take the class with him. You get a lot of free points in lab which help your grade a lot. For the tests, just study the previous exam.
Very nice and always willing to help.
Great professor and truly wants to help you succeed.

He is very knowledgeable in his field, and clearly enjoys his job. The lectures do contain graded Top Hats, and the exams hold pretty close to the content and examples mentioned in lectures. Overall, show up to class, pay attention and you should be fine.
The best professor you will ever have he goes above and beyond for his students
Gives a lot of help and wants you to succeed and gives you what you need to succeed especially if you ask for help

This man sucks. he writes notes on the board in chalk that you can barely see and expects you to remember and explain multiple different ways on exams. If its not his way, its the wrong way. If you're not his favorite then mine as well be ready for a bad grade. Random quizzes sometimes in class so you have to go. overall bad.

Dr.Stewart is one of my favorite professors! He makes lectures very interactive, and he writes what you need to know for the exam on the whiteboard. He also gives opportunities for easy extra credit.

While he says you need the textbook for the class, I passed the class with an A without reading the textbook. Everything is on the slides.

He covers all the material and there will be nothing on the exams that he didn't cover in class. Read and learn the slide shows and you will be set for exams. Homework is easy and you can tell he loves teaching. He genuinely made me interested in the class. Best professor I have ever had. He wants you to do your best and sets you up for success!

Really great professor and enjoyed his talks in class! You can get extra credit for answering a question in his class. Overall, one of the best professors I've had, and he really does care about you being successful in his class!

Easy A. Exams are really easy- I've aced every one with only high school bio knowledge and little studying. Great lecturer and really cares about the topic. Fun to talk to in office hours- I've stopped by just to chat! Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are top hat questions for credit in each lecture.
He loves to tell super fun stories and kind of gets of track. He once ended class early because there was a bug on him.
Almost every question on the exams are taken from ungraded Top Hat questions asked during lectures. If you pay attention in class it's the easiest A you'll ever have.
Amazing professor

Professor Stewart was my first professor at ISU, and I loved him. You can tell that he's very passionate about Biology and shows why caring about our ecosystem is important. He is very kind and loves when people asks questions during class. Make sure to pay attention and not talk, because he WILL call you out in front of the class.

Dr. Stewart sparked my passion for Biology. He knows how to lecture well and genuinely cares about his students. Don't get me wrong, you need to study to get an A, but he's the best. If you have to take Bio 211, take it with Stewart. You won't regret it!

Dr. Stewart is my favorite professor so far. He cares for his students and is very knowledgable in his field. Labs are outdoors and very interactive. Lecture exams, species identification exams, and field quizzes are used but as long as you pay attention during lecture and lab, they're not very difficult. 10/10, would take this class again.

Awesome professor. Easiest class ever. Little homework but it's very easy. Lectures are easy to understand and the lecture slides were very well written to study with. Exams are easy as long as you study a but. Highly recommend his class.
He is willing to get to know his students if they ask questions and participate in lectures. He is funny during lectures, and I would love to retake his class.

Dr.Stewart's class has easily been my favorite so far in college.  In high school, I struggled with biology and after taking his class I am confident in my abilities.  His lectures are all interesting and very easy to understand.  He also just genuinely cares about his students.  110% I would take his class again.

Dr. Stewart is very passionate about Biology and you can tell by his lectures. The class was pretty easy in my opinion if you are studying the material before the test. There are 4 tests (no cumulative final) and they are only based on what he says during the lecture (some mastering biology and top hat questions are word for word on the test).

He is really nice and seems to genuinely care about his students. His lectures are very to the point and easy to understand. You have to do a lot of studying before the tests, there is a lot of information thrown at you. His tests were kind of tricky for me personally but overall not too bad.
Legend fav isu professor

Professor Stewart has easily become one of my favorite professors at Iowa State. He cares very deeply for his students and the topics he teaches; so much so that his passion becomes contagious. He makes sure to fully explain complex ideas in multiple ways to make a hard class easy and he will happily answer any questions you have.

tim stewart is the purest man on the planet and i just wish him the best in this life. he's so fun and energetic and always takes the opportunity to help anyone who asks for it. truly the nicest man i've ever met. 10/10 would recommend.
dr stewart is so kind and truly wants students to succeed. he is extremely helpful and willing to talk with you about the material and any questions. he is so joyful and funny!

Prof Stewart is fair and wants all of his students to succeed. There are top hat questions in lectures used for attendance, but those questions were word for word on your next test, so easy points. As long as you study for the exams and put in effort throughout the semester, you can end with the grade you want. Overall, AWESOME Professor!
I love this professor! He’s so enthusiastic about his job and always comes with a great attitude! Highly recommend his classes!!

Literally the nicest professor I have ever had, he is so sweet and cares about his students very much. He uses TopHat as participation points but the lectures are light and easy to understand. You only have to take notes on the lectures to do well on the exams. Had 5 exams and I got an A on all of them with minimal studying! Good luck!

A fun class, lectures were relevant to test questions, easy to pass if you take notes in lectures and come to class. Participation is grading, online lecture questions are accessible through the internet though. Highly recommend Dr. Stewart for the professor of choice in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's so passionate about (most of) what he teaches, which makes the lectures more engaging. Just generally a kind person who really cares about his students. I hope to have him as a professor again.

Dr. Stewart is a really great bio professor, especially considering the things I've heard about the others. He really cares for his students and has a passion for teaching. His exams are not too challenging; however the questions are quite wordy and at times confusing, so be sure to thoroughly read the questions.

Doctor Stewart is a phenomenal professor. He is passionate about ecology specifically, and his love for the subject encourages his students to also admire the things that go into it. He gives great feedback, is never afraid to answer a question, and makes the class manageable for entry level students. He is kind and has quality lecture content.

Dr. Stewart is such a nice guy, and you can definitely tell that he loves what he does. The lectures are very information heavy, but most concepts are repeated multiple times after he first introduces them. His office hours are helpful, and the live tophat questions make it possible to still get credit if you can't make it to a lecture.

Dr. Stewart is a really great guy who loves what he does. The labs are outside, so it's not always comfortable, but you learn a lot about identifying animals. There are two tests for each unit: one for the natural history side and one for identification in lab. Other than the tests, there are discussion posts for each unit and occasional quizzes.

Dr. Stewart is an extremely passionate professor who may seem slightly nerdy but is great to talk to and really loves what he does. Lectures can be slightly dull at times, but labs are awesome and fun. He is really easy to talk to as well.

I felt like he cared about the student's in class and never hesitated to go over material. With covid pushing it to online, I thought he did a great job going over lecture material over Webex. Pretty nice guy and very knowledgeable. Discussions were easy and all the work was straightforward. He had office hours in person and I'd recommend him.

Dr. Stewart was incredible! Super kind and helpful, especially because of COVID. You can tell teaching is his passion and that he wants you to succeed. I hope you have him if you're in BIOL 211. He will answer basically all of your questions. He appreciated participation and loves to get to know you!

So caring and passionate about biology. Never read the textbook and just watched the virtual lectures/went to SI and did great. Take with Stewart over other profs- he gives unlimited time on online tests and cuts the number of questions to only be the ones he actually cares about. Cares about his students and is really accessible. Great guy!

Dr. Stewart is super kind and it is obvious that he loves what he does! He makes himself available outside of class should you have questions or need clarification. Incredibly nice person, you're lucky to have him!

Dr. Stewart is a wonderful educator and human. He exudes passion for ecology and really gives you everything to ensure you do your best. I have yet to meet a student who doesn't love him. I would take another class with him in a heartbeat.
Very picky and gets defensive when you question him.

Dr. Stewart is a great professor. He is very nice and truly seems to care. His tests are relatively easy as long as you go to the lectures and study some beforehand. Tophat is important in this class. This class also includes some very interesting things.

Dr. Stewart is very passionate about what he teaches, and provides everything that you need to succeed easily. Most points lie in the TopHat, so attendance is important. Otherwise, a very simple class

Dr. Stewart is the best professor I have since been to ISU. His exam is very easy and he explains things very clearly. He give away extra credit pretty much for free. Just do top hat and take the exam and A is not too far away.

I truly love Tim with all of my being. He provides you with everything you need to succeed. PowerPoints are very clear and easy to understand. You do need to study but the SI sessions are really helpful. He wants every single one of his students to succeed and he is willing to help you personally if you need it.
As long as you have the notes, you'll do fine. He gives his SI instructor a copy of each exam as well. His tests aren't hard as long as you take notes of the top hat questions. Stewie is a real gem.

He is a great professor! He gives a lot of information in the lectures but theyre all from the PowerPoint he shows. The test questions are usually from the PowerPoint that he shares with everyone. He takes TopHat attendance sometimes. Great guy that teaches the subject well and knows a lot about it! Easy homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Stewart was a great professor for Bio 211. He makes the course interesting without over complicating the material. His lectures are great and you can tell how much effort he puts into making the class interesting while also sharing his experiences in science. This is the professor you want for Bio 211.
Dr. Stewart is a great professor who really loves biology and wants you to learn the material. The tests are straight off the slides. Study those and you'll be golden.

Overall a pretty awesome guy. Lectures were honestly boring but its freshman biology so, yeah. Very caring about his students. Overall great professor. Just study the material and you will do very well.

His class is so easy and dead boring, but a lot of the grade is on top hat quizzes. He gives some homework but it's not super clear unless you check the text book website. He just rewrites the textbook on slides and then reads from the slides so you don't really have to read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Dr. Stewart is great
Awesome teacher and awesome class! He really cares about what we are learning.

Great professor, knows how to keep the class interested, has a passion for his work and his students if you get to know him. He teaches multiple classes at Iowa State so if you have the chance take one of his classes. Textbook is not needed and SI is very useful, Steven's a great SI instructor.
A good instructor but can get off track sometimes when students ask questions. I havent used the textbook but the hand outs he gives are useful.

Easily the harshest and least approachable professor I've ever had the displeasure of taking a class for. Feedback is vague and inconsistent with his unusually strict grading and crucial grading policies are omitted from the Syllabus. However, the curve is considerably weighted in the student's favor. Switch professors if possible!

Stringent professor. No use of peers, other professors, or online resources; students rely solely on his notes, which lack proof examples. Feedback is vague. He refuses questions outside office hours and often belittles mistakes, creating a toxic environment. Curve was forgiving, with the final exam serving as a minimum course grade, which was nice

Tim was passionate, but he did a terrible job of managing the class. He did a bad job of teaching us why we are doing what we are doing/why it works. If he saw a student on their phone, he would take time out of our already short lecture just to point them out and make them put our phone away, which only wasted time for people trying to learn.

Dr McNicholl gets a bad reputation because he's a tough grader but he really cares about his students and you will learn so much more than you ever expected. I first had him for proofs, and somehow even though i got a horrible grade his teaching was what inspired me to get a math minor and continue exploring theoretical mathematics in general.

By far the most nit-picky grader I've encountered to the point of it being senseless. He doesn't give credit if a proof isn't written in exactly his method. If you can avoid him, do so, even if that means taking an equivalent course at a community college and transferring the credits.

Do not take under any circumstances. You will learn a lot, but his teaching style is terrible, and his student-professor skills are possibly the worst I have ever experienced. His curve does not take into account how harshly he grades and is not flexible at all towards any proofs that do not perfectly follow his own method, unlike other professors.

Dr. McNicholl will make you work for your grade. His classroom is very organized and clearly constructed. You WILL learn how to construct very strong proofs. Go to his office hours! The only reason Dr. McNicholl isn't getting a 5 is because his final exam was unreasonably difficult and dropped my overall grade an entire letter grade.

Dr. McNicholl's class was really hard, but if you make an effort and go to office hours, there's no way you'll do badly in his class. The grading curve is really helpful, and he does everything he can to help you succeed, but you also have to put in the effort. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. The homework assignments tend to be more difficult than the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: McNicholl taught the content in an easy to follow manner. I really enjoyed his writing all of the key points and working the problems in chalk on a blackboard, but you have to keep up while taking your notes because he frequently erases stuff that is still relevant so you had better have it written down. Harsh on phone use/chatter. Honest bloke.

Dr. McNicholl is the toughest and strictest professor I've ever had. However, he is incredibly caring of his students, super organized, beyond intelligent, and provides a lot of wisdom. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS!

If given the option, you WANT to have Dr. McNicholl as a teacher. His lectures are incredibly organized and inspirational. He teaches you how to write proofs like no other, and he cares A LOT about your learning. After a year with him, I find myself leaving class with a smile every time. Analysis 1 is hard, but he makes it very clear to understand.

If you want to skate by with an easy A, you will have a hard time in McNicholl's class. If you really want to learn the material and be sure you understand it, this is the professor for you. He expects a lot from his students and backs it up with clear, precise, informative lectures. He respects his students greatly.

I didn't like the way that the class was structured, group work takes up half of most classes and calls on people to go to the board regularly. He does a good job of working through proofs and making sure. He can be seemingly rude at times when you don't understand a theory but is overall a nice guy and seems to care about teaching the class.

I was a little scared reading all these reviews when I realized he was assigned to teach this class. However, it was actually a pleasant surprise. Yes, he can be extremely tough and a bit harsh but he's actually a decent guy once you get to know him. Go to his office hours and ask questions and more often than not he'll put you on the right track.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: McNicholl is a very bad professor. I don't know what is going on in his life, but he seems to take it out on his students. Horribly rude, condescending, and frightening. Knows the material and has in-class group work, but is extremely strict in every sense. Grading is super harsh; the curved grading scale isn't curved enough for the difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: McNicholl is one of the best professors I have ever had. He had these "recipes" for every kind of problem, and was very clear in every lecture. Before every exam, we had a practice exam in class, and if you think you did well you could choose to not take the actual exam. Idk about other classes for but Diff-Eq, Take him if at all possible.

His class was my hardest yet, but he taught me to write a solid proof like never before. His approach to linear algebra is very constructive and made me appreciate math that much more. He's pretty strict in all aspects of his class, and the homework for me was SO hard. However, he's kind and helpful, and he had a big curve. Very good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. Great guy, did a fantastic job teaching the material and did a great job answering questions during lecture. As great as he is in lecture, he is the worst professor to go to office hours for if you don't understand something. Do the homework and write down everything he does. Offers extra credit.

Passionate but clear professor. Only uses online code - no need for physical textbook. Homework is online, and is actually pretty helpful for learning the content. The only grades are homework and four exams, so very exam heavy. He is one of the best math professors I've had at ISU. He is very straightforward in his teaching.

I liked his format of lectures. He writes out everything so it's easy to follow along. He provides both "recipes" to follow as well as plenty of examples. There's HW once a week which isn't too unreasonable. The best part is that you get a practice exam and you can decide to take the official one or not based on the posted answers and your own.
Made you stay awake in lecture by a unique teaching style towards math. With "recipes" and lots of examples. He goes through why something works and you don't have to pay attention to that.

McNicholl is a great professor for MATH267. His lectures are clear and he gives multiple examples of every type of problem. His homework is once a week and is similar to example problems from class. You get a "practice test" two days before the test that can count, or get the real test which is very similar to the practice one.

The ratings tend to be biased for math professors as is but his seemed especially bad so I was concerned. Took him for dif eq and have to say, I am pleasantly surprised with the quality of the class. His lectures are well thought out and he practices them before class (you can see him doing it as you walk into class). Willing to answer questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: McNicholl is by far one of the worst math professors I've had. Sure, he's a genius and knows a lot about math. He grades you on a problem through clickers questions, then he teaches you how to do the problem, which is unfair. His office hours are useless, if you can't figure out a problem he sends you to your TA. He doesn't curve either, so beware.

He thinks Top Hat is a replacement for actual lessons. But is apparently the most decent Pre Calc professor. Thank god I read the textbook or I would have been screwed. You do have to go to class though for Top Hat questions.

I did not have a good experience with him in this class.  Tests are worth 600 points each and the final is 1200.  If you fail a test your best grade is a B.  Clicker questions were made to trick us.  Lectures were not helpful, I had to teach myself. I would not recommend him and I wish I had a better experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lets be clear, I was Top 2 in High School. Received 98% in Math, What we studied is Calculus,Pre-calc at that senior year. I passed ALEKS but chose to take precalc. However this course and this instructor are ridiculous, I expected him to solidify my knowledge but he frustrated my past knowledge rather than assisting it.
This professor just went over the homework that we did in recitation. I've learned more from reading the textbook than from listening to this lectures.

Only goes over simple concepts and assigns hard problems we have no idea how to do for homework. Also, waited until the day before our first class to tell us we had bought the wrong book and had to buy another one. Expects you to be a master of everything he teaches by next class. If you have this guy, transfer to another class asap!

If you wan't to understand math instead of just memorize take him. I  really didn't want to understand math at first but after a while I started liking the challenge and was able to start figuring out how to do word problems by myself. Take him if you want to learn how to think. Don't take him if you want an easy A.

Dr. McNicholl is a tough grader but he cares about your learning. He tries to help students understand--this is the first math class where I actually learned to do word problems. For the first time I understand trig and why it is useful.

If you ever get him as a professor switch out or regret it. This course is a waste of money due to the fact he did not solidify my Pre-Calc knowledge. This course is essentially Math 140 but with a different name. You don't need this class to pass Calc I (165). He is a passive-aggressive professor who will get angry with students for no reason.

If you have any questions regarding tests, homework, or clicker questions, he makes go to your recitation leader rather through him. I passed pre-calc in high school with an A-, and got a B in his class. He was not helpful and definitely didn't care about what his students thought. He was honestly the last teacher I would want teaching me math.

Even though i  took Pre Calc in high school and i did terribly bad in this class since most of his questions were trick questions and nothing close to what he was actually teaching. Never take a Math class with this professor.

Let's be realistic, pre-cal is as exciting as a toaster. Although McNicholl can't quite make math exciting, he does teach it pretty well. The lectures may drag on at times, but you'll always go back over it in recitation. Outside of class he is very friendly and easy to talk to. Go and talk to him during his office hours, he's happy to converse!

He basically has you learn everything in recitation and then your supposed to just have it mastered.  His clicker questions are all trick questions and the tests are impossibly hard and nothing like what he teaches.

Took this class freshman year, what a mistake. Didn't solidify my precalc knowledge like i wanted to before taking Calc 1 (165). He got overly aggressive at times, at one point giving a clicker question that every answer was correct and then got angry at the class. also yelled at two students to leave once when they weren't being a disturbance.

I have taken this course before in high school. He made it hard to understand and would not explain it in a way that was able to be understood. There are also no notes offered in this class or lecture organization. Quiz every lecture worth 30 pts. All exams are 600 pts. Switch while you still can.

His tests are like nothing he teaches and refuses to make review sheets that are like the tests. The content is taught in recitation and I liked how we learned it in groups, but then you're expected to be a master at it by the next lecture. Most of your grade is made up from the clicker points you get from lecture.

Einstein once said that if a person cannot explain something simply, they should not be teaching it, this quote was directed at McNicholl.  He is useless and absolutely incompetent.  You would understand math better if you taught it to yourself.   Does not teach.  Does not explain.  Does nothing helpful.  Egoistic.   Bad human being.
Terrible guy. Very rude. Will kick you out of class if you talk when we are supposed to be working on our own.
He does not teach what the class needs to learn, and talks to  long on problems the class got 100% on. Also, I can not understand him at all
He taught everything in a very confusing way.  While trying to make stuff easier to understand, it makes it even more difficult.
Terrible teacher. Doesn't teach you anything. You're expected to basically teach yourself. Doesn't lecture at all.
Lecture was good, but recitation quizzes were extremely difficult.

It it essentially a waste of time to go to class, apart from the free clicker points. He doesn't teach you anything. Go to the recitations and try to learn the material in the best way possible. He kicked two kids out of a 150 seat lecture hall for supposedly talking (whispering) while seated in the very back. Take a different class!
Not a very good teacher. Tests are not like what he teaches. Way harder than the homework. Sucks at teaching.
Considering I'm writing this review while in class shows how awful it is. If I wouldn't have done trig in high school I never would have passed. Stay away from this guy.

This professor is horrible! He does not explain things well, his handwriting looks like a toddler's, and he can't admit when he has made a mistake in lecture. The tests are nothing like the course work and the text book is as useless as he is for education. I enjoy math but he made every second of it unbearable.
Doesn't teach a damn thing. Take this class if you don't want to be told how to do anything.

Show up for Class!! you will get extra credit points for answering the clicker questions, right and wrong.  makes his lectures available online after class as well as his slides B4 class.  The tests are hard, and the TA that I had could barely speak english, which makes it difficult to learn.
Sometimes his explanations of things are not very helpful.

Words things weird. Hard to understand what is being asked of you. Has a tendency to assume you know something even if you say you don't know it. Fails to explain new concepts. Had no clue what the FOIL method was when everyone in class told him to use it. Somewhat condescending tone when attempting to explain something in class. Avoid if possible.
Very confusing, tries to reteach things to think about it a "better" way even when I already understand and confuses me on things I already knew how to do
Made me hate math.  Terrible excuse for a professor.  No shame in saying it either.  Avoid him at all costs.

While he knows the material very well himself, he's not good at teaching it. He is very confusing because he always tries to explain why everything works, which makes things more complicated than they need to be. Avoid him if you can.
He was a horrible professer never explained anything to me. For example "could you go over that problem again?" him-"no i dont have time for that"
Poor. Cannot explain clearly. Impatient.
never explain anything very well, and when you would go through the examples the students got the answer right more than he did.

I do not know if this course will be offered again, but hopefully it will be. The teacher was open to almost all of our questions, and he gave knowledgable answers or would research our question and respond to us later. One time, he devoted a whole slide to question I had the previous class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He will ask that you watch long videos ranging from 30 minutes to an hour, use direct quotes, only for 10 points, which is not worth it, and is asking a lot for a religion course in my opinion.

Professor Chilcott is one of the best professors I've ever had! The class was heavily dependent on whether you showed up to class, but if you did, you would have a good grade. I loved this class and Travis!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor. He is highly educated in the subjects he teaches, especially Hinduism. He is a very caring and supportive professor. It is important that you show up for lectures in order to receive credit on assignments, but it is all-around a wonderful class taught by a great professor.

This man is amazing. His classes are so easy that you just have to show up, and you will get credit for every assignment by doing the bare minimum. He knows so much and is super kind. Always willing to meet with you and give you everything you need to pass the exams on one easy vocab page. HIGHLY recommend this class!!!!!

Professor Chilcott is a good professor who is very knowledgeable and passionate about the content of the course. He is really picky about some things like assignment format and desk arrangements.  Assignments, quizzes, and exams are very straightforward.  Attending lecture is definitely essential to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you prefer to learn straightforwardly, Professor Chilcott is the ideal professor. His slides may seem bland, but his knowledge of each religion makes them compelling. You get more out of this class if you attend, and 85% of the learning activities happen during class, so go to class! Study guides tell you everything that will be on the test.

he doesn't apply feedback given and then also he covers so much information and the test is only 25 questions. He gives 5 learning activities you are able to drop- not miss more than 5 classes because there is one in every class. The provided slides are not helpful so if you miss what he says then you are stuck without knowing.
Lectures teach you everything you need to know, and the study guides he uses are perfect, he literally tells you what you need to know.

The exams were written to trick you and make you mess up. I had one exam that I received a passing grade on, however the others were below that. I used Quizlet and the provided study guides to prepare days in advance for the exams and would be shocked to get my grade afterward. I would not recommend taking this professor or this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does not grade his tests well and no one can ace them. He has 25 question multiple choice tests designed to make you mess up with tricks it feels like.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super good professor, made all the topics extremely interesting. While attendance is not mandatory, if you miss class you miss out on assignments in class, and missing class can cause you to fall behind!

As long as you show up to class and do the participation assignments, you shouldn't have a problem passing this class. The participation assignments are super chill and don't take up a ton of time, and you usually have a few days to do them. The tests weren't bad. He is approachable and always there to help and answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best professors I've had. There are a lot of participation assignments, but as long as you put thought into them, you'll get full points. The lectures are pretty interesting, and the exams are fairly straightforward as long as you take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class has a lot of participation assignments, but they are really easy and there is usually very little work to be done outside of class. He really wants to make sure his students succeed and has really changed his course to make sure that happens. Great guy, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a really cool guy who really knows what he's talking about and tries to make the topic interesting when it gets boring at times. He responds to emails really fast which is super appreciated. The classes get really long due to it being all lecture but he provides you with what you need to know and the information isn't too hard, just study hard
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy HW in the class, Easy participation points for class, cool guy (very soft spoken). Cares about his students, and gives out good powerpoints. Tests are very straightforward, if you pay attention in class and take some notes the tests are very easy (All Multiple choice). Attendance points and the HW assignments add up to a lot.

I enjoyed having him as a professor. He really knows what he is talking about and is passionate about it as well. You do have to go to class most of the time because he would collect the assignment due that week on a Monday, Wednesday, or Friday and doesn't tell you what day. I would recommend taking a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a good professor but the class is structured terribly. He has long lectures with not very good notes and he tries to cover way too much stuff on the exams. If you want to do well in the class be ready to study like crazy for the exams to do well. Also has very minimal extra credit opportunities during the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Chilcott is passionate about what he teaches. If you do poor on the exams, you will not do good in this class. There is a large amount of participation assignments in class, and if you miss more than 2 it will affect your grade.

Mostly decent professor, generally knowledgeable on the topic. Almost never has hard due dates for assignments (i.e. assignment due during ONE of the three classes in a week, doesn't say which class specifically) which made me want to jump in front of a bus on multiple occasions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great prof! He seems a bit intimidating, but he is really great. He doesn't make you buy a textbook which is awesome. The class has 4 tests and participation assignment and reading assignments. He does drop the lowest assignment scores which gives you some wiggle room. He also cancelled class occasionally & we watched videos at home which was nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher, easy A if you put in the effort. He really makes the class interesting and uses videos to keep interest up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you come to class and take good notes you shouldn't do too bad. We had 3 writing assignments (usually 4-6 page essays) and 2 exams. Assigned a LOT of readings. He knows the material pretty well. Allows for questions and answers them well. Clearly explains topics and different views. Uses power points and some documentaries.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I discussed with him as the semester started. I explained I worked full time at a nonprofit and attendance would be an issue. He said we would deal with it as it happened. When it happened he told me it's favoritism to allow me to make up the grade, even with appropriate documentation. But isu sports were exempt.

200 points class. Homework and quizzes are like 40% of the class. Rest are three exams. Shows documentaries and video for learning. Major portion of the class is focused on asian subcontinent religions. Not much work and pretty easy class as long as you do the assigned work. Very helpful professor too.

This class is out of 200 points, and thats it, which is what makes the class a bit challenging. There are pop-participation assignments, but if you're there you'll get full credit. There are short 3-4 question writing assignments due each week, but are super easy. 2 participation assignments and 2 writing assignments drop at the end.

He was super nice and the tests were so easy. I just read over my notes the night before and it was all basically straight from the lecture. He gives really easy participation points if you go to class and hands out a lot of extra credit.

I found the topic to be interesting so I took the class, He does a above average job of teaching the material, however can be quiet at times and occasionally boring. He is a nice guy and makes himself available for help. This class is very possible to receive an A+ complete assignments, and tests are simple if you do the study guide.

He is new to teaching and that was apparent. However, I think he class was extremely informative. He spend a lot of time on Hinduism but the majority of India's population is Hindu. It also helped us to better understand the other religions. Grading was fair and he was very helpful giving enough time for assignments and study guides. A nice guy.

Speaks quietly. Sit at the front of the room and you won't have a problem. Learning about India and its religions from him was a very good experience. He spent the first half of the course on Hinduism but it makes sense since that is his specialty and there is no separate class on Hinduism. Grades fairly.

First of all he is a very nice guy. Second, he does use a lot of hand gestures, which took some getting used to. Overall it seemed like we went very in depth about Hinduism but spent less time talking about other main religions such as Islam, Judaism, and Christianity.

He barely speaks loud enough for the whole classroom to hear.  He talks using MAJOR hand motions which is so so so so so so annoying! He does not explain things well, you have to teach yourself. He is just not very good.
He is a very loud speaker however, does not explain concepts well.  Many of the material needs to be taught to oneself.  Tests are difficult.

She is very knowledgeable, but this does not translate to being a good professor. After having her for all of my SciTech classes up until this point, I cannot say that I have learned anything impactful or memorable from her lectures.

Ulrike is very knowledgable about her field of study and will answer any question you have for her. That being said, she is not a great fit for a professor. For example? lectures that do not translate to exam questions at all consistently; consistently has disconnected thoughts and grades heavy on exams and has to curve it every single time.
Lectures were kinda bad and hard to understand when trying to look back at them but overall the labs weren't terrible.

Ulrike is extremely knowledgeable in the stuff she teaches. Her lectures can be somewhat repetitive. I found asking any and all questions I had to be extremely helpful. She really wants to see her students succeed. Her final exams are usually difficult but she grades them pretty leniently.

Ulrike's exam was one of three final exams for ARCH 345 and she made it excessively/unreasonably long for no good reason. The final exam was harder than all other parts of ARCH 345 combined, and because the exams were changed from in person to online, she felt that this meant she could make the final take as long as she wanted with no constraints.

Ulrike is a very smart and respectable individual and you can tell she has passion for technology and architecture BUT she is not a good lecturer. You will need to ask a lot of questions, converse with classmates, and reach out to other professors if you want to feel proficient in her labs.

I have had Ulrike every semester for architecture for the past 6 semesters.  Overall I would say what she teaches is very important and even though she can be repetitive, she is a good professor.  She is always willing to help out with office hours, and over all care about her students.

She was a better studio instructor than lecturer because of the language barrier. That said, she used interesting examples and didn't water down the topics too much in the lecture course, which I appreciated. Great studio teacher - fair, helpful comments, helped us make progress when stuck, high-yet-reasonable expectations.

Had Ulrike for both 341X as well as 240X, wasn't very good at teaching, read off the slides, but If you went to her office hours she was helpful.  Overall it more depends on the T.A.s you get for her class than anything else.  Tests typically also weren't worded properly.

After two semesters of Ulrike (Arch 357 and 458) I feel like I have learned nothing. Going to class seems pointless since she just reads off of the slides anyways. The topic itself seems interesting, just not when it's taught by her.
Needs someone to review her powerpoints and tests. German sentence structure doesn't really work when writing English
No Comments

He wouldn't care about saving a baby's life; he deprives that innocent child of the chance to grow up in a civilized European country through unimaginable betrayals of his relatives and parents, condemning the baby to the squalor of turkey.

Dr. Ustundag was very personable in class and very helpful. If you needed extra help on an assignment he would help you when ever worked best for me. He also held extra voluntary review sessions before exams that were very useful. Not an easy A but if you work hard, you can get it.
He is very willing to help you either in class or durring office hours. I went to office hours several times and it was a great help. I thought the class was pretty fun and not too difficult.

A more professional based professor instead of pure academic. A bit an accent but its not that bad. A bit slow on grading also but the homework's aren't too bad since we have examples for everything and the in class work he helps everyone work through. If you can grasp the programming the class is easy.

Took this class for a natsci credit, and it turned out to be super interesting. Took this during the winter session, and it was enough time. Can go at own pace, extra credit opportunities, and tests require a lockdown browser.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Reall chill class to get credits out of the way.

Being an online course, a lot of it was self-paced. Most of the coursework consisted of reading the textbook, watching the lectures, and doing assignments related to a given unit. Exams aren't too bad as long as one watches or attends the review sessions. I strongly recommend FSHN 1010 to anyone looking for an easy natural science course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor! Quick to respond to emails, though I never met her since it was an online class. Exams are taken in a testing center. How tough the class feels depends a lot on your TA. The exam review session is super helpful—easily the most important thing to attend. Extra credit is offered regularly and only takes a couple extra minutes to do.

The quizzes have nothing to do with exams, even the practice exam, has barely relation/similar questions as the real exam. Each exam is 4 modules worth of material. Sometimes you'll get a month in between your exam others you'll get 2 weeks between, while having the same number of course material.

The class was taught by 2 lecturers, who alternated topics; this made the class more difficult because communication between the professors was clearly limited. Exams were often difficult to finish within the time given as they were short answer, but previous exams were provided to study from. In-class discussions were helpful for learning.

This was a very easy online course. The textbook is set up very well and only has you read the important things. There are weekly activities that go along with the textbook as well as a few assignment before each exam but they are very easy. The exam review sessions are very helpful and basically hand you everything you need to study for.

Attendance was mandatory, but that is the only bad thing about this class. My grade was buffered by the use of TopHat questions, and she created a textbook for us to use specifically for this class. She was also incredibly understanding about my situation and potentially having to take the final early, so 10/10 would recommend this class!!

Lecture was really easy to follow. Professor Boylston is super organized and it's easy to take notes. She is very knowledgable on what she teaches. If you miss class, the textbook is the exact same as what she goes over in class. Assignments are easy and don't take too much time to complete

I took this course online, and I have to say it was easier than any class I've ever taken, including high school. The textbook she uses is pretty handy and has lots of review materials. I never interacted with Dr Boylston but the class itself was very easy and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a natural science credit.

I took this class as a gen ed to meet my science requirement. I figured FS 101 would be an introductory course. Wrong. The exams are difficult. The average exams scores came to 68%. When confronted about the issue from students, there was no extra resources provided. I would advise to not take this class if not needed.

Tests are in testing centers, so you NEED to study and take good notes. Do the extra credit, as it will boost your grade & she has questions in class] every lecture that is graded so you need to go to class.

The TA was very harsh when grading certain assignments, but if you talk to her, you will be fine. The exams are somewhat difficult if you aren't a FS major, and require a lot of memorization. Always do the extra credit in the discussion posts and the surveys she sends out because it will boost your grade at the end. Overall, good professor.

She was a great professor and tried her best to make sure that students understand the material, but this class is not easy by any means. Studying and putting in time and energy are necessary to do well in this class.

If this class is not required for your major or you are not interested in nutrition, dont take it as it is the most boring class ever. Boylston was an okay teacher but she is completely monotone and hard to listen to for the whole lecture. Otherwise she was okay overall, tests are hard if you do not pay attention but there is plenty of extra credit

Prof. (or Dr., I guess...) Bolyston is extremely caring and knowledgeable for the subjects she teaches. Very fast to respond to questions, and receptive struggles students go through. If you like learning about food in a chemical/science words sense then this is the class and professor for you! Lovely prof. and satisfied req.
She is very kind, and the type of professor you feel actually cares about their students.

I loved this course, Dr. Boylston was very a passionate professor which made this a fun and easy course to take. Lots of exams, but there were a ton of extra credit points offered which helped to make up for missed points from exams. Would highly recommend this course!

Professor Boylston was really kind and a very sweet teacher, shes very understanding of any outside of school situations that may pop up and get in the way of your academics. Her assignments are fair and as long as you keep up with the reading and assignments, youll do good in her class! It was pretty easy.

If you are taking this class for natural science credits and expect an easy A, I highly recommend changing to a different professor or class entirely. Exams are full with unnecessary trick questions. If you want an A in this class, you'll need to put in above and beyond work. Wish I never took this class. Took so much time away from other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Boylston is a great prof. Her lectures are very informative, and she is available outside of class for questions, and she is very accommodating. Do not skip class as the in-class discussions are for a grade and are very helpful later on. I can't say she is the most tech-savvy person, but she makes up for it on knowledge of food chemistry.

Clear about her expectationsguidelines and is organized. This lady is crazy good with technology (canvas, tophat, etc). She is understanding and wants you to succeed. Helps you and corrects you if needed, but does not make you feel dumb. She is a genius yet is such a normal person and kind. Knows how to teach material to people. She's such a mom.

This was my first class with Dr.B. She made this class challenging but not overwhelming. She is one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She knows how to teach the material at an understandable level. The discussions for this class were helpful. Overall, a great professor and person. She cares about her students like they are her own kids.
If you haven't taken organic chemistry in a while, brush up on it before the semester begins. Very interesting class, so make sure you go!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Terri feels like your friend's smart mom from elementary school that helped you with your homework. She is super caring and will casually ask you about your life and then tell you about hers. Exams are kinda rough but she gives partial points. Get ready to work hard though!!!!!! Gives points for top hat and quizzes that save your grade.

Terri does God's work by throwing you extra credit at the end of the semester to boost your decent grade to an great one. She relates well to students. She's able to explain and teach concepts clearly. Exams are tough but she gives you lots of resources. Lecture can be boring. Thought this would be an easy A but I had to work for it.

Dr. B is the only science professor I know that doesn't live in a research lab and has a husband, kids, a life etc. Super caring and is always eager to help outside of class. Gives practice exams to help you prepare for the exams. This is not an easy class but she makes it as straightforward as she can. She knows how to dumb it down for students.

Dr. Boylston is a fantastic professor and a gem of a human being. I took FSHN 311 for credit, and I've never cared for chemistry but Dr. Boylston turned my least favorite subject into a challenging yet enjoyable class. She's always ready to help you during her office hours (so utilize them), cares for, and always has time for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Boylston is a gem. She explains things very well and knows to make ochem concepts understandable. She is super willing to help you if you have questions. One of my favoritebest professors I have had at ISU. A lot of class points some from participation so don't plan on regularly skipping class. She is a very fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I liked the lab for the most part. She is understanding and super helpful, but she will go over every lab at the beginning which makes the prelab work redundant and it feels like HS. The design project is as hard as you want to make it, but if you are given a bad lab group you are stuck with them for the entire semester,including for the project.
I took this class for an easy A to meet a requirement but it was pretty difficult. Lots of reading and the exams are hard. I would not take this class again.
Good teacher and understands situations can come up, do all the course assignments and you will get what you put into it.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took this as an online course and Boylston replies almost immediately with any questions you may have. I was unclear of the test material because we covered so much and she helped me narrow it down which hugely improved my grade from the first exam to the second. Would highly recommend this class with her

Dr. Boylston was a great teacher.  I took the class online in the summer and could not recommend it more.  I had one test I would need rescheduled, so I could take the class in the summer, without screwing up my vacation and she gladly obliged. Other than that the class is relatively easy although I would say it is a large amount of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Each assignment has a grading rubric.  If you meet the criteria on the rubric, you'll get a good grade.  Dr. Boylston gives chances to revise some projects and resubmit for a better grade.  Overall, an easy course.

Dr. Boylston is a mullet-rocking, down to earth chemistry wizardgenius. She knows her stuff, but never belittles with her brain power. She was more than willing to meet individually to work through questions or problems. Dr. B is hands down one of the kindest and most understanding professors I have had at ISU.
Really easy, pay attention, study for tests not much though, do your homework, get an A
She gives lots of extra credit, but lecture is somewhat boring.
One of the BEST Professor!!!
He was great.

I went to get help during his OFFICE HOURS!!!!! and he was NOT THERE. I am very sad about it and now I have emotional damage and am going to go cry. I might need to get a therapist and ice cream. #BRBCRYING
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This man was fire!!! He made me feel so special!! I wish I could take him again!! This guy was quite literally the only person who got me through my seasonal depression... Go give this man a raise because holy cow I was flabbergasted at how good he was!
He was the best TA I've ever had. He was great at helping me solve problems on the homework and re-explaining things.
Zach was a great TA and helped me on all of my assignments whenever I needed help and prepared me for the exams.

This man was decent, he made me work for the class work. I definitely would not take the class again. He was very scary at first and gave a death glare but he was super funny when I got to know him. he should become a professor and doesn't hold a review session so I was lost.
He was great TA, he was very helpful and helped problem solve issues!

If you have no prior experience with Inventor, good luck with this class. Best thing you can do is lean on a friend to help you in class. He often leaves halfway through class and leaves his poor TA in a room of 40 people raising their hands. Don't expect him nor the TA to give any valuable help when you need it. Quizzes are your best friend.

Worst class I have taken during my 3 years at ISU. Fine for 170, but fluids was a different story. Concepts poorly explained, questions rarely ever answered in class, worked problems often done incorrectly or with skipping large portions of work. Takehome exams 6+ hours of focused work and grades took forever to get back with zero feedback provided

Tim is a nice guy. He is not a good teacher of fluid mechanics. To start, in many class sessions we were given one or more packets of notes. The problem was that we were given an overwelling amount of material and the tests were impossible. If exams were not online, I would have failed every test. The tests also took many hours to complete.

I'll start by saying, this professor inspired me... to create a rate my professor account and share the horror. Out of over 70 credits of classes at Iowa State, this class was the most poorly managed. The first quarter of the class was supplemented with zero lecture sessions, tests took 6-10 hours each, and the lab TA's grade the labs unfairly.

I enjoyed Tim as a professor for ABE 170, but EM 378 is a different story. The class is entirely on chegg, but there are 4 take home exams. Each exam can be expected to take between 6 and 12 hours to complete, due within a 24 hour period. If you are taking other classes, have a job, or enjoy seeing your friends, this class is not recommended.

Sunday is a sweet guy. He does his best to explain what's going on, and will do whatever he can to make you succeed. It's important to let him know if you didn't understand what he said in front of the class, because he will do whatever he can to help you. Sometimes he doesn't get his message across to the whole room, but individually he's great.

Class was pretty easy. As long as you read the green text or used it on the quiz and understood the information, quizzes werent awful. Gives extra credit which helped us. Didnt grade assignments which was irritating. Allowed us to work in partners on everything so if I didnt understand it my partner helped and vice-versa.
Classes was a breeze and I did not know how to use Inventor before I took the class. There is a lot of extra credit to cover up for any bad results you get.

It is very hard to understand what he expects of you. I do not mean his accent (he does talk quietly so sit at the front of the class). I knew Inventor well before this class and I could just see people struggling so much because of his lack of teaching. Would highly avoid because you'll have to learn on your own with no info on his criteria.

Had a bit of prob with him: I retook a test and he never let me know my grade, gave any feedback, or didn't even  posted it on blackboard until final grades were out months later. All that despite going to his office and emailing multiple times. The whole semester I  had no clue what my grade would be because of this. You'll be fine with him though

There are a lot of opportunities to get extra credit. All the answers are online for the quizzes. Home works  require you  to put some effort and time but are not that difficult. He also offers you the chance to resubmit home works around the end of the semester.
Thank you very much.
Does not teach and is very difficult to understand. In class assignments are too long.
He didn't teach. He just facilitated.

Horrible professor, can barely understand him! Quizzes are ridiculously long, and his answers are hard to follow. Don't bother taking notes in class, you'll barely be able to decipher what he is saying, and the majority of the notes aren't useful on the quiz. GET A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR!!

A quiz and a lab are due every week. One of the quizzes has 520 Power Point slides to answer 42 questions. If you're normal you won't have nearly enough time to do the labs or the quizzes. This class is very stressful. The amount of content is ridiculous This class is more work than all of my other classes combined and I'm a high GPA student...

Good guy, really wants you to succeed. Hard to understand sometimes, hard to know what he wants you to do. If take this class, choose a good partner! quizes were hard, but should get an A with a good partner.

Awesome professor. Being a computer science PhD student, having research interest in geo-spatial data, I took his class. The most interesting part I like is the virtual lab from ESRi, this gives you a hands on real experiences of problem solving in real environment. The project outcome turned into publication in prestigious conf.

Professor Tim is amazing!! The class is incredibly easy (if you're there on time everyday) The way he does his "quizzes" are rather strange... The material was extremely interesting. We really only used one book. He wants everyone to do well in the class but has a hard time conveying what he wants students to do. So ask lots of questions! Great guy
Professor Tim is a good guy. He could be rather frustrating at times though. This class was still an extremely easy A so i would recommend taking it
Excellent fella. His teaching style was phenomenal. He wants you to pass the class. If you have the opportunity to take him, do it. Easy A.

Spent so much time discussing the history of GIS and watershed modeling, the class never made it into the lab to do any modeling.  Teaching method and approach are ineffective.  Did not prepare own lecture material.

Did not prepare own lecture material.  Could learn more by reading a textbook than listening.  Does not comprehend time required to complete labs.  Tests were so terrible, all one could do was laugh.  Office hard to find, door not labeled; inapproachable.  Would not recommend any class taught by him.
Fun teacher, very nice guy, pretty funny too.  He can be tough to understand during some points during his lectures.  But he makes it easy to pass this class and he wants you to do well.
He's pretty awesome sauce.
Real Homie
Cool dude

Underbakke was an amazing professor. He is extremely caring and noticeable committed to his work. He is always willing to answer questions and provide guidance for students! His class is lecture-heavy, but interesting nonetheless. Would definitely have him again!

He was also my advisor for when I majored in Biochem. He is one of the nicest, most caring people, and he responds to emails fairly quickly. As for the class, I didn't show up past the first meeting and got over 100%.

Best professor you will ever have. He cares so much about his students and is the best person to ask a question, no matter the subject. His tests are take home exams, and he takes the time to leave encouraging and helpful comments, even if you dont have the answer completely correct. Every professor should try to teach like him.

This class had 5 assignments. 3 or 4 of which were for completion. There is no final. He uses top hat for attendance codes but doesnt use them. Eric is also very nice. He is very pationate and the lectures are about modern biotech after midterms.

He's a really good professor that knows his stuff and loves what he does. He genuinely loves his field so his lectures are not boring and he is extremely knowledgeable. Great person to hit with questions or just talk to. Amazing research and can explain anything with ease. Definitely take him if you can.
Amazing professor! He is the one to go to if you have a class related or research related question.
