he managed to be 5 minutes late for almost ever class, then he had to set up his powerpoint, so that was an other 5 minutes, so class would start 10 mintes late. added up we missed like 4 days of class time. he looked like my ex-boyfriend so bonus there.
Very thorough w/ interesting lectures, tests are hard, lots of opportunities for extra credit, really nice
No Comments
Interesting lecture, learned a lot.  Tests are very challenging but get a lot of help from extra credit.  Also a very good curve in the class.
hes cool! but he cant help if the material is really boring!
No Comments
I really enjoyed this professor. He is an excellent teacher and is very effective in his teaching methods. He is always willing to help and is very open. His classes are really enjoyable.
No Comments
Great prof - cute, funny, and interesting. Though the material can sometimes be boring, he makes the best of it.  Nice guy.
One of the best profs ever!  If you're into psych, he's the best teacher!  All the examples helped a ton!
He is very clear, it is just a really boring subject.  I don't like how he writes his tests, but he offers a lot of extra credit which is nice.
An easy class especially if you go to the lectures, you don't even really have to read the book to understand what you need for the tests.
No Comments
I really liked the class, but it did start to drag on after awhile.  Make sure to go to lecture because he gives out small  pop  quizzes.
No Comments
EXCELLENT prof, great class. he really made the class interesting by using real life examples. one of the best psych profs i've had
No Comments
He is so cute.  He looks like a gummy bear.

Very easy class.  He uses real world examples, even if they are all about his kid and get annoying after the fourth week.  But he does a good job of explaining all the concepts.  I actually learned something in that class...
A very nice guy.  It would be nice if he didn't use so many slides though...........
Good man
Excellent instructor. Loved the class.
No Comments
Good info, but he got off the subject all the time.
The goat. Nothing further Your Honor.
Has some really good notes for AERE321 and uses them for examples in class. Sporadic in-class assignments, thankfully they're only graded for attendance.

His lectures are good and cover the content well. It's not a tough class if you just pay attention. Skills from mechanics carry over nicely into this class. I recommend taking 321 in conjunction with 322, although I don't think you have to do that.
Very clear presenter, does plenty of practice problems in class and is passionate about what he does. Helpful during and outside of class and is overall a super nice person.
Nice professor. Always trying to help. Aer E 321 is not a difficult course, easy to get high grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. 1-2 in-class participations per week. Exams are decent if you take notes and study the review material. Group project is the majority of the course, with maybe 3 normal MC assignments total. Willing to help if needed, gives a lot of feedback on assignments. Presentation at the end. Overall, she graded pretty fairly.

Professor Zhimin Xie was a great instructor. The class has a lot of lectures and requirements, and at times it could be boring, but her teaching style made the material clear and easy to understand.The workload is manageable with about one assignment a week, and the group projects were enjoyable. I would take this class again.

I was shocked to see harsh ratings for Professor Xie. Class has been one my favorites this semester and her lectures are very simplified for a 400 level class. If you pay attention to lectures and study for the class, the tests are quick and taken straight from the lecture slides. Also well spoken and her lectures aren't confusing to understand.

She was a great professor. Yes, you need to attend class and participate occasionally, but she explains topics clearly and is straightforward. The first two exams aren't bad, and the group projects are pretty straightforward. The content becomes more challenging towards the end of the semester, but she provides good exam reviews in class.

Sherry is a very very nice person, and overall good professor. The exams and practice questions are worded in a very confusing way. Yet it is nothing too challenging about the way she teaches. I took Marketing 3400 with her, and I would recommend to take that class with her as it is very vocabulary heavy and she does a wonderful job explaining.

Do not recommend at all. Very confusing directions and grading, when giving feedback it seemed like she's making stuff up on the spot instead of following the rubrics she gave. Lectures are boring and she is speaks very quietly. Wording on exams is also very confusing. Overall, she seems like a nice person but is not a great professor.
Put into groups first week for semester long project. Tests are worded horribly, but you don't need to do well to get a good grade in class. Assignments are graded tough

AWFUL! Toughest marketing professor I've ever had, she was so picky with presentations about stuff you've never learned! Her lectures are also very dry and does not relate to the test at all. Would not recommend!
Professor has a passion for teaching but the lectures themselves are dry. She could use her knowledge to inspire the marketing students but doesn't quite hit the mark.

Is kinda harsh on people that participate in class for some reason. Get put into groups in the first week and you work on a semester long project together that are broken into parts. Easy class if you put towards effort.
Repeats a lot from previous day of lecture, however is a good professor.

Class consists of mini quizzes/excels for participation almost each class, 5 small group assignments mostly completed in class, 3 homework assignments, 3 exams, and a group project (presentation and paper). Very manageable!! Very accessible via office hours and email. Would recommend to my friends. Great prof to make a personal connection with.

She's okay, but definitely not one of my favorite professors in marketing. She talks super quietly in class and the lectures are not engaging and kind of boring. Exams are easy. There's also a huge group project that you work on for literally the entire semester so make sure you're with reliable people.

Sherry is very helpful, she has a bit of leeway to allow for outside circumstances. My low B- was "curved" up to a B+ after these extra freebies were graded. Heavily dependent on having a good group and group topic for the final presentation. Exams were very tricky and quite oddly worded, don't need to do well on those to get a good grade, But help

I loved Sherry! She can be a tough grader at times, but the best thing to do is to ask questions and be sure to understand what she wants for an assignment. Participate in class and make sure you are attending to make sure you're completing the in-class work.
Sherry was a very fun professor that did a great job engaging with her students. She is a tough grader but does everything that she can to try to help you meet her standards.
Overall a poor teacher. Cares more about results rather than ensuring students understand material.

Dont expect any help from her. You have an issue with your group she says sorry hope it gets better. Didnt learn a thing in class and showed up each time. Assignments are very few. Exams are a pain because once you go to the next question you cant go back and change it if you want or leave it until the end if youre not sure. Dont take her
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super rude, wont tell you what she wants in project but will put your assignment on blast in front of others and tell you what she wants after. I used google to learn since she wont teach you anything. Claims attendance isnt mandatory due to covid but gives participation points only by going to class. Waste of time, money, and you wont learn
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: gives group projects and my group did nothing so I told her and she just kept disregarding it. I was the only person in class and did everything possible. She grades real hard and when I explained my issues with the group work she said hopefully they get better. I learned nothing in class and had to learn on my own. Would not recommend. Dont take!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall great class and very reasonable to attain an A if you put in the effort and show up consistently.

Tough grader, mostly group work and projects. 3 homework assignments and 3 exams mostly based on the homeworks. She speaks very fast and tends not to repeat herself. Attendance is mandatory as participation is required and a large part of your grade. No phones allowed during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tough grader, runs through excel assignments quick. Assigns groups for the whole semester, only gives you up to 15 minutes to do an in-class assign. due by the end of class- 12 seconds over she considered submission late. You have to earn credit slips and she chooses who can earn them. She refuses to repeat herself. Project is time consuming.

She is the RUDEST professor i have ever had in my 4 years at ISU. She isn't helpful and doesn't make topics clear if you don't understand them. You need to show up as participation is a large part of your grade. There is a final project that is very time consuming and is a large portion of your grade along with a final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is easy and tells you what days you have in-class assignments in the syllabus but is a hard grader. She gave us a D on our final group project

She was good for thermo 2. Homeworks are good practice and she gives answers to them to make sure you do them right. Exams are very fair just make sure to study the in class problems and understand the processes. She does have an accent but you will get used to it. Overall just a very nice lady, try your best and you will do well.

Bai chose 14 different lengthy topics for just one chapter, and about 10 have an alternative version to memorize as well, all for a single 50 minute exam. Made no mention of what specifically will be on it either. The amount of memorization is unreasonable. No notes allowed, just you and a steam table. Nearly all of the grade is three exams.

3 exams are 85% of the grade. Homework 15% and very lengthy. She reads off the lecture slides and just rewrites the in class example verbatim. Handwriting is rough but she does upload the example to check out later. Takes weeks to grade homework. No syllabus covering exam material, you have to wait for the lectures to know.

Some exam problems were very similar to in-class examples. She posted in-class examples and PowerPoints online for those that didn't attend class. Textbook was used, but wasn't needed because she posted the tables on the class canvas page. Grading structure is very exam heavy, but the exams were very fair.

She cares about what her students are learning and wants people to succeed. She's super knowledgeable in Thermo, and it shows. I'd recommend going to all of her lectures as she goes over examples similar to what's on the exams. Her homework isn't too difficult but will reflect what she's been teaching and can be lengthy.

Her video quality is terrible. Maybe she will re-record for the future, but as of Fall 2020, many of the lectures had a high-pitched whine which made them painful to listen to. She also doesn't really teach very well in her lectures, so the book is a must. Her homework/tests are pretty easy though.
She is very hard to understand. Super thick accent and hand writing is awful. Do not take this class with her. Deza is much better and offers much more help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not an impossible class to get an A in. She uses example problems from class as test questions so it's very important to show up. She has an accent but it wasn't a problem for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a really good teacher If you show up to class everyday. Tests are literally straight from HW and lecture, she even tells you that if you attend class (most people don't show up to class because she a little boring) . Extremely fair teacher whose goal is to help you. Don't find many teachers like her in the ME department.

Bai can be pretty boring in lecture, but she is one of the nicest professors you will ever have. She really cares about the students and wants you to succeed. Test are mostly off homework and in class examples. Definitely take her over any other thermo professor.

In general, remember stuff from Thermo 1 since it directly builds into Thermo 2. She explains the content well, but does have an accent. She isn't impossible to understand though: just pay attention and you'll understand her. Just like Thermo 1, at least get some work down for all the test problems if you aren't confident in how fast you can work.

Class is hard, being there for 1.5 hrs is harder. She teaches really slow and it's easy to fall asleep. Tests are really hard. No practice exams or practice problems, you only have your homeworks to look over. If you go in she will love to help you tho. GET CHEGG. Go to class for example problems, life savers.

She is very clear from the start that she understands her accent can make it difficult to learn and encourages students to ask questions. She even stays up late the night before homework is due in case we email her questions. Gives 100% for homework if you turn every assignment in on time. Thermo 1 is a hard class, but she's passionate about it.
She has a terrible teaching style.
Straightforward grading criteria. All notes are posted online. However, Professor Wang can be difficult to understand at times. But not enough to make the course necessarily difficult.

This class has 4 modules and the only things that go into the grade book all semester are 1 assignment the exam, and 10 points for tophat in class for each module so exams count towards a huge part of your grade. She is hard to understand during lectures and very boring, also doesn't show how to do problems on the calculator much

She was very nice and would work with you if you had questions. It is hard to understand her in class, and she goes through very quickly, and the slides can be a bit confusing on definitions and anything not equation related.

I really enjoyed this class. Lectures very heavily but if you sit up front and pay attention you shouldn't have any problem understanding the content. All of her slides get posted on canvas which is a lifesaver when it comes to the homework assignments. Tests were pretty difficult but she lets you have a note sheet. Curved the whole class at end.
Impossible to understand and flies through the material. Tests are very difficult. The final test average was an 11.5 out of 25. Shows you how well she prepares the students.

She grades everything off of 4 tests, and they are worth 25% of your grade. If you do the homework and do better on it than the test, part of that test percentage gets switched to the grade of your homework. I put everything from the homework onto my note sheet that we got for the test and did fine. Then there was a 7% curve on the class at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Wang. She explains EVERYTHING, and she was always available when I needed help. Do the homework, it's not required, but you get a curve on your test if you do better on it than you did on the test, and its the only practice you'll get.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Four tests and four optional homework, which are very closely related. Also, you get a one page note sheet on the tests. Pretty straight-forward class and professor. Lectures can be dry, however.
Super easy class. I attended maybe once a month and got an A. Exams are almost exactly like the homework and you get a whole sheet of notes to use on each exam.

4 Homeworks and 4 Tests - very closely related. Hard to understand, but explains very well. Cares about your learning. Curves class to B at the end. I didn't buy the textbook, I downloaded it. Didn't look at it at all, though if you don't already know what she's talking about it may be hard to grasp. If you want a complete understanding by the TB
She is one of passionate professor in ISU. If you have question, just go to her office and ask her. She will explain one by one.

She is very hard to understand. If you go in for extra help to get clarity it helps a lot. Would recommend getting the text book since she is so hard to understand. I would try to take this class with another teacher if possible

Professor Wang is so helpful! Great teacher and very willing to help if you go into office hours. Grade is made up of 4 tests and they get harder every test, but all non-cumulative with a cheat sheet for each exam (that you can type!). Learned a lot!

Professor Wang was a great teacher, but very difficult to understand.  She is always willing to help when you did not understand something.  Overall, if you work hard to pay attention and do good on a couple of her tests, you will get a good grade.  First test is always the easiest.

Not the easiest class but attend class and pay attention and you should be fine. She explains the materials very clearly. A cheat sheet is allowed for the exam, front and back. Exam is pretty close to the homework. She is very nice and tries her best to explain the materials to her students.
Very nice teacher, really cares about her students. Not an easy A by any means. Tests can be kinda tough. If you work hard and go to class you will be fine .
Very easy class. Follow the slides she posts and you will do fine. Lets you use cheat sheets for the test.. don't buy the book.
the teacher is very nice.and, if you work hard in every assignment before each test,you will be successful in the test..and,it is helpful for students to take other finance courses next semester.
she loves teaching, so do her students.
excellent!
very hard grader, lots of overlapping projects
Do not recommend. Not helpful.
He can't do any hands-on demo, or any construction feedback!

Chris was a lovely drawing professor, despite the class being difficult he was always very encouraging and was willing to answer any question you had about work. You must take time to work on the class projects but it always pays off. I would recommend you take his class! He's a great guy.

Amazing prof. DSNS 131 is rough, but the professors are instructed to grade harshly... Chris gives great feedback and knows how to give criticism in a real but gentle way. Just read the rubric and you'll be fine, would definitely take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I actually loved Chris when I took his class. He provided me great feedback when I asked for it and when he noticed someone struggling, he came over to provide guidance. I think most of these negative reviews speak back to the student because Chris was great in class and he gave very in depth critique which was helpful.
Great teacher, would recommend! Just be sure to read the rubric and understand the concepts you are learning. If you have questions, you can easily approach and ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He'a nice in person and well spoken but he's a tough grader and doesn't give enough feedback for students to grow.

He not only grades tough, but he doesn't tell you what to fix when you have something in error he just kinda brushes it off and says it's fine. He doesn't provide enough attention to the each person to steer them toward the right direction, he kinda just lets things play out and if you did bad it's your fault. Where is the teaching?

Chris is a good professor. His class is easy and you're given plenty of time to complete assignments. He's also very friendly which makes it a very comfortable setting.

Complaints about him I feel speak more to the student than the professor. The rubric is easily accessible and he is willing to give advice if you simply ask.

He is a pretty tough grader, and even when he does give any feedback it's not really enough to be able to improve the drawing and get a better grade for the piece. I wish he grade a bit lighter and tried to make sure that everybody understood the techniques instead of grading on bias and things he doesn't tell you about.

Asked for advice on how to improve drawings and said they were pretty well done and should worry about other projects but proceeds to tick me off for things he didn't tell me when asked, you need to be like a professional drawer to even get to a 90-95 in the class.

He loves showing examples of assignments instead of teaching the class how to use certain materials. He grades differently than he gives feedback in class. He doesn't make you buy a lot outside of the portfolio kit you're given. He expects a lot of work to be done outside class but allows work to be resubmitted after critiques for some projects.
He's a good professor. Knows what he's talking about. He's a boss. Very helpful to learn

Awesome teacher!! He really cares about each student improving their skills and does a great job at breaking it down to better understand it. He gives great advice and feedback and is very understanding! He's also super funny and easy to joke around with... ask him about his band!

Chris is a PHENOMENAL DSN 131 instructor he is incredibly helpful with spitballing ideas for the more fantasy-based projects and is usually very constructive with critiques and never judges art based on how it looks but judges instead on the effort and quality displayed. He is also very accommodating and allows extensions on projects.

Chris was an AMAZING studio instructor. He was always ready for a good laugh, and he has a good sense of humor. He also grades not based on how well the drawing would look but if you follow the rubric. He is also always open to helping students in their drawings. If you give him the time of day and respect you will love him!

Chris doesn't seem to know how to teach drawing. We were often told to look things up on YouTube, and he often couldn't demonstrate the skills we were asked to learn by the department for the class. We would be given only positive feedback during critiques and yet were docked points in grading and not given specific feedback as to why.

Chris was good at giving feedback, but there are days that he will be more blunt than others. On that day, take most of the feedback with a grain of salt. For the most part, if you get your work done on time and show up for a class, you will be fine. If you need help figuring out something that works in your work, ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was always so fun. He lets you use a lot of creativity and do things based on a topic rather than everyone doing the exact same drawing. He was really helpful on critiques and was Never mean and made great suggestions. He was clear about what was expected of you. He grades fairly. I loved this class and he made it very enjoyable.
I had her for Acct 383. Avoid if possible
The class itself is not difficult, but she is not a great instructor. She talks relatively fast and with a pretty thick accent. You are better off teaching the content to yourself.

Apart from the accent, Jia is not a supportive teacher. Her lectures are not engaging whatsoever, and you will be doing most of the "teaching" for yourself. The words she says are not particularly hard to understand, but rather the content of what she says will not make sense because of her English. If you need help, be prepared to be laughed at.

Jia wants her students to do well and respond to emails quickly. Very helpful on the project. Unfortunately, she is very hard to understand and writes impossibly small on the board in the lightest color marker to work out problems. Test are weighted heavily. Go to class. Overall, super hard to understand, which heavily impacted my learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She a good teacher, definitely hard to understand so listen carefully. If you work for it you can get an A in this class but you have to be there. She will guide you if you are confused and the notes in this class closely correlate to tests.

Dr. Jia is available for help but almost laughs at you if you get something wrong. When I was turning in a test once she looked at it then laughed and shook her head. Very thick accent and not easy to understand. Would not recommend this prof, if you can take with someone else DO IT.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Jia is very nice and available for help, but for the life of me, I could NOT understand anything she said. She knows what she's talking about, but she has the thickest accent I have ever heard. She is very hard to understand, and that's really the only reason I gave her a lower rating. She really needs to work on her accent.

Prof has no idea how to use Canvas. The class is hybrid where one section is online and one is in person. If you take it online, be prepared to be left in the dark about almost everything because the Prof does not post anything on Canvas. 80% of the links to the lecture slides don't work. Also takes a month to grade things.

I took Dr. Guan's CprE 450 and 440x classes and found it very interesting. He is very lecture heavy and requires a simple paper you need to write throughout the term. He is a lax grader and it's clear that he is very knowledgeable and he will answer any question you have. They only issue I had was he rarely gave assignment descriptions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Guan is possibly one of the worst professors in the computer engineering department. His lectures are useless because he can't bring his voice above a mumble, and his lecture slides suck. Most people gave up on project 2 because it was so difficult. Oh, and he accidentally released the answers to all 3 tests before school even started.

CprE 308 with Yong Guan is a terribly organized class. He forgot to print enough copies for the first quiz and his lecture is practically useless. Read the book instead! The second project is a waste of time. The final was especially bad since it contained unanswerable questions. Fortunately, he curved it a lot, so it was easy to get a good grade.

Cpr E 308 with Dr. Guan is poorly structured. The lectures are dry and often he does not clearly express the point he is trying to make. Since the homework was not graded, it was difficult to stay consistently engaged. The quizzes and exams had some questions out of left field. He gives *tons* of extra credit though so getting an A is fairly easy.

Yong Guan is the type of professor who will make you forget what you already knew about the subject matter before you took the class. If you know something and want to take a class with him, he will make sure you forget and start disliking that subject matter. Can't sleep? Come to his class, you will, I promise. I also took CprE 308 with him.
He knows a lot, that's for sure. But it is difficult to concentrate sometimes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Yong Guan's tests require you to memorize his lecture slides. He take random attendance, and reads off of his lecture slides the entire class period. His labs aren't too hard. If you have a choice, I'd choose someone else because you'll probably learn more and not have to memorize lectures slides in order to get an A.

A laptop and a pillow where mandatory to attend lectures. The way to pass the class is to look over the answer keys for the HW the night before the quizzes and tests. HW isn't graded but quizzes and tests make up the majority of your grade.

Obviously a very intelligent and accomplished professor.  Unfortunately he seems very shy and his lectures are nearly worthless.  Class attendance dipped to less than five people on several occasions, despite "mandatory attendance".  Most of the time your time is better invested reading the textbook (since the slides are from the publisher anyway).

This class could be fun and interesting, but this professor makes it boring and hard to understand, the format of the class is horrible lecture slides with way too many non-relating topics, 2 exams, no homework to clarify if you know what your doing, so when you study for the test you don't know what to study or if you are even doing it right.

Professor Jia creates the lecture slides directly from the textbook. In some cases, the textbook is incorrect, and he corrects these in his lectures. The material discussed in lecture is enough to get a surface understanding, but I spent many hours reading the textbook. I found his lectures to be quite enjoyable, he can be quite humorous as well!

The professor just gives lectures without much concern for whether the students understand the material. Initially, the class had around 80 students, but after the midterm, only 23 remained.  I hope the professor will recognize that it is not important to provide a lot of knowledge to make sure students understand it.

His lectures were okay, they usually started off explaining the concept pretty well, but then went off onto some really complicated example that most students would not understand. At first he refused to curve or post lecture notes, but as he got more feedback he adjusted. He assigns a lot of homework but then only weights all of it 20%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most difficult class I've taken here, hands down. Class is 80% exams and 20% homework. Exam averages are very low and homeworks have unclear grading criteria at times. Not a lot of partial credit given on exams, if you get something wrong, you're done for. First class I'm going to re-take here.
Found the course fun even though tons of student complained about it. Needs some level of maths to grasps the proofs, and NA education does not provide that level of education for maths.

Dr. Jia is relatively decent as a discrete mathematics professor. It was his first time teaching the course in over 20 years and he was continuously flexible with grading as the semester went on. Moreover, he took student feedback very often and executed on what we said within a week or two. All in all, flexible, but difficult. I appreciated class.

The material for this class was very difficult, and the homework is hard. The other students are correct in saying that the course is structured off of the berkley aima course. However he provides a large amount of clarification and corrections in his lectures. He is very available for questions and clarification, and grades fair and on time.

I was one of my hardest course. The textbook is out of date and you can't relate with the topics as no one talks about them anymore. Yet, a lot is covered.
I heard he explains good. But when he was teaching us materials I knew before, still, I was clueless!

418 is a very hard class overall, but Jia is usually good about making good lecture slides that cover the material well and have examples to learn from that may not be in the textbook. Lecture slides were always posted to canvas and while assignments and exams were hard, the grading was fair.
He doesn't care about his students at all and doesn't seem to be interested in teaching. Should focus on research instead.

The whole class is literally from UC Berkeley. Although he knows his stuff and he is brilliant but he does not do a good job at teaching. Some of the homework problems are so unrealistically hard sometimes and there are so many problems that it takes up so much time in a week to complete it.

The entire course is pulled from aima cs berkeley edu, so if you want to learn about AI just go there and work on a lot of the exercises and read the textbook given, the professor gives little to no useful input and makes me question why I am paying ISU money to take a course I could access the material for free. Take a different 400 level
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Yan-Bin is decent but he falls short in many ways. Mediocre lecturer at best. Changed project description midway through project causing me to lose 10+ hours of work. Expected to do unrealistically hard homework problems sometimes. Calls out students for being late... then showed up a HALF HOUR late once. But, he is a fair grader and tests are ok
He is a really careful professor. His lecture is really logical, and you would miss lots of amazing knowledge if you do not attend the class.

Lectures can be a bit dull at times, the homework and the exams are what really matter. His exams are fair, but a bit challenging. They're similar to the previous year exams. The homework is extremely challenging, I suggest starting it as early as possible. Avoid procrastinating at all costs. Overall, I think this class is tough, but fair.

He is a graph theory teacher, which are 400-500 level courses. if you have him for 228, good luck since he will definetly be brining graph theory to his exams and most of the projects. He is ruining student's life without even knowing. He just shows up and leaves, does not care about if he is making the course interesting which makes you hate major
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His voice never changes, which makes his lectures really boring.  He goes over all the material at the same speed. Which is too slow for some topics and way too fast for others.  On the other side, his tests aren't bad, and he posts all his slides online.

Jia is a good professor, he knows his stuff and is generally easy to understand.  There's no textbook or hw in this class.  Lectures can get really boring, but the optional recitation is pretty helpful.  I mainly learned this class from the internet and blackboard slideshows.  Almost half of your grade is based on projects, tests aren't too bad.
Not very good lecturer hard to understand. Best of the 228 professors though.

Not always available for office hours. Has a little bit of an accent, but you'll be able to understand him after about a week. Always posts lecture notes online. Projects have a long time to complete, and he will usually give extensions. Gives review tests that are almost identical in questions to the real thing. Challenging, but fair.

A year and a half into my schooling and Mr. Jia is the professor I've connected with the most. I believe it was his first time teaching the class and he did very well if my performance has anything to say about it. I didn't do very well in 227 and we were assigned a textbook to read and learn from. Mr. Jia taught us well purely with lecture slides.
Good professor overall. Notice that this is more like a math course with a little bit programming.
Very good professor. All lectures are well prepared and very informative.
Strong professor with a lot of knowledge. GIVEN that COMPUTER SCIENCE is a quantitative field and not just GUI BUILDING...he is the right person to be teaching computer, including CS 226

Tends to ramble during lecture. Has a math background so we spend a lot of time on math stuff in the assignments- polynomial root finding, numerical integration, etc, which is annoying, and not what I'm interested in.

Key to get a good grade from his class: Study the practise tests that he handed out. Use the practise test as a study guide, and even memorize those answers - They really help when you don't know how to do a problem. Just put something down from the practise exam and you'll get something.
I do not recommend taking 229 from him.  He does not know Java.  Other than that, and some syllabus issues, he is a strong professor.  He just got stuck teaching the wrong class is all.
No Comments
No Comments
Yuji is such a nice person. He made me want to go to lecture and is a great, super intelligent professor! I definitely would take a class with him again.
Yuji was awesome!!

Furukawa does mainly read of his slides, but will also work problems out on the chalkboard. He is really interested in this class, and has demonstrations that are fun to watch. HW every week took a long time for me to understand. However, he individually worked through problems I got wrong on my test (when I asked). Some extra credit is offered.

Professor Furukawa is such a pleasant guy. Physics isn't always the most enjoyable subject to take but his lectures make it somewhat more tolerable. He is a funny, silly guy. His drawings on the chalkboard and the demonstrations he does always brings up the mood.

Physics can be tough at first, but I came to like his teaching style. He gave multiple in-class extra credit opportunities that were super easy. The practice exams provided are extremely representative of the actual exams. If the content doesn't click right away, go to physics SI or the help room! An A is 100% achievable if you don't mind algebra.

Personally I went to class 99% of the time yet struggled to understand him during lectures. He has a very thick accent which was a big barrier to my learning. The exams are VERY hard and I go in thinking I understand and leave feeling like I know nothing. He makes practice exams but almost none of the problem types in them are gone over in lecture.

Dr. Furukawa is a decent professor and doesn't deserve a less than 3/5 rating. You definitely need to pay close attention in lectures and Friday recitations. Also, try to learn from the homework and study hard for quizzes/ exams. He tries his best to make a good grade a attainable even if the material is confusing for some students.

Dr. Furukawa, although an excellent individual, is not the correct professor to be teaching this course. The class is not curved, besides raising exam averages to 75%. He offered basically 0 extra credit despite people clearly struggling with the material. His lectures are no help for homework or exam questions. If you don't have Chegg, good luck..

Furukawa basically reads off the slides, so lectures are quite boring. He curves the class average for exams to 75% and gives extra credit quizzes during lecture. The exams are very hard, but going over the practice exams is your best bet.

Professor Furukawa is amazing! I do not understand why there are bad reviews. I had a great experience! Physics is a hard course, but with effort you will get a good grade. Professor Furukawa is always available. Before the final he sat with me for over an hour to go over questions I had for the exam! I am so happy I had him for a professor!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Furukawa was a very nice professor that really cared about physics and his students. However, his lectures are boring at times (he reads directly off the slides). The exams are only 20 multiple choice questions and are not curved, but he gives out a lot of extra credit in class. Recitation quizzes are not bad either, no quiz on exam weeks.

Professor only reads off lecture slides. Homework is long and basic while exams are most of your grade and hard. Doesn't go over a lot of example problems and moves on quickly. Wont accommodate student disability (my friend can't use her hands, wont change test to online for her). Really seems like the professor doesn't want you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I did not have a great experience with this class. He does not seem to care about the students. Almost like he wants you to fail. He might be a great guy out of class, but as a professor, he is not very great in my opinion. If you have the option to take this class in the spring with S. Prell instead, I would highly rec. 

Immediate Access is used.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: exams are nothing like the practice tests. You don't get your test back to see what you did wrong or if there was an error with grading. All he does is read off the slides. there is no curve, no extra credit and no communication with the TA's so sometimes you would show up for the recitation class and leave 10 min after because there is no quiz.

I know Furukawa gets a lot of negative feedback, and I'm not sure how much he changed this course, but it was not difficult to succeed in. He gives out extra credit, so show up to class! Recitation quizzes aren't too difficult and most exam questions can be found in recitation quizzes and the old exams he posts. Do the homework!! Mostly math based!

Furukawa was wonderful for Physics 131x. He gives you all the materials to succeed and is always very helpful if you have additional questions. The content you learn is challenging, but he sets you up for success if you are willing to put in the work. He curved our exams and even gave us extra credit occasionally for showing up to class! I love him

Furukawa's exams are much more mathematical and have very few conceptual questions. He gives absolutely no extra credit, and if the entire class gets a bad grade he does not curve it at all.  Some students from my class got together and asked him if the class average was below 60% would he curve the grades, he said absolutely not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He reads the equations once and then moves onto the next with barely an explanation. Also you do not get your exams back to see if there was an issue with how it was graded. If you didnt write down your answers on the take home score sheet during your exam time you have no clue.

Terrible. Its a hard class yes, but he makes it incredibly difficult for no reason. Problems done in class are nothing like exams. Can hardly understand him & he is awful about answering questions, best to go to a TA. Syllabus not outlined well, I was .03% from a B+ and he doesnt round any grades. Doesnt communicate with TAs. Worst prof Ive had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although I think he cares about his students, Furukawa struggled to teach effectively. Exams are worth about 70% of the grade, and the practice exams contain none of the information that's on exams. Homework is long and confusing. His lectures are boring and confusing, and his strong accent makes him hard to understand. All I can say is GOOD LUCK
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were actually kind of interesting and good. However, the tests and homework often had very difficult questions that werent gone over in lectures and hard to find in the textbooks. Tests were late at night despite the class being online.

Online recorded lectures were extremely boring. He just basically reads the slides and does this for about an hour for each video. This class has a HUGE amount of equations so it gets extremely confusing. Thankfully this course is extremely curved (an A is 90%) and there are up to 25 ec points. Physics does not make sense, don't take this.

Possibly the most dry and boring lectures on earth. Puts in minimal effort to teach students virtually by only using powerpoint slides. Too many equations to use and most of the course is just manipulating them in specific ways which requires algebra. I find myself struggling to enjoy this class more and more as each week passes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was completely virtual this semester. Lectures every week with homework and quiz every week. Boring and not engaging lectures. He seems nice; just hard to get to know him with virtual. Virtual exams led to pretty easy scores on tests. Extra credit points after each lecture which is nice.

I have been a straight A student throughout college but this is the one class that dropped me. He is super nice and tries to be entertaining but it just doesn't work. Exams are extremely difficult, if you feel prepared, just know that you are not. My first exam was a 55% and I worked my butt off to bring my grade back up. The curve is really nice.

There are very few points in this class, so even if you do well on the homework, but bomb an exam, it's somewhat difficult to get your grade back up. Professor does a decent job of explaining things but goes into too much detail about how to get a certain equation that he ends up just confusing you even more. Difficult class, try to get a tutor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was very difficult to understand and did not know how to teach the class. Obvious that he is knowledgeable about the material but he does not know how to teach it to students. Exams are difficult, recitation quizzes are not quite as bad as the exams. I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yuji is very passionate about physics and tries his best to make class entertaining. The class is only out of 140 pts so you really have to try in this class. He often repeats himself in lecture so it gets pretty boring but if you don't go you'll probably fail. STUDY HARD FOR EXAMS they're a lot harder than the practice ones he gives.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. F is a nice guy, but this is the toughest class I've ever taken. Get the book & work through as many problems as you can. Exams are most of your grade. Two-hour labs & recitation are only worth 2 points each. Lab TA wasn't very helpful. I felt that the exams were harder than the practice exams. 80%+ is an A though so that scale helps!

He would be an okay professor if his grading scale wasn't ridiculous. 140 points for a 5 credit course makes it so easy to fail. Full length labs and assignments were worth 2 points. Doing badly on one test can cause you to fail the class. There was no give and the extra credit doesn't help. Only about 1/2 of the equations are provided on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Yuji cares a lot that his students understand what is going on in class and is very passionate about the subject. He is easy to understand and follow and all the info you need to review is online
A- is an 80%. Practice tests are very helpful. Has 2 pop quizzes for extra credit. Only 143 points possible, with 90 points coming from exams. Nice guy, fairly engaging lectures. Stylish trendsetter.

Prof. Furukawa was one of the friendliest professors I've ever had. You can tell he really cares about making sure that he explains the material and that his students learn. The only cons about the class was that the exams were a big part of your grade. The exams themselves were fair, he gave out practice exams too which helped a bunch!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Yuji is a nice guy, but sometimes hard to understand. Class grade is very reliant on how well you do on the tests. There are only 140 points for the class (including recitation and lab) and tests were worth 20 points (final was 30). Definitely show up to every class (there were 2 pop quizzes) and make sure you understand homework (for the tests).
Does not follow syllabus. Does not care about students whatsoever.
He's very frustrating to work with. Absolutely do not take his class

After reading previous ratings, I didn't expect him to live up to the amazing reviews. However, he managed to surpass them. Eric York was one of the most personable professors I've ever had. He is genuinely a nice guy, is very lax on deadlines, and understands the struggles of the student. If you can write a decent paper, you can get an easy A.
He is good at keeping the class lively, but could be more clear on his expectation for the last few assignments. Also, using a sign up sheet is better for taking attendance instead of him taking it.

I understand some students can have good words with him, which is fine. However, I hold the opposite view. His feedback before and after the assignments are incoherent.  Make sure you have him write down the feedback before due to avoid disputes afterwards

He is the best lecturer I have met at Iowa State. He made the class funny and also share up writing skills. Really learned a lot from him about English writing. He always gives me very detailed and clear feedback about every assignment, such a respectful lecturer. Would like to take more of English classes with him.
Eric is the MAN! He teaches you USEFUL things! I wrote a total of two actual papers this entire semester, and the final project (website) was a blast. One of the best teachers that I have ever had!
Best freaking English teacher of all time.  He is very enthusiastic about his subject matter, and it shows in his students work.  Get this professor, you will learn a lot and have fun doing it.
The best english teacher ever. He lets you revise your papers until you get the grade you want.
Awesome professor.
Easily the best English teacher I have ever had and one of the best, period! He is understanding about deadlines and flexible, easily one of the best at Iowa State!
Best teacher ever! His way of teaching brings out the best in students. I feel so glad to have him as my English professor!

This was by far the most interesting English class I have ever had. It was also really easy to get a good grade in the class because he let everyone redo all our projects until you got the grade you wanted. Also, he was very lenient about deadlines.

He is probably the best English teacher I could have hoped for.  He is very knowledgeable on a wide verity of topics, and really goes above and beyond to help students grasp communication concepts.  Great teacher in general.
The best english teacher I have ever had. Period.

I had him freshmen year, and it was the best teacher I had ever had. I recommend him to all of the new freshmen that need English 150. Truly an outstanding teacher. Very, very helpful. He makes sure that you completely understand  what is asked from you.

Eric York is the greatest teacher ever. he is very understanding and will help you with anything. he responds to the needs of his classmates and will push back papers if needed. he will always allow you to get a better grade on your papers too! very helpful and nice guy

Do not buy her required packet, you dont need it, just look at answer keys on canvas. She doesnt talk about relevant information in lectures. Everything on exams are mostly formulas that you will find in answer keys and reverse engineer it from there. Recycles questions from previous hws/quizzes. Work together with your friends and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although attendance isn't taken, there is nearly an assignment every class whether that's an in-class assignment, a quiz, or an exam. Her material is interesting, and not incredibly difficult to learn, but she repeats a lot in her lectures. She also does prepare you well for exams.
I'm fairly certain she had a personal vendetta against me. Hard to understand, and for a class that is an hour and a half, the material is mind-numbingly easy.
This professor can hardly speak English no one pays attention during her lectures
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Cannot miss a class with in class assignments and quizzes every class. 
No excuses or exceptions for a missed class. Lectures are long and boring. Language barrier as well.
Moderate class if you show up every day. Lectures are boring and all the information you need to know is in the lengthy course packet. The professor does not accommodate medical issues or absences.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class material and quizzes/in-class assignments are SUPER easy. You will never be tested on something you haven't covered in class. Lectures are very boring but the class is very easy to pass.

As long as you show up to class for the in class assignments you should be fine. However she makes you buy a $30 course packet that I never used and gave paper hand outs each class that I rarely looked at and were more just a huge waste of paper. Her lectures are boring but you will be prepared for exams and quizzes. There is no graded homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are 8 worksheets throughout the semester and that is ALL you are graded on, no exams or other hw. He didn't grade a single one until the first week of Dec so all semester my grade just said N/A. Classes are boring however informational and think you could definitely learn a lot of valuable information if you are interested in ET.

Dr. Youngs is awesome as he is so passionate about embryo transfer. I HIGHLY recommend taking the lab to this class ANS 334 as it is so hands on and is literally the only class offered in the US like this. This class has no attendance but has 8 hard worksheets.
Dr. Youngs is extremely knowledgeable in his field. He will answer any question you have with ease and make you think during class.

Literally only exams are the grades so don't screw them up. If you think you've studied enough STUDY AGAIN. There's extra credit offered on random days sometimes but he will never warn you. Study his lecture notes, not your own. His exam Qs are straight from the lecture notes. Study study STUDY for this class.

Dr. Youngs is truly an amazing professor. He cares so much about animal reproduction and is incredibly smart in the topic. While this class is difficult, he cares so much about the students and does everything in his power to help you out. Go to class and pay attention, it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Youngs is amazing! You do get graded on two exams, but he gives out extra credit on some Fridays. He goes over a lot of information each class period, so I wouldn't skip. Exam material can go fairly in depth, so studying is a must. His exam review sessions are very helpful, so I'd suggest going to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Youngs is wonderful! His lectures are entertaining and he gives us quick 30 second breaks when he knows his lecture seems heavy. He gives extra credit on random Fridays so go to class on Fridays. If you do well on the 2 in-class exams you won't have to take the final. Study early because the second exam is accumulative of both unit 1 and unit 2.

Got to class as much as possible. Gave out two 5 points of extra credit for the whole semester. (not on the friday before thanksgiving break). Only grades one exam and the final. Final was 150 points and made up of 110 questions. Read instructions on exam to find hidden extra credit. Intense class. Try to get help from people who already took it

I love Dr. Youngs! The people who complain about him are usually the less motivated students. He appreciates effort. Loves to answer questions in class and his lectures are really easy to follow and stay interested (if you find the subject interesting)... totally take his class if you're ready to learn lots about repro and study hard.

GO TO CLASS THE DAY AFTER ALL EXAMS OR QUIZZES EVEN IF YOU ARE STILL HUNGOVER! He gives extra credit once per semester and it can be worth 3% of your grade. If you are late to class, he will not give it to you. Get a tutor, study often, and don't expect him to ever be flexible or empathetic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Youngs was a nice guy but has very specific test questions, aka makes you really work for your grade. He makes sure that people understand topics and that things are as clear as can be. You will need to study a lot, I recommend and at least an hour a day to pass the class since you need to get above 60% on the cumulative final to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Youngs is by far my favorite professor. He appreciates professionalism, and if you would like to meet with him, he is always more than willing, as long as you address him politely & professionally. Although he might not be the most interesting professor, he really does try to keep your attention & he does a great job getting the point across!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr Youngs does not care about his students. If a student is failing and asks for help, he either responds by saying the student should study more or that they aren't good enough to graduate / become a veterinarian. There are only two homework assignments, no SI, no offered tutoring, and no study support from the professor. He does not care.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a good person, but as a professor of this class not so much.  It is really hard to pass if you don't go to ALL the classes. If you don't show up you are almost guaranteeing yourself to fail the class. You only have graded exams in this class. There may be one other assignment, but that is it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Doctor Youngs could be a good teacher if he actually cared. The problem is he doesn't even want people to come to his office hours and if you do he will make you feel really stupid. I recommend getting a tutor because he breezed through things and it's hard to keep up even with the lecture outline.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Youngs' sheep jokes/ puns are the best.  Lectures can get sort of boring, but it's nice because he posts notes ahead of time so you can follow along (or do homework at the same time).  His tests are very straight forward and I enjoyed most of the lab components we had.

I've never had a less accessible professor. He complained when students came to his office hours. He only puts outlines of his slides online. He told students he would put notes online to help us study and then didn't put them up until the night before the exam. Grades are based entirely on exam scores, which are all multiple choice and specific
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class is difficult.  He doesn't explain class  materials well.  Is smarter than you and he knows it, while making sure you know that.  If you struggle, it is never his fault.

After reading professor Youngs great reviews, I decided to take his class. This was a mistake. Youngs does not organize his slides well. He lacks the professionalism that a professor should have. Class is based only on tests. If you ask for help he will tell you to study more.
Youngs is a great professor! He clearly cares about students. I would definitely recommend taking classes with him.

Very intelligent and helpful when you ask questions. He is respectful and fair in grading. The only thing I hate is when he tries to trick you on tests with his letter A for true and E for false or something like that. Very good class even though the material was boring (I think). He doesn't post lectures and they are hard to follow in class.

Professor Youngs is a great teacher! Come to class and  the review sesssions. Youngs recognizes the students putting in the time and effort. If you look over the book, attend lecture, and review session -class is easy. Youngs designs the class so students can succeed. I TAed for him and I see he really cares.

Youngs is a great professor and knows the material from experience. Great 200 level course if you are going to vet or med school because you study many diseases/treatments too. Also he cares about his students' future. Most genuine prof!
FINALLY Iowa State has a professor than genuinely cares about the education of their students! Take any class you can with Youngs, he's incredible!

Youngs is an amazing professor. He knows a LOT about the subject and is able to impart the info to his students in an understandable manner. The tests are difficult, but if you pay attention in class and study for them adequately, there aren't any 'out there' questions. Great class.
The best teacher ever!!! This class was awesome.  Wouldn't take reproduction wth anyother teacher!

Dr. Youngs is terrible...just kidding. One of the best professors I've had here. I wish he could teach all my classes. He has a great sense of humor. He explains things so they make sense. His stories and jokes actually helped me remeber things vs other classes where they just take up time. Dr Youngs Rocks!

Thought this class was going to be really boring but it ended up being my favorite of the semester.  Youngs is awesome!  He knows so much about the subject and makes it interesting.  Loved his corny humor as well.  Tests are kind of hard because of fill in the blank but study the old exams and you'll be fine!

He is the best teacher I have had at ISU.  He made everything so interesting and also knew that it is hard for students to keep their attention on one subject for an hour, so he would give us a "break" aka points to ponder.  Tests were hard, but even w/o the old tests I got a B on all of them!!!

Dr. Youngs is the greatest instructor of all time!  I have never had an instructor keep my attention like this before!  I would suggest you find a class with Dr. Youngs and take it, regardless of your major.  I also had him before for Animal Reproduction and he was a great instructor for that to
No Comments
Actually teaches you the subject, not speaks it to you.  Tests are difficult if you don't have an old test to study.  Enjoys a good joke, and you just might see him at the bar.

Reads directly off the slideshow and does not teach. Will tell you the steps you need to do but does not explain them. Does not help you understand the material or problems but instead just gives you the answer. Gives in class exercises but just gives the answers instead of working through them or helping students. Disorganized with quiz schedules.

The content is difficult and the class requires effort to do well. The exams were hard, but she lets you use a notecard which helped a ton. She also gives out remedy credit on the workout problems to improve exam scores. People will criticize her because the class is hard and she moved quizzes to the testing center, but she was great at her job.

ACCT 387 was the hardest class I took at ISU, but mostly because the content is just difficult. Prof Zhang's classes could get a bit boring because she just lectures off of slides & does workout problems, but she is a super kind professor and really wants her students to do well. If you pay attention and study well, you'll do fine.

I found it difficult to learn from her throughout the semester. She used other professors' assignments, so what she taught in class/how she taught was different from what we were required to complete. I'd ask questions after class, but she seemed frustrated when I didn't understand something. Aside from this, she does offer extra credit and curves.

I feel like other students are very rough with Professor Zhang. She is the best professor that I have had my whole 3 years at Iowa State. She curved the class at the end and she would allow students to retake exams. SHE WANTS YOU TO PASS. Go to her office hours!!
She cares about her students and lets you make up assignments, but very hard to learn from. The exams are pretty difficult. I ended up getting a tutor, which was helpful.
Hard to understand what she is saying, very repetitive.

Dr. Zhang gave us retakes on all of our exams, quizzes, and written project for 387. 387 is a hard class, and she gives her students every chance to succeed with her additional practice problem packet w/ answers. You need to work hard in this class, and she did her part. Most comments probably are upset. She is very nice and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a kind lady but maybe has too much on her plate? Incredibly hard to understand, poor communication, rare email responses, neglects to provide additional clarification, minimal office hours, an insane amount of technical and grammatical errors online, sparsely hands back quizzes/exams to view your errors, and gives little to no partial credit.

In class she was very unorganized and hard to understand. There was a practice exam given by another professor she used and the way the problems were computed were totally different than what she taught us in class. Avoid this professor if you can.

She genuinely wants her students to succeed. She will help you out if you let her, I was a terrible student and did not deserve to be helped, but the second half of the semester she helped me out a lot. Her Powerpoint slides are amazing, if you read them and compare to the questions and follow along she makes it very easy to understand class.

She's nice but she's not great at explaining material and her tests (especially the final) are always difficult (and the questions are always trying to trick you) and those are worth the majority of your grade. I finished the class but I feel like I didn't really learn the material. I normally get better grades... tough class and not the best teach
Her notes are very vague and dont help with your understanding of material. She literally just reads off of her slides and adds nothing new to a topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Suning is a visiting professor at Iowa State University this year, she is very nice, and very smart, and knows what she's talking about, but she just doesn't really know how to communicate/teach the subject. What she writes on the board is very messy, and hard to follow. But, her powerpoints ARE AMAZING, THE BEST ONES IVE EVER SEEN.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Very theatrical professor, but I couldn't decipher the performance. I learned most of the topics from YouTube after the first exam. Slides are bad. Assignments are basically full credit for participation. Most of the stuff I got wrong on the exams was forgetting to put a briefly mentioned formula/topic on my cheat sheet.

This course/topic really shouldn't be that difficult. Lectures and slides are hard to follow. He doesn't give students any study material for the exams and blames students for the very poor average results. Small details matter a lot for exams and the grading feedback can be confusing.
Do not take this professor. The exams are uncurved with a 60% average. Blames students for doing bad even when it is over half of the class that is failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: COM S 363 is not inherently difficult, but Cai makes it challenging with poorly structured and hard-to-understand lectures and a tendency to blame students for their exam performance. This class shows how a relatively simple course can become a nightmare for achieving a good grade. Avoid him at all costs; just walk the other way!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful. Would never take this class again and learned absolutely nothing from his lectures. Lectures are scribbles over slides and assumes everything is simple to students when no one is understanding his lectures. Exams are graded way too harshly and a little mistake can cost you big time. Steer away from this professor.

Cai is not a terrible person, but isn't a good professor. His lectures are chicken scratches over slides; good luck understanding everything covered. Gives no additional study materials for exams, and they aren't curved. Often blames the students for the poor average. Understanding the concepts is not enough; exams are different from the homework.

I love Ying Cai. He has that paternal energy where you can tell he wants his students (at least the ones who attend lecture) to succeed. He gives lots of wisdom throughout the semester which I appreciate. The class consists of some DB projects, weekly quizzes, and exams.

This course is genuinely terrible, you will learn nothing useful during the programming projects and the exams cover implementation of databases (creating one like a caveman). You will have more fun learning calculus than anything covered in lecture, even if it is easy-ish, the material provided to study is inadequate and there's no practice exams.

This class is absolutely terrible! What I thought would be a relatively easy course has turned into a nightmare due to how this instructor teaches. I can hardly understand what he says, and he grades very harshly without providing proper explanations. Also, to add, he is not that helpful in office hours either. Two words, STEER CLEAR!
do yourself a favor and steer clear, can hardly understand, tough grading

Very bad, hard to understand. Doesn't seem to care very much. Sometimes spends a whole lecture on a single slide or two just to barely get a point across.  Really disliked taking what should have been a relatively easy class.

Ying Cai was hard to understand and had trouble getting the information across to students. Most students just skipped class. Exams were not hard, but small details were really important. The exams typically had the same questions as the assignments, so you kinda knew what was coming.

He would often tell jokes during the lecture, maybe he isn't really suited for those who want to be real serious. Tests were fairly easy, but they required great attention to detail. If you miss even a tiny bit of information or wording, they take off a fairly huge points. Would want to take him again for the lecture, but not for the exams.

Ying Cai was dismissive and unwilling to offer any help when approached in office hours. Frequently demeans students for his own mistakes. My friends have had the same experience when looking for help.

During a hybrid class, a student pointed that the professor was muted. Instead of checking, the professor insisted he wasn't muted and criticized online students for not showing up. Ironically, everyone in class could clearly see he was in fact muted.

His lectures are repetitive and unclear. If this class wasn't required, I wouldn't take it.

Professor. Ying Cai is very passionate about the subject and makes sure every student learns the concepts. Awesome lecture delivery and puts in a lot of effort inside and out of the class. Responds to all the queries and gives constructive feedback. Highly inspirational. Expects all students to perform well. I would recommend to attend lectures.

Lacks an understanding of the topic (database management systems). Is unable to explain any of the topics in the class without an answer sheet reference or lecture pulled up. Lectures were incoherent ramblings. Constantly makes mistakes and explains topics incorrectly. Put no effort into checking if assignments had mistakes before assigning them.

Super sweet guy, he definitely knows what he is talking about, but it can be hard to follow his lectures. Homeworks were fairly difficult, but the exams were easier. There was a definite lack of communication on instructions for homework and other assignments.

I think he is first generation immigrant, delivery can definiitely be improved, you might find him rude or experience cultral gap. I asked him if I can miss his lecture for career fair and he said "no you should attend the lecture". Provides online recordings of lectures with caption(sometimes), helpful office hours, random extra credits in class.

Talking based on my experience with him and this class. He is very hard to understand and is very rude when it comes to sending emails. One of the responses he made to me asking about where the practice exam was "Maybe you need to learn how to generate a pdf from it". I did not see a point for that. He gives reasonable time to start the assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Worst/least favorite professor I've ever had personally
Keeping list short because of word cap
- His slides are different than the other professor (Leaves out important information)
- Incorrect answers on quizzes and many mistakes on exams
- HARD TO UNDERSTAND
- Does not provide solutions to practice exam
- Little office hours 
- MANY MORE
Would not provide study materials for final exam because graded material that has already been reviewed multiple times is, I quote, "a lot for you to review and we believe that's sufficient."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Suppose you are given a concept to learn in this class. A typical lecture slide, homework, and practice exam will MAYBE have one example of this concept. When you get to the exam you are tested on that concept but in a completely different way from those materials, so it is impossible to know how to do it due to the lack of examples and feedback.

This class is very difficult to learn from. Exams have material and concepts not introduced in lectures. There is no way to prepare for the exams other than see basic problems that Ying doesn't care to explain. If you complain enough, you can get a practice exam he made up, but no guarantee he'll give you answers or work to learn from. Don't Do it

His classes were very boring. He writes examples on top of the PowerPoint slides; they are barely legible. I asked if he could make typed versions of the answers, but he said that was too much work. He posts answers for the homework right before exams; they had missing/different questions. The coding assignments are easy. Take the other section!
He clearly knows his stuff, but is not good at explaining things. Teaches as if we already know what he is talking about.

great professor, super flexible on projects and homework. Posted all lectures and files online in case you couldn't make in person. Most lectures were breakdowns of research papers and related to actual real world issues instead of just straight textbook readings.

He was hard to understand at times and I often had to watch the lectures slowly to understand. He teaches a lot of unrelated random material but overall the class is easy. The homeworks can be unclear in what they want but the tas were extremely helpful. Exams were just like the study guide as well. Pay attention to the basics and you'll be fine.

Completely incoherent. He has an extremely strong accent and talks in fragments of speech mostly. It's near impossible to keep up with what he's saying as his lectures don't have much structure to it.

Great professor! The lectures are super important. I didn't pay attention in the begining and did bad in the midterm. But as soon as I did that, the class became way easier although the material got harder because every lecture would be about a research paper. The projects were fun and professor was flexible. Highly recommended class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: After the transition to online, the class turned into a mess. The averages on the exams went from 80% down to 55% (Even with 24 hours to do the exam online), and the professor refused to curve the class a significant amount. The lecture slides were unreadable and the actual lectures were boring. Terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He has a heavy accent that makes it hard to actually listen to what he is saying. It is closer to a series of english words said together that may or may not makes sense, as opposed to a coherent sentence. His topics in networking will probably never be useful outside of this class.

Actively engages with his students. You can really tell he cares about his students understanding the information in his class, and he is passionate about the subject. However the lectures are a test of willpower to stay engaged during the entire 80 minutes.. If you put in the time to know him and the class, he puts the time into you.

Took this course in Spring 2019. Professor Cai is a fantastic lecturer. He makes complicate things easier to understand without loss of details. And he cares about students. The programming projects were also fun.
I came in with no knowledge in programming, but now I have a basic understanding. It's cool to be able to create programs inside eclipse and run them!

No feedback provided at all and email responses were not helpful. Lots of missing video lectures and no other access to the missed material. Material starts VERY slow and then tougher concepts crammed in at the end. Test heavy and the exams are paper and pencil proctored. No EC or curve. Interesting life/coding metaphors in lectures though.

Ying is a very good professor. He has a bit of an accent, so pay close attention in class. He is a very good lecturer and brings energy to class every day. He gives PowerPoint notes and you do not need the book, but it is useful to review and look ahead. Definitely visit his him and the TA's with questions and do the homework early and check w/ him
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor and cares about students.

This professor was amazing! I learned so much about coding and came in with no background.  I recommend doing the homework ahead of time because I went in for TA office hours many times for help.  There's around 10 homeworks, 2 exams and a final, paying attention in lectures is crucial and he notices and rewards hard work.  Gives 3 extra credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I like he talked about his research. Very insightful and inspiring.
Good explanation on basic programming concepts. The pace was slow but steady in building my skills. Learn a lot!
Like his style, really excellent in explaining tough concepts. I like his lectures on ER model.
Good professor. He made complicate techniques simple and easy to understand.
Very bad lecturer, much better in one on one tutoring. Can't understand him and he explains things very poorly.
