Worst professor I ever seen! He seems not very strong in his research area.  CS587 is too superficial for a graduate! Basically you need no math or CS background at all to earn A in this class. It seems that the professor is teaching pre-school kids not graduate students!

Good professor. He was hard to understand the first couple weeks, but you get used to it.  Knows his stuff and is very helpful. About 1 assignment per week with 4 major programming assignments. Book not necessary.

One of the worst professors I have ever had at ISU! The material covered is too low level and the coverage too superficial for a graduate class. Theory of distributed programming and networks is not a strong point of this professor. Read a good book instead.
Forget this class. The prof seems to eat his words rather than get the words out of his mouth. Could really use some English lessons. Does not seem to know the material he pretends to teach.
He makes class fun. He can do a better job by giving grades back sooner.
He judged your performance solely based on your assignment and would not take time to help his students after class. Will not take his class again.

No Exams - at all. Two group assignments for course. Lectures on formula & theory, but never mentions software required. Mentions brushing up on Python in a blurb announcement. Nothing about how students need to be more than beginning Python developers. He does the same when he requires Weka. It's been over a month & still no grades posted.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Zachary was my favorite instructor of the semester, by far. He was very knowledgeable without the common flaw of knowledgeable people, being condescending. Whenever I had a question, he gave a great response. I also appreciated the humor of the class while maintaining a professional demeanor.
Love love love Zach! He made the atmosphere conducive to making friends and sharing your writing. Even if you aren't a writer, you will enjoy this class. He makes it easy to write.
I really like this professor. He very understands how students are anxious about public speaking and gives much time to each speaker. I feel I'm better at public speaking after taking this class.

Good guy. I am not a great speaker but he was very encouraging throughout the class and gave good feedback after every speech. He grades very leniently, so hard not to get a good grade and his lectures are fun too.
Zach is the kindest, most down to Earth professor or teacher in general that I've ever had. He truly cares about his students. He wants us to learn but not at the cost of our mental health
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: If I could take every class of Zach's, I would. He's the most positive, uplifting instructor on this campus, and probably ever. If you have the opportunity to take a class of his, just do it. He's really just the best person.

He's a super considerate professor. The class itself is super easy as long as you do the speeches. He understands speech anxiety and doesn't knock students down. Super easy grader and the homework he gives is doable for sure. Gives plenty of time for assignments and in class prep for speeches.

Idk why everyone is afraid of Zoz. He expects you do assignments and in return we have take home tests with a portfolio that gives you an auto 30 percent on each exam. You can resubmit assignments for regrading too so don't be scared by the syllabus.

I don't know what's up with the Steve Zoz fear mongering. There was definitely a ton of homework, but the due dates are flexible, and you can redo assignments if you make errors and get full credit. Exams are take home, this class is an easy A if you can do busy work. Statics is definitely more work idk what everyone is talking about.

You don't learn anything in lecture and he expects you to learn from the homework. At least 10 hours of homework a week, and if you miss one assignment, expect your grade to drop. The grading policy is very unclear, and he said in his first lecture, "Grading can even be based on what he's feeling that day." The other classes are said to be easier.

I had Professor Zoz for ME 231 and ME 332. While there's a lot of homework, it's helpful since answers are provided and you solve the problems yourself learning the steps. His IC problems reinforce learning from class. He's quite flexible with deadlines if you communicate, and group projects are manageable with Excel and great teamwork.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Thermo 2 in my 4th semester at ISU. At that point I had taken Statics, Materials, Diff EQ, Thermo 1, Physics 1&2, and more. I probably spent more time on homework for Thermo 2 with Zoz than I had on ALL OF THOSE CLASSES COMBINED. Probably 10-12 hours of homework a week. Unclear grading criteria, nitpicky about formatting. Lectures were good.

Do not get lured by the fact that he assigns take home exams. The amount of work he hands out does not underline what a 3 credit course should be. I got a 2/12 on a group project with 0 feedback from him. I emailed him and he responded with something along the lines of "double checked, looked fair." No rubric or criteria, vague instructions.
Could have been worse. Lots of homework. Subpar grades on homework seem to have little effect on your final grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not the easiest class, but if you show up and do what you need to passing with a decent score is simple enough. Assignments can get long, and for big group projects other people can really make it break your experience, but Zoz along with the TAs are easily accessible and ready to help. Super flexible class as long as you put in effort. No final.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He relied on his TA tons. If you miss an assignment, it's his rule that it's a negative grade when you ask about it, he bounces you back and forth from himself to the TA. Little guidance and expects you to know the program. Expects perfection if not, you will see point loss or a negative grade. I had to ask for my points back.

Professor Zoz is a professor that is willing to work with you. He is lenient with due dates and etc. He's course work is definitely challenging, but engaging. Stay on top of the due dates and pay attention to the lesson plans. If you put the effort in you will succeed. He is teaching style might not be for everyone, but it worked great for me.
Terrible grading system. Minor mistakes result in massive grade loss.

READ: For ME 449 Zoz was very knowledgeable about the subject. He goes very in-depth in every portion of an engine which is nice if you like engines. There is quite a bit of homework, no exams or quizzes. The lecture portion is very easy. If Fynn Reinbacher is your lab TA switch out immediately! Lab portion is super difficult!

I took this professor because I can deal with a lot of homework but the sheer amount of homework is crazy. This class is about as much work as 2 calc classes. He also does "subjective grading" which is just code for him giving you whatever grade he feels like without having to justify it. He also is super monotone so its impossible to pay attention
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Zoz really did not adapt to covid well. Learning in this class is hard because it is quite easy to fall behind and miss a ton during the lectures. Insanely tough grader, dont know anyone who got an A in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: On the surface, Dr. Zoz is a pretty standard professor. He gives a decent amount of homework, gives normal lectures, and is mostly accessible outside of class. Dr. Zoz's interactions with your reflect how much effort you put in. If you show Dr. Zoz you are invested in the class, he will also make the effort to help you succeed.

LOTS of homework, but it pays off. Homework is a large part of your grade, so if you work hard, you'll be rewarded and most likely do better on the exams. Lectures are dry like most ME lectures. He is very accessible outside of class which is great so you can ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Material is difficult, but Zoz presents all required information and is very lenient on the ways you choose to succeed (very lenient on due dates etc.) Easy to fall behind and don't expect Zoz to slow down to help you, but if you stay up to date and study the material you will succeed. Tests are rather stressful but doable if you prepare correctly.

Professor Zoz is the worst professor I have ever had. He has never taught before this semester, and he has absolutely no idea how to teach. He uses lecture slides from outside sources and looks at them for the first time in class. He often doesn't understand how to do the problems and just tells us to figure it out in the homework.

He has no knowledge of what he is teaching. When asked to explain one of the problems he asked the class to do, he laughed at someone expecting him to put in work. His lectures are useless, he refuses to explain how to do problems related to the tests or homework. You will have to learn everything outside of class and his homeworks are too long.
Large Language barrier. Lectures don't make any sense, but if you follow the material on your own you can learn it. Exams are a little bit tough sometimes, but final exam can replace lowest midterm.
Just reads the slides and does it quickly; he doesn't explain it well. To do well in this class, you can't rely on him.

Definition of mid. There are other professors who are better when it comes to explaining the content. He's a super nice guy, and he does mean well. The homework is infinitely harder than the exams since they reworked the course. Just review practice exams and you will be fine no matter who is teaching it. Tophat is extra credit.

The lectures are behind the homework; which is at a whole different level than anything that is covered in lecture. He rambles on about conceptual concepts while not explaining any problems we might see on exams or homework.

Zhe gets sidetracked a little bit and speaks quite softly so if you get him sit in the front if you have bad hearing otherwise he's good and accessible outside of class. When he explains more abstract concepts though make sure to ask questions because he will blow by sometimes

The class I took with him was PHYS232. I thought he was a very good lecturer, and going to lecture definitely helped me understand the material more. The homework for this class can be pretty hard, but outside of that, it wasn't that bad.
Communist

Very difficult class for a 101 course. The tests are curved which is nice, although the fact that every test is curved as-well as the final says enough about difficulty. Homework has one attempt and makes up a very large portion of the grade which can be frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: love this guy he made class very enjoyable

You will definitely need to keep up with the lectures and notes in order to be successful in this class. The only grades in the class come from quizzes every chapter and the exams. If you show up and just try, I think you'll do okay.

Dr Fei was a decent professor, but the class content itself was not very interesting. He did have really well made slides for every unit and was available outside of class, but some sections were not explained as much as was needed for the challenging tests and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a fan, don't take

The lectures are hard to pay attention to. If you have any background in physics go ahead and take the class. If this is your first time being introduced to physics: good luck. Tests are super curved. Never used textbook once. Attendance is taken but with the curve it really doesnt matter. Lecture notes posted online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All the tests are curved and you are allowed a note sheet for the exams. While attendance is part of the grade, you could not go and still pass. Most people who do go are on their phones anyway.

Homework once a week and 2 midterms and a final. Makes the tests a lot harder than the homework so using problems online to study helps. Lets you use a full sheet of paper front and back for the midterms and final. A lot harder than I expected for a 101 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: there's ~900 students in this class but still he flips through the 85 lecture slides for one lecture in like 30 seconds each and runs through all of the practice equations on the chalk board and then erases the problem in like 15 seconds after he is done with it and everything he teaches, to him is already common knowledge to everyone in the class.

Explains the content pretty well and does some interesting demos. There were a few demos he struggled to do properly, but sometimes he'd let a student try it instead which was cool. Trying to write down every word from the slides is a lost cause, but he'd sometimes reopen a tophat if the class was pretty split on the answer and let us try again.

Talks way too quickly and is not very friendly for questions. Spends probably the whole lecture on equations no examples. I did not show up to any lectures and still received an A which tells you a lot about the course and prof.

If you like watching a professor click through equations at the speed of light, this is your guy! This guy rearranged equations like nobodies business, it's genuinely impressive. That being said it is no where helpful for students learning unless you have a steel trap for a brain. Get ready to learn everything discussed in lecture on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Asad is a very nice guy, but he struggles to hold the attention of his students. His examples are often unhelpful because they are so broken up and drag on. This results in material being unclear and hard to follow. If we did worksheets and could get feedback on work, or get partial credit for showing work, the course would be better.
Best Econ professor at ISU
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Impossible to fail need to put in work to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you just need Econ 1010 for credit this is the easiest way to get it
Easiest 3 credit course I've taken
Best choice of Econ professors did barely any work for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curves tests heavy nearly impossible to fail if you show up to exams and do the project
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easiest of all the Econ professors to get credit if you want an A you will have to put a little work in studying just do the quizzes to learn the questions they're recycled exam questions
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible Professor. Can be difficult to understand at times. Uses iClicker which does not work well most of the time. Does not give enough time for exams with the amount of questions. Covers content that is not on the exams. Average for the final was 30%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ECON3010. Believe this is his first teaching this class…and that's evident. The first exam was awful. The avg was well below failing. The IClicker he uses never works and causes you to miss points when it doesn't work. He is impossible to get a hold of and most people never got to take the practice exam I heard. Highly reccomend finding someone els

Econ 301….do not take it with this professor. Midterm averages are horrible. Over half the class failed by a lot. Lectures are easy and homework's and exams are much much harder. Highly recommend taking 301 with someone different if you want to get anything out of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lctr-hvy, and repetitive. He uses something called Iclicker for daily pts, which has been super difficult to work with for us students and the TA who teaches labs. The application does weird things on its own, and when it isn't closing the question on its own, the instructor closes it way too early to answer. Just use Top Hat. HWs due @ noon Sun!?
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You are only graded on three things, a group project, a midterm, and a final. Everyone fails the two tests, so they are curved like crazy; my 34 became an 80. He is also impossible to get a hold of. He barely responded to emails, and his office hours were non-existent. The group project is just horrible
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The whole class is graded on a midterm, a final, and a project.  We were not given any rubric on the project and I received a C.  The average grade on the final was 42/120, which curved to a 57.  So, over half the class failed.  The average grade on the midterm was 29/100.   That got curved to a B, not the same curve.  Avoid him at all costs!!
Terrible teacher. Tests are way too hard for an introductory microeconomics course. The whole class is graded by two tests and a project where you are barely given any instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome Professor ! He Curves too good!  so if you get unsatisfactory grades don't worry wait for final ,he will curve a lot . He can turn your grade from d to b

Barely any practice material/homework, so it is hard to actually learn and understand content. Absolutely no reason the average on the midterm prior to the curve should have been 30% for an introductory micro course.
Curved my 22% to an 81%
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He curves the test scores. However, you are only graded on three things, two exams and a project.
Sherry the type of guy to curve a 50 to a 90 on the midterm.

Dr. Kash is the best professor I have ever had. Absolutely phenomenal understanding of marketing and does a great job making class fun & educational. Would 10/10 recommend his class for anyone looking to learn some good stuff.

Personally, I would never ever sit through another one of his classes. Ever. First of all, he has two things in the gradebook and it is mid-April of Spring Semester. In literally every single class is some sort of mandatory in-class assignment that takes forever and is not interesting at all. He also never responds to emails if you miss class.

Khash is so nice and you can tell he cares about his students. He does have weekly homework, and a couple of big group projects but nothing too hard. His tests are difficult, but he curves them and offers extra credit.
Aaron did an amazing job teaching this class, he made Gen Chem 2 a million times easier than Gen Chem 1.

He was a very good professor. When I was struggling, he was very willing to give me the help I needed and was more than willing to set up extra office hours for me to understand the material. He was very helpful and a good person to talk to. He also wanted feedback whenever I met with him so he could improve the course. He wants people to succeed
Aaron made chemistry seem so easy, this class was more enjoyable than Chem I and his teaching style was awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He made this class extremely easy, gave extra credit and good feedbaxk
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a great professor gives out extra credit and great feedback on assignments. He is always willing to help students through many hours. He puts in a lot of work to see students succeed and it shows. I recommend taking any chemistry class with him.

Rossini is a wonderful professor he made our lectures fun and easy to understand. For those who don't enjoy math too much he might turn you away as he loves to show how equations are derived and the history of them, but every test question is from the homework or conceptual so make sure you understand why you are doing what you are doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Rossini is a fair professor. Exams come directly from the HW and lectures. Nothing outside of this will appear on the exams except a couple of conceptual questions. Lectures are dry but give you what you need to know.

The content itself should be easy, but he spends hours of class deriving the equations and reading off a power point. It was not worth going to class when you can watch the same content on his recordings in half the time. He doesn't post test solutions for you to review and his tests aren't like homework. Take it with a different professor please.

Mr. Rossini is a great professor. If you wish to do well in the class go to lectures and do homework. What comes in homework is what comes in quiz and test. DO his practice test as they represent what test are going to be like. His demos are great. Test are what he gives on quiz's and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring, but I hate chemistry so it's likely not his fault.
Rossini is a Canadian legend. He is clear and straightforward, and if you pay a moderate amount of attention during lectures you should end the class with a good grade. His demos are epic too

His thermodynamics course was one of my most successful course outcomes. He explains content and then does examples. Sometimes the examples are the homework too! He transitioned online very well and is overall a great professor.
He expects you to know the material right after learning it in class, but the homework reflects what is expected on the exams, so he is very fair. Always has an extra credit question on the exam

Dr. Rossini is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and straightforward. Students with more chemistry background (like those who took AP in high school) unlike me seemed bored in the class, but it still was a bit of a learning curve for me. He is also good at answering questions if you have any after class.

Aaron Rossini is an excellent lecturer. He really understands his material and how to present it in a logical and clear manner. Show up to the lectures and recitations, pay attention, do the work and you'll be in great shape. He's understanding and easy to talk with.

Rossini himself is not the problem for the class, since most learning is done during homework or during recitation. But his choices of TAs is mediocre at best, and if you get a bad TA you'll be in for a rough time. Your experience and grade in the class will depend on how hard you work on the homework. Also you need to go to class for Top Hat.

A great professor, really helped out if you were struggling in the class (Chem 167) , I did not understand a lot of the material and did poorly on some exams, but still passed. Very generous grader when it comes to recitation quizzes and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Rossini did an awesome job teaching this tough course. It is a lot of work and the lectures can drag on at times, but he kept things interesting and always explained how what we were learning would be useful in our work someday. He is a tough but fair grader. Be prepared to dedicate a lot of time to this class if you want a good grade.
Love him as a teacher, lots of examples and often the in-class examples will be the homework. He's got a dry sense of humor and came to class with a black eye once.

ENTSP/MGMT 310 with this professor is not necessarily hard, but the exams are lengthy. Attendance is required and a big part of your grade. There is a lot of group work in this class and it ends up becoming the majority of your grade.
The class mainly focused on working with a group for the semester. Attendance is weighted heavily. Sapru genuinely cared about the topic and was very passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was extremely difficult to work with as he shot down any other ideas that wasn't his. You could see people work up the courage and confidence to answer their question or share their idea for him to shoot them down. It is extremely difficult to wake up each day and attend his class knowing that is the outcome each time.

This class is not necessarily difficult with this professor, however, he is not a kind professor. He expects in class participation, but will not hide his opinions about what you say. He often makes you feel incorrect and that your ideas, if not exactly his, are not worth sharing. I would not recommend this him if you are looking to enjoy MGMT.
Lots of word counted papers that are not hard but very time consuming. Need to be creative and work well in groups
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you want to pass this class, you must go to the lectures because he doesn't post the notes on Canvas. He also does mini quizzes at the end of some lectures, and if you're there, he gives you the answers and full points. He is a wonderful professor and is very passionate about everything he teaches!

I felt like this class was so emphasized on the little things that I often forgot about the big picture. But overall, this class was a nice class to go to and forget about the overbearing stuff throughout the day. Lectures are tolerable but be mindful on the homework's and exams. The exams can be tough, but with enough studying you should be fine.

Aaron is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are engaging and easy to understand while providing vast technical knowledge. There are handwritten notes given during the lectures, so if you skip class, you will probably not do well in the course. Exams are easy to study for and he always excited to help if a student has a question.
Don't take his Geo 100 class. It was so difficult. He's not a bad guy but that class was terrible. I took it for a science credit simply because I thought it would be easy. I was so wrong.

Overall, the class was not difficult if you pay attention and look over notes but there are a lot of small things that he pays attention to that make no sense for the sake of the course. He is very passionate and good to listen to but, I feel that he knows this course isn't taken seriously by most, so he makes the little things more important.
Very dry lectures and tough homework. He expects you to care about rocks as much as he does and treats a 100-level course as if it were a 400 level.  Do not take if you want a relatively easy class.

Aaron is probably one of the best professors I have had so far. There is not a lot I can say about him that hasn't already been said. Make sure to give your full attention to him during lectures. He really wants people to be engaged. He really likes rocks and volcanoes so make sure you talk to him about that stuff.
Overall this class was really easy to follow and understand even without any geologic knowledge. I found it to be pretty interesting and he teaches it in a really simple way.

This class was asynchronous, but I loved how the instructor put his personality into the materials we were given! My critique is that the materials were hard to understand as a person who isn't in a science field. Wish the class was more non-science major-friendly. I learned a lot, though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Intentionally made more difficult than a typical entry level course. Wordings for quiz/exam questions were often vague or unclear. Have to take an exam about once a month. C averages for exams. Lecture quizzes are quite annoying and don't test understanding. Prof Wood is overzealous in course expectations. Memorization is required not understanding

Great professor who cares about his students. If you take in-person, make sure you go to the lectures or you may struggle a little bit for the exams. If you attend lecture its an easy A. Gives plenty of time to ask questions. Class itself isn't too difficult. (ENVS-324 is cross-listed with GEO-324).

This course was mostly interesting but the wording was purposely made more difficult than it needed to be for a 100-level course. The professor is easy to work with and you just need to review the slides before taking the weekly quiz. The final was a paper that I wrote the day it was due and it was graded within the same day.

I am honored to have taken a class from someone who oozes so much passion for their area of study that it's contagious. Amazing guy. Class is super tough for 100 level, so you will have to study and work hard for it because it is a LOT of information. If he wasn't such a great teacher I would have been far more overwhelmed than I already was

Aaron Wood is one of the best professors I have had. He posts great lectures that make things very clear. The visuals he provides went a long way in helping me learn. Lecture videos got long at times, I had to break them up. But he's a great professor and really cares about students. He also gives good feedback. Reach out to him if you need help!
Quizzes are very difficult. Lecture material is very dry and poorly worded. I would not recommend this professor to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wood gave good and clear to follow lectures. He had slides to go with the lecture content and would filter out the important stuff and write it on the whiteboard for your notes. There were in class activities, but if you were present you are only graded on participation. He gives amazing feedback after exams so you know what to study

I think every Ensci student should take this class. Wood does a great job explaining in detail every single energy source in a non-biased and informative way. He brings up a lot of important points that I would have never thought about. Take it online if you can, super easy. Wood is a great example of a caring, informed and approachable professor.

This is a very easy class, but Aaron cares way too much about little things in this class that doesn't make sense. He seems to prioritize little things, and care way too much about technicalities. Overall it is still an easy blowoff class, but just annoying in a lot of areas.

Attendance not mandatory but in class activities were given and graded for points. I liked him, but he hand writes almost all his notes on the board and they are not on canvas. The class was very interesting and important, but I found it depressing because we basically just calculate how many years before earth is destroyed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Relatively easy class if you watch the lectures and take the weekly quizzes. Also offers a lot of extra credit to boost your grade. He is an extremely slow grader and at times took weeks to respond to emails.

Professor gives homework with very little applicability of real life. He discounts points and tries to be strict in things that make no sense. Overall, I feel this course was a total filler and it is basically about how to measure the footprint of building a coal mine, how bad oil & gas is. It is sad that there are professors like this.

Insanely hard grader, I've watched the majority of lectures and did the readings in the textbook. Barely anything on the exams was in either of those. Did not explain why short answer questions were wrong. Quizzes and homework do not tell you what the correct answer is when you finish so you can not learn from mistakes. Terrible course/Professor.

Took his online course but met him before it started. Great guy who incorporates FANTASTIC dad humor into his readings. Really knowledgable, understanding, makes his online lectures fun. I will definitely try to take more courses with him.

Really good professor. Very helpful with any questions and wants students to succeed. Lectures are kinda boring if you aren't really interested in the topic, but he does his best to keep your attention. Gives out many opportunities to raise your grade. Study guides are available for every exam. Would definitely recommend this professor.

I took this class as a half semester 1 credit class. Pretty easy and straight forward, there can be a lot of reading if you want to do really well on the quizzes (7 to 10's out of 10's). Extra credit was provided for our final paper
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Wood is so nice and caring. He genuinely cares about his students and wants you to learn. This class was very easy if you watch the lectures. His exams are a little tougher than the quizzes but he always gives you a chance to make up points. Overall, he's a real gem. 10/10.

Aaron is a fantastic professor. We had hardly any homework, and only one paper to write the entire class. Exams are done in the testing center and can be difficult if you don't study, but he provides a study guide of all possible topics. Extra credit offered several times throughout the semester. Pretty easy class overall, highly recommend!

I loved this class! Dr. Wood was very accommodating with absences and you can tell he really cares about what he is teaching. He was very nice in all the interactions I had with him and even mailed out a letter mid-semester to students who had done well so far praising them for their efforts. Would 100% take a class with him again!

Took GEOL 103 online with him and it's the worst online class I've taken thus far. His quizzes were incredibly difficult and he's a very strict grader. He is also very rude when emailing or being asked for help. Everyone I knew who took it had a C or below in the course at the end of the semester. Don't recommend this course.

I really enjoyed this class even though lectures were dry at times. Hes a really great professor that wants you to do well. Tests are in the testing center. Extra credits available at the end of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Aaron is awesome. This class was a little dry at times but he made it do-able. Study up for the exams, they are in the testing center so you can take them when you feel ready. He gives you like a weeks window to take them. Homework can be challenging but the extra credit out weighs it, so don't sweat it.

I loved this class. It was a very easy class to complete, but also very informative. Weekly modules are interesting. There is a weekly quiz and a paper at the end. As long as you read through the material, it should be very easy to do well in this class. When I contacted him with specific questions, he was more than willing to help me.

Lectures can be a little dry at times but are better than many other online classes. Exams are a bit rough but he provides study guides for each and drops your lowest score. Homework can be challenging but ample extra credit opportunities can give you a 5% boost at the end. Super quick with emails. Genuinely wants you to succeed. Great guy.

I took this class as an elective- my major's in JLMC. I've had no prior experience in GEO, but ended up with a C-. Class is lots of interesting info. He required 2 papers, weekly quizzes, 3 math-heavy hw assignments, and 3 exams + a cumulative final. Drops lowest exam & quiz. I'd say it's worth it. He's a good and fun guy willing to help students.
Good guy. good lectures
By far one of my favorite professors at ISU. If you need to fill a tech elective, take this class.

I took the online portion of this class and boy was that a mistake. If you are not interested in geology I would recommend not taking 324 with him, it is super boring and his online videos will put you to sleep. His quizzes are only worth 3 points each which sucks. The only plus side to his course is he gives out extra credit, but its not easy.

Genuine professor who lectures well. I wasn't really interested in the material but he  made it pretty understandable. Random in-class mini quizzes happened sometimes, so going to lecture fairly often is your best bet.
If you are only a little interested in geology, you're going get more interested! He uses analogies often (usually dessert foods) and is very easy to understand.

Dr. Wood is great. He is very knowledgable in his field and does a great job of making the material interesting and easy to understand. I used and enjoyed the textbook but you could easily get by with just the lecture slides. All the exams are based on material covered in class. There were often in class activities so its good to go to class!

This course is very simple. You learn the basics of dinosaurs. I thought it was interesting. The course itself is not difficult. There are weekly quizzes and a final paper. I found the quizzes to be a little difficult as well as the paper but it was nothing to the extreme. I would recommend this course to anyone interested in the topic or for fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the most passionate professors I've met. Truly cares about what he is teaching, but understands that you might not. Gives lots of extra credit and is extremely fair on grading. Also makes sure everyone understands before moving on. Would recommend taking a class with him.

Really good professor. I took this at an engineering topic elective just because it sounded easy but it was an extremely interesting class. I did not expect to enjoy it as much as I did.  He makes lectures interesting and even though the class was in the morning, I would still make it out of bed and to his class just because it was so interesting.

I took his class because it seemed like interesting information, but then I found out he was teaching and got super excited. He's so down to earth and is always willing to help you out if you don't understand the material. He doesn't grade harshly and all of his classes are pretty easy, so it allows you to actually focus on the material. Fav prof!

I took the online portion of the class.  Pretty simple:  put forth the effort and you will get an A or a B.  If you don't, you won't.  Even though I was an online student I met with Professor Wood on a few occasions for questions and he was helpful and available.  Learned a great deal in the course and I will take another class of his again!

I was a little skeptical about this class since it is about dinosaurs, but I was wrong. I absolutely enjoyed this class and would definitely take it again. The only things in the grade book are the weekly quizzes and the final paper. You definitely have to read through the content he posts online in order to do well on the quizzes.

It's best to go to class because he sometimes has in class questions for credit. Very easy to understand and if you go over the power points before the test you will do fine and make sure you do the online assignments. There is no need to buy the textbook for this class.

The class itself is not bad. You can't get an A without trying, but you'll get a good grade if you participate. As for Professor Wood, he's great! He loves feedback on his lectures and really makes sure his students can succeed. He's a good lecturer and I enjoy going to class. Taking a class next semester with him again and looking forward to it!
He is very nice, approachable, friendly, and thoroughly covers each topic. The lecture can be dull but it is very easy to get a B and with a little extra work you can definitely get an A.
Really goes above and beyond compared to other professors I've had at isu.
Baker is not a professor, he is a grad student. He tries to make a dull subject interesting but rarely succeeds. He's a good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Mr. Baker is the best stats professor ever! He is funny as heck too! Oh, and he is soo hot!
Tests are tough, but he is willing you help you if you see him during office hours.
Classes are REALLY long and he rarely goes over examples. Nice guy but seriously, need to get better at teaching
Very passionate about the class and made the class seem as fun as he could.
Great professor, super passionate, cracks a joke or two. Super organized and it is very easy to find information.

Physic 2 used to be evil, but Lekha saved the course. I stopped going to lecture after a couple of weeks and just did the Tophat from my room. The exams never tried to trick you, me and my roommate would practice and review previous exams a couple days before and would do great. Definitely go to SI Exam reviews because those were SUPER helpful.

I stopped going to lectures like a week in and just learned the equation sheet a couple days before the exams. The exams are easy if you know how to use the equation sheet and know the variables. Definitely take physics 2 at Iowa state the department fully changed their program. I bombed the final and still easily past. Would recommend!

Great professor who does a lot of great demonstrations to aid with understanding. He has an accent but it is fairly easy to understand explains the concepts well. Lots of extra credit offered in an already fairly easy course so if you put time in to study and go to lectures it is easy.

He is a good professor, but you definitely need to have taken at least one physics class before taking this class. He tries to cover a lot of material in only 50 minutes, so he often rushes through and skips over necessary steps when solving problems. Understand how to derive the formulas and combine them. He does offer a lot of extra credit!
Dr. Adhikari made physics extremely easy. Averages being extremely high shows it. He gives tons of extra credit

he was always very enthusiastic about the topics. H used demos often and explained the topics in great detail. his accent isn't very heavy either. made a boring class entertaining with his jokes. if you have to take PHYS 231 he is a great option.
Lectures by Prof Adhikari were always really engaging, and the examples were found on the HW and past exams. He allowed discussion with the Top Hat questions and was just overall a funny professor.

I would absolutely recommend Dr. Adhikari! His lectures are enjoyable, and he takes care to answer all student questions while still getting through the content. He offers extra credit just for attending lectures and clearly loves teaching. 5/5 would recommend.
Very engaging lectures, he clearly is an expert and loves to teach. Would highly recommend.

Actually a hilarious dude. Made lectures so entertaining and engaging even through some pretty boring topics. Just make sure you're on top of your stuff conceptually on this exam, or it can bite you on exams
He knows what he's talking about. Reinforces concepts. more like a high school teacher in the way he interacts with students. Overall, very caring and understanding guy
Good professor. tells you what you need to know. concise and to the point. Understanding and kind to students. Would recommend you go to all lectures. Lots of extra credit with top hat questions.
He seems very passionate about teaching physics. Very nice person and provides a lot of examples.
Uses good teaching methodology.

Great professor! Always explains concepts clearly. He has a passion for teaching. He's hilarious too. Brings in humour into his teaching to keep students engaged. Really helpful in office hours as well. He really appreciates it if you ask questions as well.

A good lecturer, sorta all over the place when explaining concepts but very good at actually demonstrating. Many opportunities to get extra credit, usually just by showing up and doing the Top Hat exercises which are a very good way to reinforce the concepts before you do the homework. Made up for the mediocrity of AP Physics lectures during COVID.
Great professor, clearly passionate about subject and teaching. Exam review lectures are great as he will listen to students for feedback.

Amazing Professor. Physics is definitely not an easy class, but Dr. Adhikari does a great job of explaining the subjects. I had very little physics knowledge coming into this class, but he made it one of my favorite classes of the semester. Tests are fairly straightforward, and you will do great if you take the time to understand the material.

I loved class time with Dr. Adhikari. He was always engaging and making the class laugh. Seems like a great guy and definitely knows his stuff. Ask lots of questions, and he will always answer them and try and help you out.

Dr. Adhikari was a great physics professor. He is so kind and even though it was an hour and a half lecture, I found myself laughing and engaged in almost every class. You can also tell that he just really cares about his students' wellbeing. He would often encourage us to smile or take a breath to relax.

Awesome lectures! He never failed to come up with a creative way to illustrate complicated concepts. To explain cross products he literally started drawing on the floor. Throwing dry ice into the lecture hall, the personification of physical variables in equations, and lots of great explanations of course.

Class was quite difficult because it was hard to sit through his lectures. Didn't really understand what examples and stuff he was going over in lecture. If you took AP physics in high school you will be fine. Just do well on the tests and you will be set.

Dr. Adhikari is very enthusiastic about physics and keeps lectures interesting. His accent isn't hard to understand. He posts lecture notes to canvas but it is much easier to understand in lecture. Try not to fall behind at all, this class can move very fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had him for Phys 221 & 222 and received an A/A- respectively. His lectures are great and would usually contain everything we could possible need to know. Missing lecture would have greatly set me back

Lekha is enthusiastic about what he's teaching, and definitely tries to make sure the important topics are understood. In-class questions are easy extra points, and the material in his slides is good too. Can be a little hard to understand at first due to his accent, but having had him for 2 semesters now, it isn't bad.

I've had this prof for both 221, got an A no thanks to him, and i have him for 222 now. He is very hard to understand due to thick accent and doesnt teach the material well. Be prepared to teach the whole course to yourself. Attend SI and get a tutor if you want to even think about getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Professor Adhikari for lecture and recitation. I would highly recommend him for both. He is always was willing to listen when asked a question. Smart guy with a fun sense of humor that makes a topic that normally drains you to a topic that excites you when you get the problem right. Class normally averaged 60%-65% on test, so hard class.

Very nice, enthusiastic guy. His lectures were entertaining and probably more interesting than other professors' due to his unbridled enthusiasm about physics. When the professor is excited about physics, it makes lecture so much better. The class as a whole, however, is a disaster. I'm amazed that I got the grade I did. Great professor, bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Adhikari adds energy to his lecture and explains physics better than the other professors. I attend lectures for Professor Westein and Professor Whisnant as well, but they don' t make the material come alive like Dr. Adhikari does. If you struggle with physics I strongly recommend Dr. Adhikari.

Dr. Adhikari is the best!! Super helpful during recitation, you can tell he loves physics and teaching. Really wants you to succeed, and actually cares about your learning. So glad I got him again for 222 next semester.

Dr. Adhikari obviously enjoys this topic and he made attending lectures worthwhile (and even fun!) He is super engaging and explains difficult material well. I would not have enjoyed this course at all if I had a different professor. Physics 221 is a really difficult class. But that is the department's issue, not the professors!
Extremely passionate about physics and is pretty goofy sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Funny guy. The class is difficult, but he does a good job explaining.

He makes physics easy to understand and his tests are clear and understandable. The top hat points in class may seem useless but they matter so come to class as often as you can to just get some extra points.

Prof. Adhikari was a great prof when compared to the rest of the PHYS221 lecturers. He made class enjoyable and fun to go to. He is passionate about what he does and likes to share what he knows with us. Class is not required, but there are extra credit tophat points for up to 2.5% of the grade. I know people who didn't go to lecture and failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class with Professor Adhikari was very interesting. He is very passionate about physics and it definitely shows during his lectures. His grading criteria is very clear, so as long as you put forth the effort (read text, go to class, look at lectures, and do homework), this class shouldn't be too difficult.
It is a very tough class but he was very excited about the topic and tried his best to explain. He also has an accent so it was hard to understand if you weren't focused.

Dr. Adhikari has a helpful and energetic teaching style, but for me was hard to understand. In comparison to the homework, recitation work, and personal studying, his lecture aided me the least in my learning.

Dr. Adhikari is pretty good teacher. He is super enthusiastic about teaching, and he tries his best to help you learn when you need help. If you can sign up for one of his recitation sections, I would highly recommend it.
Dr. Adhikari is a great teacher but definitely is a little bit of a challenge to understand.  He is very energetic and tries to keep physics from being as dull as it can be.
funny guy who loves physics in his recitation you will get a lot of help. he is the nicest guy and will gladly help you.

Great prof. Very excited about the topics. Had him for rec as well, very helpful and positive. You do not need the book, they actually teach you. Lectures posted, past exams, worksheets, quizzes. Lots of work, lots of material. Completely manageable for a 5 credit course. Mastering Phys online HW was trash, unrelated info., only thing I didn't like

Dr. Adhikari seems to be a very smart guy but isn't a great teacher.  His accent is strong and he often speaks quickly and not very clearly, making his lectures and recitations difficult to understand.   He seems like a good guy though, and a fair grader.

You get what you put into it.  He seems to be a great teacher and explains concepts in a way all will understand. Grades fair and will answer questions about grades very willingly. If you follow along, go to class, and somewhat pay attention you should be able to get a mid B no problem. Definitely have to work hard to understand the subject matter.
Good professor. Very fair with the grading and the lectures while mandatory were very useful.
Lectures are useful and the course is well organized, absolutely no problems at all with grading, super easy to get an A. I felt that I learnt a lot, would definitely take this course again.

His syllabus was so condescending, I felt like I was back in high school. All of the learning is done through the homework and pre-class tutorials because his lectures never get to the point. The Packback forum he makes you pay for is also completely worthless with everyone asking stupid questions to fulfill their weekly quota.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I personally think his lectures are 90% of the time are not useful. He often gives a lot of speeches about the current economy, what's going on, or his prediction about some events, which are related to economy but not necessary to Microeconomics. A lot of readings an assignments are required. There are extra credits and the grading system is easy
The worst professor I have ever had. He cannot teach what so ever and wastes time during lecture. Do not have this guy has a professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Deiter is full of himself and tends to not talk about econ in class until the last 10 minutes. There are a lot of things to do for his class. The grading scale is nice tho, 83% A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. Each point you get in exc  1% grade boost. Lectures not great, lots of rambling. Too much material: hw, book, videos, lecture, Tophat. Pretty straightforward grading, though. 2 tests, worth 80%. Also, 83 is an A so that helps. Make sure you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: All the points in the class come from 4 grades: homework, 2 exams, and a final (attending 90% of the lectures makes the final optional). With a very easy grading scale, 83% for an A, and lots up extra credit points, up to 8%, turns out to be a very easy class. All exam material comes from online homework and TopHat questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: ECON101 with Deiter is not a smart decision. He goes off on tangents often and will talk about random stuff half of lecture. There are TopHat questions and if most of the class gets them wrong due to him not teaching well, he will act like everyone is stupid. Do NOT take ECON101 with Deiter.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy A (83%!), but the class is extremely boring. He reads sport news for about 40 minutes and ends up talking very briefly about economics in the last 5-10 minutes (and that's what you need to know for the exams).

Econ is a hard subject to learn no matter the professor. Deiter is very knowledgeable but often forgets students don't know the subject yet. His lectures are easy to follow & the exams are multiple choice. However, knowing what to expect on the exams is unclear & difficult. Exams are worth 75-80% of final grade but he grades on a generous scale.

I HIGHLY recommend not taking Econ with Deiter. You won't learn anything in his lectures because he talks about random stuff half the time so you will end up having to teach yourself. You only have 3 grades for the whole semester so you have to work really hard. I had 100% participation so I got to opt out of the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Only 3 grades are in the grade book for this class. You must do well. I found myself teaching myself Econ because Deiter gets extremely off-topic in class. Allows you to opt out of the final if you attend 90% of class. Exams are filled with trick questions and is very rude and calls students out in his 400-person class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is just not good at teaching. I have heard he is a good advisor but teaching? No. He cant speak without going uh um every other word, which is hard to focus. Gets off topic all the time. Have to learn on your own. Im also pretty sure his farms have went bankrupt, what gives him the right to teach Econ. My advice? Find a different teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I came into this class thinking it wouldn't be as bad despite the negative comments by other people. I was completely wrong because this class is extremely tough. Get ready to teach yourself Econ. NOT AFRAID TO CALL YOU OUT IN FRONT OF 400 PEOPLE!! He doesn't understand students don't know as much as him so he teaches at a very advanced level.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He tends to be kind of mono-tone but the class is straightforward and if you can pay attention, you'll be fine. Do not need the textbooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Deiter is very knowledgeable and tries to make things interesting. He has a very generous curve on the class and rewards students who attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I failed my first test, got a D on my second one, a C on overall homework and was eligible to opt out of the final because of good attendance and still got a C overall. Not much is in the gradebook but he is very generous with the grading curve to give everybody the chance to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Deiter is very cut and dry, his expectations are laid out for you and if you don't meet them you won't do well. Put in the work and you will be fine. Econ 336 is an Ag selling class and by far is the most useful class at ISU 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Deiter is a really good professor. He definitely knows his stuff and is a very fair grader. He made economics as interesting as it could be. There are only two tests during the entire semester, so doing well is a must.

Deiter is a well-respected professor and has been at the university for literally 40 years. Show up and you will definitely pass. Small papers during the year, and 2 big ones due at the end, NO exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: If you have a dry since of humor then you and Deiter will easily get along. Also, GO TO CLASS!!! As long as you show up 90+% then you don't have to take the final!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The ex credit at the end of class was nice, but didnt help much. It was frustrating taking this class because economics in general to me is boring, and i feel like its something you either get or you dont. I liked Deiter's examples, it's just a boring subject that shouldnt be as in depth as it was. If you have any doubts now just get a tutor ASAP.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ron is a great person, and class can be fun. However, for a 100 level class this class goes way to far in-depth. Homework will take along time and if you have ever taken and Econ course before you will struggle guaranteed. Attendance is taken, and you do receive points but he is a firm believe that if you show up, its to benefit yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely boring. Only 2 test grades and an average of all your homework in the grade book. Grading scale is easy, 83% is an A but an 83% isn't easy to get. If you have 90% attendance and get the option to opt out of final
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Deiter is a top-notch lecturer; he uses his lectures as a way to both cover course material and roast individuals on anything from making poor economic decisions to not having a significant other. His Economic Pickup Lines were also very helpful. Dr. Deiter knows what he's doing, and you'll learn a lot from him if you put in sufficient effort.

One of the worst professors I've ever had when it comes to actually learning. His exams are pretty hard, but the grading scale is ridiculously easy. He also curved our overall grades. I went to almost every lecture, did all of the homework and other assignments and would have gotten a D in the class without the curve. With the curve I got a B

Dr. Deiter was my worst professor of my freshman year. A typical class is filled with him rambling on about his recent golf outing and life lessons. Barley any econ is taught in class (I would know since I attended every lecture) and you are left teaching yourself. He'll probably read this to future students and mock it. All I can say is good luck!

Get ready to teach yourself Econ. He never stays on topic in class. He thinks he walks on water. If you want the extra credit he offers you literally have to thank him. He's not afraid to yell at you in front of 150 people. He's the worst professor I've ever had. Many told me not to take it with him. If you have the option, choose someone else!!

He is the worst- rambles on and on about random things and before you know it, class is over and you have to teach yourself Econ. So many different websites you have to buy for homework, videos, etc... awful awful awful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Ron's lectures are really interesting and he has a lot of great examples to share. I'm glad I took this class with him. What keeps me coming to his classes every week are the extra credit tophat question, and his attitude he display. I would never consider being an econ major, but he made it bearable even though I still felt lost in the class.

Deiter's 101 has the most relaxed grading scale. 80%+ is an A.  If you don't go to lecture, read the book and check the study guide for specifics on the exam.  If you go to class, he's pretty good about covering the materials and offers extra credit points via TopHat questions and for asking him questions that he thinks are "good".
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Although Ronald is not the best lecturer, he is a likable guy who cares about fairness. I barely did any work (crammed before tests) and still got an A. There is a very generous curve so if you learn the basics you should be fine. If you're not looking to learn and still get an A, this is your guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ronald Deiter is a savage. Not for the feint of heart. He loves to ask trick questions and then smack talk the entire lecture hall for getting the wrong answer.

Deiter gets straight to the material... once he gets to the material. It usually takes awhile for class to get going. It seems like he doesn't really have much to teach each class because he usually has a long introduction/review. The class is very easy, and he's a solid person.
Ron Deiter is a Great professor. his grading scale is very good. if you come to class and pay attention, do quizzes, homework, you will get good grade at the end.

Ronald Deiter is the man. Students love him. Check Yik Yak after a lecture and it's all about how cool he is. You don't need to go to any lectures, he can leave the quizzes out of your final grade. I would recommend going anyway. The book is all you need+access card. He always has an inspirational quote or a joke to make Econ more bearable. Deiter

25 random quizzes at the end of class, so attendance  is mandatory. Tests average around 60%, curve at the end is 80% for an A. Not the most interesting class, but He's a good guy, and throws jokes in occasionally to keep you interested. Also offers random extra credit that can really help at the end. Probably the easiest A I have ever received.

Good dude. Really friendly and positive. Econ is simply a boring subject, it is difficult to make lectures enjoyable. Sit close to front to refrain from distraction. You must go to class even if its "optional" it is the only reason Im passing. Do homework ahead of time. Exams will average 60 percent.

Deiter was really funny and he always came to class with a great attitude, but you NEED to go to class and force yourself to pay attention. Most kids you see in class will be on their phones, don't be one of those kids because you will be extremely confused when you are studying for the test. Show up to class, even if its boring as hell.

Lectures are very long, the homework takes forever to complete, he blames students for not doing well. He did not include in the syllabus that there would be homework during dead week or finals week.  If attendance didn't matter, you wouldn't go to class because you would learn nothing at all.

He has a great grading scale. He understands that some students are just bad test takers. His lectures are long/unorganized. He'll drag on about stuff the he thinks is relevant to his teaching, but leaves students confused on how it relates. Tests are tough. Will only blame students for poor test results despite there being a low average for test.

Econ 292A is a career readiness seminar class. Only meets once a week. Big waste of time. Don't take it if you don't have to. All he does is sit up there and lecture you about how today's generation is bad at everything and if he were an employer he would never hire you... Turn in a perfect resume, it is junk to him. Your work is never good enough.
Boring lecturer but has a fairly easy grading scale.  Showing up to class is helpful for the tests but not mandatory.  Only 6 homework assignments but they took a little while to complete.
Cool guy, lectures can drag on. Really easy grading scale. Would recommend going to class every day.
Deiter is a very boring lecturer. I took great notes for the first test and got an 80% but couldn't stand going to class and did poorly on the second and third tests.

One of the better Econ101 teachers you'll have. Tests are tough, but study hard and you should be good. Also in this class, 80% is an A and homework is graded the same weight as the three tests you take. Homework pretty easy, few assignments due every few weeks. Takes attendance too. Not a bad class.
Make sure you go to class, it is part of final grade.

Tests averages will be low, around 50%. Read the book for tests. There are no quizzes on Mondays, only Wednesdays and Fridays. Write the current event paper, easy extra credit. Don't miss quizzes, extra credit for good quiz attendance. YOU WILL THINK YOUR GRADE IS MUCH LOWER THAN IT IS, WAIT FOR THE END OF THE SEMESTER, HIS GRADING SCALE WILL HELP.

This guy sucks. There's a 13% grading curve which sounds nice at first, but by the end of the year you'll be begging for a 100% grading curve. The class average on tests is always around 50%, yet he finds a way to blame his students. Over half the class is him talking about his family and sports, as the last 10 mins he rushes to catch up. GOOD LUCK

Deiter is an interesting guy. He acts like a "no nonsense" professor, but also jokes around quite a bit. He warns you that this class isn't 'all about sports', but it pretty much is. The economics portion of the class is mainly vocab. terms and concepts from the notes. Most of class time is spent talking sports, etc. He is also a very quick grader.
He is the worst econ teacher out ther

Personally, I thought Deiter was a pretty good professor. If you like dry humor and witty comments, he has a lot of them he uses in lectures. He has quizzes at the end of class most days so attendance is important. Has good lecture notes but he can be a bit confusing to understand at times since he moves quickly through material.
IF you want to do well DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!  His lectures are so boring and his exams are supper hard.  The ave in other ECON 101 classes are 70, and it's 45 to 50 in our class!

Deiter is a terrible teacher. Rambles on about stuff that doesn't need to be talked about and is the most boring lecturer I've ever had. He mentioned that 75% of my class had a D or F going into the second exam. That isn't lack of effort by the students that is just crappy teaching. Do not get this professor.

For having a positive attitude, he sure complains alot. Take notes in class using any form of technology? Prepare to be called on and humiliated if you get the question wrong. He is very unprofessional to the point he trash talks my lecture to his other classes. Take that as you will..

I was excited to take this course, but Deiter is awful. He's just an econ teacher who likes sports and therefore thinks he can teach the merger of the two. He spends large amounts of class giving his analysis of sports news and talking about his fantasy teams. He also might have a gambling problem, but I can't confirm it.

He is probably the worst teacher I have ever had in my whole life, including my fourth grade teacher who sent me to the principles office for working ahead. He is pretty much an arrogant ass. He doesn't teach you much and if you don't get a tutor you will be screwed. very boring lectures, but he talks about golf and thats cool.
Easy grading scale but tough tests.  You won't just slide by you will have to work for every percentage of your grade.

He has good intentions but he is a crappy teacher. He goes over one topic for three weeks. I really recommend getting the book. It is helpful for the homework and his tests. You don't really need to go to class because he doesn't cover everything but he has in class quizzes that are easy points.

Sports Econ with Deiter is awful. He spends the first 30-40 minutes EVERY DAY analyzing current sports news and when he finally gets to economics he blows through things because we're running out of time and you don't get the chance to write notes or comprehend any of it. If you want to learn anything at all in this class, buy the textbook.

Dr. Dieter was my favorite professor I had this last semester, His test are pretty tough, Econ lectures aren't very exciting but he tries to keep the lecture interesting with jokes and extra credit questions. Homework isn't to bad, is keen on having students have positive attitudes. He also has a really easy grading scale.
Hes a pretty funny guy. Definitely covers the material well and tries to throw some corny jokes in there to keep it interesting.  Worth it to pay attention, reading 160 pages instead is aweful

Interesting guy, lectures are pretty straight forward, no real surprised show up on exams and they are all multiple choice, plus 80+ is an A so it is not terribly difficult to achieve. Has a clear interest for Economics and will answer questions from the class if people ask them. Overall very enjoyable.

This is an interesting class and you most likely won't be falling asleep. However, I found that little of the material actually related to Economics. Test questions that I most commonly missed were more about sports trivia and sports knowledge than economic concepts. This makes this class difficult for someone who doesn't know much about sports.

Professor Deiter tried to make lectures fun and exciting. He wrote out his notes and then would publish them to Blackboard before the Midterms. He engaged students by give a $1 and a bonus point on the exam for trivia questions. In-class quizzes were given at least once a week. Reading the textbook is essential. Hard exams, huge curve (won't fail).
got a C and two D's on tests still got an A- in class. Very nice guy just tests are very stupid and hard.
Entertaining class. He is very helpful. However, doing homework is a must. Don't think you'll pass with doing work.

He is a nice guy, but I cannot grasp his teaching style.  It's extremely frustrating to learn from him if this is your first Econ class.  The only thing that made me pass, is his super lenient grading scale.  The entire reason he has it though is because few can pass without it!
Yeah he really isn't a good professor. His class test averages are usually failing. I don't know why he is still a teacher.
Horrible teacher, I hate him.

I cant stand this class. All of the notes given during class are on paper on an overhead. Most notes are quickly covered by another piece of paper (never to be uncovered again) so you cannot copy down everything. On top of that, the notes are not posted on BlackBoard. Also the homework is done on a 3rd party site that costs $30 to access.Ridiculous
positive attitude, Deiter is awesome!

Encouraged positive attitude and kind of funny. Wasn't very clear during lecture went by some topics really fast. Overall nice guy willing to help. Oh and in this class he has an unfailable grading scale, Basically, anything above an 80 is an A and anything below a 48 is an F so  it's really not too bad at all.
HATED this class. points are almost entirely from tests.
Boring class, attendance was not required but there were random quizzes. Super easy grading scale 80% is an A.

He is a great professor. I have a hard time focusing in any of my classes but Professor Deiter makes it somewhat interesting with trivia, quotes, and brain teasers. He has an easy grading scale. I did not have a problem with getting a good grade in this class, I just put in a little effort.

Deiter is the man. His positive attitude may steer people away but honestly, it has rubbed off on me. He explains the concepts of econ in an easy fashion. The grading scale is really easy. 80% is an A. You would have to put in effort to fail this class.
The class was easy and he is a cool guy. He loves sports and positivity quotes. Class is not mandatory but he has a quiz almost every over day. They are easy.

Deiter is not a good professor.  He moves through lessons so fast so he can tell fifteen to twenty minutes of boring jokes.  He says a lot of things about positive attitude which is not what you will leave with after this class. He could be good if he actually explained economics.  Funny, but not good as a teacher.
Nice guy, but a horrible professor. Only take his class if all are other ECON 101 classes are ful
Was this a class in Economics or Attitude. It was hard to tell, but easy class if you know your concepts.
He talks a lot about attitude, and doesn't clarify concepts

He's a nice guy, and a good person in general.  He definitely knows his stuff.  The lectures are incredibly boring, but you only need 80% to get an A.  To counteract his lectures, he gives you free points for taking frequent, easy quizzes, and you get $1 if you guess the daily trivia question.  Boring lecture, but good teacher.
Gives you an A at 80%. Lectures can get pretty boring but he keeps it interesting with trivia questions.

He was a good teacher. He is in to being a good person. He starts the day off with an inspiring quote. His tests aren't that bad. He has quizzes twice a week that you want to be there for. He has a pretty easy grading scale. 34 points of quizzes, then 3 tests (2 out of 33, one out of 50). He doesn't trick you.

His lectures are incredibly boring. He should use clickers but he instead throws candy at people as a reward for participating. He always has a cliche "positive attitude" quote that adds no value to the class. The course is easy but this professor isn't very good.

Deiter is an overall good professor! He will spend an entire class period reviewing over stuff if people have questions? ASK QUESTIONS! But just so you know. He's obsessed with sports and positive quotes!! He has in class quizzes about every other day, so I suggest attending class. Easy points!!!! There is no homework to help raise your grade tho.

Deiter is awesome! It may have just been because the class was econ of sports but I loved it. The tests were pretty easy but because this was the first semester it was offered don't count on it being this easy again.

Material is easy, professor is good. Positive attitude talks get a bit old after awhile.  Luckily class is curved so much.  Class is about 60% Econ and 40% football, golf and having a positive attitude.

Unfortunately, econ 101 is a required class, but I think I knew more before this class than I do now. Deiter talks way too much about golf, and positive attitudes, and does not spend nearly enough time on econ. The website is a great way to see when there will be quizzes so that you know which days to attend, and which to skip.

This class is hard not going to lie. The grading scale is curved so you only need an 80% to get above an A. Don't let that fool you though. Tests are very hard. I would say about 50% of the time he talks about random (positive attitude) and the other 50% is about econ. Really didn't comprehend any of it. Make sure you study his study guides.

This class is horrible! The professor tries to help you, but that work and exams are too hard. Class is exam based-fail the exams and you will fail the class. It is curved like crazy because it is so difficult to get an A
he spends about half the day talking about positive attitude not econ. then the other half talking about econ just talking no structure. He also talks about his life way too much.

He dosen't have any structure to the class, and dosen't have any notes or lecture slides.  He just gets up and talks and you have to learn from the book.  Talks about positive attitude a lot, which is fine, but we get tested on econ, not positive attitudes.

This is a very easy class to fulfill the 300 level requirement for many Ag majors.  Just go to most classes and pay a little bit of attention and you will do fine.  The class is based on group work so if you don't like group work, don't take the class.
his grading scale seems like you'll pass with a guaranteed A,but be ready for some very hard exams, try to find old exams, and do all the extra credit you will need it

He's a funny guy, keeps things interesting by telling jokes.  Puts some students on the spot sometimes with the "hot seat" game when he calls students down.  He's really into having a positive attitude.
Great!!
I thought that Deiter was not a very good teacher.  A lot of the test questions were very random and vague.
Tries to keep class interesting which works fairly well. If you know anything about economics this class will be easy! If you are cheap, don't bother buying the book, I haven't used it once.
I enjoyed him as a teacher. I thought he kept the class interesting and fun. I enjoyed how he relates things back to economics, I can actually use this stuff in everyday life.
He's boring, I mean REALLY boring, but his grading scale is easy, so it's not hard to get a good grade
