He talks about random things and oftem mentions farming which puts me to sleep immediately since I have no idea about anything to do with farms. He's funny though. I do enjoy his jokes...and his cat story cracked me up!
Good guy, Good teacher, makes it simple for those who don't get it easily.

Deiter might be the dumbest teacher at ISU.  In his econ class he probably uses the first half of class just talking about whatever.  Probably some sports team that nobody cares about, or maybe his diabetic cat.  Who Cares?!  I pay to learn.  You should still go to class cuz he gives random ass quizzes.  The class is easy, but a waste of time.
OMG, Deiter is such a jerk.  He doesn't like VEISHEA.  I think that he is arrogant and very boring, but the class is useful.
Great teacher!!!! He makes the material easy.  He is the reason I picked up an Econ minor for and Engineering degree.

He does a very good job of relating economic concepts to real-world examples. Thoroughly explains everything; you do need to go to lecture though. If you like sports, I would highly recommend him for 301.

Boring class.  Didn't learn anything from going to his lectures, but I went because he has in- classes.  It was a tough class and not fun at all.  Would definitely reccomend trying a different Econ101 teacher.
Good teacher. Goes nice and slow and provides several real life examples. Econ makes sense because of him. Adds humor and inspiration to his lectures which is good.
No Comments
Fantasy Football is all he talks about. Hard class, but a good teacher. Tells dumbs jokes, but gets sympathy laughter.

Super cool guy, would usually show up to class in shorts and a bar/football shirt. His teachings could've been more straightforward but definitely knows his stuff and does a good job given the complexity of some of the math. Would recommend!

I adored Prof. Jenkins. Super down to earth guy, made materials so easy to understand and there was only one homework and a quiz each week which was very manageable. Also if you took the practice exams over and over before the actual exams the questions were identical which made it easy to do well. I would take a class of his again in a heartbeat.

He is an extremely knowledgeable professor who very clearly knows what he is talking about and communicates what he knows very effectively in his lectures. If you have questions of any kind, he answers them with the upmost respect and knows exactly how to answer your question. Difficulty ceiling is fairly high to start with, though, so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice professor, went in and reviewed my exams, and he did a great job making sure what went wrong. Also went back and regraded problems when Pearson was a little too harsh, tough class, but I wouldn't blame him for it. Ensure that the practice exams are well-embedded in your memory before taking the actual exams, as they are very similar.
Made simple math way more confusing then it had to be. Didnt like the way he did problems. Great guy though!

I would not recommend him for introduction level classes. He teaches using a math heavy vocabulary, making it hard for those who don't have a tremendous amount of experience. Personally, I did not bother showing up to lectures. As it would be harder for me to depict what he was trying say, than it was for me to learn the material on my own time.
I was in Math150. He was so easy to understand. Practice tests were identical to exams. he was a little disorganized but so nice and really knew what he was talking about. would take again.

He's a chill person and he's good at explaining concepts in a more intuitive way. He does difficult practice questions, but its good prep for the types of questions you'll see on quizzes and on the exam. Overall his explanations are very helpful because he breaks everything down into small steps. The class is hard, but not because of him.

One of the best professors I've had at ISU. Lectures were very theory heavy which was nice so we didn't just have formulas thrown at us for 50 minutes. Office hours are the best out of every professor at Iowa State. Super caring and wants his students to succeed.

Professor Jenkins is a truly kind and helpful professor. He is always willing to take questions and assist students during office hours. Math 240 is a difficult course but Jenkins will absolutely help you pass if you put in the effort. His lectures are taught well and always beneficial to learning in this course. Awesome professor all-around.

Michael is the best teacher I have had so far at ISU, and the best math teacher I have had in general. You can tell that he loves what he teaches, and that makes it so much more enjoyable to attend class. The exam questions can be tough, but he does a great job teaching you what you need to know and not wasting time on garbage.

I had Mr. Jenkins for Math 166 (Calc II) and he was by far the best lecture teacher for all secitions. He uses the chalkboard and walks us through solving very difficult problems. He is very easy to follow along with and doesn't spend any extra time teaching garbage that you won't need. He is the BEST math teacher I have ever had and I reccomend.

Adrian is super helpful and very genuine. He creates really hard test questions, but I feel it is better to have a professor who writes the hardest questions so you get prepared for them in class. 10/10 love Adrian.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Even though this is the hardest class I have taken at ISU, he teaches well and cares about his students. MATH240 is a class that takes a lot of time outside of class and he is always willing to help you during office hours. His class is test heavy but go to his office hours and you will see the benefits.

Jenkins is my favorite professor I have had at ISU. He is an extremely caring individual who truly wants students to succeed. In MATH 240 a lot of studying is required outside of class, but his lectures help basic understanding of difficult concepts.

Prof Jenkins is the best. My favorite professor I've had throughout college. He's funny, personable, knows the material, gives good advice, but is also a very tough grader. He makes the class difficult, but he also makes it able to succeed in the class with hard work. Accessible outside of the classroom for help and is a cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor with absolutely brutal exams. If you can pass his classes you can pass anything! After almost failing the first exam he set up a time 3 days a week to help me work through problems until I was more confident. Take every opportunity to seek help if needed he really cares about you and will do a lot to help if you ask.

Adrian does good working examples and giving feedback, but the class is very test-heavy with recitation quizzes and exams being the only thing of substance in the course. The class is very quickly paced, and had I not taken it in High School, I would have struggled. Adrian's office hours are a life saver, a definite must when taking this course.

Go to lecture and do the homework or else you'll get behind. A good amount of memorization of formulas but nothing absolutely crazy. I recommend doing the readings before the lecture, not after, so that you are introduced to the topic before he covers it in class.

Adrian is a nice guy and you can tell he really knows what he's doing. He understands that many people taking Math 145 just needs the credits and are done with math which is nice. The curve saved my grade because exams are hard. Quizzes once every week so stay on top of homework to prepare because questions are right from the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: To begin, Adrian is a good guy. However, I didn't really enjoy his teaching style and found myself just reading the book or watching videos on the topics instead. The class is very fast-paced, with a quiz every week and three exams that are 10x harder than the homework. If you go to the lectures and study, you will definitely pass this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Professor Jenkins for Trigonometry and it was one of the worst experiences of my life. The quizzes are either you pass with a 100% or you get an F and drop an entire letter grade. Do not take the class if you don't have to. His lectures make you more confused than you were coming into them and his exams are stupidly hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His class is very dry with mostly "proofs" of the equations and some elementary examples. We were really only graded on midterm and final. Gave no hw so you don't know how you were doing on a subject until the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had him as my calc 1 lecturer. He was an absolutely fantastic lecturer. Most of the class he worked through various examples on the board and challenged us to solve the problems but then worked it out for everyone who couldn't figure it out. He had plenty of funny jokes throughout and kept us engaged. It was very easy to copy the notes he gave.

Not my favorite but not the worst prof. Class was kinda boring but he made the points clear and concise. The biggest problem is the lack of grades and feedback. The material is easy enough to understand but he only had us do 3 hws and gave very little feedback on them to better understand what we were doing wrong.

Jenkins is definitely an interesting lecturer. He moves quick so there is no time for you to be on your phone or doing anything else during class. If you prefer classic chalkboard notes, he's a good choice. I attended his lectures and watched Butlers videos on my own time to better understand the material and hear it from 2 different perspectives.

Jenkins was my favorite professor this semester. Jenkins was able to not only make a lot of the topics understandable, he genuinely cared for the people who attended his lectures. Jenkins is famously known for putting some of the hardest problems on the exams and he also uses a varied range of problems in class to help us learn. Use his help hours!

Professor Jenkins was very available outside of class with office hours nearly every day. He is very helpful during office hours and will help with nearly any question that you may have. During this semester he wrote some of the more difficult questions on exams so listen during lecture because he gives difficult practice questions. Very good prof.
If you show up and listen you will really like him. At first he will seem a bit weird but he grows on ya.

Jenkins is one of my favorite professors at Iowa State. Not only is he an amazing teacher and very knowledgeable, but he is also very accessible. He seems to really want us to succeed in this class but also for our future actuarial exam. The class might be difficult, but it is very comparable to actuarial exam so it is very good for preparation.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures do not make sense. Only exams are counted for grades (weekly quiz small portion) He legit said: "I'm not gonna teach you everything but you are still responsible to know everything in the book." If you have to take class GET A TUTOR ASAP. Assigns homework but doesn't give answer key so you never know if you are doing it right.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I think Adrian is very hard to understand. His lectures simply don't make sense. Sometimes he skips over material and makes you responsible for learning it, especially important parts. I recommend switching professors if I were you. He is an extremely tough grader and his tests match none of the homework.
He writes tests that are not fair. Our first Exam average was a 43% and most people dropped the class within 2 weeks. Would not recommend, not a good experience!
Our entire grade was comprised of exams, and nothing else really had a big effect on it. The exams were BRUTAL and I would definitely not recommend taking him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I don't understand the lecture but if you skip class, you won't get access to any of the lecture notes. I learned through the homework which is A LOT! He's a good lecturer, maybe it's just me not being smart enough. The test are tough. No weekly quizzes so the test does account for BIG percentage. Thebfinal exm was the toughest.

Despite his tough exams I think his lectures are quite useful and engaging. He uses examples straight out of the books, and connects it to his lectures. His exams are pretty brutal, and it really tests whether you know the material or not. He's a great guy though, just pay attention and put effort in the class and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Adrian is a great guy, and is extremely knowledgeable. He does seem to do a lot of proofs, which eventually turn out to be quite helpful. Not everything he says or works out on the board will make sense right away, but eventually you'll get it. His tests are difficult, but manageable if you know your stuff. Wish I had him for future Calc classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Adrian is a great teacher and person. You can tell he actually cares about students' well being. His exams are quite hard, and he grades very harshly, but in the end it all works out. He lets you use your calculator (and he encourages you to put notes and formulas into it), which is something that all math professors should do. Recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Jenkins is an experienced professor, his calc lectures were clear and his way of explaining is straight forward. However he will go tough on you, he prides on his tests being the final gates of calc. If you put the time, work and are sure of your bases you can pass. In office hours he explained hard problems thoroughly.  Amazing professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think he's a horrible professor. He enjoys giving hard exams. This year he couldn't complete the course so he just went over the exercises quickly. I had the worst experience ever.

I was very lucky to have Jenkins for calc 2 and calc 3. When it comes to mathematics, he definitely knows his stuff. His lectures are very informative and mostly easy to listen to. If you want to do well in his class, make sure you attend every lecture. Do all the required online homework, and do some of the suggested problems from the textbook.

One of the first professors I had at Iowa State and he set the bar high. His tests are definitely challenging but he gives you a strong curve. Does a great job explaining things in class and will answer questions thoroughly.
Exams are brutal. Interesting guy and really loves what he teaches. Makes it easier to pay attention

Dr. Jenkins does an excellent job teaching the material. His explanations are clear, and he seems to have a good grasp of what the students are thinking. He really encourages and teaches us to grow our way of thinking.  Crazy difficult professor and course though.

I've heard that in upper calculus he does a great job teaching, but with this class he did terrible.  Did not seem to want to help students at all, and encouraged people to drop. Nothing could help prepare us for the exams for he pulled a lot of the questions out of no where.  Usually an A student, ended with a B only because of the huge curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very difficult. Good at teaching high level calculus, but this guy doesn't mess around. No curve until the very end. Best math lectures I've ever had, but by FAR the hardest tests as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer, don't miss class. However he offers no materials at all online so the textbook is your only resource. Test are very hard and not curved, he curves the course grade at the very end only, so you don't get any real sense of where you stand in the class until the class is over and he posts the final course grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jenkins is a genuine guy but that doesn't make up for his teaching. He gives homework that is not graded and there is no way to look up if you go the answers right to make sure your even doing the questions correctly. Also his teaching and the book do not lineup at all so the homework doesn't help anyway. God help me as i go into this final exam...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His class is HARD. He may be a good professor for higher level calc classes but when it comes to trig he did not do a great job in my opinion. He warned us at the beginning of the semester that the homework questions would not prepare you for the exam because they are not hard enough. Homework is also not graded and no answers in back of book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great math professor, he's sardonically funny and loves to tell you how hard everything is going to be. He teaches with lots of examples that helped me learn how to do the problems even when I didn't get the theory. He makes hella hard tests but he curves so everything comes out alright. You can tell he cares about his students.

Very good professor. Glad to hear I have him again next semester. Tests count as a good amount of your grade percentage. Overall a very good professor who knows the material and is willing to answer any questions you may have.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Adrian is the best math professor that I have had while at Iowa State. His class is very difficult and he prides himself on having extremely hard test, but he teaches the material very well. If you actually want to learn the material he is the professor to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor is the best I have had for math. He is very good at explaining things, and will answer your questions well. He is extreamly transparent about the difficulty of the exams, and what will be on them. However to succeed in this class because of its difficulty you have to spend A TON of time working problems. Course has a large curve
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Exams are brutal, but he does an excellent job of going over the material and preparing you for the exams. One of the best professors I've had here. He's there to get you through the material and puts things into real world perspective. Hopeful to have him again for the rest of my math classes here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor i've ever had. When in need of help, he does NOTHING to help you.
Great lecturer. Knows what he's talking about and proves it. Fantastic person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best math teachers you will ever have in college, perhaps in all of your academic life. But you need to have a study plan that works for his extremely difficult exams. And don't even think about skipping math homework, those homework quizzes need to be perfect.

Michael Adrian Jenkins was somewhat of an interesting professor. He makes his class look really hard, and if you want a good grade you definitely have to work for it. Curve? Oh yeah, expect it especially with low averages such as 40 in the class. Practice from the book, go to office hours and go to class and you'll be in great shape.

Go to class. Write down all the examples and definitions. If you don't understand it, you may need to go back and re-decipher your notes. If you ask questions, Adrian answers them pretty well. Once in a while his methods were confusing, but for the most part it just took some practice to get the hang of.
Not very clear when explaining things, doesn't prepare you well for exams

Adrian is a great professor. He is one of the few that wants to make sure you are going to pass. He gets his point across in lectures and will point out the equations at the end to be sure you at least get that down. Do the practice problems he gives and you are sure to pass.

Great lecturer, tough class. He's really good at explaining concepts and teaching you everything you need to know, that being said, tests are tough (which prepares you for midterm/final) and he grades tough. Grade is 80% exams 10% attendance and 10% quizzes. Do the optional homework, he pulls quiz questions directly from it.

He teaches fast and efficiently.  Zone out for five min and you're lost as hell.  Miss a class you might as well drop.  Very hard tests and a tough grader.  He has a decent sense of humor.  He wears the same thing almost every day.
Jenkins is a goofy dude, but he knows what he is talking about. Overall, he is a great teacher that does enough practice problems in class to understand the concepts. Great teacher.
Adrian is a goofy guy, but honestly incredibly personable with a very firm understanding of what he is teaching. He explains things in a very follow-able way. I highly recommend him.

Hard and fast paced. Everyday review needed to pass. Half the class dropped. Prides himself on low test scores. Averages in my class were 49-64. Book and his style don't mix ( differences in what topics are emphasized) and only used it for practice problems. Practice problems necessary for comprehension. DON'T MISS CLASS IF YOU WANT TO PASS.

Teacher's tests were difficult and often did contained concepts that were rarely talked about in class.  Seemed to always blame a poor class average for tests on the students and did not accept responsibility for any errors in teaching material or prepping students for the tests.

Adrian was great- always helpful. He will prepare you better for the calculus series better than any other professor. He explains things clearly, and manages to make abstract concepts intuitive. You will come out of his class with a far deeper understanding of calculus than any other professor in the calc 1 department.
Good teacher but very tough tests. Must prepare

If you want to actually learn Calculus, Jenkins is the professor for you. His tests are way harder than the rest of the sections, but it makes the midterm and final easier. He explains exactly what's going to be on the test and goes through problems very systematically - he explains the thought process at each step. It's a very hard class, though.
He is good at explaining concepts but his tests are hard. If you want an A you'll need to really know the material.
Puts material that was not covered in class or in the book on quizzes and exams.

I have taken Calculus previously & I thought this class would just be more of a review. But, this professor's teaching style and harsh grading have made this review session into a full blown nightmare. His lectures tend to go off on wild tangents which makes the material hard to understand. Mr. Jenkins takes pride in having such a high fail rate.

He was by far the best math teacher I had for explaining what we were learning, especially compared to the other  Iowa State math teachers. However, more than half the class either dropped or failed. His clicker questions are trying to trick you as well as his test questions with many kids getting 0 out of 25 if you don't get the right answer.
Very good teacher. Very difficult. If you have an open mind he is great

Jenkins class is very difficult and you definitely need some previous calculus in order to understand. I ended up with a B- final grade that got curved to an A. The SI exam reviews are very helpful. I used these and some of Jenkin's practice problems to study. What I really hated is the homework. It takes forever and doesn't help much.

If you want to know your Calculus as well as any student on campus, Jenkins is your guy. Best lecturer I've had.  Taught me Calc I & II. Tough exams but it will serve you well on the departmental midterm and the final. Knowledge is unmatched. Jenkins has his signature daily attire of a chalk-dusty sweater, shorts and sneakers; comes ready to work.
Jenkins is a decent professor. His test are hard because he fails to go over example problems similar to the ones in class. Though, if you are struggling visit him and he will help you.
Great math teacher Follow him in class really learn a lot His exams are hard though
He explains concepts fairly well, and if you do the homework, attend class, and do the suggested problems, the tests shouldn't be too bad.

I've had Jenkins for Calc I, II, and III. He is a good teacher and explains what he expects you to know for his test and especially the finals. Do the recommended problems and examples. Really likes to put "tricky" problems on tests that allow him to cover several concepts with a single problem. But overall, learned a lot and did well on the finals

He was hard to understand. He spoke english well but what he was saying made no sense. I couldn't talk to him one on one due to other classes but from a student who went to class almost every time his class was hard. He tried to trick you on every exam he would never give you something simple. Averages could be as high as 60%. Great guy, hard class

One of the best lecturers I've ever had. Explicitly states expectation for exams and equips students with all tools necessary to get an A. Clearly answers any and all questions. Provides problem-solving methodology and algorithms when appropriate. All told,the class is still difficult. NOTE: do Exercises given in class-very helpful on exams.

Extremely good lecturer-one of the best I've ever had. Explicitly states all expectations for exams and provides students with all tools necessary to get an A in the class. Clearly explains problem-solving methodology and algorithms, if applicable. Answers all questions. Very helpful during office hours. All said, class is still hard.

I had him for class he tells you to drop out for the first half of class. the tests are very hard and barley correspond to what you learn. He's better than some teachers though so if you have him he's not the worst..but he's not even close the good. He also makes you my math lab (online homework) pay attention to that! and Do his suggested problems
Goofy teacher but really knows his stuff. Need to have self discipline in his class or you will do bad. Most of your grade comes from your test score.

ABE 3160 is A LOT of work. There is a lot of homework and in-class tasks that take up a large portion of the grading. Adina is a decent professor, though much of the work is done on your own. There's not much teaching going on in this class, as it's almost a flipped classroom with lectures online from 2020. Overall, she's serviceable, and that's ok

Adina is alright at helping out. the class is very intensive and covers a lot of information in matlab. most the class is how to code differential equations in MATLAB. most the class is homework (5hrs a week) and 3 exams. you can work with classmates to complete homework. exams are online and open canvas. this class will keep you busy for sure. c

If you show up, actually watch the video lectures and complete the assignments, it's a fairly easy A. Dr. Howe provides good feedback to questions and doesn't often beat around the bush. She gives extra credit opportunities and grades very easily if she can see that you understand the fundamentals. She doesn't count off for silly mistakes.

Isn't willing to work with students when they have concerns or do not understand the content in class. Not only does she not teach her lectures in person, she only bases your performance in the class on 3 exams and homeworks with no other opportunities to show effort or redeem yourself. Would not recommend this professor.

This class is taught via pre-recorded lecture videos compiled by various professors who have taught 316 so the lecturing done by Dr. A was more worked problems than anything else. Be ready for lots of homework as this is a learn by doing style class. If anything was unclear/you had a problem with your code, she was very helpful during office hours
Do not take this class in Spring, the Fall teacher is better. Not the best experience of Iowa State Professor.
Horrible professor. The TA basically taught the class.

I think Dr. Howe did a great job for how tough the material is and the number of students in the class. It was difficult to keep up with the assignments and material but i was also taking 12 other credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Solid choice for TSM 210, a caring professor who respects students opinions and works hard to interact with students
The best TSM 210 professor
Dr. Howe is can be a good teacher, but lectures are not her strong suit. She often incorrectly solves problems during lectures and is not clear with examples. She can be helpful during office hours.

She is so smart that it is hard for her to teach the proper items most of the time. Sometimes while working on a class example she will compute the answers wrong and have to go back. Come to find out she had been using the wrong formula since the beginning. This happens at least once a week. The powerpoint lectures are mediocre at best.

knows his stuff but is insistent on NOT answering student's questions outside of lecture. ghosted students several times on whether the course would have a curve and completely ignored you if anything you ask is unrelated to course material.

Aditya is clearly very passionate about the things he teaches, which definitely makes it easier to pay attention. However, you simply will not know what grade you have in this class until you receive your final transcript. Every other professor at Iowa State has figured out how to show weighted grades in Canvas, so Aditya has no excuse not to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont count on him to actually teach you anything. And be ready for a several grade drop once he does his "curve", one of the worst cases and professors I have ever had before.

If you take this in spring be prepared to not enjoy springbreak. Had an assignment due in the middle of springbreak and an exam the day after you get back. Lectures are a was of time, you are better off googling everything, but he give not only quizzes on canvas but in-person exams.

Aditya knows his stuff, he just can't teach. I attended EVERY lecture, yet I learned more through YouTube videos and self teaching - quite literally everything else but lecture actually helped me learn. The TAs did a better job than him. You won't know your grade AT ALL throughout the semester until your final grade shows up on your transcript.

This was probably the most poorly organized class I have had. No one knew their grade throughout the semester, and the grading scale, in particular, was unforgiving. The topics were hard to pick up from the lecture. Professor Ramamoorthy also writes fairly hard exams, and the quizzes are weighed heavily. The class was harder than it needed to be.

I feel like this is a hard class to teach. Ramamoorthy is an okay guy but the way information was presented is not very good. Lectures were okay; reading the slides can be more helpful than listening to him at times.

Aditya knows his stuff and tries his best to make sure students understand what is being taught. But I found I had to do a lot of out of classroom study to understand what he was teaching. Topics are presented in a way that is difficult to understand at times.

Like most math courses here, expect overly theoretical definitions and fairly difficult exams. Biggest change I'd recommend with this class is lower the grade weight of quizzes and make them less frequent. Other than that it's not that bad.
You have to put in the work. I would ask him questions outside of class and go to recitation. Some very difficult exams but if you understand the material you should survive.
Absolutely abysmal. Avoid at all costs!!!

Ramamoorthy was the best professor I had this semester. He was extremely caring after the semester went online and really tried to make the transition seamless. The class wasn't terribly hard but not extremely easy. The lecture slides were great and the homework's were fair, as well as the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Hands down, one of the worst professors in the department. Grades on attendance EVEN after coronavirus pandemic. Reaching out to him means absolutely nothing, as he is set on following pre-defined guidelines throughout the semester. Exams are based on topics he hasn't even discussed. Treats you like a Math/Statistics grad student. Avoid if possible
Really good at making exams and quizzes, he makes them fair and reasonable. Homework also helps you prepare really well for quizzes and exams.
Very math heavy. Learned a lot.

He treats the class like a theoretical introduction to signals and systems without getting into the meat and potatoes of it. It is much more like a math class than an Engineering class. His tests do not match up with the homework at all. Be prepared to leave this class more confused than when you started and expect big curves at the end.
terrible textbook, no examples, always wondering why nobody understands material. isn't it obvious, rewards texters with tootsie rolls

This professor makes the class (vert bio) as hard as possible. I spent more time studying for this class than I did for the “acts” in highschool. I would say this professor has the mindset that this is your whole life so u might as well so good. However if you're like me and a full time student and working a job you WILL struggle. Good luck!

Dr.Adams is one of the most passionate and inspiring professors I have ever had! His love for the natural world is remarkable.  In regard to the class, it is just a LOT of content.  It is all very interesting but just know to succeed you must study and take quality notes.  There are 3 big exams and 1 final each worth roughly 22% of your grade.

I had him for fall 2020, so it was a weird semester. He explained concepts really well and was super understandable about anything that came up. He recorded the lectures so that you could view them after the class which is what I did. If you don't at least watch the lectures though, you probably won't do well. No textbook use. Heavy on power points
The lectures are quite entertaining. The tests are somewhat difficult, but running through the slides before taking them usually helps significantly.

People in ANS and NREM always complain that this is a difficult course, but if you actually listen and do the SI worksheets before the exams you can easily pass. Lab is enjoyable and Dr. Adams gives great lectures.

I enjoyed Dr. Adams in this course. He posts his powerpoints on Canvas and it worked well for me to study the slides in order to get a good grade. My recommendations are to not purchase the textbook because it is not used and to get the seminar paper done earlier in the semester. He does not grade attendance except for the in-class assignment days.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Adams is a fantastic and engaging lecturer and person. Really enjoyed this class but would be lying if I said I didn't get frustrated by his unnecessarily harsh grading and tricky (almost "gotcha") exam wording.
Dean Adams makes lectures so much more interesting than just sitting there reading off slides. Tests are pretty hard since they cover a lot of topics. Definitely made me realize my study habits suck.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Lectures were always entertaining and it made class worth waking up and going to. Tests were easy if you show up, pay attention, and study. Genuinely a nice guy and fun to talk to, one of those people you can tell he loves what he does and it shows, 10/10.
Great teacher on the subject. Very test heavy, that are pretty hard. Go to the SI sessions. The book is not used at all.

Adams is fantastic. Enthusiastic and very caring. Tests are tough but doable with effort and memorization. Lab is great and really rounds out the course. The breadth is the most challenging aspect of the course. The book is worthless. Go to lecture, pay attention, go to SI, and find someone with studyblue.
Really nice guy and funny. The material itself wasn't always interesting, but he usually made it worth going to class

There's a lot to learn in this class so the lectures tend to be very heavy. But the topics are soooo interesting. The tests are mostly vocab and have short answers that are worth up to 4 points. In order to get a good grade start memorizing vocab right away. Adams is super cool and is really interested in the subject and it shows with his enthusiam

The content of this class is pretty straight forward but you have to study your ass off to get a good grade because the exams are fill in the blank. He is not very helpful, I had emailed him multiple times for help and his responses were always very short and a bit condescending.

This has been my favorite class so far! Dr. Adams makes it enjoyable to go to class and explains tough concepts in an easy way to understand. The tests are all fill in the blank and short answer as well as a lot of memorization, but if you take notes  and understand the material you will do fine!

Dean was my favorite professor so far. The class was hard because it covered a LOT of information, and you pretty much had to know everything. But learn ALL the vocab (make notecards!) and you're fine. He was super enthusiastic and hilarious, and he organized the lectures really well.
The only difficult exam is the second one. Otherwise, as long as you learn the vocab, you will do well on the test no problem.
Awesome class.  Awesome teacher. Very enthusiastic.  His tests are straight from the lecture so just take notes and youll do fine (:
Best professor i have had hands down! He is very interesting to listen to and will keep you awake in the morning.
Tests are kind of difficult and specific. He's interesting in lecture, which is good because you have to go (textbook is useless and he does not post complete powerpoints)
is very enthusiastic about what he is teaching. this makes it easier to pay attention!
He is a fun teacher, he makes the material really interesting and is very passionate. His tests can be difficult, with weirdly worded fill in the blanks!!!
Dr. Adams is a excellent teacher. He is very lively in class and makes it very interesting for you and him. He deffinatly ranks top among the professors I've had at ISU.
Dean Adams was an awesome prof. He makes learning fun, plus the subject matter was interesting but he knew what was up.
Dr. Adams is interesting during lecture. He is high energy and highly passionate about what he teaches. His tests are a little wishy washy. Take this class for the easy grade.

This class isn't that hard but it's pretty much impossible to get an A. I scored within the top ten every single exam and still only got an A- because he barely curves the class. The first lab practical is impossible.

This guy is hilarious and extremely weird, but it's a great class. Plus his notes have words missing so you are pretty much motivated to attend his lecture b/c the missing words aren't on WebCT. Attend SI or download the worksheets online and you'll do fine, trust me. His tests ARE difficult but it only makes you want to study more...
This class was very interesting but also very challenging.
This class is really hard but he keeps you awake and interested.
Great class, awesome professor.  One of the few classes I can honestly say I looked forward to attending at ISU.

Notes are nice because they're print off from WebCT but still keep you awake in class because you have to fill in missing words.  Not the greatest prof but not terrible.  Acted weird sometimes so that made it entertaining.  Exams were pretty difficult b/c fill in the blank and short answer

He explains concepts really well and is very patient if you come to office hours not having understood a single thing. The content can be difficult but he certainly doesn't make it more difficult than necessary.

Professor is nice overall, teaching might not be his best suit, but he really cares for his students. He kept the weekly quizes easy.  I would say exams are definetly long and difficult as they need more time and two hour format wouldn't have been bad. But it is better to take with him than with lutz.

Pavan is one of the worst professors I've had. Lectures are super basic, but homework and exams are way harder and feel like a completely different class. Our second exam average was ~50%, and he tested heavily on CYK, algorithm (CNF, NPDA etc. were on the Homework but not exams), overall the class felt confusing, unfair, and badly designed.
extremely bad teaching, full of attitude, keeps changing goals and manipulates grade, unapproachable, disconnected, gets stiff, obsessed with wedding-talk, never professional and helpful

Cares a lot of about the topics he teaches. Does a good job answering student questions. Topic is very hard and theory based - his teaching is good but you are required to self study because stuff like this doesn't soak in magically. Very hard class but well worth it and you learn super useful stuff.
Pavan is a horrible teacher. He does not seems to care anymore about students success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Just Awful!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pavan is a great guy. He really seems to care about students. That being said, lecturing is not his strong suit. They often became long and hard to follow due to monotonous teaching & sloppy handwriting. Hard exams, hard homework, and hard group projects. Do not take this course with 327 or any other time consuming class.

311 is supposed to be one of the hardest CS classes. It seemed reasonably difficult, but there might have actually been a normal curve with a mean at C or C+. A lot of people failed. 435/535 was incredibly difficult and interesting but it was 90% grad students, so it seemed to be geared toward them. Lectures are filled with information.

The lectures got a little boring and lengthy at times. The projects were fun, the homeworks were hard, and the tests were impossible. Midterm average was a 50. However, Pavan is an insanely nice guy. He'll curve the class and often give points back as long as you talk to him. Plus what are you gonna do, take 311 with Jim?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor seems to be less enthusiastic when teaching. It almost looks like  someone else ask him to teach this class. He try to finish the content as soon as possible and most of students prefer googling the topics than learning from him. Assignments are not that hard if you know bit of java.

He is very clear in his explanations and writes code in class to explain various topics. The class has almost 8 or 10 TA's, and about half of these actually know the concepts very well. There are three exams in this class -- first one is super easy, second is a bit difficult and the final is the hardest. Fair grading and good quality of teaching.

He was a horrible teacher! Could not understand him, tried to get help and he sent me to the TAs who were too busy to help.  There are no tutor or SIs so you are basically on your own if you don't understand coding. I would not recommend this class with this professor!

Subject is tough. Pavan is a good teacher and explains  clearly. Attend his class regularly.His English might be a bit fast, but not hard to understand. His homework are key for score. Exams are similar to homework. But, he is very smart and tests you based on what you know. He will post the class notes. No textbooks required.

Explains concepts very well in lecture, don't use book at all if you go to class and take notes, recitations are super useful and tests are easy if you payed attention in class and understand material
LOVED this class. My favorite class this semester. Loved how Pavan taught the class, and loved learning to program. Very interesting
The thing is Pavan is a very nice man so its hard to write this, but he is not a good teacher. There are other profs teaching this section. DO NOT TAKE IT WITH PAVAN!

Explained most topics very well. Accent not a problem. Knows material quite well. Delivers most lectures with no resources/notes save a marker. Most lectures on whiteboard only. Lectures fairly boring, but much not new to me. Homework is where I really learned & was my biggest test prep. I think course would be too hard for a 1st programming course

Pavan is an extremely knowledgeable professor who uses useful and meaningful examples on the board. Attendence for this class always gets extremely low by the end of the first month so has a small class feel. Also 60% of the class fails because 60% of the class doesn't attend class.

He is extremely systematic. The course is difficult no doubt, but I feel with a little more hard work I would've done a lot better. I think he is a great professor and tries his best to get the concepts across.
Really knows the material. Lectures can be somewhat boring (mostly due to the material). Has an accent but isn't hard to understand. The homework took a lot of time.

Pavan is more than happy to help. His lectures are informative, but his notes on webct need improving if they are to be of any worth outside of lectures.  If you have trouble with foreign accents, choose another instructor. His isn't bad, but I've heard some mention it. I don't personally think anyone who pays attention would have trouble.
Couldn't understand him at all, but he put up good notes on Web-CT.  I came into the class with prior knowledge so it was really easy.  Class average though was in 60-70% range.

Was not very clear, and they don't understand that if you are programming for a profession, it's not just one person working on the program, but many people to get the desired outcome. If you even get help from another student you are charged with academic dishonesty and have to go through the judicial process, because they have sticks up their but

The class is not easy, thats why you have to pay atention all the time. Dont miss class, and understand that practice is what defines your grade at test time. Look for the other teachers lectures and learn from all three of them, to get the correct idea. Practice practice practice, to pass with a B. LOL.
He is a perfect teacher
No Comments
good professor, explained the material well. class is not easy by any means but it's not supposed to be.

Audri is by far the worst teacher in the CS department. He is unclear, moves too fast, and doesnt seem to care about the students. I think like 60% of the class is failing this semester! He is really bad, take this course with anyone else you can.

This class is a great way to earn an easy A and have an outlet for stress. You don't have to be a yoga expert to take this class. Just show up, participate, and put a little effort in. There is one presentation and one outside activity you have to do and then write two reflections. Equipment is provided. She also incorporates pilates to the session
Cynthia is amazing, just show up to class, and there's not many assignments.

For something like dance, she was fairly strict. Very monotone and expected you to have a base of knowledge coming in. If you have already taken dance, you'll be fine. If this is your first, it's fairly difficult.

Cynthia is quite a lady. She has a bubbly, energetic personality. Her classes are rarely structured which leads to some interesting lesson "plans." Sometimes it is hard to take the class seriously but you just have to go with it. Grades were not in until posted on Accessplus. She is very accommodating though, but you must communicate.

I took Dance 250 (yoga) with Cynthia & Janice. This class is amazing, I highly recommend taking it! You can only miss one class, & you have to do a presentation and write some reflections. But overall the class is really relaxing and fun. Cynthia was really good at reading the room & picking a good routine for the day based on how we were feeling

Cynthia is great. She really knows modern dance and some of the exercises really helped me generate more interesting choreography. Her classes can get a little repetitive, and the reading was that useful to me, but definitely a worthwhile class if you're interested in choreography!
Very nice. Doesn't really understand the concept of a constant beat. But really nice.

Cynthia is a really nice person (though not very clear) and it's easy to pass the class if you show up, but Ballet I was one of the worst classes I've ever taken. Doing pretty much the exact same routines every single day throughout the semester really made the year drag on. Again, it's easy, just not very enjoyable in my opinion.
Cynthia is very helpful.  Class is mandatory though.  It was a good break in my day from normal classes.  Only buy the book if you plan on taking more than one ballet class, we never really used it.

Dont take online- makes easy class way harder. The Canvas page is poorly set up and info is inconsistent. Doesn't respond quickly to email, and grades are entered rarely - it's a fight to get what you need. There's 3 recorded lectures per module, and they are incredibly redundant. Also requires online group project. Helpful in person at least.

Really enjoyed this class. I did not attend lecture but I attended labs. He would post the Top Hat questions at the end of the week. The concepts weren't hard even without the lecture, and if you were struggling there were plenty resources available. Kinda felt bad for him having to lecture over spreadsheets. Overall easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, class time was unnecessary, as most of it felt wasted by Adisak rambling about loosely related topics without saying anything of actual substance. The TAs for the course were phenomenal and extremely accessible and helpful. But I will say Adisak is extremely kind and always tries to make class fun for his students.

Probably the easiest class I've taken, the exams are pretty specific and very vocab/memorization based and at the Testing Center. Up to 10% extra credit if you do DataCamp Exercises. The exams aren't worth much, you can fail both of them and still get an A in the class. Labs are the most important, weekly.

Class is an easy A, most content can be completed without reading or watching videos. Adisak seems nice, but good luck getting a hold of him. I sent him 10 emails over the semester and received 0 replies. I honestly have no idea what his role is in this course, since the voice in the lecture videos is not his.

Adisak is very kind and cares about his students; he will likely grant any extension. The class is an easy A, but it is taught very poorly. You'll learn very little from the lectures; the labs are only partially relevant. Class was consistently behind schedule because of how often he goes off task, talking about something unrelated.

Mostly easy, with lots of YouTube videos covering the mid-level and cumulative assignments. You don't really have to attend class. Easy class overall, he even opened assignments up for us to redo over thanksgiving break.
Useless and boring lectures, but the class content is easy.

THIS IS A FAKE ONLINE CLASS. This class was advertised as fully online, meaning it would include online exams. This was also on the syllabus, but then, during the semester, the professor administered both midterm exams in person through the testing center. Do not take this online, if anything you might learn more in person.

Adisak is a really nice guy, but his lectures were not helpful. This course has a substantial amount of homework, and the only way to truly learn it is by attending the labs. The homework was very frustrating and was just busy work. If you can take this class online, I would recommend it. It was overall easy, just the workload was annoying.

The online class format is very difficult to follow. For a class with no coding prerequisites, the pace goes extremely fast. I would have liked to see more in-depth lectures, rather than covering topics quickly.
Funniest guy ever.

This was the Intro to AI Class but I couldn't find it on the list. As long as you tried and submitted mostly clompleted work, you are good to pass. He's very passionate about this stuff but sometimes can be confusing.

His lectures were so boring, which I feel bad for saying, because he genuinely wants to help you if you show interest in Data Science. However, most of his lectures consisted of him just rambling about vaguely related topics until much later, when at some point he actually talks about the subject matter.

Honestly, this is just a ChatGPT class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: His lectures are him rambling and not actually teaching until the final 5 minutes and then go over the class period time. You will have to learn everything by yourself through Zybooks in super long assignment because he will probably not teach you much. I would say take the class with another professor but he is the only one.
This class is easy if you use AI or copy from what the TA shows. Will you learn something valuable from the lectures? No.

The lectures were unhelpful and didn't provide the necessary information. Most learning had to be done independently, making Zybooks assignments difficult due to little guidance. Labs felt like just following the TA rather than applying concepts. The course lacked clear instruction and integration, making it ineffective. You will learn nothing.

Overall wasn't too difficult of a class and Adisak was ok at explaining material. His lectures weren't too beneficial to the weekly assignments and you'll find yourself doing everything on your own. I would recommend taking this class online if you get the opportunity.
The overall class is light. Adisak is a great guy, but the lectures are boring. If you do all the work on MyLabIT, you'll get an A. His TopHats are worth credit but very easy questions.

The class isn't very demanding, and the professor is nice. However, having this as an in-person class feels pointless since most of the work is self-explanatory and can be done from your dorm. I didn't gain much from attending, though the online assignments, while sometimes frustrating, weren't too bad overall.

Adisak was a great professor. Though the class was boring he often made lectures fun. He was very kind and gracious when it came to answering any questions I had about the class or homework. Attendance isn't mandatory but in-class participation through Top Hat plays a big role in your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Adisak is a decent professor for this easy course. Lectures can be dull, but staying on top of labs and homework makes it manageable. unstuck AI was a helpful study tool alongside the free textbook.
Overall if you attend class and lab you will be completely fine. He is a little bit hard to understand at times but overall not bad.
Adisak is a helpful professor and a decent lecturer. Com S 113 is an easy course so long as you stay on top of labs and homework. Lectures are pretty boring but if you pay attention you will learn.

this class is not as difficult as some people make it seem. attendance is required for labs, but the labs are only there to help, so GO TO THEM! If you do all your homework and get good scores on the end-of-week assignments, you'll get at least a B pretty easily. with some extra effort, an A is not difficult to achieve. He also added a small curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found this professor hard to engage with. I'm sure he knew the content well, but I don't think it always came through in his teaching. Often found myself having to teach the material to myself outside of class even though I went to all the lectures.

I am only a month into the semester, and I can already tell that this is going to be my easiest class. Professor Adisak is very kind, and willing to make any accommodations. Attendance is not mandatory, however, I recommend going because he practically gives you the answers to all the homework and quizzes every time. Very minimal work and very easy

He is very good at answering questions if you have any. An extremely approachable professor. Online work is heavy via Pearson. Would recommend getting them done in advance before the lecture and lab. Lectures have Tophat questions and there are quite a few, so if you usually skip, your score might be affected.
By far the strangest and funniest class I have taken. Attendance isn't mandatory, but the tophats do contribute to your grade. Doing the lab work ahead of time would allow you to not go to lab.

Mr. Adisak has been a great professor during my freshmen year. One of the most important qualities for a professor is understanding the student body. He extends deadlines when he sees students struggle with a certain topic or module and genuinely wants students to understand the topic.

Stupidly easy course. Noone showed up to lectures after the first week as this course can be done all virtually. Grading is often unclear and TAs have wildly different criteria. There is a focus on visualization using software which is nice. Not sure I got much out of this course, but it made this semester easier. 1-2 hour time commitment weekly

All of the content is covered in lecture videos, so the in-person lectures are very sporadic and irrelevant. Going to labs is key to doing well in this class. Quizzes have multiple tests and are fairly easy, but the tests are on topics covered once (but they're online). Overall, this wasn't a hard class, but expect to be on your own for most of it.
Adisak is a great teacher, he cares a lot, he is fun, funny, and engaging. On material both difficult and easy, he has a way of making it all seem like the easiest thing in the world.
Pretty easy class. Lectures are kind of useless because you learn everything through the homework but the professor is a nice guy.

The class itself wasn't super difficult but the knowledge for the exams isn't very similar to what you do for homework. It takes a good 2-4 hours every week to complete the homework. This class also uses Top Hat for attendance which is kind of expensive. You are also constantly working ahead while trying to complete the previous week.

Very easy class if you get the slides from the TAs, but they didn't advertise it. Lectures used tophat and were extremely annoying. You learn two chapters ahead the entire time, which is confusing and not at all useful. Only takes around 3-4 hours per week.

The class is pretty easy if you keep up with assignments. I learned the majority of the information from the homework and didn't learn a lot in the lectures. Labs are optional if you finish the homework for the week.
Hands down the easiest to understand professor I've ever had! I love how clear and concise his lectures are!

Just finished my summer online semester with Sukul today. I pulled out an A. However, I do have a couple of serious problems with his system. Grades were messed up all the whole semester, and he doesn't respond in a timely manner (usually 2-3 days, after I send a follow up). Good, funny guy tho... my main beef is that he doesn't seem to care much.

Com Sci 113 is a very easy class. Did not need to attend lectures during the week. Labs are required but the work is generally easy and the TAs walk you through it. Adisak is a very good professor and very funny as well.

Very little engagement between professor and student. Attended a few classes and then never went again. Still got an A because the TA's just gave you the answers for the labs and the homework was based off the lab. Could have been an arranged course with no lectures. Not a bad experience, but not a great one.

Adisak is a pretty laid back dude. I only went to like three lectures at the beginning of the semester and still got an A for the semester. The TAs are generally really helpful with the MyLab stuff as well. Honestly if you sit down and spend an hour on this class a week, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This course was easy, but I couldn't understand the professor (because of his accent), so attending class was a waste of time. The assignments are pretty straightforward. There is a book, but I never used it. Adisak does a good job of answering questions/giving good directions. I don't recommend a mac computer (makes course a bit more complicated).

The assignments were incredibly easy if you can figure out how to finesse the MyLab system. Don't go to lectures as the assignments are just figuring out where specific buttons are located on Excel/Access. Go to the labs as they literally can do all of the homework for you. The course was 75% homework and 25% exams - get homework done & you'll pass

This class will use a decent amount of time, you spend about 45 min a week on the homework and then you have 2 100 point mini tests each week which is about 2 hours of your time. Do not go to class, but go to the attendance mandatory labs, that is where you learn the stuff for the weeks homework.
The classwork itself is a grind but this professor definitely does his best to make sure everyone passes with optimal grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Adisak is a great man who is very understanding. He will give you the benefit of the doubt and I respect him a lot

This class is so easy if you have basic tech skills, but Adisak consistently misses the ball with teaching. He gets ahead of schedule, goes on long rants about things and doesnt even know the answer to some of his own questions. You can learn more from the videos within the homework than you can in class.

Easy class and very few requirements for work. However he puts very little work in his class materials, and would just throw articles and websites in expecting everybody to just read from the materials. The materials he pass on would not match the classs progress, the final projects requirements are completely out of nowhere.
Definitely my favorite class at Isu, so fun and Adisak is a super nice person.
Really funny, pretty easy class if you've done anything with excel before.

Adisak is a really great guy and very funny. His class can be challenging sometimes especially when you have lecture before you have taken notes for the chapter since he is always one week ahead. The TopHat questions he made us do during lecture were sometimes challenging but easy to get a good grade if you attend your lab.
Really fun dude and all-around an easy class.

Adisak, or Daddysak as he said we could also call him, is awesome, I had his class online, the course is pretty easy, you use MyITLab for the assignments, they're due every Monday at 6, tests are okay, the second test was a little difficult, but the final isn't cumulative which was nice. He also has great memes in lectures. You'll love him.
Meme God
You could just as easily not show up and learn from the modules online in the textbook. He's a great guy but his lectures are futile.
Sukul is such a great guy. Very nice and funny!
He is super funny. Labs are frustrating but it's not his fault. Maybe you and a friend can split the textbook cost.

Adisaks class is a lot of fun. He is a hilarious teacher, who essentially goes through memes half the time in class. If your looking for an easy A, take this class. However, if you actually want to learn something, I would suggest looking elsewhere. Adisak is a poor teacher and hard to understand at times. No one pays attention is lectures.
My favorite professor so far. The lectures are entertaining and he likes memes.

Great professor and class. The lectures didnt really teach me much but the professor always made it fun. As long as you do the homework and lab projects youll do fine. Everything is graded In a reasonable amount of time and the class is pretty easy if you try. The professor was great and he genuinely wanted all the students to do well.
Great professor! Easy class!

The class is very well structured and the assignments aren't that bad. Adisak is a funny guy and I enjoyed lecture (although it was boring at times), but it's not necessary for passing class. He uses TopHat for attendance so most people just signed in online from home. He seems to know what he's doing and he genuinely wants you to do well.

Took COMSCI with Daddisak and was really enjoyable, little hard to understand but addresses it and will clarify if you ask. Although lecture was boring, he was funny. Very accessible outside of class through a class Facebook page he makes to post memes and to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funniest professor I've ever had. Lectures aren't required but you'll want to go just because of how funny he is. Lots of homework projects but it's all step by step in the textbook. Exams are easy if you go to his review session in class. 10/10 would take again.

He is okay. His accent is a bit difficult to understand, and he goes through the lecture extremely fast. There are quite a few extra credit opportunities throughout the class. Do the homework and attend the labs, and you will pass.

Lectures are kind of a joke. I went to every one but I definitely didn't need to. He was kind of hard to understand during lectures but he still made the lectures interesting and he pretty much tells you the answers to the top hat questions. The class was so easy I passed with over 100%. Just go to your labs each week and you'll be fine
Good class better professor. Can tell he genuinely cares about his students, has a good sense of humor and sets you up as much as he can for you to get a good grade in the class.

Love the guy. The class is super easy. Just do the homework and you will pass, and remember to show up to the lab times. You can have a cheat sheet on every exam. Extra credit will help if you miss an assignment.
Daddyask is the best professor at isu
Great professor who makes the class fun to go to!
Big Adisak fan
Really great professor!
WE ALL LOVE DADDISAK.
Adisak is a great professor who cares about his students.
Big ol 10/10

He is honestly one of the best professors I've had so far! Literally just go to class and the labs, do the assignments and study the night before for exams and you're golden! He's really funny and gives extensions if you ask in person! I loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You will get an A if you do all your hw and make notes for exams

He is a great professor who makes thi class fun. The lectures are a bit are to follow sometimes and a little rushed. Other than that, show up for class and get the homework in on time and you shouldn't have a hard time passing.
Great class! You have 3 assignments due every week but the TAs are super helpful and its easy if you just dont procrastinate

Lectures arent 100% required, but he does top hat pretty much every single day, and he pretty much gives you the answers in class. Definitely attend your labs. You get a cheat sheet for exams which is really nice. 10/10 recommended Dadisak!!

Possibly the best professor I've had in 4 semester of college. Adisak is hilarious, and the best part about his ComS113 class is it's a cakewalk. Plenty of extra credit opportunities in class to allow you to end with over 106%. Just do your homework and labs, and make sure to make note sheets. Yes he does have an accent, but it's easy to understand
As long as you show up to the lab and follow the TA it is an easy A.

Great person, very funny teacher. However, his accent is very hard to understand. If you do some of the extra credit theres no point in going to lectures for attendance points. Youll still end up with a man A or B. Top Hat is accessible from home during lectures. Lab is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Absolute beauty, he LOVES memes and is one of the most entertaining professors out there. The whole class calls him daddysack and he loves it.
good job

He is a cool guy, but his accent can be hard to understand. Make sure you always do your homework, and do it right because they take off points for little things. The tests are okay if you do your homework. Plus, you get a cheat sheet on all of the tests. He does TopHat questions in class and basically gives you the answer to most of them.

Adisak is a hilarious professor. The lectures are pointless but labs are where you learn everything. Go to lab once a week and it is an easy A. He goes over everything on the test the lecture prior to the test and you get a cheat sheet, front and back. There is extra credits, definitely do them and he adds extra points to our test grades.

I'm so torn on how to review Adisak, so I'll rate him as a professor, and not the class. Honestly, lecture is pointless; you learn everything in labs. However, Adisak is very knowledgeable and from my understanding, wrote the book that you'll be using. He's also hilarious and gives tons of EC opportunities. Put forth some effort and you'll be fine.
Awesome sense of humor and prepares you well for tests. Gives lots of top hat points in lectures and lots of extra credit.

Adisak is a great professor with an awesome sense of humor. My class called him Daddisak. You definitely need the textbook but you can just share or borrow from someone if you have lab on different days. The lectures are boring and not helpful but definitely don't skip your labs. You can use a note sheet on the tests and he will curve them too.

Loved Adisak, or as my class joked with him, Daddisak. He has a great sense of humor. The class is simple, follow the directions word for word with the homework and you get 100%. He adds points to tests to bump up grades. Also puts an extension on nearly all assignments if asked. Awesome guy, would retake the class just for him as my professor

Adisak's accent was really hard for me to understand unless I paid extremely close attention, but since his lecture slides and notes were on Blackboard anyway, that didn't end up mattering. Adisak more than made up for that shortcoming with the amount of memes he would share in class, and his overall hilariousness, which made class entertaining.

Adisak lectures 2x a week and a T.A. teaches lab once a week. Lectures weren't helpful for me, but had to go anyways for attendance points. Lab is where you learn step by step how to do that week's hw, much more useful to help pass the class. Overall, adisak is nice guy but spent too much time trying to be the 'cool teacher'. Lab attendanceEasy A

He's a nice & funny guy, but his lectures are confusing and boring. Attendance isn't really mandatory, but he uses TopHat almost everyday. He allows a cheat sheet on the exams, and he gives pretty big curves too. He makes a facebook group page and people always post the HW assignments on them, so you don't have to buy the book.

Dr. Sukul is one of my favorite professors at ISU. He can be hard to understand at times but overall this is a fairly easy course. As long as you do the assignments you can get an A with no problem. Plus he lets you use a cheat sheet during the exams.

Super easy class with a cool professor. He tended to ramble, and his accent would come in thick as he deviated from his original point, but otherwise was good. Tests were super easy. He interacted over facebook and was very easy to reach. Also gave us his personal cell number if needed.... All in all , good guy, but super boring(and easy) class.

Best professor I had. There is a lot of workload every week but he is very flexible with the submission dates. He interacted with the students through facebook and his explaining throughout the lectures are very clear.

Made lecture fun but had quite a bit of top hat so I would suggest going to get those points. The labs were fairly easy and homework was easy as well. Tests were somewhat tough but you had a note sheet for every test which was a major help and he offered like 4 extra credits which I would HIGHLY suggest doing. Overall fun professor.
Great teacher and tries to make the subject fun. One of my favorite teachers. Lets you use a cheat sheet for exams and the homework isn't too difficult as long as you attend the lab.

His lectures are boring but you get credit for attending (10% of your grade!). The course quality really depends on your TA. I had a great TA, so I enjoyed the course, some of my friends did not. Didn't even open the books because they posted the pictures of the assignments on the class FB page. Not a difficult class.

Lectures normally don't make much sense you can't understand him very well, but go for the top hat points (if I even get points for that). 3 Homework assignments a week and lab required. Not an enjoyable class.

Adisak is very funny, students tend to love him as a person. But as a professor his class is a little much at times. Count on 3 Excel/Access assignments a week. He lets you use a cheat sheet on the exams, but no worries, you could write down everything from the lectures down on your cheat sheet, and the test will still be difficult.

Adisak does what he can to help students, but his tests are difficult and there's too many assignments, lots of busy work. There's a strong language barrier, you don't learn anything in his lectures. I wouldn't take another class of his.

It's not that the class is necessarily hard, the hardest part is making yourself attend the lectures. He's funny and full of memes, but the lectures just drag on and attendance is kept by a semi-faulty app *TopHat* and while it is accessible from outside of the hall-questions are thrown in which only a physical attendee would know.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Adisak is hilarious but sometimes difficult to understand during lectures. The class itself is pretty easy in my opinion.
hard to understand, unorganized, allows one day for tests (will be stuck in VERY long testing center lines), not a great professor
He is the nicest professor I ever have.
Adisak is hilarious!

Content was very boring and almost no one shows up to the lectures despite the fact that attendance counts for part of your grade. He's really nice but it's hard to understand him through most of the lecture. Content of the class is pretty irrelevant but it's really easy in my opinion. If you put in the effort you'll get an A easily.

This class is very easy. Clicker points are 10 percent of your grade but he gives you the answers. All of your home work is very straight forward and your other assignments are easily done in the lab. You get to make a full page front and back note sheet for all of the tests and there is one extra credit assignment at the end of the semester.
Loved by students. He is willing to go the extra mile to make sure everyone understand. He has setup many helpful tools including the course FaceBook to help. Overall great professor.
Adisak is a great professor! Fun and entertaining class. Best experience on ISU so far.

Adisak is a good guy. More interested in becoming your friend than teaching. Not very professional but a lot of students like that. You can't understand him very well but if you go to labs and somewhat pay attention your very likely to get a B or above.
Give this teacher a raise and his own meme

Adisak is a great guy, however I felt he was more interested in trying to befriend/be liked by his students, than actually making sure we grasped the concepts of what he was teaching. Going to lecture was nearly pointless due to the language barrier in a large auditorium, but the labs were VERY helpful.
Hard to understand. Go to labs and you'll pass the class easily. Exams are easy.

Really easy class. He's hard to understand sometimes, but his PowerPoints are there and he is willing to go the extra mile so you do understand. He has setup many helpful tools including the course FaceBook to help. Overall great professor.
He is amazing! Best professor or teacher I have ever had. Loved by all students:)
Adisak is a great professor and I would not take the course with anyone else.
Really great class. Adisak does a lot to help everyone out. There is a Facebook page to ask questions, you can use a cheat sheet on the tests, and he drops your lowest homework and lab score.
Great instructor, would recommend  his class to anyone

Very outstanding professor. In all honesty, he can be hard to understand at times, but makes up for it with the Facebook Page he created for the class.  The lectures can be a bit boring, but it is important to go to them because lecture attendance is a decent chunk of your grade. Try HW assignments early in the week then talk to TA for extra help.
He makes himself readily available to students. If you go to lecture the assignments are easy. Definitely take his class!!

Such a great professor. If you have a chance to take this class  you should take it. It's not a bad class. Adisak is very helpful if you need help. Always enjoyed going to class and was always looking forward to see what funny thing he was going to say in class. Great just great!
Awesome professor! Easy class!
Gives good explanations and makes class fun! Awesome professor!

Such a great professor. If you have a chance to take this class  you should take it. It's not a bad class. Adisak is very helpful if you need help. Always enjoyed going to class and was always looking forward to see what funny thing he was going to say in class. Great just great.
Best professor ever
This class is huge in Fall. Adisak always try to help you when ever the problem is. He is my favorite professor so far. I learn lots of new tricks from the class.
Thanks for everything. You're amazing
Adisak is a beauty. No problems getting an A just do your homework and go to lab
