A favorite among many students.  Lecture attendance is required, even though you learn very little from them.  While he can be difficult to understand sometimes, his lectures are funny and relaxed.  Most of the learning comes from lab projects.
It's a boring class, but Adisak makes it a lot more fun than it should be.

Adisak is the one prof who really cares about the students. if you have a question or are having trouble with the homework hes always there before/after lecture to help out and is always reachable by email. Really fun lecture too, there are clicker questions but he keeps the class up beat and hilarious.

If you can find any other professor do it. Language barrier is unbelievable and makes it almost impossible to focus in class. Lectures are mandatory because there are clicker points but they are only for attendance. Everything else is easy. I learn 0% of the course from him and 100% from my lab TA. Good luck

This guy is savage. Very knowledgeable, quite hilarious, and likes to try new things in lecture. Not afraid to call students out that are trying to beat his clicker point system. If you have basic computer competency then you will get an A in his class with little effort, unless you don't do the clicker points that is. Hit or miss on using books.
Amazing Professor and very easy class

GREAT professor. He's so nice and is pretty funny. Lectures are long and will take attendance points, but its an easy A class. Just do the homework and go to the labs. He also posts the pages of the textbook every week that correlates to the assignment, so technically you don't need to spend money on the textbook.

This guy is the best professor I ever had. Class content is easy for me since I already know most of it. Still having a good time in this class. Getting A from Com S 113 is easy, just keep turn in assignments on time. Adisak also making a solution on Facebook page for you to verify it.
He's a really nice guy. He has a strong accent but he's great. It seems like he really likes to teach.

One of the best professors that I have had. Teaches the materials, very helpful, and great guy all around. Tests aren't  too hard, just come prepared with everything that he puts in his slides. His lectures are often hilarious and he is very passionate about teaching.

COM S 113 you have 2 lectures with him and one lab with TAs.  He takes attendance by clicker/questions and gives points. You can not understand him no matter how close you sit. Nice guy and will try to help but you must reach for it. Recommend getting Access and Excel books. Homework every week - 1 Hw, 2 "Labs" BUT you can do them all in LAB.

This course is so easy. Three assignments per week: super easy hw, one in lab exercise and one capstone project. Just go to lecture for clicker points (10% of grade), I preferred to teach myself from the book. You get to have a front/back 8.5x11 sheet of paper with notes for the test: just put definitions/equation examples on it and you'll get an A
Great guy, good teaching

You can tell he's a nice guy but all the learning is done out of class because his accent is so strong.  I went into his office hours a few times and he is awkward and barely speaks English.  He deducts points for every minuscule mistake and you will never know why because his comments are written so poorly.

I took his course as a pre-business student.  He is extremely nice, will go over and above to help you and knows when the class struggles with topics.  He wants people to participate in class but the subject matter is tough to get enthusiastic about.  Got a 4 for clarity because he is soft spoken and can be difficult to understand on occasion.
He is very helpful, you can just go to see him even a small probelm
This look like an easy class but trust me it is not. Just go to class and listen to this professor will save you days reading books for exam.
this class is good and I learnd a lot of useful techneqe from this class. If you attend lecture section then it will save a lot of time on prepare for the exam.
This class start off very easy on few first week but turn to be quite hard. Content is useful anyway.

The class content look pretty easy at first but turn out to be not.  CS113X have a lots of assignment so you need to prepare and you will be fine. This professor give you something that useful beyond whats in book.
He is nice and helpful instructor.

He know about a computer problems and seem like he willing to help all student that have a questions even the class is huge (900 students). He got a bit of accents but his slow talk and extensive explanation make it understandable.

Honestly it's been a while. I don't know why he just popped in my head but I had to comment. Mr. Achter changed my life. He went from being my teacher at ISU to sitting in on my masters thesis at Bethel. He reminded me why my heart is in helping youth. I only have so many characters but he is the best.

Chuck is the best professor I have ever had. His way of teaching is unique and you can tell he really cares about each one of his students. His class helps future teachers so much and it was a privilege to have him as a teacher. Class is easy if you go every day. There are several paperspower point presentations, but they are not overly hard.

Chuck is probably the best instructor I have had so far at Iowa State. His enthusiasm and the knowledge on the topics helps tremendously. Attendance is required, and there are 3 unit exams, that are fairly easy if you study. A class I enjoyed going to!

BEST TEACHER EVER! For once I actually enjoy going to class. Everything that we learn is interesting. You really get to know the other students in your class. Chuck is VERY helpful and the best teacher I have had at ISU so far.
Most inspiring teacher ever!!!

Achter is a great guy. At first I had my reservations about his teaching style, which seems more appropriate to middle school. However, I warmed up to him quickly and he turned out to be one of the best teachers I've ever had. He really does care a lot about his students and wants you to become a successful teacher. The class isn't too hard either.

Class was very informational.  If you go to class, listen, and study for tests-you'll be fine. Fun, did a lot of presentations/projects.  He really does care about future teachers and wants to help his students. Great guy
Very sweet man. Will do anything for you if you need it! Tests weren't bad if you could study hard.

Great professor that truly cared about what he was teaching. Easy grader as long as you keep in touch with him and stay active in the classroom. One of my favorite teachers in 4 years of college. Just don't miss class our you will lose points.

One of my favorite teachers. Kept class interesting and liked to switch things up as opposed to listening to direct instruction all day. Loved how he integrated group work into his class. Allowed me to meet several new people. Is biased, but didn't bother me at all.
keeps lectures interesting with personal stories

Easy and helpful - yes. Good teacher - no. Picture an entire semester of being taught by a condescending Mr. Rogers. Do not correct him when he's wrong, it will affect how he grades your work. One unit was basically a lesson on how to stereotype groups of people. This class had a profound impact on my desire to teach - it took it away

Achter's a good teacher.  He knows the material & presents it in an organized manner.  Like almost all CI classes, attendance is mandatory. I agree that he can be biased, but it shouldn't affect your grade per se. He has favorites. I wasn't one but it wasn't a problem. Expectations are clearly defined and an "A" is definitely achievable.

Worst professor of my life, BIASED!!!! He shows so much favoritism it makes a dictator look nice. If you can take this class with a different prof please do, but if you are from Minnesota he will love you, because that is one of his positive biases.

Chuck Achter was my least favorite professor all semester. He couldn't stand being corrected, even if it was a simple mistake. He treated everyone as if they were in middle school and had no respect for his students. His beliefs on teaching are too old fashioned. To him unique is wrong. If possible get a different professor.

He is very experienced and tries very hard to connect with everyone. His enthusiasm and activities are good for awhile, but considering we are college students it got a little old. If you go every day and smile, you'll pry get an A.
One of the best teachers I have ever had. He really cares about his students. I loved this class.

Achter is a really good teacher. Sometimes it seems as if he's treating you like middle-schoolers, but he's just trying to show you how a good teacher teaches. Attendance is part of the grade, go EVERY day. Most assignments are pretty easy.
Achter is picky on presentations you give, and all the info you need is in his power points.

Amazing professor, he really does care so don't be afraid to ask questions during class or even get advice after. He has many years experience in being a principal and has seen a diverse range of teachers.. class can get hard but he's understanding if you need help.

GO TO CLASS and be on time! I missed out on getting an A in this class last semester just because I had 3 absences and the limit is 2 (he didn't make this clear in the beginning). We had several presentations, mid term and final exams, and a term paper. Not too bad.

This teacher is not good.  Make sure you go to class, his attendance policy is not clear in the syllabus, you will miss 10 for each absence after your second.  I lost my A this way.  He is a biased grader when it comes to presentations and papers.  I chose not to go into teaching because of this man and my other CI classes.
Seriously! Chuck is a great teacher for anyone thinking of entering the teaching profession. All class activities, and his teaching style are very relevant to your growth into the profession.
AMAZING PROFESSOR!! Shares his knowledge and many of his first hand experiences with teaching.

Chuck is a great guy and willing to help you out even after you leave his class. He can tell he cares about his students and bettering the program. You can learn a lot in the class if you put forth the effort and get an A without much trouble. Great class.
Chuck is a wonderful teacher! You can tell that he enjoys his job and his students.  He is there to help whenever it's needed and he reminds me of High School teachers.  GREAT TEACHER!
He made class fun! I did poorly in the class only because I didn't go; if you go ever day and participate then you will succeed in it!

Chuck brings back the memories of how teachers were in high school.  He is very helpful, doesn't single out anyone, and is open to any questions or comments.  His class is very hands on, so make sure you go.  His class was one of my most enjoyable classes I took this year.
Great prof.  I learned a lot from him and he knows his stuff.  Make sure you go to class though, missed 3 classes and lost me my A.
Will do whatever he can to help his students.  Great teacher!
One of the best in the CI department, and will do his best to help students.
While this class was better than taking 311 with Dr. Acevado, it still was a hard class. I felt that the material on exams were highly specific for the analyses learned.

I will have to say that Dr. Acevedo is the only Prof. I know that makes you work for your grade. I had to study hard to get a good grade but I learned a lot and I am happy for it. She respects the students and she really cares about our learning

If you want a demeaning prof who doesn't respect you, Dr. Acevedo is right for you. She has no understanding of student problems. Constantly told our class we were stupid. Blatantly ignores emails from students. Harsh grader and doesn't explain where the points were lost. Lecture slides are not enough but expects us to learn it all from there.

While I disliked the group work and how harshly the discussions were graded,I enjoyed the topics and I felt like I learned a lot.I felt like she disrespected the students a lot because she would call the entire class stupid/lazy because we did worse than the previous years and didn't go to office hours or she'd say students' questions were stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There are assignments in class every day which are worth a large portion of your grade but she grades very harshly. She can be very negative toward students when they ask questions. Told our class that we were dumb when an exam average was lower than a previous year. Doesn't post any answers to assignments, practice questions, or previous exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Acevedo is my favorite Prof. I had to study hard for this course but I learned so much! Everything I learned with her paid off in my senior courses
She is a very caring Prof. and seems very interested in our learning. The first few lectures were harder to follow but it gets better once you get into the rhythm  of the course
Great Teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: The lecture slides aren't enough, so you have to study from the textbook. Quizzes are on every chapter, but she doesn't post the answers of the quizzes on BB and the feedback given isn't enough to know the right answer !!! She posts sample exams but again doesn't post answers on BB!!! Hard to understand ... Take it with someone else if you can

Sometimes hard to understand but really helpful teacher.  Gives extra credit on exams.  Ask questions and follow powerpoints.  She basically tests from the powerpoints and in class discussions.  Tests are long and tough, but she gives a good review sheet.  Easy A if you study.

Dr. Acevedo is a great Prof!!  She really puts time into the material as it reflects in the detailed lectures.  The lectures can get boring but that is with almost every class at Iowa State.  She is very easy to talk to and is always willing to help if needed.  Go to office hours, ask questions and pay attention to the power points.  EXTRA CREDIT!

Ackerman may not be the most skilled at teaching, but he is an old pro with war stories to supplement learning. If you ask a question, Ackerman  makes you think and work to get to the answer by asking you more questions, which is a useful method in higher studies. Lectures are unorganized, but lab is fun, and exams are tough.  Ackerman is AWESOME.

As a senior in biology, Dr. Ackerman's lectures are bar none the most worthless I've ever attended, in any discipline. Mandatory attendance via clickers, otherwise nobody would show up! Rambling, generally incoherent lectures that make 50 minutes feel like 2 hours, useless powerpoints, and tests that don't cover the material from class. Avoid.

Terrible professor. Unorganized and not helpful. Won' respond to emails even when you remind him in class that you are going to. The only way he'd meet with me is if I did it right after lab. Avoid him and his class.

Avoid at all costs. He doesn't even understand what he's trying to teach, and he doesn't use the book that you're told to buy. Have to be in class for points (when he can figure out the clickers) but wastes most of the class talking about his sons bowel movements or his smelly infected tooth. NEVER RESPONDS TO EMAILS! Seriously AWFUL!

This class has participation points via Clicker. The PowerPoint notes are pointless and the readings don't help for exams. What he teaches in class isn't what he tests you on. He told the class if we didn't understand something to use wikipedia. Very generous curve at the end of the semester but the class isn't worth the stress.

Worst professor ever. Completely unorganized all the time and has never answered any of my 7 emails to him throughout the semester. He never knows what he's talking about and grades terribly on tests and won't listen to you (or email you back) if you prove him wrong. I would never recommend him or his classes to anyone who actually wants to learn.

Do not take this class. He talks too much about his personal life. He's rude to students and will not answer questions. He gives bad grades on tests and labs and will not explain why. He wont grade tests until a month after you take them. He also does not know what he's talking about and doesn't understand technology and you will learn nothing.

Dr. Ackerman is the worst professor that I have ever had. His lectures are random and do not help you for the exams. I was in his lab section and he refuses to help you in anyway. He asks you questions when you ask one and runs you in a circle avoiding an answer. Also, he smells like liquor most days. Exams online, easy A, useless professor.

Worst professor I have every had at ISU.  No reason to attend class, all tests are online.  If you can google well you will do fine, but you won't learn anything.  You don't have to actually try and learn anything in lab either, because none of it pertains to the lecture.  I feel sorry for the next bunch of students who have to sit in his lecture.
Best ever.

This is easily the worst class I have ever taken. All he does is go on and on about his military experiences. I learned nothing. He constantly questions students in lecture. Does not have a clue how to use technology. Does not give clear expectations to students in lab and then doesn't understand why we did not do what he wanted. Do not take it.

This class is terrible. The lecture notes do not make any sense, and he rambles on in class about pointless things. Never answers emails. Tests are manageable...I didn't get the book. Lab is also pretty terrible. Little help is provided by the professor or the TA.

Class attendance not required. Exams are all over the place (sometimes all lecture based, other times straight from book, "four square" almost useless). Poorly organized class, lab TA awful and often blatantly states he will not help you. Exams you take online, which helps.

Overall, this class was not hard. HOWEVER, he is the most boring lecturer I have ever had at ISU. Pretty much every class was a fight to stay awake, and most of the time I lost. He does provide all his in class lectures online via Canvas, and the midterms/final were all very easy. Do be aware that he has an accent that is hard to understand.
He's a funny dude and likes to make jokes and is nice

All tests and quizzes were on canvas which made this class extremely easy. All slides are posted from the lectures, but attendance is taken on Tophat for points. He is super nice and I recommend taking this class from him!

I would say that the in person top hat was pretty tough, but you only had to get like half right for full credit. Talked about dissecting rats and experimenting on them a lot. Was a very nice professor and cared about the students. I would recommend this professor

One of the best lecturers I have had over my past four years at ISU. If you don't care about more technical psych topics/ neuroscience, this might not be the best class for you... But if you enjoy this kind of stuff, you should definitely take it! 

Martin is incredibly knowledgeable and has some really interesting stories about his past research.

Dr. Acerbo is a funny, caring professor. His classes consist of weekly Packback discussion posts, weekly online quizzes, and then 6ish online exams which are all in a lockdown browser. In class, his lectures can get slightly boring, but the class is very easy overall!

Dr. Acerbo was very entertaining in class and made the material easy to learn. However, he can get stuck on tangents that drag on and delay lectures. There were weekly quizzes and exams every other week but they weren't very difficult. Attendance was mandatory because of Tophat. Overall, I would recommend any of his classes!

Has a thick accent making it hard to understand, cannot stay on track with lecture going off on side stories that don't relate causing us to go over and miss information. Grading on assignments is not clear, he does not remember own syllabus or assignments. Will blame students for not being prepared when he was the one neglecting to read emails.
Martin made every lecture interesting and he's really good at explaining the content.
Dr. Acerbo is a pretty nice guy that made lectures pretty funny, but also interesting. The pack back was easy to do and the exams were online.
Very boring class. He does not stay on track with lectures, so it is hard to pay attention. He is very funny. Every assignment is online and there are lots of quizlets.
SO difficult to understand and never answers email. Very easy class! The exams are online and all google-able. The lectures are SO boring.

Dr. Acerbo is great! He knows what he is talking about and he actually teaches well so he doesn't just read off slides. I really enjoyed taking this class even though it was pretty difficult. Make sure you read your book! Also, most of the test questions are on the quizzes ;) It is a lot of material at a really fast pace but it is taught well!

Dr. Acerbo is an excellent professor who brings a lot of experience from his research background to the teaching environment. I have taken multiple classes with him. Expect larger classes to include online discussion boards (Packback), long lectures, and daily quizzes (TopHat). Smaller classes are much more interactive and less formal.

I thought his lectures were hard to understand because of his accent. He is super nice and will answer any questions that you have. Toward the end of the semester, attendance was extra credit because attendance wasn't mandatory.
He is a very funny professor and is very lecture heavy. All tests and quizzes are online which is nice. He is very kind and has good grading criteria.
MY FAVORITE PERSON EVER!!!! i love this man with my whole heart, i would do anything and everything for him, amazing prof too
One of my favorite professors. He always will answer questions and explains well when confused.

Dr. Acerbo is very funny and is a very good teacher. He was always fair with grading. However, you must be prepared to be memorizing and understanding ALOT of material. Personally, I filled two and a half notebooks with material. I read the book some, but you could certainly make it without the book.

Dr. Acerbo has done some really interesting work! (He'll talk about rats a lot). I thoroughly enjoyed his PSYCH 315 course. The material is difficult if you are not well-versed in anatomy and physiology. Dr. Acerbo explains concepts thoroughly, especially if you ask questions. The textbook isn't a necessity, but it is helpful.

Dr. Acerbo wants everyone to succeed. He is always open to questions and is really helpful for a class that is hard to teach online. Some of my friends were in other sections online and said their professors were awful.

PSYCH 315 with Acerbo was a walk in the park, and that's coming from a biology major. If you're a psych major, this class might be very challenging but having a solid background in bio is super helpful for this class as there is a lot of basic biology involved. Teacher is goofy and very helpful. Tests were just straight from slides as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: pretty good teacher, good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Acerbo is a decent Professor but he flies through the slides. There was extra credit which helped bring my grade up. Exams are medium difficulty but there are lots of quizlets and study blues that are helpful when studying.

Psych315 w/ Acerbo was significantly harder than his 310 course. The drugs are hard to keep straight, and his powerpoints are more confusing in this class. Knowing the quiz questions helped in 310, but not in 315, so you really have to study and can't cram. He does his best to water it down though since he knows it's a psych course & he tells jokes

Dr. Acerbo has a lot of experience&is very funny. He expects you to work at learning the material. Uses Tophat to get points in class, &gives online quizzes. Test are multiple choice w/ some short answer, but you truly have to understand the material, or you won't pass. Can get by without the book, but it definitely helps. Keep up with the material

If you want to do well in this class, make sure you have a good amount of biology-knowledge because this class if FULL of bio stuff. I have very little experience with bio, but I still got an acceptable grade. Content is SUPER interesting. First part of class is meh, but gets better. He is super funny. 4 exams, 13 quizzes, 1 extra credit option..

Acerbo is an awesome instructor. The class is difficult at times especially if you don't have any biology background. He is a funny instructor and makes class enjoyable to go to. His exams require some studying, but he mainly pulls questions from his old quizzes. Definitely a course I would reccommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I thought this was going to be a psych class, lol NO. This is intro. to psychopharmacology, aka it's EXTREMELY biology/neurology heavy. That being said, the book is extremely helpful and the lectures are interesting. He uses top hat and weekly blackboard quizzes. I'm retaking it now that I know how hard I have to study, but I'm actually excited
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a great prof, really passionate about the subject and throws in lots of funny jokes.  All you do in class is lectures and clicker questions, I recommend going and other than that the book is not that necessary. One of the only psych classes I have ever really had to study for. It seems like he is always doing really interesting research.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Acerbo is very funny and able to keep class interesting. At times he does get off topic. It is sometimes hard to decide what information is important and what is not. All in all he is a pretty good professor and I would recommend him to others.

Dr. Acerbo was dificult to understand at times. His lectures were very long and didn't give me much direction as far as what was important and what wasn't. There were also many instances where he would give announcements as people had already started leaving, which made life hard as he never posted announcements on blackboard.

Dr. Acerbo is one of the funniest teachers I've had so far. I don't know why everyone complains about the accent, it isn't bad at all. He helps you a lot if you to him in his office hours, and if you ask questions about the test right before he usually answers them. His tests are mainly the old quizzes and he makes good study guides.
Nice guy who liked to keep class informal. He only graded the final paper and presentation but was a pretty nice grader.

Pretty interesting class. He teaches a lot on the biological level though, but that's is understandable. Not many tests but they can be difficult if you don't review the quizzes. He asks the same exact questions from the quizzes on his tests. Attendance isn't needed but you need to go on some days for a few in class quizzes.

Acerbo himself is pretty unclear in what he want's out of an assignment, has a thick accent and a monotone voice, but his TA Anna is the hardest grader I have ever encountered. Beware these two, especially if she is the one grading the assignments.

His accent can definitely be hard to get past, but he will clarify anything you don't understand. It is a psychology class, but he teaches it like a biology class. Pay attention to quizzes, most of his exams are based on the quizzes.

Acerbo is one of my favorite professors. He does have an accent but he also realizes this and lets you know that if you need anything repeated or reworded he will do so. Read the mini readings he assigns and pay attention to quizzes & class notes. Most exams are from them. VERY interesting class!!
Hard to understand sometimes and pronounces some words incorrectly.  Very knowledgeable about the materials though and is more than willing to explain additional information during office hours.

He is rated much lower than he should be. Strong accent, but if you read the book and notes you will be okay. Use the quizzes to study exams and you will be golden. I am a bio major so I had a little more background. He is funny and a nice guy-underrated on here.

This course was oversimplified and the professor did not string anything together. As a result, you end up with a poor understanding. If you are interested in neuroscience, take this with someone else. If you are taking it because you have to, you will have to memorize a lot of "pointless" information. Very boring, strong accent, and cannot teach.
Hard to understand, he has an accent. Class is boring and he doesn't follow the syllabus. Pointless to go to class, didn't have class quizzes until last few weeks of class.

Has an accent, very hard to understand. Study guides are useless. Tests are very hard, cover every little detail. Quizzes are easy, online, open-book. Class is worthless to go to unless there's a quiz (only 4 in the semester)

I think this was Dr. Acerbo's first year. He was very nice and taught well. The tests questions were mainly taken from the quizzes questions we had previously, making the tests fairly simple. He is helpful and overall did a decent job teaching. Although, I feel like we just skimmed the topic of drugs and behavior so that was kind of a bummer.
Brenda is amazing! She listens to her students and helps whenever there is even slight confusion.  Makes sure you do the best you can. Awesome!

Brenda is great at what she does. She doesn't just read off the slides because she really does know what she is talking about. The class is very difficult, but Brenda is very helpful. Going to class is vital so you can learn the materials and participate in the in class activities.

Brenda is an AMAZING professor. She is the best professor in the whole apparel program. She is so willing to help and while she expects a lot out of her students she doesnt expect anymore than what her students are capable of.
Brenda is a great instructor! She is so understanding and she really encourages you to do your best!
great

I had the night class, it was my first one but wasn't that bad at all. class is pretty much all participation based so just show up and say a little something as long as you kinda know what you are talking about. He will kinda make fun of you if you dont or repeat what was said
Rajshri is one of the most intelligent and interesting profesor that I have ever had. She challenges the student into thinking independently. She really knows her subject matter.
Ask questions during the tests, she pretty much tells you the answers. The tests are kind of confusing, but the class is interesting and easy.
I felt this course didn't have anything to do with Marketing til just about the end. I don't think she does a great job at teaching, but does tell examples.
The first two tests are somewhat easy and it progresses into something harder. The class projects at the end of the semester can be time consuming. Just stay on top of the material and you'll do fine
she does a great job! She is a wonderful prof, one of the best I have had hear at ISU

She is very knowledgeable in the subject of Internaional Marketing, having traveled the world extensively and having been involved (and still is) in an international business.  She is also the sweetest, most understanding professor I've had.  It's impossible not to like her!  Just read the book and study the notes for the test.
Her tests are challening, but she is the sweetest lady ever and would do anything to help her students out! AND she understands if you fall asleep in her class!
No Comments
No Comments

Notes:  You better memorize everything.  Book:  Read every sentence.  However, the book is tough to read due to lack of clairty.  Always, always, always attend class.  The report is a cake walk if you follow the checklist to the 'T.'
Nothing was explained to the degree she expected us to know it.  The book sucked.  She's not up to date on foreign policies: not good for teaching an international class.
The paper and presentation were not explained well.  She expected a lot of things that aren't standard and didn't let us know.
Cares about students' opinions and wants you to succeed
Really nice grader. You have 2 open note exams, 2 group research projects, and 5 case studies. Lot of guest speakers that are interesting where he takes attendance.
One of the best professors I have had. Truly cares about his students and doesn't try to trick you.

Dr. Grover was a great professor for SCM 461. He made the learning interactive and engaging for everyone. Attendance was only mandatory for guest speaker days. Dr. Grover, really cares about you doing well and will help if you reach out. Overall great guy and professor. I would recommend.

Rambles, hard to understand, and has mistakes in content and slides. Most slides are read straight from the textbook. Mainly equations with no explanation. Shows no work in examples. Acts like he is available outside of class but really was not.

While his lectures weren't necessarily the best, since at times they often felt monotone and were very boring, when it comes to accessibility and caring about students he's one of the rare professors who actually cares, that is, if you talk to him outside of class.
Very good at articulating new information and gives plenty of time for group projects and is very understanding when it comes to late work or technical issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall pretty good, for 324, you can tell he really cares and has the class structured in a way that makes it very easy to get a good grade.  For projects, he is more than willing to lend a helping hand.  Can make material that would be more boring somewhat entertaining.
Lecutures can be mundane and monotone but he loves what he does and that's a good thing. Projects can be a bit difficult but everything else is pretty smooth.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice person, not a great teacher. Attendance mandatory. Accent might make it difficult to understand and lectures are very boring. Quizzes/Projects are not made well, no partial credit because it's nearly all multiple choice, but you can make up points by going to the TA. Class isn't difficult though, exams are online, and ask for help on projects.

Please for your sake do not take this class with Agba. He literally just makes his slides straight from the textbook and reads right off them with no deeper understanding. The projects are awfully made with no partial credit at all if you get something wrong.

I would have never attended the worthless lectures however attendance is required. He seems like a nice guy but is one of the worst teachers I have had at Iowa State. Lecture rarely correlates with the given projects. This may just be a bad course to be fair.

He is a very nice man, but awful at teaching. He blows through the material (for the first half of the semester we ended early almost every day) and he doesn't really teach. He doesn't elaborate on any equations and some of them are so long that only two can fit on a slide and those slides he spends no more than 30 seconds on.

Dr. Agba seems like a nice guy, but he's not the best teacher. He sped through lecture material and didn't give you time to write stuff down. He would also waste a lot of time talking about MathCad, which is something we never used for the class. Attendance was graded and there were also in class activities, but he gave the answers to them in class

He does not care. His homework is due the day of the lecture. You have less than a day to do the homework, because the lecture covers the homework that is due that same day. He is a bad teacher, but a nice man. It is like this is his first time teaching. He does not give points back that you deserve. And sometimes he is rude.

He does not teach. He talks about the materials. No help and he does not care. You have to be at every lecture, mandatory. He does not should how to do any calculations. Does not care and has a think accent. Very hard to understand. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!!!!!!!!

Nice man, not great Teacher. It is just sad. Just do not take him. He made me feel bad about myself. Homework on MathCad is just too much un needed work. Homework is good homework. You could learn something if you can learn by yourself. Do not take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a bad teacher... He does not care... Gives you no time to do homework. Don't take this professor. If you can teach yourself then you will be fine. He does not teach and can be very rude. I regret taking him for this class. Such a mistake. Also MathCad is terrible to use for homework

He is very hard to understand him because of his accent. The class is formatted in a good way, and he is kind of helpful. He says he cares about his students, but honestly, he rather have you fail than drop the class. He makes you use MathCad to do all you homework. MathCad is not great, and makes homework take longer than it should. Lecture is bad
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His ME170 class can be challenging if you don't have prior experience using CAD software. When there is homework it can be long and challenging and usually involves creating complex solid works parts and assemblies, which are graded intensely. However, Agba is very understanding and a really smart professor and you will learn a lot in this class.

While the content of this course wasnt particularly absurd he is unable to help students who have no or little experience with Solidworks. He is very hard to understand and when asking for help you hardly ever get a solution. Since I struggled at the beginning of the course and most of the assignments were at the beginning my grade suffered.

Agba is a good choice for any class, but this is pertaining to ME270 only. The class is group based. Assignments are straight forward and the grading is fairly lax (but that kinda depends on your TA too). Show him respect and he will return the favor ten fold. Awesome professor who is really passionate and will push you to succeed.

His project descriptions and drawings are often wrong, but if you get it wrong be ready to fight for your grade. Walks through the projects in class but often does them incorrectly. Do not forget to do an online quiz, he will not have any sympathy for you. Overall a cool class that sucks because of the professor and his skewed expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hard to understand and doesn't explain much, if he does explain, he jokes so much that you don't know what was and wasn't a joke. Inconsistent Due dates and workload, takes forever to grade assignments and takes off as much as 50% credit for minor mistakes. If you don't have someone in your group who knows how to use SolidWorks then good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Can't teach

Advanced CAD and Simulation with Dr. Agba goes over lots of features in Solidworks, and touches on ANSYS, MATLAB, and MasterCAM. Over 80% of the projects are Solidworks based. You MUST know how to use SW when you come in to the class. He doesn't go over basic functions. Class is weekly project based and you work with a partner on all projects

Had some difficulty understanding Agba. All class projects are done in pairs and it's not all just run of the mill SolidWorks. Expect some MATLAB. Attendance is mandatory and he sends a sign-in sheet around every class period. Not a bad instructor but also not the best I've had in the department.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: ME325 with Agba is one of the easier A's you can get in the program. As long as you show up to the lectures (attendance taken) and do the once or twice weekly homework, you'll be fine. Exams were open book/note. Lectures were incredibly boring though, and I felt he went off on tangents a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you have any experience with CAD programs it will be the easiest class you take all year, if not, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class was almost all group work, so try to sit near people you could work well with. The work was easy, just frustrating getting everything in the correct format and to his standards.

Dr. Emmanuel Agba's class is one of the easiest you can get for ME 325. Gloria Sterns has group projects so if your group doesn't do well then you will get a poor grade. ME 325 class with Agba is fairly easy, you only have homework, quizzes, and a final project. The class average was super high when I took it, I would highly recommend him.
Homework is alright. You will have 2 group projects to work on and a final presentation. Attendance is part of the grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super great guy and not a hard class at all. Definitely take advantage of the Solidworks help provided.

Good teacher.  He is helpful and is available during office hours.  Has practical, real life examples for problems.  Used what i learned in this class directly in my internships.  Nice guy in office hours.

Agba is a great guy. But he is sometimes hard to understand because he likes to mumble and doesn't take time in class to explain the assignments / projects. He also likes to have multiple assignments going on at the same time in addition to the big projects. And he and his TA are never on the same page so be prepared to be confused.

Agba is a great person and that's pretty much it. He has multiple assignments going on at once and he doesn't take class time to help you. Was never on the same page as the TA for grading and projects. Overall not that great of a teacher.

Agba is just as clueless as the students forced to sit through his hellish class. He feels the need to require students to use MathCAD software for homework assignments - which is an absolute waste of effort. Extra hours spent formatting homework to make him happy rather than learning the material and preparing for the exams - which are handwritten

DO NOT TAKE MACHINE DESIGN WITH AGBA. He requires you to use MathCAD for homework assignments which causes atleast 1-3 extra hours (per assignment) trying to get MathCAD to perform the action you want it to. Don't bother taking notes in class as he speeds through the slides. Only thing you can do is make a killer cheat sheet. Rough grader too...

Very friendly and caring guy. Sadly, his insistence on using MathCAD (which no one had used before) for homework assignments added unnecessary time spent on homework. He gave four tests. Two were extremely easy and the other two were really tough. Expect the syllabus to change several times throughout the semester in terms of due dates.
Helpful in Solidworks and group projects. Make sure to do keep your homework neat and organized, he will take points away. Directions aren't always straight forward. Office hours helpful.

Dr. Agba has troubles clearly stating his expectations for assignments... his syllabus due dates do not necessarily line up with when he expects projects to be completed.  Overall his class is easy but his communication skills make it seem more difficult.
Dr. Agba is an awesome teacher! He is always willing to help and really wants his students to understand the class!
His schedule was WONKY and he even answered his phone before class finish.
First semester teaching the class.  The schedule was a bit wonky, but at least he was pretty understanding.

After dreading the thought of taking fluids, I can say this dude made the experience great. His lectures are engaging, and he's very accommodating with questions and exam layouts. The class is inherently difficult, but with this professor and a lot of time studying, it becomes manageable. This guy is the golden ticket to fluids success.

I really liked him for fluids. Lectures were mostly derivations of the equations you need. He's also a very funny guy and his accent is not a problem. Exams are very fair, just make sure to go through the homeworks and the recitation problems. He gives you everything you need to do well as long as you show up and take notes on everything he writes.

I loved Abhay for fluids. Very knowledgeable (he is a fluids researcher) and he is very funny at times. Cares about his students and wants to answer your questions. He also made the homework/quizzes/exams a reasonable difficulty.

-over 50 assignments (incl. smartbook)
-regularly made mistakes in examples when teaching concepts
-exams made up 80% of grade
-pop(ish) quizzes, announced lecture before
-very unforgiving grading on exams (class avg on exam 4 was 59.8%)
-not great at teaching: reads from the lecture slides and then fumbles examples on the board
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely a time-consuming class. There are readings that go with every lecture with examples similar to the homework. Homework every week 8 to 20 problems and takes a long time, but understanding them is the best form of studying. On tests, there was at least 1 problem very similar to a homework problem. there were 'pop' and some regular quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ossama is a great man who clearly has love for his work. However, the way he sets up his class is less than optimal. Homeworks are worth nothing, so your grade is made up mostly by 2 exams and a project, and the exams were both very difficult. He is really great if you have a strong interest in astro, but for me that was not the case.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Abdelkhalik was excellent at teaching the material, but his grading criteria could be clearer and some of the assignments were graded very harshly.

Professor Abdelkhalik is easily the best professor I have had in college. He sparked my interest into astrodynamics and allows you to understand it in a simple but very intuitive and effective manner. He has also inspired me to take one of his Graduate level courses after taking his undergrad course. Overall amazing professor.

Still taking the class but Ossama is an absolutely wonderful professor and explains Astrodynamics very well. His lectures are clear and concise and he explains the concepts in an easily understandable manner.

She is very interested in everyone's perspectives, has an unforgettable laugh, and allows for creativity in essays and projects. Heavy reading material for the first half of the semester. Be prepared to discuss readings each class, and remember key terms and discussions for exams (10 short-answer). Be on top of your game and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Intersting course and Dr. Dubisar is very caring for her students and wants everyone to succeed! Be prepared to write, exams are in person and she requires you to be very specific and connect multiple parts of the course. Heavy on reading material, but if you take decent notes and attend class the exams and papers are fairly easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Dubisar is one of my current favorite professors. I'm an animal ecology major so taking an English course was new to me. She was very encouraging, responds quickly to emails, and provides a safe space for answering questions in class. There are readings and a quiz for the first 10 weeks. 2 papers, 1 final video project, and 2 exams total.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The tests were really the only part of this class I didnt like. They were 10 short answer questions that I had to reference the textbook multiple times to answer. It took me hours to do them, however there are only two. The grading criteria was somewhat unclear, but the professor seemed very caring. The textbook was interesting and the papers fun.

I took this class Fall 2015. Dr. Dubisar is a very fun, positive person. She loves to hear everyone's ideas and encourages students to share their perspectives. It is evident that she loves what she does, as she gets excited about new ideas and themes. This was a fun class that got us thinking in new ways.
The subject matter was interesting, but she assigns way too many readings. Long readings. Honestly I wouldn't recommend this class.

I don't believe the other raters took Abby's classes. She made lots of time in & out of class to offer help, was humorous and courteous of even the most asinine opinions in class, and let me make up a test with almost no warning that I would miss it. There was a fair amount of reading, but the material & tests were pretty easy with the study guide.

This professor definitely has a superiority complex that she makes evident when she speaks to you. As another rater said, she is closed off to others' opinions and often makes students feel uncomfortable when they exemplify incorrect understanding, rather than working to guide that student's understanding in a positive way. Not the best instructor

The reading is often excessive, the tests are confusing with no guidelines given as to what to study. She is not helpful at all or reasonable about deadlines. She is VERY closed to others' opinions and has outright told the class that our opinions are wrong.

She is a bad teacher. When asked to clarify or specify on something, she looks at you like you're dumb and repeats herself. She doesn't put grades up so you have no idea how you are doing. Not helpful at all.

Very unhelpful. When you ask her a question, she'll respond by sending you somewhere else, like the library, to answer your question. Gives no direction. Read the book b/c she gives reading quizzes all the time.

This class was discussion based and took a lot of time when it came to discussions. Had to reply to 5 different people on 5 different days and if you didn't he would dock you points. He also made you purchase the book that he wrote, which was kind of odd. The book had a paper that you had to write about during the end of the semester.

This teacher is amazing. We had conversations as a class that stimulated deeper thoughts. He grades pretty easy, as long as you put effort. He's understanding so if you miss class or an assignment, he will give you an opportunity to do a make-up assignment. I will say I don't recall us actually using the books that were assigned to this course.

Pretty straight forward and easy 3000 level class. A typical week involves either a 300 word reflection paper or a discussion board that requires you to post six days a week, which is a little annoying and makes the discussions more dry than they already are. There are three exams in this class but they are graded at 50% of your grade.

Terrible online professor. Had a technology issue and he was unable to work with me to figure it out. Dropped my grade from a 86 to a 53 and is going to make it impossible to get above a -B. Terrible communication skills and extremely rude. Unhelpful. Loved the class, strongly disliked this professor.

Kusow didn't actually teach much. His TA did most of the communication and grading. They expect you read and basically teach yourself. Lots of tedious discussion posts and film reveiws (he uses the same films from af fam 201). Overall seems like a lazy professor. Not the best at communicating especially in person. Easy class though
Thanks kusow

SOC330 online is okay. As long as you do the readings, assignments, and discussions on time, you'll be fine. He occasionally makes mistakes on exams, which is good because he gives you points back if he finds one. If you don't do the readings, you won't do well on the exams. Overall, interesting lectures and solid gen ed choice.

Kusow is a very knowledgeable professor. He is from Somalia but his accent is not hard to understand like other reviews have said. He wants you to learn and very much appreciates participation. Assignments are worth it and not too difficult (article reflections etc). He is very nice and very understanding!! Many assignments in class, don't skip!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Where to begin... This class is a complete joke. Should be considered a 100 level class. Lots of easy quizzes, one paper, 3 exams. If you have the textbook, it will help clarify things for the quizzes and exams, but definitely do not do all the assigned readings. His exam questions can be very misguiding. Very easy A.
Abdi Kusow may be a genius, he is very intelligent and really knows what he is talking about. The class is kinda unorganized but the assignments are very easy.

Extremely unorganized throughout the entire semester. Was unclear with instructions for projects and assignments. Lectures were close to pointless as he did not necessarily follow the text. Discussions and lectures had nothing to do with the tests. He also has a thick accent which makes the lectures almost impossible to understand. Would avoid.

He failed in trying to transition this to a web-blended class at the beginning of my semester so there was a lot of confusion. Show up to class for easy film review points. Lectures and discussions are pretty hit and miss. The class is an easy US diversity and and easy A

He was a very fascinating professor and understood the topic in depth. His lectures were interesting and I enjoyed his class. He is not very quick when it comes to grading, but if you are attending class you should do just fine.

He is probably one of the most illiterate professors I've ever had. He fails to put when exams and quizzes are due on the syllabus calendar, and when confronted he will not let you retake them (fine by me). If I 500$ I'd drop his class now. HORRIBLE!

Very nice guy. Pretty thick accent. He was unorganized though when it came to uploading lecture slides & grading our papers. Went off on tangents, didn't stick to textbook materials. Use his lectures highlighted points & "Quick Quiz" to study, and CengageBrain.com's quizzes for exams. Extra credit. Easy attendance points. Got an A.
Good instructor. He gives plenty of opportunities to earn a good grade ie extra credit

He took the time to learn everyone's names, and would call on people for answers in class. He's very knowledgeable about AI, and took frequent trips during the year to promote AI capabilities overseas. The TA usually taught in his absence. A very project heavy class, but it's pretty easy. He gives good feedback on your work and the class is smooth.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: ISU is lucky to have Abram. He's so smart about AI & always goes to do keynote speeches in cool places (Hong Kong & England this semester) & then tells us about it. He is one of the nicest most helpful professors I have ever had & gives you 100% as long as he can see you're trying. 10000% recommend. super interesting class to anyone not just AI ppl

ENGL 222x. New AI course that's very engaging. Abram puts in significant effort into the lectures, and listens to his students. Very unique class, but don't skip. Most points come from in class activities. You won't be bored, I promise. Homework was minimal to none, and grading policy was super light. Easy A, would absolutely take again.

Abhay has easily been the most impactful professor I've had in the info systems field. His ability to be engaging even through the dull areas of the curriculum was very much appreciated. He's got a sense of humor, makes himself available & truly cares (if you show you do as well). My grip would be the delays in grading updates.

He starts off the semester by talking about how boring the course material is going to be (which it is), but he works really hard to make the content engaging and interesting. He really cares about the success of his students and doesn't put up with those who don't care about the class and aren't willing to put in the effort.

Prof Mishra is a fun instructor, helped make some bland material somewhat interesting. Exams are challenging but he allows a note sheet which makes them pretty easy. Group projects/assignments were pretty easy and the final presentation is fun if you choose a topic you care about. Show up to class and joke around with him and it will be a good time

Prof. Mishra's class is super easy if you show up and pay attention. The material is taught very well and he is always willing to listen and help with whatever you need. He many times stayed after class to talk about material and life. Genuinely an amazing guy that could not have been a better prof to have at Iowa State.

Excellent professor, the best I've had in the MIS department so far. Very clear on expectations, really knows his stuff, and wants to help you if he can. Material is heavy on technicalities by its nature but he makes it easy to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very good professor but the material is very boring and stale. If you don't go to class then more than likely you will fail. He cares a lot about your success and is disappointed when you don't meet expectations. However, he does not do a very good outlining what his expectation are. If you go to class, pay attention, and do your work you'll pass.

Mishra is very knowledgeable and genuinely cares about your success. He wants to see your growth. He gets disappointed when you don't meet expectations, but that's because he cares about you. This isn't an easy A, but out of all the courses I've taken at ISU, MIS 320 with Mishra has been one of the most useful classes I've taken.

We had a group presentation at the end of the semester. This professor stopped many groups and berated them DURING the presentation. At one point stopped a group and accused them of cheating on the presentation work, asked the class if these students cheated. Was very unprofessional and awkward. Avoid prof at all costs. The class was easy tho.
Abhay is a cool, nice guy. His slides are dense and sometimes stale but he cares about your learning and well-being. He also gives out snacks and cash rewards!

He's not bad! Very willing to improve/change things up when he's given feedback. His class is test heavy (you'll be fine if you prepare a little/have a good cheat sheet), most assignments are group assignments (find a good group to work with), and you do need to participate and pay attention in class (he really appreciates people who speak up).

By far the worst professor I've ever had at Iowa State University. He is a very tough grader and does not give good feedback on assignments only check marks. For the group projects he did not have any grading criteria and expected you to know what to do with no information on the syllabus or on his slides... Will not take again.

I had Aldaco for 309 and 319. He cares more about his students than just about any professor. He will spend a lot of time helping students. He really likes it if you can speak any Spanish. Getting a good grade from him is easy as long as you put in the required effort.

I've had him before, but unfortunately, this class was just a mess. It's impossible to get 100% on anything because "no code is perfect" and there aren't many assignments they grade on. Nothing was clear, and things were often changed last minute. Hopefully, they'll prepare the course better for the future. (don't do a game as your project)

I like Aldaco, he has a genuine care for his students. He put up cardinal and gold balloons in the classroom to make it a more inviting environment before the first day of class :) which was a nice gesture. 319 is generally very easy, you get out of it what you put in. Lectures sometimes felt pointless because it was a lot of copy and pasting code

This was hist first year for CS309 and it was an utter and complete disaster. I really hope that he gets better after adjusting to the curriculum, as I have had him past years for other classes and he has been great. But man, he is really not good for CS309. His lectures are more so rants that repeatedly tell you to work on your project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is probably the best, most likeable professor in the department. He gave great advice on my carreer, helped me with my classes (his class or other classes too), and is very friendly and enuinely cares about his students.

Given his high rating on this website, I was extremely excited to take Aldaco's class this semester. Unfortunately, I do not understand why he was given this rating. Taking COMS 3090 this semester, all I've been greeted with are boring, insignificant lectures that do not cover the proper material you need to complete demos and assignments.
One of my favorite professors I've had. He genuinely seems to care about helping students succeed. He is very helpful, and I found his lectures on the better end of other professors here.

Second time having Aldaco, and I still hold the belief that he is one of the best COM S professors Iowa State has. Such a caring guy who looks out for each of his students and makes every effort to equip us to succeed in the real world. Each lecture is well made, easy to follow, and entertaining.

Professor Aldaco genuinely hopes to see his students succeed and although English may not be his first language he puts in the effort every lecture. He prints out optional worksheets some lectures that make the class far more engaging. Attendance can make or break your grade, overall a very accommodating professor. 8.1/10.

This class is extremely easy and only gets hard in the end. I passed it all easily only because I had prior experience. Other classmates say he is not a good teacher which I believe so too but he is a very nice person and really cares about his students. He will do everything to personally help each student. Very great guy

COM S 319 with him was great! I also took COM S 228 with him as well. I would take every Computer Science class with him if I could. He is easily the best professor in the Computer Science department and the nicest and most caring professor as well.

I did not like Aldaco at first, but he really grew on me. He genuinely cares about his students and gives a lot of advice towards the end of the semester.  228 is generally a slog, with a ton of information and tests that are seldom easy. But I felt more prepared than my friends who had Georgi.  I would take him over Georgi 9 times out of 9.

Super nice professor who cares more about the students rather than research. Lectures were good but there was just so much material to learn, I ended up doing lots outside of class. Worst part was information on the exams was limited and all the practice exams didn't align with the actual exam, except Aldaco wasn't the prof who wrote the tests.

Great guy and great professor. 319 is pretty easy, the homework assignments leading up to projects give you most of what you need in order to complete the assignment, which I really like. Attendance isn't mandatory but he certainly notices who shows up to class. If you show up to class he'll be super friendly at office hours.
He is a great and understanding professor that pushes students to try out new things in their final project.
Professor Aldaco is a really good professor that goes out of his way to make sure you are succeeding in the course. I could not tell you how many times he has helped me out.

Watch canvas, assignments are posted before discussed in class. Easy class. "Class assignments" were copy paste from the slides, given 2 days to turnin. A lot of zybooks, normally given a week to turnin. Had about 5 "team homeworks" that were very similar to the class assignments, given 2 weeks to turnin. Midterm and Final projects were simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aldaco is an outstanding professor. Makes 319 very easy, you can choose not to show up to class and do your projects last minute and still get an A due to the grading criteria. He is very lenient on extensions. He will individually grant extensions and also give to the whole class if requested. He also responds to EVERY post on piazza. Outstanding

One of the best CS professors I've ever had at Iowa State. Genuinely cares about the student and is extremely passionate, wholesome, and genuinely nice. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, going to class helps a ton. It's a fair amount of work, but doing ZyBooks, attending lectures, and asking questions in Piazza makes it easy!

Aldaco is an excellent professor. He puts a lot of work into creating his lectures and provides lots of extra material for studying outside of class. He's very understanding and accommodating in extenuating circumstances and did everything he could to make sure everyone succeeded.

Nothing against him, but I'm not too fond of his teaching style. He copies and pastes code and expects us to understand what is happening. He goes way too fast in lectures and is sometimes hard to keep up. He gives out extensions like crazy and is willing to work with you to make sure you are successful, which is rare in the CS department.

I loved taking this course. The professor is very engaging and is open to feedback about the course. Hes very undersanding and is willing to work around any issue you bring uo to him. Hes the first professor I've met at ISU that actually cares about students success. Would highly recommend him for any class

Full disclosure I did not take this class with him, but I have heard so many great things about him that I thought I should leave a review.  I wish I would've taken this class with him as the professor.
This professor is extremely accommodating and kind. He truly wants each and every one of his students to succeed. By far my favorite SE/COMS professor.
This professor was very accommodating and kind. He truly cares about his students and wants each and every one to succeed. My favorite SE/COMS professor by far.
Good professor actually teaches material based on where the class is. Frequently pushes due dates if class is behind.

Abi is very knowledgeable and the class was interesting. This was a 4-week class, so A LOT of material was covered in a short period of time - with a lot of time-consuming assignments/projects. Make sure to watch the movies and lectures because quizzes cover questions from them. She is slow to grade, but very fair. I would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Abi was really nice. You can tell she cares about her students. I had a rough semester and she was always willing to work with me. This class was heavy on group discussion but it made class fun. It felt as if we kinda controlled the class and what we learned.

Abi is a very kind person and passing her class was really easy but the way she teaches is unenjoyable. Lectures consist of her reading at you from an ipad making it hard to actually absorb anything, but there are no exams so passing is still super easy. Most points come from reflection papers so if you don't like papers don't take this class.

I really loved this class, I thought it was interesting and I learned a lot. Although Abi does lecture she gives opportunities for you to speak to your groups or create a conversation which is nice and keeps the class interesting. Homework is scheduled so you know when to expect it which is really nice. Overall she is caring and is really nice

I took this class in 2007 and it doesn't seem that anything has changed based on the reviews! He stood at the podium and talked the entire time, basically reading his slides word for word. It was extremely hard to keep my eyes open and mind-numbingly boring.

Boring class. As long as you go to class and take the notes and study them you'll get an A on all the exams, I did :). Also, he gives pop quizzes, another reason to go to class. I wasted money buying the textbook, it has dust on it.
He means well, but it was not a fun class...very boring.
I <3 him.

Horrible.He has no idea what he is talking about and if you have any Psych background you will probably do bad in this class because a lot of his information is seemingly made up.He is also very insulting to the differently abled population and talks as if we should assume none of them can do anything.He needs 2 B FIRED.Like yesterday!
He is a very lovable man! Teaching is his world!

This class needs to be updated big time! His info is oversimplified and lacks important details.  He can't hear very well so often doesn't understand questions.  He goes too slow with content and often needlessly rambles.  Tests are pretty easy.  You'll get more from the book than him.  ISU please replace him.  The subject deserves better teaching.
booorrriiinngggg

Not very helpful, lectures are hard to understand, and does not give out study guides which is vital because there is a lot of material that is covered in each lecture. Also, attendance is not mandatory but there are surprise pop quizzes!

He is a funny man, definitely entertaining during class.  You take a LOT of notes.  I recommend taking them on your computer if you don't want your hand to cramp.  Attendance isn't mandatory but there are random pop quizzes during class.  Study your notes & maybe read the summaries in the book & you'll be fine.

I have never been to a more entertaining class.  The material is boring, but you will definately be kept entertained with his computer noises and radom things that he does...not a very good teacher overall, but entertaining.
If you raise your hand in class you're golden.
Nice guy and very helpful!

Means well. I only went to this class about 6 times this whole semester and ended up with a B+. Also there are tests out there so try to get your hands on one of those. A little ove half of his currents tests have those questions on them.  I never even bought the book either...Good Luck.
I liked Abelson a lot. He kept class interesting. The only grades are tests. Go to class and study the notes and you should be pretty well off.
great!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Someone needs to make sure this man never teaches a class again.
This class is very boring. The tests are the only thing your grade consists of. If you don't do good on the test, your grade will be bad!

I thought Abelson was a pretty good professor.  His tests are straight forward; therefore if you attend class on a regular basis, fairly simple. He's really goofy acting, but that keeps class somewhat interesting.
He is really funny, what a wierdo but I like the class and I do well in it without trying too hard.
could be a very helpful class but taught in a very pointless matter
It's a very easy class and he's very passionate about what he teaches.  He's kind of a goof, but he's funny and it's a very easy A....

Lectures were pretty boring but if you go to the majority of them you will get an A in the class and not have to read from the book.  His tests were fairly easy although a few gramatical problems.  VERY nice man and tries VERY hard.

He is an awful teacher who uses absolutely terrible sounds for his slides.  He reads word for word off of his slides and is incredibly annoying to watch and listen to.  If you don't have to take this class DONT
No Comments
I hated the sound effects!!!!  And I hear he still does them!
No Comments
Sometimes, he just doesn't know what he is talking about.
He reads off of his powerpoint and it gets REALLY boring
He always seemed to not be up to speed on technology for displaying notes!
I thought he was pretty boring, although, he can be funny and is very helpful.  He is a really nice guy.  His tests are OK, but you have to actually read the book and study the notes.
Classes are pretty boring, but the tests are easy. He's a nice guy, he tries hard. A for effort.
Old Geoff is a true playa, he is a **** that knows his stuff and I couldn't ask for a better teacher
No Comments
He is one of the few professors that doesn't let a class of 400 stop him from getting to know his students.
No Comments
Geoff is one hot mama
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
The guy knew his stuff, and was funny w/o trying to be.  Little boring though.
No Comments
He is very helpful on a one on one basis.
No Comments
He is mean, you'll figure that out.  He gets irritated quickly!

I took SE 1850 with Shakil Ahmed during Fall 2025. This class gives the basics of coding and he wants to make sure that everyone grasps the concepts. Allowing students to ask questions and having in-class graded activities. He uses metaphors consistently to help people remember and wants to make sure students effectively learn.

He truly cares about his students and frequently pauses during lectures to make sure everyone understands the material. If you don't understand something and ask a question, he will stop everything to explain it clearly so that you and the rest of the class are on the same page. He also provides plenty of coding examples to reinforce concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a rare kind of personality — always present and genuinely invested in our success. He frequently reminds us to "learn and earn". He even brings in guest lecturers from industry to keep us engaged and motivated. He asks for feedback in almost every class, making us feel heard and supported. I feel very fortunate to have him as my professor.

Prof. Ahmed is a very engaging instructor. His lectures make coding feel exciting and approachable. I also learned how to use ChatGPT effectively, not just as a tool, but as a helpful learning companion rather than something to rely on long-term.
He's the best. As long as you show effort, you will be just fine.

He is an amazing professor! It was awesome going to his lectures and he explained everything so well. He does emphasize that everyone should get 100% on exams, and I can clearly see that after I took this class. Study for exams and do the homework's and you will pass easy.

I found this class unnecessarily tedious, but he is a very fair professor. If you show interest or want to learn, he will help you. He offers office hours for himself and a couple of TAs who help with the lab sections. I didn't love the class, but as long as you put the right foot forward, you will learn something and get an A.

Professor Shakil is very caring and respected, he teaches the fundamentals of C programming in very clear and simple terms. He was kind enough to recommend me for a scholarship after only the first few weeks of the semester. Tests are not easy, but very reasonable if you study at all. Would absolutely recommend his courses!

He is more than just a professor—he often addresses us as "friends," creating a welcoming and interactive classroom environment. He is always willing to listen to personal struggles and goes the extra mile to help student/s (me) stay on track. However, his class is also rigorous, with a heavy workload of assignments and exams.

I enjoyed the topic, the instructor, and the labs. This is a well-structured class; I found it a great learning experience. Professor Ahmed is an excellent teacher, and I appreciate having him for this subject. He occasionally shared relevant stories about the course, reinforcing my confidence that he was the perfect person to teach this topic.
Amazing professor that cares about his students, but his exams are a bit hard.
He is highly motivated to excel in the classroom, complemented by his approachable and humble demeanor.
Prof. Ahmed explains the material very well, and it's clear that he completely understands the ins and outs of coding in C.
He is a sweet and kind professor and willing to help you if you have any questions
Excellent Professor
The professor is very easygoing. I had no programming background, however, after attending the class, I have improved significantly.
He will provide you with tons of examples and make every effort to ensure you succeed in the course.
He uses ChatGPT for all of his lectures and exams
Very helpful professor.

Excellent professor with depth knowledge. Make sure to visit his office hours. Visiting his office hours is highly advisable, as he goes to great lengths to understand individual situations and support students in achieving success. However, the course is very heavy with lots of assignments and require a quite a lot of effort.

Didn't go to class that often, but when I did, he was rude. TopHat is taken in class for participation. There are many ways to earn back points throughout the semester. TAs in the lab are more helpful. If you do not go to the lab, you will struggle. The class itself is pointless if you have general knowledge on Excel.
The professor is very helpful and flexible. He cares about the students' success.

I found immense pleasure in this class, and despite facing some initial challenges, I believe there is significant room for improvement. The professor's distinctive teaching style benefitted me, showcasing remarkable flexibility. The broad spectrum of topics covered in lectures contributed to a truly enriching experience.

This class was infuriating and the professor is the most unhelpful teacher I've ever met. You could tell the other professor was running the show. The material taught with the homework and lectures is not what's on the exams. I only showed up because TopHat participation is part of your grade, otherwise the lectures are useless.

His lectures were always pretty good and he seemed to always want everyone to actually understand the material. Not requiring attendance was also nice, you can decide whether or not you need to go to every lecture.

It was difficult being a student for Ahmed. His lectures were heavily focused on examples. I can see why he would do this, but I feel like there's not enough focus on understanding concepts. Your grade is heavily weighed by exams and he doesn't have exam review sessions, which I think is ridiculous. No matter how hard you study, it won't be enough.

Kamal's 310 Class is very lecture heavy with him using obscure examples. Kamals class is also weighed pretty much on Exams, 60% each exam being worth 20%. Quizes are also tough being in person for those. He also never has a exam review calling it unnecessary but has lectures on stuff not thought on the exams. Do not take
