Professor Kamal's course is very difficult. It feels like there's too much information being taught and not enough time to learn it, and should realistically be a four-credit course. He weights his three exams as 60% of your total grade. If you do well on everything else, you will still get a C if you do badly on the exams.

Lectures are long and boring, he tries to compress what should be 5 credits into a 4 credit course. Exams were almost the entire grade, you could have perfect scores on everything but an exam and end up with a c
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For CprE 310, the lectures are a snooze fest and not worth going to. The quizzes and tests have nothing to do with the homework. Not necessarily his fault, but his two TA's were kinda just pointless. Not a fan.

Kamal honestly isn't a bad professor. My gripe is his lectures tend to get boring. And he also doesn't seem to manage his lecture schedules very well. We were still learning new material in the last lecture of the class. I would not really want him again, but if I saw him on my schedule I would not drop the course because of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is terrible. Not sure how he has any good reviews, maybe he's better at teaching other classes that are not CPRE310. His lectures are boring and not very helpful, however, they are required. He doesn't give you material to study for the class. And this semester, his Ta's were less helpful than he was. Good luck with 310, it will suck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Regularly late and unprepared for classes. Put material on exams that he clearly stated would not be on the exams. Incredibly unresponsive when asked for help, rushed through the class to cover all the material regardless of if it made sense to the students. Definitely seems like he would rather be doing research, yet he keeps teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A very ineffective professor. Lectures are a chore to sit through, and his handwriting is difficult to read, even for someone with bad handwriting. The grading criteria is unclear, there is little correlation between the textbook and exams. It is very difficult to study for, he covers a lot of topics but not enough examples to help you understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kamal is an alright professor. His accent can take some time to get use to, but it is not that bad. His handwriting is a different story, try and listen to what he is writing instead of looking at what he is trying to write. The class is not that bad and as long as you understand the homework the exams are not terrible. He also gives a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty good at giving lectures with lots of useful examples. Tends to drag on and get very boring though. He posted lecture videos online so all you have to do is watch those and go take quizzes.
He's a great instructor but his grading scale sucks and he's a tough grader.  Also he doesn't curve at all. When I took 310 with him the average of the class was about 65%-68% and he didn't help ....
We had to do labs even during the dead week. Also, he was still teaching stuff on the very last day of the class. He needs to manage his lecture schedules.
Good
Good prof.
Very good prof., but the course needs hard working .

Excellent professor. His class is going pretty fast and filled with quite lots of stuff on modern network tech. Homeworks take some long time. Exams are OK. A time consuming course. But you have to take it given you study is in any sense related with networks as there is no better advanced computer network course on network performance like this.

Lectures followed textbook nicely. Students should feel comfortable with C programming before taking this course as socket programming is expected with little instruction. Overall difficult course but definitely worth taking.
Good lectures but his tests are unreasonable. They're badly made and badly prepared for.

Dr. Ahn sometimes lacks organization and communication skills. His notes are mostly useful, but he occasionally writes off to the sides of pages in a confusing way. Test questions often have small mistakes, leave out necessary info, or require contradictory assumptions. Must solve his way exactly to get points. Does not seriously consider feedback.

411 is a very tough course. Some of the exam problems are unlike the practice and can be difficult to prepare for. However, it is difficult regardless of who is teaching. I still think Dr. Ahn is a great professor who wants students to do well. He is readily available for help during his office hours and explains information in the lectures well.

reviews.comment: Benjamin Ahn is the type of professor to prepare you for the wrong material. He will spend time going over various problems only for you to take an exam that's worth 40% of your grade on material that you've never seen. Of the 3 exams given in AerE 411, one out of the eight questions given were covered in review.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahn is the best professor in the EM department. He gives great lectures that are based on student learning rather than the professor just flexing on what he/she knows. Being in his class was the difference between an A and a C for me. I'd highly recommend him for the toughest class I've taken so far.

From my point of view is that he tried different kind of teaching test on us but he didn't realize it was engineering education. He don't know the basic stuff , like the direction and sign convention which made me very confused. All he doing is giving the equation and then put numbers into the equation without any reasoning.

Dr. Ahn is uncommon because his phd is actually in Teaching Engineers. He does research on his students by using sections as data points  and varies class parameters. However, no matter the classroom parameters he will take a vested interest in your education. He also has a cool Korean/New Zealand Hybrid accent.

Dr. Ahn is hands down the best professor I've had at Iowa State and probably ever will. He genuinely cares about his students and realizes that everyone learns differently. He is super down to earth and approachable. Class is easy if you have him. I would take literally any class he teaches because he is that good.
Fantastic professor. Very knowledgeable and caring of students. He will do whatever it takes to help you learn the material.

Ahn is one of the best professors that I have ever had! He is super helpful in office hours and will do whatever he can to make sure that you the material. Mechanics was extremely easy with Ahn in charge.
He's always available to answer my questions. Email him and he'll reply you in like less than an hour! His lectures are clear and helpful. Often work out example questions with students in class.

Professor Ajmera is a nice person in lecture, but writes absolutely evil exams. They are impossible to finish in time and you will get no diagrams or pictures, but long wordy explanations of each problem statement. There is truly no way to fully prepare for them. She will ask for feedback but do nothing about it so don't be fooled.
The practice exams are nothing like the exams

Dr. Ajmera was very helpful during office hours and always encouraged questions in class. She created a fun environment in class with her extra credit Wordle and seemed like she genuinely cared about the students. She did a lot of examples in class and even posted more on Canvas.

She made the class full of busy work. Didn't want to listen to students' suggestions. Made different exam than the other section. Explanations in class were very confusing. Never had time to meet students.
I liked his class. Has a bit of accent. But overall very clear and audible.

reviews.comment: Just got my grades. Very Happy. Professor Aziz was a big help throughout the semester. I was struggling initially. But he emailed me and talked with me personally to sort out the issues. He really cares about his students. I would highly recommend his class.
Nice Professor!

reviews.comment: Fantastic Guy ! Answered my email even at the very last moment before the final exam. He cares about his students. Take his class!!

Pretty good professor. Lectures can be boring at times but Stat isn't my favorite. The class isn't too hard as long as you listen what he says. There's weekly online homework assignments and 3 exams including the final.

reviews.comment: Came here to give him a 5/5... Great Guy! Take his class.

Ahmed is a real one, enough said. 5/5.

reviews.comment: Great Professor ! Explains everything carefully. Do a lot of worksheet in class. That helped me a lot in the Exam! He was very caring. Did give me extra time to explain what is going wrong after I didn't do well in the first exam.

He brings up tons of supplementary (Worksheet, HW, Practice Problems) materials to help you understand the topic! Nedd to attend classes to get a respectable grade. He is very accessible and reply emails in a flash.

reviews.comment: Learned a lot about basic microeconomics. Sample exams were helpful for me. He was very accommodating.

He's really hard to understand and at times isn't even sure what he's trying to say. I've learned lots of things in all of the classes i've taken so far at ISU but I have learned hardly anything in this class. He's a nice professor and will accommodate your needs but the class is tough and you need to work hard for a good grade.
Class was pointless, I learned more by teaching myself. Many times he seemed unsure of what he was teaching and had to correct concepts already reviewed.

The lectures are not the most fun, but he doesn't make the material hard to understand, and provides lots of examples. He assigns homework with every chapter through a third party site so sometimes it's easy to forget an assignment. Gives an opportunity for extra credit at the end of the semester that can raise your grade by half a letter grade.
He was a nice professor. I like that he gives examples sometimes that helped me to understand things clearly. Gave us slides. Exams were tough though.
Not a bad class. Very complicated material as well as complicated teacher. Has accent, but not that bad. At times good teacher, but other times made it super complicated. 4/10.
The notes and lectures do not seem to flow into exam material at all.

He gives long lectures that pointlessly go in depth on simple topics. I've done nearly all the homework without even looking at my notes or paying attention in class. He also has an accent that can make it hard to understand him, though he usually gets his point across. I definitely would NOT recommend taking his class.

Professor is nice and wants people to succeed but does not teach very well, would just walk in and start babbling about some topic with no basis. We had a grad student teach a section and that section everyone did significantly better in. If hes still teaching just read the book from copyworks, itll probably do better for you than the lecture.

Ajjarpu is fine, I guess. A bit unsympathetic and impatient. Lectures at 8 a.m. -- only 20% of class attended. Closed note exams were 75% of the grade (painful). TAs were helpful outside of class, but professor was not great in office hours. Mild curve applied at the end of class. You WILL get through this class with him, don't worry.

His lectures are hard to follow. His organizational skill are poor, which makes it hard to find important document. His speech patterns are broken. He will often not finish sentences or thoughts before starting new ones. When he prepares for class he presents coherent and informative lectures, but it is not a common occurrence.

Not a great time in power with him. His slides are confusing and his spoken notes aren't much help either. I recommend buying his notes and teaching yourself the material. The homework is sparse enough (every few weeks) but takes 4-5 hours to complete. Tests are difficult and rely heavily on equation memorization. Pray you ride the curve.

reviews.comment: Good

I found class hard to follow. He uses "this" and "that" instead of the nouns they represents, while pointing to variables as he's describing how to calculate the equation which makes it hard to write notes because you have to watch what he is pointing at to know what's going on. He is very unorganized. I had difficulty finding assignments. ACCENT
Speech is sometimes hard to follow but just ask if confused and he will clarify. Exams properly test the material. Homework can be hard but is only 5% of your grade so it is not crucial.

Ajjarapu knows his stuff but sometimes lectures would often be scattered and I would walk out not knowing what we did that day. Tests are pretty easy but homework's are pretty long and tedious.  Shouldn't be too hard to get a good grade in the class. If anything is confusing just go to his office hours and he clears it up pretty well.
Terrible, literally the worst prof I've seen. Never announce important info on BBL. Very strong accent, poor attitude towards teaching.

This professor is terrible, he never responds to email, he has a strong India accent which makes lectures hard to understand.He posted textbook required before semester started then after that he asked us to buy a different one, wasted me a lot of money. Also, he never gives partial credit for exams.
Perfect professor, knows his area very well, and teaching ability is also good. Very helpful and perfect adviser. Strongly recommended...
Prof's lectures are dry and generally unhelpful, but that could be attributed to the class being at the crack of dawn and most of the semester being winter.
I really like him,
Terrible lecturer. Took 2 months to return tests. Only 3 homeworks during the entire course which didn't pertain to any exam material. Example: Average exam score on the second midterm was 45%

I think i attended altogether 10 classes all through out the whole semester counting exams.  Still left the class with a B+ in EE303....hated the course, and his teaching wasn't that great either.  Power is a boring subject, at least for me it was, and to top it off, his lectures were really boring.
Doesn't know how to use the lights or projector.  Class time is basically a joke.  He just reads another professors scanned notes.

Very nice guy that knows his stuff but has trouble teaching it. Has a thick accent. Very helpful if you go to his office hours.  Tips:  Study his slides like your life depends on it, the tests/quizes will be just like them.  Go to class because you need your own notes to decifer his. Go to his office hours and he will basically give you the answers

Very poor instructor.  Does not communicate material well at all.  Completely unresponsive to emails.  Most of the class never attends during non-quiz days.  During the quizzes and final, it was apparent that a good portion of the class was cheating.
Talk about boring... if there isn't a scheduled quiz, about 25% of the class comes. Quizes aren't bad but sometimes pulls somthing out of left field. Watch out for the final.
Was getting an A until the final.  The average on our final: 25%
I got an A in EE 442 with Patterson, then took 448 and failed both tests, dropped the class. Retook EE 448 with Patterson next sem and got an A.

Dr. Appelgate is a very influential and helpful professor. Her class was extremely eye opening and taught mathematical concepts in teaching. She expects students to do their work at a high level, but at any college level course this should be expected. Definitely recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mollie is awesome!...I honestly don't understand the other review posted on here that rated her poorly. She is very funny, entertaining, and guides great conversations with great questions. The only downside is that there is a lot of reading to do, but it is interesting and relevant to what we are going to do! I wish she taught more classes...

I do not feel ready to teach math after this class. Mollie gets lost in conversations in class and doesn't stay on track for things that need to get done. She assigns homework that takes hours but is worth just 3 points. She has high expectations but doesn't help you reach them, or even explain how to.

She is a fun and caring professor.  She lets you have the freedom of combining the mediums you like to work in with printmaking.  She is very understanding and helpful to both new and experienced printmakers.  Overall, she is one of the best ISA instructors!

An excellent teacher, who articulates her passion for printmaking in how she teaches.  I am an Art major with not much previous interest in this medium.  I have increase interest but also a strong fundamental foundation.
Really nice and helpful, knows her stuff, wants you to learn.

I really wasn't looking forward to printmaking before this class, but April was so enthusiastic and open-minded that she actually made it fun and interesting.  I felt I got a lot from this class and wish she was teaching more classes in my curriculum.
No Comments

Great instructor, very helpful and fun to listen and talk to.  Even though I didn't really like the process of lithography that much (I prefer the immediate results of other media), the class was still enjoyable.  She's really into printmaking and is very knowledgeable and talented at it.
shes very laid back and friendly. shes very helpful

I had April for intaglio-one of the BEST teachers I've ever had. She cares about her students and about art so much. She's great, demanding, but only because she wants you to do your best. Plus, printmaking is totally fun!

After the beginning of the semester I almost dropped because it seemed too much for me. I stayed in the class, but it was really tough. There are no paper exams but a "game show" that is pretty confusing and she didn't give much guidance on how to prepare so the first round went pretty rough. Overall the class is stressful
Very good instructor, well-prepared for class materials and complete analysis of classes. Quizzes are not hard at all if you read the reading materials carefully.
She works hard to make sure her students do well. Will pressure you do come to class prepared and makes sure to talk to you if you even miss one class. Overall, she's a great teacher.

Amazing teacher! Truly cares about her students. The class itself is hard (its Chinese for god sakes). But she is very fair and the easiest of all the Chinese teachers! You will learn so much from her. She has a witty humor about her too! AMAZING LADY. Her English is good, but sometimes she makes minor grammatical errors... 他是很

She's amazing. Yes, she moves quickly, but she's one of the most accommodating, understanding people I know. She is extremely fair in grading, and she encourages students to be the best they can be. She is a true inspiration, and her class is an absolute blast.
She is so nice and helpful.
A professor whose primary care is teaching. You'll learn a lot.
She wants every student to succeed.  Knows the material and uses discussion to help students understand it better.  Good professor.

She is wonderful!  She made me want to really learn the language so well, and was the best teacher, although a bit demanding.  Great experience.  Because of her, I am going to China this summer to practice!
Very enthusiastic and kind.  Learned a lot.  Interesting class.
Dr. Mu really cares about her students.
Easy job for Americans but hard work for Chinese students.

Dr. Mu is very sweet and she cares A LOT about her students. She truly wants each student to be happy and do well. However, the format of Chinese 301 doesn't work. It is confusing for American students, useless for Chinese students, and frustrating for all. Class projects do not contribute to the real goal of the class: learning Chinese.

She is very much invested in student learning but is extremely unclear about due dates and explanations. Chinese 301 format is flawed as it is but they're trying to improve it so hopefully will get better. Grades easily on Americans and makes busy work for Chinese students since they're in an intermediate language course. Frustrating course

Very good professor.  Lots of reading to do.  Be very specific when you answer on tests.  The research paper is hard, but if you do your best and be creative, you will do fine.  Do interviews if possible.
class gets progressively worse through semester. interesting material but boring lectures. he has monotonous voice. extremely hard tests but a huge curve. on the final, my 31/60 was a B+.

The class is not really difficult. It's mostly discussion and the tests are essay. The one thing I didn't like was the lack of clarity on what the paper was supposed to be about. He was a good teacher though who was enthusiastic about the subject.
I really enjoyed his class!
No Comments
No Comments
One of the best profs on the ISU campus!!

This is a very interesting class and Aigner's is very enthusiastic about the material. The readings are all interesting, and the class is based alot on discussion. The only thing I didn't like were the essay tests.
The Professor has an infectious enthusiasm for the subject and combines fascinating readings with relevant personal experience to successfully transmit knowledge.
No Comments
Excellent professor, makes finance come alive

Answers emails well, but that's it. Still surprised I got an A. Quizzes were 30%, exams 20 and 25%, and SB 25%. Not having many points made it difficult. Lectures got worse as the semester progressed, and quizzes/exams BARELY related to content. Make sure you understand everything to the fullest extent beforehand. Took as a Winter Term course.

reviews.comment: Would give quizzes and exams that would include basically nothing that was presented on the problem sets throughout the whole class. 3 projects were given throughout the semester, which would be gone over in class, but she would go too fast and not explain how she would get any of her answers or interpretations.

reviews.comment: Tyagi did a nice job leading EE 491 in the Fall 2021 semester. The course was a bit of a joke with endless, mindless writing and busy work. Still, Tyagi graded fairly, showed up consistently, and appeared to take interest in student projects. My group got an A easily. Not sure how he'd be in a more traditional EE class.

Really disorganized. Didn't use Piazza and instead just bombards you with emails. The class favors non-industry projects since it's a design course. If your client already has the design planned, you have to pretend you came up with it yourself and will be graded based on their design plan.

Dr. Tyagi is a great lecturer and clearly knows what he's talking about. He does every lecture seemingly from memory and is ready to answer questions every time. His answers can be somewhat cryptic: "make any assumptions you need to"
Great professor. Cares about his students. Works out of the book most of the time, but in a good way

Dr Tyagi is a great professor. The exams are a little tricky but it is pretty easy to know what will be on them. He based it off the types of problems seen in the homework. He gives amazing lectures. He doesn't usually read off the slides, in fact he sometimes barely touches them. He has a wealth of knowledge and is great at breaking things down.

here's what you need to know about him: - He is a great monologist, he has ease explaining complex topics of the class. HOWEVER, he is not so good at answering questions, and clarifying stuff for students. - His labs are exactly an application of the lecture topics, quite long so take your time. - Exams will be tight on time. Look over the HW.
I have absolutely no idea why Dr. Tyagi does not have a 5/5 here. Amazing professor. He starts off complex topics like they are a story. Very knowledgeable.

Professor is very knowledgeable and is able to delve into any detail you desire during lecture. He uses textbook slides as a guide to stay on topic rather than just reading them at the class. 4 out of 5 students never attended lectures but the ones that did had a great relationship with him and we learned a lot. Prepared us well for hw and exams.
He doesn't do a good job clarifying the course materials, you'd be better off with another lecturer.
Switch to another professor if you can. He explains only the basics in lecture, but the homework is brutal and leaves you feeling confused. Doesn't do a good job of clarifying information.
Well the only bad comments that I have is about the final project. No orientation at all! Some projects are really easy, and some others are way harder

Not recommended!  lousy lectures, with almost no preparation.  gives assignments during dead-week!  projects are not well explained, you learn no tools/simulators at all! Tools are really essential for processor design, simulation and design space evaluation.   Again, Not recommended, or take the class and be prepared for disaster :(

Very knowledgable about his subject. However, he didn't pay a lot of attention to the class this semester. Lecture notes were always a mess, and not clear. Also, we had to watch 4 previous recorded lectures because he was travelling. The final exam was an oral exam which was really nice and tests if you understand the subject or not.

very low quality. no preparation at all.  He traveled twice in the semester (4 lectures out of 27) He gave us 3 assignment during the dead-week and they were due in less than a week before final. His final is an interview! Never explained projects but he wants u to excel in project! I dont recommend taking any class with this instructor.

He can explain/draw out any course topic at will so lectures don't have a particular structure. Explains well if you're paying attention. Strong effort needed to put into practice if its new to you. Homeworks were a real pain and ambiguous but force familiarity if you do them. Labs are of great significance. Labs + final proj = a fair 45%
hard not understand.Destroys all my interest in embedded system.
Can't understand what he says. Has a backwards way of teaching and destroyed my interest in a computer related career in 2 weeks.

Great prof, knows his stuff.  My only problem was that you are expected to do the labs before you get lectured on the material, which is very confusing. Also the his homeworks were very indirect in what they wanted. All and all a good lecturer.

Extremely knowledgeable and can easily spend a half hour lecturing about any curve ball you throw at him.  Packs a lot of info into lecture, but makes sure it is all covered well in lecture notes.  Homeworks reasonable.  Need to pay attention and distill the important info from lectures but you will learn about all sorts of orthogonal topics.

Lectures are lousy, mumble mumble, stutter stutter, zzzzzz. Its very hard to follow his talking and figure out the point he is trying to make, I tried hard. Comp Arch was a potential thesis topic when I started my MS, this guy turned me off completely.

He knows his stuff and was given some award for Engineering or something.  The lectures aren't too informative but make labs and homework a little easy.  You'll be learning most things through the homework and labs O and I learned asm during the test.
Seems to have some enthusiasm in the course material.  The class did not follow labs.  Had to learn everything from labs.  Lectures are worthless.

Despite what others have said, I actually really liked Dr. Appy. He actually wants you to try in order to succed rather than just handing it to you. Appy is the representation of stubbing your toe every day after waking up. In all seriousness, his exams are extremely tough and he doesn't cover the material in depth and expects you to memorize a whole textbook and its concepts. While other classes were scoring 80s on the first exam, Appy's class scored 40-50s, and 36% of the course would fail.

David Appy is not a professor I would recommend to any student. Our class was not provided with supplemental instruction, no reviewable lecture notes for studying, and no test prep of any kind. Other sessions were allowed a note sheet and was mc while our exam was completely free response. Class avg was 49% and only 8% were graded an 80% or more.

Gives "practice" for homework that is worth only one point, then refuses to give practice exams / ANY type of resource to prepare for tests. Tests are a different format than all other professors and include info not taught in class.

Dr. Appy is one of the worst Professors I have ever had, this is coming from a senior. I would HIGHLY recommend NEVER taking a class from him. You will fail. His tests and even homework is so hard. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am flabbergasted by the ridiculousness of this teacher and his class teachings. Not only could he not deliver a lecture without going off on tangents about politics and anything else that had no relation to the topic. But he would also fabricate numbers on very publicized events to fit his own biases and make it part of the "lecture learning".

Dr. Appy is really funny and seems like a nice person. However, I don't understand his teaching style and I had a hard time grasping the material. He moves at a very fast pace and expects you to read the book before every lecture. The exams are very difficult because he doesn't explicitly cover the material that is on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Appy knows his stuff and is a good presenter so you won't get bored. He's accessible to help. Dry sense of humor. I would really have enjoyed him and his class more if I were better at chemistry. His tests are harder than other teachers; questions not always straight forward, some tricky questions . He did curve grades but ever so gently.
Dr Appy is the type of guy you want to go have a beer with, not the type of guy you want teaching you Chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: His tests are incredibly difficult, but he genuinely cares about the students. If you make an effort to ask questions and get help with what you struggle with, he is very accommodating. By far my fav prof this semester
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His exams are nothing like what is taught in class. Even reading the book doesn't help with him. He didn't provide a study guide for his exam. Highly recommend not having him as a professor. Find another teacher if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Appy may be hard to understand but once you get past his accent he is very knowledgable. He also incorporates some humor. Sometimes he does stumble with explaining things in class but plenty of extra credit. Tests are not very difficult if you do the study guide, final is very hard. Participation is key and do NOT skip lectures!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Definitely the least professional professor I have had my entire time in college, (this is including another one of my professors who uses texting slang in notes and announcements). Passive aggression in his announcements about students not doing better on an 'objectively easier' exam and refuses to consider it was due to his teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are everywhere &dont follow how it goes in the book, he goes on tangents for 20 minutes and proceeds to tell us that its not important. The tests are worded difficultly & dont reflect what we did in class. Notes are not posted online. Hes easy to talk to & funny but sends announcements about how hes disappointed in the tests, can be rude

Everyone putting down Dr. Appy and I LOVED HIM. He made class super interesting and I was engaged when learning. Go to class because he doesn't post lectures after. Take good notes and READ THE TEXTBOOK. Also make sure to really focus and challenge yourself on the homework. He uses HW and text for exams; focus on application- he makes you think!!!

The tests are nothing like what he goes over in lecture, so he is setting students up for failure. If you want to do well, memorize the text book. The averages for the tests were around 50% each time. He has also made multiple announcements on canvas that he is disappointed in the grades that students have achieved.

Appy is something... However, that is not to say that he is a bad professor. Appy will test you on everything, exposing the weaknesses that you thought you could hide. While Appy's tests are notoriously difficult, they are not impossible by any means. If you want to succeed, read, attend the lecture, and REVIEW HOMEWORK! He curves heavy as well.

Easily one of the worst professors Ive had. There were extremely low exam averages throughout the semesters, which were then followed by rude and condescending emails sent to the students. He berated students in emails for not understanding a tough concept- a simple reflection of his ability to teach the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Appy's tests contain relevant information as long as you pay attention and read the textbook. He offers extra credit, and is really understanding. Provides students with 3 HW and 3 quiz drops. First professor I have had that cares about the well-being of his students. As long as you do your work, it isn't unreasonable to get an A/B.

This man is the most unprofessional professor I've ever had. Says he's "disappointed" in us after the class average in his completely-random-content-filled exams is below an F, and says he "needs a drink" after grading our work. Nice to know what Appy is doing in his free-time cause it sure isn't anything helpful.
Class average for test was 40% very difficult no matter how much you prepare. lectures are unorganized as he just handwrites notes on a pad of paper, no slides or anything.

Very difficult. The only 3 other people I know in the class also have to retake it. Only graded materials are exams& 3 point homework assignments, & exams are extremely difficult& nothing like practice tests. He told us he had to reread the book to understand& recommended we do the same to pass which with classes and a job no student has time for.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My experience with Appy was horrible. He is fantastic at chemistry and is very smart. However, he is incredibly rude to students and sends consistent passive/aggressive emails. He is not very approachable and the material is incredibly hard. Lecture isn't mandatory but if you want to pass, go. Get a TUTOR FOR THE CLASS. They will save you.

Professor Appy is a fantastic professor. Although the class has a bad rep for being difficult, he really spends all semester telling you exactly what you need to do/know to do well and if you follow his advice you will do great. He seems passionate about teaching and his lectures are always enjoyable.

Dr. Appy is a nice professor but his exams are very difficult. Although they are curved it is still difficult to get a good grade. It is important to go to the lectures but sometimes he gets off topic in discussion and shows things that don't relate to the material on the exam. Also, there are chapter worksheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The toughest thing about this class is that the exams are not multiple choice. They were all open ended and there are no study guides. He does a bunch of demos that are not on the exam. He will spend more time on discussions than teaching material. You must make sure you understand the material well and might have to teach yourself some of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Appy really tries to have his students get a good grade in his class. However, if you don't read or participate in class, his teaching technique won't be beneficial for you. To ace this professor, just read, participate, and visit him in office hours. His tests are pretty hard, but with the pop quizzes and extra credit, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Appy means well, but as he says during the beginning of the class... the TA is better at teaching Organic chem than he is. Wouldve rather had the TA teach the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I think he had good intentions, the delivery of the course wasn't successful. The class average was extremely low, and his attitude toward the students was at times very disrespectful. If you ask any questions about the exam or grading criteria he gets visibly frustrated, and he gives little assistance to students. Also often goes off on tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Great professor and seems to really care. I can't say the class was easy, but if you put in the effort, attend SI, do the practice tests, and take time to study and actually understand the material, it's rewarding. Flash cards and SI sessions were what saved me!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Appy was such a cool guy. He's down to talk about anything and just lets the class head in its own direction discussion-wise. There's one paper but you have all semester to do it and you get a cheat sheet for the tests. Some exam questions get kind of specific, but there's extra credit offered on all of them. We barely even talked about chemistry.

Honestly I did not enjoy Appy. I approached him multiple times asking for help and his first solution was to tell me to drop. The homework takes hours and does not prepare you for the tests. Khan Academy was my best friend in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Appy was an awesome teacher and he really cares about his students success. He makes learning chemistry and science fun.

Chem 163 was a SUPER HARD class for me personally. With the ridiculously hard and LONG lab, the whole class is worth 5 credits. If possible, don't take it with another hard class. I got a tutor which was a lifesaver. There is a large curve, but virtually no extra credit. TAs teach lab and recitation. Appy was a fun lecturer, but content was extreme

Appy is awesome. I took organic chem with him last summer. I spent 2 hours every single day after class with him going over the homework problems. Though organic chem is really hard, he truly cares about his students and if you put forth effort you'll learn it and do well. Cool professor but kept drawing shapes on the board...

Dr. Appy has been by far my favorite professor yet. It's hard material but he loves what he does and he cares about his students. He is willing to help you out and he loves students seeing him during office hours. Also, 10/10 funniest man ever. I actually ended up enjoying the class and that's mainly because Appy taught it.

Dr. Appy is the man. His lectures contain all the information you will ever need plus he posts them online. He's funny and loves what he does making his lectures enjoyable to go to. Study his practice exams and the real exams will be easy. By far my favorite chem class/teacher.

Chem160 is a class he's never taught before, and I thought it was excellent. As long as your classmates are willing to engage in discussion, the classes are interesting. The lectures are easy to follow, and he is passionate about the subject. There is no homework so attendance points really count. Tests are average difficulty. 10/10 I recommend it.

If you have to take organic chemistry, take it with Appy. He relays the information in a way that makes sense. He is humorous and loves what he does; he cares a lot about his students and how they feel about the class.  The homework assignments are on Sapling and are pretty long but they aren't impossible.

Enjoyed his class, teaching style, and personality. I had this class at 8 am and honestly didn't mind getting up for it. He made class interesting and clear, even if you struggle with chemistry, which I do. If you do the homework and pay attention, you should easily pass (I got an A!).

Loved him and his teaching style. I found lectures to be engaging and funny. The class is difficult, tests make up most of your grade, and the online homework was awful to use. Go to lectures, ask questions, and opwork hard. Dr. Appy definitely cares, and is always willing to answer questions.

Awkward teaching style. Wishy washy and goes on tangents about things unrelated to Chemistry. Gets things wrong in lecture and emails corrections frequently. Blames poor grades on students and not on his teaching. When most people are in the 30s that probably means something...
He's all over the place, pretty hard to follow. Going to class really doesn't matter as long as you make the notes up.

Great personality, horrible at teaching. He is not specific with the reactions and does not explain each step thoroughly. He skips ahead a lot. The class mainly depends on exam scores and my class average was about 60-65%. Homework is a ton of work but barely worth any points. My tutor taught better than him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Appy was overall a great professor. However, he is very specific during lecture and you need to pay attention in order to truly understand. Textbook was extremely helpful and 99% of all test or quizzes comes straight from the book. Be prepared to work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, and very open to help lock in concepts after class. He expects his students to come prepared and put in the effort, be he expects it in a reasonable way (he'll tell you he won't drop his standards to accommodate lack of effort). With that said, he prepares students for success.

Professor Appy is an overall good guy and you can tell he genuinely loves teaching and cares about his students. I'm honestly not understanding the material but that's because I'm not trying very hard but it's still my favorite class just because I enjoy learning from Appy so much

I could tell he cared a lot about his students. I had him last year and he always showed up to the exam reviews to help us with problems and to let us know what kind of questions to expect. I honestly didn't end up with a good grade in this class but that's because I did not try at all. But he is always happy to help his students!
He hand writes lecture notes, and homework is a lot like exams. Office hours are very relaxed and helped me out a lot.
This was his first time teaching Organic chem, and I think he did great. He made the hardest class of my life bearable, and was always willing to help us with homework outside of class. Nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took this Spring 2015. I appreciated that he made those with computers sit in the back row to minimize distraction. Going to class wasn't mandatory, as lectures were also online, but if you skip, you will NOT get the grade you want. Keep up on homework, attend lecture and pay attention. If you do this, you should be okay. He wants you to learn.
Good professor, you just need to study hard like most of college class, then you definitely will do good in this class, good luck to every one

Appy seems like a good teacher at the beginning of the semester. When you take your first test, it is nothing like he teaches you. He basically is setting students up for failure with the difficulty of his tests.

Very tough class. All exam scores ranged in the low 50-60's. Even though I always did well above this average I ended with a C+ in the class. Appy is a very funny guy, but a horrible teacher. Curve should have been way higher with respect to students scores. I recommend any other teacher but him.

Great guy, terrible professor, seems great until you get to your first test and none of the material relates to what you just 'learned'. Averages have been 58% on all the tests throughout the entire class with no curve. Reschedule get another teacher
Class is interesting with demos and fun facts. I loved the class but the exams are tough. Not much homework and no quizzes either so your grade depends on your exam grades. I love Dr. Appy so much ;)

He is a phenomenal teacher! He really cares for each of his students and his lectures are very clear. He also writes all of his notes, which allows you to easily keep up with the pace he is going and keep notes as well. He is extremely helpful during office hours- go to them! His tests are hard, but this class is not supposed to be easy.
He's a great professor and is very easy going. He knows what he is talking about. He is very down to earth and loves when the class asks questions.
Fun lectures but hard exams.

Class exam averages were really low but there was still no curve for the class which personally I found completely ridiculous.  Expect long homework assignments every week, they are worth a significant amount of your grade and they are not easy.  I put a significant amount of work into this class and still got the worst grade of my college career.

Dr. Appy is funny and very nice but his class is difficult. He puts his lectures online so attendance is not necessary but things make more since if you go to class. Tests were tough and I often found myself going into the test confident then reading the questions on the test and having no idea what it was talking about.

Dr. Appy is a great professor if you've already had some background with chem. I found his lectures to be simple because I took chem in high school and did well. The online homework is finicky but helps comprehension. Tests are graded tough!!  You may know your stuff, but little mistakes can get you. Overall, great teacher and would recommend.
Didn't curve the class. Test averages were very low and final grade average was very low. Take Chem163 with someone besides Appy.  I didn't learn anything.
He really cares about the students. Tough material. Beware of fill in the blanks on tests.

One of the best professors I've had so far. Hilarious guy who really wants to see you succeed. Lectures are both amusing and helpful. Tests can be tough if you do not study. Contrary to other comments, what he teaches in lecture IS what is on the tests. Read the book if you need extra clarity. Get help if needed. Wish I could have him again.

Appy is the worst  professor I've ever had... tests are nothing what he talks about in class. Makes the class way harder than it needs to be. Many of the TA's were confused about his questions and expected students to figure it out. TERRIBLE

He seems to be a really nice guy until you take your first test. No matter if you read the text book, do the homework, study for days, go to class every day, you will flunk the tests. He puts the lectures online which is nice, but it really helps if you go to class. He refuses to help you if you ask. Take it with a different professor if you can.

You think you know everything that is going to be on the tests, you do all the practice problems in the book and homework, read the book, go over your notes, go over the past exams that are posted,  and then you take the test and it is nothing like what you've learned. Good luck if you have to take it with him.

Appears to be a nice guy in lecture but once you take your first test you'll change your mind. The tests are hardly what you learn in lecture so read the book. His multiple choice questions on his tests are impossible and meant to trick you. Unless you have a strong chemistry I really recommend taking it with someone else if you can.

He puts past exams up with keys as practice for your exam but they are never even remotely the same material. The homework and its usually around 50 problems and it takes hours/days, and half the time you type in the correct answer and it says its wrong, and its only worth ten points of each chapter. Puts lectures online so attendance isnt required

He is a very good professor. Tests are difficult if you dont go to class. GO TO CLASS he makes lectures interesting and funny. Puts lectures online. Students like him. Grading is sometimes unclear. Notes are very important and he writes them with you so you to make sure you get it all down. He makes the subject interesting by his clarity & detail

very good professor. helps to have a background in chemistry. he also puts video lectures online for if you have to miss class. really knows what he's talking about and makes jokes a lot which is entertaining. tests tend to be more conceptual so make sure to study that and know the math as well

Unless you have a very strong background in Chemistry, I would highly recommend taking the class with someone else. He seems like he is a great professor in lecture because he explains things thoroughly and the examples seems easy. However, the tests are extremely difficult. Don't expect averages above a 50% and not that much of a curve to save you

Nice teacher overall. The classes are confusing and would not recommend taking an early morning class with him! Definitely read through the textbook. The tests are really hard and didn't always follow what was discussed in class. Truthfully, the majority of the class was below a C. I would look into other options prior to choosing him.

Dr. Appy really knows chemistry and he is very passionate about it. Very friendly, funny, and his lectures are interesting. He tried to do a demonstration every week. His tests are fairly difficult though, so study up. Visiting office hours helps a ton and when  talking one on one with him, he is super nice
Extremely passionate about chemistry. Good sense of humor and is very good at teaching. Beware of the tests, however, as they are hard.

The exams are like a foreign language. Very different from what you cover in class, the class averages on each exam were around 50%. Huge curve at the end of the class was helpful to final grade. His lectures are interesting, but not helpful for exams. Choose another professor who goes over problems in class if possible--he was my only option.
His lecture are great. However, he is the toughest test giver in the whole gen chem department. The curve is a lifesaver though.

I didn't know what working hard meant until I took Dr. Appy's class. If you want to pass his class you must work above and beyond throughout the entire semester. Homework assignments are EXTREMELY long and tough, and exams are quite difficult with very low averages. Study and get a tutor it definitely helps. Take advantage of the cheat sheet!

Dr. Appy expects a lot out of his students.  His tests are much harder than examples you do in class.  Don't take chem with him unless you have a strong background in chemistry.  Average exam scores were in the 40-50 range.

Dr. Appy knows his stuff and is very passionate about what he teaches, however, his tests were very hard and you really have to know the material in and out to succeed. If you are really good at Chem, then he is a great professor to take the class with. If you aren't I highly recommend taking it with someone else.

He explains things really well in lecture, and seems to really care about his students. Unfortunately, the exams are a lot harder than the examples in class and you don't get a whole lot of time to work out each problem. The averages so far were 55 and 48, and he does not curve the exams. Unless you have a strong background in Chem, don't take him.

Dr. Appy is my most favorite professor ever. He teaches with ease, a lot of cool demos so you actually understand better. If you pay attention in class and write notes (he hates laptop) you'll get an easy A for every exams. Beware of the final exam though. It was hard but I still managed to get an A for his class. Good luck !
Exams were kind of hard, but if you really do the homework, you will be fine. One homework every week, graded on completeness. Dr. Appy has been my favorite professor so far at ISU.

Lectures follow the book closely.  1-3 extra credit questions (ECQ) per test are on somewhat obscure topics.  If Dr. Appy gets excited about something in class that's an "aside", it's a prime target for an ECQ.  Genuinely cares about students' overall well-being.  Attend class and read the book and you'll do fine.

By far my favorite professor so far. If you're familiar with Chem it will be very easy. Lectures are not boring at all, he is very humorous, clicker questions every day, small % of grad. Is always willing to help you if needed. Makes the topics very easy to understand. Exams are kind of difficult and cover a lot of material. I highly recommend him!

Probably one of the more interesting professor's I've ever had. Inspirational and hilarious. Tests are tough if you don't go to class. Skip class? You won't pass! He's pretty hilarious but I feel like most of the class don't get his jokes. He's easy on the eyes too!

Appy makes class fun and actually talks to the students. He understand that chemistry is hard for most and is always willing to help. LOTS of demos during lectures. His notes are great and interactive, really easy to follow. Homework is a little tough and the exams are relatively tough as well.
Dr. Appy makes a clear effort to make a connection with his students and be in direct access for any concerns or issues. Best eight AM you could have.
Very good professor. Tests are tough, but if you put in effort, you'll pass easily. Come to class. Read the book.
He was my favorite teacher. He likes to make jokes.
Dr. Appy is really cool. The class can be tough  but he does his best to make things interesting.
His tests are very difficult. Enough said
Great teacher. NEED the textbook to pass, since a lot of homework comes from it, and studying out of it for tests is pretty much essential. Clicker questions daily.
Dislike
He's the best teacher i have ever known. He will help you all the time. He's so sweet!
Mufit, you are awesome!!!
Mufit is the man. He made the class fun and interesting. He knows what he's talking about (especially in ceramics) and is generally the greatest professor of all time.

This turk is exceedingly rude to students! I sent him an email about what i should do if i got a 30 on the exam after seeing that there were several 30s scores posted. He replied "you shouldn't be concerned with the grades of other students". CANNOT TEACH IN A LARGE CLASSROOM DONT TAKE HIM

I bet the guy would fail this course if he were to take it himself from a real teacher. Dr. Akinc should not be teaching, he really needs to start taking classes in materials science before he retires. It's never too late to finally learn something! Does anyone still want to take his class?
hmm.... not my favorite...

This course is awfully boring. The instructor's slurring speech makes it totally unbearable. I once asked him what's the difference between silicates and silicones and he failed to answer. He mumbled something in his broken English and literally said: I would need to check in the book!!!!!!!!!!

This professor seems to know nothing about his material. Always reads from slides, has horrible accent (he's turkish), and can't explain anything. Makes you feel totally dumb and humiliated. Where do such mediocre teachers come from?? Don't sign up for his class, if you can.
No Comments

This class is entirely group project based so if you're lucky w your partners it's easy but could be made difficult depending on your group. She can be a tough grading on exams, but she does allow note cards. The exams are taken in your groups so if you disagree with a partner about an answer it can affect your grade. The labs are fun and hands on.

Sheep science was a lot of fun with Dr. Powell this semester however, she switched to project based learning instead of giving exams. My group got along fine but if you are assigned a group that didn't mesh well, things will be very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really like Dr. Powell and her lectures are pretty decent. Sheep science was not something I was very interested in, but a class I had to take. This class was interesting, well-structured, and the labs were out at the sheep farm a lot doing some cool stuff. Although if you don't have a car, make friends in the class or you are screwed.

I learned a lot about the sheep industry with this class. I loved the hands on labs with this course. graded on weekly quizzes, drops an exam, lab worksheets and tophat points. Go to class for tophat. Do extra credit if she offers. She is nice, but can come across as moody and is very "my way" with grading. Exams were very randomly specific.

Solid class with great lectures. Hands-on labs and graded on weekly quizzes, lab sheets, Tophat, and 2 unit exams. Does not make the course overly complicated but you need to attend lectures and labs. Small class size if you're into that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 100% would take again. Highly recommend her!! :)

I love Dr. Andreotti! She is super passionate about biochemistry and the world of science in general that you can't help but be excited with her. She is kind and encouraging to students and she can see potential in everyone. Her paper writing assignments were informative and interesting, I learned a lot about unknown figures in chemistry!

Dr. Andreotti is passionate about her subject and wants everyone to do well. She saved us money and didn't require a textbook, instead she provided us readings and problem sets that were more than able to make up for it. There was no homework, all of the grades came from exams, but she made it very doable. You are LUCKY if you get her. She's GREAT!
Great teacher. Best Ive ever had. I wish all my instructors were this good.
Great professor. Really wants you to understand what she is trying to explain to you and is very helpful

Amy was kind, engaging, and one of the best professors I have had. She made evening classes enjoyable and always lifted the mood with humor. The classwork was interactive, manageable, and interesting. I highly recommend taking any course with her.

One of the best professors I've had! You will learn the most by showing up to class and participating. There are short homework assignments every week that are simply completion points. Most of your grade comes from exams, but Amy does an amazing job at giving extra credit and explaining what will be on them. Highly recommend her as a professor!

Amy really cares about her students and their learning. As long as you put effort into your work, she will give feedback & help you make revisions to get the grade you want. Very understanding and passionate professor.

Prof Walton was very supportive of my learning as I navigated the content. I found the topics in this course to be pretty difficult, but there was never a time I felt like I didn't have the support of my professor. She responds quickly to emails and is very understanding. The class was hard, but it would have been 10x harder with a different prof.

Man Professor Walton is one of the best professors I've had. She cares about her students, you can tell she loves her job, she grades professionally but is also lenient when it comes to her students. Take her class if you get a chance, you won't regret it.
Amy Walton is super helpful, I took her ENGL 150 class as an arranged class but she was always available to talk to and help out on assignments and provide feedback.

I took the online version of ENGL 220 but at the testing centers it was called LING 220 (?) The diagramming assignments were a little excessive - Very time consuming. Make sure you take good notes from the beginning because the class only gets harder. You're only graded on participation and the 5 exams, so one bad exam can really screw your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: How can you NOT like Amy?! She has so much energy (which I loved). Sad I can't take her again.

Amy's an exceptionally dedicated, kind, and caring professor. She genuinely wants the best for her students by providing them with extra practice, study sessions, and feedback. The course can be challenging at times, but if you stay on top of the game you'll be fine! If you ever have any questions, Amy will usually respond less than 24 hours.
Amy is a gem. The class isn't hard; it's the most objective English class you'll take, which is why I liked it. Would take again!!!

Excellent in every aspect. Cares about the material and her students, great at teaching the information, great feedback. Decent sense of humor (It is that English teacher sense of humor). Take if you can.
Amy is extremely caring and understanding. Her classes are great and I learned a lot in them, more than any other prof at ISU. Be sure to read assignment sheets thoroughly. Highly recommend.

Amy loves her job and it's obvious. The class has long homework assignments almost daily, but I didn't find them too hard. Amy is always available to help and she explains things in a way that makes it really easy to understand! I found the tests and the "Major Assignments" to be pretty easy. You NEED the textbooks because you write in them!

Amy is a great professor and she values student feedback. She is funny and outgoing and a great personality. I really enjoyed 220. The class itself is kind of difficult, but Amy encourages coming to office hours and "grammar parties" to get extra help.
she is amazing!

Amy is so awesome, and it's clear she's passionate about music. She seems to really enjoy teaching and is very attentive. The class is easy, and you get points just for showing up! 10/10 would recommend.

There are lecture quizzes every day, but they're relatively easy and can mostly be completed online. Occasionally, there are a few questions that require you to be there in person, but not often. You also have to write four handwritten pages in total, but it's only one page about the music events you attended throughout the semester.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Amy is amazing. Her lectures are very entertaining, and she cares about all of her students. Be sure to attend class to receive participation points. Take Music 102 with her!!!!
Her lectures are very entertaining
Super easy but you have to go to class.

It is a good class whether you know much about music. She is very entertaining and makes the class fun. You are graded on in-class quizzes, textbook quizzes, and concert papers. reviews.comment: Lots of writing in exams, make sure you understand the content and can make connections. There are weekly reading assignments I'd recommend doing if you want to get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I am taking this class online, and it is one of the most organized online classes I have taken while at ISU.  The lectures are interesting.  Quiz every week, three critical thinking papers per semester, three tests. LOTS of  reading. She is clearly passionate about this subject.  I respect her a lot.  Great class.  Lots of work, but great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took the online portion of this class, and although there were lots of videos to watch from her lecture online, it was really interesting. I learned a lot about women's history in this class. You really have to watch her lectures and watch the videos in order to do good on the quizzes. She also gives you the questions on the exam before taking it
Nice professor, lectures kind of boring, knowledgeable, cares about her area of expertise, beware of pop quizzes, lots and lots of reading, tests aren't too hard if you stay on top of reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not only do you have to listen to her give online lectures for 3 hours, but then you have to read 100 pages out of a textbook, take an online quiz and write a 2 page essay every week. Not to mention the tests are all short and long answer questions.

Online class was incredibly inconsistent. Provides no grading scale in syllabus. Essay exams may focus on obscure topics that have only been covered on one slide. Quiz, essay, and discussion due each week.. Although they are easier points than the exams. Unless you need this class, stay away.

I'm interested in the topic.  Professor Bix's lectures are interesting.  She gave out a study guide before the test, but it was just a long list of all the required readings and lecture topics.  I would recommend with some reservations.
she was very long winded and insisted that we only lecture. It was a long semester
She took a topic that I had no interest in, and she made it very interesting.  I learned a lot more from the class than I was expecting, and her demeanor was pleasant.

Very passionate about her topic, regularly dances and snaps her fingers around the lecture hall during sound and movie clips. Her TA grades very fairly. Buy the textbooks or you'll struggle with the weekly papers. Her voice is very high pitched but you'll get used to it. Solid professor overall.

She is a great lecturer. Keeps lecture interesting with pictures and video and song clips. When she dances it makes my day! She loves her job, TA grades fair. Reading amount is INSANE. Learn how to skim. Weekly papers, quizes are basically free points. Essay exams. Notes collected so you ahve to attend class.Fun and fairly easy class!

This teacher was nice to my face, and rude to me in e-mails when I had a question about my grade. She was completely unhelpful. The TA lost 3 of my papers and I had to redo them because they blamed me for it. Don't take a class with Bix.
She grades fairly and makes class interesting. She can repeat herself sometimes. The amount of reading required is insane, I couldn't keep up with it because I'm not good at skimming.

Her voice is somewhat reminiscent of a pubescent boy.  If you can handle the voice, however, this course is great.  Essay questions on the test and half is take-home.  Just pay attention in class and you'll do pretty well.  She has in-class quizzes, but they're just to make sure you come.

Interesting topic. Heavy use of powerpoints, great if you bring your laptop. Tests are essay and a take-home. In class quizzes are basically attendance. Don't expect to make it past the 1960's, if that. Quite a bit of reading, but can skim and form a decent essay.

Really interesting class. I was getting A's on all take home tests and pop quizzes but somehow ended up with a B+? There's a huge research paper (18-25pgs). All in all it's one class from ISU that I'll never forget.
She was a great teacher, but her TA graded harder than she did on the tests! She needs to train her TA's better on how to grade.

This was not an easy class, but it was very fulfilling and interesting. 2 take home tests, all essay (5-8pg), and final (18-25pgs). If you participate in discussion and do the reading (skim, b/c there is alot) you can formulate a pretty good essay. This class has made me a better writer, and better versed in medicine and women's issues.
WAY WAY WAY TOO MUCH CRAMMED IN ONE COURSE!!
Great class- hope they offer it again and I hope that Amy teaches it. She's extrememly smart and a great teacher.

"Going once, twice, ok cool" be prepaired to hear that A LOT!!!! Class is very hard, lots of reading, tests are all essay w/ take home part thats 5-8 pages, and she isn't the best at actually teaching-leaves it up to the TA's

It was okay, sometimes she could have better with the lectures, sometimes I felt like they were not helpful just going through it while not explaining. Stat 226 was way easier IMO. Her labs were kind of difficult but if you pay close enough attention you should be okay.
Test heavy class, sometimes over simplifies some concepts and makes them more confusing but she's a good instructor.
3 Exams: 80% of the grade. No feedback. Does not care one bit. The review material is nothing like the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She explains things in super complicated ways and they could be simplified way more it is really misleading.

Gives good lectures that cover the material thoroughly enough that there really isn't a reason to not make an A. Gives students every resource possible to be successful without creating grade inflation. I'm not sure she cares much about the students as individuals, but she will make sure you're successful in her course.

Prof Peterson was an amazing professor in my opinion. She always answered my questions well and was always there to help out when needed. Personally I did better on Stat 326 compared to 226, and I think her teaching played a great part in that

The class makes absolutely no sense. The professor is nice, but the lecture material is awful. If you don't have friends to work on stuff with, you're not going to do well. The review sessions have the wrong answers sometimes. I even tried getting a tutor, and the tutor couldn't even help me get the problems right.

326 is hard; it is very time-consuming and can be very confusing. Lectures are hard to learn from, but she posts videos going over every slide. Make friends in this class to help you through assignments.

Good Prof, tough class. I enjoy math/logic classes; however, exams were worth 66+% w/o the EC from 226. Prepare to work hard and spend oodles of time. Prof responds well but isn't very helpful in her responses. Labs, HW, lectures, and exams appear to be done by different people, and no one ever checks with one another. "A" student, 1st B+ ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: STAT326 is a difficult class. Some concepts are in-depth and take a lot of time. As others have said, the labs can be difficult and time-consuming, but the resources to get them done are all there. The exams are also somewhat difficult and need to be prepared for. However, I do think that she has the class set up well, especially for the content.

She gives all the needed materials to succeed. There are a lot of study resources and if you study hard then you should be able to do well in this class. She also allows 4 pages of notes for tests which is really helpful. It can be easy to get confused so don't fall behind on the material. I also recommend the online section, as it saves time.

She does an amazing job teaching statistics and, for someone that understands math well, it makes the class that much easier. It was kind of daunting to see how the exams were weighted, but of the four exams, one is dropped. Acing the first exam and doing well on the second essentially guarantee that you won't need to take the final.

Anna is a great professor. Her lectures taught a lot and had many examples during lectures to make sure you understood the material. There isn't a lot to study for the exams besides the extra homework. She had her TA teach sometimes, and that is where it got confusing because she wasn't the best

Exam Heavy course. Lectures don't make a ton of sense and don't really coordinate to labs, homework, and especially exams. Go to all your labs and do the homework. Go to SI, I can't stress enough. Even if you got the lab done, go to the SI to learn the material and ask questions. Easily the hardest corse I've taken at ISU.

Professor Peterson is good; she provided practice exams and was responsive to emails. She taught the material pretty well and did many practice problems during lectures. She posted videos of the material on Canvas as well (more condensed than class lectures). STAT 326 is a tough course, so prepare to practice the material and take thorough notes.
Definitely could've made the material more correlate to the exams and labs.  Material taught was way easier and didn't help me when it came to taking exams on my own and/ or working on the labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be ready to do bad. This class is by far the worst class I've had to take. Lectures make zero sense and show you very little about how to do the labs and exams. Labs are impossible to get 100% unless you work with multiple people. Practice exams are nothing like the exams. Exams are impossible to prepare for. Good luck

This is the worst class I have ever taken at Iowa State. Did I go to lectures? No.I sure tried to go but every time I went the content made 0 sense and she just rambled. Lecture stuff was not at all relevant. She's a nice lady and one of the only stats profs. able to understand. Exams are way harder than practice exams class sucks all I got to say.

This class is extremely confusing as it seems like everyone goes into the exams not knowing one anything and somehow still get B's / C's on them idk how. She doesn't know how to teach but instead uses a PowerPoint (that isn't in order) to briefly goes over them.

If you did well in STAT 226, you should be fine for this class. But be ready to teach yourself a lot of material. The exams were confusing and were always set up to be more difficult than the labs and practice exams. Overall, Prof Anna is nice, but I felt the lectures did not prepare me well for the exams.

This class is brutal. Lectures are maybe 25% relevant to examples and things on the actual exam. Going to lectures and paying attention is nearly impossible. Labs are terrible because when you ask your TA's questions it is never a direct answer, half the time you ask them a question they try and play mind games making you even more confused.

Tests are weighted heavily and there's so much content and no way to know what's on the test. Lectures and labs often didn't pertain to the few things tested on, so you'll either do really well if you're good at what's on the test or you're screwed. Boring lectures and notes are hard to follow and don't help if you look back on them to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely boring professor for STAT 326. Often times the lectures do not pertain to what shows up on the exams. Labs are extremely extremely difficult to complete in timely manner and have minimal questions. Exams are heavily weighted and worth 60% of you grade. Exams are extremely difficult. Locks final grade so you can't even see until accessplus
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her for stats 326. Lectures were extremely boring and spent way too much on stuff that wasn't going to be on the exams. Labs were helpful to learn material but the TA's weren't the best. All in all, the class wasn't too difficult but just extremely boring.
Lectures are super boring but necessary to do well on tests.

Professor Peterson is super smart and knows what she's talking about. If you need help, she's really good at explaining things. She gave the option to go to in-person lectures or watch the online lectures, so it was nice to have the flexibility. If you practice the problems throughout the semester and ask questions, the class isn't difficult.

This was one of the toughest courses I've taken so far in college. She was a good professor but went through the material very fast. If you have to take this course, I'd recommend you take it in person with her. The grade was mostly based on exams which were very tough. Group projects every week. Good professor but difficult course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard all around. She's good at teaching in comparison to other professors, but I'd highly recommend a tutor regardless. The labs are hardly like what will be on the exam, but will give you some practice. You can't skip notes or you'll be thoroughly confused. Get a good study group and communicate with lab partners.

Good lectures, just not enough relevant content. Feels like when you get to the lab, the questions are completely in left field. Why use JMP when you don't have to use it on exams, excel would be more useful for the business world. Anna is a great professor though and will help outside of class. Get a tutor early if you think you might struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Peterson did a pretty good job of teaching this stats class. She went through lots of review problems, let us submit review questions before exams, and was quick to respond when emailed. Sometimes sped through the notes a bit to fast, but there was online recorded lectures to watch after class as well.

Ive taken this class twice, the first time I took it online and was only able to learn off of 5-10 videos that were 1-5 minutes in length. In-person is just as difficult because she rushes to solve problems and struggles to allow students to understand the content.

I felt this class was pretty easy if you can follow basic rules. There are group labs that can be more challenging, but with a group very doable. I also found the homework pretty easy. The exams were very similar to homework and easy sample test questions. Would recommend!

This is a very hard class, but it is manageable if you reach out with questions and do all the labs and homework. The TA's aren't very helpful, so reach out to professor Peterson if you have any questions. I would recommend this professor, she's helpful and the way the class is structured helped me learn.

If you have a question, it's best to reach out to Prof. Peterson instead of her TAs. They don't answer your actual question. Make sure that you do well on the earlier exams and assignments, because the later ones are very hard. Start early on your Labs. Don't bother looking through the practice exams; they are pretty different from the real exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you thought stat 226 was tough, get ready. 75% of grade is based off exams like 226 except the practice exams are NOTHING like the real exam. With Covid there are no SI sessions. I needed that in this class to save myself. I have a F going into the final at 58% because I bombed one exam. Best 2 exams averaged for a 4th exam score, no curve.
I dont really like this class. I feel the class just copy and paste from the previous year. The video quality is very bad. And her tone is very very very boring. VERY BORING VERY DISCONNECTED
