This class is extremely difficult and if I didnt have Dr Peterson as a prof I probably would've failed the class. Go to her office hours she is always willing to help and walk you through problems. This class is so hard but if you utilize her office hours and the TA office hours it can be done.

This class is tough. You have to put in a lot of effort in studying for the tests in this class. Lectures were hard to follow and didn't make much sense. Lab is where you can learn, but mostly you need to figure it out on your own. Much harder than Stat 226 was, get ready to study hard.

Dr. Peterson is a good professor. Take notes in class, understand the slides, and most importantly review practice exams and you will be fine. I found the labs to be interesting for the most part. Most of the exam problems were variations of examples in the practice exams or in-class examples.

Lecture goes by fast, and her writing is very difficult to read due to how fast she writes and her penmanship. However, the lecture material is very important for lab, which is where you really will learn the content. Try to get a good group for lab; it will make this class much more doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Anna is really hard to understand in class and writes super small so I suggest sitting in the front. Go to labs because they are where you learn most of the content on the exams.
Stats is hard in general, and Anna does a decent job with lectures. The tests are difficult and graded tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's really nice, and for someone that understands statistics, she'll be a perfectly fine professor, but she might not be the best if you struggle with math concepts since her lectures tend to be pretty fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: STAT 326 is pretty easy if you did well in 226. The lectures are somewhat boring and she writes a bit too fast but she's easy to understand and knows what she's talking about. The labs are helpful to learn the material better. Overall, she's a solid teacher and it's not a hard class, it was probably one of my easier classes this semester.
Put in the time and you will do fine. Labs help but be active. Dr. Anna will respond to emails and is easy to meet with outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson is one of the nicest professors on Iowa State's campus. She is clearly very intelligent, but often has trouble conveying the material in a lecture setting due to her speed. This is a tough course and it requires more than your average effort. I would recommend going to office hours regularly nail down the material. Exams are 65%.

First off, this was a tough class. Homework was easy points each week (like 8 multiple choice questions) and there was a 2 hour lab each week as well. Lab wasn't too bad because you could work with a group. Lectures were awful - taught myself almost all the material. Would be nice to have in-class worksheets. Go over practice exams well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: basically, this is a teach your self-class. She explains some items but it is important to read the notes before class. Also, a lot of groups participating in class.
The lecture seemed to drag on and on and on. I feel like I get more out of the team activities than her lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I liked her. I took STAT 326, which is a rather difficult class. She assigned lots of homework, but so does every other professor in the world. Has good study resources for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't buy the book. If you pay attention, Dr. Peterson will tell you everything you need to know. Actual exams are super similar to practice exams. As long as you understand the practice exams, you'll be just fine. There are a bunch of TAs for lab, but I had Dr. Peterson. I would recommend her if you can get into her lab (groups assigned randomly)

This class is tough, you have to actually watch the video and take notes and what you don't understand in the video go in and ask her. The TA I had wasn't that good so I go to Dr Peterson. keep activities you do in class and look over after class and study those for exams. The videos online is dry but really that is the only source of info you get

This class was hard if you can't figure out statistics on your own.  Teacher would give in class activities but never actually went over the answers to anything.  Would give her lectures online and have the majority of the class just be team exercises.  Didn't really help me in learning the material...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This course was okay. The team based learning actually wasnt too bad. If Dr. Peterson lectures try to stay awake, its so boring. The labs are kind of fun, I never minded going. There is no homework. This entire class was average, but I do feel like I learned some valuable statistical tools from it. I rate this course higher than I rate Dr. Peterson
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's nice and tries her best to be helpful. She posts lecture slides with a voice over. I absolutely can't stand her boring, unenthusiastic voice over for the slides. Lectures are almost completely useless, you just attend so you help your team with the team activity that you have every class.
Honestly a great teacher. Go to class and actually pay attention. The labs will be super easy then and the tests even easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The class was fine and not as hard as I had envisioned. If you did well in Stat 226, this class is about the same in difficulty. She gives you old practice exams which were similar to the exam itself. Having not really paid attention in lecture (very boring) I scored an A on the exam. However, weekly labs suck and can be challenging sometimes.
The class itself was very boring in my opinion but it wasn't that hard and the teacher really wasn't that bad. I hardly tried and skipped a couple labs and am probably going to get an A in it.
Barely helpful. Always required to use JMP to do analysis, boring lectures.

Honestly, I don't understand why this Prof gets a bad rap. Go to lecture, study, and visit office hours and you will get results. Anyone who complains otherwise is lacking in at least one of these three categories. Peterson provides plenty of material to prepare you for exams; from personal experience is very approachable and wants to help.
You have to fill in notes to understand concepts, she is really smart and nice but lectures can be really advanced. The tests are also extremely hard.
Single hardest class I've ever taken.

Professor Peterson seemed like she was really smart with statistics however I never understood a word she said. I even asked her for help one-on-one, thinking that my lack of understanding came from a big lecture, however it was equally if not more confusing. I had to teach myself how to do everything in order to pass this class.

Dr. Peterson is a good professor she seemed to know a lot about Stat 326. The labs are nothing like he lectures she gives in class. I would really recommend you to attend every class because the material adds up. 2 tests, labs, and the final test are each worth 25% of your total grade. My TA was not so helpful during lab. Don't need text book.
Wasn't a bad professor. Lectures were boring and read straight from the slides. Class attendance not mandatory. Toughest part of the class were labs which were done with minimal TA assistance.

Shes a good teacher. Its a stats class what do you expect?! Lectures are done on the projector over slides from the book company I assume. Have to go to class to learn the material and add stuff to the notes that she writes and examples.

I am surprised by the comments here.  She really wants her students to succeed.  Go talk to her 1 on 1 in office hours if any of the material doesn't make sense in class.  The problem is that the material is cumulative so you can't miss any classes. I actually thought it was students being rude sitting the back laughing during the whole class.

The TA's do all of the work (office hours, grading, teaching in labs). Go to labs because that is where I learned everything, not from her lectures.  She was kind of rude to the lecture group.  Tests were ok on difficulty. Do the labs and homework and you'll be fine. Some test ?s come from homework and labs

After reading these comments, she's not THAT bad. I skipped class half of the time and didn't study for any test, but still got a good grade because of the extreme curve. She is extremely helpful one-on-one, so don't be afraid to go to office hours. You can tell she wants her students to succeed. Overall, 3.5/5.

Horrible Professor. I wish she knew that no one understands a word she says. She knows her statistics but does not know how to effectively teach it. If you want to pass this class, you need a tutor, cause you'll understand the tutor better than her. Useless, useless, useless!
She tried to over explain and re-explain in different, more complicated, ways which made her confusing.
Seriously awful. She knows her statistic information but she is a very poor instructor and should have persued a different field. Avoid at all costs.

If you want to pass this class, attend every class. The tests are extremely hard, the labs suck, and the homework(optional) is time consumming. Her tests are nothing like what you do in the labs, and seem to come out of left feild. So, if you haven't been to class, you will fail. Also, don't buy the book, you don't use it.
Hard exams, she explained the material very well, you need to attend every class to do well in this class

She is awful.  I repeat. AWFUL.  If you have to take this class, avoid avoid avoid.  It might as well be an online course, all she does is read slides and copy notes from her own notes.  She fears anyone asking a question.  Tests are extremely challenging.  DO NOT BUY THE BOOK.  One of the worst instructors I've ever had.

If you need a U.S. Cultures and Communities course, take this one. There are typically weekly or bi-weekly tophat reading assignments, but you can do them all at once and not have to worry about it. I finished this course with an 110% due to extra credit. No exams either. Professor Popillion cares a lot too. I highly recommend!

Great class if you want to get your electives out of the way, but you can still put in the effort to learn a lot about the subject. Taking it online is very much a case of getting out of it as much as you put in.
An extremely kind woman who is very good at making something extremely uncomfortable comfortable.

Dr. Popillion is a great professor. There are no exams in this class, rather there are weekly homework assignments through the textbook. There were also 2 discussion posts in total. She is very caring and understands if you need to miss class for any reason. She also allows 6 classes to be missed throughout the semester. Very easy class!
Easy A, ended with a 104%, lots of extra credit opportunities, provides good feedback on assignments, interesting course would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amy is a great professor and this is a good class for an easy A

I've had this professor for many classes and she truly cares about her students. Her lectures are engaging and she's really funny. I've taken both online and in person courses through her and I would highly recommend taking in person classes so you can listen to her lecture.

She is very involved w/ the class and in responding to emails. Participation is graded and done using a Top Hat code. Participation within the weekly activities that are planned is important and a large chunk of grade. Short(er) writing assignments every other week also graded. No midterm, no final. She is very fun and inclusive.

She is super nice and relatable, especially taking into account she's teaching a human sexuality class. You get 6 classes you can skip the whole semester without affecting your grade/participation which is nice. She respects you and your time, while also acknowledging that we are young adults who still laugh at dirty jokes! 100% recommend taking!

Just took the class for a gen ed. The content of this class is very in depth so be prepared. No tests/exams, just 2 assignments per week with the occasional 1 page essay. The class is very easy and is layed out very straightforward. Highly recommend taking for an easy gen ed.
I absolutely loved having her as a professor and she's flexible as long as you communicate with her.

HDFS 276 was a wild class that I highly recommend taking. Professor Popillion is great, and I learned a ton from both lectures and the textbook. This class is really easy, you just have to read the textbook and answer some questions along with a few assignments through out the semester that are pretty simple.

This was a very fun class to take and Amy is very knowledgeable on these topics. While some of the material may be weird to read about, she always gave warnings before any sensitive topics. She also has everything on Canvas set up in an easy, accessible way so you know exactly what's expected of you. Easy assignments, just try and you will do good.
Great professor with a super easy class. She makes students know that she cares, and she will help if you reach out.

Extremely kind and cares about your overall grade. Helps you out with your grades and scoring if you reach out about a concern. If you show you care, she will help you out. Extremely personable and sympathetic.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took this class online and is very well set up. I learned a lot through the lecture slides posted and the textbook. There was no final for this class, it was just a 30 question quiz per unit and they were very guided and easy. There are also many discussions/extra credit opportunities that will boost your grade up as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I've taken. Dr. Popillion is incredible. She is passionate about what she teaches and that shines through her lectures.

She is very into class participation, so be ready for that. Some of the things she said in defense of some types of abusers made me uncomfortable, and she would sometimes speak about topics that she had no personal experience in as if she was an expert. These were deal breakers for me, but otherwise, she was an okay prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Participation was taken through TopHat, but she has multiple ways you can get points back if you miss a lot of classes. No final, easy grader focused more on what you learned versus your grade, so she gave points easily. One of the kindest teachers, and the class was super fun. I wanted to read the textbook, which says a lot.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Super knowledgeable and you will learn a lot in her courses. She should honestly write a book!
Super interesting lectures, not a lot of work.

Professor Popillion is a good professor. The class is weird and some of the topics make you uncomfortable for she does the best she can to try and make everyone feel welcomed. Exams are open note and book, take on your own time, with no camera. Also, lots of extra credit that is pretty simple. Attendance is taken through TopHat at the end of class.
Loved the class, great class for gen ed!!!! Professor Popillion was amazing
Dr. Amy is a fun professor with a lot of stories in class

literally the best. no exams, only quizzes that are open note open book and you have about a week to complete, and can come back to it after starting. she makes the class easy so you actually can learn and i think this is super effective. tophat attendance is takem. shes also super chill and creates a very comfortable environment
She's the BEST! Gracious grading policy, great material that makes sense, things I actually LEARNED & not just memorized. Never panicked. I wish she wrote the rule book for all professors to follow!

This may be only my first semester at ISU, but this woman is the best professor/teacher I have ever had. She gives you feedback and explains how you can be better. Holds interesting lectures and gives you so many extra credit opportunities that you can pass with flying colors. She is so friendly and easy to contact. Amy is the best!

She is the best. So approachable and easy to connect with. Very empathetic and seems to be in-touch with the struggles college students face. Provides useful real-life resources for mental health and sexuality. Never skipped class because I loved going so much. She makes you think hard without making the class too hard. Amy, youre the best.

Very easy class. Amy teaches the class in a very interesting manner and makes topics easy to understand. She gives a lot of lee way in grading so if you miss any assignments your grade will still be fine.
The best professor in ISU. Period.
Only two test that she gives study guides for. Not to many assignments and they are pretty easy. Attendance is required and is worth a good amount of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best class at Iowa State. Easy A. You learn about interesting things. That's all you need to know.
She is an amazing professor that teaches really interesting material. Would highly recommend taking this course

Amy is a great professor in that she is personable and you will learn not only about her, but also her husband and kids just by going to class. She is also very clear about grading and as long as you pay attention in class you should pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: easy, interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Amy is hands down one of the most approachable people i've ever met. Her lectures are very helpful, as well as very enjoyable. She makes class interactive, and also very personal. She really wants her students to succeed, and will always do what she can to help. I really enjoyed the class, and would definitely love to have a class with her again.
Awesome

Professor Popillion is my QUEEN. Attendance is required each period but Amy did a great job picking out the most relevant material. The class period goes quickly and you can chill on your computer if you sit on the side of the lecture hall. This class should honestly be required for all students because the relevant content and the lax grading.

Dr. Popillion was an amazing professor. She is so genuine and truly funny. Her class was very interesting and she would have guest speakers sometimes which was a real treat. There are only two tests in her class, but they cover a lot of material. She maps out study guides and she has quizzes every week that help for the test.
Very respectful and easy to talk to. Great professor for engineering trying for U.S. Diversity credits
Mrs. Popillion is a cool professor and shares information from her personal life to contribute to the class. The class is easy and has plenty of extra credit if you somehow struggle in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. She incorporates her own life into her lectures to make it more relatable. She makes a study guide for every exam and overs a ton of extra credit. One of my favorite professors at ISU.
She is a great professor! She tells you how things are in the real world instead of sugar coating it. I would recommend her 100%.
Lots of extra credit opportunities

Easy class and interesting as well. I would for sure take it with her. There are weekly quizzes but you can find the answers pretty easily through notes and stuff. Tests are exactly like the study guides and she offers quite a bit of extra credit. As long as you do the stuff you will pass no doubt.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Amy is not just a phenomenal teacher, but a phenomenal person. I learned so much in her class, I feel like this should be a required course for all students. This was my favorite class all year because the topics are interesting and very relevant and important to everyone's lives. Don't hesitate to take this class!

really interesting class, amy was a good speaker and really made all topics relevant. exams are super easy as she gives you a study guide with everything on it a week before. top hat is important and attendance is taken every class. its pretty easy to get a good grade in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not sure who wrote that you never know what will be on exams, as the study guide literally lays out what will be on the exam exactly. Amy was great and made it super easy to get a good grade! Definitely take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Classes and homework are super easy, however, you never know what will be on the exams. The class is still an easy A though! Get ready to be pushed out of your comfort zone!

One of the best professors I've had so far. She is very engaging and really cares for her students. She is super funny, gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, makes study guides that will help you ace the test, and brings entertaining speakers for class. 3 writing assignments are given in the class but they are not too difficult. Take the class

Amy is literally one of the best professors I have had at Iowa State. She is caring and passionate about helping students. You will leave her class knowing more about yourself. She gives study guides for all of her exams, and as long as you do them you should ace the exam. Honestly, I would take the class all over again just because I enjoyed her.

Dr. Popillion is one of the sweetest, most caring instructors I have ever come across in my time as an undergraduate student. If I had the time, I would take ALL of her classes. She listens to her students and actually tries to help them whenever they might come across an issue, whether it be personal or educational. You are not a number to her.

Human Sexuality was so interesting and enjoyable. Amy makes lectures fun and light, but knows a lot.  There are 3 tests that are all multiple choice and she gives a study guide with exactly what's on the test.  Top Hat attendance is graded and there are weekly online quizzes that are really easy, plus 3 writing assignments. Fun, easy, interesting!

This class is a great class to fulfill a diversity credit and also learn a lot about yourself. Amy always makes the lectures engaging and encourages participation. If you don't want to buy the text book there are ways around that (use the internet). The 3 essays you have to write can make you learn a lot about yourself if you take them seriously.

You learn a lot. She is very down to Earth teacher and truly cares bout her classes. Lectures are usually full every class period. If you do the study guides you will pass the class. Go to class because you get extra credit at the end for attendance. Speak up in class too.

She cares about all of her students and explains everything really well. She makes an already interesting class so much more interesting by keeping you engaged and makes things interactive. One of my favorite classes for sure.

She is very open and helpful for any chapter we go over. Her lectures are super interesting and makes class more fun. You have to buy Top Hat which cost 50 dollars  but the questions and attendance code gives you extra points. I would definitely recommend her as an instructor.

She was a very clear and understanding professor. She told you exactly what to expect on exams. If you show up to class most of the time, and are willing to put in 30-45 minutes outside of class a week on average, you'll easily get an A.

The course content is pretty interesting. Amy is a great teacher! Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does take In-Class points randomly throughout the semester. I didn't find the tests too hard. There's a few papers but they weren't too difficult either.

Amy is very nice and always understanding of students. She is willing to help anyone and is a good professor and person overall.  Pay attention and do some light reading and you will get a B or above.

Although this class is not for the faint-hearted, I would hands down vote Amy as the best professor that I have had in my college experience. This class really opened my eyes to sex and gender, as well as numerous other factors that we judge others on. The papers may seem scary, but they're really just self-reflections. Good luck!
If you put effort, you will get an A. Super interesting and she makes it really fun to learn about.
Do the study guides, this is the best way to study. Easy course and great professor! The class was one of the best classes that I've ever taken here at ISU.

Her tests were  a bit difficult and one of my harder courses during the semester. But I had a problem understanding something so I emailed her and right away she clarified it. She went off of the text book a lot which I think is good for the type of class she is teaching her guest speakers are informative

Dr. Popillion was an awesome teacher and I am so glad that I had her for this class. She works with you as long as you ask her questions and do your work.  You can also tell that she wants to see you succeed in her class. She also works hard as a professor and commits completely.
If you fill out the study guides then you'll ace the test. The quizzes are easy and weekly thru blackboard. Don't procrastinate on assignments. But overall easy class if you put some effort in.

Dr. Popillion is an amazing teacher.  Her tests are pretty much word for word what her study guides say.  She will respond to emails very quickly and you can usually reach her late into the evening.  Exams are easy as long as you go to class and somewhat listen.
Easy class if you read the book and do the reflections, also there is group work on some days and clicker points. NO EXAMS - NO FINAL.

Dr. Popillion is one of the most incredible professors I've ever had. I took HDFS 276 for my US Diversity and was glad i did. She teaches the class with superb clarity and is always openpatient to talk to us about anything. She sends out a study guide question sheet that, if you answer it all and study it well you can ace the tests. Wonderful lady

This class was beyond easy. There are clicker questions for attendance points, and each week you write a reflection over a chapter in the book. There aren't any tests and there isn't a final -- just a couple of papers and a couple of projects. You'll have to go to the Ames Public Library to check out children's books for the projects.
Amazing professor
Teaches in a great, interactive style. Encouraged to participate, but not required. She's awesome!

Does not accurately provide information during lecture. Questions on test are lazy and vague. The study guide for the same test often does not match up concepts. Demands that proper grammar and spelling is used in the small writing assignments, but then fails to do so in her assignment instructions. Rarely uses logic. Honestly the worst I've had.
Very nice professor. The class is great just don't procrastinate on projects!
Excellent teacher, she always made class interesting.

Most of the material is common sense, but going to class is interesting. Online quizzes once a week, all the answers come straight from the textbook and the exams come straight from the reviews. Excellent class

I had her for human sexuality and it was probably the best class I've ever taken. Took it to get my US diversity credit for engineering. Lectures are very interesting. Easy to get an A-, but you have to work for a solid A. Review the study guide before tests and read the book. Extra credit is pretty easy. Recommend taking this class.

Amy is a great  teacher who is very passionate about the content she teaches. She is very helpful and always encouraging students to meet their potential. I wouldn't consider her an easy grader- but if you put effort into your assignments and make an effort to learn and keep an open mind, you will do well.
Pretty easy class, kind of interesting. Some days were pretty boring.

This class was interesting, but not as easy as people say.  The tests are the study guide but the online quizzes are from the book and I would find the answer in the book and it would be wrong.  She grades the paper really hard, but she is a really good teacher.  Easy A or A- class, but it is more work than I had thought
Super easy and interesting! Tests are exactly what she gives you on the study guide-- Easy A!
Very nice
She is a helpful teacher.The class with her will be easier compared to the other sections
She is Amazing!
Amy always made class interesting and had a very warm and nurturing style of teaching. She is also very knowledgeable and helpful.
NO COMMENT
Amy is wonderful! She genuinely cares about her students and creates an engaging learning environment!

Amy is awesome! She loves teaching and loves helping out her students. It is not required to go to class but you will want to because the topic is so interesting. Plenty of extra credit offered - no reason to not get an A and have fun and learn a lot in the process!! My favorite prof at ISU

Easy topic and class work. Does in class points which is annoying. She will go on random tangents and **** out the class for random things. Gives LOTS of extra credit. The class is very focused on education majors which I am not so it got bland at times..
Great professor.  Made class fun and interesting.  Relates well to students and is very easy to talk to and responsive to questions.  all around a great course and prof.  she's cute too.

This was a pretty easy class. All of the quizzes are in order from the book which is a great way to earn easy points. Tests are word for word from the NOTES. The professor is helpful, but sometimes has a rude attitude.

Amy is an amazing professor! She loves the subject area & her excitement about being in class in contagious. She's also very accommodating and will help you out in any way she can. There's a lot of EC for going to lectures. Overall this class was made my favorite ever at ISU because of Amy. She's awesome! Take this class!! You'll learn and have fun

Amy is an Awesome professor. Se graded extremely fair. I thought I was going to fail this course, but for my surprise she curved grades and saved me. Overall I talked to her very often, as she is EXTREMELY friendly
No Comments

The quizzes are given over just the text before it is discussed in classs which makes it seem easy and pointless; The grant and research paper portion makes up for the easiness and gives the class some point. I really enjoyed the prof as she was very fair in grading the group projects when my group didnt contribute much of anything.
No Comments
The content of this class makes it hard to stay interested.  She gives quizes before the material is discussed in class which can be frustrating.
loved this class, loved the prof!
The class content is very interesting, and she just helps it along.
No Comments
great professor!
Very informative lectures- pay attention, and you will do well on exams. By far one of the best professors I have had.

awesome class and awesome professor. somerville is very likable and makes good connections with students. class is SUPER interesting if youre into that stuff.very lecture heavy so make sure you take notes on like everything because they WILL be used in class and lab.

Loved this class! Prof Somerville is a great lecturer and I found the material very interesting. Attendance in labs are required. Exams are multiple choice and easy as long as you pay attention to the lectures and study. I would not recommend this class if you're not interested in the subject.

Lectures and labs are required. The lecture is led by the teacher, TA leads the lab. YOU HAVE TO TAKE NOTES IN THE LECTURE! Very note heavy. Lots of homework in the labs, but doable if you pay attention. Tests are awful, average was about 60 - 70% across all the students. The teacher is a very nice, cool dude, but the lectures are really boring.

He is very passionate about his class, so passionate enough to have a no electronics rule so that he knows you are paying attention. Quizzes every week that he is a little too picky on your wording of answers, but he gives you several sample questions before hand that he'll pull from to make the quiz, and all the answers come from the slides

Great professor, very passionate and makes concepts easy to follow. He's helpful and clearly cares about teaching. Tough grader with high expectations, but everything is fair. Weekly quizzes, but you'll the questions beforehand. You'll learn a lot if you put in the effort. No electronics policy

He grades everything very honestly and objectively, it can be tough to get 100 percent on the quizzes, but you get so many drops it honestly doesn't matter if you are diligent. Most things are graded anonymously, and he is very committed to integrity. He really knew what he was doing, and this was one of my favorite courses that I have taken.

His lectures are very interesting and engaging. He makes every concept entertaining and I look forward to class every day. He is a little knit picky with grading and finds small areas to take points off. Pretty much everything is handwritten, so if you hate writing, I wouldn't recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes are each worth ~7% of your grade. Have to do what he calls a "test prep," which is handwriting answers to 10-12 questions before you are able to take the quiz. Test preps are worth ~3% of your grade each. The final group presentation is worth 10% of your grade. Participation and attendance are mandatory and part of your grade.
Professor Anderson made class very fun and engaging. He is a great guy and a great teacher.
If you want good grades, don't take this professor. He's an amazing teacher but the toughest grader ever. I won't recommend this professor to anyone. He's going to F your gpa up!!!
Great professor, very passionate about what he teaches so its easy to pay attention in his classes.  Attendance is mandatory and there are a lot of hand written assignments

he is very passionate about teaching and making sure you know the material. it's a unique course structure designed to retain information. very many psychological concepts, but overall things you'll need to know to be successful in the workplace. if you want to half-ass schoolwork i wouldn't suggest.

He is a good teacher who has put together a unique set of material, but he grades INCREDIBLY hard. MGMT 3710 is suppose to be one of the easiest classes in the school of businesses, but it is really difficult with Marc. He assigns weekly study guides that take hours to complete that correspond with weekly quizzes which he grades intensely.

Marc Anderson was one of the better instructors I have taken at Iowa State. While he is a stickler for grading with the quizzes, he was pretty fair. Lectures are extremely informative due to his use of clips to demonstrate concepts. Assuming there's inclement weather, do not expect him to cancel classes if the University does not.

One of the best professors I have ever came across. His lectures are very insightful, well prepared, and he teaches very well with passion. I have retained most of what he taught because of his style of teaching. His weekly quizzes are helpful and very doable. His short videos in class are great addition to learning.
Overall great prefessor
This class is probably my favorite class I have taken so far. Engaging lectures, shows movie clips as examples and gets his message across clearly. I would highly recommend this course.

He had a quiz every Friday that was handwritten, and before that, you had to write the equivalent of a paper, and you had to take about 14 of these. To be fair, you did get around 4 drops, but even if you dropped the quiz, you had to still fill out the paper. Overall just an incredibly annoying class
Weekly quizzes and quiz preparations graded pretty tough. Need to attend almost every class and be ready to listen in class during lectures
Great professor! Lectures were insightful, cares about his students. Weekly quizzes...he grades them tough, so make sure you know your stuff.

Greatest teacher I have ever had. Lectures were amazing and mandatory. There was a lot of quizzes, but you are informed of what will be on them before hand, your grade on them is largely dependent on the effort you put into preparing them. Absolutely recommend this class.
I have ADHD and I can pay attention to this guy's lectures without taking my medication. Really good use of technology to help convey the information and reinforce understanding.
Great inspirational teacher who really cares about his students success.

Professor Anderson is really great! His lectures are interesting and his assignments/quizzes were pretty standard (no tests). Be sure to do the weekly quiz prep (the same short answer questions are on quizzes). He gave us a few papers (1 or 2 pages) and those were easy (pro tip: he prefers personal examples in papers). I highly recommend his class!

No exams, but rather weekly quizzes that are essentially memorizing material taught in class. Attendance is taken and not many absences are dropped, so be wary of that. He also does quiz preps right before the quizzes, which are helpful, but choose your wording carefully because he will dock a lot of points for a small error. All in all, good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No exams but weekly quizzes with long quiz prep assignments. He is a tough grader, especially on the weekly quizzes. There was an easy group project at the end which was nice instead of a final. The lectures are good and very helpful for doing the weekly quiz prep but the quizzes are largely memorization, especially the list based questions.
The lectures were entertaining but there was 11 quizzes for the entire class that took up a good part of the grade. However having an easy group project instead of the final was nice though.

Professor Anderson was great! His lectures were entertaining as he often showed video clips that went along with the material. No exams or finals, so that was definitely a plus. 11 weekly quizzes, but only the top 8 are scored, and he gives you the questions beforehand. If you have to take MGMT371, take it with this guy.

Marc is awesome and he presents the material in a really interesting way. I really loved this class and learned a lot from the lectures. If you show up to class and prepare for the quizzes, it shouldn't be bad. He is one of the most interesting professors I've ever had.

Marc genuinely cares about his students and what they learn. Marc teaches material that matters in the real world and he makes the class fun by showing comics and movie clips. He is picky for the weekly quizzes but he gives you the questions before hand so if you prepare they are fairly easy. I would highly recommend Professor Anderson.

Lectures are interesting but it's not even necessary to show up. NO FINAL and NO EXAMS which is great. The main portion of this grade is 13 weekly short-answer quizzes. Your performance on these basically determines your grade. He's a very tough grader on them so you need to study the exact answers to questions if you want an A.

Professor Marc Anderson is a great Professor, he sets up with all the tools that you need to succeed. Through his lecture slides and his examples, he did a great job explaining all of the concepts. If you put in the time and effort for the work and attend his classes, which are very enjoyable, you should have no problem.

Marc is the best professor at Iowa State University. He truly cares about his students and helping them learn. This class is fantastic with him and I looked forward to it everyday. The assignments aren't long and are easy if you are intelligent. TBH everyone here giving him a 1 just aren't smart enough to see the value in what he does. GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved taking management 371 with Marc. He was a fantastic teacher who really cared about the individual learning of his students. His classes were super interesting and fun to go to, and he really gave you a lot of tools to be successful. This was one of my favorite classes at Iowa State.

Funny and nice guy. You take weekly quizzes, however these quizzes were very benefical to my learning. He is a very picky grader but if you put in the effort, you will do good on quizzes and assignments. No final which is a plus.

There are 11 quizzes, 8 are dropped, answer 3/4 questions in 15min, and they are out of 6 points. You take a quiz every Monday and it takes about an hour to study for it. He gives you a list of 12ish possible questions and then picks 4 to put on the test. He does grade a bit hard but amazing professor and I have never loved attending class more

Marc was the best professor I have had at Iowa State. He is so committed to his course and life time learning. As long as you pay attention in class, you will get so much out of it, including a good grade. He gives clear instructions for the quizzes and if you pay attention, giving the correct answers on quizzes is not hard. I LOVED THIS CLASS!

Professor Marc has very interesting lectures; he always made the class very interesting. However, I would say be prepared. Your grade will not just be handed to you; therefore, you must be willing to work hard. He is a very picky grader, but as long as you pay attention and study hard, you should be golden on the quizzes.
No tests, only weekly quizzes, made lectures interesting and easier to pay attention to.

This guy is great. Fun lectures, easy but challenging & rewarding assignments, all around terrific guy. One of the few classes that I genuinely looked forward to. Anderson enjoys the material and is happy to answer any questions. Also it's very possible to come from HSPM 385 buzzed af and still pass class sooooo... Just take the class, trust me.

Professor Anderson is fantastic! I learned SO much from his class. He really teaches beneficial material that you will use in the real world. No tests/quizzes but he does do weekly assignments and short answer problems that you will have to work hard to receive a good grade. I highly recommend taking his class, he is a great professor!

Dr. Anderson was a great professor! He's amazing at explaining concepts and really cares about his students. I looked forward to going to his lectures, which doesn't happen to me in many classes. There's a lot of assignments/short papers, but they're not extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You will have a lot of homework, but if you pay attention and take good notes during lectures then you will be fine. There is a big group project at the end of the class, but no exams. He is very animated so lectures are interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson was an amazing professor. Very knowledgeable and passionate about course topics. He always wanted to learn more and had great ways of applying concepts. No exams but the course has a lot of assignments. The assignments arent hard if you take good notes and stay on schedule. Lectures were always entertaining. Would 100% take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Initially I thought for sure I was going to give this prof a bad review because the grading was very tough and I didnt like how we had to hand write our quiz answers (entire pages worth). He truly cares about the course and that is why he is such a harsh grader. I learned quite a bit. Recommend if you like a challenge, pass otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Is very exclusive in his teaching. He repeatedly lacked diversity in his lectures and took no responsibility for it. He acts as he cares about his students, but never does.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really tough grader, will take 0.1 off an assignment for no major reasons
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is not as bad as the recent posts suggest. Yes, he is a difficult grader when it comes to problem sets but those are essentially quizzes to the class. Every other assignment he is a more lenient grader and I've gotten A's on papers that took me 30-45 minutes to write. There is a good amount of work but it is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the worst profs I've ever had. Makes you do so much work for a class that doesn't mean anything in life.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring. He grades incredibly hard and is beyond picky. The question sets are 36% of your grade and luckily for you theyre incredibly hard to get an 80% or better on so if you care about your GPA and grades then dont take it with this guy! Also, Ive learned absolutely nothing about management. This class is just psychology.

Your grade is almost a gamble. You do these question sets (you basically get a 0 if you dont word it exactly how he would word it) and he also randomly selects the questions he answers so basically you just hope he grades the ones youre confident with! This dude grades like we are in grad school. I would HIGHLY suggest getting a different prof.

This class should not be as hard as this professor makes it. He is so picky and will not give you a good grade unless it is the exact answer that he would've said. There is TONS of pointless homework that is basically just busy work to make up for the fact that there are no exams (which is the one and only positive). I suggest changing your prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Is not a great professor, acts like he cares about his students but doesn't. Is a really tough grader for no reason. His lectures are not enjoyable and wastes a lot of your time. Weird guy
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is the best professor I have had in four years at Iowa State and his class was SO interesting! His grading was 100% fair - he gives you study guides every week and answers are pulled straight from slides. He enjoys humor in papers! Can not say enough great things about this class! Also, there are no tests! TAKE THIS CLASS!

He is a good professor in management. He tried to make his lecture fun. He can make a good and clear explanation for course materials. But taking his classes, you have to do lots of work. Every week quizzes, application papers, and special assignments though you do have to take any exams. He is a little picky but he is fine

Overall this was a fun course. Professor Anderson is a fantastic professor. There is a weekly quiz and a weekly 1 page paper over an assigned topic and those are a large sum of the grade but he gives you the questions for the quizzes and the topics for the paper. He makes the course fun and makes you think. I'd highly recommend Professor Anderson.

Weekly quizzes and papers. He tells you he wants to quiz answers to be HIS way, so hes supper picky, but you have to figure out what he wants. Quizzes are 35% of your grade, its rough I wouldnt recommend taking it with him because of this structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ignore all of the negative reviews about Marc, because this guy puts his heart and soul into this class. Sure, he is a picky grader and makes you work for your grade. But that's HOW IT SHOULD BE. If you want to learn from a professor who knows his stuff, take Marc's class. If you want to slack off and be lazy, go elsewhere. He is one of the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Marc doesnt allow technology in his classes. He is a very picky grader. On the quizzes he wants it his way, if you get credit for one part of a question, but didnt get the second part of the question right he will deduct points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Marc is good at trying to make his lectures relevant or giving good examples. He tries to be funny by telling jokes of the day. The one page papers (every Friday) are easy, but if you don't follow the format to a T, he will dock you points. No exams, but the quizzes are a big chunk of your grade every Monday, & he is the pickiest grader which hurts
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you want to spend your weekend memorizing his quiz questions for Monday's quiz take him, if you have a life on the weekend skip him! He is EXTREMELY picky on how he wants the answers to be they basically have to be his word for word. Quizzes every Monday at the start of class and 1 page papers (that aren't given to until Wednesday) due Friday.

Dr. Marc is unique, His classes are never boring. If you want to learn, take his courses. I learned a lot about personalities in management and their overall effect. I wish if I took all his courses in graduate school.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I looked forward to attending his lectures everyday, he makes sure the lectures are interesting with relevant material. He even includes a joke of the day, and shows several movie clips from great films. There is no textbook or exams, but there are weekly quizzes and weekly application papers. By far my favorite course/professor at ISU.
By far the best mgmt prof I have had. His lectures are applicable to real life and i learned a ton. I wish I would have told him how great his class was.

There are a lot of papers, but luckily they are short one paged papers. There are no exams, only weekly quizzes. He can be a picky grader and doesn't give much feedback over why you missed points. Overall, it was a very interesting class!

No big exams, a small quiz and paper every week. Most interesting presentation style of any class I've had so far, and I took a lot away from the class. Less work than other classes and you learn more!
Fantastic professor, interesting lectures. Regular quizzes and papers instead of large tests. Does a great job of teaching applicable and factual content. Would definitely recommend!

Marc is an awesome guy. He really puts his all into making the course applicable to real life. The course was very informative and helpful content. Marc is very picky when grading. Everything has to be said just the right way.
Passionate and a great teacher. If you give minimal effort and show interest in the course you will succeed. So much applicable material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: There is a paper and a quiz almost every week, but if you show up to class the material is pretty easy to grasp. His lectures are intriguing and fun and you learn something interesting every single time. There are NO TESTS and NO TEXTBOOK. He does not require much reading and he is always available to answer questions or give help when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: I took Management 371 with Marc and I couldn't have been happier with that choice. Hands down the best teacher I've had at Iowa State. He makes it very transparent what work is to be done, and his lectures are the most interesting I've ever sat through. Marc really focuses on teaching you things that are truly useful in life and in the work place.

If anyone has anything negative to say about him as a professional its probably because they're a bad student. I absolutely loved his class and actually learned and retained so much, I had to go tell him that and I never usually give teachers recognition, if I didn't graduate I'd take his masters class. Hes very knowledgeable and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The guy is a joke. Read's Dr. Seuss in class, shows irrelevant videos, does not honor his word, and wastes class time. His classes are a waste of time and money and quickly lost respect for him as a professor. How is this guy qualified to teach a graduate class? Students would laugh at him behind his back (likely his online dating stories).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson was one of my favorite professors from Iowa State. He treats his students like adults; tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed and then it's up to you to follow through. He puts a lot of effort into the class and it shows! You won't be disappointed with him!
Super great guy. No text book or tests!! But, papers due every week as well as a fairly difficult weekly quiz. Know what's due when it is due and you'll be golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are no exams at all. A quiz on monday (he gives you the questions over the weekend and picks 4 from a list of 10-12) and a one-page paper due on friday that comes with a prompt. There is no textbook, just show up and learn. Most topics are very interesting and can be applied to real life. He's also super into jokes and video clips. Easy A.

Best professor I've ever had. Can be a tough grader, but fair and unbiased. A lot of unique concepts to learn. Does a great job demonstrating the material and applying real life examples. The clip project was fun, as he uses the best ones as examples in his future classes. No textbook, test (weekly quizzes), and no final are nice.

Marc makes class fun and interesting. There are weekly papers and quizzes. A really easy group project at the end of the semester. No tests or book. He gives you the quiz questions in advance and the powerpoint slides are posted after each class. Attendance is not mandatory but his lectures are fun to listen to and makes the quizzes easier to take.
No exams or final and you do not need a textbook. Weekly quizzes and papers. He makes the class really interesting and has been my favorite professor at ISU.
Very good and knowledgeable professor. Doesn't have tests but gives weekly quizzes and short papers. No book, so showing up to class is necessary. One of the best professors I've had at Iowa State.

Makes you work for your grade, but it's a rewarding class--he makes the material really interesting. You don't need a textbook and there's no final. However, there are weekly quizzes and papers, both of which he grades strictly. Gives extra credit periodically. There's a fun and fairly easy group project.

He looks for very specific answers on the weekly quizzes, often times something small not included in the notes. Many of the answers to the quizzes are related to examples he gives in class. Doesn't offer much extra credit, so take advantage. Isn't very clear with what he's talking about, just kind of talks. Mediocre at best, not an easy A with him
Be prepared to work for your grade, but there is no final so it's worth it. Application papers and quizzes each week but they are manageable if you take the time to review class material.

Anderson is extremely helpful, there are NO exams, but the class will keep you busy. You have a weekly quiz, but he gives you all the questions & you have a one page reflection paper each week.  This course material is very interesting, lots of video clips, fun activities, jokes each day, clear explanations. Wonderful class and a phenomenal prof.

Marc is one of the best professors here at ISU. He really cares about teaching and tries to know each students individually. The weekly applications papers and quizzes can take some time to prepare for, but it's very doable. The class is very fun to attend and he definitely made it so by his joke of the day. Always has a big smile on his face.

The commitment and dedication, Marc offers to his students, is overwhelmingly outstanding. The course material is challenging, but you can be rewarded with good marks, if you place a decent amount of effort in. Importantly he perfectly engage students in discussion,teaches in manner that is invitingly different, than the norm of text book teaching.

One of the better courses I have taken at ISU.  If you expect to get by with minimal effort, Dr. Anderson is not for you.  If you are willing to put in the work you will learn a lot from him.  He requires a steady stream of work throughout the semester, but most of it is simple.

I don't know if I just had bad luck with this guy but everyone in my class was attending class everyday and doing terrible on the 4.5 point tests. I did well on the application papers but it wasn't enough to keep me from failing the course, so I had to drop. I thought he was quite strange and graded very harshly. I would NOT recommend his class.

By far one of the best Teacher and class I've ever had at iowa state!  A little bit of busy work but extremely easy if you put the little effort forward.  Extremely easy and fun project at end of semester. Marc's class was by far the most fun one to go to!

Solid teacher and solid class. The examples that he used were really helpful in learning the material. He has you write your name on the last page of any assignment you do, so he isn't judging your work before he reads it/grades it.
One of the best professors I have had at Iowa State.

Totally awesome class and professor, upbeat and always in a good mood! Very engaging, don't let the no textbook fool you! Learned a lot about myself and others also. I recommend Marc to anybody interested in becoming a better person and becoming more aware of their surroundings and actions.

Best professor. Actually teaches students rather than focus on research then lecture and let them learn on their own. His technique will ensure you learn way more than in any other class. A lot more weekly work but not hard. If you want to learn, this is the class. Plus, if you keep up, you will definitely do well.

One of the best teachers I have ever had...He uses many examples to help you understand the material?he uses different class activities to keep the class interesting...I have learned more in this class than any other class I have taken during my years of studies. I am now more confident and feel more prepared in becoming a manager. GREAT PROFESSOR!
One of the only professors that actually cares about his students and how much they learn. The best professor I've had @ Iowa State, anyone would be luck to be in Professor Anderson's class.

My favorite professor at Iowa State!! He made class fun with various activities and class related tv clips. Weekly assigments were easy since they were about your own life and how it relates to class material covered that week. Marc made me actually want to come to class for a change. Great Professor!!
Great course focussed on video/image processing.
Exams were a bit of a time crunch but I thought he did a good job preparing us for them. Great lecturer.

Participation in the lectures isn't mandatory, but I recommend it. The class pace is fast and Stoytchevs' lectures were the easiest way for me to learn; way better than anything I found online. He is very approachable, loves Star Wars, makes & puts jokes in his lecture slides, really great guy and teacher. One of the best professors I've had.
His lecture slides can be overwhelming but they help immensely for exams. Really funny guy.

Professor goes through material fast in lecture. He uploads all of his slides. His slides include ‘animations' of circuits, gates, and computers. It's very helpful. There is a weekly homework that takes roughly 3 hours to complete, if not more. His slides help immensely with the homework though. He allows a lot of notes on exams. He is funny too.

points were fairly distributed, which is a big plus.
exams were difficult but not impossible.

My boy Stoytchev has some of the best slides in the business. They make following the circuits pretty easy. As others have mentioned, the exams are a bit of a time crunch, but he provides some extra points on them, The labs are very straightforward and logical. The homework can take some time but are not too crazy. He is the best prof I've had!

Great guy who genuinely puts effort into his teaching. In CPRE 281, the slides he made are the reason I was able to learn most of the material. Exams were hard, very little time especially for exam 2. Also, I didn't really enjoy his teaching style because I wasn't able to focus very well. He did too much reviewing.
He is a great professor who helped me get a better understanding of computer science. The class is challenging but not overly difficult and he is supportive and answers questions thoroughly.

Amazing, hilarious professor. He is excellent at teaching complicated things. His powerpoints (which are 100s of slides long) are amazing resources that he uses to teach by creating "animations" of circuitry. We started the year by learning simple boolean expressions and ended with studying a genuine microprocessor, all credit to his teaching.

I think you can understand the content without going to lecture. But i would still recommend going. He does clarify questions if you have them. He's kind of belittling. labs are time consuming. I would take as many timed practice midterms as possible. He often puts problems that you've never seen on the exam. does not give extensions on hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Stoytchev is hilarious and very good at explaining things. However, his exams can be stressful as they are always a crunch for time.
Great Teacher very intensive course but you learn a lot. His course is everything you need to learn about digital logic and computer engineering.

Stoytchev really cared about making his lectures engaging and he is very passionate about digital logic. The slides are 200-300 slides long so beware, but this is because of animations that make it easy to learn when you miss. The labs and homeworks are time consuming but help out a lot for the exams and the final project. You'll have to earn it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I found Digital Logic to be a relatively enjoyable class. Stoytchev's lecture slides are all available online which makes it very easy to review and he responds to emails very quickly. His lecture slides do tend to be on the long side (around 200-250 for each topic) and a lot of it is either review or animations. Learned a lot though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is great and taught very well. You can tell he is passionate and cares about giving the students a good education. My only complaint would be that (early in the semester) he used class time to heavily encourage students to wear masks (completely fine), however, he didn't post streams of the lectures online :/

Prof. Stoytchev has great lectures that he puts a lot of time into. He does a great job of explaining content that the book either leaves out or does a poor job of covering. All of the tests also felt pretty reasonable and I never felt like I was being set up to fail. One of my favorite classes in terms of content, would recommend to anyone.
Assigned work over breaks, broke ISU policy multiple times, attempted to enforce masking. Be cautious if taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Stoytchev cares about his students and provide you extensions if you need it. He will make you work for the class but you learn from each homework. He gives extra credit with every homework so if you feel like falling behind you can catchup easily. He cares about teaching and his students

The lectures were the best part of this class, and everything was explained very clearly. There were never any surprises, and his lecture slides are amazingly well crafted to teach the material, in addition to just being a great professor. The exams were also very fair and easy to prepare for without being too easy to challenge you. Great class
Dr. Stoytchev really cares about students and makes things more enjoyable with humor. He puts in lots of work to ensure quality content and gets exams graded and entered within the day.

Stoytchev definitely tries to make his lectures very enjoyable along with getting the information to you. He talks through slides which can be found online on his website which is always nice to look at in case you miss/decide not to go to a class. The homeworks and final project were very consuming but they helped me learn a lot of material.

Stoytchev was a decent instructor. The lectures were simple at the beginning but quickly got more complicated, take notes! The weekly homework was fairly long. Stoytchev communicated concepts clearly and effectively. He always stayed after class to answer questions. One of the hardest classes I've taken at ISU so far (I'm a sophomore).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thought he explained things pretty clearly. He also seems to care about his students / the quality of his lectures. Some of the homework questions felt misleading and confusing is the main complaint I have. Get ready to put some time into his course as you will have 1 lab and 1 moderate homework due most weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Stoytchev is without a doubt the best professor I've ever had. It's always apparent that he's passionate about what he does. 575 is a lot of work, but it's all valuable and genuinely fun. His teaching made me fall in love with computer vision and signal processing. I guarantee this will be the most enjoyable and memorable class you take.
Easily one of the best professors Ive had

Stoy is a phenomenal lecturer who puts a great deal of time to ensure his lectures are quality material. This is an incredibly difficult course, however, and I highly recommend reading. You have to put in a lot of effort. He managed to make a course I found rather boring initially, incredibly interesting. Super engaging lectures, don't skip them!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Gives clear concise instructions and easy to understand lectures with a good amount of humor and charm sprinkled in to keep things interesting and fun. Homework was reasonable and informative typically linking up with what was being taught in lecture or in lab. Tests were graded and submitted the same day.
Great prof, actively tries to make the content of the class interesting and is enthusiastic about what he does. Tough grader, and his exams are equally hard (or I'm just dumb).
Funny Guy with a lot of star wars references on tests, usually for extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Stoychev was the best professor I've ever had at ISU. CPRE 281 was a difficult class but he tried his best to make us understand everything. You could see the effort he took to make the class enjoyable as well. He really cared about our learning and I left this class remembering everything because of his teaching.
Good teacher. Class gets much harder as it goes on. Lectures are hit or miss. Either dreadfully boring or hilarious.... but it is dreadfully boring material.

Stoytchev is a very good prof. His lectures can be a little technical and boring at times, but he mixes in some humor and he is very good at breaking down concepts to help students understand. I barely touched my textbook but went to class and did just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at ISU. Attending lecture is key to doing well, which is enjoyable because of Stoytchev. After the first exam, I did not take any notes--he posts all his slides online. Just go to lecture and pay attention, do labs and homework with the slides as reference.

Pretty funny guy and definitely knows what he's talking about. Class starts off pretty easy and then the last third of it just completely flew over my head, and the final project is a brutal one. Definitely give yourself ample time for homeworks (can take multiple hours as the course progresses) and the final project. Overall, great class and prof.
Stoytchev has got to be hands down the best professor I have ever had at Iowa State. His lectures were worth the time and he is super helpful outside of class too. Class was never dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: He explains things very well in lecture. There were three tests, open-book and notes. These accounted for more than half our final grade. They had 130 points but were graded out of 100. Reading is not necessary if you go to the lectures, but the book is helpful for homework. He tends to go very slow in lectures, but it is better than going too fast

Professor Stoytchev is a great professor and is pretty humorous at times. He mostly reviews the book reading in class but there is a lot of good explanation of the material and information for the labs in class. The lecture PowerPoint slides are online on his website but for most lectures you'd better be there if you want to understand it.

Dr. Stoytchev is by far one of my favorite professors. The lectures are entertaining, but at the same time helpful. The exams are very fair and the grading criteria are clear. He is not monotone at all and is quite engaging. I would definitely take his class again.

Great teacher, you don't have to go to class, but I would highly recommend it. He does a great job explaining the concepts. He will bring in props if he thinks that will help him teach the lesson. Funny and enjoyable guy. Exam are very long though, almost everyone runs out of time before they finish. The exams are 130/100 to compensate for that tho
Best professor I've had at ISU. Really wished he taught more classes.

Great professor who clearly spends a lot of time planning out his lectures to make them clear and easy to understand. Tells you exactly what it is that you are expected to know for exams, and the labs were also not overly challenging. The final project did take a lot of time so make sure to not put it off!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best teacher at this university. I have never seen a professor work so hard to make sure his students were understanding the material. He has an anonymous feedback forum on blackboard which he reads regularly to make sure the student's are happy with his teaching. Make sure you've watched every episode of Star Wars before taking this class.
The best teacher i have had at the university so far.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stoytchev the first class told us he wanted everyone to drop. He did anything but want us to drop. He was a great and funny teacher. 10 out of 10 would recommend. Except the final project was super hard. Start early.

Alex is a great lecturer and you can tell that he really puts a lot of effort into his lectures. There is about 1-2 hours of homework for this class each week which usually is pretty easy. The final project is by far the hardest thing in the class and you should plan to spend a lot of time on that (It took me around 30 hours in the lab).

Stoytchev is probably the best professor I have ever had at ISU and maybe ever will have. 281 is a boring class in my opinion but he makes lecture fun because of his sense of humor. Always go to class cuz it starts easy af then goes 0-100 and sucks at the end. Overall, don't take this class if your prof isn't Stoytchev.

Honestly one of the best professors I have ever had, lectures are very funny (you will know what I mean syllabus week), he does a great job of teaching the material and sets you up to get a good grade if you put a bit of effort in. Takes feedback seriously and is probably reading this right now. take the final project seriously though.
This guy was great. Class material is difficult, but I wouldn't have it taught by anyone else. Be prepared for Star Wars and Matrix references and test questions.

If you attend class everyday, do the homework, and study, you will pass.  Stoytchev set the gold standard for teachers at Iowa State. All other teachers pail in comparison to his outstanding attention to students, willingness to help, and his simply outstanding slide shows. By far the best teacher I've ever had.

The first 2/3 of the class are cake.  The last third will blow your mind.  The class doesn't really require extra studying (just before exams) as long as you've done the homework an mini projects.  Some of the lectures are kind of repetitive, until the end of the semester.  Then it will destroy you if you don't try.

Alex has such a perfectly concise way of speaking that he only says exactly what he needs to which makes him the perfect professor for this class. The only exception is the little jokes he slips in, but his humor keeps some of the drier subjects tolerable. Also take him seriously when he says there will be Star Wars exam questions.

Overall pretty easy with the exception of a few homeworks. Exams were easy and he gave lots of chances to get 100 on them.  Stoychev explains concepts pretty clearly and if you don't get it he is willing to stop and explain again. Seems like he cares about students he teaches. On top of it all he is really funny as well. Great professor overall
He has a great sense of humor and explains really well .But you have to work hard to get an A in the class.

He's funny and he thoroughly explains everything in a simple way. I would recommend him for any class he teaches. Also, wait to by the book. He walks you through all your of options the first day. Everything is posted online, don't have to attend.
He makes classes interesting and fun. I learned a lot from this course.

Alex is a great professor, and his class is very interesting.  This was my favorite class so far.  He posts good power-points too.  The homework takes really long for this class, but its do-able. The class itself was hard, but if you take time to get to know the material well, then you should do fine.

He's great! You will be challenged like none other, but quite frankly this will prepare you for further classes in CPR E. He also loves Star Wars & the Matrix as well as makes a lot of jokes about Russia, America, and the movies above.

Alex is awesome.  His lectures are very good and his humor fits the demographic of his students well. He is very approachable and cares about his students succeeding.  However, the homework is stupid-difficult. Be prepared to ask for a lot of help. If you've never programmed before, you're gonna have a rough time, but Alex will definitely help you.

This is a very fun class. Stoytchev does an excellent job engaging the class for new concepts and old. This is a problem solving class, and the homework does escalate in difficulty rapidly. That being said, you will learn the material well.

Alex was a very fun professor to have. He's funny and is good at explaining concepts in lectures. However, the homework was far too difficult. We would learn basics in lectures and labs and then be given homework that even the TAs didn't know how to solve. Overall the class was enjoyable but way more difficult than it should have beeen.

He is a nice guy and helped me after class, but the course was ridiculous. It is way too hard and time consuming and you can spend hours doing the homework and end up getting no credit for it. Didn't really learn anything in lecture or lab because the concepts are covered to fast. Not a fun class at all.

Alex is a very funny guy. He clearly knows what he is talking about. I had no programming experience before taking this class and I'm doing well. It is a lot of work so be prepared, but if you are struggling, talk to him after class. He is open to students comments and lenient. I easily recommend him.

Best professor I've had thus far  mostly due to his good humor and lecture style. The ex-soviet jokes are entertaining and keep the class from becoming too dry. The only complaint is the learning curve for this class which is incredibly steep for those who have not programming in C or programmed at all before.
The best professor I have had!!!! Very helpful!
The best professor I've had!!!! Very helpful!
The best professor I've had!
A completely awesome professor.  He's a lot of fun fun to have as a professor and he really makes the class interesting.  I immensely enjoyed having him.
If you take this class, TAKE ALEX'S SECTION. That is all.
Funny professor and he kept the class interesting. It did take a while for us to get our grades back from the homework, but other than that it was ok. Class is extremely hard.
Makes the class very fun.

Funny, which helps keep you interested in attending class and paying attention. Lessons are also pretty easy to follow, and an actual demonstration of the lesson in code is usually always done, so you can see firsthand what he's talking about, which is a big plus too. The class overall is somewhat difficult, but one shouldn't have too much trouble.
Great Teacher! Homeworks are easy(only 30 mins max) and labs are interesting. He keeps your attention during class! Great Prof all around
One of the best teachers I've ever had. He makes CprE 185 the only class I actually look forward to going to.
Alex does a great job, and keeps class interesting.  I really wish that he taught more classes than he does.  I'd definitely suggest taking his section of any class he teaches.
