Hilarious teacher.  Always keeps me awake!

Humor in lectures was great. Alex did very well illustrating topics and provided good examples. Labs extremely beneficial for learning and applying new material. Loved the fact that exams out of around 130 - made for a great grade booster since I could always score around 100. Homework got really time consuming and annoying near end of course.
Great teacher

Really easy, I thought.  You can get 135% on the exams, though he cuts grades off at 100%.  They are open-book and open-notes.  The exams are part written and part programming (in C).  The written parts are more difficult, at least for me.  I didn't learn much from the lectures, but the labs are useful.

Ive taken many computer science classes before this one and found this to be the easiest one yet. Its sometimes hard to understand what he is talking about at times,but he does a good job trying to explain it to you. He is willing to work with you if you have trouble with problems. Homework is easy compared to other classes. claims if you try=pass.

Like stated before, being a business major, I though it went quite in depth but I don't know everything about java before I enter the class.  Going to lectures and the homework are VERY important to passing the class  The exams are quite long but they are open book and notes so not too bad, just long.

Alex is an awesome professor! He really cares about his students and if you talk to him he will help you pass the class. He adds humor into his lectures to help you listen. You DO have to learn in this class, otherwise the tests will be pretty tough. Pay attention and get help from the TA's, and you should be able to get through this class fine.

This guy didn't know how to teach the novice programmer.  I passed the class but not because of any help he could give... I studied and I think that he may want to try to find another class if he is teaching!

This class was very hard for being a class for the nonprogrammer.  Alex did, however, try to offer as much help as possible.  Weekly homeworks are worth only 2 points and take at least 2 hours to complete, in my case.  The exams take a very long time, as well.  One "hour long" exam took, on average, 3 hours.

Alex is a very knowledgeable professor. His lectures were great and he had the right balance between lecture slides and in-class disucssions. Anyone who is interested in robotics, AI, or human-computer interaction should take whatever class he is offering.

honestly, do not attend lectures. It's not worth your time. You are better off to watch the lectures at home in 1.5 speed. Homework is due at 5 PM and it is very easy to forget about it. He is very kind and understanding if you talk to him outside of class, it's just very hard to sit through his lectures as he talks quite slow sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Myers, but know quite a few people feel differently. This class was delivered fully online, and it is definitely the students' responsibility to learn the material from the lectures he posts. Exams were difficult, but you get a front-and-back note sheet. The final was not cumulative. The class is curved at the end of the semester

A lot of people have complained about this class. Overall, it is a very difficult class to take with him, but I found that if you attended the extra lecture sessions that he provides you can do very well within this course.  Exams are worth 80% of your grade and homework was 20%. You really do have to put the time in to this class to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Myers is extremely passive aggressive and teaches at a PhD level, expecting his content to be common sense (spoiler- it's not). He will yell at the class and make comments implying we are dumb :( The homework is easy, the exams do not have most of the content he warns you about. Testing center exams, notecard, but the class is  unnecessarily hard.

The professor taught Bio313 alongside Professor Vollbrecht. While the professors were kind and respectable, the course set-up was very annoying. Grades remained locked. Lectures were VERY slow-moving but there was TopHat for extra credit. Don't recommend these professors for this course as nice as they were.

His hand writing is atrocious, good luck trying to make sense of it. His lectures will put you to sleep if you aren't properly caffeinated. Not all the material on the exams is covered in class so prioritize reading and taking notes on the textbook.

I feel that Dr. Myers struggles to convey information to students clearly. Myers had to go back many times to correct lecture mistakes and does not follow the slides well, leaving you more confused. I am generally very charitable to professors and find the reviews on this site often too harsh, but I wish I would've listened to what I heard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Teacher is a nice guy and knows a lot about the subject. His lectures are pretty boring though but it's hard to make this class interesting. Class has 6 exams (5 are graded) and online quiz's and thats it. Does have extra credit. Offers practice exams for the exams which helps a lot, exams are difficult though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I thought the lectures were very good in reference to what was on the tests. I wish I had studied more because this class was fascinating and could have been an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not great at explaining topics. Exams are difficult. You better have a good TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't be afraid of all the fearmongering about this classes difficulty, it's really not that bad if you ignore whatever Dogandzic is saying and just learn it on your own. He is not a very good teacher and also sort of rude. Also the labs are not very helpful. Also he shaves in the state gym locker room.

Stay away do not take his class. If he's teaching, skip a semester or take another professor if possible. He doesn't help with anything, and if you ask for help on exams or homework, he will tell you to look it up or figure it out.

Absolute disregard for what his students understand. Example problems are seen by him as "trivial and not worth covering," and honest questions are met with a blank stare and mimicry. Avoid at all costs.
In general, his lectures were very entertaining, and he can be very helpful. Would highly recommend for this course.
He insulted many students in lectures, when they asked questions, and even in the exams
Save yourself the trouble and take the course with someone else.

If you take the class, it's not impossible, but be ready for a semester of pain and stress. Exams are worth most of your grade, but good luck doing better than a 60%. Labs are easy but not really helpful for the rest of the class. Homework is time-consuming and graded harshly. Luckily, there is around a 10% curve at the end of the class.

He lives up to the poor reviews. I wanted to like him, I thought, "he could not possibly be as bad as his rating makes him seem." 
Nah, he was worse! 
He flies through presentations, note-taking is not possible during the lecture. 
The exams are so ridiculously hard, homework is not any easier.  
Do yourself a favor: avoid this professor!!!!

The worst professor I've ever had. I've never seen someone so incapable of teaching. The lab is all Matlab, which does not help you with the material. The lectures confuse you more then they help, as it's impossible to understand him, and all he does is ramble about random things. If you ever see him listed as a professor for a class, drop it.

It was difficult to understand his teaching method - he assumed that everyone understood the materials he gave before coming to class so that he could go through the lectures fast, so I had to self-study.

Difficult to understand. The lectures are not useful and it ends up becoming a self study course. He posts online resources that we are expected to look at and learn from, instead of teaching it himself. The underlying concepts of EE224 are actually not too difficult, but the professor faces it in a way that is impossible to understand.

Despite having over a decade of experience, he can't teach to save his life. Lectures are incoherent, no quality practice material or examples, and long/confusing HWs. You will get a poor base understanding of 224, despite its importance to the EE curriculum. Take this course with someone else or at another college. Do avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This has to be one of the worst professors that I have ever had the displeasure of meeting. He can't teach to save his life, even though he's apparently been doing it for so long. I would highly recommend trying to take this class at any other university or just in general online over the summer or winter.
Good prof.  Fair grader, and his Canvas material is good.  His lectures can tend to be a bit fast and he will sometimes go on tangents, but he does a good job of spending enough time on what matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genius. Hard, but a rare teacher you likely won't appreciate until you have a professor that comes to lectures unprepared, unenthusiastic, and lacks canvas resources, which is unfortunate. Pay attention to the lectures, ask questions, and read the notes he posts! Be willing to dive in and you'll learn so much from him in one semester. Amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I've taken so far. He skips so many lecture slides and makes it even harder to understand by overcomplicating things. Homeworks are like mini-tests, ranging from 5-9 pages long. Exams barely include homework content and are hard. He refuses to post the answer key for midterms so you cant use them when studying for finals.
This professor doesn't teach anything. The lectures are confusing at best. Explanations are non-existent. Do not take S&S with this professor. You won't learn anything.

This professor makes simple concepts way more complicated than necessary. His teaching skills are non-existent and students do not learn any of the necessary content. Other universities cover way more topics and actually teach students something. You will learn nothing from this professor.

Saying the same thing louder does not count as an explanation to a question. You will not learn anything with this professor. Find a different section, or a different school to learn signals and systems.

This class was the most useless class I have ever taken. The content in this class is supposed to be the foundations for the rest of the electrical engineering curriculum. However, the professor was so bad and incompetent at explaining concepts that students that skipped all of the lectures averaged higher on exams than the students that attended.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS! Took this class and it was his first time teaching it in a decade! 10 years! Bro should not be teaching this class, is teaching it like a 400 level on an introductory course. Had a friend retaking this class had already passed it in a prior year, said he is making it way harder than it needs to be, was way easier before.

Lectures aren't always the clearest, however, lecture notes get posted, and if you read the book when you have questions, it tends to be very helpful. He is not good at answering questions in lectures and seems to only know one way of describing any given topic. Homework is difficult, exams are relatively easy in comparison.

Lectures are discombobulated. Class just sits in silence while the professor talks and no one understands the points he is trying to make. Unfortunately the only prof teaching the class. ISU needs better professors.
He will tell you when you are wrong but will give you plenty of opportunities to learn.
Having Dogandzic for EE 424 was great. He provides very nice typeset notes that can for the most part replace the recommended textbook. Exams are open note, and not too crazy difficulty-wise.

He is a great professor. The material is new to most students and that is why the subject is difficult. Easy to understand and does useful in class problems on the board. Homework can be a bit tricky, he is helpful in his office hours. Weekly quizzes count for a big portion of your final grade take them seriously. He's got a good sense of humor.

Despite what most students say, I think Dogandzic is a solid professor. He explained material in a way that made sense, and weekly quizzes ensure you actually know the material when the final approaches. In lecture he does move pretty fast, it seemed difficult to keep up at times. Also, his exams were difficult, but far from impossible.

Quizzes can be tough and should be taken seriously from the start. They have a substantial weighted grade. Labs are fairly easy. Hw isn't bad. His lectures can be boring at times. Overall, the class was good but you do need to pay attention as best you can.

He makes the material more confusing than it already is. The recitation is pretty helpful but the professor makes the lectures are hard to follow. He comes off as pretty rude and is a hard grader. Overall he is a bad teacher.
Will be tough

Dr. Dogandzic makes signals and systems I  a  difficult class; however, you can tell that he spends time preparing lecture material and exams. He expects students to match his work ethic. He tries very hard to answer any questions that a student might have about homework or class material.  Expect to be challenged in the class.

The biggest problem with him is that he assumes that you understand things and think like he does, but if you ask for help it is there. He takes a little getting used to. The exams are more difficult than they should be.

To be honest his accent is not that bad, what's bad are his teaching skills. I'm still unsure what what's actually going on in class. His assignments are designed to be difficult and advanced so you never really understand the basics of what you're doing. I spend hours going through the notes and re-watching recorded lecture and get no where.

I attended every lecture and Dogandzic still made it impossible to learn this material even with extra effort.  Confusing, rude, and ignorant are his top 3 qualities.  Makes you feel terrible about yourself in lecture; calling you out when you can't answer an example and says "you should have learned this in XXX class." Don't take his courses.

He is very hard to understand and some of the quizzes are pretty difficult. Make sure to leave plenty of time to read the text. 224 also comes with a recitation during lab time so that is a good place to ask questions. Asking questions in class does not work out well.

His accent is far from incomprehensible and even makes the class more enjoyable with his odd sense of humor. Quizzes are graded fairly. Printed hints and equations on homework and quizzes are very helpful; theorems are included where most teachers might expect you to remember them. Everything you need is always present in online lecture notes.
Not good at teaching anything.

This guy is horrible.  He has a very strong Russian accent and has no teaching skills.  Weekly quizes are worth 40% of grade with no partial credit on problems.  The problems out of the book are do-able but he makes up his own impossible problems.  The class average was about 60%.

Do not expect to ask questions in class. He answers questions with "You should have learned this in (insert class name here)" I have heard the same complaint in 224 as well. Has very thick Russian accent as well. Very difficult class.

The biggest complaint I had with this class was that it was not related to anything in the real world.  All material was abstract.  USE THE CD-ROM from the textbook -- it has solutions to problems that are very similar to those in the book.  Good luck trying to figure out what will be on the quizzes (really 4 problem exams).  Lab is all MATLAB.

Very fun professor, a very positive person, and someone who clearly wants to see their students succeed and will help where she can. During dead week, I submitted the physical pieces of my game prototype, but I needed them for a video. So I messaged her over the weekend, and she came to her office so I could pick them up immediately.

I have taken 3 courses and projects with the City of Ames with her. She is very inspirational and passionate! The classes are also very helpful for the real world yet creative to the mind. 

Our recent class collaboration with another university was also interesting and with insightful takeaways.

The class barely skims the surface of smart/ sustainable cities topics. Alenka uses the class to pursue her own research goals and expects students to put in time outside of class including weekends to help out with "Play Ames" a community engagement initiative. It feels like students are free labor for Alenka and the city of Ames.
Loved this class & professor Poplin! It is super easy to follow along the labs & the TAs are also super helpful. The labs can take a long time to complete but fairly simple tasks.

Alenka was one my best professors I have ever had. I have learned a lot in this course from her brilliant teaching techniques and respectful behaviour. She was super knowledgeable, supportive, respectful and care about students. She was my motivation to do my thesis in smart city and I am so glad that I took this course. SHE IS THE BEST

A fun professor but in the classroom, she is very unclear and ambiguous with instructions for assignments and will assign a lot of unreasonable homework. Sometimes, she will interrupt you while you are trying to speak to her or in group work. Very micromanaging including on group projects.
fun class. Usually full of freshman who dont answer questions, so if you speak up and make yourself noticeable, you will pass and she will love you.
Even though you are not required to be in class she will have quizzes that go towards your grade so it is best to go. She was my favorite professor this semester. I highly recommend. Very nice lady.

Her class was only out of 100 points. She does give extra credit, but lectures have a lot of extra material that does not matter. She gets on many tangents. The labs are interesting, but lectures can drag.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors I have ever had

Great professor! Always explains the requirements for the homework and provides clear feedback. Readings are interesting and not long, lots of useful online resources, interesting class exercises and activities. She inspires you to create and apply the knowledge you get from the readings. Highly recommend!

Great class! Readings are interesting, homework requirements always clearly described, constructive feedback, always available for advice and assistance. Inspiring, professional and helpful professor! She motivates you to create and express yourself while following the existing game design rules. Highly recommend to take it!

Fun while learning was the motto of the class. The assignments were well described and if the instructions were followed, it was easy to score well. The professor is very helpful, understanding and gives ample opportunities to earn extra credits and work on the assignments. Would highly recommend taking this class or any other class of hers.

Don is a pretty good professor. His lectures are clear, and he gives good examples. He does have an accent, but as long as you are somewhat decent with deciphering accents, you should be fine. He is quite helpful with his examples, and gives a lot of good tips and tricks with what to focus on and what to move on from.

Overall, a great professor; some reviews mentioned his accent being difficult to decipher, but I had no issues here. Although I will say he sometimes struggled to help students with questions during lecture, where he seemed to not quite grasp what was being asked.

A great professor who strives to convey a clear understanding of the material in class, which is greatly appreciated. Going to the lecture is optional, like most math classes at ISU; however, you will most likely have to go if you want an A.

Dr. Kumudu is a great professor. He does a good job explaining the deeper ideas behind our math and genuinely wants to teach the students. He also encourages students to ask questions and go to his office hours, and he is very accessible outside of class.

He's not a bad teacher, and you can understand the material, but his accent can make him difficult to follow most of the time. When you ask questions, he often just refers you to the formula sheet, which isn't always very helpful. Because of this, you'll end up teaching yourself most of the material.
Good professor

Very hard to understand and, honestly, not a good teacher. Gives very boring lectures, and the material and examples he covers in class are nothing like what is actually tested on in quizzes and exams.

This professor asked for feedback many times during lectures to make sure we were following along and encouraged us to ask questions if we had them. He is a very nice guy but sometimes his accent made it a little difficult to understand what he was saying. I wish he did more in-class examples, but overall he was pretty good.

Don did a great job with his explanations and the notes that he provided were useful to an extent, but I understand that not everyone will get a lot from viewing a bunch of notes. Regardless, he clearly wants you to succeed and his office hours are very useful. Also, he doesn't come off as condescending like some Math instructors tend to be.

This was my second time taking MATH1650 and it was way better this time around. He was very caring about the content we were learning and always had examples ready to go. He would be able to answer any question I would have or anyone else had. Although, he can be a little fast sometimes when working through his notes, just ask questions.

Lectures were pretty bad. His slides seemed like he was just reading from Wikipedia and went over derivation of formulas out of context for 30 minutes just to walk us through his work for 2 example problems instead of solving it with us. His office hours are good, but lectures not so much.
He's so sweet. He genuinely cares about his students. I went to his office hours once and he really wanted to make sure I understood everything. I would love to take another class with him again!!

He's a great guy and although at first it was hard to understand him, it took me only a few lectures to understand his accent. He always posts the lecture notes ahead of time so you can look at it before the lecture. His notes are very clear and neat as well, and he does provide a lot of useful tips for quizzes/exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took math 1400. Great professor, funny guy. Honestly, I didn't pay too much attention in lectures and learned from the weekly homework and discussions. Most of the class content I learned in high school.

He is a super great guy, and he makes sure everyone understands what is going on throughout the lecture. Notes are uploaded in packets so you can follow along. Sometimes, he gets excited and makes a few mistakes, but other than that he is pretty good.
Incredibly sweet and nice guy. His lectures are very clear and helpful. Love him

He is so sweet and funny in his lectures, and makes differential equations easy to understand. He has note packets uploaded for you to print out and follow along with him, which really helped. He is rather heavy on theory sometimes and can go a little fast and make a mistake or two, but is overall a great and caring guy.

super easy class because there arent even real assignments. you just have to listen to a few podcasts and give ur response, attend class, and do some other attendance stuff. no real homework or projects. this class honestly didnt really feel like a class, just weekly discussion with strangers on a designated topic. interesting class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class has 3 exams (MC & Essay) & final, w 1 drop. 350 word paper and reading before every class. Class not mandatory, but you must participate certain # of times. Material itself is not difficult, but you have to make the effort when it comes to reading it and writing responses 3 times a week. Tuckness is a good professor, lectures are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: It feels like poor teaching to allow students to succeed the entire semester then drop them 11% at the end of the semester to fit your loose participation standards that have no backing. If you are unable to handle low student attendance, set an attendance policy or accept that students can teach themselves your material.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Alex Tuckness knows what he is talking about but if you are not keen on writing essays I would not suggest taking his classes. The exams are essay based and he grades harshly. There were daily one page papers that has to be done for his class and there is one large paper due towards the end of the semester. I would probably not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Alex is very intelligent and nice, however, this class is not easy. Three things you need to know before taking this class; Participating matters, yes you need to speak up almost every other class. Get ready to read SO many papers, articles, documents, and complete many many papers (2 a week).Tests are extremely difficult, so pay attention in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: As long as you do the readings and pay attention in class, you'll do fine. He is more than willing to help explain topics if you ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good profesor

Professor Tuckness is exactly the type of political science professor you do not want to wind up getting. With a clear political affiliation in mind, he lectures and selects course material in favor of his political position. He also uses the platform Tophat to ask insensitive questions about marginalized groups. Would not recommend him.

Really good professor. Attendance matters two major papers and a final with reading before every class. Stay up with the reading and it’s not that bad. Cold calls in class and grades on participation. Overall not that bad, not an easy A. Very smart and helpful in clarifying readings. Go to class and read, and you’ll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He does a good job at keeping us engaged in class, he made special accommodations for me and went above and beyond to make sure I had success in class, the only thing is the class if definitely not easy - it requires a lot of reading and thinking and writing. But if you're able to do that, you should take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Alex Tuckness is a perfect example of what can happen if a kid from the Ozarks goes to an Ivy League school. He's teaching from a 100% biblical world view and is part of the Baptist hierarchy that runs Ames. He has no business teaching political science.

Dr. Tuckness is incredibly smart. His classes (took 333 and 235) were super interseting, but they were both a lot of work. "1 page papers" on every reading were required, and most readings took a while. Tests were essays, but he said all the answers in class. So yep, you better go to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is extremely rude, will pick on you in class. He makes you read 30-40 pages for every class and you have to write a paper every week and either you get a 0 or a 1 in that paper. There is nothing in the middle but either a 0 or a 1. High suggest you not to take a class with this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Classes are run by him as a facilitated discussion or debate, assisted by top hat questions which are graded for participation. Uses the Socratic method to randomly call on students so you have to pay attention to the in-class discussions. Have to read a chapter and write a one page paper for every class. MC tests are difficult but go to office hrs
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuckness is definitely a knowledgeable guy. However, this class is pretty hard. If you are a visual learner- I would not recommend this class as he doesn't do power points and just lectures. There is a one page paper due each class so if you don't like writing I would not recommend. Overall, nice guy just super hard class.

I have taken pols 235 and 333. Basically the same set up. A reading and one page paper are due for every single class. You can miss one week of these with no penalty. Love the lectures but expect to read 20-40 pages for every class. Essay tests that are pretty difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good Professor, presents theoretical topics well so you think about all the different aspects.
Harsh grader, but facilitated a good learning environment that bettered my ability to think about our society and how it was shaped.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Not a poli sci or phil student. Took Pol 235.  Tuckness was awesome.  Demanded a fair amount of reading and papers, but always applied to in-class discussion and the tests. Great use of Socratic method.  Class was one big pointed discussion and debate, which he did a great job of keeping on course, worthwhile, and civil (when heated).  Great prof!

One of my favorite professors. Really makes you think and goes the extra mile to make class challenging and worthwhile. Very respectful with great stories and discussions. In reality, very helpful, funny, friendly - just lays out the rules and follows them consistently! Higher level courses also very good.

Dr. Tuckness is great. Lots of the papers and exams require you to acknowledge both sides of an argument, which I thought was great, it really forced you to think. I thought the class was really interesting and relevant. He does a good job of getting everyone involved, and hearing both sides of an argument. I would definitely recommend his classes.

Bright man, very clear and tries to run classes in large part on discussion. While not an exciting lecturer, has an excellent grasp on material and unlike some professors tries to apply it to ordinary life. His exams are not difficult but require at least some studying and paying attention in class. Take his advice-do the readings twice. Great.

I took POLS 235. This class is NOT a cake walk, but IS worth taking.  Prof. Tuckness is an interesting lecturer, and the texts we used were challenging but worth it. You MUST show up and you MUST study for tests to survive this class! He's changing the actual class format for Fall so not much to say there. Would totally take a class with him again.
Challenged me to analyze both sides of common arguments and evaluate the strongest arguments

I was very intimidated at first but after the first couple of classes I realized that Dr. Tuckness was a really great professor and didn't make you afraid to ask questions if you didn't understand. He made the class fun and easy to learn I highly recommend his classes
Tuckness is an extremely knowledgable prof, but seemed a bit unapproachable.  In addition, the amount of work involved and the expectations he had for test essays frequently made this class hellish.
It is a difficult course, but definitely interesting. It gets tough to get all of the one page assignments in, and attend class everyday. An A would require quite a bit of work.

An interesting discussion class. Not too demanding, but not a piece of cake either. Good teacher with a good teaching style. If you like political philosophy and don't mind reading and writing then this would be a pretty good class.
if you like poli sci and are a decent writer, this class is very do-able, although labor intensive.  if you have trouble writing, or like to skip class, avoid at all costs

I've never had to work harder for an A (it is possible- just do all the 1 page assignments and take the final) but I've never learned more in the process.  Tuckness really makes you consider your stance on an issue, but does so tactfully and is very respectful of all students.  Unquestionably one of the best profs I've ever had.

He teaches his classes in an interesting format to engage students. The reading are also not that bad. The difficulty comes in understanding the readings and being able to discuss them. If you like political philosophy it is a good class.
Great guy, interesting lectures.  The 1-page papers for every class get really old really fast, though.  Know's his stuff!

He is a wonderful and engaging teacher who makes the material interesting and relevant.  I really love his class even though there is a lot of reading.  You have to write papers for every class which sounds bad but is really helpful when you prepare for tests.  If you try, you'll do fine.
Professor Tuckness encourages discussion and assigns challenging readings.  If you want to think and learn, take one of his classes.
It was a very interesting class and he taught it well, but was definately difficult.  If you're looking for a good class academically, look for his classes but expect to be challenged.

Insane amount of readings and assigned a large paper to be done over our break. Grading is rough, even though lessons are quite unclear. He likes students to feel stupid. Don't take his classes if you want to learn anything remotely practical.
Incredibly difficult class. Received study guide for final one week ahead of time, with three pages, single-spaced, of terms and concepts we need to know. Definitely needed more time.

Dr. Armstrong was a spectacular professor for a difficult class. He made a topic that I struggle with engaging and interesting, and he was very understanding with his grading. This class is difficult, but if you put the effort in to attend and do your best, Dr. Armstrong and the TAs will make sure you get the grade you want.

Midterms weren't terrible as long as you paid attention and reviewed in lab. Final absolutely destroyed my grade despite doing well on everything else. Extra credit given for attending all labs and participating in reviews. Exam questions are tricky as they can be very specific but not the hardest class if you put some effort in!

Does a good job making boring material as engaging as it can be. We have assignments that we complete in lab, quizzes in class, two midterms, and a final. The quiz and test questions are written more difficult than necessary to prove understanding of concepts. The final was very hard, but he grades on a curve. Respects feedback from students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Usually im not a fan of stats stuff, but Dr. Armstrong was so funny & made the material interesting. Quizzes every day motivated me to pay attention. The tests are tough, but manageable if you study. I wish I could take more classes with him, he made a 2hr class go by quick. His dad humor is amazing & he knows his stuff

This class shouldn't be hard, it's just incredibly boring and Patrick does his best to make it interesting. There's a quiz every class period, but they're easy and help you learn the material and figure out what's important. Read the book if you don't understand what's going on in class, and get ready for some specific exam questions. Good luck!

He's a great professor, explains things clearly and tries to make it funny. The content though is just so boring and most seems kinda useless. Had a couple of quizzes that weren't covered in class well, but his tests aren't bad. COuld update some of his examples

Psychometrics is a class full of very dry material, but Dr. Armstrong does a great job of making the lectures more-than bearable. 3 tests that are always going to be harder than you think (even though most of it seems pretty simple) The lab is pretty easy, able to get most assignments done in lab (except for the short paper) Don't bother buying bo

Tried making the class more interesting since the topics weren't always exciting. He is a nice guy and I enjoyed his class. The TA grades homework and helps explain topics in the discussion session that may have been confusing during class.

Considering the material is pretty high level and dry, Armstrong makes it interesting and accessible. He has you hooked from day 1 with his hilarious stories and funny videos and he is very smart and makes it easy to understand. Even though this course was required I would definitely take it again.  Also, ask him about his black shirts.

Armstrong is a great professor for this class, as he tries to make the extremely boring material fun to learn. He gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit and curves the final grade pretty strongly if the class average is below a B grade. The exams are tough though, so do the extra credit!

Armstrong is a fantastic and hilarious professor. He tries his best to make sure the science of testing is interesting and easy to understand. There is a lot of technical knowledge and statistics, but it is incredibly easy for a 400 level class compared to my previous experience.

Attendance is not mandatory but you might miss quizzes. 440 is the bane of many a psych student's existence, but it is a necessary evil if you want to be at all ready for graduate school - or even able to intelligently read research literature. The topics are tough and the lab is pointless, but it's good info.

This class helped to prepare me for graduate school. Thanks to PSYCH 440, I was much more prepared than my peers for graduate level statistics and measurement topics. If you aren't going to graduate school, I can see how this class might be pointless. If your degree is a stepping stone to selling insurance, yep, this class is worthless.

He is a very funny professor that uses a lot of youtube clips in the lecture. The material isn't the most interesting, but he does a good job at keeping the students interested by using modern pop culture references. Ask about his black shirt!
You gotta read and pay attention. Ask questions

Patrick does his best to make a boring class interesting. Lecture and discussion groups seem to drag on a lot longer than necessary. I had a great TA who although boring lead great exam reviews. Don't waste your money on the book. Pay attention in discussion and you'll do fine.
Armstrong's funny but his tests  are honestly terrible. The study guides were worthless. Got an A in the class but at the expense of my sanity. Recitation was semi-helpful at least.

It sucks that the class is mandatory but he at least tries to make the dull material interesting. If you pay attention in class and study tests should be easy. He also curves the grades and is very fair. Gives extra credit just for asking questions and doing the survey at the end of class. Great professor specially for a required class.

This was one of the worst classes I've taken.  I'm going to get a good grade in it, so it's not that I'm frustrated.  I just find this class to be somewhat pointless.  I didn't learn as much as I expected out of a 400-level course.  Armstrong is funny and tries to make the material somewhat interesting, but it's nearly impossible.

I think you are all crazy.  I like Dr. Armstrong, and I am really enjoying this class.  His videos and stories are hillarious.  I also thought the tests were really easy.  Maybe you guys just need to stop whining and pay attention.

Super boring class! It was hard to stay awake in that class or pay attention. Dr. Armstrong would use the exams to show how much he knew about psychometrics by wording questions so that you were confused when you read them. Why is Psych 440 required????!!!!

Horrible. Psych 440 should not be required. He was dull and read directly off the slides, and the TAs in my lab gave us the answers to our assignments. I learned absolutely nothing and I went to every lecture.
Boring class, HUGE curve

I enjoyed the random slides that he would put up at the beginning of class and his sense of humor, which seemed to be pretty dry.  That's about where it stops though.  The course content was boring to begin with, which isn't his fault, but he didn't seem to do more than skim the surface of the topics we were covering.  This was particularly irritating when it came to exam time because even if you felt like you had spent a fair amount of time studying, it was all worthless because seemed to test on stuff that came out of nowhere.  He also seemed to have a particular knack for writing trick questions.  Even though my actual percentage was about 75%, I ended up passing with a B+ because he grades on a curve and everyone did badly.  Also, he can seem kind of intimidating, but is actually fairly nice if you talk to him and don't whine about something that you're unwilling to take responsibility for.
Material was dull, but I believe Prof. Armstrong did try to make it as interesting as possible.

440 is such a horribly boring class, I found it a pain to just go. He has kind of a cinical sense of humor, i think that's why some people thing he's rude. Kind of a stretch to say that the tests reflect what he teaches in class...

What can I say except AVOID THIS MAN. Makes 440 unnecessarily hard and is disrespectful when talking one on one. Sure, with the huge curve you might end up getting a decent grade, but why put yourself through the hassle? I don't really understand why this man is teaching.

Excrutiatingly boring.  Writes up power points, then reads powerpionts to the class.  We are juniors and seniors in college.  We can read.  Thanks.  Tests long and hard, inadequate examples or explanation of concepts in class

The tests are very difficult and the assignments take major effort, but he is very willing to help and will walk you through the assignments.  I have an A range GPA, but will have to fight for at least an A- in this class.

Professor Arora was very difficult, he would go through 60 slides a lecture and not give students time to take notes. I am an advanced level horticulture student, and this class is my only D on my transcript. You study to pass, not succeed. worst teacher at Iowa State.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unbearable, absolutely no constructive feedback.

He obviously knows a LOT about his class but does not know how to teach it. I have never in my life struggled so much with a class; the highest grade my semester was a C+. Study HARD for all quizzes and try to get past quizzes from other students, that's the only way I passed. Do not skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Masterclass in how to fail as an educator.  He made multiple people cry this semester.  He's clearly smart and knows a lot about his subject, but is honestly just an awful teacher.  You can tell how little effort he puts into his work, but he is oblivious.  Hated every minute, never had a worse class or experience during my time at ISU.

Take hort221 with Cynthia if you don't want your gpa to be destroyed. I'm a student who gets A's and B's, only C on transcript is this class. Pathetic teaching and tests crammed with information. Good luck, you'll need it.

This professor is very tough with grading, almost to the point that if you do not word it to his standards, it is wrong. The class itself is very boring, just going over long lecture slides for over an hour. Tough grading, and long lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Be at lecture and be ready to write notes. In hort 221 all exams are crammed full with a large amount of material on there. You study to pass his class, not learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exams every week it seems. Rajeev has a strong passion for this class and excepts his students to put in tremendous effort to get a good grade. Rajeev is easy to confront with questions. Be ready to memorize every bit of information and apply it to the exams... nearly 40 slides per exam at 9 exams makes this class difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great professor and very nice but the sheer speed at which we go through lectures, plus having a quiz pretty much every other class, makes this a practically impossible class. Not to mention he grades extremely strict. If you think you have a general gist of the concepts, be prepared to fail because he grades on VERY specific things!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He has a slight accent but fairly easy to understand. Everything you need to know is discussed in class so take good notes. The few classes I skipped were the questions I struggled with on the exams. Semi-tough grader but easy points can be earned in lab to boost your grade. Extra credit offered both on exams and in lab.

Dr. Arora has a clear passion for teaching and plant physiology.  The slides are easy to understand because he bolds and repeats the major points multiple times.  The quizzes are a combination of fill-in-the-blank and short answer (mostly).  The information is necessary for the horticulture field in particular and he gives it very well.

It's messed up that he doesn't use a book, but he puts everything you need to know for the exams in his slides, so remember EVERYTHING from them. Sometimes he mentions things in class, so that's where attendance is important. The good thing is, if you go to him during office hours he will answer all the questions you have.

He's knowledgeable and approachable. His interest in the subject is palpable at times, although the lectures left me feeling a little lethargic on more than one occasion. Watch out for the laser pointer!

This guy is awesome. He has an accent but hes understandable. if you need help he will help you. his lectures are interesting and everything in the test is stuff from lecture.Very nice guy too.If you ask questions then he will  be more interactive. talk to him and he will like you more.

Impossible teaching style. No book, based all of his tests off of every SINGLE piece of information on his slides. Even the students who were able to invest a lot of time in this class had a very difficult time understanding where the questions came from. No advice, good luck.
Archer is an amazing teacher. He jokes all the time in class. All exams are open-note, so make sure to take plenty of notes.

Overall, pretty simple class, does a reverse class with online lectures and discussions in class for attendance points. Very test-heavy. About 3 hours a week are needed outside of class to get lectures done. The grading and attendance methods are confusing, but doable.

I really enjoyed my religion class with him. He is a great professor and very interesting to listen to. The only thing I would worry about is the at-home lectures you watch/take notes on outside of class since they may take some time. He will cold call but only on questions given beforehand. Tests are open-note and always reflect the lectures.

Best class I took in college! I'm writing this 3 years after taking his course. I still think about the class! I made a lifelong friend who is different than me in every way. He does grade heavy on attendance but it is nearly the only thing you will get graded on. Tests are almost a formality, the attendance matters, but you'll never be bored.

Fun lectures but calls on people randomly and if you can't answer his questions from the video from the night before to his liking or if you're not there he counts you absent and takes off points. Very interesting topics discussed in class. Funny guy. Random worksheets throughout week that count as attendance for points too. Canceled class once.

Dr. Archer was great! I would definitely recommend taking this course and there is absolutely no bias from this professor. He teaches Islam the way it's supposed to be taught and there are no opinions.

Overall, an amazing professor. He is clearly passionate about what he is teaching, and is often taken off topic, engaging in interesting conversations. A large part of the grade was around attending class and watching the videos before, but besides that, there was no homework. Highly recommend this class.
LOVED him, and it is obvious he loves what he teaches. He uses empathy and laughter to lift up his students and prepare them for success, even outside of his classroom.

In class, we primarily review videos and texts for homework, with the actual learning being in homework videos outside of class. The instructor is overly strict about attendance, marking us absent for simply having a phone on our desk. If all the learning occurs outside of class, what's the point of attendance?

Attendance is required. All tests are open notes online at home. My only real issue is the final exam and the required attendance. The final was all essay questions and cumulative, but they weren't straightforward things. The other exams were definitions and straightforward definitions. Just didn't feel like the class prepared me for the final.

Such a funny, knowledgeable, and unbiased religion professor. Knows his content by heart and doesn't read off of slides, you can tell he has a passion for what he teaches. Never makes fun of cultural backgrounds or specific religions and is open and accepting to all. would take him 100 times again!!
I love this professor so much. Mr Archer is clearly very passionate about his job and makes sure his lectures reflect that. Easy to understand, funny, and respected by the class. no phone policy.
Awesome professor! He's so nice and accomadating! His lectures were so interesting and I'd take another class by him if I could.

I registered for more classes with him. He is amazing. His lectures are amazing. The format and syllabus are very clear. As long as you watch the lecture videos, take notes, and attend lectures you will be fine. You will never be bored in class. He is very fair and respectful to all cultures and backgrounds and deserves a 5/5.

Dr. Archer is one of the most respectable professors I've ever had. He truly valued his students and taught his class completely unbiasedly. I was very impressed with his ability to provide facts rather than opinions in a religious course. I definitely recommend taking a course with Dr. Archer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was pretty enjoyable! You definitely need to attend lectures. This will help your test scores and overall grade. He calls on 3 random people while in class, so make sure you do the homework. Overall, I thought his class was pretty fun and I would suggest taking it.

Super interesting class, super interesting professor, DEFINITELY recommend! But try to actually learn and understand the material, exams are not black and white answers but require a lot of critical thinking. However, if you attend lectures and watch the 3x a week videos you'll be fine. Class is like 90% exam scores or something but they're easy.

I found the videos and lectures interesting. He clearly cared about the class! I spent a fair amount of time every week working on organized notes from the video which definitely helped me out on my tests. Definitely at least watch all the videos if you want to know whats going on and attendance is part of your grade.

Your grade for this class consists of only exams and participation. There are 6 total exams, 5 unit exams and the final exam. He will randomly call of 3 people each class to answer questions from the lecture, if you're not there you will receive a 0 for that day. But it deducts from your overall grade!! Be careful missing classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor that made the class very interesting. The class is fairly easy if you show up and make sure to watch the videos before class. A large portion of your grade is based on participation. There are 30-60 mins of video lectures to watch before each class period, but that is the only thing you need to do outside of class.

Dr. Archer was absolutely fantastic. You have to watch a 30 minute video before each class (3 times a week) but that's basically it for homework in the week. The videos are dense, entertaining, and genuinely enjoyable. This class covers a lot of material, but he makes it easy to succeed! Highly recommend this class and Dr. Archer in general.

Dr. Archer is one of the best professors I have had. He is clearly passionate about the subject and does an amazing job relaying that to the classroom. This class is extremely informative and fun to take part in.

He makes a really easy class really entertaining and engaging. There's virtual lectures as homework with clearly stated review questions. If you can answer those questions in class when called on randomly, you are set. The tests are all multiple choice, and if you study you'll be fine.

The professor is very approachable, although he may appear a little scary in the beginning. He is very dedicated and passionate about the things he teach, which can help make the class be more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Archer is very passionate in the topics of class. He makes you really question "normal" aspects about your life. He is probably my favorite professor at ISU, very considerate and wants you to participate and learn.

Dr. Archer was one of the best professors I've ever had, he's super woke and really makes you question your surroundings and things that seem normal to you. His class is super informative and you really take away a lot.

He tells you from the bat whats to be expected. Hes a great guy and is more then willing to help you out with any problems. By far one of my favorite professors Ive had here at Iowa state. Makes class extremely interesting and informative

The kindest, nicest, and most helpful professor I have ever had. He actually wants you to do good and will help you achieve that. As long as you read the notes and do the practice exams, you will get an A. Iowa State is better off because of professors like Dr. Ghosh and I can only hope I will have him again for another course.
Good class, good prof. Took stats330 online and enjoyed it.

This professor is an absolute sweetheart. He provides lots of examples during lectures (all posted online afterwards) and frequently checks to make sure everyone understands the content. The homework comes from problems in the textbook and aren't super difficult. Exams are pretty easy if you understand lectures, and you can bring a cheat sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I should have gone to class a fair bit more during this time. Don't let yourself get fooled at the beginning, it does get somewhat harder but overall not that bad. Arka is one of the best Professors I have had. He is very reasonable and easy to work with. I liked him a lot. That's about all I have to say, he's a good guy.

The professor spent 15 minutes every day of the first few weeks attempting to figure out names. This is the only professor that has ever had an exam, class and a quiz scheduled on THE SAME DAY which was changed after complaints. Expect to learn the content on your own and not go to lecture, it feels more like elementary school than a college course

This is halfway through the semester and I love the way he teaches. Dr. Ghosh does not require textbooks and instead covers all distributions, their pmf and cdf using intuitive examples and vocabulary during the lectures. The difficulty of the quizzes and exams are on lower end making the course easy to pass for students who just want to get done.
Arka is one of the few professors I've had who took the time to learn everyone's name. He gives plenty of feedback and makes it easy to ask questions surrounding the lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a decent amount of work, but the professor is very caring and has a lot of knowledge about the concepts in the course. He makes sure that each student is following along during lecture and even gets to know everyones name.

Highly recommend for STAT 305. Weekly homework that isn't too bad. Gives out example quizzes that are very similar to the actual quiz. I really enjoy his voice during lecture, very clear and he always seems like he's in a good mood.
If you can, definitely take Stat 105/305 with him. His practice exams are almost identical to the real tests and he is very nice. Would highly recommend him over any other stats professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: He is super nice and he likes to get to know everyone's name in class (even in a lecture). His tests are similar to his practice tests, he explains things well and just overall a really good professor. Only problem is that lecture can be a little boring but other than that, I would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Arka is a great Professor. The tests are pretty much the same as the sample tests he gives with slightly different problems. The final is 40% of the final grade, otherwise a great professor with a pretty easy class.
Arka was a great teacher, and his tests were VERY similar to the sample tests he provided.  The homework is reasonable, and he is more than willing to interact and help his students.  Take his class!

Good professor, encourages participation and thinking with the material, desires for his students to learn the material, and genuinely wants to teach things. Also, he uses a book that is unironically a good read.

This professor's lectures are still used for ANTH 2300. If you are NOT an anthro student, he can be pretty difficult to understand, however his lectures are pretty one-to-one with the quizzes and writings. Not "open book," however, it's an online class and you are not required to schedule through the testing center. Nothing is graded by him.

AM IN 210 was one of the easier classes I took at Iowa State. The exams were really the only things that counted toward the final grade, which were pretty easy since they were open book/note. The textbooks are accessible online in pdf format, so DO NOT buy them through the Iowa State bookstore.
Dr. Arndt, one of the best professors. Not for every mind/brains!

The actual graded assignments are easy because he allows open book and often does take home graded assessments. However, his lectures just don't really make sense. I tried to follow them but I often couldn't, he has a tendency to ramble, and his notes on the board consist of singular words with arrows pointed in various directions. Easy A, though.

He loves what he teaches. His lectures are never boring because he actually goes over the material that he makes you read very well. Sometimes he can be a little confusing only because he gets excited about what he's talking about. Even though participation/discussion matters, there's no pressure. He tells you what he wants, when he wants it.

He's hard to understand because he ALWAYS using big words that nobody EVER uses. You're allowed to use books and notes on tests, but it can still be a little challenging. There's a 5 page paper at one point and a 15 min group presentation+ a 10-15 page paper. However he grades pretty easily. Overall easy class where reading is not neccessary.

Peculiar fellow. An example of something he might say in a lecture is, "So you see, the sort of hierarchical allusion to egalitarianism in this situation has to do with the roles that were implied by the postmodern, existential, caveat that is sort of, embedded within a rather, how do you say, differential adherence to normative influences."

Dr. Arndt was one of the best professors I've ever had. He was clear in his expectations and was very approachable. Getting help from him was very beneficial to my grade. He is just an all-around nice guy. Definitely take his class if you want to learn so much about anthropology and Native American cultures.

Dr. Arenas is an excellent professor. He is a good instructor and does a mix of slides and handwritten examples during class. He gives LOTS of extra credit to the point you can get over a 100% on each exam. He is funny and very caring. I wish he taught more classes!

Great professor. While some of the homework can be challenging, he provides useful feedback. Can get help outside of office hours. Go to lectures to stay on top of exam prep, as he will give out extra credit opportunities. Most of the problems you'll see on exams are very similar to in-class examples. Makes lectures worthwhile and interesting.

Prof. Arenas was great to have, gave a lot of extra credits on every exam during the class and even solved examples which were similar to the exam problems. Go to class, do the homework and attend review sessions and ask questions. He also responds to emails after hours to help you for homework's and has a clear understanding of the content.
Great teacher. Had him in the mornings and he made coming to class worthwhile. Definitely one of my favorite professors/classes at Iowa State

She is not a good professor at all. She was never in class at all, did not provide any feedback, would not show up then email an hour into class saying she was going to be very late or not coming at all. One time even canceling our review that was crucial for developing our design for our final review. HIGHLY ADVISE NOT TO TAKE HER.

I have only been in Anna's studio for a few weeks and everyone in the class is already very frustrated with her. She clearly doesn't prioritize her professor job and has bad time management. Our field trip was horribly planned and very few of our stop were aware that we were coming. She is also hard to listen to because she rambles frequently.

1. shows up to less than 1/3 of classes and cancels them 30 minutes after they start
2. you will have zero grades in canvas ever and will receive your first and only grade when it is final in workday
3. will only respond to questions with “you should know that”
4. never had a syllabus- flying by the seat of her pants
5. doesn't respond to emails

While Anna clearly has a lot of industry experience and is a talented designer, this class felt very disjointed and thrown together. Many of the lectures felt like they were thought of the night before and the assignments were no different- there were many that were talked about, but they were either never posted or posted much later than promised.

Anna and Leila's professional practice class finally gave me some of the more technical knowledge I hoped to get out of my time at ISU. Out of all the classes I've taken here, this may have been one of the most useful ones. The class also had a (very refreshing) low pressure format that focused more on content delivery instead of busy work.
Amazing would recommend for all to take!

Please don't listen to the obviously fake reviews saying she's great. She grades extremely hard, and on the preexam, she asked the most mind-trickling questions that everyone gets wrong. I missed one homework assignment, and my grade dropped 7 percent. She thought people getting a low B was great... Ruined my GPA taking this "easy" class.

By far one of my favorite professors. She is a tough grader but she is also always willing to help if you ask her for it. One of the most approachable professors at Iowa State and doesn't ever talk down to you. I would 100% recommend this course with her.

Lots of Busy Work, She told us that the average of the class was normally a C no matter what, and that she rarely if at all gives A's/High B's. Takes weeks the grade (less than 30 people in the class). No clear syllabus.

I took this class thinking it would be an easy summer class to knock out my marketing credit..WRONG. Tons of busy work with a project where she says you'll get a C if you follow the instructions and have to go above and beyond for anything better. Shes a tough grader while taking weeks to grade stuff with only 20 people being in the class. BAD

Such an amazing professor! Dr.G truly cares about her students and will do anything in her power to help you succeed. This class can be intimidating because of the sales roleplays, but she really does everything she can to make sure you are prepared and confident going into them. I absolutely loved her and would recommend her 100%.
Dr. G is genuinely one of my favorite professors that I have had here at Iowa State. You can tell she genuinely cares about what she is teaching as well as her students.

Dr. G was so nice and truly cares about her students. However, 442 was basically all about group work to do outside of class. When you have 5-6 group members and all of you have jobs outside of class, it makes it nearly impossible to get the extensive amount of work done. Overall, the class was good sales experience, but not great for busy people
She's super sweet and I would 100% take again. A lot/most of the class is group work. Just show up and participate and you'll do great.

Dr. G is a great professor! Her class teaches you so much, and it was one of my favorite classes taken at Iowa State. She truly cares about her students and their success. HIGHLY recommend taking this course with her!

Dr. G is a great professor who cares about her students and their professional development. In her class, you learn the principles of what it takes to be a successful sales manager then get to apply these principles through the simulation. I would highly recommend taking her class if you are interested in sales and/or management!

MKT 442 with Dr. Goreczny is great, I highly recommend taking this course. It counts as part of Iowa State's 'Professional Sales Certificate' which is another thing I recommend pursuing if you are interested in sales! This class is one of the core sales classes in the Ivy CoB and it taught me so much. Fun simulation with an awesome professor!

Dr. Goreczny is a fantastic professor! She really cares about her students and is always there to help you succeed. Interesting class to get the perspective of a sales manager. Highly recommend taking this class with her.

I didn't know what I wanted to do after I graduated. Her class helped, but also meeting her in her office and talking with her after class helped. She really cares about her students. Her class helped my confidence and helped me get through so many interviews. I am now graduating with a great job!

Interesting teaching style, seems to care more about mentioning her PHD and research paper than actually teaching course material. Although, it wouldn't matter if she did given how easy the class is. Easy A but get ready to be called "Y'all" an aggressive amount.

Bastawros is a great and inspirational teacher. He teaches science, not textbook nonsense, and knows what he is talking about. I took him for fracture and it was just an amazing experience. Just attend lectures and enjoy the journey.

One of the least organized professors I have had. Even before Corona break, we were way off track. Decent at explaining in lecture, but speaks above the comprehension of 85% of the students. Has only taught this course once in its entirety. Got mad because so many people emailed asking questions but didn't clarify confusion.

The grad course under him was fairly well. Though tough homeworks, the tests were simple and the final was a project presentation which was a swell option. Really helps out if you need any help both  in and out of the class. Really a great atmosphere during the class though sometimes the subject kinda gets very dry.
Very nice funny guy. He knows a lot of stuff. Care about students. Good professor overall expect sometimes not organized enough

eidetic memory. Go to class. He is one of, if not the most, memorable professor I had in my short higher academic career. He is highly intelligent, and interesting, complex, and intimidating. However, I realized by the end, he really only wants every student to achieve their absolute best, and to learn and explore to their greatest potential.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: READ!!!! Hector Avalos will intimidate half of the class to drop in the first day. If you get past that, he is by far the best professor I've ever had, and I disagree with every one of his views 100%. He comes off as scary and uncaring but will become softer as the class gets more comfortable. Know your stuff and study hard. By far the best classes
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Avalos is a fantastic professor and definitely one of best that I have had at Iowa State. Knows the bible like the back of his hand. Be prepared to read every day as he is fairly demanding. I put more effort into this class than some of my upperclassman level engineering courses. It will be worth it in the end as you will get a lot out of it.

Avalos is an insane professor. As far as textbooks, you only really need the bible. He has an insane memory and will know your name the first day of class. He doesn't use powerpoints and you are expected to take notes as he talks. Honestly the most interest class I've taken at ISU.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Avalos is intimidating at first... scratch that, the whole semester, but he is an amazing professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable about the Bible.I would highly recommend taking his courses, but be prepared to work hard for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Incredibly intimidating at first, but has one of the biggest hearts. Wears sunglasses to every class, tells awful dad jokes, and loves to troll. Read and then read again. . Get ready to know your classmates by their last names. He made me question so many things and for that I will be forever grateful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very intense. Very very smart man though. He could probably read you the entire Bible without looking at it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best professor I ever had in all 4 years at ISU. Hands down. I took 220 as an elective, and it is the only class I recommend to people when they ask. It's hard, and you have to be ready to learn. Have an open mind going in and you will glean a lot from the course. Avalos is an amazing person and educator. Can't say enough about him.

-Offers Extra Credit - Funny dad-like jokes - tests are very hard This class has been by far my favorite class that i have taken at ISU. It was a catalyst to my faith and helped me understand the Bible better in a historical way. Seriously loved this class. Hes intimidating at first, but he will lighten up and make corny jokes. 10/10

Avalos, very knowledgeable. However, his teaching strategy, intimidation, is so futile! He also quizzes you on everything he says & writes on the board(he follows no coherent flow of tactic; basically writes all over the board-whatever pops in his head) If you get it wrong, "10 points off". He turns an enjoyable subject into an academic nightmare.

I don't think I have ever respected a professor as much as I respected him. His knowledge of the Bible is outstanding. Not once was he unable to answer a question. I was expecting a biased course but he gave a multiple viewpoint approach. As long as you behave like a responsible college student and the work, you will enjoy this course.

He is easily the best professor I've had at ISU. Do the readings or it will cost you. But lectures fly by and are filled with interesting information. If you're willing to spend some time and do the work, you'll probably get more out of this class than any other you've taken. Well worth it, in my opinion.

Incredibly intelligent when it comes to the historicity of the Bible, but I found him intimidating. Tests are pretty difficult, but if you study well in advance then you will do fine. I enjoy this topic and loved the biblical readings. I honestly learned so much, but you must study and keep up with the class load. It's a fulfilling course for sure!

He is the most humble person that you will ever meet that he makes a list of people every morning who he thinks he is humble and magically, his name ALWAYS ends up on the top. Dr. Avalos is a professor that is very funny. He likes to troll you if you are a Christian but it will strengthen your faith, if you are one. By the way, he always wins.

My favorite professor I ever had - and that is saying something! If you are interested in the Bible, it would almost be a sin not to take this class - he is a remarkable scholar and person. The class is tough at first but stick with it - it gets much better after the first few weeks. Wish I would have taken Dr. Avalos' Old Testament class too...

I loved this class!  Dr. Avalos is a fascinating professor.  If there is anything you ever wondered about the Bible, this is the class to take.  The class consists of Bible readings and discussion.  I highly recommend studying with this great scholar!

Dr. Avalos is the most knowledgeable professor I have had at ISU. He is very intimidating the first few weeks, but stick with it. I never had a problem with the "bias" other people have mentioned and have never learned more in a class.

I have never met a professor with a more in depth knowledge of his subject. He has never been offensive or demeaning in class. Yes, he is an atheist but he never teaches from only one point of view. His class can be difficult at times since there are a lot of readings. His English is perfect, idk what some of the other people were talking about.

Dr. Avalos is very biased and intelligent. He does provide more than one viewpoint, however he seems to miss or mistake obvious possible explanations about the materials (Bible.) Whether he does this intentionally, or on purpose it is hard to say. I feel he is a good person, but I feel bad for him because he seems to harbor a great anger towards some things that happened during his childhood church experience. Told us stories that confirmed his bitter recall of those times. Has a good heart tho.
Great life-changing professor! uuuhhh... if you don't take this class, you are doing a great misdeed to yourself! This is what you would hope for as a dreamer, and get it at ISU.

Great Professor, he does a great job of telling all views of an issue or subject. While not pointing out which one is "the correct" view. This leads people to see him as anti-religion. I know that during my time in his class I was witness to many people gaining a broader view of the bible.
He's really scary the first few weeks, but that's only to scare off the cats that don't want to be there. His classes are totally worth it in the end.

I took Intro, New & Old testament classes from Dr. Avalos.  He is very smart, and has most of the Bible memorized.  Even on the first day he has everyones name memorized.  Class is INCREDIBLY easy.  There are two tests and both are simple.  He is EXTREMELY biased against all religion, but if you know that going in, he makes you think.
This was my favorite class. He really has the bible memorized! Class always keeps you on your toes, but if you do the readings before class your fine. Take this class if you can!
much like everyone else he is spectacularly objective in his teaching and helps you become a scholar

He came in on the first day and took attendance from memory, he does not grade students based on their beliefs, he is able to convincingly argue any side of any argument, really does have the entire bible memorized.  If anyone wants to argue with him, they'd better know absolutely everything about everything.

New Testament class- Always interesting, never a dull moment in the class, he lets the students decide what much of the discussion will be about and is always up for answering questions. Very approachable and personable. Textbooks arent used but there is a lot of reading from the bible and different works.

Probably the smartest professor I've had at ISU.  He makes you think critically about the Bible and understand the different viewpoints.  Reading takes up time, and class participation is required, but there isn't much homework outside of readings of the Bible.  He gives a midterm & final with a study guide, which I like.  Class is never boring!

Dr. Avalos is an incredible instructor. He demands the attention of his students every moment and expects their full participation; in exchange, class is never boring. Dr. Avalos's English is perfect and he speaks very clearly.  His mastery of the languages of the original biblical texts allowed us greater understanding and overall comprehension.

An impressive scholar. He teaches a hard subject with much to digest. Someone mentioned he is hard to understand. He is from Mexico and Spanish is his first language but he also speaks very clear English, Hebrew and Greek, which adds to his credentials as a Biblical Scholar. He encourages critical interpretation which makes many uncomfortable.

Very stimulating style of class - seminar. He is biased, but does make students think about many different positions. The course is worth taking, but should be viewed with a critical eye. One of the best teachers I took at Iowa State

claims to be valid because he is "impartial" to subject material, yet clearly, and vocally, is against or unfavorable toward material presented.  Professor Avalos has a distinct pre-suppostion that orders his manner of teaching, yet refuses to recognize his own bias.
He has all the wrong answers to all the right questions.
His broken english does nothing to strengthen his typically convoluted arguments. Class is ridiculously easy, however, if one has been exposed to works such as Atheism for Dummies.
