Well, he gave the Honors Seminar the same test as his 300 level relgion course.  Interestingly, I got an A with 1 hour of review immediately before the test.  However, people in his real class faired far less well.  Beware the red ink if you don't work.

Very intelligent, has whole Bible memorized.  Awkward that he is an atheist, but still a very informative class.  Tries to come off as intimidating, but class really is not too difficult as long as you keep up and read the material every day.

He doesn't teach at all and half the time you can not even understand him because he is just babbling and making zero sense. He moves on even when no one knows what he is talking about and then the icing on top is he just hands us a packet with content we did not even cover to complete by the end of class.
Class was pretty easy, nothing to complain about was pretty mediocre overall.
Dudes just not a good person in my opinion, jumped to conclusions about work and wasn't very nice
David runs the PHYS 221 and 222 Labs, the Labs are completely useless, they serve no purpose and are a waste of time and money, however he is an amazing person.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While he is not very good at lecturing, (very little student interaction) he makes terrific use of in-class problems that makes the homework MUCH easier to do.  He is friendly and more than willing to answer any questions asked (and is quite knowledgeable).

Lecture is nearly worthless. Read the textbook and go to the help room/SI to figure out the homework. Study the old tests for exam help. LOTS of material covered but exams ended up being slightly more straight-forward than the homework, thankfully.
Without a doubt, having this professor will make you doing well in his class near impossible.  In my opinion, instead of going to his lectures, read the book and save your self from a waste of time.
Super Canadian physicist destined to weed out all sorts of monkeys in Physics 221 by doing Jedi mind-tricks. Oh Canada!
GOOD GOD. RUN.

This teacher is utterly useless. His lectures, apart from being boring yawn-fests are not related to the exams and finals whatsoever. I haven't stayed awake in class for the last three weeks so obviously I'm not gonna do well on the tests! He also assigns completely useless homework.

He was a pretty good prof. He's the stereotypical physicist. He explained the stuff pretty clearly I thought. My advice: study a lot and don't miss any lectures so you don't fall behind. Also, do the tests in the old-exam archive and you'll do fine on the real ones. They don't change much in style from year to year. Its a fun class if you keep up.

Terrible teacher.  His lectures are aweful and so are the tests. The only good part about him is his video on youtube.  Other than that take the class from Paula, she's much better and its well worth the switch.
By far the worst teacher I ever had. I was planning on minoring in Physics until I took this class.
RUN. JUST RUN.
He knows physics very well, he just can't communicate it. Physics as a class is very hard, be warned.
He does a lot of odd motions and is basically horrible at his job.

Aside from the homework and quizes being utterly useless for exam prep, the lectures being pointless, and the exams making you feel like a deer in the headlights, Attwood is (insert random positive comment).

Definitely one of the worst teachers I have ever experienced. He can't explain anything without stumbling over himself or messing up what he's trying to say. He overworks examples in lecture, wasting time and getting behind the other lecturer. He is totally unqualified. I don't understand why people think he is a "smart guy." He is not.
A total idiot. Going to his class is a total waste of time. I seriously haven't gone to class for a month because it would just be waking up to laugh at his idiocy. Try to get Paula AT ALL COSTS.
Specializes in failing students. Core engineering class, and I didn't learn a thing from it.
canada's finest

Gives out a ton of homework...but what do you expect 221 is a weed out class. Tests weren't that bad, except for the final which was ridiculous. One of the worst lectures I went to. Other than clicker points and laughing at him occasionally, lectures are pointless.

Assigns insanely hard homework and the tests are impossible the only way it is possible to pass is the huge curve of 600 out of 1000 points is all you need to pass with a C- and usually he curves 10-20 more points at the end.
Just plain awful!
Seriously painful to sit through the lectures.  WebCT homework was fine, but his weekly written assignments were so hard even his TA's couldn't solve them half the time.
I do not recommend taking his class.  He is not a good teacher at all. Take Professor Herrera-Siklody's lectures...
Terrible professor.  Wouldn't recommend to anyone taking.  Couldn't explain questions if asked.  Incredibly smart person, no sense of teaching.

If you want to be an engineer, get ready to be weeded out.  This class sucks from day one.  You lose a ton of sleep and weekend time to get straight A's and B's on all the homework & quizzes, only to get buried alive by two IMPOSSIBLE unit tests that carry all the weight of your overall grade!  Take physics somewhere else!  YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!
Web Ct was horrable and the test were horribly hard
Bad, reminds me of Bill from king of the hill.  Likes to make ambiguous gestures.

The way he flails his arms about in lectures can be distracting.His weekly homeworks that he makes up are completely pointless and most of the time completely irrelevant to the task at hand. 85% of them were just difficult busy-work. His redemption comes in the form of his tests which are not as difficult as they could be. Keep up and you'll be fin

The lectures could be kind of boring, and the weekly written homeworks were just plain scary, but you learn a lot -- and he makes non-evil exams, especially the final. He obviously cares about physics, and it shows. Very helpful on the WebCT forums.
I dont like this class..

A professor in every sense of the word. He explains nothing, does no examples in class and doesn't not describe where he got equations from. He spits out equations, does some lame physical representations, and says we better un-confuse ourselves before the test.
Atwood is an ok prof, but his lectures are boring.  He belabors the obvious and overexplains examples, so half his lecture is time for sudoku. Also, his homework problems are very difficult.
does this guy think that running through prefab powerpoints is a substitute for real teaching?!!!
Very unclear, has a lot of "trick" questions.

when i took his class a year ago he was pretty good. dont understand why he is getting bad reviews recently. he does good job keeping up with students on webct and his powerpoint lectures are very helpful. he does good job summarizing things u need to know for each chapter.
Get out of there before he eats you alive!!!!!!!
very unclear on explaining concepts

Very quirky lecturer, almost to the point of distracting from the material.  Homework was mostly irrelevant challenge problems with solutions that no college freshman could hope to arrive at within a reasonable amount of time.  Tests got progressively harder, with the final averaging a failing score with no curve.  Incredibly worthless professor.
I didn't learn much from the class....
No Comments
Poor at communicating to students

Poor lecturer.  Assigns homework that is very hard and has nothing to do with the class.  Wrote a final that averaged under 50% and didn't curve.  Is sometimes helpful on the messageboard, but more often he confuses.  Avoid if you can.  Paula Hererra was a much better leacturer if you can get her.
He assigns extremely difficult, irrevelant homework and his tests are unfair
just a weird ol man

Homework was very hard, and the tests were a nightmare. However, it was his first time teaching, and he was very helpful and trying to improve. He should get better from now on. He's a nice guy, but not the best prof yet.

Dr. Atwood's lectures usually put me to sleep, and the homework and tests were difficult, but the quizzes and prelabs being online scored lots of points with me.  Plus, he was on WebCT all night it seemed answering questions.  Overall, a fairly good teacher.
Good teacher, very dedicated, always had quizzes and current posts online.  Seemed like a nice guy, even had a physics party last semester.  Immediately responds to your questions on WebCT.
His tests are hard, but he curves pretty fair.  Covers material pretty good.  His test questions are harder than any other questions, homework, group problems, etc....
Very neurotic wonderful guy. He really cares about his students. Also he is very passionate about physics.
Very nice, smart, helpful guy.  Very quick when answering questions; somewhat interesting lectures. Great overall
Needs to go to speech class to learn how to speak in front of people.  I got distracted from all the um's and a's.  He seems to know his physics though.
No Comments
He is one cool nerd. You gotta love this guy! He does have funny body language.

This guy is definitely Canadian.  Has very strange body language but it is hilarious to watch him in lecture.  Loves physics and is very entertaining about it.  Tests are fairly harder than homework problems and such.  He is a genius man!

I think he really loves physics and tries to make it exciting for the students.  However, I feel the tests are not quite represntative of the homework and such.  This could be improved on a bit.  Other than that, a pretty cool guy.
He is some kind of super nerd from the other dimension. Very knowledgeable about physics in general. Very weird in many ways... He gotta be Canadian.
Makes Physics Interesting
Despite English being my least favorite subject, he found a way to make coming to class always fun and engaging. Gave lots of feedback for writing assignments and made in class activities enjoyable.

Knowledgeable guy, very helpful with assignments when you ask, very flexible with the needs of students, and forgiving for most late work (I wouldn't try turning in major papers late, though). Overall a great guy and will help you out if you seek it.
Very helpful, very knowledgeable, and an easy grader. Everything is very clear to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I like him a lot as a professor he guides you threw all the assignments and doesn't throw it at you he also encourages students to ask for help and feedback so our assignment is best to our abilities
Great programming professor. Willing to go over same content over and over if you still have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Would not recommend at all. She gives assignments a week before she teaches the content of the assignment. Doesn't really consider the situation of the students, will not hesitate to give the entire class a 0 if she suspects malicious activity in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: helpful and kindness. Come to her office instead of asking TA.

She's a very good programming teacher! She explains things very well and is willing to answer all of your questions. If you have any experience with programming or python in general, this class should be a breeze. If you have no programming experience, you'll be fine as long as you show up to class and take notes. Overall great programming teacher!

I have done java before but not python. Had difficulty catching up with material because I was late to add the class. She was very helpful, specially one to one. She also had sound java knowledge which helped me in smooth transition between the two languages.
Grades fairly. Lectures are either OK or exceptional. Recorded lectures makes it easy when I cannot attend class.

Poor lecturer - I learned more form the textbook.  He's clearly here for research.  To top it off he is egotistical and hates being wrong; he would rather argue until failure than admit he might not be right.

Dry lectures, poor hand writing on 100% of class notes, tough to understand, and the lectures do not align with homework, nor does the homework align with the exams. A quizzes are also 2 days long, 50 min each and worth 25% of your grade; some quiz... I recommend taking the other section, even if the curve saves you.
Horrible handwriting, boring lectures, ridiculous tests. Overall a terrible teacher.

Attinger is a good teacher, you just have to give him a chance. Sometimes, he's much more into proofs rather than concepts, which I don't prefer, but if you go talk to him, he's very helpful. He's also hilarious, and an interesting person. He also is very generous in his final curve of the class. Read the textbook and study, you'll be fine.

I have no idea what the rest of the people on here are basing their opinions on, Dr Attinger was easily the best teacher I've had at Iowa State. I've learned a ton from him and I'm honestly hoping I'll be able to take more courses under him! Take his class if you want to have the elegance of fluid mechanics presented to you as it is.

Attinger definitely makes you work hard, but if you do the homework and attend class regularly you can do well. He set's the class average at a B and then a standard deviation above is an A. Overall I think he is a very good professor - one of the best ones I have had in college.

The worst professor ever and all my classmates agree, very knowledgeable but lacks basic teaching skills, he doesn’t know how to explain the material at all. His style is unpredictable, confusing, and very rude and distracting and will get off topic for any reason! He is more of a researcher than a teacher! Avoid his class!!

I was warned not to take this class in Spring because he teaches it.After completing my BSME degree I can say this was the worst professor in the M.E. department. I failed every test (so did the class average) so the class was curved drastically. Lectures were worthless as Attinger only complicates material. I retook 335, LEARNED it, and got an A.

I took Fluids with Attinger last spring and it was a great class. Yes,it is a hard class but this is a junior level ME class. Attinger is a great teacher who is really good at laying things out sequentially and explaining where the equations come from. Homeworks and exams are tough, but if you study what he says will be on the exam, you'll be fine.

Dr. Attinger has to be one of my  most despised professors of the last 8 years. He spent far too much time in theory and almost none in real world application. He's a research prof and blatantly told us he was excited for the semester to be over so that he could get back to his research. I learned absolutely nothing from the course.

I really appreciated Professor Attinger. He was difficult but provided a great way to learn. The homework were difficult and graded harshly they provided helpful practice for the tests. The tests were very difficult but the average is always a B. Work hard, study hard and fluids will be a very interesting class.

His semester started off a little rough, but that is because he is a new professor. As the semester went on, his grading eased, his explanations of topics got more in-depth, and he worked more example problems into lecture.

This guy spent way to much time going over the theory and not enough on working out problems. Homeworks are graded harshly and discourage students from even attempting them cause most likely you only get half the points at best. Exams are ridiculously hard, overall the class was made harder than it needed to be.

This guy is literally one of the worst professors I have ever had. On the first day, he told us that he “demands respect.” Well unfortunately, he doesn’t deserve any. He’s an awful teacher and makes things more difficult than they need to be. His grading policies are inconsistent and change from week to week. I would not reccomend him to anyone.

I had Dr. Awino previously for CHEM 177 and he was not my favorite, so I was unsure of how CHEM 331 would be with him. However, Awino is much more passionate about organic chemistry and it shows in his teaching. He has a thorough understanding of the material and wants to see his students succeed. Great professor for CHEM 331!

I had to take multiple courses with Professor Awino and wished I had never had to take a class with him. His accent is very hard to understand, and I'm pretty sure he doesn't know what he is talking about half the time. When people asked questions, he would talk in circles and contradict himself, leaving everyone much more confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chemistry is anything but easy here at Iowa State especially the ACS final that Dr. Awino gives at the end. His extra credit saved me and allowed me to end with a decent grade but this class definitely challenged me. Although Dr. Awino knows his stuff, his accent makes him hard to understand at times and his lectures were hard to follow.

Dr. Awino may not be the best lecturer in the world, but he does want his students to succeed. The exams weren't very difficult as were very similar to the practice exams in canvas, which helped to know what material would be on exams. He offers extra credit, curves grades(an A was above 91% and an F was below 45%) and bumps grades up.

Nice man, not so good prof. I recommend either having previous AP Chemistry experience or taking with another prof. He would circle things on his slideshows so much that not only could you not see what he was circling but, he also wouldn't explain the topics. Hopefully, your recitation TA is good at explaining the topics or you might struggle.

He seems nice (ish), but he is genuinely terrible at teaching the material. He will not teach, he just reads the slides and circles a lot of things and then is shocked when everyone does terrible on exams. He is also incredibly hard to understand and lectures were ABSOLUTELY miserable. Save yourself a semester of pain and take a different prof.

Dr. Awino stuggled to explain problems in a way the was easy to understand and if you aren't paying close attention during the lecture, it's easy to get lost, especially when he is working out problems. If you are someone who likes to write out all their notes, I would suggest writing the skeleton notes out before class.

Average to good professor. In 177 lectures aren't mandatory, but they're good to go to. The only lecture I had trouble with was one about sigma and pi bonds, usually he's good at walking through example problems and explaining concepts. It can be difficult to understand him at times though, his microphone setup often had problems. Not much homework

Don't get me wrong he is a nice guy, but an awful teacher. People complain about not being able to understand him but if you focus you can make out what he is saying. However, he often doesn't explain what he is doing or doesn't explain things very well, so you are left confused. My TA helped tons so hope for a good TA and you should be fine.

Awino is one of the worst professors I have ever had. My friend died and I wanted to go to her visitation which was at the same time as one of the exams. He told me that I should've notified him sooner.... sorry I couldn't plan when my friend died. He basically talked in circles at lecture; at 1/2 semester, I joined Winter's Canvas course.

Dr. Awino isn't a great lecturer and exams are very hard. Exam review sessions with the TA were usually more helpful. Homework could be excessively long toward the end of the semester. If you didn't take any sort of advanced chemistry classes in high school, good luck.

Was not a good professor. Tests were very difficult and averages were below 50%. Lectures did not help and barely went off the PowerPoint. Exam reviews would go over one thing and the actual exam would be completely different.

I took 331 with Winter and HATED IT. Awino was much better at teaching. Make flashcards of the reagents from the slides and you'll be able to do 70% of the test easily. Sporadic tophat, exams are pretty straightforward for ochem 2. If you didn't do great in 331 don't worry you don't use any of that info and tests are less tricky. No adaptives!

Chem 331 with Awino was one of the worst experiences I have had with college so far. He does seem like a kind person, but he is not a great teacher. He never seems to have a lesson plan and teaches the most simple and basic problems. Once you get to the tests you feel like something completely different. I wish I could write more. So frustrating!

After coming from chem 331 with Winter, Awino made 332 a walk in the park. The exams were all very straightforward. As long as you look at his lectures and review old exams you will end with an A. Each exam had extra credit on it, which made it easy to get a good grade in the class.

Chemistry is hard but Professor Awino is a genuinely nice person. His slides are well organized and easy to follow. Attending his virtual lecture sessions and reviewing his previous exams helped me do better.

Dr. Awino is pretty hard to understand as it is, but online with his poor internet makes it basically impossible. He also does not directly answer questions, but he'll tell you where to look. If you don't find the answer after looking where he tells you I wouldn't be surprised. Thank God this class was open notes and open Google when I took it.

Awino is a far better person than he is a teacher. It may just be due to a busy life, but 177 lectures seemed to be jumbled with incorrect answers and tended to be cut short by the class time. Don't switch out of his 177 if ya have him (he is very kind and will cut down tests on missed content) but do be wary that it may be more work on your end.
Tests are difficult but go of the mill for ochem. You could do much worse. With work doing well is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Awino made sure the course was clear and fully functioning when we switched from face-to-face to the online course delivery during COVID-19.
His lecture notes are easy to follow.
WHO IN THE WORLD HAS 60% OF AN OCHEM PAPER ON TOPHAT???? HIM.

Awino is a really great guy, hes kind, but he just isnt a great teacher. He moves through lecture really slowly and it causes you to fall behind where you should be at. There were a couple weeks where the content of lab was ahead of what had been taught in lecture because he moves slow and messes up example problems in lecture

He is not very good at teaching. He often explains the easier concepts and speeds through the difficult ones. Sometimes it seemed like he didn't know what he was talking about. Lecture was only useful for tophat. SI and previous exams were the most useful for exams.

I stopped listening to his lectures after the first two weeks. He makes mistakes on problems and I get confused - instead I watched YouTube chem videos (highly recommend). He is a kind and caring prof, but I didn't click with his teaching style. Always go to class, he sporadically does TopHat quizzes.

Thick accent but you will get used to it - he is very knowledgable and works out lots of practice problems in class. Gives extra credit for answering questions during class. Tophat is for accuracy!! tests are difficult but he works through examples in class, posts slides, and really wants you to succeed. hard class, won't lie about that!

If you are a student who struggles with Chemistry, this professor may not be for you. Awino is very knowledgeable about what he teaches, however he is not effective in teaching it to others. It has nothing to do with his accent, just his teaching style. Try to attend every lecture, in case he throws in a random online quiz. Do every assignment.

Tests are all multiple choice with plenty of extra credit given throughout the semester. Awino has got some cringy chemist and dad jokes but makes the classes enjoyable. Randomly plays short videos before class like AFV, fail compilations, and Mickey Mouse clubhouse once! Class wasnt too difficult but requires effort. Not a lot of homework either.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chemistry is traditionally a pretty difficult concept to grasp, especially if the last time you took a chemistry course was in high school. Awino is kinda difficult to understand, and he doesn't really explain difficult concepts well, so it is very easy to get lost. Tests weren't too hard if you go to the SI exam reviews but prepare to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Here's how to do well in Awino's chem332: Go to class mainly for tophat. Use the slides he uses and memorize them. That's it. Make flashcards of all the rxns on the slides and study study study. Don't trust notes taken in class because he messes up too much during class for them to be trusted. Trust the slides. They're just from the text anyways

The class overall was very simple, there wasn't much homework and all of the exams were multiple choice. However, Dr. Awino isn't a very great professor, he doesn't do a great job at explaining the complex topics in class. He will also skip over things which come back later to be very important.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Chemistry is just hard in general and it does not make it better when you cannot really understand your professor. He tries to make it understanding, but he flies through the slides like he is racing and many of us our lost on the last slide. Exams are pretty hard but SI sessions and practicing previous exams saved my butt. You have to work hard
Best professor Ive had for a science course, tests are fair and all multiple choice. Youre lucky if you get Awino instead of another Professor because it will make your life so much easier

He teaches you the basic things during lecture and then gives recitation quizzes that are a lot harder. Then on the tests there are questions that literally could be either one or its about something he skimmed over. Recommend going to SI sessions and getting a tutor. He likes to confuse you on tests so be prepared. Not a good experience for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor! thick accent, hard to understand at first but you'll adapt! uses McGraw Hill Connect for homework assignments, extra credit for answering questions in class, tophat for points. solves many problems in class, lectures are highly useful. night exams but he attends and sometimes helps answer questions! hard class, but he's very nice
Absolute comedian. Mad man. Cracks up at his own terrible dad jokes. Local legend. Truly deserving of the full 5 stars.
Good lecture notes, solves many problems in class.
Contracted the course for Honors. He is friendly and inspiring.
Lectures are easy to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Friendly, open minded, and easy to approach.
Had him for CHEM 177 as well. Not very friendly in one-on-one conversations. Is not accommodating, so don't be sick on the day of a test.
Awino holds review sessions before the exam that are really, really helpful. He is a good teacher, but I also read the textbook and did a lot of practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Awino is great. I'm currently taking chem 331 as a summer class and he genuinely cares about his students. He does confuse himself in class sometimes. He does have an accent, but it was still easy to understand and did not hinder my learning. He makes fair tests and grades super fast. Really nice guy, will always help if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Gives good advise on how to study organic chemistry
Prof. Awino is the best teacher I have had for organic chemistry. He explains the concepts in a way that is easy to understand.

If you have little to no chemistry knowledge, this is not the teacher for you. There were many occasions where the information he provided was wrong, but corrected on the test. Very confusing. Did not learn anything useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I was really scared of organic chemistry before enrolling into this class. I however liked the way Professor Awino presented the material in class by solving problems on the board.

Hard to understand, unclear grading scale and useless office hours. He claims he won't change your grade in the interest of "consistency" yet you can have the same answer as your neighbor and get 50% less credit. Do not go to his office hours he will try his hardest to belittle you for not having a Master's in Chemistry and perfect understanding.
Poor teacher, hard to understand, doesnt have students best interest in mind, doesnt cover all needed material- switch your section while you can
He curves the grades and means well for his students.

Never take Dr. Awino. Accent is very thick, understandable but handwriting is also difficult. Is very condescending & laughs at students when asking ?'s. Lectures are repetitive and whole chapter never covered. Doesn't allow makeup tests which other professor does -UNFAIR. Stupid hard recitation quizzes. Would NEVER recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Solves relevant problems during lectures, appreciates class participation by offering generous extra credit, and provides good notes that are easy to follow.

Very responsive to questions that you may have, always available for questions. Sometimes, he won't give you an answer to your question because he wants you to figure it out yourself. That can be frustrating. But would recommend for o chem.

Dr. Awino is an awesome prof. This is my second time taking OChem, I got a C+ the first time and finished with a 98% with Awino. His test questions are straight out of lecture and from the chapter packets he posts online. If you review his chapter outlines and lecture material you're golden. He is very approachable and willing to help!

Took this class in the summer and Prof. Awino did all his notes on the board (although he also posted a handout on Canvas after the chapter was completed). He explained the concepts really well. The course is hard with lots of material to cover. By attending Prof. Awinos lectures, I was able to understand the synthesis in a better way.

Awino presents information he doesn't teach it. Be prepared to have to re-go through his slides and teach yourself. I would recommend reading the textbook and studying with others. He is very bad at explaining any questions you may have and is impossible to meet with outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Awino is a good professor who expects a lot from his students. It definitely helps to read the book in my opinion, as his lectures are basically supplemental material from the book. He expects a lot from his students in class and expects you to remember your CHEM 331. His tests aren't ridiculously hard, the class just takes a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Awino is such a nice guy and a good professor. Ochem 2 is definitely not easy, and he knew that. He did his best to make the class manageable, and you could tell that he genuinely cared about his students.

Prof. Awino provides well organized notes. He expects you to read them before coming to class. Overall a nice professor and made the course a lot easier than I thought before I started this class. Beware of pop quizzes that are directly from what is discussed in class.
Chem is a difficult class, and Awino was difficult to understand, which led to increased difficulty in the class. I sometimes felt like Awino wasn't even sure what he was supposed to be teaching.

Awino is unqualified to teach Organic Chem 2. While I DID WELL in the class, he does not have the ability or knowledge to explain the concepts and proficiently teach this subject. You must show up to class for top hat, he does posts slides, but clicks through them with lacking explanations. Therefore use the book it is good, and teach yourself.

Dr. Awino is a kind and caring person. He tries to get everyone involved in the lectures (even though the class is the hardest thing ever) and is supportive and polite if (when) you get the answer wrong in class. He's super busy though, so if you need extra help get a tutor. Good professor, super hard class.

The lecture for this class wasn't very helpful to me. A lot of the information covered in class was straight out of the book. The first test was stupid easy, the second was impossible, and the third was actually sensibly written. He gives the impression that he still has a lot to learn about teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a bit hard to understand in lectures, especially from the back, and goes a bit fast in lectures. However, he covers almost everything you need to know in them and lets you know what you need to memorize/practice. Had 5 total exams with one being optional. Exams were multiple choice heavy with some short answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Awino is very helpful and accessible outside class hours. He took time to teach me chemistry. We met at least once every two weeks in his office where he taught me how to intepret and understand chemistry concepts. I am very proud that it paid off at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Awino is a little hard to understand because of his accent. I did not feel like we covered important topics thoroughly in class. Online textbook isn't really needed, but does have good practice problems. Lots of quizzes for the course and you have the option to retake a test to get a better grade. Awino also curves certain tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Awino did a great job teaching the material. The recitation quizzes were easy, and many exam questions are covered in class. He is also very friendly when grading them. Hand-writing is not an issue, and his accent is not thick, and it is easy to understand what he is saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Awino was a great professor and made lecture enjoyable with his quirky sense of humor. His tests were not too difficult and I was able to get a good grade by attending class and some SI sessions. I would say he is a rather easy grader and would highly recommend him.

Awino was a great professor. Tests were somewhat tough but if you study well enough you will do fine. Most exam questions come from tophat questions, recitation quizzes or in class examples. There is online homework assigned that isn't too difficult. Some exams were curved based on average scores. Exam's are 400 of the 600 points available in class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Awino is a very caring person but he is not the best lecturer. Personally chemistry is not my strong suit and I ended up dropping but this was not his fault. The assigned homework is a lot but it really helps to understand and practice the material. The recitation quizzes were difficult. Even from the front I could never read his handwriting.

Dr. Awino is a very sweet and caring professor. He does have a heavy accent, which can make it hard to understand him sometimes, but you will adapt. Overall, the class can get hard and overwhelming, but if you look over the slides he posts online and form a study group, you will be fine. Don't fall behind!!

Awino is nice, he has an accent but it's usually not hard to understand him. What he teaches is hard to understand sometimes because he doesn't thoroughly explain. Lectures are helpful and he takes attendance through TopHat. Overall, it was okay. Better than some of the other chemistry professors I've heard.

You can tell Awino cares a lot about his students and he wants you all to succeed. Although his lecture aren't the best, if you go to class and answer the top hats he literally gives you the answer. We told him our recitation quizzes were too challenging so he made them easier (not to mention the quiz questions came right from the book).
Does a good job of modifying class to fit student needs, not the best lecturer / explaining difficult topics.

Awino isn't the best at lecturing but he is very caring about his students and wants us all do well in the class. He is always willing to answer questions and he is willing to help us get an A in the class.

As long as you do the work on your own and understand general chemistry you'll do well in his class. His accent is a little hard to understand most of the time, but you'll get used to it over the semester. Make sure you ask questions and do all the homework and TopHat questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The course itself is tough and Prof. Awino makes it even harder by expecting us to read ahead of time and solve online homework assignments. However, the hint provided for every question is helpful. Its also easy to make up any lost points through extra credit which he provides almost on every weekly quiz.

He wants students to answer questions and problems which doesn't work well in a large lecture hall. I wish he would teach material in his lectures instead of expecting us to have read the chapter in the book before class. Overall, if you can teach yourself chemistry and do the end of chapter problems in the textbook, you can pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Literally anytime someone asks him a question he makes someone else in the class answer it. Most of the time nobody knows, so lots of time is wasted. He doesn't think you can be successful unless you work in groups, even if you prefer to work alone. If you get a question wrong on tophat or dont understand a concept he tries to make you feel stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: during pop quizzes, he walks around and helps with problem solving. Also encourages people to work in groups
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's hard to understand, and rushes through the material to get it all done in time. Barely goes over examples in class. Lots of homework, quizzes and tests are hard. Basically you'll need to teach yourself chemistry, the lectures are pretty useless but they are mandatory. Switch professors if you get him. He is a good person and friendly though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He doesn't care if you're learning or not all that matters to him is getting through all of the subject material. Get ready to teach yourself chemistry.

Prof. Awino is knowledgeable and highly respected in class due to the way he responds to each student needs. He accompanies every concept he explains by a sample exercise problem and then involves the class by inviting one of us willing to come forward to lead the rest in finding a solution. Active participation in class is something he values.
My man here is the best. A little hard to understand with his accent, and he kind of skips around during lectures, but he is a great guy and will try to help you as best as he can.

No ME professor wants to teach this course and their interest in the course will affect the students interest in the course or the major. He is a very tough grader and has little interest in the students success. He just goes through the physics problems and the MATLAB on PowerPoint slides and does not explain anything. I loathe this class and him.

No professor wants to teach the class. He's smart, but he's not very good about transferring his knowledge to students. I got an A, but it wasn't easy. I hate the class, but the professor didn't help.
Not very helpful in lecture, rambles about his work with NASA, and doesn't give clear solutions to problems.  I'd probably switch classes if I saw him as the professor again.
very hard to understand. not sure what he is saying. confused by his words, strange vocab and hard words. smart guy though

Not helpful at the least. Extremely hard to understand due to his accent. Quizzes frequently on material that was never covered or discussed. Also does not follow his own syllabus. Easily one of the worst teachers I've ever had the displeasure of being assigned to.
Does not teach at all. Reads of a power point to students who are just learning MATLAB. Doesn't explain anything. Shows zero interest in the students.

Class was not structured very well. It went very slow and seemed to beat the dead horse with the basics then sped up quite rapidly at the end to cram in the advanced material. Professor seemed to busy with research to put any time into the class and showed up unprepared mroe often than not.
Bad professor.  Does not teach, which is bad because the material is hard.  Best days of class were when he was gone and the TA sub'ed.

Terrible.  This class is useless, the professor isn't interested in teaching and dodges out when I went to office for help.  The lab has nothing to do with the lecture.  No exaggeration, this is the worst engineering class I've ever taken

Now that I have completed my math degree, I reflect on my professors and can easily say that Dr. Athreya was the best professor I had at Iowa State.  He was able to make the mathematics comprehendible to us and his purposes and practices were clear and consistent.  Compared to some of his colleagues, Dr. Athreya is superman!!!
The best math professor that I have ever taken a course from.  He is excellent, thorough and well spoken.  He explained Diff EQ with ease.

Prof Athreya is a bomb teacher, I really didn't understand anything about Calc 3, but then again the class was terribly set up with 3 teachers and Dr. Athreya being our final one, if he would've taught the class all the way through I would have done great, but the curve was great, I received a 72 on the final and still got an A- in the class!GREAT!
No Comments
Hard to understand at first, but you get use to it. Class is fairly easy if you are good at math. Easy compared to other diffy Q profs.

She was known as the workout nazi by my class. After a week you will definitely be referring to her as "my pain in the a%& 258 professor". The class is always taught by her and a grad student ALWAYS pick the grad student, they are usually pretty chill
She is a great teacher. Great personality and very helpful.
No Comments
Not a very hard class but you still need to show up and pay attention. Besides it isn't hard to motivate yourself to come and listen to this babe.
258 is not a hard class but you have to make sure you show up because alot of what you learn is in class and makes up the test. Its easy if u know something about fitness and health.
No Comments

Well she certainly sets a good example in regards to fitness.  258 is easy if you just show up and do what you are supposed to.  259 is harder since you have to know a lot about weight lifting and fitness instruction.
Even though this is a 100 level class, it can be challenging. She keeps your interest throughout the entire semester and is very helpful any time you need her.

Joe seems like a really nice guy, but he is not a good professor. His exams were extremely difficult and included material that we either never talked about or discussed very little. Each exam was 200 points and had like 30 questions. The grading scale itself makes it feel like you are set up for failure from the beginning.

joe was an ok professor. you could tell he really enjoyed the subject, but he was very bad at conveying it. his tests were extremely hard, and he even tells u to read the textbook. too bad the textbook doesn't even help or correlate to what he's talking about at all. exams 200 points, each question worth 5 pts. truly a class set up for failure
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Test and homework were extremely difficult, often covering things that were footnotes in lecture. Tests were 35 questions worth 200 points. The only extra credit offered was through TopHat questions during class, which you had to get right to receive points for

Really nice and experienced professor who explains concepts in an easy, straightforward manner. A lot of the course content is through video tutorials, while in-class time is for showing examples and getting help on projects. Projects are quite fun, and he gives a lot of creative freedom. Easy to talk to, very chill guy.

One of the best classes I've taken at ISU. He doesn't talk a lot in class since we watch tutorial videos (he made them himself) and you just ask him questions in person as needed. Even without him teaching a lot hands on, I still learned a lot from this professor. I've even decided to take more 3D modeling courses next semester.
Austin is a very understanding professor with knowledge in many different areas of digital media. He gives good advice on workflow, sound design, pretty much any Adobe program, and 3D software.
Exams are online and open for a week, they are also open-book book open-note. Excellent teacher, very nice. Some labs were canceled do to weather.

I thought this class was very interesting and Peggy is very easygoing as long as you do what you are supposed to be doing. The lectures were detailed and everything from the quizzes/tests came straight from the material.
Like two quizzes per week but if you attend lab, they are very easy. Every time you attend lab, it was extra credit so that was pretty sweet.

He was a great professor and I really enjoyed his class. He also gave great feedback on homework and was accessible for questions. This class wasn't super difficult as long as you paid attention in class and took notes.
If you email him, don't expect to get a response. I had to reach out to his department to get him to reply to my emails. The class is pretty easy but this professor is terrible at communicating.
I enjoyed this class with Dr. Mendoca and felt that I learned a lot for food science. Exams were easy because Dr. Mendoca gives exactly what is on the exam which is nice.

Mendonca's lectures consisted of him mainly reading off the slides which can be tedious after a bit. I would still recommend showing up because he does add side notes/drawings that are not in the powerpoints. Before exams, he tells you exactly what will be on it and what kind of questions. In total, seven HW, four exams, and one group project.

She is caring, lenient, and always willing to help. She will search for your question if she does not know and get back to you quickly. Clear communicator, responds to emails fast. She has not only helped me in this course, but in life and career goals outside of class. She is a class act and would definitely take a class with her again if I could.

Tanya is super friendly and always ready to help. She's very enthusiastic about what she does and it shows. There is a group assignment every week plus a final group project which wasn't really difficult but you're stuck with the same group the whole semester. There's very little homework outside of class time. The content is relevant as well.
Super nice professor and very lenient. Also gives extra credit which helped a lot.

Unprofessional throughout the entire semester. Will NOT give any leniency whatsoever on late assignments. Does not care about you or your grade. Replies via. Email are vague and very much so inattentive.
Super easy class and pretty fun as well. Haytko teaches it well.

Austin was great! I learned a ton from his orientation class and he really gives you information that is applicable now! Sometimes assignments can be a bit difficult, but it's not too bad. I learned a lot and he truly does care for his students. Just don't be late or you'll get on his bad side.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Terrible grading. Unreasonably docks points with vague feedback like "it needs more detail". Follows a rigid template, with any deviation causing major point deductions. When questioned, she responds condescendingly with, "I am not going to talk about changing your grade", displaying an arrogance that implies, "I graded it, so it cannot be wrong."

Don't take this class unless you love English, have time, and enjoy writing long proposals. You must dedicate much time to composing/designing the projects for a decent grade. The professor goes as low as taking points off just by underlining headings. All of the work is usually done in your free time and not during class time, which I found absurd
Very subjective grading, unclear purpose statements for assignments. Overall a very vague class; hard to get an A.

ENGL 250 with Jenny was one of my favorite classes the semester I took it. Some of the work was busywork, but a lot of it was preparing for the big, main projects due. She was always very clear with expectations for assignments and gave helpful feedback. If you follow the feedback from your first project, you will do better on your second, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I hate English but I loved this class. She is extremely knowledgeable, passionate, and an amazingly good teacher. Genuinely a very nice person as well, she is more than willing to help you in and out of class time. Go to lecture, and try a little and you'll do well, learns lots, and you might even like it. Probably the best professor I've ever had.

Aune's a tough grader; she likes to find the most minor and subjective flaw and deduct points. She seems to have an idea for what each assignment should look like, and if you don't meet it, she'll rip your work apart, even if you've met expectations on the rubric. Find another English instructor who doesn't expect the immaculate conception.

A lot of this class felt like busy work and I didn't really get anything out of it. She is a really tough grader and she expects very few students to get As which is annoying when you don't even want to be in the class but its required to graduate. Would like to see more opportunities to get points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grades mostly everything from one really generic rubric and grades very inconsistent.  There was a lot of homework for a class that nobody wants to be in. Had a friend try not nearly as hard with a different prof and got a lot better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Really a great professor. I took an online class and always email her to ask questions or made f2f appointments. She was always there to help me. I have learned a lot!

My section was specific to bioscience majors, and I loved it. Jenny did a great job of tailoring the material to the class and was flexible with due dates when asked. Assigned papers weren't too long and the books we read were actually interesting.

For an English comp class the atmosphere was very laid back but the expectations of the assignments were very clear.   Read the assigned books and participate in class discussion, put effort into the papers and projects and it's not hard to get a decent grade in her class.
jeanine is so great! she is very causal and lets you re submit your papers after she puts comments on them. very good teacher and would recommend to anyone taking eng 250
Terrible.  The quality of your work has no relation to your final grade.  The students she likes get good grades, the rest don't.  Extremely unprofessional.  Avoid at all costs.

Interested in what she's teaching. Gives a 15 minute leeway after class has started for students who have a longer walk between classes to get to her classroom. Available during office hours and happy to meet with students and make adjustments to help the student succeed.

Jenny is very relaxed and pushes back due dates a lot. It's nice because she is very flexible and understanding if you need more time. She also gets that students are stressed about finals and we did nothing after thanksgiving break, which was a huge relief.

Great teacher! As long as you keep up and get the assignments done, you will be fine. And even though she grades kinda hard, you can redo every assignment so just ask her what to improve. I got behind so it was harder but she was understanding and gave me extensions. But DON'T fall behind. It's an interesting class, I liked it!

Jenny was a very nice teacher and very helpful. We got to rewrite all our papers and she gave a lot of feedback. I do not think this class was challenging but it was interesting. If you are looking for a biology focused english class that is prety simple good class to take!

She is a very hard grader and it is so surprising because when you go in and talk to her she is says that it's good but when it's time to turn it and get a grade back it is not what she said. She is SO late on turning paper's back. I can't believe I got my final grade because I worked very hard in this class.

Jenny runs the class very unprofessionally. She makes assignments and projects seem unimportant even though they are your grade. She allows rewrites on all of the papers and she sends helpful comments in emails to guide your rewrite. Attendance is mandatory. It seems like you're failing, but your  grade ends up being much better than anticipated.
The stuff about the work is true. The stuff about her being an awesome teacher is also true. I got a lot out of the class.

Pretty helpful, but it was a friggin microbio learning community and im an LAS major, hence it was confusing. However, I thought would get a low D in the class but ended up with a B+. I was t.o.'ed to learn that all my friends in english 105 hardly had any work, but Jenny makes you work your butt off.

Jenny was a very good professor.  She was very helpful whenever you needed her, and was always reachable.  I had a few problems with her forgetting about my questions, but only very sporadically.  She grades hard, but let's you know exactly what you need to do to bring a paper up to "A" level and lets you turn in multiple revisions. Great teacher!
Already been said, but she is very unclear and grades very hard. I hated her, I barely passed the class because of her bad teaching. She makes eng 105 a lot harder than its supposed to be.
Jenny is horrible! she is very unclear and makes the student do 10 times the work to get the job done.
No Comments

Very unclear about assignments. better agree with her, otherwise you're wrong all the time. very inconsistent grader, makes excuses for her mistakes. bottom line, she is a total ****! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
No Comments
Jenny was a tough teacher and was pretty unclear with her assignments.  It seemed as if we did 5 times more work than any other section in 105.  I would not recommend anyone taking her.

Class consisted of her assigning a short story and having students discuss in groups without any guidance. Papers assigned were vague. You must parrot her opinion on a text in order to get a good grade. Took a subject I enjoy and made me hate coming to class. Take 231 instead.

Jenny Aune is a feminist, socialist, Kerry-loving witch.  NEVER disagree with her on any issues you hapen to be debating in her class, or else you are screwed.  The "suck-up" table in my class got all A's while everybody else got a C+.  Worse "professor" in the world.  F you, Jenny Aune.
She was very personable and helpful.  However, her grading was tough and often times it seemed difficult to understand what exactly it was that she wanted from an assignment.
No Comments
No Comments

She TRIES to make english applicable to your field of study. However, if you're not in the AgBus/Hort learning community, the projects are boring and difficult. Otherwise, she's a great lady--- she's always willing to help you out!
No Comments

She tries to have intersting classes, but they just don't work out.  Grades papers hard and not consistent with how she grades.  Projects are dumb, and watch out if your in with a learning community and your not in that learning community.
Autumn Cartagena is also an Open-Option advisor. I highly recommend switching advisors if you get her. She is not very helpful.

LAS101 was the biggest waste of time. It sucked the life right out of me at 8am. I thought It would help me explore majors but all It made me want to do was pick a major so I could get out of taking LAS101. She had lessons that were supposed to be inspiring but it was just a waste of time and no one gained anything from the class or professor.
The most awful class Ive ever taken. A complete waste of time, not to mention 8am. I never know when assignments are due or what course materials are needed. DO NOT TAKE DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cartagena is genuine and kind, but this class is an unprecented, unbeaten, monumental waste of the limited number of breaths assigned to my very being in the short time I have been granted in this life. I once sat in my front yard and watched concrete solidify for 6 hours, and I believe I learned more from that than I ever could in this course.
the biggest waste of my time. we took personality quizzes, everyone hated it. mandatory participation and attendance to class, job fair, etc.. declare a major and get out while you can

Attendance is mandatory and class is at 8am, but only a 10 week class and only once a week. Weekly quizzes must be completed, but take only around 10 minutes and have unlimited tries. Additional assignments involve attending major exploration stuff & a career fair. Class is what you make of it. Autumn is very friendly & will always help if you ask!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The worst instructor I've ever had in any class. Ever. Period. LAS 101 is absolutely terrible and useless in helping to choose a major. To top it all off, it's an 8am. DO NOT TAKE. If I could give one piece of advice to incoming LAS students it would be to do anything you can to not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very boring 8 am class. Seriously dread going to the class every day. It does not help with helping you pick a major. She comes off as very annoying. You are put in to teams to do all of your work and every one receives the same grade so you better hope your team works well together
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is annoying, not nice, and the class is completely pointless. The tests and quizzes are unnecessarily difficult and I dreaded her class every week.
Since everything is online, she does little to inform you of the things that should be completed before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pointless 8am class, needlessly difficult quizzes and tests. Barely helped in picking a major and way more work than a 1 credit orientation class should be.  Avoid taking this class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: very unreasonable when it comes to assignments. Most of the assignments given can be completed in less than 10 minutes but are graded for 50+ points each. If one of these assignments isn't submitted in her very specific way she will give you 0/50 with no remorse. Let's keep in mind this class is an orientation class.. she is unkind in many ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really boring, you just come in listen to  a speaker and get no time to work on the huge project in class

I'm actually confused as to why this is a class and also why it's needlessly complicated and unorganized. You never know when the due dates are and she only ever puts things on Blackboard. The "lectures" are completely pointless and it's an 8am class, AND attendance is mandatory, so good luck.

For the love of God don't take this class. It is supposed to give you info on different majors, but they test you over every detail of every major school in ISU. The assignments are tedious and needlessly complicated and the blackboard is terrible. She put me in the wrong group and complained when I didn't turn any of my assignments in, which I did
It was advertised to help open option student find their major.  Was revealed halfway through that this class is not for that at all.

Actually the most pointless class I have ever taken. I really didn't get anything of value for taking it, and the professors don't seem to understand that most people are not there of their own free will and do not enjoy the class. The class is needlessly difficult and convoluted, and the group-based aspect of it only served to cause frustration.

Extremely unorganized, you never know when things are due. Most of what you do in class is completely pointless busy work. Does not actually help you pick a major or be a better student. Every week there is a quiz over trivial things and they are oddly difficult. Often enters grades wrong. Lots of group activities and pointless discussion

Van Auken is a really nice guy and he seems genuinely interested in developing classroom discussion and hearing the opinions of every student in the room. That being said, I left the course feeling like I hadn't really learned anything due to the lack of structure. I expected more from the class, but it was still enjoyable.
Howard is a great professor, and the sweetest professor. It is nearly impossible to not do well in his class. If you go to class and do the assignments you will get an A. Easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Howard is a wonderful professor. He understands that students do not like to be lectured, so he breaks up class into small sections to make it interesting. He is very passionate about helping students and if you need help with anything, he is there. I would recommend this class to anyone! He also doesn't believe in expensive textbooks, mine was $5!

Howard is an excellent professor that wants his students to do well. In my section of the class, we were only graded on our business plan assignments and two exams. Overall this was a very easy class and unless he changes the structure I would highly recommend taking it.

Howard is about as easy going a guy as you'll find.  He brings food to class all the time, usually candy, sometimes even pizza.  You'll get an idea of what it's like to start a business from the class.  Seems like it was too easy to be honest, but I don't know how I'd teach that particular subject any better than he does.  Pick your team carefully.

One of the best classes I have taken at ISU.  There were no tests, homework, textbook, or final - just a group project and 5 easy 1-page papers.  The class was mostly discussion based and he kept things fun and interactive.  I highly recommend him as a professor.
He isn't a good professor at all and really doesn't teach you anything.  He has a huge ego and wants you to stroke it.

Ayo is the best studio professor I have had so far- he truly seems to care about the development of his students and wants to create an environment that fosters creativity and growth. He can be hard to reach via email, but he is constantly coming into studio outside of class hours to speak with students.
***Had for 302*** Probably my favorite professor. Great guy and helps you learn so much. Sets very clear expectations and instructions, unlike many studio professors.
Really nice.
Someone who truly cares about your goals.
Great great greaat!

Ayo is easily the best studio instructor I've ever had. It's been 2 years and I still look to him for advice on projects and stop to say Hi when I see him. He will help you evolve as a student and develop your work further in one semester than I ever thought possible. Great guy.

Great Instructor, He always finds comedy in things and is a generally great person to be around. His Grading scale seems to be very fair. Has great insight during reviews and loves game of thrones. Overall great guy (helps supply materials when he can and helps find a cheap and affordable way to make your projects!)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ayo was a really great instructor for studio. He gave good input and honest feedback, while looking for the positives. He regularly came into the studio outside of class hours to see how everyone was doing and went above and beyond to teach and help you figure out how to best present your work.
Her lectures were dull as can be, and she would frequently mess up her own example problems, but she posted all her notes and her exams were graded extremely leniently.

Transition to online mode in the middle of semester was smooth and online tutorial for lab assignments helped a lot. Recorded voice on PPT files was very helpful with instructor writing on the slides.

The lecture slide being available before the lecture was helpful. The escalation of the labs was very good, it was a nice steady learning curve compared to other classes I have taken. The textbook was not used.

Continuum mechanics can be very dry and difficult course. However, Dr. Sheidaei makes it easy by few things which are class note, class activities, and assignment. She drives equations from scratch which helps to understand the subject matter and the limitation of each formula. This course helps me a lot to understand the litreture in my research.

Dr. Sheidaei clarified all questions regarding the homework. Examples being accessible for the student at all time. The topic concepts were related with real life applications making everything easier to understand. The only thing to improve would be a bit more explanation on what material need to be submitted in the laboratory.

That was the first time she was teaching this course but she did a good job in covering all important topics. Continuum mechanics is not an easy topic but she made it easy for us. The material I learned help me to follow other courses I take.

This is my first class as a graduate student at Iowa State. Avoid this teacher, she simply copies notes on the board and doesnt answer questions because she does not understand the material. She spends the whole class time copying derivations on the board without explaining. If you go to class you can get an A, but you wont learn anything.

Azhan was the best TA I have ever had, and he is the primary reason I could get to classes on Friday mornings. His compassion and dedication to teaching students is amazing. He also makes the recitations fun, which creates a beneficial learning environment. He was really funny too, would definitely take this class if considering!

Azhan is a great TA. His class discussion was so helpful and he knew how to explain things in a way that made sense. I am so thankful to him as he offered extra office hours to help me review the practice exams.

An amazing TA. Lectures are clear and easy to follow. He always makes sure that everyone is able to understand the material and checks up on students. Not only is he a good teacher, but he makes the lectures fun by being funny. Would be lucky to have him.
The best teacher/TA. Literally the gold standard. Consider your self so fortunate if you get him as your instructor.
Awesome, he will be a great professor

He explained everything in a way that actually made sense. He's very caring and really wants to get to know everyone in the class which is very appreciated. He really tries to help you understand what's actually going to be on the exam. He will go out of his way to make sure you succeed, which is so appreciated.

Azhan is a chill and caring person. He will explain things over and over again in different ways to make sure you understand the content. He cares of his students and even takes the time to create slides that are easy to read and a good summary of what we need to know. If you can get him as your TA, He's a very good teacher.
Overall a great TA. Taught the coursework well and was understanding with students.
He's awesome. If he's an option you will be successful

Professor Azhan was easily one of the best professors I have ever had. He maintained communication and consistently provided encouragement throughout the semester. He was always willing to help and answer questions. He genuinely wanted everyone to do well, and even offered lots of extra credit assignments. I would definitely recommend, he's great!

Since the first week, Prof Azhan was very thorough with the course material, and very accommodating to the students' needs. He answered our doubts and questions. He also offered extra credit opportunities based on the lectures and exam reviews throughout the course to help us maintain our grade while also successfully learning the course material.

Professor Azhan is very knowledgeable and he was very helpful during office hours. He even held extra office hours upon my request, as I could not attend his office hours because of work. Also, the weekly worksheets and Webex notes helped me a lot in the course.

Professor Azhan has been very helpful and compassionate in this course. He has worked with me to ensure that I was able to do my best in the class and understand the concepts. He was very flexible, and he replied to my emails super fast. He made sure every student had all the resources they needed Including checking on our mental health every week!

Professor Azhan was beyond amazing! I cant say I am great at chemistry, however professor Azhan made it very easy to under sand lectures. Homework was very light and extra credit was offered. He truly wanted all of his students to succeed. He worked around students schedules to make sure he was available to not just a few students but everyone.
He answered all questions and spent a lot of extra time helping the students out with anything they needed
Hes pretty cool goes through the work with us
Best TA to date, taught extremely well, had the students understanding at the forefront.
Very good teacher who worked hard to get us prepared for our finals.
Best TA I've ever had.

Although I didn't receive the highest grade in this course, (something I blame on the course itself) Azhan was amazing as my recitation instructor being very social with us and just a guy we can talk to. If he taught calc I would exclusively go into there.
Very helpful and knowledgeable!
Getting Azhan as a TA is basically the greatest thing that had, has, and ever will happen in your life.
Azhan is the best! I wish we could have TAs more like him in my other courses.

Azhan is absolutely awesome. He is the best teacher I have ever had! His classes are really interesting and his lectures aren't boring at all. I don't like chemistry at all but he has the ability to simplify the most difficult concepts. He is knowledgeable and willing to help students. I would love to learn from Azhan in my upcoming courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Azhan was my TA for CHEM 178 Recitation. He is funny, caring, and has a passion for teaching Chemistry. He may not be the best at time management (i.e., he often speeds through material near the end of class when we have to take the quiz); however, he really does want all his students to succeed and makes an effort to get to know everyone.
He is very understanding
He is the best and he knows how to explain things

I'd recommend signing up for this class with a friend if you can bc there's a lot of partner dancing. Just embrace the silly activities Janice has you do and you'll have fun. You get 2 excused absences, but more are easy to make up.

Janice is a lovely woman, but by all standards, a horrific teacher. If you have no dance experience, do not take a class with her unless you absolutely need to. Students with zero experience or knowledge are expected to keep up with the professionals and hobbyists, even in 100 level classes. You will get no help or feedback, just a failing grade.
I absolutely love Janice! Show up and have fun and you will enjoy your time!
I love Janice. She has so many good stories and is so good at explaining yoga and techniques. She truly has a kind and happy soul and I am so glad I was able to take Yoga with her. Highly recommend.

She's very quirky! You will show up and learn dances for your attendance grade. You will be graded on attendance, projects, and discussion posts. All you have to do is participate and do your assignments, and you will get an A+. Be prepared to embarrass yourself because you'll do a lot of weird dances with people you just met, but they're fun!

Shes super flexible on grades and submission dates (though don't take that for granted). Shes also so sweet and has so many fun stories to tell! Overall, she's an amazing teacher and is very knowledgeable on dance, would definitely recommend. As long as you come to class and do the bare minimum you will succeed in this class.

I love janice so much. she makes my heart happy, and has so many stories to share. this woman has truly lived and is excited to share her experiences with the world. just be willing to participate and youll be fine.

Janice is one of the best people to get to know, as long as you show up and do what she would like you to do, you will be fine. The four projects that she has you do are really easy and doesn't expect a whole lot out of you to do. She is super caring and in tune with things that are happening in the world and is passionate about it.

Just show up and have a great time! Janice is awesome and makes the learning feel fun and not like some terrible drag. There is a LOT of swing dancing in this class, so beware of that if it's not your thing. One presentation, go to one show and go out dancing once. Otherwise, show up to class, do what's asked of you, and you'll have a great time!

This class was extremely easy! There are 4 (easy) big projects, and several smaller assignments. There are presentations for 2 months (which got boring), but other than that it was a very fun class! Make sure to show up for class, as attendance is taken almost every day. If you show up, you should get an A (I have over 100%)! Great professor too :)

This class was a lot of fun, although it could feel like a waste of time some days. Janice usually did a nice job creating variety and interesting classes. Her syllabus and Canvas could be very confusing, but asking a question or two solves that easily. Go to class, do your work, and this is an easy A with plenty of EC and make-up opportunities.
Janice was definetly my favorite professor! She is so fun to listen to and learn from and has the best laugh!

easiest class ever and gets you an international perspective credit. Honestly just show up and you will get an A. All she cares is that you are there and participating. No exams or quizzes just three projects which are basically links with three sentences for each. They all relate to different topics: project 1 movement, project 2: dance history...

I took ballroom dance with Janice & it was super fun! You can take this class at any level, you don't have to be experienced. Keep in mind that you only get two skips all semester, so it's important to show up. But she's a great, funny prof & it was a great way to meet new friends!

I LOVED having Janice as a professor! Although she is not great at using Canvas, she makes the classes fun and involved. You do not have to have any experience in dance to enjoy this class. As long as you stay ahead of the deadlines and show up to class, you'll get an A. She offers plenty of extra credit and ways to make up class as well. 10/10
Janice is amazing, so inspiring and hilarious.
I really enjoyed Janice's class! It was fun and truly an introduction to ballroom dance. Janice is very nice. Attendance is required, though there are many makeup opportunities if something comes up.

She's odd, quirky, and unpredictable. In the end, she is a nice lady that just wants you to do your best and have fun. The class is utter chaos, there's no structure or no syllabus. However, she is very flexible and works to accommodate whatever you have going on. It's just a dance class. nothing too crazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took yoga with Janice and loved it! She is so funny, wise, knowledgeable, and flexible! She was always so smiley and positive. Janice loves jokes/funny stories, and her laugh is so contagious. This class was the best part of my day. 10/10 recommend this class to everyone! its the stress relief that I didnt know I needed.

Such a sweet lady! She really cares about her students and cares about dance. A little scatterbrained sometimes but its overall easy just make sure you show up (attendance points) and do the assignments. I wish she used canvas because its pretty unclear whats going on when
Very interesting and fun class. Janice has so much energy and is a great professor, but you definitely need to show up for class and put in the effort. I highly recommend this class and Janice!

Janice is a delight. Show up twice a week and dance. You'll meet a lot of new people and have fun doing it. You are only graded on showing up and trying your best. You aren't graded on your ability. Genuinely cares about all of her students and desires nothing more than to share her love of dance with her students and the world. A real gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Janice's yoga class is awesome. Twice a week you show up to relax and do some yoga. On Thursdays there is a different teacher, but she's awesome also. The whole class is on coming and doing yoga. You only have three papers besides yoga practice. Two reflections and One outside activity. Easy A. Great break from classes.

If you are looking to take this class with a significant other and hope to dance with them often, I would not recommend. She singles couples out and makes sure they dance together the least amount possible. Made the semester very long. If you are looking to meet new people then this is a great class for you!
