Talk about my spirit animal... Janice would be the definition. I took Dance 160 (ballroom) just for fun and to learn some moves, but I never knew she would make me enjoy it so much! She really cares for what she does and genuinely believes there is good in it. Even if you're awkward, take this class! Lots of fun people learning fun moves. Love her!

I loved Janice's class (I took jazz)! I cannot dance at all, but she never got on me for my two left feet; she just let me catch up at my own pace, and found the good parts of my, um, eccentric style. Very easy class, and VERY fun, even if dancing isn't a personal strong point. Her music and humor sense is also terrific.

Yes this class is needed for teaching, no it isn't useful. The majority of the class is spent trying to catch up on what Janice is saying. She hops from one tangent to the next and doesn't really give clear instructions for the final projects. Aside from that, she knows her stuff when it comes to gymnastics and dance.

One of my favorite classes that i have taken here at ISU. I took it with a lot of friends which exponentially added to the fun! Learn swing, waltz, tango, merengue, salsa, polka, yada yada who are we kidding? swing is the best. You have to go to 1 show, (3 talking points) go out dancing once (3 talking points), and a short, very easy presentation.
Janice keeps things light. She just wants everyone to have a fun time and come away with an enjoyment of dance.
She's a wonderful, warm person and although the class isn't taken very seriously, it's stress relieving.

Make sure that you go to class. She gives you two free absences, but after that, your grade drops significantly if you do not make the absences up. Her mind is in a thousand places at once, but she is very entertaining if you have a good attitude. Participate and have a good attitude and she will favor you!

She's very scatterbrained and it can be hard to follow what she's saying. This can make it difficult to do assignments. However, that being said, she grades VERY easily. If you go to class and turn in the assignments, you'll get an A.

She is a great person, but will throw a lot at you at a time. She is also not very clear in what she wants for the assignments, but if you ask, she will gladly explain it further. Come to class, attendance is mandatory and so is participation.
Loved everything about the class and Janice!  Fun, freeing, and easy A if you go to class

I was expecting more of a challenge. I wanted to learn more than just the basic steps but it was hard when the whole class isn't on the same page. Classes were really unorganized and frustrated me when we would only dance for 15 minutes when the class is 50 minutes. It was a good break in between classes though.

Janice is a really fun teacher and encredibly personable. In class we pretty much did the same stuff everyday :( BUT its only a 1 credit class and it was great for stress relieving. She is so nice and honorable.

Haha, the "random teachers" that taught the "weird dance moves" for the Jazz class were actually Vintage Jazz teachers. Janice was trying to get her dancers more in touch with true Jazz roots. Too bad some people don't want to experiment with their body.

Janice's classes aren't typical, but if you're open to it and stop worrying about it, you'll do well and have a good time.  Come to class and be willing to try something new. She is personable.  The more you put into class, the more you'll get out of it.

I was in Jazz II but if you want to "dance" don't take it.  We didn't do anything in class related to jazz, she randomly has other people teach us the charleston and other weird dances.  I was expecting to do typical jazz/dance team type stuff and we never even did a full out regular leap. All we did was hop around the room.

She loves the 'outgoing' student.  Very few classes are organized.  I once learned the same dance in the same week in ALL three of my dance classes I had with her.  She does pick favorites, and she gets upset if she doesn't get involvement.  She also assig

Janice is an awsome teacher, she is very down to earth and easy going. She will show you and teach you everything she know, if you ask her. If you don't then she will only want to makes sure you have a fun time. It is only a 1 credit class.

She was absolutely awful!  Get any other professor you can, if possible.  Is not understanding if you miss class, and grades you harder if she doesn't like you.  Publically critisizes you - on CENTRAL CAMPUS.  And in front of other classes.
I learn lots of tap steps in the class, but I needed to ask.

This class sucks. She talks in wierd voices and hits people with rolled up newspaper if you can't do everything perfect. If possible, do not ever take a class with her. you will regret it for the rest of your life. you must be an expert dancer to not get hit with the newspaper. beware.

Janice is extremely easy if you have danced before, but otherwise you're screwed. She doesn't really teach steps, she just shows it to you and expects you to know how to do it. Also, she is very scatterbrained/spacey and watch out when she's in a bad mood.
She is the worst teacher I have ever had, but easy if you do not want to learn!

Barbara is amazing! She provides constructive criticism and allows a lot of room for creative expression in her assignments. She gives many examples of how to incorporate art into an elementary classroom and the projects were fun. If you really listen to what she is saying she says some quite quirky and funny stuff. She is a unique and kind soul.

I am an el ed major & I had to take this class to meet a requirement. The fact that art is required at all is asinine. I tried to get into 209 with the other professor because that one is only 2.00 credits & 211 is 3.00. This class was insanely boring & a waste of time. I skipped regularly, I felt like I was losing brain cells in that classroom.

Barbara is by far one of the best and most caring professors I have ever had. She helps each student feel they are of true value. Her unconventional yet monumental teaching approach helps students create personally authentic art. She has an incredible capacity for inclusiveness and diversity in the classroom. An easy 10 for Barb!!
Barb iz da cooliest

Barb is an absolute sweetheart. She cares so much about her students and pours herself into helping them with their goals and aspirations. She has an interest in psychology as well as photography and is great to talk to. Show up to class and give it your all and you'll do great!

Barbara is such a sweetheart. She is extremely caring and wants the best for all of her students.  She couldn't say one mean thing about anyone.  She has such a large passion for life and photography.
Professor Caldwell is really an inspirational teacher that trys not to put down students but critique them in a positive way.  She is very fair with grading and very helpful in class.

She is a very friendly, encouraging, caring professor. In 229 she almost never said critical comments about student work. In 329 she did say more about technical aspects (mating, toning, clarity) during critique. She is an really easy/fair grader. She genuinly nice person and very easy to get along with.

I loved this man!! Amazing professor with a fantastic personality and sense of humor. His lectures were super entertaining and never boring like most history lectures seem to be. Three super easy exams and five reading assignments over three books. Super caring man, too, who was always willing to help me when I needed it. Easy, fun class!

Dr. Bailey was one of the most interesting professors I have ever had. He is super funny and does a great job when teaching lectures. His slides do not say a whole lot of information so I would advise to write down EVERYTHING he says because thats where you get the details. He requires bluebooks for his exams and they are all writing.

Class was somewhat tough if you struggle with history, make sure you read all your sections to understand the material. Tests were difficult to prepare for but not hard if you studied a lot. He could get the material across very well in class if you went and listened so I would highly suggest not missing a class, had to work for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Loved Dr. Bailey! He makes the lectures very interesting and doesn't take himself too seriously (so he corrects himself as needed). Take thorough notes and you should be fine for the 3 exams that aren't cumulative. Go to the recitation section because attendance is mandatory there. Overall, I had a great time in class!

Going to lecture is like watching a really interesting documentary. Grading depends on the TA, but shouldn't be too bad. Only buy the book of primary sources, you'll probably never open the actual textbook.
Lectures were fun to attend and would recommend him. Only homework you have is a few writings for recitation. Reading the text book will definitely benefit you.

Dr. Bailey is a great public speaker. Makes History sound interesting even if you're not interested. 3 Exams + a discussion section every week. Memorize 50 IDs and unclear essay portion for studying. Attendance not mandatory, except discussion where you just need to talk here and there. FINAL ISN'T CUMMULATIVE! Can be easy if you're good w/ essays.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a very good professor. He makes the lecture interesting and you want to listen to what he talks about even if it didn't interest you. Attendance is not taken but it would be very hard to pass without being in lectures because he gives the specific answers to his essay questions. Easy A with only a little effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: its an easy class

Bailey was an excellent professor - you can tell he enjoys the class and has taught it many times. His lectures were a joy to be part of as he turns history into a story rather than a bunch of boring facts. Keeping that in mind, you'll need to memorize A LOT of dates. But if you put in effort and read the book, not tough to do well
He was a great professor.  He had a true passion for this course and was always available to answer quick questions after class.

Bailey is a great teacher for both history nuts and regular students. He really knows his stuff and can answer questions beyond the material. The papers are 2-3 pages long, very easy, and spread out. Know your dates and stuff for his exams. Those are the only thing that make this course difficult.
Dr. Bailey is refreshingly passionate about his work.

He was a great professor. His class involved three papers based on readings and essay exams. If you pay attention in class, take good notes and memorize dates for the exams you will be fine. It is easy to tell he loves what he teaches.He has a sense of humor which makes class more interesting.Tough grader, but he tells you what he looks for in exam

Has a great voice for lecturing: clear, loud, and he makes very efficient use of his time. Keep up with the assigned readings, attend lecture, take notes, and the tests are very manageable. He has a great sense of humor (if you can appreciate it) and manages to be both informative and entertaining. An all around cool guy and great professor.

Dr. Bailey is a fantastic professor and one of the best in the department.  He is an expert in his field and is always helpful for those who want to learn.  His tests are definitely not easy but if you are paying attention in class they are not difficult either.
LOVE HIM! Makes material interesting and he's very passionate about his subject. Great lectures that are perfectly timed

Have had him for multiple classes, and they just keep getting better and better. Really easy to understand and take notes for. Also, once you get to know him in class he begins to joke around with everybody and has a good sense of humor. Take all of his classes, they are AMAZING

The best professor I've had at ISU.  It's clear he puts a lot of thought and planning into his courses.  Anyone who is majoring in history should definitely get in his classes.  I could not disagree more with the smug comment.
Smug, smug, smug.  I certainly didn't get a friendly vibe off the guy.

Perhaps if you love this period in history it's ok. But you are handed a sheet with 50 terms that you have to memorize and there's no emphasis on anything in class so you just have to know it all. Hard but passable... I guess.

This is my 3rd semester in a row with him.  Each class has been awesome.  Great professor in lecture halls and brings the same way of teaching to smaller classes.  Speaks at a moderate pace and very clear.  Also his classes are perfectly timed and usually end with only a minute or two left in the class.
Has kind of a creepy attitude toward grad students - much harder on them than undergrads.

Extremely willing to help anyone who goes and asks for it. Not just in class, he helped me with  advice for graduate school.  Very matter of fact.  Very cynical and funny in class, if you can understand his humor.  Does grade hard on the Essays.
Probably the best professor I have had at Iowa State.  My Recitation TA was an ass, otherwise I would have really enjoyed the class.
Class is pretty easy, so up and pay attention, books not important.
Really good lecturer, made class somewhat fun to attend
Great Professor! I highly recommend taking any class you can with Bailey. He teaches history as it should be taught in large lecture

Bailey is one of the best professors I've had so far. He handed out an outline for every lecture and as long as you took notes based on it, the tests were easy enough. Papers are REALLY short and you're not tested over the extra reading materials. Great class.

Great professor and the way he teaches the class is wonderful. Details are critical in tests, the concepts and being able to relate class material are. It was a really fun class and the workload was not too much or little. If you need to take a diversity class and this fits your criteria, take this class; you won't regret it.

This course covers western civilization in depth.  The texts and lecture notes are both needed to do well on the tests (which include multiple choice, short answer, and essay).  Professor Bailey does a good job of covering material and making it interesting! His power points make the stories easy to follow.
He doesnt cover a vast amount of information but what he does cover is ver in depth
Loved the class overall and he covers a lot of material. Tests are moderate but not extremely hard. Lectures require notes and his power point is very well laid out. He is also funny sometimes

Treats lectures like story time, makes for an interesting change from the usual dull droning. Only class I've taken that I didn't fall asleep in but you do have to know the material for the tests(essay format).
Great Teacher, knows his stuff. Very Interesting lecturer.
little bit of a temper problem, esp. if you're an athlete and have to miss anything.....
Just a very nice guy and a very good teacher.
Extremely hard to begin with... not quite what I expected on the tests. He wants to know lots of dates for the essays-- good lecturer, tests were just rough.
No Comments
very knowledgable and interesting to listen to, class was fairly easy, just a lot of reading and discussion as it was a seminar course

Knows his stuff, seems like a nice enough guy to students, but watch out if you need to make up an incomplete - he doesn't know university procedure, gets defensive and nasty when it's pointed out to him, and hounds you about not having made up his test - as if his class is the only one.

Made lecture fairly interesting. Notes were basis of his essay tests. Not an easy class unless you read the text and study a lot. Essay tests were not bad if you did this, but if not, many failed or dropped.
Made it easy to undersand and also did tests in 1/3rds of the class so you dont need to know then whole history of the western world at one time.
Excellent lecturer...  being a history major, I've had quite a few history profs and he is one of the best.
Made history a story, which makes it so much better to pay attention in class.
The Best Ever!
No Comments
No Comments
Never have I seen a professor that gets upset when you take notes. An interesting lecturer, but ran out of material with 3 weeks left and kinda rambled for the rest of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worse course and professor, speaks very fast and assume things you must know. Does not explain alot basic definition.
Nice professor, but lectures were hard to follow and I stopped attending them. I just watched Butler videos instead

A professor who cares. He might go a bit fast during the lectures but when someone asks a question he makes sure to stop and to answer the question until the student gets it. Makes the lectures interesting by telling stories that relate to the topic. Or sometimes just funny and interesting stories. Gives good feedback when you ask a question.

Nice person but horrible at teaching. He went so fast in lectures and gave little to no time to write things down let alone time to actually comprehend and understand the topics. I quit attending lecture after week two and just watched Steve Butler's videos, it got me an A and I feel comfortable with Calc 3 topics because of it. Just watch Butler.

One of the worst professors that I've every had. He is such a tough grader when it comes to exams. You could get 80% of the question right and still only get 1-2 points on the question. He's very unapproachable and doesn't understand why people struggle to learn when you approach him about it. Doesn't curve the exams even if the whole class fails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Basak doesn't provide any feedback. The coursework is heavy, and he tests on new material and grades absolutely unfairly. Please, DO NOT take his class. I regret not dropping this class earlier in the semester; now, my transcript has a poor grade.

For a three-credit class, Professor Basak wanted students to show up for his live lectures (5 hours a week), watch his recorded content (another 5 hours a week), and read many chapters from the book. He grades exams very unfairly, provides absolutely no feedback on what you did wrong, and tests you on new material. Please, do NOT take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. His lectures are so disorganized and impossible to follow along so all learning will be done on your own. Test were ridiculously difficult with very few familiar problems, yet he still always seemed disappointed that the class average on exams was <50%. If you have him, save yourself and drop it.

His lectures were extremely difficult to follow. I learned nothing about the course material by attending lectures. However, attending lectures is the only way to do well on the exams because the exams are completely different from the homework. Exams cover the same material, but it is presented in a way that makes it seem like new material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Spending too much time telling people to get off their phones, very disorganized, phrases questions on quizzes and exams very differently from the textbook.

Even if I got A on this course, is was worst math course I did.. He always says "I dont Know". He also never make his own sylibus and say "do not trust this". I just study alone because he just copy and paste textbook example . Last, dont ask him any questions he always make student fool when they ask something.

He's very short-tempered. Spends half of each class time yelling at students to get off their phones. Doesn't explain things well. Very proof centric for a non-proof class. Makes things harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Fails to competently relay information to the students. Doesn't explain definitions of terms in an understandable way and only uses trivial examples to demonstrate the topics. He does not seem interested in the students at all and is rude when seeking information. Simple class, awful instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring in lecture, cares too much about the fact that he's losing people's attention because of how poor he is at maintaining it. I only used the textbook because I needed it to fill in gaps where I couldn't focus on his boring style.
Great lecturer!

Dr. Basak is very passionate about mathematics and loved teaching this course, but he made you feel dumb at times for not understanding the material. The tests weren't  terribly hard, but he'd always have homework due the day after exams. He'd complain about students behavior and go on tangents almost everyday. Indifferent if I would take him again

Prof. Basak is pretty cool! He sometimes goes on tangents and rambles about non-relevant topics that he cares about. He wants you to really KNOW the material. He's not gonna go easy on you but he is really cool & you can tell he wants his students to succeed. He sometimes feels bogged down by students who are behind. Definitely would take again! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very interesting lectures. Likes to describe how the mathematics is connected and applied to other branches of mathematicsscience which really makes the content interesting. Very firm understanding of the subject which rubs off on students. Very personable and cares about you learning the material.

He sometimes gets very caught up in over-explaining simple things or delving into tangents, but overall he's a very good lecturer and a genius mathematician. You really should go into his office hours if you have any problems whatsoever. He was way more helpful than most professors I've had.
He will not follow the course syllabus and teach you theory when you want to learn application. He would not be a bad professor if he taught what he is required.

He was my favorite professor throughout all of my other computer science classes. The lectures were very engaging as he was clearly very passionate and loved what he was teaching. With that being said, this class was still very difficult. Highly recommend taking classes with Basu as your professor.
Great professor, you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. The class is very hard and needs a lot of study time to do well on exams and homework.

Lectures are energetic and upbeat; he is clearly well-versed in all topics covered. I think he was a little too heavy on covering the theory. Exams are hard, obviously, but there is plenty of review material from all recitation quizzes. Was a little weird to have 5 written assignments and only 1 programming one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in terms of actually teaching the material. Very good. Ok, goodbye.
His office hours are invaluable.
I really think he is rated a little generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is not easy so you shouldn't skip lectures. The piazza response time is insane, it felt like he always had it open. Although he will indicate what sections are covered from the textbook, he does not really follow it himself and the class is overall very lenient on the math/proof jargon as compared to textbook's heavy usage.

Basu is a wonderful professor and gives super engaging lectures. The material of the class is really hard, but he teaches it well and is always available for questions after class, via email, and on Piazza. He really cares about his students. I would take another class with him if I was ever given the chance. Probably my favorite COM S professor.

I agree with everyone else here that Basu really cares about what he teaches, and it shows through his lectures. I say attendance is non-mandatory because he posts notes, but the lectures are so enjoyable you'll want to go every time. The homework and exams can be difficult, but there are lots of extra credit assignments if you choose to do them.

He really enjoys teaching the topics in the course, and, at least for me, this really pushes me to do my best work and always helps to keep me engaged in this class. Basu makes everything he teaches interesting and enjoyable, but still keeps it a challenge most of the time.

Was good at explaining things outside of class with regards to the course. Very knowledgeable in his field of study and more than willing to discuss your interests in programming regardless if they pertain to the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I had Basu for 311. Easily one of my favorite professors of all time. He's so great with helping outside of classes. I basically lived in his office hours. He's very easy going and if you're stuck but show that you care he nudges you in the right direction. Super awesome guy. Really cares about students and wants everyone to understand.

SB  one of my favorite people of all time.  The class itself is pretty neat, requires some logical thinking; nusmv & provers are kind of a niche field but learning to think that way is wonderful, get beyond just hacking it out.

Great professor! Willing to explain topics until students are sure they understand them. Very easy to talk to about grading issues and disputes, and very willing to make grade changes and do regrades if you have a good arguments for doing so. Just very helpful overall, and a very pleasant person.
Hands down on of the best professors I have had. Easy going, and understands if you have other classes!
Easy class, your project group will make or break it.
Don't take this class.  First half is a review of 309, second half is a review of Cpre 485.  Assigns the first 'busy work' i've gotten since middle school.
No Comments
Overall, a good class and professor. 2 big projects that are worth a lot of your grade. Otherwise, it's just a quiz and discussion per week. A bit annoying, and not the clearest grader, but fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ramesh was an amazing professor and overall really nice guy. This class was easy if you show up and do your work. You get attendance points, there is also a weekly quiz and discussion (both online). There's a critical essay and research project that are lengthy but overall this course is fairly easy, and Ramesh is very easy going.

Balayar is a kind man; you can tell he is passionate about this subject. However, I did not find him helpful to my learning this semester. His responses to my questions were not clear and made me feel dishearted. He was also a harsh grader for larger projects. I did not find his instructions clear and would probably not take another class with him

Ramesh is an amazing professor, he cares about you and your understanding of the material. Class participation matters, his classes are ones that you must attend. He assigns weekly discussion posts and two papers throughout the semester but they are manageable with ample time assigned for these assignments.

Ramesh is one of the nicest professors on campus. He does take participation and attendance seriously, it's because he cares about what you are learning during the time that you spend with him. He lays out his expectations clearly and is happy to answer questions. He won the Department of Sociology Teaching and the College of Ag Advising Awards.

He is incredibly knowledgeable and helpful and cares deeply about his students. The textbook is necessary, and you must cite it for the papers and discussions. Since it was online, there were only discussions, quizzes, and papers, and it was not difficult. Take this course with him - it's an easy A and interesting material.

This class was by far not my hardest, but it could be time-consuming, especially the mid-term and final. They are both 8-page research papers that take a lot of hours of research and writing. He is a reasonable grader for them, but they do take a while. The questions for the essays are insanely specific and hard to write about.

He was really caring about his students and was generally pretty specific about what he wanted for assignments. He respected everyones opinions but occasionally could be condescending. Phones and laptops (outside of note taking) were not allowed. Overall he is a very good professor and gives good feedback. If you do what he asks, you will succeed

I would highly recommend anyone looking to take an environmental science course or sociology course to take SOC382. Homework was light and it is easy to get an A. It is an easy course while also providing a lot of great information. It is also very clear that he cares about each of his students.

Professor Balayar is an amazing instructor. He has a real passion for his subject area and you as a student. He answers emails quickly and is always available to meet. Due dates are always manageable. There are weekly discussion posts and quizzes with a final exam and an in class presentation.

Ramesh is a great guy. He has a lot of experience with the subject matter of this course specifically. His class is very structured so it's easy to know when things are due. There are weekly quizzes and discussion posts that are very manageable. Two long papers and a presentation are also around the end of the semester but he grades reasonably
Great guy who knows his content first-hand. Is very personable and cares about your success as a student.
Amazing professor, great class content

One of the best people on Iowa State's campus. So genuine and sweet, responds to emails quickly, and knows first-hand the struggles that he teaches about. Is very passionate about the topics he discusses.

Ramesh is one of the nicest professors as well as one of the best teachers! Lectures are usually slides but he explains everything really well, and if you have any questions he will help you understand any concept. He has a deep passion within the subjects he teaches as well! He is so fun to speak with and to be in his class!

Ramesh himself on the first day in SOC331 said I am not a professor, which only foreshadows his greatness the extends beyond the course. He is a very friendly professor and he deserves everything positive. He really wants everyone to participate however it is a little hard because the class was in the morning. Course content is clear 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ramesh was one of the best professors I've ever had. So caring and willing to help at all times. One presentation and two academic papers. Quiz and discussion post a week but manageable. Attendance is taken but gives 4 skips. He is awesome and the nicest professor. He is one of the few that actually cares about you.
Super enthusiastic about the class, and very knowledgable about the subject matter. He managed to get me interested during an 8 AM class!
A really cool lecturer who definitely had a lot to say regarding environmental issues. Only real problem was that the class was at 8am so I was incredibly tired most mornings in class.

Dr. Balayar is a great sociology professor. I took SOC 348 to fulfill my last social science credits and it ended up being my favorite class this semester. He facilities a classroom environment that's conductive to learning and there isn't too much (hard) homework outside of class, just weekly quizzes and discussion posts.

Ramesh is a great professor for this class. He has loads of experience within this area and it is super interesting to learn about if you are considering taking a SOC class. Lectures can sometimes be boring but he makes them fun with jokes. There are two long written exams that can be a hassle, but other than those, Ramesh makes class fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Talks very slowly and mumbles sometimes to the point where it is difficult to understand a complete sentence or statement he is trying to make. Lectures are boring, and wish he would do more to actually teach us.

He's very nice and means well, but unfortunately, he is not the best teacher. His lectures are often confusing, and they don't help much with understanding the concepts. However, it isn't that difficult to get an A. Just make sure you review the slides and do a little studying on your own.

He was a great professor who explained concepts well and the labs were also very well due to how-to videos to complete them on our own time. The quizzes at the start of the lab are directly from the lecture slides. Exams were hard. Attendance is extra credit. Getting an A is possible if you attend class, do labs and HW well, and study.
He is very hard to understand and was borderline passive aggressive when asking questions about my final. He is not very helpful he just assumes we know everything even though he doesn't teach well.
Very nice guy but not a great professor. Hard to understand and I really only learned from the TA in lab. Wish I took this class online instead.

Professor Lidicky: nice guy but a poor professor (for data science). His accent was a bit hard to understand, and he didn't have a good read on the class's knowledge (asking very basic or difficult questions). He expected participation, but hardly anyone wanted to. The coding assignments without walkthroughs were difficult and took a lot of time.
Such a pure man. Tries to make things easier for you, and always has a smile on his face. Gives out jelly beans sometimes. Calc is just a hard class, but it's really not his fault.
I enjoyed this class. Lectures were informative and well paced. He really cares about his students, but he can sometimes be hard to understand as he has a fairly thick Czech accent.

Bernard taught our math 165 class over winter term. I appreciated him taking the time out of the holiday season to teach a 6 week higher paced introductory math class. Clearly cares about his students doing well

Awesome guy, but didn't learn a ton from the lectures. The class was pretty tough even though I already took calc in high school, but his curves are VERY generous. I liked him, but he can be a bit tough to understand (both his speaking and handwriting).

Great Professor, really cares about his students, sometimes a bit hard to understand. His test are very hard but he has a good curve on them at the end, he makes it fun and tries to be as funny as he can be(which is made more funny by his accent). He is always accesible outside of class, get help if you need it hes a very smart man and knows math
Great in lecture, fair grading
Good professor. He's a funny guy but he's from the Czech Republic so he has a bit of an accent. I didn't have a problem understanding him but I know some people did.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed learning from him. He made class fun and inviting, and also included the occasional joke or two. He is a great lecturer and makes sure we do a lot of examples and understand the material we are covering. 10/10 would take a class from him again! P.S. His accent is great!!!

He is an amazing professor to have for calculus.  He knows the information well and is helpful when you go to his office hours.  He keeps the class fun and there is minimal homework.  The exams can tend to be hard, but the curve at the end of the class makes it all better.  Also, has an amazing accent.

Has a very thick accent and is very difficult to follow and understand. I personally gave up on going to his lectures and I would read the book, read his online notes, and look at examples in homework and in our recitation classes in order to take my own notes and to teach myself the coursework.
Mix of group work and lectures during class. He was very open to constructive criticism. Nice and funny.

The homework was kind of hard, but the exams had problems that you would expect. Not sure if he always does this, but he let us turn in the solutions to the problems we missed on the exams to get half the credit back. This really helped me on a few tests. Overall not a bad professor. The subject can be difficult at times though.
I can say with nearly 100% certainty that this individual will be getting into the kingdom of heaven.

Chill and understanding grader, gives excellent feedback, it's comfortably very easy to casually strike up conversations with him, he's funny, and honestly just makes class enjoyable to attend. He is supportive of his students. overall I would 100% recommend.

Gus has been my favorite teacher at Iowa State. If you like Alice in Chains, Gus is perfect! He incorporates modern ideas into the class, which really helps you understand the course material. The effort Gus puts into his slides for class is far beyond that of any other professor I've had.

Gus is the goat. He is very funny, helpful, and lenient. Also, he loves to talk about relatable stuff and make class interesting, and not just another boring English class. Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had.

Gus was the best professor I had my first semester of college! Cannot recommend him enough! He was super chill, an easy grader, gave great feedback and very helpful. He made a boring subject in my opinion super fun. Also very approachable, feels like you're taking to a friend! Take his class if you can!

Made the class super enjoyable. Easy to work with and communicate with. Provides great feedback and is always supportive. I highly recommend him to anyone. I actually looked forward to his class most days.

Super cool guy. Very funny and his "lectures" more like high school class size lectures were always fun. Moves at an easy pace and assignments are basically completion graded. He's very easy to talk to and is very willing to give extensions. Highly recommend.
Gus is a fantastic prof. I genuinely cannot recommend enough. I was excited to go to class (which definitely isn't true for anything else) because he was like a friend. 11/10

Mr. Bhattacharyya is one of the best professors I've had at Iowa State. He is a very interesting person with a lot going on, but he always makes time for students. Whether it is something about class or you have questions about business, he is always happy to meet and talk with you. Definitely recommend taking Bhattacharyya if you can.

Professor Bhattacharyya had poor communication of grading standards, expectations, and assignments. The first half of the semester was entirely self-paced completion of short quizzes, and the second half includes weekly discussions and emailed team negotiations that are not graded until they have all been completed. 0/10, would not recommend.

Ryan is an amazing professor. He is a professor of practice so he is very busy. The work was not hard and his lectures were very interesting. There are group negotiations in the 2nd part of the class that are not hard but do require good communication.

Great, caring teacher and a decently easy class. Grading consisted of 15 packbacks throughout the semester, 2 (bigger) group projects (consulting reports), and 4 "position papers" of 1000 words each. Attendance was taken every class, but there were no quizzes/exams/tests on any of the lecture material. Don't use AI at all. Very nice grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had here. He gives zero guidelines for any assignments and proceeds to make fun of students if they don't get the assignment right. Even if he didn't explain it. I would avoid him.

Terrible professor. Required attendence just to sit there while he reads the textbook from his slides. He gives no guidance to assignments and his canvas page is awful. He is entitled and likes to embarrass kids in front of the class during their presentations. He thinks he is tech savvy but it's basic knowledge. He has a burning hatred for AI.

Ryan clearly does not care about being a professor. His lectures only include regurgitated textbook material, and all he does is ramble off slides for an hour and 10 minutes straight. His canvas page is impossible to navigate, where he posts important assignment information across the syllabus, files, and the announcements. Feedback is also rude.

Ryan is awesome! He is extremely knowledgeable and experienced in social entrepreneurship. Engaging lectures. Only bad part was it took him until the end of the semester to grade all of the mini essays.

Ryan was a fantastic teacher. He shared many personal stories about friends or personal business experiences. I can tell he is so experienced in the business world and has such a large network. He has lots of wisdom and knowledge to share, so I found the class very interesting.
Great professor and very knowledgeable. Enjoyed his lectures and material presented in class.

I took this class online and it was super easy. There is a quiz due every week up until Spring Break and Packback discussions due every week. No other homework, no exams. There are two papers due at the end of the semester, so start working on those ahead of time so they don't come out of nowhere. Professor B is great and cares about his students.

Interesting lectures, and interesting professor in the best way. He teaches quickly and to the point, and quizzes are the exact same. Textbook is a "for dummies book" you only use half the semester (free pdf online), no exams. Group project heavy and he does not grade quickly. Great communicator and very understanding!

Ryan is a good proffessor for 478. He makes the classes interesting with discussions where the whole class can chime in. He makes some pretty dry material a little more interesting. Also, he cares about students personally and wants us to succeed in life. Easy A and a good time.

He just reads from his lecture slides, but he is very relatable and approachable. He does not post when quizzes are ahead of time so you have to really stay on top of it so you don't miss any. Second semester is all mock negotiations that were very enjoyable and great for learning
One of the best professors in the entire college, take all your classes with him, he is a real gem. Ryan cares about students, grades easy and likes a hands on experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class is great because he educates you on real world topics. The class is seminar style and open discussion. He is well respected in the industry and a great resource to have leaving college. Knows insight on real world and great for anyone interested in entrepreneurship. Really smart guy.

The guy does not communicate anything at all. Be prepared to just have to figure everything out by yourself if you have him. Don't expect help in his class either. He doesn't remind you of anything or give you any heads ups. Sometimes he says he will build groups and then doesn't do it. Not an enjoyable course at all, especially as hybrid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Best teacher I have had at Iowa State University and is very intelligent. If you go to class and do the assigned work you will get a good grade in the class. He gets to know everyone in the classes and would take again in a heartbeat if he taught any of my other courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: No tests was real nice but be ready to apply topics learned in class with 3 presentations. Some In class quizzes (not told what date it will be so its a surprise). Be ready to do group presentations. Overall Ryan was awesome and well respected within the industry he works in. Very approachable and down to earth

Took 2 classes with Dr. B. He challenges you to think differently but also makes use of the actual textbook and material. Gives quizzes throughout the semester and also does extra credit. He works with you to help you do well. Very accessible to students and responds to emails and texts. Brings real world experience to the class.

Awesome professor. He connects the theory to real life scenarios better than anyone Ive ever had. Probably the best professor Ive had in 4 plus years. Gave us every chance to get a good grade. Dresses nicer than any professor Ive ever had and easy on the eyes too. :-)

Absolutely loved this course! I hate 8 ams but was excited to attend his lectures. He does a great job relating his own stories to make it interesting. Really easy A as there are no exams! There are 16 quizzes online and they are straight definitions from the textbook! Some of the quizzes are pop quizzes in class though! Extra credit available!
If you go to class and take notes using the empty slides she provides youll be fine. She does not post lectures online unless you have an excused absence or class gets canceled
Professor Bergman was great. Easy class, with fewer than 20 McGraw-Hill topics to learn for smart books. Lots of opportunities to get extra credit.

I really like Prof. Bergman, she lets it be known at the start of the semester she's a pretty no-nonsense kind of person but she really isn't that bad. Everyone gets a note-packet to follow throughout the class and it's very important you take that note packet seriously because it is centered around the entire class and is the main source of info.
She makes it clear what you are expected to know for each test. There are 5 in total. A good 3-4 hours studying for each test should lock in at least an A-. Some homework but not excessive.
Bergman is a great professor and lecturer. You will learn quite a bit in this class, and as long as you show up and take notes you can easily get an A.
Prof. Bergman was great. It felt like I had a good understanding of the content taught in class. She's a bit intimidating, but overall a great teacher.

Sara Bergman has been one of my favorite accounting professors at ISU so far. Her lecture notes are set up as fill in the blank, so you have to go to class to get the notes. She sets up amazing study guides for her exams. She also goes through a lot of workout problems with you, basically the same as the exam just different numbers.5 smaller exams!

One of the best accounting teachers at Iowa State. I totally recommend her as a professor. She is fun and engaging! Her teacher ability is top tier. She is such a good professor that it felt like studying for exams were not stressful because I understood the material 100% based on what she taught us!

Bergman is a fantastic professor, the concepts are challenging but some of these reviews are simply baffling. If you are complaining about no extra credit, no curve and having to read the textbook outside of the class, perhaps college isn't for you. You have to put in the work for her, but she will absolutely help you get the results you desire.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bergman clearly states her expectations, is an exceptional lecturer, and is accessible outside class. Lectures have countless examples and real-world applications. She shows exactly what will be on the exam. If you are unable to adapt to her standards, it is more of a reflection on you than Bergman.
I emailed this professor many times with questions and always got very unprofessional responses that were not helpful at all

No offense to other people, but this class wasn't hard. The content itself is simple, math is basic algebra. The practice exams are similar to the real ones, and you get 5% extra credit automatically. 

It's an entry-level class, not a weed-out, so don't be worried. You got this.

Do not take her class!!!! I repeat DO NOT!!! I took this class as an online course and it was more on the difficulty side. Her exam reviews are totally different from on the test. Also, a hard grader, does not accept late work whatsoever. It's like she wants students to fail. There a reason a lot of students failed her class. Take our advice.

Professor Bergman was an excellent lecturer who cared about her student's success. She responds very quickly to emails and will answer any questions before the test. Her test reviews were very helpful, and she makes sure you are prepared for the exam. The end-of-year project was slightly challenging but not impossible. Great teacher.

500 of 750 points were exam-based, w/ 4 points per question, and horribly worded. Her practice exams told you what wouldn't be on the exam, Not the worst responder, but certainly not the best, especially for an online class. I really hated how much she pushed SI, basically using it to teach rather than teach the material properly herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are 5 exam and one project in this class. However, her study guide is helpful and she wants you to succeed. This was my favorite class at Iowa State, she is an amazing professor.
Great professor, don't skip any lectures. Goes through important stuff and methods regularly. Responds to emails. Cares about your success.
Solid professor

I loved her as a professor, despite how hard the class is. She is very good at explaining the material and takes times to run through practice problems during class. The exams require a decent amount of studying, and she is a tough grader. She also gives weekly announcements, which are a great way to keep up with the material discussed.

From the start of this class, it is clear to at least this professor that it is meant to weed out students. There is a clear rule that there will be absolutely no grade curves within the class even if a majority of the class fails, and in which my class, that actually did happen. Also, know that there is no late work accepted.

I took this class online and it was by far the worst online class i've ever had. She was not good at responding, not helpful, and you have to do a lot of your own research to good on exams. There is also no extra credit or curve for this class.

This was the class I was most nervous about this semester. Prof.Bergman was AMAZING. I wouldn't recommend taking Acct284 with anyone else. Her lectures are concise and detail oriented. I never needed to attend SI or office hours, but it's amazing that those are provided. Her syllabus was clear and you know expectations going in, which was great!

Bergman is a great prof. One of the best lecturers I have had imo. 5 exams two of which are really short 50 instead of 100 pts. 400/620 points are exams. Fill in the blank slides for note taking. Very good study guides. Exam 3 is pretty diff so watch out for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class online which was not the issue. Homework was very self explanatory but when it comes to exams and the projects there are very little instructions to help you out, she doesn't respond to emails if you don't word it correctly, and her exams are so hard.

Professor Bergman was a solid teacher for Acct 284. There were maybe one or two questions on the exams that were not covered during the lectures and were in the textbook, but for the most part if you attend her lectures and put forth effort to understand the concepts you will do fine with the exams. She was also accessible after class if need be.

Honestly one of the worst professors I had in my two years at ISU. Very strict grading criteria and no leniency. The tests are weirdly worded questions, it's like she's hoping you fail the class. I took it online and wouldn't recommend it. Take it with another professor! Also, this is a 200-level class and it's been my most difficult...just sad.
Not a fun professor. Very strict and no understanding. I had an issue with grading, and she ghosted me. Probably the worst professor I have had.

Took ACCT 284 during the summer 8week class for three creds. On the syllabus, it boldly states a minimum of 30 hours a week and more if you are struggling. The class was easy to follow, but the tedious hours of homework and lecture videos were confusing. NO CURVE so it's easy to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bergman was my favorite professor at Iowa State! She is also one of the most caring and respectful professors on campus! If you have questions, go to her office hours! She is more than willing to help you in any way she can! Professor Bergman really inspired me to specialize in tax.

I am not an accounting major nor am I very interested in it, but she made the content actually pretty neat and applicable. Her lectures are really good. You fill out a note packet in class which makes things easier to follow and keeps you engaged. I really struggled with the tests though (which is what hurt my grade so much). Go to SI test reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Didn't give extra credit. No grade curves. Entirely online. Final grade relied way too much upon tests (About 70% worth) Would not recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bergman is very nice and answers emails quickly. The class is doable if you watch the lectures and do all the assignments. Solid choice for acct284.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Decent lectures but no screens are allowed out during class, which I liked since there's less chance of distractions but others probably wont. Class is well laid out but kinda slow moving, but Bergman at least makes it somewhat interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking Bergmans classes. Covers lectures very quickly and is hard to follow. I had to get a tutor who explained everything she taught but in a much simpler way. Is not lenient on grading whatsoever.
Very organized course and does lectures very clearly and at a good pace. Super nice and definitely the prof you want for this class.

TAKE BERGMAN IF YOU HAVE THE CHOICE!!!!! Her lectures are so clear cut and super easy to follow. The material is fairly easy already but she makes it even easier with her lectures and teaching style. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bergman is very kind and willing to help if you ask her for it. She teaches the content well, and is more than willing to answer your questions in class. She is very sweet, and responsive to questions for the project. I really enjoyed this class, and wish she taught more accounting courses so I could have her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bergman did an excellent job teaching financial accounting. ACCT 284 is known for being one of the "harder" classes in the basic business curriculum, so be sure to show up to class, take good notes, and complete assignments on time. Also, if you need help outside of class, she is always happy to assist.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is a little difficult, but Prof. Bergman is a great teacher. She covers all the content very well and really cares about us as students. She's willing to meet with us if we need help, and she plans her class out very well. I would definitely recommend taking one of her classes. She is super nice and very caring and respectul.

Professor Bergman was very easy to understand and she made learning fun. She always looks at the bright side of things. Even when class is interrupted by construction. She also let us go 10 to 20 minutes early each class!

Acct 285 is a difficult course, but Sara explains difficult topics well and makes sure everyone understands. Gives a lot of in class examples. Exams are difficult, just go through the practice test and in class problems. Wish I could have this teacher the whole semester but she had to leave due to having a baby

Makes sure her student's know what are going on. Shes still answering emails for students even after having a baby, and having a sub cover for her. She even made sure everyone had access to the online homework by reaching out to the company hosting our homework website and giving extended free trials. Textbook is nice, but only needed for homework.

He was not a great lecturer since he made a fair amount of mistakes in examples and has a tough time making explanations for what is going on.  However, he does make this class much easier than many of the other professors.  Easy homework and easy exams.

Avoid AT ALL COSTS. Lectures are too quick for anyone below 200 IQ to understand, along with the content in the lectures having absolutely NOTHING to do with the content on the quizzes or in the exams. You will be forced to teach yourself as this man is too caught up in useless derivations to do his job properly.

Really light workload, exams range from super easy to super difficult, but extremely generous grading curve. You have to try to fail. Very inexperienced teacher, had a lot of problems with preparation.  She obviously knew the subject very well but her teaching skills were not well developed.  Overall grades were unknown to the students until the very last moment, little feedback was given.

Teacher is nice but super disorganized. Also, not very good at teaching, jumps into complicated topics and examples in a class that's introductory.
Such a great professor, he does not grade hard and keeps labs fun and lets us work in groups.

Overall an interesting class but was extremely disorganized and is always very behind on grading. The labs were death by excel sheet. Nice professor and obviously very smart but his teaching skills a bit lacking.

Very nice guy! I took this class hoping to learn more about tractor power, and while I learned more, it was very difficult information. Awful professor, avoid if possible. Took until finals week to start grading HW assignments from February yet managed to grade exams within a week. Awesome professor. Very knowledgeable on topic and willing to help as long as you ask for it. Labs are fun and help with understanding material.

Professor Biggs genuinely wants to live in a world where everyone knows what he teaches in this class. You should go to class because they are fun if you lean into it, he gives 111 points total and a 93 and above is an A so not hard to get an A (he's a lenient grader), and be prepared to be wrong a lot.

This class can be challenging to grasp, but everything is easy credit except for exams. For exams, just review the practice exams as they are very similar. Lots of opportunity for exam retakes and extra credit. For all other assignments, just show up to class to get credit.
Very sweet and understanding professor, one of the best I've ever had! The class is hard, but as long as you participate, you will do fine.

Lots of chances to improve grades in the class, retakes, corrections, and extra credit to name a few. One of the few teachers that actually cares about understanding the concepts and learning the material. Class is challenging at times, but the professor makes it really easy to follow and understand.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor was very helpful and willing assist me when I need help outside of class. When it came to grading as long as you showed you understood the content at least one time he would just use that towards your grade. It actually wasn't a hard class, just challenging.

Biggs is a little bit scattered and the organization of the course is a little all over the place, but he's super friendly and knowledgeable. Very willing to meet with you and provides you with lots of videos and other resources to understand the material.

reviews.comment: Classes are like mini-lectures so be sure to pay attention
he is the best teacher I have ever had. his class is so easy. I love him

Explains everything very well and always helpful when answering questions
Hard class if not passionate about Philosophy

Logic problems take a couple of weeks to understand but once you do, the class is a breeze from there. Barely any homework, but you get used to it, so set a reminder so you don't forget when he actually assigns something.

Prof. Biggs is a fantastic teacher. He clearly does not care how well you immediately understand the material, he only cares that you learn. The only "exams" in the class are small quizzes over each unit, and after each quiz, we spend a day simply going over the quiz. On top of that, a few of the more difficult quizzes can be retaken

If you go to class, pay attention, and do some of the reading, you should be fine. Try to sit by people you know or be sure to introduce yourself to the people around you. He often asks you to "talk to the people next to you" when discussing a difficult topic, so it's important that you're around people that you get along with and understand.

Decent professor. Great lectures, but terrible with administrative things (responding to emails, grading quickly, posting readings with enough time to read them before class). I wouldn't take another class with him, but he really cares about students actually learning something from the class and modifies the class to include topics of interest.

He really wants students to understand the material. He also gives points back on exams which is huge. Attendance is not mandatory however, he gives a very good lecture. Should be a class to easily get a B in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best prof I have ever had. His class is a little hard to understand but he rather you understand than fail. He is willing to answer any question and help you with whatever need. You will pass the class as long as you show up and do the in class activities and quizes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Biggs is a good teacher and wants to make sure everyone understands fully. He provides good powerpoints and lots of note pages. Best professor I've ever had. He is very approachable and it's honestly incredible how much knowledge he has. He always has a very well thought out and intelligent response to any questions. While the material is pretty difficult, his lectures are very engaging and he is clearly passionate about what he's teaching. I wish he taught more classes.
Favorite professor yet.. cant find anything wrong with the guy + hes a freaking genius in philosophy. If you show up and care, there is no reason he wont give you a good grade

Great professor. Thought provoking and eye-opening.  attendance is mandatory, but there are randomly in-class activities for credit.  You will have to earn the extra credit, but it is available all semester.  Cool guy.
Great guy, amazing lectures. Really cares about the material and the students.
Great lecturer!
Great lecturer, but its hard
Good lecturer, but its a difficult class

Going to class is a must if you expect to get the points from activities and quizzes (which you will need if you want a decent grade) Only 104 points in the class total with possibility of 4 extra credit. Material is difficult to understand, but he does a good job of trying to explain it. Is willing to answer any questions and is very helpful

Amazing prof! Great lectures that keep you from falling asleep and make the material very understandable. Gives in depth feedback on papers and is always willing to help with questions. Long boardsskateboards to class, and super attractive.
Very relaxed and chill lectures, online exams, group projects/presentations.

Amazing teacher, really helped us learn. Even though it was an evening class, always gave us food and usually let us out a bit early. Overall, pretty easy and straightforward and would highly recommend.
Professor was very knowledgeable about the topic. The course approach is very much so you get out what you put in. I enjoyed the final group project even though my group mates could have been better.

Interesting and memorable classes. We talk about interesting topics, we get guest speakers, and the classes aren't too hard to do well in. He's a great communicator and charming guy. He also gives snacks, which is great. Exams and quizzes aren't too hard if you attend class. Make sure you attend class and get involved, and you'll do well.

Took for Mis 301 and Mis 340. 340 is just a little more complicated but still super easy, and a nice guy. He brings snacks, and for the 301, He tried his best to bring in guest speakers. Exams are either take-home or in-class, but both are open books and notes, and he ensures you're ready. They are more wight on writing parts from exams

2 at-home exams and a couple of light group projects. Lectures were extremely easy to understand and follow along with, and were quite interesting. Weekly 5 question quizzes. A couple other at-home assignments as well. Engaging and enthusiastic professor. Could not have asked for better. Perfect class. Extremely satisfied.

Devon was a super cool professor. Not my favorite topic so classes were a little boring, but he tried his best to keep us engaged. A few group assignments that were relatively easy. A few very short assignments. Brings treats to class for students. Exams were online but some written questions. Would definitely take him again!

His teaching style was a little unorthodox compared to others, but definitely more engaging. Would 100% love to have him again, and really appreciated the guest speakers he brought into the class. One of my favorite professors at ISU.
His teaching style is a little different than normal, but hey, so is entrepreneurship. He's overall a pretty good guy, and he expects more from us than regular professors.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bill Malone is an entrepreneur and is the best person for teaching this course over entrepreneurship. Would recommend for everyone. By the end of the semester he likes to break up classes with speakers who have started their own businesses. If you put in the effort in the project you will get an easy A.

Bill is a great teacher! He is enthusiastic and funny. 367 is the study abroad class and it was an easy A. We had 2 assignments the whole semester.. very easy group presentation about a business industry in Italy and then a 1 page paper after the trip. The trip to Italy was amazing and super fun! Would recommend as an easy MGMT elective.

Bill really cares about the material he is teaching to his students and wants them to understand the real world practicality behind it. He knows real world business very well since he operates his own coffee shops. I would highly recommend him if you get a chance to take his class.

313 with Bill is an easy A for sure. If you don't like to participate/talk in class, it may be a struggle because he makes everyone talk. There is 1 test, the final, for the whole semester.. super easy! As long as you meet the requirements for each assignment, there's no way that you won't get an A! You need to get the book- very necessary.

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher with amazing personality, would recommend any classes he teaches

Teaching style includes being told to look at poorly constructed and confusing slides that often do not reflect actual lessons from class. He has terrible grading structure. Gives terrible feedback. Thinks he has the right answer no matter what. Can't debate him at all. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!

The worst professor I've had. Read directly from hard to interpret slides and only required us to meet 1 day a week. Offered to meet us in office hours but left to work with others every time I went. reviews.comment: FSHN 220 was a super interesting class, and loved how Erica taught that. Loves to get to know her students, and absolutely loves participation in class. There is a non-zero amount of work across writing, and group projects, non of incredibly hard though. By far one of my recommended electives if you can take it.

One big group project at the beginning, then after that just a lecture on the region of the week on Mondays and eat the food on Wednesdays. She taught well, and gave good study guides for the quizzes. Pretty clear course structure and Erica is super nice and genuine about her passion for food. You'll get a good grade if you put in genuine effort.
Nothing to complain about.  She knows her stuff and how to help when cooking things.

hes not very good at actually teaching, he tells you certain things and expects you to know them even months later, i think he has an inferior teaching style to other professors and i would say his style is inefficient to the average student. he is also a very rough grader and only sometimes gives partial credit.

This class does not cover difficult topics. The professor requires far too much work out of class between homework every week and exams every other week. Ridiculous you only get 2 credits for this course. You won't get much out of the lectures. Most of your learning comes from the homework.

He explains very very clearly what will be on the exams ahead of time, which is nice practically to feel ready for the exams. His exams are in the testing centers. Pay close attention in lecture and do good note taking because it is a lot of content at a high pace per exam.
Bad lectures
Literally the worst professor I've ever had. Why is a 2 credit class so difficult? He can't teach to save his life. I wish ISU would hire a different professor to teach this course.

Homework is tough and based on textbook he wrote. Lectures tough to follow. Not very helpful over email. Very little (to none at all) partial credit on exams. Seems to want to see students succeed. Allowed a retake. Homework is the only study guide for exams, so do it. Receptive to student feedback, added partial credit on exam 3 to help grades.

Did not enjoy taking EE4480; attendance was mandatory for the entire class, with online quiz problems at the beginning, middle, and end, so you could not leave without losing points. The exams for this class I also found to be extremely challenging and don't offer partial credit, and they are not multiple-choice. Did have good extra credit.

For a 2-credit class, this class is unnecessarily difficult.

Bigelow's lectures are decent as he is very knowledgeable on the course. His textbook is even better.  Attending class is crucial as he gives basically free top hats points. The homework is exactly like the exams and requires. Test are on canvas and are graded with zero partial credit.
The professor is awful to handle. He grades the papers without any partial marking . A lot of HWs in his course.

Thinks that putting jargon on the disorganized lecture slides and then talking about it as fast as he can is teaching. Homework is about 10 times the effort compared to exams. Rely on external sources to learn and understanding each homework problem and you'll pass. Gives one word responses when you ask questions through email.

reviews.comment: 10% of the grade is a daily TopHat that has roughly 10 questions each. You will lose points when learning new material. Has a great attitude though and allows exam retakes at the end of the semester.

Teaching is not his passion. Thinks that he can do no wrong, and fails to prioritize his student's needs. Class structure is overwhelming and unnecessarily heavy for a 2 credit course that can't be Applied Towards A Degree In EE. No homework solutions and example problems aren't helpful. I wish there were other professors that taught this course.

Easily could and should be an online class. Does not help use friends to get homework done/understood. Exams are fine other than the fact it should just be paper in class from the get go. Not test center were a slight mistake messes it all up.

Does not help in a helpful way, limited office hours, few quality examples, doesn't post homework solution so get them from friends. Worthlessly strict attendance/tophat. He gives you everything you need in both lecture slides and note sheets to do well on homework and exams. Do the homework and understand what you do. Exams are easier than the homework. He knows what he is talking about but does not know or more likely does not care about teaching, he just reads the slides which are full of equations which are hard to follow at the speed he goes through them, more over he does his tests online we're partial credit does not exist. Disorganized when the class starts, does not know how to work a laptop and is not the most pleasant and easier professor to talk to or get help from even though he says to ask for it.
Average to good professor overall. Just need to remember what each equation on the formula sheet is for. If you do the homework, you will be alright.

I feel that he was very educated on this area, but it almost felt like he didn't take teaching this class seriously. The material you learn in class was very basic and read off slides, but the homework can be very difficult and time consuming compared to the things we learned and did in lab. Exams are taken online so there is no partial credit.

Nice person. There is tophat, at least during my semester. Tests were online for my semester in the testing center. The homework was the best way to study, and for the homework looking at the examples in the textbook helped and were similar.

Coming out of EE442 being so easy, many are caught off guard by the structure of 448, majority of grade comes from exams, which are canvas-based, so no partial credit which hurts some students as well as being given no review material or practice problems to have an idea of what will be on the exam. Lectures can be hard to follow but informational.

He's an ok professor. However, many students struggle because he doesn't have many example problems, and he doesn't do a good job explaining the ones he has. He seems to gets a bad rep due to all of the ME students that don't learn or understand the equations.

Dr. Bigelow gets rated more harshly than he should for this course because it's a topic that MEs are completely thrown into without ever having any experience in. Honestly it's not that bad of a course, and if you actually do the homework assigned (to be fair there is a lot of homework), there's no way that you will do poorly on his exams.

Professor Bigelow is a pretty good professor. He makes you buy a note packet, but I think it was really helpful when working on homework and quizzes. The lectures could be kinda confusing. The homework is very similar to the tests. Tests are hard because you only have 1 hour. The final was optional. He also offers easy extra credit.

reviews.comment: Bigelow gives pretty good lectures that he puts online so you don't have to go to class. Tests are somewhat straight forward. Will help you if you reach out with questions.
Very inconsiderate and doesnt give practice tests.

Dr. Bigelow does a good job of teaching EE448. The class material really isn't that hard with the provided formula sheet. He makes class interesting, and seems to be a fair grader. There is weekly homework, and the exam problems are very similar to the homework questions, so it is very much worth doing. The labs are not very well organized.
Professor Bigelow gives hard exams, but if you complete all his homework and understand it well then you shouldn't have any issues.

The class was well organized, entirely pre-recorded lectures. He was helpful during office hours and let you know what was expected. Several attempts on the hw which is nice. The final was pretty easy, given a huge formula sheet. Put in the work and you'll do well.

The HW's are quite time consuming. There's 8 HW's & 2 quizzes weekly. The notes packet is purchased from the book store to turn in & get graded at the end of the semester. He provides his textbook, but it isn't necessary. There are 4 labs & 1 is in person due to corona. The class is time consuming & the lecture examples are not helpful for the HW

reviews.comment: During the Pandemic, you think you could email him and get a good answer for the extremely hard homework. Very vague answers... waste of time. He says he likes to help you with your homework, please email. Well, he doesn't give you answers. He just confused me more. Tough class, study hard, because quizzes and exams are hard. Lectures don't help!!!

It's a tough class, which is fine, but it's made much more painful by the fact that he decided to grade our notes (must match his exactly) for 15% of the grade. So get ready to use all of your printing credits on 272 pages of notes. Didn't even teach the class, just used video recordings of a previous year.

Lots of homework and quizzes weekly. Be prepared to sink a lot of time into this class if you expect a good grade. When I took it, the final exam was worth 40% and the other majority were homework and quizzes. Everything's on canvas and lectures are recorded (audio and video), which was nice and convenient. The material itself is pretty difficult.

reviews.comment: No second chances in this class. Your grade is comprised of the final and the weekly quizzes basically. You don't get any tests in this class besides the final so you have no idea what it looks like or how his tests go till you take it. The weekly quizzes and homework were insanely difficult. He was dry and boring and not worth taking class with.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's decent. Lecture's aren't bad, best thing is he posts video of all of them. His homework and quizzes are a pain is the biggest thing. There is a lot of work to do and they count a lot toward your grade. Thing is you likely won't get a choice on who to take for EE448 anyway.

He has vastly improved his teaching from before. There is lots of homework but in his office hours which are recorded he will go through the steps to solve each problem. Quizzes every week but are online and super easy since it's just the homework with different numbers. Lectures are also recorded so you don't have to come to class.

So it sounds like he dramatically changed the course from years past - exam averages are much higher. There is no textbook now and exam problems are VERY similar to homework. If you know the HW well, you're set. The HW will take a long time if you leave it for a single night, otherwise it's not that much. His lectures are good, he did a great job.

I came into this class terrified I was gonna have a really hard professor who made things ridiculously difficult for no reason. Maybe because I had that expectation, he wasn't too bad.
