He assigns a ton of HW for a 2 credit course, but he's fair. All lectures are recorded and it's super helpful. Get someone to do HW with and you'll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Posts lectures and office hour videos that explain the material and difficult homework questions efficiently. Tells you exactly what he expects on the exam. First exam was difficult but he still curved it generously. Gave extra credit for filling out evaluations. people complaining about him should stop whining and start working instead. Great Prof
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He might teach other classes better but despite going to the lectures and taking notes when I sit down to do the homework I always end up turning to Chegg after several tries. Similarly the first test was nothing like any homework we had seen. Also if you take this class fall semester prepare for a test the Monday after Thanksgiving break.

After the first exam came back and the average was in the low 40s, he had to put a curve on top of the curve. Then the homework literally got un-doable. half of it was stuff we never went over in class nore exists in the book. This is the class where chegg teaches you more than the teacher and book and im anti chegg.

All exams are now on blackboard and done in testings centers.  Did not curve even though test grades were well below past semesters and he curved those classes.  Not helpful at all when asking questions.  Homework does not reflect what his lectures go over at all.   He teaches this class like everyone is an EE major when they are all ME's.  Avoid.

Test every other week. Many people struggle, and lack of partial credit can result in very low exam scores. Very labor intensive homework and quiz due every week. Professor is not very responsive or helpful through email or office hours. Lectures are recorded and posted online. Does not do minus grades, so your grade may be rounded poorly.

Bigelow decided to switch to all online tests for this semester, which was not fair at all for the students of the class. The exam scores were around 10-15% lower than usual, because of the online tests. The average on all tests were around 68-72%, and there was still no curve. Bigelow is a lazy professor who doesnt want to grade actual exams.
Bigelow is a very boring professor. He just reads off of a powerpoint. The tests were online which can really hurt your grade. Boring class.

He gives very simple and few example in classes, but hw and quiz are not the same level with the examples he gives. Hw and quiz are very difficult and he never talk about difficult problem in class. It's  little help for his hard exam.

Office hours recordings are extremely helpful to complete the homework and prepare for exams. Don't waste your time going to/watching his lectures because they are pointless. Ruthless grader on exams, if you have an incorrect answer you miss at least half of the points, DOES NOT BELIEVE IN PARTIAL CREDIT even if your process is correct. Good luck.

Very stuck in his ways and will not make any exceptions for anyone, he is a very stubborn teacher.  Exams are either very easy or out of left field.  Marks everything wrong if you made a mistake early on in your calculations, so  check your algebra.

He is very clear on his expectations in exams. Exams are like homework questions, so if you do the homework yourself, you should do fine for exam. Another nice thing is that he records his lectures and office hours, so we dont necessarily need to go to lectures. He gets confusing at times while lecturing so I guess the recordings help.

I wasn't a fan of his teaching style at first but it grew on me. It was very nice that he recorded all of his lectures. He often tells you what will likely be on the exams and is very fair about grading for the class.
He is a good teacher.  I love that he posts all of his lectures and office hours online; I only actually went to class the first day.  The homework is really long though.

Biegelow is a great teacher. Puts lectures and office hours up online. Office hours usually walk you through the homework. Try to do the homework and not just copy his office hours and you will be prepared for the exams. Homework is a bit time consuming, but well worth it.

For a 2 credit class, the work load was honestly way too much. Way too strict at times. Don't even try to copy assignments because he will report you to the dean even for slight similarities in homework. Scheduled an exam at 4pm on the friday before thanksgiving break and also on the friday of dead week.
His office hours basically completely go through in relative detail exactly how to solve every homework problem. He will never give exact answers, and he is strict on academic dishonesty.

Records all lectures and office hours. The office hours are worth watching if you're struggling with HW which is gonna take a while. Lots of drops early on so be ready. 4 tests in half a semester so be ready to study a lot. They look just like HW so do it and you'll be fine. Doesn't give out minus grades either.

Be ready to spend a lot of time on homework. If you spend the time and learn the concepts from the homework, you'll do just fine.  A majority of the test questions are from the homework with changed values. Watch his recorded office hours. They are a big help with the homework.

I can't stand the guy. Constantly tries to make jokes in class that never land. He provides information that is useless to MEs just to demonstrate how smart he is. His notes are not very helpful for the homework. I, personally found him unbearable. Others seemed to think he was okay, so it depends on who you are. Good luck!
He posts all the notes and recorded lectures online so no need to attend. Homework is long, but is great test preparation.
Not near as bad as people are saying. I actually enjoyed the class.

This class will be very hard if you already do not have a high understanding of electricity concepts. He will skip a lot of steps to do most of the problems and you will have to find extra assistance to cope up with the course. His grading is ok but I feel he should take a lot more interest in trying to understand what students might not understand

Very impressed by himself and his knowledge. Pretty useless for ME's because he is way over the heads of most in the class. Homeworks take hours. Unfortunate part is that is who you are stuck with taking it from. I suggest finding a EE major and having them help. Also, labs are totally worthless and not even the TA's know what we are to do.

He is not a bad teacher, but can be hard to follow sometimes. The class was pretty fast paced so be prepared. He records all his lectures so if you miss class its not a huge deal. Don't rely on the recordings because he has been late posting them on many occasions.
Was very good and nice to everyone helped lots.

This class was not so much about ethics and more about how to be a good little corporate employee. The grading process is unclear. If you buddy up to him you will receive a much better grade. It is ironic considering this is an ethics class. Obviously hand-picked to teach this class by whatever corporation gave the school the most money.

Ben is a very knowledgeable and inspiring lecturer. His lectures made this course one of my favorites that I've taken at ISU. Sure, the prompts for the papers and discussions could use some polishing, but the passion Ben brought to class made it something I looked forward to each week.

Great professor. Cares about his students and is lenient on grading. Passionate about the topics being taught and is great at teaching it. Lectures are great and interesting. For this class, the entire grade comes from biweekly writing assignments that are pretty simple, just write 1000 words and relate it back to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: His lectures were very boring and most of the learning comes from the textbook. Overall, still an easy class, just a lot of textbook reading each week.

He is very nice and responsive to any questions you have about tests etc. He writes clear study guides for the material and the study guides are always accurate to what will be on the exams. He actually lectures as well as reading off slides. His lectures can be boring and hard to stay focused in but overall is very great and the course was easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The class was not difficult at all; it was very lecture- and book-heavy. He is a good guy, but the lectures are very boring, and it's somewhat challenging to interact. You do some group projects that are pretty easy, but his communication for the project description and the purpose of the project is really, really bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class shouldn't be super hard in theory, but what I ran into is having questions on the test that aren't discussed in class but were discussed in the book briefly, so really make sure to read the book. The thing that helped out my grade a lot was the extra 10 SONA credits that you can do, that is 20 extra credit points, do them!

Prof. Block is an amazing professor, a brilliant architect, a nice educator, a constant traveler, and a great fighter with cancer. We became life long friends ever since I took his studio roughly 10 years ago.

Dave Block is the most amazing professor I've ever had.  Not only is the information interesting, he is an expert and often uses humor and real world examples to hold your interest.  I thank Dave every day for the education he provided to me.  In his retirement he will be greatly missed.
what a badass
Awesome teacher, nice guy, funny.  Exams can be a little difficult, difficult to know what material to study.  You learn alot.
Likes to have a few pets. Tests are wordy.
great prof.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Very fast at replying to emails and providing feedback and grading papers/discussions. As long as you turn in your discussions and papers on time with effort while following the rubric you can get a pretty good grade in the class. Exams are hard and are worded difficult, but if you study and review throughout the semester it's pretty manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
I have now taken two classes with Professor Bouffard. His lectures are great. He is always interesting and never bias. He is pretty relaxed on grading papers as long as you put in effort. 
His courses are test heavy which can be difficult but he always offers extra credit which is generally pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not very personable and is very passive aggressive in assignment feedback and emails. LONG proctored tests that are made up of obscure questions. The few assignments of the class are a huge chunk of the final grade and are uninspiring. I understand the Criminal Justice professors are limited, but based on other people's opinions, i'd skip Bouffart.
Tests are pretty hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeffrey keeps it real.

Tests are HARD, do the study guides!! Writing assignments require you to go over the powerpoints in depth & he's not an easy grader, so carefully read the prompts and material. "Requires" txtbook but I didn't buy & didn't really need it. If you need this class, you'll be ok, don't wait til last minute to prepare for tests, it's a ton of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There was little I learned that I didn't already know from other CJ classes. You NEED the textbook for the papers & tests. 7-8 papers, very easy, only 10 pts each, & they only have to be 2 pages. 2-3? tests, HARD, not all the answers can be found in lectures or in book. Use study guide he provides & fill it out before test, then look at it on phone

I LOVED Professor Bouffard. You do have to write a lot of papers but they are only 1-2 pages each. He is an easy grader and gives you feedback on all of your assignments. His exams are worth a lot but if you do the study guide you will pass easily! I definitely learned a lot in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take this course. His exams are most of your grade and weighted. Extremely tough grader. Tests suck, even if you prepare for them. Study guide doesnt even help. Save yourself and your GPA, and dont take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: i really enjoyed dr. blankenship's class. attendance wasn't required, but the lectures aren't recorded so you should definitely go to class. he is very nice and his classes are really relaxing. research credits are required and getting them done early can get you extra credit.

GO TO LECTURE. Every time I would miss class; I did bad on the exam. You have to memorize a lot so take good notes. Blakenship was very nice, and his lectures were ok. I only went to discussion the first 2 weeks and occasionally before exams. Research is required, try and knock those out in the first month and do extra ones if your grade needs it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures aren't like the most interesting thing or anything but he does give you like all the information needed, the class is very hw reliant as he only gives weekly quizzes but they count for most of your grade. He is very nice though and if you need will occasionally reopen quizzes for students to get their grades up.

One of the best professors i've had so far, lectures are relaxed and easy to understand and listen to. Consistent grading and provides plenty of resources to pass the class. Also has a really nice voice.

Dr. Blankenship was an awesome professor. I don't know what other people who said he was boring were expecting, because he keeps lectures interesting and you can tell he is passionate about his study. To succeed, you should go to his lectures (his explanations are better than reading the slides at home) and do the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A good guy and very helpful, but he's super boring. The lectures, recitations, and assigned readings do not line up with each other so it is student responsibility to get everything structured nicely in notes & study guides. This class is not an easy A and is a lot of memorization. Attendance is not taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was very easy. There were weekly quizzes that were easy and on quizlet. I never went to lecture, he did not really add useful info that was not on the slides. Before tests he posted a study guide and if you knew that you are good. I would go to discussion before tests to review as well. Overall very easy class.

Overall super easy class. He isn't super heavy on canvas so it's important to keep up with due dates on your own (although he provides frequent reminders in class). He gives a long length of time for pretty much all assignments so it's really easy to get ahead if you want to. Super chill prof, would recommend.

Professor Blankenship was very informative. He ties class topics to current media and other interesting things that really make this course fun. I recommend this class to anyone who is interested in communication or psychology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: eh, I would've taken with a different professor if I had know he was awful.

This class comprises 4 exams (final is not cumulative) and research credits. You can earn extra research credits, which helped my grade. Blank is a terrible professor because he is extremely boring and doesn't mention half of the things on the exam in class. If I didn't have my Student leaders from comst 104 I would not have done well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Blankenship was a high-quality mediocre professor. There wasn't much special about lectures, and he kept everything simple. He gave you the content necessary to do well on the exams. He was just a plain and simple lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class and learned a lot; it was pretty interesting too. Dr. Blankenship is very knowledgeable about this subject. This class had a research component. There was no homework or quizzes. Grades came from completing exams, and research credits. (There is a replacement assignment if you don't want to participate in research.)
Great teacher. Tries his best to make lectures intresting.

Blankenship's class was pretty easy! Got an A by attending lectures most of the time and not doing the reading. Studying for the exams based off the study guides are the way to go. Super kind professor and seems to care about what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Solid to easy class. Quizzes and lectures every week but just pay attention and you will be okay. Easy to tell he cared about teaching and tried his best to make the lectures interesting. Reading/skimming through the chapter is important, would say more than the lectures. Got an A and learned some interesting stuff!

Only one quiz every week always do at the same time and date. Lectures are interesting, but most of the content seems surface level. Lectures aren't long, but make sure to skim over the book. Extra Credit is offered based off of extra research credits.

Lectures are filled to the brim with material I will never use in my life, and it is super boring. Worst class I've taken at Iowa State, didn't learn a thing, still got a B. I went to most lectures while my friend went to none and he got an A. Seems like the more psych classes you've taken, the better grade you'll get in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are really boring and people often don't show up. He gives partial notes, but they make no sense unless you add lots of context from the lectures. The exams are almost the only place you get points from, and they're crazy difficult. You have to understand things about the concepts he never even mentions in lecture.

For homework & assignments, you will have to do 10 research studies(just participation) for the class or write a paper over some study. There are 4 exams throughout the semester(final isn't cumulative). USE THE STUDY GUIDES! Blankenship was hilarious and did his best to make class interesting. Not very many people show up to lecture, and still pass

Need to attend class for notes to fill out the study guides. 5 Exams and 2 assignments with extra credit opportunity. He is extremely caring and one of the nicest professors I have ever had. Enjoyed the class and tests are over the unit you are learning, no cumulative tests.
doesnt really teach any of the stuff that ends up being on the test and the lectures are pretty boring, so you might be better off just taking notes from your book and Quizlet.
Honestly the lectures got very boring so I didn't end up going to many of them but as long as you study the study guides for the tests and do the research studies you should be good.

Kevin Blankenship is a nice and caring professor. He wants students to learn. I enjoyed his class, but it can get boring. Make sure to do the research credits and use the study guides for the exams and you will pass. The book can be useful in going over the study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: honestly this dude was boring af, but its not that hard to get an A or B, just do the extra credit and study the study guides before the test. The only thing you are graded on is the tests and the research credits so do them. You should get the textbook as well because it helps you understand the information that he didn't really cover.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Blankenship is cool and wants students to learn. The material is pretty abstract and he recognizes that so he will do whatever he can in order to help you to understand. Have to do the readings to do well on the quizzes, and take notes in lecture on what he is saying instead of copying the PPT notes. His also has some pretty fun assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I think he generally cares about his students, he does this by offering a decent amount of EC. I would've finished the class with a C+,but instead got a B just because of EC. The only thing that frustrated me was the study guide he gave never really correlated with the exams. You have a 10pt quiz each week, just read the chapters & you will do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Definitely knows what he's talking about, but doesn't see it from a learning perspective (over-elaborates on the stuff that was easy and glosses over the complex topics) With tests and quizzes you just have to gamble whether or not to follow him or the textbook. Every quiz had a mistake or "misinterpretation" due to wording, so prepare to speak up.

Has no idea how to make tests, admits in class that he messed up things but doesn't seem to care. Seems to be more caught up in his research then actually teaching the class. Thinks everything he says is super clear when it isn't and won't explain it differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy, but I found the class to be extremely boring. Don't really need the textbook, but it's  very helpful for the study guides if you're not gonna pay attention in class. Study guides tell you exactly whats gonna be on the exams. You can get up to 20 extra credit points for doing extra research studies.

You don't need to go to class because he post notes on blackboard, however he leaves some fill in the blanks on the notes that he usually goes over in class. Do the study guides, they are basically the test. Do the extra credit research!! Easy points! Good and pretty easy class, need to study for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I actually enjoyed going to his lectures, but you don't have to always go because his notes are also online. He makes all the material very reletable. Not a lot of homework and tests are pretty simple.
Interesting lectures if you actually listen, but mostly everything you need is in the textbook.  Very nice guy and very good professor. The class has a lot of extra credit to bump up your grade.

Easy A as long as you study for the tests. Tests are average, not too hard. No homework in this class other than participating in studies. You also get extra credit for participating in extra studies and as long as you do all the extra credit, it should be an easy A. Nice guy too, really helped me during my tests when I had questions.

Eh.  He's a nice guy, but he rambles and I'm generally confused about what we're supposed to know come test time.  Attendance isn't mandatory but the lecture slides are incomplete online, so it's only more confusing if you skip.  He's big into pysch, so be ready to participate in research studies outside of if you want to pass.

Great teacher, very easy to understand! His classes aren't too hard but tests are based on a lot of in class topics. The tests aren't too tricky if you've paid attention and looked over the notes. Funny guy, cracks jokes in class so it makes it fun! Always willing to help. I would highly recommend!

His lectures are boring and I stopped going to class halfway through the semester. Don't forget about the research credits. Do well on the tests because there are like no points for the class. Wouldn't recommend this class but it's an easy A.
He liked to cuss in class, but it was pretty comical. He was fairly easy. If you did study guides before the exams they were fairly easy.
His tests are straight forward and the class went by quickly. He gives out study guides that usually correlate pretty directly with the tests. Easy to get a AB if you give the time and effort.
Super easy class. Study the study guides, and you'll get an A on every test. I went to class twice all semester and passed with flying colors.

This class is cake. Super basic, super easy, barely ever went to class. Blankenship cares a lot more about his psych experiments than some BS intro class, so he makes it pretty easy. Do the extra credit research participation and its an EASY A

Very easy class, I barely even went. If you read the book and take notes before the test, you will get an A. Do the extra research credits for extra credit (worth the time), make sure you get the research stuff done earlier rather than later
Great professor! So helpful, tests are straight from the study guide, lectures are interesting! Would take another with him!

Dr. B is honestly THE best teacher ever. He is very helpful and responds quickly. He has a funny, dry sense of humor. Even topics that aren't that interesting he manages to make bearable. I highly recommend him and wish he taught more classes.

I really enjoyed this class! His lectures can get long if they're on a dull topic, but he does a great job relating it to things you already understand or do everyday in life. The research credits are easy and he offers them as extra credit.
KEVIN IS THE BEST GUY EVA. keep it up kev! Class is always interesting, never want to skip a day with him!
Interesting lectures and easy course material. Some of the tests were a little difficult but not too bad.

Actually a super interesting class if you pay attention. He's kind of monotone and his lectures can get kind of boring, but the material is pretty easy to grasp and he provides a lot of helpful examples. Tests are pretty easy if you complete the study guide. Do the extra 6 research credits to give you a good grade boost!

Kevin is a fantastic teacher. I really learned a lot from his class. His presentations were really insightful and even humorous. He encorporates a lot of Psychological research that I liked. Come to class, print the powerpoints and take notes on them, have a fairly good grasp on the short chapters and there's no reason not to get an A. Great guy.
Really easy class, only went to class twice and got an A in it. Just read the chapters before the test and you will do fine. Kevin is a really nice teacher.
Interesting and easy class.
Easy, fun class.  Interesting material.  1/4 of test questions are related to class-only lecture.  The rest is out of the book!

Easy class. Watched TONS of youtube videos and movie clips. No attendance needed for this class. Tests are EASY- ppts online and hardly anything out of the book. EC is offered so you really should get an A in this class, no problem. He's a pretty boring prof, but I just don't think he cares about his 101 class.

This was such a worthless boring class. The topic is interesting but the way Blankenship presents the information is super dull.. I rarely went to class after realizing how useless lecture was.  Read the book and fill out the study guides to get an A.

I've taken over 100 credits of college coursework and I've never had a professor who was late and unprepared for class more than Blankenship. If you want to watch YouTube and hear him talk about TV shows he likes then go to class but you won't learn much. Tests are mostly based on the book but there are points where he disagrees with the book.

He is probably the most boring professor I've ever had. He is very nice, but doesn't know how to keep the class interested. You could legitimately never go to class, read the book, and get an A on every test.

This is honestly the easiest class I have ever taken at ISU. There should be no problem whatsoever in getting an A. He offers a ton on extra credit and the tests are really easy but you have to fill the study guide out. Basically he gets all the questions from the study guide, so just memorize it. Go to class, its very helpful.

He is so nice and very handsome. I love him very much. Even you didn't attend every class, you can also very easy get A. Also, he is very cute that when he wants give some extra credit, he will mention it on Web CT. So even you can know which class you can go or not. He is absolute nice person.
You could tell that he enjoyed what he was teaching and that he wanted his students to be interested as well. Take the class.. not only is it an easy course he is easy on the eyes.. cute guy.

She actually cares about your learning. As calc 2 is very difficult, she works through problems well and always answers questions. Lectures can get boring at times, but it's more so the content than her. I found her to be helpful and excited to teach.

Great professor, Calc 2 is a difficult class, and she does her best to prepare you for the exams. She is super willing to answer questions, and she likes to get class participation, which can be annoying to some, but a lot of the time, I found it helpful. She often answered questions and took time to slow down and explain things.

I took Calculus I with Heather Bolles during Fall 2025. The class itself is a very relaxed and easy to understand environment. She is very thorough in her explanations, going more in-depth into the reasoning behind certain mathematical decisions. My only issue was that lecture material was behind the due homework.

Dr.Bolles wants you to learn, but in lectures, she often rushes towards the end to fit everything in. She wants to stay on track for the exams, but therefore skips essential steps in the material. Exams are moderately complex and heavily weigh on your grade. She does provide multiple resources for help, including meetings with her.

Wastes time with ice breakers and tangents - then complains there's a lot of material she has to get through and rushes through the actual lecture which she never finishes.

You'll teach yourself the material because she certainly won't.
If I didn't already like math she would have made me hate it. Terrible teacher.

She is an amazing professor with a sense of humor and she really caters to student's needs. Her lectures have handwritten notes and practice problems, so its easy to follow along in your own notebook. She gives good advice on what to study for exams and she takes time to answer student's questions. This course is hard, but not because of her.
Calc 2 is a really hard class but she explains concepts well with a lot of examples. Very helpful in office hours.

This Calc II class is challenging, but the professor is helpful and engaging. Attend all lectures, actively participate, and utilize resources like unstuck study and the textbook. With dedication, you can succeed in this course.

All the Calc 2 Professors get a bad rap. It's a hard class, and I would say the lecturer doesn't matter as much as other classes, because at the end of the day it's all about the Quizzes and Exams. With that being said, I think Bolles did a good job at explaining topics and went over a fair amount of examples. She can go off on side tangents.
Realized she was good after having a true bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Proactive and very helpful during Help Hours and other times outside of class. Makes you feel confident in what you know and it feels more easy asking her questions than other professors.
Teaches good. You need to stay engaged and answering her questions to make class more fun. Lectured are great and go by fast for me.

Teaches like she is bragging about how much she knows. Extremely boring lectures which go onto extremely long side tangents unrelated to the material. Class is basically just on exams. Never finishes lecture on time and rushes material just to stay "on schedule".

She is very kind. She is very engaging in her lectures and she wants you to succeed. She can go kind of fast, however she posts her lecture notes for you to review. Definity recommending going to help hours. Calc II is a weed-outclass, so do not fall behind.

She does a great job at listening to students and tailoring to their needs.  She is very compassionate with what she does and very intentional when in conversation.  She genuinely cares about her students, you just have to take a second to get to know her.
The class was not easy, but that was not her fault. She explained everything you would need to know for the exams, you just had to be able to remember and apply it.

With Calc II, you are going to struggle to find a great professor no matter what, but she was not the best option. Teaches as if she's trying to prove how smart she is, skips a lot of steps while teaching, and rarely picks examples that apply to quizzes and exams. Nice and helpful in help hours, but not didn't enjoy her teaching.

Dr. Bolles is a wonderful professor who truly cares about her students. This is a tough class, and she knows it. She does a lot behind the scenes to ensure that the tests and quizzes are fair, while also encouraging students to become problem solvers. If you take this class, be ready to dedicate a lot of time to mastering the material.

Dr. Bolles is a good professor. It is clear she cares about all her students. She has a great understanding of calculus and can answer almost any question that comes her way. She explains concepts very well. Sometimes she goes a little fast and I did sometimes find her lectures a little boring which led to me missing important information.

The exams in this course are impossible and affect your grade so much. Heather is nice and willing to answer questions, but she writes near-impossible exams. Calc II is a whole other beast than Calc I and will make you question your existence.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Calc 2 is just hard no matter who your teacher is. She is very kind and good at explaining concepts but if you don't put in extra effort and attend supplemental instruction then you probably won't do well. She engages well with her students and is very kind.

One of my favorite aspects of the class was how Dr. Bolles would dedicate a good chunk of the lectures around exam time to plenty of calculus practice. I like how she incorporates practice outside of homework to help understand calculus. Calculus 1 is doing to be a difficult class so make sure to keep up with the work constantly.

Dr. Bolles is a great instructor, especially for calc 1. She is thorough in her explanations and won't hesitate to answer any questions in class. Make sure to take advantage of help hours if you struggle in class. Personally going to lecture was the best option for me because Dr. Bolles goes over good examples of problems.

My experience with Professor Bolles was fine honestly. I think the setup of Calculus 1 and 2 at ISU is unnecessarily rigorous, but Prof. Bolles did a good job explaining calculus concepts and trying to incorporate student feedback. She tends to go fast through problems and material, but is responsive to questions and helpful in office hours.

I have Bolles for Calc 1 and she is a solid professor. I stopped going to lectures because we are provided with videos of the material covered in class and going to class was not the best use of my time. Now she is not a great lecturer, but she is fantastic in one-on-one office hours. She will work with you and make sure you understand.
made calc unbearable

The homework is literally useless only good for keeping you busy. Lectures are a complete joke its not even her teaching. Be prepared to fail because more than likely you will. Even if you suffer nights studying you will be unprepared for exams. She does teach, you teach yourself with little to no help. If other classes are like this, I am transfer

Heather Bolles is in charge of the calculus program (1-3) at Iowa State. I luckily only had to survive one class (Calc 2) under her tyranny. Her system is set up in a way that encourages memorization over learning and an intolerance of small algebra mistakes rather than focusing on calculus techniques. Take as few calculus classes as possible!
She does not care about her students and refused to make accommodations for the rescheduled final exam that was announced the day of.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She doesn't care about her students. She will not make accommodations for you in any way.
She does not care about the students and the organization is all over the place.

All she did was look over and supervise the course. Not helpful and did not seem to care about the students. Lectures were prerecorded videos that can easily pile up if you fall behind. Class was a big joke. She simply sat back and claimed to teach the class while collecting a fat paycheck from the university. Students really suffered

The worst experience I have had at Iowa State. Her structure for the whole calculus curriculum at this university is an absolute joke. The HW and lectures are simple to understand if you only watch Steve Butler. The quizzes and exams are difficult. She will expect you to solve total curveballs to what was learned in class. She was never helpful.

Would not recommend. Class was online with pre-recorded lectures from other professors. She only a makes announcements. Level of difficulty on tests was not covered on homework or help sessions. Right at the end of the course she changed the grading scale so that grades were lowered. Save your time and energy and take math courses at DMACC.

When I reached out to her for advice for improving my grade I was left with little to no advice and no idea of how to move forward. I prepared for exams using the textbook and practice exams given and still performed poorly on the exams, and quizzes. Very expensive course which is taught through previous recordings from professor Butler.

Difficult class but what d you expect for calc 2. Lectures that were given were recorded by steve butler, which makes sense considering it would require a ton of work for her to record a whole new series. HW was easy, quizzes were somewhat difficult but were manageable. Exams were very difficult, more difficult than in-person exams.

Gave us prerecorded lectures to look at the whole semester and didnt care about the students. Proceeded to sit back the whole semester and collect a paycheck from the university despite not lifting a finger.
class is more about finding a way to complete the assignments than learning anything.

To quickly sum her up. She isn't the teacher, she tells you via email once you join her class it's taught through the person e-text. Every assignment including exams is made and graded through that. You pay her to respond to emails as she doesn't have any classes to teach. And any attempts to reach out result in a rude email. Very rude. Non-caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Bolles is a great instructor who works through examples and really tries to set a lot of her time aside to help her students. That being said, Math 165 at ISU is set up to be difficult, and I think she does the best she can at making the course and content tolerable for her students.

Team Based learning would work for you only if you are willing to work really hard outside the class. Group projects and quizzes will boost your grades up so much compared to other sections in the course. The exam weight for the final grade was less which helped! And Dr. Bolles had very effective office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Team Based Learning is part of her research, I believe. She'll explain it in more depth, but basically you're assigned a group and you complete team quizzes and project together. It makes it difficult to know how much you (as an individual) know for the test because everything is done as a team. Good luck and you have to work hard to get an A or B!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is reversed format. What this means is you have in class work with your assigned group. How you do in this group and homework determines nearly 60% of your grade. There is no lecture in class, you must watch videos on your own. The homework consists of 3 assignments a week and post quiz's. Also, 4 class tests, plus a cumulative final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Team Based Learning is not fun. We were required to teach ourselves the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Honest and object review: TBL is something I don't recommend simply because of how much more time it sucks up than regular calc, and engineers already don't have a lot of spare time. The videos were so boring, and I never learned much from them or from the quizzes. Be aware regular calc has weekly difficult quizzes, so I'd ask upper classmenformore
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: In case she is using the TBL method, you are screwed. There is barely any class without a quiz, ends up giving up 4 test/assignments for each topic. Exams are not at all easy. Only good thing about her is there is lot of extra credit. Works with Dr Elgin Johnson to make our life miserable. Try to to get out of her class asap.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Bolles is a very nice lady but not a very great math professor. Unless you enjoy doing tons of homework that doesn't pertain to the exam and teaching yourself the subjects, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bolles is passionate about math, caring, and a good person, but the Team Based Learning (TBL) process does not work for learning complex calculus concepts and solving calculus problems. In TBL, there are so many homework assignments and projects and I feel that I focus more on just getting the assignments done than actually learning calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bolles is a great person, but the Team-Based Learning style just does not work for Calculus. She barely lectures which means you have to teach yourself. There is a ton of group projects which has much more advanced applications of Calculus which is what the exams are based on. Having understanding and nice team members is helpful as well.

Dr. Bolles is a very good teacher, I personnally like Team based learning and believe it helps in future classes with remembering concepts past that semester. I do think if you end up with a team that doesn't pull their weight, you could be screwed, but Bolles is very helpful and will likely move you if asked. Bolles is available for office hours.

Dr. Bolles uses the "team based learning" style of teaching which means that you have to teach yourself the material outside of class and then do group projects in lecture. This isn't the worst way of learning especially under Dr. Bolles because she is very helpful, but I believe a traditional lecture is much more productive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Uses Team Based Learning, which basically boils down to the student needing to teach themselves the material on their own time by watching hours of videos each night, while class time is used to complete group projects. If teaching yourself calculus on your own time isn't how you want to spend your semester, I would highly recommend a new professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher. Explains concepts very well and teaches concepts well if asked one on one. You learn the concepts much better than other calc students but you have to put in much more work than others. There is usually a project or team quiz every day and some of the projects help and enforce your understanding while some don't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I would recommend her office hour 100%. She grades harshly, but if you take Calc 1 you need to know what you are doing. This is a team-based learning class, so take that as you will, I ended up liking the class and my team, so it was a good time. She makes you work for your grade but is really passionate about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult especially if you have the team based learning section. It's a lot of work and you have to do a lot of studying. However Dr. Bolles made calculus bearable. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS. She is amazing at explaining concepts that will stick with you for the rest of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: her class is group project. Depends on the group mate, you will have easy semester or hard semester. IT is your own luck. Almost every week, their is an group project and it takes a big part in grading. If you skip class, it affects your grade. Extra credit exist. If you participate half of it, you will get 3% more at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I had her for Calc I my first semester here so it was my first college level math class. I ended with an A, but it was by no accident. There's a lot of work you have to put in to be successful in this class, but Bolles does a great job of explaining things and is very helpful and accessible during her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Don't take this class!!!! Worked 1000 times harder than other calc students at ISU and I was still failing. Lots of homework and quizzes everyday!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Team based learning just does not work for math. Our entire class was based around doing extremely hard calc based group projects, which was what the tests were designed around. So if you can't understand the group projects, you'll never be able to figure out the tests! She barely lectures and is a hard grader.

Bolles is a sweetheart. She cares about her students. But the structure of the curriculum and the way the class is taught in general is not conducive for learning Calculus. There is some form of assignment due almost everyday of the week. The exams were poorly written. Some super long with short spans of time & others were short but graded harshly
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Team based learning kinda sucks. Dr. Bolles rarely lectures over the material unless it's the iRATs and tRATs that you've already done twice. There's lots of different types of assignments to keep track of and it's manageable if you know what you're doing. Wouldn't suggest team based learning to someone whose never taken calc before college.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Avoid her class unless you like working in groups, getting excess homework and failing tests.

Dr. Bolles is a solid choice if you're taking 165. But here's the thing: she makes you take online quizzes called IRATS before lecture. They're fairly difficult at times, so WATCH THE VIDEOS. Attendance is mandatory if you want a good grade. If you take this, I hope you like teamwork because that is 90% of the class. Overall, I would pick her.

Dr. Bolles knows the material very well and she can also explain it to students in a way they can understand. She is very willing to help students during class. The class is very team-based and it helped me out a lot because I could talk to other students and Dr. Bolles personally. I left the class with a very good understanding of calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bolles is very kind and always willing to help. She explains things very thoroughly and clearly. On the flip side, this class has no such thing as 'lecture'. All the learning is done outside of class in 10+ hours of homework each week. Her exams are difficult and the team-based learning setup is frankly ineffective. Still a very sweet lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class is set up in such a way that you have to teach yourself the material. The videos provided are slow and at best of little help (depending on how much you can learn from watching someone read a slideshow word for word). The teams are a poor excuse to avoid having to lecture, and the assignments are more tedious than helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She explains things really well.

Almost every concept in this class has to be self-taught in your own time, and there are two graded quizzes before Dr. Bolles even says a word on the content of each section. This is a lazy and ineffective way to teach, and I would strongly urge anyone to enroll in a different section if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Heather is a great professor. She is extremely helpful during office hours, but the course itself is very difficult. You have to come to class already knowing the material. I suggest to read the textbook. The videos provided are hard to understand and sometimes unhelpful. You really have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: A picky grader but is clear on what she expects on exams and prepares you well for them. She was very helpful and good at answering individual questions. Difficult course material but an effective teacher.   Her teaching style requires a lot of outside reading  of the textbook for short quizzes on material that hasn't yet been covered in class.

Dr. Bolles, I believe, has good intentions for the class. The way she used team teaching though was just ridiculous. If you haven't taken calculus yet I would not take her as your professor. She has great intentions but trying to watch videos instead of learning the material in class was ridiculous.

Avoid her if possible. She has the worst method of teaching. There are graded quizzes over a section that have to be taken before the section is taught in lecture. Her tests are pretty tough, and the way she grades them is ridiculous. I did well in this class because the SI leader was able to explain everything well.

Dr. Bolles was one of the most frustrating instructors I have ever encountered.  The lack of actual lecturing and excess of work graded based upon a group of 4 or 5 people is a terrible way to effectively teach individuals.  The tests are way too long and requires more work than needed to demonstrate understanding.  Too much conceptual nonsense too
She over complicates a lot of the problems and don't expect the tests to be anything like the homework, you have to REALLY understand the material.

If you have Team based learning try and get a different section because it was not fun and many people did not do very well. She didn't lecture a single day and we had to learn all of the material online.
Good teacher. There if need help.

Getting help is hard, and the the tests are always way to long.  The quizzes and group projects are so hard that sometimes she gets tripped up, even though she made them.  I would never recommend this professor.

Best math professor I've ever had. I had her for Calc 1 and 2. A lot of people don't like her because the clickers and reading quizzes can be hard. Lectures are very well explained and thought out. Very good at understand and answering students questions in a way the understand. Calc 2 is supposedly the hardest math class at ISU she made it oreasy

Dr. Bolles was the best math professor I've had at ISU. She was extremely clear in all of her lectures, and even though the clicker quizzes, recitation quizzes, and exams were very difficult, they were all very fair and she prepared you for every single one. Much better than any other calc 2 lecturer

The tests that she writes are extremely hard even if you know the material well.  The homework assignments are behind what we are doing in class and the online quizzes are are days ahead of class. Material has to be learned on your own time because class I filled with pointless group projects. One positive is her Blackboard  is organized well.

Dr. Bolles is the best Calculus professor at ISU. She does many examples in class, follows through every step, and has helpful office hours. She is always there to help you if you need it. Most importantly, she is VERY clear and ensures that we have a strong understanding of the fundamental concepts to calculus. There is homework, but it helps!

I had Dr. Bolles for Calc I, and thought she was great. Her tests can be hard, but if you follow along during lecture and put in the effort to learn the material, you should be fine.  She explained things thoroughly in lecture, which really helped. Reading quizzes are great! These let you learn in your own way, then in lecture she explains  it
Her lectures are very confusing.  I had a tutor along with the class all semester so that really helped.  Clicker points every day.  It seems like that's all we ever do in that class

Makes you teach yourself.  There are graded quizzes online before she has taught the material, In-class clicker quizzes before she has showed you how to do it, and MyLabsPlus homework that is way more difficult than the in-class examples.  If you draw her, switch sections.

Dr. Bolles was a really good teacher I thought. She does lots of examples and if you ask a question she will answer it and go through an example.  I like the way she did her tests because they were 5 questions, but only 4 got graded so you could pick your worst question to not get graded.

Im in the fall 2014 class and the exams are switched and much harder than the past exams she gives you. My tutor confirmed that this semester's exams are much harder than spring 2014's exams. Average on our exams are in the 50-60% range

She definitely knows what she's talking about and wants her students to learn. I found her lectures to sometimes be helpful. But sometimes not, because all she did was go over examples. Make sure you take your time when taking the reading quizzes because they are very tricky. The sample exams that she provides are very similar to the actual exams.
Professor Bolles knows what she's talking about, but her quizzes and tests are always completely different than what you expect and don't make any sense. I don't recommend having her as a teacher.

Dr. Bolles is an excellent professor who demands excellence from her students.  She is fair and thorough, and if you enter her class with a desire to learn and a basic understanding of differential calculus, you will learn a lot.

Most teachers are helpful and lenient with grades for efforts.(SI classes, tutors to show you have been trying) but not Bolles, you can be 0.39%-1% from the grade you need to move on and she won't show any leniency at all.  She wasn't a very helpful teacher either. Just went over examples. Exams were cmpletely different than what she went over.

I thought she was a great teacher for Calc 1. She went by examples rather than just lecturing, so that was nice. Her grading really pissed me off (because I got the correct answer, but she'd count points off for something stupid).
Bad teacher all around, not recommended.  Terrible exam/quiz writer and hard grader.  Should not be teaching.
Professor Bolles is a great teacher who enjoys watching students learn. That being said she sometimes has tendencies to go off on non-related tangents that no one really follows.
Math is a hard subject for me and she really helped and made sure I understood things...great teacher!

The content of this class is very boring, but Dr. Thompson is a great teacher and incredibly approachable and willing to help. The tests are very easy and you don't need to put forth a lot of effort in the class. Just go to class everyday, because your grade drops everytime you miss after 2 absences.
Hated the class, loved the prof!!
Great class, I looked forward to it everyday. test are a little difficult, and grading is very picky
great teacher! knows how to really talk to the students and she always makes sure that everyone understands what shes talking about!
No Comments
Very helpful and easy to talk to. Unorganized at times, but overall a pretty fair and effective professor.
Looked foreward to class everyday!

She makes a point to know all her students names and interact with everyone. She comes off kinda harsh at first, but she know's how to control her class and work with everyone and helps you actually learn something.
G.O.A.T, simple as that. Great dude, great professor, just show up and study a little and your good.

This professor is very humble and genuinely cares about the students and learning. The class is not very difficult, but you still feel like you learned something. Tests are pretty much all multiple choice. Attendance is part of the grade but it won't hurt your grade if you miss a few times.
Decent professor. Lectures weren't the most engaging and grade was heavily based off exams and the weekly homework assignment.

Great guy and even better professor. Lectures were valuable, and offers a lot of points to balance out exam grades if you didn't do so well. Amazing to talk with after class and is truly a wealth of knowledge in the supply chain field.
Great guy! Very approachable and easy to talk to, and he rewards those that show up regularly with extra points.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kip was an amazing professor. He takes class attendance but doesn't involve your grade very much. He has random in class worksheets that helps your understanding of the material. He is very to the point and is a very nice professor if you ever have to get in contact with him or ask him questions. He made the content easy to learn.
I had him for SCM 301, Great Professor!
I have had kip for like all of my SCM classes, and he is a great professor overall. Relaxed, no-nonense, and grades fairly.

TAKE THIS CLASS, he swayed me to add SCM as another major. He is fantastic. One of the few great teachers at Iowa State. He is, without a doubt, my favorite teacher I have ever had. Explains well, teaches well, uses real stories, and makes the class very engaging. He is what you would want in a professor. You can tell he cares about his students.
Great professor. Usually lectures by PowerPoint slides so if you dont go you can access online. Had for a few classes, all have a few papers and few tests and quizzes. Super chill guy

Likes powerpoint lectures. Has some homework assignments , none being too difficult. Likes to make jokes . Can skip a few classes but I wouldn't do it too much. Had him for another class as well. Has routine medium-difficulty tests.
This is a great professor! She makes class extremely enjoyable every single day. She also formats her class in a very effective way. This was in my top 3 classes I have taken at Iowa State so far!

Ginka is very fun. I was always excited to go to her lectures! She gets to know every student and is enthusiastic in lectures. The class is not too tough if you keep up on her practice problems. Would definitely recommend her.

Ginka was an awesome professor to take. She really got to know you and would also answer any questions you had. The class was difficult, but she made it manageable and entertaining. Would recommend taking 310 with her if you are choosing between other options.
Good engaging lectures, funny, but very knowledgeable. Will answer any question you have.
Made a tough subject as manageable as possible. Would make jokes during lecture and keep everything light hearted. Overall a 10/10 professor.

Ginka cares a lot about her students and will make an effort to learn your name and ask you questions. Her lectures can sometimes feel rushed, with a lot of material to cover. However, she gives you material that prepares you well for exams. There were 5 homeworks, 3 quizzes (one drop), and 4 exams (one drop). Overall, she was a great professor.

Ginka is just a fun lady. I don't think I learned a ton in class, I had to do a lot of independent learning, she wont spoon feed you, but she CARES A LOT. She just wants to interact with her students and truly cares whether or not they are doing well. She will learn your name and call on you sometimes but isn't rude if you don't know the answer.

Few things in the grade book so it is important to do well on monday quizzes and friday exams. Review problems and homework problems are the most helpful for tests. She is super kind and really tries to get to know everyone and their names. Lectures are a bit confusing, the mathematical problems are what you want to focus on to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buy the book to be able to do review problems for the exam. Her lectures are great and she teaches everything you need to know. Formula sheets given for each exam, but she makes you work for it! If you can take 310 with her, definitely do it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a funny, helpful teacher who wants you to earn an A and learn something valuable. I highly recommend taking her class. Do the practice problems and you will get an A.
One of the best Finance teachers I have had. Class was difficult but I learned a lot. Grading scale makes the class more stressful than it should be.

I liked this teacher, she makes class fun and has a good sense of humor. There are no assignments so if you are a bad test taker this isn't for you. However, the tests were graded at a pretty steep curve (for a business class) so that helps.

Exams are super hard. She does a terrible time explaining things. When you ask a question she doesn't answer the questioni well at all.  I'm normally a 3.5 or above student, I studied for 8  hours spread out over 3 days and still failed the exam. Awful teacher.
Very helpful instructor, high grade, she made the average of the class's grade between B+ to A-, a must take class if u wanna get a high grade
Very hard to understand. Try avoiding this professor. Exams are super hard.

She was a pretty good teacher. The class is very structured with a quiz the monday before a test that Friday. It's pretty easy and she explains things pretty well. I have no complaints, and I feel like I learned some stuff as well!

Terrible teacher. Just reads off slides and is really boring class. Can't understand what she is saying due to her accent. If your a finace major you have to take her course so all you can do is try and do better than the average on her tests and quizs and hope the curve is really low.
terrible teacher. flies through everything, cant understand her at all, talks soft and points out hard ways of doing problems instead of short cuts. do not get her as a prof

Although only about 1/4 of the semester was in person, I can tell Dr. Hernandez really cares about the history he teaches. His lectures are very informational and he provides insightful answers to questions. It is a shame that the course had to go online for over half the semester.

If you care about history, you won't think his lectures are boring. It's obvious he cares about the material and his students. Make sure to participate in discussions and ask questions. There is lots of writing assignments, but they are short for a history course. Grades easy as long as you show that you understood the readings on a surface level.
A solid professor all around. Although his lectures can seem dry at times, he clearly knows the material. He is also accessible outside of class and gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nice guy but lectures are dry and the homework is pretty dumb.

Nice guy but is pretty awkward to talk to, and his accent is tough to understand. Lectures are super dull, and some of the assignments are pretty pointless. He is also a pretty hard grader, which doesn't make things any easier. I would advise you to STAY AWAY from him as a professor.

The lectures are incredibly boring, hard to understand and you cannot let your mind stray for even a second or you'll miss something. He's a super nice guy, the class isn't that hard and grading is easy, but he's definitely not a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice enough guy but the worst and most boring lecturer I've ever had. It's an 80-minute class and lectures could easily fit into 50 minutes. Talks around in circles a lot and only grades based on two exams, a book response, one essay proposal, and one essay. I wanted to take more Latin America history classes, but I won't from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor so sweet and genuinely fantastic, caring, approachable and supportive. Lectures are clear and engaging, with one weekly discussion and easy participation. He offers an online discussion option for those who can't speak in class or have excused absences. Every assignment is meaningful, making entrepreneurship exciting and accessible.

You can tell he cares about what he's teaching. It helps a lot that he has a bunch of real life business experience as a venture capitalist and investing in real estate so he actually knows what he's talking about and isn't just blowing smoke. Talked to him after class about real estate on occasion and seems like a great dude.

This class is primarily project based with a few being individual but they're mostly group projects. His grading on the projects is through, but the exams are really easy. Just know the case studies and go through the slides and you'll be fine. He also curves the exams as well.

Professor Mueller does a great job in this class of introducing lecture content and facilitating interactive discussions designed to illustrate the use of the introduced tools and principles.  You can tell he actually cares about the students and is happy to meet with you outside of class. Group projects are central to class and can be fun.

Weekly case discussions are a highlight of the course. The course is primarily project-based. Dr. Mueller grades the projects extremely "thoroughly", do not expect to get 100% on any of them. Assuming you exceed his criteria for what is "exceptional" on the biggest semester project, then the final exam is optional, but don't bank on it.
Lots of busy work, doesn't really know what he's talking about.

He's not a bad professor he genuinely enjoys lecturing and wants to be there, which is awesome. He properly prepares you for the exams. There are two flaws, though: the exams are on paper, and you have to write a lot. Also, group projects often get 9.1 or 9.2, never a full 10. Overall, it's an easy class, just wished I had a better group
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mueller is one of my favorite professors at Iowa State. The lectures were amazing and I always looked forward to going to class. Attendance and group projects are huge in this class, so if you skip class a lot, you will lose valuable points. Overall, he is a great guy and his lectures were amazing.
Great guy, he loves teaching you can tell because he always has a positive energy. he really cares for all students. cool class overall.
Fantastic teacher, show up and attend class and you will do fine.

I would recommend this prof to anyone. His lectures are very intriguing and very enjoyable to watch. Class is made up of weekly lectures ranging from 30-45 min and 2 writing assignments that are easy to understand while allowing you to actually comprehend the information.

Mueller brings energy to every class. Only two exams total. Not that much HW. Group project that lasts the whole semester. If you show up and participate in the case study's you get free points. If you do not want to raise your hand in front of the class you can participate in an online discussion board. Not a hard class at all. Take his class.

All you have to do is participate in discussions, and do group work. he's kind of a tough grader and doesn't warn you much in advance for big assignments. Keep up on the syllabus and participate in class and you'll be fine.

Summer class was fast paced. In-class activities, discussions, an on-going project with mini milestone projects throughout the class, & 2 exams. He doesn't provide feedback unless asked, but he's willing to help if you have any issues. He can be a tough grader, so CONFIRM you include ALL of the information in paragraph form on the project & exams!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not expect to get a response.
Great professor, which made going to class easy.
Great class. One course project, 2 exams and weekly homework. Easy if you watch the lectures.

Mueller was honestly my favorite professor from a class I have taken over the past 4 years. You can tell that he actually cares about helping you understand the material he's teaching. His feedback is detailed, so you know what to work on or correct moving forward. His lectures are amazing, never boring. Made an acct just to rate him honestly!
Very inspirational professor made learning easy

Professor Muller is hands down the best instructor I've had at ISU. He is energetic and engaging, and it is obvious that he cares deeply about entrepreneurship and wants to pass that experience on to his students. Classes go by so fast. I had a blast in this class, and the final project was one that I actually invested in and was passionate about.

310 with Mueller was one of the best classes I have taken at Iowa State. The class was based around a midterm, final, and one main group project. Prof. Mueller gives amazing feedback during every step of the way, he really wants the student to succeed. His tests are also very straight forward. 310 with Brandon Mueller is a must take class.

Brandon is an amazing professor, I wish I could take every class with him. He cares about his students and makes lectures fun and interesting! We have a midterm and final and then semester group project. He also offers extra credit! The concepts are easy to grasp if you show up to class or review his powerpoints. Class isn't mandatory, but fun!
Mike is a very helpful and passionate teacher to a decently hard course. I would suggest taking him as he cares about your success and wants to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Bootsma made learning law very enjoyable. Each lecture is a great time, and he's very passionate about meeting each student. Most passionate professor I have ever met, and he loves seeing his students work hard.
The Goat. simply
Funny guy- always willing to help out, not a particularly difficult course either
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bootsma is by far one of the better professors at Iowa State. He's not one of the professors that reads off slideshows, he actually cares about his students and genuinely wants you to succeed. He is always there to help you and encourages you to talk to him if you are lost. The exams require a bit of studying but are not too difficult.
I never skipped a lecture, BY CHOICE! this man loves his students so much. he will never waste your time, and will ALWAYS help you when you ask.
The best professor at ISU. Makes lectures engaging and fun. GO TO CLASS!
amazing professor
Very engaging lectures. Exam review sessions were also very helpful. Love Bootsma!
Be sure to attend class and to go through the textbook, exam reviews, and other available content and you will get an A. Bootsma is great at teaching and giving clear guidance

Grading felt VERY subjective/moody - the rubric for PPT was made AFTER assignments were due. Getting 10/10 felt like a moving target. Interesting class, but poorly taught, with many grammar errors and little clarity on what he wants. 3 exams worth 60%, 20 MC questions, and 7-9 short answers in an hour 15. He thinks he's nice, but beware his lies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor was very knowledgeable about the topic and you could tell he wanted you to succeed. Lecture videos were very nice weekly and the exams weren't that difficult.

Hands down the best instructor. He is extremely accommodating, funny, and chill. While his exams are weighted 80% of your grade if you attend the review sessions, do the readings, and attend the lectures, you will do just fine. I enjoyed taking ACCT 215 with him. I strongly recommend anyone who is taking ACCT 215 to take it with him.
Professor Bootsma makes this class fun and engaging. He provides great study resources like practice exams, and is always willing to meet one-on-one. Unstuckstudy was a helpful study tool too.

Bootsma is an amazing professor who actually cares about his students. Attendance isn't mandatory, extra credit for the lecture before break. Makes his lectures fun and entertaining. He gives out t-shirts and prizes, very engaging. He does lots of examples/stories. Recommend watching online videos, 1 hour video for the whole week of lectures.

I took this class in person but would recommend taking it online. The lectures are all entirely available on Canvas and I personally didn't feel that attending in person added anything to the learning experience. Mike is very willing to answer questions and wants students to succeed. This is an easy class if you put in the minimum effort!
My favorite professor in the College of Business! He has won the voted staff award almost every year in a row.

The class is test-heavy, but Mike is always there for his students. He is easily accessible, even willing to make arrangements outside of office hours to meet with students and help them out, whether it pertains to class or their personal lives. He is truly caring and a very great professor. He makes class interesting with stories and humor.

Bootsma is a great man, and will thank you for coming to class...just about every single class. Some may say he's weird, but c'mon, his teaching ways are what should be emulated by the Ivy College of Business. I wish more professors were like him, seriously.

One of the best professors at Iowa State. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures are fun. He always made his class fun by making it very interactive. The exams are not that hard, if you study, it is pretty straightforward. I would take a class with him again.

Bootsma is the man! Took his ACCT 215 class and although the four exams were a strong majority of the grade (350 out of the 400 pts) he provided practice exams and very solid lectures/notes to help with the exams. Most exams got 4-6 point curves as well. Was great at explaining terms and concepts in class and made class fun and engaging to attend.

Bootsma is the man! He has great lectures which are easy to take notes on and he always post them online so you can follow along. He explains terms and ideas very well that is easy to understand and provides practice exams which are EXTREMELY helpful to prep for real exams which are all multiple choice and usually get 4-6 point curves. Smart guy.

Overall a really great class. Lectures aren't required to go to but Bootsma is really funny so it's always worth going and so you don't miss material. Prepares you really well for exams and is always willing to meet with students outside of class.

The BEST professor at Iowa State. Makes every lecture so interesting with funny skits and humor. Gives genuine real-life examples that help. The exam simulations are very similar to the actual exams. Try and get him for Acct 215 if you can.

AWESOME. He is so funny and made online acct 215 so great. He answered emails within a day and always gives a little extra credit on exams. You do need to watch the lecture videos and read a little bit of the textbook to understand the content but he makes it enjoyable!

In order to succeed you need to memorize all the content. There is a lot, but it is doable. He responds to emails quickly and wants you to do well. I found the online class very doable as long as you keep up with the notes and make sure you're retaining everything before exam day. Really nice guy

He is the Goat. Even though it was a law class, he made it entertaining. I would say take this man if you can. He wrote a textbook, but you don't need it to pass the class. If you sit near the front, he will try to remember your name, and that's always nice. Overall it's a hard class because its mainly exams, but a -B is the average
The GOAT. Take any class he teaches and don't think twice about it. He is caring and pretty funny.

Amazing professor who truly cares about his student during and after the class has ended. Clear grading and good lectures. Up to you to determine what grade you get depending on how well you study. Lots of material to learn and comprehend. 4 tests, a quiz/chapter, exams get curves most of the time. Would def recommend over the other ACCT215 teacher

Professor Bootsma is super accessible. I took this class online but he always made sure to let us know how to contact him, and he responded quickly to emails. He's an engaging & hilarious lecturer and really wants his students to succeed. It's a fair amount of reading, but interesting content.

He is a great professor. He cares a lot about his students and is willing to work with them if they struggle. He is funny, cares a lot about all his students, and wants to get to know each of them. The exams are somewhat difficult if you do not study, but if you do, then you will be fine.
Awesome
