reviews.comment: Dr. Burke is an incredible professor! This was a very discussion heavy course but the classroom environment felt very safe to share ideas. Dr. Burke cares about all of her students and works with everyone to make sure everyone does well in her class. Despite this class being at 8am, I was always excited to come to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Burke is an amazing professor. I had her for a class during first semester of my sophomore year, had her for another class second semester, and I chose to take another of her classes this semester. She is an incredible lecturer and is always willing to take input from students to make class more discussion-based. Take one of her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had after five years at this university. She's authentic and passionate about every topic covered. Very refreshing, and I feel very lucky to have her as a professor. Can't stop raving about this course and professor to my friends and family.

Brianna Burke is an absolutely amazing professor- so knowledgeable and willing to share her brilliant thoughts on any literature. There are a decent amount of readings, but they weren't too long and they were mostly enjoyable. Be prepared to contribute to class discussion. You really get what you give in this class and your grade will reflect that.

one of the best and most authentic professors at isu! really knows what she's talking about and cares about students. class was straightforward - readings as homework and then discussions about those readings in class. very few assignments, which was nice, but that mean grades were based on just a few things. great class, though, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved this professor! She was great! The class is pretty fun and lots of discussion.

If you hate in class participation and discussion do not take this class. In the past it is what I hated most, but for some odd reason I found myself sticking it out for this class and ended up loving it. Dr. Burke is a one of a kind professor (she would hate that cliche) but it is true. If you ever get the chance to take a class of hers, do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Burke has many great qualities and a few condemning flaws. The biggest one is that she can be a bit pretentious, which I hated, but then and again the woman is very intelligent and she clearly knows her stuff. She's passionate also and she is willing to help and give you feed back. She's actually kind of amazing. I would recommend  her classes.
Burke is a wonderful professor. She is opinionated but I have enjoyed the classes I have taken with her.

Professor Burke is one of my favorite professors ever. She truly cares about this class and art overall, and was my most relaxed and enjoyable class to be in. Wish I could retake this class again and again.
Burke is by far one of the best professors I've had at ISU. Super fun to work with and knows and cares A LOT about the subjects she teaches. I would retake her classes in a heartbeat.

Brianna is a phenomenal educator. She handles difficult topics delicately and professionally. Come into this class with an open mind, participate in discussions, and do the readings and you'll pass! I would recommend everyone take a class with her!
Dr. Burke is amazing. I learned so much about the world and myself. I want to take every class with her! She cares a lot.

This was an interesting class, but Dr. Burke's rhetoric on white privilege, progressiveness, and the occasional how evil the US is in the world becomes ad nauseam. It seems like she really likes to hear herself talk, too, no matter the relevance of the subject which, of course, is annoying also. Unnecessarily tough grader too.

Brianna is amazing! She's super nice, and she really brings the class to life through discussion. This was my favorite class I have ever taken in college. She gives great feedback and pushes you to improve yourself and think about things that you wouldn't normally think about. I'd recommend anyone to take this class!

This professor is very rude. She wasn't helpful AT ALL. She makes you write response papers and then bashes you on anything you say in class and calls you unintelligent. I would stay away from any course that this professor teaches. A very RUDE woman, and I know I'm not the only one she was rude to.
shes amazing

Fantastic professor. Demonstrates her dedication to education during every class. Every class is extremely interesting and pertains to every field within the Uni. This particular class should be required by the college, particularly at an early age, because it really helps one understand their ultimate career path.
Great professor. One of my favorite professors! She is smart and passionate. Participation is big in class. She will push you but in a good way. I highly recommend taking any class she teaches!

She is a very passionate person, and that comes across in her teaching. You have to participate in her classes in order to get a good grade, but she is very helpful and friendly. Grading is fair, if a bit tough.
Byeong-Young Cho was helpful if you asked for it. Unfortunately, I didn't learn very much in the class. He was entertaining and made class worth showing up. Get started on the TUP early.
Byeong-Young got stuck with a less than interesting class, but his willingness to laugh at himself and the subject make the class much more enjoyable.

Dr. Cho is a great guy with a dedication to reading and to his students. The class assignments aren't too difficult overall, though some are time-consuming. He is wonderful to listen to and tells some interesting stories from time to time!

Jana is a really awesome teacher who only expects respect in return. If you show her that you're making an honest effort she will be on your side to the bitter end. She teaches history from the perspective of a historian so she emphasizes personal research over memorization. She does NOT tolerate cellphones in her class and will call you out on it.

In the Western Civ class, she gives the questions to answers before tests, so that helps, but because of that she also expects you to put a lot of effort into answering them. The book you have to read is absolutely horrible, so boring, big, and a struggle to get through, but needed for the test. Very funny and interesting in lecture.

I liked her in my thesis writing class but if you ask for her help outside of class, she will most likely avoid your emails and will not stay to her word. If you trap her in her office hours she is fun to talk to.

This class is somewhat interesting but may be difficult if time is not dedicated for tests. Long reading assignments are given three days a week and it seems overwhelming but reading it all isn't worth it. Meet with TA's before the test to review.

There is a lot of reading to do but you can mainly just skim the pages. She is so funny in lecture and easy to talk to. DO NOT use your phone in class because she will call you out in front of 200 people and make you leave. I would definitely want her as a teacher again.

She definitely liked to look at the Feminism aspect of early Western Civ. She really ruined what should have been a really interesting class. Tests are blue book tests(All writing), so if you do not like to write, heads up.  She also uses a textbook that SHE WROTE. So good luck selling it back.

Amazing, her lectures are gripping. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and is the best ever.  The text book is a collection of reading specialy selected by her and is a wonderful read.  The only class I actually love to go to.  Plus she is a babe

Jana makes class fun and interesting. The syllabus looks difficult, but she is very lenient and understands you have other things happening in your schedule. You aren't just sitting, listening to lecture the whole time. Totally recommend her and this class if you want to learn more about global history.
Worst Professor at Iowa State. Avoid her at all costs. Frequently will take time out of her terrible lectures to randomly verbally assault students. Worst experience of my academic career.
My favorite professor by far.  The syllabus looks intimidating at first glance but if you put the work in you'll easily do well.  I highly recommend any class with her.
Jana is an amazing Professor, Historian, and person. She will do anything to help you if you need it and her classes are fun. Definitely some one I'd drink beer with.
She is pretty funny and keeps class interesting.  The syllabus can be scary but it isn't that bad!

Most likely the best professor at Iowa State.  She actually TEACHES, not just lectures.  Fun in class, and compassionate and understanding outside of class.  All assignments are helpful to learning, and most readings are very interesting.  I have taken her classes several times.

Very entertaining professor and very easy.  I disliked the readings and mini papers that we did, but the rest of the material was good.  Western Civ. 1   I took it in the summer and she let those who wanted to not have to take the final.  It was nice!

Jana is an awesome professor, she is always very helpful if you ask for help. Her classes aren't that easy but only because she expects her students to work at a high level. I would not skip class because not only do you miss important things that you could not gain from readings, but Jana makes classes entertaining. You never know what she'll say.

Jana is one of the best.  Her class is always hilarious and you will learn a lot.  You may be a bit intimidated at first, but she's not out to get you, she just wants you to actually THINK.  She's always willing to talk with you about papers and is generally very flexible.  Go to her office hours even if you don't need the help, she's a blast.

She has been the best professor I have had so as an undergrad. Her classes are very engaging, thought provoking, and just fun. I really looked forward to class with her. If you just go to class and actively participate you will do fine.

Dr. Byars is by far the best teacher I have ever had.  She knows her stuff, she's extremely fair, fun, intelligent, and relate-able.  If you pay strict attention in class, read what she asks you to read, take decent notes, and above all: THINK CRITICALLY, you will pass with flying colors.  Dr. Byars truly makes historians out of her students.
Shes a fun teacher who wants to get her students to think. One of my favorite teachers at Iowa State.

Excellent teacer.  Takes the time to relate everything learned in class to something worthwhile. Great for people who get the point of studying history. Very willing to help students, I took my papers in two or three times before turning them in and she was always happy to see me. I am going to take classes just to learn from her. Best Stories Ever
Great Teacher! Really enjoys what she's teaching, and helps students. At first I was a bit intimidated but she has become one of my favorite history professors.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Extremely personable, helpful, and knowledgable. You can get off topic with a side conversation during a lecture and still learn relevant information. If you are interest in politics at all, you need to take a class from Dr. Bystrom at Iowa State.

I took her Women in Politics class and she was pretty great. We have 3 tests, and she reviewed for each of them the class before, basically telling you what to know. Couldn't be much easier. Weekly reading quizzes, which if you scan the chapter headlines and boxes, you'll do fine. I only showed up for tests and the weekly quiz and I got an A!
Very interesting class with a lot of reading. But she clears everything up and guest speakers are interested.

Nice guy, attendance wasn't required and the lectures were a bit boring, but the course was overall really easy. There were a few people who only showed up on the mandatory quiz days and from what I heard they did just fine. He gives out occasional extra credit which is nice since if you do it right you won't have to take the final.

Overall chill guy. Very easy class and he is able to effectively communicate the material to the class in his lectures. No surprise twists or turns here. Show up to all of his classes and you will pass. He does grade exams slightly harsher than all of his other stuff, but only ever so slightly.

This class is fairly easy. He is extremely monotone, so be ready to try to stay awake in class. He grades heavily if you don't put exactly what you want. You only have to show up on Fridays for Friday writings, which are completed alone or in a group.
You would think this would be an easy class but he is a tough grader. I recommend doing all the extra credit and get as many points as possible but it goes by points not percentage

Worst course I've ever taken. Professor was degrading and made you leave class feeling depressed. Extremely rude when you ask about a grade given, and expects students to just read his mind for what type of writing he wants. All grading is subjective, so don't get on his bad side or he will make your grades suffer.

Prof. Butler is super chill. He is kind of monotoned, but his lectures are easy to understand. Just go to class and do the writing assignments in class. In class essays are the only thing I studied for. He usually allows group work and lots of extra credit. I honestly don't do the readings, and I still got an A.

He was an okay professor. Granite I barely showed up to class because most of the material here is common sense. He would also say to not use ChatGPT for assignments just about every time. Felt like he was out to get the people who use it. One way or another professors will have to adapt to AI.
I recommend attending lectures, I attended every one and did well in the class. Take notes on everything, because you can use the notes on homework and some exams.

Unengaging and made class dreadful. Phil 2300 is supposed to be a fun class that most students enjoy. However, I had a terrible time in this class due to Professor Butler's teaching style. Although it was an easy A, I would not take him again. Look for a better professor who will actually make class worth going to.

Dr. Butler is a great professor- he's one of the best ones I've had. He's a great lecturer, and is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, which makes class engaging. He provides useful feedback on assignments, that help you develop stronger arguments. If you attend class and read the material, you will do well

reviews.comment: While he's pretty boring his lectures are straight to the point and easy to follow

Dr. Butler teaches by reading from his own notes, which isn't very engaging but makes it easy to know what content will be covered on writing assignments. You can use notes for writing assignments, so attend as often as possible and write down everything he writes down.

Professor can be boring sometimes during class. He uses only a single tone while speaking during class. His teaching style is old school. You will need to take notes during classes. He is definitely a tough grader, he will always find a way to deduct your points in Friday writing assignments. He likes do a sad/stress face during classes.

reviews.comment: You definitely don't want to miss class, especially Fridays. I thought he was a great professor. He can be a little intimidating but he wears Doc Martins and the lecture is never boring. Everything you need to know is always in the notes - but make sure to do the readings.

Very easy to do well in this course. Do not buy the book for this class. He references it a few times, but it really isn't needed. Going to class and coopying his notes is really all you need to do in order to do good on his exams. (A lot of people don't go to class). There are some Friday Writing assignments which are required to be at class.

Attendance wasn't mandatory, but notes displayed in class were necessary for papers and exams.  Weekly participation in groups.  He was not too difficult overall, but he was a hard grader.  He is not very personable and always seems sad.

All around poor professor. Emailed him for almost 2 months back and forth to settle a missed pop quiz due to medical necessities and it ended with him ignoring my emails. Also carries an aura of depression into class daily. If possible take somebody else.

Professor Butler provided ample opportunity to work with the material and gain extra credit. He was very willing to answer your questions clearly during and outside of class. The tests are laid out pretty nicely following the lecture notes. Would definitely take the class with him.

Professor Butlers class was a good experience. Phil 230 is a pretty straightforward class; as long as you write down the notes that he provides in class, youll do just fine. A few in class writing assignments but nothing too hard. Butler has a monotone voice, and a basic presentation style, however, he does crack some golden jokes ever so often.

reviews.comment: Great professor for 230. It's lecture heavy and notes aren't online so you really have to go to class if you want to pass. He also gives extra credit for participating.

reviews.comment: He kind of has a monotone voice, but I really liked his class. It's obvious that some people just don't have an affinity for philosophy, so that's the reason that this class could be difficult. It is also difficult if you don't like taking notes or listening to long lectures. I really liked his jokes and lectures! He also lets you out early a lot.

Professor Butler is a really good choice if you're going to take 230. He makes the material so clearly outlined and easy to understand in his lectures that doing the readings becomes unnecessary. Show up to lecture and his class will be an easy A (doesn't post notes online). Grades easily and offers some extra credit.

reviews.comment: It's about what you'd expect from a freshmen level class, however he can be pciky somewhat with his essay grading.

reviews.comment: The most important thing for this class is to attend lecture. Professor Butler gives you everything you need to know for each quiz and exam. If you can answer his in class questions on the reading you will end up getting extra credit points.

reviews.comment: In order to do well in this class, you need to go to class. Monotone voice, but is pretty funny sometimes.

reviews.comment: He's a little bit of a hard grader, especially when it comes to written assignments. However, he is more than accommodating if you need to move a test because of an academic conflict. He is always available during office hours and is more than happy to help. He has a monotone voice but cracks some pretty funny jokes sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took PHI230 to fill an elective. If you arent majoring in Philosophy, do not take this class. As a student from another major, I had a hard time understanding how to understand how people from the past understood things. On a test, I responded to a long answer question and was literally given a 0/10 for the answer. Not 1 or 2/10, a stinking 0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He explains the content very well and goes through the notes at a good pace. The tests are fine as long as you review your notes. His voice is also very monotone, but he's a pretty chill guy. I personally thought that the class was interesting and he always let us out at least 5-10 min early.
Does a pretty good job teaching the necessary material. Test questions are tricky sometimes . He is stiff at first but after a few weeks of class he loosens up.

The graders are terrible. On every test/writing assignment, my friends and I would put the same thing and one would miss points and the other wouldn't. If you go to Butler about it, he won't do anything. You pretty much have to see into the future for the writing assignments and figure out the specific word you need to use or you'll miss points.

Show up and copy the notes and you'll do fine. He offers extra credit opportunities and study sessions before every exam. He's really good about answering questions and making sure students understand. He's an easier grader if he knows you, so participate by asking questions or answering questions in class. Dry sense of humor but very laid back.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was a really good teacher! At first he seems blocked off, and reserved, but once he starts lecturing hes actually pretty funny. I liked his lectures becase it clarified what I did not understand from the reading. Literally everything on the test was from the notes so make sure you study your notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dry sense of humor which is always nice. He clearly explains the generally outline of the course and it is 100% accurate. No homework, everything is in class and guided (besides exams). Philosophy goes in a big circle but he fills in all the gaps and gives you a good grasp on the ins and out of the class. Great instructor for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Butler is a solid professor.  Pretty laid back and funny.  However, his material and teaching style is a little dry.  He lays out his notes very clearly so take good ones and you'll be set on the test.  He begins each class with a review of the previous so if you skip its not the end of the world.  Didn't use the textbook very much

Found him to be a great teacher who really understands the things he was teaching. Will crack a few jokes in class and the only assignments are a few group writings on Fridays. I found the essays on the exams to be tough sometimes because it seemed he was searching for you to say a specific word, so make sure to understand the topic.

LOVED this professor.  His class had no homework besides a few readings and he made things very easy to understand.  No papers, clear lectures, study guides and tons of extra credit.  I will be trying to take more of his classes in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Solid at explaining things, throws in the occasional joke. As long as you go to the lectures, write down all of his notes, and pay attention, it should be an easy class. He makes it interesting enough where you won't space off too often. Enjoyed taking the class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Travis is an awesome philosophy teacher. I struggled at the start of the semester, but talking to him early on really helped me understand how he structures his lecture notes and gets his ideas across. He has an extremely dry sense of humor and it can be hilarious at times but cringy at other times. Do not skip the lectures if you want to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher. He explains the material for the class well, he also has a dry sense of humor which makes him hilarious. I would highly recommend him for a professor, especially for this class.

I really enjoyed him! he has a dry sense a humor which lightens up the class a bit! Make sure you go to class and take nots, if you do that, you will be set for his tests. Readings are not necessary to get .

GO TO CLASS! The tests are straight from the lecture, so take good notes. Exams are pretty straight forward and he will give a review sheet. Make flashcards to memorize the concepts. He provides some opportunitie to gain extra credit. Get the extra credit (Grand slam) out of the way early. Its 10 points of true extra credit. 200 points in the class

He was a very easy to understand, and he is very good at reviewing in class. His class was one of my easiest classes I've ever taken at Iowa State. He is an amazing lecturer because he understands the material. He explains the concepts in different ways to help everyone understand, GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS! If its at 8am though, good luck.

He is a really good lecturer and keeps your attention and also makes things so easy to understand! He explains everything in depth so the tests are relatively easy. I would definitely take another class with this professor again.
He is soooo boring! I had this class at 8 am and almost fell asleep everyday!  I would recommend a different professor! Don't get the book! You won't use it ever!

His lectures are very detailed and basically all of the reading information is covered in class, but that also means you have to go to class.  The exams are essay and short answer with a few multiple choice in the mix.

Butler is an interesting teacher. Hes your classic old guy philosopher with a kind of hipster twist. If you go to class and take the same notes he has on the projector, you will get an A because they are verbatim what he asks for on his essay style tests. Do the extra credit for some extra padding, and you will be fine.

He is very clear at the beginning of the semester on how the points will be distributed. He can be a tough grader in that he may not always have the clearest of feedback in order for you to improve on. DO NOT buy the textbook, he goes over the readings the next day. The only thing that messes with your grade are the in class Friday writings.

He is a very straight forward teacher, the expectations are clear and it is easy to pass if you attend class. He is also funny and easy to listen to most of the times, but can be boring at times as well. Overall a good teacher and good experience taking his class
Great class. Show up every class (never miss), takes the notes, go to the review session, go to office hours, and DO THE GRAND SLAM EXTRA CREDIT! And you will do fine.

I would absolutely recommend trying to take this course with Butler. He actively gets to know his class, and explains concepts with clarity. He has a witty sense of humor, and makes even abstract concepts very simple. Just attend his lectures, and all of the writing and exams are a piece of cake. (Honestly I did not buy a textbook and I was ok.)

Teacher does not care if you miss class and do not get the notes. So make sure to attend class. He will not provide you with any notes that you miss. Exams aren't too difficult. Make sure to study notes. The notes are the material he puts on his exams.
Definitely a professor you want. Easy to understand and gives great examples. Just go to class and get the notes and you shouldn't be worried at all.

Great professor with a good sense of humor. Although the subject matter is a little boring, he throws in some jokes that make class less painful. Tests are straight from the notes and study guide. Easy A if you put in a little effort. Expectations are clearly outlined. DON'T BUY THE BOOK

Although monotone, Dr. Butler is a very competent teacher. Exams are based entirely off of notes (you do not need to read the textbook). The notes are lengthy, but are clearly outlined and defined. Very easy, although I believe attendance is necessary to earn an A.

This guy is very monotone! Beware if taking it to early you will fall asleep. He does give out a lot of extra credit to help your grade because tests are all your grade is based on. Must go and get the lecture notes or you are looking at an F. Class wasn't horrible but you have to put quite a bit of time

Does speak in a monotone and has a very dry humor but if you go to class and take down the notes he gives you they are all you need to do the study guide and the test is basically right off that. I did bad on the first couple test but did the study guide for the last couple and almost got 100% on each of them.He does give a lot of notes though.

While his humor was kind of dry, class was hardly boring. He clearly knew his stuff and when he didn't, he admitted it. I didn't need the book too much and I kept getting A's on the tests. Make sure that your essays are longer and chock full of information - they are graded a bit strictly. Easy Extra credit, though.
He has a great sense of humor, which makes class entertaining and engaging. He is also clearly intelligent, which made me trust what he was saying even more.

He can be pretty funny once in a while, he has his moments. His voice is monotone, his tests were pretty hard I suggest reading the textbook and his notes aren't online so go to class and you will be fine.
For an entry level class, he treats it like it's a 500+. Tests are long essay and must be PERFECT to get any points. Avoid him if you're taking 230

this guy is a joke. he circles around his point so much, that he leaves the class almost entirely confused. tests are mostly essays, and impossible to get full credit on. he tries to be funny, but fails. if you ask him a question after class, he still fails to make you any less lost. monotone

Almost impossible not to get at least a C(has an awesome curve only need 50% to get C-). Ususally boring but does say some cheesy jokes that get laughs. Go to class and take notes. All I did was study the notes for an hour or two every test and got an A-. I would def. take again.
monotone but has a sense of humor, tests right out of notes. gives a study guide that if you fill out and study a little bit you should be fine. Doesn't expect too much

It wasn't a hard class... the test were all the same and came mostly out of the notes.  The way he talked the first day about exams... I thought they would be a lot harder, at least he would grade them harder.  If you go to class and participate in the extra credit you should do fine... but I took it in the summer

Good sense of humor, but a lot of people miss it because he is a little monotone. Go to lecture, take notes, study a little before the test and you should get a good grade. Very fair and not tricky at all.

If you enjoy a class with a lot of cheesy sarcastic humor, than this class is for you.  He has way too much expectancy of students in a intro class or at least most students first class into philosophy.  If he were to give you a study guide talking of a multitude of things to study, ONE might appear on the test.  He tries, but fails...
Would talk and talk about not about what was on the tests.  All tests have a large section of essay that has to be perfect or you miss a lot of points.  Poor teacher.

Overall good teacher. Must go to class and take notes to do well, but easy if you do. Some of the topics seem a little obscure at first, but he does a good job of providing examples (often very odd) and keeping you interested. I didn't read the text book at all and did just fine.

Avoid this guy for 230 if you can. Hear he is good on the upper level classes, but does treat 230 like one of his upper level classes. Either know your stuff on the tests or fail...simple as that. Tests are 40 point essays. Which are graded hard. Even if you know the correct stuff, if you don't show above and beyond, don't expect  to pass.

I don't think it's so much that he's a bad teacher that it's just a crap subject with a lot of names and ideas to remember. He's a nice guy, and he can be funny in class if you catch it, but any time before 11 you probably want to avoid- he has a monotone voice.

I never read the book once...i wouldnt even get it. Make sure you take good notes and pay attention in class. Study for the tests. I did all of this and then went to a study group the day before the exams and always did well on the exams. I think I got an A or and A- overall.

Not sure how anyone thinks he is a really good teacher. He is so unclear when trying to make a point, and he loves arrows that go nowhere and make no sense. His tests are hard and he grades tough. Only good thing is he offers extra credit. Wouldn't recommend taking 230 with him.

He is sooo random, but very funny. Although it is a big lecture class he tends to interact witht the students. He does give pop quizzes which sucks, but they're for extra credit. His grading for the tests are kinda confusing and the reading materials are way boring.
He's a great professor, I wish I had more like him. He makes a somewhat dry subject interesting and I really enjoyed the course. Go to class and use the review guides to study.

He is a great teacher.  Makes class interesting, so everyone doesn't fall asleep.  He makes sure you know exactly what you need to know.  Also, very helpful outside of class.  I thought I would do horrible in this class, but he helped me understand all the material and helped me know what I needed to focus on.
I have trouble understanding the point of what he is talking about.  He is very funny and is probably a really good teacher in upper level classes where kids know what is going on.
No Comments

Good person to take intro phil with. He makes the material interesting by getting student input and inserting humor. You NEED TO ATTEND CLASS AND/OR  READ ASSIGNED MATERIALS to do well. The study guide tells you exactly what's on the test. He takes the time to answer questions. Surprisingly, I think I learned something and actually liked the class.

This was a very easy class.  to be honest I think I would have done better had I gone to it more often great sense of humor.  Basically had to know the jist of each philosophers thinking and apply it to situations
Great teacher... makes the class very interesting by using humor... the MC part of his exams were kind of difficult but the essay part made up for it... if you semi-try and then you'll get a B

his sarcastic examples and simple note taking make the material much easier to understand than other teaching methods. I didn't read a single essay that was assigned and got an A...he goes over everything in class, but you definitely have to take notes and study them before the tests.
Gets a kick out of himself and throws in some sarcastic and weird humor to make the class interesting.

Funny guy; likes the sarcasm.  I hate philosophy, so I thought class was boring, but he threw in some humor every now and then.  Tests aren't so bad if you know background on the philosophers and their theories.
Class kind of hard. Must go to class if you want to do well on tests. Texts not much help since all the essays are written by philosophers and hard to understand.
M.C. sections of test were hard/bad. Funny teacher though and overall pretty easy.
Hilarious teacher, interesting class
You get to take exams twice and there are a lot of assignments to bump your grade up.

I really liked her, use the study guides as she teaches to follow along. Then use the study guides and slides to make your cheat sheet for the test. Class is just memorization, taking about an hour memorizing anatomy over the span of the test week worked well for me.

Very polite woman but moves at the pace of Lightning McQueen. If you like taking hand written notes you will maybe be able to write down 1/8 of what she says. I do not believe that she is a bad teacher at all and she is very helpful outside of class I believe that her rating would be at least a 4.5/5 if she taught easier content.

Dr. Manz has been my favorite professor so far at ISU. You can tell she really cares about her students. She uses TopHat for extra points, and she gives extra credit opportunities. She is very sweet, and explains things very well. As long as you review your notes, do the homework, and do the practice tests, you can do well in this class.

Dr. Manz made an effort to help us understand the material and encouraged us to ask questions. I wasn't a fan of the group work, but it was nice to bounce ideas off other people once in a while. The exams were more focused on applying the concepts learned in class than things like sequencing events. Definitely recommend reading the textbook.

Dr. Manz has attendance points, but you can do them at home the same day if you miss class. This course is a great entry-level anatomy. The material requires some review, but you should be able to get an A with not a lot of studying. She keeps the lectures engaging!

I personally loved Dr. Manz, and she made the lectures interesting and easy to focus on despite the level of difficulty. Uses TopHat and Mastering Biology for each lecture day but it helps get a lot of buffer points in the grade book. Lowest exam was dropped but everyone takes the final. She offers lots of easy extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Manz taught the first half of the class. She was better than the second professor. I understood her more. I personally found this class challenging. SO MUCH INFO CONSTANTLY. I wish the class would have slowed down some.

Prof. Manz is a nice person, but the exams are in the testing centers, and they're nothing like the practice tests at all or anything that she talks about in the lectures. Her lectures are very vague, and she goes super fast. I got much of my information from the textbook, mastering biology, and google, and it still wasn't enough to pass her exams.

Dr. Manz is a good professor & thoroughly goes through the content in lectures, but there are A LOT of topics that are gone over in lecture, especially if you are in the 80-minute lecture period; it can be overwhelming. There are worksheets weekly where you have to work with an assigned group. Exams are difficult, but you get 2 attempts and notes.

She is a very nice person but her lectures were hard to follow, the tests are open note but still very hard. There is a lot of homework but it's pretty easy to do. Attendance is mandatory because there are in-class worksheets and we had assigned seats which I personally didn't like.

Dr. Manz is a very nice person however, the way she taught 212 this semester wasn't great. She would talk very fast during lectures and taking notes in class was almost impossible. The exams were very challenging even tho they were open note and way she lectured wasn't very engaging. We also had assigned seats in lecture which wasn't the best.

She is a super nice professor and cares about her students, however, she talks so so fast during her lectures and does not explain the information all that well. I would suggest downloading her PowerPoints before class and then taking notes on what she says rather than what is on the slides. Tests are HARD and we had assigned seats in the lecture

Dr. Manz was overall an amazing professor, she gave lots of extra credit opportunity and it was obvious that she really wanted all of her students to succeed. She made the lectures very clear and will help you if you don't understand something. I would take all of my biology courses with Dr. Manz if I could.

Ive had Manz for bio 212 and now 255. She really cares about her students. Anatomy is hard just because there is so much content, but she puts out so many extra points with top hat, homework that you can keep trying till you get 100 on and extra credit. Her tests can be difficult, but she is a great professor. The lab is pretty difficult though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: THE best professor I've ever had. Manz is very knowledgeable and has super interesting lectures. She has a bunch of extra credit opportunities and makes it so easy to study for the exams. She is super organized. However if you don't attend the lectures you are really going to struggle in the class. She was also great in 212 as well.
She's super sweet and really knowledgeable about anatomy. She did review sessions before every exam to answer question too.

Dr. Manz did a fantastic job of presenting lectures. The slides contained all the information you needed to succeed, and practice could be found in homework, TopHat, and practice quizzes. She explained things very well, used models, and encouraged active learning. 10/10 would take again.

Prof. Manz is a wonderful lecturer who to some people comes off as slightly boring. She lectures in a way that makes it easy to take notes and follow along. The tests she writes though lean more to the difficult side of things as they are about applying the concepts to ideas not discussed in class. She will answer questions in class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved having Dr. Manz as a professor! You know pretty much exactly what to expect from her exams because anything you need to know for the exam she makes sure to put on the lecture slides. Her slides are available online, but I'd still say go to class because there's some rare little tidbits that aren't on the slides but could be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Manz was a pretty good professor for this class. The tests from this class are hard, which means you have to work for it. Powerpoints in this class are easy to follow and understand. She also makes TopHat questions participation points, which is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Calc is easier. somehow

Huge shoutout to Professor Chad Cardani-Trollinger at Iowa State! His detailed and motivating feedback pushed me to grow, and I kept referring back to his comments because they were so inspirational. It's rare to have a professor who cares this much about students and their investments in their future. I'd highly recommend taking a course with him.

Dr. Chad is one of my favorite professors at Iowa State University. His classes are so fun and engaging. He makes the content interesting and I genuinely enjoyed going to class. He cares about his students individually and is always willing to help you out personally and academically. Would highly recommend this class!

Dr. Chad is an amazing professor who cares about his students and their success. The class is very engaging and he offers plenty of extra credit to keep your grade up. The environment of his classes are very fun and easy to be around. I would recommend this class to everyone no matter what major as it enhances your skills in all areas.
Great professor! Makes the material relatable, funny, and interesting! I learned a lot and look forward to taking another one of his courses.

A very enthusiastic, charismatic, and enjoyable professor whom I definitely recommend to anyone who is interested in leadership diversity. I took the class online and had plenty of time to ensure my work was overachieving the required curriculum. Plenty of extra credit opportunities and an overall great class.
Chad is awesome! Definitely my favorite professor at ISU
He is so funny and perfect in connecting to students. If he teaches a class, take it.
Dr. Chad was the most caring, inspirational professor I've had in my 4 years at ISU and brings an awesome perspective on life. Highly recommend taking him for any class.

A nice change of pace for engineering students. Dr. Chad cares about his students and their learning. Assignments really get you to reflect on yourself without writing too many papers. LDST is a US diversity Gen Ed that should be taken by everyone at Iowa State. You will not regret taking this class with Dr. Chad!

Dr Chad is one of the best professor in Iowa State!! If you're looking for U.S. diversity credits, you should definitely take this class. The assignments are engaging and really make you reflect on your own leadership experiences. Plus, he's always willing to help when you ask for assistance. Recommend!

Chad was super careful about creating a safe space but still allowed his awesome personality to shine through. The class was super easy as everything was so theoretical it was hard to be called incorrect.

Chad is one of the best professors I have ever had at Iowa State. I had multiple times where I had to miss or forgot an assignment and he was super caring regardless of my irresponsibility. He is always challenging you to be your best and is an AMAZING professor, would 100% recommend.
One of the best professors I had throughout my time at Iowa State!
Dr. Chad is a really fun professor! He really cares about your leadership journey and as long as you do all of the readings it is a pretty easy class!

I have been recommending taking this class for U.S. diversity credit to everyone I know. Dr. Chad is the realest and kindest professor I've ever had. Your grade is based on the effort you put in--there are no tests or papers. Very few assignments with flexible requirements and due dates. Assignments take about an hour a week.
Hes always there for the students and he really cares. Hell go above and beyond for you!

The class is "ungraded," so you get out what you put in. If you show up to classes and participate, you can get an A pretty easily. He's open to all political ideas, even if he may not agree with them. Definitely focused on growth mindsets and effort over ability.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is the most laid-back professor, and as long as you show up and discuss the topic with peers you'll pass. Makes you feel welcome no matter your political beliefs. For the first time in close to 3 years at ISU, I can comfortably share my points of view without fear of it tanking my grade. Great class with an amazing professor.

I have never had a professor that was so obviously interested in how people are doing in class and how well their students are learning. I am genuinely sad I won't get to take another class with Chad, it was really one of the best classes I've ever taken.

This is my final year at Iowa State and I can honestly say that Dr. Chad was one of the best professors I have had. He is great at communicating feedback, working with students on an individual basis, and making the course fit for you. His grading style allows for more creativity and understanding than any other course I have taken at ISU!

Dr. Chads classes have a grad school vibe which lets you do your work when youre available to put the effort in. He is very understanding and fun to be around, and he appreciates an individuals creative outlet/ wants that to shine through in your work.

Dr. Chad was so helpful when I took Leadership Studies. He really cares about your progress not just in the class, but as a leader and a human being. Toward the end of the year, I was really struggling with coursework and personal issues, and he responded promptly to all my communications, and made sure that I would be able to succeed in his class.

I really enjoyed Dr. Chads class and I would definitely like to have him as a teacher again. The assignments were challenging and made you really think. He was detailed in his responses, quick in his email replies if you had a problem and a fun teacher overall.

I had Dr. Chad for my last leadership studies class. One thing I do appreciate is his "suggested" due dates which is taking 10% off per day an assignment is submitted late (eg. past it's "suggested" due date) rather than not accepting the assignment at all. He makes the class more fun through his humor and also provides extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Chad was AWESOME! Allowed students to have input on the class schedule and activities. He was very open to new ideas and wanted to students in any way possible!

Dr. Chad is Awesome! I took his class, LDST 322, as an elective. I have never had a Prof. care so much for me as a person. He wants you to succeed not just in the class but also going forward in life. He is also the most accessible and helpful Prof I have interacted with. He worked with me to raise my grade and was always prompt with emails.
Dr. Chad is really amazing. He truly cares about his students. He will help you and thoroughly work with you with your troubles.

Dr. Chad is a fantastic resource for students who are truly interested in leadership after college. His content is engaging, funny, and helpful. He is always willing to go the extra mile for his students and will happily help you through topics and conversations that you need extra help with. Dr. Chad will deepen your experience studying leadership

Chad Cardani-Trollinger is a teacher who is there to help and understands the college struggle. If you need help or extra time just be sure to communicate because he really just wants to see you grow as a person and put forth your best work.

I had Dr. C-T for my first leadership class and really enjoyed him! He wants to help students succeed and is very easy to get into contact with if you have questions. He made the class fun with his Dad jokes and all around fun and helpful personality!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This was my last semester at ISU and my first class with Dr. C-T. He's probably the best faculty member I have ever had. He know's his stuff, works to help us learn it, and really cares about his students. And he's really damn funny. He has very high standards, but they are super easy to meet. I highly recommend taking any course you can from him!

Never trust anything she says. If she says a quiz is going to be easy, study super hard for it. She told us readings would be lighter next week. There were over 70 pages assigned for that week. Just plan ahead, study a little bit everyday, take a lot of lecture notes, and ignore what she says.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Celia could seriously update her course materials. She passed around resources in class, and the publishing dates ranged from 1974-2006. This is unhelpful as it does not provide resources we would actually use. Her slides are outdated as well. Maybe it's because Celia doesn't want to take the effort to update her materials, or what. It's annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is my second course with Ceila. I am running out of patience for her as a professor. Not to mention, she keeps dropping the r-word in the name of "history." It's one thing to acknowledge that it happened but to continue harping on it is grossly inappropriate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You will get carpal tunnel from how much reading and handwritten notes she requires. I cannot feel my thumb and it is tingling as I write this because I just spent 3+ hours taking notes for her class. It is week three and I am over her and her class.

Used the r-word continually during a class lecture despite being a special education professor and advocate. Shocking and inappropriate. 

Her one-minute papers go against everything else we've learned in education courses. Also, she does not input things into the Canvas grade book and encourages you to keep track of your grade in the syllabus.

Celia is one of the best professors. These other reviews are inaccurate. She holds us accountable to do the readings and assignments because she cares. If you do the work, go to class, and participate you will do fine. We are used to classes that are "easy", so when students have a professor that actually holds them accountable, they struggle.

She was so disrespectful to those with learning disabilities despite her being a special education teacher. She actively compared children with autism to Nazis. She also doesn't post the lecture slides because she doesn't want anyone to copy her work.

She engages in conversation, gives great experience examples, and engages with the whole class, but she often will not answer questions to further explain something she already has, you also always need to keep up reading one of her three readings in case there is an in-class quiz. She has good projects that help you learn, but she grades them hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is literally the worst- Hard grader, gives little to no feedback, unapproachable, makes you feel stupid, makes no accommodations, and is so rude

Celia is interactive with students and allows us to share personal experiences to have a better understanding. She does give a lot of assignments but all those assignments I have learned a lot from. She is very easy to approach. If you are respectful, show up to class prepared and discuss you will very much enjoy this class. Just do what she asks

Celia's class requires work, but she is usually flexible if you talk to her beforehand. She does have one-minute papers for the class so take good notes from lectures and text. She does list all assignments for the semester in the rubric, I recommend writing those dates down, and knowing when they are coming up. Overall lectures are engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Grades the worst in the whole university. You can pour everything into an assignment and she will give you a terrible grade on it and say you are wrong. Has a lot of projects she makes you do that are impossible to get 100% on. Also, there are 'one-minute papers' so you're forced to do the reading with no heads up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Celia is definitely there for her students and will bend over backward for you if you miss a lecture. Three required texts though? C'mon.
I had him in my first semester for engineering chemistry, and he barely taught anything and got constantly off task.

Thermo is a TOUGH class, but Dr. Thompson has made the course very laid back, there is 5 homeworks (they are really long), 3 exams, and a final, the exams are really easy since he gives study guides and practice exams, he also lets you take the exams home to get points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Thompson is a very chill professor, he gives great lectures and has an easy course structure. He has 3 midterms, with 1 drop, and you can get up to 75% of your points back on all midterms by doing the take-home portion. He lets the class vote on when to take the exam. The rest of the class is homework. Thermo is tough, he makes it enjoyable.

Caleb is a great teacher and makes notes during class, making it easier to get clarification mid-lecture. Skipping class is an enormous mistake as attendance makes it much easier to learn the content. I don't understand the people who say he didn't teach things fully, I never had to look anything up outside of what he gave as notes + HW was easy.

Dr. Thompson is a mental health first professor. He will give you an extension on any homework for any reason. He will move his exams based on student feedback and he understands the stress they cause. Dr. Thompson gives 75% points back on his exam reworks. He is an amazing professor who cares for his students and truly has passion for teaching.
Great professor who made it fun to attend lectures made chemistry very easy and enjoyable

Dr. Thompson is actually a life saver. I went into thermodynamics expecting the worst, but he made it so enjoyable. If you want to ace thermo without losing it, take it with him!! He's so funny and kind and he never stops slaying. Actual goat 10/10 YESSS LETS GO

Caleb is not a great teacher, as I constantly had to look up videos on how to do things on the homework, as they would all take about an hour to complete, and there were usually five or six homework assignments per week, and some things we wouldn't learn until right before the due date.
The guy is happiness incarnate. He also speaks what's on his mind, which makes him quite funny. He sometimes gets sidetracked, but it's not horrible, don't use AI to do homework and you'll be fine.

He is a great person, but not as good a professor. He is funny and tries to relate to us, as he is younger, but he often sidetracks. I might sign up for his class again but I'm not sure. Chemistry is not for me, so I personally did not enjoy his class. There are three exams and a final, but one does get dropped, which is very helpful to your grade.

Dr. Thompson is a wonderful professor whose strength is his genuine commitment to helping students grow academically. He is understanding of test anxiety and is always willing to offer homework extensions. His teaching style is traditional, and he is hardworking and intelligent; a good grade is achievable with him, but it requires effort.

I don't understand why Caleb gets a bad rep, he is a great instructor that cares about his students learning the material. I had him for chemical thermodynamics which is not a simple class, and I'm willing to bet most of the negative reviews for him from that class are people who barely attended or spent all of lecture on their phones.

Caleb Thompson is a good person, but not a good professor. He continuously goes off on tangents that are not related to chemistry, and compared to other 1670 classes, we were about a week behind, which affected our quiz scores because we were given quizzes on material we hadn't learned yet. Most of the lecture time is wasted on mindless yapping.

Couldn't teach, so the recitations are the only way to learn. But the lectures are funny. He once ranted for 15 minutes on why Psyduck was the favorite Pokémon. And how he has trauma of rainbows as a Gay man.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is very perfect. His advantage: flexible schedule for homework due date and exam time; Also listening students' suggestions for homework and exam; hard homework but middle level difficulty exam. His disadvantage: sometimes may make a little mistake on exam+homework, but you can directly tell him and he directly correct the mistake.

Caleb really cares about learning over grades. He is the most generous professor I have ever had at ISU, and his generosity did not clash with my learning of thermodynamics. He breaks down topics that are very complex and mathematically dense for those who do not possess high-level math knowledge.

This man does not k o what he's talking about 90% of the time. I watched him explain electron configuration for 30 minutes wrong realize he was wrong but time ran out. If you have never taken chem before and you have him as a professor I'm so sorry
Rough class
Tough to learn anything
He loved to joke around and talked about what he thought was funny
He made a lot of jokes and didn't teach much chem
I left class early almost every day
one day he showed in a bunny costume and that's all I need to say
I would not want to take his class again, he got off topic very very easily
tough teacher

Dr. Thompson is a great guy with an amazing personality, and he is very funny. But he is not a good professor. He was behind schedule the entire semester which resulted in many topics being removed and some of the exams being revamped. His lectures were not useful. Great guy though.
It was his first semester teaching but in every way that he fell short he also was gracious and helpful to students. His class was relatively easy and he was always chill about students' needs.

It was his first semester teaching, and you could tell. However, he is a really nice person and wants to see you succeed. You can tell he really tries to be a good professor. I think he will get much better with time. His study guides were very helpful when studying for exams.
He's a really nice guy and is really smart, but it's his first year teaching and it shows. He struggles with the actual teaching part. I think he will get better though.

Caleb is a really nice guy, and gave me words of encouragement when I was going through it during finals. However he's inexperienced, and he isn't a great lecturer. A good teacher does does not deserve hate. Funny guy, and will help you outside of class if needed

Lectures covered the content of the exams, provided a good number of examples during lecture. Passed exams with homework/lectures/recitations. Sometimes goes off on tangents, but all content was covered by time of exam (though sometimes slightly behind)

He goes off task/topic frequently, which causes him to be behind on material. He doesn't teach how to solve problems similar to test material, mostly theoretical knowledge. Your recitation TA needs to be great to get a good grade, or self-teach.

he is a good person and obviously knows his stuff. It is his first year teaching so I hope it will get better. He gets off topic really easily and just kind of whizzed through a lot of things without explaining how they relate to other topics. the textbook comes in clutch tho

While Dr. Thompson can occasionally get off topic in lectures, I found his lecture style very engaging and he was by far the best professor I had this semester! I also felt like he was very caring for his students and he went above and beyond to help troubleshoot problems.
Be ready to teach yourself everything, he is very unorganized and not prepared for lecture.

Ill get to the point... if you have his lecture, you are quite frankly cooked. His lectures are so pointless you could teach the class better first try. If you love wasting your time and tuition then this is perfect for you. The exams cover completely different information than whats covered in lectures so you might as well teach yourself.

reviews.comment: He is genuinely a nice person, but it ends there. This is by far the worst lecture I have ever had. Sometimes, I wonder if I would be more successful in this class if I didn't even attend lectures. Be ready to teach yourself just about everything.
Very caring towards students, and will reach out to you in emails fast. Practice questions during class are a waste of time though. Often gets off track in lecture.

This professor was honestly pretty bad. He was hard to hear, cursed a lot, got off task so easily, gave the most dull and uninformative lectures, and often did not even teach on how to do the material. I relied on tutoring, SI, and teaching myself the material on my own to succeed in this class. I would not recommend whatsoever.

Excellent professor! She takes the time to help you one-on-one if you need it, and I learned so much in this class that has helped me throughout the architecture program. She is a tough grader, but you truly get out what you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Its supposed to be an intro level class. I'm not an artist and i've never really been into art and drawing. This class was difficult for me. She grades hard but she also expects you to know things you might not know.

reviews.comment: This is a very interesting class but Celinda made it very difficult students with other teachers scored way better than us I dont understand how she grades. She gives the toughest projects and is a very tough grader. If you are trying to get into your major I would highly recommend dont take her Awful teacher I will not recommend anyone choose her

Stamy assigns more homework than any other 131 professor. Her grading scale is all over the place, and doesn't give feedback on your work until after you turn it in. Do not take 131 with Celinda, she is one of the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Celinda is awesome, and she's helped me out on many an occasion. She does give a lot more homework than others do, but each assignment helps prepare you for the next project. She's always there after class to give feedback and help you out. She'll even talk you through a mental breakdown (like she did for me). 10/10 would recommend.
Dropped this class because of how handwritten-heavy it was, and the lectures were not particularly helpful for me.

Overall, you're better off using Butler's videos. Within her lectures, she spends the first ten minutes correcting mistakes she made in the last lecture and an additional 15 minutes finishing up the previous lecture, leading her to constantly be behind on the course content. Her time management is poor, but she will get the required content across.
Has no time management skills, will use over half the time reviewing from the previous class, and you will not learn anything. Also has British accent.

reviews.comment: This professor is a real gem – if you enjoy being ignored and left to figure things out on your own. reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super egocentric, he may seem nice but in fact he isn't, super lazy on responding emails, do not care about students
I would never recommend taking courses with this professor. This man is narcissist, and he thinks he is better than than than others. He may act nice, but he is the opposite of that.
He would just go through the slides in the class and ask students to read the book before going to the class. It's hard to learn things from his lecture. Exams are challenging.

Class can get a bit dry sometimes, however this could have been because the class section fell behind the lab section so we were learning about stuff we had to figure out. Very nice guy and one of the better teachers here
Good teacher ! He is very helpful if you go talk to him. He gives about ten homeworks and an easy project and grades them very generously, he also provides a detailed list of what can be in the exam.
Great professor!
Amazing professor!!!

She is a super sweet person and, by far, one of my favorite professors, but not necessarily the fastest when it comes to grading, and some grades were not put in until the end of the semester. Ask questions it helps a lot, as sometimes expectations are unclear. You work a lot outside of class; some projects require around 30 hours outside of class.

Celinda was an amazing professor. While the workload was a lot, she provided good feedback and prepared the class for our future in our programs. This was a class I looked forward to going to every day. She helps everyone, and if you put in the effort, it will pay off

She expects a lot out of her students but you are rewarded well for your effort. She gives very clear instructions and gives great feedback whenever you need it. If you are deciding between profs for this class, I would highly recommend her, I loved being her student!

Celinda was an amazing teacher. She offers great feedback and always makes her expectations clear. You have to work for your grade but hard work pays off. There is a decent amount of outside class work but it prepares you for the projects and builds your skills. She cares about her students and wants them to thrive. Favorite teacher I've ever had!

Really good teacher and makes it clear that the way she grades doesn't change and if you grow, your grades will improve. She also writes plenty of notes on the rubric so you know where to improve. She can make anyone a good artist as long as they apply themselves. There's weekly homework on top of actual work but if done- makes a good buffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is great, but she is a very hard grader. She also assigns a lot of the work to be done outside of class. She spends a lot of studio time reteaching what chuck taught already in the lectures. She also has very specific expectations and you dont always know what she wants when you do your work. Also her and my personalities just didnt match up.

I was very nervous about taking a college level design course, especially since I am not a design major and I was just experimenting with design, but Celinda made me feel at ease! She cares about every student, and while assignments can be difficult you will learn a ton. Shes a fantastic teacher, and Im sad that the class is over.

Celinda is really nice and gives good feedback. She really does get you to do your best. She also makes everyone get to know each other which was nice. Projects are tough though and take up a lot of time so don't give yourself a heavy schedule with this class.
She is such an amazing professor. Always ready to help her students to understand and know more.... Excellent illustrations in class and she will help you if you are having any difficulty

Celinda is AMAZING. She is kind, and never puts students down. As long as you actually do your work, you will be just fine. She wants her students to be successful. She gives wonderful demonstrations, and she understands that sometimes the best way to learn is to do it yourself. If you are confused, she will answer any questions.

Celinda is an incredible teacher; the best 131 instructor at ISU in my opinion. She genuinely cares for each of her students and will do everything she can to grow her students ability on an individual level. Her grading scale is tough and requires lots of work hours, but its fair and her critiques are extremely beneficial. 10/10 would recommend.

Celinda is very nice and really cares about her students. She is great teacher and I learned so much from her. She was very clear about what she expected from us, but she is also extremely understanding and praised my class for all of the good things we were doing. Awesome experience with her in my first design class!

Celinda is a great teacher. She will honestly teach you how to be a great drawer, and she actually cares about her students and gets to know them. She'll also accept resubmits on drawings. She does expect that you put a decent amount of time outside of class if you want a good grade, but that's pretty much how all of the desing core is.

Celinda is by far the best professor I've had so far.  She cares so much about every one of her students and really tries to get to know you as a person.   She gives awesome feedback and will answer any questions you have.  I didn't really know how to draw when this class first started and coming out of it I feel so much more confident.

She is the b st teacher I have ever had at ISU! She want us to succeed in class and care about her student. She nice and easy to talk to, she also gives great feedback. I highly recommend you to take the class with her.
Celinda truly cares about her students.  She is an awesome professor and an even better person
Best 131 instructor! Super helpful and I learned a lot! She is amazing!

She is a really cool person and is always there for you if you need help. Don't get turned off by her initial impression she comes off strong but will warm up to everyone quickly. Personally I had a tough time in this class because she expects everyone to produce extremely good work even though you can't make the quality matching her expectations.

Celinda is great. She 100% cares about what she teaches and will be there when you need help. She is friendly and extremely easy to talk to, but don't think you won't have to work for your grades in her class. Her expectations are high for her students, and you need to work hard to succeed. If you put in your time, she will take you far.

She is very willing to help you if you feel like meeting with her. She is passionate about drawing. She loves seeing us succeed; never yells at us nor make us feel terrible. Very encouraging!   It doesn't matter who your proffesor is, DSN S 131 is always hard (aka lots of all-nighters) that is just the nature of this class.
best teacher I've ever had
Absolutely LOVED Celinda. She is fun and helped me improve so much through out the course. She knows her stuff and is very helpful.
Very insightful

10+ things due/ to do a week, for an intro level class an insane course load. Her tests are EXTREMELY specific and will have questions on the tiniest details she mumbled under her breath. Do the million assignments

reviews.comment: Cinzia Cervato is one of the most uncaring, and unkind professors I have had the displeasure of encountering. Genuinely, worst professor I've ever had.

reviews.comment: Be prepared for lots of homework every week. Do not take if you just need an easy science credit. I spent most of my time on this class and still ended up having to get a tutor. She is very hard to understand so you really have to pay attention. You will end up taking each exam twice, once by yourself and once with others.

Do not take this class with her if you just want an easy physical science credit. There are usually around 6-8 homework assignments per week and they are extremely time consuming. She is also extremely hard to understand and rude at times. The tests are also dumb, you have to take them and then retake them again with a partner.

This class was about as free as it gets. Show up to lecture and take 10 minutes to do the extra credit and you'll be fine. Lectures are fine, some days are more interesting than others, better than most of my professors.

Going into this class and seeing all the awful reviews about her was very scary, and throughout the semester I've had 0 issues whatsoever, she is not awful, not rude, and honestly a pretty easy class, all the homework answers can be found online, tests are based on what she talks about in class, lots of extra credit opportunities.

You will NOT pass if you don't show up. Tests are also NOTHING like the study guide. Also get ready to read so so much, and assignments (up to three a week) take about 40 min each. This professor is not very friendly and is extremely difficult to work with. I took this course thinking it was an easy natural science credit, I was really tricked.

This class is for people that like Geology, not those looking to fulfill their gen-ed requirements.

Dr. Cervato is extremely knowledgable in her field but she is very rude and mean. She does not respect her students and she is not a caring or accommodating professor at all.

So she did mention in the beginning of the semester that her grade averages have been a B- for the past few years and did say that if you want a good grade you will have to put in the effort and participate. Hey, so unlike a lot of people here I am an actual Geology major and I really enjoyed this class. reviews.comment: She is a nice teacher but there is a lot of work.

reviews.comment: She is arrogant or extremely stupid. She honestly believes Geology is this amazing and very easy thing.
