I would take any class with him again. The class does have some extensive readings, but you only had to submit a 1-2 page response. His lectures are super fun and are discussion-based; he definitely makes learning fun. He would also show pictures of his cats to us. Great professor!

Craig is the best professor I have had. His attendance policy is flexible, if you email him before missing a class he excuses it (to an extent ofc). He is caring & always makes sure the class is enjoying what we are doing. There is a one partner project in this class that you can easily make fun! Would take a class with him again in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Awesome dude. Showed pictures of his cat sometimes. Readings were heavy but not too bad because we just had to do a ~1 page response about what we liked or thought about it. Would take him again, and wish he taught more classes so I could.

Craig is the best professor I've ever had! He is incredibly kind, funny, and makes a topic like rhetorical analysis fun to learn. He is super chill and he gives great feedback on assignments and papers. As long as you do the readings and the assignments, you'll do fine. He makes sure to answer any and all questions well. I loved his class!
Craig is THE BEST! He is so funny and genuinely cares about his students so much. Participate in his class and you won't regret it. I would recommend him and his class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved this class because of the professor. Craig made every student feel very welcome and even took the time the first week to learn everyone's names. The actual class is very discussion-based so If you do the discussions you should be ok. There were 2 major papers but you were allowed to choose the topic. The book is needed for discussions.

I really enjoyed this class solely because of the professor. He cares about the students and if they are understanding the readings. And, there is a TON of readings, you 100% need the book. Also, attendance is mandatory because a lot of the class is based around the discussion. There are reading responses and quizzes based on the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor to have! He is always there to help in any way he can. Big paper coming up? He cancels class to set up mandatory meetings with students to talk through and help with the writing. If you have a chance, take a class with him. You won't regret it

Professor Rood is one of the best English professors I have ever had. It's very obvious that he cares a lot about all of his students and wants to hear everyone's opinion during class discussions. Although there are quite a few papers and some speeches in his class, the class was interesting and helpful.

You are expected to learn exclusively from the textbook, and the first time you see material in class is for a quiz. Team quizzes are rushed so you have no time to talk through misunderstandings. Grading system is absurdly complicated for no reason. Spends a significant portion of each class doing a good luck ritual instead of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Grading scale is terrifying for a last semester senior, especially if you want to get an A or a B. If you miss a single point on a homework, the best grade you can get is a C in the class. You mostly learn by yourself and you lose incentive to learn as soon as you miss a point because you can no longer get an A or B
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. Someone needs to teach him how to teach. It feels like I am paying for a class to teach myself. Most of the classes are solving something as a group. The grading is awfully complicated for no reason whatsoever, and the exams and assignments are very unclear (he seems to be confused himself). Just switch professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good professor! Work hard and stay on top of the class, and you'll be okay. In-class problems helped prepare for exams. Quizzes are sometimes tricky, you really need to know the topic. He doesn't lecture much, you mostly do in-class problems and learn the material outside of class. Ended up really liking this class style.
This teacher is absolutely terrible, if you end up with him as your only option drop the class immediately and take it another semester. He fails to teach the topic and his tests are ridiculous.

This professor kinda has mental problem to talk about academic dishonesty every time. He does care about it, but not about teaching in class. Exams are really hard, in-class projects are not even similar for exams. No idea why department let him to teach this kinda great class. Highly recommended to take this course with another professor.
He tells you right away he won't teach you in class, and he doesn't. Just group activities and quizzes. The tests are nearly impossible to finish in the time allowed.

Terrible experience. He does not teach he merely posts a topic on the board and tells the class to talk about it. Quizes are all online and no partial credit is given. I highly recommend taking this course with another professor
Very clear grading and drops multiple quizzes. Just show up and an Easy A/B. I was late for a TH Exam and he emailed ME! Saying it's reopened and to get it done asap without me even asking. W

Curt is very lecture-heavy. MANY exam questions will be based purely on what he said in class. Be prepared to take great in-class notes. Exams are very laborious. There is a take-home portion with approximately 60-70 questions and an in-class portion with 50-60 questions, for all 4 exams. He is clearly very knowledgeable, but not the best teacher.

Curt is a terrible professor, specializing in deliberately failing students.  His exams consist of 150+ questions, with some referring to subjects not covered in class.  He is not willing to work with or understand the needs of his students. The man is smart, but sly and uses backhanded comments.  Would not recommend taking his class.

Curtis is a very nice guy and he knows what he is talking about. However, if you are planning on learning anything or understanding the "topic," you are on..well Good luck. His lecture slides are terrible, he will talk about something completely different on every slide, you don't know what to write down or not. Probably shouldn't be a professor.

Curtis was a bank president for many years, and it shows in his teaching style. He is awful when it comes to conducting lectures. His slides are interactive but his style as a teacher is hard to retain information for tests. He also places a lot of questions on quizzes around what "I mentioned in class" and not based off of the textbook material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curt is an experienced banker and it shows in the lectures. He doesn't teach his classes like a normal professor, so it can get confusing sometimes. If you take some notes you will get an A, the tests are directly based on what he says. He curves all the exams and is an easy grader on projects.

Curtis is a great professor and I loved taking 445 with him. The class is heavy on terms and lecture material, but the tests and assignments are clear cut and easy if you pay attention in lectures. Hoff does a great job introducing banking to his students, and I appreciated his knowledge on the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall very informative class. Curt is a great professor with a lot knowledge. Some of his lectures can get dry though. This class is difficult to fail as only 40% of the grade comes from exams and each exam is graded on a curve. Overall show up to class and study for the exams somewhat. That will get you a A or B.

He use a lot of acronym that you can have no ideas when he mentioned that in class unless you asked or you are from banking background.  Weekly quizzes since the class is only once per week. Every word that he said will be on the test, so make sure you understand every single word. Should ask question in class for participation points. Hard for me.
Hard course but really helpful
Dr. Curtis is no longer at Iowa State, but he was one of the best professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was very helpful when questions came up or students had abstract questions. Would 100% take a class by him again. Very down to earth guy. He does not post slides online but attending the lecture did not feel like a task.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is single-handily one of the best professors here at Iowa State. He is very knowledgeable and caring. He does whatever he can to help you succeed. As long as you participate he is willing to help you get extra credit and to prepare you for future courses. Without him I couldn't imagine where I would be in college today.
Bryan did a great job of explaining everything. Lectures weren't required and going to his or other professors' office hours were very beneficial.

Great recitation teacher. Very caring and helpful when asked questions. Provided detailed illustrations when I asked him where I went wrong on a quiz. Possesses a very strong geometrical perspective on problems. Overall a great professor.

This is for his ECON 2090 class. Very clear grading criteria consisting of 3 exams, 5 quizzes, and 1 final. He lets you drop your worst score of the exams and quizzes respectively. There are also a few excel homework assignments but he walks you through them in class. If you pay attention during lectures and write good cheat-sheets you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MAKE SURE YOU TAKE THE OPPORTUNITIES HE OFFERS TO EARN BONUS EXTRA CREDIT. I GOT 70'S AND 80'S ON MY EXAMS BUT THE EXTRA CREDIT BROUGHT MY FINAL UP TO A 93%!!

Only assigns 3 homework assns through the entire semester. Writes on the chalkboard and rarely uses slides. Started the semester off doing well and after spring break seemed to get worse each day, wouldn't respond to emails promptly and wasn't helpful when asked about the few homework assignments he gave. Drops lowest quiz and exam scores though.
Heavy accent. Took a little getting used to it. Super nice and helpful if you have questions. Lecture heavy but not a lot of homework.
Andres was very clear about what would be on exams and would review in class. Exams and assignments were straightforward. He made the class very easy for students to succeed.

Want an A? Just do all the quizzes and practice set, the problems in the exams are totally the same! This class is very easy, you do not need to show up. Just stay home and read the lecture notes uploaded. Then, you are good.

Had him for ECON 101.
He is a great guy and answers email questions very quickly and makes topics clear to understand. However, in lectures, he yaps a lot and I can only understand about 60% of what he says due to his thick accent. Tests and quizzes are really easy and if you take notes from lecture slides you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Andres is a great guy outside of the class. Econ 101 consists of one homework assignment each week which had unlimited attempts. Then 1 out of 3 exams are dropped, previous to the final. All exam questions are pulled from homework, practice sets and top hat questions. Attendance is not mandatory, but once I skipped once I never went back.
Very good professor. Tests make up most of the grade but aren't difficult. Tests are mostly made up of in-class and homework questions. I enjoyed this professor.
His lectures were very straight forward and the exams were multiple choice. I really enjoyed this class.

You really have to force yourself to pay attention in class to learn anything. The quizzes are pretty random, and he usually will leave it up to you to figure out when stuff is due. His canvas page is organized but ambiguous.

Most material for the exams in in the lectures and PowerPoint. Go to class to study before exams and have a group for the quizzes at the end of class. Also, you have one presentation on something related to banking. Not an easy class, but fun and very informative for finance majors.

Share book w/ friends. Don't waste your time reading it (just need it for take home exam) Advice for class: print off presentation slides and write down every word he says. There are take home exams that will use info he talks about but is not published anywhere (book/online). GENEROUS CURVES GIVEN for each exam. Work hard on the group project

Curt has a very simple theme to his class: show up, be attentive and you'll be just fine. Many people slam him for making this class "incredibly difficult," but it's actually an easy class altogether.  It does help if you have previous banking experience, but it's not required to do well in the class. No textbook necessary. Pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Curt is a pretty awesome professor. Cuts to the chase and gives you straight forward answers. The average for the first two test were 60% but curves up to 80% average. A few people had over 100% for the exams. Textbook isn't required but will help for the examquizes as some questions are only from the textbook. Awesome class, would take it again!

Cullen was an amazing and engaging professor. He really cares about his job, and assignments are not hard just writing, and they are intriguing topics.I found his class to be so interesting, and the topics of di scussion made me think so deeply about things i had not considered before. I loved this class, and its simple if you put in little effort
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely is passionate about what he's teaching and cares about his students, but sometimes grading or assignments can be unclear. Really nice guy, but I wasn't a huge fan of his class although I could be biased as I'm not much of a philosophy guy.

Professor Padgett-Walsh is a nice guy but not a good teacher. He just keeps talking the whole lecture time and he NEVER responds to emails and he NEVER grades until the very last week of the semester. I was almost failing the class the whole semester up until the very last week until he graded everything. Not a good professor.

This guy is not good , one of the weirdest grading criteria's I have ever seen. It is December 17th, and this is the first time that I have seen my grade all year. Do not take class with this guy, because I am sure that his grading scale goes to all classes.
Professor was alright. Lectures were extremely boring but it is mandatory. Not a bad class but be prepared to be bored out of your mind.
Great professor. The class was setup with the ability to retake quizzes and get clarification on what was missed. Overall great class for learning and discussing.

A great and caring guy who clearly understands and loves his job. He uses such insane examples that I will never forget. Attendance is 25% of your grade, but he is lenient on late work as long as you communicate.

Cullen is a good professor, he knows so much about philosophy as a whole and is not afraid to share it. Class has some papers that are not too challenging, the quizzes could be difficult if you do not study, but overall great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A must take for everyone at Iowa State. Best class I've been in

Highly recommend taking this class with Cullen and he is the only professor you should take this course with. Super easy and had interesting debates about society. Can not recommend him enough he was a great professor.

Highly recommend taking this class with Cullen and he is the only professor you should take this course with. Super easy and interesting topics with the class having interesting debates about hot topics in society. Would take more classes with him.
Class was not difficult, but Cullen is clearly educated and cares about what he teaches.

Yes, this class requires you to write many papers, but most of the 750-word essay assignments have the same prompts and just ask you to expand on a philosopher's ideas. What really kills people's grades is not showing up to class. Overall, he is super accommodating, and if you need help, just show up to office hours.
Participation was about a quarter of the entire grade, so make sure you go to class. He also only updated the grade book once throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you do not like writing, this class can be frustrating regardless of the professor. But he goes a nice job making topics engaging and interesting.
Great subjects and conversations

Never responses to any emails, very hard to come in contact with him if you want to meet for office hours. Takes forever to grade, I was failing the class until the end of the course once he started grading assignments. Quizzes are very hard. Good guy, very laid back, but would not take this professor again.
The goat of PHIL teachers
Professor jumps around a lot and the lectures are pretty boring. The class itself was pretty easy. Not a topic I enjoy, however, so I decided to rate the professor higher than I would otherwise.

Excellent instructor. Prior to PHIL 235, I took PHIL 230 with him and thoroughly enjoyed it. I strongly recommend this course and instructor for anyone looking to have an easy Gen Ed and US Diversity credit. There are papers and 3 quizzes, but they were fairly easy.
Very cool professor, cool with extensions.

Cullen is by far the most chill and funny professor I have had at Iowa State. He is very lenient with late work; just contact him first. He is funny and an easy grader. Just show up to class, as he used TopHat for attendance points. The only con to Cullen is he doesn't read his emails.

He was incredible at fostering an environment of productive discussion, while also being funny. He understood that students had other classes and was more than willing to grant extensions to papers. I cannot recommend him more, as he is funny, understanding, and incredibly insightful.
Big Chiller
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of papers but they are not too bad. Very funny guy who genuinely seems passionate and cares about his students. Always offered office hours if you needed help. Class was not too difficult outside of papers.

Cullen is a great teacher, insightful, caring, and really funny. The class is easy, but you also gain a lot from it. i see others complaining he is inaccessible outside of class, but they could easily go to his office hours if they truly tried to email him four times with no response. If you give the class effort, this won't be a problem.

He clearly cares about the students, and he is very passionate and knowledgable about the material he's teaching which keeps the class engaging. There's lots of discussion posts and a few papers, but thats about it. It's a relatively easy but interesting course.

This professor is not easy to contact outside of class. He will never answer emails or any messages on Canvas. Going to class is extremely pointless, as all of his lecture notes are on Canvas. Not going to class can screw you over in the long run as he submits the attendance at the end of the semester. Heavy papers and lack of communication.

Very caring and fun professor! His lectures were very informative and fun to listen to. He isn't the best at responding to emails, so be sure to talk to him before or after class or during office hours. He is very generous about deadlines, so long as you ask for it and note it on your paper. Do your work, and this is a super easy and enjoyable A!
Very helpful and sympathetic, respects students.

Very interesting lectures, not biased but moral. Open to discussion and questions, covers every point of view possible for philosophical approaches. Mildly complicated topics, really have to analyze what you're reading. Lots of good self evaluation through the amount of papers/writing he assigns, but very fair, follow the rubric and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good professor, but will not reply to any emails. I emailed him about 4 times throughout the semester and never got a response to any of them. There's a lot of writing, but the papers are graded easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He decided to personally review every single student paper to check for AI the last week of class... students were given no information and it's over a month after the semester has ended and I still have no grade. Written work in class can take months to be graded. He will NEVER respond to ANY email you send him. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

I had Padgett-Walsh for PHIL 230, and it was an all-around great experience. Lectures are not required, but I would go just to listen to him talk. Make sure you do all your paper, though, as the class is primarily based on writing with him.

Walsh is a super kind professor, I personally do not attend the lectures, many people don't. There is 2 long essays due, they aren't difficult, they just take time, plus he gives you topics to choose from. There is also 6 response papers that are 650 words long and 4 quizzes throughout the semester. No midterms or final.

Very kind and easy-going professor. Attendance is 10% of your grade, but showing up is not hard. There are response papers and two long essays, which are graded generously by TAs. There are also a few quizzes that are not bad, and you get two attempts. Overall, had a good time in this class.
This professor is super laid back and easy to get along with. He respects each one of his student opinion.

Ok, so on paper, you could get an A by never going to class. most of the class is weighting papers which aren't bad, and then there are 3 quizzes. The quizzes can be a little difficult, but there are MC and online overall easy classes and he will push the deadlines back if you just talk to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures can get a little boring at times, but he tells fun stories. Participation is somewhat mandatory because he assigns random Packback polls in class. Readings are optional, and there are weekly packbacks and biweekly papers.
Horrible at replying to emails
The besttttt I recommend 100% easy A I promise

He's definitely not for everyone, but for nerds like me his class is very enjoyable. You can skip every class, but you'll be missing out on thought provoking discussions and some top tier dry humor. The papers seem like a lot, but they are graded very generously. You don't need to be a good writer to get full point as long as you follow the rubric.

I took philosophy 235 to satisfy a humanities requirement and loved it. He facilitates productive, engaging discussions in class and makes it easy to want to show up.

You definitely can do well in this class without going to all of the lectures, but it is easier if you do.

This guy will put you to sleep, his lectures are that boring. The essays are really annoying and honestly a waste of time. Topics included were too broad and not that interesting or intriguing. Was very disappointed in this class and expected more from the professor.
Lectures were very entertaining. Allows you to work with others and use notes for quizzes. Papers are graded pretty easily just take some time to do

The best in the business! Take him if you can! Just 6 short papers, 2 long ones, and 4 quizzes. Go to class if you want to learn something to write about. You'll get a good grade if you can demonstrate a base knowledge of the concepts in class and put in genuine effort. CPW loves philosophy and explains it well. Highly recommend for Phil230!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: he was a good professor. the lectures and material are kind of boring at times, but he is very knowledgeable about what he is talking about. there are a lot of papers, but if you need an extension all you have to do is ask and he will give it to you. i would take another class with him!

His class is very easy as long as you do the assignments. There is a decent amount of writing in his class. However, it is generally pretty easy to write about. His lectures are very entertaining, and he uses real-life examples during his classes.

One of my favorite professors! Very knowledgeable and always makes lectures interesting. Very funny guy, and is very caring about the well-being of his students. Phil 230 was really really fun with him and there were always interesting topics and scenarios to discuss. Pretty easy class too, just a few papers. Highly highly recommend.

He is a good professor and good person. He makes lectures engaging by telling stories and giving good examples. He also does in class discussions which I find productive. He usually answers emails within 10 minutes of sending to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Walsh is a great professor. His lectures are well done and interesting. He is very flexible with deadlines and a genuine guy. Would recommend for PHIL 230
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class and he had it set up if you missed class you can still get attendance points for polls etc. He is funny and very approachable. Very essay heavy every other week you need to write a 650-word essay which isn't too bad and he's very flexible with when you turn it in. I hated doing the long essays 1600-2000 word ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Padgett-Walsh was very amusing. His lectures were interesting and his personality was open and approachable. This class has a ton of papers, but he's very lenient with deadlines. I was able to get away with not reading the papers that went with the lectures because he goes over them during the lectures pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the most personable professors Ive ever had. Will for sure go down as one of my favorites of all time
Great professor. Lots of papers that are "required" to read but honestly not too important. A good amount of papers to write so be prepared.

Grade weighted heavily on being in class, though you can miss class and write papers to make up for it. Philosophy is hard, but he explains his stuff very clearly, and tries to keep philosophy interesting. Definitely planning on getting his section for PHIL235 because I'd love having another class with him!

Pros: Great sense of humor, easy to talk to, and wants you to be successful. Cons: The boundary between personal or professional can easily get blurred. I'd advise not becoming very personally comfortable with him whatsoever. It's better to keep things professional with this professor. Be careful.

Probably my favorite class I have taken at Iowa State and I am going to be a senior this year. For a class that is very opinion based he was amazingly unbiased and listened to everyone speak. I wish more people in my class would have participated in this discussions as it tended to be the same group of people. Great teacher!!

Amazing guy. Really caring and enthusiastic. If you're having a mental breakdown, he's really understanding. Lots of papers. Quizzes are pretty difficult. This is one of the few professors who actually care about his students. 10/10 would take again. He made my first and only philosophy class enjoyable.

Straightforward grading: go to class, write the papers and you'll get an A . Lectures are sometimes interesting, he makes boring stuff somewhat entertaining. Great guy, understands students and respects you. Unit Quizzes are tough, but you don't really need to do good in them if you write solid papers. Over all a good class to take with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic about his work, knowledgeable, gives good contextual examples to explain concepts, flexible with deadlines if reasonable, straightforward grader (TA's grade papers I think) This class is set up well for us to learn. Very fun and engaging.

Beware the False Syllabus. Cullen tends to deviate from the schedule on his syllabus. By a LOT. Do NOT put in the assignments ahead of time. Come to class, keep track of assignments, or they WILL slip past you. This is NOT an easy-pass class. Cullen makes the quiz questions deliberately difficult to answer, though not unfairly so.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He has you write a lot of papers over reading materials that can be extremely difficult to understand. He usually breaks down some of the readings during lectures and he gives great lectures. You get points for going to class and Id recommend going to this class anyways. Quizzes are extremely hard if you dont take your time or study.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very understanding prof who seems to care about your learning
Lots of papers but they are graded very easily. His quizzes are impossible though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Theres an essay every week and the lectures are very boring. Each essay is 700 words and the long essays are 1700-2000 words about impossible topics. The quizzes suck and the TA that grades everything gives little feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher but doesn't respond to emails
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: When it comes to Professor Cullen Padgett-Walsh, it's a class where you'll be tested on your stamina and perspective.  This course is rather straightforward - no curveballs, you're essentially being taught in lectures where the material includes videos and then given a word assignment to complete, with a solid paper essay at the end.  Dedicated.

Attendance is mandatory! you can only miss 3 classes before he docks points from your grade. There was weekly 600-700 word essays to write and then there are 3 long essays that are over 1000 words each. Lots of writing and gives little feedback. There are also quizzes that are very hard. Lectures are very interesting though. Really have to work.
The professor assigned 8 'short' (650-700 words) response papers and 3 'long' (1800-2000 word) essays. It is a lot of writing, especially if you aren't interested.

Very laid back professor. Learned a lot from him and he ran a discussion basedencouraged class. Went into his office hours a couple times and he is very knowledgeable and helpful. Sometimes he was a bit lazy and not specific on assignment due dates but graded very generously.

Cullen was great. A really nice guy. I actually looked forward to his lectures because it was largely discussion-based. I expected to be force-fed opinions but it's not like that at all. He basically presents various ideas and allows the students to feed back different points of view. Essays were a pain but manageable. Don't miss class.

Reasonably easy. If you are a god writer you'll be fine. No tests or quizzes. Just weekly essays. If you do the readings you dont even need to go to most of the classes. Or you can jsut go to class and not read. He is very approachable and easy going. Overall good professor trying to make a dull topic interesting

The professor is really easy-going and approachable. He makes jokes that aren't always gold, but they still make me laugh. 500 word journals are due each week that are worth 15 points. No exams, instead there are 4 'Long' (1100 words) Essays due throughout the semester. As long as you keep up with work, it's an easy and enjoyable class.

I absolutely loved Cullen as a teacher. He puts out a very unique vibe. He explains things very clearly, and genuinely enjoys helping people understand something they don't get.Can't rate him high enough1

Fairly straightforward and easy class. He is not the best communicator or explainer however. Often times students will have to approach him in person to get their questions answered. He either doesn't check email often or doesn't respond to all inquiries. He also isn't very quick to grade and return assignments.
Easy class. Good professor, very knowledgeable. Easy grader.
Professor is interesting and helps the class understand and debate over different views on the subjects of the class.

Professor is not easy to understand as he uses tons of vocab words that are very hard to know the definitions to. Makes you write journals every week that have to be over 500 words, and only worth 3 pts! Ridiculous! Makes it very very difficult to get an A. Wish I would have taken it with a different professor.

A discussion-based class. He will ask the class the topic of the day or what they thought of the media presented. His lectures are not in standard format (Word, PowerPoint, etc), so taking notes will come in handy. The online quizzes are difficult even after reading the material, but he always goes over everything completely in time for the final!
Explains things well.  Has a decent sense of humor. Easy to pay attention to. Likes to involve the class.

Really interesting class that I would definitely recommend taking at some point. However, Cullen does not outline how he will grade the class, or strays from what's provided in the syllabus. MUST make an effort on the quizzes because they play a big part in the final. Attendance isn't mandatory, effort, however is. He's a really intelligent prof.

This is an interesting class. One thing I didn't like is I have no idea how I did on the final paper, final exam, or papers  written over the semester.  He wasn't good about reporting grades. Regardless, the class is worth  taking.  It opens your eyes to a lot of things.
Easily my favorite class. Professor Padgett-Walsh is highly intelligent and is able relay his knowledge in interesting and often funny ways. A+!

The name of Turbo-Tim lives up. He talks fast and has some of the most content full lectures of any class I've taken. Minimal outside of class work if you go to class and pay attention. Very interesting and I really enjoyed the class

This class with Dr. Cullinan was a mixed bag. While he's knowledgeable, his teaching style can be hit-or-miss. The quizzes and exams were challenging, but using unstuck study and the free textbook helped me stay on top of the material.

Professor was extremely disrespectful to students regularly and created a very hostile environment. Did not make lectures particularly effective. Exams were almost the entire grade of the course and they were unforgiving.

This class with Dr. Cullinan was one of my favorite classes ever as a mechanical engineering student. I learned A LOT from his lectures. The "quizzes" that were really homework assignments were not bad, the exams were similar to the quizzes, and the TA office hours were very helpful and offered multiple times each day of the week.
A decent professor often wastes time during lectures due to random rambles. Super test dependent, and there are too many lecture slides to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He goes fast in his lectures. He's very knowledgeable in the field, but his ego gets in the way. Not really there in his office hours. The lecture slides have a lot of content that isn't important, but gives good insight into the industry. Better suited for grad level courses I feel.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good lecturer who lets his ego get in the way of a truly great class experience. Well structured course.

Very well-respected materials scientist; cares very much about the education of new engineering students in MAT E 273. Enjoyed the class, was straightforward, and 10 points of extra credit on each exam.

He has expectations that students will take time to understand the content. Considering the difficulty and large amount of content, this is not unreasonable. Taking time to understand the content makes the class very easy. No homework, only quizzes with 3 attempts which are easy to get 100% on if you attend class and pay attention. Funny guy too.
Tim is awesome. He is a great guy and he really cares about the material (wink wink).
Lectures slides heavy with information and quizzes after every lecture. No curve anymore. Teaches the class as if everyone has been in the field for 5+ years.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The instructor himself wasn't all that bad. He seemed interested and engaged in what he was teaching, just taught it poorly. I enjoyed having him but he got into information useless to the class often. It was nice getting an insight into the field, but made it difficult to study for/take the exams since you don't know what was and was not useful.

After the first exam he told us "if you didn't get over an 80%, you are at risk of not passing." that's super unhelpful and it's also a discouraging thing to tell your students. I also tried to go to his office hours and he never showed up even after I emailed him. Also doesn't give exams back or post answers so you have no idea what you did wrong.
3 Quizzes a week. 1 after every lecture. Exams are ridiculously hard, can't just study lecture slides.

I took MATE 273 with Turbo Tim. This class is extremely difficult and covers a bunch of content. What I like most about Tim is the insight that he gives into the industry. Pointing out things that he has personally used in his experience working. Yes the clas is hard but don't put all of the blame on Tim.

He always went way over time during lectures. He wouldn't let us see any of our exams or even meet with him to discuss them. He repeatedly threatened to get rid of the grade curve because 3 or 4 our of 200+ students would talk during lectures.

Daily quizzes are about 5 questions with 10 parts to them consisting of selecting all that apply from a selection of typically 7. Sent out an 8000-character email to everyone threatening to lower the grades of everyone due to 5/300 kids talking. Teaches this class as if we are all Ph.D. students. Can't get anyone else he's the only teacher for this

I wish there was another professor for MAT E 273.  Turbo Tim has a tendency to go fast, and he throws in a lot of unnecessary side information so it is hard to know what you will actually be tested on.  Slides are also overly complicated and indecipherable outside of class.  The class curriculum has potential to be good, but Tim makes it pointless.

I had to take this class twice & Tim is by far the worst prof ISU has to offer. Lectures are far too complicated than necessary and a horrible job is done to help students throughout the course. Doesn't give back exams because, "Exams aren't a learning opportunity." Be aware, appears nice and friendly until the first exam, then turns hostile.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The learning environment Tim Culling created was horrific. I never felt like my questions would be answered without being scrutinized at the same time. There was too much lecture material to comprehend in every lecture, and it also seemed he got off on students not understanding. YOU ALSO DON'T GET TO SEE YOUR TESTS AFTER TAKING THEM! BOO TIM

The class is structured horribly. For studying you get an easy practice exam which is nothing like the actual exam, 15 lecture slides, and 15 quizzes all of which are very difficult without the help of the TA's. To get a good grade go to help hours and meet with the TA's. Honestly just get through the class are never look back at it. GARBAGE CLASS!

Materials is a very interesting subject with great engineering applications, but Turbo Tim makes a general engineering class very hard. Going to the lectures is the only way to learn the material, and the slides make no sense without the commentary. The math is annoyingly hard as it is not covered well at all, and you don't get tests back.

Tim does not care about his students at all. He canceled five lectures and makes the students make up the work independently. He also threatened us with fewer attempts on daily quizzes because of a few students out of hundreds. He should just talk to those students individually instead of messing with everyone else's grades.

Tim has to the be the worst professor Iowa state has seen in a while. I refuse to call him doctor because he does not deserve that level of respect. It is actually an insult to other doctors to consider Mr. Cullinan in that crowd. He makes a class (that non material engineerings should have to take) extremely difficult. I will be lucky if I pass.

Tim is very arrogant and narcissistic. In my opinion, he does not care about us as humans. He gives a study guide, but no answers to check yourself. He gives practice exams but no explanations. His lectures are hard to follow and he goes off on tangents & boasts about himself. I think he sucks as a teacher and a person
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: With Mat E 273 being a required course for almost all engineering disciplines to graduate, and not being  a prereq for basically any classes, it has no business being this hard. The exams are practically a guessing game, you get tested on the most obscure, oddly specific facts. He makes the class very hard, and seemingly wants students to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MatE 273 can be challenging--there's a lot of chemistry, which many students have probably forgotten. Dr. Cullinan was always very accessible and friendly outside of class. Tests were rigid, mostly because of class size. Changed my major to MatE because of this class. TA'd for 273 the following year. Great teacher, tough (but fascinating) course.

Dr. Cullinan is an absolute power trip and has no business being a professor. He continually makes bad jokes while he is lecturing in hopes of a reaction from the 400 students in the lecture hall, then proceeds to send out nasty emails full of threats about the course curriculum changing due to students disrupting his class.

Turbo Tim is an intelligent man and seems to know a good amount about materials engineering, but he is not a great teacher. His lectures go so fast that its impossible to take notes along with him. To do well in this course it must be your top priority. Visit the TAs often and don't save the quizzes till last minute. Take this class elsewhere.

I have to admit he lives up to the title Turbo Tim. He lectures fast, and you have to be on top of taking the important notes. Exams are out of 110%, three quizzes a week with 3 attempts, online. All exams are multiple choice, so no partial credit. He is engaging and encourages questions in lecture. The math can be hard, as it is not covered well.

Turbo... This class was very interesting and can be scary at first. Work hard by doing the quizzes right after the lecture, go to office hours, and really learn the material! The exams can be tricky, but if you do the quizzes yourself and spend 7-9 hours a week on the class, you will pass with a good grade. The "curve" isn't really a curve IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures so fast it is nearly impossible to take notes, but slides are posted so it isn't that big of an issue. Provides many resources for tests and answers questions fast. Exams are straightforward and simple, also include a curve.

He lectures fast; you must take notes to stay engaged. Slides are packed with info and if you don't go to class you won't know what it means. Only curve was built into tests. Do not fall behind on Quiz/HW. He answers questions all times of day, and QUICKLY! Answered my questions at least 3 times out of class. Tests are scantron. Nice guy, but no BS
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He has way too much information that he spews during lecture/on his slides, so knowing whats important and whats not is tough to figure out. Theres so much fat that can be trimmed and so much simplification needs to be done to his slides. Its completely oversaturated w unnecessary (but interesting) info. Missing class will leave you far behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good luck in this class. Dr. Cullinan makes this class way harder than it needs to be. The lecture slides are super confusing so if you miss a class, good luck trying to learn that topic. He also says "your welcome" for not making us learn some super hard thing that no one gets during the lectures. Also the tests are nothing like the practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pathetic being of a "professor." I'm sure he knows a lot about MATE but he knows jack sh!t about how to run a class. The pathetic being who posted before me who received an A likely cheated on all the exams and everything he said was a lie. The lectures sucked a$$. I got a B, but I managed to get an A in engineering mechanics and dynamics. SMFH
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures were very good. You need to be sure to know specifics for the exams though. If you take good notes and understand the math you'll do fine. Just pay attention to the lecture and give some effort to understanding. Good note taking is essential to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures & quizzes given aren't bad. Making the exams more conceptual-based is logical, but not being able to go back to past questions is unfair. Compares exams to FE but only about not returning them. The syllabus says you can use lecture slides on exams, but white words are riddled throughout, so you can't ctrl+f when in a crunch.

It appears his only focus is making the course impossible to cheat on, which he did, but he also made it impossible to learn. The the three exams are purely trivia contests and make up 85% of the grade. Once you submit an answer you never see the question again. He doesn't even give multiple choice question answers back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is essentially a trivia game. You can only see the test questions one at a time and there is no going back. Don't ever think about making a human mistake in this class. Ever. Also if you happened to come across the ISUbarstool post on Sept. 21 the email is an accurate representation.
Not much material at lecture and lecture pdf. Exam comes from stuff that's not listed on the lecture pdf. grading criteria is clear. 1st exam is easiest. should get good on first exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TIm is just a bad lazy teacher. He does not give your exams back., so you don't know what you did wrong. He does not answer your questions great. He is very vague. Exams are 85% of the grade. The tests are very hard, and his lectures do not prepare you. He is a very lazy professor when it comes to helping you. Bad arrogant teacher. Just the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tim's ego only grew more as the semester progressed. The mode grade of the class was a 74 and the average around there too. His lectures were ultra boring and he usually used them to flex about his research. He tries to be funny in lectures... but he's not. For online classes, I highly don't recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So, Tim is a terrible Professor. He never answers my question well. Very vague answers. Exams are extremely hard and are worth 85 percent of your grade. His lectures are below because half the time the lecture is not on the exam. You need to find need to be an expert to get an A. I studied too much, and got nothing from this.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best way to prepare for exams are by redoing all the quizzes. Second best thing is to read the chapter summaries in the book, as it also explains all the equations. He includes memes in lectures, and is a wholesome guy in general. Overall would recommend.

He doesn't prepare you for the tests since his practice tests are easier than the test. The lectures contain A LOT of information that is both relevant and irrelevant to what you need to know. Also, the lectures provide barely any example problems to relate to the homework, which are Canvas quizzes. Overall, it's more difficult than it needs to be!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable of what he is teaching, but a little too much. He constantly goes on tangents that are rather irrelevant to tested material. He will acknowledge that we don't need to know it and then explain it more in depth. Never receive your old tests back to know how you did on specific questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cullinan is very engaging in class, which in turn keeps you focused during lecture. He clearly tries a lot to make you laugh and helps keep the lectures light, but he also goes extremely fast and you absolutely have to go to class to understand the content on his slides. Do the quizzes by yourself, read the book, and study lots for the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: To be fair, he has a very good understanding of the subject, but in my opinion he failed to deliver that understanding to the student. Along with that, the structure of this course is very tight which means if you did badly in one exam, you're lost! The most highlighted problem in this course is that it only is given by one instructor - terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Cullinan is very enthusiastic about what he teaches and that goes a long way. The lectures are very thorough and available as a resource for doing the homework after each class. He grades exams pretty generously and offers opportunities to make up missed homework. I can't complain besides the convoluted exam seating but that's pretty minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a likable guy and is clearly very interested in the material (heh, pun). However, he's very lecture-heavy. He has great and informative lectures, however, the notes he posts are atrocious for the purpose of self-learning. It's very difficult to learn the stuff on your own because they're so overwhelming. Easiest to just attend the lectures.

The MAT E 273 class itself provides you a lot of opportunities to succeed and get an A. Dr. Culinary himself is a great professor and does his best to make the high amounts of content in each lecture as interesting as possible. Was definitely the class I would look forward to most.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Material heavy class with tests requiring effort. Study the powerpoints and sit through class and the tests are manageable. Extra Credit is offered and it helps with some quizzes you may have done poorly on throughout the semester. The grading criteria is clear from the beginning of the semester and the class will most likely not be curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tim is a very interesting lecturer in a non very interesting subject for me. He kept my attention throughout the semester and made lectures interesting. The worst part about the class were the quizzes that you get as homework for every lecture.

Dr. Cullinan is an excellent communicator, and he goes to great lengths to make his lectures interesting and to make very clear the major concepts that must be understood for the exams. If you come to class, do your homework, take advantage of abundant extra credit, and ask frequent questions, you'll have a great time and learn a lot.

It's hard to figure out how to study for this class. Powerpoint slides and quiz questions will cover the entirety of the exams. I think Tim is great at teaching but needs to work on clarity. The biggest struggle was finding answers to quiz Qs and figuring out what to study from Tim's massive pwrpoint slides. Don't get lazy and you can get an A.
Take advantage of the exam review sessions! Don't skip lecture, the demonstrations help you understand the material. Go to office hours or the help desk if you become confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tim is an excellent choice for anyone taking a materials class. He is clear on what is being asked and gives you everything you need to know in the lecture slides. Homework is not hard, tests are just homework questions, and each test has a built-in curve. On top of that, he offers easy extra credit that you should take advantage of.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tim is almost weirdly passionate about materials science. Tough class but a good guy. Very clear grading criteria with extra credit opportunities. Top hat in class

My advice for 214 with Cullinan is to pay very close attention to lectures. He posts his own slides online, but they are not enough to study if you didn't understand the material the first time. Go to his office hours as soon as you can if you didn't get something. Also, try to do your homework early you will need the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Rarely finishes lectures. Tim releases homework as canvas quizzes after each lecture and gives you a week to do that. Of course, since he didn't finish the lecture, you don't know how to do the material on the homework, so the next lecture, he rushes through the hard stuff to catch up to where he wants to be. Find some friends in the class to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Biggest tool I've ever met, cares way too much about students opinions of him and acts like he's still an undergrad. Class isn't that hard. Just grind 2-3 days before the tests and you'll be fine. The lab is super easy but the homework difficulty varies between slightly difficult and insanely time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I find his lectures refreshing, He doesn't throw formulas at us and expect us to know what its practical purpose is, he explains the concept and shows how to find it, than shows how it applies to our career, That seems to be lacking in most courses. He is helpful outside of class plus the exam is basically the same thing as the practice one.

His lectures are pointless. His classes are a waste because he talks about real world examples for 80% of the time, and when it comes to the exam, you're completely unprepared. His exams will be the complete opposite of the one practice exam he gives, which he only started doing because he failed so many students the semester before.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is difficult. The 3 exams cover lots of material, and could include random questions that we discusses only once. Quizzes every day that aren't too difficult. The textbook is not necessary but it helps sooo muchhh to read. His lectures are difficult to listen to because its all hard stuff but he does interesting experiments!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. My only complaint is that sometimes it is hard to know what material covered in lectures is actually going to be tested
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tim loves what he does and is super smart but his exams are ungodly difficult. Lectures are 5% math based, exams are 95% math based. Lectures are super interesting and the Top Hat is super easy. 3 exams, third one doubles as the final. The only HW is daily quizzes on Canvas. I'd advise to study the math on the quizzes to prep for exams. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He puts an entire textbook on every slide and cruises thru around 40 slides each lecture. Impossible to take notes. Cant reach outside of class b/c he always cancels office hours. Tests are just memorizing random facts

Tim is super passionate about his material but this causes him to lecture on things he finds interesting that aren't relevant to the information we need to know. His tests get progressively harder as the semester goes on but they aren't too bad. Has Tophat for accuracy so you have to go to class to get those points. Posts all his lectures online
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Had to go to class for tophat and there were quizzes after most lectures. He made the class very easy to get an A. I did not like his lecture style. He went through so many slides and a lot of it was unnecessary. He tried to entertain the class too much with weird facts when he should really consolidate the material to half the number of slides

While the course material itself was interesting, Tim made it almost impossible to get a good grade in this course. He provided little to no test prep, and very easily could have provided more but refused. The tests are each 35 questions but out of 30, but THEY ARE DIFFICULT. If I had a different prof I guarantee that I would've done better.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dude seems super chill, but don't let him fool you. His exams are pretty hard and he gives you next to nothing to prepare for them. Homework wasn't too hard. Unfortunately, he is the only professor that teaches this class. He is very passionate about his work, I'll give him that. Exams are 75% of your grade so do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Homework was easy enough to get a good grade but challenging enough to reinforce concepts. Lecture was fun and engaging. Grading was more than fair. Extra credit was given generously. Great course
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I Really like Tim as a person, but there are a few things about the class that make it difficult. He spends a decent amount of time on tangents that are not tested on, and there is a very large amount of material on the lecture slides. Pretty difficult exams, but doable if you spend the time to take good notes on ALL of the lectures (outside class)

Tim is the best professor I've had at Iowa State. His lectures are very valuable and relevant to the content you're being tested on. If you do the quizzes and don't cheat on them you should be fine. The tests are very hard but if you put in the work you should be able to get a good grade. He knows his content well and is very helpful.

Good guy but no textbook and very little outside resources for the class.  Tests are based completely on lectures and a little lab work.  Can be difficult to get to him during his 2 office hours a week to ask him questions, decent at emailing you back though.  Doesn't utilize lab much, most days lab is cancelled.  Fun teacher, difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Excellent person, decent teacher. Cullinan is an incredibly tough grader in all aspects of the class. The exams are more of a test of how well you can create a cheat sheet than a true test of knowledge. Be careful going to in depth on short answer questions in his class. unless you word things exactly as Tim wants them you will lose many points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Decent professor, always enjoy the labs, tough grader, but tells you pretty much exactly what he wants. USE THE NOTES SHEET WELL for tests and quizzes. Labs are very interesting and talking about playing with 1/4 to 1/2 million dollar equipment is a great conversation starter. No textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Hes a good lecturer while you are in class and keeps it relatively interesting. However, very rarely does his information actually transfer over to assignments. Tests are way harder than you expect from his reviews as well. They are now night exams and no longer at testing centers. Doesn't ever actually do calculations during class either.

READ THE BOOK. Homework comes from lecture slides and book. Testing center for tests, do the practice problems he gives you as you go through each lecture with redoing the homework and reading the lecture slides and you WILL get good grades on the tests. 1st testeasy(get the highest you can), 2ndhard, lastnotsobad. follow these rulesgood grade
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The exam and quiz questions are always vague, not sure what he wants in particular.

Cullinan is very knowledgeable about materials science and this makes it a lot easier to learn from him.  Even if he doesn't cover a certain topic during the lecture, it might still come up on the homework. Despite this, everything you will ever need to know will be hidden in the lecture notes somewhere.
Makes MAT E very interesting and cool. Heavy focus on Aerospace applications. Tough online homework but the answers are in that days lecture notes.

Cullinan is not a prof I would take again. He tries to make the lectures interesting but goes a little to far and things become distracting. Just find someone to do homework and study with and you'll be fine though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Is not very informative during lectures, assumes that the student knows everything and lectures are more like review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: A great class with interesting demos

He is a great guy and a good professor. The topics you cover can get boring at times but he honestly makes it as interesting as possible. The demos are fantastic. All the material you need to know is given in lecture, but the review sessions are also very helpful. Overall not a very difficult class if you attend lecture and put in the work.

Tim Cullinan is a good professor and a good man. While MATE273 is really not that interesting, and usually not that challenging, he does his best to make the class bearable. Not that it's possible at all times, but he does care about the topics and sets very clear criteria for success. There's plenty of extra credit on exams too, so don't panic.
Great teacher! Helpful and attractive!!!

Lectures are not super interesting, but not terrible. He tries to make it interesting with jokes and demonstrations. Really not a very hard class. Gives practice exams that are almost exactly like the tests. Try, and you will get above a B.

He is a very straightforward professor. He gives lecture slides and he doesn't intend for you to take notes. If you pay attention in class and do practice exams and problems before exams, you shouldn't have too much of a problem getting an A.

His lectures are so boring, and you can easily be fine if you don't go. Just know people in the class and in the other lectures to get the password and quiz answers that you get every day. Know the conceptual stuff, because that is where I lost points on the tests. make a good cheat sheet and you will do well.

Lectures are boring, but they give you all the information you need to do well on the tests (no book reading required). He does a really good job of letting you know what the grading is based on and what you need to do to get a certain grade. The material isn't too tough, so if you pay attention in class, you should do fine.

Probably the most boring lecturer i have had at Iowa State. Long lectures in which i have seen several kids sleeping in class. Review sessions were very helpful however. All tests have an online format which I personally do not like but I know some do. Also you get little to no feedback on exams due to the online format.

The class seems easy at the beginning, but don't let that fool you. You have to study to get a good grade. He mostly reads verbatim from the lecture slides, but you still have to go to class to get the quiz passwords. If you don't like online homework, quizzes, or tests, you may not enjoy the class, but you have to get through it and it's not hard.
It's okay if you like vague tests and misleading information.

Lectures are long and it is hard to stay focused. He stands on the stairs reading off the lecture slides. Tests aren't terribly hard but you still need to study for them. Overall, wasn't a horrible professor, just could be dry at times.

Professor Cullinan is a great professor. His methods are clean, and his course is fun. He does exciting and often funny demonstrations in front of class most days, and always has a lame but funny joke somewhere in his lectures. The class is not too difficult, but still worth attending lectures.

"You will pass this class if you do something". This quote sums up his class. exams are online and aren't very hard if you make a good equation sheet (watch out for his second exam though). Final is optional. The guy loves the stuff he talks about, and is knowledgeable, but can be hard to pay attention to in class if he drones on while talking.

3 exams all online and extremely easy. On the first test like half of the class got 100. The other tests were harder but still very easy. The final is optional and can't hurt your grade. Very little homework. Totally aceable course. Tim is likeable, knowledgable, and reasonable.

The tests are hard with lecture heavy memorization as well as taking the time to read the background in the textbook. She does give numerous tries for extra credit, but keeping up with the material is a must first. The material is hard but the textbook and homework assignments help. She is very nice and does care about the students I'll say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cunnick presents the best lectures out of any professor I've had. The material is always up-to-date and she is amazing at explaining concepts in detail. This is the hardest B I've worked for and I must say, it was well worth it. Each exam has a case study portion and questions on the in-class exam are open-ended and fill-in-the-blank.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: So much work for this class. The material we learn is very interesting but expect to spend a couple hours preparing for exams with study guides for each chapter. There are three exams and each exam covers 10-14 chapters. She is very approachable and available outside of class if you need help. To help your grade, each exam has a take-home part.

She is such a wonderful person and she really enjoys micro! You can tell she loves her job and it makes the class worth it. The course is dense with lots of vocab, make sure to fully do the study guides and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer and extremely intelligent in the field of microbiology and infectious diseases. Her lectures are incredible and informational. Tests are extremely difficult and requires a lot of studying, but she models them off of past exams which she posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is horrible. I came to her about questions regarding to the honor program and she was heartless and did not care if I graduated with honors or not. I emailed her MULTIPLE times and she NEVER emailed me back.  I had to meet with her in person just to get an answer out of her.

Dr. Cunnick is amazing! She's very caring and is very good at emailing you back in a timely manner. Her tests are slightly tough, but if you read through the old exams and keep up on the study guides you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor, she explains things very well. She provides past tests prior to exams which provide a great use to study for the exam. Tests are extremely difficult as they are only fill in the blank and essay. Exams are derived only from lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tests are difficult because they are not multiple choice. There are fill in the blanks and free essay questions. She gives an ample amount of extra credit and there is a group project at the end. Overall class material is clear but there is a lot of information so make sure to study.
Dr. Cunnick will destroy you. You deserve it. You're weak. And you'll be better for it. You will thank the good lord above you got a solid C.

Joan is a great professor, she really cares about her students and is very helpful during office hours. I found the power points to be particularly helpful so definitely go to class and listen to what she has to say. The class requires quite a bit of effort to study in order to pass so make sure to actually study!

i would click tough grader twice if I could, she is an excellent professor and expect a lot of effort from you. If you don't understand the material she is more than happy to help you understand and give extensive study guides for tests. as a micro major i thought  this class was tough but you can do very well if you put in the effort and study.:)
Great professor who knows a lot about her field. She was always willing to meet outside of class and was very helpful. I would recommend this to all BiologyMicrobiology majors.

one of my favorite classes. she has a great sense of humor and is smart. material was very relevant to the medical & health field. attendance is mandatory since she did daily clicker questions. (fall 2012)

Best class I have ever taken! The information is interesting and up to date. You have to put the time in and you will do well. Fill out the study guide questions and know answers to past exams and you will do well. Great professor! Always willing to go out of her way to help students! I highly recommend this class.
A good teacher and very enthusiastic. Takes a long time preparing the tests, this is reflected in there fairness. Should know the material taught in the book less than that covered in lecture!

Good teacher.  will meet with students anytime outside of class to answer questions.  Reading the text book is optional but is really good for supplemental information.  The open book tests take a long time!  prepare like you don't get to use the book, saves a bunch of time.  She is very excited about immunology.

2 open book tests, 1 closed book, and a take home final so it was fairly easy. The open book tests are way too long, so be prepared. Most of the class didnt finish the open book tests so everyone lost about 20 points just because they couldnt get them done...class was kind of boring, but go for the clicker points
No Comments

Dr. Cunnick does a great job explaining this class, especially considering that, with the term paper, it's considered graduate-level. The only bad thing about it is that the class is at 8 in the morning, in the Winter, on the North side of Campus, which really blows.
I will always take a class where Dr. Haynes teaches!
Cindy is so caring and is truly passionate about what she teaches. If you are interested in plants you will love her classes/

Cynthia is pretty nice, I liked listening to her in lab and lecture. Tests are online and homework isn't tough. PassBack is a tad annoying but other than that you'll get an A, just show up. You also get like 7 house plants, a jack-o-lantern, and a great bundle of flowers.
Cynthia is great, but attendance is a big part of your grade. Show up to lab and lecture. Tests are pretty simple if you listen in lecture and review.

This class is all about Corporate Social Responsibility, though she will maybe rename it Sustainability, We mainly have current event discussions weekly, followed by a lecture and a case. So far, even though it is a long class, you are engaged, and the time goes by quickly as long as you eat dinner, as the class for this semester is 6:40 - 10 PM.

You're graded only on very few things, one of those being attendance. You need to show up or you'll miss out on free points. She lectures for a very long time from one set of slides and it can be boring at times. Overall though, it's a pretty easy night class you can take, and she is a great person that has a lot of experiences to share.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No exams as they are replaced with take home papers for midterm and final. Lectures are extremely long and provides so much information it is almost too much, which is why her having echo available is so helpful when reviewing information. Homework consists of cases, papers, and reflections.

This class replaces exams with take-home midterm and final papers, based on class learning. I enjoyed how engaging her discussion get as I always leave class having learned something new. Echo  was available for classes which was nice to go back and review information for the papers and topics you maybe didn't understand the first time hearing it.

I took ACCT 489 which is one of the easiest classes I've ever taken but also one I've learned the most and the first I had the ability to use critical thinking for. She did a great job of not incorporating her own opinion and instead encouraging students to think and challenge their own ideas.

reviews.comment: Absolutely wont recommend taking her class. The most useless course youll take with someone that themself dont know basic accounting concepts, I am unable to work my head around how shes been teaching for so long. Just dont waste your money on taking a class with Cyndie

Gives you a ton and expects you to write a whole lot. She wants you to read from the textbook and copy and write answers to her homeworks from the book. There is so much writing that makes this class an English reading writing course more than an accounting course. I dont recommend her class especially since her own concepts arent clear

reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Lectures can be long as she reads straight from the slides. Also, there is homework assigned for each chapter of the book as well as a take home final, but overall a very straight forward class.

Had her for Acct 596 and 598.  Lectures can be boring, she reads power point slides to us that she makes available.  Her discussion of cases is better though.  Lots of homework for these two classes, especially 596.  Pretty relaxed grader of exams though, as long as you sound like you know what you are talking about.
She was alright, I got irritated that she didn't make the answers available to the book questions that she suggested you do...but other than that she's about as good as you'll get for 386.

This is one of the best teachers I had at the univeristy. your going to have to work, but if you don't get it...go talk to her. she ended up being more of a friend than a prof by the time I graduated...I still keep in touch with her and I graduated in 2001
One of the worst teachers ever.  You must teach yourself if you have her.  Nothing is prepared before class
Good class. Tests are striaght from homework and notes.  Learn a lot

Terrible terrible professor. Avoid her at all costs necessary. There is not point in going to lecture because you learn nothing. Goes off on tangents about things that are irrelevant to the course. Exams and quizzes are extremely hard, she does not make them she has them go random from a 500 question bank. The averages for things were super low.

reviews.comment: Amazing person. Super sweet and accessible. I really like her! The class is difficult because there are difficulties with canvas. I really don't blame her though because she found out she was teaching this class two days before it started. I really don't think the tech difficulties are all her fault; department should help her.

Knowledgeable but just not a good teacher overall. Whole class is curved because averages on homework and exams are bad. You pretty much have to teach yourself how to do everything. Would not recommend unless this class is a last resort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Seems like she knows her stuff, just cannot teach it to a class. Very nice lady but expect to literally teach yourself everything by reading the book or looking up the homework problems online (every assignment can easily be found online)

I am completing a second degree, with a Finance minor.  Throughout my public education, military training, community training courses, and over 200 semester college credits, Cynthia Campbell is the worst instructor I have ever experienced. I took my complaints and issues to the Department Chair, the department is aware of her sub-par abilities.
Went from my most looked forward to class, to one I didn't bother showing up for.

Worse professor I have had over my four years at ISU. Homeworks are long and self taught. Class is boring and useless. Formats for test are unknown til day of.
