Class was interesting, and tests were easy. I skimmed the chapters, went to class. If I didn't go to class, I just read over his powerpoints which are all online. If there's one thing I dislike about class, it would be the journals, but it's not like they're hard to do. Love his Simpsons clips.

Unlike some of the previous reviews, I found the tests to be very easy! To get an A all you have to do is attend class, study lecture notes day before test, and maybe read micro-connections in the book. Class was interesting, but I felt like more material could have been covered/emphasized. The text book is a page flipper and fun to read!
The class was extremely interesting, but the tests were very difficult.
great professor who gets to know his students even in a lecture class

Dr. Schweingruber is one of the best teachers I had all semester! His lectures were interesting and I loved going to class. The homework is really easy and is only about once a week, turned in online. I am not a sociology major because of this class.

Very interesting class.  The tests are slightly difficult because he often puts in tests questions that are from lectures,so I would strongly encourage attending class.  You should frequently check his website on any articles he puts up because he will put those on the tests.  You should either take notes or go to his website and read his key note
Really informational
Very easy to relate to what he is teaching but tests are very hard so just have to study, but dont have to go to class :)

His lectures were sometimes interesting and easy to follow but other days it was easy to lose interest. The only downside of the class was he made the tests pretty difficult so you have to study to do well.
Very nice and interesting. relateable

GREAT professor! The one class I actually wanted to come to, and it has nothing to do with my major! Readings are very interesting and the in-class discussions are fun! Read the summary notes he posts online before the tests and it's a guaranteed A! I learned a lot from this class and would recommend everyone to take this professor!

Good professor, attendance is necessary, because you'll get asked questions on the tests that were only covered in lecture. The book isn't too bad, just know the terms for each chapter as well as the micro connections, and you'll do fine. Mini-essays were a breeze, as well as the project. I recommend taking him for this course.

Amazing class!! Very interesting, the book is one of the best textbooks I've had to read so far! He posts the notes but usually not until way later. Tests aren't too bad, just go to class because on the test he will put "according to lecture..". Also, make sure you know the "Micro-Macro" sections in the book. GREAT CLASS!I reccommend it to everyone
I like him as a teacher and I've learned a lot from him.  He usually keeps class interesting and we often get out early!!
Fairly interesting class. Not a big fan of his grading. Each test is 25 percent of you final grade, so you cant do bad on any of them to get a good overall grade.
Not bad but don't fall behind. Make sure you get all the points you can outside of the tests.
Interesting book, easy reader. Lectures are interesting also, sometimes a little long. Funny guy and pretty genuine.
very interesting lectures i really liked going, you can either go to every class  and skim the book or go to no classes and just read the book, either way works
Good teacher, fun to listen to, tests are easy if you go to lecture and pay attention.  Those stories he tells about his family during lecture will probably be on the test.
Very good teacher, easy to understand, involves students in class discussions

Tests are about 70% over lectures and about 30% over the book material.  I never read the book, and got about 70 percents on the tests...so that's what I'm basing this on. Lectures tend to be a little on the boring side, depending on the topic, but I'm not really interested in sociology anyways.  One big plus is no comprehensive final...THANK GOD!
He made the class harder than it needed to be.  The material was interesting but he explained it in class more on a grad level.  I learned more from his note than in class.

He's a good professor and does his best to keep lecture interesting with movies and clips from "The Simpsons".  He loves sociology and is always interested in new ideas and opinions.  The textbook is awesome and the tests are easy IF you do the reading and go to lecture.  The class project is easy, too (I did a photo essay = fun).
I found the class and tests to be generally easy, but his lectures were sooooo boring. I found very little motivation to actually attend class since his slides were online.
Very interesting and intelligent. You still have to study to get a good grade, but overall its a great and interesting class.

This professor is a sack of**** anyone who has him beware!  I took his class and did a volunteer project, there was mis communication over it and even though I did the paper he gave me a 0 on it. he then went to Iowa state officals and claimed I misled him now I have to go to isu court!!!! He loves to fail ppl his a raging liberal!!!
Very interesting class. If you just read the book and pay attention in class its an easy A
Tests were definatly too hard for an introductory class.
Awesome guy, loves what he does. He loves discussion, and kept my attention throughout his lectures. Moderate studying is useful, but don't kill yourself.

The most interesting class I have taken at Iowa State. I had a great time doing all of the assignments and the class discussions were a blast. I never missed class and read all of the assignments on time. If you study the study guide, memorize the terms, and ask questions if you are confused about the writing assignments you will do fabulous.

Mixed bag... Although I think he did a good job teaching a huge introductory course, some of the lectures were really dull and some test questions were ridiculously specific.  Still, with a good set of notes and reading the text, it's easy to get an A, plus he offers extra credit.  Like others said, he let gomers take part in class discussion.
Arrogant - pretty full of himself. He lets the morons comandeer the classroom discussion.

Wayyy hard for 100-level class!  If you want an A, make it to lecture every day and study the micro-macro texts and the research texts in the book.  Class is very boring & information is common knowledge, but is hard to remember because it's so easy.
Wow this class had a lot of assignments, but I found him to be very understanding and helpful in you getting the most out of the class
Very weird. Says MMMMMMMMK all the time!! His tests are kind of hard for a 100 level class because the questions are way too specific.

Very good professor.  Definitely as easy A if you attend the lectures and actually read the text book.  If you don't plan on doing that, don't take Soc with him.  Good material, keeps the class interested 95% of the time.  Tests are difficult if you didn't study.  If you study, good prof.

Schweingruber's class isn't as easy as people make it sound. Half of his tests are questions like, "according to lecture I said..." and the other half is stuff like, "according to the article blah-blah in your textbook..."  t could be easy if you dedicated quite a bit of time to it. A hard 100 class

I didn't mind this class at all.  I went to most of the lectures, but didn't for it.  I did good on all of the test without reading.  For the tests, he has notes online.  I would suggest studying those and looking over the photo essays and micro-macro connections in the book.  It's a fairly easy cla
So I dont really understand why everyone likes this guy. I think he is boring, and his tests are not easy like everyone says!
I really like this prof! He has funny stories and makes the class really interesting I thought. Just make sure to read the book before the tests.
He's a good guy, brings up some very interesting points about sociology.  I recommend this class because it's decent and he's just nice guy who loves teaching.
very good at explaining what is going to on test and makes lectures clear.  Takes time to get to know as many people in a big lecture class as he can.  very wiling to answer questions
Very straightforward. Not hard to get an A if you go to class and read the assigned readings on time.

He's a funny guy and has a lot of information, which you have to pay attention to for the tests. As long as you go and pay attention and write down some obscure facts, which are needed for the test, you'll do fine. I recommened taking a class with the Grub.
Make sure you pay attention to the lectures because they are a big part of the exams.  Good prof.  Made the atmosphere a little more light. Fun class to go to.
not impressed with his class at all, didn't find it fair to include minute details in the tests, i went to every class, but was still unable to get all the little stuff.
Best. Bar none. Fair, balanced. Challenges you but helps you along as well. Great class discussions. I wish he taught all my classes! Learned a ton.

Cool teacher, gets the crowd into his conversations, if you go to class and study even a little bit or night before exam, you will do fine. Need to buy book and his T.A. is hot fine chic. ONe of the reasons why I actually went to class. Great class.
The best teacher I have ever had.  I love his class and his teaching.
Lectures are very interesting and keep you listening.  I learned a lot in that class...good prof
THE BEST!!

I wouldnt call him funny, more of a dry sense of humor that only he thinks is funny. Has a lot of test questions from the lecture. such as "according to lecure I said..." **Make sure to do the extra credit.
Very straight from the book in lecture, but puts a nice spin on lecture with a lot of discussion.  Material is very easy to understand after lecture.

I love Dr. Schweingruber. I think he makes the class very interesting and bring up good discussion points and really helps people to think about things clearly. I know he's made me become more open minded. I would definitely recommend him for Soc 327.
No Comments
No Comments
Funny, good teacher. Notes online.
No Comments
A really nice guy, has large lectures and makes effort to get to know people and tries to make class as fun as possible.
he makes an effort to know names in large lectures, interesting, and has a sweet pompadour
Come to class on movie days, it WILL be on the test!
Very good professor. Do the extra credit though
No Comments
He knew my name in a 500 person class.  He is awesome
No Comments
No Comments
He makes a very interesting subject even more interesting because of his humor.

Great guy, hard to understand as he is very sarcastic....that or he hates me. Really knows his bread. He asks a lot of very theoretical questions that make you think. Mandatory attendance, he will text or call you if you aren't there. 10/10 on knowledge. Knew everything about anything in the room. Also no bathroom breaks are allowed.

Really knows his stuff. If you ask a question about something interesting, be prepared to talk about it... he will talk your ear off, but its usually pretty interesting. If the chance provides itself, he will make a meme about it and put it on the wall. Overall, great professor and very interesting guy who genuinely cares about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was grouped based, groups are assigned on the first day. Overall the class is fun and hands-on. There are lab reports that you and your group do after the class and they were 3 to 6 questions. There are a couple of projects as well.

324L is very group based and you briefly skim over many topics. DeLarm does a good job at running and organizing the class. He understands students' issues, and if you need to make something up, he is very flexible. Overall a fun, hands-on class.

Very intelligent professor. Socratic seminar is intimidating at first, but you get more comfortable with it over time and learn a lot from it. I recommend for any political science student or general pre-law.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dirk's teaching method is not for this class. CJ3200 is a judicial processes class so I figured I would be learning about the American court systems. Instead, he used the socratic method and went over texts that were very philosophical and had nothing to do with courts or laws. Don't take this class if you want to learn about the court system.

Dirk is a great professor, after a few lessons I had already begun to think more critically than before. His Socratic method style of teaching is super intimidating but if you are up to date on the reading you are usually fine. If you are looking for an easy class this is not it, but if you want to actually learn something take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Difficult class, but may have been due to harsh TAs. A lot of course content to get through, but it's mostly enjoyable and interesting. Definitely a must take if you're into political theory.
Awesome class, it's a bit of a roller coaster, but you learn a lot about politics and partisanship!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, but always make sure to do your reading. His Socratic method can be intimidating initially, but if you give a smart answer, he won't go after you. The class discussions are a great way of learning the more complex nature of the subject. The six quizzes were easy; for me, my lowest score was a 94%, otherwise it was all 98 or 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His classes heavily utilize the Socratic method which sounds great on paper, however if you don't provide an answer that he thinks of as "correct" he will gladly belittle you into never offering up another answer. He is incredibly knowledgeable about that topics he lectures on, however it comes off as a massive superiority complex.

Dirk is an awesome professor who makes class very enjoyable. One thing I will stress is to read and come with questions, they do not have to be complex questions. Dirk does teach socratically, so be ready to answer questions; he forces you to think with the questions he asks you. 15/10 professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is cross-listed with Criminal Justice. I would recommend CJ students not to take this class as it is more designed for Pol Sci students.  Compared to traditional CJ classes, this is much harder. It is an amazing class, and if you want to go to law school, I highly recommend taking it, as he teaches in the same style as law school.

Dirks Media class is amazing. It will change the way you think about the world around you. Attendance is not mandatory, but you must participate in class throughout the semester or you will not receive a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dirk is an amazing professor. If you want to go to law school, take his classes as they are taught in the style that law school uses. He is intimidating at first, but once you get used to his style, it gets much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've loved every class I've taken with Dirk. He is super knowledgable and passionate and wants to help students see his perspective, but he can come off as arrogant because of that. His readings are interesting but dense, you'll need to read a lot to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dirk's socratic teaching style creates engaging lectures to keep you on your toes. He assigns a lot of background reading to make sure you come to class with knowledge of the topic he talks about. Most of the points come from unit tests that are easy as long as you come to class. Skipping this class makes it significantly harder to succeed.

All classes are 6 quizzes (drops lowest grade) and a final exam. Attendance not required but I would recommend. A lot of reading before class, and kind of lectures as a law school class. He is a really interesting guy and it is a pretty easy class. Just do the readings and understand it to a point and you will do really well

I have met very few professors that are truly passionate about teaching. Dirk is by far the best professor I have ever had. He teaches in the Socratic tradition with makes for an amazing classroom experience. The literature is engaging and prescient.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dirk is incredibly intelligent, which occasionally comes off as arrogant, but only for those who have not done the readings! If you do the readings and can contribute to class conversations regardless of your understanding, you will do just fine. Dirk wants you to thoroughly understand the material (NEED to for tests), hence the heavy reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dirk is a challenging but engaging professor. His Socratic method pushes you to think deeply. Readings are essential - try unstuck ai alongside the textbook for helpful prep.

He's extremely intelligent and pretty intimidating but don't be afraid to speak your mind, just make sure you can back up what you say. He enjoys communicating with his students and will challenge you but you get credit for being able to speak up in class. Make sure you actually do the readings because it will count in the long run.

He's pretty left leaning so if you're looking for a more centralist professor I would try to get Susan Laehn. Other than that he's extremely intelligent and the lectures are very engaging, they make you think. Lots of reading but it counts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I could see why some people may not like Dirk, but I had a great experience with him. If you are thinking about law school, take a class with him! His classes are structured like law school courses. Lots of reading, but if you know your stuff when you come to class, he will like you and you'll do well. Have an opinion and be able to defend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was a little nervous at first because of his teaching style, but you learn A LOT. Get ready to be called on, and make sure you are up to date on the readings. Will definitely take classes with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dirk will call on you, he will challenge you, and he will make you think. Dirk is the professor you NEED in college and he is the best there is. 10/10 recommend all of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dirk is the most inspirational, talented, and kind professor I know. He has fundamentally expanded my intellectual spectrum and instilled within me an inquisitiveness that I didn't know I had. His classes are challenging, but how else would you learn? I promise that if you put in the effort, you will take away more than you can possibly imagine.

Dirk is the best professor I've had at Iowa State. I am much more confident in speaking in front of class. You need to go to his classes, read the book, and participate in order to pass. You will learn more from his classes than you do from any other class. Don't let the first few days scare you away, it is a great class to prepare for law school.
Super smart charismatic professor with a high level of expertise in what he is teaching

Dirk is absolutely the best professor at Iowa State, if you are looking for someone who will make you grow as a student and a person Dirk is the professor for you. He is the smartest person you will ever meet and if you are ready to challenge yourself then take his classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Deam is by far one of my favorite professors on campus. His teaching style is unique, and I learned so much throughout this course. If you want to go to law school in the future, I recommend taking a class or two of his.

Dirk is one of the best professors at Iowa State. Would recommend his courses to anyone. His method allows for a complete understanding of the content of the course. The readings and films are great, and this course opens your mind to media and politics. Worth the take. Would take it again.

Dirk is an amazing guy! The Socratic method he uses to teach his classes is very interesting and engaging. He is a very combative person with his students but in a good natured way and will only make you better. I plan on taking every class he teaches because of how good he is.
You have to do the readings or else you will be so lost in class. He is by far my favorite prof I have ever had and I will continue to take his courses

Dirk is my favorite prof by far, Ive taken several of his classes and all of them have been an amazing experience. You definitely need to read the assignments because he will be asking you questions and challenging you. He is such an interesting person and cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Unique way of teaching through seminars, puts students in a position where they interact with the materials. References the readings a lot, so make sure to keep up with them, tests are also very close to readings.

A great class to take if you want to go to law school, if not I would not recommend it. You have to do a lot of reading of cases and really know the cases because he uses the socratic method to stimulate in class discussion. Great professor who is always willing to talk to you about class materials as well as law school prospects
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Uses socratic method in class so be ready to talk. Make sure to do the reading and have some thoughts on it. Take good notes during class discussion and use them on the quizzes and you should be okay. Dirk is an amazing teacher who would love to talk to you more about the class materials
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading make sure you order your textbooks before the first day of class, you will need them day 1. great prof would 100% take his class again, try not to be intimidated by him, hes not mean i promise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Deam has TA's that do the grading due to volume of students, so it may take a bit to get your quizzes back, but he gives incredibly good feedback, is very approachable, and cares about students. No slides, he just asks questions to the class and it's actually very easy to absorb and 100x more interesting than any class I've ever taken here.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dirk is a really valuable professor that anyone should take advantage of learning from while they're here. He can be pretty intimidating but the content you learn from him is invaluable. He does cold call but if you do the readings and work through your thoughts you'll be fine. Ask him questions when you're confused but don't try to outsmart him.

Only grading is available through Socratic seminars, so if you are not a talkative student you will not do well. He is always unavailable through email, you have better luck emailing the TA's than you do him. I have sent 6 emails this semester and have received 0 answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 90% of the traditional "lecturing" is done by the readings with only 10 to 20-minute explanations done by Dirk when he feels he needs to clear concepts up for the class. The rest is completely done by the Socratic method of teaching. His tests can be tough but that's just because he wants to see if you understand the concept not just memorizing.

Dirk is one of my favorite professors I have ever had. From his choice of readings to his renowned lecturing style, all parts of the class have been interesting. I have to say he has inspired me to do and strive for excellence where I thought I could never reach before. Don't feel afraid to answer questions in his class either. Great Class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this course as a required class for my poli sci major in the fall of my freshman year. This prof is by far the favorite I've had at ISU and made me feel like I'm expanding my mind every day and really learning. There are a lot of readings but they're necessary for most classes. Overall, I LOVE this prof and highly recommend him!

Dirk pushes his students to come to their own conclusions and to truly understand the material, rather than just reading it. The best way to describe it was that I felt like he was pushing me to think/learn more so than teaching. Do the readings or you will be lost. Also, the jazz lecture is funny lmao
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class my very last semester at Iowa State and can confidently say I learned more and was more engaged than any other class I took. He has so much first hand knowledge of the material, you'll learn from the lectures more than you ever thought. The class is not easy, however. I HIGHLY recommend going to quiz reviews with the TA.

Dirk is absolutely amazing. The readings are absolute beasts but you NEED to thoroughly understand them to do well in the class. Participation matters and if you come to class you should be ready to talk. But Dirk's style of questioning is nothing like I've ever seen and he pulls the answer out of you even if you don't realize you have it in you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dirk is the best professor I've ever had. His classes aren't hard if you pay attention, minimally participate, and keep up with the reading. Attendence is NOT mandatory, but encouraged. Every reading assignment, lecture topic, and quiz is laid out in his syllabus, & his finals are open-book and can be done in a few BB pages. Quality over Quantity!

Take advantage of meeting with the TA for this class. Quizzes are difficult and you really have to thoroughly read the books. If you have questions, any questions at all, make sure you address them during class because you are graded on participation, plus it helps you in the long run. Take this class as serious as possible. NOT an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Con Law was probably the hardest class I've ever taken but also where I learned the most!! AMAAAAZING prof, reading, & class period!!
The BEST prof in the dept!! I took ALL his classes plus TA'd for him and learned SOOOO much from him! Take any class you can from him-he is SOOO intelligent!!

I loved Dirk. The class was very thought provoking and one of my favorite classes at ISU to date. HIs class is very lecture heavy and he expects participation in discussions for a grade. If you do the readings, go to the lectures, and participate you are going to do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wow. Dirk is by far the most profound thinker and lecturer at Iowa State. I cannot get enough of his classes. I learn and absorb information like a sponge due to his participation heavy Socratic method of teaching. I love the process, though I could see it not being for everyone. Nonetheless, for me, I am infatuated with Dirk and his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: What is there to say, he's great. I feel like a better American citizen for taking his classes. He is what inspired me to become a teacher.

Dirk is hands down the best professor in the political science department. He challenges you and makes you work for it. He genuinely wants everyone to understand what we discuss. If you don't participate, you won't get the full potential out of the class. He is intimidating only because he's so knowledgeable, but he's a great guy. 100% recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great instructor. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I studied for the final for, and I counted, 159 hours; but Dirk is still be best professor I've ever had. His class is very valuable for those looking to go to law school, but also rewarding for those who aren't.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dirk is great, and the class is very interesting. Watch out for the groupies that take every class with him, they're kind of annoying.
Hope you like reading...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Readings are due for every class and classes are discussion based about the readings. Very knowledgeable and an overall great class.
With amazing characteristic and special style of teaching. However the course Do require a lot of reading and he does care about peoples involvement.

Dirk teaches with the socratic method, and class participation is 20% of the grade. There is a lot of reading for each class, but you know well in advance of when it's due. I learned a lot because he made us think and find the answers rather than just give them to us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dirk is the best professor I've had at Iowa State. He is an amazing lecturer and uses the Socratic method asking lots of questions. You also watch lots of movies. His classes are always interesting and insightful, but make sure you do the readings so you can participate in the discussions. If you get the chance, certainly take a Dirk class.

Dirk has been one of my favorite professors at ISU so far. He is pretty intimidating on the first day but a really great professor and very knowledgeable. Class is very heavy on reading so be prepared to read and participate in class. Class is graded on participation and 6 quizzes. Go to class, you will learn a lot. Highly recommend Dirk!

Dirk Deam is by far the best professor I have had in my entire college career. If you enjoy thinking deeply, and truly learning lessons then any one of his classes is the right class for you. Every class of his is eye opening and insightful, all he asks of you is that you attend classes and come prepared.
Lots of reading that must be done in order to participate in class and do well on the quizzes. Great guy, definitely knows his stuff, and gives good feedback throughout class.

The Socratic manner in which Dirk has class discussions was definitely one of my favorite aspects of the class. It was very conducive to learning the class material, while also forcing students to defend their statements and practice critical thinking. If you get a chance to take a class with Dirk Deam you should absolutely do it; you won't regret.

This class is fantastic and has good material, the discussions of the readings are the worst part. There's so much content covered in class that you wouldn't do well if you missed. Doing the assigned readings is the most important. TA's grade quizzes and are kind of hard. It takes a lot of work but if you do it you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Showing up to class and reading the assigned chapters is necessary if you want to be successful. If you do that and make an effort to participate theres no reason not to get a good grade. Always come to class prepared with questions to help your participation grade.
Go to class and do the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dirk is by far my favorite professor I've had at ISU. You really need to get it together to pass this class. Do your reading and take notes- you'll really need them. Go to class and actually speak up, 20% of your grade depends on it. He is absolutely brilliant, just ride it out and you'll be thankful.

Professor Deam is one of the most intelligent educators I have ever taken classes with!  If you go to class, take good notes, READ THE ASSIGNED READINGS, and participate in the discussions you will do fine!  Shakes your hand at the end of the semester after you finish your final, overall a super classy man and a respected professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Deam is the most intelligent educator I have ever met.  If you take all of his classes you will have earned yourself a world class education in the art of Political Science.  His classes are not hard if you attend lecture and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Deam is hands down my favorite professor at ISU. He teaches by Socratic method, which is sometimes frustrating but really helped me prepare for law school. He also gives great advice if you're planning on going to law school. Con law is a great class. 10/10 would recommend.

excellent professor. I've taken so many classes with him. Deam has a polarizing effect though, you'll either love him or hate him. If you want to learn something and really experience what a college level course should offer you, I'd recommend anything with Deam. the only reason why people don't like his classes is because they're challenging.

He's brilliant don't get me wrong but wow is he tough. I was confused all semester long but walked out with an A. He forces participation which is scary and the readings can be a bit tough, but it's interesting to hear his stories
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I didn't like the socratic method, which involves a lot of dialog between Dr. Deam and poorly prepared, often stupid students, eating up time when he could be sharing his wisdom. I get why he does it, and he himself is great. It's amazing how super-smart professors Pol S are (Deam, Tuckness, Urbatch) when the students are mostly so dumb.

Great professor and great class.   Be prepared to read a lot in this class.  If you are not interested in putting in a lot of work do not take it.  However, if you do the readings and go to class you will finish with a good grade.

If you want to take one of the best classes ever in your life, you'll take a Dirk Deam course, no matter what your major is. If you're poly sci, any of his classes will be amazing, if not, his best course outside of poly sci is pol sci 335, the space class, its outstanding and you won't regret it.

One of the best, perhaps the best professor or teacher I have ever had in my academic career. The engineer-turned-lawyer-turned-political scientist is a wizard in the Socratic method and is extremely intelligent in all categories of politics and engineering, among many others. If you have to take any political science class, take Dirk Deam.

Dirk is by far the most inspirational professor I've ever had. He understands the idea of liberal education and embraces the socratic method. Doesn't use powerpoint, instead discusses with the students in the class and makes them figure it out. Instead of having it handed to you, you have to work for the information and figure it out for yourself.

Attendance isn't mandatory but I wouldn't have done well on tests just from the readings, I have missed a couple lectures only this semester and usually just text a classmate and ask what the assigned readings are for the next class. A LOT of reading. Just make sure it's done before tests.

This class is a discussion based class. He expects you to participate (in fact it's part of your grade) so be ready to defend your argument based on evidence from the readings. I had to study a lot, but I learned so much from this class and came out way more educated about American politics, and a better student over all.

Dirk is one clever guy. You will have to participate in class discussions, and he will tear you apart (even if you're correct). You kind of have to have some tough skin, but the guy really does care about you as a person. Really wants you to be informed. Shakes students' hands at the end of the semester... very classy.

Dirk was an amazing Professor! Make sure you believe strongly in what you are going to say as he WILL tear your response apart to make you prove your point. Adored the TA also, super helpful when he was confusing. Make sure you understand why each reading is in the lesson and you will pass.

Easily the smartest man on campus. If you don't take a class with Dirk, I feel sorry for you. All I can really say, because this man will make you think in ways you never could have even imagined. It is not going to be easy, and you will have to work, but after a few lectures, you want to do the work, simply to participate well.

This is my first semester taking one of his classes and I am definitely taking 235 next semester! Dirk is crazy smart and the class really makes you think. While attendance isn't mandatory, it's pretty much required because of class participation. Be prepared to read all the assigned material to pass. By far my favorite class this semester!

Dirk Deam is by far my favorite professor at Iowa State. As an engineering major it is refreshing to learn from an individual who is interesting and happy to show up to class. Mr. Deam loves what he teaches and make you want to learn the material. Some of the connections he makes are really cool. You'll have to work hard, but its worth it.
Take a class with Deam before you graduate, you will not regret the decision. Brilliant professor who cares about what he teaches

Best professor in the department. He can be very intimidating, but if you do the readings and come you class, you'll do fine. I loved that he used to Socratic method, it really pushed you to think, develop a position, and hold to it even as he tried to pick apart your argument. If you can write well, that will help a lot on quizzes.
Dirk is a wickedly smart individual. His class was genuinely thought provoking and interesting. I bull*hitted my way through most of the exams and never received a grade lower than 75%.

Dirk is a god. This man is way too smart for his own good but he really keeps the material interesting. At the rate I am going I will be getting my minor in Dirk Deam... his classes are that interesting. Con Law is a doozy if you hate to read but worth it if you are heading to law school. Same goes for 421.
Great class, love the proff.

Ask a POL S student about the faculty and Deam's name will come up. You need to take at least one course from him to see what you think - take 215 or 319 early on in your career to see if you want to move on to 420/421. Not as difficult as some people claim; a well-organized argument is all it takes on exams, you can go light on facts and figures.
Same readings used for most of his classes. Very abstract style that can be difficult for some students. Pay attention and take lots of notes.

I really enjoyed discussions but I am one of those people who don't like to be called out in class, so be prepared for that.  Also, do the readings and even read ahead.  ATTEND CLASS REGULARLY or you will not do well at all.

He is amazing. He really knows his stuff and the class dicussions are worth coming to even though he has a loose attendance policy. I loved this class. But beware, if you want to do well you MUST do the readings and take notes. The quizes are difficult.

Really sharp guy, definitely worth taking! He can be intimidating at first though. Be prepared to do lots of reading & take thorough notes or you will regret it at Finals! All quizzes and final are written essay style. Oral argumentation is worth 20%. He picks people randomly for this so be prepared! If you do the work you will do well and enjoy it
amazing teacher,Intimidating but teaches you so much! Love him! do the readings and go to class.

Good professor but he is VERY Intimidating! Keep up with the readings or he will chew you apart, also dont take the class if you are scared of speaking out and being shut down because he requires it for the class. But overall a very intelligent person and very interesting class if you're not too scared to show up.

Easily one of the scariest men I've ever had the HONOUR of meeting. He kept class interesting, but don't dare go on your phone or do anything he doesn't tell you to do. All in all, he is an absolute genius. I don't think I could praise him enough.

LOVE DIRK! I made the mistake of not taking his classes until my senior year- had I experienced the Dirk earlier, I would have taken him every semester. Dirk makes you think, he challenges you. I'm not a science person but love love love Space class. I can't say enough good stuff about Deam.  TAKE HIM!
Its a matter of fact that he's the best professor in the department. Challenging and well worth it.

Great professor! His use of the Socratic method will make you think more critically about the subject matter than any other political science class Iowa State offers. Having taken Deam's classes made my transition to law school much easier.

It doesn't matter what class you take with him, but you MUST take one of his classes. There aren't many professors that actually make you think. I'm always excited for what the next lecture/discussion has to bring. Do your readings and you'll be fine.

Dirk Deam is by far the best professor I've had. He is incredibly knowledgable in his field as well as everything else...he is intimidating at first because he teaches using the socratic method, but if you do the readings you'll have a really enjoyable class! Always do the readings, you learn so much more if you can offer opinions in class.

By far the greatest teacher I have ever had. Makes it so easy to get interested in Political Science. Uses the Socratic method so you must be prepared for class. His discussions are very interesting and fun. I would highly recommend his class even if its not related to your major.
genius
Wonderful professor. It's not often that you can sit and have a real conversation with a professor.

Dirk is my favorite professor I've had at ISU. You learn so much from each lecture, and they always go by fast. His tests are fine as long as you study what you talked about in class and really know the readings. He's the most intelligent man I've met, and he's so down-to-earth and thought-provoking during class.

Greatest "senior lecturer" I have ever had. You will learn lots if you go to class and know your information. It's not hard if you follow along and becomes very fun once you get into it. Also he hates being called Deam. Call him Dirk. Seriously. Don't be afraid to speak up. Even if you're right he will try to shoot you down. Stick to your guns.

I absolutely love Dirk but I would have rather taken it with someone else.  Make sure you go to class, participate and keep up on the news.  My downfall was the current event questions.  I never knew what he was looking for, so I didn't know what to remember.  Don't take his class if you get scared easily.  He loves to pick on people.

I was interested in Political Science, but it wasn't until after I took this class that really decided to make it my major. Deam is a tough grader but very smart man. I learned a lot in lecture, and honestly wish that it was a requirement to take his class before being able to vote.
Happy to say Professor Deam is also my dad.  Great professor, great dad.  Do the readings, speak up in class and you'll realize his classes prepare you for more than the final.

By far one of the best professors at ISU.  He can relate to just about whatever your major is.  Everyone should take a class with this guy.  You can't just wing the in class discussions either, you have to do the reading to even have a chance at answering this guys questions.  Do the reading, show up for class/quizes and you should be fine!

Dr Deam is hands down the best professor I've had at Iowa State, and Pol Sci 335 (space class) was the only class I've never even been tempted to skip.  Great at using the Socratic method and great at getting solid arguments from students.  Really made me see that not all lib arts classes are a waste of time and effort.
This professor makes all the money in tuition worth it!
One of the best teachers I have had at Iowa State.  His class is in no way easy but he makes it interesting and engages students well.
I wish Deam was my dad.

The messiah of all political science professors and the smartest person you'll ever meet. It takes a few weeks to learn how to do well in this class. Do the readings, speak up, and study the cases for the quizzes. The quizzes are tough, but graded fairly. A+ professor, you're not getting your money's worth if you don't take a class with him.

Awesome class! Lectures are fun. Just be prepared to defend you position. Do the readings or sparknotes them and it will help you follow along. Quizzes are hard but Final is open note, open book, and participation in class will help your grade.

Excellent teacher. Probably the smartest person I've ever met. Respects students, and their views. Not afraid to challenge students. You WILL feel like a deer in headlights when speaking in class. Don't be afraid to speak up and argue though (it's actually required, and fun). Readings are helpful. Can be very funny at times. Take him at least once!

Excellent teacher. Probably the smartest person I've ever met. Respects students, and their views. Does not shy from challenging students. You WILL feel like a deer in headlights at times in class when speaking (part of grade is for discussion). But class is very fun. You'll understand more if you keep up on your readings. take him at least once.

Probably the best professor I've ever had, although, I didn't really think so at the time. The class is challenging, but if you read, come to class, and participate it's not too bad. Do not take this class if you don't want to read. He knows his stuff and expects you to know what's in the readings. Overall not a bad class. Great professor.

Don't take this class with him if you are a conservative! He will attack your beliefs everyday.  The guy was a bit of a jerk in teaching this class. The class could definitely be taught without being a jerk. Shook everyone's hand at the end of the semester, helped me to respect him a little bit more.

Very hard class. You can study the material and get all of the points to his essays (All quizes are essay) but yet still fail the quiz. If you miss one minor point you lose 3-4 out of the 5 points possible for that problem. He's flipping crazy! He knows what he's talking about but expects too much for a low level PolSci class.

He is the best professor I've had so far and really engaged me into the world of political science. and I liked his socratic method of teaching. His class was the only class during my first semester i ever looked forward to. my advice: take good notes and pay attention! his questions are difficult but they do a good job in provoking thought. :)

Deam is a genuinely nice guy. Talks to you like an equal, and he has a great sense of humor. His test questions ARE difficult, and he does assign a lot of reading, but he is very approachable and makes class as tolerable/fun as he can given the subject matter.
Super hard......I have a 3.5 and I had to drop.

Dirk was a great teacher. I kept on hearing from people here and others that his class would be difficult, but it wasn't too bad. I tried my best and got an A in the class but then again, that's just me. You just have to show up to the class discussions and contribute once in a while. And be interested in the material.

Easily best prof I've ever had, he single-handedly inspired me to change my major to poly sci and pursue a law degree, I also had 215 and 235 with him, teaches using the Socratic method and does it well, very smart, read the material and come prepared to class, even if you don't read, bluff and argue a point like you did, you'll get the points
easily the best teacher I have had in all of my years of going to school.  you will learn even if you don't want to and he makes it fun, I would encourage everybody to take a Deam class
AMAZING, best professor i have ever had, if you have the chance take this professor.  it's definitely not easy, read, participate, and take notes and you will do great  MUST HAVE TEACHER
I love him!!!!

AMAZING teacher.  Its a tough class because you HAVE to read and participate and there are only 5 quizzes, the final, and participation as a grade.  But, Dirk is here to teach and you can tell he loves to do it.  He teachers something like 8 classes I think, so he isnt one of those professors that is here to do research and just has to teach some.

One of the best teachers within the department, if not the best. If you're a major, you should go out of your way to take his classes. If you're a nonmajor just taking 215 and lower-levels... um you'll want him too! If you want a stellar grade: Participate and read (Pretty much the same advice for every other class you'll ever take though
He's the best teacher ever.  Lectures, texts, and films are great.  He's also my dad.  He's a great dad, too.

Dirk is an amazing teacher! I had fun going to class everyday, and I would recommend him to anyone! I will say that the reading is a must. If you don't do the readings, you will be really lost. His class is all discussion, so you have to come prepared and you can say whatever you want, as long as you can back it up with good thought.
Pretty much the best professor ever! He makes class enjoyable and interesting. He's one of the smartest people I have ever met and he is an amazing speaker! Highly recommend him!

Prof. Deam is a MUST HAVE professor at ISU. He is smart, sharp and committed to very productive/efficient class time. Prof. Deam helped prepare me for success at DePaul Law School, and wrote a fine recommendation to wit. A wonderful teacher who deserves to be a Professor rather than a Lecturer.

Very intelligent.  Class scared me at first before I figured out what he was all about but its awesome!  Cares about his students.  Easy to talk to and funny.  Arguments in lecture are awesome.  Don't expect to get an easy A from him though. You will have to work your butt off, but yet it will be fun, Keep up on the readings.

wow, awesome teacher.teaches by asking questions and makes you defend those answers.makes a dry class pretty interesting. assigned seats and picks a row during class and calls on you to answer questions on the reading, READ THE READINGS!!!!if you don't, be ready to look like a idiot when u try to explain concepts out of the book. good class....

Deam's class is thoroughly enjoyable to the student who is interested in law.  Deam has a thorough understanding of the material, and though his teaching method is sometimes frustrating, you leave the class with an idea of what law school is like.  He plays favorites, but it didn't really bother me too much.
Great prof, but class takes a lot of reading. Everyone I know who has taken a Deam course has received a B in it. Also, be ready to argue! Socratic method. Good course- I learned a lot.

Be ready to argue with him, and against your own opinion if possible.  2 essay assignments/sem. 420 is more challenging than 319.  Read the cases very well. Need 2 blue books for each test. Great professor!

Dirk Deam has all the qualities of an excellent professor. He not only teaches his students the subject at hand but also introduces them to an entirely new way of absoring information. I would highly recommend any Deam class but only if you're seriously interested in the subject matter.
Honestly, an amazingly intellectual individual. Completely compelling and enthrawling. I love to hear his mind work and I'm not even a poli sci major
Was probably the smartest man I will ever encounter in my life, and he knew it.
Dirk is the only reason I made it to class when I did show up at 9AM. He's insanely intelligent, normal, and fun to listen to.
I have loved every class I have taken with him!

I really didn't like this class. I thought it was stupid to make class discussions a requirement in a lecture of 200 students.  Its awfully difficult to participate, especially if you are quiet like myself.  If it were a smaller class like 30ish students then it would've made more sensse.

Deam is one of the most intelligent profs I've ever had. His classes are dicussion, and very entertaining. Your grade is determined by three papers and one exam. You have to read one book a week. The class was interesting and I learned a lot, but it is difficult to earn a good grade. If you take the class, PARTICIPATE IN CLASS DISCUSSIONS.
His class is good if your into theoretical stuff and a "search for a deeper meaning" ..but it kinda feels pointless to go to class because he doesn't test you on anything he says in lecture.
No Comments

Can I just say...I LOVE DIRK DEAM! His classes are intense and it's hard to take notes, but you walk out of his classes 10 times smarter than when you walked in. He is one of the most brilliant men that I know and iowa State is lucky to have him.
dirk.  dirk deam.  politics.  public space.

Pros: You'll learn a lot about argumentation, law, and yourself with his Socratic dialogue of teaching. Cons: He has a TA that won't comment more than ten words on your paper, so good luck figuring out what you can improve on for next time.
it is a course that is hard to understand what is being said.

Very interesting classes, cool guy.  My favorite prof at ISU by far.  Papers are easy if you can write, which, if you are a Pol. S. major and you can't write you should be shot.  TAKE HIS CLASSES, YOU WON'T REGRET IT.
Incredibly intelligent.  Don't expect an A+, but do expect a great class that will both interest and challenge you.

GREAT teacher. Best ive had at ISU. Incredible intelligence and rhetorical skills.  If you think you know everything, he will prove in short order that you do not, and that is my favorite thing about him!

Pros: Great class, brilliant professor.  Teaches with the Socratic method, so expect to be challenged, questioned, and provoked.  With his methods, you'll learn something about the topic and about yourself.  Con: If you're an overachiever, don't expect an A-triple-plus.

One of the best classes I've taken as a political science majors, and by far my favorite professor. Incredibly helpful, always willing to meet with students and discuss anything they want. Take any class you can with him.

I go out of my way to get Deam if I can for Political Science classes, he expects a lot and you  aren't assured a good grade (though if you are trying, he notices), but you are assured of learning a lot about the topic as well as vasting improving your ability to convey thoughts and ideas to others.

Extremely good prof.  Best in the department, and I have taken almost all of them.  His classes are always my best class of the semester, and 361 will be my best class of the year.  Very informative group discussions are the keys to Deam classes.  If you take his class, be prepared to talk a bit.
Interprets everything into lawyerese... Very informative, but difficult to take notes and prepare for an exam.

This guy is the smartest teacher I've had. He cares about his students and makes the class interesting. He doesn't lecture, he debates, and it makes everything more fun. My favorite prof. I've had yet. Just go to class and come ready to think and you'll have a lot of fun.

Very smart teacher, probably my favorite at Iowa State.  I took 215 with Hutter and failed.  Took with Deam and got an A-.  Goes to show what a difference the teacher can make.  I hated Hutter and loved going to Deam's class.
I honestly think he is a genious! He is so intelligent and I truly learned a lot from him.  He rocks!!
If you have the notes from class and make him think on your essays you will be fine. A very deep thinker and very funny
Great class.
He's tough but you learn so much about Politics, Law, and how to succeed in classes. Great stories, great guy- glad he's in the dept!
Very interesting class that provokes a lot of thought. Not very hard if you pay attention to his notes. Really nice guy with a lot of knowledge about politics and law.
Challenges you to think and expand your thoughts
learn a lot but picky, tough grade
Go to class! He is so great to listen to.. but has a quiz once a week! really and interesting guy, hes done everything!
One of the best professors in the Political Science department.
No Comments
Dirk's da man!
Good professor, law background helps
No Comments

Dr. Deza was a great professor for thermo. Instead of homework, there are quizzes. These aren't bad, and honestly, it takes you the same amount of time to study for them as doing homework assignments would. She does go a bit fast in lecture, so make sure to take notes before class. Very generous grader and gives lots of partial credit
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Deza is my favorite teacher here at ISU. She is very through with her notes and in class problems. Her tests aren't the easiest but she is fair in her grading. I would have loved to take more classes with her.

Professor Deza did an amazing job conducting every lecture and ensuring every student understood the material precisely. She shows compassion for others and lets us know she cares about our overall performance. She performs the way every professor should perform: professional, understanding, helpful, and charismatic. Great professor = great class.

Dr. Deza really is a very caring and understanding person who wants to see the success of her students. Her lectures are not the greatest, learning material can be very confusing just based on slides but she goes over examples in class that make material easier to understand. She hosts her own review sessions that are AMAZING for learning material.

Had Professor Deza for ME 335 and 436. Lectures were not great, often found them hard to follow. Quizzes and exams were tough, but she is more than fair when it came to grading. Tries to understand where students messed up and give as much credit as possible. Had to use scientific calculator. Very understanding Professor, willing to work with you.

Really nice professor, willing to help you understand. No homework. Occasional extra credit given if you attend class at the right time. Go to office hours if you need help. Exam and quiz material are all covered in class but study and do practice problems.

She's one of the most caring professors I've seen. She will do anything to help you. Her office hours are great. Use them. One weekly quiz and no homework (although I would've liked homework to practice). She posts practice problems on canvas, DO THEM! They're really helpful in understanding content. Take thermo 1 with her and you won't regret it.

Having Mirka Deza for ME 160 saved my life. The horror stories that I have heard from other classes has made me very thankful that I had her. She structured her class very well and actually did a good job teaching the material. 10/10 would recommend especially for early engineers.

Professor Deza tells you exactly what you need to know to do well in her course. Lectures have both content and example problems. Posts relevant formulas and practice problems on Canvas. Hosts regular virtual review sessions for students. One quiz every week, and 4 exams.

Dr. Deza is by far the best professor you can get for thermo. She works through examples in class and always answers student questions. She will also take time out of her day to help you on understanding stuff in class, even on late weekend nights. She makes the class material seem easy even though it's a tough subject.

Professor Deza cares!! She is amazing and can't recommend her enough. She runs through examples in class that help out during tests. No homework but you have to be on top of your work and ACTUALLY read the textbook. I did not as much which is why I got a B haha. Highly endorse this teacher for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Deza is an extremely good professor to take ME 332 with. She makes the class very simple and she prepares you for exams and quizzes. There is no homework in the class, but there are weekly quizzes. She is always willing to help. If you pay attention you'll do great in the class.
Professor Deza doesn't assign HW, but gives weekly quizzes instead which motivates you to study more.

Dr. Deza was a great introduction to engineering at ISU. Super nice and knowledgeable. Took time out of her day to answer a few questions I had as well as allow me to retake a missed quiz. No final exam, project instead which was much better imo. Would highly recommend her to anyone.
Awesome prof. Her lectures are exactly what you are tested on, there was no homework, and she is willing to help you through questions. By far one of the best thermo profs at ISU.

Dr. Deza can come across as a bit intimidating at first, but shes really nice and caring. She was very responsive to emails and always did her best to help. Tests were representative of the lecture material and handout problems. You should try do the recommended practice problems before exams, they help a lot.

She comes off cold but is very nice and helpful. Weekly quizzes are easy enough if you pay attention in class and do some practice problems. She is the queen of partial credit. I learned a lot with her and put in very little work compared to the other thermo professors. Definitely would want to take another class with her.

Dr. Deza is a very caring professor. She wants students to learn and get a good grade. She is very open to feedback and giving students the best options. Exams were good representations of material learned. There is no assigned homework, but practice problems help with in class quizzes. Exams and quizzes were graded very fair.

She wants you to learn and understand thermo! She gives problems & tables from the textbook, so you don't need to buy it. Each week she provides problems to work out to prepare for the quizzes, which are HELPFUL. There's also review sessions & office hours, or she's always available. 4 tests & 7 quizzes, it's a lot of work, but ask ?'s it helps!!!!

Worst professor to take Heat Transfer with. She did a bad job documenting the lectures and only half the answers are recorded. Class such as heat transfer has lot of new concept and very detailed problems, I was really struggling with her. Also, she is a tough grader. Exams were basically something out of the examples for class. Stick to ME 170 plz

Thermo didn't come to easy to me, I got below average on exams, but still managed a B. She allows opportunities to make up points, and cares you do well. The real key is to go to the review sessions and understand all the practice problems since she didn't assign homework for us. She answers questions over email well.

Dr. Deza is an amazingly caring professor. She bent over backward multiple times for myself and other students to help us and it was very clear she wanted the best for us. She is not the greatest lecturer, but still makes the material easier to understand. I have a lot of respect for her and how she has handled the class. LOTS OF PARTIAL CREDIT!

Deza is my favorite instructor at ISU. She is an absolutely amazing teacher for ME231/332 and I highly recommend taking her for both. She is extremely caring about her students, is very straightforward with what she expects and is a fair grader. She breaks down all thermo concepts to a basic level so it's way easier to understand. Highly recommend.

She has been by far the most caring professor I have had in the engineering department. She has given us so many chances to improve our grades including letting us retake a question from the first exam, giving a few exam points back to everyone, etc. Highly recommend taking thermo with her.

Dr. Deza is a great professor that really cares about her students. There are no surprises on her exams or quizzes and they are very similar to problems done in class. If you attend class, she will give you extra credit on the exams. She truly wants to see her students succeed. If you get the chance, take thermo with Dr. Deza!
The class was extremely easy and very little work. I enjoyed the group projects though. The projects were what I would imagine thermo 3 would be like.

Struggle with Thermodynamics? Take it with this professor. She allowed retake on exam 1. Extra credit on quizzes and exams. Show up to class, she'll give you participation points. A lot of make up points. Do her suggested problems, you'll ace the quizzes. Responds to emails quick, will meet outside class. She really cares, and I learned a lot.

Deza was a pretty good teacher for ME170. She was very understanding for deadlines and listened to the class. On the other hand she was very disorganized and assignments often only up for a couple days before they were due and grading is very slow. Don't expect to know your grade and be aware of last minute changes due to disorganization.

Deza is the sweetest lady who truly wants you to succeed in engineering. She is new to teaching this class but I thought she was awesome. She understands that learning SolidWorks can be frustrating & is lenient on deadlines to allow you to learn the material. Would highly recommend doing well on group projects which account for over 1/2 your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the ME department. Made many accomodations for students with the career fair. Gave a ton of partial credit for wrong answers and gave good feedback. Gave the solutions for the exams and quizzes in class afterward to help you improve. Great in-class examples and lectures. Hard class made doable by a great professor.

Fluids is gonna be tough no matter who you have. Deza was alright, tended to do a lot of example problems in class which were useful. On the days where it was all lecture and no examples it would be really hard to follow along.

Her practice questions coming from the book that she gives are similar to the tests. She does a lot of examples that are helpful. I sometimes had a hard time understanding her accent but shes a fare grader and good teacher nonetheless
Dr. Deza is a great teacher and she will tell you exactly what will be on the exams. Take thermo with her.

I took fluids with Deza and she set up the class very well. Her lectures were normally just example problems and explaining new concepts. If you go to class, do the homework, and work through her in class examples you will be fine in this class. Her grading is fair and her tests weren't hard if you did the examples and homework.

Lectures are a bit boring at times and can initially make the material seem hard, but Deza does a great job of going through examples. If you do the recommended practice problems for each quiz and test, it's not hard to get A's.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She expected a lot from students coming in, but when the exam 1 average was below 50%, she offered a retake in order for students to actually learn the material. Very helpful during office hours. Primarily works examples during class. Does not use powerpoints or post worked out solutions, so attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very clear on what you need to know for exams. Study and you will do fine.
Awful professor, does not actually teach the class. Instead of teaching she rather just copies her notes down over and over again and considers this her "lecture." Do not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Had two classes with her this semester, taking thermo 2 with her this semester for a reason. GREAT professor! Study hard for every quiz, don't cheat off chegg, she WILL FIND YOU LOL! Practice tests are very similar to real ones, just study variations of those problems and you'll be set, besides going over old quizzes and reading lecture slides.

Quizzes every week, matlab helplabmust, if you have questions during tests and quizzes she's willing to help, ask specific questions in lecture, show up to class because she gives a few points EC on a test if people dont show up to lecture. A very good professor. Just try hard, ask questions and respect her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hard to follow along, very unclear, tough grader, the list goes on...
Good intro to engineering concepts and MATLAB programming. Requirements are clear grading is fair.
Take her for thermo. Makes it very clear what you need to know for exams.

She sucks at explaining projects and assignments so you end up getting points taken off since her TA grades them. Not an easy A if you don't know her expectations. Half the time she doesn't know how to answer your questions. She will either direct you to a tutorial on solidworks or a youtube video.

Started off rough with failed quizzes, ended the semester strong with an A. She does drop assignments and the class is fairly easy as long as you do the example problems in the book (they're very similar to her exams/quizzes). Thick accent, but easy to pick up. She does kind of jumble her words a bit though. She's also very helpful and emails back.
Very helpful, works through problems in class, and is a very easy grader. Gives lots of credit for work, and makes the subject easy to learn. Gives random extra credit for tests for attending class

has heavy accent. However, can understand pretty well. The real challenge is understanding her in a complete sentence. If you ask her for help it will be there and will be very useful. Ask for help on anything you are struggling with. There is a group project that will require a good amount of time.
Good teacher, exams are easy if you study the practice exam and your homework. Overall a good teacher

This is a hands on class. You use Solidworks and your brain daily. Missing class is a deadly mistake. Its a learning curve but things are explained well. Office hours Solidworks help is great. Usually lets class out early.

She was a bit jumbled when it came to when we did what (Engineering or programming) But she knew what she was doing. She was also helpful and emailed back quickly. She tells you exactly how to pass, and I had fun in the course. Her accent does make it tough at times, but she either writes down what she's saying or you can just ask her to repeat it.
Hard to understand. Smart but not good at teaching.

She is pretty good, can be a little boring during the statics portion....her homework is usually ungraded but I recommend you do it, and it is straight out of the book, as well it would behoove you to do some of the extra questions too because they are on the quiz.  The quizzes are all open book, but can be a bit difficult if you don't do the work.
She is a good professor, who helps the students to the best of her ability.

She was really helpful. Make sure to get help in her office hours because she tends to spill exam questions when she goes on explaining. She is also the best in teaching Matlab. If not for her I wouldn't have got an A

Extremely difficult to understand, nearly impossible when talking into the microphone. Not helpful when you ask questions. Smart, just not any good at teaching the material. You are better off reading the book than listening to her PowerPoint.

Good professor, definitely recommend taking him. He is very educated and ants his student to succeed. I had missed an exam and he allowed me to go and retake it. He knows his stuff. Would take this class again a million times.

Dr. DeLisi is a great professor and person! He is a well-known criminologist, and his expertise is obvious in his lectures. The class consists of 10 attendance checks, a bibliography, and two papers (one 7-10 pages, the other 10). Since those are the only assignments, you have plenty of time to complete them. He also gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Delisi is one of the best professors I've had at ISU! His class isn't attendance-mandatory, but I highly recommend attending the lectures and listening to him speak, because he truly is an inspiration! We only had four exams and a paper as our final, but besides that, he had no assignments or other coursework that contributed to our grade.

Matt Delisi is the best professor I have had so far. He has had firsthand experiences in the topics he teaches and is an all-around wonderful professor!! The class itself is very easy, and you get what you give to the class. The lectures are very interesting, and he makes them fun to learn about. I would recommend him and this course to anyone!!
Fantastic professor for criminal justice. Would highly recommend his class for an elective. Has engaging lectures and very knowledgeable about the field. Very interesting and kind professor.

Dr. DeLisi's class was my favorite class I've taken at ISU. His lectures were extremely entertaining, and the topics we learned about were fascinating. There were 2 assignments throughout the semester and then a final paper on your research done. Attendance was randomly taken, so make sure you're not skipping too much! Definitely a great class.

Dr. DeLisi was a fantastic professor to have. He has experience with the criminal justice system and has so many interesting stories to tell. He is a very fair grader and if you go to every lecture you will easily pass the class. No homework besides one paper that you have the entire semester to do and all 4 exams are online.

Dr. Delisi was AMAZING. His lectures are extremely interesting! He uses real life cases. He is extremely kind, caring, and an easy grader. All 4 tests are online. There is no homework all semester, other than one 6-page paper over a book he wrote, but it honestly is not hard. I highly recommend taking this class!

Dr. DeLisi is my favorite professor I have had in my whole academic career. He is a great man with awesome stories! He makes lectures entertaining, and they are worthwhile to attend. His tests are easy 100% if you go to the lectures. Four exams are worth 100 pts each, and an essay that is six pages is worth 350 pts. The paper is not hard. A++ Class

I missed a test because I misread the date and time, and he emailed me the test and let me take it whenever I felt most comfortable. He was very sweet and cared about his students getting good grades in the class. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT!!! It's an interesting paper, and it will 100% boost your grade.

He was very funny and sitting in his class felt like listening to a fun criminal justice podcast. He is very smart and includes a lot of his own personal experiences working with inmates. If you pay attention in lectures and take notes the class is a breeze. I feel like I retained a lot of vital information from this class and I would recommend it.

Literally CJ240 was the class that got me through my first semester. 10/10 prof. Really cool guy; talked about Lil Wayne and showed us pictures of the cop from paw patrol. On a serious note, he's understanding, keeps it real, and is obviously passionate and well-versed in what he teaches. I'd take him for all my classes if I could.

For his class there were two large papers, no quizzes or exams, however the papers do take a lot of time and dedication to write. He is very knowledgeable and flexible if you need to miss class, just let him know and he won't dock points.

This professor is amazing in many ways. He has very engaging lectures and topic to discuss. He is so knowledgeable about the material, and it helps that he has real life experience in criminal justice. He is very understanding is you do not do well on your exam there is a chance to retake and better your score. He wants you to succeed. He is great!
Excellent way of teaching and loves to engage with student, had him as a professor 2 times and he's the best!

Matt DeLisi is the best professor I have ever had! I WANTED to attend his classes and was sad if I missed one. He was super engaging and used tons of real-life examples. The class is super easy to understand and VERY easy to get an A in. Highly recommend!!
Matt is awesome. I was excited to come listen to his lectures. 2 papers and attendance were the only things graded, so it was very easy to do well. I learned a lot. I wish he taught more classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Top favorite professor, for my class it considered of two papers and 10 random attendance checks that's it, however his class was so interesting I didn't even mind going. His material is interesting and always prepared. Very understanding if you communicate with him. If you have the chance to take his class, do it.
No top hat, lectures were easy to follow and entertaining. He is very compassionate about how his students do.

Delisi is a great guy. He's a great at lecturing and keeps the class engaged. He's very knowledgeable about the topic and it shows. There are 4 exams to take online (not proctored) and he posts all the notes online. Attendance isn't mandatory and I didn't use the textbook once.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Make sure you attend lectures and pay attention. You will do well. Great guy.
such a fun prof, he wants you to do well, but if you're not going to class at least kinda regularly you're gonna bomb your exams and those are the only grades you get, but there was no final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher, easy tests. Straightforward notes. Lectures are fair, very respected

Has really interesting and good lectures. However he does attendance randomly ten times throughout the semester so you have to attend if you want to get a good grade. Only grades attendance, an annotated bibliography, and a final paper. Theres no tests or homework.  I never opened the textbook and still got an A.
