He does not go very in-depth on any topic. He kind of blows through things, assuming we will read the book and know the material 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is the 3rd professor you'll have in Psych 101 and by far the best. Makes boring topics seem interesting and really tries to connect with his students and make them feel confident in what they're learning about. Does an excellent job of covering everything that will be on an exam.

By far my favorite professor at ISU. He is very helpful and teaches for everyone with different learning styles. I had an 8:00 am lecture and he made it more enjoyable. I would definitely recommend him as a professor.
He gives good lectures and helps you really understand material. Gives lots of examples. Sometimes he acts a bit weird/creepy. As a person, I really don't like him. As a professor, not bad.

He is a hilarious teacher, who tries to cater to everyone's learning style. It isn't difficult to stay engaged in class and he is always doing something interesting. He tells many stories that relate to the class material,that makes the class more relatable. He is a little quirky, but he is effective in teaching and you can tell he loves to teach.
This has by far been overly complicated and not worth it for a supposedly easy class
Hilarious professor, really engages the class.
Great lecturer!! He makes the course interesting. Make sure you don't miss any homework; he refused to give me an extension for an assignment that I missed..

No one else can engage a 300-person lecture like he can. With his brilliance, hilarious quirks, and clear delivery, he will spark your interest in the subject matter. His teaching style made a profound difference in my willingness to learn and succeed in the class. You will be privileged to have him as a professor.

Dr. Gentile is a little weird, a pretty good professor overall though. Tries to make class interesting. Easy to understand. Test is pretty hard, and there is a lot of reading. It's important to go to class and read the book in order to do well. Do the extra credit, it'll help your grade a lot.
Words cannot describe how awesome this guy is. He the BEST teach I have EVER had....seriously. He finds a way to keep everyone listening. Exactly what you hope to have as a professor and person.

Intelligent and funny prof. He is excellent at the art of teaching. Fantastic, balanced lecture. He is the most difficult of the three professors you have in this course, but also the best. If you don't study well, he will make you want to learn how.
I hated psychology until I had Dr. Gentile, he clearly enjoys teaching and is very good at it. His class isn't easy, but if you pay attention and class and study for the tests you should be fine.

He presented a lot of very interesting information, and in a very engaging way - especially considering the size of the class.  I also have friends who have taken other courses from him, and they love him as well.

Dr. Gentile was the best teacher for Psych 101. He simply is a really funny guy, but he's intelligent like none other! Reading the text and attending lecture is GREATLY suggested. Uses great examples in lecture!
Awesome Teacher! His classes were interesting and kept my ears open. The videos were refreshing and he made the whole class laugh multiple times. This is a professor I would take again!

This prof is frickin HILARIOUS! So good at what he does that I look forward going to class every Tuesday and Thursday. He uses all ways to learn the material and he throws in hilarious gags and twists. So hysterical and brilliant!

Dr. Gentile was a phenomenal teacher. He is the first teacher I've ever had that attempted to appeal to ALL different styles of learning. He made the material so easy to understand that I barely had to study for his test. Absolutely awesome guy, VERY interesting way of teaching

great professor. even though it was hard to make myself go to class at 8:00 a.m., the classes i did make it to Dr. Gentile kept me awake and interested. the test isn't too bad, just make sure to take notes during class. he is a good teacher and uses lots of vidoes to mix it up
Very engaging and humorous, though a handful of comments on sensitive topics were unintentionally harsh. Take good notes and read the book, and the class is pretty easy.

he is a super energetic fun and crazy professor. he keeps lecture really entertaining which is nice at 8am! has a little bit of something for everyone! go to class, you get a lot out of his lectures! fun class and professor!
- this guy was GREAT i was iffy about being a psych major until i had the second section of my psych 101 class with this guy..he really jump started me back into it!!
A Very Good Teacher, He kept me interested the whole way through!

Very good teacher. I did not enjoy the first part of Psych and had trouble on the test becasue of the methods. Professor Gentile made class fun and helped change my methods of studying and i managed to do way better on the test. GREAT teacher
Played a lot of video clips which keep the audience interested instead of just lecturing the whole time.

Dr. Gentile is nuts (but in a good way). He's zany and rather protean with what he does during lectures, but it's entirely interesting--demonstrations, videos, examples, and he dances around. He does dwell on hating creationism, though. Just go to class and dabble in the books and you shouldn't get below a 90% even before the curve takes effect.

I don't know what people are talking about when they mention his "hard" tests.  Going to class is extremely helpful.  You can do that in place of the book as most of the testing info comes from class.  He has great examples and seems very involved with and interested in this class.
Made class interesting, but exams were harder than ever.  For an introductory class exams are very hard.  I took 200 level classes that were easier.  Great professor, but made exam a nightmare
Good visuals & examples
He is a funny guy. He makes a lot of jokes; he is more interesting than the other professors. He likes to show video clips.

One of my favorite Profs. I found most of Psych 101 dull and the temptation of skipping usually won over, but I didn't skip a single on of his lectures. He is actually the reason I decided to stick with Psych (and I love it).

He's very funny. I liked this pof but for any1 who is planning to take psych 101 i advice them to think more about it!  its not easy to get more than B in this class that's if u did ur best.  I already passed econ 101 / 102 with A but I passed psych 101 with C & 4 teachers would teach u psych 101  there's like 2 other teachers really boring!
Great teacher. Knew material well, and was able to present it in a way that was easy to understand.
Great professor, very interesting material. Best of the four teachers for this class. Exams are easy if you put the time into study and take the online quizzes.
I liked how he used all of the different learning styles. He is a very nice guy. AND he's got a sense of humor...I wish he wasn't married ;)
Dr. Gentile was an awesome teacher and made the class fun!
He is very helpful if you have any questions. Makes the class interesting by involving the students with music, video, and demonstrations. Nice guy.

He was by far the best teacher teaching this class.  He actually made the class fun, unlike Dark, who is super boring.  I liked that we watched movies, then you can actually see what hes talking about, and im not just saying this cause I know he reads these..
I actually like going to class. Interesting and funny teacher.
very helpful!
He made this class worthwhile to go to.  His lectures were easy to follow, and made the class fun!
The class in general sucks, but he's the best of the three I've had so far. He makes the class fun!
Pretty cool teacher...he shows movies a lot which are WAY more interesting than other prof teaching technices...
very good teaching techniques but honestly, pepsi and coke taste exactly the same
He is interesting and makes class fun, but he is weird, im glad im not his kid, takes his job seriously, pepsi is so much better, i like how he adapts to everyones learning style, its nice.
pretty much rocks :)
Made class interesting.  I felt like I knew the material really well for the test.  But make sure you study his teaching may create a false sense of security.
professor gentile is my favorite professor by far.  he made class very interesting and i actually liked going.
He made class interesting! I wouldn't go so far as to say he's hot but he's not bad looking.
r u crazy??? he's not hot at all.. :(
Very interesting lectures! (Finally, a lecture worth going to.) Make sure to read, though. The exam's a doozy.
the most awesome teacher EVER!!!
Really hot! He could make any topic interesting.
Take psych491 you get more out of it then most classes. And Gentiles lab just rocks.
HOT!!! (and a good teacher)
No Comments
No Comments

Disrespectful. I was late twice and missed class once but followed all the rules with my group members to stay in the loop but still gave me attitude when I was late the second time all semester. Grades things late and doesn't give any constructive criticism, literally one the feedbacks was “this DEFINITELY NOT enough to fill 2 minutes” like what
Professor Dukes is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING! Lectures are very engaging. She is very passionate about what she teaches and is always willing to answer any questions throughout the semester.

Co taught with Smiley, never could agree on anything wasting our project work time. When we asked for suggestions on our project, she just took points off and didn't explain anything. Only reason she didn't get a 1 is because it's an introduction class.
Tries to threaten students out of taking the online course by making them fear the class. Flags assignments as AI even if the assignment has 0 usage of it.
Very fair and honest grading. If you go to the lecture you will thrive in this class.
Amazing love her

The class has good content and is easy to understand. The professor was very kind and gave great examples of the content in class. The exams are online, and you can take them within a one-week period. Homework once a week. Recommend this class and professor overall.

Dukes was fine. Exams were all online and very easy. Attendance is not required but I would go to class and listen because most test questions were straight from lecture. You really do not need to study, if you do not know a test answer they are easy to look up. A little homework was given but not much at all.
Prof Dukes is super nice, unlike her associate professor. She is a more approachable person and will answer your questions. Attendance is mandatory, and you will fail if you don't attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dukes co-teaches this course with Dr. Smiley. This class is a combo of guest lectures and a big group project. You must attend class because attendance is graded even though the class is only offered at 8 am. Many little assignments lead up to the course project, so stay on top of those. Also, you read a lot of research articles for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you can avoid taking this class online, do so. Dukes is an okay lecturer but easy to zone out or skip if taking online. Generally, if you complete the assignments, you get full points, but you must watch the lectures to know when assignments are due because not everything is in the syllabus. You must keep up on the Canvas page for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lisa Dukes is an okay professor. She makes lecture fun by occasionally throwing in a game for the class. She also had a webbex where you can watch the lectures. I ended up not going into class half the time and watching the lectures instead. Tests are the hardest part but they aren't bad. she grades easy on papers/projects

Shes a really nice lady and gives really good and engaging lectures. She doesnt give you a lot of homework so you have to read the book! The tests should be kind of common sense, but what she lectures about isnt usually on the test. She also has random assignments that are in class only so its best to come to every class.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mostly reading articles/taking quizzes.  Careful reading and comprehension useful for getting good grades.  Teacher is quick to respond to emails.  She gives extra credit when you complete class review.  Most of material covered gets students excited for more kinesiology!  Teacher open to questions and wants to help.

Very easy class, most of the stuff was common sense from a high school health class. If you go to lecture every day you won't really need to study. She takes attendance every day but only sometimes she assigns a journal or couple points. Definitely a freshman class.
Take a course with Durbin and you will miss the days you were taking statics at ISU. Do everything in your power to avoid this professor.

Tough to know what to expect on exams. 20 minutes on an exam is not long enough. No partial credit given. "Partial credit would be unfair to the students" Prof. Durbin. No review or studyguide available before test. Felt like I had to teach myself because teacher wasn't supporting students' learning.

Tough course structure. Exams are single chained problems with limited time, so small errors can affect the entire result. Grading focuses on final answers, making it hard to demonstrate understanding. Communication and clarity on expectations requires enormous improvement. Be prepared to rely heavily on the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are not good and it's hard to figure out what we should expect on the exams since he does no form of review. Missing one class has the same penalty as not doing a week of homework. Everything is based off of coded calculators that you just need to figure out on your own. Overall not a good experience. Take this with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Learned more from the TA teaching for 3 days than the entire semester with Durbin. Not sure why he is a professor.

He does not give you notes. No partial credit on exams. Only one question exams with multiple parts. Exams are 20 minutes. Bad teacher overall. missing a class takes 1% from your total grade. No office hours. He is only teaching because he has to. Lectures teach you nothing. Take class from someone else. Exam 1 average of 40%, and most got a zero.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unlogical and unreasonable grading ideology (attendance is 1% per class, can only negatively impact you, Final is ~50% of your grade, says partial credit is 'unfair' to others). Rambles through his unclear and inefficient notes, and seems to be almost perpetually confused. A nice man overall, but not one who should be teaching a high-level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every lecture sounds like the first one he's ever given, he didn't post any notes for the first 3/4 of the semester, he 'doesn't believe in' partial credit on exams, he exploited a loophole in university policy to avoid giving back graded exam papers and the final was worth 48% of your final grade. 350 characters is not enough to describe him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor does little to actually explain concepts and only talks about his “code” which is fine if he'd actually show you how to make sure it's correct. He also does little to explain the logic behind topics and instead throws equations at you.

He lectures well, but mumbles a bit. Homework is doable but not easy, and graded essentially on completion, which I found helpful. Exams were the vast majority of the overall grade. Exams were tough, but not impossible if you put effort into studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He sounds like he is talking to himself. His notes are written just to remind himself what to teach. Just scrolls through the notes and ocassionally writes equations on the screen. Very egotistical- he stopped posting notes because some students did not show up in his lectures. Homework are equivalent to 3 courses. Exams are super hard.

Paul Durbin is extremely knowledgeable on the topic of compressible fluid dynamics. Unlike many engineering professors, he is humble and quick to acknowledge his mistakes. Dr. Paul Durbin is very fair paced individual when it comes to his lectures. Attending his lectures and paying attention will greatly improve your experience in AERE 311.

The midterms were the last 20 minutes of lecture and they were on a projector. Each exam was 13% of your grade and the final was 48%. Each HW was work 1%. Lectures were helpful, but he is a soft spoken professor. Deferred to TA and avoided talking with students at all costs. The average on one exam was like a 3.7/13. Stay on top of this class!
He is very knowledgeable. But most of the time I didn't really understand his class. His assignments were hard and only worth 40% but probably took up lots of your time

Wasn't clear with teaching. Sporadic and hard to follow sometimes. The solutions given with McGraw Hill Connect weren't the methods he wanted you to use. Stated that if you used that method (using tables instead of equations) you would be cheating on exam. Waited til the day grades were due to curve and made a 55 a B-.
The class was confused. Homework was out of two points. The final was 50% of the grade. This one hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No partial credit, even for questions that were worth 8% of our final grade. Impossible to understand during lecture. Was accessible outside of class and did respond well to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I went to every class did every homework and had a great experience. As long as you never miss a lecture, your notes will ALWAYS tell you how to do the homework. I spent just a few hours the night before the midterm reviewing every homework problem and earned 100%. Only mistake:didn't study thin airfoil theory enough before the final to keep my A+.

Terrible lecturer. Mumbles quietly and occasionally laughs at his own jokes. He's obviously brilliant and sometimes you'll get a gem of understanding from him but not often. Read the text and be able to do all the hw backwards and forwards without your notes. Very difficult midterm and more difficult final.

Very hard to understand in class. Speaks VERY quiet and relies on a crappy microphone to make his mumblings louder. Seems intimidated by the students because he never makes eye contact and talks like he's really nervous. Not very enthusiastic. I came in for extra help a couple times. He helped some, but made me feel incompetent in the process.
Gave hard tests,
Amazing professor, easy course.

One of the best professors in the statistics department. Incredibly helpful office hours and fast email responses about the homework, and this course is extremely important for learning and using R for real-world applications. If possible, choose this professor every time.

I actually took STAT 330 but that wasn't listed as an option.
Anyway, Somak was one of the best professors I've ever had. Fun and down to earth, but stuck to the relevant topics. I learned so much in this class. I hope he keeps up the great work!

He is the best professor I have seen at Iowa State University. Never seen someone so passionate about teaching. He loves to teach and help each and every student outside the class. The materials are so organized that you won't have to look for anything else.

Dr. Duwe is a decent lecturer, but the project policies in this class are a nightmare. Project grades rely too heavily on reports rather than whether your code actually works. If your partner drops the class, you are forced to finish a pipelined processor solo. The course asks for feedback often, but nothing ever seems to change.

Took Duwe for 381. He's a nice guy. Super smart and clearly passionate about computers. This is by far the hardest course I have taken at Iowa State. You will work very hard in this course, but he is generous with grading.

This class takes a lot of time, however, it is very rewarding. Duwe is very generous with assignment/lab due dates which I really appreciated for this class. I had to spend a large part of my Thanksgiving break working on the labs. This class covers a LOT and I think that Duwe does a good job at getting through everything, even though it is a lot.

Dr. Duwe is a very competent invididual who knows everything he talks about, or lets you know if he's not confident in his answers. His courses are extremely hard but rich and can push people to a breaking point on completing all provided content in full, but his courses are curved hard and do not punish people for taking a risk in a hard course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Hands down the hardest class I've taken at Iowa State. Duwe is a really cool guy though. While I do think the course could use some changes (specifically more TAs and better exam prep), you can tell he's really passionate about the material. I wish more professors were as lenient and charismatic.

Really neat class. Professor Duwe has been one of the best professors I've had at Iowa State. This class was a lot to digest, but Duwe is incredibly helpful and wants to see his students succeed. Course content moved quickly, and the assignments/labs were sometimes slow to digest, but Duwe is great at listening to how students handle the content.
A professor who clearly knows his subject well and loves to teach it, very good at answering questions and humorous to top it off.

He definitely cares about helping students learn, but it feels like the stuff he teaches in class isn't what he grades on. Unless you're one of those people who have no life and are not involved in anything outside of their major, you will do poorly in this class. I will say, it feels like he would be a good professor for advanced classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, 482x was very lecture heavy however, and the lectures were very dense. Often felt like the lecture was just an hour and a half of information spewed at you. Would still recommend, interesting class, very knowledgeable, helpful and kind professor.

I'm a straight-A student, but extremely frustrated with the nature of the lectures. He drops us into a new programming language (VHDL, here's a VHDL manual)... You would expect him to teach us how this language works, but instead he tells us that he's hidden bugs inside of his lab assignment and that we get to find them! Hope semester gets better.

Reading research papers may seem intuitive but receiving feedback on your evaluation of a research paper (like you do in this course) will help shape your research skills.  The homeworks and exams are challenging but doable and you will learn a lot.

Professor Duwe provides a conducive environment for learning about machine learning hardware.  He works very hard and cares about your experience.  His assignments are challenging but doable and he grades fairly.

Duwe is a great teacher to work with as long as you put in a LOT of effort for 381. The 381 class itself is broken, there is so much material to learn it makes it one of the most difficult classes I've ever taken. Prepare to spend all of your time on homework and in lab, I suggest you take a light semester load. Great teacher, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: A lot of people don't like him because of the difficult exams and content he teaches. Despite the long hours you'll spend in lab and studying for exams, it feels very rewarding. He cares about all his students, and is more than willing to help you out if ask him for it. His stuff seems challenging, but it's mostly just shock factor in my opinion.

Duwe is the best Prof I've had at ISU. He's passionate, gives great lectures, is accessible outside of class and cares enough to learn every students name in a class of 70+. The amount of work in this class is VERY high. If you are looking to learn and fully understand a subject, he's perfect. Not an easy A, though.

The lab in this class is absolutely ridiculous. Each week we're told by Henry Duwe that "Hey guys, this lab will take a lot of time, so be prepared!", but he does nothing at all to help prepare us for this "long" lab. "A lot of time" does not even begin to cut it. It's as if he thinks we are only taking his class this semester. Avoid this man!

Professor Duwe was willing to meet on my schedule whenever I was unable to meet during his regular office hours. He was really good at going over complex material 1 on 1 and in lecture. On top of this he was a super personable guy that was more than willing to share some tips and tricks for succeeding in the field of Computer/Software Engineering.

He was hands-down the best professor I've had. I have yet to meet a professor as personable as him. Contrary to most, he genuinely cares about his students and wants them to learn the material. Seriously, go to every lecture, put in the work, and you will succeed in this class. Visit during office hours and he will thoroughly help w/ the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Duwe did a real good job of building off of student feedback to make the class more informative. His ability for allowing regrades was very nice. The class is very heavy though, so be prepared to show up and pay attention to his lectures. All the lectures are required, in class assessments every day. Very applicable to modern day life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It is literally impossible to receive 100 on a homework unless it is a pass fail assignment. Assigns over break and expects an incredibly large amount of time out of class would highly recommend you take this course with electives instead of other core or else you will have a very hard time. My opinion drop unless you're only taking 12 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I'll preface this with the class has yet to conclude. Unless there are severe curves taking a class with him is signing up for failure he enjoys creating a classroom where only for those who excel. Not a very good lecturer and treats a class where only one person responds to his questions as understanding. AVOID THIS MAN
Has attendance quizzes, but gives the answers to the students that are in lecture. Very easy to meet with him outside of class. Group Project (2 students per group).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: As it has been noted, it was his first semester teaching so there were definitely some issues. His lectures are not the best, but he cares about student feedback and changes his style accordingly. Additionally, if you have an issue with a TA or come talk to him outside of class is very nice and will work with you. However, the class is ROUGH.

Duwe's a really fair grader and tester and does his best to respond to student feedback and make the class manageable. You need to put a lot of work into this class, but it was never unfair. He and the TAs are really helpful. There are practice tests available for everything but the final. The final project is no joke and can hit your grade hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Cool guy, however, his lectures are basically the exact same thing (word for word some days) as the reading in the book. The tests are brutal though, the topics and questions are fair but there is too much to do in 50 minutes. This class would have been much better if the tests were night exams and lasted for 2 hours
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very long exams; not enough time to finish. Won't explain a simple question because he believes that "students should teach themselves". In class is like skydiving and that bird you just saw fly past you was the information you needed to know. Lecture slides aren't labeled by subject and are up to 150 slides long so google before wasting you time.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Kevin in Pricipes of Horticulture as a lab instructor. He has no idea what he's doing. Overall I'm sure he's a really nice dude, but it so bad at teaching. He always had some sort of conflict with our lab time and cut it to an hour or less, which is fine but we felt rushed and never knew the purpose of our work. Try to avoid him at all costs

Professor Deurfeldt was a good professor for globe 211. Lectures sometimes were random, and was not very organized, but were very easy. Lots of guest speakers for this class. There is a large paper that is done over the course of the semester, but if you know how to write a paper it is really easy. I would recommend him!

Kevin was a great professor and cares about his students. It is never his intention to give students a heavy workload or a hard time. He provides resources and his own time to see his students succeed. I can't see any reason why anyone would fail this class.
Kevin is super kind and loves what he does. Would totally recommend him.
Very easy, doesn't really know what he's doing, easy grader.

Dustin did a fairly good job teaching this class, especially considering it was his first time teaching when I took the course. On the positive side, we were allowed a note sheet for exams, one exam score was dropped, and extra credit was offered. 

If you put in the effort to understand the material, you should do fine. If not…it might be rough.

Although this class wasn't the easiest, Dustin tried to give us as many resources as possible to do well. He sometimes uses words that may be too academic or advanced for his students, and not all of the material he presents is useful. I wish he had spent more time going through the process of each reaction we had to learn. Not the worst professor!
Great guy. Made a very tough class interesting. Wish him the best in the future.

I had this professor during his first semester of teaching this course, and overall he did an amazing job with the course!  His practice exam exams were incredibly helpful! He really wants you to succeed in the course the office hours were helpful. I encourage to take it with him. I got a A with not going to lecture a lot (not the case for others).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dustin clearly cares about his student's success in his class. He is always willing to help clarify concepts or adjust the course as the semester goes on to help the class succeed. Great experience. Would take again.

Lectures are very much powerpoint heavy and the class is mainly based on pattern recognition. He allows double sided note sheet on exams and lots of review resources for exams. 5% extra credit was given. Most patient professor ever, even with dumb questions. Overall, he is not trying to screw you over and he wants you to do well. Highly recommend.
He posts exam reviews which is everything that will be on the exam. The first homework assignment is time consuming. Group projects are graded and not given feedback which can make it difficult.

Chuck makes FIN 301 pretty simple: show up to class and pay attention to the lecture (take notes during the example problems, as they are very similar to the HW and test questions) and you'll be fine. 301 only is graded by 4 HW assignments and 4 tests so it is imperative to do well on all of these in order to do well in the class. Not much elsetoit
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Duong is a good guy the only critique I have is he speeds through the lectures so fast it was hard to keep up. Thankfully this class is more based on group work. Half the days are saved for briefings or presentations.

Professor Duong is a great professor that gives you a good foundation to learn more advanced courses in Finance, however you must attend his lectures to pass otherwise you won't. Some details about the topics or answers to his examples will not be available in his slides on Canvas. He doesn't bog you down with homework, only 4 pieces of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Duong is very kind & wants to help his students. The class itself was boring because it was lecture-heavy. Beware that the only things you're graded on are 4 homeworks and 4 exams, so it's not very much work but the pressure is high for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Duong as an instructor even though I struggled a bit. He wasn't great with explaining things super clearly in class, so I recommend going to his office hours early on.

Truong is a decent professor, but the material and lectures were sooo dry. The group projects and investing were really fun, but that was because of the fun students in the class. The tests are completely short answers, but if you study they aren't bad and he gives you an idea of what the questions will be.

There were only 4 homework assignments and 4 exams, so it is not a lot to be graded, but the class is extremely curved. Professor Duong is one of the most caring professors I have had at Iowa State, and I would love to take another class with him. He answers emails quickly and will set up time outside of his office hours to meet. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice thing about the class is that he drops the lowest homework and exam score. The tests are a bit difficult without preparation. It is absolutely necessary to attend each lecture. Overall a good professor. Easy to understand and he shows his steps clearly.

Finance 301 is a difficult subject, but Chuck lays it out very concise and clear. If you pay attention in class and attempt the examples he does, you will set yourself up well. Make sure to take the homework as seriously as the tests because there aren't many points available. Overall one of my favorite teachers I've had at Iowa State so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chuck cares about his students. His handwriting is easy to read and he is easy to understand. Only having 4 assignments and 4 exams is nice, but be sure to prepare appropriately for them. Exam problems are exactly what he goes over in class + deeper conceptual questions. The math, for the most part, is simply using the formulas.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was taught in a way that clearly made sense, where as learning from the book was almost impossible. Graded on 4 HW's and 4 Exams, very generous grading scale. Attendance is a must though, as he does not provide the answers/solutions to the examples in his slides, so you must attend class in order to get the answers. TAKE NOTES!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Truong is very helpful whenever you have questions. I met with him several times outside of class to go over homeworks etc. sitting towards the front is beneficial as he tends to write small on some things. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is extremely hard. It is almost impossible unless you attend every lecture and you have to study hard to do well on the exams. However, Truong explains things well and tells you exactly what to look for on the exams. Most math questions on exams come straight from the homework. Only graded on 4 exams & homeworks w/ a curve. Get a Chegg
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Finance is overall a hard subject but the professor is terrible at explaining things. He is also one of the most inconsiderate instructors I had. I was extremely sick during the semester and he did not care. Overall class average for the tests is 63-70% so that says a lot....

Solid teacher. Finance is hard, but the grades are completely curved. Thought I was going to get a D, but ended up getting a C+. His explanations for concepts are sometimes confusing, as he will explain things assuming you already know one thing or another, but he is very willing to help if you're struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult. He is hard to understand and speaks very quietly and writes on a black board. If you don't sit in the front 4 rows you won't hear or see anything. The exams are worth 75% of your grade and there are 4 written homework assignments out of the textbook.

The tests are pretty much exactly the same as the homework and class examples and during the exam review he will tell you exactly what you need to study for. The homework is not too bad, but make sure you get all the points here, all homework's equal one test, so easy points!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Get a financial calculator. Only 4 tests graded and 4 homework graded. Can be difficult to understand but he shows how to do the work so you can understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I think all professors that teach FIN 301 get a reputation for being tough because this class is tough in general. Professor Duong is a very helpful professor thatll go through what you missed on your homework assignments and exams to help you understand the material. He also gives you all the information you need to know for your exams.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher and explains things quite well. The class is extremely difficult and would recommend everyone taking to be prepared. The tests are 25 questions and there are 4 of them. The test are quite difficult. Homework is all on Chegg, so get 100% on all of the hw because together, all the homework equal one test

He means well, but the class is very difficult especially if you know nothing about finance. You need the book because all homework questions are from the book but all answers are on Chegg (God bless). There's a big curve but that doesn't make it any easier. Go to class or you won't have any idea how to work the problems. Doesn't post online.

The class is super lecture heavy.  While he explains the formulas that are used, he utterly fails to explain what you are doing in terms that an individual with little to no knowledge of finance will understand.  Over the entire course, you are graded on only four homework assignments and four tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Duong is a nice guy, and his intentions are good, but the class is very lecture heavy. He teaches you the formulas needed, but doesn't really explain why you're doing it. It's very difficult to understand what he's trying to say (at least if you're not well-versed in finance), and tests aren't easy.  There was a curve at the end that saved me.

You have to buy the book to complete the assignments. Sometimes he was a little difficult to understand because of his accent, but he had very good examples and always made sure to ask if the class understood the material before moving on. No attendance points, class grade is based on 4 assignments and 4 tests.

He does a lot of examples in class that are very helpful for the exams and all of the homework answers are on Chegg . He also tells you all of the topics that are going to be on the exams so you can study the correct material. Overall he is easy to understand you just need to go to class to see the example solutions.
His FIN301 class is the most difficult class among other professors. If you want to get an A, refresh the class registration page again and again.

This class is tough no matter who you take it with. After hearing from other students it sounds as if he is one of the better ones to take Finance 301 with. He goes very fast during lectures, but tries to get students to understand.   Grade is based off  of 4 test and 4 homework assignments.  He does have a nice cure built into his grading system

Let's face it, FIN 301 is a very difficult class. Truong tries his best, but is often very confusing. He'll help you if you go to his office though. Sit up front, take good notes, and get a financial calculator. 4 homework assignments, 4 noncumulative tests, no project.

It's simple, if you do not attend class, actively participate in class and do not do the required homework... you will NOT pass. The entire class average on tests was 60%. Advice: purchase your financial calculator before or within the first two weeks of the semester or plan to play catch-up all semester long. Textbook required for homework.

He is very hard to understand and he writes a lot so you need to be able to copy everything that he writes on the board. His tests are hard and he does not give review that corresponds with the test. By far one of my hardest classes.

Overall the professor isn't terrible but the structure of the class is setup for failure. There are 4 tests that are worth a combined 90% of your grade, the other 10% being HW. What is taught in class and the in class examples he gives are very easy, then the questions on the test are very difficult and nothing like what was taught.

Professor Johnson is a rare gem that you cannot find quite often in the engineering school. He is very knowledgeable and willing to get engaged in discussing various topics that goes beyond the class content. He is fun to talk to and very engaging. 

P.S. I warn you, if you have not learned the prerequisite thoroughly be ready for a tough ride.

Does not explain concepts well and expects everyone to have had the exact same experience as him. Usually teaches engineering courses from a physicist's perspective when students haven't been trained in that manner. Frequently gets frustrated that when students are confused by how he explains something and they ask for clarification.

Worst professor I have ever had the misfortune of taking a class with. Has no understanding of how to teach concepts instead of just glazing over them because he knows them so well. Is also frequently rude and hard to communicate with.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very scattered, poor lecturer. He is too smart to teach an intro class for materials. Always talks about his achievements in class and diverges from the lesson plan often. Very hard exams, need to study very hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my scm 3010 class with Michael Dwyer. He has lots of great stories and experience. He definitely cares about his students and engages with the class, however attendance and attention in every class is required if you want a good grade.

He was not a very good teacher. The slides he talks over all class are about useless, and the information on the slides don't help with the exams making it feel useless to be there. Literally just read the book instead. He seems like a nice guy, but the teaching is dreadful and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lowkey a strange guy but like chill overall

Michael is pretty energetic, but it felt like he would rant to the class rather than actually teach the information, which made it hard to learn. There are 3 exams total. Every week there is a 10 question quiz on canvas  regarding the upcoming chapter. Occasionally there will be additional assignments. Uses top hat so showing up is important.

His classes were very important to attend. Even though I never really understood what he was saying conceptually, once he did and example for the class it made sense. Super good at answering questions and office hours helped a lot with him. Overall, I liked him, however classes could be seen as boring.

I enjoyed Fillmore as a lecturer for linear algebra. It's a tough class, can often be more conceptual than calc and problems require a lot of time and a lot of memory as to how to do them. Also harder if you haven't taken DiffEq. It's clear Fillmore is super knowledgeable in his field, nobody was ever able to ask a question that he couldn't answer.

Lectures are fast paced as there is a lot of material to cover but the material is way easier to learn and understand. He will do multiple example problems per topic. Makes sure everyone is following. Will stop and answer questions clearly. Complete topic reviews for exams. No butler videos, go to class! Practice exams are Qs from book and are good
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy was so boring and you could tell what he was saying did't even make sense to him. Was so unconfident and not helpful at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worthless study guides. Lectures with almost no examples that he does in sometimes under 30 mins for a whole chapter. and just overall poor teaching. He seems like a nice guy but he shouldn't be a teacher. He's confusing and has made me think about turning away from STEMs entirely. for the first time in life I dislike math as a whole.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The subject of Calculus is not easy, however it is also not extremely difficult. Plenty of people on YouTube teach calculus flawlessly, and make it much easier. However Dylan Fillmore is the exact opposite of that. This class is full of extremely fast note taking, homework assigned days before the due date, and completely useless study guides.

Odds are, if you're taking one of his classes, you have to take all of them, but once you've taken one, you've taken them all. His lectures are pretty dry, and he uses the same family of textbooks (Norton Anthologies) for all of those classes. The formatting, assignments, and grading criteria are nearly identical across the board. Defines average.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not much to say. It was a very boring class. I took it online and probably would have passed with an A had I remembered to do all the homework

ENGL 250 is a course no instructor wants to teach. It's boring, class sizes are huge, and the expected output is just not the same as what you'll be doing as a senior. Dr. Eason seemed to make an effort to care about it, though, and chose a text that fit extremely well with my learning community. Very lenient with grading, and charismatic too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed taking his class. He's very reasonable and gets on your level. He does take attendance but you're going to want to go because most of what is discusses in class is what will be on the exam. One group presentation and one paper during the whole semester. Very easy to get a good grade as long as you show up and study before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is both laid-back and eager to argue with you. This class will give you the think-space you need as an English major, and will still be generally interesting if you aren't.

Genuinely cares about each of his students. Always pauses lectures to make sure students are understanding the material. He will never give you unnecessary readings outside of class; they will all be discussed. I took this class only because Eason was the professor and his classes are so engaging and interesting. He is the best prof in the ENGL dep

He clearly cares that students understand the material, not that they can regurgitate it onto a test/essay. Show up, make an occasional comment, and do the work and you will get a good grade in his classes.

There is a ton of reading for this class! and participation is huge for him. He's super smart and knows the content well. There is the occasional pop quiz. His class is only 100 points, so each point is crucial to your grade. He is really funny and super cute though!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Eason is a fair grader and is very dedicated to his students. His lectures weren't too heavy and he gave my class plenty of time to ask questions and take notes during class time. He also usually utilized group discussion time, so I suggest always doing the readings - they are manageable and he appreciated our contributing to discussion.

I've found him as a very fair, relatively easy grader. I took an Ag English class on accident and he has somehow made it interesting. Stay off your phones and he will be pleasant. I only bought 1 of the 3 required books and I did just fine in the class. No pop quizzes, at least not in the 250 section. Overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Eason made the class so much more enjoyable.  He makes the criteria of each assignment clear in class and he's really nice.  The best way to succeed is to go to his office hours.  He gives really good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Eason is one of my favorite teachers of all time. He makes his class interesting, and makes it clear on what he is looking for in his assignments. He offered to help anyone figure out their learning style at the start of the semester, which helped me tremendously as a freshman. He can be a tough grader, but his office hours are very helpful!

I'm an English major, and this has been the best literature class I have taken. I learned so much in this class and I loved how organized and helpful Dr. Eason is. He made the class fun. Also, the red pepper up there ain't no joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is an easy class, but you have to read or else all the pop quizes will add up.  If you study then the exams are super easy. Enjoyed the literature, but a lot of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: First off, Prof. Eason looks like a young Ethan Hawke, he's incredibly handsome All right, he's a good teacher and offers extra credit throughout the semester to help you improve your grade. The course overall is just bleh and it wasn't designed by him. That being said, he is a rather tough grader. Make use of his office hours for help on papers!

Very poor instructor. She rarely provides helpful feedback & brings her bias and drama to class, intending to indoctrinate her students. Her grading is inconsistent. It seemed like she was more interested in making things difficult than actually helping students learn. Wouldn't recommend her class to anyone.

Not a fan. Said she was going to grade one way and she graded the complete opposite. Followed all the rubrics to a T and never got the grade I wanted. Resulted in going to have a essay tutor help me and still didn't get the grade I wanted. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very disorganized, unclear and unfair grading when compared to grading rubrics, did not give grades according to the points she gave to students. STAY AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She was really disorganized and always had different due dates listed for each assignment. It was hard to communicate with her and she never answers her emails. Strongly do not recommend her.
Love love love him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: First of all, I can tell Dzekoe has a good heart. However, sometimes he is mean.  He prohibits 101c students from speaking their native language. It is ok to advise us to speak English in class, it is not ok to point fingers and order us only to speak English. It didn't happen to me, but as an immigrant, if he'd do that to me I'd leave the class.
Good guy, but beware, he is one of the harder teachers out of professors for English 250H. He gives different types of assignments, which are harder and due dates are sooner.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He makes a point of asking how each student is doing. As long as you try in the class, everything should go smoothly. There are a few projects, but they are all longterm, and he will cancel class for a week-ish while he does individual meetings with everyone to give them feedback. Pay close attention to assignments and be prepared for surprises.

Dr. Dzekoe is a great professor who cares a lot about his students. He makes the classroom experience very engaging and gives great feedback. The class was a bit disorganized, and he had to explain some of the projects a few times. Overall a good class and a fun experience.

I would definitely recommend this professor! He can be a little unorganized but he is very helpful and accommodating. He always asks how you are doing and makes sure you understand what is going on in the class.
he is ok but when it came to asking him for help he wasn't very helpful. he never responded to any of my emails or calls so it is hard to get ahold of him for class help.
He's the most awesomest professor at ISU!! you wouldn't wana miss any of his fun & useful classes..
Very Good Professor. Extremely helpful. He knows his****!

This should be a much easier class, but I worked my butt off to get a B. We do a LOT of partner assignments, including a huge research paper and presentation. Make sure that you have a good partner, or else the entire semester will be awful. Get on her good side by coming to class & doing well on individual assignments, then she'll like you.

Lack of proper guidance through course. Doesn't communicate what she wants done. Grade report comments indicate you did a good job but actual grading doesn't correlate. Overall, worst professor I've had at Iowa State University. Someone needs to reevaluate her credibility as a professor
Avoid at all costs. First language isn't English. Can't stay on topic to save her life. Pretty strict on grading while giving little guidance on what is expected
I went into this class deans list student and have been getting C's on every assignment.  Just switch sections
she is nice while talking to you, but that is it, she fails everything else, in case you have her for as a teacher just change your section
She doesn't grade very fairly. She tells you what to do, but doesn't explain how to do it very clearly, and she is just very confusing. She doesn't seem to know what she is talking about.

While she is extremely nice and enthusiastic about the class that is about all she has going.  Very confusing. Wastes a huge amount of class time but still makes you come sit through it.  This is absolutely the class at ISU I have learned the least in and I recommend that anyone drops this if they get her.

Edward cares very much about his students learning. He puts out practice tests with solutions that are very similar to the real tests. He does a very nice job reviewing and trying to keep the class involved, although his accent is heavy.

Ed Yu is a unique character. He is a funny guy who takes time to crack some jokes. Personally, I had a difficult time understanding him. Lectures are mostly review of the slides, which he uploads onto the internet. He seems to care about his students and their success.
Professor Yu is a gem.

He was a very funny and cheerful guy. His exam papers were very easy, you could get a perfect score in every exam if you understand the concepts well. There were a quiz and a homework set due every Friday.
He is a blah lecturer, but the material is very simple. If you just look through the powerpoints you can get good grades on tests.

Not a whole lot to say about this class.  I filled out the study guides and looked at the practice tests to prepare for the exams and found the exams to be easy.  Dr. Braun explains things well and tries to keep things interesting.  Plenty of chances to get full clicker points--only needed 55 out of 80 possible clicker points.

I enjoyed Dr. Braun. He was thorough and clear. His lectures interested me in Microbiology and I found what he was saying applicable to my life. Study for the tests, but he supplies all the materials needed to pass online. He kept my interest during lectures.
Has clicker questions and gives random homework in class. Is very helpful. Tests are easy, just look at study guides (short) and practice exams.
Boring, monotone and unhelpful. Didn't like the guy at all.

Nice guy. The old exams are up on WebCT and he has a large portion of the questions from old tests on the new tests. He is very passionate about wanting everyone to get vaccinated for every single thing possible to keep the public safe. I found that funny. He can sometimes get boring/monotone.

This guy is very excited about microbiology. Lectures are boring, but the class is easy. I know there is a lab but i didn't have to take it. The tests are just like the practice tests. Make sure you attend lecture, he gives in class homework's sometimes. He also gives extra credit.
I love EJ. She is the sweetest person ever. I love how excited she gets about the topics that she teaches about. I love her.

E.J. has a very fast-paced class. She hops right into the content and is teaching the entirety of the 2+ hours of class. Her directions can be unclear, and you will need to ask a lot of questions for clarification. Assignments are not created on canvas, and you can only find them in the syllabus.

EJ's classes are incredibly fast-paced, which can sometimes feel overstimulating. She wastes time during class and gives massive assignments during the last five minutes. Her rubrics are unclear, which adds to the difficulty of being told about an assignment five minutes before class ends.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is a decent professor who is very knowledgeable about Non-Destructive Evaluation, but the course format is set up to heavily weight exams. These exams generally ask weird questions and yield low average scores. A good professor to take this class with, but do not take this class for Tech Elective Credit unless you are completing the minor.

I had this professor for TSM 116 and it was pretty easy. there are a few group projects but most of the work is by yourself. there are weekly assignments and in class assignments but they are easy. he actually ended up canceling our final at the end of the semester.

Although there is homework and in class work for nearly every day of class, the work is straight forward and usually only takes an hour at most to complete. The group projects were fun and definitely my favorite assignments of the semester. If you work hard, and go to class you should have no trouble gettin a high grade in Dr. E's class.

Dr. E. does not teach. He simply has you follow a book and if you don't do it the way he wants, that's too bad. When asked questions, either he responds reasonably and answers the question or he makes you feel stupid and doesn't describe anything. He has a god complex and won't 'dumb anything down' to explain (his words).

Eisenmann is a great teacher, although he does tend to have a sink or swim approach to learning. If you reach out to him he is always willing to help, even during class. He is able to explain concepts clearly and concisely. I suggest seeking out his classes and taking as many as you can.

Sucks at helping you understand the course work when you ask for help. He is really racist in my eyes and he also limits how many questions minority students can ask him. If he calls you the wrong name he doesn't care to correct himself. Overall I would not want him as my professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher who is teaching equally terrible, boring content. Spends most of the class deflecting questions and making students feel bad for wanting help. Also for some reason likes to wear a cowboy hat to class like it means anything. Anybody that says they enjoyed taking a course with this instructor is lying to themselves and to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good at being sarcastic and sassy instead of being understanding or helpful in any way. Often times will get frustrated when students ask for help, and will also pick on students for not understanding something. Also gets frustrated when students can't answer certain homework or test questions even he though he didn't cover that material. Sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are fine, but he assigns a ridiculous amount of homework that often doesn't make much sense or goes over things he didn't cover in the lecture. He also calls on students at random during lecture, and if you don't understand something when you get picked, he'll often call you out on it and embarrass you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Eisenmann has very few students who like him because he assigns homework every class period and doesn't give very good instructions.

Too much homework and also he definitely takes the class way too seriously. Maybe that's just because I declared very early on and so this class was useless, but I did rate him a 4 because his expectations are very clear and he is very good at conveying information.
Mr Eilers is super chill

The class was okay. Nothing special. Lots of lectures and guest speakers. The class was helpful in chosing my major but there are lots of pointless quizzes and assignments. Can only miss class twice. Mr. Eilers was very helpful outside of class class with registration, declaring my major and answering any questions I had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took the required ENGR 101 course for my Aerospace major and this class was a waste of time. If you have to take it, just spend the time and do all the work for the class the first weekend and then you never have to worry about it. The worst part is that participation is required and is 60% of your grade. Not fun. Otherwise, he's a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a recent grad of the Aero department I can say that Brad was always helpful and willing to go above and beyond helping guide me through the curriculum at ISU. He always offered assistance and guidance in a professional and caring manner. Im glad to have had him as my advisor.
All you have to do is show up. Do the homework in advanced so you don't forget about them. The class is a joke pretty much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mr. Eilers is awesome! He really helped me a lot outside of class when I needed help with my 4 year plan and scheduling classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was pointless and a lot of work for a zero credit class. The exams are over obscure material (but there is extra credit - pay attention to his "box" activity at the start of the semester) and there is a lot of busy work for homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Mr. Eilers doesn't really teach the 101 class. He does a few lectures at the start of the semester, but it is mostly just guest speakers. The class is boring, but the homework is easy and as long as you show up to class that's like 40% of your grade. There is extra credit on the exam which is nice because the questions are kind of obscure
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This review is more about Brad "the adviser", not Brad "the professor". The class was what you'd expect, pretty cut and dry basic college 101 stuff. But if you ever need help with anything outside of class, Brad is great! He helped me so much last year during my first 2 terms. Do not be afraid to ask him for help.
Mr. Eilers is ok but the class is pointless
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Brad is the best adviser in Aerospace. The ENGR 101 class is kind of pointless and boring but it's an easy class if you just show up
He is really boring and annoying most of the time. You have to show up as attendance is mandatory otherwise no one would come to class.
The class is suuuuuper easy. Brad is awesome and was very helpful this semester, sadly I will be changing majors :(

Lots of valuable information about the Aero program, engineering, graduation, how to read your degree aduit, and other things. Most of the guest speakers are pretty good. The course is an easy A as long as you show up. The quizzes can be a little tricky but Brad offers extra credit so its very easy to pass. Brad is a great adviser and wants you to
Easy class but kind of boring. Brad seems like a nice guy though and knows a lot about advising & the Aero program

ENGR 101 was super easy!! As long as you show up and pay attention you will do fine in the course. Mr. Eilers is listed as the instructor but only teaches about five lectures throughout the semester, the rest are guest speakers. Mr. Eilers is very helpful if you have any advising questions.
His TA is a better teacher than him...

Tim's 326 class is pretty straightforward. It is well organized and you understand how you will be graded. The wastewater plant and water treatment plant designs were the hardest parts of the class. Tests were also difficult. It is important to study a lot because there is lots of information he may put on the exam.

I had Ellis for a few classes, and I didn't realize how terrible of a teacher he was until I started studying for the FE. I am pretty certain I didn't learn anything from his classes at all. We spent more time doing busy work and sitting through his dry lectures than learning what would be pertinent to the FE. I hope they find someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of useless group projects and field trips. Hes not a bad prof, hes just really dry with his lectures. He covers all his bases and explains things in a very mediocre way.

Class was entirely from monotonous lectures where he reads the examples from the book. As long as you follow along in class you will do fine, but classes are extremely boring and I didn't get much out of the class. The final exam is optional if you do well on the exams during the semester.

He is a great teacher. He shared a lot of interactive and funny stories. He took us on field trips to the local landfill, which was very helpful to see. He had us write a long research paper as well as do presentations. His exams are tough, but as long as you study, you will be fine. If you are having troubles or needing help, he will help you out.

If you've taken CE326, you know what you're getting. He loves to write out notes on his computer. The exams are tough but fair. This class covers a TON of material but if you go to class and really try to learn the material you'll be fine. The term paper isn't terrible and the presentation of it is easy. Be sure to choose a topic you care about.

takes 3 weeks to grade exams. Course is packed with information. Tests are hard, but 40% of the exam is over 2 computational problems. Test setup is the same as practice exams, but go over course objectives to make sure you study all the material, it won't be 100% the same as the practice ones. Good guy, just difficult to follow during class.

Lectures are packed with information, gets old very fast. He's teaching method is solely copying his notes onto an electronic whiteboard, the hand writing is hard to read so if you don't show up you're going to be struggle through reading the slides he puts up.  Assignments and labs are marked very freely, its hard to drop a mark in them.
Lectures are dense with a lot of information. He's a pretty knowledgeable guy, though. Tests can be tough, but the homework and lab assignments are graded really easily. Fun field trips!

I took the course online and it was a pretty easy course. They labs get a little tough and monotonous but doable. The exams you gotta be prepared for because they can be a little tough as well but not if you studied. They are pretty similar to the practice ones he posts. Overall I didn't learn that much but I did receive a good grade.
I don't know but he was good in his topics and not a frindly one. He claim oersonal meeting is optional, then he'll grade you less if you didn't visit him personally.

Eliot is a good teacher, don't get me wrong, he's very knowledgeable on all engineering topics, and I learned a lot from his ME1700 class. I'd have to think about taking him again, though, because there were multiple times in the semester when he would yell at the class and humiliate the class.

very smart and knows what he is talking about. sometimes can be a bit rude about things but doesn't sugarcoat anything. maybe a bit too heavy on how the graphics work instead of introducing strategies on how to model things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He might be one of the smartest people I have ever met. He can come across as arrogant, but does care about the students. The class was very useful and I felt like I will actually use the lessons in real life. Only around 5 group essays (2 pages) and one interactive (i.e. participate in a debate or similar). Take it if you want something useful.

I absolutely loved Eliot! He was very real and always helpful whether or not it was class related. He pushes you to think outside of what you know and gives a lot of freedom in the class as far as what assignments you do. It is a very fun and interactive class, so plan on always going. He's very flexible and I cannot recommend him/this class enough

I had asked for clarification on where to submit a project through email, and instead of replying he read it in front of class the next day to shame me, asking, "Does this sound like someone who attends class?". I had not missed any classes the duration of the semester (even though he didn't even track attendance?). Arrogant, rude person.

Do what he does, not what he says. Eliot is amazing, but there is a steep learning curve as he is trying to prepare you for the industry. One assignment told us to include 3 orthogonal views, but what he actually wanted was the minimum number of views required to fully define the figure.

Everything is done in groups. He gives poor feedback on the 5 papers in the class. Arrogant guy who will spend class time talking about whatever he wants. Semi-interesting, but overall very frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: A total of 5 assignments, and 2 participation grades. He relies on student participation for discussions, but has a habit of mocking or critiquing student answers. Fishy activity happened with the grades, where everyone was getting A's on papers, then the highest was a B- on the 3rd one with no explanation. He loves kiss-ups. Avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Eliot is a great professor! He knows what he is talking about and really cares about his students'  success. He likes to talk a lot but he gives  real world examples that apply to what you are learning. Eliot does a great job at explaining things but wants you to find the answer on your own.  You learn a lot of useful tools  in this class.

Eliot is an awesome professor, he can be rather intimidating but overall he is an awesome professor! If you need any help go see him in his office hours, their really isn't a question he can't answer.

Eliot is AWESOME. That's right! He MAKES us call him Eliot. Extremely helpful and frequently gives us real world examples. Not just is he a professor, he's an engineer with John Deere, a lot of his stories come from experiences there. You'll learn a ton about engineering from this man. Would love to do research with him in VR.
He is awesome and a tech wizard! Great guy too
Eliot is awesome. The class is very straight forward. No tests, he doesn't believe in them. The assignments can be a little difficult but he is helpful.
Great prof! truely cares about his students. Much better than your other choices.
No Comments

He loves the sound of his own voice.  The class really wasn't as much work as he made it sound.  But be careful because he might think everyone in your team is against each other.  For the most part he's a good guy and a good teacher, but he loves the drama.

He is so-very educated in his area of study. He gives the information out in a very easy-to-digest format. And he does it with such enthusiasm. Dr. E is a great professor and is very knowledgeable of the content. The exams are very specific and somewhat difficult to study for though.

Not my favorite type of teaching done by this professor. Lecture slides do not contain enough information its rather him speaking the whole time. If you are not very interested in exercise this will be a harder and boring class. Exams are quite diffcult to study for as well since it is very lecture heavy with little to no content on the slides.

HE IS AWESOME! Passionate about what he's teaching and it shows! You will actually enjoy attending lectures, he is very engaging and material is highly interesting/applicable to real life. Tests are kind of hard so definitely study, but this is my favorite class I've taken at ISU so far! I definitely recommend taking his classes!

I LOVE HIM SO MUCH. I look forward to goin go his lectures every day because of how passionate he is about what we are learning. He is like a king in exercise psychology so he knows what he is talking about. Tests are kind of tricky as they sometimes relate back to studies you talk about in lecture. Also big project towards end but lots of help.

Paddy is by far one of the best lecturers at ISU. You should go to class, but videos of the lectures are posted online if you ever miss anything. He is incredibly down-to-earth and will give you a lot of great information and ways to apply it in your own life and in your future career. Tests can be specific, so be familiar with the lecture slides.

If you show interest in class and out, he will respond well to all your questions. He's interested in seeing you think outside the box and make connections between what you have learned and what you already know about exercise. Great prepper class for my field. Knowing how my patients will respond to exercise prescriptions is very valuable.

So far the best teacher that I have had at Iowa State! The course material is interesting in general, but it helps that he is very passionate about it. He adds in information as he goes through his slides and asks questions to keep the class engaged. The study guides are very useful and the assignments are designed to help you in your future career

The best professor in the kinesiology program. Dr E is full of enthusiasm every day in class and the material he presents is quite interesting. If you attend class, pay attention, and give a solid effort, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. E is awesome. He knows what he's talking about and you can tell during class. Don't get caught sleeping or texting, he will call you out. Tests match what was presented in class, make sure to review the study guides. Huge project at the end, DO NOT leave it until the last minute. Assignments throughout the semester build up to the project.

This has been my favorite professor at Iowa State. He's funny and makes the subject matter very interesting. The tests were more specific than I thought, make sure to study well. Also, he says you don't have to go to class, but you should. There aren't a lot of assignments, but they count for a large percent of your grade, so try your best on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Ekkekakis is probably the best teacher at ISU. He is extremely passionate about his field, is funny, eloquent, and genuine. Go to class, no textbook needed (said so himself), pay attention, print out his slides before every lecture and you should be good. Also, don't tweet bad about him or you will get roasted in lecture lol
He's the best professor I've ever had. He actually gives a crap about the students and what you learn. His passion for what he does pulls you in. Don't skip class!

The hardest class I had all semester, but he's an incredible professor. His lectures are amazing and he tries to make some very dry topics entertaining. If you pay attention (which shouldn't be hard), take notes and study those notes, you should pass. There's an 11 page paper at the end, but there's plenty of help available for it.

Dr. Ekkekakis was hands down one of the best professors I had the chance to work with during my time at Iowa State. I am finding that as I continue on in the professional world, what I learned personally and through his classes is carrying over so well that I'm now ahead of my peers. Still one of my favorite people today.

You will do well in this class if you make the effort. He enjoys students who try hard to learn instead of just excelling points wise.
