I went in A LOT to review test matter, and he's great to help you out if you missed lecture. His slides are fantastic too. This guy is literally an exercise psych genius;  get ready to be impressed and motivated.

Funny guy, but lectures are very slow & long. Fell behind a lot on the syllabus. Use the TA as a resource for the final project.. he's very helpful. Study the study guide for the exam & you should be good. Don't need to go to class.

My favorite professor at Iowa State by far. He is funny, friendly, and very passionate about what he teaches, which makes class interesting. He doesn't use the book at all but bases his tests off of the lectures so make sure to show up. Also, don't be on your phone a lot because he will call you out.

He is one of the best professors I've had in a very long time (since freshman year). Passionate about what he teaches & wants each & every one of his students to not just pass, but to learn. Class is very easy if you show up, and you pay attention for the most part (just stay off of your phone). Good sense of humor as well -- and that always helps
He has been one of my favorite professors at Iowa State. He is very passionate and enthusiastic about what he teaches. He makes class interesting.
Great at covering what is going to be on exams. He is very passionate about the topics.

Awesome professor! Relates content to why we need it. Tests are tough, but attend class and study and it won't be as hard. Some homework assignments but are very interesting. One big paper that is tough but worth the while. Favorite class!

Great professor! He's very passionate about what he teaches and keeps class interesting. He's also very helpful in person and by email. Doesn't use the textbook. Go to lecture, because there are pop quizzes. If you study the lecture notes, you'll do fine on the tests.

Great professor. Very enthusiastic about the material and has sense of humor. He is picky about texting/sleeping in class, so just don't do it and save the embarrassment of being singled out in lecture. Attend class, as his tests are based from his lecture notes, and has the occasional clicker quiz in class. Fun class. Highly recommend.

hilarious, clearly loves his job and is interested in what he teaches. didn't use textbook. tests were fairly hard in my opinion. (i'm a 3.6 student) attending class is extremely crucial in getting a good grade since notes all come from lecture
Alright guy.  Very strict, if you text or fall asleep in his class he will kick you out.  Lectures are pretty interesting but he repeats material a lot.

easy class and he makes it interesting. he has a great sense of humor and knows his subject. i didnt put in much effort and got an A. but he has no problem with giving a lot of low C's so go to class.
Super fun professor! She uses Top Hat questions for attendance.

I've really come to appreciate Carolyn as a professor. She's very knowledgeable and gives helpful advice that has actually made a difference for me. I wish she taught more classes.

She uses TopHat and Lectures, which is fine by me. Like others have said, this class is easy if you put in minimal effort.
Very relatable, uses everyday scenarios in her lectures. Unique way of teaching and getting everyone involved. Big on teamwork and bonding so be prepared to work in groups.

This class was a walk in the park. It is completely team and participation-based. You are graded by your peers based on how often your team contributes to the lecture. It is very easy to contribute and you still get points from your team even if you are not in class. The exams are also very easy, you do an individual exam and then a team one.

This class was very easy but also kinda pointless. She spends all of class going over a PP and using TopHat, which missing a few points will lower your grade. The exams/quizzes aren't hard but use your "resources" when doing them. The nice thing about tophat is once it hits 100 points in the grade book, any extra tophat points go in as extra credit

This class is set up very odd. The lecture quizzes and case studies are worth very few points, however, you can retake as many times until you get 100%. The unit exams are not over any material you'll do, it's just over the textbook which I think is odd. It also is worth a lot of points and will tank your grade if you miss even 3 points.

I have mixed emotions about Carolyn. She has a great personality and a positive attitude - however, her powerpoint presentations don't add up to her quizzes. She doesn't grade very fairly either...make sure to look over rubrics and ask questions when needed.
Terrible class. Requires attending a symposium for 50 points??? I've never enjoyed a single class I've had with this professor and would not take any of her classes unless required.

Professor Elbert was fine. She uses tophat, and I mainly did it from home because it just covers basic lectures. It's a very easy class if you take notes and pay attention.  She made us go on a field trip to Jack Trice and made everyone late for their next class... So I didn't love that.

Super easy course that was required, kind of pointless because the lectures take like 5 minutes to go through and can take the in-lecture quizzes as many times as you want. The exams are super easy too. Also took AESHM 287 in-person... most boring class ever and also grades super easy.

Her class was extremely easy, almost to the point of uselessness. She'd spend the entire lecture going over a slideshow and using tophat, and the actual tests were based on textbook information and none of the slides. Also, if you miss a TopHat quiz due to an excused or unexcused absence, you get a zero. I had a doctor's appointment and got a zero.

Carolyn was not the best. Her online lectures were fine, but sometimes the lecture quiz questions were not related to anything she was talking about at all. Her exams are THE WORST! She picks the smallest details in your reading and puts them all on the exam. Socratic saved my butt for those quizzes. Don't take her unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was genuinely surprised to see all of the negative comments about Carolyn on here! I took HSP M 101 online with her and thought it was an extremely easy class. As long as you know when things are due, she gives you the entire week to complete the readings and assignments. I'm sorry, but it's on you if you fail her classes because they're easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Carolyn is a great person and is very nice but as a professor, she is terrible. Too many stories and goes off on tangents during class so you are forced to read the book cover to cover and memorize every little thing. Her "study guides" are absolutely nothing close to the test to be prepared to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I like Carolyn's personality and believe she gives insightful lectures. However, I have a major problem with her exams. Most of the class agrees her test questions are tricky (worded different, could be multiple right answers but her answer is the only correct one, & some questions we don't even learn about so she requires you to read the textbook)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rarely Replies to emails, tells you to watch a video or read. Pre-Test, Case Study and Unit Test over 4+ chapters every unit (5units total). Learning is difficult because she does not teach. Basically, a class that you will teach yourself.

There were two separate textbooks used for the class and I read every single page of them. If you want an A, get ready to read a lot. Although this was an online class, shes very helpful and is willing to meet with you. It was a more difficult class, but if you can stay on track with the course its manageable. Awesome professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: This "professor" has been the worst I have ever had. I will never take a class with her again. She is disrespectful, condensing, and does not teach. You learn nothing and then the final is impossible. The only way to get a good grade is do all of her "extra credit" like joining her club. Self serving much?
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The study guide she gives is useless! If you are mandatory to take this class, you must get all the extra credits she provided. The exams are difficult, the certificate FINAL is VERY VERY DIFFICULT!!!NO KIDDING!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Club Management seemed like an easy course. The material itself is pretty interesting. I go to every class, take notes, fill out the study guides, study hard, and STILL get C's on the exams. Everyone got about 50% on the group project for missing a few things. Run your consultant report by her before turning it in. Only take this if you'll work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Her study guides for the exams are useless. She just put each title of each page on the study guide, which means you need to read everything in the book. The certificate test is horrible and difficult.

This class was pretty horrible. It was online, and very textbook based. The professor was so unforgiving and quite rude at times. The due dates were weird and did not have any pattern. The tests are really hard - even if you use your textbook and the internet. I didn't like Elbert at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The reading follows the class exactly so you have to go for participation points but you don't have to actually pay attention if you read the text. The group project is horribly confusing. You're supposed to be working on it all semester but she never says what you're supposed to be doing until 3 weeks before its due. Survivable, but not fun.

She doesn't take the time to help her students, I emailed her and she never got back to me so I just lost out on the points. Thankfully she gives extra credit. The study guides have nothing to do with what is actually on the test.

Gives attendance points for participation. Lecture long/boring. Tough grader. Group project is busy work. Weekly quizzes hard even if you think you know the material. Final is unfair, a certification exam based on textbook (you have to know the material better than she teaches it). Doesn't communicate well. Not an easy elective class! Don't take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The quizzes are once a week and go very quickly. In order to do well on the quizzes and exams  you must do the readings. If you go to class and participate you will get half your points. If it is recorded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Group project was really fun!  She gives extra credit, and the lectures are relatively interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's a wonderful professor but you need to go to class otherwise it will affect your grade.  Fun class to take though and the field trip is fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She was nice but clicker points are mandatory but can hurt your grade. First test is easy but second test is hard. Definitely HAVE to go to class or you will not pass.

She was a very good professor but the class was at 8 a.m. and it was a 70 minute class which seemed to go on forever. She posts all the prezi's before classes so there is no need to get the Walker textbook. There are daily clicker points so go to class!
Attendance is not mandatory as she posts the exact lecture powerpoints onto Blackboard before class even happens.   Study those and you will pass the class.

The class is fairly easy as long as you do the case studies and semi-prepare for the quizzes. She takes questions straight from the quizzes for the tests. The group project is pretty easy. Our was only 8 pages total and we got a perfect grade on it.

She's very passionate and made me excited for my degree! It's an entry level course so not difficult. The only graded material were three 100 point tests. I didn't show up to every class and studied before the exams, but if you go to the lectures you probably won't have to study that hard before tests. Speaks clearly and is willing to talk to you.

Very nice professor, and you can tell she is passionate about what she teaches! However, this class is a LOT more difficult than I thought it would be. The quizzes and exams are tough, and the material can be dry. Event students, if you're looking for an easy class to take from the list of 30 credits, I would recommend you keep looking.

Even though I dropped this class, Stines was a great professor who could actually teach the class at a reasonable pace while covering all topics for the day. He filled in notes during class, giving us time to write everything down and pause between steps if there was confusion. Overall, great professor and responds terrifyingly fast to emails.

I am not a fan of this professor. I have taken many of his exams (as he was a course coordinator for another class I have taken), and they are abysmal. Always poorly written, tons of typos, and overall just a lack of care in his teaching overall. Would not recommend and will not be taking a course from him in the future.

Explains concepts fairly well although he does tend to move through some steps too quickly or not explain them. He offered great insight into what would be on the exam and also how to approach the questions. He helps to make a difficult calc two class a bit easier.
Super generous with credit. Lectures were clear and thorough - never had any trouble keeping pace with the class. He also responds to emails unbelievably quickly.

Elijah had to take over our Calc 2 lectures because our original professor got sick the whole semester. He was a very good replacement and his lectures are very solid He posts all his notes beforehand and provides clues and examples for what will likely be on the exams He's very blunt and honest about how he feels about questions and exams but good
He's a pretty good professor and explains things well.

Dr. Stines stepped in when my previous professor stopped showing up, and my grade has skyrocketed. He explains everything in the lectures so well, and he writes the tests, so his exam review lectures are amazing. Make sure you go to class.

I took Linear Algebra in the semester of Spring 2023. He was very lenient when grading the quizzes and exams, for example, he would look through the answers of every individual student and if you got one part wrong and the automatic grading made you get a 0, he would give you half points. You can really tell he cares about his students.

Took linear algebra online and the class is set up very clearly. He posts lecture videos that are very clear and easy to understand. Homework, weekly quizzes, and exams are all of MathLab and are quite easy compared to previous calc classes I took at ISU. The online section also had open note quizzes, exams, and final!

Stines is a good professor. He makes the class hard enough for students to learn the material, but lenient enough to allow people to still do well in the class. He's not the greatest lecturer, but is still fairly great. Overall I really enjoyed his class and if I had to, I would definitely take another with him.

Lectures where helpful, and only require you to make small jumps in logic. Uses top hat every lecture. There is a lot of homework, but after one assignment is due, you usually have a week to do the next one. The assignments are very helpful for learning the material so male sure to do it. Drops 1 exam, 2 quizzes and adjusts homework and tophat.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: A solid professor that made lots of puns and made lectures pretty enjoyable, considering it was Calculus 2. Doing all the homework (unlimited attempts thank god) will net you some possibly much needed extra credit. Barely passed this class, but that's more so on the course material rather than any issues with Stines. Pretty nice guy overall.

Stines is a really great professor, he gives a lot of examples usually similar to what will be on quizzes and exams. Quizzes are very easy if you do part of the homework ahead of time most problems are very similar. He is very friendly and helpful during office hours.
By far the best math professor I have had at Iowa State.
Spoke clearly and showed many examples in class. While explaining though he often skipped over important steps which made understanding the material difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Ridiculous amount of homework in this class. Absolutely ridiculous. Tests are really easy, and Stines posts video recordings of his lectures online which is super helpful. Stines himself is a decent lecturer and occasionally funny although at times he can get boring.

I highly recommend Stines. His lectures are focused on actually doing problems which sets you up well for the exams. Expect weekly quizzes and a fair amount of homework. Good sense of dad humour and easy to understand. Does problems on the fly during lectures so expect occasional errors.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Difficult class, but a good and fair professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The lectures aren't very helpful and the tests are very difficult. His class is just watching him solve problems and tophat questions to check attendance. Don't be afraid of other people doing well in the class as many are repeating it.

Great professor and lecturer. He goes through a ton of examples and posts his recorded lectures on blackboard. A lot of assigned online Homework every week. Do all of it, and early before recitation as they are  the basis for class quizzes and they will help you understand the concepts. The tests are not multiple choice. It is possible to get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Stines is a good professor. He is able to explain the concepts most of the time. He made exactly two mistakes in his entire semester for Calc II, but other than that he was able to answer my questions and teach class. He posts all of his lectures online with practice tests. The homework is long, but really helpful and crucial. Would recommend.
The teacher to have if you're semi intelligent and want a B or higher in Calc II
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Elijah is pretty decent.  He made lots of errors in his work during lectures, and sometimes went to fast.  He posts his lecture videos online which is very nice.  His exams are pretty clear cut, and he gave out extra credit.  While there was a lot of mymathlab homework, he gave full credit at 80%.  Overall, I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Elijah is great. He posts his lectures and recordings of what he says and writes on blackboard. He is mostly focused on helping the students succeed and only tests you on what he teaches you. He also grades based on your understanding of the process, not getting the end result. But be aware, there is a large amount of homework on mylabsplus.

Eli is super nice. He's always willing to help during office hours, posts tons of resources on blackboard (practice tests, lecture recordings, etc.). His lectures are clear and his use of the projector worked very well. Too much (online) homework. Easy grader: grades based process rather than correct answers. End of the semester is tough.

If you are looking for a Calc3 Professor you cannot go wrong with Stines. Fantastic Prof, Test you on what he teaches you, and is always willing to help. I can not stress taking his class enough. I had a bunch of friends take math 265 at the same time as me and they all had a horrible time with it. don't skip a sure thing.

This is one of the easiest classes I've taken so far at ISU. This professor is excellent at explaining all of the material and teaching you how to do the math before quizzes and homework. He uploads everything online too so if you sleep through your 8am you'll be okay. Also there isn't class friday after a test which is always nice.

By far the best math professor I have have had at Iowa State.  His electronic notes are very helpful. His videos are very helpful. His lectures are very helpful. He makes great jokes in classes. Let me put it this way, my class liked him so much that we gave him a standing ovation during the last lecture of the year.

Pros Excellent job of  explaining course materials in lecture; put videos of all his lectures on BB.   Tests are humorously easy,10% extra credit available. Cons Class questions are answered sarcastically.  He lied to about what was on the final spent a week reviewing material that had nothing to do with the absurdly hard final dropped me A to C

Great professor overall, his lectures were extremely helpful and he could explain the material very well . He did his best to not test us on material from previous calculus courses so usually integration required nothing beyond simple u substitution. Gave us one dropped exam. Homework was done in large sets with 60-100 problems due day after exam.

Elijah Stines is a great calc professor, and obviously knows the material very well.  He is clear to understand, and uses lecture time effectively with good example problems.  I attended his lecture because my professor was awful, and he is the reason I got an A.  Tests are fair & a good measure of understanding.  Seems to care about his students.

Stines is a great calc teacher. I have had all good calc teachers and he is still by far the best. Attendance isn't checked or graded but you absolutely have to go to learn. If you do then it will be an easy class. Reviews for tests are spot on and cover everything you need to get an A. Had trouble with the last chapter but you get a dropped test.
Tells you whats on the test the lecture before. His tests were basic and straight forward.

Really enjoyed his Calc 3 course. He describes the topics in detail during lecture by using quite a large amount of examples. Alongside this, he uploads both his lecture notes and video recordings of the lecture for each class. His tests are extremely fair and he notifies you what you should understand for each test beforehand. Would recommend.

Very good at explaining where the math in his class comes from, and all of his tests are very fair. He does a good job of preparing you for his tests, and is a lot better than most of my friends professors. He posts youtube videos that are extremely helpful and I would definitely recommend taking calc 3 with him.
Explains all the material very well in lecture, with lots of examples. Will also make video lectures for material that's more in depth, for additional examples.

Calc is not an easy subject, and I'm not even very good at it. I was scared to take this class but he made things very clear and explained well. I recommend going to class every day so you don't fall behind. Overall a good professor.
He rushes through everything he teaches. If you ask a question during class he becomes very short with you. Doesn't ever curve a thing. If you get an A on the homework, it's hard to fail the course.
Helpful during office hours. Really good reviews for the exams, he sometimes used problems from the exams as examples in the reviews!

Too much time was spent at the beginning on easy concepts and then sped through the hard stuff. He really knows the content but leaves out explanation of a lot of the key steps along the way that he just assumes you know. Also, he has a way of making you feel stupid when you ask any questions. He doesn't curve grades either. Overall OK professor.

I did not like this class at all. He rushes through problems and doesn't explain the material very well. He expects you to understand the problem when he goes through it, and if there are questions he becomes sarcastic and short with you.
Presents the material in a clear, easy to understand, way.  The exams are short and he goes over everything on the exam before you take it. Easy class!

This is just not a review just to make the guy look bad. He rushes through problems, grades on only Tests and Homework in MATH 160, and can be a smart alec to students who just ask questions because they do not know what is going on. Not a good professor at all in my book.
Very easy class. Simple high school math material. Answers for homework is given and tests are short and brief. Spends a lot of time reviewing. Very easy, but extremely boring.

Really nice guy and willing to take time for any questions. Rushes through material and skips steps that would help to follow the process. Due to his pace, if you miss understanding a small part, it's easy to get lost. He makes sure you know before exams what is going to be covered.

This professor is capable of teaching the topics. However, he skips a lot of steps in his work and your notes are near useless outside of class. If you make a mistake early on in a problem you will get continually docked for it. VERY harsh grading. Avoid unless you do near perfect on everything or want to take a hit on your GPA.
hard to understand. skip many steps and cannot understand the notes when i going home and want to study.

He is an excellent teacher. No surprises on tests and quizzes. He is very easy to understand. Lectures may move fast for some, but he doesn't mind stopping for questions. He made it very easy for me to follow and absorb the material. As a result, I didn't need to put in many hours outside of class to be successful.

Exceptional Teacher. Really makes sure his students understand the material. Answers just about any question you might have in class. Really seems to take an interest in the subject and his students. Make Calculus easy and engaging for me. Would highly recommend. Plus there is EC
Taught a little fast but had a good presentation otherwise.

Professor Eness is honestly a great guy, hes super nice and a genuine dude but he is not a good professor; he even said that himself on the first day. Driving to campus on the days I had his class had me wanting to turn into oncoming traffic. Try to get another professor if you can. Other than that he's an awesome dude

ENGL 309 online workload is much heavier during the first half of the semester than it is during the second half, so be prepared for that. There were a few issues with instructions over the course of the class, but he is fairly quick to respond to emails. Communicate a lot during the group project, and you will be just fine.

Lectures are only relevant to the class 50% of the time, and even with the relevant lectures, I found it very easy to get stuck on assignments/not know what to do. However, I hardly tried on main assignment of the class and got a decent grade. Didn't grade major assignments until the last week of the semester. Nice guy, just odd class structure.

Grading criteria was very confusing but a quick email would clear it up. Lectures were confusingly created, but once you got used to it, it was fine. Group project at the end which I am never a fan of. Two main projects overall and you do it in parts throughout discussions which helps out. He was not a fast grader, took a while for all of it

There is no clear guidance on what to do for assignments, you basically have to go off the examples & then what other students help you with. Takes a long time grading, so when the next assignment comes, you do not know how you should change. This class also has nothing to do with reports.

Professor Eness gave great feedback, but was somewhat inaccessible outside of class. It was hard to get a response through email, specifically. His feedback on papers was specific and helpful and the range of material covered in the course is pretty well-rounded.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is a ton of work but it is proposals. Theres also some group assignments and a big paper at the end. Everyone is graded together and theres no team evaluation which really sucks. He takes long to grade and most feedback is from the students in your class.

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS WITH THIS MAN. The first day of class he told us that he still sucks at teaching after 6 year. He is the most long winded teacher I have ever had and over shares about his life. It is so uncomfortable and does not to pertain to the work we are doing in class. Also the Canvas page has more information then he does.

Mr. Eness is highly knowledgeable about tech. document writing, however, has great difficulty communicating with students. For most assigments the students had little idea what was being asked of them to do, and in lecture, Eness would ramble on about unimportant things. Class structure is 2 days lecture, 1 day work time. Fight for your grade. GL

Cathy was an awesome professor and gave amazing feedback on papers and projects. She seemed to be a pretty easy grader, and her one on one meetings were super helpful. She is good at explaining what we need to do and doesn't give too much homework outside of essays/projects. She is easy going and fun to talk to.

Cath was one of my favorite professors this semester. At first I thought it was going to be a long year, however she really gives great feedback on your work and makes sure that you understand all the material you are given. If you show up to class and put in the effort you will be just fine.

Cath is really nice, and she knows what she's talking about. Though, she doesn't do the best job explaining the recommendation report, just gives you the criteria and some samples, then tells you to go to work on it. Does a good job giving feedback on all the papers, though she can be really nit picky and a tough grader on the project and papers.

Cath is an excellent professor. As long as you do what is told and participate in class, you will do just fine. She is extremely helpful on papers during conferences. Class focuses on food, do the readings and you will be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was a good professor who was willing to work with students and their needs. She makes the effort to schedule meeting times outside of class that serve as conferences to discuss progress on papers due. Writing exams are relatively easy if you read the essays given. Most introductory classes are directed towards a specific topic (such as food).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class isn't your usual blow off English class. Tough grader on the exams and essays.  She also keeps track of participation and has strict rules about attendance. If you miss up to 4 classes she will then take away points at the end of the semester. She is willing to help but this won't be a show up and pass class.

I personally love Lisa Enloe. I had her as my advisor all 4 years, and as a professor in HDFS 491 throughout my internship process. She is extremely helpful with any questions or issues you might have, and responds to emails very quickly. She's also almost always available and willing to meet in her office. Super nice and cares about her students!
Nice person, boring class

In general, Lisa is a terrible professor. Her material covers dull, unnecessary information. It is not beneficial or relevant to students' interests. She is also unhelpful and difficult to work with. For projects, she does not give you an outline or example of what you're supposed to do, so it's almost impossible to understand what she wants.
I loved Lisa's class. She is so helpful and attentive to the thoughts and concerns of all of her students.

Lisa has very boring content to present and therefore her class can be pretty boring, but she tries to keep people involved. She has a lot of experience and if you are willing to listen you will learn from her!

She simplifies everything down to elementary level but then she tests over stuff completely different that is in the book. The class is very boring and shes not a good teacher. She is a nice person but this class is pointless. The content is common sense but tests suck.

Lisa is generally a nice person, but a very strict, uncooperative instructor. She rarely makes any personal allowances, despite documented excuses or reasons (such as graduation or job interviews). She takes forever to return assignments and does not utilize the course website. She often seems to not understand her own lecture notes and can be dry.
Very nice.
Nice lady, boring class
BORING!!

She is reasonably knowledgeable, but doesn't follow her own syllabus, and will change presentation dates and due dates without updating her schedule. She lectures past the time the class ends, and he lectures are a little dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I agree, Mira is an excellent professor. You need to show interest in the course content and TRY to advance yourself. If you do these things you'll quickly realize that Mira has many useful insights.

Mira is G-R-E-A-T. She wants to see effort and growth in her students. If you don't exhibit effort and a desire to expand yourself she won't care about you. But that is not a bad thing. This is college, and if Mira is one thing she is efficient and she focuses her efforts on the students who most deserve it. So if you don't like her, try harder!!!

cares only about the very talented students. can't even be bothered to learn the rest of the class' names. i had the woman for 3 semesters and she still called me by the wrong name.  She does make you think outside the box but takes it to such an extreme that the projects have to real use in the real world.
one of my favorite teachers by far! loves what he teaches and always has great stories. as long as you show up and show a little interest its a great class!
He is awesome! You can tell he really wants everyone to learn. Video quizzes and two major tests make for an easy class!

Loved having him as a teacher. He's such a nice guy and states that he just wants you to be interested in biology, so therefore the class is easy. Attend every day and you'll get an A with no problems. He's very helpful. The downside is that he doesn't have much control over the classroom, so people talk a lot.

Prof Enger is a great teacher. Essentially, you show up to class and you will get an A. In-class quizzes involve watching videos and answering questions from a packet. Also requires no book. Has a great sense of humor, class is fun and you don't have to stress out about the tests because the questions come straight out of the quizzes, no surprises. You learn alot as well.

His teaching effectiveness is not as well as it could be. He is kind of spacey, but he is really nice. As long as you attend class for the video quizzes and study the study guide and quizzes then you should do well.
Video quizzes during each class (fill in as you go). Final and Midterm are pulled directly from the quizzes. Very interesting. Hate Biology, but LOVED the class. I'd take it again lol.

Very easy teacher. He hands out practice exams with answers that are identical to the actual exam.  There are a ton of movie quizs for points and those questions are also on the test. Easy to get a good grade if you just use what he gives you.  Not to good teaching the material at all, he had to look up a lot of our questions.

Video Quiz practically everyday, so you want to make sure you actually come to class. Each quiz is an easy 20 points though. Actual test was difficult, but most of the questions were off of the videos so all you really need to do is take the time and study!
Enger is a great guy... he wants everyone to learn as much as possible...his stories and videos are great! So glad I had him as a teacher!

I HATE science classes (psych major) but I would def. take this class over if I could have not taken Bio 101. (I got a C+ in Gen 260 & D in Bio 101.) Tests are hard, but my class's study guides were word-for-word-cut-&-paste. Just keep on top of things & go to class because videos (with 20-30 pt. worksheets) are shown ALL the time!

I love Dr. Enger! He is extremely nice, and tries to be funny. He does get off topic during class, but usually shows very good videos. The exams are hard, but if you actually read the book you do well.

This class should just be renamed Genetics for Psych Majors.  It seems like a hard class (the tests are awful) but he gives tons of extra credit, and the cumulative final was made up of questions directly off old tests, so it's easy to do well on it, and that really helped boost my grade.  He tends to get off topic alot, but he's a VERY nice guy.

He is getting so old, that he is not a very good teacher anymore. I learned from the videos he played. Don't get me wrong, the videos were excellent and I learned a lot from them. BUT, I did not like how if you didn't try to work the system, you didn't get any extra credit. (hint: become a suckup)

Dr. Enger is a good guy.  Unfortuneately his class was not interesting at all. Knowing full well he had a class full of Psych majors (which I think happens everytime the class is offered) he only spent one day on behavioral genetics. That day was interesting, but 90% of the class was always boring.

SCM 486. Insane amount of busy work and essays, exams averages 75-80% just slides and practice exam. Grades essays extremely hard. Class not hard just massive workload and I learned absolutely nothing in this class that will help me in the real world, she just reads slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: SCM453. So far, the averages for exams in the class are extremely low, and she will not curve them. Very tough grader and will take points away for silly reasons. There have been multiple case studies. Also, discussion posts, textbook assignments, and traditional math assignments every week. You'll have to dedicate so much time outside of class.

For SCM453. She is nice, but this class has so much useless busy work. Multiple discussion posts, textbook readings, and mathematical assignments every week. Exam averages are in the 50s and 60s thus far. Meanwhile, another section my friend is in is averaging exams in the 80s, indicative of Kohnke's poor teaching of the material.

For SCM 453. She is a nice person and will help you in office hours but she just reads of slides in class and our main form of hw is writing some discussion on packback. For our exam we had no practice exams which has been a thing in every SCM class I've taken so far. The exam average was a 56 with a high of 86 and she refused to curve it.

She typically reads directly from the slides and this class is very lecture heavy. We only met two days a week, so to make up for the third day we had a lot of busy work to do. There were a lot of papers and group project "deliverables" throughout the semester. We also had packback polls during each class to get attendance points.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took SCM 450 and SCM 486 with Khonke. In 486, it was bearable in 50 minute segments, but 450 was one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. Just reads off slides almost the whole time or spends time in NetSuite showing us stuff we won't ever use again outside of the one project. She seems like a nice person, her class is very boring.

I took SCM 486 and hated it. The lectures are not interesting, she takes points off for unnecessary things, and I would not recommend it. Her tests have lots of fill-in-the-blanks which don't make sense considering the amount of content you have to remember. She doesn't like to regrade and is so frustrating to talk to.

I had her for SCM 486. A ton of busy work, completely pointless. Had a lot of project "deliverable" No real world application from this class. She shows NO examples of what she is expecting from group or personal projects. If you can get another professor, I would advise you to.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's nice and an okay professor at best. Issue is she's teaching an absolutely horrible course in SCM 301. Boring lectures where she just reads off the slides, and those slides are copy/pasted straight from the textbook. This makes lectures basically pointless. Exams are stupid hard and assignments are tedious.

Absolutely disgusting experience. Yes, she is genuinely kind, besides when it comes to teaching. Atrocious lectures, unbelievable amount of homework, packback homework was pointless. Our first 2 class exam average scores were 62% and 69%. A lot of material within the exams isn't found in lectures or even the textbook. I wish I could give this a 0.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Interesting projects throughout the course. My only gripe would be the exams, specifically the midterm. The questions are very specific and do not cover broad topics. Remember that chapter you skimmed? Well, there is definitely a question on that. If you read each chapter and review PowerPoints youll be fine.

I believe the general reviews here are misguiding. Professor Kohnke makes the course easy to understand and accessible. The midterm exam and final exam are only worth 15% of your grade each. Exam questions can be specific, but if you understand the general concepts of each week, the exams are not that hard.

Professor Kohnke is a great professor, however, the exams are very specific that it seems almost impossible if you didn't read the exact question out of the textbook. I did alright in the class, but the only 2 exams we had brought my grade down an entire letter. The lectures are okay, just reading off of a PowerPoint.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: exams are pretty hard. i didn't read but i recommend you just use the powerpoint and take book notes. exams are hard and long. dry long boring lectures. lots of homework esp since we went online because she thinks we won't learn. she emails back fast and extra credit. fast grader. you get participation points but its not really mandatory.

Do not take her section as a night class. She talks the whole 3 hour time slot and reads straight from the slides. She makes you think the tests won't go that in depth but they do. Bring the test study guides to her office hours (which she only has for one hour before the test) and ask her all of the questions if you want to do well on her tests.
Most boring lectures Ive sat through. Reads straight from the slides and expects you to know all the calculations when she has mentioned them once. Lots of online homework worth 50 points each.

Mrs. Kohnke taught the traditional way. She would almost always lecture with slides and would post the material online for studying. No participation points!! Lots of online assignments and quizzes which were mostly easy. The tests are well detailed and worth a good amount, so do study. Felt like I really learned something from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very helpful, but only if you ask for it. Grading scale is set from the beginning and there is zero room to mess up. Tests are extremely detail oriented. Must go to class!

Great professor. Very willing to help. The homework is online and she will check it for you and help you get to the right answer. Lots of in class practice, it breaks up lecture and gives you more exposure to the material.

lectures are fast paced and packed with content, but skeleton notes provided. homework and exams are BRUTAL, long and hard and not graded very fairly. Accomodating too if you communicate. Helpful during office hours.
Good at math

Emily is very sweet but is not very thorough with the material. Her lectures go at the speed of light and you likely won't pass this class unless you have a good basis on the material. She is not great at responding to emails and seems very disorganized. There is not great communication between the professor, instructor, and TA's in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Emily Heath is a good professor. She goes through her lecture slides and answers all of the student's questions... but she goes at the speed of light. You would be writing down notes and before putting your pencil on the paper, she would already be at the next slide. Quiz every week. Exams are extremely hard, with 50/100 being the average.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good professor, loved this class very much.
Homework takes 10 minutes to do weekly quizzes. Two solo email-type projects and 1 large group project. Easy A, good professor.

Great teacher and mentor. Have taken a couple classes with her and I have grown so much as a creative through her teaching. Very kind person who is accessible outside of class and lets you have fun within the classroom. If you're even remotely interested in creative writing, I would recommend taking one of her classes. My favorite prof. I've had!

I had Emily for speech, and she made it easy for students to understand expectations, improve their speaking skills, and get a good grade in the class.  The speeches can be difficult; however, she will help you develop a strong speech.  I recommend you take her section of the course as she is very helpful and will take majority of late work.

I really loved this class! Emily is so good at giving lectures that it feels like she is telling a story. You do have to rely on yourself for note taking because the slides are only images and titles, but you can tell when a topic holds more importance versus another. Not many graded things so do quality work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class! Just make sure you don't miss or turn in late any assignments because it's graded on so few thing. Extra credit for office hours and she's very engaging to listen to. There is a lot of memorization, so figure out early how to get that down and you'll be fine. Attendance is graded so don't miss any lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Morgan was really fun to have. She makes her lectures interesting, even if the material isn't as exciting. There are three 600-word papers, but they are really easy once you start. Both exams are open-note and fairly simple as long as you take good notes in class. As long as you pay attention and turn stuff in on time, it should be an easy A.

Loved Prof. Morgan! She is very well spoken and I found her lectures to be very interesting. All quizzes and exams are open note. Lots of reading. A few short writing assignments. Show up to class! Overall I enjoyed this class and I'm excited to have Prof. Morgan again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class!! Make sure you take notes in the lecture, and you can basically copy your test review on the test. Would definitely take it again.

Took this for my final ARTH credit, really great class and a lot easier than other ARTH classes. Attendance is the only way you'll pass - tests are open-note, so your grades depend on detailed notes. Few other grades, 1 paper and a couple discussion/reading posts. Great class and her lectures were interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very interesting if you like history. Class mainly online but works well that way. Readings are long and boring. Do those before recitation, not due date. Provides extra credit through her and TAs office hours. Class has lots of points. Essays have easy requirements at 600 words. Dont miss quizzes! Very funny and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Emily Morgan is a very knowledgeable professor and her lectures are (in my opinion) very interesting. If you watch the lectures you will be fine with both the quizzes and exams. There are also papers and I found these to be the most challenging part of 183. Make sure to show up for the Friday discussions or else it will impact your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Emily's lectures are really boring, not gonna lie I almost fell asleep in most of them. The readings she assigns are very long and don't pertain to what's covered in lecture but she asks a ton of questions about them on exams. Make sure you go to class on test review day, she'll go over almost everything on the upcoming exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable, makes her expectations clear on the first day of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a really good teacher and is extremely engaging. I would strongly suggest picking her as your prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved DSNS 183 because of Emily Morgan! She gives awesome lectures. Even thought the material could sometimes be boring, she somehow made it interesting. The class is definitely easiest if you show up to class and do the readings. The exams are pretty easy. She's also really funny. Very fun and interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Make sure you take notes in this class, unless your memory is fantastic. She talks really fast sometimes, so it is hard to get all of the information processed into by brain before she moves on to the next slide. Overall, I wouldn't say she is a bad professor. All you have to do is make an effort.

Emily tries to be funny, but most of her jokes are crude. Presentations are clear, and exam content is all from lectures. Don't buy the $100 textbook, it is a waste of money unless you plan on skipping many of the lectures. She always has a clicker slide at the beginning and end of the lectures, so don't leave early!

I had her for DSN S 183 and ART H 281 and you can expect the same for both classes. The book isn't necessary. All you have to do is show up, pay attention, and take good notes. Once you learn how to memorize the stuff, it's simple and straight forward.
Long lectures with lots of info. Be sure to take notes

She's a great professor! Everything she talks about in class is on the test.  You don't really need to worry about buying the book. I never used it and did just fine.  There's a lot to memorize for the tests but they aren't really that hard if you study!
THE best Art History professor in all of Iowa State University. Extremely passionate, funny, and engaging. She will make any student in any major appreciate art history.
Funny, Witty, and SUPER KNOWLEDGEABLE. Tests were hard, but it's college, get use to it.

She was a ok teacher...She gives you like 50 images and makes you remember everything For each test but only tests you on 10 images (dates, photographer, title, what type of print) TOO MUCH To remember ... She needs to make you learn not just memorize material.

She is really passionate and knowledgeable on the topics covered for the course. She's pretty witty and very entertaining. There is a lot of memorization, but once you figure out your method, it becomes pretty easy. I paid attention in class everyday and never read the books and got an A in the course.
Awsome Professor! Prof Morgan is very knowlagable and will help you understand even the most difficult of pieces and histories. I Highly recommend her!

I've had her for multiple courses. She consistently had not responded to emails to the point I reached out to other professors teaching the same course to get an answer. She also is horrible at technology to the point that it almost doesn't make sense for her to teach an online class.

Emily Godbey was by far the worst professor I have ever taken from. She has a dry personality, reflected in her teaching, as her lectures are extremely boring and shallow. She is extremely hard to communicate with, and if you get in touch with her, she often comes off as rude and snarky. All in all, make sure you read the course textbook.
Super nice, entertaining, and easy to talk to

Professor Godbey made her expectations clear and provided ample opportunities for students who wanted to succeed.  In fact, I think she made the course easier than it should have been.  Learning requires effort and the students who struggled did so because of their lack of effort.  Don't hang a professor because they expect a student to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online to fulfill a general design education credit. If you want to do well, be prepared to read the entire book, highlight, and take key notes. I can tell she cares about her students and she wanted us to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Emily Godbey was the worst professor I have ever taken from. She was extremely difficult to work with and I often found it extremely painful to attend her class as I learned nothing from her course. She says that she cares about her students and wants you to succeed, but she puts in the bare minimum of work and is an unpleasant character.

Shes alright. Didnt love her at first b/c she just sent us to websites to read and watch. When emailing was super aggressive. Changed 1/2 way tho to lectures, which were ok. We read PDFs too, which were alright. Tests could be tricky, because closed book on lockdown browser. Didnt learn a ton. Didnt love this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bad professor. Sends out readings that anyone can find online. Accuses class of cheating after a couple of quizzes stating its not "Mickey Mouse University," her lectures consist of her flashing pictures on the slides and talking in the background making it very hard to take notes. Threatened to proctor quizzes when students asked for more time.

She is the worst professor I have ever had. At first, she just sent 30 links to articles on a website that you then had to memorize every minute detail of in order to pass the weekly quizzes. Then she changed the layout after complaints and uploaded a video of her complaining about actually having to teach the class. She puts in no effort at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't waste your money taking this class at ISU with her. If you can take it literally anywhere else, do it. All she does is send out 20-40 links to a public art history website and expect you to memorize it. She basically just makes you pay for public information and then wants you to take the class seriously as if she's the one teaching you.

Claimed that we're all cheaters and threatened to record us during weekly tests because she doesn't like that we as a class asked for more time on them. Doesn't teach the course at all, just posts links to videos you can find online for free. Wants you to memorize every little detail in the videos. Doesn't like it when students ask for help.

Teacher is unbelievably rude and wants students to fail. She has no sympathy, no lenience when it comes to her students, but will easily take a weekend off and tell her students to not contact her. Extremely hypocritical when she assigns an ungodly amount of work and doesn't even teach. Yet expects students to know everything in less than a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is very biased. The teacher doesn't teach but the Khan Academy narrators are clearly Christian who state Christian beliefs as facts which is very uncomfortable for non-Christian students. This is taught at a public university and the professor needs to realize the idea of the separation between Church and state.

The worst professor. I think her main goal in life is to bring down students' GPA. Her TAs are not any better. They will make one comment on your submission but take off two points for fun. Wants to be called a "Dr" but does no real teaching to receive that title. I can honestly say no good things about her. Let's pray one day she will be fired.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Basically paying tuition for the credit and the weekly quizzes but not the education. Teacher sends out 25+ Khan Academy links a week (which are free), and expects you to have them memorized from Tuesday afternoon to Saturday at midnight, must set aside at least 2 days to focus on just this class. If you can take this course elsewhere, do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wants to be called "Dr" Godbey when all she does is send Khan Academy links and is rude to students. Does not teach AT ALL and everything is on your own in this class. Quizzes ask the most detailed questions so make sure you actually read and watch the material. Teachers are getting paid to send 30 links a week while the TA's do all the work.

The info. I learned did not relate to me being in a design major whatsoever. It was not useful. Be prepared to read the textbook and lose interest and become bored easily. They're terribly long like 30-60 average pages of reading. The tests were hard, with essays that were excruciating. Studying a ton of flashcards and only having 5-10 on the test?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Shes a nice professor. If you go to her asking for help you'll be fine. Her tests are easy and fast. She does lots of quizzes but the lowest 2 gets dropped and only have 3 exams. The final is the 3rd exam and is non cumulative.

It's hard to find professors that care about their students as much as Professor Godbey does, especially in large lectures. Always willing to help and very knowledgeable. Study the provided flashcards and do the reading and the tests are fairly straightforward.

Professor Godbey is a little strange, but don't let that fool you. Shes very kind and wants everyone to do good, going to great lengths to help students do better. She has little 2 point quizzes at the end of her lectures you fill out. What you talk about in lecture will be on the tests, only some of the images will be used on the test.

She's a little quirky but it's okay. Tests are straightforward, slide IDs, a couple short answer, and multiple choice. Lectures can be  boring and hard to take notes over but if you do the assigned readings you'll be fine. Quizzes over the readings from blackboard. They vary in difficulty but lowest 2 are dropped.

Godbey was great for both of the design history courses I've taken. She's very clear with expectations, which are completely manageable. Not to mention, very personable and down-to-earth. I could listen to her photography lectures all day, plus the course content is very interesting!

Professor Godbey gets the job done. Her lectures are not mandatory, but there are 4pt quizzes at the end of each class. Most of the time, she ends up speaking about a piece too long and consequently cuts out large parts of history. The exams are fair, mostly slide IDs. I did not need the textbook for this course, I instead used the Platos Cave tool
Very good. Clear and fair expectations, and she's FUNNY! Recommend to others.

Nice personality, but not the greatest at teaching. Often over-elaborates answers to student questions. Tends to ramble on quite a bit, and it became hard to know what to take notes on. Definitely read the book, take the best notes you can, study for the tests and you'll likely do quite well.

She's quite quirky which some found annoying but I enjoyed. Tests were fairly easy if the materials were studied and understood well. Tests and papers were returned in a timely manner. Lots of discussion and little lecture.

She would not come to class without any warning or letting the TAs know. Class was cancelled at least 4 times. When in class we watched a lot of movies but the tests were really easy as long as you reviewed the book and her review list before the test.
cancelled at least 1/3 of all the classes. forgot to show up to scheduled field trips. class was incredibly easy but really frustrating. among the worst professors i've ever had.

She's not that bad. Different, which used to annoy me, but then I got over it. She's a decent person, which is a lot more than can be said for other professors I've had. Oh and she actually listens to students and what they want which is nice. That said, lectures can get pretty boring.

Single worst professor I've ever had. Generally just does not show up to class at least one a week, without evening informing TAs. Arrogant, rude and seems to have absolutely NO knowledge of the subject she teaches. Rarely lectures, just puts in a movie which often does not have anything to do with the subject.

Very easy class if you do the reading and and participate in the online discussion. A few 25 question multiple choice tests over the readings with a few slide identifications. I wouldn't call her a great professor, a little scattered, but overall pleasant.
Good class. She's FUNNY!!!!
She recites what's in the textbook and ridicules students when taking tests. Fell asleep sometimes because the class was extremely boring.
Challenging but clear. Gives vocab lists and slide lists which help a lot.

Attending class and taking notes is a must (like any lecture). She gives super easy pop quizes, usually at the end of class. The tests are straight forward and she provides an outline of concepts/vocab/slides to study.
Lacks clarity, a willingness to help.  Moody and sets expectations far too high for students.  She's the 1st or 2nd worst professor I've ever had.
Nice but isn't great at grading in a timely manner or responding to emails. I dreaded coming to class as it felt like everything could be online. I'm glad it's over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very nice and accommodating when you need it. She also manually checks your papers and offers grammatical or simple fixes to your paper. However, it feels like she doesn't always give a clear instruction on what needs to be fixed, and you most likely can't get to the "Excel" territory in your writing.

One of my favorite profs I have had at Iowa State. She is super accommodating if you miss a class and does not give extra assignments other than the required papers as some other 150 and 250 profs do, and I had her for both. Super sweet and wants you to succeed. Leaves good feedback and is not that tough of a grader. Highly recommend her!

Overall great experience. Very clear in what was expected from you in this class and if you needed help at any point along the way she was there to help you out. You can tell she really cares about what she is teaching and wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown is a fairly easy professor. His quizzes on the reading are super easy if you've actually done the reading. However he doesn't seem to really care about his students. He doesn't respond to emails, he doesn't grade his own material and instead has his TA do it, and he didn't allow for makeup work, even if you had a valid excuse.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Eric Brown is a really good teacher. He gives clear grading criteria and has very simple assignments. Be prepared to write a bunch of papers throughout the semester, but they are super simple and easy. Also, be prepared to read sections of the book before class as the attendance quizzes will be based on your reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Easy but boring lectures. Midterm is open note and no other exams until the final.
Great professor! He is kind and understanding while being well respected.

Although extremely dry and boring subject material, Dr. B has set up the class in a good way. Takes attendance through class participation, but it's a hybrid with a weekly online, at-home learning component in place of class. Lectures boring, but plenty of hilarious clips to make up for it. No writing. Only real test was the final, which was easy.
This class was hard but one of the best I've ever taken in my entire life.

This class was extremely easy. There is really no reason to show up, except for the fact that he sometimes gives out random in-class points. The material is very boring and dry but he makes up for it by showing plenty of The Office clips.

Really no reason to attend lectures, although he did give out random attendance points every couple of lectures. Very boring subject material, but what do you expect for a basic management class. Super easy class, just do the friday online quizzes while using the book or the internet to get a 100% on those. The actual exams are a bit more difficult

Class is extremely boring. Barely went and just did my notes from the textbook. Brown is a great teacher though, he tries to make lecture as interesting as possible. Lost a little under half of participation points for not going to class and still got an A.

When an instructor uses clips of The Office during class to help further a point he is trying to make, you know he understands how to set himself apart from other instructors. He understands that class gets boring, and does his best to keep your attention. Helpful power points, helpful material, no pointless busy work.
Very good professor!! Cares about his students and is willing to help whenever!! I would take classes from him again in the future!

Dr. Brown is a great teacher. He really cares about his students and is super nice and easy to talk to if you need too. AESHM211X is a great class to take if you want a GPA booster as well as to learn something about leadership and yourself. I highly recommend this class as well as any class with Dr. Brown!!

Eric Brown was a great teacher! One of my favorites so far at ISU. Really enjoyed what he was teaching, very easy to understand, and really cared about the students. He really wants his students to do well. 287 is a very easy course. Some random attendance points, exams are open note (online). Great course and great teacher. Hope to have him again!
Literally coolest teacher ever, very laid back and chill. Definitely get him as a professor! Would love to have him again!
Very Nice, Showed enthusiasm for what he was teaching.

Such a nice guy! Take this class if you're looking for something fun that won't stress you out! I liked that it was a blended course, so we didn't meet at all on Fridays. I learned a lot about leadership- highly recommend him.
Best professor ever! Class is interesting and the online portion makes me less stressed.
He's the man.

287 was a relatively easy class. All assessments were given online and taken on your own time (except the final). Recommend for an easy course, but expect to want to skip class a lot because of how boring it is and also because all slides are posted online. Very nice and helpful guy. Seems a bit nervous in front of large groups. Overall, decent.

He's a solid teacher. He takes forever to enter grades though, so that can be frustrating at times not knowing what you have in the class. His year end project is super easy and it accounts for 20% of your grade.
Good class! Easy.  You NEED to go to class to get participation points.  You watch lots of movie clips of The Office and others, which makes it interesting.

Ebrown you freaking rule!  I love this guy.  He never gets mad at the class and is always willing to accommodate you.  He makes dry material interesting by using clips from The Office.  How could you not love his classes?

Very easy going guy. Never gets upset or looses his cool when people talk in class. His powerpoint slides have certain parts that need to be filled in so it is important to attend class. Also there are random attendance checks so it is important to go to class and get those easy points. Tests arent too hard. I recommend him as a teacher.

Professor Wilgenbusch is very organized and  has a clear calendar which she reviews with the class every new lecture. She provides well thought out feedback and there are no surprises when it comes to any upcoming tests or assignments. She is also very knowledgeable on her subject and has a study guide made for each test. Great professor.

Very nice professor who dove into the texts very well. Would always take her time to greet people in the class, even those who sat all the way in the back. Weekly assignment was very easy and exams were straightforward if you went to class and did brief studying before.

Erin is THE professor to take PR courses from. She is incredibly helpful and kind, the kind of professor that wants to see her students succeed!!!! 4240 is not difficult, but the concepts can be difficult. Just apply yourself, do the work, show up to class, and you'll be fine. I love this capstone class!

PR 2200 was an amazing class to take, especially when first starting out in college because she doesn't bombard you with work and papers. She does take attendance but will drop 3 at the end of the semester if you miss some. She always goes over the study guide in class and it is exactly the same as the test. Overall, a great class to take!

Professor Wilgenbusch was a great instructor. She was harsh and blunt at times, but got her point across well, which was all that mattered. She has a study guide review in class, which is extremely helpful. She uses tophat for attendance, which goes in the gradebook at the end of the semester, so it is mandatory. She allows 3 absences all semester.
Shes entertaining during class but sometimes didnt seem worth it to go since material was all posted on canvas

I loved Erin's class - she is really great at making lectures interesting and involving the class. She uses tophat, and you also have an assigned group that you answer random questions with. But I always did well on tests in her class because she went over the study guide question by question and also shared the slides and information.
Easy class, be aware of random attendance points on tophat
She actually made it enjoyable to go to class.

Wilgenbusch is the professor I want to take every Greenlee class with. She understands how a student learns, and so she taught this class through terms you need to know for the test and gives real world examples on them. She is very kind and overall a great professor!

Make sure to always be overly communicative and on time. She is definitely a person that will teach you about how the corporate world works. Try to gain a professional relationship with her only. And if there are opportunities that she gives you make sure to thoroughly research those opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Erin is an incredible lecturer and professor. She makes a lecture heavy class really interesting and engaging, and cares about her student's success. Tests are worth the majority of your grade, but she gives a review day and almost everything ties back to the study guide. Cannot recommend her enough!
Loved Her. She respects your time, and listens to student feedback. Was very clear in her lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Erin is a great professor and is great at her profession. She brings modern topic into play, along with how everything about PR has come about. She currently works in PR alongside being a professor, so that allows her to explain modern day examples that are key to the industry. I loved this class because she does a good job of catching attention.
10/10 Easier class. Great teacher, had clear grading criteria, and posted lecture slides. As long as you have the study guide, you're going to ace the test

An amazing professor, she is understanding and very knowledgeable. She uses top hat for extra credit at the end of the semester. it is a lecture heavy class but she makes the lectures interesting. This is an easy class if you need the credit.

If you are a Public Relations student Erin is the person to know. You do need to read the textbooks and take light notes. There are 4 exams. No cumulative final exam. Lectures every day. No group projects. 5 point HW assignments are due every week.
Erin is a great teacher! I love her lectures, and I learned so much! However, you should show up to class to understand everything and get all of the deadlines for assignments & exams.
Prof Wilgenbusch provides all the things necessary to succeed in her class, if you don't succeed it was more than likely that you didn't do the one assignment a week.

PR 220 is a very straightforward class and Ms. Wilgenbusch does a great job teaching it. She provides you with all the materials you need to succeed in her class and it will be your own fault if you fail. Highly recommend!
online was hard with her. we did a hybrid but i got selected to be 100% online. she would often talk to the people in person and not the people online.

PR 220 was the second class I've taken with professor Wilgenbusch and I was glad to have her again. This course was similar to JLMC 101. You have a weekly question to answer relating to what has been said in lecture. Easy exams(4), lowest drops. TopHat with every lecture. The book makes things a bit easier, but it's honestly not a necessity.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Erin is an awesome professor. Gives all kinds of extra credit. Literally, show up, pay 70% attention, easy A. Also, I actually really enjoyed her lectures.

This class was enjoyable. Erin was a great professor and made the material interesting. Assignments and tests were easy if you study. Attendance was not mandatory but she gives points via tophat participation so definitely show up for that!

Go to class and you'll get a good grade. Textbook is required for homework but most questions are common sense so you'll find you rarely use it. She is an amazing professor who really cares about her students and her lectures are fun. Attendance isn't required but it'll make the class super easy. Go to in class review for tests.

Lectures are very interesting if you are into media and history. She is very laid back and really nice. You will have 4 exams in total, but she drops one. Weekly homework over topics in class. So many easy EC opportunities so make sure to take advantage of those as you can get up to 40 points. She does use Tophat so go to class to get easy points.

I got over 100% in this class with Erin. Take this class even if you don't need the credit. It's a ridiculously easy GPA booster and it's kind of interesting. I only went to class on syllabus day... This class isn't even in my major, just an elective. TAKE THIS CLASS ERIN IS AWESOME. Extra Credit is offered a lot and for a lot of points. HW is EASY
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tophat for lots of EC. You maybe should go to class for that and the review session before the exams but other than that you can learn everything from the tophat slides and google the terms on the study guides she posts. Drops lowest exam. Lots of other EC. Easy A but shes a qualified PR professional so her lectures are relevant and interesting.
Extra credit lectures available. Homework just graded for completion. Easy class.

Erin is one my the BEST professors I've encountered at Iowa State! She is so knowledgeable and has a lot of field experience to share. Even at 8 AM, she works so hard to keep her lectures relevant and interesting. Only 5 exams (drop one) and a short weekly assignment. TopHat is extra credit! If you have the opportunity to have Erin, take it!

Erin is the best PR professor at ISU. This class is a big group project, a medium sized single project and group discussion posts every week. Erin is a great, funny professor who truly cares about her students.

I LOVE this professor. She is a PR Professional and she knows what she is doing. She is passionate about what she is teaching and makes her lectures (even at 8 am) very interesting. She says the textbook is required and that you have to read it, but I didn't even open it once because I got so much interesting information from her lectures. Tophat

Great professor. One of the easiest courses you could possibly take. She gives you the test the week before the exam so you have the chance to look over and just memorize the answers. She's a very respectful professor and I would definitely take the course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! Her lectures are amazing!

Erin is a PR Professional and is extremely knowledgeable. Super easy tests every 3 weeks as long as you go to the review classes and study. No need to read the textbook, everything is discussed in lecture or can be found on Quizlets online. Easy homework once every week, Top Hat participation counts as extra credit. It's set up the same as JLMC101.

Even though this class is at 8am, Erin really makes it enjoyable. Super easy tests every 3 weeks as long as you go to the review classes and study. No need to read the textbook, everything is discussed in lecture or can be found on Quizlets online. Easy homework once every week, Top Hat participation counts as extra credit. Interesting course!

Although the lectures can seem long, Wilgenbusch is amazing to listen to. She uses TopHat for every lecture with questions that give you participation points and tests are every 3rd week at the testing center.

I love her. She's super awesome, understanding, and really knows her stuff. Extremely experienced. She's funny, and doesn't grade too many things. There's exam grade and then a tophat extra credit percentage at the end of the semester but she also has extra credit things here and there.
