I had JLMC 101 & PR 220 with Erin, and I LOVED them. You can most definitely tell she is enthusiastic about what she does. It is clear she is highly experienced in the PR field and has a great network. She offers extra credit, lectures are interesting bc of the way she speaks. No quizzes just tests -she prepares you very well for them

Don't bother buying the book. She never said anything about the weekly assignments, so make sure you check the course calendar or you will completely miss easy (and needed) points. She puts all the notes online so attendance isn't necessary, but go to the reviews if you want exams to go well and answer the tophat questions from home.

Here's what you do. 1.) Don't buy the book 2.) Participate in the top hat lectures, either in class or at home 3.) Go to the test review Friday's, she gives you every question on the test 4.) Do the weekly writing assignments and extra credit opportunities 5.) Pass with a 100%.
She is a great professor, but make sure you go. A good amount of tests with weekly questions. Review days before every test. DO NOT pack up early.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Erin is very caring and is always willing to work with you. If you show up to class, you will be able to receive extra credit points for TopHat. However, if you miss a class, you won't fall too behind. Every assignment (short 100-200 word essay each week) and test is very manageable. Take this class if you want an easy A while also learning a lot!

Super easy class. Mrs. W makes it exciting and connects with students on a modern level about social media platforms and the history about communication. It may seem like it's a boring topic but she makes it captivating. If you pay attention and put in a little effort you can get an easy A in the class.

Erin is great, but I found her lectures boring. You don't need to take notes or even really show up as long as you attend the exam review section - she tells you everything you need to know and additional study isn't usually necessary to get an A. The only writing you have to do is submit a short, 250 word essay following a prompt. Easy, easy, easy

Erin is very personable and makes the class a breeze. I studied  for about 10 minutes before each test and never got below a B. She's really fun to listen to, but be prepared to take a couple notes on the material not in the slides. She likes to go off book, so don't even bother reading it.

She is incredibly nice, knowledgeable, and experienced. She always tries to help students and her classes are easy to pass as long as you put in the required amount of effort. She is always in your corner as a student and very helpful in all areas. She cares a lot and makes you a better person and journalist afterwards.
Awesome teacher. Always in a good mood during lectures, very clear about assignments and tests, and she makes class interesting. If you have a chance to take a class with her, DO IT.

Most points in the course come from in-class assignments. Plenty of assignments throughout the semester, but overall it helps in learning the content. Tests are more practical than in most classes.  Can be a tough grader and isn't afraid to take off tenths of points, but rubrics come with almost every assignment which helps.

Great professor.  Really knows what she's talking about.  You won't get a syllabus outlining your class schedule - but you will instead have to check your course calendar on Blackboard which can get annoying.  Check for weekly assignments she puts on Blackboard - otherwise you won't know about them.  Easy A.

She is clear in what she talks about but a lot of the lectures are unnecessary to attend. The review for the tests she expects answers from students, otherwise will not help, but tests are not bad at all.

Erin is very nice and teaches a very interesting and fun class no matter what. She is very passionate about PR and her students. However, sometimes she talks to the students like we're children and can come off as very condescending. Show up to class for sometimes random class points. Very easy.
Erin is a great professor that is easy to talk to. She is very relatable and cares about her students. If you have the chance to take a class from her, do it!
Erin is amazing. She's clear, entertaining, and knowledgable. She made me feel that  I'm on the right path as a PR major.
This is the best teacher I ever had at Iowa State! She is so nice in and out of the lecture hall. She connects current information to different things in the world and that helps you learn easily

Very easy intro class, didn't even for most of the semester. Quizzes online for each chapter -- answers are above the quiz for you. Go to lecture day before test, she gives you the question bank -- easy A in the testing center. Pulled an easy A in the class overall.

Erin is the reason why I want to take on a career in Public Relations. This class is an easy A, but I enjoyed hearing her lectures. She is very knowledgable on the subject and is a professional in the field.
This is the easiest class at Iowa State. If you need an easy elective, take this class.

JLMC 101 is possibly the easiest class offered at Iowa State. If you look at the course calendar on BlackBoard, you will find out what days you have to go to class. I can honestly say that after the first test I only went to this class on review days. She gives you every possible question that could be on the test, you just have to find the answers

AWFUL teacher. Class is pointless and she teaches things so irrelevant. Uses guest speakers and videos as a way to not have to teach. Don't even try e-mailing her, she won't e-mail back. Test questions are either easy or make no sense. Won't own up to making bad test questions.

Professor Wilgenbusch makes this class as easy as could be. All of her assignments can be retaken until you get full points. The Friday before every exam, she gives you all the questions that will be on the exam. She gives you a full week to take exams as well. Super easy class and it is super easy to skip as well. Highly recommended!

Erin is an awesome professor. She really cares about PR and that shines through in her lectures. She provides study guides for every test so make sure to go to the class before the test opens up. I would take any class I could with her!
Totally cares about her students.

Her helpfulness was minimal when teaching this class. She gave very little direction as to what she expected from assignments and then would grade harshly. I found this teacher to be rude at times as well and very hard to listen to as her lectures were uninteresting and dragged on.
Great teacher. Gives you every test question in class. Down to earth and lets you watch movies occasionally
Easy class, gave all of the test questions beforehand and you just had to look them up in the book. Would've done a lot better if I went to class, but almost pulled an A anyways

The subject itself is not hard at all, and you can miss half the classes, show up for review days and be fine. There are sone in class points that you might miss, but overall she makes the tests fairly simple, and she is entertaining in class.

This was the easiest A I have ever gotten. You don't have to go to class except on the review days where she gives out all of the test questions. There are assignments online each week, but you can do them as many times as you want and they are only 5 multiple choice questions. She offers a ton of extra credit. It is impossible to not get an A

She is very different in 321 than 101. Very tough class, should only take if you are committed to PR. No extra credit, and attendance is required. Lots of in class projects that she has you do on your own, with little or no help. Negatives aside, she is still one of the best in Greenlee.
She gives test questions the class before test week which rocks, but sometimes the test questions are trivial and not that important to the overall class.
Super easy class. I haven't been to the lecture in over a month, and I currently have an A.

Great prof! Super easy class, and all test questions are given out before the test is posted online; essentially, everyone can and usually does get an A. If you do not attend class, which many people don't, be sure to come for review sessions and be wary of occasional in-class points.

Love her! She's always very peppy and her class is fairly easy! Gives you the exams before you take them so all you have to do is find the answers and study that. Will definitely take another class with her :)
She is always happy. Class is pretty easy. You don't have to every class to get a good grade. And she has great school spirit!

Had here for 101 after Barbara Mack tragically passed away. She was even totally ok with everyone calling her Erin. She was way too easy in this class. Taking 321 with her next semester, hopeful easy again

She teaches quite well. The classes are fun and interesting with discussions on current events and videos.Just attend the class regularly, study for the exam and you can easily have an A. Make sure to go for the extra credit opportunity events.

Wonderful teacher. She's a master at the subject. Assignments are fair and representative of the class. Took this as a communications elective as a science major. She made me interested in all aspects of PR. Put effort in to the class and it's an easy A. Easily my favorite teacher I've had at ISU.

Don't need to go to class at all. There are random in class points so that helps in the end but the tests are crazy easy so it's not the end of the world if you miss them. Everyone I know got over a 100% on basically all of the tests. She's a good teacher and actually knows what she's talking about. Very nice.

Intro to PR was definitely an easy A. Attendance wasn't mandatory but approximately 5-7 random 5 point assignments were given through out the semester so it was smart to attend. She was really knowledgeable on PR but seemed to maybe strongly dislike journalism. Overall, I enjoyed the class and passed with hardly any effort at all.
Easy enough class. As long as you show u, you'll get a good grade. There wasn't a ton of work to do outside of class. She was nice and encouraged students to ask questions during class.

Nice enough to talk to, she is polite however very difficult to deal with when working one on one. Here assignments were almost always unclear and usually graded rather harshly considering we had no idea what we were supposed to do. Several times our class was given the option to redo an assignment because she was not clear on what she wanted.

im not sure what everyone else is writing about. myself and others included found this teacher to be harsh and to the point. she is not forgiving or that nice. also, the class i took with her was NOT easy and there was quite a bit of homework (which she typically poorly described, which results in frustration and confusion).

Journalism 220 was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken at Iowa State and Erin fully acknowledged that. She's a really cool professor although her lectures pretty much just consist of her reading slides. Go to class to get all of the in class points and you'll get an A for sure.
She is extremely kind and helpful.  She is a very honest, gentle person.
Erin is an excellent professor. As long as you don't skip class, you will do all right in her class, as there's practically no homework.
Cool, fun class.  We do most of the work during the lab time so there's little homework, but she's a hard grader.  You should be prepared to become a good writer in this class.
PR class

This class is for PR majors ONLY! The professor runs down reporters daily. She teaches the class how to manipulate reporters. Attendance is a must with the in class assignments. A journalism student will be disappointed with the representation of their profession.She accuses journalists of doing what PR does-"spin"-the journalist's job is to unspin

Very easy class!  If you want an easy A this is it.  I think I got over 100% in the class.  She offers very generous extra credit.  But you really do have to go to class because that's where a lot of her quiz questions come from.  So go to class, pay some attention and you'll get an A!
No Comments

There was a lot of reading, quizzes, and assignments. It was very difficult to keep up each week. You will defiantly practice your Spanish writing, compression, and speaking in this course. The reading is very intense so be prepared!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A really good and engaging teacher, showed genuine interest in the topic of the seminar while letting students view the class through their own perspective. Canvas posts and final projects were great opportunities to research what interested you. The main issue would probably be heavy amounts of reading, but this allows for freer discussion time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. L is very well versed in the class and it's evident with how he prepares class. Took the class accelerated online, so it was a lot of reading and assignments but he always made sure students were prepared and available for any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The class can be difficult because it is commpletely in Spanish, however if you put in the effort to study and review the material before and after class you will be able to do well. Dr. L is very gracious and understanding but does expect you to participate a lot in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Four week online class that was accelerated! It was self-explanatory on Canvas with heavy work load, but if you stay on top of the assignments it is easy to pass the class. The textbook was used for the homework, quizzes, and tests. He provided great feedback on any assignments or quizzes. Also, there were 4 speaking quizzes only 2-3 min each.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: this class was a little rough. lots of participation, randomly called on students when it was clear that we didn't understand what was going on. this class had a crazy amount of homework in it. other teachers don't assign the amount he did

Dr. Ladner is very strict in his grading, but he is willing to help outside of class and strongly encourages students to speak to him during office hours. He typically graded all assignments in an extremely timely manner which was nice! He's nice and as long as you participate in class, you'll be fine

Professor Ladner is very critical in class to the point where someone does not want to answer his questions. His tests are easy and so are his extended responses. His lectures are difficult because he only speaks in Spanish. For example, when learning a new tense, its hard to absorb because its in Spanish.

The rumor is that 50% of his class will get a C- or lower and that was me even though I study and attended class. The test were in the testing center and they were really hard. I'm currently in a 102 class and getting an 89%. I liked him as a person, but hated him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took Portuguese as a trail class and overall Ladner did a good job. Very content heavy in the beginning but he learned how to adjust to our learning and saw realistic time to be dedicated to class. He appreciates participation. Quizzes were limited, but homework every class (either language, reading, or both). Passionate and humorous. Truly cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ladner was one of the best Spanish teachers I have had over my eight years of learning Spanish. He was always there to talk to kids if they needed help and always told students he was available for office hours. You have six tests and two big exams, otherwise it's just papers. Be ready to write research papers though, otherwise, very little hw.

He's not a bad professor but needs to work on being clear in what he wants and not contradicting himself. He's the kind of guy that if you call him out on something, he'll deny that he's wrong unless the entire class agrees that something's amiss. Overall, not a bad class. He's pretty helpful if you show willingness to learn.

Makes the class interesting, I was able to pay attention throughout every one of his classes without spacing off, and that's saying something. The grading in the class is a little tough but if you put the necessary work in you'll do fine.
Dr. Ladner essentially taught everything in class, however the homework that was assigned required the reading of the book. Very easy class if you put in the work.
Very helpful for everything, is available almost anytime of the day if you have questions, is willing to explain anything in more detail if necessary.
Professor Ladner is a very good instructor. He will make you put a lot in but you get a lot out of all the work. I'd take another class from him.
His lit classes are great.  He makes it all interesting.  It feels easy after taking the class, but that's because he's good help.
No Comments

This is my third semester with Ladner and I have never heard any of my classmates complain about him.  He's very nice, and very helpful.  It can be a tough class because there's a lot of work to do, but he goes at a good pace.
Such an awesome professor!  He is really easy to get along with and makes class fun- as hard as that may be to believe!  Very helpful and relaxed enviornment everyday.
He is a really fun professor! His tests are a little difficult, but if you go to class and do the assignments you should have no problem getting a good grade.
He is really funny, and likes to make u laugh. His teaching ablility could use some work, but I would suggest if you want to have fun in class sign up with Ladner.

He is a totally cool teacher! He likes to make jokes and have fun. He makes class very interesting and tries very hard to help you understand the material. The tests aren't too bad, just make sure you go to class.

Mr. Fujii was an outstanding TA throughout the course. He was always well-prepared for sections and took the time to break down difficult topics in a way that was easy to understand. He was patient, approachable, and genuinely cared about helping students succeed. His guidance and encouragement made a big difference in my learning experience.

Mr. Fujii was absolutely awesome! I loved having him as my TA, truly a great guy. He had great communication and he was able to break down hard topics into more manageable ideas to aid in my understanding! Loved having him 10/10.
Mr. Fujii was a great TA to have. He was always very willing to help me with understanding the content. The content itself is relatively difficult, but Mr. Fujii tried to make it digestable.

He is very knowledgeable and clearly understands the material; however, the lectures can feel monotone and dry. He typically goes through slides quickly and then focuses on practice problems. Attendance matters for points, and his office hours are very helpful if you're struggling. Overall, I really like him and his class. Get to know your profs!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I liked him

All he does is click through slides all class that are so information dense it's impossible to take anything in and learn. Needs to break things down to a basic step-by-step process of how to solve the problem.

He is an okay professor for dynamics. He reads off slides and posts the slides on canvas so you don't have to go to class but he does use tophat to check attendance. I succeeded in this course because of all the practice that he posts for each exam. Pretty mid professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. He is always willing to answer questions during or after class. Plus gives in-depth email responses when not in class for homework problems. He provides supplemental example videos for extra practice which I found helpful. Overall, you are provided with all the resources you need to do well in this course if you work for it.

I think some of these reviews are a little outdated. I took dynamics with him this semester and had an excellent experience. Secor is there to make sure you learn the material effectively. If you listen to what he has to say, you will do fine, he has excellent advice. Responds to emails in a timely manner, helpful outside of class.

The professor was a solid dynamics professor. Lectures are a bit boring and there are expectations to watch videos and read lecture notes ahead of class so examples can be covered. Lots of midterm exams but grading is very lenient, plenty of review material and strategies to help students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class heavily reliant on mechanics of materials. Exams are super specific on mechanics of materials content with tricky calculations with little preparation in class. Lectures are just reading off his slides. Higher order thinking questions dominate the exam despite only being glanced at in class. He makes you work for the answers.

Class is taught heavily from a mechanics of materials perspective. Every chance he gets you are forced to do in depth analysis of how different processes react. Lots of emphasis is put on higher order thinking questions where you need to relate concepts to questions. Exams are extremely specific compared to  what is taught in class. Boring lectures

I'll give this professor the benefit of the doubt as he's only been teaching for 1-2 years; however, his lectures were pretty boring. The averages for exams in my class were pretty low, as there is so much content to remember. He allowed us to use a note sheet for exams which was nice. There was one group project at the end of the semester

The professor is incredibly boring, reads directly off of slides, and does review kahoots. None of this helps to teach the absurd amount of unnecessary topics in this class. The exams are too difficult/packed for the allowed time, especially with the curveballs that are put into them. Combined with the harsh grading this class is worse than ME 345.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Secor is fine, but 1st year professor is ROUGH. His lectures are boring, doesn't give example problems, A LOT of material, and he doesn't have an ME degree. 2 exams determine entire grade, they're super long with calculation's that have 5 parts for each question. Class is not interesting, unless you're into manufacturing. Final is group project
He provides very simple to read lectures but does not elaborate on many topics. However, he is more than willing to meet outside of class to improve understanding & meet accessibility needs.
He I literally the definition of I'm just a chill guy (love the 423L) it's hard bit very rewarding and the instructors are lovely

Jeff was a great lab instructor!! He was always willing to help students when needed and give his input. He wants students to learn and enjoy lab. There's a final presentation at the end of the semester which is very easy. Overall, I'd highly recommend taking this lab with Jeff!
I love him so much. SO kind and cares for students.  Crazy intelligent, amazing at explaining concepts, and willing to have in depth conversations.  Highly recommend him - he is the best!
Good class

Brilliant guy who is very well respected. Class lacked structure but I liked it. Essner is very caring but incapable of "dumbing things down" so you'll have to do your own research and be motivated to learn by yourself. Do not take this course if you have not taken genetics/upper level biology classes (even though they are not prereqs)

Clicker questions are a thing, so go to class. Homework is really easy due to quizlet. Tests are hard. That one topic that he had on the screen for less than 20 seconds? Yeah, there will be about 5 questions on it on the test. I emailed him before about clarification on the syllabus and his only reply was check the syllabus.

As long as you come to class, you're fine. The majority of the available points in the course come from in-class worksheets and clicker questions. The tests are semi-difficult, but he drops the lowest one and only puts material from the lectures on the exams

Ridiculous class. Crazy hard. I have always been a straight-A student and before this class, I hadn't gotten below an A in all of my college or high school careers, but I was consistently getting low Bs and Cs. Don't focus on big picture. For the exams, you must know every little detail. One exam was over 2 months (10 chapters) of information.

He's a great guy, very nice and easy to work with. However, he will do a lot of work for you in between lab sessions so you don't learn as much as you could. Also he's pretty ambiguous so you kind of have to fill in the blanks yourself. This class is fun; give it a try! Genetic modification ftw!

Very difficult to keep up with during class. I stopped taking real notes due to the speed. Does not clarify well and is very monotone. Assigns far too much LearnSmart homework without providing ample amount of time to comfortably finish. Over all he makes a very difficult course all the more frustrating.

Does impressive research, but that doesn't make him a good teacher. Speaks in a soft high-pitched voice, and describes things ambiguously. Frequently confused and skipped the chapter on sex organs because he "does not have the emotional maturity." Nice guy, just too timid and out of place when trying to mold young minds. Avoid him if possible.

He is a decent enough teacher. Lecture is mandatory because of clicker points, but those really saved me in the end. I averaged 55% on all of the tests and still ended up with a C in the class. The homework is easy, and about half of the test questions come directly from clicker questions.

EXTREMELY boring class and professor, the content put people to sleep every class. The homework was easy but the tests hard. He is a very opinionated professor and states it often when talking about GMOs. If you don't have to take this class then DONT, take a more interesting class with a better professor or get a different bio212 professor!!

This man should not be a teacher. He has a difficult time being clear in his explanations but is willing to help if you ask. He is an OK teacher the class just sucks. I would recommend just paying attention in class and taking notes after because it is almost impossible to keep up with him.
A hard class with a great professor. He explained things as best as he could and was always willing to answer any questions he was able to.

He was quite usless and didn't really help me if asked. His lectures were fast paced and i couldn't keep up taking notes (even WITH a computer to type). His classes are mandatory with clicker quizzes and in class activities (that don't really help at all). He has a thing about having 30min lectures and 15 min "activities". not.good.
You have all day for his online tests, you can do participation online (including extra credit) I have taken a few of his classes and would continue to do so in the future.

He can be a little dull but overall a good professor, he opens up time to discuss during class so he isnt talking the whole time. He gave lots of opportunity for attendance points fall semester in case of covid or not coming to class and completing over the requirement became extra credit. Really easy to talk to and makes it easy to talk in class

Kyles lectures were hard to pay attention to and were dull. The content was interesting but it could have been better. He is very willing to meet during office hours for clarification over subjects. The exams aren't bad and the papers require time but it is possible to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pauli is one of the most approachable professors I've ever had. She cares about her students and wants them to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She cares about her students and is very approachable. Also incredibly experienced and explains concepts clearly. I definitely recommend her.

Amazing, amazing, amazing. Tries hard to keep classes creative and engaging. Very seasoned in broadcasting and communication and incorporates her professional expertise into classroom. Encourages meaningful conversations. Not just a personable and humorous lecturer, but beloved by all students and very genuine. I cannot recommend her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Eshbaugh is a phenomenal professor! I've taken her a couple of times and by far my favorite. She cares about what she teaches and has great stories to include so nothing feels like you're just being taught material. She's also the head of gerontology so getting in good with her opens a lot of internship and job opportunities no matter your major
Awesome
Very good in all aspects. It's too bad she left.
Elaine is now in KS City; But she was a great proff to go out and get drinks with after class!!
Excellent teaching skills. Genuinely interested in my success.  Hope to take mroe of her classes.

I learned probably more from this class than almost any other one I've taken. She's really nice and wants you to do well. The tests were harder than I thought they would be, but you just have to do the study guide. She can be really funny too.
Best teacher ever, makes difficult subjects duck soup. Excellent upbringing and genes are apparent here. Im sure she will make a fine full professor.
Really fun.  Great storries!
makes topics interesting, gives good study guides for exams
Great teacher, very intellegent.  She is willing to help everyone.  Knows her stuff very well and has a nack for helping others understand what she is teaching.

Wow! Had a lesson with him and not only is he extremely nice but he definitely gives you a confidence boost in the process. In a department where you can feel inadequate, he makes you feel so good about yourself. Very wise and reassuring!

As a music teacher, he is increadibly supportive and you always leave a lesson with him in a positive mood.  Those of you who hated english with him is probably because he doesn't teach english....you rated the wrong professor!

Oh come on...  He really is very nice and has a great sense of humor.  I have horrible performance anxiety normally, so I should have been a wreck singing for him, but he made me feel very at ease. :)
No Comments

Shes so nice and welcoming and always trying to help students

Thank you Eunha Jeong

This class was really great. Dr. Lena is a very easy person to communicate with. Attendance wasn't mandatory but very highly recommended because there would be in class activities but you could make those up at home. Her review sessions before exams are very helpful. She is super accommodating and will always try to work something out with you.

Amazing professor. Clear and easy to follow lecture slides. Has great knowledge in the field as well. Easy to do good if you follow her notes and lectures. Highlights things on quizzes/exams in red so super easy to understand and do good.

Very nice and understanding professor, but her lectures are very boring. For each class she has power points consisting of 30+ slides and she reads each one Word. For. Word. Unfortunately, you need to go to class because she does in class activities after every single lecture and you will fail if you miss those.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She really cares about the students and tries to make sure that everyone understands. You need a scantron so you may want to buy a book but it's all in the lecture!

Do not take a class with this professor if you have a choice. The lecture is useless; he speaks too quietly and is completely unintelligible the entire semester. Any studying or learning you have to do is on your own time. In-class quizzes twice a week on nothing you've learnt in class.

This professor was awful. I dropped within two weeks. Please do not take him. He doesn't even go over the content and instead rambles on about something else. There was no syllabus or clear instructions for what to do.

There are also in-class quizzes and the TAs do everything for him. I would never take a class with him again.

Professor Choi tends to veer off on tangents often during his lectures and doesn't really project well to the class (if you're in the back of the lecture hall you won't hear him). He is a kind person, however his teaching leaves a lot to be desired. Thankfully it doesn't matter because ECON 1010 is a cakewalk.

The class is not very difficult due to the extreme curve based and many extra credit assignments that were extremely easy to complete. Though the professor consistently rants about subjects not included in 
 and at times goes against the information included the two weekly quizzes that account for a large portion of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst Teacher I have ever had. I don't know if it is the fact that he talks about Square Watermelons for no reason, Bullet Trains or the fact that he started the first ever class with, "Hitler was a bad guy but....". He had no structure at all, would get lost in his own thoughts and start talking about random things.

He talks about random stuff all class. I didn't learn a single thing from any lecture I had to learn everything on my own through the textbook. Also he made us take a quiz every Monday and Friday which is unnecessary.

Do not take Econ 101 with Eun Choi. There are quizzes every monday and friday over things we don't learn about in class. I would reccomend reading the book and doing practice questions there if you want any success in this class. The quizzes and tests are the only grades in the grade book, but there is a huge curve which helps. Don't take this.
Read the textbook he doesn't explain anything and spends the class talking about whatever he feels like that day usually about his trip's to China or Korea.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: talks about watermelon cubes, soju alcohol, wine making, hurricanes, a pond from his homeland that was filled with concrete, crappy lecture presentation on docs that was made right before class. TA's that interrupt during the middle of a quiz/ exam for common knowledge. only thing that is nice is the practice quiz/ exam.
You gotta use other resources
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No homework, which was a win, and quizzes every Monday and Friday. Lectures on Wednesday are pointless. A big grading curve as a 76% is still an A-. This helps as the tests are very challenging. He is easy to get in contact with outside of class. Most people will do decent in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drop this class as soon as you register for it. It's been a nightmare trying to figure out what material I actually need to study to pass any exams or quizzes, both of which make up the entire class grade. No class should have to have a grading curve that turns a 75% into a 95%, however it as saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would highly advise you to drop this class if you registered. Quizzes twice a week and three exams are the grading criteria. His lectures do not cover much of what's on the exams. Two things saved me from his class: only reading the textbook (only going to lectures for quizzes) and the insane grade curve. Good luck to you if you have him.
Lecture Is awful Two quizzes a week
No point showing up to lectures.
he goes on tangents and is extremely difficult to understand. doesn't cover the topics for the quizzes and there are two quizzes each week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst lectures I have ever sat through. Professor talks about vacations he has taken during lectures instead of teacher students the material of the course. Would highly recommend dropping and getting another professor if you have the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You don't really have to show up (even though he says you should) and most of the test answers are on CourseHero because they're take home. Homework should be done yourself because they take an effort to catch people copying off CourseHero so just be careful of that. Overall, easy A especially if you want to get done with your liberal requirements.

Dr. Eslinger is the BEST professor I have ever had. Yes, Religion 210 is a very easy course. However, Dr. Eslinger really cares about his subject matter and presents it in a very unbiased manner. Lectures are not mandatory to get a good grade however I attended every one because I enjoyed listening to him. Great guy, Great Class.

Dr. Eslinger is awesome. Sometimes he talks really fast during his lectures and it's hard to keep up (but honestly half the class doesn't take notes). Show up to class because he gives extra credit for attendance on low attendance days. You do one assignment a week and have to answer 5- 6 questions. You use all 3 texts, but you can share some.

GREAT PROFESSOR!!! I had friends that were in Religion 205 and they had twice the amount of homework and material was much harder. Prof Eslinger allows you to take tests online at home so you are able to use your resources, even the final! He also posts his notes so its not mandatory to go to class, but he does give away points some days!
You can take all tests at home and some of them are online. You do have to read a good amount for each week but with reading and going to class you should be able to get a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazing. Weekly reading assignments take a lot of time, at least if you want to actually learn the material. At-Home online exams with lecture slides posted. Don't let this deceive you, as a lot of the tested material is spoken/watched during lecture or buried in the textbook. You will pass, but an A requires effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is such a good professor. He is very passionate about what he teaches and makes the subject very interesting. 10/10 recommend taking a class with him.
Great prof, very interesting!!
I switched from a 10am to an 8am just to have him and I have no regrets. His lectures are entertaining, the class isn't to difficult, and all assignments are open book.

There is a good bit of writing for the weekly assignments. However there is no required minimum or maximum, write until you feel that the question has been answered. Mr. Eslinger gives wonderful lectures and most importantly, is very fair. When we covered modern religions, there was no bias. Just the facts.

Easy class, but all the lectures were very interesting and I learned a lot about religion and culture. Eslinger is a very interesting guy and has an intriguing background. The big textbook is recommended for weekly assignments, but save your money and find the rest of the smaller books on the library website.
He is the best

He is a super nice guy and good professor. Often extra credit points for coming to class on non-homework days because nobody comes. The lectures are very boring and you don't need to take notes since all tests are at home, open notes and usually get 100%. I have 3 extra points than available in the class. Weekly reading assignments are super easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easiest class I've ever taken. I missed a total of 2 points.

He was a great professor and I really learned a lot in this class. He is a very interesting person and made the lectures interesting. As long as you show up to turn in your homework and fill in the blanks on the notes, it is the easiest class I have ever taken. The people who do poorly put no effort into the class.
Lectures were engaging and very helpful. Most amazing thing about him is that he shows a lot of cool videos and tells stories behind the text. The best professor I've ever had at ISU.

Eslinger is a fantastic professor. His lectures are great and he makes them as interesting as possible. All the exams are open note, open book and are over things he says or you watch during lecture so if you don't attend lecture you will not pass. Weekly assignments don't take that long. He truly cares about what he teaches and his students.

All of the tests are online open note, the lowest grade I have gotten on a test is a B. There is a weekly assignment that is over each weekly chapter about 4 questions. There is also extra credit opportunities. Go to class! Sometimes he counts attendance points and also print out the slides and fill them out. They help on the tests!

Eslinger is a very good teacher. He seems to be very organized, friendly, reasonable, and knowledgeable. Presents the material in an unbiased fashion. Tests are open book/note. Weekly homework assignment takes about an hour a week.

Loved him so much I went out of my way to take another class with him next semester. Incredibly clear and helpful. Tests are all online and open-note (final included). Has many extra credit opportunities. One of the best professors I've ever had. I will miss him very much when I can't take more of his classes.

Brian is probably one of the best professors I've ever had! He's very helpful and will answer your e-mails within the hour. His lectures are very charismatic and he keeps you interested. He truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed. The class overall is very easy if you show up to class, as he does a lot of attendance papers.

I had 205 and 210 with Eslinger, and they were the easiest classes I have ever taken. He is always so excited to teach and knows so much about religion and uses many stories, videos and examples . There were short weekly homework assignments, open note exams, and attendance. There are tons of EC opportunities. Impossible to get lower than an A.

Great professor, actually teaches what he loves. Easy A too, open book tests that are online. A weekly assignment that takes about an hour. Sometimes he takes attendance points. Great class, highly recommend.

Great Guy! Makes religion so interesting and knows exactly what he is talking about. He aims more for you to learn and diversify yourself then making it hard and all about grades. Definitely would take all the classes he offers.

I have never been so inspired by a professor. He led amazing in class discussions free of judgement or bias. The class itself was so easy, you can get a A without trying. The students always bragged about him, we even invited friends to come see him speak because it was just that great. Best professor I will ever have and definitely a role model.

Eslinger is easily my favorite professor at the moment. He gives such great insight, has tons of experience in his field and will reward you for coming to class. Sitting in the front is recommended if you want to get to know him. Very lenient and understanding if you're unable to come to class, don't print your assignment, etc. Print out his notes!
Show up and get an "A".  Open book tests.  Unbelievably easy.

Overall, I thought the professor was good. The class had a weekly reflection assignment, so be sure to stay on top of that. Otherwise, all of the exams are on blackboard, so that was really nice. As long as you read, or at least skim the chapters, you'll do fine. Attendance isn't mandatory, but the lectures were interesting.
He is a good professor. Has 15 HW during the semester and you can miss one. The exams are online and all multiple choice. Overall, an easy A class and a well structured course!

Dr. Eslinger, by far one of the best instructors at ISU. He is very enthusiastic and does his best to transmit the material to the students in an engaging manner i.e. through movies, pictures, and in-class activities. His tests are open note and most, if not all, the questions come strictly from the book. I definitely recommend you take him.
Professor Eslinger needless to say is the best professor I ever had. He is really really helpful and will reply the emails you send within the hour most of the time. BEST PROFFESOR EVER!

Professor Eslinger is by far one of the best professors I have had at Iowa State. He is very helpful and very merciful when it comes to missed assignments. You don't have to go to class but he will have pop-assignments without warning so watch out for that. I definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Eslinger is extremely knowledgeable about world religions.  His class was super easy and if you are interested in learning about religion I'd definitely recommend him.  Just be aware, lectures can get pretty boring some days.

Dr. Brian Eslinger is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is funny, respectful, genuine, and is very smart and willing to make time to meet with his students outside of class for help or any questions in general. His 205 class is pretty easy, and if you don't miss anything, you won't have any problems getting an A. Great guy and professor!
this guy was the best professor i ever had. great at his job

AWESOME AWESOME Teacher.  If you dont get an A in this class then you are doing something wrong.  All the tests are online on blackboard not in the testing center.  He enjoys teaching and makes it fun for you
best. teacher. ever.
Very easy but you actually learn something as well. you can tell he loves what he teaches

It's not simply that his course is easy, but that he passionately lectures in a semi-participatory style that is not intimidating in the least. Very smart, very approachable. Quizzes occasionally feature tongue-in-cheek answer choices, so he has a great sense of humor. Plus, looks like Bill Nye. That can never hurt.
Amazing
Very good professor. Knows alot about world religions and is definitely and pluralist. Engages students in discussion and assigns very simply homework. Great professor and good person.
The best
SUPER SUPER EASY. plenty of extra credit. lectures through powerpoint, which is posted online. Tests/quizzes were all multiple choice, very easy.
Best professor to take Relig 210 with. Really knows his stuff and keeps class interesting. Definitely recommend for diversity requirement!!

Easiest professor you will ever have. It's not necessary to go to class except on quiz days and when you have to hand in homework. He lets you use notes for your quizzes and sometimes work in groups. Super easy final exam as well. Best class ever!! Take it for an easy A and a super cool professor!
really good teacher.  energetic about the topics and the material is actually interesting.  easy quizzes/tests and a good class to take care of your US diversity credit
Literally the easiest A I have ever received.

Easiest class ever.  I went to class but it is definitely not necessary.  He's a really nice guy, get to know him. Book has website, so you don't need to buy it.  I definitely recommend this class for your diversity requirement!

This is my 4th year at ISU, and this was the easiest class I have ever taken in my college career. No need to buy the textbook, no need to really even go to class. Your whole grade is based on 5 easy quizzes - just study his slides an hour beforehand.
Class is pretty easy if you read through all the notes he gives out. No tests, just quizzes worth 20 points every 2-3 weeks, and a reflection paper at the end. No final. Awesome class.
Very interesting class.  Eslinger gave tremendous insight to the class and made it easier to learn.  His structure of the class made it easy to learn and fun.
Nice, easy, and very caring and passionate about what he teaches!!!!!
Easy tests, not a lot of homework, AWESOME man. I learned a lot and he's passionate about what he teaches.
Really nice and caring professor

He is one of the most caring, nicest professors that I have ever met. He got us things many times (when he didn't have to). His personality rocks and he teaches the class really well. He's always available as well.
boring teacher, not the best, but if you put in work it's not too hard and you should do okay.  Make sure you know the readings and short videos inside and out for the exams.

His class is very boring. Mostly reads off of powerpoint word for word. Don't learn a lot about Spanish storieshow to analyze them. One 250 word paper per week, one story to read for each day. SUPER easy testsall homework is online. Gives good feedback, though is tough on grammar. Easy essay gradertest grader. Doesn't prepare you for Span 333

he gets his words jumbled up and gets confused and has to correct himself a lot, which gets pretty confusing. But overall I would recommend him for a teacher because he is really helpful and a pretty easy grader.
BORING RANTS ON AND ON ABOUT NONSENSE.
he teaches the class like its your major, don't expect a break. speaks only in Spanish, usually correcting himself multiple times. pretty sure its a Filipino dialect and not true Spanish

Very good professor who cares about his subject, teaches well by using Spanish at all times. Rather easy if you pay attention and do the assignments. I did not actually learn that much from this course, but it was still an enjoyable experience.
Taken to fill a diversity.  An easy pass, but don't bother with this class if you actually care about the subject matter.  Attendance, 6 X 200-word essays and two essay exams are all he gives.
I took this class for my diversity requirement. It was completely useless. I never felt that there was any specific point to the class. Take something else if possible.

GREAT CLASS! He is the best Spanish teacher I have had so far at Iowa State. The entire class is spoken in Spanish but he does a great job getting the information into terms that you understand. He keeps you involved in class so that you don't fall behind and gives a study guide for every test. I would take him again in a heartbeat.

Great class lots of info. Prof. assigns lots of readings. WebCT quizzes are easy as long as you've read assignments and have his notes. Big exams are recycled WebCT quizzes questions and a few essay q's. Had PP for class and some old videos. He really tried to make class a lot of fun. Nice professor.
Enthusiastic, flexible, fun class.
No Comments
No Comments

I wouldn't recommend taking a class with him. He was very prideful and the students were always wrong, he never was. I don't think he was really helpful either. I did like his lecture slides but I ended up teaching myself the entire semester and I always went to lecture

I did not like his teaching style. I pretty much taught myself. Also he seems to talk very condescending towards the class. He had an exam on vieshea friday. His exact words were "I wanted to see how it affects the scores" 3/10 at best
....not good. Not good at all

Great prof. Problem was that class was @ 8AM so nobody attended much. I attended almost all lectures and got A. Has easy 1.5-2 hr. lab. Recitation class has quizzes and homework at the end of the week. Gives you one side of paper for equations on tests (write as much as you can on those). He is from Ukraine yet very clear. Great slides.

Dr. Levin is a great professor. He took extra time out to help me with things I didn't understand. When he does explain things he does it very well and in a way you don't understand. He is very passionate about physics and it shows so that made the class very interesting. His accent is really cool too!

One of the best professors I have ever had. He really made me excited about physics and I didn't think I would ever enjoy it. He make sure I understood everything and took time out just to explain things to me. He makes class very interesting and is kind of funny. He also has a very cool accent.

He definitely wants you to learn, and he loves teaching.  You can tell he's still interested in intro physics, and he wants you to be too.  He doesn't explain everything thoroughly, but what you miss in lecture you can figure out in recitation.

Only requires a 74% in order to get an A. That doesn't mean you can goof off though, you still have to take the time to learn the material.  Try to do well early in the semester--attend lecture, do assignments, prepare cheat sheets for tests, etc.  I did really well throughout the semester and only needed 19% on the final to maintain an A!  His accent is a bit tricky to pin down early in the semester, but it gets easier throughout the semester.  I would recommend *not* taking notes from powerpoint because he posts them all online within an hour or two after class.  Its easier to figure out what he's talking about if you just watch and listen.  Just take notes from stuff he writes on the board.  Class seems much more challenging when you're in lecture and the HW questions seem like they may be challenging, but they end up being fairly easy if you know what all the variables stand for.  All in all, this class just requires a little bit of time to get the work done.

Awesome guy!  Has passion for what he is teaching and it shows!  He wants you to pass, that is what's important to him!  Great teacher... he got me excited about physics.. and I am an english major!!!
Good professor.  Mumbles during lecture a bit so sit up front.  He made the class worthwhile and interesting.  Not an easy class (no matter who teaches), so I had to give him a 3/5 for easiness.

One of the worst professors I have had thus far in my college career, terrible at explaining things and the personality of a toddler. This woman should be a preschool teacher, not a college professor.

Was good about giving information, but not good with technology. There were multiple "technological difficulties" that interrupted the class each lecture, which made her not very respected by the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She goes through lectures quickly and theres always tech problems. She doesnt take the time to completely explain concepts or answer students questions. The math is pretty easy, it just takes some practice. You get a periodic table that you can write notes on the back of to use during quizzes and exams. 3-4 graded TopHat questions every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Stephanie is very willing to help her students whenever they need. She is a bit socially awkward and sometimes moves through lecture too fast to actually answer questions. She explains most topics very well and puts all her lectures up online to rewatch. The class itself isn't bad especially if you took chem in high school. Overall, a mediocre prof
She goes through material too quick and always has some sort of technical problem. She is also impatient and doesnt answer questions well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Was a very good instructor. Made use of all alloted class time but did not make the class drag on. Made sure that everyone felt welcome and seemed happy to help with any questions.
The professor is very chill, and he allows late submission, which is really helpful if you like to procrastinate. His lectures are okay, but it's overall a really fun class.
Ryan was as fair as an instructor can get. If you put in the work on papers he will grade you accordingly. He made the class a lot more manageable with his wittiness.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor with such an amazing knowledge of computational linguistics. I would absolutely take another class of his.

Evgeny was inarguably one of the best professors I have ever had. He cares for his students, makes time to support them, and did nothing but his best.. History of EngLang is an intensive course, but if you go to the study sessions w/ him and TAs, you'll do a lot better. He also was very gracious and helpful after Rona hit, and things went online.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor and person. I audited his grad class, and I was fascinated by what he was explaining about computers, the more complex it was. I struggled sometimes to follow but I didn't complain. He did manage to spark an interest in me to go into his area from plain linguistics.

He did coding research in Russia and changed to linguistics, yet still knowledgeable, passionate, and easy to understand. He straight up said that he hates teaching, but does more than any other professor to get input on class policies, takes the job very seriously, and is funny. Only complaint is that recitation (every 2/3 classes) was redundant.

He is extremely enthusiastic. He is hyper-intelligent in that he is fast with his smarts. Lectures are fast and condensed, questions are opened up to more answers than what you asked for or they are given direct simple answers (depending on the question). As long as you keep in mind that he is very interactive, you'll do great.

Evgeny is a darn good professor. He absolutely knows what he is talking about and is pretty good at conveying that. He can start to speak really quickly if no one stops him, it sort of slowly builds up until he is just flying. He lets students have a lot of input on the class (we voted on book, attendance policy, etc.). Hilarious (but crude).

The first thing he stated on the first day of class was that he is teaching as a punishment by the university for unproductive research. He is Russian and pretty humorous at times. You can tell Evgeny is a smart guy, but most of the things he said went over my head. Attend class, otherwise you won't understand the material and you'll be behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Evgeny is hilarious, even without meaning to be.  He gets excited about the smallest things and goes on tangents about them.  It's clear he doesn't like teaching very much(he flat-out told us this in class), but if you ask him about his research, you can see that he really does love this topic in general.

Don't let his long name and accent fool you--Evgeny is a pretty good professor who knows his stuff. He's better at explaining in than many English-speaking teachers. No textbook use, and I didn't have to take the final because my grade was high. Just take notes and you'll be fine, he wants everyone to succeed--he listens to his students' complaints

Evgeny is a great professor. He is extremely passionate about linguistics and technology. He adjusts the class so that everyone can be successful and he allows you to work in groups. He also provides lots of class time to work on assignments. On top of all that, he is willing to help students and wants everyone to get an A. Go to class, get an A.
This guy is the man. He knows his stuff and will do anything to help a student if they are an advocate for themselves. Extremely on spectrum, but that is what makes him so entertaining.

Evgeny is probably one of my favorite professors. He can sometimes talk over some people's heads without realizing it, but he explains everything rather well. He obviously cares, and he tries to make the class interesting. It's hard to cater to El Ed and Ling students, he does a pretty good job.

He caters to the students who understand the material and is a people pleaser. He taught us more material we did not need to know than what we did. I gained nothing from this class. He is nice  but that does not mean he teaches well.

He's a very intelligent and interesting professor. He clearly knows his material, though he occasionally loses the class because of this. However, he is incredibly focused on student learning and will change the class to accommodate to the students very happily. He re-shifted the grades of the class and gave us the option of canceling the final!

Evgeny is by far one of my favorite professors of all time. He is very funny, knowledgeable and helpful. He uses a lot of experiences from his background to connect with topics learned in class. He can be very blunt in correcting students mistakes, but don't let that keep you from asking him questions!

Evgeny is just the best professor ever. I am very lucky to have him as my professor. Although he sometimes might need more teaching experience, but most of the time he is doing just great - very understandable, informative and entertaining.

Great professor. Does a great job of teaching the difficult topic of when language and computers meet. Lots of hands on activities. One odd thing he does is a spoken mid term, but I found it easier than a standard one. Extra-credit opportunities. At times boring but overall a great professor.

Absolutely horrible professor. He is an extremely knowledgeable professor, and is very passionate about the subject. However, the manner in which he presents the material is jumbled, doesn't flow together, and is seemingly pointless most of the time. He should probably stick to a career in which he works on computers, rather than teaching students.
Knowledgeable and passionate about subject. Presents material in a manner that engages interest.

I had this prof in the 1980s. Unfortunately, there is not a category for rating her intelligence. I still remember her and what she taught to this day. I am a copy editor and what I learned has had a great impact on me.

Helen is obviously a highly intelligent individual who has published in peer-reviewed journals and has a wide command of the theory of rhetoric and communication. However, her class sessions and assignments were distressingly vague - to the point that had to take an Incomplete to finish my papers in 506 - but happily, she gave me good marks.
Horrible teacher. The class should be straight forward and easy but she doesn't explain anything with clarity. She has quizzes and a final exam which is ridiculous for an English course.

Absolutely TERRIBLE! Worst teacher I've had at any level. Grading isn't too bad but I couldn't stand her, her stupid assignments, or her awful job at trying to explain what to do for those assignments.
worst teacher i've ever had at ISU, avoid at all costs, she's not a real tough grader but she'll ruin the class and make things more difficult than they need to be

I loved Judi. She was so caring & nice, I wish class had been more than just once a week. Since the class is repeatable I am going to try to take it as many times as I can. She took us on interesting field trips and introduced us to great professional connections in Ames. I am not a business major, but I feel like I actually learned useful things.
If every teacher was as helpful as Judi I wouldn't hate going to my other classes.  Best Instructor at ISU by far.
No Comments
Extremely tough grader. If you are not a favorite, don't expect a good grade (ROTC seems to make you on her good side).

As much as she really helped me to understand the class, she was an incredibly strict grader. She once told me she found an old essay of hers from college and would've given it a B. She expects everyone to be perfect writers. I don't think anyone got a solid A in that class. And a group project due the day after Thanksgiving break was brutal.

Horrible professor. Terribly unclear with every assignment she gives. Extremely hard grader and picks out every single little flaw in your work. At the end of the semester, she gave us a group project a week before Thanksgiving and and made it due the day we get back. When asked how this would work, she responded with "you'll figure it out".

Belittled students and made it clear she was above all. Very hard grader leaving no room for error. Gives you a chance to correct your essays but doesn't give much back in the long run. I tried to switch sections but it was too late :(

Very tough grader.  She never says what her political views are, but makes it very obvious and if you side with her in your papers, your grades will go up. I was a 4.0 student in high school and this is the one class my 1st semester of college where I didn't get an A.

At first I didn't really like the class and would have liked to change sections, but after the first few assignments, it got better and she became a more fun teacher. The syllabus is very important to keep you on track in the course. If I had to do it again, I would still take her class.
Not a good professor. Multiple students have had rude experiences with her as well as rude comments written on their papers. Worst grader I have come across at Iowa State.
Worst teacher I've had. Extremely hard grader and her instructions for her essays are very broad and confusing. Drop the class while you can.

This professor is the worst professor I have had throughout my schooling.  Her grading is tough, she treats people as inferior and she gives several pop quizzes from the book.  Her instructions are very broad and when you ask for her help she leaves you clueless.  If you have her and want to get a decent grade then switch now!

Unless you have the capability to write like an author or professional writer, switch out of this class. She wont work with you or help you outside of class. She is an impossible grader. She is funny the first couple weeks, so don't let that convince you to stay in her class. She becomes rude. Goodluck if you're in her class and don't switch.

Unless you have the capability to write like an author or professional writer, switch out of this class. She wont work with you or help you outside of class. She is an impossible grader. She is funny the first couple weeks, so don't let that convince you to stay in her class. She becomes rude. Goodluck if you're in her class and don't switch

Prof. Eyestone didn't make the class particularly enjoyable even though English is my favorite subject. I liked her a lot, but her teaching seemed very unimaginative and by the book, especially for an honors course. Overall a fair professor, just didn't do enough to make the material new and engaging.
She is a tough grader. She is very opinionated and likes so express her political views.
Nice person but a very tough grader. We didn't do much in class.
She's quirky and fun. A pretty tough grader for essays, but lets you use notes for the midterm.

Did an amazing job at teaching the material made it fun and cracked jokes and had a tendency to bring treats around test time and after test time when the class did well he also explained everything clearly and went over things as many times as needed 
Best econ professor I have had

Mr. Butcher is an awesome lecturer. He's young, so he understands if you have other commitments interfering with class or homework and is willing to work with you. He also brings cookies to class from time to time. If you attend lectures and office hours with questions you have, you can no doubt pass the class.

Butcher was an amazing professor and taught Econ really well. I felt like I actually learned something from him. My only complaint was that the exams were weighted a majority of your grade (80%), but as long as you go to office hours and pay attention it's not too difficult to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Butcher does a really good job preparing you for exams and helping you know what you need to do to succeed. He is enthusiastic to help students in office hours, and he is very funny and interactive in class as well. Occasionally he skims over topics he deems less important, but as long as you review them in the textbook  you'll be fine
Dr. Sabzikar is a pretty humorous and easygoing guy. His course materials are quite organized and grading was lenient.

He was a nice human being, but not a good professor for me. He came to class unprepared, and wasn't helpful in office hours. He would just do the problems with no explanation, and would fly through the problems in class. He said the material we were doing was "easy" which was a little condescending.
He is one of the best prof so far. He also solves problems on the board, which is easier than PowerPoint lectures.

Was not great at explaining class content, often chaotic and unprepared. He was a very funny guy and lectures were somewhat entertaining. Exams had many difficult proofs, but you can have two note sheets. 20 points available of extra credit on each exam (usually around 70 points), make sure you copy down the proofs and you should be good.
Farzad was amazing, the class material is just extremely difficult. He goes pretty easy on the grading as a result. Would definitely recommend him as a professor for any stats class.

Farzad is a fun guy who genuinely cares about his students. When our class didnt do all that well on our first exam, he took ownership of it and reevaluated how our tests are written. I had the option of watching the lectures online, but I think Farzad was much more effective and enjoyable in person.
Very good professor who knows a lot about the material for this class. Always happy and willing to answer any questions.

Farzad is by far the best professor that I have had here at Iowa State. He is incredibly caring, and always takes the time to answer students' questions. There is a lot of homework for this class, but most of it is not very difficult. If you simply show up to class and do the homework, this class is an easy A.
Excellent professor, easy to get along with and always has time fore questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Farzad is a good teacher who is accessible outside of class. Hes very knowledgeable and tries to make the class humorous. You can get an A if you attend office hours, study lectures, and create a good cheat sheet.

Stat 588 is difficult if you are not great at calculus, which I am not. Despite this, Dr. Sabzikar has EXTREMELY lenient grading practices. If you do all the work you can get a passing grade. Dr. Sabzikar explains things clearly, gives homework that is not a waste of time, and is accessible outside of class. Take this class from him!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class had a slow start and introduces the concept in a fluid manner and raises the speed as the time goes but the quality of the class does not decrease. Is very helpful in class and the grading is great.

Really great, friendly professor. I was struggling a bit in the course and went to his office hours. Not only did he clarify the material, he also assisted me in succeeding on the final exam. We identified the key areas that I was struggling with (mostly time ) and figured out that I needed to familiarize myself with the theories a bit more.

Inspirational professor, who makes the boring course interesting. He has a deep knowledge which also makes this course difficult.  I will recommend this professor although one has to put a lot of effort, but in the end one will learn a lot from this course.   Exams are difficult, but he doesn't give much home work. He is open for opinions.
As a non STAT major student, this class was very challenging to me. But Dr. Sabzikar made the lecture content be clear and interesting. And he respects every student. Good professor!
Very chill professor. Genuinely cares about students and won't put too much on your plate at once.

Carol was a very kind and understanding professor. She responds to emails and is always there to give feedback. The Her class was very fun and flexiable to be in, however, her feedback was not very helpful most of the time. If you're seriously looking to improve your graphic design skills, I would reccomend a different professor.

I really enjoyed having Carol as a professor. She was always pretty nice and understanding. She does things a bit differently than other studios, but I enjoyed the way she did assignments. She also gives you much creative freedom as long as it follows the general project guidelines. I recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clear and concise grading criteria allows you to express yourself in your projects and let you have a lot of creative freedom.

Learned a lot in this class. Mandatory notes in class sucks, but honestly it really helped me keep up with class and understand the content. Loved her as a professor, she was very kind, understanding, and accommodating. Be prepared to try hard in her class but communicate with her and you'll do great.

I found that she was not very understanding with illness and doctors notes. She interrogated me regarding my doctors note implying that I was lying even though I was not. She assumed I was trying to take advantage of me and made me cry.

Lectures are directly from the textbook, and she makes you do guided note-taking during lectures. Exams always had an issue with them, such as formatting or incorrect answers. Quizzes are random throughout the class, so attendance is crucial. Seems like a caring professor, but makes the class harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a very nice teacher and seems to care about all of her students. All her tests are open note/textbook, but the tests are difficult. It was hard to find any of the information in the notes and textbook. There is also a project done throughout the semester, which is fairly easy and she graded it easy.
She made attendance mandatory cause showing up is pointless. You can only miss three classes in a semester before your grade drops a letter. She's nice but lectures are boring.

Feb is super nice and caring about her students. Her canvas page is a little overcrowded and hard to follow because things aren't broken up by the due date. She made attendance mandatory towards the end of the semester because nobody would show up. She made in-class assignments and only got a grade if you went. Overall, good but wont take it again.

She was an excellent instructor. I took her course online, and it was really easy. All you had to do was participate in the learning assignments and follow the writing process. Some major assignments were boring and took time, but you could choose what to write about. Overall this was an easy class. Would highly recommend the online version.
She was awesome. I loved having her because she was aware that students had outside lives and jobs and didn't want to overload students.

She has her class so poorly set up. Nobody knew what was going on in the class at any time. Not to mention the class feels completely useless. Her canvas page is so overcrowded that you cant even figure out what has been assigned by looking at the website.

Very passionate about what he teaches. He's a really nice grader and gives actually helpful feedback. He doesn't post the slides, but if you're confused he's really easy to get in contact with (office hours, appointment, email) and he gives really good, in depth answers. Provides study guides for the test that are really detailed too. Amazing prof.

His lectures were very engaging, although I don't think I learned much. A lot of mostly easy group projects. Exams are based entirely on what was discussed in class; most of the questions are obvious if you listen to lectures or go through the study guide. Didn't enjoy MUN b/c I didn't have enough background knowledge to join the discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I could tell that he cared about what he was teaching. He went through his slides really quickly and doesn't post them or give them to you if you are absent so have a phone or friend that can take pictures of the slides. He does a Model UN topic which is quite interesting! I however, did not learn much..

I actually looked forward to going to this class. We learned some interesting things and had the opportunity to look at/compare different countries. The HW/exams were graded very reasonably (if not a bit leniently) and he seems like a nice guy. I did sometimes feel like I didn't have enough background info on the topics we discussed, though
Honestly hes a pretty easy grader. I wouldve had an A if I hadnt forgot about some of the assignments that really didnt take long at all. He definitely sets his students up for success in his classes

I would highly recommend Professor Feinstein. The course itself was extremely easy. I attended the majority of the lectures (which he does grade attendance) and ended up with an A in the course. Many of the exams questions are repeats of the quizzes that you have already taken. In addition, the three big projects are pretty simple.

I really enjoyed this course and the professor. The class was very discussion heavy which worked well with the small class size we had (probably 8 to 12 people). We also had a lot of reading but it was never unmanageable. Additionally, our exams were at home with a lockdown browser and open notes which was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took his pandemic Polistics Class and it was amazing. He has awesome lectures and really interesting examples related to nationalism and the pandemic. Highly recommend this class!! He is a VERY smart professor. His class was so applicable to what we are going through today.
One of the best classes I've taken at Iowa State University. He is really interesting as a person, and as a professor, he will challenge the way you navigate the world. Gracias Scott. :)

He seems like a nice guy, but his syllabus is his mess, his lectures and slides aren't helpful and any kind of clear grading criteria are nonexistent. I learned more about Eastern European politics from the constant videos we watch, and the last 5 weeks of class were a complete waste of time, because they were almost entirely student presentations.

Pretty good professor, obviously knows what he's talking about. The textbook was way too in-depth; you could get a good chunk of it from the lectures but not all of it. Exam review with the TA was very helpful.

The textbook for POL S 251 is very difficult to read and does not do a great job explaining the various theories. However, you can find very good youtube videos and articles to help you understand the concepts. We also did a lot of activities and discussions in class to help us understand topics. Difficult class, but with effort you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY
