reviews.comment: Obviously knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches, but still inexperienced and prone to rambling. The department may have dictated textbook choice, but it was a major problem. It is written very academically and makes little sense to over half of the students, yet the readings are essential to get anything over a C in the class.

The reading was way too advanced for an intro class, the lectures were very unclear and messy, and he refused to give us even BASIC guidelines on what to study for exams other than "read the textbook and study your lecture material". The only good thing was the T.A. I wouldn't recommend him as a professor - way too hard for an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great overall professor. Does a good job teaching about international topics. Has group presentations, guest speakers, and videos to help break up lectures. If you study you will do fine on his tests. Also, pretty easy essay grader.
Some students complain about the lectures. This is college and at this level it is not difficult to take notes and follow the lectures and readings.

Feinstein has a much better grasp on these topics than the other IR professor does- as I dropped his class previously. Lectures tend to not make much sense but the readings are clear and his TA gives extra sessions before the exams. Not having a study guide is irrelevant, if you read and go to the extra sessions you'll easily get an A or B

100% lecture with little to no context powerpoint slides. No study guide for tests so you have no idea what you'll be asked. Just told us "Read the chapters and the extra readings and you'll be fine." First test average was 53%. Really smart dude but do not take if you don't understand anything about Pol sci materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Nikki! Labs were a little boring, but engaging and I always looked forward to listening to her mini lectures and hanging out with the horses. Easy A as long as you show up to every lab! Practicals are copy and paste from the things you do in lab, so be sure to practice! Anyone can take this course, either for fun or equine experience!

She will either show you someone else's lecture, ramble for 50 min or not show up till the last 10 min of class. Attendance is mandatory even though she doesn't always show up. When I did chores I was told it would only be 2 hours but I was there from 2-7 and everything was still not done. Just please be wary of this class or any classes with Nikki

This class was ridiculous. DO NOT TAKE unless you want 1 credit for free labor and terrible tests. You are taught nothing and you are expected to do way too much. I wish I could fit in here how much this class destroyed me this semester. You get no additional points for any of the insane amount of work you do, only for attendance to unhelpful labs

ANS 332E is the equine reproduction laboratory. Sounds fun at the name right? You will be required around 2 times a week to do foal watch shifts are between 8pm-1am or 1am-5:30am, and you will receive both shifts. You are paying an excessive lab fee to provide free labor. I beg of you to consider your job and other classes before your sign up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think this class would be better in person, although I enjoyed it and thought Nikki did a great job teaching the material. The lab portion was fairly easy and I wish it would have consisted of more than just cleaning stalls and other chores. Overall, it was a great class and I was able to learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class, especially with Nikki as she is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to equine. If you already have quite a bit of horse experience, this class can get a bit boring at times but there's a lot to learn and Nikki does a great job making sure everyone is comfortable with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The equine repro lab is an amazing class! You put in a lot of work for the amount of credit you get. You gain lots of real-life experience working with mares, foals, and through the foaling process. The class isn't an easy A, you have to work for it. Go to the optional Friday class for extra practice! Ask questions and put in a lot of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class is to help build you knowledge and experience with equine, so if you haven't taken Equine Science, this class will be quite tough for you. You go over a lot of practical things that occur within the equine industry. You also have to do 30 hours of lab work by helping with chores, or help with foal watch in the spring semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nikki is extremely knowledgeable about horses, and she does a great job explaining the basics to people who have little to no equine background. She's quite blunt, but she's not rude about it. She'll help you in any way that she can, though she is a very busy woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lab practicals are easy, but lecture exams are killer. There is a career project where you have to interview people in the field, I did not expect that. I did not find this class helpful at all, except in making me want to drop my an sci minor. Quiz dates are not on syllabus so you must check bb regularly. Labs seemed like a waste of time.

If you have past experience in showing horses at a competitive level you should do just fine in this class; if not good luck! I had to work very hard in this class and her tests are VERY difficult. Her test questions come straight from the readings so read, read and reread!

Nikki is honestly one of my favorite professors ever. She is super scary at first but she actually is the sweetest most helpful person once you get to know her. DO NOT take the class if you genuinely do not have an interest or do not want to get to know about horses.

217 was one of the coolest classes ever. I was seriously terrified of Nikki at first (I would email other prof about the class). If you show genuine interest then Nikki will like you. As the semester went on she became more lax. Make sure you get all of your 30 hrs in. They're obnoxious, but it's a good life lesson.

Ms. Ferwerda is completely incompetant when it comes to lecturing. When I took the class it was almost laughable to watch her try to teach. She isn't well informed. She should stick to riding horses, rather than teaching student about them.

Nikki is a very nice teacher, but I don't think she's that great. I didn't know anything about horses going in, and I feel like she assumed we all grew up with a horse. Her powerpoints are kind of busy and not well organized, which makes it difficult to study for tests. The class is okay; it can get kind of boring. The lab is pretty fun, though.

Feve is a good teacher; at times, he's a bit hard to understand, but he really lets each group go about their way and figure things out. He's a bit of a harsh grader, and it's very difficult to get full credit on an assignment, but as long as you go off the examples and follow the rubrics/schedule, you should be fine.

He is a horrible grader. Impossible to get a good grade on any assignment. Assignment requirements are vague and confusing. His lectures and extremely long with very little meaning behind his words. I thought he would be chill but he is not.
Prof Feve was great at explaining topics with deep detail and went over everything plenty of times. His lectures tend to be a little dry and dragged on but besides that he's awesome!
Made the class easy and straight forward consider yourself lucky if you get him.

A pretty good teacher with a lot of knowledge about SOLIDWORKS, can pretty much solve any problem you have on assignments. Quizzes are the worst part of this class, since the information you need is given to you in video lectures which are a drag to get through. Projects are laid out well, but you will need to work outside of class on them to pass.

Feve's is very simple. You'll go to class and work on a project that's due by the end of the week and probably finish it halfway through the class. The Reverse Engineering Project and the weekly SolidWorks project are most of your grades and he doesn't grade hard at all. Just hope you're put in a good group because you'll be with them all semester.
Very kind. Assignments are easy if you follow the engineering drawings properly

Good teacher, but a lot of the class was group work and basically following along with the stuff on Canvas. He's a nice teacher but sometimes he'll talk at a medium volume and allow the rest of the room to carry on with side talk making it hard to hear him. The course is an easy course really no matter who you have but he is a nice guy, funny too

He's nice & smart but his assignments were unclear and difficult to understand. He would start by lecturing and repeat himself for a good 30 minutes with what could be said in 5 minutes. Also didn't budget enough time for the CAD portion of the project. The paperwork - drawings and MPIs - was easily 80+ documents and the CAD took such a long time.
Very dry lectures. Never felt like he was very friendly to me when I asked questions. Only professor in ME170 that has exams..

Feve is good guy, but he's not always clear as to what is being asked. There have been many assignments where people didn't understand what we were supposed to be doing or rather, how something is supposed to be done. Things are graded weird and it isn't uncommon to lose points without being told why. Lot's of 'homework' plus two big projects.

ME 270 is a group project class, so the group you are put with can determine how your semester will go. However, Sebastien is a great professor who cares about his students. He gives great feedback and grades fairly. He is a good professor.
Great class! Would take a class with him again!

I really like Feve as a professional, but his class is just downright ridiculous. This is a 100 level design class. Students are not given any pertinent instruction on how to go about each project. This course needs some re-designing.
Easy class just show up everyday, make friends with your group members, do your part of the projects. Projects are easy and there is few

Feve is a really great guy. I took ME 170 and ME 270 with him, and enjoyed both semesters. He has good advice for the projects that you have to work on, and he is pretty funny in his lectures. He made what could have been a terrible class into a good one.

Professor Feve is a cool guy. He is French and has an accent but has lived in the United States for awhile so he's easy to understand. His lectures are pretty boring and you kind of need to figure stuff out on your own. It's an easy class though.

270 is a different kind of class, much more student work in your team, less lecturestests. That being said, Sebastian is always there to answer questions and wants to help you learn and succeed in the class. His funny stories keep class interesting, too! Don't buy the textbook, I haven't opened mine yet once.
Easy class but I feel like it could be improved on. Over all, good teacher
Very confusing explanations. Not very good at specifying what is needed on assignments.  Jokes are very awful and not funny. French accent is quite awesome.

Alright class. Came in with a solid knowledge of SolidWorks so I didn't have to ask a lot of questions. Yes, there was a bit of homework but not a lot of online homework. Nice teacher, which helps a lot.
Great teacher. Homework wasn't too bad and this was actually my easiest class for the semester.
Cool guy, not great at explaining things.
the most helpful teacher I have ever meet

Never tells you what his requirements are for homework so it is impossible to get full points. He is also less than helpful when things go wrong. Tries to be funny but one-on-one he makes you feel dumb.

This professor gives out more homework than the others, but its manageable. The class does not take up your life as others may suggest. If you are a good student you should get an A if not, you should probably switch majors!

He tries to make jokes sometimes and they just don't work. He grades pretty tough and he rarely tells you when homework is due. It's really frustrating. If you have the chance try and get a different professor.

I've never had another teacher who doesn't mention when homework is due. Of course, the amount of work he assigns is ridiculous. Rarely is there a class when something is not due. His french accent is the only thing that makes me pay attention to the incredibly boring lectures. I wouldn't reccomend to take Feve's class if you have a choice.

I hate this class. Feve assigns so much work, he truly acts as though this is the only class students take. If you are not even remotely interested in the class material, taking this course is comparable to hell. If you must take it, find some other professor.

He really wants students to develop good engineering fundamental through his class. Very patient and helpful outside the class. Only thing I don't like about this class is that Sebastien's exams are kinda long for fifty-minute format.

Material was very interesting to me. Has an interesting teaching style and way of grading assignments, where comments are aggressive. If you know the material and understand it, you will do well in this course, but be prepared to do a lot of homework and large research paper. Overall the course was great, but teaching was questionable to poor.

I took plant breeding with Dr. Salas who was incredibly knowledgeable about the topic. I love this topic but quickly became discouraged by her strict lectures, harsh grading, and expecting students to memorize and comprehend every word she said. She made no exceptions and was condescending towards students. 
Great class, scary professor

Dr. Salas is the absolute worst teacher I have ever experienced. She belittles students and purposely makes them feel stupid. People are afraid to ask questions during class. If you ask her a question, she tries to make you answer it in front of the class. Asks tophat questions before explaining material. DON'T TAKE IT WITH HER.
Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor is awful, she gives students grades based on how much she likes them. She thinks she knows everything and can't learn from anyone or listen to reasoning . The reason she thinks that is because she has 3 years of experience in the industry. She is intolerable, a terrible excuse for a teacher, and not very intelligent.

Disrespectful to students and very autistic. She refused to explain the materials when asked, mostly because she doesn't have understanding of the materials. Homework is full of busy work. Class is easy, but she made it so unbearable because of her attitude and lack of knowledge. ISU needs to find a better instructor.
Very subjective and rude. She will not listen to you. It's difficult to learn from her because she doesn't explain well but there are more resources available online to learn the material.

-Does NOT work with students in any manner and is incredibly harsh at grading
-Does NOT harbor a good learning environment for the class
-She is VERY subjective
-Go against her reasoning and she WILL NOT listen to you
-Furthermore, She goes at problems in a reactive manner while dealing with students
-I Would NOT recommend taking the class with her

Renee is clearly the worst prof at ISU. Although she can't teach and doesn't know the material, she's very defensive to suggestions. Everyone doesn't enjoy working with her. I talked to people in industry who worked with her in the past, and they overwhelmingly got the same impression of her! Surprise surprise!

Renee still can't deliver material clearly and can't teach well. She is also not open to feedback, very defensive, and condescending. The worst instructor in my entire time at ISU. I feel bad that all ConE students have to deal with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fleming brings their career experience and turns it into a realistic capstone class that prepared me well for my career. The projects were time consuming, but were real world content. They has realistic expectations and were willing to work with students who were having difficulties. I wish Prof Fleming came to ISU sooner.

Professor Fleming does not respect the students and expects you to meet her 24 hour assignments. Unreasonable assignments, does not grade big projects until final exam, Harshest grader. Doesnt treat the course as a learning experience, expects you to have internship experience to do well. I advise students to change majors if she stays teaching.
I love her. Yes, some of her lectures seem long, but she makes sure that if you try, you will pass, and she cares about everyone, especially the people who care about the class. Love her to death.
If you stay on top of things and lock in a good team for the semester group project, you'll be fine. She is very strict on attending class and lectures feel long.

She was awesome. A little bit unorganized at times but she explained concepts well. Heavy lectures and exams. You get one front and back note sheet for exams. Some topics are covered on exams and barely talked about in class but overall, it is a great class with a great professor!

Susan is a great professor who loves what she does. She is so funny and personable and engages with the class every lecture. It is very easy to pay attention in her classes. If you listen in class, you will do fine. I don't know why she has bad reviews, but don't listen to them.

not super organized but very caring and funny. The concepts are simple enough that you can catch up if you miss a lecture or get confused. Take the time to talk to her after or during class, because she's always down to help.

you either hate her or love her, but that's up to you. If you take the time to do the work and get to know her, she's a hilarious lady and loves her job. very busy though, so grading is often delayed. If she had more TAs, I think she'd have better reviews. Overall sweet, just needs some organization.

Professor Flemming was one of the best teachers I have had at Iowa State. She genuinely cares about her students and is always willing to answer any questions (content and non-content). Her lectures are clear and understandable, and if you get to know her she has a great sense of humor. 10/10 recommend her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although Susan is genuinely a pretty nice person, I would not recommend taking any of her classes. She is very unorganized and often includes material that is irrelevant for exams. Attending lectures is pretty important as you receive daily class points, and make sure you have a decent group for the group project!

She was asked to make more reviews, and then told a student, "No, I don't want toYouou should have been taking notes and paying attention." She was talking to someone who had taken notes throughout the class and paid attention. Very Rude.

In class and during review, she would talk about topics that wouldn't be in the lecture slides. These "Concepts" we would have to know, but we would never talk about them in class. She would then put questions about other random "concepts" that weren't talked about in the review or lectures.
She said we would talk about questions that we got wrong in class, and then wouldn't and claim "there wasn't enough time" and then speed run all the topics.
Don't take her class, take MKT 3400 with another professor, it will save you a lot of stress
She will have reviews for exams and then tell you at the end that we haven't learned this topic, but it will be on the exam.
She references the textbook throughout the class, but then tells you the textbook is wrong and that the lecture slides is correct, and then won't post the lecture slides for you to study.
She doesn't even know her own material, you also have to fill out papers in class, that you don't get to keep to help you study. A little pointless.
For the final review, she had concepts and questions that we didn't learn about in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was very inconsistent with out-of-class material, and for exam reviews, she would either have things or not, and wouldn't tell you.
She lied in class

Her class wasn't set up good, she would speed run the lectures and not take time to actually explain things. She is very unorganized and often forgets to do things. She would forget her notes for the class. She would expect you to know everything, but then spend one second talking over every topic. Don't take her class, it sucked.

Susan is one of my favorite teachers I have had at ISU. She keeps lectures engaging and fun to be there. She also states that the class itself is not hard, its just a lot of work and knowing the material. If you study and show up to class you will pass. There is a group project but its fun. This was one of my favorite classes this semester.
If you have to take this class and marketing is not your major DO NOT take it with her. A lot of homework, projects, and attendance assignments every class.

Participation and attendance is what makes or breaks your grade in this class, people who dislike susan are often those who aren't willing to show up every day or who don't participate. super sweet lady, funny, and caring. Group project heavy but I thought it was an enjoyable experience moreso than my other group project courses.

- Won't share extra material for exams

- Skips over lecture slides then puts them in exams

- Doesn't take time to fully explain material, seems like she was more focused on getting through the 70 page slides rathe

Susan truly cares about students learning from the class. Attendance is mandatory and lectures are slide/textbook heavy. Semester-long group project. Exams are hard but allows 2 pages of notes and provides a detailed study guide. DO THE OPTIONAL HOMEWORK! They're tedious but the extra credit you get from them can basically replace your exam scores.

She knows what she is talking about when she lectures but acts like we should be familiar although it's a foundations class. She is very nice and has a lot of energy; the workload and material we cover is crazy. Studying feels impossible because it's so much, and you don't know what's important. I wouldn't take it with her again.

I love her so much. She is a super sweet, funny lady who clearly loves her job. lots of group work but it's not bad. (and I don't typically enjoy group work) If you participate and show up to classes you'll do just fine! Exams are pretty easy and all content on them is covered in class.

This teacher does a really good job at explaining the concepts of marketing and gives projects/assignments that further your understanding. You will pass if you show up for class and do all of the extra credit assignments. The client project is also a really big part of your grade, but she offers feedback in person before you turn in each section.
Fantastic teacher, class is oriented around in-class activities and group projects. If you do the optional exercises, of which you get credit for, you will pass the class with flying colors.

Interested in marketing? Take 340 with Susan! She explained the concepts of marketing super well and inspired me to pursue it. Show up to get credit for attendance, participate in the semester long group project, and have an easy to navigate note sheet for your exam and you will do well. Recommend doing the 'optional' learn-smarts. Loved this class

She is such a caring person. She always asked about my well being even when it got hard. She is also so funny. Like her class is entertaining. It’s a tough course but she is genuinely one of the nicest professors at Iowa state. Idk how people can dislike her.

Susan is a good teacher and knows what she is talking about. Her class is set up with a series of bite size lectures and is broken down by the day of what should be done for that day. Great course, and easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor expects that her class is the only one a person is taking during the semester. I have her this semester spring of 2021 and we have a 4th exam the week before our final. There have been 4 major projects for this class already and on average you will have been 3 and 8 assignments every week. The most work I've had to do in any class.

She was one of the few teachers to format a class in canvas well. Some of her assignments seemed a bit trivial, like requiring us to write papers on the career fair as upperclassmen. Her grading criteria are weird, she expects you to go above and beyond to get anything higher than a B, but she rewards you for going to feedback sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Do not take the class with her... she doesn't tell you clearly when things are due and didn't tell my class when an assessment opened up until the day it opened. Wish i liked her but she is just not it :/

Susan is extremely unorganized, and acts more of a friend than professor. She doesn't give clear instructions on any assignment, but expects u to know what to do. She doesn't do a good job of explaining when things are due, and she doesn't know half the time when things are due. There are 2 exams and a final and you will defs need to study for them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very good at showing the jobs out there
Very good at teaching how to code. If you try you will pass the class. Make sure to ask questions.
Just an overall amazing guy and this is by far my favorite class

Dave is hands down the BEST professor I've had during my time at Iowa State. He genuinely cares about each and every student that comes through the meteorology program. He is a tough grader and a strong believer in doing work on your own because he really wants each student to have a solid understanding of the material.

He made us get proctors for our online summer class. I had to drive 30 minutes away from my home and pay for someone at a community college to proctor my exam. Has he never heard of lockdown browser or screen monitoring. Nice guy though I guess, class was easy. Literally the only class that fulfills a natural science credit that isn't bio or chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dave puts in exponentially more effort into his teaching than most of the people in the department. He cares about the students and respects you if you put in the work. He gives a lot of tough love, but in meteorology, you need it.

He covers a lot of material that doesn't matter to the class which then makes him get behind on the actual material (causing him to rush it) so it makes it much harder to learn. He barely goes over examples for harder problems so good luck on the homework. He also gives pop quizzes so if you don't know the material every second you won't do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dave was phenomenal. I would jump at the chance to take more classes with him. He cares about the subject and he cares greatly about making sure you learn it. He even had study sessions outside of normal lecture before exams. He was also my adviser which he was also great at. It was an honor to know him.

Dave is a character. He makes his class fun and entertaining. He has good and bad day, like all of us. If you need an elective, this is a good one to take. You just have to show up and you will pass the class. Not many homework assignments although you do tophat in class for attendance and participation points. You can tell that he enjoys his job.
Great professor that made learning  meteorology fun. You have to show up to class if you want to pass with an A. Tests are somewhat difficult depending on how much effort you put forth.
Easy homework. Hard tests

Dr. Flory was an alright professor. His lecture were fun and engaging. He can be a bit rude if he catches you texting or goofing around in class. His test are pretty brutal, even if you cram for them, but the curve was pretty good. I didn't even take the final and was still able to get an A.
Good professor, you need to be in class to get the participation points. Would highly recommend to friends. Not an easy A but totally worth the work. Do the forcasts everyday and you should be fine.

Was told this is an easy A science credit. Turns out it is somewhat challenging. Tests are crazy hard, but aren't a huge part of your grade. Also 85% is an A in the class. Lots of points come from being in class and participating in class exercise so you can't skip. Cool professor as well.

I took this as an elective because it sounded fun. Dave made class interesting and was pretty funny. The exams were pretty tough, but they aren't a big portion of your grade. Other parts of the class were forecasting, blackboard homework, clicker (attendance) points. The class was pre-curved and 85% is an A.  I would recommend this as fun elective!

This guy is amazing even if his exams was hard but you can get an easy A if you just attend the class, I don't know anything about this class until now and I just study one day before the exam and I got B+. So I really recommend everyone to take the class if he want an easy A.

This guy is amazing. I had very little interest in weather before this class. With him teaching, I understood and learned a lot! He is very clear in his lecture. He's laid back and understands we are college students. He constantly offers help to anyone who needs it. He keeps the class entertaining and practical. Easy A if you do the work.

I've had him for multiple classes. He makes class fun and enjoyable. If you go to lecture, do the assignments, and listen to what he's saying, you'll do fine. You can get an A if you do the work. He is easy to talk to and answers any questions you may have. Time really does fly by in his classes.
Very fun and entertaining class. Very helpful, if you ever have a question and email him, he will get back to you in a timely manner.

Flory is very clear in his explanations and what is expected of you in his courses. Perfect labs are a rarity, and his grading is usually quite picky but this encourages students to put forth the most profession work. Work your butt off to avoid getting on his bad side and you should do fine. ALSO: DO NOT forget to forecast!

DO NOT expect an A in his class without working for it. His grading can be very difficult as he bases it around the class average, but as long as you are "above the average" you should be fine. He is very helpful inside and outside of class and is always willing to answer questions. I loved his classes.

Flory's a good teacher that made class fun, and it was a very easy A. However, I was upset that he taught the material so slowly that we veered way off the calendar; he got so busy that a grad student had to teach the course for him, and we had our last three of the four exams crammed in at the last month. At least the grading was forgiving.
Flory is the shiznait!!!!

Flory is really awesome. He wants everyone to do well in his classes. He may be a very hard grader, and a hard assigner, however he wants to help you learn. He grades based on a class average, so how you do depends on how the class does. So it's rather hard to get a perfect in his class, but its hard to fail too. Take his classes. Very funny guy!

I would recommend taking his class any day! He's really friendly and understanding, but comes off quite sarcastic. He makes this class really easy to pass as well. There's lots of busy work, but as long as you do it, you'll get a good grade.
He's adorable!! the nicest and most helpful guy ever! easy lectures to listen to, most points come from lectures so go and you'll do fine on tests.
No Comments
WOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!!!
He is a great teacher and advisor he is awsome I learn so much from him!

Flory ROCKS!! He will explain anything in such a way that everyone understands! He does like to explain somethings in very long physics equations on the board, but just ask him what that means and he'll explain it!! He really helps to get you interested in the class.
Flory is the****, he is usually a cool dude, except when he gets PMSey
Good teacher, Doesnt give out many As but cares about your interest in the class.
No Comments
No Comments

In comparison to all other comments, Floros seems to not care one bit about helping his students learn. He doesn't had out example sheets to help guide students when he does those examples. He turns his back on the students, and solves problems without reading the questions out loud. Exams are 20 Quantitative questions, you have to teach yourself.
Was not a good teacher, a self-taught class but is insanely hard to teach yourself. Avoid

Yianni has high expectations for anyone who intends to succeed. His lectures cover the chapter's concepts, and we go over examples. If you do not expose yourself to the material ahead of time, you will be lost. He has a Greek accent but speaks directly and is easy to understand. He is very smart and you can really learn a lot if you try.

As stated in previous reviews, Professor Floros is a very low quality teacher. I would strongly recommend you avoid taking his classes if you can. He is extremely difficult to understand, does not have a good command of the classroom, yells in class, and makes the material more difficult than the textbook. AVOID

This is an upper finance level class, however he expects us to know about options and futures going into the class. This is extremely difficult and 100% of your grade is based on 3 exams. Not clear during lectures and goes way to fast during lectures. Overall an awful professor.

He only assigns 2 HW assignments which are 20% of the grade. You can pick any 2 assignments you want so I recommend doing them on the first 2 chapters because those are the easiest. Exams and quizes are tough but the practice versions he posts are very similar. He also curves the averages to a B-, B range. Hard to get an A, but hard to get a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't get the bad rap for Professor Floros. He gives a lot of material (mock exams) for you to study for quizzes and tests. Only 2 homework assignments all semester. Quizzes and Tests are curved so that a B is the average. If you have questions he is always willing to answer them during office hours. Have to go to class to understand material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Stay away... Floros could be the worst professor at ISU. The guy knows little to nothing about teaching or finance.

He is a very disrespectful professor. No help when it comes to learning. It almost as he feels as if he is above teaching this introductory course so he makes it very tough. Quizzes not too bad. Tests impossible gives 20 long questions that you have to get done in an hour. He is Greek very thick accent so even harder to understand. WNR.

The only good thing about this class is how much he curves. Most averages on his exams are 12/20 (B with curve included) b/c the material he teaches in class is much easier than what he expects you to know for the exams. Doesn't like to teach things on a calculator and expects  you to do all equations by hand.

I enjoyed Yianni as a professor.  The only knock against him is his requirements for assignments and projects were a bit unclear at times.  I enjoyed his lectures; he is very knowledgeable and clearly enjoys what he does.  I would recommend taking him.

Floros is a pretty cool guy... if you do what is expected of you. Otherwise he can be kinda rough. Go to class, take good notes, copy down the problem examples. You don't really need the book, quizzes/tests come from his notes and the practice exams. His tests are tricky, but curve is extremely  generous.

Don't buy the book, you don't need it. Attend class, it helps a lot. Study the mock exams/quizes he posts online and you will get an A on the tests. Personally, I didn't care for Floros, he is an arrogant teacher and gets ticked off if you don't speak up in class.

Class is not mandatory but if you want to do well, GO.  I highly recommend getting the calculator as this can do most of the test questions for you. And he shows you how to use it.  There is no homework. Quiz/test are curved.  He doesn't post scores online, so he leaves you wondering what your current grade is. He is Greek if that matters to any1.

Tim is such a nice guy and this class is an easy A if you put in a little bit of work. Theres a lot of group projects and a lot of homework. I would recommend taking this class with a friend who you enjoy doing schoolwork with to be part of your group. Lectures can be a little boring and he will call you out for answers if theres no engagement.

I would highly recommend this class with Florer. He's very caring and passionate about this course, If you pay attention in class you will do well. This course was very easy, the only thing I would be cautious about is the group project work, over half of your grade will come from group project points so choose your group wisely. Great course!

In this class you have both individual assignments and team assignments, where teams are decided on the first day of class (can be with friends if you want). Many of these assignments are short papers answering a set of questions from a case study. He will go through each chapter's content during lectures and give you time to work on assignments.

Tim is an amazing professor. He really connects to his students and wants them to always succeed. He is willing to help your group for CAPSIM. He is such a friendly professor who wants to help his students in class! His BUSAD250 course is not very lecture heavy, so make sure you go through the notes on your own! Exams are mostly vocab & application

Timothy is a very nice guy. In MGMT, his lectures were very unappreciated and he put a lot of effort into the class. He has very fair grading procedures and gave out study guides for the exams. I would recommend if you are able to take advantage of the resources that he provides.

Florer is a wonderful professor. Lots of group work so be smart when picking your group in the first week. Class if 50/50 lecture and group work. Lectures can sometimes get long but Florer is quite knowledgeable and has lots of past experiences. Exams are easy by using the study guide that he provides. Without it the exams are hard.

Great guy and knows management well. The class is simple if you show up and get all the assignments done. The exams are harder but if you understand the lectures, book, and PowerPoints you will be ok. Great professor, gives good feedback, and very helpful if you have questions!

In this class with "Timbo" you will find nothing less than a waste of your time and the tests have nothing to do with your hw. He is a god awful prof, and I don't suggest anyone take this bum of a prof. MC tests, but again nothing to do with the class.

Easy A, the class is all about CAPSIM, which is an online fake company that sells sensors. It teaches a lot but is easy to get behind. If you understand CAPSIM you are golden. The exams for business/marketing topics are the only thing that can bring down your grade. Tim himself is an awkward dude, but nice.

He was a super boring professor. Honestly, he didn't explain things well, had us do a whole bunch of busy work, and the tests were difficult but seemed meaningless. Honestly, it's just a big review of the business core, so take this course last. I would definitely not take him again as I heard there were others who were easier.

The class is mostly group based. The professor was always willing to help when we had questions. We never really learned how to actually use CapSim but as long as you do all your assignments and study a little bit for the exams you'll be fine. The lowest exam out of 4 gets dropped and there are some extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Get ready to do 10-15 assignments a week plus a simulation with a group that makes no sense. If you email him he repeats himself and basically doesn't help at all. Tests have 200+ terms to know and he tries to "trick" you with multiple choice.
A good amount of HW but easy to get done, assignments in class that are easy to do. Test also were pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Not transparent at all, Make sure you don't take the final he will wrongly tell you if it will hurt your grade or not.

Lots of little projects but they aren't hard. Tests are simple and based mostly on homework questions. Lectures can be hard to follow along with sometimes but he is a great guy and offers help if you need it. Fun class and great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really enthusiastic about business
Tim is an AWESOME guy! Wish he could teach all my classes!

Love Timothy, very caring professor. I would say yes go to class, its not mandatory but you should. If you pay attention you will get real life business applications out of the class. If you put effort in, you will get something out of this class. Its an easy A only if you put effort in.
Good ol' Timothy. Funny dude. Easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a good professor and he cares about students.

Professor Florer is a great guy and is willing to help with just about anything. The capsim stuff is kinda tricky but he will help you along the way. Tests are pretty simple, but you gotta put in work with your group to succeed

Florer is a great person who truly is excited about his job. He cares so much about his students. If you have a question, he will be more than happy to help. He gives you almost every question thats on the exams. Only complaint is that he isn't very clear on how to work Capsim, the simulation program you work on through the semester

Tim is a nice dude but still a bit unexperienced at teaching. The lectures are subpar; But he gives them his best shot every time. He does however show an effort to learn his students names and respects his students. His classroom is a stress free environment and he offers many easy in-class assignments which offer a fair amount of points.

This professor truly cares about his students, and he took the time to get to know  a lot of us by name. Although lectures were not extremely engaging, he did everything he could to help students achieve the grade/results they wanted. He even held extra study sessions before exams. Easy tests. One big online project.

Florer is an awesome person, and he truly cares about you as a student. He is just not the greatest professor. The lectures were almost pointless, and he would try to use real world examples that didn't pertain to the topic. The exams were easy, and most of it was common sense questions. Sadly, I did not gain any knowledge from this class.

Easy class, mediocre professor. I had Florer for his first semester as a professor, and he's a great guy and excited to teach but has a lot to learn. Lectures were not remotely engaging, and throughout the course there was very little to learn or be graded on. He was very receptive to my questions as I strove for an A, but I ended up 2 points short

Ethics with Dr. Fila was great. It felt like a nice break from the rest of my classes. It wasn't free, you had to do a lot of readings and there were a couple essays but as long as you are engaged with the idea of ethical decisions it's all straightforward. I strongly recommend speaking up in class, it makes the lectures a lot more fun.

Dr Fila genuinely cares about students and actually wants them to extract something useful out of his courses. You'll be encouraged to think rationally. Really chill, smart professor who I enjoyed interacting with. If you put in the work, he will absolutely notice and you'll do fine.

Nicholas Fila(or as we liked to call him Nick Fil-a) was a decent teacher. He clearly cares about his students and the topic that he teaches. He assigns heavy reading so prepare for that. You will also do a lot of writing but he doesn't grade it too harshly, as long as you show that you thought and sort of cared about it you are good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took EE 491 with Professor Nick Fila. The class was a strange senior design course, so I may not have the best frame of reference for his instructional ability. Nonetheless, Fila was helpful and engaged all semester in a class that included way too many mindless busywork writing assignments. I enjoyed all of my interactions with Fila.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: She was terrible and seemed like she hated her job. Always making snarky remarks
Tara was great, super easy course and gives you plenty of resources when you are new at Iowa state if you look in canvas
Super easy A, and Tara really just wants to help you get into Iowa State.

Nice professor who makes a required 1 credit class more bearable. She explains the transition to college well and helped us through class registration, advising, what to expect in the business school, etc. Attendance is mandatory! You meet for one hour each week and all the assignments are participation along with extra credit - easiest A ever

This class is super easy, but a percent of your grade is attendance. You only have 1-2 assignments a week which takes me max 30 minutes to complete. You get peer mentors and groups so you are able to meet people and talk with them. Tara is really easy to understand and she does class activities as well as has interesting guest speakers.
She's a cool girl. Required class and she makes it a little better.
Very tough class. Need to study the material. It's crazy how hard it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really good professor. Class is easy if you show up. You do in class things and each time you skip you lose 5 points. She gives extra credit. Tests are sorta hard but given the chance to do it twice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Just show up to class and do your work and you'll get an A. The work is not difficult and Jan teaches this class great. Also had her for 362

Jan is great, the teaching assistants not so much. One of them in particular is condescending and straight up rude. Over all, its a relatively simple class and the group project is pretty fun if you like museums.
This class was fun and not too hard.
Jan does ok teaching this class. She reads right off the slides which is boring. Attendance is important because of the in class activities.
Grading is hard with no explanation!

She was somewhat helpful but not overly willing to help w/ anything. Going to class was only mandatory because she would do random in class points (which obviously help in the end). You have to fill in gaps in notes, so it's not hard once you're there. She tries to make this class harder than it needs to be ,though. Medium work load.

Really boring as a teacher and really unimaginative. She literally takes her slides out of the book word for word and even uses the same pictures as the book does. The only reason you have to show up to her class is because she has these pointless activity points. The class itself is really stupid and she makes no effort to make it interesting.
the class is interesting enough.  The lectures are a bit boring.  Jan seemes to always get mad at me even though i really don't do anything wrong.
Good teacher and explains things really well!!
She is a boring teacher who always reads the powerpoint slide to students in class.
Make sure you go to lectures and pay attention. She doesn't always post the slides online so make sure to take notes! You can use notes/readings on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was really interesting and fun. The group project was really fun, as I enjoyed creating a restaurant. Attendance is essential in this class if you want to pass. Only negative are the tests. Many of the questions are tricky and based on her opinion.

You must attend class in order to pass. She is a great professor and really knows her stuff! Don't take this class if you think it is going to be an easy A. The tests are difficult and she does make you work for your grade. She is very understanding and cares about her students. She actually takes the time to get to know her students.

She doesn't ever seem like she fully understands what she's teaching, yet expects you to know what she means. Her tests are mostly "all of the above" which doesn't actually test anything. And the project? Don't expect a good grade no matter how much work you put in and even if you meet or exceed all of the expectations. Horrible teacher.

Terrible professor who makes terrible tests. Her slides and lectures aren't that bad and the assignments are really easy. But the tests try to trick you. I did not enjoy the class and she is not helpful to students.

Class is disorganized, students are lost.  There should be other prerequisites for the course that better prepare you.  Class environment is boring and graduate students are from other countries and don't speak English.

awful teacher. like most the other comments said, she is rude, and impersonal and not helpful and will give you a bad grade on the project unless she likes it, regardless of how much effort you put into it, and her exams are hard.

Tests are extremely hard even though they are open note.  Must attend class, that's a huge part of your grade. The restaurant project can be fun but you MUST do something she likes or you will get a bad grade. She's very knowledgeable but rude a lot of the time and very impersonal.
Class seemed harder than it should have been. I went to basically all the class except for like 3. The subject was kind of fun. Average rating...

Dr. Fiore class is not easy, but I respect her since she makes you work for your grade.  All you have to do is show up to class which is 1/4 of your grade.  I found her to be very knowledgeable on the topics she teaches and is also strict, yet fair in her teaching and evaluating students.  At Iowa State she is one of my favorite TC teachers.

Found Dr. Fiore to be very unhelpful with my success in the class. Isn't willing to help students and overall a rude woman. The class itself is hard with multipule choice test question options ranging from A-I, it doesn't test your knowledge, it messes with your head.

Dawn is a very caring advisor/teacher. Very slow & hard grader, but not horrible - won't destroy your final grade. If she docks you for something she'll give you reasons/areas for improvement. Follow the rubric and other pointers she gives exactly. Textbook necessary to answer a few quiz questions  and written assignments but otherwise not really.
Really tough grader, and will take points off if you don't follow the rubric exactly! (ex. make sure your margins are 1")
Really heavy grader.  Make sure you follow rubric to a T

As long as you show up and hand in things, you will be okay. Make sure you really pay attention to what is wanted and how she wants things. Pretty tough grader and not really a people-person. Comes off very cold and harsh. Be sure not to slack off.

She is NOT helpful, never makes time for any of her students unless you bother her a lot, and if you need an appointment with her, be sure to ask about 3 months before you actually need help. Even after she no longer has Event Management students to advise.
Read the book and go to class and you'll be alright.  Class is boring but not really her fault.

The class isn't too difficult, but make sure you go to class because she gives out little in class assignments for quite a few points. Be sure to read the chapters for the test and you should be GREAT!

Awful at explaining topics and does not answer questions clearly. Makes incredibly rude comments when critiquing the group project. She didn't even update the syllabus or deadlines on Blackboard from 2015 so all of the dates were wrong. Would not recommend any class that she teaches to anyone.

She is extremely rude, doesn't seem to care about students. Has no problem calling students out in front of the class for not following directions but will not explain ANYTHING. I wouldn't take one of her classes again, I'd be surprised if she works at ISU much longer.
Took this class and was excited about it. Disappointing attitude and class etiquette from the professor. Very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class isn't bad, her attitude is though. Would not recommend.

Not only is the the rudest professor I've ever had, she's unorganized and right out frustrating to deal with. Emailing her with questions will not get you anywhere, she responds with, "I touched on that in class please refer to your notes." LIKE WHAT.  Brags about how much money and things she has. Also requests proof if there is a family death.

Ann is a great professor. You will not pass the exams if you do not attend class because notes are given in class only, never posted online. There are several homework assignments throughout the semester, but not hard. There is a 10-person semester-long group project, also. Attendance is mandatory and will lower your grade if you do not attend.

Fornoff was one of my absolute favorite professors in COMST. Her courses are lecture based and your grade will be determined by attendance. Her classes were always fun and she finds ways to make learning about COMST interactive for the class. Easy exams due to her having review days beforehand. Best professor of my life.

Dr Fornoff was very fun to have as a professor! She really showed interest in helping her students succeed. You need to attend her class because there were a few days where she threw in in-class responses that you can only complete if you are in class. Other than that, her class was very fun, and very interactive
Dr. Fornoff is very approachable and is always really well-prepared for class. She never has a boring lecture and provides clear criteria for all her assignments.

This class was very lecture and note heavy.  About 3 exams and a good amount of papers and presentations with an assigned group at the beginning of the year.  I didn't have the best experience with this professor, but it didn't get in the way of anything.  Very good at explaining and answering any questions.  Learned a lot of critical information!!

GOAT of the Communication Department. Fornoff is a super easy grader and the class is exceptionally easy. Even if you do struggle, she is tremendous at explaining the important class material. Do the work and study the night before, and you'll be just fine.

I had her for interpersonal communication. She is an amazing professor. She has so much knowledge on the subject but doesn't talk down to you. Loves to answer questions and loves when you ask questions. She does a great job of incorporating what we are learning into real life.

She is a really good lecturer and she is amazing at applying theories to real life (especially the coronavirus to communication). She was easy to talk to about homework and to ask questions. She is an amazing professor and I would definitely want to have her again.

I had the privilege of being with Professor Fornoff for her first semester at Iowa State. She had never taught this class before, and made it fun and interesting. The class is about research methods, as long as you went to class and did the work you can pass with flying colors. Exams are very easy, willing to help if you don't understand something
Helpful and learned a lot in the class, cares for the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not worth the time honestly. Didn't get much out of it.

The class was not helpful for FCP students. Instead of gaining client experience, software knowledge, or even personalized feedback in the capstone course, as students we were fending for ourselves to create the final plan. His lectures were usually irrelevant to helping us create our assignments. Really disappointed with his low-effort teaching.

Professor is genuinely passionate about what he teaches. Very smart and charismatic, excellent lecturer. Homework is light, but is actually useful and relevant to the course. Makes lectures interesting and engaging. Also respects that students have lives outside of school. I learned a lot from Dr. Fox and am really glad I took this course.

Took this class 100% online, lots of assignments but if you put forth effort you will get 100% on all of them. The professor and TA provide great feedback & were very accessible. Quiz every 2 weeks but use the textbook to get answers and you'll be fine. No final either - great use of a class for international perspectives requirement. VERY easy A
He is a great professor and he's funny. However, prepare yourself for the TONS of homework! And of course, there's a quiz every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Fox is a good guy but his teaching strategy is lazy. Prepare to do all the work outside of class & to teach yourself the material. Then, be tested on very specific small details. Lecture is mandatory but he simply restates what you read in the chapters assigned. Class is non-thought provoking and a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Is very much like a high school teacher, albeit a fantastic one, has a regular schedule for assignments and out of class readings, attendance is basically mandatory but you won't mind going. Fox is one of those teachers that is fun to listen to, Highly recommended.

Fox is one of the most intelligent people Ive ever met. He has an incredible grasp on personal finance and financial planning for families. He breaks things down so theyre simple to understand and ties everything back to the big picture. His biggest strength is being able to get his point across and make sure you understand the topic.

Favorite professor I've had at Iowa State. Really knows his stuff and does a great job at making it relevant to the student. Puts a lot of personality into his class and is an extremely easy grader. Learned a lot in this class.
Rodney Fox is probably the best professor at ISU, right behind Wenzhen Li.

310 with him will make you feel like you're failing at life since the grading is incredibly harsh, but you will likely end with a grade higher than expected. There were 17 extra credit points you could get in the class because he knew the grading was VERYYY tough. Best strategy to pass is to work on everything with your classmates, never alone.

One of the most prepared and respected professors I had at ISU. He knows what he talks about and has high expectations. If you want to learn, take this class with him and work hard. Ignore the low ratings on this site: many students in his class expected to pass without doing the work and were not prepared on the prerequisites.

Fox is easily one of the smartest professors in the CBE department and is worth getting to know outside of class. The first couple of weeks were overwhelming, but the class gets easier if you commit to learning outside of class. Exams are extremely difficult but open book with an equation sheet. Good luck passing if you don't attend lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fox is very kind and knowledgable. however I think he is only used to teaching graduate level classes because he teaches in a way that assumes you already know what he is talking about. The assignments are not graded so you can't tell how you're progressing in the class. Quizzes are only conceptual yet exams require calculation. Good luck Charlie
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I had. I do not understand all the negative comments: you have to work to get a good grade with him and many of my classmates were only complaining and blaming the professor. Do your part, study. Prof. Fox will teach you a lot.
He is the best teacher for ChE 310
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the most prepared teachers I had. He is very fair and his explanations are clear. My class had a lot of students who didn't do the work and blamed it on the instructor. He was however great and always available.
Fox is the worst prof. I have ever had at ISU. Couldn't understand anything from his class. Homeworks were not graded. Entire class was graded on 3 exam, 33% each.

Where do I begin..... Prof Fox is a very knowledgeable about computational methods. He just doesnt know how to relay that information to students. He only grades exams, which all had awful averages. Majority of students werent learning the material. He has the option to sub an exam or three, but penalized EC for it. Switch asap and actually learn
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Two words, good luck! Barely learned anything from the class. Exams were way harder than the in-class, hw problems. Grading was harsh as well.

Where do I even begin? I didnt learn a single thing all semester, and I dont think anyone else did either. I would honestly reccomend putting off a class over taking it with Rodney, unless you want a C- and absolutely no knowledge over the topic
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and switch professors. You'll walk away actually learning some of the material and get a better grade. It's incredible how little the entire class walked away knowing after a whole semester.

Fox is one of, if not the worst professor I've ever had. Don't expect to learn anything from his class. It seems like he does the bare minimum to get the material to his students. His lectures are incredibly boring an uninformative. If you have him for class, good luck.

Homework isnt graded so it was very hard to find the want to spend hours working on it. Lectures were very boring and monotone. Goes way too fast and assumes his students understand everything he shows. Hes definitely a knowledgeable guy, I just dont think he understands his students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class was graded entirely by the 3 exams - 33% each. The final was optional to replace the lowest of the 3 exam scores. Exams were all fair but difficult. Fox is extremely knowledgeable but the pace of the lectures was way too fast at times, and he often assumed things were obvious when they really weren't. Class average was curved to a B-.
I took Computational Methods last spring and Fox was a fair professor with fairly easy homework assignments and more difficult and more heavily weighted exams.
Not upto the mark

The worst professor I ever met in my life. This professor's grading criteria was very unfair. You should take an A or else you will get a B grade. There is no grades between A and B. The professor won't reply for your emails once you get grades

Please Don't take this course otherwise your GPA will be f**ked up 

If someone faces this issue, REPORT
This dude was literally mining bitcoin in his office when I went into his office hours. And didn't help me with my question.

Bao is extremely unorthodox, and unorganized. He either doesn't know how to use canvas or just avoids using it which can make it difficult to find certain materials. His teaching style, however, is rather fun and engaging. He will randomly dive into topics he finds interesting and generally they're fairly related to the course content.

One of the stupidest faculty you will ever find. He did not respond to the email. He does not give any feedback on the project proposal. Later during the grading, he will say it is not related to the course topic and he won't give you marks. Easy course to get A I guess but barely you will learn anything.

Forrest is very knowledgeable in programming but cant teach sadly. He was upset that a majority of the class was failing and told us that he'd rather be dying on the beach on D-Day than be teaching us. The first week without teaching us anything, he told us our lab assignment was to program the Taylor series. The worst organization I have ever seen
irritable guy, terrible course, anyway the score is not bad, Good luck.

Needs to find a new profession and needs to seriously stop with the whole teaching thing, I've never experienced a class so unorganized and graded so badly. this is. supposed to be a introduction to coding class and he put problems on their that even the kids that have taken years of computer science get wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: professor knows alot about topic , but has 0 skills in explaining it to students. There was only 2 test that the average was very low and there still wasn't any curve. I could have learned more from YouTube videos than from going to lecture.

Extremely unprofessional, several typos during exams and homework that made it extremely difficult when it should not have been. I do not understand how when creating an exam you are not checking over every detail possible. I do not understand how in such a setting this would not only be encouraged but a requirement.

We did not receive one homework assignment that did not have several unnecessary typos that he would have to correct for us throughout the time it was available. It made doing homework early almost impossible. There were also several typos on the exams that had to be corrected by the professor while we were taking it. Unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This man is a knowledgeable teacher. However, he doesnt communicate with his students very well and can come off as rude. Some of his stuff isnt explained well.

no foundation to the class materials. starts very sloppy. pop quiz is 0 points in form of solving problem or coding on paper. 30% for quizzes and 60% for exams. it says its an intro but you need to know how to code before you start this class. lab is not graded either. his problems has many syntax errors and doesn't explain well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lisa's personal opinion will always overshadow your own ideas - prepare to have to compromise in terms of creative freedom. The projects for this class were unnecessarily dragged out for their simplicity as almost every class consisted of small group meetings. Our canvas grades were also wildly mishandled and inaccurate the entire semester.

Lisa assigns busy work projects that drag out significantly longer than they need to. She also grades based on her personal preferences and not the student's actual ability. Every class follows the same structure where you meet in small groups with her while she provides little to no actual feedback. Avoid her by any means.

She does not explain anything well and make sure you don't miss any classes because she can't put in assignments, but if you miss one day of class, she will put your attendance in right away. If you have the chance change professors asap. Not worth the stress of not knowing what is due, and she will be very disrespectful about your work.

She's not terrible, but certainly not good. Her grading system is terrible and makes it difficult to get an A. She relies on the TA to do the actual teaching, and assigns a lot of busy work. Textbook never got used so that was a waste of money. She reuses her content for multiple classes too, so don't bother taking more than one course with her.

Lisa seems to have decent intentions, but as a professor, she is extremely disorganized, leaves most of the teaching to the TA, consistently shows up late, and never communicates expectations to the class. One of the most infuriating professors I have ever had. I can confidently say I learned nothing from her this semester.

If you're looking for a studio professor, do not pick Fontaine. While the College of Design lacks good studio professors, you are better off with just about any other section instructor. She will rip you apart during critiques with very little respect. It's "Lisa's idea" or it sucks. I would NOT recommend her to anyone.

She claimed to care about mental health and her students but never skipped an opportunity to slam someones work just because it didnt reflect what her style is. She also sent emails out to students checking on them, but would leave those who were struggling with nasty emails, saying they would never survive in the real world.

Lisa is literal a sweetheart. She has about 3-4 projects a semester, but they're worth doing. She gives great feedback and is kind and understanding. She is very specific about what needs to be improved with your projects, but it is well worth it in the long run. You have to work for your grade and projects, but it reflects your work you put in.

Listen to your peers and avoid this woman. There is a reason her class is the only one left open at the end of registration. If you love confusion, frustration, and buying books to never use? Go ahead. If you're thinking "Oh it won't be that bad" well yeah- I thought that too. Not worth the aggravation.

She treats GD majors and everyone else differently. Other majors- be prepared to learn to do everything how GD does it. You are generally berated for doing things any other way. She doesn't let you finish your sentences and makes bad assumptions based on your half-finished one. She doesn't know how to use the programs Restricts creative freedom

Overall very opinionated and can be manipulative when it comes to creative freedom. If you want someone bounce ideas off, take another class. If you wan't to learn something new and stretch you abilities as an artist take anther class. If you like have little freedom for project this is the class for you.

Oh Lisa. A teacher who at first you may find unorganized and easily flustered will eventually prove to be very caring and dedicated to her students. I had her for 281 and was not a fan, but once I got to know her better in 474, she was a different person. She cares so much for 474 and will prove to be a GREAT teacher if given the chance!

Lisa is an excellent professor of design. She makes you think deeper and your work and put the effort in to truly get design. In my opinion it is her tireless, insightful, and on-target critiques of work that gives graduates the backbone to receive feedback in the real world, but more importantly how to reflect on their work and the work of others.
Very sassy and gets frustrated easily, hard to get things out of her especially when you really need something. Mostly a useless class.
VERY opinionated. Will tear you apart during critiques. 0/10 would recommend.
She contradicts herself like no other and is really sassy and snippy.
Savvy in the exhibition design area.  Unorganized and frustrated easily.   Ask for grade updates throughout the semester.  In addition to turning in assignments, make sure she actually receives them.

extremely unorganized, does not explain any of her assignments, gives bad grades to people who did the assignment correctly, requires attendance even though she shows the SAME stuff EVERY class period, gives no assignments for the first half of the semester, then has five due all at once. Worst professor I have ever had.
Cares for her students and is understanding. Needed an extension on a project and she gave it to me. The class wasn't time-consuming either.
Very nice professor who cares about her students. The class was not hard as long as you do your work and participate in class.
Decent teacher, first time so mainly just followed the premade ISU Comm layout: Typical English class with papers and presentations. Tried to encourage participation and small jokes. Very sweet

He clearly knows his stuff, but he is just bad at explaining what he intends to convey. Frequently goes off on a tangent or confusingly explains concepts that he tests. Office hours & questions in class often are unhelpful, as he re-explains in the same convoluted way, albeit with a different sentence structure.

Dr. Peters is one of my favorite professors I've had.  He's really funny and knows what he's talking about.  Take good notes in lecture, the exams always had some pretty difficult math that wasn't covered the best in class, but if you take the time to understand it prior to the exam you'll do just fine.  IE348 is not a hard class

Take this class with students you work well with and get in the same lab group. It will make this class 1000x easier. Attend office hours and pre-exam hours to fundamentally understand the material. Review all previous exams, most problems are just duplicated. There are lots of curves both on the exams and final grade, so if you give effort=pass.

He moves through A LOT of material at a quick rate but is unbelievably knowledgeable and pretty funny throughout lectures. Not always the most exciting topics but super helpful/practical information. Tests can be tricky but he gives you every previous test to study from and answers any question in his office hours. Super awesome professor!!

One of the best professors in the IE department and my favorite at ISU. Go to class, study the material, go to review sessions, understand theory, get an A. He will go out of his way to help students throughout the class. Don't be a student who starts asking questions last moment and you will do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Frank is a good professor but probably the worst grader. He is the only one teaching 348, so try your best to pass his class. Old exam questions and exam reviews are the key. to at least pass the course.

Okay so 348 is NOT a hard class. Literally go all the study sessions and bring a copy of the past tests. He will give you the answers to all of the questions. then study the answers and know the general theory behind them. if you do this the test will be easy. is not you will fail. there is no other way. many have tried many have failed. its easy.

Great lecturer and helpful with answering question. Only complaint is that his exams make you think harder than you anticipate. Study things much more than you normally do and make sure you know the EXACT info you need to answer the questions. He likes to throw in trick questions.
Dr Peters is extremely arrogant and unreasonable. I get challenging your students but the tests were completely ridiculous and his grading was extremely harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Just avoid him

Frank was an awesome professor for IE248 this past semester. He was extremely helpful both outside of class and in class helping students get their questions answered. He was frustrated that students did not do as well on the tests as he thought they would, but it was a lack of effort on the student's part. There were more than ample office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Energetic and loves what he does. Outside of lectures he is quite laid back and will sit and chat with you over anything course-, industry-, and/or career-related. Material can get quite technical, but he somehow manages to make it interesting.

Funny guy, knows a lot about the subject.  Exams are tough (expect to not know what he is asking half the time), class attendance is a must because his online notes are superficial.  Lab is a blast but reports take a long time.  Always available for office hours, even though his wife was diagnosed with cancer this semester.

Don't care for this professor. He makes his class way more interesting than Dr Rivero's but he likes to make things complicated. His tests are ridiculous, unreasonable and sometimes it is hard to understand what he is even asking.  This class would be a more interesting if he did not threaten students with an F - for not having a 60% test average.

He is a very passionate about metal casting and definitely knows what he is talking about. Make sure you pay attention in class because he will quiz you on the content he talks about during class. Dr. Peters is very approachable and willing to help you understand the material . Make sure to study previous exams and ask any questions well before.

He's a great guy and has a passion about what he's teaching.  Honestly go to class, study like it's an engineering test (it is), and land a good lab group.  If you do all that, it should be an easy A.  Otherwise I could see why people do poorly.  You can't just coast through this class.  ITS ENGINEERING, GET USED TO IT.
NEVER HAD A CLASS WITH HIM BUT HE IS A NICE GUY! HELPED ME ALOT ON ORIENTATION DAY!
Teaches things that are more applicable to industry. Doesn't teach out of any textbook.
Tough class with tough exams, but Peters gets excited about the material so he makes it fun to listen.
Very interesting well taught class.  Probably has one of the best teaching strategies at iastate.
good guy
not good...
He sux, avoid!
HE does a good job of going through some potentially boring material. You must go to class daily though. Liberal grader, good instructor. and free candy!!
Bad. Hard to follow in classes, exam questions are unclear. He is not horrible, but avoid him if you can. PS: has a lot of power in the IE department
My favorite teacher at ISU!!
Think that he is funny but sucks like hell never take his class or you will be regreted
potentially the best professor I've ever had

Currently 6 weeks into the semester, and I can confidently say that she is the laziest professor I have had yet (I am a senior). She doesn't respond to emails or grade anything. She says the homework is supposed to be posted on a specific date, but it hasn't been posted yet (it posts the day after it's supposed to).
