Easy class if you go to lecture and pay attention. I learned stuff but could've learned more. We used JMP to do most statistics, which is a good program for introductory stats. We barely did any math. She's a nice person.

Not great, not bad either. She's really chill tho.

Taken multiple courses with her, never got grades back until the day grades are due. Doesn't respond to emails. Very lazy professor. Wouldn't upload new lectures/homeworks for weeks at a time. Gave updated course timelines then missed them. For 5147 (Theory) she got so far behind she had to cut about a third of the course and combined 2 exams.

Her lectures are incredibly boring, but they are not difficult to understand. She loves taking overly long pauses, which contribute to it. The exams, homework, and labs are all super easy, and lab attendance is not mandatory. She also rounds up lab assignments, so you don't even have to do particularly well on them.

Genuinely the laziest professor I have ever came across. It is currently 4 days after the semester has ended and I am still missing a MAJORITY of my grades including the first 2 exams and about 60% of the homework. It took Amy over 5 weeks to even get a SINGLE grade in the gradebook. I have emailed multiple times to no response. Talks very slow.

Didn't have to do any learning outside of lecture. Its rare to find a professor who actually lectures during class time instead of telling you to watch 100 videos before class. She lets you use notes on the exams, and the lab quizzes aren't hard.

The only complaint is the slow grading pace, but 4770 is an easy A course, so it is not that bad. Definitely focus on your R skills as you will learn a lot, and make sure to use the same language about hypothesis tests as was written out on the slides.

Professor Froelich may be my favorite professor I have had at ISU. My first semester here I had a lot going on and she was extremely understanding of my situation and very helpful in finding a way for me to succeed. The subject itself is clear, easy to understand, and very interesting. A wonderful professor and a great class! Thank you Froelich!

Great professor. Easy to understand assignments and homework. The 3 exams were easy as well as long as you do the labs and are familiar with JMP. Froelich was easy to understand and office hours were helpful. Would recommend.

Froelich is a nice lady and was very accommodating, but is not a good prof. All of her assignments and exams are Canvas quizzes, which maybe is a good thing because she's a notoriously slow grader.  Her lectures are incredibly boring. She takes long pauses in between sentences for no apparent reason. If you can avoid taking a class with her, do it.

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS IF SHE TEACHES IT! My main issue with her was that she is the most boring human I have ever had to deal with. And she teaches statistics so it really doesn't help. And every couple minutes she will pause for 2 minutes of silence as if she said something mind blowing. Please do yourself a favor and pick any other prof.
Very nice lady, just couldn't stand lectures. Stopped going to them after two weeks and still managed an easy A-.

Dr. Froelich does take a long time to grade things. It gets kinda annoying. But her class is pretty easy. She makes it pretty difficult to not pass the class. She is very approachable as well. The labs are confusing though. I recommend putting in good effort to the homework and labs, and you'll do fine

All I want for Christmas is my grades returned. Froelich continues to give false promises about grading timelines. It's ridiculous that professors enact strict deadlines for assignments but yet fall short on their own deadlines with no repercussions. Tip: use your exam note sheet to copy the research question answer formats on the slides

Inefficient, disorganized professor who inexplicably takes forever to grade things. I haven't had a grade returned in almost 7 weeks, and I have yet to see my midterm grade. Won't answer questions about how grades in this class will be assigned. Every assignment we have is busywork. Lectures feel like a waste of time, better off using the slides.

She's just so disorganized and irresponsible. She takes forever to grade things, and won't answer questions relating to final grades. Seems like a nice person, but is by far the worst professor I've ever had. I have no idea how she plans to finish grading everything before the semester is done, I haven't had a grade returned in over a month.

Dr. Froelich, while nice, was not present during our semester of STAT301. She was frequently late to class and was absent for our final presentations in lab, preventing us from doing said presentations. Her lecturing style is okay, she explains concepts decently enough but she speaks very slowly. You will not know your grade til after the semester.

Explains the material well and is easy to talk to, when you have questions. My only 2 complaints are the fact that until the very end, I never knew what my grade was because it took a long time to grade exams. Another complaint is that the professor is not exactly organized and is late to class a decent amount of times.

Basically, she doesn't grade anything until the last week of classes. I had no idea what my grade was for the two exams I took until May. I couldn't tell how I was doing in the class really. She does care about teaching so go see the lectures. The R Code is extremely helpful. I suck at Statistics and still managed an A- somehow.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice woman and like her personally, but she is the most disorganized professor to ever live. Constantly late to class, never grades anything ever. We wrote our first exam in February and did not receive our grades until May. May! Posts announcements saying she will do things and then does not do them. The class is easy, but it is not worth it.

She gives really good codes and material to help individuals with limited experience in R and genuinely cares about her students. Her downfall is grading in an untimely manner but to make up for that she is an easy grader and often grades homework for completion. The course is very repetitive of Stat 301 but that isn't her fault at all.

The class can get dry, but Froelich does her best to make it interesting. She gives students a lot of materials to succeed on exams and homework, and the tests are pretty straight forward. Don't expect anything to get graded in a timely manner, but if you have concerns you can talk to her to get help. Very caring and understanding of any conflicts.

Applied Categorical Data Analysis. Interesting underlying material (chi square distributions), bogged down through really dryboring biology and medical studies with very little social science applications. R programs given sometimes do not work. Very latelast minute arbitrary grading and posting of previous solved testsHW's. Avoid if possible.

Never looks like she wants to be in class and sometimes goes MIA and just has T.A.s teach for multiple classes in a row. Not helpful as she is very short with you. Notes rarely include examples which makes the homework harder than it should be. Expect to be lost in a class that should be super easy.

Dr. Froelich was a great teacher in this summer course. She was a clear lecturer, and presented topics slow and steady, periodically seeking student feedback. She scanned and uploaded tidy class notes, as well as solutions for class-time problems, each day of class. Pleasant, friendly, and approachable for office hours. Fair and relevant exams :o)
she is very  irresponsible.

Dr. Froelich is the best statistics professor I have ever encountered.  Her methods are focused, purposeful, and very clear.  If you go into her class wanting to learn the material, you will not e disappointed.  I only wish I would have had her for more classes.
She just care about her project not student anymore.

Tries to be nice, but is unprofessional and not consistent about what she says she will do and what actually happens. Seems more concerned this semester about helping her grad student do research than the well-being of the undergraduate students who are also paying tuition.
An excellent professor!  She made statistics interesting and understandable!

Probably the best lecturer I've had here at ISU. She makes it super easy to learn the material and she doesn't expect us to know stuff she never explained like many other professors do. Very easy to get a good grade if you just go over the study guides.
Goes into a lot of detail and takes the time to make sure everyone understands how to do the work.

She's a great teacher! She is very interested and works very hard to make sure everyone understands everything and is very willing ot help. She has a great layout for notes and the homework is straight from the notes. The quizzes, homework and lab's cap of at a certain percent so it's really easy to get 100% on all of that.

Given that I didn't buy the book, it was a bit difficult to study if I missed a lecture, but otherwise not too bad.  She isn't a great lecturer, but it was about what I expected out of an intro Stat course.

I honestly felt like I was wasting a lot of time here.  She wasted so much class time with ridiculous activities and pointless stories about her life.  Its nice to get to know your professors a little, but really, you can go too far.  She often showed up JUST before class started and wasted class time setting up.

This was my first real stat class, and she didn't put the material in context very well - but given it's a theory class, maybe she's not supposed to.  The first test surprised me in difficulty, but after that I knew what to study and the rest of the class went well.

She's not as bad as some of the other reviewers say...  If you go to class/labs and understand the basics, you'll do fine, though parts of her tests can be a little tricky.  She is very interested in developing interest in the subject.

Dr. Froelich taught the course well.  Apparently, what I found relatively easy my fellow students found incredibly hard.  Dr. F tried to help the students whenever she could.  However, if you don't study and have no concept of statistics, well, Stat 342 is likely a BAD CHOICE as an elective.
If you screw up once, you better drop the class b/c she won't help you and she'll basically tell you you have no hope.
This class was horrible.  I'd take 104 if you have a choice since all the 101 sections are the same. She seemed like she really didn't enjoy teaching and she was kind of a ****.

Dr. Fretwell is one of the best profs I have had at ISU. She is engaging with her lectures, speaks clearly and concisely, and performs fun demos throughout the course. There are a good few EC opportunities both on tests and outside. I'm not an engineer/physicist, but I found this course very interesting and worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Fretwell is an incredible professor. Her lectures are easy to follow and entertaining. Her course is set up for student's success and we all appreciate her knowing that physics can be difficult.

Good professor. The exams are hard, but you can definitely pass if you put towards effort. Ask questions! Exams are not like the practice ones posted. Make sure to attend class in order to get credit for the lecture quizzes. She is very welcoming and I can always count on her to email me back if I had any questions!

She is wonderful! She is very kind, understanding and good at teaching. She uses lots of examples and will explain a concept 5 different ways until you get it. Lecture quizzes come without warning, and she communicates with her TA's!

She is SOSOSO amazing!!! Definitely take her for physics 132 in the spring semester. She is always available after class to answer questions and the exams, and overall class grades always have an incredibly high average. She will always help you get the content hammered into your head. She's great!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fretwell is a wonderful professor. She really made me enjoy the class. I did have to put in a lot of time studying outside of class, but that is more do to the difficulty of the material, and not the professor. The class does have help hours, which are very useful. If I could change one thing, I would make more practice exams.

Highly recommend her for any physics course! She made the material as easy to understand as possible, was always available for help, and made her lectures very interesting. You could tell she was really passionate about physics.

This is one of the most down-to-earth college professors I have had, she is kind and, most of all a human first! Really appreciate her passion and knowledge for physics and would love to have her for another class!
She seems very caring, but just doesnt teach all that well. Its pretty heavily curved, and the homework/quizzes make it easier to get a better grade. The tests are pretty tough

Dr. Fretwell did a good job dumbing down the material as much as she could for it being a physics course. Exams are stressful because it never felt like there was enough time and I would really just put my best guess down for every question. Good thing is that exams are open note. She did get a lot of students for using Chegg so BEWARE.

The lectures were all posted at the beginning of the semester. Her lectures do not explain any concepts whatsoever and expects you to know how to get from step 1 to step 4. Exams are HARD. Averages are usually around 55-70%. The only reason I did good in this class was because I had a tutor.

She got me to love physics. Her lectures are very in-depth and had plenty of in-class examples of physics principles. For each exam, she posts two past exams as well as review quizzes for each chapter. For tougher topics, she posts mini-lectures. She is super friendly and is more than willing to spend extra time outside of class helping you learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There were quite  a few exams and they were extremely difficult. You have to be smart with the cheat sheet she allows for the exams. My tip is to get a tutor and always go to recitation, otherwise you will not do ok on the exams. There was a nice curve at the end. GET A TUTOR

Do anything you can to get Dr. Fretwell! I got destroyed in 111 due to taking it in the summer and having Dr. Al-Saquer as a professor. Dr. Fretwell's lectures are clear and well explained. I got an A- minus in her class just by paying attention in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A nice enough person, but comes off scatter brained. Lectures are demonstration heavy and rarely help you understand the material. Exams are difficult and often focus on areas that were brushed over in class. If physics is your forte then you could succeed, if not the class is hard to follow and results in memorization not learning.

Dr. Fretwell is the best science professor I've ever had. Never miss a lecture; I sat in the front and took good notes that she had posted beforehand on BB, took my time on tests and did all practice exams. She answers questions really well and is easy to understand. Very approachable. DO the homework and don't miss the quizzes!

Treats an engineering "What are the odds class" like a life or death decider for an engineering student. More homework problems than every class combined. Treats each class like a keynote speech that they will make a feel-good movie about someday, where the main character is teaching a new generation the things that got him to the top in this world
Professor does not give any partial credit for exams and it is absolutely ridiculous

Material for the class is thorough, but his lectures tend to be terrible. There's way too much information on slides, and then he rushes through them so quickly that we're usually out of class 30 minutes early. The homework is also graded needlessly hard, the TAs only care about getting the exact right answer and not about the methods you use.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His philosophy is that you should be able to teach physics to anyone, so he tries his best to make it easy and simple to understand. I found this helpful for understanding general topics but not preparing for exams or quizzes. If you take him, look at other professors notes for example problems and look at online resources and past exams to study.

Dr. Frank's expertise on additive manufacturing shines in this course. Lectures are very interesting but make sure to pay attention and study for the quizzes/exams as that's the only graded content. There was a mini project which was easy and stressless. Good grades across the board. Highly recommend this class if you are interested in 3d printing.

Dr. Frank is an amazing lecturer! If you come to class, really pay attention, and study for a few hours before exams and quizzes you will be fine! It is so nice that there is no homework or projects. Just quizzes and exams. Need help --> go to office hours, he is more than happy to talk. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend this class over EE 442. Although it is a whole semester long instead of half, the course itself is so full of information, and I truly felt like I learned so much. The professor is so responsive and grades all tests himself, which is really helpful in consistency. The lectures are funny with real world examples as well.

Frank makes his lectures interesting but there are few resources to help you study for tests. He doesn't post anything online or follow the book so you have to go to class to know the material even though he doesn't take attendance. Class is super curved because test averages are pretty low

His tests are difficult, but he does this because he wants you to remember the material. He makes an effort to get everyone to understand the content in lecture. His office hours are very helpful, and are great for studying for an exam. He's a great guy all things considered.
Good professor, fair guy. Tests for this class are conceptual but his grading policy is liberal, lectures are interesting.
Honestly! One of the best professors at Iowa State! need more professors like him!

This class isn't realy a representation of his teaching I feel like, but he seems like he cares about the students, and wants them all to become IEs. Really nice guy, just makes you really pay attention in class with no distractions. Otherwise you can lose points very easily.
brilliant and fun to work with.:)
Great professor! Made me excited to be an industrial engineer.

Go to class,study all the notes thoroughly. He is extremely helpful if you go to his office hours. Labs are intense but that helps you for 348. Exams are hard and again those help you to prepare yourself for 348 !
Matt Frank was an awesome professor.  Make sure to go to class, and he will make engineering interesting.  Lab was super easy and I went to every class.
You must go to class to do well. He makes it really interesting too. The exams are difficult, but if you study they aren't too bad.

The lab isn't too bad, and he is a great teacher. He is easy to listen to and makes the class interesting. But his exams are miserable. They're not impossible, but make sure to read the questions carefully and go to class. It may seem like there are multiple ways to answer a test, but he's usually looking for something very specific.

I enjoyed having Dr. Frank as a professor.  Definitely one of the best professors I have had so far at ISU. Best advice for doing well in this class is to NEVER MISS a class period.  All exam questions are based off of in class discussions.  If you listen well in class, take notes, and put some work into the lab you can get an A.
GO TO CLASS!!!  "Life doesn't come with notes and neither will my class"  ...just a fyi... but Dr. Frank is a very good professor!
He was a very fun teacher...probably the best IE teacher there is.  Tests are easy as long as you study.
He will drive you crazy with is grading on tests, but the class was a lot of fun to sit through and he makes the material interesting.
easy going. he can be quite funny in the class.
the labs suck, but that's not really all Dr Franks fault (he inherited the class from Peters). lecture is kinda boring, unless you are a manufacturing nut. 348 is probably 10 times more fun than 248.
One of the best instructors in the dept. Easy material, he makes it fun.

I don't know who the other rater had for IE 248, but it wasn't Dr. Frank- his tests are frustratingly unbalanced.  Tons of material is covered in class, and then the exams are only around six questions- so if you forget ONE thing- BAM!- you've just lost 15 points. Oh- and the labs blow.  Badly.

His lectures were PAINFULLY long; if you don't come to class, you will fail based on attendance points alone. His exams were STRANGELY hard (class averages around 50%). With his refusal to post any review/practice exams, it's almost impossible to study for exams. While not impossible, I cannot stress enough to take SCM with LITERALLY ANYONE ELSE.

Nice and funny to a certain extent. Pretty difficult for a 301 class. Tough grader - no regularity to assignments/schedule. Read the chapters before class; the slides are just photos that he explains in his own way. Not much review for exams - he'd tell us to make our own questions to practice. Tophat everyday. Said if we miss 5 classes, we fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He doesn't post dates or have regularity of what day assignments are due so they are easy to miss. He likes that his class is hard and the average score on the exam was in the 60s for a introductory core course.

The professor knows his material very well; however, he has trouble teaching it because the content is always confusing for me. He tends to use profane language and offensive remarks in class. If I were a supply chain major, I would have switched majors.

Frank is a very personable professor; I will give him that. However, he takes too much pride in making the class extremely difficult. He gives almost no exam prep and wonders why we all do so poorly on his exams. The slides make no sense, and those are the only things we get. Take with another professor if you care about your grade.

Professor Montabon created a lively and fun class environment by talking about interesting topics that you wouldn't normally see in a classroom. Keeping the topics interesting, helped keep me engaged and made it easy to participate in lectures. All good things to say about Professor Montabon, and would recommend taking this class as a SCM elective!

He wants the best for both you and the project/assignment given. This means he is tough on you and pushes you to be the best you can be. Overall this class was fun and helped me grow as a student. I can see this class being one of the most impactful classes of my college career.

He's a very knowledgeable SCM professor. His exams are tough, and he takes joy in it. However, he'll make funny jokes during lectures and ease the complexity of the content, making time fly by. I recommend taking him but be prepared for a challenging class and grades that may not be great. Also, I recommend going to his office hours if you can.

Professor Montabon keeps the class engaging with discussions on current supply chain topics. The workload is manageable if you stay on top of it. Unstuck AI was a great study tool that helped me prep for the papers and presentations.

The Good: Frank was a personable teacher and made classes fun to attend. He made an effort to answer questions in class when needed.

The Bad: It seemed Frank took pride in the extreme class difficulty. If you care about a good GPA don't take this class with him. Grading was hard, limited exam prep was available, and speaking in class was required.

Frank Montabon is a good professor overall. He runs the class on articles and lectures on current events affecting supply chains, but he keeps things interesting and is upfront about his biases. He can be a tough grader, but his criteria are fair and you have to put the work in. There are a few longer papers for group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Frank is one of those professors that every SCM is bound to have throughout their major classes. He is awkwardly funny, lets loose in this specific class, and makes class more fun than tough. I appreciate him because you can tell he truly cares. Show up and participate? You'll get a good grade!

He actually tries to prepare his students for the professional business world after college while teaching one of the most interesting classes. As long as you put effort into the class, you will be fine, even though he is a tough grader compared to most professors.

Frank is a solid guy. But sometimes, he is very nick picky about the smallest of things. Like a spouse who tries to find an issue in little things. (For example, he sent an email questioning why people went to the bathroom during 1 hour and 15-minute class). Like relax, we are human and have to use it.also a Harsh grader , but for good reasons.

Montabon is one of the funniest professors I have ever had, so his lectures are very entertaining. The course is pretty difficult, and you need to stay up to date with homework and the course material because he does not really go over previous assignments and exams. He is very light-hearted and easy to talk to if you have a problem or questions.

Professor Montabon is a very helpful professor! I attended office hours multiple time and he reviewed practice problems with me. The exams are tough but studying and asking questions will get you along way in the course. I would recommend taking this class with Professor Montabon. The course is very interesting and I really enjoyed the content!
Most of the problems we encountered were due to the company we were working with but Frank worked to try to fix them. Intense class, but fun and rewarding.
Outstanding class experience.

Professor Montabon is a very solid lecturer and all around great guy. His teaching style allows you to earn your grade instead of receive it. He pushes group work a lot and participation will be a very large part of your grade. I would 100% take another class with Frank and I recommend any and all students to try a course with him.

Frank is very knowledgeable and makes the class interesting with his humor. This class can be difficult, though. There aren't curves or extra credit, and the exams can be rough. Some questions go into greater depth than what we discussed or practiced for the class. Be prepared to spend some time on this class and don't miss out on easy points.

Prof. Montabon is great. I love hearing his dry humor at 9 am. He does a great job giving examples from his own career in order for you to understand the concepts better. However, his tests will catch you off guard if you don't study. He is super knowledgeable, hilarious, and responsive to his student's needs. Highly recommend taking his class.
Wish we would go over the homework more in class but other than that Frank is a solid choice.

Absolutely loved his class. It's solely graded on 4 HW assignments and 4 exams so make sure to study for them. Really tough exams but it's manageable if you go to class (his lectures are really good), take notes and study hard! Would recommend if you're planning on majoring in SCM, he genuinely wants you to learn and understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 491 with Frank is awesome: he is there to answer any and all of your questions. His dry humor humans him and he has real life experience to relate to the class. It is a lot of group work but Frank will be there whenever you need him. Highly recommend!
SCM491 is a very tough class that Professor Montabon made very enjoyable. He was very helpful both in and out of class. I feel he is a tough grader, but he is a fair grader as well.
Great opportunity to work with a real company on a real business problem while getting international experience along the way.

Professor Montabon, is a really cool guy. He believes in making you work for your grade, but not through busy work and other pointless grading. He is really good at explaining things and helping out with group projects. Basically, if you put in the effort (like actual effort), you will pass. (RIP Chile)

Frank is a great teacher! He may seem intimidating but he wants you to learn and he is there to help. A better class if you are better with math - he goes through the math fairly quickly and there aren't many opportunities for practice. He teaches conceptual concepts great and I have a greater appreciation for SCM thanks to him. Participate a lot!

Montabon is a great professor. He really wants you to leave his class with a strong understanding of the material. Show up to class!!! His exams are based off of his lectures, so make sure you're taking good notes. His exams are difficult. They're usually 25 questions multiple choice, so if you study hard you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Montabon is a fantastic, passionate, and caring professor. You can go to him for any questions or confusions. Absolutely a top professor at Iowa State University.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you show up to class and take the homework seriously you will pass with an A. My grade was due to one botched assignment otherwise I would have had an A. I attended every lecture and felt the textbook wasnt necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Montabon is a great professor and does a great job keeping his lectures interesting, especially for those who may not enjoy learning about SCM. One homework assignment due before each of the tests, and the final was not cumulative. Attendance is necessary, but being in his lecture is worth it. Makes fun of White Claw and other non-craft alcohol

This is a tough class with Frank. None of the material is that hard, but rather he makes the exams difficult and grades with the mentality that you must earn your points. Don't let this deter you from taking the class with Frank. Take notes before class and be prepared to listen attentively and discuss actively. Accept the challenge to get better.
Excellent professor. I would recommend him to anyone taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He manages to make a dry subject like supply chain management interesting and fun. Great lectures most of the time and the tests/homework are easy if you study the lecture slides and go to class.

Fantastic lecturer and makes supply chain interesting to learn. Homework is hard but if you ask for help he is willing to help. Exams are extremely difficult so make sure to study or else good luck. Gives random attendance quizzes so class is basically mandatory. Frank makes an effort to get to know every student and make a personal connection.
He is a really difficult grader. Please avoid him at all costs (In the interest of full transparency, he instructed me to leave this review)

Frank is one of the hardest professors at Iowa State. He does not give nearly enough resources to do well on exams, the class average shows it too. Frank is very quick to put the blame on the students for not studying. Beware of his participation points. You are expected to have an input at least 3 times a class. His humor is borderline offensiv
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Frank is a killer professor, I recommend taking any class with him. Lectures are engaging and really helped me understand the material. Tests and group projects are tough and worth most of the grade, but there is usually a curve at the end. A class with Frank may be harder, but I guarantee you'll have a better understanding of the material.

Super sarcastic with a bit of cynicism. He'll give you a hard time, but nothing truly offensive. He takes the whole class time, so don't expect to get out early. He knows the material, so listen to him if you want to actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer that gives insight into real world supply chain topics. Participation matter to him and you are graded on that and your attendance. Gives hard tests but grades the two group case reports that he assigns easier. Very knowledgeable but be ready to do a lot of work for a good grade. Learn a lot in this class from him.
Frank wants you to learn more than just wanting you to pass. Be ready to work hard but walk away knowing more than you thought you would.
Super funny guy.  Teaches practical knowledge that you will need to know when you're working for "real money." Go to class and participate, its worth it.
Read the book and go to office hours to pass
The class is very difficult but he is a great teacher and lecturer
Great Teacher and lecturer although grading is hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great class but don't take unless you specifically need it. Prof is awesome but grades are very difficult to come by.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Frank is 1 of my fav profs so far. He makes the lectures interesting and practical. There were 4 tests (combined concepts and math). Math was easy and conceptual part was fair; practice the worksheets & read the book, you'll be fine. There were pop quizzes; show up, you'll get full credit. 2 group projects were okay. You'll learn lots in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is an amazing teacher that will give you a hard time but he makes sure class is fun yet productive. If your a marketing major he will give you hell, all the time about your major.
Great guy. Very helpful. Understanding. If you're kind and respectful to him, he will be to you.

I highly recommend Frank as a professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable about supply chain and shares his knowledge with students. His teaching style emphasizes learning and applicability, not memorization and facts. Be prepared to work hard in all categories of class (homework, projects, participation); you will rewarded for the work put in.
Great professor, learned a lot! Tough grader. He wants you to participate in class a lot (which is part of your final grade).
Good teacher. Lectures are interesting. Participation is graded.
This Prof Really knows his stuff. The Lectures are somewhat conversational, but do the reading or he will start assigning points to in class activities to force participation.
If you go to class and complete the homeworks, you'll do fine. Frank is a good guy.

Make sure to really participate and go in if you need help--he doesn't want you to fail, even though the class is hard. Lectures are worth going to cause he is so funny, it makes class go by quickly! All in all cool class but be prepared for a tough class.

I took this class as a tech elective, and I really enjoyed it. Frank is a realist and conveys the material extremely well, just go to lecture, and pay attention for an "A." He is also funny, which works. The exams are tough, only because of the memorization of terms and ideas. The math is easy (multiplication with a calc.) I highly recommend him.
First day he said truth in advertising about himself. He also said no curve and said it was a tuff class. But he did a great job making lectures fun and informative. A+ professor in my book.

Not a business major but he explained concepts clearly enough  to understand. He is incredibly helpful, but you have to make the move and ask the questions. Can come off a bit arrogant, but would definitely take more classes from him - he knows how to teach and how to make it entertaining and interesting.

Frank is the by far the best professor I have ever had. The class was not super easy, but he is a very interesting lecturer and keeps the class fresh and engaging. I honestly love Frank and would marry him if he asked me. Shame he is married, and that I am a dude.  He also gives very helpful life tips and has very interesting career ideas.
He is always there for you in his office hours and will go out of his way to help you understand. Show up and try your best. Dude is a bro.

Frank is by far the best professor that I have had at Iowa State so far. He uses his real world consulting background for class examples. That being said, don't expect and easy A or even a B if you don't put any effort into the class. Reading from the book really helps as some of the examples Frank uses in class builds from book examples.

Frank is a great guy... but perhaps not the greatest professor. Lecture slides were vague- you have to pay close attention to everything he says during class. Study, study, study for exams. Read the book. The saving grace is the two group projects- he grades rather easily on those.
very helpful and U learn a lot for ur career but can be a GPA killer

Prof Montabon was a very good professor. Every class was filer with examples regarding everything we were discussing. He was down to earth and very willing to answer question during class. Also quick to email back. I never went in to talk to him but I'm sure he'd be just as generous. I only used my book for extra examples for math. Overall goodprof

One of the best teachers I've had at ISU. While this was not an "easy A" course, it reassured my decision to be a supply chain major. Extremely knowledgeable and has the best interest for his students.
Great professor. Definitely knowledgeable about supply chain management and will make you work for your grade as you should in any class.
Very knowledgeable professor, keeps class interesting with jokes and stories.

Montabon is one of the best professors here at ISU. He gives lots of real life examples and how it relate to the course concepts. He tries to make every class fun and yet educational at the same time. All the homework are very doable as long as you put in some time and effort, and you can also compare it with the TA. I highly recommend Montabon.

Montabon is a great professor and an awesome guy! The class content can be hard to grasp but he explains it so that it relates back to college and real life terms. I highly recommend Montabon, especially if you're not a SCM major you'll want him for this course as he thoroughly explains content.

Prof montabon was hard, but I loved it. He challenged me to grow in ways I didn't know we're possible.  His class last spring left me yearning for!  I wish he were teaching scm-485.  I guess prof grawe will have to do.

Frank is a fun and entergetic guy to say the least. The class is canned as they all teach the same material and use the same night exams. He could do better with getting grades out and communicating grade related issues. Overall, he's a lot of fun, especially early in the mornings. He may not be the easiest of instructors for this course however.
Great teacher, always made class interesting and was always willing to help his students.

This class was my 8 am and I was more than happy to actually get up for it. Very enthusiastic and uses easy real life examples to help understanding. Always keeps the class lively and makes us want to listen. Very helpful if needed and was a riot to have every morning. Grade based on some attendance, homework (hardest part) and tests.

He is the most enthusiastic teacher I have ever had. It was so easy to go to class because he made it fun by cracking jokes. Use the TA's to help you with homework and you are guaranteed to get 100% on them. Tests are multiple choice. The only bad thing is that he doesn't give a study guide and other teachers do.

Keeps the class fairly interesting. Class seems like a rehash of the 485 and 424 classes. Has unreasonable participation standards of his students. Book was rarely used and the tests were difficult to study for.

His sense of humor makes the class interesting. Tests were tough..Harder than SCM 424. He never tells the class when things are due or when the test is until a week before, which blows. In addition I felt the slides aided in my learning very minimally. You can try using the book to learn, but it has errors. Recommendation?=take with diff. teacher.

He makes class interesting with his sarcastic sense of humor, but he does not prepare students well for the exams.  If you want both an interesting class and a good grade, take it with Jennifer Blackhurst. I ended up having to go to her lectures in addition to his, because her exam reviews were extremely indicative of the material on the exams.
Had him as a professor in australia omg are all professors in the us that hot!! I couldnt wait to go to my lectures every week you guys are very lucky

Very knowledgable in subject matter, has real world experience so he actually knows what he's talking about. VERY cynical about anything and everything. Wants the best for you and your future, so def take him if you can.

Print the slides, they help a lot.  Go to all classes, all the homework = a test grade.  He is a great professor, the material is boring so he tries to spice it up with jokes, that aren't the best.  If you sit in front he will pick on you like a stand up comic might.  Do the problems, do the problems, do the problems - best way to study.

same jokes over and over, talks about how students have had trouble with certain material, yet covers it for like 5 minutes.  attendance is basically mandatory because he has random homeworks and none can be dropped.

He means well, but I agree with many that he spends a lot of time trying to make stupid jokes. Go to class so you can get 100% on assignments. Missing 1 dropped me to a 94% on homework. Tests are best 4  of 5. You do have to study, but if you go to class & look over slides, it's really not too bad. He's great at communicating ?s to the whole class.

idk how ppl rated him arrogant and such bt go to cls and u'll know why he's one of my fav prof. entertaining while learning. thumbs up! tests are not easy tho, bt if u pay attention and never miss a class. tests are easy
Great teacher, his class is tough, but he's extremely helpful. Definitely go talk to him during office hours.
Ya really gotta show up for class to learn stuff.  He's got a dry sense of humor, but ask him about home brewing and it'll open a new door!
Engages class everyday. Knows his stuff. Homeworks can be a little unclear at times but very helpful if you go to his office and ask questions. One of my favorite professors at ISU.
This professor is great. Some may question his grading practices but hard work pays off.He needs to implement the use of "carrier pigeon" on contacts. Overall I give it a two thumbs up.
Great class. Montabon knows his stuff & is very passionate about  the subject. Practice your presentation skills, he really watches for quality not quantity.

This guy is sharp & knows his stuff. His office hrs helped. He also drops by the computer lab to see if anyone needs help on HW. He tracks & grades attendance/tardies, so be there every day & on time. He uses a lot of sarcasm, but never mean-spirited.
Frank Rocks!  Learned alot!
he hides in his office...

Hard class but as long as you try hard, ask questions, and show up for class you will do fine. Frank has terrbile sense of humor but willing to make fun of himself and get into light "trash talking" with students.
I give him a thumbs up.
great class. watch grammar in papers--they need to be perfect!

He cares about the students who care, doesn't so much about the ones who don't.  You must get on his good side by participating a lot.  He likes to have fun, but can't go an entire class period without using his "Montabon French".  Lastly, he needs to have his wife pick out his clothes!

I absolutely loved this class.  The classes were really interesting.  He brought in alot of outside information to the class.  The professor makes sure that all the students are engaged.  He is very smart and knows what is going on in the industry.

He tended to focus on topics/ examples you as a student couldn't relate to and didn't have back ups, which made it seem that he wasn't sure of his audience for the class.  He doesn't let you have time to aCtually  figure out problems before he tells you the answers so it is hard to tell if you know the information for the test.

Class was so boring. He is not the best lecturer. He assigns group members for projects so that wasn't the best situation.  His test are split half and half with multiple choice and short answer. There is a lot of reading of really boring articles.
Very nice guy, a little unclear about homeworks, but willing to help you
arrogant, his test suck
No Comments

Frank is an awesome professor!! He is funny and seems to really want his students to do well. He is always available during his office hours, and is very helpful. He seems to enjoy the subject matter and it shows in his teaching. He is also involved in the ISUAPICS club,& encourages students to join

Frank's lecture style is easy going with some bad jokes thrown in.  He's pretty arrogant if you ever go in and see him in his office.  He doesn't really listen, and you know that b/c he doesn't really answer your questions.  The class is super easy, though, so just show up and sit through it

Gwen was one of my favorite professors I've had at Iowa State! She made the lectures extremely interesting, she covers interesting brands and companies during class. MKT 447 was mostly group projects and participation points that are easy to get by attending class and answering questions here and there. Definitely recommend taking a class with her!

Gwen is very experienced in the work world, and translates that into class by using examples that she has done to help students learn. She is by far the best professor I've ever had at Iowa State, and I would take any class that she teaches.
Amazing professor, my favorite at Iowa State so far. Her class was very engaging, and I was never bored. I wish all of my classes were taught by her!

This is a hard class. Not much guidance for projects but he goes over some cases in class. He doesn't like to post stuff so if you miss it in class you just won't have that information. Tests are tough too.
Professor Hood was great - the class itself is tough. Go to class, take notes, and study what he recommends and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I think the class itself is fairly hard so I give him a pass on some of it.  I don't think you are going to get a much better teacher for the material.  With that said there are a few things that while not super important he is a stickler about such as no phones and he won't give out much information to keep other than the slides.  Quizzes are hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Fred is a very clear cut professor. There are three projects, two exams, and two quizzes. You can choose your partner for the projects which is nice as well as labs available if you are struggling with the concepts. I never used the book, but it could help if you are unfamiliar with finance concepts.
His exams are hard.

Hood is a great professor for 327. He makes the class as interesting as possible and is always willing to help you IF you ask for it. The class itself is not the easiest, but definitely not the hardest either. If you go to class and take good notes, you'll do very well. Do not buy the textbook.

A little scattered in his lecture approach. He tests over material in his lecture only, even on historical tidbits that you thought were just there to provide context. He's a tough grader, but will help if you ask for it. Read the slides thoroughly, and understand them to get an A.
He was a great prof and he was nice to look at as well!

I would give him an average rating. Sometimes he was unclear about the material, while other times he taught it very well. He's pretty passionate about what he teaches but when we did poorly on an exam, he blamed us for not putting in enough effort. I find bonds to be very boring so don't take this class unless you have an interest in them.

This class is not easy. Go to class and take good notes and you will get an A. Otherwise don't expect to do well. He is a decent teacher. Likes to read off slides. The majority of the grade is the two tests. The quizzes and projects make up the rest of the grade. Projects are easy though.
Extremely difficult course! Refuses to use or show students how to use financial calculators. Strictly formulas...sucks
Extremely difficult course! Refuses to use or show students how to use financial calculators. Strictly formulas...sucks

Bad teacher! Having experience on Wall Street does not mean you can teach the subject!  55% class average on first test and claimed it was our fault for not studying. All test based, no homework or quizzes.

The professor is extremely inconsistent. She is nice, however she never reminds students when something is due until its just about due. Her grading system is terrible, very inconsistent among groups and was a very tough grader.

I took SPCM 312 with her and she was amazing. Her grading is easy and she understands that not everyone loves public speaking. There are group speeches which I really liked because they are based on business projects. Class is mandatory because she thinks you need to have an audience for speeches. No exams only 7 quizzes throughout the semester.

Prof. Fulton was really laid back during class. She uses the 'Un-grading System' to grade your essays. Basically if you meet most of the requirements on the given rubric you will get full credit. If you do not, then you will receive half credit but you will get a second chance to turn in your essay to get full credit. 10/10!

Super nice and cares a lot about her students. Class can be boring at times but that was expected with a class such as speech. Definitely was able to improve my speaking skills and my confidence while speaking to others. You HAVE to show up to class everyday or you won't do well as attendance is a grade.
Class content is pretty boring honestly, but she did a good job of teaching the class nonetheless
She is a pretty attractive and pretty helpful lady.
One of the best TAs I've ever had. Much more helpful than the professor

TA for Speech 212. She is really funny and helpful as a TA. She gives you the grade you deserve for each of your 3 speeches in class(small size).  One of my favorite classes to go to and way better than lecture.  Come to class and expect to have a good time.

Ms. Futhey may be  tough grader but I got so much out of her class. I never got below a B- and I didn't put in 100%. I think she is a great teacher that only expects a lot because as college students we should be putting effort into English. It is very important in today's society. Her class even inspired me to change my major. Would take again!

She is a very tough grader. If she want's to be super hard, she can teach higher level English Courses. I am a very good writer and she always just tore apart the work. She expects WAY too much from kids straight out of high school.
She's a grad student but acts like she is a professor. Grades off her own opinion and refuses to give A's. Take English with someone else.

Joe is one of, if not the best, professors I've had. He obviously is very passionate about what he does, and his lectures are very inspirational. He cracks lots of jokes and is very down to earth. The class itself isn't really hard at all and there is no final exam which is really nice.
Joe Sample is such a wonderful man and professor. He is passionate about what he teaches and loves to crack jokes in class. I enjoyed having him as a professor :) Also no final!!
Easy class nice guy
Joe is one of the best professors I've ever had. He takes time for his students and provides opportunities for growth. His teaching style is amazing and everyone I've met loves him

An incredibly understanding and compassionate guy who will do anything he can to help you succeed in his class. There's an easy quiz over every chapter and one group project at the end of the semester that is not hard at all. He makes class fun and engaging, and makes an effort to get to know his students and connect to them. Genuinely a great guy

Joe Sample is one of the best professors I've had in my two years here. He is so willing to hear from his students, help in any way possible, and eager to share knowledge in his class. Very helpful as well!

literally the coolest professor I have ever had. He is so thoughtful and open with his students. He is understanding and engaging in class. Every student in my class loved him. We did not have many assignments in this class and I was still able to learn a huge amount of information. Super passionate and hilarious!

Not clear about due dates but easy class. Only two quizzes and then a big paper and group project at the end. You will read an extra book but it is an interesting book. For example I got to read Tuesdays with Morrie for my paper. The class is very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Understanding professor and grades things quickly. He reaches out and remembers students but not in an overbearing way.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Gary makes such a difficult class easier to manage. He is very kind and understanding, tbh i submitted so many assignments late but he accepted them with no penalty every time. He is a stickler on grading, but he thoroughly explains what you need to follow and why!

Gary is great. He's really funny in class but I will say he puts in a lot of work when it comes to grading. That being said though he's willing to give some leniency on deadlines and late assignments which is very kind of him. I would recommend taking this class with him and I'm considering dropping my journalism major lol.

If you show up and do the assignments, you will be completely fine in this class. Attendance matters to do well, but Gary is super accessible outside of class and is always willing to answer questions. The majority of assignments can be revised and there is often work time for assignments during class where he will give out advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hard class and shouldn't be that hard on assignments. I think that he should be more easy and not grade things so harshly. If you don't like to write and do anything in journalism don't take this class he is goofy. Even if you attend the class you can only fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I have never disliked a class or professor more than Gary.  If you mess one single thing up while writing a paper, you automatically fail.  He expects a bunch of college students to be perfect writers.  Unless you are a professional writer, you wlll dislike Gary and his classes.

He was tough but fair. One of the most difficult professors to please. He was good at giving extensions. If you miss class, you must explain why before or shortly after to receive partial attendance credit. Be prepared to fail your first 2-3 AP quizzes. It gets better.

SO GOOD! Gary is great and gives really good feedback. AP style is annoying but all tests are collaborative so work with others in the class to make sure you get all the points. Assignments are relatively easy and his grading is as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gary is a phenomenal professor. If you have the chance to take his classes, DO IT! He really knows his stuff & is very passionate about media. He's legit a Greenlee LEGEND!! 201 is a great course. You learn a lot about PR, AD & JLMC. Gary gives great feedback but makes you work! This course is a good way to see if the media industry is for you.

Gary is an outstanding professor who deeply cares for all of his students. He gives students the option to make up nearly all assignments if they aren't satisfied with the grade they received. He knows AP Style and the ins-and-outs of the industry very well, and he helped me understand journalism a lot better. Take any class you can with him.

The man knows AP style like the back of his hand, plus he has a solid foundation of public relations and advertising, too. The class itself is scary at first BUT TAKE HIS ADVICE. Read the news, work long and hard on the AP quizzes, and push yourself to get better as a writer. This class will tell you if the industry is right for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take any and all classes with Gary.

Very nice and down to earth person who would give grace if you asked. Lectures were fine, went over a lot of content found in regular high school English classes. Yet, he made it fun to be there and would give extra credit during some classes. Very lenient on papers and would give a good grade if you made quality work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took this class summer 2025. It's a hard class to take over summer as you really have no direction, and have to rely on the textbook to learn. The reports weren't challenging but take time. Overall fair grader and responds to emails in a timely fashion. If you have questions or concerns, he's always willing to help.

Awful class, very boring, unclear assignments/projects. Almost makes it purposefully confusing. Changes things last minute. Attendance is mandatory yet you won't do anything with your team till 1-2 months in. He will be randomly gone and take points off even if he asked you to do it.

Really easy course and crazy easy grading. Attendance is super weighted, and essay feedback was very delayed, but neither had a very big impact on the class experience. Very few assignments, but by the time they were introduced in class, it was a pretty quick turn around to turn it in.

This professor is an easy grader, gives good feedback, and answers any questions students might have. All of the professor assignments are straightforward. As long as you plan your essay topic before hand you will do great in this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is hardly available and struggles to get back in a timely manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I do not really enjoy public speaking, but this professor really made me enjoy the class more than I should have. Very nice and caring guy who cares about the success of every student. Created a great class environment throughout the semester. Light grader and gives good feedback. 100% recommend taking speech with this guy.

The class itself had a lot of homework, but none of it was very hard. Lots of SmartBook assignments and discussions. Mr. Galletley was very understanding when I had a tough group to work with. When they didn't do their parts or put in as much effort as I did, he gave us different grades to reflect that. He was very understanding and helpful!
Class was really easy to pay attention to because he made it so engaging.
I think he's the most engaging professor I've had since being at Iowa State. I feel he really wants his students to succeed. Great energy and atmosphere.
One of the only professors I've found worth listening to here. Actually cares and runs a successful business himself.
HE CARES about your success in the classroom but mostly outside of it. Mission is for you to succeed in the real world and pushes you in the classroom to help you succeed outside of it.

DO NOT TAKE ACCT 215 WITH TIM YOULL HATE YOUR LIFE. He is actually a horrid professor, he will fly thought material and not explain anything then expect you to take test questions about it. He will spent 3/4 of a lecture on material that isn't even tested on. I regret taking this class with him so much. He is a TERRIBLE professor. He cannot teach
Great guy and makes lectures fun, love this dude

Tim Gartin is a great professor, who makes class fun with fascinating personal stories related to the legal concepts presented. 

The class is exam heavy, but I wouldn't listen to any of the other ratings saying they were super hard. Just pay attention in class, take notes, and review before the exam, and you'll do just fine.

Be prepared to study a lot of terms for each exam. You will be learning new material for the next exam on the week you're taking the prior exam. You will need to learn a lot of terms. He is an understanding and caring professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor i have had at iowa state, he actually is passionate about the subjects and makes class very fun to come to, he explains everything very well and conceptually and it helps a lot with understanding the stuff that's on the exams.

Tries too hard to come across as fun. Hard to know what we exactly need to know for the tests. Feels like he just free balls his lectures; scattered everywhere. Always asks questions to students to participate, but we never know the answers lol. He should take it as a hint we aren't getting what's going on. Lot's of memorizing needed for this class

He might do a good job explaining how it might relate to real life since he is an actual lawyer, but it doesn't correlate well with what we need to know for the exams. The tests all involve trick questions. We never dive deep into content either. This course is just a big information dump. and 5 exams is crazy.
Very exam heavy class, if you do not do well on exams, your grade is going to be bad, no extra credit or any other help, have to be a good test taker
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gartin owns a law firm in Ames, so he is able to provide professional insight during his lectures which adds some value. He is a pretty good lecturer and has a lot of good stories to tell. The only bad thing is that he goes through the slides at lightning speed. I would recommend only writing things down in class when he says they are important.

Gartin is an engaging professor and passionate about his material and brings a lot of value to lectures. After class, he answers quick questions students may have about the material. The class is very exam and vocab heavy, so take of the textbook to succeed. However, he outlines the way in which the class will work and makes it easy to succeed.

When I first started this class, I was annoyed of all the readings and he didn't allow computers in class. However, Gartin is very passionate about the material, and his lectures are interesting. He shares stories and tells you what you need to know. I recommend attending lectures, even if they aren't mandatory. He also calls on people randomly.

I personally loved taking ACT 215 with Tim.  You have to show up to class and you have to take notes with pencil and paper.  If you show up to class and take notes you will do great in the class and learn a lot.  He really tries to make the lectures worthwhile and interesting with his personal experience and I would advise taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gartin is honestly a great professor. He has a lot of real world experience and tailors the lectures to great personal stories about his law firm and cases he has had. Yes, he doesn't use slides and doesn't allow computers. I thought this was going to be an issue, but it's much better. Take him if you have a change and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class online. It is difficult to watch his lectures because he does not provide any visuals whatsoever. You just stare at his face for hours. The good thing is that the tests are open note and he is really nice about curving. He even let us retake an exam and added a curve on that too. If you want a good grade its worth taking with him.

DO NOT TAKE GARTIN. Absolute worst teacher I have ever taken in all my years of school. He is a horrible professor don't even know how he got hired. Highly recommend taking Bootsma because if you take this class with Garin you will be drowning in reading and have no help whatsoever from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take this class! With Tim, it's well worth an 8am. He shares real life stories, a plethora of life advice and is intriguing to listen to. You can see and feel his passion for his work as an attorney. It's clear he practices ethically and is a high-achieving attorney. You'll need the book & it's worth showing up to class -it'll make tests easier.

Tim Gartin is not a good professor. I took him for 215 and his only class is at 8 AM. He does not let you use your computers to take notes and he also doesn't use a powerpoint. He also doesn't write anything on the board. He believes the best way to learn is to listen to him. Take Bootsma.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Khan for Linear Algebra (MAT 207) my first semester at Iowa State. He's a really nice guy with a good sense of humor. My only complaint was a lot of what he covered in lectures was wildly different than what ultimately ended up on exams, which were created by multiple professors in the department. Super accessible outside of class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a nice person, but is lectures can be hard to follow. His handwriting isn't the best. Butler videos helped me more than anything.

I took MATH 385 with Khan. The class is missing a pre-requisite that it should have, which is linear algebra. Do not take PDE without taking linear algebra. I was able to struggle by, but it was not enjoyable. Attendance is not mandatory and he posts lecture videos, so I'd suggest skipping and watching those instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is clear that Khan is a newer professor and doesn't have much teaching experience yet.  I don't think he wants to go fast; he is kind of forced to due to the material volume.  That being said, he was a very good and straight forward teacher for Calculus 3.  He shows solid example during class, and he really wants his students to do well.

I went to several different calc three profs to see which one I liked best. Khan was the one that I enjoyed the most and could actually sit through an entire lecture with. Highly recommend going to the lecture and watching Butler videos afterward to work with the material. The class moves pretty fast, and Khan did a good job explaining the topics.

Khan is a nice guy but a horrible professor. He's very inexperienced and doesn't seem to care about changing his teaching style to be effective. His writing is illegible a lot of the time, and he makes simple algebraic errors. Do yourself a favor and just watch the Butler videos instead - they'll be more helpful than ever attending his lectures.
Khan teaches Calc 3 well, but teaches very quickly. A lot is gone over each lecture. Make sure to keep up with content.

He was a new professor when I took his class for Calc 1. His lectures were a bit of a shock when I had only taken high school level experience to the class. The tests were extremely difficult and so was the homework, but once you get used to it the class becomes a lot more manageable. Albeit new, Khan wasn't at all a bad professor

You are better off watching Butler videos than going to class. Khan is a newer professor, often made mistakes, and has a lot to learn. Very smart just figuring things out still. The class is exam heavy and the exams are ' not about getting the right answer but about getting as much right as you can.' it's designed for you to fail. Don't freak out.

A lot of other students seemed to think he was bad and that he didn't know what he was doing, but he does. He can make mistakes with simple algebra in lecture, but he knows his calculus. All the calculus sections are coordinated so you can go to any lecture, or watch lectures online. I like Khan cuz he shows applications and related math tangents

While khan may have a low rating during the time I am writing this review, it was also his first year of teaching Calc 1. Other than maybe starting out the example problems with an easier question, I've learned a lot during this class. He's a truly nice professor and has already grown so much in his teaching style throughout this semester.

I am taking this class Fall 2021. He stated that this was his first teaching calc1 at Iowa state, I would say he has improved a bit since the beginning of the year. The biggest complaint I have is for him to slow down. When working problems, he will go too quickly where he makes small mistakes and students cant keep up with the content.

You are better off watching Butlers videos online. Going to Khans lectures just makes you more confused, and students are constantly having to correct his simple mistakes. Hes also the king of um and uh. Hes a nice guy, but not the best at teaching Calc 1.

Just watch the Steve Butler videos, Khan is a math major and he teaches the principles of Calc which is way too confusing. His lectures are nothing like the homework or quizzes. 90% of this class is teaching yourself. Do yourself a favor and go to every SI meeting and go to help hours.

Lectures are pointless. You are better off getting a longer lunch and teaching yourself. I started watching the Steve Butler videos on canvas corresponding with the in person lectures and they were the same. Khan copies butlers vids word for word. Dont waste ur time. When he doesnt copy he messes up the problem and students correct him

Lectures went by very quickly. The material was crammed into a 50-minute block, and some of the material didn't even pertain to the HW. One semi-helpful thing is the ability to redo HW problems and get an okay-ish summary of what you're supposed to do. Mainly a "teach it yourself" course. Edit: Was okay since it was his 1st year. Room4improvement
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lecture heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Gassmann is amazing, he made such a huge effort to keep the class's attention even though it was a Monday night class. I would absolutely take him again and you should too if you have the opportunity.

Amazing. Amazing. Amazing. Mike goes out of his way to learn everyone's names and teaches a very fun class. He is inspiring, wonderful teacher, and makes the class easy for everyone to succeed. Whether you're taking this class for fun or for credit you will have an amazing time either way.
Genuinely the BEST teacher I have ever had at Iowa State; he is the one that made me find my love for sales.  He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed... truly the best.
Absolute gem of a human being. Take his class, he is sure passionate and incredibly good at his job. If you are reading this take the class. If you are reading this as Mike, you are appreciated.
Mike is an incredible professor who is truly there for students. He makes classes and the sales role-play engaging and practical. I learned a lot in this class and got great feedback.

Greatest professor at Iowa state bar none. I truly believe that he is the only professor that has taught me anything in my 4 years at Iowa State, and it is because of his experience and personality. He made it easy to come to class and made lectures something you felt you gained a lot from just listening to his experience.

By far one of my favorite professors I've ever had. His lectures are entertaining and is super helpful when it comes to understanding material. He uses real life experiences to teach and is very knowledgeable about sales. Helped me better understand my passion for sales and gives great advice. Would 100% take him again.

Mike was the most incredible professor I have ever had here at Iowa State!! I was actually bummed out when he  would cancel class! His lectures are engaging and beneficial and he really cares about his students greatly. He even drives all the way from Cedar Rapids to teach at Iowa State, Mike is one of a kind!!!

Mike is, without a doubt, the best professor at Iowa State. He genuinely cares about each and every student he has. I have never gotten to the end of a class and thought to myself, I wish this class had gone on for another semester. If you have the opportunity to take any class with Mike, take it. Easily the best professor I have had ever!
He was very successful in industry and you can really tell why. He gives a lot of examples from his past career and the entire class is just overall very interesting

Mr. Gassmann was an awesome professor. He made his lectures fun and interesting, and he took the time to know everyone's names. The quizzes and tests were all online, which was nice. We had a group project to present at the end of the semester, but throughout the semester he helped us work through it and make sure we were on track! He's a good guy!
cvbnmfdghj
As an english class, everything we did in this class was expected. No surprises. Most of the work is team based. Prof Gasior was a very fair grader and gave feedback when asked.

Nice professor as long as you do your work. Attendance is mandatory and you can not miss more than 3 classes or you will be dropped from the class. Hard grader but allows you to revise on most papers so you can improve your grade a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Zach is a great teacher for English and he really gives interesting information in class. He is very helpful and cares about each individual it seems like. He is tougher in grading sometimes, but lenient in the beginning.

This was a half semester course. There were a few prezi presentations, films, videos, chapters, and articles to read/watch each week and then an discussion, assignment, and quiz. As long as you do the work, you get good grades on the assignments. Overall, easy class and learned really interesting things! I would recommend!

I took the online half-semester version, and it was intense. About 2 chapters of reading, multiple documentaries, a research essay, and a test every week. Some of the quizzes are over more trivial topics, so make sure you have a text version of the documentary transcripts that you can ctrl+F on. Grading is pretty easy, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Discussion and reponse, 1-2 page paper assignment, and quiz were biweekly. Discussions were fine, but assignments were harshly graded; detailed papers are essential. Quizzes were challenging (I got average 50%-70%). Take thorough notes from all sources; no Quizlets available. Modules took 7-9 hours; manage your time wisely and you should be okay.
Cares a lot about his students' success, encourages creativity and is a great resource.

Joel is awesome. He is a professor who actually wants you to do well which is a nice change of pace. He teaches so we can learn and not just memorize stuff. Everything in this class is applicable to a future in advertising. I enjoyed doing the homework and projects which is weird to say.

I have had the privilege of having Joel twice. My first experience was mediocre. More recently, my experience was less pleasant. Very little interaction with his students. It is difficult to remain engaged during lecture. He seems like he has given up.

He is awesome! He is so kind and sweet and actually want you to learn and do well. HE cares about your work and how you are doing. He is an actually teacher. Instead of just professing his knowledge he teaches you it and makes sure you do well. Also if you forget to turn stuff in he will let you turn it in late and not doc you off any points.
Class is somewhat difficult but the workload for an online class is manageable.  You will need 3-4 hours a week at least for this class.

Standard advertising class--- show up, group up, do presentations. Joel knew a lot about the brain and this class was surprisingly interesting. Fun professor as well. Exremely laid-back, which sometimes sucks because a little direction is needed from time to time. I'd recommend him though.

Joel is a nice guy but his teaching lacks a lot. We learned absolutely nothing in this class. We had 8 total projects to do throughout the semester and we worked on 1 worthless project the entire semester then the rest were just due at the end of the semester. Grades you by how he likes you. I got A's and B's on projects but then a C- in the class.

Joel is a very easy-going guy, doesn't demand too much of his students, just wants honest work out of them.  Sometimes his technical knowledge of the field seems a bit dated, but overall knows what he is talking about.  Don't be afraid to be creative in his class - he likes that.
Joel is a great guy, very helpful, keeps class fun.  One of my favorite profs so far!

If you can do not take any classes with Dr. Geiger. He seems to not really care about how the students are doing or if the students know the content, as long as he finished his slides. Which often do no contain exercises examples. We had him have a question on the exam about a topic he barely covered, and did not solve a single problem. Really bad.
grade is very low without any reason

Dr. Geiger is quite knowledgeable, but the way the course is taught is ineffective. There are no breaks from start to finish with this course - labs and homework every week, including weeks where there is an exam. Geiger usually teaches too slowly to cover all the content in his incredibly long lecture slides, so get ready to learn on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: lots of resources available on his website, but refuses to use canvas, makes the TAs run everything from canvas to the exams.  Grades are slow, communication is minimal, and he drops huge end-of-semester bombs  final projects.  He's very fair on grading and the curve, but its a hell of a workload and you'll be on your own unless there are kind TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things
