reviews.comment: He seems to care more about the research he does rather than the classes he teaches and has been absent most of the semester. I believe the TAs teach more of the class and grade more of the class than he does. Learning a class on your own may be effective for some but it does not work for me.

Dr. Geiger has pretty high expectations and he wants to cover a lot of content. It goes pretty quickly, but he gives very good lectures and seems to care a lot about his students. I'm glad to have taken this class with him.

Refuses to put class on canvas. Can't check my grades in this class because of is. He confuses himself when he sees his own slides. Whole first 2 weeks lectures were about history and not at all used on homeworks. The book is the only thing doing the teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, very enthusiastic. Homeworks are long and difficult, but you learn a lot. Exams are straightforward and graded fairly.

One of the best professors in the Electrical Engineering department. The labs and homework are very time consuming, but if you put in the time and effort this class is worthwhile! I would take any class that Professor Geiger teaches!

Get ready to put at least 8 hours a week for this class. Its a lot of work and some of it isn't easy. Worthwhile class for students going into VLSI. Geiger is very smart and can help, but be ready to know your stuff and don't expect to be spoonfed answers. Tough class and somehow managed to get an A, just stay above average on tests. Labs are long.
He's a brilliant man. Should take this class seriously. Past tests help A LOT
Enjoyed his lectures!
He is one gem of a professor. I would take his class again and again.

a lot of negative reviews for dr geiger, but in my opinion he's actually one of the better professors here. yes, he assigns the most homework and his tests are difficult, but he posts old exams and offers review sessions. his lectures are very clear about what is important and although i'd dread it, i would definitely take another class from him

WORST Professor I ever took a class with. I would advise you to delay a semester rather than taking a class with him. He doesn't careeeeeeee. I don't know why he's doing that. doesn't read these rating? Why? why? Why?
This is the first time I put some time in a course and I fail. In my opinion this prof gave us a hard time and he the avg was low and he didn't curve. Try to avoid this prof as much as possible
incredibly petty rules, boring class, undoable amount of work, presents the material in a confused way,

Geiger is a difficult prof: labs and homeworks are incredibly long. Tests are poorly written and hard to finish. That being said, he does scale the grades as appropriate. Lectures contain useful information, but are sometimes hard to follow and apply to classwork. I heavily recommend checking out his office hours for help, he knows what he's doing.

Extremely difficult professor. First class I've ever failed. The class started with eighty people, but only thirty attempted the final. He did try to help us by eliminating our worst test score, but thats not much help when his tests are impossible. There's usually three questions per topic: one basic, one difficult, and one insane.
a really good teacher. he's the TOP professor in the analog circuit. if you really want to learn EE, you should take his course. at the same time, enjoy long HWs and sooo long labs. good luck.

Geiger is a hard teacher, but he really cares about his students and wants them to understand the material.  Multiple times he spent almost an hour with me in his office and explained concepts. He really knows his stuff.  He takes attendance randomly and gives quizzes based on a students guess between 1 and 10

Arguably the worst professor I've ever had, teaching-wise.  His HW assignments are way too advanced and confusing compared to what he discusses in lectures.  Labs were a mess, not even the TA's really knew what was going on, and the labs regularly took 1-3 hours to complete beyond the 3 hour lab time.  Helpful if you talk to him in person, though.

Wow.  Geiger certainly is brilliant and knows EE inside and out.  However, he's not a teacher.   He teaches 200 level classes like they are post-grad.   When the class average for an exam is repeatedly in the 30-40% range, something is terribly wrong.
Geiger is a good professor.  Expects you to work, but knows his stuff.  Very impressed

The class was ridiculous.  He loads the work on like no other. He gave us a gigantic HW due the Fri before spring break and an exam the Mon we returned. He pretended he didn’t realize it was spring break, BS, it was clearly labeled on his schedule. Expect to work on your final proj all night for the last 3 weeks of the semester.

One of the hardest classes I've taken, and it shouldn't have been.  He flies through math during lecture and misses the point of questions asked during class.  We had retakes for 2/3 exams and the avg was still around a 60%.  He is completely unresponsive to student feedback, even though he seems like a really nice guy.  He will expect 20hrs/wk+.

Great professor, but must put in lots of extra time for an A. I rarely paid attention during lecture, but got A's by attending his review sessions and understanding the homework problems before tests. Highly recommend attending review sessions as he does 75% of the kinds of problems that appear on tests. Prepare for hard exams, long hw, fun labs.

The volume of the material was very dense.  For our 3 pre-final tests, the first one's average was low enough to have a retake.  The second one's average merited a take-home retake, and the 3rd one was heavily curved (he would have done a retake if there was more time lift in the semester).  Basically, he's hard.  Dips heavily into VLSI too.

Horrible.  Goes through his lecture slides WAY TOO FAST and explains things 100 miles an hour with his notes at very top level approach.  He does not post notes till AFTER class, so good luck trying to write anything useful.  ALSO NEVER SHOWS UP, and seems not to care about what you think, very ignorant.  This instructor will give ISU a bad rep.

dont take unless you have GIS and coding experience

By far the best professor I've had yet at Iowa State. She's the best lecturer in the Computer Science department - period. She's also extremely accessible outside of class and she actually cares about teaching her students. She is fun and understanding.

The course focuses on stories and themes from the Arabian Nights books. She provides very clear grading criteria and course includes a module each week with discussion boards, quizzes, and one final paper at the end of the semester. You can work at your own pace as everything is due on the final day of the semester. Wonderful & interesting course!

take her class if you can for WLC 370B. It's one of the most interesting but low-maintenance classes you'll take. It requires one quiz and one discussion post a week, and then a final essay. If you put in the work and do the assignments in a timely manner, you'll end up with a perfect grade in the class! She cares so much about each student!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

Nice

Teacher was very helpful and available to answer questions. She used a lot of technology in the class and made it more fun.

I love Tricia so much!!!!! I have never felt so cared for in an educational setting. She genuinely wants us to be the best teachers we can be. Absolutely amazing!!!!!
Tricia cares more about her students than any professor I've ever had. She will go to bat for her students. And she brings treats every week!
TRICIA IS THE BEST! I love her as a person and as a professor. I would give anything to have her as a professor again. Take her class and participate! You will learn so much!!!!

Tricia is a wonderful professor. She cares about her students' success, not just in her class but their careers. She is one of very few professors whos class I have left feeling like I gained valuable knowledge. She does not take it easy on us because she wants her students to become better teachers. She is fantastic and brings treats every week!

Mr. Kim is actually super nice, understanding and likes to help students. He does take a long time to grade and he is not scared to take a point off for every small mistake.

Not very familiar with MLA 8/9 which proves frustrating while writing papers. Takes a really long time to grade, and he is not afraid to take points off for each and every mistake. Disorganized Canvas page which makes it really difficult to follow the course content. I think he is a nice person, but I would literally never take again.

Mr. Kim is so relatable. Very flexible with turning things in and grading. Super reliable and emails back fi you have questions. Super accessible outside of class. The work is so easy and there is a lot of time to finish it during class.

Brian is the best professor I have ever had. He made the class environment feel more like friends than classmates which was important for a speech class. Questionable class

This dude is the goat. He understands the importance of speech skills like nobody else and it's very clear from listening to him talk. Actually so impressive how he managed to get such great participation from the class. Definitely one of the best professors I've had.
Easily one of the best professors at ISU. This guy somehow made a public speaking class enjoyable, as well as got us ready for any possible public speeches we may do in the future.

Brian creates a great environment in his classroom and is very good at what he does. He brings real-life experience into the lessons instead of relying on a textbook. The material is easy to understand as long as you pay attention in class.

Professor Gillette is an overall fantastic person. He is the first Professor I had at Iowa State, where I had no doubt that he had all of the student's best interests in mind. Gilchrist is a very nit-picky grader, so be prepared to understand each topic so that you don't get unnecessary points deducted. His grading is unclear and seemed bothered when I attended office hours to get clarity on a topic I couldn't grasp.

Dr. Gilchrist was a painful professor to learn under. His grading is extreme and refuses to help you in an email other than further criticizing your work. He picks on students and acts like he knows everything. On assignments, he doesn't explain why you get something wrong and lazily grades papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It's a traditional survey course for English majors and his grading/policies are pretty rigid. If you do the readings, pay attention to his lectures, and are good at answering multiple choice questions his tests are easy. The group project is a pain. He's sarcastic and funny and very knowledgeable but puts his foot in his mouth every so often.

Great guy. Extremely smart. Hard class

Good guy. Know what he is talking about, but difficult to follow. Very helpful if you ask questions.

Good Luck and that's pretty much it

What ever you do, do not take this course from her. reviews.comment: The class was easy but go to class otherwise she notices and will not like you.  I missed classes due to family emergencies and she was not sympathetic.  Not a good professor. I'm glad she left Iowa State, but wish it would have been sooner.
class is a bit boring. But interesting sometimes. Nothing much to say, but easy A if you smart

Class was straightforward. Exams were open book which was required since lots of tables and formulas needed to be looked up. Always very professional and easy to understand even though English is not her native language. Also very available and willing to help discuss any questions. Overall, my favorite C E professor
Open book tests made this class cake. Homework is worth a ton of the grade.

This class was taught by 2 instructors, this was not a good decision. It was hard to learn from two different styles. Nadia at least did examples on the board, and has lecture notes online. The HW is all done from the book, and the example problems in it are good. The Tests are just like the HW and the examples. This class was verrryyy boring!
Helpful course with great instructor.
Great professor!
Good professor

Dr. Betcher was a wonderful professor. I wish I wasn't graduating next semester so I could take more courses with her. I enjoyed every class, and she's extremely engaging, knowledgeable, and passionate about literature and her students. I would highly recommend her British Survey course. The reading selections were excellent, as were her lectures.

Dr. Betcher's class really is a load, but she does care for her students. I consistently go to her for letters of recommendation because she is so respected, knowledgeable, and considerate. You have to read or else you won't pass (and there is a lot!), and she is also a tough grader. Her grading and classes pushed me to be a better student, though.

I was a little nervous going into the class because of the bad reviews, but she was a wonderful professor. You can tell she cares about her students and I have learned so much from her course. At times it can be challenging and she can be a tough grader, but put in the work and your effort will pay off.

I was very nervous before taking this class because her rating was not extremely high. I am so glad that I decided that it was worth it. She has been the best professor I've had while at ISU and has helped me learn a ton from the course. Cannot recommend both ENGL 2370 and Dr. Betcher enough.I encourage all students to explore more of her courses.
horrible. did not give good grades back for months. I had to go into every office hour just to understand her directions. group project at the end sucks

THIS IS THE WORST PROFESSOR IN THE HISTORY OF THE WORLD!! Do not take this class she makes every assignment impossible to get a good grade. Everything you do is wrong! Do not take this class! She makes it impossible to get a good grade. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had a bad experience in her online 302 course. There's a problematic juxtaposition between expectations and quality of instruction. She's an unforgiving grader, but expectations and overall INSTRUCTION are poor. Constant communication/office hours were required to have a clear idea of assignment expectations. Her availability was poor, too.

Grading takes forever; she's accused the whole class of plagiarism not once but twice. If you actually follow her instructions, she's still not happy; either you "stole" from her provided template or didn't account for something random. She's more into running for city council in Ames than helping her students learn.

Dr. Betcher is the hardest grading professor i have ever witnessed in my college career.  I am a typically A student and will have to retake to get a better grade. If you do not cite your sources perfectly you will get absurd amount of points taken off for "Plagiurism". Avoid this prof. at all costs

Gloria is an awful professor. Avoid her at all costs. She makes this class more work than any other class I have ever taken at Iowa State and is by far the hardest grader I have ever had. She talks down to her students in emails and belittles them after simple mistakes. If you have to take Gloria get ready to work a lot and be graded poorly

With Gloria, this class is 10x the amount of work than other profs. Heavy emphasis on group work and it takes forever to grade things. She makes rubrics unclear, and you will not know what you did wrong until four assignments later. Take this class with literally anyone else, especially if you are a STEM student; this class is not worth the time.

If you want to do twice the amount of work take this class with Gloria. As the very end of the semester I was about .25 points (out of over a 1,000) from an A- verse a B+ and she didn't boost my grade and actually hurt my grade by removing extra credit I received from earlier in the semester.

Overall an easy class, very dependent on the final group project that starts in the middle of the semester. Betcher does the best she can to set her students up for success, however some of the work assigned is genuinely pointless. She is a hard grader but if you follow her rubrics your fine.

This professor takes the longest time to give assignment feedback of any professor that I have had. Her assignments build off of each other, which causes problems when you have no clue how you did on previous assignments. When talking to her via email, her directions/assistance are unhelpful and vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super harsh grader! Does not realize that students only take this class since it's a requirement, no one actually cares about it.

Professor really knows her stuff, however, classes were heavy in lecture and the information throughout lecture was not relevant to projects working on in class. More on the harsher side of grading things, however, provide extra credit and office hour opportunities. I would try and find another professor that makes class more enjoyable if possible.

She was a harsh grader even when you hit all the points, never satisfied. She had a report, presentation, and an exam all due within a week. The online homework was long and difficult, never talked about in class but had to take test over.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is offered only on Monday nights from 6:10-9 pm. Nine times out of ten, you will be there the entire time. Make sure you're prepared to talk about the reading. That is what this class is all about. BlackBoard discussion posts, class discussions, mini-quizzes, and two test make up the main portion of our grade.

Gloria is a very good English professor. After we watched the films, she always held very interesting discussions. The class was light when it came to work and only had three papers and two tests (the final paper was even optional). She graded very slowly but was very responsive to email. She grades papers fairly but she was very nitpicky.

I didn't enjoy being in Betcher's class at all. She didn't really teach us anything and she NEVER graded our papers. She had only graded one of my four papers going into dead week. I wouldn't recommend her at all.

I am not particularly interested in medieval literature, but Gloria really made learning about this subject quite fun. She used to be an editor, so she grades her papers rather harshly, especially in grad classes, and cares about grammar. Overall, she's very helpful, very kind, and very knowledgeable.
she made watching and discussing war movies an interesting topic for someone who is not particularly interested in the grit and grime of war.
No Comments

Loved this professor, Made each student feel important by learning their name and an intersting thing about them. Must read to be good at the class, has pop quizzes, but overall an amazing woman. She is also very empathetic with students needs.
She has made learning Medieval Literature fun.

Dr. Gleason was able to take a course that could have been interesting and turned it into quite possibly the most useless class I have ever taken. Stupid!

I know he can be unclear at times, but if you reach out to him, he'll be glad to set up a time that works for you and do his best to reach a solution that makes you comfortable. Class is easy. Gleason talks to the class like we're 5th graders.... undermining your abilities. He wants you to work in groups, but then gets annoyed when you collaborate. Dr. Starns really cares about your success. Any questions you have she will work very hard to help you understand. During her lectures, she talks through concepts and prefilled-out examples. Dr. Starns is a good and caring person who is knowledgeable about the things she is teaching (SolidWorks basics and features, basic Engineering concepts, etc.) If you are new to SolidWorks, be prepared to spend time with the program to really figure out how to use every feature, as she can sometimes be too quick with her explanations and examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

Despite being a CAD teacher, she is not good with SolidWorks. You and your peers will need to work together to learn the material if you have no prior CAD experience. She's a little dramatic about professionalism but overall it was an easy class. Don't buy a textbook for this class.

Dr. Starns is very respectful to students. She is very knowledgeable on her material as well. Very reasonable with offering extensions on assignments and being available outside of class. When she talks to the class she is a little all over the place. Sometimes she forgets things or messes up the math which makes it confusing.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed having Professor Starns in class. She was incredibly knowledgeable, and had clear and effective lectures (though she can go off on tangents sometimes). It's very clear that she cares a lot about her students and has a passion for both her field and teaching.

Really tough class with really tough group homework assignments. Gloria really cares about her students and she is very knowledgeable about the subject. She will help you if you try hard and have a good attitude. Hope to God you get assigned a good group. Otherwise ask to ditch that group ASAP.

She's tough, she's blunt, she cracks down on academic dishonesty like the hand of god.   Say what you will about Dr. Starns, you can't help but respect her. She's a tough teacher for an already tough course, but she undoubtedly knows her stuff and is willing to teach if you're willing to learn.

Gloria really cares about her students and will take the times to make sure everyone understands her class as long as you show her you are willing to work for it. She respects her students and lets them be creative and take projects in any direction they want to, and allows for creativity.

You will spend countless hours crying because you have no time to study for other classes and Grading was worse than getting hazed. When it comes down to it I  did learn a lot but my other grades suffered. She is super kind but for real like 15 hours per week on projects. The other teacher's section problems seem like macaroni art compared to hers.

Gloria is a professor where if you do not exhibit behavior that she deems "professional," then you will not do very well in this class. Very biased professor :/

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

BUT she is willing to help and clear things up if you don't understand.  She will see you more if you ask questions, and strive to do better.  Go to her office hours and ask for help.
Hands down the best ME instructor at ISU. If I could take every class with Gloria I would. I also had her for ME 325, excellent course and learned a lot. She does make you work, but is very helpful!

This class can be hard, if you don't use your resources. Resources as in office hours. if you go to her office hours you will have no problem getting an A in this class, Shes helps students who are willing to help themselves.

One of my favorite professors in ME. She really cares about the teaching aspect of being a university professor and takes a keen interest in her students' questions and projects. Very approachable and kind.

She is by far the best professor I have ever had. She is helpful and there to help you. I haven't met a nicer professor here at Iowa State. I hope I have her again. The projects in her class are somewhat time consuming, so be prepared.
Exceptional Teacher and Very Nice Lady

She is a hard grader and there is a lot of work, but she makes you understand the material by the end of the semester.  Attendance is required through "discretionary points" which can drop you an entire letter grade.

Good Teacher, extremely helpful if you have questions, as long as you ask!  Lots of group work on some projects.  She does go a little fast in the beginning with the Solidworks stuff.  But if you have an issue Ask!! Overall she's good, I want to have her for all my other ME classes.

Overall I liked her as a person, she was great to talk to but I found myself confused in when we were trying to learn matlab.  Also the homework takes forever so don't wait till the day before to start.  Look over your graded assignments too, i probably gained back 50% of the points on homework because it was mis marked.
great teacher.  willing to help. energetic. knows her stuff

Dr. Starns is an extremely knowledgeable professor, and she will be glad to help with any questions you have in class. She has quite a bit of real world experience, and applies that to everyday class lectures.

Great Professor. has a good real world experience as a consultant.  very helpful. can site most of the equations from shigley's from memory. covers much more material than other professors and gives much more in depth homework.  be prepared to work hard, but you will leave with a good understanding of one of the most core (useful) classes in ME.

She was a decent teacher overall.  The problem I had is that whenever we had hw assignments, you either did it perfect or you almost failed it.  She was very willing to help you, but her help was often incorrect or just in general useless.
She is one of the best professors I've had at Iowa State. Always willing to help if you ask.
No Comments
Great teacher!

Pretty good teacher overall.  Her homeworks are very intense, start them early!!!  She understands the subject well but sometimes doesn't explain it as well.  This is one of those teachers that are difficult but they will work as hard as you to help you understand it for a good grade.

He makes it very easy to understand the content, and all exam questions are addressed at some point in class. Grading criteria is somewhat unclear for timed writes, but overall it's a very manageable course.

Mr. Gilchrist is semi smart regarding his topic but he's so harsh. He's very condescending within your papers and he will grade you as if your trying to become a phd student. Overall the worst professor I've ever had and a disgrace to Iowa State. I'm in a list of 400+ classes and this was my favorite to be done with.

By far one of my favorite professors at Iowa State! I had him for 260 in the fall and 226 in the spring and I will be taking as many classes with him as I can! Definitely be prepared to read, if you skip out on reading assignments you're not going to do well!

reviews.comment: He is just plain awful. His feedback is terrible, he would tell me I did well on an assignment but I received a terrible grade. My friends in other sections have received much much higher grades on the same assignments but with poorer quality. I do not suggest him for any class.

Professor Gilchrist is a very tough grader and sticks directly to the book and allows for basically no personal "spin" on assignments no matter how small. His feedback is almost always negative and condescending. DO NOT take an class with him unless you want a disappointing grade.

Somewhat a difficult class, but having a good group for the projects makes all the difference. Be sure to look at the rubrics for every writing assignment because he strictly sticks to those. Will give decent feedback if you ask but it might be easier to ask fellow students. Not too hard to where it took up all of my time, which was nice.

Prof Gilchrist was an extremely tough grader. Our group papers were looked over by our entire group multiple times, and he still gave us a failing grade sometimes. The rubric and expectations were unclear at times which contributed to this.

As a person, he is wonderful, and I could spend hours talking to him. As a professor, he is very vague in his project directions and never says when assignments are due. Tests are relatively easy if you pay attention in class and write notes, but on the pop quizzes, he only allows handwritten notes, so beware. Attendance not mandatory but helpful

KJ's class has been the worst class I have ever had to take throughout my academic career. The class was disorganized and unnecessarily hard for many projects. The rubrics wouldn't align with assignment descriptions and expectations for supposedly "simple" papers, were extremely high. His class was confusing, burdensome, and very uninspiring.

Pick another professor for english 302. He grades very tough and said our work was "some of the best he has seen" but gave us an 80 on it... ? The grade received does not reflect the amount of work and time spent in this class. No one got above a 90. So take it with a different professor because the other ones aren't as tough graders.

He's a really, REALLY harsh grader. By that I mean I don't believe a single person in the class got anything higher than a 95%, with most people being well below that. Directs you to the book or syllabus with any questions or concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: K.J. was very knowledgable in Shakespeare and he does not let you forget it. His lectures felt endless and his tests contained things that were not relevant to the course material. He also uses "plickers" which are an unnecessary, time-consuming way to take attendance.
Lectures are interesting, show up to class or else he fails you. Tests are pretty hard/written to confuse you so make sure to study from all angles.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed him as a professor. Content was not too difficult and if you come to class, you'll pass the class. He really knows his stuff.

reviews.comment: It's a traditional survey course for English majors and his grading/policies are pretty rigid. He's sarcastic and funny and very knowledgeable but puts his foot in his mouth every so often.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: After talking to people in other sections, he seems to be the toughest teacher for ENG 302. When you ask him a question, his answer is always, "it's in the syllabus (or book)." Must wrote memos (most not even graded) several times a week. Takes attendance every day. Smart guy, but can be arrogant and rude sometimes.

He'll warm up to you more if you show up and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Go to class. Sit up front. Consistently raise your hand and participate: even if you say the wrong answer, the brief embarrassment is worth the participation points. reviews.comment: This will be a class you're excited to go to but, this course is more difficult than the ave. 200 level: lots of readings, impossible pop-quizzes, and fast paced. reviews.comment: Way too much work for one class. Every little assignment turns into a project.  Take this class with someone else.
Gilchrist is not my favorite, but he's not awful. His tests are really hard and are worth a lot of points in the class. His pop quizzes are confusing, even if you read for class. SO MUCH READING
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgable on what he teaches, but he knows it and isn't afraid to show it. He can be helpful but you have to be careful because sometimes it can confuse  you even more. Throughout the semester it just felt like we were playing his little games just to get by and pass the class rather than learning the course materials.
He is the hardest grader  I have come across. He loves to talk about himself and thinks he is funny. His sense of humor annoys me the wrong way and never lets up.

There is a ton of reading. If you keep up, you'll do ok. His overuse of puns and bad jokes distracts from the actual learning. He knows his stuff and engages students but be prepared to go off topic. Insightful class with good information.

Expect to read a lot, pretend this is the ONLY class you are taking, it should be 5 credits and not 3 based on difficulty, what he covers in class is irrelevant to quizzes. He honestly is a pretty good prof, but he certainly acts like he is the most important of them all. His rules are firmly set and he is a stickler about them (if you are late to class, it's best to not even go). His lectures are all over the place so it's hard to be sure what is test content and what isn't, but he knows the most interesting things.

Wasn't bad. He's the king of puns. Be prepared to read a lot. Essential to get the book before the class starts. He is set on his rules and won't give leeway, not necessarily bad but can be frustrating.
Don't take a class from this guy. He has a thing for WW1 and the holocaust. Most depressing class I have ever taken. Unless your into that sort of thing

Gilchrist is very knowledgable in the subject and that's obvious from the start. Read materials pretty extensively. He jumps around in notes a lot which makes things difficult. Review days are extremely helpful. Everything on the tests is something that he has hammered into your head all semester long

This professor is very interesting and helpful.  Attending his courses is like listening to commentary on a documentary- very interesting and entertaining.  He is a stickler for MLA format, but it is easy because he will go over everything with you if you ask. He makes works that are easily very tedious and boring fun and relatable.

Coming into class, I disliked English; Dr. Gilchrist changed that. He was very professional and knowledgeable. I learned so much from this course that I can apply to my career. He comes off as a hard-ass at first, but is really a great prof, who wants you to succeed!
Gilchrist has an interesting sense of humor, but I learned a lot of really relevant information from him.  I loved the hands-on learning.

gilchrist is professional and friendly. The reviewer below is full of it; I did the project that person's talking about, which was a research thing for developing the class.  I appreciated the opportunity. Great class for a required class.

Dr Gilchrist helped me on many things in this class and met me at his office and spent a lot of time on email answering my questions. I see business documents very differently now, thanks to him. He was very professional, but but also.

Today when a student turned in his final I heard a student admit to Gilchrist that he plagiarized on a paper. It takes some kind a person to get a student to confid that. I learned tons in this course, and his grading is, as someone siad, gracious as well as fair.
He's completely fair in grading, even gracious.  Let me revise an assignment that was failing so I could learn. Decent guy.

Sometimes he is hard to follow just because he knows so much. He can come off as pretentious just because he is so knowledgeable. He's good at discussing the texts and making important connections between literature and the time period.

I don't believe his grading is bias. It is hard to get an A in his class because he expects a high level of detail on tests. He's very helpful if you bother to take initiative. Be careful during lectures;I never had trouble with his notes, but he likes to jump around.
His class content is excellent - he's very knowledgeable. His grading policy is very strange so pay attention.

Wow, what a truely awful teacher.  I'm a senior with a GPA above 3.75, and I got the lowest grade I've ever had in a class from this professor.  His grading system is ambiguous and completely biased.  Avoid at all costs!

Watch out! This professor does not grade off of a "point" scale. He gives basically everyone a "B", regardless of work quality.  As mentioned before, he DOES have favorites.  Group projects are not graded equally. He's big on plagiarism. I would spend hours checking my sources, and he would always find something to criticize.  Avoid if possible!

I really liked this class.  He had a clear syllabus that required you to work, but as long as you showed up and did the readings it was no problem.  I learned a lot and appreciated his sense of humor.

I liked this course. He's on his game and tells things like they are with some humor. I don't notice favoritism but he grades according to policies except he let me correct some missing citing instead of counting it as plagiarism which he was told to do. Good class. Learned a LOT.

This "teacher" is atrocious.  If you give play to his liking and suck up you'll do great in this class.  Any deviation from what he wants is treated with harsh grading and a general distaste.  Not a fan of new ideas.  Get out of his class if you tend to think for yourself or you will be oppressed and forced to change if you want to get a good grade
If I could drop this class without the risk of losing my honors housing... I'd be gone.

Oh man, the WORD PUNS! So many word puns, so many of them absolutely terrible. Aside from that, everything that's said is true- a very tough grader that reluctantly gives out As, but an amazing source for learning the material. His advice for professional business communication is extremely useful, and you WILL improve if you take his class.

He is very up on himself and even though he says he will help students, it is hard to get him to do so. He is a hard grader, but only for a few people who do not tickle his fancy like his favorites. Our class atmosphere was bad and it may have been mostly because of him.

Give it up. I'm learning a lot in this class and Dr G does so much to help students. What a gripe the one person had below-must be a millennial who didn't grow up. I'm not writing perfect memos, but I know now what they should look like. Dr G sticks to the books.

Dr. Gilchrist does talk after class and has office hours that I visited twice for help before work is due. Very approachable and funny. Knows his subjects. Never talked about flight in the office or in class. (?) WTHeck is that about? What obsession? None I see. What small people come up with from pet gripes. Got a life? I like this prof and class!

Really enjoyed this course.  Dr. G. is really easy to joke with, and dishes them out just as easily.  He gave me good feedback to improve my writing.  However, the fact that he doesn't use WebCT is frustrating.  Additionally, I'm unsure what he wants as far as participation, because I participated daily and still my final grade was dropped for it.

This identity course was hard but good. We looked at identity by postcolonial, education and other viewponts. I spent time in his office going over drafts before they were turned in. He doesn't spoon feed. He gives instructions, helped revise with me, but I did my work. As for plagiarism- real consequences for crap work?! Go figure.

I was out in the hall waiting to talk when the guy below was talking to him. He was nicer than the "student" deserved (and said nothing about not understanding English). Plagiarism isn't a "minor" offense-like stealing is a minor offense. He taugh from the beginning how to do sources. I'm getting my grade cause I did it right.  Great class.

Don't be fooled by his bad jokes and seemingly-friendly nature. He nearly reported me to the dean because of minor plagerism errors. I absolutely loved the people I met in my class, but the Identities course was the worst I've taken thus far. Dont be surprised if you are accused of plagerism, half of my class was at some point during the semester!

He gives little time for "big" research assignments. most people in my class say these are the worst papers they've ever written simply because he doesn't give much time to do them. He gives little feedback on grades unless explicity asked, and he uses the word acadamia too much. He is very pompous. And don't mention Des Moines if you're from there
After taking this class, you will be able to survive any English assignment! He makes you think, makes you work, and he rewards those who do.
Do NOT take the "Identity" course. Ever. Also, most convoluted grading system I've seen. Doesn't use WebCT.
No Comments

The loser below is cryin about nothin. I like this class! There's a lot of work, but he helped me revise a paper on his computer. Sticks to grading policies,but I don't want a sloth to get the A I'm gettin. What--College is work?! I heard he doesn't put up with plagarism, but he gave someone a chance to revise a faulty paper. He's great.

The textbook definition of pompous college professor jackass. Don't take any of his classes unless you want to put up with constant BS, huge workload and CONSTANT nitpicking. Do not expect any improvement in your writing skills.  And who goes by "K.J."?  Honestly.

He is a great teacher.  He gets you interested, he's not at all boring and he really wants his students to do well.  You have to study for the tests, they aren't easy.  And the papers you right have to be well-done.  It's not a blow off class at all, but it has been my favortie class and he has been my favorite professor.

I've gotten high grades on all assignments and exams. Went in with my paper before it was due; he helped me with some problems in it. Don't know what's up with princes/princesses who say he doesn't help.

Probably the most unhelpful professor ive ever taken a class from.   Definitely THE WORST prof ive ever had. I strongly urge anyone who is considering taking a class from him to think twice. He totally ruined Literture for me
Ungodly amounts of work! Try and find another teacher to take this class from!

He's a hard grader but fair. I went to his office and he helped me revise and helped me revise an assignment before the due date. Very approchable and friendly. Seems the students who dont want to work trash him. His class is work but it's like any job I've had where I had to actually work.
Pompous ****...that's all I have to say to convince you NOT to take Engl 302 with him.

Very interesting lectures and assigned readings.  Gilchrist really knows his stuff.  I've never had a prof more willing to help during office hours with papers, etc. before.  If you have any trouble understanding something, go to him right away--he's a big help.  Do papers just as asked and you'll get along fine.  Very funny prof--love the puns!

I was in the same class as the one below. In my opinion he dropped because he didn't want to study. Gilchrist has the course exactly as described and made it not only relevant to the stuff we read, but also to current events. No use busting a gut because you got the grade you deserved.

He is in the running for worst professor I have ever had at ISU.  I actually dropped the course a few months into it.  I am an English major in my 3rd year, and I would strongly suggest that anyone reading this avoid any classes he teaches.

I notice all of the negative comments are from students in Engl302 a required class for non-Engl majors-students that are Engl majors enjoy his classes and other students must find it challenging because they are not skilled readers and/or writers. picks great books and inspires hard work-GREAT! :)

Gilchrist is great.  He's nice, unlike what someone below said, but sticks to policies in his syllabus. He doesn't confuse real work with butt kissing -  good for us who actually do some work. He's funny, but you have to know how to laugh.

Hard grader, but entirely fair & friendly. He looked over my work anytime before grading and showed me how to revise-no guessing game, by the text. He has a dry, quick sense of humor, not wild. You may not need a developed sense of humor to take his class, but it'll help make it fun.

deceptively nice--sets unrealistic expectations for students (especially when his assignment sheets and syllabus are filled with errors).  he also makes horrible, horrible jokes that i cannot imagine anyone finding funny.  there it is(you understand this sentence if you have ever taken his class..)
AWESOME Shakespeare class. Lots of puns- watch out for those.  Papers and tests require lots of preparation, but if you're in class and take good notes you won't have any problems. Great prof.
Great professor, wants you to learn
He makes the class harder than it should be. He tries to make your writing too perfect. It's his way or the highway in writing. It's hard to make him happy.

Friendly. Grades hard but fair. He gives lots of stuff on readings. Everything on exams *is* given in class, but have to take good notes. Helps in office hours; gave me chance to revise. Not a playtime class, but fun.
very picky with paper form and hard grader with them, puts things on test that were not talked about in class. has lots of puns. If have question have to go to his office hours.
Great teacher, loved his Shakespeare class.  Learned a ton, just have to keep up with the readings.  As the other reviewer mentioned, watch out for his  punny  nature.

Very nice guy and prof, tought the class in a manner that was demanding yet always within our grasp.  I learned a lot about literature from this guy, and I bet you might too!! (watch out for his puns, though).

If he doesn't like you (this is obvious) your grade will reflect that. He put my grade in wrong and I ended having to email him. I doubt he will change it.  He is the last fair professor i have ever had. If a professor doesn't like you it doesn't mean he can lower your grade.

Final Project and Final Exam make up 45% of your grade. Gives a lot of homework, pilled it on even more than usual for dead week. Tests are impossible, lectures are terrible. He is extremely unorganized and unhelpful. He is a nice person, but terrible professor, thinks we should already know things from this class that we haven't learned.

There are 6 days left of the semester and Glatz's section has over 60% of their grade to go. Same test as the other section, same final project as the other section. Additionally: an extra exam-final and multiple assignments to fit into deadfinals week.  Lectures aren't bad, the material can be learned, but an extreme amount  of extra work.

One of the more engaging professors in the ChE department. Expects students to be able to think on exams and bring all of their knowledge together rather than just repeat what they did on the homework. He actually pushes the students to learn rather than spoon feed information.
He basically needs to retire. He doesn't care about student success only about how soon he will retire.  Offices hours aren't helpful if he doesn't like your questions.
refuse to answer student question after class, real tough grader. The test he gave to us mostly only contains 2-3 questions. If u messed up one problem, u will fail the test.

Good professor, genuinely cares about his students but he can be very frustrating at times.  He's extremely particular and tends to be very subjective. To do well in his class, make sure you understand the material as best you can before asking for help, bite your tongue and give him what he wants, it will save you a lot of headaches down the road.

You'll only do well in this class if you are naturally smart and can teach yourself everything.  very arrogant and will not help you with your homework in office hours will tell you to read the book and maybe you should change your major
Best Advisor Ever! Sad to see her go.
She's the best adviser ever
Best adviser on campus!

Best adviser on the planet. She has a hilarious yet quirky sense of humor, but she's fabulous. She is there for the students. In my case when I was first scheduling, she actually called up department heads just so I could get into my desired classes, even though the sections were closed!
Vivacious energy.
Great advisor. Great source of knowledge for some of the secrets of ISU, such as easy classes to take for certain requirements.
Quirky, but she'd stop at nothing to help you out.  Thank you, Gloria.
Easy class, and she's a good advisor, but has kind of a dorky and annoying sense of humor.
just the best 101 class ever. very helpful and informative. she was also very fun and had lots of great stories.

Take this class! Get the pdf version of the text and use the search function for each test. While there is assigned reading, its not necessary (I'm dead serious). There are a couple of 1.5 page papers, but they're not strenuous - simply opinion-pieces. (Seriously though - take this class. Even if you already have a full load.)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She doesn't know how to use a computer so don't email her your assignment and expect a grade or a reply. The class averaged a 54% on the midterm exam, after that she allowed open note and open book. Gave extra credit for printing her lectures.

This professor is absolutely horrible at presenting material. She is extremely biased towards certain races and genders. The class is easy, and it is easy to get a good grade, but sitting through the classes are terrible. Half the time I was in class it was spent trying to comprehend what she was saying or what she had typed. DO NOT SUGGEST HER!!!!
She isnt very organized and not clear with what she wants.  Overall, its an easy class.  You get to use notecards for the tests which help out a lot.  Put in the work and you'll get an A

I love Dr. Jones Johnson! She tells it like it is and makes it very easy for you to get an A, as long as you go to class to get extra credit and actually try a little. I hope that I get to take another class with her.
Easy teacher so long as you attend class for extra credit. Notecard for the tests. Very opinionated!Can have some wacky ideas. Overall a fun class and a easy A... If you're not brain dead.

Worst teacher I've had at Iowa State.  She gave me the only midterm since I've gone to school here and I ended up getting an A- in the class.  Very disorganized and clueless to everything that is going on in class.
Dr. Jones-Johnson is hard but fair. She gives extra credit constantly and knows what she is talking about. Coming to class helps alot!
All participation based.   She offers MASSIVE extra credit, but dont count on getting by soley by that.
Everything we do in class is useless.  She is disorganized, offensive at times, unfocused, and random.  I don't even know how to begin to study for her exams.  She actually LOST my first assigment.
Confusing, unorganized, lost my assignments, not focused.

She is hirlarious! Although she tends to trail off on her own stories, she is very helpful and she gives out a lot of extra credit on attendance and different activities, so make sure you go to class often!

She is very disorganized. She also said things in class that I wasn't sure were absolutely true. She is kind of like one of those crazy ladies who is so passionate about something that she loses sight on the facts. Grading is not clear at all, but the class is still pretty easy especially if you have taken other soc classes. Just do all the work.

Test material is directly from class notes and from terminology/concept definition and analysis assignments. Unfortunately, very little of it is actually covered in class. Often, class was useless as it didn't relate to my grade very much. Discussions were always interesting and provoking, both emotionally and cognitively. Quite passionate teacher!

Intimidating nature lol, Passionate about class, but EXTREMELY unlcear and confusing. Going to class is a waste except for the extra credit, which is based on poitns, but she only says that she looks at your "points" and adjusts it, but never says exactly what these "points" are worth lol just arbitrary "points"
Class was interesting, but notes and overheads were useless.  Liked the prof though, disorganized but very passionate about what she's teaching.
She is so nice! Her tests are very reasonable, and she helps you get prepared for them. I really liked her.

The instructor had a lot of knowledge about the subject, and did a good job demonstrating it to the students.. the only thing that really sucked about it though is the notes that she put in reserve, they were very bad quality and waste of paper..

I thought this was a really good class. Dr. Jones-Johnson was a bit intimidating the first day, but after a week or so it was much better. She is a good person and a good teacher. She always had time for me
No Comments

Class is basically a waste of time, but easy.  Her overheads in lecture are insanely small and thus pointless.  She seems to lack a lot of knowledge about modern society and pop culture, it's funny though.  Not necessarily *bad*, but not recommended.

He is constantly late to class, though he grades students to be on time. Doesn't directly answers questions. Definitely take notes, he doesn't send his copies until the night before the quiz or test. Does provide lots of information, but the quizzes do not cover all he says - it is hard to distinguish what will be on them.

Old School Teaching. He knows a lot of information but does not siphon out the important stuff from the non-important stuff. Just straight up INFORMATION OVERLOAD!!! The test go over a lot of info but the style is good, study. Do not procrastinate on the projects. They'll bit ya in the ass if ya do.

Made subject boring, for what otherwise could have been a great topic (particular interest of mine). Self indulged and pompous, speaks in third person. Nice guy, but doesn't answer question until about 3rd or 4th time asked.

Old teaching style and ancient powerpoints drove me crazy. I had a very hard time getting interested in what should have been a very interesting subject. Start the project ASAP. Don't go overboard, though. Definitely encourage practice tests, USE THEM.
No Comments

He's my advisor and he's been very helpful.  Always willing to make time for answering questions and doesn't believe in a stupid question.  It's been great to know him.  If I ever have him for a teacher I'll be sure to comment again.
AWESOME TEACHER! Best Spanish teacher I've had at Iowa State! She is super helpful, and easy going. The class is kind of difficult, but she makes it really fun. :)
Jesse is a wonderful teacher, I loved this class!  I had it at 8am too, so that's saying something!  Note that the Spanish classes at ISU do have a LOT of hw and it will take quite a bit of time.
She is really good and interactive teacher.    If you've taken spanish in high school, this class will be pretty easy.

Really nice and funny guy. He tries to scare you at the beginning of the semester claiming that the class is super difficult, but I got an A without doing any of the extra credit. He allows students to argue test questions for credit which is nice to combat trick questions. You have to understand that he is a very blunt person, but great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class, great prof

I loved the content of this course. The controversies discussed in this class were very interesting and I would say that taking this course was beneficial. However, the way he treats his students can come off as disrespectful. He has a way of making you feel stupid for not having a good answer. I cried more over this class than I should have.

Prof. Chaves has one of the most fun classroom environments I have ever been in. She is a pretty easy grader, and she is understanding of the fact that you are going to make mistakes. For anyone taking this class who is intimidated by the final, I really wouldn't worry about it. As long as you show you are trying she will cut you some slack.

I only have good things to say about Professor Chaves. She is very personal and knew my whole class by name. The class definitely isn't easy, but she teaches the material so well and makes the lectures very fun. At least for me, she didn't grade too hard. It felt nice to be in a more personal classroom. Definitely take Spanish with her!!

I LOVE Professor Chaves. I was nervous at first about the class and its difficulty, but she was very gracious and helped me better understand the language. She made the class fun and we were always laughing. She does give a lot of homework and the exams are decently difficult, but if you pay attention in class you should have no issue at all.

Celeste is very willing to help students out. For example, if you miss a class, she'll let you make up your missed work without docking points for late work (only if it's on paper). You will need to study for this class to remember all the grammar rules and such, at times it felt like we were moving too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher for beginners. Very helpful in clearing doubts.
Professor is too harsh on grading class participation. Expect this to be used to knock down grades.

I had Profe Chaves my very first semester here at ISU. I only had a class of about 15 people and it was super nice because she knew all of us by name. I could tell she genuinely cared about us and wanted us to succeed. Whenever I had a question and would email her about it she would always respond right away. She is a fairly easy grader also!

They switched the class to an online module and classes are recitation now. Homework is online and teacher goes over important stuff. I don't think I would have passed if not for Celeste. She always preps us for the chapter exams and made sure we were ready for the final. Great stories when you get her talking about Argentina.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed going to this class  every day. She is a really nice woman and a pretty easy grader. She has a cool input since she is from Argentina and makes learning in the class fun. I really recommend.

I absolutely loved Celeste. Hands down she made me want to come to class and then to want to learn the Spanish language. We had pop quizzes which she always made obvious were coming. And the tests were literal replications of the studyguides, just with different questions. Hands down take this class. Do work hard though, some people didn't pass.

Celeste has a great sense of humor & always made class interesting. Literally one of the best professors I have ever had. There are lots of hints before the pop quizzes so don't worry about them. She is super helpful & I wish I could have her for all of my Spanish classes. Participate & you will do well. Great professor! Definitely recommend her!

I loved Celeste! She is so funny and helpful. She gives "pop" quizzes  but gives you plenty of hints of when they'll be coming up.  I would take another one of her classes! I recommend taking her class!
Celeste is super nice and approachable. She grades kinda tough on tests and compositions, but overall I really like her.
She is an amazing teacher. Super nice and helpful! She does give pop quizzes but they are very easy

Celeste is a wonderful professor! She truly cares about students and wants them to succeed. She makes class interesting with her stories about Argentina. I wish she taught all of the Spanish courses at Iowa State! I was never tempted to skip class for an unexcused reason because I looked forward to learning from her everyday!
Wonderful professor.

Great with students, and encouraging everyone to work with one another. She as a great sense of humor and very good at explaining things in both Spanish and English. Celeste is also not afraid to go off the planed agenda and go her own way from what the coordinator has planned in the class.

Wonderful professor! She is very approachable and willing to go the extra mile to explain concepts that students do not understand. She has a great sense of humor and makes the class fun and inviting! This is the one class I never want to miss!
Great guy would take again! 10/10
Goce is a bit of a quiet speaker, but if you can actually hear him his lectures are great.

Dr. T is very organized, well-spoken, knowledgeable, and great at communicating. Since this course is experimental, it makes sense that there were few assignments and these assignments were not very lengthy, but I would have benefited from smaller, more frequent assignments that I could get regular feedback on or make me ask more questions to learn
Dr. Golemo is an amazing director. He is super kind and pushes us

Dr. Golemo is a talented and fun band conductor. He cares about all his students and makes an effort to get to know each and every person in the ensemble. One of the best conductors at the collegiate level.

Doc is one of the most respected collegiate wind band conductors and after even just one week with him you can see why! He really knows how to shape an ensemble and he loves his job, his students, and music. Always ready to lend an ear to any of your needs and make himself available outside of a class. A real gem.
Best Professor ever and deserves every second of your attention and respect at all times.

Doc is the most caring and personal professor/director one will ever have for a band. He takes the time to learn every individuals name in his band and will personally thank you for doing your best. He is understanding if an emergency comes up as long as you email him early in the morning. Every human should strive to be as caring as this man.
Great teaching style, really cares about students and getting to know them personally.
The most genuine and loving professor I have ever had. He really cares about each and everyone of his students!
Amazing professor! Learns about each of his students by name, and about their hobbies, etc.! Great to be around and very knowledgeable in music!

Doc is incredible. Once he knows your name he never forgets it and will ask you how you're doing in the hallway when he sees you. He never has to raise his voice because everyone respects him so much. When you play in his ensemble you WANT to make him happy. He is unusually good at intrinsically motivating his students.

Absolutely amazing experience in this group. He is so genuine and gets to know you beyond just the time you are in class. His door is always open and willing to meet with you about any issues or questions you have. Overall a great educator. We need more Doc's in the world.
I love Dr. Golemo, He is a great conductor and musician.  Iowa State Music Department needs more Golemos
Extremely nice, passionate and willing to help at any time.
Great teacher who really understand the subject. Always knows what he wants from the ensemble.
Great teacher! Nuf Said
Doc is great! I'm taking band for fun, not for graduation credit. I probably would have quit playing my instrument by now if I didn't like him so much.
Doc is the coolest and nicest man in the music department! :)

HOT HOT HOT (kidding) he's the chair of music department and teachese Wind Ensemble 111. fun classes. meeting 4 time a week but, if you hav conflict he lets you miss thursday sometimes. not all the time. he's willing to have every interested on as long as you enjoy the WE. Lovely songs and great conductor. I recommend this WE. and professor.
Fun course.
Doc is just plain awesome!
Coolest guy in Music Hall!
No Comments

Took French 1070, but it wasn't an option. This class is, as expected, a lot of work, but Neysa made the course as digestible and fun as possible. She's an amazing professor who cares about every student she has, ensuring that no one is left behind in this incredibly fast course.

I took Spanish 102 with Neysa but IDK how to put it in as the course. But she was probably the best professor I've been with at ISU. She is very nice and really wants you to succeed. She understood we were at a basic spanish level and was very patient with us and understanding.
She's awesome and actually cares about her students. Had her in Spanish 101 and taking another class ofhers this spring!
Awesome Professor! Participate and show up to class and you will pass. Takes time to know all of her students and is wonderful at teaching difficult material. 10/10 recommend for French!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Neysa is a amazing professor! She makes sure you get a full grasp of the language by repetition in lectures and homework. She is a easy grader for exams and gives amazing feedback. Be prepared for homework every night but it is not very hard avg. 45 min. Tests are easy if you attend class. Attend class and you will pass. Amazing passion for french.

Awesome classroom atmosphere! Loved showing up each day and learning new vocabulary! Neysa is super nice and has fun with the class. Don't be afraid to speak up and share your knowledge! She won't hesitate to help or give feedback. Going to miss this class.
I learned so much, and I enjoyed attending class 4 days a week. A very refreshing class amongst my finance classes.

Neysa loves the language and her job and it really shows. She's very willing to help, all you have to do is ask. She is also up to helping you learn more about anything related to French. Lot of extra credit opportunity and she rewards you for hard work and improvement. She's a smile-for-a-smile type of person. You get what you give in her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Neysa! She's awesome; always willing to answer questions and is super understanding if you can't pronounce something or mess up often! Attendance is very important, but if you can work with her to not miss all your points (I had to miss a few days). 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Neysa is amazing. Loved the way she taught french. Really helped students on pronunciation. Overall, fantastic French teacher!

She is a great professor. Helps students with any question and is great about watching for struggles during group work and assisting with pronunciation and context. She isn't a tough grader, but participation is a must. You have to be there to pass, but you learn so much throughout the course that the policy makes sense.

LOVE HER!! She's very passionate and is very clear with what you need to know! Very good at answering questions! Homework every night but not a lot. Quizzes are easy, tests are moderate just study and you'll do just fine!

She is really good at explaining things. She is definitely there for students and wants to help them learn French. Attendance is mandatory and you can automatically fail due to attendance. Homework every night but it's not too long. Exams are straightforward. Need book every day.
Couldnt ask for more. Makes the lectures fun and interactive. a Little strict on attendance and homework

Very passionate about French and makes the class a safe space! I was terrified to take a foreign language but she gives you the confidence to try and you won't get punished for mistakes. As long as you try you shall succeed!

Entertaining lectures, influential style of teaching. Always there to help if required, plans in advance and lets you know. Well organized. Frankly only thing that might need improvement is class missing rule to be brought down.

Very involved class: homework is constant and attendance is mandatory. But Dr. Goodman is very clear and consistent about course requirements, and very lenient if you show effort, and helpful if you have questions or are struggling. She is also very open to suggestions in regards to the class and test structure, which is nice.
She's a great, energetic teacher. French is really hard though and the class is way too fast paced unless you've learn another European language. Have to study a LOT to keep up
Love this class! It's a lot of fun and she is very helpful. The tests and quizzes aren't hard if you study, even just a little.
Love, love, LOVE!!! her. Shes an amazing professor! I loved the class so much that I'm taking 102 next semester!

She grades very easily, and she is super nice and friendly. Her tests and quizzes are not that hard, but you still learn the material. I got an A this semester, and I hardly every opened the book except during class.

Neysa's French is very easy to understand and she is patient with students, waiting for them to answer instead of calling on them. If you have difficulty with French grammar, she is consistent in teaching 201 to 202 and tests only on what she's taught.  She occasionally checks daily hmwk, but only grades occasional turn-in work. Bring books daily!

I tried very hard not to miss a day of class! She is the best, is very encouraging and NEVER intimidates a students. I had problems with speaking before her class and it gave me a lot of confidence. Interesting, relevant, and a lot of fun!

Very patient with students.  If you do the homework (at least the stuff required to turn in) then he class is very easy, especially if you've had high school French to level 3 or 4.  Some of the students that were in FRNCH 101/102 seemed to struggle a bit, but she's willing to answer any questions you may have.
Very laid back and a tough and good teacher

I loved Monica, she was motivated and made the class highly interactive. You are required to participate but she also helps you when you are lost. The only hard thing was the midterm and final. The weekly readings were interesting and insightful. She learned everyone's name and brought speakers to class. I wish I could have more classes with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very confusing coursework on what is expected and she is terrible at communicating when you have questions. Watching lecture videos every week to keep your grade up.
Terrible online teacher. Does not know how to use canvas.

Honestly one of the best professors at Iowa State that I have had. She is very clear on expectations and always gives good feedback. Class is very much participation based however the way it was taught just helped me understand the material better. Reading material every week. Only had two exams, were super easy and study guides were given out.

Monica really does know and care a lot about the content that she teaches. However, she is very set in her ways of what is correct and what isn't.  She doesn't really go too into depth if you have a question. Random in-class assignments. Group work the whole semester. Not the best at introducing projects and assignments.

Monica is a really good professor but she has high expectations of her students. She assigns a lot of readings per week as well as written summaries, lectures are also participation heavy and participation point count a lot towards your grade. That said, she cares a lot about her students and helping them succeed and also is extremely passionate.

Monica presents all concepts through powerpoints that are all available on canvas but has some info blocked out, so be sure to write down everything you see as important on each slide when she presents. If you dont, she has great communication over any topic you need clarification on. Exams are very easy, just come to class

Monica is a great professor, and I would love to take her again. 414 required a bit of reading with chapters but did not require much effort. Her exams are relatively easy if you prepare, and she tries her absolute hardest to make sure you know the information. She is very responsive and has great communication.

Monica is a lovely woman & knows her stuff, she wants to make sure everyone has a voice & feel included, because everyone is different! If you participate with your group, you get points, if you talk in class, you get extra credit. LOTS OF READING & typing for HW, you don't have to do every week's, but it does help for the group in-class work.

This class was straightforward and the material was really boring. Just another prereq class ISU makes you take. Gordillo is decent professor. Grading is fair, not curved. Memorize terms and you should cruise through the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This professor is amazing! She actually CARES about her students and does her best to get to know each and every one of them. Her teaching is clear and she incorporates a lot of group activities. She is by far one of the best professors I have ever had.

Took her class during summer online. Was very easy, got an A just by watching her lectures which are offered as extra credit. The exams were not too hard, I recommend reading the book since her accent is sometimes hard to understand. Gives really good feedback, and listens to her students! Overall would take if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You work in teams the majority of the time and do i/trats along with a group project at the end. Must participate and attend class, has random in-class assignments that can't be made up and worth lots of points.

Monica (as she preferred to be called) has very high expectations. She had in-class group assignments nearly every class period, the opposite of what she had said at the beginning of the semester. Make sure you do all of the TopHat, as it will really help you at the end of the semester if you are just a few points away from a better grade.

Her lectures are so boring. My only motivation to go was the extra credit TopHat and occasional random in-class assignments. Her exams are poorly weighted. Most of her exams were worth 240 points for 40 multiple choice questions. She has extra credit, but it's pretty worthless with how heavily weighted the exams were.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not my favorite class. She has a thick accent. If the class isn't prepared to discuss, she tends to get pissy. Up to 25 points of extra credit. If you get a crappy group for the project, you're kind of screwed. 5 iRats and tRats throughout the semester. Pretty boring lectures if you aren't doing an activity that day. You also HAVE to participate

This course should not have been so difficult. Professor Gordillo's teaching style is unique, this was a class of 150+ and she was very active in interacting with her students. She can be difficult to understand at times and the material is never really as clear as it should be. In-class assignments were like pop quizzes, never given a heads up.

She is a really great teacher another example of if you do your best and listen you will get a good grade. There are a lot of terms and concepts you have to know for the test. Make a quizlet and study it twice a week and you will have an easy B or A. Also there is extra credit if you come to class and answer top hat questions correctly.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is a breeze, if you show up for in class assignments and extra credit top hat questions, and review vocab terms before exams you will get an A. Very nice woman but it is very easy to space out during her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's a great teacher. If you take the time to study casually for this class you'll do great. She does not handout A's but with that being said if you don't get atleast a B- in her class you might want to consider a different major.

Didn't learn anything useful really. The tests are easy, however be careful because if you miss a few questions it heavily impacts your grade. You CAN skip class; however you'd miss out on the Tophat extra credit (10 points boosts your grade 1%). Also, beware of skipping because there's 4 group assigns worth 15 pts and missing one will drop 1.5%.

She is knowledgeable about the material, but disorganized. Lectures are hard to follow, and tophat is only used for extra credit. It's easy to skip, but she assigns groups at the beginning of the sem and throws random large point group projects in randomly. Tests are really heavy point-wise, but not too hard to study for with the book and quizzes!

The class is straight-forward. Show up, pay attention, study for quizzes and tests and you will do fine. The content is interesting but you definitely need to read the book in order to fully understand the material. Overall, I would take the class again as there are group projects and is an interactive class. Makes the class go by fast!

If you don't read the textbook word for word, you won't do well on the exams. You have to know everything before the exams a week prior, because there are individual and team IRats that cover the textbook also. Always in class assignments, so if you skip you lose many points. Honestly wouldn't recommend her to anyone. Sooo much info in one class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: My class was online and it was pretty easy. Worst part was having to watch the several 40 minute lecture videos each module (which are graded). Assignments were easy and quizzes/exams weren't bad as long as you looked over the powerpoints. She gives several extra credit opportunities.

Professor Gordillo was a fine instructor. The class was super boring no matter how hard she tried to make it be interesting. Puts students in teams for the whole semester. Uses TopHat for extra credit. Random team assignments throughout the semester, so go to class just in case. Nice woman, doesn't have good grammar and it shows on exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a team based learning class.. iRat/tRats and group assignments & project. She takes attendance & has group assignments almost everyday so you can't skip. She is a good lecturer & gives great examples which makes it easy to learn. Easy tests, not terrible project. I would recommend Monica b/c she is super nice and sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Gordillo is an amazing professor, but difficult to understand. She offers lots of opportunities for points and is a very kind person. Make sure you attend class for lectures and read your textbooks because exams are slightly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Show up to class and pay attention and get an A. She periodically does Top hat and in class assignments for credit, so don't miss those. One of the easier classes I have taken in college that many people fail because they don't try at all. Some group work. Dismiss early every day since it's a 1.5 hour class. Read the book to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a good professor. If you're considering skipping class, just go to class and do homework in the back, Top Hat questions are randomly worth extra credit. Quizzes and exams are super easy but the extra credit will be required to get above a B+ since it's easy to lose points on them. Missing two questions is worth 1% of your final grade...
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY
