reviews.comment: Only reason to show up for lecture is for the top hat which is all EC and the 10pt group questions she'll randomly assign about 1 in every 8 lectures. At home online quizes and testing center exams that are horribly worded. Buy the book and read all the chapters because quizes/exams are exactly out of there. She also drops your lowest exam score.
She and her lectures are very very hard to understand

seems like a really nice person but did not enjoy taking this class at all. Lectures are extremely hard to follow and her powerpoints and videos are cluttered and straight from an old book. Doesn't give you a good idea of what are on tests and asks a ton of tophat questions every single class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took this class online in 4 weeks and thought it was pretty straight forward. She basically tells you everything you need to do, by providing many good examples. I butchered her with lots of questions and she basically told me answers for the test. Gives out extra credit and asks for feedback from class. Take this class online.

She pushes you to work for your grade and makes the class challenging. She doesn't lecture so you have to read and study the slides but she cares about all of her students and makes herself available so that you can get help when needed. There are point in class all the time so you do have to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: You can tell that she really cares about her students, but is not a great teacher. She uses the powerpoints directly out of the book and they are not helpful at all. She expects participation and will sit there until someone answers. She is hard to understand and her tests need to be checked by someone else because they are written extremely poorly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are a lot of in class quizzes and team assignments to make sure you come to class. She posts powerpoints for each chapter so you dont need the book except for the case studies. There is a major group project at the end so make sure to pick a good group. She does give extra credit if you show up to review days before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The lectures were no help and I didn't learn anything from her. Taught myself out of the book for each test, which she gave no test review or study guide for and just said to read the book/ make note cards. The tests are extremely tough with not knowing what to study. Comprehensive final, no study guide. I would NOT recommend her. Heavy accent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not a great professor. She favors certain groups and students, and if she doesn't like you, she wont give you good scores on in class assignments or projects. Would not take it as a night class, and would also take it with a different professor is that is an option.

International Management was super interesting. However, she assigns a ton of reading, in-class activities, and expects a lot of participation. Go to class and take good notes, you should be fine on the exams if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Favorite professor so far at Iowa State. She does an excellent job with relating the material to real world situations. Attendance is highly recommended and it helps to contribute in class when it comes time for the tests. She emphasizes the importance of independent learning, but is very helpful with questions. I wish I had another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: PARTICIPATION MATTERS. And keep track of it. Choose a good group for your project and the class will be a breeze because you work together often. Exams are simple if you take notes using her slide handouts and if you read the book. Participating is also really easy if you read or at least skim the book, and then she'll like you too.

A big group project and presentation for this class that isn't too bad. You are graded on participation so make sure to participate. Monica is a tough grader. You get weekly quizzes or group work and we answered the questions, but apparently not to her standard because we never got 100% on an assignment. You also will never get out of class early

She was super helpful with rescheduling tests and assignments for interviews.  Very enthusiastic for lectures.  Seems like she enjoys teaching a ton.  I liked the in class assignments so there was no homework.
There were lots of case studies that you have to read for quizzes in class. The tests are pretty easy. Participation is one of the biggest factors in grading for sure.
Expects too much class participation. Exams aren't really over lecture content. Lecture content is straight from the book's suggested power point slides.

Participation is mandatory but skimming the chapter before class(or during class) or even just commenting with an opinion will get a sufficient participation grade. Makes you write papers singlespaced. A lot of group work, if you're not in class you don't get those points. Reviews a lot to make sure you know the material. Very kind & encouraging.

Tests are nothing but material from the textbook, so if you wanted to skip class, you wouldn't be missing out. She does require clickers, not the app even, but physical clicker themselves. Walks around the lecture hall and lecture is more like a conversation, not just reading notes off the slides in class. Hard to focus b/c of intense accent.
She speaks horrible english. Tests are really hard. Don't use the power points, use the textbook! Questions are found right in your textbook. She uses clicker points a lot so be in class.

I could not stand this professor. She was almost impossible to listen to during lecture and when I was listening all I could think about was her accent. She gives no rubric or no clear expectations of assignments and chose our group for us.. CHAOS. No test review or study guide. Worst teacher I've ever had.

PARTICIPATE!!!!! She is HUGE into participation points. It is a decent chunk of your grade. If you hate group work, you won't like this class. You have a group project that goes the entire semester. Tests are tough, so make sure you are prepared.  Don't have to go but she gives pop quizzes sometimes so I would go!

This is one of those professors where you wonder why you are showing up to class, to hear her ramble about nothing. Her "discussion" questions are numbingly obvious to the point that no one answers them, and then she thinks we're just lazy. It's an easy A, unfortunately in-class HW makes attendance mandatory.

She's a nice professor and helpful if you have questions, very energetic. The class itself was pretty boring. She basically asks a bunch of questions and will wait (and wait and wait) until someone answers. Read the book if you want to do good on the tests.

Not a good teacher. She tries really hard, but students don't get engaged. She will ask questions and walk throughout the classroom until she gets an answer, right or wrong. Not very good with grammar (pluralizes too many words), but can be understood. You will learn nothing from her and will have to teach yourself. In-class assignments are given.

Got absolutely nothing from this class. Monica has no real world experience as she has never worked in industry. Tests were easy as they cover only topics from in class. The book is not necessary. Must go to class because of the in class quizzes.
Professor Gordillo is a nice professor and willing to help out most of the time. The tests are pretty easy but you must attend class to take in class quizzes. Book is a must for her class.

The exams were very easy. The hardest part of Gordillo's class is making yourself show up. You get absolutely NOTHING from lectures and will find yourself doing everything except paying attention. Her accent is think. Unfortunately she does class points every week (nightclass). I got a B just because I missed too many in-class points. Easy A or B.

Not the best teacher ever but she doesn't have some credibility since she graduated from Cambridge. Her classes are almost useless and she is very critical with her assignments and in-class activities so do them well. Her test makes you think and you REALLY need to know all materials well to do well.

Bad english, hard to understand. Yells into the mic so you'll leave with a headache everyday. The material is easy but its hard to follow her during class. HAve to teach yourself! Her tests are opinion questions so you need to know everything really well to understand what she's even asking.  You'll leave the test thinking "did we even learn that?"

She has terrible grammar because she does not speak English well. Her teaching style is not to teach but to have the class teach. She asks questions and won't say anything until class answers even if no one knows the answer. She ALWAYS says those answers are exactly right so I feel like she might not know what she is talking about.

Monica Gordillo is no more than a professional student. She loves to flaunt her many degrees in various areas of business and management yet has never worked in business or a management position. Because of this, she teaches strictly from the book and uses the publisher's PowerPoints. She teaches solely on theory with no practical aspect. Useless.

I took this class for my business minor and was happy I chose to do so. She is by far one of the best professors I've had at ISU. She does a great job of keeping the class engaged while integrating real world examples to the concepts. I HIGHLY recommend taking this course, it's interesting and if you put in the effort, an easy A
BORING! Disliked the class a lot. Tests weren't bad but did need to read to understand topics.

She is really nice. Puts in a lot of effort to get the class involved. It can get a bit boring, but that's just the way it goes. Tests aren't too bad. You will have to present twice on "Management in the news" and that's actually the most boring part. Final group project is straight forward and easy.
Pretty straight forward and easy class.  I didnt even buy a book because her tests are straight off her slides.  As long as you go and put a little bit of effort forward its a breeze.
Most boring class ever. Uses clicker for bonus credit. Tests are MCQ and pretty straight forward.
I liked her teaching style.  She requires attendance, and participation.  She is nice and helpful. Good teacher.

Everytime I leave the classroom, I think to myself "Well, there is three hours of my life I will never get back..." She spends so much time on a single idea. She really needs to put more content into the class. Attendace is mandatory, as is participation. She accepts pathetic answers from other students, it's really sad...

Tests sucked and so did the project b/c of group members, better to take class with people you know.  She is funny in lectures sometimes and very easy to get along with.  Tests have multiple repeating questions so know your stuff.

take this class with about 3 of your friends, otherwise the group project will make the semester seem an eternity. read the case studies thoroughly, you can get a lot of points in class discussion. class is lecture on some days,  discussion over case studies on others. she makes the final project easy to do well on.
Bad teacher i wish i did not take this class with her.
No Comments
Incerdable amount of work, cases are interesting, uses students to grade for her on participation and projects.  Very frusterating, you will learn, but very difficult.
No Comments
He is a great professor and teaches very well. I received such a low score because I missed more recitations than what is given to you. If you attend lecture and recitations, it's an easy A.

Miller is one of the best professors I have ever had. He's very caring and funny and makes lectures engaging. Chemistry is hard, but Miller made it understandable. Exams can be difficult, but there is a practice exam that lists the concepts. Textbook isn't very necessary, but there are practice problems at the end of chapters for extra studying.

Very good lectures and he mixes in a bit of humor to keep things interesting. He's earned the respect of his students by having great lectures, being approachable, and being fair with grades. Makes good use of demos to supplement powerpoint lectures. Hw is tough, but with enough time it's feasible. Very pleased with both the class and professor.

Dr. Miller was such a great professor! His lectures were so helpful in understanding and applying the material. Most of this class is knowing formulas and completing various math problems as it applies to chemistry. He gives great examples in class that make the homework easy and his exams aren't too bad if you study.

Dr. Miller was very straight forward with expectations. Lots of tests, but they are straight forward. A lot of other points. Great at giving homework and worksheets that help with understanding. Lectures were extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gordie is very knowledgeable and his lectures show it. His online lectures are easy to follow and he explains things well. There is a weekly online assignment and worksheet which were great for practice and understanding. The grading scale is amazing and isn't so test heavy. The first week was a bit jarring for me but the class got easier.

I loved Gordie! His lectures were amazing and he explained everything really well. Attendance is not mandatory and all lectures are online. He offers a lot of extra credit with the weekly assignments and homework. The homework was pretty tough but was not impossible if you asked for help. Gordie is amazing, 10/10 recommend a class with him.

Great professor, really passionate about chemistry. The homework assignments are very tedious and require some out-of-box thinking. Exams were pretty hard for me even after reviewing lecture notes, recitation quizzes, textbook readings, and having a tutor since the start of the semester. Lots of points so the tests are not the end all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A great professor that will answer any questions after the end of lecture. Go to the class, don't skip. I hardly had to do any studying because the lectures were so easy to understand and when I did. He had recordings of everything he said online. Homework was the hardest thing and the help room will give you the answers after talking a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really was a great class, lectures were consistently understandable and interesting if you wanted them to be. The homework seemed a bit harder than the course, but you dont need full points for full credit. Extra credit was very generous if you just did the weekly assignments, and the final was 90% multiple choice. Great instructor overall.

He's clear with what he expects you to know, phenomenal at lecturing (he's funny, speaks clearly, gives important examples). He actually gives you a chance to pass a difficult class. The only complaint is his HW sets are pretty difficult. Other than that he's the man.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gordie's lecture are top-notch. Really easy to take notes from and he posts all his powerpoints online as well. Homework is somewhat challenging, but helps in understanding the concepts well. Exams are fairly straightforward with mostly multiple-choice and some computations.
Gordie is a very nice guy, but his tests and homework assignments are very challenging. He has a slight curve (88% A), but good luck getting an 88%.

The lectures are good. The homework was usually pretty easy but the phrasing of the questions at times made it hard to understand. It always felt like we weren't given enough time to do the quizzes. The tests were pretty straightforward as long as you kept up with the homework and recitations. Miller is very helpful if you go to his office hours.
Really interesting lectures, tests aren't too bad if you do the homework and go to recitation

decent professor.  Sometimes his wording on test and assignments can be confusing.  He does't use my chemistry lab he has written homework that is turned in about every other week and it is usually longer than you expect and really hard.  Never wait until the day before.

This was a good class. He posts study guides, which are helpful. He doesn't expect you to memorize formulas, he provides them on his tests. Recitation was difficult at first, but the amount of time given to us was increased halfway through the semester, because people were struggling. Lectures are pretty clear. He's understanding and helpful.

The homework is a little tough, but it's only every other week and is way better than mastering chemistry. Just do it at the chem help center or in groups and it's not too bad. Lectures are interesting, clicker questions are easy, and he is funny and interesting. One of the best professors I've had so far.

Dr. Miller has been by far the best professor that I have had during my whole time at Iowa State University. He genuinely cares about all his students and want to make sure everyone in the class understands the concepts. His homework is very difficult but definitely prepares you for exams. He is always there for students and is a great guy overall.

I did very well in all aspects of the class except recitation. You are pretty much never given enough time to complete the quizzes, and they usually are very hard quizzes. I basically flunked that portion of the class and got A's and high B's in exams, homework, and in class activities. Also, the homework is really hard, GO to the help room.

I took this course as a requirement for medical school admissions. Although I was finance major, I found the class pretty easy. You need to make sure you do book problems to keep your skills up and also attend class to get easy clicker points. I also found SI to be helpful along with the Help Room. Use the resources available!!

This was my second time taking 178 (previously had Irmi) and was expecting the worst. But, Miller was one of the best chem profs I've had. His lectures are very clear and thoroughly explains how to do the problems. Yes, the homework is a pain but is a nice grade booster. Study old exams and quizzes and exams will be straightforward. Good class :)
Very clear lecturer. Dr. Miller is passionate about making sure that his students learn something. Best chemistry professor I've encountered at Iowa State.

Very clear and concise when it comes to explaining topics. You know exactly what topics will be covered on the exams. Homework is quite challenging but he curves it and the end of the semester. Good stories.
Very clear in explanations of concepts.  Pay attention to the practice problems they are similar to tests and quizzes.  The homework is difficult, but definitely prepares you for the exams.

I think that Dr. Miller is probably one of the best general chemistry instructors that Iowa State has. I usually find myself scared and lost in chemistry classes, however he made gen chem so much more enjoyable! His homework assignments are very tough, but if you utilize the help center in Gilman you will be fine. Study and attend review sessions!
Good guy. His homework is almost impossible, but it is on a curve. He likes to curve a lot and he explains the material very well most of the time!
Overall one of the better teachers i have had at Iowa State. Not the easiest course in the world but he wants you to succeed which is a nice change compared to many professors.

I wish I would have put more effort into this class. He's a decent lecturer and expects you to have an idea about what you're going over in class before you get there. His homework is impossible but if you go to the help room, the TAs will do their best to help you.

My favorite Chem professor at Iowa State thus far. He was very clear in lecture. Homework was only due once every 2 weeks, but was extremely hard to figure out. I always had to go to the help room for that. Otherwise, he gives you everything you need to succeed if you save his quizzes and worksheets.

Dr. Miller is a great lecture. I had his wife for CHEM 177 and I enjoyed them both. I am an engineering major so this class was a general requirement. Overall, I found the class interesting and the lectures very helpful. Also for each exam he would create an outline, and you will do well on the exams if you fill them out.

Professor Gordie is about as good as his wife is at teaching. He's good for research and that's about it. Tells you equations and whatnot in class, but doesn't specify when to use them. Homework (and tests, not to mention)is impossibly hard. Doesn't tell the TAs answers, so no one knows what to do. Get a different teacher.

Gordie was my first Chem professor in college and, while the course was challenging, his enthusiasm for the material reminded me why I chose my major. He wrote a book, instead of having us buy a super expensive textbook, and it followed lectures exactly! He also is a very encouraging professor and a great reference to have farther down the road!
Gordie was an awesome teacher, not always the clearest in lecture but talk to him later and it all makes sense. Overall a great guy to talk to outside of chemistry as well.
I did not enjoy him as a teacher. His experiments always failed and I had to go to his lectures because of clicker points. Beyond boring.
Very fun professor, very knowledgeable. Never got bored in his class. Taught to the students very well. He wanted everyone to succeed. Would recommend him in a heartbeat!
Absolutely wonderful teacher, loves his job loves students to learn. Bought us pizza for mole day and took the entire class bowling before finals!!! Never will have another teacher as good as him
He is a wonderful teacher. He really enjoys his work and prefers people to LEARN rather than just get the right answers.

Gordie is a great guy who wants his students to do well, the class is hard, but youre the one who signed up for the adv. gen. chem. Homework is hard, but if you meet with him, he makes things much clearer.  Look over old tests when studying-extremely helpful. dont buy the book unless youre one of those people who actually reads the books

Dr. Miller was overall an amazing prof and he is readily available for any questions.  The homework was INCREDIBLY difficult and his tests were beyond tricky.  I found myself in the help center a lot which didn't do much good anyway.  Dr. Miller is a great prof but the class itself is really hard.

He's a really nice guy and has well-planned lectures.  He's fair and has good review sessions before exams.  For 201X we got a speaker every week from a different department and I thought that was cool, although some people didn't.  Overall the best chem prof. I've ever had !
Very nice guy and wants students to do well. His test are alittle tricky and are not always the same content as old tests. Review everything not just old tests.

his notes are very organized and easy to read. speaks very clearly and easy to follow along. his voice does make me tired though. seems very willing to help students in whatever way. he tells you everything you need to know for exams. use old tests to study!
Pretty good at what he does. Speaks clearly, and moves at about the right pace.
Made chemistry easy to learn and fun, great teacher.  Enjoyed the class until he left, which was halfway through the semester when Song came in.  After that I REALLY wished I had him.
He is a very good teacher. He really knows his stuff!  Much better than Song
he is good but he moves pretty quick
Took over class at semester, and screwed everyone to achieve his coveted bell curve.

The professor was able to convey useful information about teaching in a classroom. Her teaching style was very beneficial with having amazing lectures and labs. Definitely a hands-on class and helpful for getting experience with teaching.

Professor Grote was a very nice teacher who gave our class a lot of guidance in terms of being a teacher. Instructing an elementary PE class each Monday was a fun way to practice classroom management. I learned a lot from her.

I really enjoyed this class! Professor Grote shows how much she cares about her students and what we do in class. She is kind and really easy to talk to, especially about work for class or any questions you have.
She is a very easy teacher. She graded everything accurately. She is very nice and easy to talk to when needing help with work or having any questions.

I loved having Lisa as a professor! She was caring and really wanted the best for us throughout the semester. She was very transparent on what she expected of us and even though she was a pretty tough grader, everything was clearly laid out and she went over what we needed to gain full points multiple times before assignments were due. I loved her!

I really enjoyed this class. Professor Grote was transparent and very easy to get along with. She was a hard grader but since she was very transparent with that she expected, she expected work turned in to be good and along the lines of her criteria.

Professor Grote's main goal is to see her students improve and enjoy the class. She was extremely kind and caring, but had goals she wanted you to achieve. She made the learning environment fun and gave meaningful feedback that helped you learn from previous assignments.

I loved having Professor Grote in class! I've learned a lot more about classroom management and behavior management in her Kinesiology class than I have in most elementary ed classes. She is very caring, and her lectures are very engaging. You also get great real-world experiences, and she prepares you very well for classes and teaching.

this teacher was amazing. She allowed us to defend our work if we got a grade we didn't think was fair. She was also very open about her life which allowed her to bring real world examples into the class. The quizzes are easy as long as you attend the lectures.

She is very flexible with things going on in and outside of class, cares a lot about her students, and is very passionate and knowledgable about her class content. This makes for very interesting and informative lectures, and the field experience is even better. Highly recommend!!

I would take another class with her! Attendance isn't mandatory but she does mark if you are there or not;Points are assigned with lab days because of the discussion afterwards.  Very accommodating and a fair grader.  Few big assignments so it is moderate commitment for the semester.  Labs are actually really fun! Especially with the preschoolers.

Lisa was a great teacher! She is very passionate about what she teaches in class, and she truly cares about her students and our work! She was very encouraging and gave us great advice for being a future educator! I would highly recommend taking her class!

Lisa is an excellent professor with clear, engaging lectures and well-organized assignments. Expectations are always clear, and she offers helpful feedback along with valuable co-teaching opportunities. Working with lab school students is a highlight. She's approachable, supportive, and truly cares about student success. Highly recommend her class!

I would 100% take a class with Lisa again. She was always easy-going and very understanding. If you show up to her lectures, you will do just fine. She is very open to feedback, and you can just tell she cares about her students. I would definitely recommend this class!!
Great professor! Super fun class! Show up to lecture and lab. Submit assignments on time. She lectures once a week and you usually get out early!

Lisa is a great professor; she gives instructions well, sharing her own experiences in the education field to provide a real-life perspective. Lisa is great to talk to if you ever have any questions or concerns, and is always willing to listen. This class truly helped set me up for success in my academic journey. I would highly recommend Lisa!

All assignments are clear and not tricky. Lisa does a great job lecturing, making her lectures engaging and easy to follow. The highlight of the class is working with the lab school kids. Lisa always makes expectations clear and does a great job communicating with her students. She gives you many opportunities to co-teach and improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was a great class. It was so fun working with the lab school and being able to create our own lesson to teach them. If you show up and take notes you will do well in this class. Each lab is graded so try not to miss those. Professor Grote is a fair grader and easy to approach. She will answer questions and help you if you need it.
Lisa was great! The class was really fun if you put in the time with the kids!

Lisa is a down to earth professor who understands that life happens. You will get good grades as long as you show up to lectures and labs. For all assignments there are clear rubrics provided and she is willing to clear up and confusion if needed, you just have to ask!

Lisa is a great professor! She is really caring and adjusts the course based off feedback, so is open to change. The lectures can be long but they're only once per week and are worth it for the quizzes and exams. The lab component is very engaging and useful for teaching.

Lisa was a great teacher with easy assignments if you come to class and stay up to date on readings. The rubrics sometimes can be confusing but nothing you can't clear up by asking her about. Would definitely have her again as a teacher!

I loved having Lisa and her class. She is a very positive person, and you can clearly see that she cares about what she is teaching and the students in her class. She provides very good feedback and is open to helping you with anything you may have questions about. She isn't a strict grader, really. She wants you to have fun and gain experience!

I would absolutely take her class again. She was very helpful and wanted us to do well. We had so many group teaches that were not graded, just so we could get comfortable in front of the kids. My favorite professor by far.
The other reviews are outdated. If you give effort in class and show up you will have a good time and get a good grade. Take her class!!

Take health if you can. Working with the students was fun, but I never felt comfortable being watched by Lisa. She was very condescending. She'd ask for feedback from her students but it all felt like gaslighting. She also didn't have a close relationship with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and all of the negative comments are outdated. She was very kind, easy to talk to, made expectations very clear, and was eager to help. This class is partial lectures and partial lab experience with the lab school kids. Lecture days go from 9-10 and lab days go from 9:40-10:40. Great class and teacher I learned a lot of new things.

Great professor!  Her lectures were engaging and the activities were fun!  Some classes were learning content from her PowerPoints (which were well laid out), and some were just learning how to teach a certain physical education skill in the gym (which was really easy!). You'll teach a couple of lessons at some point, which are not too difficult!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor is very blunt and sometimes rude. If you miss three or more classes be prepared for her to not like you and grade your assignments harsher. If you want a good grade, stay on her good side. Otherwise, this class is not homework-heavy and is pretty easy if you show up.

Show up to class and you'll be good. This professor is an average grader. The one thing is her rubrics are vague with little detail so it's hard to understand what she wants. Had to ask MANY questions when it came to the projects. Definitely wouldn't consider her a professor that has close relationships with students.

Professor Grote is amazing! She is very understanding and tells you exactly what she expects. It is a fun classroom environment and we learn so much by interacting with the kids! There are no surprises in this class and everything we do is helpful and useful.

Professor Grote is a great professor! She is very clear with her expectations and gives clear rubrics to help us find success as students. She is accessible outside of class and is very personable and understanding. She doesn't require attendance but attending class is enjoyable and will adequately prepare you for exams! Definitely recommend :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is actually very fun. Grote is very knowledgable and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lisa is the most difficult professor I have ever had. She's passive aggressive and a harsh grader. Towards the end of the semester she tried showing "empathy" towards her students because of how many complaints she received. I would highly recommend signing up with a different professor if you don't want to be stirred in with her drama.

I do not recommend taking a class with this professor. The assignments are very tough, and teacher is a bit harsh. Taking a class with her has left me stressed. Save yourself and consider another course or professor!

I really enjoyed taking a class with Professor Grote. She is specific about what she wants on assignments but if you follow the rubric, you will do fine. She gives really great feedback and taught me a lot of great things. I feel like I have taken away great knowledge from this class.
Very tough grader, is not very clear. Was a very difficult class for no reason, could be easier but teacher makes it extremely difficult.

Horrible teacher, would not take a course with her again. very passive aggressive. Does not help students, never explains content well. And is a harsh grader. Asked question ones in class and she was very rude. Do not recommend !!!

Ted is an awesome professor! He is super knowledgeable and brings a unique perspective to the world of design. His lectures may feel long but he finds ways to make them fun and engaging. The weekly assignments and discussion usually tie into the assigned readings or videos, which can be long.

People who dislike him are people who are not willing to broaden their knowledge beyond bare requirements (IMO). He was hilarious, kind, and brought up (mostly) relevant and interesting topics that encouraged students to think more deeply about design. He really cares about his students. Also 10/10 voice to fall asleep to.

I took his design in context class, he's pretty chill. The lectures go on for a bit long, but he enjoys what he talks about which makes the class interesting. There aren't many readings. The TA's do grade pretty harshly, especially on the quizzes. Besides that, my only big complaint about this class is the GTA assignment... iykyk.

Don't take Ted's design in context lecture. He talks for SO long about information that isn't relevant. Attendance is graded and also participation. He directs all questions to the TA's who grade hard for some reason. He doesn't open the quizzes until 6pm on Fridays and they close on Sunday. Very frustrating.

- puts a lot of research and thought into the lectures to make them interesting and relevant to the class
- makes an effort to engage with students and hear their opinions about the content of the lecture
- very understanding, gave multiple extra credit opportunities, and a few extensions on quizzes
- 10/10 great prof. who cares about his students!
Ted is the best prof. Take every class he offers especially field travel. Everyone loves ted
Greatest professor ever! Take any and all classes that he teaches
We love Ted. Ted is an OG. Must recommend ted
Ted is Daddy
Great professor, very knowledgeable, and answers emails extremely quickly & thoroughly if you have questions.

Travis Grager was one the best instructors I've ever had. His class was very well organized, and even when the homework assignments were math heavy, his presentations slides walked you through all of it.
Easy class taught by a good professor
Professor Grager has been one of my favorite professors thus far. The assignments were clear, he was well articulated and a very fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is one of the teachers that actually care about the students and takes the time to answer questions and ensure the question is fully answered. He is very willing to adjust to better suit the learning needs of students. One of the better aerospace engineering teachers at Iowa State.

Grager is the best choice for 261. As the senior design professor he is very good about structuring the class around information you use further along. He has a lot of background experience in the industry so any outside questions he can answer. His lectures are very easy to read and it is always easy to tell what is important. Best aero professor

A very kind, helpful, and experienced professor. He knows what he is doing, and is a great help to teams as they work on their Senior Capstone project. He is easy to talk to, and gives well informed answers to students' questions. Travis is great at what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Kristen is an amazing professor! She genuinely cares for her students and wants to help them succeed. She understands when students are struggling and puts in the time to help. Yes, you are kind of thrown into design here at Iowa State, but I didn't take art in high school, and I loved having her as a professor.

Kristen can often leave instructions very confusing and leave a lot unsaid. She has a weird vibe and the studio she runs has a loottt of work included in it (which isn't really her fault but she doesn't make it any easier the way she talks to the group) that said she actually isn't the worst for 102, I actually did like her, and grading is simple

I gave her the benefit of the doubt but she proved my gut right at the end of semester. She enjoys making her students feel dumb and watching them struggle. She admitted to lying to the entire class and was smiling about it and laughing at the fact we were getting screwed over. She is required so be aware of her real personality.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kristen is such a genuine and caring professor! She wants you to do your best and she makes sure to push you towards that goal. This class is tough, the projects are long and you are in for a lot of late nights but Kristen helps to guide you along. She is a bit vauge with her answers to questions you may have but it only pushes you further!
She was awesome! Super kind and helpful. She will make an effort to meet with you one-on-one and give you feedback.

I took my first studio DSN 102 with her and she was AWESOME. She is always willing to help and listen to your ideas and help you tweak them. Overall an amazing professor. Only not so good thing is sometimes it takes a bit for her to grade.

I highly suggest attending the lecture rather than reading from the textbook. He is willing to provide simplifications of the material and real-life examples of the concepts. Beware, he can be a tough grader BUT is more than willing to meet during his office hours to discuss where you can improve.

I liked John as a professor, sometimes the class got a little boring but that's personal. The only things that went into the gradebook were exams and participation which made doing well on exams essential. The practice exams were very similar to the actual exam which made doing well in the class pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he is is clear with what he wants from students and expectations. very easy class and the notes are crystal clear. very easy grading. show up to class and you will get the A
A lot things to write and read. But he is very helpful when you have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great with providing outside help when you need it, but you have to make sure to use all available office hours and emails. Willing to work through any confusion about the material in class if you are confused and reached out for help. Material for the class is not heavy, however, you need to stay on top of things and watch the lectures to pass

Initially extremely unclear of expectations. If you are wondering something, be sure to ask him. He is always willing to answer any questions, just doesn't go out of his way to give all possible information right off the bat. It is frustrating. Not a bad instructor, just be prepared to communicate A LOT to understand what is expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Would you like to endanger your GPA and scholarships for a grammar course of which the content will never, ever be useful to anyone? Would you like to have multiple serious talks with your advisor about dropping your second major in your senior year due to one single professor? Then this is the professor for you!

This professor really added a lot of stress to my load. Beware, no one got 100% on her papers. She takes forever to grade (sometimes more than a month). She has daily homework that is graded only some unspecified times and the homework is overly extensive and is over material you have not learned and have to idea about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gray is fairly friendly but not understanding. She expects the students know as much as she does. Beware she will take a month to grade assignments and expect you to turn in the second paper 3 days after the grade and comments for the first are handed back. I wish the expectations that are held for students were reciprocated by the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is not timely whatsoever in grading papers. Frustrating to get assigned a second paper without the grade for the first one. Most of class time was spent going over the homework that was due. She had very in-depth slides and sometimes TOO many slides. Only like 3 things are taken for a grade until the last 3 weeks of school so beware

reviews.comment:
This was not the course I took.

She is not good at giving timely feedback, responding to emails, lecturing, or facilitating in class discussions. She is good at making slides, having in-depth instructions on assignments, and the very late feedback she gives on your writing is actually helpful.

She breaks confidences. Don't tell her your secrets.
The course is tough, but Dr. Gray is super clear and friendly in her teaching and is always open for help during office hours.
Her class was the most difficult class I've ever taken in my entire life, but she is very open to one on one time if you need the help.
I genuinely enjoyed his lectures for COMS 311, which is saying a LOT. I cannot imagine a better processor for this class in particular, so definitely recommend overall.
Prabhu is a good professor and genuinely cares about his classes. He wants you to pass and will adjust the class difficulty accordingly.
Awesome professor, makes concepts super easy to understand. Class is very hard though
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prabhu is an excellent professor. His lectures are very informative and super clear. You can tell he has spent years refining the content delivery. He is probably the best professor I have ever had.

Class is INCREDIBLY difficult. At midterm there were two homework assignments and the midterm. Thats it. The other 3 assignments were crammed at the end of the semester. In lecture though, you can tell this guy has genuinely mastered the material. As long as you can keep up with him he is very good at teaching. Just wish there was more practice.

311 is known the be THE hardest undergraduate class at ISU, yet he taught this course beautifully. He knows his algorithms and doesn't use unnecessary jargon. He explains concepts visually and always asks if we have questions. He actively advocates for easier exams in this course and only teaches the information that you need to be successful.

He is super nice and good at explaining concepts. This class is mostly for people who aren't comp sci majors, and it feels like he understands that and makes it pretty easy to pass without putting max effort in. There are occasionally graded in-class homework assignments. Tests are easy and you get cheat sheets.

Overall programming is difficult. He is literally the best programming instructor who truly teaches you how to code and not just talk about himself. his exams seem similar to the practices so if you read, attend classes regularly, and review lectures you will learn more. Unfortunately class went online so it was harder too watch lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I was in the online section so I'm not sure about how available he is outside of class, but I loved his lectures. His dry humor is great. He makes everything very clear and gives plenty of time to complete the homework and projects. Definitely recommend doing the homework , it will prepare you for the tests.

Dr. Prabhu wasn't a bad professor. In 207 the assignments are not very difficult, but students should be sure to check their code with many test cases, one mistake and you can lose 10 points on an assignment. 3 tests. The 1st test (15% of grade) was very easy, test 2 (20%) wasn't too bad, the final (25% of grade) was very difficult.

Dr. Prabhu helped me a lot in this class. He is willing to help you out if he believes you are a good student. The TAs were also very helpful and it was nice that the lectures were all recorded and posted on Canvas. The assignments are pretty easy if you attend the lectures, but after the first exam, the exams are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Taken online; wouldn't recommend. Class was hw heavy, 11 worksheets, 6 assignments which are coding projects. The syllabus did not specify how many there would be, their point values, or due dates. There were not rubrics available until after grading. 2 tests; 1 cumulative final. Test 1 easy; 2 is difficult and tight for time. Relied on TAs heavily

Expect to show up to class unless you want to get 0's on worksheets in the grade book. His lectures are great though and he usually explains the material very well. He often gives help with programming projects in class, too. Overall a good class and as long as you regularly attend class you'll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Prabhu is an incredible lecturer! He does a great job making the lectures clear and concise. There is about one in class activity a week- which isn't graded for correctness, it just helps to do it well because the homework is almost exactly the same as the in class activity. The tests are exactly like the homework so that's nice.

Prabhu is a great overall professor. His lectures are informative, and he always makes sure to review content with activities in class. This class is tough if you don't go to class. He doesn't post any notes online. His tests are mostly based on homework questions, and sometimes he even gives you a cheat sheet. Really nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good, enjoyable professor overall. Main problem you might have is he uploads nothing online so if you miss a day it would be hard to catch up. Slight accent, easy to get used to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: a pretty good teacher, but he does not post notes online so if you miss class you need a different way to get the notes. lots of written homeworks, class is not on blackboard either
Great class. Great professor.

Before taking this class I had heard how great of a professor Dr. Prabhu was, and now I could not agree more. He is easily the best instructor in the computer science department and the best I've had at Iowa State.
Gives great lectures, and has a dry sense of humor that complements the material well. Whatever material isn't easy or trivial is very well explained.
He is definitely the best instructor in CS dept. Some of the material can be hard, but he is great at explaining the material.
Easy to understand and learn from. He makes the quizzes very easy to do good on if you pay attention. Through and through one of my best professors I have had and probably ever will have

Prabhu is a very concise and engaging professor. He has a great philosophy of keeping things simple in order to understand the material and providing amble time in class to master it. If you go to class and actively listen, it will be a great class and you'll learn a lot. He is also a very interesting man and is fun to talk to in office hours.

Dr. Prabhu is definitely one of the best instructors in the CS dept. His teaching style is clear and easy to understand, and he's quite helpful during office hours. His classes don't require extensive studying outside of class, and the assignments and exams are fair and sane (unlike in some courses I could name).
Very good professor. He has a strong grasp of what he is teaching and is able to effectively explain it to his students.
He's a great Professor. Well, organized. Give plenty of examples and works at a steady pace. He gives away points with in class work which are perfect practice to test the class subjects.

Extremely good professor. One of the best I have had. He goes over everything in lecture, then through class activities, then through homework,then through tests giving you plenty of opportunities to learn the material and learn it well, yet always throwing in a few things to make it interesting. You also always know what is going to be on tests.
completely useless and just tries to make a students life more difficult without too much reason.

It's an easy class if you actually attend.  Prabhu himself is rumored to give you better grades if you visit him during office hours frequently.  His door is often shut but he is there, he may act busy but it's just a show.  He'd really much rather teach than do research- he'll even joke in class about how he avoids the dept head's phone calls.
He is good teacher.  Very organized, and present class in an easy to understand format.  He uses a lot of examples and that helped me a lot.
Amazing.
One of the greatest instructors at ISU.  Makes the rest look bad.
Excellent instructor - the best I have had at the university.

Amazing professor and even better person. Really down to earth guy who you can clearly see has a passion for biology/genetics. He is very enthusiastic with how he teaches his class. All exams were take home and the homework was fairly easy. Very nice guy.
He is AMAZING. His lectures are entertaining, I learned so much, and he is just a good person in general. He might be a top 3 prof I have had.

Dr. Gupta is the most amazing professor I have ever had. He is great at explaining things thoroughly and preparing you for the topic at hand. He is also clearly passionate about his subject. Lots of homework is assigned (4 assignments a week) but they are short and simple. Exams are online and can be a bit difficult, but his class is worth taking!
I took 428 which is cell biology he is awesome he makes the concepts very easy/fun to learn and his passion and intelligence show while teaching.

Dr. Gupta is a very good professor who is passionate about the subjects he lectures on. His exams are pretty difficult, so you have to study a lot to do well. There is homework due before and after class, and about two hours of readings per day that is required to do well on homework. The class was really interesting, and I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bless this man he is AMAZING! Mo is such a good lecturer and he makes hard topics easy to understand! He outlines exams so you know exactly what to expect. He is probably the best professor i have had.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good professor, pretty much tells you exactly what you need to know. Very nice, and funny guy. Tests are pretty easy as long as you pay attention and study a little bit, definitely go to class to get the most of the lectures as well as easy participation points.

Professor Gupta is amazing! He really cares about what he is teaching and how the students are retaining the information. He gives a lot of homework, but it is super easy and a good way to prepare for his tests!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Gupta is very apparently intelligent and is passionate about the subject. His tests could be difficult because he wants to see that his students really understand the material. However, he is very approachable and meeting with him during his office hours to review for the tests makes a huge difference.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: a great teacher! Had her for chenchem2 and it is not easy simply because of the subject matter but she does a pretty good job teaching it. go to office hours and get to know her its very helpful. for gettinng a good grade in GC2 you just have to put in the work, she offered a small notecard during our midterms.

Dr Gupta came to teach our class in the second of half of the semester at UNI after Dr Harwood. She taught with great ease indicating that she has a great experience teaching chemistry and a vast subject matter knowledge. For many of complex concepts, Gupta had been very patient in explaining them to us and showing many examples of problem solving.

She is very smart, but very hard to follow. Overexplains everything manytime forgetting to mention details regarding equations. spent most of the time reading the book as not to be confused by her lectures. Gets many of her own examples wrong and very often rants on tangents that are not helpful. Leaves most of the class lost.
Very picky and sometimes hard but in the end, it helps you as a student.
Great teacher wants everyone to learn and succeed. She is not a point distributor but a keen teacher.

Really enjoyable. Very helpful and knows the material she is teaching. Also has a great personality. She also gave us extra points for the end of lab questions, which really weighted our grades positively, whereas some TA's take off points for missed questions but don't add any. Liked her a lot.

Tanya is very thorough, I was in her lab and recitation. She comes well prepared, is very helpful. Our labs were conducted in what is called SWH style. Whatever it is, I  learned a lot than my seniors who did non-SWH labs. my understanding and interest is renewed and I am now majoring in chem. Thanks to Tanya and Greenbowe's lectures.

I took CHEM 1670 with Thomas Greenbowe during Fall 2025. The class went over the basics of chemistry and was overall a pretty average class. Greenbowe was very willing to help and engage with students. Going over all the necessary concepts for the class. He is definitely a kind and respectful individual.
He was one of the funniest professors I have ever had. However, he didn't explain the material very well, and his pacing was poor.

As a person who has taken honors chem in high school, and has little to no interest in chemistry this was probably the most difficult class to take. Be prepared to learn a bit on your own. The professor goes through the lectures fast and glosses over important stuff. Keep a tab with the slide notes open so you can keep up. Nice professor,hard class

Made the tests very easy as long as you made sure to look at what would be on them. Lots of chances for extra credit and the homework can be done easily at the help center. Ended up with over 100% in the class.
invested in student success. great musician and chemistry teacher

Greenbowe has to be one of the best professors I have ever taken a class with. All of my friends who took organic chemistry with another professor constantly complained how hard the course was or how difficult their professor made the class, but I never felt that way with Greenbowe. He really makes sure you understand the fundamentals

He is an amazing and entertaining person! Such a sweet guy, but his teaching skills are not the best they could be. Lectures are really important to attend. He is confusing at some points, but also the material is super confusing as well.

You may not have enough individual attention since this is a big class. However, the lectures are very clear, and if you need any help - they are always there. He gives so much extra credits, my final course percentage went over 100%, so yeah!  Great professor!
I'm very glad I had Greenbowe for my first semester, he really does care and it blows that this was his last semester.

Amazing lecturer but, he will make you work like crazies for your score, numerous quizzes and homeworks a,d tests. If you take his class you will understand everything about chemistry but will need to detach from your social life
decent

One of the best teachers I have had at Iowa State. He explains the topics very well and tells jokes to make the class interesting. It isn't too hard if you pay attention and complete the homework assignments.
good teacher but moves really fast
Greenbowe was a great teacher, class was normally pretty interesting and to the point.  He is a funny guy and knows his stuff, would highly recommend him as a professor.

I can say with confidence that Greenbowe was by far the best professor I've ever had at Iowa State. He keeps his lectures entertaining yet still relevant to everything that we need to know. He makes topics easy to remember by relating them to real life situations, & puts all of his lectures on BlackBoard which is great for reviewing before exams.
He was an excellent teacher in 1993.

Greenbowe was hilarious and he usually kept me interested.  His class was tough for me because my high school did not prepare me well at all for college level chemistry.  My friends who took AP Chem in high school were fine.  I had to work my butt off to get an A.  I had a tutor and went to every SI session.  Just make sure you study and work hard.

Great Professor.  Relatively entertaining lectures that taught the material well. As long as you paid attention in class (there are easy clicker pts) and did the online homework you could get a decent grade. There are also plenty of resources to study from such as SI and the book problems listed.  I  did neither, which is probably why I got a B.

Greenbowe is hilarious. He was always cracking jokes but he also did a good job of teaching. I loved going to chemistry because of him. I highly recommend him! The class isn't hard if you pay attention during the lectures.

He makes funny jokes but is hard to follow and goes out of order when teaching topics in class. Haven't had chem for 3 years so it was hard to keep up, if you take AP Chem you will be fine otherwise you're going to have to study!! Oh and NEVER used my textbook I wouldn't buy one!
Really funny, class is easy if you have background chem, but as my last chem was as sophomore in high school I died a little...but still loved the professor!

He is humourous at times, has helpful, funny hints to remember topics. Occasionally isnt there to teach, so the head TA teaches. He is god awful; might as well not go. The tests are fairly easy if you know how to study.
Greenbowe was very humorous, and always prepared for lecture. It isn't the most interesting of subjects.. but he does a pretty good job. Tests aren't that easy, but they aren't terrible

Greenbowe is fully prepared for lecture. He tries to teach the concepts to a level that will be understood by the students. He likes to liven the lecture up with lots of jokes and also interacts with us to make sure we are understanding the concepts. Take CHEM177 with Dr. Greenbowe

Greenbowe is really passionate about chemistry and he makes lecture flow smoothly most of the time. He is very understandable and makes a lot of dorky jokes, puns, and comments! He interacts with students more than other professors in class.
hes and awsome teacher. he really cares about the class and have a great sense of humor. hes probably my favorite professor. class is real hard and need to study for exams
it is a good pro, that is my opinion. But actually, I think that masteringchem helps me a lot. Not the pro.
Very intelligent, you can tell he has been doing this for a long time. Can rush through lecture at time but there is a lot of material to cover. Overall a quality professor.
He rushes through every lecture and makes confusing comments. He seems unfocused because he's always trying to be funny.
when ever I go to his class, that will be it for my day. I love attending his class.
He seems very nice and considerate in lecture, but when you meet with him, he makes you feel stupid and isn't genuinely  interested in helping you achieve.
this guy is awesome. his lectures were never a dull moment, and he was very clear about the point he wanted to convey to class. i would recommend him in a heartbeat.
He is a wonderful professor. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. I was in a huge lecture and never found myself bored. Would recommend him in a heartbeat.
he's really into teaching and is understanding and will help you with anything you need help with
He is a great teacher! Always keeps it fun, and has a great way of teaching!

GREAT....easiest way to put it.  He makes the subject interesting and tests are not too easy and not to hard.  The SI secessions are very helpful and anytime that I wasn't quite getting something after class I would go down and talk to him and he would be able to explain it.  If you have a chance to take class with this guy do it!!!
My friend Aaron Schroder is absolutely in LOVE with him!
He is Hilarious. Show up for class, pay attention, and do homework and you will be fine. Also, reading the book helps alot too if you don't understand.
he keeps things interesting and he's pretty funny

I enjoyed having Dr. Greenbowe as my professor. He is very enthusiastic about chemistry and genuinely wants his students to do well. He uses  humor to help explain chemistry, making the class much more enjoyable. Overall a pretty good professor

A little to enthusiastic about a subject that is really dull.  Makes too many Star Trek references.  Always chooses bad songs to play in the beginning of class.  Needs to open his eyes and stop pecking the board. If you are smart, the class is easy.  If not, you will fail. Be prepared to work.

greenbowe is very funny in a woody allen kinda way.  the only reason i didnt scoop my own eyeballs out with a spoon is because he is funny.  i didnt learn much from him, but that might be my fault because chemistry is not my strong suit.

Greenbow is a fun and helpful teacher. He's a great transition from Highschool to College level for he not only knows the material he keeps class interesting and interactive even though it is a large lecture. If you keep up with the homework and take notes, you are sure to do well in the class.
Greenbowe actually made chemistry fun for the first time in my experience
The class is easy if you remember high school chemistry. I probably wouldn't have gone to class if I didn't have him-he made class a lot of fun and everything was very clear

He is hilarious! I do not like Chemistry in the slightest, but he makes it a little more fun, and a bit understandable. Tells lame jokes that somewhat relate to Chemistry, but they're pretty funny :-) I would definately recommend him over the other teachers from what I've heard.
Biggest **** i have ever met
Greenbowe is hilarious. He makes morning lectures really fun and hey - even I can stay awake. His review sessions are awesome. This class takes hard work, but Greenbowe's the man.

I honestly used to HATE chemistry with a passion. Then I took 177 with Greenbowe and I'm considering major/minoring in chemistry! He's a fantastic teacher, relates very well with students, he makes you look forward to going to class.
Awewsome
Sweat teacher. Went to the study sections and asked what was going to be on the test and Aced the test.
Always keeps class interesting, and you can tell he loves his job and wants to make sure the students learn.

Very fun professor. Had him for 163 and waited until the summer to take 231 so I could have him.  He understands not everyone is a chemist. Shows passion for what he does. A little bit quarky. His graduate student for 231, Jake, is awesome too.
he rocked my socks

Greenbowe was an amazing lecturer. He was very entertaining and kept the class interesting. He gave helpful review sessions and was good at teaching what you need to know. Thought the class was very easy too.
greenbowe didnt seem to be that helpful, he is an overall good professor. I didnt have a very good chemistry background and i kind of struggled through the class

Greenbowe is a good instructor. he tries to keep you interested, and does his best to make sure you understand the info. sometimes he goes too fast but recitation usually helped. tests aren't comparable in difficulty, so study hard for all of them or you might be unpleasantly surprised.
Very good teacher, keeps you listening

Dr. Greenbowe is pretty much amazing - between blowing stuff up and the rock and roll analogies that he uses in class, he keeps lecture fun and interested. He keeps the students involved and explains things very well - he even holds review sessions before tests. Uber cool professor - take chem with him if you can!

He was the best chemistry teacher I've ever had.  It's always been my worst subject and I've basically hated it in the other chem classes I've taken, but he made it so much more understandable.  He's a great teacher.  In my opinion, you want him for chemistry no matter what if you can get him.
his lectures are entertaining but u must work hard to earn good grade.
No Comments

his lectures are very effective, even though i have a hard time with chemistry, i like how he teaches...i learned a lot.  hes also funny, he keeps things interesting.  he doesnt ramble on like other professors...he is very cool guy
one of the hardest classes I've ever taken
No Comments

I have experienced several bad experiences with Dr. G.  He was not understanding or helpful when my dad died. My roommate was raped while taking Chem 177 and he told her that he needed proof b/c it was one of those stories that can just girls make up.  What a ass.
One of the best Chem. teachers I have ever had.  Great sense of humor!
Does a great job at explaining the concepts.
I hate chemistry, but he is a good prof, funny too
He is the best teacher that I have had at Iowa State.
Professor Greenbowe's lectures were very entertaining and effective.  He also made the effort to visit our lab, helping me work through a concept.  He's values learning by doing.

I love his analogies, but hate the godzilla.  He is a very clear, precise, easy to hear professor and I was lucky enough to have a TA who could explain things that I didn't fully understand.  if you go to lecture and actually pay attention you should have no problems learning the material.
His lectures are very entertaining.  He is an excellent professor and knows a lot about chemistry.
The gradin curve was fun. 15% curve I can't argue with that
Could never get help.  This man pointed me to a TA who in turn pointed me to the chem help room.  Both men did the my time is too important to help you act.  Really, really disappointing.

Breaks chemistry down into fun analogies. This was my most entertaining class--- the demos are great. You can definitely tell that Greenbowe loves his job! The material is difficult, but I'm glad I had this prof to lead me through it.

He is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. He always is willing to help and doesn't make you feel like an idiot. He uses Led Zeppelin, Star Wars, and Harry potter to teach chemistry. When combined with vodka and liquid nitrogen, GREAT class
Makes lecture entertaining sometimes.  Class is not very difficult.
I hate chemistry, but still enjoyed going to class cuz professor greenbowe is such a cool guy. Go to his study sessions before the exams! they're very helpful!
Very knowledgable about chemistry, but moves through first-time demos and problems very quickly.
No Comments
No Comments
Makes chem fun, teaches well
Great guy and has a good appreciationg for Rock n Roll
Won me over by playing classic rock before class!
Examples and explanations are always clear- he really strives to make class interesting, and truly cares about students performance and comprehension
cool
No Comments
Very easy to follow, great sense of humor
love the incorporation of rock n' roll
great guy, very funny, does good demos
good teacher

Very energetic and made the lectures fun; there were several cool chemistry demos! Extra credit questions were given each class. There were a lot of homeworks, but they were all questions similar to the exams, so it is great practice. Overall, not as difficult as I thought it would be!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really connected with this teacher without even speaking with him. He just seemed like a very nice and chill professor, and his lectures were important to go to because participation was 5% of the grade. The material was somewhat difficult but it is what it is. He gave us a ton of surprise extra credit which was amazing, but don't expect it.

This professor uses tophat for attendance, yet his lectures are just him reading off the slides, so I'm not sure why he thinks that any student is getting more out of attending. He answers questions vaguely, as it is very clear that he doesn't have the answer half the time. He does experiments, but doesn't spend enough time going over problems.

Dr. Gundlach-Graham is a good lecturer who tries his best to keep his students engaged in the material. He performs lots of experiments during class, and his lectures are easy to follow. Make sure to go to class as he does Top Hat questions for points. His tests are very fair.

Overall an average professor. Make sure to attend lectures since TopHat points are 5% of your grade. Each exam has an in-class and canvas portion. The in-class exams are decently easy, but the canvas portions were very poorly worded and even if you knew the material, you were bound to make mistakes based off of the bad phrasing.

Alex is probably one of the best professors I've had at Iowa State, especially in the chemistry department. He genuinely cares for the class and makes an effort to teach. Pay attention to lectures and practice the OWLs before exams; they should help you. He gave my class bonus exams that couldn't harm our grades but help raise our grades.
Nothing anymore but boring class, too much reading materials. Graded by a few things and learn everything by yourself. Do not choose this class.
General speaking, a boring class. Only a few questions(2 of 10)are graded in homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a lot of content in the class. He talked very superficially in class and did not elaborate on the principles. After finishing the class and watching the ppt, you would find that you didn't seem to be in class. If you want to learn well, maybe the video on youtube is what you need. Every Friday, there is a quiz on literature.

This class is not as difficult if you are able to show up and apply yourself. Alex is very accessible and gives great feedback when you ask. I highly recommend watching lecture videos and attending the extra help session he host because he provides you with everything you need to be prepared for test. The class has some difficult content but doable
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Me no like
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lisa Gundersen is not rude or unfair, but genuinely does not understand how to teach. Her analogies often make no sense, and she only ends up confusing you. If you took AP Micro/Macro in high school before taking this class, only show up to the first couple lectures. Her lectures genuinely made me forget content I was proficient in.

For an online 101 class, it was incredibly difficult. Homeworks didn't match up to all of the reading you had to do, so getting a decent grade was near impossible.  Professor also wasn't the best at getting back to e-mails in a timely manner.  Would suggest taking this online while on campus so you can at least ask for help directly.

TAKE ECON 102 ONLINE WITH LISA. This class could not be easier: test questions are directly from the "practice" problems for each chapter on Aplia.  You can work ahead, which is super nice for online classes. Hands down, super easy A, and I feel like I truly learned the concepts.

What an easy A. Usually, easy As don't teach you anything, but the platform Lisa uses is extremely helpful. Three assignments for each chapter: reading, graded problems and practice problems. PRACTICE PROBLEMS ARE THE ONLY TEST PROBLEMS. I cannot explain enough how insightful the questions are and how much I have learned just from memorizing ?s

I took this class online thinking it would be easy. The online homework doesn't match up well with the reading so it is hard to get full credit. It took me after my first test to realize the optional practice questions are what she uses for the test so try to memorize them. There are practically no resources besides the econ help lab.

I took Econ 102 online. The homework was quite difficult.. I would recommend a tutor. The chapter "lectures" were just PowerPoints and not very useful. For each exam, she provided about 300 practice questions. MEMORIZE THEM ALL. If you study those questions, you will do fine on the tests. Do ALL homework.

I took her class online, and it was an easy A. All of the test questions come from the review questions online. There are a lot of review questions, so be sure to start studying early. If you do the aplia assignments and memorize the review questions, it is an easy A.

She makes the class extremely easy (although it is my mandatory class lol). Really Clear and her slides are very helpful. She uploads every slide online but if you do not go to the lecture, you will not get the graphs of the slides. But dont worry, you can find all the information from the textbook including the graphs. Easy test with practice!

TAKE THE ONLINE VERSION OF THIS CLASS!  Do the practice problems.  They are word-for-word on the exams.  There is almost no way to take this class and not learn something.  Highly recommend for "easy A".
Easiest class at Iowa State University. Take the online version and review the practice questions before you take the test and your guaranteed to get an A. Highly recommended.
Easy course online, tests extremely easy. The test questions are exactly the same questions on the practice sets. Never really interact with professor. Little work involved

I highly recommend the online class--I made the mistake of taking econ 101 in lecture, and got a B just because I couldn't stand learning about y=mx +b week after week, so i quit going to class. The online class forces you to learn, and Gundersen is good about returning emails, etc. I recommend Econ 102 online as an easy A! the exams are EASY :]

Econ 321 is the easiest 300-level class ever, and also a scarce U.S. diversity credit. She teaches it in a simple manner and without much economic rigor, and she's nice and helpful (*if* you need it). I'd have no qualms recommending this class to anybody since it is so easy, unless you really dislike classroom debates and giving presentations.

I took the online version of this class and the material is what it is, but she never answered e-mails and took two weeks to get test scores up.  Tries to intimidate students at orientation with her "its harder than if you went to lecture" speech, but either way its just macroecon.  Recommend the online version.

The exams are impossible to take. Questions are worded so horribly it leaves you no hope in figuring out the right answer. She tells you how hard the class is, and trust me its not because the material is that hard to understand, but the professor would rather over complicate exams and show off bad grades in the class to pass it off as difficult
She is inconsiderate of her students.

I had her for the online version and she was very helpful when I visited her office hours.  The class was easy even though I didn't get an A.  I slacked off because it was easy.  I recommend taking economics online because you'll fall asleep if you take the lectures.

This is an easy class - skim the readings, go to class and you'll get a good grade. The material is way to easy to be a 300 level course. If you like debates/arguing sides, this class is definitely for you. Gundersen is quick to make her own points on the issues which can be annyoning but otherwise the class is easy and fairly interesting
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

This class is hard as someone who focuses more on human micro than plant micro. There are 3 exams and an end-of-the-semester paper to write. The class is very memorization heavy so I recommend studying in advance as the tests are long. I'd say it's hard if you don't study or catch up in lectures fast. No test but she does give papers to read.

Dr. Beattie let us know about deadlines at least a week in advance, her lectures were really interesting and showed she was passionate about what she had to teach. I thought they covered the material well. One review or two over the lecture slides was sufficient for the tests. The grader was super generous as well - both for in class and lab.

This is a tough class and Dr Beattie has high standards. But she works extremely hard to make sure the students can meet those standards. She was repeatedly flexible about deadlines and assignments and was just super nice and approachable. 
Lectures are cool if you like plants and bacteria, but don't take as a filler class. Not an easy A.
