Very interactive, visual class. Dr Beattie is a caring teacher who is excellent at presenting complex material and encouraging class participation. This is the best discussion-based class I've ever had. Assignments were challenging and somewhat time consuming, grading was strict but always mixed with encouragement and positive feedback.
What she teaches and what she tests on are completely different. Good luck asking any questions because shes never clear or gets easily confused by what you ask.

There arent any study guides provided or practice tests. The information provided in lecture tend to be structured differently than what appears on tests. The assignments are crazy difficult. I had to apply what I learned in my genetics class versus simply using the info from micro. There is no good way to study for her class
Don't even consider taking him for MIS 310. Only he'd know what he talks about in class lol.

Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had at Iowa State. He is super unhelpful when it comes to helping students and comes off borderline disrespectful in emails. He is also very hard to understand in class and goes off topic during lectures frequently.

Very hard to understand and goes off topic frequently. Never highlights deadlines or assignments in class, leading to confusion. Exams look different than what is being taught in class. Having a notecard during exams will make or break your grade.
This guy should go back to GM

Often went very off-topic and gave extremely vague in class assignments. Note sheet helps alot on exams, otherwise you would be cooked. Be careful with the final he set a 4 PM due time unaware testing centers are open until 10 during finals, which can prevent you from taking the test if you go later and if he doesn't extend your time you get a 0.

I wish I could select different tags for this rating. If you end up in this guy's lecture, just drop it and take it another semester. This class is mandatory for all business majors at Iowa State, and this class should not be the way it is with this professor. He is the least understanding professor I have ever had to have a class with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures did not provide much value. The only saving grace was having a note sheet for tests otherwise you would be cooked. He liked talking about professional experience and it is interesting, but it has nothing to do with the test or homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a marketing major this class was pointless to me. I gained nothing from the class as a whole. There are two tests, midterm and final, not cumulative but very hard to study for. He hardly gives you any instruction on what to study for exams. There is also group project that is worth a big part of your grade, again hardly gave any instruction on.

He did not know how to run Canvas and was not organized well. When going over the exams, he claims he could not give out topics that would be on the exams, so it was very difficult to study. The class average for the final was 70%. He never specified exactly what he wanted for assignments and projects. Nice guy, just not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was not structured the best, but he is open to new things. Grading was not very specific, and tests and quizzes were easy, but tests were difficult to study for.

It was his first year teaching and it is apparent. His lectures got very off track and made learning difficult. Exams were faily easy, but he put out a lot of conflicting information regarding assignments and group projects. Nice guy, but class structure was confusing and could have used proper planning.

His delivery is disorganized and often drifts off topic, making it difficult to follow the main points. He includes unnecessary jokes that distract rather than add value, and his tone tends to be monotonous, which makes it hard to identify what is new or important. Overall, the lectures lacks clarity, focus, and structure.

I took HCI584 online class. Professor Harding genuinely cares about students' success. I learned the Flask framework in Python in the class. I could make an appointment every week to discuss my project for about an hour. It's so relieving that someone tries to explain back-end coding. I truly am glad I took this class.

Professor Harding is a great professor, but his TA was awful at giving feedback on assignments and made a few grading mistakes which gave some other students anxiety and raise pitchforks. He gives a lot of extra credit and practically gives you answers if you ask questions in the class Slack channel. Funny guy, made learning Python easy.

Professor Harding has three, one hour lectures a week and they are all over the place. He is very scatter brained and it is impossible to keep up unless you pause the lectures and come back. This class took an immense amount of time. This class is way too hard for non-coders. He should have focused on and overview for HCI students. DO NOT TAKE.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Three hours of lectures every week. Professor is all over the place with his lectures. And he has a smart ass response for people with questions. How dare you ask a question during his incredibly confusing lecture.

I am so mad at myself for not dropping this class on time.

FIND ANOTHER CLASS FOR THE REQUIREMENT

Would not recommend. Zero clarity on his lectures and assignments. Three hours of lectures each week, with the subject all over the place. He is smart, but he is all over the place and happy to bring you down a peg if you ask a question. FIND ANOTHER CLASS FOR THE REQUIREMENT

No textbook, but it's important to read and understand the pdfs given. Quizzes require a good working knowledge of the material before you take them (timed). If you take the time to read, you'll easily pass. Homework takes time, usually based off of 60 min videos have to watch whole thing. Midterm/Final almost exactly the quizzes/homework questions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm still trying to understand why this is a core requirement for HCI. What this teacher doesn't understand is that we are non-programmers. Yes this is a graduate class but you are not teaching computer science majors! Stick with the fundamentals of Python and allow us to absorb the material instead of expecting the world out of us.  DO NOT TAKE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Harding is great. His lectures are a bit convoluted but he gets his point across. He wants you to succeed and gives you all the necessary information to do so. He hands out his lectures on paper prior to class and you are able to use notes/the book when taking exams. He is very helpful if you need assistance outside of class as well.
horrific

This teacher is the worst! He don't explain nothing to make this subject make sense AT ALL. There is no way u should take this prof if u can help it!!!! Stay away from this one and take a different class that u will have a chance of understanding.

Need to show up to all labs to pass the class. Weekly assignments but they have a clear outline and step-by-steps to complete. Large amount of points available for extra credit, highly recommend doing. Attendance is taken most days. I got just around a 60% on midterm and finals and still got an A in the class, so no worries.

I barely showed up to class, unless it was a case study day. You have many case study days within the course, I would recommend showing up to those, as those are a large part of your grade. A few larger papers within. Overall, you really don't need to show up and take notes on lecture days and you'd still be fine. No Midterm or Final.

Very chill professor and pretty easy course. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but I still went to most of the lectures because usually they are interesting. In terms of work: you'd write a total of 4-5 400-word essays (with good guidelines provided) and do 19 easy online quizzes + extra credit opportunities. Grading is not tough.
Bro is the chillest guy on earth. Would 10000000% take again. Willing and able to help everyone, even if they didn't show up for months. Clear, simple, and easy. Thank you Dr G

Dr. G is a very kind person. he is very easy to communicate with in person and is very approachable. The TAs are very helpful and give great feedback. Class is not mandatory just keep up with quizzes and assignments and show up for case study days. not a ton of reading just a couple paragraphs once every couple weeks.
Amazing professor!
Very clear teacher. Follow his directions and try to attend class as much as possible. Will accommodate a lot of circumstances if you communicate early.

Dr. Gudmunson is honestly one of the sweetest professors I've had. He's very caring and it's clear that he wants his students to succeed and will reach out and follow up with you. He also gives out plenty of opportunities to raise your grade and is very flexible on meeting. I would definitely recommend Dr. G and I would take a class with him again!

Dr. G is very passionate about what he is teaching. While sometimes it got frustrating we would only get thru a couple slides in our allotted 50 mins, he was always using personal experience and examples to connect the material to real life. He was more than willing to work with his students and made labs easy to follow along with.
Dr. G was a great professor and I enjoyed his class a lot. There were a couple of projects but they were not too hard. He works hard to set you up to succeed in his class.

This professor is very informative through his lectures. They are very slide heavy and have a lot of information. He makes sure that we understand the material before moving forward and if we did struggle, he would go back and re-teach. Good amount of extra credit and it shows that the professor wants you to succeed in his class.

Amazing professor, easy work, and an interesting course. There is only one group project that meets once a week for most of the semester. You can definitely skip non-group project days. Quizzes are on quizlets everywhere. The syllabus says what you will be doing each class (so check to see if you can skip or not).

Dr. G is awesome. He is a very sweet and kind professor. There are so many extra credit opportunities in this class and they are very easy. One time I had to literally pretend I was talking to a baby with a doll and got extra credit for it. There is a lot of work for this class but he gives out many opportunities to complete.
He was always willing to work and help his students!

Dr. G had never taught HDFS102 before when I took this class with him. He was a kind professor; however, it felt like he was as confused as we were. It was sometimes hard to know what the grading expectations were. Regardless, it was evident that he cared about us and was always willing to help.

Dr. G is a good professor. I found myself not going to class because it was too early not because of him. its extremely easy to get an A. You get 20 extra credit points for coming to class the day you signed up to be your small group's leader, which all you had to do is write down the group attendance.

As one of the few non-financial major people that took this class, it is doable. He rarely answers emails, which isn't fun. Tests are open note and there is a huge extra credit project, both saved me. HW is super easy but daily. If you at least try, you will be fine. Anyone can pass with the massive extra credit points. He is really nice and cares.

Dr. Gudmunson is easily one of the most kindhearted professors I've had. He genuinely cares about his students, and he puts in a lot of extra time and work to make this class as beneficial and stress-free as he can. I would highly recommend this class and Dr. G!

Dr. G is not a good professor. I have reached out multiple times via e-mail to ask questions and never got a response back. The class is not that hard as long as you go to class and listen to the little details because that is what the exams are over. To sum it up the class is really just him reading off slides.

This class was very frustrating, lectures were reused and slow. They were voiced over slides and you never build a relationship with the professor. We went 5 weeks without hearing from the professor and had 15+ assignments to be graded with 3 weeks left. The class itself is not difficult if you pay attention to details.

He is a nice guy but not knowledgeable about this class. He has one subject per class, so learning the material is always switched up. It was confusing most of the time. When Covid19 happened and class went online he pretty much neglected the class and would rush to post vague lecture videos. Also was absolutely terrible at responding to emails

Ok this is for Econ 378: Gudmunson is a really nice guy but super underconfident. He would ask our class if what he was doing was good enough, dude no one is going to answer that on the spot, just be confident in what you teach man! Hes not a super smart guy and makes many errors, but the class subject is great! Easyish class and U.S diversity!

He is such a kind and caring person. His class was interesting and he tries his very best to relate the material to each student. He gives opportunities to up your grade and he will meet with you at any time to help you!

His lectures are pretty dry. I think he has a PH.D in Family Studies and he teaches a retirement planning/employee benefits class. I think be understands a lot of the material but has a tough time explaining it to students. Its not a terribly tough class, but I think it could be taught better.

Dr. Gudmunson is honestly one of my favorite professors at ISU. He is so nice and caring and will give you opportunities to raise your grade. He is also willing to meet with students outside of class if they need help with labs or understanding the material.

He's a very soft spoken, nice guy that is lenient on late assignments. Lecture is 3 days a week and quite boring. Lab is once a week at 8am. SPSS is used which is really confusing software. No one had any clue what was going on or how to do the labs. The tests are all multiple choice/not extremely difficult if you read the book and know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You must attend lectures to do well because the quizzes are all based off of class lectures. The class is more so based off of the worksheets he gives you instead of actually learning the information.

Dr. G is a very caring and kind professor. His class is an easy as as long as you attend class and lab lectures. The assignments seem daunting, but if you attend class and read the assignment they're a breeze. The TA I had for this course wasn't the best, but Dr. G is awesome and very helpful!

Did not know the topic very well. Often couldn't answer questions that came up in class. His worksheets and formulas often had errors in them. Timing and communication about the weekly quizzes were very inconsistent. It took him the whole second half of the semester to grade our midterm project and midterm test. Easy A but a wast of time and money.

Dr. Gudmunson is a very nice professor. The labs and homework assignments take a while to do, but if you can read directions it tells you exactly what to do. They are a great way to boost your grade as the tests tend to be difficult. Just study the guide he gives you and it is pretty much an easy A.

He is a really nice guy, but class can be really boring. It's a required class for the HDFS major, so you have to take it even if you're not interested in research. He talks really quiet so it's hard to pay attention and be involved in class. The lab assignments are confusing with the program that is used, you have to go to a computer lab to do HW.

Mitch is a great prof. He has notes that you can download and follow along with and fill in during his lectures. He stops and takes time to answer questions as he goes through problems making them easier to understand. Calculus 2 is a difficult course but when he skips steps it is the simple algebra you should already know going into the class.
For Calc 1, I loved having him for my recitation. He explains things so easily, it makes calculus sound simple. He does a great job at helping people understand the problems.
Good explanation, very nice and respectful professor
He gets a 3.0
Good dude, good lecturer, cares about your success, and is passionate about the material. 5/5
Good professor, made calculus simple.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Math 1510 He skips explaining steps which makes it hard to follow the lectures. Frequent mistakes during the lectures were called out by students. Solution sheets posted were often followed by a corrected version of all of the mistakes students caught. He adds in all 0's at the end so expect a drop in your grade and Canvas grade isn't reliable.
I had Haeuser for my Calc 3 Recitation. He is a really nice guy who just wants to help students learn and he was very helpful during help hours.

Mitch is an okay professor; this class was incredibly hard. I read some of these ratings and can't help but wonder if they did it to themselves. The class attendance was poor which is why exams are low. Yes, his teaching style is odd and hard to follow but if you attend his office hours and he will sit down and make sure you understand the material

For Bus Calc (Math1510), I struggled to get through every lecture, as he is truly a terrible professor.  He doesn't know how to teach.  I went to different tutor sessions that weren't special but made so much sense.  I don't know what makes him such a poor teacher, but it is impressive.  The average score on the first exam was a 37%.

I had him for MATH 151 and he was horrible. The average of our first exam was a 38% and nothing like the practice exam. He acts like he's Socrates speaking to a bunch of children, even though he just graduated last year and is an awful teacher.
Mitch is an amazing professor, he is very knowledgeable in Calculus and is great at explaining. Great caring guy.

Professor Hebert gets a bad rep but he genuinely wants you to succeed in his class. He does make mistakes during lecture and it might be a bit hard to follow, but as long as you put in the effort to go to office hours you'll do fine in the course. Super generous with his exam grading as well.

I really like Dr. Hebert. Go to his class and pay attention, he does not post notes online. He teaches what you need to know. Homeworks are hard, but office hours are helpful with him and his TA. Exams are reasonable and graded fairly. He gets a bad rap, but he is a nice guy who wants you to succeed.
Bad handwriting, have to search to find the homework, not tech savvy, not very good at explaining, basically just explaining theory during class, and doesn't really explain equations.
Hebert is an extremely nice and approachable man. Lectures weren't always the best but he was almost always clear on his expectations and graded very generously. Helped calculate the head

Not a difficult class at all, but his lecture slides are full of mistakes and he just confuses himself even more when he tries to rederive his already incorrect equations. He cares about his students and is willing to answer questions, but go to his office to get questions answered. Unless you know hieroglyphs you won't be able to read hw solutions

Great and kind professor, but he usually got confused with the material he taught during lectures. Show up to class to get daily top hat points. Get a chegg account as homework is near impossible. Open note tests, so take good notes. He's VERY GENEROUS with partial credit on tests, so write something if stuck and he won't fail you on exams
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, but makes a challenging course even more difficult when he is continuously making mistakes and getting confused in the middle of lectures. First part of course isn't bad, but once more challenging topics are introduced, it purely becomes a "partial credit" class ( which thankfully is very gracious). Get chegg for hw, you'll need it
For 2730 attendance was only mandatory if you wanted to take the quizzes. Professor Hall is very flexible and understanding.

I took CLST 2730 with Alexander Hall during Fall 2025. He was a very engaging and interesting professor, you can tell he definitely is interested and cares about the topic. The class primarily went over the readings from outside of class and had a graded quiz to go along with it. I really enjoyed how he ran the class.

People are tripping. Great class. It was a lot to read but he makes it known immediately. Anyone complaining either A. is unable to commit to reading a couple stories a week or B. are mad they couldnt get a free elective. Also attendance WASNT mandatory, you don't HAVE to go to class? Exams were easy too, if you studied and read like you should.

Not an easy class and Dr. Hall is nice but not the best professor. All the graded material is from readings yet attendance is mandatory. I made public reviews on Gimkit for each exam called "ISU Mythology exam # (1,2, or 3)". (I can't find the third exam so I posted the link in exam 2)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: don't take this class for a free elective. there is LOTS of reading, and exams are hard because they cover SO MUCH content. averages are around 70%. lectures are boring, but you have to go because there are quizzes at the beginning. theres a lot of participation points though, which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor wasn't my favorite. He became upset at the class one day and complained about a review he got on here. He also told the class, "Its not free credit, its easy credit" for additional reading and visiting office hour assignments. I immediately dropped the class. Test everyday in class as well with homework during weekends.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take Greek and Roman, it is so much work. I do more work for this class than any of my engineering courses. The tests are also pretty hard because you have to memorize so much. Also there is a quiz at the start of every class and then after the quiz you have to just sit there and do nothing while listening to him discuss the quiz
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He teaches the class in the least usefull way possible. You do a reading before class, quiz on it for understanding at the beginning of class, and then he talks about the reading for the rest of class. Attendance is mandatory for the quizes but then there is no point in staying for the rest of the lecture cause you've already tested over it.

He stated there is a lot of extra credit but later mentioned it is part of the credit to pass the class, therefore required and not extra. He stated the first exam would be easier and based closely to the practice (42 question practice and a 70 question exam). The exam also had a book which was never mentioned in class at all nor posted about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely outstanding. Really entertaining lecturer and delivers information effectively. Grading scheme is very clear and as long as you follow the rubric and stay on top of homework then you'll have an easy time in class. Projects are fun but still relevant to learning much about ancient religion. Cannot recommend him highly enough.

This professor is amazing. He's hilarious but extremely knowledgeable about the subjects he teaches on. For this class you a book of the Metamorphoses (roughly 50 pages) at the beginning of each week. When I read The Secret History I never thought a professor could be charismatic enough to inspire cult activity. Dr. Hall makes it seem possible.

Dr. Hall is a wonderful lecturer and this class was a lot of fun as it's mostly a ton of fun group projects. If you're group sucks, it can make the class hard, but that's not Dr. Hall's fault. One thing I didn't like was that he was super particular about how we used sources which is a good skill but he was hard to please. Overall, wonderful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr Hall was so enthusiastic and genuinely showed that he enjoyed the topic he was teaching. That made every lecture fun and helped drive me to want to go to class.

Although I do not need to take any more classical studies classes, I am tempted to take another just for Dr. Hall!  Although there was A LOT of reading, I didn't mind it because the other work for the class was minimal. Dr. Hall is a very understanding man and teaches everything with an infectious passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall is an absolute icon. Every MWF I looked forward to this mans class because he was so funny. He has a passion for Greek and Roman Mythology like no other. Lectures aren't required but I'd recommend going either way because there is always something interesting this man will talk about. And trust me, he will go on unhinged rants.
He dresses spiffy and makes class enjoyable and fun and explains everything with heart. uses class questions to form class lectures.

Latin 101 is a fantastic class. I rarely write reviews on RateMyProfessor but I cannot recommend this class with Dr. Hall enough. He is so funny, and while his quizzes are frequent and tricky, you will know so much Latin by the end of the semester. He makes class entertaining, and he grades very generously. It's not an easy class, but it's so fun.

Professor Alexander Hall is very knowledgeable about what he teaches and really tries to get his students engaged, he is also willing to take time to answer your questions fully. Even though he gives out a lot of reading he tries to make it as interesting as possible by understanding the literature and making jokes along with the class.

Such a funny guy and made coming to lecture so fun. Lots of reading, all we read in this class is the Iliad, the Odyssey, and the Aeneid. Interesting, but he breaks it down really well in class so it's easy to understand. He is a great guy, highly recommend his classes!!

Dr. Hall is very knowledgeable about Latin history and would tell us random stories relating to the topics he covered. There are a lot of homework assignments, but most are fairly quick and easy. Participation is super important because he takes a grade from those and being prepared definitely helps. I loved him for this class and as a professor!

Both the class and professor are amazing! Dr. Hall is an astoundingly good teacher. If you get the smaller class and you're with him, the readings always get to have a crazy interesting conversation. Arguably the best professor I have ever had.

This is by far the coolest class at ISU! You recreate a sacrifice for the midterm and a cult initiation for the final! Dr. Hall is so passionate and knowledgeable about Greek and Roman Religions, it makes this class a blast! The only downside is that you work with a group all semester so good luck if you get a slacker.

Amazing class and professor but there is quite a bit of reading between the basic textbook along with the two companion books and weekly homework/quizzes. Amazing at answering questions during class time as well as during office hours/email. He genuinely cares about students and is really good with personal matters interfering. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall is a great professor and I loved having him for Latin. The activities in class are both fun and important for you to be present for. If you don't show up to get proper translations and to review, you won't get good grades. You can tell Dr. Hall enjoys the criteria, enjoys teaching, and cares about his students. Great class, great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall is a great guy and he really tries to make his class enjoyable and so his content is easily understood. He goes into great detail when going over translating and parsing, and going over homework in class makes it hard to fail. Great class and looking forward to LATIN 102 and his Religions of Ancient Greece and Rome course!
Professor Hall is an amazing guy and an even better teacher. He genuinely loves the course material and it shows in his lectures and commentary.

Dr. Hall is absolutely incredible! He is animated and engaging. If you do the reading (which is always fun to read), it's very easy to get involved in the discussion. You'll get out what you put in. I loved and looked forward to every single lecture. I will be taking every single one of his classes. Easily my favorite prof ever!

Dr. Hall is AWESOME. You do have something due every class, but its pretty formulaic and no surprises. Tests aren't super hard, but they do require a fair amount of studying and ACTUALLY reading the material. Its also a pretty discussion-heavy class, so you get out of it what you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor, lectures were exciting and very hands on. He is always willing to help out and loves telling stories about the ancient world! If you are looking for an Arts and Humanities course I would 10/10 recommend Dr. Hall's class.
Possibly the best professor at iowa state. I would take his classes again if I could.
He is a fantastic professor. Really cares about his students and tries to make learning fun. I love his group project centered class for Greek and Roman Religion.
Highly recommend his Greek and Roman Mythology class.

Simply fantastic. Makes learning fun and not in a corny way. I found normally quiet students engaged in class material. He still expects you to participate and work but, I found that most of the time I was excited to do so. By far my favorite professor.

Dr. Hall was one of my favorite professors from freshman year. He always made class interesting and came up with some really crazy activities that took a boring topic and made it more fun to learn about.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pol cares lots about his students. I'm confused by the negative reviews here, bc each time I reached out to him for help he was very prompt, caring, helpful, and genuinely wanted to see me do well. He is a tough grader, but he gives very specific rubrics of exactly what to do to get an A. Offers some extra credit, clearly loves his job. Nice guy!

Easy class to start & lots of extra credit. Had a 92, but failed our final group project (the class av. was a 65% and the highest grade was a 76%), which brought my grade down to a 79.85. I asked for an explanation on why we failed, but he gave none. unacceptable that the highest grade was a C. Do not take with pol. Biggest slap in the face!
Grading is harsh, which makes it difficult to get the grade you want especially since everything is team based. Not the most organized course.

He's a tough grader. Not a ton of work in the class. But we had a group project for part of our final, which tanked everyone's grades. He graded it 2 days after the semester was over, the average was a 65%, which brought my final grade from 99 to 85. 
Not a bad class overall, but definitely a punch in the face to get that grade after all the work.

Where do I begin? He weighs the final project, which is a group project in an online class which isn't always the easiest, very heavy. He grades the final project in the last day of the semester then gives out an overage of a 65% of it. I think majority of the class had their final grade drop a full letter grade with no explanation.

One of the hardest graders I've ever had. Doesn't give clear instructions and will take off points even though you have what he wanted. You can argue your grade, but odds are he'll lower it even more rather than help you. He gave extra credit which was a lifeline. Would not recommend taking MGMT with him.

Professor Pol is one of the hardest graders I have ever had at Iowa State University. He says to go into detail for the case studies but only allows you to write one page to answer 4-6 questions. Also, for the final project, good luck because he will deduct points even though you have it in your report. Lastly, he barely gives any instructions.

Pol's lectures aren't super interesting, but he's a good guy. Exams make up 24% of grade. Final project+presentation 28%, paper is 10.5 single spaced. Participation makes up a good chunk, so just answer a few questions for each case study, and you will be fine. Exams are super easy gives out a kahoot that is the exact same as the exam nearly wfw.

Lectures arent super interesting but he covers almost everything you need to know. Exams are almost exactly like the study guide if he gives one out. Show up for case days so you dont have to write a paper, and be ready for group work spread out throughout the semester. Very nice man, just a bit quiet.

He is not clear about some assignments and grading. Thankfully the syllabus was modified during the semester.   Discussions in class are helpful but he might get defensive sometimes which leads to stressful somewhat atmosphere.

MGMT 583 is one of the best class I've ever taken at Iowa State University. The class discussion was really helpful, brought me a lot of thoughts and learnings about innovation. It may have lots of assignments and exams, but it's worth make an investment.

Great teacher. Very into what he teaches and super helpful. Expect to read and participate. Participation is a lot of the class. Tests are all straight from book. Need to attend class for 20% of your grade.

Professor Pol honestly saved my semester. He is a really understanding guy and will try to help you in anyway that he can if you go in and talk to him. Overall he made the class very interesting, although at times it was hard to understand him due to his accent.
Very nice professor, and very helpful. There may be lot of assignments and test, but the subject is overall very interesting
Weekly tests, text book is your life line. no essay type questions. group work is important. Makes you work for that grade. also you learn a lot.

Overall good teacher--would definitely recommend. He makes the lectures and cases pretty interesting. Tests are really easy if you read the book. Class participation is a must! There are several smaller group assignments and one group paperpresentation, but they aren't too bad.

Pol is a good guy who teaches the class well. He's from Ecuador and his accent is still thick, but his English is great. Exams are straight from book and video cases aren't too bad. Participation is a must. Would definitely recommend this class.

Pol was a wonderful teacher. His English can be a little hard to understand since he is from South America but he does care about his students. He also makes very funny comments and has a dry sense of humor. One of my favorites in the College of Business.

Pol can be pretty funny. The class can be interesting as well. The tests are easy so long as you use your book to study. Questions will come straight from the book. The kicker is the final group project. The project is very difficult and complex. Coordinating with group members only adds to the difficulty, so work on it as soon as possible.
Difficult,  avoid his classes if possible

As long as you show up for class you'll do fine.Make sure you attend on participation days at least!  Exams are all based from slides/textbook.  Make sure you work on the final project throughout the semester rather than waiting until the end.

Class is hard to go to as he just reads the slides. Quizzes on case days.  Tests mainly over power points.  Test were long, but pretty easy.  Great class!  Group project, but it is easy and he grades pretty fairly as well

I found it really hard to go to class, and often skipped. His lectures really aren't that great...the extra stuff he talks about isn't on the exams; he takes his questions straight from the test bank from his book. The only reason to go is to take the quizzes, and he doesn't always announce when he's going to give them.
Great teacher, goes directly to the point, very entertaining, shows videos, has dry humour, very helpful, has real world experience
Best teacher I have ever had at ISU, serious but approachable, friendly, and knowledgeable.  HJelps you preparing for tests in class

The lectures are an absolute joke.  Unless there is a quiz that day, don't bother showing up, you will be asleep within the first 5 minutes.  Utilize the online quizzes offered through the book.  50% of test question are pulled from the same test bank that the quiz questions came from.

If it wasn't for the extra credit attendance points, I would never attend class. Class is oftentimes incredibly pointless and boring and will not help you do well on the exams. You might be better off just reading on your own.
I really liked this class. K-P tables were hard, but ask him for help and he'll give you feedback. Tough on class discussion--read cases, participate, and you'll do fine.
One of my favorite professors that I had.  He really likes class participation.  If you participate you should never get worse than a C+.
I took international business with him and it was a totally useless class. His lack of knowledge and real experience made it boring and unbearable.

One of the worst profs I have had at ISU, what does attendance and participation have to do with international mgmt topics? nothing, the material is so boring and easy that he has to grade on something other than course topics, he is very rude and doesnt really care about students, avoid this prof

I was aware that he was tough, but it has been a semester from hell.  I have had Pol for both 414 and 478 and I feel dumber for having taken either.  The classes were a let down, the professor was unclear and VERY unflexible.  He didn't seem to understand that there is ALWAYS a subjective part in every situation.  Avoid Pol whenever possible.
I was looking forward to this class, unfortunatly it was taught by Herrmann. He's rude, very unclear and impossible to find for office hours. Avoid his classes at all cost!

This class was challenging.  He has a pretty heavy accent and is a tough grader.  The class was pretty interesting.  He takes attendance so plan on being in class everyday.  The project was pretty easy though and it was worth a lot of points.

He is very unclear about the project.  If you ask him questions, he will just tell you to read the project guidelines on the syllabus (which are extremely vague). The project is too much for a semester class, but the exams aren't too bad though, that's about the only good thing about that class.

He is very unbending in the requirements for his project.  But his tests are easy and all you have to do is read the book.  The easiness of the tests is more than made up for in the difficult project.  Average diffculty class just don't butt heads with him.

The guys is cool! ...you just have to read the textbook and go to class. On the exams he uses the same questions from the class quizzez(+ more of course). But if you have attnded class it will be cool.
What a jerk!
No Comments
The project is alot of work and he grades tough, he is overall very nice and a good Professor.

Paula is a good lecturer and wants her students to learn the material. Some of her lectures overcomplicate some of the actual math components of physics 2, so I learned a majority of the work from doing practice quizzes/exams, come exam time.
She is the only reason I passed physics 2. Very fun to listen to and enjoys what she does
pretty chill, a good physics teacher

Good lecturer and will teach you the tricks that make certain questions a lot easier. I would recommend going to her lectures if you can because I learned a lot more in her lectures than going to a different professor. She does a lot of tophat questions on exam review days, so I would usually solve them before class to make sure I had time.

Took an online class with her, hated every second of it. I was lost within the first two weeks of class. Her lectures are very slow and boring, she's a very shallow professor and her classes just aren't fun. I would avoid her for pretty much any class she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I get accommodations for ADHD, and she was very understanding and made me feel heard. You can tell she's passionate about physics because of her energy during lectures. Class is kinda tough, but that's because it's physics, not because she's a bad professor.

She is a great professor and was always very helpful in answering any questions you may have. PHYS232X (The new 222) is a tough class though, I would really recommend making use of the textbook even if it is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Herrera Siklody! Her lectures were super easy to understand even though physics was never my strong suite. You have to do your HW and read the text to understand the test, but I actually found that once I did that I enjoyed the class a lot. She is always helpful, passionate about the class, and was one of my favorite profs!

She's a really nice physics professor. She really tries every lecture to make sure what she's saying is clear to the students, and she has a nice sense of humor. Very easy to understand and I'm glad I had her for physics.

You either like Paula or you don't. Her lectures were sometimes too fast or too difficult to understand. I find that the class itself is already difficult enough, and she makes it more difficult with the confusing lectures. She doesn't curve, so get ready to do a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Paula is awesome. Super fun and enthusiastic. She let us play with liquid nitrogen several times throughout the semester. She is also a great teacher. 222 sucks, but she made it bearable.

Paula is a good professor that likes to do in-class demos (which are helpful and fun to watch).  Class is tough in general, but she will answer your questions so you understand.  Uses clicker questions (not for attendance) to see if students understand topic, which is nice so that she can move on in explain the topic further.  Study with old exams!

I believe she is a good professor, but her avenue of teaching was difficult. She uses PowerPoint, which, in practicality, doesn't work well with anything math-like (you'll ignore her and write, or listen and forget it.) Good speaker, but I went to two lectures regularly; preferred the other who taught with a chalkboard.

The course is difficult, but professor Siklody guided us through difficult times. Her lecture slides are very crucial. Make sure that you study them thoroughly before taking the exam She is a wonderful teacher with a cute personality.
I found her an amazing teacher. Although it's hard, so far it is my favorite class!

Paula is not a very valuable professor. Her accent is hard at times to understand. And her office hours are nothing to get excited about. The main bonus to her class is that she does a lot of in class demos. However, her lectures consist of slides and no actual instruction on what it means. Her tests come off as impossible to prep for.
Has a think accent and does not teach anything. You can look the slides up online and do all the homework without attending class.

Way too hard headed.  Doesen't like to help outside of class, and says you should find your TA. So her office hours are pointless.  Also her accent is really hard to understand at times.  Great if you just like to hear someone talk, not so great if you want someone to explain things to you, which is what a good prof should do.  Horrible teacher.
good teacher

Paula has enthusiasm for what she does and it helped keep me interested.I had her in the summer so the class was more interactive which I liked.For teaching a hard class she does a good job, the reason most people don't like her is because they are struggling with the class. It takes a lot of work outside of lecture which is not her responsibility.

Paula was an ok lecturer but she's the best you'll get for 221. Whenever we'd do problems she'd skip the math assuming we all knew how to do it. The recitation and labs were extremely helpful.  The exams are almost impossible and have nothing to do with what you learn in lecture. Do all the hw and study your ass off for exams and you might get a B.
She is nice and very helpful. It just that her lectures go very fast in a 50 minutes time frame make it harder to understand. As long as you do your work, you'll be fine

She was extremely helpful and explained it to our level.  She was always willing to make specific worksheets for whatever we were having trouble with and would stay after class just to answer our questions.  Wonderful teacher!

Decent professor, very friendly and what not. Class is rough, material covered much faster than usual classes. Be sure to cram and get a good grade on the test, it will help all the slacking you do during the semester.

Paula is a okay teacher but goes to fast sometimes and doesn't explain somethings very well.  She isn't the head of the physics dept. but the tests were really hard and the homework was time consuming.  Go to SI and get a study group together and you'll pass this class if you do physics 4 days a week.

Lectures are technical, quick, and boring.  I ended up learning more by myself and from supplimental instruction than from lecture.  Tests are difficult, but there is plenty of time to complete them and check over your work.

this class is difficult. paula does a good job of explaining things during the 8am lecture. her slides are very clear. i didnt like how she tries to squeeze all of her slide in 50 minutes-it was hard to pay attention to that technical of material for the entire time. hard class, she is better than the other guy

Very good at explaining any off-the-wall subjects in class. She is 10 times better than the other Physics lecturer. I am signed up to go to the other lecture but I go to hers to actually get something out of lecture.

Paula gives good lectures, but watch out for the exames.  over all, she is not willing to help students on the homework outside of lecture(thats what TA's are for), and after the final grades were posted she left ames without telling anyone in advance
She really know's what she's saying.  She explains things clearly and quickly.  The work is challenging enough to keep me interested, but not too challlenging to lose me.
Great lecturer and easy to talk to if you actually take the time to go into class. She likes to make sure even the dumbest people can understand the concepts and materials.
Good lecturer. Hard class.

Shes a good lecturer, much better than the other lecturer.  The class is very hard.  Written homework is often more difficult than nescessary.  Tests tend to have awful averages, and aren't scaled much (if any).  You need every point you can get, so work hard.

Paula gives very good lectures.  On occasion she "misses the mark" on rigor of derivation (either way), but she tries hard to bring the class along all the time and it shows.  The class is not easy, so I cannot give her easy points, but if you get a chance to take it with her TWO THUMBS UP!

Paula does a good job explaining the material usually and she puts it in understandable terms.  She is WAY better than the other prof that teaches the class.  Even though she does a good job, the class is still hard.
I think she's a pretty good teacher--definitely a better lecturer than Atwood.

If you want to see derivations for every physics formula, u'll enjoy this one.  Not the best presentation, but she knows her stuff & is the better of the two 221 profs.  Tests will give u a run for the $, but the curve's pretty good.
She does a pretty good job of explaining things for physics. The difficulty is mostly because it's a 5-credit physics class; she can't be blamed for that.
I found Paula's lectures to be very unhelpful, but such may be the nature of the course regardless of professor.
No Comments
She's not a bad teacher... probably better than most teachers I've had. She explains things very clearly and in a way that's easy to understand.
No Comments
No Comments
Lectures consist of her working a problem and expecting us to take for granted her solutions.  Unfortunately, she's the better of the two Phys 221 lecturers.
No Comments
lecture not like; homework, quizes, labs, tests, midterm, or final-->sucks
No Comments

Heidi is a professor who is very passionate and knowledgeable about what she is teaching. With that being said, she is not an easier grader. The exams and projects are difficult, and she doesn't release your grade until after the final exam. You are most likely not going to get an A in her course, but you will learn a lot.
You can tell Heidi cares a lot about what she teaches and genuinely wants you to learn. Her tests are difficult but she is willing to help if you ask.

Liked her as a person, be prepared for incredulity long and hard exams. Only midterm and final plus quizzes makes up your grade basically. Super hard tests which is the reason I didn't like the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heidi is really one of the best. Don't expect her to coddle you - she WILL get you used to the cold hard truth. But giving honest feedback doesn't mean she's heartless; Heidi cares more than you realize and is always willing to go the extra mile to help her students succeed. I'll really miss her when I graduate.
Heidi speaks nothing but the cold hard truth. She's tough, but seriously cares about your professional and personal growth.
Ive had Heidi for 2 LA classes (not an LA student) and she has always given AMAZING lectures that keeps everyone engaged and interested. She is a very kind and caring professor!

Heidi is one of the best. She can be a bit abrasive but in my opinion that is very necessary in this field. Tough love WORKS in design. She truly wants her students to succeed and every time I walk out of her class I feel like I am a better designer. Heidi really knows her stuff - if you have her for a class, use that knowledge to your advantage!

One of the most easy to work with professors I have ever met, and also very understanding and willing to help you get back up if you fall behind in class. Professional and funny. Will definitely take again
She tells you how it is and her critiques can be crushing to the faint of heart. She grades fairly and makes you read because reading is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Grow some tough skin and you'll love her

Heidi was by far my favorite professor. She tells you how it is while telling you what you need to do to improve your design without inadvertently making it hers (which a lot of professors do). I graduated back in '08, and all of my positiveness that came out of ISU (which wasn't a whole lot) came from her lectures and studios.

It is funny that all of the comments on here are coming from students early in their design degree.  Heidi challenges you to become a better designer, person, and helps you wake up to the profession.  Her being tough on you is in your best interest.  If I were you I would listen to what she has to say.  Btw...it only gets harder after school. -alum
she couldn't be more negative, judgemental, and abrasive!! Don't let her insecurities distract you from being creative.

Heidi is an amazing teacher.  She knows how to push you to try to achieve more, and is very knowledgeable. Though she is not afraid to critique your work, she does it tastefully, and provides good examples of possible solutions to any problems she may point out.
Very good teacher, pry the best in the department. She really challenges you.

Heidi Hohmann is one of the best LA teachers you will get at ISU. She spends time with students and respects many of their decisions. All though some days she's very moody you can live with her due to great teaching ability.
Good luck getting a good grade in that class. She is a good teacher, but hard as hell to please, and incredibly moody. Wear light clothes at review, because she will tear you apart.

Heise is a great Capstone professor. Chill guy with industry experience. He will not micromanage your team, but he will provide good input when asked. Try to stay ahead of deadlines and apply the knowledge you learned and this class will be an easy A.

It is a very fun class; he tells lots of stories from his experience in the field. Class does get decently harder about halfway through, but as long as you pay attention, it's fine. You can tell his goal for the class is to give students an easy tech elective that they can enjoy while still gaining some great knowledge.
Prof. Heise consistently showed up late to class, did not appear to have a good understanding of the projects being worked on, and was generally difficult to work with.  Would not recommend.

Jim was my favorite professor.  I enjoyed his design classes and projects.  I feel like the overall design of his class was some of the best job preparation I received.  He would give compliments that were meaningful and give constructive design criticism derived from his long career of review.

Jim Heise is a charismatic professor with vast industry experience and knowledge. Be sure to ask him about his career and share your interests with him; the stories he will share with you are priceless, and he will give you advice on how to reach your goals. Lots of groupwork, so make sure to scout through the class before the first group project
Very smart person, inspirational. Fun quotes. "I want to go peacefully like my grandpa in his sleep, not screaming like the people in his car"

Passionate is a great word for Heise, he really enjoys teaching and gives great anecdotes for the real-world. This class can be really easy or really hard depending on the project and the group members. My only complaint was that I didn't feel like there was much recourse when I ended up in a group with several terrible group members

Suspension design with Jim is an interesting class... The material is somewhat complicated but he makes it easy to understand. Unfortunately, the group homework assignments can be super confusing and time consuming. Lectures are fun and full of stories. You will have to do a semester group project. He doesn't grade things very often
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heise is a great prof, well respected by students and faculty, soft grader as long as you communicate with him, and it's obvious that he loves his job. He loves to tell long winded stories which are either really satisfying and funny or super distracting depending on how much work you are trying to get done that day haha

Jim is an awesome professor! He's incredibly passionate and actually cares about his students. He teaches classes and concepts that apply to REAL LIFE! (Imagine that in an ME dept!) His only downfall, as mentioned in another comment, is that he tends to over-extend himself with University clubs and such. Great prof! You won't be disappointed.

Heise is awesome. Lots of times the more seasoned ME professors become real arrogant and don't care about your success. Heise is always super helpful, is super sharp, and goes out of his way to ensure you have the tools to succeed. On outside projects he is even helpful and gives his expert opinions. Mr. Heise is a real asset for the M.E. dept.

This applies to 415 and 270 both.  He's really passionate and can be a great teacher.  His one fault is that he overcommits and gets too busy to help everyone.  Get on his good side early on in the semester so he'll take the time to help you later on.

You will be VERY happy in getting Mr. Heise for an instructor. He truly enjoys teaching this class and it shows. Go to class, lectures are boring but most all homework is done in your group. Very easy to approach and ask questions. He knows way more than you will about math modeling so hold on but he takes as long as you need one on one.
Great professor! Easy to work with and get along with.
If you listen to his instructions and follow directions you'll get an A. This class is HARD not to get an A in. If you get anything lower than a B you'd have to be retarded.

Did not supply our group with things necessary for the project. However, he did supply the other groups with materials needed for the same project but not mine. Had to get on his case several times before he would get anything done for us, and eventually just had to cut him out of the loop and get things done ourselves.
No Comments

I've never had Dr. Hill as a professor, but as an advisor he certainly leaves a lot to be desired. Expect to fully utilize your 30 minute advising appointment with him and not get a whole lot out of it. Although he does have moments where he is really helpful, those aren't common. He's a nice guy, but I've never seen anyone excited to talk to him.

Good teacher but you have to go to class otherwise you will be cooked. He knows what he is talking about but does not follow and standard/notes and goes off on random stuff. Only 5 quizzes and 3 exams total for points in his class so you will need to try and study. lowest quiz gets dropped. would recommend a differnt prof. for this course.

Not the best experience for me. Grade is completely based on exams and quizzes, which you never really know what to expect for any of them. He's very passionate about what he teaches but doesn't teach it well in my opinion. Take a lot of notes, as that will be you best resource as you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible experience
Requiered attendance, not difficult class but takes a lot of effort. Feel like he would only give a few students A's. All essay based.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I thought he was a nice guy, he also took all my transfer credits, unlike my new advisor. But I had a failing grade in his class and he didn't reach out to me. But when I got a new advisor she let me know.

I thought that he was a nice guy. But in class, it is very hard to follow along with the notes. He will just put up terms and talk for the next 50 minutes. Also, there is no real study guide for the tests. But I thought he was an easy grader, I half-a**ed a lot of my tests and got a decent grade.

I currently have Prof. Hill as my advisor and I wish I had more positive things to say. Hes very unhelpful and doesnt look at students case by case. He makes you feel rushed and just gives general info. He lacks positive energy that student need when making tough decisions. He doesnt give direct answers. Hes the worst adviser Ive had so far.

Dr. Hill was seriously a wonderful professor. Medieval history is not the most exciting and it can get pretty complicated, but he made it interesting and easy to understand. We had a midterm and a final. He assigned a 12-page paper with very clear instructions and I loved writing it! He also gave great feedback on paper before turning it in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kevin is very reluctant to help his students. He is my academic adviser and made me feel as if I was a burden to him when I went into his office hours. Did not make an effort to reach out to see how I was doing as a student. He is an awful adviser and I believe the History department could benefit if a new adviser was chosen.
Good adviser, enjoy his lectures, very knowledgeable, tougher grader than other profs I know, not always sure what he's looking for, sometimes test questions too vague
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: While taking this class, I thought it was the most boring class I've taken. However, after being done, I'd have to say that it was the class where I learned the most. If you don't like traditional lectures, don't take it. If you like specific detail with tying into the big picture, by all means, take it! Expect to be at class and do the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you want to take a class with someone who is so incredibly patronizing, this is the class for you. Day one he told us that technology for learning is a scam, and that if you don't take notes his way you will fail. He gets off on tangents that have nothing to do with class. He is super long winded, and not the most helpful guy in the whole world.

Dr. Hill isn't an overly nice guy... He got super mad 3 times in class because people weren't paying attention. Quizzes and Exams are all the points and it is very hard to figure out what exactly will be on them. He almost grades them as if you have taken the class before.

By FAR the worst professor I have had at ISU.  He grades as he he thinks he is carrying the torch for some bygone era. Throughout my college career I have averaged a's on my papers, my 2 lowest grades in college came from him.  His lectures are monotonous recitations of information, with little synthesis... strongly STRONGLY advise against!!!!!!!

This man is a joke as an history advisor, ive gone to his office several times for help and he refuses to answer them in an helpful manner. When I asked what I needed to do to get into grad school he simply said, keep your grades up, and that was the end of the conversation. Instead of meeting with students he simply email's R.A.N's. absurd.

Have yet to have as a professor, but as an advisor he is great IF you go out of your way to see him. If you can't understand his jokes then you should not be a history major. NEVER sugar coats, but that is very helpful for his role

If you're a history major, you'll probably like Dr. Hill.  He has an odd sense of humor that only true nerds will pick up on.  I actually wish I could go out and have a beer with him.  As far as ease goes, I've only taken his summer courses, but they were very easy. Getting 400 level credit without writing a term paper is amazing.

Dr. Hill isn't a bad professor; most of the negative comments feel like personal vendettas. He's a traditionalist and serious about history, so if you can handle old-fashioned lectures and writing you'll do fine. However, reading the text is a must. He's helpful and funny if you understand his geek humor, so he's okay if you have to take his class.

Lectures were often confusing at times and tests were not anywhere related to the majority of the material covered. He's a better advisor than a teacher. Better bring a laptop to his lectures or else you are toast!

He was a great teacher and he's a great adviser. He'll help anybody as long as they go and see him. He's definitely no frills. But he sweats, a lot. And it's distracting. But other than that, the class was easy and I like him as an adviser.
Not very helpful, doesn't seem interested
Kevin is the most helpful prof you'll ever have, a damn good advisor if you take the time to see him. You'll learn a lot and be interested but make sure you keep up.
He's actually a really nice guy, just not quite as personable as other profs.  Fair.
GRRRRRReat. You just have to have the right type of personallity. If you are stuck up you'll hate him. So get over yoursleves
He was unhelpful as an advisor and seemed disinterested in anything I had to say.  Overall it felt like he wanted to be left alone more then help people.

Never had him for a class, but he was my adviser for the short period of time I was a History major.  He acted rude, and it seemed like he was trying to push me out of his office when I met with him.  Very unhelpful.
Keven is rather dry and boring; he could be more enthused about life. He is the academic advisor, and is (at least) honest about ISU. He isn't particularly great; but, he isn't bad either.
He is my counsler and he is very unfriendly, rude almost.  He offered me no help, and I can't get into any classes I need.  He is want is wrong with ISU.
wow!!!!  What a guy!!!  top ten on my list
Summer class with him. Very nice and helpful - willing to answer and clarify questions. Fun class!
Very bad, communist professor

Pros:
-No homework besides group projects
-No tests 
-Extensive feedback on projects 

Cons:
-Unorganized labs unrelated to class material and assigned with little to no instruction
-Arbitrary grading not following any rubric 
-Quiz questions not covered in textbook or lectures
-Very little of material from the syllabus was actually covered
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hill himself is a half decent person, but it's almost like the man put no thought into this class. The lectures do not match with the lab material, so whats the point of going to class when the labs are the only things graded? The labs half the time don't make sense and he expects you to read his mind for vocab quiz definitions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although Dr. Hill is a nice guy, if we ignore the weird sexist comments, the way his class is organized is a mess. He just skips over lectures he doesn't want to do even if it is important for the labs, he doesn't cover vocabulary that shows up on quizzes until after you've taken them, and his definitions on the quizzes are his opinion. Good luck.

An honest review: he won't let you study from your test in fear of cheating. so you'll have to go to his office hours, only half of what you read if that is on the exam, good luck with the quizzes since I've met no one who knows where he got the definitions from. labs are fun though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Hill expects students to do college-level work and holds the students accountable to their work ethic. Some students view this as being difficult.  He is more than happy to help. All you have to do is ask.  If you read the reading materials he assigns and pay attention, you'll do fine. The amount of work you put in will determine your success.

Hill is a really solid professor. He cares very much and is very passionate about his field. Super nice guy too, isn't ever afraid to crack a joke or anything like that. I went into the class not really caring about the subject and found myself very interested in learning the material. Tests can be a little hard if you forget to study tho.

Dr. Hill is one of the best professors in the Anthropology department. He's passionate about what he teaches and that makes the class worth while. His grading is incredibly straight forward and laid out in the syllabus. Anyone can do well in this course if they follow the directions and work hard.

His class was okay except for his stupid questions. He started out with 100pts for engagement, and he would deduct you 10pts for wrong answers if he asked you a question by chance. A lot of the time they were specific things. Also did not like having to give up an entire weekend for a trip.

Hill is a great teacher he really knows what he's talking about and is willing to help you. He's funny and gets really excited when hes talking about archaeology. He expects a lot from students but only because he wants them to do well. He's also super hot!

Dr. Hill is a great guy and fun to be around but if you aren't dedicated to reading the book then you will struggle in the class. His quizzes are based entirely on the readings and the tests require knowledge of the readings in order to do well on them.

Very nice guy funny and helpful BUT his tests are ridiculous. They are half on the actual material related to AmericanIndians and half on the names of everyone and who ever set foot in the site. Instead of focusing on the AmericanIndians themselves as the class would have you believe he prefers to test you about the people found each site.

Hill cracks me up. His tests are hard, though--take good notes, especially on anything he lectures on for more than 5 min if it isn't on the powerpoints!  If you respect him and the material he will respect you.  He's nicer 1-on-1 than you think he will be; don't hesitate to ask for help.
he was really fun and interesting to listen to

Entertaining mannerisms (rocks on his feet when he gets excited) and phrases ("I'll bet you a burger"), gave the class a lecture on race and the evils of eugenics like we were naughty and he'd caught us all at a KKK convention, obscure test questions from lecture, reading the book helps only slightly on tests.  Focus on lecture/lab reviews.

Hill was a great teacher, but students who slack off have a problem with him. He can seem mean, but he's just joking. He has great stories to add to his lecture material and offers lots of out-of-class opportunities. Take good notes and you're set.
Asks some pretty obscure questions on tests.
I love his cheesey jokes and he is hot, so why wouldn't you go to class every day?!

202 doesn't seem that hard at first but trust me it get more difficult. he says that tests are "pretty easy" but don't be fooled. i agree with the above comment that alot of the material that you study isn't on the test and vice versa.

I really enjoyed Anthro 201, so i was really looking forward to this class. I enjoy going to class becauase the material is quite interesting, but the recitations are pointless and the tests/quizs are pretty hard. He is really bad with getting his computer to work.
This class is impossible, the test are insanely hard and the test material can never be found, avoid this class at all cost!!

The professor was AWESOME. He kept class interesting and was down to earth. However, do NOT take this course. The lectures are interesting and keep your attention, but the test material is not in the lectures. He tests over very obscure details. Even my TA said that Hill made this class ridiculously difficult. Stay away from 202!
No Comments
Hill makes class fun, a little corny with his jokes, but serious about teaching. I'd take him again. The mullet has to go!
I guess this guy is a love-hate teacher.  I was one who didnt like his teaching though and thought the class was too narrowly focused and didn't cover enough material.

Good professor. Makes class interesting and fun by being personable. Cares about his students and totally goes out of his way for them and gives them opportunities to do actual hands-on research. He does expect you to work hard and produce your best work possible. Highly reccommend if your goal is to learn.
Wish I had taken a different class
No Comments
pretty good teacher, but a complete ****
This guy is a great teacher. If your late for class he will break you down, thats life. He is a bit quirky, sports a mullet and is a really rad, approchable guy.
The review right below mine hit the nail on the head.

Hill treats people with little respect unless they are Minions doing his research for him, blaming errors on others and makes unfounded accusations. He has made errors in his anthro information, never correcting himself. In the company of women, he has made appalling remarks about the sanity of women who chose to have a career rather than a family.
He is suck believe me

He's a dick about attendance, and generally has contempt for students.  He can be very rude to females.  He doesn't believe in helping students learn outside of class, and his organization level, while better than most, still leaves too much pertinent information out for an introductory course.
Must go to class.  A dick about tardiness even 1 minute.
Funny guy and always willing to hand out extra credit.  He looks like the croc hunter and is very sensitive about his mullet.  Great instructor for keeping an interest in what he is teaching.

He's got a great sense of humor and is very willing to work with you if you make the time. Steer clear of his pet peeves (tardiness!) and tell him how much you love his mullet and you'll do fine. His class turned me on to becoming an anthro major!
I went to every class and every recitation, but when I asked him for help, he wouldn't help me.  Also made a rude statement to me.

He didn't like me because I didn't take notes.  And made a point of learning my name because of that.  All in all though I still finished out his class okay....  Totally agree about the crocodile hunter thing though.
Remember to do the online assignments and come to class, and you'll do just fine.  Anyone who complains about his sense of humor is just overly sensitive.

Go to all lectures, pay attention, read the book, and don't forget to do the online quizes and you should do fine.  You can't be too sensitive because his humor can be biting sometimes, but he's just as good at taking it as recieving it.

He doesn't give hard tests if you study, he may not seem nice in class, but his is very helpful and friendly if you talk to him after class.  I enjoyed his class, he is a very smart guy in his field.  He has a mullet!
Difficult tests, sometimes overly sensitive about people coming in late, but not always.  And yes, he does look like the Crocodile Hunter.
too sensitive about people who come into class even one minute late, hard tests, kinda looks like the crocodile hunter

She was nice, but I would never take a class taught by her again. She is unorganized to the point that she messed up my grade. I tried emailing her about it, but she never responded which didn't surprise me. Ruined my 4.0.
Avoid classes led by this instructor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She gets off track very easy in class and often wastes class time. She gives a lot of writing assignments (group and individual) but takes too long grading. When you need feedback from one assignment to move on to the next, you are lucky if you get the feedback you need 24 hours before the assignment you need it for is due.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Magic, religion, and witchcraft. And absolutely fascinating class. Congratulations to Dr. Hill for undertaking such an intense topic. Inspiring .

Lots of papers, cared a lot about her work. Wasnt my kind of class but I could see where others would enjoy it. There is also a 100 point take home final and a 100 point final paper that are due on the same day so plan ahead for these
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Hill is an amazing professor! I took this class on a whim and loved every second of it. No tests besides a take-home final. There are a lot of papers that you write for this course, but they are much easier than a test and require little to none outside research. This is an interesting course and I would recommend to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Hill's class was very easy. I never took notes and I retained the information very well. The class covers simple topics that are easy to understand. Additionally, participation and attendance are the main grades. Only test the whole semester was the final which was take-home. Loved this course and happily take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was probably one of the worst classes I have taken at Iowa State! You would attend class one day talking about a topic and then the next class period completely switch to something new with her expecting you to be an expert on it. Also the final which is take home was impossible and she didnt curve it. 10/10 recommend you dont take this!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She may say missing a few lectures wont impact your grade that much... until there are 6 tophat questions each day you miss and a whole week of class with none. Sorry I was sick Ill tell my body never to do that again so I can attend anthro. Think that 79.9 is gonna be a B-? Think again! No percentage scale, only quality of work based on letters
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Christina is a nice person and wants us to do well. If you talk to her, she will help you figure out what you need to do for assignments. Overall this class was pretty easy. There was a lot of discussion during class too. If you show up to class, you will be able to pass the tests easily.

Christina is a really nice woman. She wants you to learn and do well. The class is basically all papers that you write in groups, which she grades really tough, but it all gets scaled in the end. This class is a decent amount of work, but if you talk to her about what she is looking for and try hard you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I have absolutely no idea how I ended up with a good grade in this class - I spent all semester terrified of failing. TA's do more work than the professor, and when I tried to even ask my TA questions all I got were vague answers. There's a lot of busy work that's graded VERY harshly. Harder than it should be for an introductory class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. knows nothing about the class work she has assigned, hands everything over to the grad student TA's, and cannot answer questions for herself when asked by students. TA specifically told me she had been hounding Hill for a month to make a rubric for our final paper, but never received one. No tests all semester, but a final with no study guide
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: honestly the worst teacher i have ever had... do NOT take this class expecting it to be an easy credit. she grades super hard and does not give clear ideas as to what she wants you to do for the assignment. she gave me 4/25 because she changed her mind as to what the assignment was AFTER i turned it in..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Drop this class now. She changes her mind about grading criteria after you've already submitted the assignment. Doesn't offer a review of ANY kind for the final exam. She thinks everyone is there to be an anthropologist.. too much work for a general education course.
Passionate about what she does, specifically Native American Ethno-history. If you talk to her any issues will get solved.
