reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The homework directions can be vague, and section discussion needs to be revamped. The amount of materials in this class makes sense though. Topics such as race, class, and gender are complicated - you shouldn't expect to mindlessly breeze through. Ya'll should stop putting grades/diploma on a pedestal, and take actual learning into account.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is nice, but the course is SO HORRIBLE. I would never recommend it to anyone. lots of reading, lots of writing, and very VERY very tough graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Do NOT put off the reading in this class or you will fall behind and never catch back up. I recommend doing the homework ahead of time as well. That way you CAN fall a day or two behind and still be able to catch up. The lectures are interesting and her voice isn't annoying. Just pay attention to the syllabus and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took this class to fulfill one of my gen. ed. credits. Unfortunately, this class has very little to do with actually learning and studying content, but going through a lot of "busy work" and weak discussions in sections. I haven't learned anything substantial, and I am one who loves school and will usually go the extra mile for a good class.

She's not very good at talking about assigned homework. She expects students to rely on the syllabus which would be okay if the directions there were clear, which they aren't. She won't tell you what she wants but expects you to know and grades accordingly. Also Grad students help grade and they mess up, often. Had to have her change my grade twice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent teacher, cares about the student.  This was an amazing class  and I learned so much.

I have taken two classes from this professor and she is the best one I have had in college so far. She's extremely knowledgable on her subjects and loves getting her students interested. The work load is very light and revolves around a lot of interesting class discussions. Take a class from this professor! She's amazing and very fun!

I LOVE Christina! She was so helpful for me and the class was incredibly interesting. She made sure questions got answered and was always available to students, if they took the initiative. She is a great intro prof because she treats you like a college student and makes sure you know that she is there to help, but not to baby you through the class
Terrible at replying to emails, or not at all. Final exam had questions not mentioned during lecture/powerpoint/section. Talks down to you.
the tests are easy if you come to class I got at least a 76 on all tests with no studying
Worst professor I've had at Iowa State. Does a poor job preparing students for exams. Would not recommend taking any of her classes.

It is much more useful to sit in bed and read the textbook and one (of many) of the required reads instead of attending a lecture. The clicker points are the only useful parts of a lecture. I would not recommend this class.
Awesome at getting her students interested and engaged in the class. The homework load was pretty light and a lot of it was just interesting discussions in class.

I was very excited going into this class, and I am left disappointed. Professor Hill has tried to defy past reviews by reading questions directly from slides and allowing students to tell us about their own culture, I have not learned a thing in this class, and her expectations for the class are too high.

Worst class I've taken at ISU. All she does is read off of slides, and half the time she doesn't even know what the slides actually say. Useless as far as help goes. Never answers emails. She's hardly an adequate professor. The tests are too specific and not enough on understanding concepts. Don't take this class. Not worth the time.
She is not a good teacher! The tests are so specific and all she does is read off of her slides. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!!

She is helpful when you ask her questions. There is A LOT of homework and the exams are difficult. She does however take suggestions for improving the class (like making study guides for exams, etc.) Pay attention in class and read the book and you'll do well. (Also the class is curved.)I personally liked her as a professor.

She just reads the slides. Clicker questions aren't just attendance, you have to get the questions right also. A LOT of homework every week and everyone fails the exams. Seriously. Also 2 presentations and 2 papers. Not helpful and her laugh gets annoying. She's a very poor teacher. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. It takes up a lot of time

Hill is a funny and nice prof. BUT she's also kind of a putz. The class is sposed to tell you of the cultures/peoples of Indians in N.America which it did but us the STUDENTS had to it this in groups instead of the TEACHER, good use of thousands of dollars, huh? She grades papers stupidly hard and her tests are way too specific. Take 210 w/Jen C=EZ

This class was very interesting and makes you think about other people's perspective. She does not take attendance, but if you don't go you won't learn the information for quizzes. There is a group project you work on a lot, in and out of class. No exams and lots of opportunity for extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There are a lot of technical difficulties in this class. She frequently posts assignments that we were supposed to have a week to do the day before theyre due. Maybe shell be better in class but Id steer clear of her online class. I dont have time for 160 page reading assignments. They can sometimes be that long. Also difficult to contact
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Easy course for meeting US Diversity requirement. She and the assistant professor are very knowledgeable. Many of the topics are just a rehash of any personal finance class you may have taken in high school. TopHat questions during most classes so make sure to attend. Tests are easy if you do the studying for it. Cheat sheet is allowed on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amanda a very good lecturer, she loves the topics and goes through the presentations well. She teaches along with another professor who is passionate. You have to go to class because attendance is taken randomly, and there is additional top hat questions. Pay attention and take notes, and do well on tests. No homework so take quizzes seriously too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amanda teaches along with another professor.. She is very passionate about the subject and goes through the lecture well. Attendance is taken via tophat and it is random. The notes are not online so you have to go to class. Easy class if you pay attention and take notes. Participation is through tophat and not many ways to boost your grade up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is by far the most pointless class I have ever taken. Other than this class being a GPA booster, there is no point. Some of the speakers that were brought in talked about diapers the entire time and I felt rather uncomfortable with some of the comments made by some of the speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Guy below me is wrong, and is probably just mad at his grade. Yeah, it was a tough class, but you should expect that by now. He was always available to help with the projects and homework, and his tests were manageable. He was very fair in his grading, with plenty of partial credit on tests.

class turned into a crash course second half of the semester. Made us do homework sets that had little relevance to the exam material. I spent more time on this class than all my other ones. I hated this class, and Hillier for thinking we all have the time to do all this work.
This guy can teach well, tell stories, and manage to mostly keep class interest for a somewhat boring subject
Awesome professor!!!

One of the best teachers I've ever had.  Keeps class interesting with stories and isnt too serious.  Tests really arent that hard and he does a good job of preparing you for them.  I've had him for 2 classes and really enjoyed both.  Would recommend to anyone
No Comments
He always busy and never set the exact office hour. not helpful. the test is not easy but still can be solved.

He posts lecture notes online, but good luck reading his handwriting. Class is mostly based in theory and his tests are almost identical to his practice exams. You'll probably get a decent grade from him, but you probably will not learn anything.
His exam is not hard and he posts lecture notes in the BB. He is a really good professor.

He cannot stay on topic and focused the class on all the wrong things. The books and homework were not much help. The tests were not bad until the final. The final project was tough, and it was hard to tell if you were on the right track. He did not offer much help when confused.

Nice guy and is more than fair when grading. Tests are easy and very similar to the sample tests he uploads, with a few minor changes. His lectures aren't helpful, as he mostly focuses on theories and rarely goes through the practical applications you'll see on the tests. If you only care about your grade without learning much, he's your guy.

If you have the choice, DO NOT take this man's class. I don't recall learning a single thing in the classroom. All he does is teach theory, which is okay if he would ever apply it to real world examples (he doesn't). Don't ever expect him to have anything graded for at least a month after it is due, including tests.
He is a really nice guy and told great stories. But Dr. Hill is getting a bit old and unorganized. As sad as I am to say this it is probably time for his retirement... :(

Honestly nice guy, but obsessed with theory and we didn't finish all course objectives. Didn't learn overly much either. Homework is tough, tests relatively easy. Never uses powerpoint so take good lecture notes. If you like theory he's your man,  if not, better try another professor. The project wasn't too bad.

Nice guy, but not well-suited to teaching.  Lots of lecture material strayed from the course objectives, leaving students missing key pieces of knowledge needed for 357.  Tests were very similar to practice tests.  Assignments and tests were usually returned over a month after submission.
I agree with the post below. His tests are really easy, but it takes him  a month to turn grades in. He would be a good teacher if he was more organized

A nice guy, but aggravating at the same time. Do not expect him to have anything done on time. Don't even expect him to go over the material for homework before its due. The only thing you can assume with him is that hes not going to have anything done, and he will post your final grades well after its due and grades are out.

It can be hard to understand what he is getting at in lecture but SI helps and he is very fair with grading. He is very helpful if you ask him direct questions and he is very nice and understanding when you are sick. :) only one of my teachers that cared that I had gotten the flu. Very nice guy. Clearly loves what he is doing.
Enjoyed the class and he has great stories to tell overall very fair in grading.

he is worthless, he for an intro cheme class he doesn't explain the practical application of his teachings.  This makes it hard to apply what you learned in future classes.   He should not be allowed to teach!!!!
His teaching is just way over intro ChE level.  The book is not helpful.  Fortunately SI was very helpful.  The homework was pretty much impossible, but the exams weren't too awful in comparison.
Absolutely the worst grader I have ever hard. She's great in the classroom but tears you grade apart on her computer. Not fair or just, at all. Don't take her unless you're wanting your GPA to drop.
So so!!

She is no longer at Iowa State. She now teaches at Indiana. Eng-W 131 is an awful class to begin with - Lavinia makes it 10x worse. She assigns  a ton of useless homework that takes a lot of time and is only worth .5% of your grade. The assignments would be tolerable if they actually helped our writing in any way. Avoid taking this class with her.

She is full of herself. One of those teachers that doesn't believe in giving out A's in the beginning of the year - that should tell you enough right there. She will "help" you in office hours, and then critique some of HER OWN SUGGESTIONS. She'll tell you to do something one way and then grade it differently
She is good teacher and tries to help the student.
Likes to send assignments in email without discussing in class. Can be unclear about certain assignments at times. Overall, pretty good for how long she's been teaching, though.

The different teachers of this class use the same materials. Get the notes packet. The lectures are pretty boring, but it's worth going for the participation points. The team exercises, practice problems, and exam reviews that we did in class were helpful. Otherwise you'll be lost trying to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you attend class and take notes, you'll be fine in this class. Homework and participation make up a lot of the grade, I didn't do great on the exams but still did well overall. She was helpful in office hours.
The class material can be difficult but the professor brings her work experience in to make the topics seem more real-world. She will meet and help with the topics as well.
terrible at teaching content and bad at explaining what is being taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Holmstrom is not an exciting lecturer so to speak but she's always willing to help students understand the material- I found her to be approachable. The class is fairly easy if you show up to lecture and actively engage with the material and assignments.

It is almost like she is learning the information with us. She is belittling when someone asks a question and often doesn't give an answer. The exams in this class are difficult. Not only that but there are few questions but each multiple choice question is worth 4 points, making it almost impossible to do good in this class.
She did not know how to explain concepts, made class unbearable to attend, and completely skipped pages of notes assuming we all already understood on our own.

Holmstrom is a good professor. Took her early morning MWF class and did not experience any issues as others have stated. 
-She relies heavily on slideshow but do take notes and do the examples to make everything easy
-Accessible in and out of the classroom
-Easy to talk to
-Low homework
-Content is linear and builds
-Excel project is easy to follow
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You do not want her as a professor. Lectures are useless to attend, as she sporadically jumps around the content making it impossible to follow. Often got frustrated when we didn't understand the material she didn't teach. Material given to study with is outdated and unhelpful--exams are highly conceptual, and she doesn't teach the concepts.

She isn't a good teacher. It seemed that she gave up or lacked the motivation to teach and explain the material. When seeking assistance she just directs you back to the slides on canvas as well as the slides she provides about metacognitive learning. Nice person but would recommend picking someone else.

The textbook is hard to learn from. There was minimal extra credit and she did try to be helpful but also struggled to understand why students were not doing well and would get frustrated explain something. I asked for extra work problems as the test always seemed so different and she said to read the book more. She also to a while to respond.

This professor's teaching ability is nonexistent. The over-reliance of vague powerpoints to supplement a "meta-cognitive" learning pedagogy absolutely destroys any actual constructive ability to reflect on your errors you may have when asking a question about the assigned work Absolutely awful. You might as well buy a tutor service instead!

She is a nice professor and her course page is neatly organized. But outside of that her teaching skills are non existent. The PowerPoints are incredibly vague and the way she presents the material makes it almost impossible to learn anything. You will basically have to teach yourself and learn the material on your own time.

This class was the biggest waste of time. It claims it is a agronomy class but the professor couldn't know any less about agronomy. Nothing that is gone over in lecture is on the exams and every lecture always keeps you guess ing about what actually just happened. Take this class with ANYONE but him.

DO NOT LISTEN TO PEOPLE GIVING BAD REVIEWS. Dr. Hornbuckle is THE GOAT. I highly enjoyed Agron206, lectures were engaging, digestible, and exams were extremely predictable. Homework assignments were very minimal as well. Would highly recommend taking this class :)

This class will rip you apart, not from difficulty, but from a professor who simply can't teach. AGRN 2060 (Fall 2025) was mind-numbing, disorganized, and the worst use of lecture time I've had in college. Painful, pointless, avoid at all costs. Take this with literally anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Hornbuckle. This was my favorite class ever. It was pretty easy, and I found it so interesting. Dr. Hornbuckle is funny and has a really good time lecturing. He makes concepts straightforward and uses fun analogies. Tests are very clear, you know exactly what will be on the test.

Really friendly and helpful professor. Tests and assignments make it hard to get good points as they cover material that is incredibly complex and not fully covered in lecture. If taking this class to fill nat. sciences major req, would highly advise against, may ruin gpa
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super hard grader, has no compassion for students, doesn't allow you to actually learn from your assignments and tests.
This class was extremely hard. Material was very difficult to understand and exams flunk your grade so easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is a very easy going guy and cares about his students. Although I don't feel like I learned much agronomy skills in this class. This class is great if you like math and research but there was no physical skills that would help me in the future.

Sets you up for failure. He does not allow good study material and leaves the class guessing. He also adds in random grades after final exams to tank your grade, if you think you are in good standing it can drop. He has a comprehensive exam at the end but does not give any feedback or allow you to see what questions you missed on previous exams.0%

Dr. Hornbuckle is very friendly and caring. He genuinely cares about teaching and his class. The work was very manageable, and the lab periods were very informative. I enjoyed how we were taught how and why to do something before we had to do it and were being helped along the way. There's feedback on every assignment, so you know how to improve.

I love Dr. Hornbuckle.He is VERY clear about what he expects from students and provides MANY resources if you are struggling with stuff. He is very willing to help you so just reach out, he's very nice & genuinely wants to get to know you. The lab reports were long and annoying but you get used to it and figure out how he wants them done after one.

Fun professor with interactive lectures, genuinely wants students to succeed. Uses Tophat and you need to show up and take notes if you want to do good. Exams are tough, there are 4 and one gets dropped plus a final at the end. You get bumped up an extra letter grade on final grade which helps.
He seems to be very knowledgeable and cares a lot about what he is teaching. He often has some small experiments and likes to get the class involved in the lectures.
Enjoys hosting exams that contain questions that we have never talked about in class and exams are nothing like the practice exams.
Professor Hornbuckle is a cool guy, and his lectures were easy to pay attention to. However the exams are pretty difficult. Take good lecture notes.

You can clearly tell that Dr. Hornbuckle loves what he does. He puts all his energy and time into ensuring students are successful. Agron206 was one of my more difficult classes but he made learning the material both fun and interesting. Great professor. 10/10 would recommend.

His grading system is bogus. You never know what your grade is in the class since he grades off points and not percentage. SUPER FRUSTRATING. He makes you work for your grade. Tells you to study the chapt. objectives and then he pulls the exam questions out of thin air. Get the textbook. He's not good at lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is easy as a whole but he is a tough grader. Write lab reports every 2 weeks in which no one in my whole class ever got a 100% on. Grading criteria unclear week by week. Overall a trash class and professor but it is required for agronomy majors.

Great guy, he is passionate about what he teaches and his students. He has some weird experiments and analogies that help solidify understanding of content. Top hat questions are everyday but you only need to answer over 50% to get full points regardless if you got it right or wrong. Pretty easy content as long as you keep up.
Makes it extremely clear what is on tests, which arent too difficult. If you go to class and do your homework, youll pass. Study a little, easy a.

Hes a good guy and real smart. Lectures are dry but go to half of them bc if you get >50% completion on top hat you get 30pts. Tests are tricky and hw is too. Very specific questions. If you take good notes you'll be fine. Grades by points earned, not %. I got a 72% which ended up being a B-. Class is not as easy as you think when you sign up.

Hornbuckle is a memelord. A lot of the material covered in class is rather dry, but Hornbuckle sometimes throws in some interesting demonstrations and jokes that get the class engaged. The textbook is good to have but not mandatory. He gives you 2 weeks to complete assignments. After every exam, he goes over what you can be doing to do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lots of lab reports using ShareLaTeX. Otherwise, it is a pretty easy class.
He's really funny and knows what he's talking about. Very passionate about what he teaches. Gives a great and engaging lecture.

Lectures are interesting and there's the occasional goof or gimmick that will get the whole class to laugh. Showed up one day and he was blasting music and throwing candy into the audience. Gives you plenty of chances to makeup for missed points and makes the grading very very clear about what you need to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hornbuckle is a great teacher for this class, gives decently entertaining lectures with a few jokes sprinkled throughout for mnemonics. Tests aren't too challenging, homework assignments are short and can be done multiple times, and you need to answer 50% of clicker questions (not correctly, just do them). Aritt is good too.
Very heavy on Lab reports that you perform together with your class. This was the first year this class existed so hopefully it will work out the kinks next time around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great Teacher, is very nice and wants you to pass. have to show up to class at least 50% of the time for clicker questions.
Great Professor!

Dr. Hornbuckle cares about his students and communicating the material effectively. He is very meticulous in deriving the mathematics and careful in identifying all the variables. He presents analogies that help students understand. Assignments are lengthy and sometimes a little bit repetitive (this has downsides and upsides).
Clear and makes interesting analogies. Tries to target multiple learning styles. I thought the class was too easy but I still learned a lot from it. Very willing to help.
Point system is very confusing, professor takes a long amount of time to respond to questions, bad at clarifying information. Analogies make information even more confusing.

My favorite professor so far. He creates really great analogies to help us remember. Once sang "Dew Point" to the song True Love as a way to remember dew point. His tests were not bad if you pay attention in class and do the practice tests.
This class was so much fun, Hornbuckle did a great job explaining things, read the readings and go to class and you will be fine. Also the review sessions with the TA are VERY helpful
Good professor, tries to make sure you understand everything thoroughly.
He's a good professor
Uses metaphors and analogies that can be difficult to relate to material
Enjoyed the class.  Very willing to help his students.  Mixes up lectures with clicker questions for easy points.  Lots of examples.  Made the class interesting but could baby at times.

One of the best professors I've had. Why? There's a lot of diversity in lecture which is great for different learning styles, changes things up (mixes in short stories and in class demos), great pace, fairly easy and he's very personable. Acting in class was good for amusement - like falling down due to the "crushing" weight of the atmosphere.
Very boring.  The way he babies the class is ridiculous.  Treat us like college students, not 5th graders please.
Very funny professor
Pretty good professor. Does a good job explaining things, even if they are mundane. Love his clothes too.

Watch out for that random seat thing. He'll getcha one of these days when you least expect it. It's especially embarrassing when you don't even know what the hell he's talking about. Other than that I seemed to have gotten a better grading with him than with Arritt. Crazy. I enjoy the class though. Meteorology is interesting.

This guy babies the class so much it's ridiculous.  He's a nice guy and wears some pretty hilarious clothing combos.  He's basically a tool that gives out a bunch of candy, and it's a lil disturbing how he knows some people's names in a class of 350.  Put off but went to class and crammed night before each test and got an easy A or i hope i will.

I'll agree with these guys.  He is rather boring, monotone, and he does use poor analogies.  However, he is a really nice guy, and, as far as I'm concerned, taught meteorology really well.  I'm glad he's my professor for that class.  He's SO much better than Professor Arritt!
Very boring with horrible analogies.  He's nice but has a hard time relating to students and teaching.
Quite possibly the worst lecture class I've ever had... very uninteresting to me. Never had a problem with dozing in class 'til I took this one...

Overall a good professor. If you want to do good on exams, you have to be actively listening in class, as his slideshows make no sense on their own. Uses attendance as a way to decide if your grade should be brought up at the end of the semester. My only thing with him was that he talks incredibly slow and takes a long time to get through slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor, especially coming from someone who struggles with chemistry. He tries everything to encourage the learning of his students. Just study and pay attention and you will be good!
Failed to make the class super interesting for me. Was still a valuable learning experience, but I would review all my options prior to taking him.

Professor Holme is a good professor who explains things through lectures pretty well. There are very few demonstrations in this class, so take that into account. The course aligns directly with the lab. Lots of slides and a lot of reading and homework. He is accessible outside of class and is pretty understanding. Exams are difficult though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sometimes the lectures would drag on, but he had materials to help you understand the material. The course is very test-heavy, but if you study and come to class, you will be fine. Other than that pretty easy course just do the work.

Awful. Rude. Dismissive. I attended every class, went to SI sessions, got a tutor, went to the chem help room, and was still barely understanding the content. After class one day I asked him for extra guidance since I was struggling and he basically told me "IDK what to tell you". Had to drop the class since it was affecting me so poorly. AVOID HIM

His lectures can be boring and he uses TopHat. The exams suck and are usually 8-12 questions, 4-6 points each so missing one question can tank your grade. He did offer resurrection points that brought my grade up a ton. Buy the ACS study guide for the final, study hard, go to class and you will be totally fine.

Did not like him. Lectures were BORING. 5 in class exams were given out before final exam and he would give out "study guides" that did not help at all. I recommend buying the ACS study guide because this saved me for the final exam. Homework is very frustrating and takes a long time. If you have him, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eh. His lectures were quite boring and I found it difficult to stay engaged and keep up. His grading policy is nice even though everything else was meh

Lectures are useless honestly, he doesn't really explain the material all that well. One thing he did that I liked was the extra credit opportunities at the end of the semester. But overall this class stressed me out.

His class is very lecture heavy. I often found it hard to keep up and retain what he was saying as he over explains with vocab that only a grad student would know. We only had 5 tests before the final, but each question is weighted heavily and so are the exams as a whole, so if you get 1 or 2 questions wrong, your grade is screwed.

Dr. Holme's teaching style makes the class unnecessarily difficult. He rushes through explanations and flies through PowerPoint slides, making it hard to take notes or understand the material. The exams are another issue. They're too close together, worth very few points, and just a few mistakes can tank your grade. Would not recommend.

He's a decent professor, but I didn't like the way he taught. I went to maybe 10 lectures and they all confused me. Did the TopHat questions from my bed. 

I was already familiar with the material of the class so I was able to do well. In discussion sections I ended up teaching the people sitting next to me weekly. Not the worst, just not for me

Very lecture heavy. His teaching style wasn't my favorite. It feels like he talks around the point and never really makes it very clear. Test are multiple choice but still not easy. Test are also very heavily weighted so if you do bad on one, it will drag down your grade. He uses TopHat in class for points. Overall, nice guy though.

Entertaining guy, passionate, knowledgeable. Participation in lecture counts towards grade. Tests are short but multiple choice and heavily weighted, if you miss two or more questions you won't get an A. Decent amount of homework but easy. Caps off points available in each category, very easy to reach the maximum which I liked. Some extra credit.

He cares about his students and I can tell he loves to teach, but I personally did not like his style of teaching, especially for chemistry. Between the poorly explained slides and the random tangents on candles and wild fires I did not learn much from lectures. Exams did not really match course material. Easy homework and TopHat points though!

He relates topics in Chemistry back to the central topic so you understand how the chemistry is applied. His lectures are good. Go to class and get points from TopHat. Homework is pretty easy as well. You don't need to read the textbook. Sometimes it is hard to hear in the big lecture hall but overall would reccommend taking this class with him.
Very engaging and try's his best to make sure everyone understands.

Average professor. My main issue is that we had to write an essay, which no other chem professors make us do, and it was graded very harshly. Lectures were insightful and enjoyable, but the way he grades is very confusing. Holme kind of does his own thing and is different than anything I've seen in the chem department. Very interesting experience.

He knows what he is talking about, but sometimes he is incredibly boring. He also made our section write a paper even though the other sections didn't and it was about something that we didn't really learn in the class. The tests weren't too difficult, but they varied in difficulty. He does Top Hat, but it is the same code every time.

Holme was an okay professor. He's the only chem professor with an essay in his curriculum, but he grades it relatively easily, which might help your overall grade. The tests are hard and may mention topics that don't seem relevant. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are easy participation points during each lecture. No text book needed.

He has a system where you can earn more pints than there are available. Overall, I don't think he grades that rough seeing as you can score partial credit on quizzes, granted, those can hit pretty heavy. There are a lot of points given for participation.

His lectures are extremely unorganized and long. The grading style of this class is also one reason I hate it. Tests are 25 questions multiple choice, but 1 question could be worth anywhere from 3-4 points each. So your grade could tank easily. All around I just do not enjoy my time in Holmes class. His class has costed me many tears.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a good professor

Dr. Holme is an alright professor who likes his job and teaching. However, his lectures tend to go over A LOT of topics in just one lecture and constantly add to what is already on the slides, so it is important to pay attention. Tests are pretty difficult, but as long as you practice the OWL before the exam, it should help prepare you.

This class is not hard to get an A in. Holme is a fine professor but the tests can be difficult. If you go to class and pay attention, and do the homework, you'll be fine. He does use TopHat, which are easy points. If you don't pay attention or don't try, you will not succeed. Reach out to him if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Holme focuses on the big picture and sustainability for the first half of the class. There was a 500 word paper due halfway through the course, which was a decent part of the grade for the class; it was fairly easy. Towards the end of the course, content gets more in depth and difficult. The teacher knows his chemistry and encourages engagement

He's an okay teacher, lectures are kind of hard to follow. I highly recommend going to class because he uses TopHat and those points are essential for getting a good grade. There is an essay which is easy to do but none of the other Chem177 professors have an essay. Tests are hard but you get to retake 2/3 of the tests at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are content heavy and he rambles on about how the class content relates to the outside world way more than actually focusing on the main lesson. Tests are extremely difficult and averages were about 65% all semester. Have to write a paper which none of the other profs do. Had to get a tutor to understand anything that was being taught.

I took AP Chem in high school so I already knew the content and didn't have to study too much. The tests weren't too difficult, but the class average for each test was 75%. He mumbles a lot, so it can be hard to understand him. However, I do appreciate how much he emphasizes sustainability in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you did not take AP chemistry during high school get ready to struggle. You can tell Holme really loves chemistry but is not good at teaching it and often adds unnecessary concepts to the exams. Lectures are pointless but mandatory, as he uses tophat for attendance points.
He is not a fair grader along with rambling in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: he makes no sense whatsoever. he takes attendance points for lectures. if he didnt do that itd be okay cause im just learning it independently but he will mark u for academic misconduct for no show. if u take this class u will be learning independently but u still have to waste your time by showing up to class just to learn nothing. im good at chem
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are really helpful. Tests are on the harder side but nothing too bad. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are "exit tickets" or pop quizzes that you take at the end of class. He is really responsive and overall a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Holme applies chemistry to the real world. He responds to emails in less than an hour most days. You can tell how passionate he is to help kids learn. Unlike most chem classes, you must write a paper, but it is an easy way to boost your grade.

Overall a great professor I came thinking that Chemistry was going to be hard, but it wasn't, I had taken AP Chem in High School and didn't receive the credit to pass out of Freshmen chem but he made the class enjoyable. He could acutely teach and made the class an interesting place I also was able to declare my major in Chemistry becaus of him.

Professor was horrible. Class averages on exams were 60-70%. He does not "believe" in extra credit. He does things completely different than all of the other chemistry professors. Tests are only 15 questions worth 60 points so you are basically screwed. I did everything I could to raise my grade and still barely passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was a great teacher. I wish I would take all chemistry classes with him. He makes you think beyond just learning information. Everything is related to relevant, real world problems.

Holme is by far the worst professor I have ever had. During lecture he does no run through problems and expects you to know them on your own. He may run through how to do a problem one day, but then he will totally dismiss it and just expect you to understand every problem that is given to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the worst professors I've had here at Iowa State. The class is HEAVILY graded on tests which are once every two weeks. He does not give much information on what will be on the test, and always states that his practice tests are not what is going to be on the actual exams. This makes it hard to even know what to study for..

Good class if you took AP Chem in high school. If you haven't taken AP Chem, DO NOT take this class. Holme is very bright but uses an "engineering type" of teaching and if you are a straight forward type of person then his lectures get confusing. Hardest class at ISU. He does not check emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took both 177 and 178 with Holme, and I absolutely loved being in his class. His teaching style is very effective and he is a great person and a great teacher. He gives a lot of opportunities for students to improve their grades and is very good at giving feedback. Holme adds a lot of personality to his lectures, and he makes chemistry fun!

No curves. If you review his study guide it is point on. switched from one class to another pretty tough and gives you an extra credit "exam". TA and professor give you two different answers. You can Tophat from home but you should go to class if you don't understand the material. You should go to tutor, study, read, and prepare for your class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: A real conceptual teacher. I was in his honors section and he taught me wonders. He does grade tough and has more difficult exams than the other profs, however, he is much better at teaching and will prepare you more for the future.

I got 100 on every assignment and 100 on the paper we wrote. Based on three tests my grade was still very poor. The only way to boost your grade is study a month in advance for the final. Holme was very negative towards his students and at one point assumed the people not sitting at the front were deaf or just careless because of their seating.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you have a bad grade. Sucks. You can't recover from it. He literally will examine you on things that are not covered very well and you are souly responsible to figure things out with the textbook outside of class. WORST CLASS. If I had another teacher I would have passed.

Got 100% in attendance, homework, quizzes, and the paper. Didn't do the best on two of the tests and got a bad grade in the class. His test have random questions about material he maybe mentioned for 20 seconds during a lecture.

He is a nice guy but you have to do well on the tests to do well in the class. He moves very quickly so I would recommend rewatching his lectures, going to SI,and getting extra help if you struggle with chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Test-heavy, not a lot of opportunities to recover from bad grades so make sure you do good on the tests! Attendance is graded, he's a good lecturer but he goes fast so if you struggle with Chemistry get a lot of outside help; they really want you to read the textbook. Holme is very condescending when asked questions! Also does not round up grades!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was really hard to pay attention to.

Dr. Holme is a fairly decent professor. He obviously knows his stuff which can often come across as arrogant. He's decent and gives you good feedback if you ask for it. His lectures are usually pretty quick paced but he does a decent job of explaining things. Not my favorite professor but far from a bad professor.

I had him last fall and at the beginning of the semester I really enjoyed his class. But by the end I didn't care for his attitude and how he spoke to students. He would talk down and was also passive aggressive. But his teaching style was good, but if you had a hard time understanding chemistry in high school I would go to the SI sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: From what I heard while taking the class, he is the easiest general chemistry professor. Mostly because hes been teaching for awhile. He made material easy to understand but he would go on tangents unrelated to the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected

reviews.comment: Great professor! Posts slides before each class and lecture recordings after. Uses lots of examples and practice for difficult concepts. You can tell he really cares about his students. Tests are tough but he provides lots of resources to help you do well. Would definitely take a course with him again.

Dr. Holmes tells you what you need to know the exam and final, but he does not teach it. He briefly goes over topics and his tests are very difficult. He does offer two retakes which helps a lot. You may go over a unit for a week and not one question from that unit will be on the exam. Extremely passive aggressive as well. Go to SI to pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Holme knows his stuff and has a tendency to go fast in lecture. Outside practice and studying is definitely required for his class. Overall a really good class and as long as you try hard you'll be fine.

Overall a pretty good professor, he lets you retake two of your exams at the end of the semester in Chem177. He's tough but very fair and as long as you read the book and do the homework you should be fine.

Cares about the students and wants to see you succeed. His lectures are fun and he makes it interesting. He does his exams so he tries to make it fair.  If you have questions go to his office hours he will be happy to explain it to you. As long as you go to lecture, read the book, do the homework and practice you will be alright.

Dr. Holme is funny and enthusiastic, but chemistry is really hard. He tries to make the class fun, but be prepared to study. I was retaking chemistry from high school where I got a really good grade, but ended up with a B- in his class. The tests are difficult because they're from the chem department, so go to SI and ask questions.
Highly recommend if you can get his class!

Dr. Holme was always super enthusiastic and made the class fun. Chem is a lot of work in general but if you keep up and go to class you'll do just fine. Oh and study for tests, they're standardized within the department and can be kind of difficult.

Lectures were fairly interesting and helped with understanding the content. Clicker points made up a large percentage of the grade (over 8%) so it is helpful to go to class. Pretty funny and definitely knew a lot about chemistry.

I started out this semester with full confidence I was going to ace the course with Dr. Holme. As the semester went on, I started banking on maybe getting a C. I ended up with a B-, so I can't complain. Not the grade I wanted, but not worth retaking. Study. Go to class. Go to SI. Get a tutor. Chemistry is hard, so be prepared to work.

Took this class for a science credit, and really didnt mind it. It had interesting content in it, and Holme was a good teacher and really knew what he was talking about. He should really get a laptop case for his stuff, he uses an old cardboard box to carry his stuff around. Hes a good professor and interesting class.
He is pretty funny and he really explains concepts well in lecture. He uses clicker questions every day so go to lecture. His grading is very fair but also pretty easy.

He's a really interesting professor. He makes things very clear in class and make sure the students understand. He gives students the chance to actually learn the material not just do things for points. Tests are pretty straight forward.

Holme is a really good professor, he helps his student learning chemistry by different methods. However, the huge problem is that he separate his lecture and the tests. Basically, his lectures doesn't cover even 10% of the tests. Other than that, he is a really good teacher.

His lectures are good but he doesn't seem to cover the material given on tests completely. Overall a really tough class and not the best teacher for it, especially since he is more engineering geared!

He's a good teacher that makes lecture interesting.  Be warned that clickers are used daily to check if you're showing up so go to the lectures.  If you don't the a fair chunk of your grade could go missing.

He is very goofy but that makes him hilarious. From his background n chemistry you know he is very very knowledgeable in the field. Chem 160 is a joke so you might as well enjoy the class with Professor Holme!

I originally heard he was a great teacher, but being in his class this semester I realized he is not. I am a good student and always advocate for myself. I have not heard back from him 2 separate times via email and when I talk to him in class he blows me off. It is his last semester at Iowa State so he might have given up. Very disappointed.

Professor Holme is seriously one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's a very nice guy and is flexible with deadlines if you talk to him. The tests are primarily open note, and anything on the test is covered in the notes during class. Loved this class and Holme also!

Professor Holme, or "T. Holme" as I like to call him, is a boss! Undoubtably the best professor I've ever had. Exams are difficult but managable. If you do well on the final, he will go back and change your grade from the previous exams. You can literally go from a D to an A! He is a genius and unbelievably helpful. Awesome guy.

Attendance is a must due to clicker points. If you print the lectures slides as notes you will do well. Pay attention during class as 95% of the material on the exams is covered in class. Basically, the only grade that matters is the final. Since he gives resurrection points, if you do poorly on previous exams, your grade can easily go from C to A.

He is a great professor. The course work was very difficult but he made the class enjoyable. He goes out of his way to help (has review sessions, virtual office hours, etc.) especially during finals time. I highly recommend him as a professor and I wish I could take more classes with him.
He makes the lectures interesting and they seem to go by really fast. By using clicker questions he gets you involved and it doesn't seem like such a huge class. The tests are challenging but doable.

Holme would definately fit in on the Big Bang Theory cast if your trying to get a mental picutre.  Hes cool but Chemistry is just not my cup of tea and I am I smart guy, yet I've failed almost every test! Pretty hard class if you have no chemistry experience.  If you like Chemistry it should be a breeze!

Dr. Holme is a great lecturer. He wrote the textbook, so he definitely knows his stuff, but he makes it easy to understand. Lectures aren't dry, he even throws in a little humor sometimes. I highly recommend him.
Lectures are clear and not boring. Doctor Holme does his best to keep the material relevant and fairly easy to understand. Not an easy course, but if you put the effort in, you will be rewarded.
Good teacher and easy to listen to. Makes class interesting. Not much need for the book, since he is the author and his notes are very comprehensive.
Could pretty much make up all of your tests in the final so very helpful.  He was pretty funny and he really knew what he was talking about.

Good professor who really knows his stuff.  Lectures were on topic and provided a good overview.  The tests were fairly difficult and were graded very strictly.  However, you can make up loads of points on the final.  Go to class because clicker points are big.  Difficult class but still pretty good.
Good teach and a good guy. This class is tough unless you put in the work. Go to the lectures and read the book and read the book and read the book. (the book is the key to this class)

Prof. Holme makes great strides to ensure that his students understand the material, but the grading is un-necessarily strict.  The TA's are unforgiving when grading exams and quizzes, with little to no partial credit being given on long problems. Also, the occasional substitute teacher talks to the class like they're retarded. It hinders learning.
Great teacher. Wrote the book. Class doesn't take up too much time.

Good teacher. makes some very nerdy jokes.  Got through the first part of the class okay with prior chemistry knowledge.  I did have to read the book towards the end but overall the class isn't that hard if you do the work and take notes.  He is a good teacher, he knows his stuff(wrote the book).

Decent.  Chem 167 for a lot of people is one of those classes you HAVE to take but don't really want to. I didn't think I would have to attend lecture  as I took Chem in High School, but he grades you on clicker questions in class so without going you loose a significant amount of points.  Pretty disappointing.

Takes a little time for the student getting used to having 500 classmates in your class, but I am sure he doesn't mind having this many because we all have to buy his book. We also have to buy retard clickers that are expensive to replace just so we can prove to him that we are paying attention in class.

Prof. Holme is a good lecturer, he really knows his stuff and he attempts to make lecture interesting by breaking it up with clicker questions and discussion. Tests are kind of hard, but if you read the book, and go over the study guide, it's easy to get a good grade. also take advantage of all the extra credit offered.
He is not a bad teacher, but does took too much about insignificant things on a regular basis.
he did write the book. he knows his stuff. lectures are confusing, but you can allways talk to him in his office; hes very open.
good

pretty good professor. he is very easy to understand and wrote the textbook, so he konws his stuff. some things are a little confusing and with 400 people in the class, it usually doesn't get cleared up during lectures.
A good teacher who knows his stuff.  He wrote the textbook! Lots of opportunities for extra help.  Some lecture things can be a bit confusing.  Tests aren't too bad, just do some thorough studying.
Not a good professor
No Comments

Holme is a decent professor and a nice guy. He's easy to understand, but not always easy to follow. I didn't think his lecture notes were very helpful. I would recommend trying to take the class with Greenbowe if possible because he uses more examples and explained things more clearly. If you got to Holme's lecture regularly, you'll learn from him.

Hollander is an excellent teacher, gives practice exams just like the real exam. He makes this course easy. Oddly nobody else in the class seems to try at all? I'm shocked at peoples lack of effort. Students just won't show up for group presentation days, the exam scores are low even tho he gives you the questions prior to the exam, I find it odd.

Dr. Hollander has a wealth of information that he gets so excited to share that knowledge when given the opportunity. I met with him multiple times over the semester to discuss specific aspects of the class. I especially appreciated how he would explain the context of historical events.

Great professor who loves to explore many specific details regarding Greek civilization. You can tell that he's truly passionate about this subject and enjoys teaching and as such it's enjoyable to learn from him. Major projects were essays, which were typically not difficult as long as you followed the rubric. Very approachable and knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hollander is very passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are informative and sometimes entertaining! He is a very kind professor, but grades by very few things. Expect to read A LOT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors

He tended to be very vague in his directions for assignments and covered so much content in class that it was impossible to tell what I actually needed to know. The lectures were a mess, so it was super hard to follow along. If you're a history person, this may be for you, but as a Classics minor, this class sucked.

Great professor, had him for the first time Hist 211 was offered (then 211X). Was easily reachable by email and in his office, and even went out of his way to meet me after Ross was closed from the fire. Also got along well with his TA and seemed to communicate with him well. 10/10 would take again
Pretty funny, but a bit of work
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: David is an awesome teacher. I just took His201 as an elective and it was worth it. You will do a lot of reading and a small amount of writing (1 page papers).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I loved going to the lectures and hated when they ended. You have to remember a lot for the tests including dates so studying can be a pain. Nothing discussed in recitations is on tests and is not useful to learning the actual material, but attendance is mandatory anyway. The TA I had is not lenient if you have trouble printing and is very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hollander is very good in lecture and makes a very clear and coherent point through his facts and slides. His TAs are terrible. But he is very fair, and requires a lot from you but do the work and youll be fine.

Dr. Hollander's class was a very fun and interesting class if you like ancient history. His lectures are entertaining and I looked forward to going to class every day. He is very knowledgeable and takes time to answer questions in class. His study guides have everything you need to know on them so preparing for tests is a breeze.
As long as you show up for class and take notes, you should be fine. Tests aren't that hard and he is really clear with what he is looking for in your answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Hollander is really passionate about his topic and that bleeds though into his lectures. For those students who want to put in the extra effort this class is very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hollander is great lecturer in my opinion. He's passionate and informative. Tests are easy if you go to lecture, pretty much all term based. Go to the lectures and recitations and pay attention and this is an easy A. Don't even need the textbook really, but you'll need the source book for the recitation papers which are easy. My TA was awesome.

Lectures are interesting, but skips over a lot of important information that you will need for test. Read the book. Study guides give you exactly what you need to know for the test, however beware exact dates need to be know and there is a lot to remember. Not the class to take if you're looking for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lecture is only interesting if you are into what he is lecturing about.  Attendance is not mandatory but do not fall behind.  You will regret it when you start studying for the exam.  Do not take if you're looking an easy-A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is dry/boring lecture heavy with participation based recitations. There are 3 tests based on very specific term definition (who what when where why), an essay that has to be incredibly in-depth to even get full credit, and readings, to the point where you are given a passage and have to define it like the terms.  Twice a unit papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor is definitely one of my least favorites I have had at Iowa State. His lectures are extremely dry and hard to focus on, I had a hard time staying awake many days. His tests are very long and difficult, class average was always under a 50%. He gives review sheets, but they are extremely broad and really not helpful at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very passionate, and funny if you enjoy historical humor. This class requires that you work, I didn't read the textbook until two days before the test and it took me 17 hours to complete the review guide, so don't fall behind. The review guide is exactly what is on the test so study that and you're fine, I got a 95% on that exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely boring lectures and very hard to stay engaged during class. The professor is very long winded in his explanations which makes it very hard to stay awake in class. Review sheets for tests are extremely extensive and would be much more beneficial if they would cover more of what is actually on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor! Very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. The key to class is studying and completing the reading responses. As long as you study and attend class, the course is easy.

Very boring to listen to in lectures. Study guides covered extensive details but less than half was used on exams. Recitations were pointless and didn't go over anything from lectures, but go because it is graded on attendance.

His lectures weren't all that interesting but you learn everything you need to know. Before each exam he gives you a list of terms and essay questions (which are all covered in the book and lecture) and if you study those, it's easy to do well on the tests. Recitation was pretty irrelevant but attendance is taken so go. Overall, a good prof.

I think he's a great professor.  It's better if you're engaged with his class, and ask questions, because they help with the essay part of his exams.  Extensive list of vocab/term words that you should study before exam.  Exams are fairly easy if you at least go to class and take good notes plus go to your recitation (always helpful).
opinionated and difficult

Dr. Hollander is a nice guy, but he can be pretty dry during lecture. Is enthusiastic about topics he likes such as the Romans. Tests were extremely easy, just use the study guide he provides. Reading the textbook isn't really necessary. TA was great, graded everything on completion. If you want an interesting professor look elsewhere.
A really smart guy, but not an amazing teacher. Most of the time he's speaking AT you instead of TO you. The tests are fairly easy.

Hollander is so boring, his lectures aren't really relevant to the tests...which are vocab words and essays...ALL OF WHICH CAN BE FOUND IN THE BOOK! just buy the book, go to you recitation, study vocab, you'll pass.. i went to the lecture twice and passed with a B+
Dr. Hollander is a great teacher! his lectures are super easy to listen, and outlined ahead of time online, I completely recommend taking courses with him.

I took History 201 with him and I loved it. But I'm a history junkie. Dr. Hollander is kinda hard to hear sometimes but if you just ask him he'll put a microphone on. He's very book heavy for the tests.
Very nice guy.  Easy A for me.  I would love to take more of his courses.  I took Roman Civ.

I thought I would really enjoy Hist 403 - I thought wrong. His lectures were all PowerPoint slides and would give us information that was completely pointless to the class and our two tests of the semester. I decided to save myself from a lifetime of carpal tunnel and stopped taking notes. He seems to have his favorites, too. Never again.
Dr. Hollander is a great teacher. If you have an opportunity to take his class, do so. Just be sure that you do the readings.

For a lecture class with 200 people in the room, Dr. Hollander does a good job pushing through all of the material. For a lower level class the test are a lot of work, but there is a lot of material and its his way of making sure you know it.  Do the work and you will get at least a B.
great intersting professor. test are a little hard
He is very passionate about teaching, which is a rarity at the collegiate level. His lectures are interesting. I just wish the tests were more traditional multiple choice tests.
Great professor. Makes class interesting. Study key people and you will do just fine.

I had him for half a semester while Bailey was still in Europe.I could not focus on what he was saying because he is always moving his hands in circles.He had three different positions in which he rotates his hands.You will get lost in these three positions and the circles and you wont be able to pay attention to him.
I would not recomend this class at all. The tests are really hard and that's basically all your grade is in this class.
This guy is a very bad professor.  He makes no sense in class, the TA sucks, expects way too much out of intro-level undergraduate level students.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS
The class is hard to begin with (had to write 3 papers, 1 25pg paper) but he gives you all the materials you need to succeed. He'll help you out if you go to him.
He is a good teacher but very boring.  He tries to make class fun but he can't.  His test are easy if you study a lot.

Read your book, and pay attention in class. This guy is good and has a dry sense of humor, but for the love of God, turn your cell phone off and don't do anything to make him mad during class. Can be an elitist, but he's a good professor and thats all that matters

I wanted to take this course because I am studying abroad in Rome.  It ends up that this course deals a lot with reading literature from the time period we discuss in class and then going over the history.  It doesn't sound that interesting, but he is very passionate about the subject and made me like the class :-)
No Comments
Getting outdated, program pattern is great, condescending but manageable, self-consumed

Dr. Rajan is a great professor who really cares about his students. Throughout the semester he has an anonymous survey where you can make suggestions on how to make lectures better. He really does listen to them and tailors his classes around the students learning styles. The homework assignments are hard and long but the tests aren't bad.
Probably the best professor I've had at Iowa State. Really cares about his students and class.

This is a relatively easy course in 2018. He writes his own interpreters on top of java to create a lot of mini programing languages intended to highlight the current topic he's teaching at that time in the course. He's a nice guy, if a little condescending. Solid 5/7 in terms of respecting students. However to his credit: very fair class.

Great professor. It was an advanced class the broaden knowledge about programming language. Got to read a lot of articles, but they are all state of art. You have to present 1 paper by yourself, expect to spend time on it. Also, 1 big project. It helps that he made you do several deliverables to keep up with work. Love the class
learned a lot in this class,  homework are long but cover new concepts that you wouldn't see in other courses
Lectures were difficult to understand but homework helped a lot. Very interesting content to the class and he respected us greatly. Restructuring the class to not be taught in Scheme was a huge plus.
Many.. but nice hws
Very good professor, would take another class taught by him.
Hridesh is a great professor. He cares about his subject material and passing that knowledge on to the students. He is also a good human: sincere, funny, caring.
Spoke through his hand and was rather unclear. The course was in Scheme which made it difficult to want to learn, but Hridesh was a fairly decent teacher.
I agree with everything the previous rater said. Hridesh is an excellent instructor that constantly tries to improve his technique.

Overall I can't say I enjoyed 342, but that's more due to the subject material. EOPL Scheme is a terrible language to do anything useful with, and you'll spend much of the semester fighting with it. Hridesh himself is a very competent instructor and is helpful in office hours. Perhaps a bit condescending, though, and way too enamored with Scheme.
Hang onto everything you hear in this guy's class, it's all pure gold. The anti-pattern lectures were the funniest. He's a true programmer - quality, humor, and occasionally jittery.
Ok. Told good jokes once in a while.

Great prof - very helpful and willing to work with you.  Wants to make sure you learn from his class, unlike most professors.  Also wants to make sure you get a good grade in his class.  One of the best in the ComS dept.

A very good lecturer who teaches in an effective and intuitive way, with a good mix of examples and theoretical discussion. After-class help hours are amazing since he takes the time to make sure you know the concept and is good at understanding where the textbook homework may have left out details.
