JLMC 406 with Catherine was the best. Her slides are super easy to follow, the book was relatively cheap, and there are no tests. LITERALLY NONE. Expect to write a lot of memos, but they're only a page each, and the group project is really easy too. You can tell Catherine loves teaching and is super passionate. Easy A with a great teacher!
Bosuk is an engaging and fun lecturer who clearly cares about and is knowledgeable in the content that he is teaching.
Good teacher but dont expect him to actually care about your personal life. If you need extra time or extensions, he wont care and you are on your own.

Bosuk was a great Professor! His mind is really fascinating and he offers good feedback. Would take DSNS 102 in the spring. He sometimes doesnt leave enough feedback, but overall he does an adequate job. His projects that he assigns are much more diverse than the other professors, so I would take him again. Will push you to develop a story in art.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bosuk is hands down my favorite professor I have had so far. He cares so much about your well being, is willing to help you in whatever way possible, and genuinely cares about you and your work. he gives fantastic feedback and is always accessible. He has responded to me multiple times at 3 am and is definitely the best professor you can have !!

Bosuk Is one of the best professors I have had up to this point he brings a unique energy and outlook into the design studio. He allowing students to take risks and explore a multitude of styles while having fun with it. He expects high-quality work but is very good at aiding students to reach that level of effort and thought.
Bo is a great 102 professor. Very knowledgable, kind, and really wants his students to succeed. Gives good feedback and makes class fun!

Bo is a great design professor. He gives you great individual feedback and will push your limit to make you a better designer. He's funny and giggles a lot, makes class fun and he's very understanding if you are running behind on a project. Would reccomend for 102 prof!

Bosuk is such a nice professor, he is so willing to help with whatever. You can talk to him about anything and he is a good listener. He, understand design and really seems to have a passion for sharing his knowledge with students. He loves donuts!

Her class is very boring, HUGE stickler about deadlines and WILL NOT work with you to accept any late work/ extend your deadline, even if you explain your personal matters. Class has been in session for less than 1 month and she has cancelled TWICE already. When she does attend class she's late. Reminds me of Roz from Monsters Inc. She's rude.
Ms Hyatt is so sweet! I'm so happy to have her, just listen to her and you will do good! I Love the dog!
Shes real helpful and seems like a nice ladie, but wait till you get your paper back.  Watch out, shes a very strong feminist!

This was the best class I ever took!  This class helped me out a great deal.  I loved that she was so interested in the subject.  The class kept me very interested and challenged me a lot.  I am so glad I took this class!!!
She cancelled class more than once a week, when we did have class it was extremely boring...
No Comments

Unbelievably interesting class.  I loved how she was so interested in the subject.  I learned things in this class that I will be able to take to my future classes.  Definitely sign up for her course if you get the chance.

WHATEVER YOU DO, DO NOT TAKE A CLASS FROM HER! SHE IS THE WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD IN MY ENTIRE LIFE. SHE WILL GIVE QUIZES ABOUT STUFF YOU SHOULD NEVER HAVE TO KNOW AND GIVE YOU BAD GRADES ON PAPERS FOR NO REASON WHATSOEVER. sHE THINKS EVERYTHING IS A POWER GAME AND SHE HAS TO WIN.
seems to be unclear on what exactly she wants to teach. changes her mind and "lectures" on the most dull, boring subject for sooooooooo long time. That class hurt my brain.

Unbelievably boring.  It's like she's always searching for something to say to fill in the time.  She takes info that can be explained in 5 min. and drags it out for ever!!!  She's partialy blind or something so she has a seeing eye dog that makes weird noises through out class but she is CUTE!!!

I have Schneider for CHE 357. His lectures are beyond boring and are usually extremely hard to follow. The exams are really hard and sometimes he decides not to post any homework for a given unit, so you have absolutely nothing to practice with or study from. Resort to the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Schneider's lectures were generally quite informative. He is very knowledgeable on the topic and is willing to help. The exams can be tough, but the course also had an adjusted grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Schneider's class is difficult and challenging, but definitely worth it. He genuinely cares about his students and is very easy to reach outside of class, despite his busy schedule. If you want to learn a course well take it with Schneider.

My problem with this class is you arent able to see how you are in the class with the homework. He will assign super hard homework problems but he wont give you the answers to them and his grading is unclear to where you messed up. His practice tests are irrelevant to the material that will actually be in the test. Overall it's very difficult
Exams are way hard but he's a great professor!

Dr. Schneider expects a lot out of you and gives you what you need to get to his level of understanding. Material is more difficult but gives you an actual understanding of class. Super helpful after class and office hours even with his busy schedule he will make time for you.

Schneider is wonderful. His exams were difficult but fair. The content itself is not what stumps most people, it's the way you study that counts. Take his advice and go talk to him during office hours. He's incredibly helpful, and he also has a good sense of humor.

He is super smart and knows exactly what he is doing. That being said his hw and tests are super hard, so make sure you are prepared. Very clear speaker, but like most ChE teachers, he uses a ton of technical words that takes some getting use to. Side note: he says measurement and process weird and it kinda bothers me

Good Professor, Makes an extremely boring class as interesting as it possibly could be. Homeworks and group homeworks were hard, but helpful and he is always willing to help in office hours, but the subjects are very confusing and you usually leave still confused. His tests are EXTREMELY hard, but you are better prepared for 357 if you have him.

he is helpful.BUT!!!!! I don't know what he said at all. plus his hand writing is horrible.Never post the hw solutions or explain the hw during class unless you go to his office hours. But even when you go to ask, he will keep asking you more and more questions and in the end, u still get confuse.

You should read his online notes prior to class and the chapter prior to the week to understand the concept, 1st. You will learn how to think as an engineer in his class, but if you want a Candyland Class, switch majors. Chemical Engineering isn't designed to be easy or everyone would be one with the salary you make after graduation.

You should read his online notes prior to class and the chapter prior to the week to understand the concept, 1st. You will learn how to think as an engineer in his class, but if you want a Candyland Class, switch majors. Chemical Engineering isn't designed to be easy or everyone would be one with the salary you make after graduation. ~D.R.
. does not know how  to teach at all. Given super hard assignments, expect us to learn everything by ourself.

Horrible Teacher. Knows his stuff about fluid dynamics but has no idea how to actually teach it to students. Is super unhelpful at office hours, answers questions with questions. STAY AWAY FROM GETTING HIM AS A TEACHER!!
Great Guy. Good Teacher. Always eager to help and is enthusiastic about the subjects.

He knows Fluids, but he does not know how to explain anything to his class, much less have you understand it. He'll mess up equations, incorrectly define variables, get lost during class. Homework/exams are not like class examples or anything! Very nice in person though.

I have to disagree with this last post, Schneider is not a bad professor. He's gonna challenge the **** out of you, and but he's always there to help you understand, he expects you to make the extra effort. He's a very difficult professor, but believe I know more about Fluids because I had him.

Student beware!!! He is a horrible teacher, to say the least. He pulls equations out of thin air and doesn't explain how he got them. He refuses to post homework solutions after assignments have been submitted. He is never available outside of class. His test are also unrealistic. DO EVERYTHING YOU CAN TO NOT GET THIS TEACHER!!!!!!!!!!

EE577: Dr. Dobson uses a confusing grading scheme, two exams make up 82% of your grade, and the exams must be taken on Sunday night from 7-9PM.  This includes the final, which was Sunday night before finals week.  Further, these exams are "take home," but still closed book, so what's the point?  Makes it much more difficult than it has to be.

Professor Dobson is a very engaging lecturer with a good sense of humor. He covers the material very well and wants you to succeed. The class is very test-heavy, and you never really know your grade, but if you do all the work asked of you. You will end up with a good grade.
Dr. Dobson was a fantastic professor. His lectures were engaging and very understandable. Easily one of the best classes I've ever taken!

Tough subject to teach, but Ian does a decent job. Sadly, you get no feedback on your exams and he makes you memorize derivations of every equation. If you don't get a good group, you fail, making it a roulette with your grade. Memorize the homework and you have a fighting chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super unorganized and assumes you already know the content. Every homework is deriving theoretical equations and expects you memorize dozens of complex equations. Would not recommend!
Very good professor. Make sure you go to class and take notes. Exams are VERY similar to homework so make sure you know it.
Amazing professor. You will pass if you do homeworks diligently.

He is a terrible professor. Expect to have lots of homework and for it to be graded but not be given solutions. He believes tests are for assessment only so you will not get your tests back and he discourages you from coming in and learning from them. No lecture slides are posted. Homework is graded on a alpha beta scale which is confusing.

Ignore the rater below, this person/group complains when the going gets tough,  lookup "Santosh Pandey". The same group of delinquents complained about him(5/5 ratings beforehand). You should be wary of the opinions of fellow students. They are not as educated as any professor and their thoughts/opinions not as intellect. With age comes wisdom.

Doesn't Provide any feedback or answers for Homeworks. No lecture notes/slides, so take your own. But it is only offered at 8AM, so good luck staying awake or paying attention, as he is not a particularly engaging or interesting lecturer, especially with no slides.  Went to office hours,  he was decidedly unhelpful.  Tests  CURVED.  Horrible Prof.
Great professor.  A little hard to follow in class if you're not engaged.  Go to his office hours.

As long as you go into his office hours before the tests they are a breeze. VERY fair curves on all exams, but no solutions on the homework sets made it fairly difficult. All in all, a nice guy who is more than willing to go the extra mile to help you out.
One main issue I had with him is that he would not provide solutions to the homework. Also, he refuses to hear arguments about grading on exams. He did curve the exams generously however.

Igor is overall a good professor who I would recommend, the class seemed a bit disorganized at times but he is very sweet and understanding, always offering help and does a good job explaining most of the design topics covered in class. The class did not feel difficult and I barely ever had to work on anything outside of it as long as I showed up.

Super sweet and understanding, willing to work with you if you had things come up. Attendance is graded, but he allowed 2 classes to be missed before it would affect your grade. Super easy yet educational class--I learned a LOT but also never ever felt stressed by this class.
He is the sweetest professor. I love how understanding he is. He'll never make you feel stupid for not knowing something. He is patient, and he gives good feedback.

He is a nice man that will not go after you for not participating. I took his class online and was allowed to have my camera off and microphone muted the whole time, which I liked since I liked to work on other classes' homework during this time.
He's a very considerate and passionate teacher. For me it was my first design class ever but he made it fun and informative.
Very powerful teacher, gives clear and concise feedback and is readily available to help.

He explains everything really clearly, has really helpful handouts that summarize the class exercises. There is always time left after he does a tutorial to ask for help. He also encourages you to show your artistic talents and make the projects more fun.
I learned to work with a lot of powerful tools

As a freshie in college amidst this pandemic, I feel super privileged to have gotten Professor Wistey as my instructor for this class! She gives great feedback on assignments, is kind and caring to all her students, and is genuinely invested in your success in her class. She's also good at communicating deadlines. (very helpful in an online class)

Ms. Wistey has a great interactive and discussion based teaching style. The papers and assignments were very easy to complete. She also gives amazing feedback on your writing, and really helped push me to become a better writer.

I had Ms. Wistey for English 250 and loved her! She was an amazing teacher, awesome feedback on every assignment. When you struggled with a paper or presentation she offered help and she was a very fair grader. I would definitely take this class again! As with every English class at ISU, you need to actually attend class.

Jeff is the best instructor I've ever had. He is nice, knowledgeable and has a good sense of humor. He is generous as well-not just simply being kind but help the students to learn. For example, when the class didn't do well in a quiz, he will give an extra credit quiz not just curve the grades. I'm now even more interested in plants because of him

As the leader of the Hort program, Doc Iles can come off as a no-nonsense professor. But he's the sort of professor that believes in tough love. He's not a hard grader by any means, but you have to put int he work to get a grade--and that work is not hard at all. Good-natured, good-humored, and always a blast to have class with him in the morning.
This guy is the ish! I seriously never had a dull moment in class. And the tests were take home tests, what more do you need?!?!?!

Dr. Cho does a pretty good job of explaining exactly how to solve the problems. He won't reteach you knowledge you should know, like trig or simple integrals. There is a level of assumed knowledge for this course. But do the work, and don't cheat and you will accel. at this course. Great guy, good teacher, solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: In Ho Cho. is a solid professor for structural analysis. He is very accessible and willing to help out with any question. He gives out in-class quizzes, but these are generally very easy and he will help/answer questions. Tests are very similar to homework. To do well, go to class, work on homework in groups, and do not cheat on the homework.

Dr. Cho is fantastic. The course could be learned on one's own, but if you show up and does what he says you will be solid. Extremely helpful and available outside lecture times. Very timely email responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The chosen topics for this class is really good and interesting. You have to be present in class since almost every class has an in-class activity. Get prepared to get ZERO, since there are no extensions or partial credit for late assignments even if you are sick, which does not make sense. Other than that, I loved the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Cho is actually a very solid choice for structures. The homework follows what is learned in class. The tests are rather straight forward, and he doesn't design them to trick you.  The group project at the end of the semester is very easy. Overall, go to class, pay attention, do the in class assignments, you'll pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Online class was VERY difficult. Reading the book doesn't really help. Pay very close attention to the lectures & take good notes. His grading is outrageous and makes it difficult to get a B or higher.

Very hard exams.  I would avoid this professor if it could be helped.  He seems more interested in what we didn't know rather than what we did know.  I did well but I had to throw more time than what should be required for an entry level biology course.

This class is difficult to begin with, it would be nice to have a professor that helped. He does not respond very quickly to emails. I went to talk to him after a test. He asked my opinion as to why I was not doing well. We reviewed my test and the only thing he kept telling me was what I had told him! Not a helpful professor at all!

Dr I. made it clear that he was a reborn Christian and a creationist, and after a few very difficult exams, students started saying things like "Jesus loves you" in discussions, which I found annoying. His exams are hard, and 3/4 of the class failed or got a C. He answered e-mails quickly but didn't seem to know the answers to many questions.
Lectures can be quite boring; sometimes monotone voice

Do NOT take his course unless  it is a matter of life and death. I was a straight A student until I took it! His exams are IMPOSSIBLE. At the end of the semester, 40% of the class had a guaranteed F and 23% a D. Yes, he is nice, but it hardly matters when it comes to passing the course!! He says he curves but he does NOT.
Professor Ingebritsen was very helpful if you tried to get help.  He's not an easy A, but you learn something in the process.
if you want to take an online course, sign up but if want to be taught something, find someone else. very difficult tests. if you have to take it, read the book a lot.
His lectures were not clear, it felt like he did put a lot of preparation into them. He had a lot of "guest lecturers" which I found more helpful and easier to understand.
This guy is probably the worst professor I have ever had.  His tests have stuff on them that he doesn't tell us and aren't even in the book!

Incomprehensible. Her accent is the bad part - she just won't answer questions. Makes you feel like an idiot for not understanding chamfer angles like you've been studying it your entire life. Tough grader, not very helpful outside of class. Definitely makes you feel like just another face in the crowd instead of caring about you as a student.
Lectures were OK at best, but the criteria you're expected to know for tests isn't clear at all
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Had her for 248 and 448 and I don't understand anything taught in these classes

She is constantly needing to be corrected in class. Doesn't seem to know the material. Doesn't work with students AT ALL if they have conflicts. Homework solutions are often incorrect. doesn't post grades to grade book. Doesn't follow university policies. She hands back tests in a giant pile and makes you search through hundreds of tests for yours.

Doesn't allow questions in exams, doesn't show up to exams, doesn't post useful notes, messes up during in class problems, has mistakes in posted homework solutions, words exam questions poorly, can't answer questions to a satisfactory level during class, makes students purchase textbook for use during exam (no pdfs of texbooks allowed)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Requires students to buy the textbook. Literally you can't complete the exams without the textbook. She is also a terrible lecturer and confuses students even more after they ask questions. She can barely answer questions and explain theory. Only upside is that the exams and quizzes are super easy and the homework isn't required.

Her teaching is mediocre and her test are easy if you studied really hard for it. However, she is a horrible lecturer. I went to her office to clarify on something she taught in class. I end up being more confused after going to her office hours. Her homework solutions are wrong and incomplete. She was also late for her office hours sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Requires students to have the TEXTBOOK for exams instead of printing off relevant tables. Awful at answering questions both in and outside of class. Doesn't show up to proctor exams and won't let TAs answer questions during exams. Doesn't seem to care about students understanding the material. Answers inclass questions with "that's a good question"

Had Rivero for IE 248 and I did not like the course but I have really enjoyed her IE 448 class so far. I believe this is the first semester she is teaching it but the grading criteria is a lot more lenient than Jackman's. I took this class with Jackman and had a bad experience, now I am enjoying it a lot more and learned a lot more with Rivero!

Rivero was arguably the worst professor I've had at ISU. She was unhelpful outside of class and pushed as much work on to her TA's as possible. She didn't seem to understand the material all that well when people asked questions and her accent made lectures super distracting. Her exact words when asked what to study: "Just memorize the slides"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Well Rivero is just an awful teacher. Never in my life have I ever had a professor that was just unmotivated at teaching. Straight up the worst IE teacher. Be prepare to memorize everything. At least in the final she told us what was coming. . . sort of. Just a horrible professor she needs to start caring. It gets easier towards the end.
Probably the worst class I've ever taken at ISU. Be ready to be taught by TAs instead of her. Lab reports are ridiculous, tons of memorizing. I hate this class!

Rivero really left me with a bad impression of Iowa State.  She refuses to help you unless you consult with a TA first, even though your schedule may conflict with the TA's office hours.  The grading is ridiculous.  On tests she expects the exact word-for-word answers from slides.  This class requires intensive memorization so study daily!!

Took this class because it was required. Tests and quizzes are over very specific questions. You must write down what she says word for word to get credit. Doesn't let you know what your grade looks like at all through the year. Don't expect a high grade in the labs (which amount to 35% of your grade) overall worst class I've taken at ISU.

The class is honestly one of those IE classes you have to get through. Be prepared to memorize literally everything in order to succeed in the class and to spend a lot of time writing the lab reports and proofreading them thoroughly before you submit them in order to try to get a good grade on them. She says that's not true but DO NOT believe her.

She is very strict and nit-picky about grading. If you don't have EXACTLY what she wrote down it's wrong. She says it's not about memorization but it 100% is. If you can memorize concepts and definitions then this class will be pretty easy.  You must attend class though or you will fail.

Nice woman, not a very good teacher. She gets better as the semester goes on though. Class attendance is mandatory otherwise she fails you. In this class your TA is your best friend. Never gave us any idea as to what our grades were, so no point in trying to guess what you are getting in her class. Homework is optional, and no Friday class.
She just writes the notes on the blackboard but her handwriting is horrible.  She is a nice woman but not a good teacher.

The amount of work for this class is ridiculous. The way tests and labs are graded is ridiculous. Be ready to spend hours and hours on boring lab reports and then get a grade like a 50 or a 60.  Anyways, this class  has the potential to be an interesting class but it isn't.  Worked my ass off and ended up with a D

Course wouldn't be that difficult if the tests were simplified a little bit. She grades tough on these tests and she feels like the lab grade should make up for poor grades. She is extremely boring and at times a huge jerk about the way she talks to her students. Not a good professor.
The WORST teacher I have ever had. She is unreasonable, rude, unfriendly, overreacts and does not present information well. The material wasn't hard she just is an awful "teacher"

Dr Rivero is a nice lady, good professor but this class is a lot of work. The first Solidworks lab assignment was  very challenging and so was the first lab. Grading is harsh. Unless you are a Manufacturing nut, the  lectures are going to suck, one of those IE classes you just got to get through but it will be very challenging.

Professor Minefee is incredible! The lectures are interesting, he stays up to date on world news, and I am learning so much without a lot of pressure. He really wants you to learn and help you in any way. The assignments are not stressful, but I still learn a lot by doing them. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

Highly recommend this class and Professor Minefee. He is very engaging in lectures and cares about his students. The material is interesting and he structures the class in a way that you'll actually learn the material with what you do. Overall, great professor and class.
Great Professor. Gets to know his students and actually cares about them. Willing to help if needed. Would recommend his classes to anyone.

Really nice guy if you are open minded. Lots of papers but they are short and easy; I am not a good writer at all and I did well in this course. He gives lots of readings but you can get by if you skip a couple, just be willing to discuss. You can usually make it up even if you don't read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Grade was based on 5 papers, book report, final paper, and attendance. Gives good questions to help you write paper. Class is just about educational diversity, so in-class discussion is mostly about your high school experiences. Good class if you're open minded and super nice guy.
Nice guy. Easy class.
I loved this class! It is completely reading, writing & discussion based, so if that's not your thing then avoid. But this class really made me think and applies many different skills!

This professor bases his class off of articles and essays. There are no tests or quizzes, which was nice, but there was a lot of reading and writing. This was an easy class. He required you attend class, but you could miss two within the semester. I would recommend this class if you enjoy writing and want easy.

Isaac Gottesman is a strange dude but his class is pretty easy.If you are good at writing papers then this class is for you because it is ALL papers,so if you can't write papers you are screwed. This class is extremely repetitive. You cover the same material the whole semester.If you want easy choose Isaac.If you want to learn choose Charles Achter

Isaac was an amazing professor. He pushed our original ideas of teaching and education to a new limit. He helped us understand the career we were about to enter. There were no tests-all essays-and they were all opinion based. His teaching style was great and was always available to talk. If given a choice, try to get Isaac.
Excellent teacher, very clear and patient. Her accent is not a problem.
No Comments

Great teacher--if you're looking for a 90-minute nap! Doesn't spell check powerpoints. Very confusing. Went to all classes before first test and got a D. Didn't go to class again except for review days before the second and final exams, and got B's.  Download notes from class website and use classtime to do online homework. No attendance taking!
Really was not a good professor at all. Material covers in class did not represent what was covered on the test well at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures are scattered with random information and little structure. Expects students to completely understand immediately and often takes frustration out on students during lecture. Avoid this teacher if you want to do well in chem

Some people really struggle in this class but I thought it wasn't that bad. She expects you to read the book before coming to class which nobody does. Fairly difficult homework every 2 weeks, some homework ideas aren't covered in lecture. My TA helped fill in what she didn't explain. Tests get curved pretty hard. Don't buy the book, it's useless.

Honestly if you have her on your schedule: switch. You will not have a good time in her disorganized lectures in which she is teaching you something totally irrelevant and will not be on the exam or she is showing you a useless demo.  Her homework is a mixture or random things that are not covered in lecture, in the book, nor in recitation.

Worst class I have ever taken at Iowa State. The tests sometimes are over things we never did in class, she is quite disorganized during lectures, and the lectures itself are extremely boring. I honestly learned more from my foreign TA during recitation. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

Worst professor I have had at Iowa State. The class consists on lectures in which she doesn't entirely understand how to teach. We're given homework with absolutely no information on how to do such problem. Most of the tests are nothing we learn in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: No need for her to be at Iowa State since her only answers to questions is to "look in the book".  The difficulty of lecture questions to homework assignments is unreal.  Homework is very difficult, and gives little instruction.  There's more instruction about how she will take points off for your name, section, etc.  CHANGE YOUR PROFESSOR.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took this class like many thinking it would be an easy science credit. I was wrong. While the class got off to a VERY rocky start I will say that it was not all terrible. The class is structured so that you can get a lot of points by doing simple things. This professor loves what she teaches and is very adaptive. The class can be easy if you read

I went into Chem 160 for an easier route to fulfilling one of my science credits for my major, little did I know Dr. Irmi would make this class so difficult. Her lectures are unorganized, she doesn't explain or go into detail about the material, tests don't match up to context, and is extremely unhelpful. I do not recommend this class.

Really just comes down to how much you put into the class. If you do the homework, study for tests, and go ask for help from the professorTAs, you'll pass with a pretty good grade. She didn't really help teach us some of the specific problems until a third of the way in, but I really learned a lot from the TAs in the recitation classes.

She doesn't teach. The rare times she did examples in class, she got confused and messed up halfway through. Her homework didn't cover what we were supposed to know for tests, and she never taught us what we were supposed to know either, so there was no real way to succeed in her class unless you remember everything from AP chem. Worst Prof ever.
Attendance is graded so you don't want to miss lectures, and you want to make a habit out of doing homework every day. Overall tedious course.

She is terrible at the lectures. Half the time she makes you look up the rest of the lecture when she runs out of time. She has cool experiments in the lectures. She is helpful when you ask her one on one but class wise not so much. Mastering chemistry for days!!!  Nomenclature test during resitation. Test suck but she does put up old ones to help.
Mastering chemistry for days. There's a graded assignment for every lecture. She never gets to everything she wants to in the lecture and often shows wrong numbers when working problems.

Avoid at all costs or get a good tutor. She is smart but not a good teacher. There is assignments over class materials before lecture so you don't know how to do any of it. Tests are hard and not like anything on quizzes. Never gets through lecture. Basically a self taught class

Irmi is a smart person but is not as good at relaying the message to the class. I hated coming to lecture because all she ever did was blow stuff up. The demonstrations took forever to set up so we would not get through everything.
Wonderful professor, easy quizzes and exams! (:

The course is intended to be fast-paced and difficult, but it's even more so with Dr. Irmi. I felt rushed in everything and dreaded lectures. This is the first class I've ever struggled in and the one exam I did exceptionally well on, I taught myself the entire material. If it weren't for recitation I wouldn't have gotten anything.

Dr. Schewe-Miller seems to not be able to take critique from students.Throughout this semester, she told my lecture that she knows she will get bad course reviews and she did notcare. It would be nice if  she would have reflected upon her teaching and realized that is was not working.  She is a nice and smart person, just not a good teacher.

She is generally very unprepared for lecture and rarely gets through all the material. Can almost be harsh and short if your trying to get help,which youll need since the lectures are borderline useless but attendance is mandatory. Fairly excessive workload with 4 homework assignments every week plus a quiz. Easily the worst professor ive ever had
If you want to spend an entire semester teaching yourself chemistry, you've choosen the right professor. She rushes through lectures and never explains anything.
Classes, are boring and very fast paced

Terrible professor.  She rushes through all of the material and talks about information not relevant to the topic you are supposed to be learning.  Plan on teaching yourself because you won't be learning anything from her
Worst professor! Rude and cant understand her. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

I depended on the textbook for the entire class. Lecture was useless. If you want to teach yourself and take easier tests, take her class. If you want to learn in lecture but have slightly more difficult tests, find a different section. Overall, she was a poor teacher, but the class was not difficult at all if you just spent a little time studying.
She spends much of lecture time with technical difficulties and boring demonstrations. Print off the lecture notes and read the text material and the class isn't difficult.

She is a horrible lecturer, she spends too much time on little things that are unimportant and does not go over equations. Read the book and get a tutor, I wish I would have switched sections. She is a professor here for research, and that's it.
Teacher is very knowledgeable but lacks teaching ability.

Nice person during office hours, horrible teacher. Always rushes through material, shows stupid demonstrations repeatedly that have no relevance. When I emailed her about her course her responses were very rude.

She's a nice person, but she teaches about every little detail, and then doesn't always have time to cover all of the important stuff. Her class goes much faster than the others, and has more tests. Her in-class reviews are also not helpful at all. I would pick a different professor if I took this class again.

Irmi is extremely nice and a great person but she's not the best teacher...she rushes through things and doesn't explain them very well. You basically have to teach yourself by reading the textbook and a tutor definitely helps. The chem homework she gives us doesn't really help either half of the problems never show up on the tests. She's okay.

Many people do not like Irmi, but I would have to say that I didn't mind her at all.  She sometimes doesn't explain things very well, but if you use the textbook as well, the class is not impossible.  Also, her tests are super easy!! I liked her :)
Terrible cant understand TA's if you take the class get a tutor or your done
She was more excited about her little experiments then she was about teaching the class. And the exams were impossible. Don't bother with her.
Not good teacher
Just a really bad teacher.  Never finishes her lectures, she rushes through everything and has no clue how to make anything understandable.  You're going to have to read the book for everything.
She has many technological mishaps, but has a sense of humor. The sometimes odd analogies she gives help you remember things.
The only good thing about her is that she gives out lecture slides before class to have. Everything else is bad.

Stresses the importance of working chemistry problems, yet does not do any examples any of them in lecture. Homework and recitation quizzes are worthless in preparation for exams, exam questions are much more complex than anything she prepares you for, especially if your prior understanding of chemistry is minimal. Get a tutor or a different prof.

She is one of the most unorganized lecturers I have ever had. I am a senior in chemistry, and her class is among my least favorite classes I have attended for my major. Her husband is amazing, and apparently it hasn't rubbed off on her in the slightest. In addition to her disorganization, she also puts WAY too much coursework out. It is staggering.
Easily one of the worst professors I have had. Does not teach the material, is harsh. Most people left her lecture and went to the other professor's. Would not recommend under any circumstances.

Do NOT take chem with Irmi. She goes through pre-prepared slides that don't have anything to do with tests, quizzes, or homework. On top of that, she barely gives you time to even look at the slides. When looking at scores on a test, she says "that's too bad" instead of actually doing something about it. Awful instructor.

She is a very smart person, but a terrible teacher. In class she goes through the slides very quickly and usually runs out of time and rushes at the end. She also has a lot of technology problems which makes class run late. Doesn't explain things well or is really complicated. She is foreign, but understandable. SI Sessions help a lot! Hard exam
She doesn't explain things very well and it is hard to keep up with her.

Some people found her rather difficult, but I liked her lectures and teaching style. She did sometimes go a bit quick, but other than that I liked her humor as well as her real-world connections to Chemistry
Terrible professor, does not work examples or explain concepts behind problems. Look for another professor if you're in Chem 167

I recommend taking chem 167 with a different professor. She belittles you when you ask her a question. Doesn't cover the difficult material that makes up exams and quizzes. Doesn't explain the problem solving and says, "that's basic geometry," or something of the sort. Overall, the class is difficult but if you put in massive time, you'll be fine.

She doesn't cover the same materials that the other sections do, making the quizzes and tests extremely hard. I would recommend going to other professor's lectures instead because they're easier to understand. She doesn't take enough time explaining the mathematical problems, instead talking about less difficult material.

Not the easiest professor to understand but speaks fairly good english (she's german). Exams involve a lot of math and not as much on basic concepts. TA's are a great help and so is reading the book. She goes very fast in class and uses clickers every day. not always the most helpful and sometimes gets off topic in class.

Irmi really wants her students to do well, she just doesn't always clearly explain the information. The course content is kind of difficult, but if you go through her old tests and the recitation quizzes you'll do fine. The book isn't really necessary, her notes give you all that she expects you to know. Overall, not a terrible class.

When she lectures she goes by the slides very fast and she reads the slide once but doesn't really explain anything after that. For homework and in class quizzes all you need is 80% and you get full credit for them. Study for the exams because they are hard. She said she was going to curve the class but then she didn't.

Horrible Professor. She assumes that you know every bit of Chemistry before taking the class. She doesnt explain concepts very well, she turned an easy study night into a cramming night before the final. When it comes down to the clicker questions, if it doesnt work after two tries, she says that half the class wont get points. GET A TUTOR!!!

She does not do a good job explaining concepts in lecture, she assumes everybody knows the material before attending, and the tests are extremely hard.  I highly encourage getting a tutor for this class.

Not a good professor. She went through things really fast and could never work the clicker points correctly. She did keep it somewhat entertaining with her humor but otherwise it was extremely boring. Really hard tests, and pointless review sessions. GET A TUTOR.
Hard to follow. Said one thing and did another. This class made me hate chemistry.

Overall, an ok teacher, but she did skip over alot of points and was all over the place. The only thing I liked was that she tried to make it simple despite the fact the chemistry is just a hard subject to learn. She did initially tell my class she would curve but did not in the end, so don't rely on a curve. The final is brutal as well

I think she was a very good professor. At times she went a little fast but the homework helped clarify key points to understand. Reading the book really helps for the test. My only complaint was that the only way to make up a test was the optional cumulative test.

This was her first semester teaching and she doesn't know what?s going on. Instead of teaching, she goes off on tangents. She expects us to know all the info ahead of time and our lives to be about Chemistry. The lab is quite easy, considering it doesn't cover any lecture material. Overall I would say she does a poor job of teaching this course
Teaches way to fast.  Commented one day that it was "not her job" to teach the equations even though thats what the test covered.  Jumps all over book and does not sync labs with lectures.

She jumps all over the book, and expects us to know everything before she teaches it to us, including things we've never even heard of before. She wastes too much  time complaining about people who hate chemistry and know that they will never use what is taught in this class. Very unorganized and inconsistent ways of teaching.

If you have to take a course with Dr. Yuan, find a different course. Feedback/grades would take over a month to receive so I never knew what my grade was. Insanely hard grader. I attended her office hours for help, questions were not answered, and I left even more confused. I would not recommend taking her classes.

My experience was quite unsatisfactory. Dr. Yuan consistently exhibits unresponsiveness, and it appears that her busy schedule often hinders her availability. Seeking help from her yields vague results, making self-teaching a more viable option. Additionally, the lectures are outdated. She is by far the worst professor I've ever had!

Dr. Yuan simplified the concepts and made them very easy to understand. The homework is not hard to finish and is just average level, but you have to pay attention to the team projects, cos your teammates will grade your performance through peer evaluation.

Often cancel her office hours. Even during her office hours, she never tells students what is correct answer when someone have question. She only think highly of her own academic research and ignores the feeling of her students. The course material was even five years ago. If you want to learn something new, I would not suggest you take her class

One of the worst professors I have had at ISU. Considers it cheating to work on assignments with classmates. Gives vague feedback on assignments. Only cares about her research and getting tenure which, judging by how many kids go to the dean to complain, hopefully wont happen. Dont recommend and if you get her switch out now.

At all costs, do not take this course with her. It will save you stress in the long run. I could go on for hours why she is a bad professor, just save yourself some time and take this course with a different professor.

Worst professor in the history of teaching. Brags often about her capacity to fail seniors and drown students in debt. Unlikable personality and combative disposition. DO NOT take this class with Yuan. Take it elsewhere or fail. Class average on an open book open note test was 45% no curve.

she is a tough grader and will tank your gpa if you take her.She doesn't seem to want her students to do well as she asks for too much for assignments.

He is cool and good at teeching and he bought me beer and his field trip was cold but it was fun and I liked it but it was on a saturday so that was bums bc I couldnt go drinking but the beer made up for it so thats good
Very intelligent prof and an extremely talented lecturer. His courses are 'must takes' for anyone interested in geology at ISU.

Neal is highly intelligent and loves what he teaches (glaciers!). Lectures are thought provoking and intense. Exams are hard, but if you study and grasp the concepts, you'll do fine. Labs are great, really tie into the course nicely. Great class.

Great guy!  I had no interest in geology prior to taking this class and I learned a lot.  Neal is extremely intelligent and it shows.  He's very helpful, all you have to do is ask for it.  Tests are pretty tough, but if you study you should be ok.

reviews.comment: I took 101 with him and barely got a B, I took 102 with Amani got and A. Not the best professor teaching wise, but always available to discuss your concerns. If you think this class is hard or that Rudik is not a good professor, you're honestly not giving it any effort. Rudik is always super enthusiastic about teaching and does his best in lecture. He lectures well and clearly. He answers questions promptly, and though the content could be challenging to some people, it's not because of him.

Though she is a tough grader, she will give you the proper feedback to make sure you get the good grade. She seems to care about her students and will connect with them through jokes and stories. Makes a typically unpleasant subject bearable.

Really creative and engaging. She sharpened my writing skills and really pushed the class to think deeper about our writing and the world that inspires it. I would recommend this class to deep thinkers and anyone looking to improve their writing.

She is so passionate and funny. Really cares about what she is doing and puts a lot of effort into the class. Somewhat tough grader but gives very detailed feedback. Very enjoyable for an English class. Not too much work either.
Shes really nice, you might spend the entire class talking about one topic so be prepared for that. Dont need textbooks. Make sure you staple your papers or she will not accept it.
I had to leave for a medical issue mid-semester and she was very accommodating and helpful. I learned a lot throughout the class and it was not too difficult.

reviews.comment: Very easy class, group oriented for most assignments. Packback assignments were very easy. Very relaxed class, she responds to emails quickly and understands when things come up in group activities. Exams were online using Lockdown Browser.

Wow! Everything about this class was extremely easy. Only spent 3 hours per week and got an A. Highly recommend taking this course online with friends for the group aspect. There were some delays with emails, but she is very forgiving and the grading scale and components make it hard to get anything less than an -A. Great course.

Janell communicated well with students, especially with the class being online. The rubrics were clear and she graded according to them. Pretty unorganized, but if you stay on top of your assignments you will be fine. Overall a good class.

I have taken 2 of her classes MGMT 478 and MGMT 472 and both were the same. She is extremely unorganized, for many assignments you will have to email her because she forgets parts of the descriptions. Her classes require a lot of time with all of the assignments and the assignments are long! Be prepared to write 2-3 pages single spaced every week!

She is one of the worst professors I have ever had. I cannot believe Iowa State would hire someone who is so unorganized. DO NOT take her as a professor for 478. Literally anyone else is better. I could have taught this class better than her.

She is the most unorganized professor ever. It was never clear what we had to complete for the week and she would randomly add assignments on like a Thursday at 5:00 due the same night. She also created in-class meetings for an online class which she scheduled at 8:00 AM on Saturday. It seems like she was trying her best to make class hard.

Everything aside from the quizzes and tests are group assignments, you have to use Packback TWICE a week (as in, two deadlines per week as opposed to most having one), if your group doesn't put in effort you won't pass. Horribly organized class page in Canvas--No assignments page, everything hidden under links, NOTHING is explained. Terrible.

reviews.comment: This class was super unorganized and no lectures. if you work a lot don't take this teacher she gives you discussions everyday and doesn't grade until the end and doesn't explain anything unless everyone complains. grading is not clear and takes long time for her to grade. Open book exams and lots of extra credit hard to fail.

The most unorganized, messiest professor I've ever had. Even more so because it's an online section. Her tests are extremely detail specific, all from the textbook. Even if you read the chapters/slides exams are still difficult. The average for our exams are about 58-66%. Lots of group work and short windows of time to get things done. Slow grader

The class is set up so that you read the chapters, take a quiz on the reading, and then spend a week having her go over the textbook chapters in powerpoint form. I went to class for the quizzes and group projects and got an A from reading the book. 40% of your grade is based on if your teammates like you. Took her all semester to grade assignments

The class is centered around group assignments which are simple. Prior to every chapter there is a quiz full of trick questions. In order to get a good grade on this quizzes you HAVE to read the chapters with great detail.

You'll never get full points on anything because even if she has a rubric, no one's perfect (even if it's opinion based). You're also tested on material not yet learned which ends up being 10% of your grade. She's never prepared, doesn't know what she is talking about, and thinks that she's always right even when the textbook proves her wrong.

reviews.comment: The class has a lot of tests: 4 midterms and final, but the lowest exam (including the final) is dropped. Lecture slides and notes are very well put together, and he goes slowly. Dr. Appuhamy is very approachable and always answers questions if we need help. Overall, this class is tough, but very achievable with good studying.

Nutrition is not an easy class by Dr. Appuhamy did a great job giving us the information we needed to be successful. He did get into the very fine details in class which made it hard to determine what to study for exams.

i think this class is just hard no matter who the professor is. the exams can be rough but just go over the homework assignments and in class exercises because they are on the exam. lots of material. do good on the first 4 exams and u wont need to take final.
Explains everything in a way that makes it very easy to understand. Also very lenient when grading exams.
Is hard to work with especially if you have testing accommodations in the exam reviews were horrible hell skip over subjects and not go over them

reviews.comment: I thought this professor was fine, the material was hard and you had to work for your grade. I thought he did a good job explaining the material and going over exam reviews. This class wasn't my favorite as the material can get confusing and it was hard to take online but I still did well and the professor was good.

reviews.comment: Always well prepared for the classes and caring about students. Class notes are informative, clear, in order, concise, easy to follow and full with related cartoons and recent research findings. Grading is very fair and directs students to think twice before answering during exams. Honest, well respected and an in-depth knowledge of the subject.

Professor Ranga was my favorite professor this year. He really cares about your success and will even do review days over hard subjects. His tests and quizzes are not hard if you study. I really wish I could take more classes with him.

I have never had a professor as passionate about their field as Andrews. For those unfamiliar with RusHist, he loves to ask where you are struggling to understand and will incorporate that into later lectures. Attendance is only required for the 10 discussion days, but you won't want to miss lectures. Two essays, midterm/finals vocab & essay exams.

I could not recommend a better professor. He is so kind and attentive and cares so much about all of his students. If you reach out and communicate he will help you out 100% of the time. I always tell all my non history friends that I wish they could take him because he is so amazing!! Take his classes he's a distinguished professor for a reason!!

By far the nicest and most caring professor I have ever had. He dedicates himself to making sure his students are successful and will do anything in his power to make sure that happens. The lectures and readings can be dense, but his love of Russian history is infectious.

Having Dr. Andrew's during my second semester was like my saving grace. During the semester, I had a death in my family and had to miss some lectures. Dr. Andrew's expressed genuine care and concern for the things I was experiencing and even offered to set up personalized lecture summaries for me so I wouldn't fall behind. Love this guy!

Dr. Andrews is a fantastic professor. He truly cares about his students' well-being and desires to help his students succeed as much as possible. His lectures are dense, so skipping lectures is not advised. He is also great at giving feedback and is accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Andrews has been the best professor I've had at this school. The entire class is lecture and they're very important/dense, but he makes sure you have time to take notes and always asks if he needs to repeat things. He offers a course packet that lays out all the terms needed for the course as well. 8 essays (5 being just 1 page).

Only negative is that there is a one page paper every week worth 1 point which can get tedious BUT cool professor/class

Really caring guy that made the class very accessible for a non history major. He gives long, but interesting, lectures. There was a lot of reading assigned for this class and you need to participate in class, but it was usually interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: My first history class at isu and I loved it. He gives you a term sheet for each lecture so you know what to take notes on. He would tell us to circle the ones that will probably be tested over. I definitely recommend this professor.

Professor Andrews is the definition of a professional. He cares so much about all of his students and genuinely wants to see you succeed. He is very accessible and friendly, and will go out of his way to help you however he possibly can. I cannot stress enough how much he cares about you, and not in a superficial sense.

This guy will bend over backwards to try and help you. it is refreshing to know that a teacher cares so much about his students. highly published, highly respected, this man is truly a great teacher all around. Bro tip: he gives you everything you'll need to know on tests just study and you'll be fine. you can live without Kishlansky textbook

Dr. Andrews is probably the best history professor at this university.  He is well published and is extremely knowledgeable in his field.  Unlike many of the other instructors I've had, Andrews is a true professional who wants to impart knowledge on his students.

James Andrews is one of the finest professors at ISU. He is devoted to both his work and student learning, and goes out of his way to answer questions and to clarify content. Some of the content in the class can be confusing, but Andrews is there to help. Also, no Russian is required. Higher level analysis and writing are however.
very helpful, intelligent and wise. One of the best professors around campus.
Very good teacher. and nice.

Dr. Andrews is not your typical professor.  He demonstrates a genuine interest in student learning and is always willing to help his students.  It's no surprise that he receives a lot of recognition by his peers.
Dr. Andrews is a very good professor who actually cares about student learning. It is very easy to do well if you read the textbook, take a lot of notes, and attend lecture.
One of the best profs I have had.

Dr. Andrews is one of the nicest and most helpful professors I've met. He is genuinely interested in students succeeding in his class. He can be repetitive at times, but that just makes sure you don't forget to write anything important down.

Andrews is a very nice guy and he knows his subject very well. However, his lectures are hard to follow and they are very boring. If you're really passionate about history, he's the professor for you but if you're just taking his class to fill a requirement, be prepared to snooze.

Prof. Andrews is one of the best professors at Ia. State.  He's extremely knowledgeable, well organized and very helpful.  At times, he can be a bit talkative and repeat himself, but all in all, I think he does it because he just wants certain difficult subjects to be clear before he moves on.
A great prof; very friendly, very knowledgeable, very enthusiastic.

Good course and professor... VERY repeative and a long-winded but not bad. Covers topics for a long time and moves slowly but not bad and is very helpful and will clarify anything if you ask him, hes very nice. Tests are all writing though
he's the ideal history professor... enough said.
Fabulous, Fabulous, Fabulous.  He will go out of his way to help students who are struggling, but trying hard in his class.
One of the best profs I have ever had.
Smart and very good at his job. He can be a biot long winded and repaeats himself alot but that only helps clarify things that are normally complicated.
Excellent Prof, you'll learn a lot, and his passion for the subject is infectious.
An excellent course, much better than expected.  It was very interested and I have learned alot more than I knew.  Not very hard either.  A lot of information given by the Dr. Andrews.

VERY broken sentences.  Takes 40 words to say a ten word sentence with jumps forward and back during.  But he speaks clearly and the class was mildly interesting.  Overall, I got a better grade than I expected and it was a pretty easy class since I didn't even buy any of the books for it.

Good professor, is very involved in what he is talking about and teaching. Clealy is very knowledgeable.  One down side everything is related to RUSSIA.  It is his speciality but there were times where I was sick of hearing about Russia.  Overall though a great class and teacher.
A fascinating course taught with good authority.  Clear, concise lectures allow for a maximum learning potential.  Dr. Andrews was very willing to go the extra mile for any student.
Russian history is very complicated but he made it much easier to understand and remember.  Very accommodating and genuinely cares about his students.
This class is run by the TA's. That is to instruct the entire course, including lectures, assignments, projects, and even simple class activities.

Not recommended for graduate student with no prior knowledge to take. Kind of boring yet not teaching useful things.
Recommended if you want to get some plain credits without further expectation.
Nice research focussed course.

The class has absolutely zero value. Thank god the attendance is not mandatory because I'm pretty sure I saved some braincells not going to class. The class does not follow best coding practices. It was a great experience for me! The course was easy, with lots of good discussions and great presentations.

The only saving grace in this class was that attendance wasn't mandatory. The class content wasn't relevant to the homework and you really just learn everything on W3Schools. On the plus side, the class wasn't very much work until the group project at the end.

I didn't attend lecture after the first week since the content was completely useless and full of rambling. Anything you need to know for this class, you will need to learn on your own. You spend about one week per topic and are then considered a master of it. Read W3 schools for a few hours and you'll learn more than he teaches.

The lectures and assignments are not really related. You have to learn all the material by yourself. He just provides links to the stuff you need to learn. He put an in-class quiz on the day of the career fair, which is very unusual since all my professors in other courses knew that there was a career fair and hence did not give any quizzes.

This class was an unmitigated disaster, and that's coming from someone who did well in it. He knows his stuff but he needs to get his act together or nobody will learn anything but frustration from him.

I took this class online, and the lectures were quite boring. Luckily, the lectures are completely optional as you will be teaching yourself everything. Went to his office hours for some questions I had about testing and all he did was tell me to watch the lab and that's it. Only got a decent grade bc class is an absolute joke.

WARNING: Do not take his senior design projects. This guy was my senior design adviser. Has zero knowledge on the project and does not know what he wants. Changes requirements all the time and then you'd get in trouble for not completing the project. Even a freshman in business knows more about computers than he does.

You need to focus on lecture slides, do the homework and work on your group project as a team, which was the most fun part of the class! It is an easy A, although of having lots of homework and heavy lectures!

Jannesari is the physical manifestation of "Death by PowerPoint". His slides are mostly fluff, which he will read verbatim. There were no tests except for a comprehensive final exam, which naturally left students cramming the entire class in a single week. The exam and group project led to a massive end-of-term difficulty spike. Just laughably bad.

Jannesari as a professor was not the best. The class itself had no real purpose and would fluctuate on topics before you could actually get a grasp of what you were being taught. However, the class was by far the easiest core class I've taken. Put in the time and you will get an easy A.

1) He does not speak loudly or clearly whatsoever 2) You will, to the professor's own admission, teach yourself throughout this class. 3) lectures almost always have nothing to do with homework 4) Written work is very rarely clear english. This is only the start. I hope to never have him again, hes honestly the worst professor Ive had to the date.
Never had a professor speak worse English. Literally can't understand a word he says and that is after already going through over 2 years of STEM profs.

The class was pretty straightforward and easy: you just need to do the homework and the group project and you will ll get a good grade. I was scared for the final exam but the lecture slides and the practice exam were the best resources and help you get an A.

I like the homework and the group project. The lectures were interesting specially the parts on UI and UML. It was my first experiences on UML in this class and I learnt how to use them . The parts on Web development and nodejs was fine and I could extend my knowledge. The exam guideline was very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Its pretty unclear what this class was supposed to be about. The lectures were boring, and graded things just seemed like busywork. However, his graders were entirely reasonable and forgiving no less, unlike the rest of the university.

This class was my first experience on software engineering and web development. I enjoyed the lectures in this class and learned interesting topics. The class has lots of homework but they are easy and not really time-consuming. This class has a final project that I enjoyed and the intro to web development class is a good.

The lectures in this class are completely useless and do not teach you anything. What you need to know for the homework is pretty much self taught. However, the homework is easy and are not time consuming overall. This class has a final project that I enjoyed and the class is a good intro to web development. This class is not time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Janneesari's lectures are kind of dry but honestly, it's the material, not him. He does a fantastic job of getting the class to participate in class (for those who showed up). He's very accessible outside of class, and the TA's are very helpful as well. The class is pretty straightforward, just do the work and you'll get a B+ or better.

I liked the first part on basic stuff, user interfaces and exploring few programming languages with few labs and interesting assignments. Second part, the team project was the best part of the class and I learned so much working in a team. The combination of theory with a series of coding assignments allows you to get actual experience on coding

Early part of the class was pretty good - easy homeworks giving an intro to a couple different languages and styles. The last few weeks get pretty crazy, however, because you get a big group project followed by a final worth 40% of your grade. Ali has pretty boring lectures, but the slides he gives you are an amazing resource by them self.

Worst professor I have ever had. No organization to the class, I didn't learn anything, overall biggest waste of time of my college career. The class was an easy A and I still feel the need to come on here and give this guy a bad rating. Avoid Jannesari at all costs!
very simple

The thing I disliked the most about this professor was the fact on how unorganized everything was. He changed the weights of different parts of our overall grade multiple times. The tests were challenging simply due to the fact that one had to read over 1,000 slides of content. As he said, "Just go over slides for tests".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: When I took the class we did not get a formal Syllabus until dead week. Grading criteria is very vague, no guidance for exams. Reads off lecture 100+ page lectures slides for lecture.

As a professor - He is fine. He cares, he wants you to learn, and he knows what he is talking about, but boring. BUT WOW WAS THE CLASS A MESS. He was brand new to ISU this semester and was firing from the hip. He missed a lot. Unclear expectations and the communication in the class was bad. Has some real potential once he gets settled I imagine.

Jannesari was the worst professor I ever had. He had no Syllabus until the last week of class. There was no solid rubric for any grades. He had many assignments due during dead week which he randomly created and then later realized he couldn't do that. He doesn't use the mic. He doesn't listen to criticism. It took many months to get the grades

Very unclear course. Assignments take a very long time to be graded. Topics covered in class are almost never applied. It's very unclear what we were actually expected to learn. No study material was given except his lecture slides, in which there were hundreds. Very poor class all around.

Throughout this course, expectations and instructions were very unclear. There was little documentation for what was expected for assignments, and especially for the group project. There was very little suggestion for what would be on the exam as well. He suggested we review his slides, which was hundreds of slides from the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Jannesari expects his students to know class content, but has no drive to apply content. By taking COM S 319, be prepared for the most unclear class ever. There is no clarification for grades on assignments and homeworks, and the group project has no cohesion to content in the course at all. Group projects are evaluated on a group basis only.

She was very sweet! I took Math 1950. Got to know everyone in class, and was very accessible. She was always willing to help or provide extra explanation. Attendence is graded but doesn't hold much weight, and if you show up even for a few minutes or need to leave late, you'll still be marked present. Good class and good professor!

I took MATH1950 with Sharon, not 1960 but it wasn't an option for this. Sharon is incredible. She is great at her job, she is always willing to explain something again, she is very understanding, and she does an amazing job. At times it can seem like she is a little scattered and running around like crazy, but that did not bother me personally.

I love Sharon! She makes sure you understand every bit of the class. If she sees that you are confused she will do anything and everything in her power to help you. I don't think I have ever enjoyed a math class more and it was all because of her. If you have the option to have her as a teacher DO IT!
she allows y0u to learn

Sharon is a really dedicated professor. I had her for both 195 and 196 and she is the kind of person who goes above and beyond to ensure we understand the content. She is always available after class in her office if you need to ask her anything and her review lists before exams helped me ease my test anxiety.

He really wants to get to know his students, which I enjoyed, and it was the first class at ISU where everyone collaborated during class. It was refreshing to have casual/material-related discussions. This class was group work heavy and you had to put effort into your work. His grading style is to push his students to their full potential.

He is legitimately the most down-to-earth and sociable instructor I've ever had at Iowa State. I strongly recommend anyone take him for any English class! He provides clear and understandable feedback, which is a must for any instructor.

For most, 302 is an easy A class but not to Dawson. He'll praise you on a paper, you'll do the same thing for the next paper and he'll doc you points. The material is dull, and overall subjective. Attendance is mandatory but class discussions are similar to lectures which are similar to readings. He loves his ego! Overall, I don't recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor D is an amazing instructor! He creates a welcoming environment and is always willing to meet during office hours. His detailed feedback and revision opportunities helped me improve my writing. The class is engaging, well-structured, and highly applicable. I learned a ton and would highly recommend him to anyone!

I cannot recommend him enough! He is an amazing professor and cares about his students. He would try to get to know his students on a personal yet professional level. He was always super helpful when reviewing the emails we had to write, and he also gave examples of poorly written emails for us to go over and dissect. He doesn't grade hard either.

To anyone who is looking for a great professor--take his Engl 302 BusComm class. Not only does he care about us learning how to write, he cares about us as people. Sometimes he spends the first 5 minutes asking about our day or our weekend. It's great. He sent me an email shoutout about how I contributed in class & I felt seen and appreciated.

The only thing I didn't like about the class was the content. I feel like he tries to make it not so bad, but the projects were long for sure. He is a super nice guy though and if you put in effort it won't go unnoticed.

Professor Dawson's lectures were fun and interactive and required everyone to participate. Though I'm not someone who likes to talk in class, he created a space that made it easy. He encourages office hour visits--go to them. He was always willing to help. He cares. That was huge for me.

Professor Dawson is a great professor. I am I transfer student and he is one of my first professor at ISU. He took time to pull me and a couple other transfer students to check in on us. Other than that he understands that we have other classes and activities outside of his class. There is barely any homework.

Professor Dawson is a fantastic instructor, and actually cared about student's learning and life outside of school. Some days he would just chat to students for the first 5-10 minutes of class. He is very avid on sharing in class, and would wait in silence until someone does. It was a bit annoying at first, but a couple weeks and everyone talked.

I thought the rubric was very sparse and did not fully capture what he expected out of an A assignment. Some assignments I would think I deserved an A and would receive a B. Hardly ever gives out maximum points . Hard class to compete with other honors students.
Always willing to meet outside of class. Very thorough feedback. Very clear with lecture materials. Always checks in to make sure everyone is on the same page.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Didn't think I was going to like this class, especially since it was required. But it ended up being my favorite class so far this semester. Professor Dawson met with me outside of class to help with my essays, as well as my resume and cover letters for the job fair. He cared about helping me figure things out. That was huge.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Dawson's English 302 class was one of the most useful courses I've taken at Iowa State. He's not an easy teacher by any means. I had to work really hard to get the grades I wanted. He was always willing to meet outside of class. He was always willing to give me feedback on my drafts. His lectures were interesting with fun discussions.

Professor Dawson is an extremely tough grader. He uses rubrics and rarely (if ever) gives students the full possible credit. In my case, I felt like I had met every piece of criteria required by the rubric and still did not receive the maximum allowed points. It was unlike any other professor I've had who used a rubric for grading.

Mr. Dawson is a really good professor and he cares about you doing well in his class. He does grade pretty harshly but on a few of the assignments you can revise them. Class was always pretty interesting. He is young and likes to make class fun.

He was awesome! As a student who never talks in class, he presents class in a way to make you feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and answers. His class is always fun and laid back, but super informative. Also gives great feedback on your short story. Overall, my favorite professor I have ever had!

He doesn't use blackboard so your class grade is hypothetical until the end of the semester. We only had 3 assignments: 1 individual essay, 1 presentation, 1 group essay. He grades really tough on the essays so beware but he's very available for reviewing your writing so take advantage of it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a great instructor. Even though he makes you work for your grade, it will help you in other English classes. ALWAYS ASK QUESTIONS. Picks favorites in class, so get on his good side. Homework doesn't take that long but if you don't do it don't even bother showing up for class. Overall great guy, funny.

Mr. Dawson is a VERY difficult grader, but he does give you help as long as you seek it out. He is insistent on participating in class, not just showing up, so if you don't like sharing your opinion in large groups of people I don't recommend taking a class with him.

Although Mr. Dawson was a VERY hard grader, I understood he had high standards and expectations of us as students. He was always willing to help, but only if we went to him during office hours, which saved my grade every time. He made us work, but I think I'm better for it. If you're just looking for a blow off class, don't take this one.

Although there was a normal amount of papers given in the class (it IS a level 200 class) he was always there to help and make your paper the best it could be. He was hilarious and am keeping tags on him to see when he will teach a level 300+ class!
love jr so much
extremely rude and does not care about his students, only his reputation at the university. Also uses the same music from 300 years ago, lets branch out, Jim.

Most people enjoy his choirs, but I think rehearsals run too fast. Concerts come up really quick and nobody ever feels fully prepared. You never get out early and don't really have time to ask questions or fix a mistake you're hearing. On the plus side, Rodde is passionate, so he expects effort.
