Rodde is extremely passionate about his work. You can tell it is his life. He has a lot to teach in helping you improve in singing. He does expect you to put in the effort, though, so don't just show up like it's a high school choir.
Awesome Choral Director!

Dr. Rodde is a good choral director and is able to explain the types for sounds that he wants from his choir in a way that is easy to understand. However if you are in any of his choirs, prepare to be musically challenged. Rodde demands precision, however its all in the name of making his choirs better.
Pushes your range so be prepared

"Passionate" about his career...that's the only good thing. Snaps at students (and pianist) if immediate perfection is not delivered & blames his own miscommunication/distraction on students. Consistently and casually makes old fashioned and misogynistic statements. If there wasn't a trip, I wouldn't be sticking around at all.

Dr. Rodde is the reason I decided to continue with my college education. The way he runs singers rehearsals is phenomenal, it's like no other ensemble I've ever been a part of. He has a way of explaining how he wants the pieces sung with no words. He doesn't warm us up before class, but thats mainly because of the short class window of only 50 min.

Dr. Rodde is an experienced and respected choral director. However, this is not what makes his ensembles shine, rather it is the culture he has developed around these ensembles. In Fall of 2021, Dr. Rodde handled masking disputes poorly, often pitting factions against each other and sitting back to watch the ensuing argument. Poor show of character

Dr. Rodde is awesome. I came here not sure if I wanted to do choir (because I don't think I'm THAT good), but I'm so glad I did! I've learned a lot from him and the culture in Statesmen is awesome. Whenever I needed to miss rehearsal, or didn't get a copy of one of our pieces, he was extremely flexible, responsive, and understanding. A+.

Dr. Rodde is a gem to have as a choir director. He pushes us to sing at our potential and strives for perfection from our group. He knows what we are capable of and pushes us to do better. He was real flexible this year with covid in how we practiced. You can't ask for a better music teacher than him.

Dr. Rodde is not the finest choir director you'll find, given the position at a school much more renowned for engineering and agriculture. But given the limited resources the university provides him with, he does a great job. He explains what he wants in easy ways for everyone to understand. He makes choir fun yet great quality.

Dr. Rodde really is a fantastic choir director. Despite his forgetfulness (which may be because of his age) he does some really amazing things with his group(s), and does a fantastic job of making really meaningful music/ experiences. Don't take choir if you're not very passionate about it, but if you have the passion, You will not be dissapointed.

Dr. Rodde has always been passionate about his men's choir, and Statesmen is driven to succeed because of his passion. His mood varies day to day, but he's generally proud and pushes the guys to sing better. The music can sometimes be dull, but his enthusiasm rarely wavers and that helps. Stay on his good side and enjoy your time in choir!

Demands excellence at the expense of his singers' well-being, in a way that makes you feel you're not good enough unless you're perfect. This is fine for a few semesters but hurts your voice long term. The choir produces great sound because of his focus on blending and tone, but, he is strangely oblivious to the emotional realities of being human.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Rodde is incredible at what he does. He's very organized and makes the best use of rehearsal time. Choir has and continues to turn me into a better musician and it challenges me to dive into the nuances and meaning of our music. As long as you stay engaged and don't get on his bad side, he's a really kind and encouraging director

Probably the best chorus director I have ever had. He takes people from all around campus with a same interest and gives them a chance to do something amazing. He is funny and will make you laugh during class but is serious when it comes down to it. You can tell that he loves what he does. Take his class and he will make you a better singer.

Wonderful director that gets the most out of his students. Uses trial and error to find the best sound for each specific choir. Makes each semester and each group very different than any other, and each year provides a new experience. Try not to do or say anything stupid and stay on his good side, and the class will be a blast.

Dr. Rodde is great! I love going to choir every day. In fact, it is my favorite class. Dr. Rodde is so committed to doing the best he can to make the group sound good, and because of that, the choir is an exceptional one to be in.

I've been in Singers for a few years now. Rodde is 100% dialed in to the music. This is both good and bad. Good because you know no conductor will work as hard as he will to get you prepared... Bad because he sometimes will forget that members of the choir have other aspects of their lives to deal with outside of State Singers. Worth it overall.
Dr. Rodde is awesome!  He is an amazing conductor and is always full of humor.  I always looked forward to going to his class.
Dr. Rodde is a musical genius! The techniques he teaches are brilliant! Sound quality produced by the group is spectacular, he knows how to direct a choir!
Friendly, entertaining, and will drastically help improve your singing abilities. Couldn't ask for a better conductor!
Dr. Rooodeeee
Probably the coolest choir teacher ever.  He's totally professional but at the same time really funny and intimate with the music!

Dr. Rodde is absolutely the best choir director I have ever had experience with, and I have seen a wide variety of choir directors!  His teaching style is wonderfully energetic and his music selections are exciting, challenging, and thoroughly enjoyable.
he's cool
No Comments
Sweet
What an AWESOME teacher!!
amazing conductor.  I love him to death.
Best conductor.  Usually demands and gets the best from us. Wouldn't be in the choir anymore if he left.
Awesome guy and great class.  He really loves the music and transfers it to his students.  Rodde is easily my favorite professor on campus.
Dr. Rodde is awsome. I have learned somuch from him in the 3 years I have been in Choir.  His teaching style is awesome as well. Is just a fun class with fun teacher!!

Has ups/downs. Consistently lets class out late or right at the hour, which isnt cool. i can understand it once in awhile but every time is rediculous. The music has its moments, such as Musgrave, Reconciliation, and Blago, but others like the fight song suck (it is wimpy). Id like more challenge
Sweet!  I love this class and he is a great teacher for it.
An all around good guy.  He commands a lot of respect.  Probably the highlight of my semester is being in this class.
No Comments
Just one of the guys.  Full of ideas.  One of the few classes I look forward to.
Cool guy

grading was a bit confusing. There were discussions posted due on random days of the week every week up until the last 3 week of semester. No reminders were given whatsoever, literally missed my discussion posts for the 4 first week. Group Project were ok.

This professor was awful. When taking a summer course you expect it to be laid back or one big project a week but this was not it. Group project the entire course, 3 assignments a week on weird due dates. Leaves comments that make zero sense and does not give any direction. You can ask what your doing wrong and she won't help you.

Class was a breeze besides two group projects/presentations. Had an A- going into the final, then bombed it. Made the final unreasonably hard and gave us nothing to prepare with. Posted a "study guide," but it was just the learning goals. Said 33% of the test would be T/F questions, but there were only 2 total.

Sandy has one of the worst teaching styles and attitude that I have seen here at Iowa State . She is always in a bad mood/rude and makes students feel dumb when they participate in class.  At the beginning of the semester laughed at a student's response to a question. The overall environment of the class is not welcoming and a good place to learn.
Honestly, I can tell she comes from a different background from the other professors here. She's a little old-school and sharing new ideas is difficult with her.

Sandy was friendly; the lectures were okay. There's an individual presentation and 2 case studies (which were tricky). With a team, you write one paper and give a presentation. She certainly isn't the easiest grader, but solid effort and receiving her feedback will improve your grades. In-class participation and assignments were also important.

Not clear grading criteria.  boring. Does Class Work to make you come to her joke of a class. Makes smart comments about your answers/presentations to make you feel dumb. You have to answer at least 10 times to get your grade- wouldn't recommend doing anymore than that. Joke of a professor. Projects are counterintuitive Answers email well.

Sandra is by far the worst professor I've had in the Gerdin Building. If you're a marketing major MAYBE you'll find her lectures entertaining. Her rubrics for projects aren't clear and she plays favorites ridiculously hard. Don't be participative in this class anymore than you have to be. This woman LOVES to prove you wrong any chance she can. Bad.

If you are looking for an easy A in Marketing don't take her. She is very blunt and will drill you with questions even if you try to participate. Always in a bad mood and not very flexible. Also the A is set at a 94 instead of a 93.

She teaches well by showing us real-world examples of concepts. Is willing to meet with students to discuss grades and corrects grades when McGraw hill was having problems with the program. There are in class assignments, smartbook quizzes from McGraw hill, two group projects and the final is open note.

- Shows up to class in a bad mood
- No MKT 340 professor does presentations, but she makes you do 2. useless
- Doesn't respond to emails
- Makes you feel dumb when you answer a question, challenges you to the point where you feel dumb
- No study guide for the final 
- Lost hand-written in-class assignments
- Reads class slides, no help looking back
Sandra was awesome. One test, 2 projects, and barely any homework. You choose your group wisely because you'll be with them the rest of the semester. Sandra has sarcastic humor, a good lecturer.

She is one of my favorite professor's this semester. Participation is heavy, but the more you talk and participate, the more she likes you. Go to class and participate and you'll be fine. Not an extremely difficult class by any means, but you do have to go and put in the effort to get a good grade.

You have a grade on participation, so make sure you are ready to speak up in class. The information is well presented and not too difficult. There is a big group project you have to do. This professor is very nice and welcoming

Really liked Sandy! You had to make weekly contributions which could be scary but its really not. The more you participate the more I think she will like you! I took this class during COVID so it might have been easier than a typical semester but still really like her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Jennings is a great professor!! I would 10/10 take her again. There are weekly assignments, and she does grade heavy on the 2 case studies given out. She is great to lecture with, and participation play a key role in this class, whether that be participating in class lectures or discussion posts online. I highly recommend this professor!

Sandy was okay for a lot of the semester, besides the fact that she doesn't give out study guides for exams. She does tell you during class to "remember this for the exam", but it seems like she says that about everything. It is important to go to class and participate. She grades the group assignments pretty harshly for what seems like no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jennings-Hammond is a decent professor. She seems knowledgable and genuine about the class. She is clear about the work, but DO NOT miss class and participate. If you miss class on the wrong day you can lose a ton of points for projects or case studies, and she does not care what your excuse is, you have no chance to get any points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Participation matters in this class. In-class assignments can have a major impact on final grades. Use the LearnSmart quizzes to study for exams. If you understand those questions, you will do great on the exams. Professor cares but can be challenging when asking questions in class. Tough grader on case studies. Offers plenty of extra credit opps.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very frustrating professor. EVERYTHING other students have said about MKT340 is SO true. Usually finds a way to doc points & there is no clear way to study for exams leading to bad exam grades. Difficult to learn in class. Slides, as mentioned are all diagrams which I have yet to find helpful. Class feels rushed. Would not recommend taking with her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She gives "lecture slides" that are pictures from the book. Says thats all to study for the exam which are scenario based. No help for studying and never gave clear criteria of what the exams were going to be over. Also gives 3 case studies which are hard to capture full points for. overall awful teacher avoid if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you hated this class it was most likely because you didnt show up or pay attention. I LOVED MKT 447 with Sandra and it was probably one of my favorie classes. I liked that she left it up to us to take responsibility to make our own study guides and prepare fro exams. If you go to class and pay attention you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Extremely frustrating professor. Lectures are straight out of the book and you don't need to read it outside of class. Makes you participate in class to get points by taking pieces of paper from you when you speak. Wastes class time on this and current events so has to catch up on lectures right before test. No study guides, not helpful at all.

I had this professor last year for MKT 340 and was pretty scared once I saw she was my professor for MKT 447. Exams are extremely frustrating, as she gives you no study guide and only tells you look at the lecture slides and the textbook. Bone dry lectures. Not a terribly hard class to pass, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: MKT340 is an easy class with relatively straight forward material. I did not touch the textbook once for this class outside of a presentation. You must give 2 presentations during the class - one is a current event and one is a topic expert. You must participate in class as a chunk of your grade is based on that. The participation pts are easy.

Class was super easy. If you went to class and took notes, you will for sure pass. Test are pretty easy and most of it is common sense. I would say an hour or so of studying is required to get a B on the tests. Overall, I found this class easy and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sandy is a pretty average professor, but I felt class was harder than necessary.  Lectures slides were all textbook based, which made it difficult to review material after lecture. Chapter quizzes and in-class activities were hard. Only thing that saved my grade was the extra credit.

MKT340 is a very easy class, but I would not recommend taking it with jennings. Lectures are spent reading off PowerPoints. The only reason anyone goes is because there are in-class assignments. She does nothing to help students prepare for exams other than saying: "there is an exam Friday, look on the syllabus to see what it covers." Unhelpful.

Chapter quizzes are very easy as long as you utilize your book. Lectures are super chill and she has the standard chapter powerpoints that are easy to follow. She gives you points based on if you speak up in class. Tests are fairly easy. But she does grade harshly on in class activities. Overall, pretty choice for a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures. She literally reads off a piece of paper the whole time. Gives very ambiguous instructions. Show up for class because she gives random "quizzes". Tests are easy. Group project is a paper and presentation. Not terrible, but avoid if possible.

Sandra is not a very interesting professor. She reads off of a piece of paper the whole time during lectures, it is clear to see she hasn't taught this class much. She gets mad at the class for little things that aren't a big deal. The project has little direction and she will not explain thoroughly . Do NOT take with her if possible.
Not very understanding, and unclear about how she grades things. Not a teacher I would take if I could do it over again

You should go to class, but you do not have to.  There is in class assignments randomly and you need to go to know when you will present your current event or topic expert.  Tests aren't hard if you read the chapter summaries in the back of the book. Chapter quizzes really easy.

Not understanding AT ALL. Does not take extra time with you if you ask.  You will do an assignment to the best of your ability and work harder on it then other classes and assignments but don't be surprised when she still gives you a C for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She gives a lot of in class assignments and takes points off of those assignments for no reason. There is a decent amount of extra credit that is given which is really nice though. Just make sure you do not miss the blackboard chapter quizzes or skip class and its an easy A.

Super easy class. All you have to do is show up. I put in minimal effort and walked away with a 98%. Other students who skipped a couple classes barely passed. She gives quite a bit of extra credit and the tests are very easy. Can be stingy when grading written assignments so be specific.

She is a very nice teacher and pretty fair with grading. Although attendance is not mandatory she assigns Current Events and Topic Experts almost every class period. There are random in class case studies. The tests aren't to bad mostly scenario based. As long as you take notes you should be fine in the class. Book not needed never opened mine.

This professor doesn't know how to teach. She's an extremely tough grader and is also extremely condescending. She makes her students do "topic expert" assignments which basically means the students teach the class and she doesn't. Everything I've learned in the class has been from the textbook. If you can, choose another professor!

Do not take this class with her. She makes me want to leave marketing. Her lectures are boring and she assigns presentations randomly so you have to come to class. She is an impossible grader, she expects you to write a novel for every assignment or you won't get points. She's not helpful, doesn't help you prepare for the exam in any way.

This class could be much more interesting and fun, but it's not. It's boring and dry and there's not a real reason to go sometimes. Notes are directly from the PowerPoints she posts and information mainly comes from the text book. There's a group project that is just okay. Not a great class, but not an awful one.

She is not a gifted professor. She comes to class prepared, but her lectures are dry and boring. I would not like to have another course with her. Expect chapter quizzes (vocab), exams (vocab), in-class participation activities, one current event presentation, and one group presentation. Final exam is cumulative.

The class and material is super easy. As long as you pay attention in class the tests are easy. There is a pretty miserable group project. Groups are assigned and if you have a bad group you will get stuck with A LOT of work. Overall I liked the class, but be warned to start the project sooner than you think you need to.
My experience was great. She was very clear about all expectations, was engaging, and helped as needed.

Show up to class, print the power points off and take notes and you will be fine. She gives in class points and many opportunities to ask her questions. It would be hard to not get a good grade. Attendance is not mandatory but you will suffer if you don't go.
Not clear, and never seems to be in a good mood. Struggles at retention and motivation, seems to be very stuck up.
She teaches like everyone should major in marketing.
She thinks everyone should major in marketing, and that's how she teaches it.

She had a clear syllabus that outlined the entire course that showed due dates. She would remind you when things were due weeks in advance. She even let you re-do assignments you did poorly on. All you have to do is not miss two or more classes and your fine. If you get lower then a B then you must have slept in class.

Sandra's incredibly condescending, refuses to use a website like Blackboard or Moodle to post information or track grades, and is the most impossible grader ever. There is no possible way to get a good grade in a class with her.
Very intriguing class and she did a great job sharing her passion of the ancient world with her classes.

I took CLST 3670. The material is great, but the lectures are hard to follow because of her personality and constant sidetracking. She asks for help with lessons when she doesn't know something, which is hard because you're in the class to learn, not to say what you already know. If you can take this class with another professor, you should.

If you don't like group work, this is the wrong class, but she also tends to offer the option of doing the group projects, which can be nice. Very knowledgeable, very funny. Lectures can be kind of slow and boring, but she knows a lot about the topics and adds fun, interesting details that anyone would find enjoyable.

I loved learning about Ancient Egypt, I have always been very interested in the topic so I applied myself. 2-3 lecture videos per week, 1 discussion post & a response paper or project every other week.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Moore is very passionate about ancient Egypt and it shows in this class. She knows the subject well and provides students with many ways to learn. She is pretty lenient when grading assignments and is very understanding/accommodating if you need an extension. Overall, she made the class fun and interesting, without it being too much work.

Made the ancient cities interesting. Has great patience with students. Will not hesitate to dig into a subject if you are interested in it. Gives plenty of easy points to boost your grade.  Overall, nice professor and a worthwhile class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: A stressful class, but one that is easy to achieve an A in if you show up and do the work. Homework is assigned every single day (even after tests), and it takes up a decent amount of time, but it's not too hard. Dr. Ranalli seems intimidating, but when you ask questions, he will very patiently help without judgment.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loves to assign a lot of homework. The homework and the class aren't hard, but certainly feel a bit tedious. Tests have a ton of points (400+) but are only actually worth 100, for better or for worse. He is helpful when asking questions, but can be snippy on occasion. Unfortunately, slides are filled to the brim with AI-generated images.

Be prepared for brain-melting lectures and diagramming with no definitions or explanations. His tone is belittling if you don't understand right away. Attendance is required with no exceptions, my friend died, and I missed a week of class and had to go to deans office to keep him from dropping me. There are other professors don't take it from him.

This class can be a little difficult, and Dr. Ranalli doesn't always make the more difficult concepts easy to understand. He's a super smart guy, but sometimes he doesn't know how to make others understand things. But if you put in the time and do the homework, you should be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jim was really good at explaining things, it was just difficult at times since there are exceptions in diagramming, so he wasn't clear on tests when these exceptions would appear. He does 2-3 major assignments but they are worth a ton of points. I never got below an A on these. Just take good notes and make corrections when needed
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: pretty good. answer questions. clear clarification, maybe bored
pretty good. answer questions. clear clarification
Absolutely loved him! He is very helpful and the constant practice has you master the material.

He was an awesome teacher and I really enjoyed this class. You definitely have to enjoy learning about the syntax and the different elements of grammar, but it's easy to understand if you participate in class and ask questions! He's one of the best teachers I've had so far at ISU.

Terrible at helping students. Only offers that you continue to read the lectures.  If you reach out to him with problems, small or large, he will decide to comb through your grades and assign lower grades where he feels fit. Rude via email and talks down to students who question him.

He's a nice guy and a great teacher for me. The only stumbling block for me was that his marking schedule, when he'll post the grades up, is a bit random. But other than that, he's an amzing lecturer, and I'd take his class again.
Pretty solid for first year teaching Modern Physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard to understand him sometimes. Most things covered in class are not on the tests or homework. Midterm and final are 70% of my whole grade.

Sheaffer teaches differently but effectively. Uses Piazza, not Canvas. Lectures are handwritten walkthroughs and engaging. Few assignments, so each matters. Attendance was 20% but he forgot to take it most of the semester and gave full credit. Overall a good, interesting professor - one of the better ones in the CS department.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Takes absolutely forever to grade assignments. Going into finals week, 4 major assignments that were worth nearly 25-30% of my grade total were just ungraded, 2 of them over a month since the due date. Even though he has a piazza, half the questions are just ignored and never answered.

I've taken COMS 321 and 327 with Sheaffer, he's a great professor. He covers a lot of content in his classes and goes in-depth, which means you'll have to put in the time, but neither were too difficult and I've gotten a lot more out of his classes than others as a result. Clear and engaging lectures. Highly recommended.

Presents by talking while quickly coding stuff, very difficult to follow. Requires students code in a convoluted development environment using SSH to connect to a school server. Does not know how to set it up & will not help you. Posts nothing online except some quickly written code with no explanations. extremely time-consuming homework every week
Sheaffer tends to make the classes he teaches a lot more difficult. Expect to have long and tough assignments. He is a chill guy though.
Start your first project early, the second project is way easier. The exams are take-home and should be easy if you can do the homework by yourself.

Schaeffer is fine. His lectures were very boring, consisting of him writing on a projected piece of paper for 50 minutes. The actual content was good and he is very knowledgeable. Im still annoyed that he went AWOL on Piazza during the two programming assignments, not answering any questions for weeks. Exams were all online, which was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He's really amazing. He explains everything very well and uses plenty of examples. It shows that he is extremely knowledgeable with the topics he teaches, and I would 100% take him again if I can.

He always answers questions genuinely to the best of his ability, and he really supports you and tries to help you do well.

Hardest part of this class was the weekly programing assignments, taking 12-15 hours a week, but they are the best thing to make you a better C programer. Exams were relatively easy compared to other classes, both exams were very similar to the practice ones. Sheaffer is super knowledge about everything C and Linux and is very easy to understand.
0 complaints. I think he puts in minimal effort possible on his 321 class so he can support 327 class better. Answers piazza questions every morning, great office hours.

Lectures are extremely boring, I made sure I get at least 8 hours of sleep before his lecture and still had a hard time staying awake. I get that this is theory heavy material but do something other than writing on a projected paper for the entire lecture, for whole semester. And I don't understand why he chose to teach legv8 over other asmbly lang

327 homework is easy if you put in the time. Sheaffer explains everything very clearly in lecture. Will give guiding points on how to do the assignments. 2 Test make up 40% of your grade and are tough. Exams are on edge cases that can trip you but lots of study guides around.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely helpful professor who thoroughly covers topics and answers questions in class. Written homeweorks were difficult because they were from the book, on book materials. Exams were open note, open book, online, and the same questions as in the review covered in class. The class was interesting and useful.

Actually 10/10 professor, I have zero critiques for him. His lectures are fantastic. Homeworks are pretty easy but you must not fall behind or you will stay behind. Exams are not too difficult if you study. Sheaffer is very active on Piazza and will answer your question pretty much all the time. Highly recommend

Sheaffer is extremely knowledgeable on computer architecture and explains everything very clearly. He often gets sidetracked but the topic of the sidetrack is almost always interesting and related to the topic at hand. However, LEGv8 documentation is basically nonexistent. Overall, would recommend for anyone trying to learn ab computer hardware

- Literally sent the wrong grade to the registrar (I had a B-, and a C showed up in my transcript)
- both him and his TAs are terrible at communicating with students. I emailed him and his TAs countless times, made piazza posts, and literally was never responded to.
- LegV8 ARM is super niche, almost no helpful resources besides class and textbook

Good professor knows a lot and is helpful when you have questions. The course structure could be better. Very few grade book entries that determine the entire grade for the class. Lecture delivery makes it hard to summarize or distinguish the topics that are important. Programming assignments were great and not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Only uses piazza. Grading criteria is not shared with students. Felt good about exams until I got the grade back. Lectures were interesting, informative, and easy to follow. Had weekly homeworks that normally took 5-10 hours to complete.

I really enjoyed Sheaffer in 327. I learned a ton in this class. Be warned though, if you make minor mistakes on programming homework, you'll be heavily penalized, as the points are out of 10. Start your assignments as soon as you can, you'll thank yourself later. Super knowledgeable and respected guy, you can learn a lot from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy but he is a horrible lecturer. All his courses are very disorganized as he ONLY uses Piazza which can make it hard to find stuff sometimes. His lectures also don't help at all in regards to the homeworks. He only ever types on an emacs or writes on paper and is very inconsistent with posting his "notes".

Jeremy's lectures are difficult to follow as he typically writes on a piece of paper that is presented on the board. His teaching style is disorganized, and he frequently has his kid in class which can be distracting. The course would be much better with slides that are prepared before lectures. Course should require digital logic, and does not.

Insanely chill prof. He was super understanding and approachable outside of lecture. His lectures were dry (it's computer architecture people what do you expect) but anytime his son made a guest appearance they were certainly entertaining. The class was pretty easy except for the first programming assignment in LEGv8 (why not ARM? who knows).
Lectures explain the textbook very well. Makes boring topics interesting. Laid back and friendly.

Didn't love his lectures, always was just scribbling things on a piece of paper and projecting it on the screen. Also had "random attendance checks" but didn't take attendance once until 2/3 of the way through the semester. And then when final grades were put in, he gave everyone full points because it was too much work to actually figure it out.
Great at making a dry subject seem interesting, makes jokes during lectures. Has tests and relevant projects.
Students complain about the professor changing deadlines last minute are the same students not attending lectures. I think he is very lenient and would give extra time for harder assignments.

Sheaffer's lectures are usually very good compared to other professors. And unlike 327 or some other classes, this one didn't have too high a workload either. We had 4 written assignments, 2 programming projects and three exams. The first exam was a bit hard but the other two were relatively easy, none of the assignments were graded too strictly.

Dr. Sheaffer is an extremely knowledgeable professor and explains content in a very easy to grasp manner. There are four written and two programming assignments. The written is fairly tough compared to the exams.  If you have questions, try and get them answered in class; otherwise, you will drown since emails and Piazza are not answered.

The lectures for this class weren't very useful for me, but those with little programming experience may benefit more. The assignment grading harshness can fluctuate, but was pretty lenient by the end of the semester. Don't expect to get questions answered on Piazza. Many students had mental health issues due to the load of weekly assignments.

Good lectures but his course is extremely disorganized. Extremely hard to get a hold of, he has NEVER responded to a single email of mine since the start of the semester. Canvas course essentially has no announcements, as everything is on Piazza that he barely checks. There is just no communication whatsoever.

This was a tough class content-wise, but Dr. Shaeffer was very helpful in and out of class. He was also very responsive to students needs and truly cared for student understanding + success. Good, in-depth lectures. One thing to note is only basic lecture notes are posted, so I found attendance to be required for understanding of course material.

Sheaffer is not accessible at all outside of class, so don't even try. His projects are fun, and the exams I felt were pretty fair. You do have to put a lot of work to get an A in the class, even if the material isn't that hard.

It felt like teaching and preparing for this class was very low on his daily TODO list, didn't feel like he cared. When he was asked to give study material, he responded with that he didn't have time. There was 4 weeks of no homework and then all a sudden 2 written assignments a programming assignment and then an exam all at the same time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeremy Sheaffer doesn't seem to put much effort into his teaching and is often very passive aggressive towards students when questions are asked online. While he does care about the material he teaches, it sometimes feels as though he'd rather be doing something else.

Dr. Sheaffer is a two sided coin. On one hand, he is a very good professor and obviously cares about his students, and that they learn the materials. The homeworks, group projects, and exams were very fair, and he curved when needed. However, the lectures were filled with his son playing around, and were very disorganized.

Jeremy is a really nice and funny guy, but WOW this class was not organized at all. Finding study material was very difficult, his kid was a nuisance in every single lecture all semster, and he constantly got side tracked. Also, if you need a question answered GOOD LUCK. The TAS might respond, but he surely won't.

Some learning can be done via textbook, but lectures provide helpful examples, and book material not covered in lecture does not appear on tests. Seems genuinely interested in material he presents which makes it easy to pay attention. Difficult to reach him outside lecture. Grading criteria not always clear. Grades can take over a month to come in.

While Dr. Sheaffer definitely knows his stuff, the way he conducts his 321 class is horrendous. He is disorganised. He doesn't give specific titles to his lectures, which makes students have to go on a wild goose chase. He doesn't have a timeline in his syllabus either, so it's hard to figure out where topics are. He also doesn't reply to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jeremy Sheaffer is probably a misunderstood professor by students who are just trying to pass. I came into his 327 class pretty bad at programming, but I came out way more knowledgeable. He definitely has a chill lecture style that makes you need to do some research on your own. Perfect balance imo that'll make you work hard. Also a genius.

Very poorly organized class, lectures are never to the point. HW assignments and Exams have very unclear instructions, grading almost never takes place efficiently. And there is no respect given to students by this professor.
Very unorganized and very poor teaching. No help from TAs and the professor is out of touch with the students. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 227 is not too difficult of a class. Attendance is not mandatory, but quizzes are every Friday. Attendance makes this class infinitely easier, however. Start your coding assignments early and you will be fine.

As a Freshman, Jeremy was my first Computer Science professor. I had a terrible experience both in and out of class with him. His lectures were messy and difficult to follow, and he was virtually unreachable outside of class. Not to mention he tended to be rude and condescending towards students. I would avoid his sections at all cost.

Terrible and cant handle a class with this many students. Inaccessible outside the classroom. They didnt start grading the quizzes until after the final and some scores ended up missing for some (I heard same thing happened with the last hw). Probably most people picked him up because  He is American and does speak with an American accent.

Any questions on assignments were left unanswered. For a LEGv8 assignment, he had us read instructions that were not in LEGv8, and nowhere in the textbook or online. (and completely in C, which was not a prereq) They spent months grading each assignment, and made mistakes grading students' work on each one (many of which were left unresolved)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst class and professor I've had in my 4 years as a college student. I don't know what else to say... poor organization unclear requirements. Came off as lazy and unorganized. If I were to grade the professor he'd get an F. Months to grade and little feedback. Exams are unrealistic and obviously made in spite of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sheaffer is overall an ok professor. You can tell he is passionate about the material and he does try to be fair. It was his first time teaching this class and the class was extremely disorganized. It takes forever to get any of the homework back and the exams were extremely tough, plan on spending a lot of time on the programming homework.

Professor Sheaffer was a fairly decent instructor. His lectures can be a bit dry but he makes sure the students understand the material. Much of our lecture time was spent watching him write code. The organization for the class was lacking, many times assignments were released late and not graded for weeks. The assignment length is on the long side
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is only available in class. If you are trying to contact him via Email or Piazza forget about it. He Is really smart and knowledgeable about the subject, but expects you to have a masters level understanding. Tests will be way to hard no matter the effort spent studying. Professor is really lazy, TAs Were horrid. Avoid at all costs
I cant speak for other classes, but for 227 Sheaffer was solid. Lectures made sense. the homework was often long and confusing. For 227, idk how much is on him, however.

This class is easily one of the worst, and the professor contributed to this mess of a class. I know the professor knows his material well but the organization is virtually non-existent and incredibly lazily laid out. Exams were ridiculously hard, Homework was ridiculously long, Programming assignments were ridiculous. Overall Impression, avoid.

This is the first time he teaches this course, and he expects us to be good as him. He makes this course hard as not possible to finish, and wants us to use something not specified in textbook. BTW, the textbook's lecture is fine, but the exercise is bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Jeremy is a great lecturer, he really understands C and is helpful when you need him on piazza or during his office ours, his TAs were less helpful and often terrible. The grading was not very uniform across the different TAs and was not well documented how you were being graded. Lots of time consuming hw makes this class difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Jeremey is a great professor and very knowledgeable. In 327, his lectures were very interesting. He mixes in humor and conversation in his lectures which make them fun. 327 takes a lot of time, but his code drops make the class better. He gives you exams from previous years that are very similar to the exams given to you. Class  extra credit.

Jeremy is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he does. His class is not always fun to sit in when he is giving lectures, but if you pay attention you will probably do very well. He tried his best to make homework fun and, for the most part, the class was enjoyable and not too difficult.
Fantastic
lovable guy, signed up for another class he's teaching next year

Dr. Sheaffer is really caring, and he always shows his respect to his students. He often tells jokes which helps his lecture become a lot fun and interesting. His assignments are pretty hard, but he often gives you 2 weeks to finish each.

Great teacher, excited to have him again next semester. Although his lectures can be a bit bland, he cracks jokes to make sure you aren't to bored. Overall fairly easy class, if you fall behind then obviously it becomes difficult, but that comes with programming. Cared about his students, and was always accessible. Take this professor if you can.

I had a good experience in class. Professor takes everyone seriously. He jokes in class to make sure that students are attentive and to make the studies interesting. The only downside is that he doesnt reply to emails.
Is not specific in giving information regarding assignments, doesnt reply to emails and ainam not happy to have him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: A lovely chap.

I had a very good experience in this class. Learned a lot through the projects and help is easily accessed outside of class. After the drop date he will offer extra credit for attending lecture randomly. This will be done 3 times.

I have a very good experience in this class, the only downside being the workload. I believe Jeremy makes up for this with his exceptional teaching skill, impressive amount of knowledge of C and C++(even for a professor), and his willingness to help outside of class. Easily top 5 favorite professors.

Without a doubt, the best computer science teacher I've had to date. Lectures help, but are not required. He knows his stuff and is willing to be flexible for you. You can definitely tell that he cares. I would without a doubt go out of my way to take him for a class.

I've had him for two courses now, and he's truly one of the best professors I've had. Caring, knowledgeable, good sense of humor, never condescending, always willing to help, I seriously cannot say a bad thing about this guy. If there's a section available with him, take it. You'll learn a lot from Jeremy.

Great professor who has a good sense of humor at times and is always willing to help in office hours. Lectures can be very dry. Programming labs and assignments get a lot harder as the semester progresses, especially for an intro level class. With that being said, now that I am in CS 227, I realize just how much this class helped prepare me for it.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Decent class that got me to stick with CompSci. Jeremy has no concept of difficulty, leading to an extremely varied difficulty curve throughout the semester. Lectures were well done aside from the fact that he would take half the class to write down whatever he had just said.
This class is way to much homework. The assignments are weekly and take on average 10+ hours, based on everyone I have spoken to as well as my own experiences.

Jeremy is a great professor who really knows the content well. Sometimes his lectures can be a little boring but they are but if you and your class are willing to participate, lectures can become quite interesting and engaging. The weekly projects can be pretty hard at first if you don't know c but as your knowledge of c improves they become easier

this class is super hard and time-consuming but sheaffer does a good job getting the subject matter through in a clear way. this class was very straight forward in my opinion- you get out what you put in. you should be fine if you dont let yourself fall behind

He's very intelligent, accessible outside of class, and actively encourages students to come to his office hours. However, his obvious talent in C/C++ sometimes causes him to move to quickly in lectures because the ideas are simple to him. Doesn't work from the textbooks, but they are valuable references. Coding projects every week can be stressful
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the worst teachers I have ever had. He sits in lecture and copies notes from previous semesters onto a projector. No one asks questions because no one can follow. He "boosted everyone's grades by 20% because over 70% of you are failing". Does not teach the code. Stuck with him in CS 327 too which is even worse.

Dr. Sheaffer is an alright professor. His class was decently challenging, but the curve was more than generous. Great at answering questions and is very patient when helping students. He's not as well-rounded with Java, but is (supposed to be) a genius with C. Side note: He is American and does speak with an American accent, unlike the other prof.

Lectures were fun an engaging. Sheaffer explained confusing concepts clearly and made them easier to understand. Projects were challenging at times--pay attention in class and get started on projects early. Book is optional (don't bother buying it--info can be found online/Blackboard notes). Overall a very solid professor who cares about students!

He's a good dude. Not at all condescending like some other com sci instructors. Lecture material can be difficult, but he's extremely helpful one-on-one. So I would highly recommend going to his office if you need help.

Extremely intelligent and well spoken professor teaching fundamental data structures. Found the tests fairly easy, the assignments vary in difficulty but extensions were given for the hard assignments. Assignments are time-consuming. Sheaffer is a wonderful professor but expect spelling mistakes.

Great teacher. Not a great speller, but definitely willing to help students when they ask. As far as programming teachers go, he is the best one I've had up to this point. Polite and posted all lecture notes online. Which was great for studying for upcoming tests and assignments.

Jim did a terrible job of engaging with the students during lecture. All he did was just read of a PowerPoint he didn't even make for the class. I sat 10 feet away from him and I could barely hear him because he mumbled the entire time. Only saving grace was he was a rather nice grader and gave us extra time on our exams.

This class was uncomfortable at best and mentally damaging at worst. No learning happens in lecture, which is just him reading off his slides. Exams weren't curved despite class C- and C averages due to the short amount of time given to take them and the difficulty of the content. This class IS passable, it's just an enormous time commitment.

Nice guy, just wish he would teach rather than read off lecture slides and use TopHat all the time. Most of the learning will be on your own time and in the textbook/practice problems. He expects you to know most stuff from high school. He gives out partial credit on exams, but does not give enough time to complete them.
Doesn't give nearly enough time on tests, believes class time is sufficient, it isn't
Dr. Cochran rules. 311 was a blast, and he went right along with my and my lab partner's antics. What a legend

Dr. Cochran taught physics 241 for the first time this semester and did a great job. He is very interested in the material and is a very humble guy. Really easy to approach and talk to about pretty much anything.
He knows his stuff incredibly well and is very gentle with grading.
Only down side is this course requires a lot of self learning on your own time. Otherwise, you get A for effort on papers.
Very helpful.  If you are interested in physics, get to know this guy.  He has a genuine passion for the subject.
No Comments

Shangyu is caring, compassionate, and extremely passionate and knowledgeable about linguistics! He clearly loves the subject material as well as making connections with students. Going to his class was, without fail, the highlight of my day. Show up to his classes, and he will make sure you understand the materials, and you will easily do well.

Shangyu is a fantastic and extremely caring professor. He is always willing to help students, whether that be on class material or because they need to be absent from class - he's incredibly understanding and always wants you to succeed. If you show up (which you need to to understand what's going on), it's an easy and fun class.

Shangyu was GREAT!! I loved having him, and his classes were always a joy to attend, even though attendance wasn't mandatory. He was very helpful and knowledgeable and did his very best to make every student feel welcome and comfortable. He was also VERY flexible with his deadlines and facilitated some pretty good discussions among his students.

Straight up awesome professor. The class was always interesting, and was easy to follow along. Attendance is mandatory by putting random in class tests, but other than that the class was extremely easy and the textbook assignments you could really just do at your own pace.
Joanna is a GREAT professor. She doesn't assign a lot of work to complete and her assignments are fun and engaging.
Standard 1010 class. She attempts to make it engaging and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Joanna is the best professor I have ever had. Super sweet and provides great discussions in class. Lectures usually turn into current event conversations which are super insightful and get the class talking quite a lot. Textbook is easy to go through and weekly assignments take a total of around 30-45 minutes to complete.

Joanna is an easy professor, but the class is extremely unorganized. Lots of lectures go off-topic. Attendance is not graded on an everyday basis, but there are random and occasional graded "pop-quizzes" or papers to turn in. Tests are open book. Assignments are unclear, however, they are relatively easy. Joanna is extremely understanding.

Joanna is super sweet, she really cares about her students. Class often did tend to get off topic pretty quickly, so sometimes it was a bit difficult to learn, but overall she is a knowledgeable professor who I would recommend if you're looking for a pretty laid back class.
Joanna is such a great professor, although I don't know how much I really learned throughout her class this semester, she truly is a great person and made class so enjoyable!

She is a super nice person and has fun lectures, but I don't feel like I got a whole lot from her lectures and class, as most of them were just showing us ads. She doesn't have much on the Canvas page, so if you miss class it is hard to contact her and get the materials to catch up. She can get kind of off topic in class, but is very chill.

Doesn't grade anything 
Gives Pop Quizzes 
Doesn't respond to emails 
Lectures aren't informative as you watch ads the entire time. Only reason you should go to class is the pop quizzes.
Canvas page is unorganized and unfinished
Nice but not a very good professor. She would be better as a middle school or early high school teacher.

One word amazing. Joanna is really good at connecting with her students by creating a relaxed and fun environment. I was able to have really good conversations with her inside and outside of class. She always gives amazing feedback. She is very understanding and open, making it easy to ask and answer questions in class. 10 out of 10.

Joanna is literally the best teacher Iowa State has to offer. She is so caring about her students and her classes. She works really hard to help each, and everyone one of her students understand the topics being taught.  One downside she it a little all over the place, which makes her teaching style very interesting.

Joanna is the best professor I've had at Iowa State. All she wants is for her students to show up for class and try their best. Joanna gives the best feedback and makes class a lot of fun. Everyone needs a professor like Joanna. SO MUCH FUN! You will get a good grade and learn a lot if you attend class and participate.

Joanna is one of my favorite ADVRT instructor. Her lectures are always great and very understanding. Best thing about her is she helps you out with homework if you are struggling. I would definitely recommend her

Joanna is such a great professor. She truly cares and tries to connect with students who take her courses. If you are having trouble with the material reach out to her!  She has helped me grow so much this semester, and is extremely genuine.

I only put mandatory attendance cuz she has pop quizzes. She’s really funny. Sometimes she beats herself up it makes me so sad because she’s so cool. She doesn’t give out much work either which is so nice.

Joanna is a very likable professor and easy to talk to. Classwork is kind of scattered and hard to follow at times. She does give pop quizzes but if you show up for class you should be able to get an A. Gives lots of extra credit and extensions when needed! She doesn't want students to fail.
Show up for class or fail. She cares so much about attendance its not even funny. She will give pop quizzes on days she doesn't think people will show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: ADVRT 230 is a great class to learn the background of advertising. Ms. Schroeder is a good professor, just a bit scattered with her content at times. Reading the textbook is probably the best way to do well in her class.

She is a very very chill teacher. If you go to class once a week you will be fine. The tests are all online and the work per week takes maybe 30minutes total. Very easy and entertaining in my opinion. I would 100% take it again.

If you're wanting a laid-back professor, Joanna fits that criteria. She's not strict on deadlines and graded fairly easy. A lot of her scheduling for classes was all over the place and I had a difficult time understanding directions for weekly assignments. It was frustrating attempting to keep up with the class schedule/assignments.

Communication was terrible. Lectures would be posted irregularly. She dropped off the grid for a few weeks and dropped nine at once all needing done by the following week. She never responded to her email and grading took forever.

She and her TAs never responded to emails or canvas messages and went MIA the last month of the semester. She didnt post lectures or anything. She was a nice instructor but I dont think I would take another class with her if I wouldnt have to, not very reliable.

She is very nice and knowledgable about the topics we cover in class, however be prepared to figure things out by yourself, and I would heavily advise getting to know your classmates as she NEVER answers her emails. This is supposed to be an in person class, however we haven't had class in roughly 5 weeks. Nice, but needs to be more organized
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Joanna is caring professor in most aspects. She wants her students to do well. However, she does a terrible job organizing the class. The final was all over the place and projects don't have clear instructions. She is really slow at grading. Dunno how doing in class. She's a fun prof, but her disorganization keeps me from wanting to have her again.

This might be the worst experience I have had with a professor, and many people who were in my class have agreed. Rarely responds to emails and hard to communicate with. Plays favorites and is such a huge distraction during in-class assignments. Final is 30% of the grade, majority of assign. go ungraded until after the final. Would not recommend.

Schroeder is for the most part a good professor, the big problem is her exams. Most homework and quizzes are easy and straightforward, but her exams look like she wrote them at 2 am and didn't proofread at all. There's often questions that don't make sense, have no right answer, or only have right answers but you have to just pick one.
Joanna is outstanding! She gave very clear grading criteria and was always accessible when you needed her. I highly recommend her, favorite professor at ISU!

Joanna is one of the most influential professors at Iowa State University, and if you havent taken her, get on it. Joanna Schroeder is going to be the most caring professors you have ever had, and only wants you to succeed.

Awesome Professor! Always willing to help. Make sure to show up to class because most of your points are based on an in class assignment. Great class if you are wanting to get an idea of what a crisis communications professional does.

This class was really enjoyable as you watch a lot of ads and learn what goes into advertising. She does not give out a study guide for the 3 total exams, which can make the exams a bit difficult. However, she does drop your lowest exam. Quizzes are taken in class by a code. Rarely used the book. You do a simple radio and ad project, all are fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The professor is nice enough, not brutal but not easy. If you read the textbook and go to class sometimes you should be okay. The material was a little tricky for me.

Joanna is amazing. Laid back, but productive. Has lots of networking opportunities. Gets to know each student. She really enjoys what she does and respects the students in her class. A new addition to Greenlee, but she fits right in. Also teaches ad230 and pr321. Did not need the book for 334, although she does want you to buy/use it, but i did not

She is a very nice professor and is very understandable. I enjoyed taking this class with her. There are only 2 tests the entire semester which are the midterm and final so the tests are over quite a few chapters. The questions to the tests can be hard but there are a lot of extra points that you can get so that helps. There are quite a few quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests? Not many--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is very easy online. It is a half-semester course, but you can start early to get a head start. It is organized well, and all the quizzes are multiple choice and very straightforward. The lectures are interesting, and there are even guided notes.

This was a fun & easy online course! Completely self-paced so I worked ahead during the semester. The lecture videos are fun & the work is straightforward. The quizzes were sometimes hard because they were very detail-oriented. Just make sure you take good notes & make timelines of the content.

I had previously taken HIST222 with Prof. Monroe, which was why I was so excited to take this class. However, I was disappointed by how he had to set up this class. All the lectures are online, and the class is just 3 hours of quite boring discussion. I still have a lot of respect for him, but this class was quite difficult and fairly unenjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Listening to his lectures is like watching a documentary, and he's such a good speaker, which is a bonus. Your grade is made up of three exams and a participation grade. The difficulty of this class really depends on your TA. Provides outlines for each of his lectures, which helps a lot. Don't have to attend lectures if you don't want to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class, and more specifically this professor, sparked a love for history within me. The lectures were interesting and easy to follow. He provides outlines for the lectures but his slides don't have any words so you have to listen pretty closely. He is very nice and funny. Just pay attention in class and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class and best instructor Ive had at Iowa State

Best professor I've ever had. Great lectures and if you pay attention it's pretty easy to figure out what will be on the exams. Be ready to take notes fast and to keep up with his lectures. He takes advantage of every second of class so make sure to stay focused or you'll miss something important. Highly recommend :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Hist 202 with Dr. Monroe. Great professor, easy to understand, really wants you to do well. How well you do in the class is lucking out with your TA. I got a 100% in the class effortlessly. All you need to do is take notes and do the assigned readings. He has inspired me to add a history minor too
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very very knowledgeable about the subject. Lectures are interesting and funny, and I felt like I learned so much each lecture I went to. I plan on taking another class from him just because he teaches it. History department is very lucky to have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Monroe has been by far one of my favorite professors. He is very engaging in every lecture. He is extremely proper and knowledgable but still makes jokes from time to time. You can easily get a B-A as long as you go to the lectures and participate in resitation. The tests are all in class written essays so get ready to cram in a lot of info.

Super enthusiastic and loves teaching. Lecture is basically him talking about a subject for 45 minutes with a few powerpoint pictures and occasional music. Sounds horrible, right? He never lost my attention. He knows how to tell you everything you need to know while making it interesting and sometimes funny. Makes you see why history is important
lectures are really hard to pay attention to because he does not lecture off a powerpoint he just talks for the entire hour
Outstanding guy. Loves getting questions after class. Shows true passion for the subject.
Great words of wisdom, interesting, insitefull, and helpfull
Best teacher at ISU. Makes every  story interesting and his lectures fly by! Very helpful and kind. Take his classes if you get the chance!

Seriously one of the best professors I have ever had in college thus far. He is funny and extremely knowledgeable. Every lecture is an intricately woven story that is flawlessly presented and interesting to listen to! Today's lecture ended with the audience clapping. He is honestly that good.
Amazing teacher, amazing subject! I thought it was going to be an incredibly boring class, but Monroe made it so interesting! I would totally recommend this teacher to anyone!
Very good teacher!

I have never had a professor that was as enthusiastic about teaching as Monroe.  He loves history and has great lectures that make sense.  The exams aren't too bad, they are just in essay format.  If you ever need help in the class, go see him.  He is a very nice guy that takes his job as a professor very seriously.

Prof. Monroe has been one of my favorite professors at ISU. He expects a lot, but does not make it impossible to deliver. This is not a class to skip reading in-- you really do discuss it every day. I enjoyed every single day.

Very enthusiastic, gets very worked up when teaching, which is great. Puts so much energy into his lectures and adds little bits of information that get away from the actual events to make everything more interesting and to give students a laugh.  He can start talking pretty fast as he gets more into it but catches himself and slows down.  AMAZING

Awesome professor and really great guy. He makes some pretty complicated subjects easier to learn and more interesting. I have him in the morning but waking up and going to class is never an issue because he is a great lecturer.

One of the best professors I have ever had. He will make time to help any student. He is animated and loves what he teaches. He is incredibly intelligent and just a good person. He is a fair grader and as long as you work hard and speak in class, you will do well. We need more instructors like Monroe.

Dr. Monroe is enthusiastic, eager to help, and best of all, a fantastic educator.  He balances difficult subject matter and in-depth discussion with careful guidance so that even very tough material is understandable.  You'll work hard, but never feel like you're going at it alone.  The single best professor I've had.
Great Teacher always helpful very excited about his subject lots of interesting storys that make the history more real than just dates to memorize
How can you go wrong with someone who references Mel Brooks' History of the World Part I... also he bought and sent me text books in Iraq so I could finish his History 414 class.

Dr. Monroe can only be considered an incredibly solid professor. He's is wickedly smart but not a bit arrogant, he's passionate about his subject, probing in his questions, and has fun during lectures. He practically did the research for my final paper for me on the spot. The only warning I would have is be prepared for the occasional profanities.

He loves the subject and it shows in his lectures.  Since he doesn't grade the exams the 'easiness' of the class varies by T.A.  I travelled overseas and he gave me a lot of good information on France (which is his specialty).

Monroe is the BEST History professor at ISU. I currently teach history and his impact on me was significant. Monroe cares about his students and their learning. He is very animated and LOVES what he does. Many others are more worried about being published. Monroe is always willing to help anyone on his free time..helped me on Saturdays! GREAT Prof!

he comes with energy and lots of information.  It was tough keeping everything straight with the French revolution, but if I'd actually bought a book for the course, that may have been different.  Still, even though the class is sorta tough, he grades easy and doesn't mind some humor and personal perspective in the essays.

This guy is very excited about history.  He makes the lectures interesting.  Keeps the classes attention at all times, which is hard for early morning classes.  You will definitely learn a lot in this class.  He does have essay tests, but makes them quite easy with many choices for each section.

I hate history but I was actually interested to go to class with Monroe.  He made the material less boring and he was very excited to be teaching.  Early in the morning its easy to fall asleep but this guy is awesome.  Definitely take his class if you can.
A great professor! If you have the chance to take a class with him, do it.
Good Prof. Speaks clearly and is animated enough to keep me awake, even after a rough night. He makes his tests very clear and easily studied for.Good man.
Great professor - funny, helpful, interesting.  Difficulty is pretty normal for a 400 level History course.  Love him!  I have to admit I had quite a crush going on.  Smart, funny *and* cute!
Profesor Monroe has to be my favorite profesor here at ISU.  He is very animated and makes the class fun to be in.
I thought he had interesting lectures, but I thought his class ignored women.  I know there aren't a lot throughout history, but there are some significant ones that he never mentioned at all.
He's a very animated and fun teacher who can relate well with his students.
I never thought history could be so much fun, but with this guy... you'll want to be going to class every time!

John is a fantastic professor who really knows what he's talking about and actually cares about the material. While his courses are challenging at times at the end one finds that they know a great deal more about the world than when they went in.
Interesting lectures and knowledgable.
No Comments
Excellent at lecturing!  Tells you what you need to know and relates it to what you are supposed to be learning.  He's funny too!
What a great guy!
He is great, really funny makes everything interesting.  He is very intelligent and he is very helpful if you are having trouble.
Makes History slightly more interesting, at least I can stay awake!
really enthuiastic, animated makes history actually fun...
Sacre Blu!!!!   Ooh La La!!  enough said:-)
John is very good at communicating things clearly and teaching the material. He is a very open person and makes sure he does not confuse on his assingments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His teaching style is not for everyone, and he can talk about one thing for a long time, which makes it boring. The material is straightforward. He likes to ask for certain things in the exam, and if you get the past exam, everything is very similar. Overall the class is not enjoyable, and he is not a very good teacher.
John, also called Matt, was a solid teacher. The tests were similar to the homework and his lectures were enjoyable. Gives off real dad vibes.

One of the best professors I've had at ISU. He is always asking if he can do anything to help us be more successful, which is something I wish I heard more out of professors. His lectures are also easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher, funny guy! This class got me very interested in econ (I'm now getting a minor). The tests can be challenging, but DO ask questions in class because he will explain them well and relate them to you. He goes on tangents sometimes, but it is very interesting and will tie back to engineering in the end. Always willing to help.

John was a very good teacher, probably one of the best I've had at Iowa State.  He always helped when needed, even going over the homework in class if you asked.  Also would share his experience as a Civil Engineer related to the topic.  Definitely would recommended him.

Matt is a fantastic professor. Very clear and helpful. You can tell that he really *wants* to teach, and that he likes helping people understand. If I could take all my grad courses with him, I would.

Jon "Matt" Rouse is a very energetic teacher who knows the material very well. He is always eagar to help students and to work with them. However, his grading is horrible, if you do not know the material perfectly or can do it fast enough expect to get a very low grade in the class.

He goes by Matt. He is a pretty good professor in my mind, easy to get along with. He really wants you to understand the material, and concepts he discusses in his lectures. He has good example problems. He is a tough grader, but his curves are usually pretty high.

Prof. Shen does have a very thick accent, but he is very understandable. Assignments are very clear, and he does a lot of examples in class. I really liked him because he genuinely cares for his students and wants to see them succeed. He is a really underrated teacher.

Professor Shen did a good job of organizing this class entirely online. There was a clear order of what to do each week. Some of the homework was kind of challenging, but he had an optional meeting each week to answer questions. The class does take some time with the lectures and homework, but there were no group projects, which was nice.
This was a good professor but he has a strong accent and talks very slow. Good professor but hard class

Professor Shen was awesome for BUSAD5020. I took it hybrid so I was in class once a week, and then watched lecture videos the rest of the week. His lectures gave good context and practice for homework problems. His homework is very straightforward. He provides very clear feedback and will walk through problems with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Expectations are straightforward. Dr. Shen is more than available to help students/provide resources. Homework (all calculations done through excel-super easy) due Tuesdays and there will be a help session to help you. Quiz answers are found in lecture videos. If you complete everything on time, you will be just fine.
Little homework per week. clear and direction forward, cares a lot about your success jut show up to class gives plenty extra credit as well if in class.

I am never one to go on Rate My Professor however Professor Shen deserves praise. For many business majors not interested in finance, this class can be difficult. This class is very straightforward and throws no unnecessary curveballs your way. Exams are very similar to homework, and Professor Shen even allows make-up points. You're in good hands!

Junyan is a great teacher and wants to see all of his students succeed. He does post weekly homework and quizzes, but is more than willing to help you on any difficulties you may run into. He does provide extra credit and goes very in depth in his lectures.

Professor Shen wants all of his students to do well in the class. He gives out extra and has review sessions for exams. He is also more than happy to go through exams and help with the homeworks. He has always followed up with me when I email about a homework question to ensure I understand. Sometimes the lectures are boring due to content.

Professor Shen is genuinely a great guy and really wants his students to succeed. The class was very easy and if you give a decent effort you can get a good grade. He was also flexible with his scheduling which I appreciated, and would accommodate for the student's needs which was super cool.

Good professor. Buy the professional calculator, it's worth spending an extra $10 for one of the exams. Study the homework problems and you're golden for the exams. Weekly homework. He will go over questions you have on the homework with the class. Exams are 20ish questions multiple choice, with formula sheet (No notes). Great guy

Great professor that truly wants his students to do well. Not a ton of homework or quizzes/exams but just not enough to know you're on the right track. Definitely recommend taking his classes. Lectures can be a little dry at times but that is expected with a class such as Finance.

Hard to understand through accent, doesnt explain much during the lecture so a lot is figuring it out for yourself, class is dead quiet because people arent learning and have given up on the course. look for god because he is not present in his classroom

Professor Shen wants all of his students to do well & will take the time to help them excel. His lectures are very informative, with many examples to help you fully understand the concepts. Would definitely recommend him.
Very kind professor with great lectures. Always willing to help whenever you need it.
Sweetest guy ever 10/10 recommend :)
Going to class is necessary and easier than trying to figure it out on your own. Professor Shen is professional, organized, and always prepared for class.
