That does mean that there's a lot to remember between lectures and the book, so the exams are tough- he asks some pretty specific questions! However, it's an interesting class, and he's a good professor.

Professor Shaw is one of the best professors I have had at Iowa State. He kept lectures interesting and had a great knowledge of the material. Taking 241 with him is a great way to cover an international or global perspective requirement.
his tests are hard, but as long as you read the material and keep good notes you will pass

This class is really textbook heavy. And going to class is pretty mandatory, too. The only thing I didn't like was that the course is an introduction class, but he kind of expected you to just know the terms he was referring to. Don't take this class if you're looking for an easy A. You really have to work.
Very nice, understanding professor! Allows tons of make-ups and will re-open missed quizzes, but the 2 tests are tough.
Good professor

Professor Shaw is a great guy and professor, he kept class interesting, all of his lectures were on powerpoint and the powerpoint were available online,  you might have to put time into studying for the test (there were only two the entire semester) if you want a good grade.

Really nice guy, fun to interact with. Tests are harder than you will expect. Lectures are almost exclusively PowerPoint and not very information-dense. Readings not covered in lecture to the extent that they are on exams. Don't need to consistently attend class. If you have the self-motivation to do the readings, you will be fine!

Shaw is a very good guy, genuinely cares about his students and is willing to work with them on anything. Class is a little dry and PowerPoint heavy. Definitely do all of the readings - questions will be on exams from readings that weren't discussed in class.

As long as you communicate with Kelly, he is great at working with you. I took the 4 week short course this summer, there were a few changes on the schedule, but if you can't log in everyday, you will miss those changes. Good guy, good lectures, fair exams.

I took the four-week long 240 summer course and I wouldn't recommend taking a short course with him. The schedule was daunting at first glance but I was prepared to tackle it...instead he switched everything around. I couldn't check the changes everyday like he thought I could. Overall horrible idea for a short class
don't recommend

The professor's broken English makes communication extremely difficult. She can't clearly answer student questions and often posts assignments with little to no instruction at the last minute, sometimes less than 24 hours before they are due. At one point she posted an assignment no one knew about at 11pm the night before it was expected to be done

The way Elham taught lectures seemed like she didn't even know what she was teaching us. Also get ready for tough grading on your speeches. The whole class complained about how she graded, forcing her to regrade all of our speeches. I had an A in this class and would've finished with an A, but dropped it because of her.

Dr. Khan was a very kind, caring professor who was very easy to reach out and ask questions to. Although the lecture wasn't the most exciting, engaging material, I still feel like she is a good professor and the class was quite easy to at least pass.

Doesn't care about teaching at all. Never prepared for lectures, feels like she's seeing the slides for the first time. Likes throwing shade at her coworkers and TAs, but it's not funny, just uncomfortable. Makes a lot of basic math mistakes. The upside is that she forgives math errors when she grades. Exams aren't bad and you get a cheat sheet.
It is unfair that students need to wait couple of weeks to get feedback from this professor. With all due respect, I have to say that the instructor is very irresponsible, at best.

3 total exams worth 60% of your grade. Online homework, vocab quiz, and written homework each week. Does not offer feedback on any assignments or exams. Mandatory attendance for "lab" period on Zoom. Only saw her on the Zoom once.

This professor grades incredibly tough and does not take off points proportionally, most times you make a very small insignificant mistake and she will take off most of the points for it. The homework is often confusing and very disorganized. Did not seem to be very understanding of the fact that we are currently in a pandemic. The labs are a mess.

This class was so hard. The homework took forever each week. I would spend an entire weekend just to do one assignment. The grading criteria was not clear at all. The labs were tragic. Don't get me started on the group project because those things suck and you don't get good grades on them. Lectures were decent as she explained concepts well enough
Fine teaching but she is the toughest grader. Never knew what to expect because grading an instructions didnt match like ever
Not responsive, and making easy things in an introductory course hard.
She has a strong accent, which is kind of annoying. Just does examples. Doesn't explain concepts very well.

She explains things well, heavy Southeast Asian accent. offered 3% overall bonus in the class if you show up 90% of the time. Make sure you know your stuff before each Friday because she issues in-class group assignments worth a substancial amount of your grade. Go to SI. Would recommend.

Best teacher I've ever had. She explains things very thoroughly and she's a very nice lady too. She's very warm and welcoming and her tests are pretty easy. The in-class group work can be a little hard sometimes but overall she's a great professor.

Group project grading is highly unfair, based entirely on peer evaluations rather than actual contribution. This created extreme results: one student nearly 200%, others very low. I had A's on all exams, wrote my part of the report and did the presentation but got a poor project grade. Then he said he had nothing to do with it and offered no help.
Project grading was not it!

Professor Kim was awesome! He was passionate about marketing and his research. I thought that his lectures were great, and the slides helped me study for the exams. I enjoyed the written-out parts of the exam because he was pretty lenient on them. He also gave out a lot of extra credit for attendance! He would bring in food for us, a great guy!

MKT 460 - Professor Kim is one of the best professors I've had. I took his class to fulfill a marketing elective, but it quickly became one of my favorites because he makes the material engaging and enjoyable. The exams are flexible, there are plenty of extra credit opportunities, and the assignments are very manageable if you put in the effort.

One of the best at ISU! He truly cares about his students. He would bring us donuts! The exams are short and easy, and actually cover things that are talked about in class, there will be no surprises. There are a few presentations but they are easy. A couple of reports but also easy. He is not a tough grader at all. I highly recommend!

I really enjoyed Dr. Kim's classes for sure! Unfortunately, I didn't like the McGraw Hill 5pt assignments every week that took over an hour too finish... He is easy to contact and gives a lot of chances for extra credit. The group projects WEREN'T good at all. He acknowledged hard work and helped me out! 
He also bought pizza after EVERY exam!

You will have 3 exams and final and they are all short answer questions, he grades hard - if you don't have exactly what he wants he will take points off. You have group assignments with presentations so if you get a bad group good luck. Would not recommend taking the class unless you want to put in a lot of work.

The class itself is not too hard but if you end up finding not a group that is right for you, it could be a problem. The professor does not provide help in group issues and usually responds in a mean manner. The class is ok but if you end up on in a bad situation with your group, the professor will do nothing for it. Wish he was more understanding.

I took this class to complete my MKT electives, and I think you should too! He is extremely kind, and exams may come off as if they will be difficult, but they are not! If you have a base understanding of the topics in the class, you will do well. We had to do a few presentations, but he isn't a tough grader, and the presentations are easy!

Overall pretty easy class. Theres not many assignments for this class (2 quizzes, 2 exams, 2 small group presentations, and one case analysis). The quizzes and exams are taken in class. His lectures are veryyy boring but attendance is not mandatory.
Take this class! He is a great professor!

In my mind Mr. Kim is hands down the G.O.A.T! He knows his stuff, doesn't keep you in longer than you need to be, is super caring and will remember you by name, gives you all the materials you need to succeed in the class, and to top it off he brings the class pizza from time to time.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! A lot of extra credit given, and the group work is pretty easy. There are 3 Exams in the class. Not comprehensive, but I will say you need to study. They are short answer format, but if you study it's not bad. I avg. around a 56/60 on all three Exams. Also... He brings pizza for the class like 3-4 during the semester!!!
He brings pizza and buys you things!! He rocks! Plus there is so much extra credit! I took it as a night class and we always got out early!

Gives a lot of readings in class,  which are interesting and are later tested in the exams. Had quizzes and presentations in the course. Watched a lot of videos in class too. Exams could be tough if you did not prepare thoroughly.

Dr. Kim was a great professor. He bought pizza for the class a couple of times and gave out a good amount of extra credit. 2 group projects and 2 marketing articles, but he grades them very easily. Only reason I got an A- is because I didn't do well on the final so make sure you study. Takes random attendance too.

Dr. Kim was pretty nice. Class was tues/thurs and only lasted an hour, if that. He bought pizza for the class every other week. There were sona studies, two small partner presentations, two exams, two quizzes and some EC.  He didn't put grades into blackboard, so keep track. No study guide either, but he puts *s on important slides.

Dr. Kim's marketing class is pretty easy. He does take Randomly take attendance but a lot of extra credit is offered. Lectures are ok he shows a lot of videos. There are two group projects and two marketing articles. These are both very simple and he grades them very easy. The exams and quizzes are challenging but manageable.

Steve was a great marketing channels teacher. He kept it organized, always had new material, and changed the class up with peer presentations. The tests consisted of short answer formatted questions covering in class articles, student presentations, and the main book. The class was easy but the tests are hard. He also gives EC randomly, go to class

Very nice and humble person. He's a great teacher and gives you a nice insight into the world of marketing channels. Take good notes in class because the powerpoints won't be enough, he expands on the concepts listed in the powerpoints. Tests are short answer essays, so know your stuff. Also, readdiscuss the articles in class. They are on the test

While Kim might be very talented and accomplished, she dominated group discussions, projects, and had no room for feedback from us. Our final project, meant to be designed and completed by our group, was almost completely designed by and taken over by her. She will steamroll over any ideas other than her own. Would never take a class with her again

I had Kim for multiple classes in Bpmi/Sciviz. Although she is a very talented artist and is knowledgeable regarding the major, she can be very tough on students. Be prepared for her to not take your feedback well. I wish I had a better experience, however her response to things that had occurred  with my class could be considered very immature.

I've had Kim for 3 classes to date and she knows. her. stuff. She is so caring and wants her students to learn, which is why she can be a tough grader; you have to show you put lots of effort and time in your projects and it pays off. She is very human and will listen to her students, make time for them outside of class, and is flexible. My fave.

Kim Moss is someone who is a dedicated and committed towards her students. Be warned if you are NOT  going into Biological Illustration then I'm not sure you will best fit this professor because she is apart of the BPMI studies. BUT overall WOULD recommend. I had a lot of personal issues come up and she was easy to communicate and understand!

She is very straight forward and did not hesitate to answer any questions I might have. While her grading criteria is not always clear, and you do not always get feedback in a timely manner, she knows what she talking about. She is very kind and very helpful and I learned a lot from her class. You cannot pass if you miss more than 3 classes.
She was ridiculously helpful and super nice. She really knows what she is talking about. If you need anything she wont hesitate to help.

Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but if you're struggling, the lecture points will greatly improve your grade. She has very straightforward lectures and assignments all formatted pretty much the same so it is easy to study for exams. Pay attention to the things she says in lectures. Most of it is on the exams. Her TA's are helpful.

The class is boring but very easy. You can get all your answers checked in lab for a guaranteed 100%, questions in review are directly copied onto exams, and the cumulative final was almost entirely copy and pasted questions from the previous exams. That being said I definitely learned more about nutrition and think it was a worthwhile class.

I think she was a very good professor and her exams were very straightforward if you showed up to the lectures. Her lectures at some points can be a little boring but overall I still learned a lot and the course was pretty easy.

Her tests are worded weird looking for very specific answers on exams. Lots of discussion on Packback attendance is random timing, and'll know if you're not there. Lecuter is VERY disengaging, did not want to go at all. Labs are mandatory, but slightly pointless. You just work on your own with the websites posted, then leave.

A very disengaging lecturer. I think I saw someone fall asleep at almost every lecture. She brought exams to this course, unlike her predecessor. She speaks condescendingly to you when you ask questions, especially if it's about companion animals and you are a livestock person. Easy enough to pass, but struggled bringing myself to her class.

Took her for 224, honestly not a hard class to do well in. Her lectures are very clear and all the details you need are on the slides. Her exams are almost identical to the in-class review. She cares about all of her students and will help you out if you ask for it.

Her class content was the easiest, just a review of 319 and 224. However, her exam was one of the most poorly written exams I have ever seen. She is understanding and gave extra credit to help everyone get back on their feet. She is kind. Her lecture style isn't very engaging.
Kirill is one of the finest physics lecturers I have ever had the pleasure to learn from.

He is the best quantum teacher I've met. If you are familiar with undergrad quantum (which should be the basic requirement for grad students) you can learn many things in his course. The lecture covers very interesting topics. His lecture notes are very helpful.

He spends all of the lecture talking and writing on the board with no student interaction.  When exam scores are low (averaging around 60%) he shames the class, saying that we were a failure.  Homework solutions that he makes are practically useless and lack explanations.

Terrible experience taking sports psychology. We had online lectures we needed to watch before class on Wednesdays, but they were never longer than 20 minutes. You are assigned a few group projects with little understanding or guidance on how to complete them. In-person lectures lack engagement, because it was just repeating the online lectures.

Lectures are painfully long and boring. She's nice, but lectures have no guidance and seem pointless. All exams are open answer. Lots of busywork homework, like writing assignments and papers in addition to required online lectures. It's unfortunate because I feel as though the topic of behavior change is interesting, but it was not presented well.

Dr. Werstein is amazing!! She is very knowledgeable and gives great lectures. KIN 365 was hybrid, so we only met in person once a week. There is a big group term paper, but if you get good group members it is not difficult at all.
Super sweet and understanding. She is very knowledgeable, but does occasionally seem scatterbrained.

She was knowledgeable and you can tell she cares about her students. I took her class as a requirement and wasn't ever too interested in the material, but I learned a lot from her. The exams are all short answer. She made the class more interesting than it could have been, and she kept my ADHD brain focused which I will always give props for. :)

Dr. Werstein certainly cares about her students. She wants to educate everyone on topics she is genuinely interested in and cares about. She tells good stories in class and the content is useful particularly as exercise behavior change remains a problem for many Americans. She is well-spoken and extremely knowledgeable.

Dr. Werstein does a great job of helping students learn and apply the desired knowledge. Written exams are not difficult, assuming you do the study guide and somewhat pay attention during class, you should be just fine. The beginning of class is content-heavy and fast-paced. Once we got into the groove, Dr. Werstein was interesting to learn from!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kira was an excellent professor! She assisted me with many of my projects and was quick with feedback and helping me with questions after class. This was by far my favorite class of the entire semester. She was hilarious in class and barely assigned any homework! Would DEFINITELY take from her again!
She actually cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

She is very scatter brained. I took 365 as a hybrid course with her and the online lectures were very dry. It always sounded like she was reading off a script in class and online. Many of the in-class activities seemed pointless. Easy class but a waste of time. I also never opened the textbook.

Kira is probably one of the best Kinesiology professors that I've had so far. When she gives lectures and demonstrates techniques needed for the practicals, you can tell that she really knows what she is talking about. She also does a great job getting to know her students and her tests are very easy if you go over the study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: I thought the lectures were very interesting, with a lot of information that you will be able to use in your own life. Kira was very nice, and always welcomed questions. She kept class engaging and fun, and you only go to class once a week and the rest is online. The online lectures were very organized and easy to understand as well. Great prof!
Most points come from practicals and being able to demonstrate being an exercise leader. Don't need to buy the books. Tests are pretty straightforward if you listen to lectures or follow study guide.

Break things down so they make sense, grades very fairly, the tests are not difficult as long as you study the notes, and she is very good at answering any questions you might have. She really knows what shes talking about and is very open to questions. Attendance is not required but she does ask for the occasional in-class assignment to turn in.

There's no reason someone with this little understanding of arch should feel as stubborn as she does about her opinions (which are always right and never wrong according to her). Even if you were to present her own ideas to her in final crit you will still get torn apart as she simply gets off to feeling superior despite her lack of experience.

She taught ARCH221 jointly with another professor.  She regularly mispronounced the names of international sites and buildings.  She lectured on Muslim architecture one day and completely misconstrued Muslim history and teachings as well as the purpose of many important buildings.  It was insulting.  She did not care to prepare for her lectures.

This person has never been an architect, there is no reason on God's green earth should she be teaching a graduate studio. Entire semester was unplanned, and she was very unprepared and unprofessional at times. Studio work did not have substance in regards to architecture. Horrible experience ever.

I personally really enjoyed this class. I felt like Kimberly pushed me to produce work outside of my comfort zone but by the end of the semester, I can tell it helped me. Sometimes it was confusing to know what she was looking for. Overall, she really cares for her students and is kind and I enjoyed being in her studio.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Online Arch 322 ended up being a breeze. The class format was 5 1-hour recorded lectures to take notes on every other week followed by a group webex discussion to "prove" you learned something. The lectures sometimes skipped around quickly from topic to topic but only to cover the relevant material in a timely manner.

I loved having Kimberly as a professor. She was understanding and gave me great feedback. I've reached out to Kimberly with things unrelated to ARCH 201 and she was so helpful and supportive. I looked forward going to class and talking with her. Just work hard, be involved, and don't be afraid to ask her questions.

I was hesitant at first, but once you warm up to her, you'll see how deeply she cares about her students. We would all talk at the beginning of each class to warm up. She gives great examples and helps you move forward in your work; don't be afraid to ask for help! As long as you show an improvement and participate, you'll get a good grade!

Was a pretty good lecturer which made the class very interesting and fun, but she took a long time to grade papers and tests. Also would try to bring politics into architecture class a little too much which was annoying but not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable professor who's fascinated with the topic. That being said, lectures contain a lot of "interesting" information rather than "useful" information. The only chances you get to learn which is which: exams. I completed very few of the readings and found that the useful information is likely in the powerpoints. Somewhat interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The tests are hard. Get ready to write. If you study and know your stuff, you'll do fine. The readings were more supplemental than required, and if you just went to lecture and took notes, you would do well. Pay attention.

The grading scale was not concrete because she got too personal and opinionated with her grading. The same went with her comments on essays. Her lectures were clear but also rather monotonous. Attendance wasn't a huge percentage of the grade, but you should still show up. I did really well in the class but only ever did a couple of the readings.

Kimberly is a good lecturer and clearly knows her stuff. While she isn't punctual, she is good at conveying important information and doesn't kill you on tests or papers. Show up, pay attention, read (mostly) and give it medium effort and you should do fine.

A lot of reading but it is manageable  and helpful as long as you keep up with it. The essays were easy, as long as you cover the topics you should get a B on them. Most of the content on the exams is what is covered in class. If you go to class and pay attention then the class will be rather easy but you will need to study

Her grading scale is a bit askew, everyone appears to get the same grade on projects as long as they try.  Injects herself too personally into students' lives (i.e. she makes many assumptions).  Seems to care more about attendance than quality of work in several classes she teaches, yet decides to show up late and unprepared most of the time.

I was torn between feeling bad for her because all of her students were so mean to her because of her unpreparedness for class, and shaking her as hard as I could because she is so frustrating to have as a teacher.  She wastes at least the first 10 min of every lecture trying to figure out the overhead projector set up and ruined this class.

Extremely difficult to work with. She's always nice to your face, but she has written some of the most demeaning, vicious emails I have ever gotten. She has trouble with face to face confrontation. She is not clear about expectations, but then complains that you have not done it right. She is very knowledgeable about the subject.

This was the most interesting class I have taken.  The subject is fascinating.  Kimberly expects students to read between 30-50 pages between each class which is a bit ridiculous.  If I had time, the reading would have helped, but they can be scanned and you  will do just fine on quizzes.  The papers are hard, but manageable, and the final is great
Terrible professor.  Lets her personal bias get in the way of anything students try to design, extremely difficult to work with.  Definitely try to avoid her if you can.

She has a blunt, matter of fact teaching style and is a very effective studio instructor.  She is kind of stubborn on what she will allow her students to design, but is willing to let you take risks, but she is usually right in being hesitant.  She is chronically late, but it allows for the class to have some leverage to get more time to work.

Kimberly has a time management problem; she is never on time to class and is often 15 or more minutes late. She is extremely knowledgeable about the subject but is not all that clear on her expectations of her students. I don't think teaching is her first priority. She's there to research and teaching is just the**** she's stuck with as a result.

History of the American City ... Kimberly's lectures are one run-on sentence, but are clear.  If you show up for this class, do the 4 quick quizzes and two papers, you'll do well.  She's much easier in a lecture setting than a studio setting.

The worst professor I've ever had.  Inability to communicate, constant tardiness to class (1/2-2hr ave) lack of real world/practice knowledge etc creates an atmosphere that is nearly impossible to benefit from her as a teacher.  I don't have anything positive to say about her as an educator
No Comments

Avoid this man. He's boring, he's terrible at explaining things, he constantly talks trash about other academics or textbooks, he focuses on the trivial parts of the material while insufficiently teaching the important stuff. He teaches freshmen like they're colleagues who make stupid mistakes. He curves decently, but the process will be painful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't take his class

Lectures can be very boring but he teaches the material well. He has a slight accent but it's hardly noticeable compared to many ISU professors. His hw assignments are really helpful for learning the material as they break large questions into small steps to teach you. Tests are hard but they're consistent with the material and he curves every test
A great teacher. Relevant applications and useful knowledge. Uses blackboard very well.
He isn't that bad of a teacher. He knows what he is talking about. The besides being Chemistry it isn't a bad class.
He does a great job of teaching and I think his tests are very easy.
constant lecture, its sucks
Was hard tester, but curves it so you end up all right!
Decent professor, he lectures the whole hour on the board like an effcient German teaching machine.  Lecture is boring, but he explains the concepts fairly well.

Relates concepts of chemistry to engineering well.  But doesn't emphasize important information enough for the exam. Has accent but easy to understand.  Overall does a good job at explaining concepts.
Lectures are very boring.  Not sure what he is talking about and don't care.  Can figure it out in recitation.

Very good at preparing students for the exams.  Has a bit of an accent, but not hard to understand at all.  Relating chem concepts to engineering very entertaining.  I've learned a lot about concrete, explosives, etc.  Will take time to answer ?'s.
He's all about **** memorization.  Hard to understand in class, and explains things very poorly, in attempts to relate things to engineering.
No Comments
creativity and passion

The class was more interesting than I thought it was going to be. Professor Knight is a good guy, and was very helpful in answering questions and helping students along their way for exams. His exams are entirely based on the study guides. It was a very easy class, with minimal effort involved.
Incredible amount of rambling, of which was sometimes confusing. Difficult to pay attention. Very easy to cram for though.

Is the weirdest grader and will take off random points for the fun of it. Has no idea how to work the canvas. She is quirky, I'll give her that. Take this class with another professor for your own sanity.

Find a different professor. Professor Knox is an extremely tough grader who deducts points based on her subjective feelings. She assigns so much unnecessary homework. Will assign homework over the weekend, but will not respond over the weekend. Claims to have a perfect Canvas, but it's riddled with errors.

Professor Knox was so much fun! She is very understanding and listens to her students to figure out what is best. Canvas got a little messy, but she was understanding of it and helped a lot. She created a really positive environment and made class interesting. I would really recommend this class!

Required for my major with mandatory attendance. Had significantly more assignments than other core classes. Knox is a tough grader and knows her material, but her written feedback is vague. Many of us had to ask in person. She's got a goofy sense of humor but can be rigid and insists her class takes priority. Withdrew because it was so awful.

I took ENGL 250 with her. She often didn't show up, canceled class, or moved it online on very short notice—sometimes just 10 minutes before class, which was at 8 a.m. She's also a tough grader and rarely responds to emails.

Do not take speech with her. She doesn't respond to emails at all. Her grading is extremely subjective, and she clearly plays favorites. When you ask her about your grade, she basically offers you no help in understanding how to improve.She is also extremely passive-aggressive and unprofessional, and for a business speech class it's pretty ironic.

Please do not take Jennifer Knox for speech. She makes class online less than 5 mins before. She will always find a problem with your speech. She grades hard and changes her rubric whenever she wants. Shes very passive aggressive towards students. A kid passed out while giving a speech and she made him keep going.

Words can't describe how awful Knox is. She will yap for an hour about nonsense, then grades on material never covered. She takes 6 weeks to return assignments, can't manage her Canvas course (though she calls it “the Cadillac of Canvas”), and plays clear favorites, so grading isn't based on merit. Avoid her at all costs.

Do you want homework/major speeches to take WEEKS to grade? Do you want to spend an entire hour and fifteen-minute class period rambling about nonsense? Do you want to participate in endless group work that's hard to schedule around your life? Do you want a professor who doesn't respond to your emails? Then take this class with Professor Knox!!
She treats an unimportant class like it is the most important class you will take at college. She is very hard on students and acts like she cares but she doesn't.

This professor grades harshly for a speech course and gives an insane amount of assignments for one as well. She holds you to higher standards than she would give herself and makes a class online 3 minutes before class starts. Extremely biased for a speech professor as well and is very obvious about how she will grade assignments on bias.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The description of the class was so confusing but I had to take it. after a while I figured out why Knox was different than other teachers. She told us to use what we already knew about how human nature to write. No teacher ever made me feel like I already know how to do it.

Flexible prof and really cool person. Huge group project made up most of the semester, with smaller parts due throughout. Assignments kept getting extended but when finals week came they all piled up and 3 major things were due the same day. At that point there was nothing she could do since the assignments were all mandatory Expect lots of WORK!!

Honestly, I find "funny" instructors who try to get know me incredibly annoying. I have 2 jobs and a 21 credit load and I just want to get through it and get an A. Knox was easy to contact, organized, and explained things well. The online class is NOT unorganized and it's full of pointless busy work but she streamlined a lot of that out.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: When I saw ratings on here before I took the class I think maybe I should change sections but Im so glad I stayed! Knox was most down to earth prof Ive ever have. She answers any questions in a nice and funny way. She answer my emails on Sunday. My friends who take other sections are jealous she accepts paper drafts.

Knox feedback is great. She basically tells you exactly how to get an A on every paper. She even gives feedback on drafts and other profs don't. Most students never read her feedback or the textbook or anything. They just b*tch. When we started working in groups, I had to show my team where the feedback and the rubric was and they were all :0. Sad.
Tough grader with limited feedback. I probably worked more on this class than on my engineering classes, so if you have a busy schedule, try to take the class with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Toughest grader in ISU and is not reasonable. I won't recommend her at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very disrespectful to students. She demands respect but does not abide by her own rules. She is very quick to threaten disciplinary action when she doesnt get her way or is proved wrong. Terrible professor.

LOVE her. She keeps things entertaining without being corny like some profs do. Really good and honest feedback and treats her students like the adults they are. Would love to take her class again, she's a gem.

Jennifer's poetry class blew my mind & changed my life. I liked poetry in high school but she made it relevant and gave my skills. Since takin g her class I have become very active in the spoken word scene on campus and writing poetry in general. It's a big part of my life.

Her style in class is good. She's challenging. Her lectures, in and of themselves are good as well. However, the breaking point for me is her feedback. The comments on our papers were very superficial for me; one comment on one of papers said nothing but "?". With her try to submit papers early to get as much "good" feedback as early as possible.

I actually can't believe I went three years at ISU not knowing how to write. I thought I did, but I didn't. I thought this this class was going to be a slog but it really pays off. Jennifer made the subjects easy to understand. People say she's a hard grader, but she's a clear grader. You know what she's looking for in a paper.
I had low expectations for this class, but Knox turned out to be one the best instructor I had at ISU. My friends who took the class with otehr instructors got nothing out of it.

Knox is awesome with real world experience. I got a lot out of her class. She actually read through my papers before they were due and told me how to fix them. No prof has ever done that for me. She cares about students and treats them with respect but she also treats them like adults.

For the student who said she tells you to look at the syllabus LOL. Everything was on the syllabus. Know was great but there were a lot of students that had no business taking an accelerated class. She was clear and really helpful, plus she answers emails on the weekend.I thought I  was going to hate it, but I got a lot out of it.

Often times talks over students heads to make herself feel sophisticated, very unprofessional and often times hypocritical. Picks things apart but doesn't explain logic as to why, just tells you to look at the syllabus.  If you are paying for your own school and want a fair class DO NOT take her classes

She is a really really really a tough grader. She always put requirements in assignments as many as she can imagine. It is so hard to communicate with this instructor because of her unusual logic. Please select other sections.

Knox is awesome! She's a tough grader and the course is hard but she's super funny and cool - made class enjoyable. Half assignments are individual and the other half is group work. Follow rubrics, directions, and ask questions and you'll get an easy B. No tests, announced quizzes on Mondays, and go to class/participate!

Decent guy but lectures a mile a minute, most of which can easily go over your head if you zone out every now and then. Reading the textbook is your best shot at relatively understanding the material and doing good on the exams and quizzes.

If you have struggled with biology or chemistry YOU WILL NOT DO WELL!! Biology 212 is 'recommended' but it should be required.  If you did not take 212/ do well, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!  Nice guy but assumes everyone in the class comes from an agricululture background and is majoring in agronomy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Knapp cares about his students and wants to see them succeed.  The exams are difficult so it is important that you pay close attention, study hard, and ask lots of questions!  He will be more than happy to help.
Does give points for going to class sometimes.
He super nice, but he does go through information really quickly.  However, he takes 90% of his test questions from old exams! All multiple choice!

Material covered is very hard and detailed.  His tests are 25 fill in the blank (no word bank provided) and 8 short answer questions to total 150 points.  A quiz every other week and some take home.  The great thing though is he is a great teacher and has great slides that give you all the info you need.  Just study hard and attend class.
He blasts through information at insanely fast speeds.  Hard to pay attention to.
I thought of him as a mad scientist without the lab coat. I liked the discussion he produced, although the class wasn't very active.
In attendance at his final lecture at Iowa State, absolute perfect lad.

He is a little cooky but honestly super good at going over material over and over. He explained theories very well!! people complain about him speaking of nonsense but he really was explaining how to think in different scenarios ... which is what phil230 is. His study review sessions are SUPER helpful ! i think we had maybe 7 assignments & 2exams.

Horrible professor, he talks about nothing but wild hypotheticals, and he never explains why we are talking about these hypotheticals. He just proposes insane questions that go no where. I would not recommend this professor. Definitely did not learn anything helpful from this course.
He an unusual professor that rambles a lot but if you somewhat pay attention the exams shouldn't be har
Easy A. Just show up to class get extra credit and then study his review sheet and you will do well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fair warning, this is a biased review. I hate this guy. He talks on and on about nothing important and I feel like we haven't learned anything from him. His quizzes are full of mistakes and most things come back incorrectly graded. Good luck figuring out what to study because his lectures are indecipherable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fair warning, this is a biased review. I hate this guy. He talks on and on about nothing important and I feel like we haven't learned anything from him. Take this class with literally any other professor if you can. His syllabus, tests, quizzes, EVERYTHING is a mess and seems unprofessional. There is no structure to anything he does at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: When it comes to Gordon Knight, we're dealing with a lecturer who makes significant leaps in the lives of his  students.  This is the single individual who made me want to follow Philosophy at Iowa State University.  The important thing to note is that his lectures are crucial.  You must attend and participate - or fail.  One word - influential.

I took this class Fall 2015. Dr. Knight gives interesting lectures on philosophy. He encourages students to share their ideas and keeps the conversation flowing by providing several viewpoints. If you show up, listen and participate, you should be just fine for the exams.

He's the most hilarious teacher I've ever had and is really knowledgeable. His quizzes are really hard and he has essay questions on his exams. He also gives pop quizzes. I'm glad I took it with him, but if I had to do it all over again, I would have found someone else. He's just not very clear and confused our class multiple times.

He's the least organized professor I've ever had. Thank god his class is easy. The lectures put me to sleep and he changes the class as he goes along. The syllabus changed at least three times over the course of the semester. I guess I would recommend it because it's pretty easy. I just wish he wasn't so insane

Kind of a nutty guy but such a good professor! I read a few of the readings assigned at the beginning of the semester and then decided to stop because he breaks everything down in class. So easy if you study and pay attention. YOU HAVE TO PAY ATTENTION. You can't just pass by sitting their, you need to be able to comprehend what is being said.

There are three tests in this class, all of which are essay except the final. There are some differences when it comes to his graders. Did terrible on the first test when I wrote everything down exactly as he told us to. The guy next to me got a perfect and I compared just to see and we had the same exact concepts written down.

Your entire grade in this class is based off of 3 tests. He grades super hard. If your missing just one word in an explanation you get points off. He nuts and needs to check into a metal health facility. You can't understand a word he says and he runs from side to side of the classroom when he's talking

This professor is wonderful! Definitely your stereotypical philosophy teacher, but in a good way. He is hilarious, engaging, enthusiastic, and extremely helpful. Takes you step by step through the study guides, & is very patient at explaining concepts multiple times if you're confused. attend class & pay attention. no need to read the book.

Mr. Knight is awesome!! This class is very easy and all the test questions come from the notes. This class was also very interesting and Knight made the lectures easy to sit through because hes pretty wonky :)
I felt he was unprepared for class. He provided no outline of week schedule on the syllabus to help you prepare and look ahead. Class wasn't too difficult, but did take some thinking.
Dude is a little weird but super funny and excited during his lectures. Good professor easy class if you go!
Really interesting guy. Makes lectures fun and tests are not too hard as long as you go to class. There is no textbook which is a bonus.

May or may not be on Meth since he graduated from the University of Iowa. Should probably give him drug tests frequently. Extremely hard to understand, however has so valid points about God and the truths to life.  Looks similar to a muppet, but there was no question about that on this rating scale.  needs to learn to wear a microphone

Gordon Knight is a decent professor. He is very interesting in lecture, but the material that he covers is very complex and he doesn't explain the material very well. When we would ask questions he would just say "hmm very interesting". There are a lot of readings required for this class and it's necessary to receive a decent grade. quizzes  E.C.
I think Gordon is on drugs. Seriously just absolutely high or cracked out. You can easily cheat on his tests, because he does not pay attention. Little homework and little effort put in.
The class is easy, but the topics get beat to death. I've never written fewer notes. It's frustrating to listen to him talk, half the class ends up being pointless.

It was a bit hard at the beginning of the semester but once you get use to it its pretty simple. He also tells you everything thats on your stuff, so if you memorize the stuff on the review you'll pass the test like nothing

Guy's great. Yeah you need to be a student and pay attention once in a while, but he get's excited and passionate about what he's teaching which is what makes his class so entertaining, enjoyable and educational.
Mr. Knight was a great professor. I would tell anybody required to take Philosophy 230 to take his class. He strongly encourages class participation, although it is not required.

Gordon likes to go on rants about things and sometimes goes above your head.  It's helpful to read the books he assigns but they can be hard to understand as well.  He gets really excited and likes to travel around the room and really tries to get discussion going.  Go to class, the random quizzes make up a large chunk of your grade.

He's really easy to reach out to provided you make the effort. I was shocked at how eccentric he was and it takes a really long time to get used to him. The in-class quizzes didn't really help me prepare for major tests (he doesn't return them) I'd say it's fairly easy as I'm in the A-range & didn't put much effort  except attending classes
When I first went to class I was a little freaked out with how exuberant Knight was. However, as class progressed I really grew to enjoy him. Go see him in his office hours, it really helps a lot.
Go to class and the tests will be easy.

Going to class was pretty pointless. It was hard to follow along. The multiple choice tests didn't make a lot of sense. My biggest problem with him was how long it took him to put in grades and when final grades were due at the end of the semester he added my points incorrectly leaving me with a 9% difference.

Knight's a good teacher, but the class is challenging. He is helpful as long as you reach out to him. Grades are only based on the 4 exams you take (half multiple choice, half essay). Don't buy the book if you aren't going to read it, like me. I never read the assigned readings, and I did pretty well in his class.

I thought this class was ridiculously hard. I went to every class and barley managed to pass. He gets off topic and rants about random things. The questions on exams are very wordy and very tricky to understand. Practically 0 EC.

Gordon Knight is a treat to have as a professor. He is extremely enthusiastic and knowledgable about the subject matter. He's always willing to help. He may occaisonally gallop across the classroom, but never fear, this is just natural.
This man is whack, but his class is fun. Go to class and you'll do fine. He hits the topics you need to know in class.
This class was so easy. If you attend class, you will easily get an A. The tests are short and come straight from the notes. If you take this, make sure you get Knight as a professor!
I did not buy the book and did fine in the class. The professor was very strange but class was not too hard, there was a huge curve.

My first impressions of the Prof was that he was batsh*t crazy. But if you take the time to listen and think this class will be a breeze. He does call out students but its not a big deal, just go over your notes cuz listening in class can get confusing.

Easy class. He would get upset if someone would leave early or would make comments about people not coming to class but with his easy to follow notes online along and his study guides, as long as you stay on top of that there is no need to go to class daily. If you get the study guide easy A on the tests!

Great teacher! make sure you print out the slides that he puts on his webpage after the lectures. Most of the answers to the questions on the tests can be found in those. Also reviews before tests are a must because he goes over the major questions that are on the tests.

TAKE THIS CLASS!! it was so easy. i never ever went to class, just the days that he gave the review (which is the EXACT questions that are on the test) all i did was ask prof knight the questions and he told me exactly what to write and i got at least a 90% on everyone. take it and make sure you get knight! its a guaranteed A
Awesome teachers

He is a nice guy, but he tends to start babbling.  I try to pay attention in the class, but I don't understand where he goes with some of his comments and is very hard to follow.  I would write down what he told us in class and what the book said and did terrible on all his tests.

Dr. Knight is a nice guy.  He just has a...unique way of teaching.  For those of you who don't know him, he is a very energetic guy, and many people have thought that he was crazy. However, he does teach the material well, and he gives you the questions that will be on the exams a week before. No joke! Know the Power Point slides and you'll be fine
He is very energetic about his topics.  He seems to make classtime very interesting by offering a variety of topics...conventional or not, I enjoyed his class and his teaching.  Big Dork!

I agree that this class was very easy. You hardly have to attend lecture, just get the study guide online and fill it out using the slides that are online. I'm not gonna lie, there have been a couple of times I thought he was pyscho, he runs around the room, hitting himself on the head, and he enjoys getting chalk on himself. Its quite amusing tho

Great professor.  "Engaging" is how I would describe his style.  He's goofy but gets you interested in the subjects. Tests are so easy since you get the questions for them a week in advance.  If you don't know the question, just go to his office and ask him for clarification...easy A.

Really nice & funny guy, but not really the kind of funny that you feel good laughing out loud about. In other words, he's got a very different personality. Short answer & essay tests (4-5 questions, 40 pts. total). You might feel like you're blabbing, but explain yourself fully & try to write things almost exactly as he teaches them.

Awesome Teacher. He makes this class very easy to understand and very enjoyable.  His antics are amazing! He jumped up on top of one of the desks in class and stood there lecturing for a while. Very funny to watch!

VERY GOOD TEACHER, the class was very entertaining just watching him. He definitely knows what he's talking about. I got an A in the class without reading a single book..he explains everything very well, just pay attention!
he's a nice guy who tries to make it awfully easy for you to pass the class
He's a pretty goofy guy but he know his stuff.  If you show up for class you shouldn't have any trouble passing.
ahahaha! He's really funny to watch! He showed up to class in what looked like his pajamas one day. Is out of touch with the modern world but he knows a lot about philosphy. ^_^ really nice guy.
OH MAN i Loved him, such an ambitious teacher. always happy and always willing to help. gives you pre-questions to all essays!
He is hilarious to watch! He is very energetic and crazy. He tests you on exactly what he talks about in class. Definitely recommend!
No Comments
I'm pretty sure I didn't understand a damn thing that this guy was talking about...he made absolutely no sense at all..and was all over the place...I half expected him to bounce off the walls!
Fun to watch! Tests are what is in lecture exactly. Gets his point across clear and well. Recommend.
i hate philosophy
No Comments
No Comments

For the most part everyone has to take some sort of Phil.  Take it with this guy, he doesn't give quizes, attendence, and pretty much if you show up two days before a test, he'll tell u everything to write on the essay tests...very easy! p.s. if going to class is your thing, he's fun to watch!
Wants you do to well, hands on and will take time to help you. Grades assignments quickly.

Had an issue with her where I brought concerns forward about a group member in the final group project. She pretty much told me tough luck and almost failed me. Mind you it's a required one credit pass fail class. I would have hoped that she would work with me since I made the effort to be progressive and fix it but guess not.
She truly cares. Many find her scary at first, but she means no harm. She is always there to help you succeed. My favorite teacher at ISU.

Overall, the class was fairly easy and you get lots of hands-on experience. My main problem was the professor's temperament and attitude: I found her intimidating and hard to have important discussions with. She repeatedly gave me the impression that she didn't think our conversations or what I had to say were worth her time. Just not a nice lady.
Overall, great professor! I would recommend her to anyone. The lectures are mandatory and at a weird time, but you never go to 5 pm. Lots of guest speakers, but they are all useful!
Ann Kolthoff is a professor that actually cares for her students. Super easy course if you show up to the class. Attendance is taken every day. Lots of guest speakers. READ THE SYLLABUS!

She was good for the sheep class, I will say she was accessible outside of class via email and her office hours were reasonable. Be sure to get every note from the slides and go to the EXAM REVIEWS! So helpful! Do the work as it's given, and do it well, it will save you so much time for her assignments.

I did not find this class useful. A lot of the time, us students were correcting her in discussions and she seems quite lazy. She never did any of the lectures herself, she's a tough grader and assigned unnecessary assignments. If you miss 2 classes you automatically fail, but if you show up and complete everything on time, it is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is MANDATORY; you will fail if you miss more than two classes. I didn't think the class was beneficial. Tough grader. Brings in guest lectures so she doesn't have to talk. I thought the class was boring occasionally, there was something cool.

Attendance is MANDATORY; you will fail if you miss more than 2 classes. Class wasn't very useful to me, but it wasn't difficult. Some of the lecturers were really interesting, others were not very good. Group video project at the end felt useless; if it was going to be an assignment, I don't think it needed to be a group one. Still a nice teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible.

ANS211 is based off guest lectures and so easy to pass if you just show up to the once a week class. She gives you the first half of the semester to make an infographic. And second half for a group presentation. Every week there is a current event (so easy and message points on the lecture. A pass or fail class. Attendance is taken with top hat.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He me so well that I barely had to learn the O chem section for my DAT, and even subconsciously used his tips and tricks while taking it. Lowkenuinely put on this Earth to teach O Chem.
Highly Recommend him for OChem I and II. He is just the best!!
Best professor at ISU
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice and very helpful. Also, he will let you submit reasons you should get more points back on exams, and lots of times he will give you more points.

Prof. Koeritz is so so good. He provides extensive resources for practice and exam prep so it's really easy to score a high grade if you put in some effort. Literally could never imagine myself calling OChem an easy or enjoyable class but I loved it so much and will be taking OChem 2 with him next semester! Love his baking products as well!

Yes, he is actually that good! He goes out of his way to provide copious amounts of study material and practice problems. The only reason that someone could not end this class with an A is if they are not putting in ANY work outside of class, and even then, they would maybe end with an A-. Most caring professor

Mason was a great professor, very understanding, and energetic! This course taught me a wide range of skills beyond chemistry. His exams are very fair, and he provides you with a substantial amount of material and practice to excel on them. He puts a lot of time and effort into this course, highly recommend!

Hands down the best professor I've ever had. He provides so many resources and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Built in extra credit on every exam. His dad died at the beginning of the semester, but he continued to be an amazing professor and always reminded us to tell the people we love that we love them. Seriously amazing!
Made a hard class enjoyable. Good lectures and a lot of time outside of class if you need help.
goated professor

AMAZING professor. He is one of the best professors here at ISU. He makes it easy to understand ochem and provides good feedback on any questions I have. He's also just an amazing professor. You can tell he really cares about his students. If you have to take ochem, definitely take his course!

Mason is the best professor I've had at Iowa State. Makes a 300 person lecture hall feel like a 20 person. He takes every question seriously and genuinely wants the students to succeed. He literally stress bakes over the students success. Has extra credit pre given on each exam, has really clear study guides that correlate directly with each exam.
Easily the best professor I've ever had at ISU! He makes lectures fun and engaging, and actually cares about his students. He has tons of practice problems and resources to help you succeed.

Mason is the GOAT. I have had so many professors in my time here, and by far, he was the best. I wasn't the best at general chemistry, but he made me look at chemistry differently. There are so many options to succeed in his class, through extra credit and NUMEROUS video and practice problems that he provides. He also holds study sessions!

I cannot say enough praise for Dr. Koeritz! He makes the lectures super fun and easy to follow. Because of him, the most feared undergrad class was one of the easiest science classes I've taken at Iowa State. He is clearly passionate about his work and genuinely cares about his students' success. If you're scared for ochem, TAKE IT WITH HIM!!

Hands down the BEST professor I've had at Iowa State. He is very enthusiastic about teaching and really cares about each student. He wants everyone to succeed. Organic chemistry is often seen as a daunting course, but Dr Koeritz explains it in such a way that is very digestible. If you have the opportunity to take his class, TAKE HIS CLASS

Dr. Koeritz is easily one of the best professors I've had at ISU. He is so kind and approachable and genuinely cares about his students. Organic chemistry is a challenging class, but Dr. Koeritz provides you with so many tools to help you succeed. If you need to take organic chemistry, make sure you take it with Mason!!

Professor Mason Koeritz is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. He provides what feels like a thousand practice problems so you can truly understand the material. The way he teaches organic chemistry is like a work of art, something even Picasso could not have painted better. He gives you every tool you need to be successful.

He provides you with more than enough practice problems to make sure you do well in the class. He is a very genuine guy with a fun personality to make a class like organic chemistry much more bearable.

Genuinely a great guy and a great professor. His lectures are engaging, entertaining, and informative, and he's pretty accessible outside of class for office hours and such. If you take ochem with him you're practically guaranteed to do well!

This professor is genuinely the best professor I have ever had at ISU. Organic Chemistry was one of the most terrifying classes to start because of just how many things I have heard about it. However, Mason made it a blast. He genuinely loves both his students and his content wholeheartedly.
TOP 1 PROFESSOR IN IOWA STATE. He even answered me the problem while I was studying in the library. He really care about his student
My most favorite professor of all time. It is very obvious how much he cares about his students. If you take any Ochem class I would never take it with any professor but him.

This professor is the best I've had yet at Iowa State. He is taking a challenging course and trying to make it entertaining and easy to succeed. He does everything he can to be accessible to his students and help them work through any problems they might have.
Gives great mnemonics to help remember certain reaction schemes and conditions (ie. squishy). Very helpful when asking questions or for help. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If I could take Organic Chemistry all over again with Prof. Koeritz, I would—and I don't like chemistry. He makes himself available to his students and just wants everyone to succeed. He'll respond to emails with wicked speed, every exam past the first two allows note sheets, and honestly, he's the best prof I've had-(give him an award PLEASE)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is one of the most amazing professors I have ever had and one of the best at ISU. They need to lock him in and never let him leave or kids in chemistry heavy majors are doomed. I passed organic chem 2 with a 99.9% all because of him. I would email him while studying at 10pm and he'd answer. He gave so much help to all 300 students. I love him.
He is the best! I actually really like Ochem now because of Dr. Koeritz. Also, it helps to make friends in class so you can study together.

If you have to take a difficult course like Ochem, you could not ask for a better professor. He wants everyone to succeed and that is clear in every thing he does. The class is obviously hard, but he provides so many review and practice materials that it makes the class very manageable. If I could choose Mason to teach all my classes, I would.

It's organic chemistry so expect a tough class with lots of work. But do absolutely anything you can to take it with Mason. He is without a doubt the best organic chemistry professor and maybe even the best professor in general at Iowa state. He genuinely wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The best professor to have for OChem. I genuinely think I would not have done well if I hadn't had him. He lets you have a cheat sheet on the exams, which is incredibly useful. Classes are recorded if you miss them. The homework platform is super useful. He is excited and fun in lecture and always willing to help if you don't understand.
Professor Mason truly cares about the students and their well-being. He is always ready to help us even outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If Mason Koeritz were a politician he would bring world peace. Mason Koeritz is the best professor on Iowa State's campus I had ever had the pleasure of studying under. Excellent notes, excellent lectures, excellent supplemental material. I would compare him to other professors, but Jesus Christ is more appropriate. Never change Mr. Koeritz.

I didn't take ochem 1 with him so when I started his ochem 2 class I was amazed at how easy it actually is. Lectures are recorded but I recommend actually going to class and reviewing the recording if needed. He's also super easy to get a hold of. Best professor I've had so far at ISU.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is amazing. I did not understand the content at all, yet he sat with me and worked on problems during office hours nearly every week. He offers so many extra credit opportunities and review sessions. If you can take this professor, ALWAYS take him!!

Took Ochem 1&2 with Professor Koeritz. Literally the best professor ever, he cares so much about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He is very passionate about teaching and provides so many materials to help students practice and study for exams. Ochem is a tough class, but if you put in the time and effort, you will succeed.

Mason is by far the best professor I've had at ISU! I took Ochem I and II with him. His lectures are entertaining and engaging, he does a fantastic job of explaining the content, and he's always willing to answer questions inside and outside of class! The content and exams are tough but reasonable. The homework is fun and extremely helpful.

Mason truly cares about his students. I have asked him many times to go over exams with me or to clarify topics I didn't understand. I have also had personal issues come up throughout the two semesters I had with him and through communication we figured out solutions.

Never take ochem with a professor other than Mason or you'll regret it! He is the best professor and I think anyone could agree. He is very personable, respects you, and fully understands what we go through as college kids. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Koeritz is by far the best professor I have ever had. O Chem content is known to be HARD, yet he compensates for this with his many reference items, practice problems, videos, and office hours. He is one of the most personable professors, who has demonstrated on MULTIPLE accounts that he cares for his students. Take his section! Trust!
Ochem 2 is a very difficult class in general, but the way that it was taught was interesting and understandable. Answers emails quickly and effectively. Genuinely loves his job. Very kind person.

Professor Koeritz is one of, if not the best, professor at ISU. He not only made organic chemistry comprehensible to learn but honestly even enjoyable. I have never liked chemistry but his classes may have changed my mind. He's always willing to help students and makes sure everyone is prepared going to tests. I cannot recommend his class enough.
It was my best decision to take organic chemistry with Mason.

Mason was my favorite professor at Iowa state by far. He was witty and engaging! I felt sad when I couldn't go to his lectures from time to time. Highly recommend him as a professor if you have an opportunity to have him!

Absolutely amazing teacher. He presents the content is ways that are easily understandable and interesting. He has numerous office hours and responds to emails quickly and is always happy to answer questions. His exams are open note which is awesome! He gives you everything you could possibly need to succeed.

Professor Koeritz is an absolutely amazing professor.  He really cares about how well we understand the concepts in the class.  His lectures are very thorough and you're only tested over things that are discussed in class.  He does offer extra credit throughout the semester.  Actually sad I won't be taking another class with him.

Mason is by far the best chemistry professor I've had. He really cares about his students and their understanding of the material. If you try your hardest and need to ask him, he will make sure that you understand, because his students success is super important to him. *Even though attendance is not mandatory it is essential to be successful.

Mason genuinely cares about his students' success and is the best professor I have ever had. I really struggled in gen chem and was terrified to take organic chemistry. His office hours are the best I have ever been to, and he is super approachable and helpful. He is also funny and makes lectures engaging!

Just an all-around great person and professor! Mason always reassures everyone in the class that he will help everyone in the class get to there goals for the class as long as they show that they are meeting him half way. Fantastic class.

Best professor I've had at ISU. Was concerned for taking O-chem but he made it much easier and more intuitive. Open to answering questions on examples and homework as well as having a great email response time. Provides lots of resources and recordings to understand content. Lectures are not only very helpful but more entertaining than expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Mason! He makes Organic Chemistry fun to learn, relatable, and easily understandable. I have never had a teacher be so invested in the success of the entire class, especially since there were so many people in the class. He is very easily accessible outside of class, answers emails quickly , and is always there for his students.
Mason is the clearest most straightforward professor that wants you to succeed. Makes organic chemistry seem easy.

I LOVED Mason. If you have to take organic chemistry, to do well, you MUST have Mason as a professor. He is the best professor I have had at Iowa State. He is an amazing professor and teaches the content really well. While class isn't mandatory by any means, it is definitely useful to do well in this class.

Mason is one of the best professors I have had! He made a tough class like O chem easy to understand. He responds to emails quickly/ is always willing to help with any questions. Lots of ec opportunities. Has lots of practice problems and exams are very similar to the practice exams. If you put in the work it will be easy to succeed in this class!

Dr Koeritz was a great professor for Organic Chemistry 1. He gave lectures that were easy to understand and somehow made organic chemistry into an easy class. He actually wants all of his students to pass/get good grades, and he gives out extra credit/buyback points. There is technically a textbook for this class, but I never needed it.

Mason is genuinely one of the best professors I've had at Iowa State. He is a great professor, making such a well-known, challenging class easy. He provides many practice problems and videos, which is extremely helpful when studying for exams. If you pull your weight, you can succeed in this class.

My favorite Professor I've ever had! He made a terrible course like Organic Chemistry understandable. He makes it interesting and is very understanding. I would take Organic Chemistry 2 if he taught it, that's how amazing he is. Attendance isn't mandatory and all lectures are online if you aren't in class.
Makes learning this tough course easier. Very nice, respectable, understandable, etc.
One of the best Chemistry professors, I ever had. Make sure to go to his help hours and do the optional lectures and trust me you'll be fine
Very passionate and quick to respond to emailed questions.

Mason is so caring about his students, and he has a great teaching philosophy.  Expect to still put in the work to study and learn the content, because most of organic chemistry is just doing a LOT of practice problems, but Mason provides TONS of practice, both in lecture and online.  I will definitely be taking CHEM 3320 with him and I can't wait.

I was scared to take Organic Chemistry because I have heard it's a really hard class, but Dr. Koeritz made it less scary. I am actually really enjoying the class even though there is lot of work. He has great lectures, great online resources (powerpoints and practice exams), and is always available to help in office hours or by email.

Hands down the best chemistry professor at ISU. The lectures are clear, and he does an amazing job breaking down concepts. He made OChem one of the easiest classes of my semester. Tests are a large percentage of your grade, but he drops the lowest score and gives opportunities for extra credit. If you put in work, getting an A is very attainable.

Mason is the best professor I've ever had. He's super nice and cares about his students. He lectures very well and always makes it fun to come to class even though it's not required. He offers many out-of-class practice materials, and the exam preps are always closely aligned with the actual exams. Plus, he offers easy EC throughout the course.

Best professor at Iowa State. Very clear explanations of course material. He offers plenty of resources to do well on tests (review videos/sheets, past exams). Highly recommend taking Organic Chemistry (both 1 & 2) with him!

Mason is my favorite professor I have ever had.  He is always willing to answer questions and supplies so many practice problems and exams to help prepare for exams.  He records his lectures and posts all of his annotated notes.  He also provides lots of extra credit opportunities and hosts amazing office hour sessions and exam reviews.

Dr. Koertiz was an incredible professor! I had him for O Chem 331 and 332. Before each exam he encouraged us to do our best, regardless of the outcome. Lecture was enjoyable and interactive, making it clear that our learning was more important than our grade. This was Dr. Koeritz's first year teaching, and he exceeded my expectations.

Professor Koeritz is by far the best professor I have had at Iowa State so far. I took both ochem 1 and 2 with him, and I thought that he made the subject far less intimidating. He makes a study guide for each of the mid-term exams, so I would recommend going through them. One of your lowest scored mid-terms is dropped.
Solid

Dr, Koeritz is one of the best, if not the best professor I have ever had. He made an incredibly difficult class easy. He is a fast responder to emails and always open to answering questions. His lectures are interesting which can be hard to do with complex material. Dr. Koeritz is also incredibly kind and truly wants his students to succeed.
Literally the best professor
Professor Koeritz went above and beyond in every way possible. He made a difficult course enjoyable, he is one of if not the best instructor I have ever had.

Best professor I've ever had. Great teacher, open to questions, and has lectures that aren't boring. The homework and quizzes can be a bit tough but there are many resources provided to help you learn. He is great at answering his email for questions. There is also a dropped midterm test and up to 3% extra credit which is nice.

This man is an angel! Best professor I've ever had!!! And it was his first semester teaching by himself. He's very new but he's a natural. He is able to make something like organic chem a walk in the park. Truly cares about every student and wants everyone to succeed. If I could take him every semester I would. Luckily he teaches 332 as well!

Best chemistry professor so far! Most of your grade is based on exams, but they are very similar to practice exams, and it is very easy to do well if you pay attention to the content in class. He cares about his students and made organic chemistry my favorite class of the semester. If you have to take CHEM 331, take it with Professor Koeritz!

Professor Koeritz was the best professor I've had so far! He made taking Chem 331 enjoyable, being that it is a rigorous course. He offers extra credit and is a fast responder to emails. He also offered multiple different office hour times. He truly just wants his students to suceeed! Highly recommend!

Amazing professor! He gives 3% extra credit, posts his lectures, and follows the textbook, but reading is not mandatory. Great lecturer, and always willing to help in office hours or outside of class. Tests can be tricky, but lowest midterm is dropped, and exams flow the same format as previous exams available on canvas. Be prof I've ever had!

GOATED! Dr. Koeritz wants his students to succeed in ochem and makes learning ochem enjoyable. Gives up to 3% extra credit, drops your lowest midterm (out of 4) class is curved and you get a note sheet for exams 3, 4 and the final. Hosts office hours mon-fri and is quick on emails. Exams are the same format as previous years' exams! 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easily my favorite professor that I have taken so far at Iowa State. Prof. Koeritz explains everything in a way that is easy to understand and comprehend. Any question you have at all you can email him and he will respond with step by step way to help you learn. 10/10 would recommend.
Mason is easily the best professor I've had at ISU! He's so good at teaching and makes Organic Chemistry almost simple! 10 out of 5 stars if I could.

He is a really good professor for a tough course. He posts his lectures online so class isn't mandatory, he uses top hat but it isn't graded. There was extra credit up to 3%. It's tough content but he makes lectures go by fast, wouldn't take ochem with any other professor. There's 4 unit exams but he drops your lowest one, but final is worth 25%.

Dr. Koeritz is amazing! He does a great job at explaining the material. Organic Chemistry is a tough class, but Dr. Koeritz gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit. The tests can be tricky, but they are straightforward and in the exact same format as the past exams posted on Canvas. Dr. Koeritz is awesome and funny!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Exams are nothing like the practice exam, and twice as long. You can spend as much time as you want studying, and you'll still get a low score on your exam. The average score on our final was a 60% after a curve. This professor is the reason why I switched my major. This is a pure weed-out course.
