The class was over excel, but he didn't really know how to use excel. Half of the time when he was trying to show us things they wouldn't work and he'd spend most of class fumbling around trying to fix it. No Bueno
Couldn't believe this intro to Java course would become a nightmare. Stay clear of this prof to save your grade as well as sanity!

absolutely the worst professor i've taken with . There were very little materials to study , did all the practice exam problems , and most of the exam  problems weren't even similar . Lectures disorganize coding randomly . For people who had programming experience , this is an ez course but it is not for everyone.

I hated every moment of this class. Not only was the professor hard to understand, he was unorganized, didn't know what he was doing half of the time, and didn't actually try to solve students problems. Our Canvas wasn't set up properly throughout the whole course, Pearson had many errors and glitches and the lectures were incredibly boring.

I had this professor for the Summer session of ComS 227. I feel like I did not learn nearly as much as I should have. He was very unorganized. He would get off task in many of his lectures causing us to get behind in the class. He would then put stuff we should have covered on the exams even though we had not covered it due to him.
honestly take this as a transfer class at another college
Go to class, take notes, do the homework, and you'll be fine

Posts blank slides so you can fill in the notes while she discusses content. She does pause for questions and will repeat difficult concepts. She makes herself availible every day before lecture if you need help, and the last week for the final she is doing in class review. Take quality notes and review before exams and you'll be ok!

No lecture notes get posted, so you need to go to class, but she explains everything thoroughly and has been more than willing to go over concepts again. HW and exams follow the lecture content, and no questions are asked over anything not discussed. Extra credit is offered w/ every attendance, and sometimes everyone there gets extra cred.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was able to meet with her outside of class, and she helped me with any questions I had! Nothing on the exams wasn't previously discussed in class, and the homework assignments follow the lectures' thought process exactly. Only one HW assignment per lecture, and participation points are random, but you get opportunities for extra credit all the time

Was kind of scared for this class, but all the content discussed in the lecture was relevant to the homework or the exam. Some concepts are more detail-heavy, but she discusses them well and will go over them again if needed. Takes attendance for credit, but the questions are meant to start discussions, and extra credit is offered each time.
The course felt disorganized, and expectations were often unclear. It was difficult to follow lectures because explanations lacked structure.
Harsh grader with little reason.

Does not provide the lecture notes, so if you missed class, or wanted to review, well too bad. And the homework questions asks for things that were discussed in class (ex: Describe the key features of "blank" discussed in class.) And if you don't write exactly that (like if you write more via the textbook reading) points will be taken.

She does not post completed notes so the lecture is crucial to your understanding of the class however she will slow down and repeat information if you ask. She offers plenty of extra credit for answering questions in class as well as participation grades for a cushion. She is a specific grader so she is looking for a certain answer in homework.

Dr. Koltes is great. She teaches everything needed, and lays out exactly what she wants you to know. Just pay attention and show up and you will do good in the class. Speak out for the extra credit points, this will really help at the end of the semester!

This course is graded on a scale of 1,000 points, comprising 600 points from exams, 300 points from homework, and 100 points from participation. Success requires strong exam-taking skills. Lectures move quickly with limited time for notes, and the instructor does not post completed notes, so what you write in class is essential.

If you put in the work and show up to lectures, you will be fine. I loved this course, and if I ever didn't understand anything, she would explain it as straightforward as possible. She is not a fan of answering questions in lecture because there is a lot of material to cover; instead, go to office hours. Overall, I learned a lot from this course.

If you show up to class and try you will do fine. She goes fast but is very willing to repeat herself. She is very open to questions and knows the content very well. She makes herself and other resources very accessible to students. It is a kind of intense class, but there is extra credit and a few drops on homework and exams. Overall a great prof.
No comments

I believe she fired our SI session TA because after she cancelled our SI sessions, calming it's "not useful for the students," the TA never show up to class again. She get rid of the only useful resources we had. This class doesn't have much resources, doesn't have study guide and lecture ppt, we have to take notes word by word ourself.
I hate her.

This will be the most atrocious class that you will ever take. The course is VERY lecture-heavy and and it is up to the student to write down word-for-word what the professor says at the time it is said. Despite that, the professor will change the wording, but will be referring to the same topic and will refuse questions of clarification.

Although she was a really tough grader and the exams were awful, despite most reviews, I think she does want her students to succeed. The information in this course is vital to the veterinary medicine career path, and it is important to really understand it all. Extra credit and participation points are provided! Study hard and you will be ok.

This professor does NOT want you to succeed. When students asked questions in class that she didn't "like," she responded with a snarky answer and made them feel awful in front of a full lecture hall. Your homeworks are your study guides but most of them aren't graded until after the exam. She takes attendance randomly and lectures way too fast
Dawn was so mean. She should quit teaching because she's so rude to all of her students, I'm surprised her husband hasn't divorced her yet.

She was the worst professor I have had at Iowa State.Attendance is required, there are written participation assignments you turn in in class.She does not record her lectures/post her notes, you have to attend class to learn content.She does not provide feedback on anything that is graded so you cannot see what you miss on exams or study guides.

Take good notes. Most the things you need to know aren't directly in the lecture slides and are things she just says during class. She will often go over information too quickly, with students having to ask her to repat things many times. No feedback on assignments without having an appointment with her. She gives lots of extra credit though

She is tough, but if you pay attention and put in the time, you can do well. Her new study guides are difficult, but if you ask questions, she will work through them with you. Exams have lots of question types and are pretty difficult, but can be reviewed. Definitely need to go to class to get participation points, plus extra credit if you speak.

this professor will grade you based off of HOW you filled out the test rather than WHAT you filled out, without explicitly saying how she wants it filled out. Gives no resources, examples, or filled out notes. If you dont go to class you will not be able to access the notes, unless from a peer. Graded study guides are the only homework you have.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking ANS 214 with Professor Koltes. Make sure you understand that this class is point-based out of 1,000 points not percentage-based. Everything that is on the exam is in the lecture and is multiple-choice. Every class has participation points. I finished the class with a 98%, you can do it, just put in the time to study!

Personally, Iowa State University needs to find someone better to teach this class. Forget anatomy, this class is ALL physiology. You HAVE to go to class to get participation because it's not TopHat; it's writing on notecards. Barely anything from the lecture is on the exams. Difficult class, glad it's over...

This professor messes with your grade. I have B+ on canvas but with her pre-final total calculations I have a C in the class. Avoid asking questions during the lectures because she make you feel stupid infront of the class. You have to take detailed notes or else good luck on the exams. The class average for the exams are a C.

Professor Koltes does not care for her students. If you ask a question in class, she rolls her eyes and reluctantly answers. Her exams are incredibly difficult. she says only things discussed in class will be covered on exams, but her exam questions are very word heavy, with words you have not talked about in class. She is not a good professor.

This professor talks very fast, using words she doesn't know how to explain when asked. She posts blank slides and does not post the information she wrote down during class. If you do not go to class and get the notes you will be lost. She makes her test trick questions so people who understand won't get 100%.

214 was a very challenging class but if you study for the exams you will end up ok. Dr. Koltes was ok as a professor however the lectures could've been a little more in depth and the final point total at the end was a little confusing.

Would never take a class with her again! She flies through material, her slides that she puts up in lecture are empty, and she speaks without writing key learning targets down. Most of the tests are on things we did not learn and questions are vague. She has ZERO patience for students when asking questions or even acknowledging them in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It has been almost a semester since I took this class, and I am still appalled by the way Dawn treated her students. She has little to no remorse for how she talked to us and was just so rude to everyone in the class. I am not sure why she expects us to come if she acts like this.
Little to no notes on slides, does not post lectures online. If you ask a question she will give some snarky answer back. I just hated how she treated her students.
She was an awful teacher. She puts slides up with no information on them, then she writes very minimal information on them. She gives quizzes on information that you haven't even gone over in class.

Lots of lecture videos and long reply time in between emails. Dr. Koltes is a really nice professor and her lectures are easy to understand and very thorough. She does not rely on the textbook to teach which is nice. The homework and quizzes can be tedious, but tests are doable if you take thorough notes. Worked with her for honors, she was awesome

Dr. Dawn is incredibly knowledgeable. She loves talking about chickens and many of her jokes don't land. Her tests are only over what she gets to during lecture, so there are no surprises. Tests are very easy and don't have any hard questions.

The slides are mostly blank but I find myself able to make detailed notes as I go through the lecture vids. Her lectures are very on-point and comprehensible, but some guest lecturers are confusing. Even with everything online, she finds ways to assign participation points as extra credit. Exams are curved according to how the class performed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Koltes for ANS 214 for the first semester of online learning. She was a very good professor in my opinion. You need to watch the lecture videos. This is a necessity to do good on the exams, fill out your provided notes sheets as you go. There are also participation questions within the videos. Overall she was a really good professor.

Pretty easy and straightforward class due to the amount of points available (a lot) and the detail in lectures. She's very good at lecturing, she answers students' questions well and explains key points. She posts blank lecture slides so you can take notes on them during class which is very helpful and I've never felt rushed to take notes.

As long as you study for her quizzes (which are predictable) and study from her powerpoints, you'll be fine. SI instructors are great help. Watch for when she emphasizes points in her lecture, that's how you know they'll be on the exam. Random participation points so don't skip. If you study, it's easy. She's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pointless class. Co-teachers with Burgett. Professors got to miss 3 classes in a row when students have to show up as part of their grade. To many guest lecturers that were non relevant to the course. Who needs 2 people to come and talk to students about resumes after the resume assignment was already complete?!

Koltes is an amazing lecturer. She explains the material in ways that are easy to understand and is always happy to slow down or explain something again if you miss it. She is easily accessible outside of class and her expectations are clear. Her exams are a bit tough but if you take good notes, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! She's amazing at explaining things in a manner that anyone can understand, coming from someone who hasn't taken anatomy before. She's really funny, and is always willing to talk outside of class if you don't understand something. Her exams are a bit hard, but are very doable if you go through your notes and attend lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Slides on canvas are mostly blank & quizzes are over upcoming modules, which forces you to attend class for notes & actually study as the class goes along and not cram for exams. Study the end of chapter summaries & vocab and you're fine. Exams are a bit tough and u don't get much time/question. Attend class!! Some xtra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Good prof, tests not bad as long as you stay on top of the lectures and homework

Hated every minute of this class! She speeds through material, her slides are always empty, and she speaks without writing things down. Tests are on things we did not learn yet. Tries to tell jokes but doesn't understand that she isn't funny! She also gets very upset when students pack up literally 1 or 2 minutes before the end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite class I've taken. Her lectures are interesting, and she answers questions in detail. Quizzes are scheduled on syllabus, and points vary with a couple pop quizzes. SI posts review sheets for the quizzes before and have most of the info on them. There's a lot of content, but that's because it's anatomy, not her teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is very passionate! She appreciates class participation and gets very frustrated when you pack up early. Text book is expensive, so share with a friend if possible. Only needed a handful of "End of Chapter" Reviews. The material is challenging but she does a great job compared to other professors in the past. Extra credit was really helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Koltes was new to teaching this class. In the beginning, she moved too fast and got distracted, but as time progressed she got better at slowing down and trying to get back on track when she got distracted. She wants to get the class involved but can be a little sensitive about packing up too early. She has a lot of enthusiasm!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Koltes is a very nice person who is very excited about what she does. She tends to get distracted easily in lecture but typically gets back on topic pretty quickly. She does a great job of making sure everyone has time to take notes on her lectures. There are extra credit opportunities and some "show up and get the points" quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Absolute control freak who freaks out when students pack up 1 minute before class gets out. She takes points off of your grade just for putting a book away. She quizzes on things that she has not taught yet. Her lectures aren't helpful and she uses the time to talk about how funny she is or about her husband. Be prepared to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The lecture is very boring and she does not get the material across to students. She has quizzes over material before she discusses it. She also does pop quizzes so go to class. The exams are barely curved. Go to SI it helps somewhat. Get ready to read the book chapters and study a lot.

The worst professor I have ever had. Will not learn anything from her, you have to learn it on your own. Does not have good jokes. Try to fall asleep almost everyday. Test material was rarely discussed in class.
New this year and is amazing.
Possibly the worst professor I've ever had, most time-consuming course I've ever taken. Avoid at all costs

Prof Rozier is VERY knowledgeable about anything related to computer science. The class is very useful as you learn C and git, but you have to work on the labs pretty much every day. This should really be listed as a 4 or 5 credit hour course which how much time some of this stuff takes. Exams are a very big chunk of the grade, but not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of resources available to be successful in this course. Definitely don't get behind
Definitely a tough course but probably the best course you can take.
Class is out of sequence and instructions are overly broad and unclear , lectures often contain material that was already due on previous week's labs. Labs take up 70% of the time you're awake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you have strong problem-solving skills, and some previous knowledge of Linux, this probably won't be too bad. You do get to re-attempt past HWs, so even if I got a zero the first time, with the feedback I could get a 100. If you're struggling in this course, just go to office hours. Some TAs were better than others so just try each one out.

Unreasonable expectations and workload. Routinely disrespectful to students and attributes nearly every complaint to student incompetence. Grading is convoluted and inconsistent. The only useful part of this class is the C syntax and the use of Git. Says that googling how to fix code is a bad practice.

Professor Rozier is clearly very intelligent and has done high quality work in the field of formal methods. However, she is unable to effectively convey this material to students who are taking this class with an average undergraduate's understanding of comp sci. She'd probably be ok PhD advisor, but is a subpar teacher of undergraduate classes.
Worst.

By far the worst class I have ever taken. Not a terrible teacher, but assigns an unreasonable amount of work. Prepare to spend 30+ hours a week on this class alone, and say goodbye to a healthy sleep schedule. Do NOT take this class with a heavy schedule.

Hardest class I have ever taken. It is a 3 credit course which takes up about 6 credits of my time. Be prepared for some long nights in the lab and some labs which you will barely understand your own code. Do not take with 18 credits.
Super chill professor, explained assignments super well and was very communicative.

I loved this class because of my professor! She does an amazing job of walking students through how to do projects the right way and is so easy to communicate with! There is work to do after most classes which could be reading from the etextbook, or things that get you ready for projects. Attendance means a lot.
She was overall a great teacher. The class was not that hard as long as you put in the effort and did the work. Highly recommend her and she is very understandable.
Best professor ive had so far, does a great job teaching and actually cares about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kristen is a great professor. Just put some effort in and you will do well.

Kristen Marie Neumann is an inspiring English 2500 teacher. She explains concepts clearly, supports her students with genuine care, and creates a classroom environment that motivates everyone to learn and grow. Highly recommended.

She is my goat. Wrote me a letter of recommendation for an abroad school after only having her for 2 months at that point (I got in btw). She is so incredibly nice and gives great feedback on assignments. 10/10 recommend taking this class with her.
Kristen was a very caring teacher, and I always left class with a smile on my face. She has clear expectations, so as long as you put in effort she will give you a good grade.
She grades extremely unfairly. No opportunities for extra credit. Often times gave me 5/10 on in class assignments, but gave me no reason as to why she gave me that grade. AVOID HER!!!!!!!

I had an amazing English 150 teacher so it was really sad to see how poorly of a job she did teaching English 250. An example of her being a terrible professor: I went to her office hours to ask for feedback on a paper and she told me that the paper was amazing and there was nothing else I could add to it. She grades my paper and gives me a C
Does not get any useful feedback. Grades based on how much she likes you. Overall, there are WAYYYYYY better English teachers at Iowa State than her.
She grades significantly harder than the rest of the English teachers.

I have absolutely no regrets with this class. At first, I was a little hesitant about taking a winter course, but I emailed her with my concerns and she responded really fast. She's very good about getting back to you on time. The course was a little heavy on reading, but I figured since it's only four weeks worth of classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good lectures and very clear about what is on the exams. She released a study guide with practice problems and an answer key before each exam and would host review sessions. I was not a genetics fan, but this class made me love it! There are many homeworks, but all have questions very similar to the exams.

It is hard to not succeed in her class. She provides an abundance of resources to help you. She is accessible and accommodating via email. Her exams are open note, open book, at home on Canvas. She posts exam reviews which answer most of the questions on the exam. She also drops one. The homework is guaranteed 100% if you attempt them.
This professor will go out of her way to help you succeed.

Dr. Kraft is one of the best professors I have had at Iowa State. She goes the extra mile to provide clear and concise information, and makes time to be available for questions. This class is NOT an easy A, by any means. If you're willing to work for it, you will do well. 10/10 professor, 100% recommend!

reviews.comment: Dr. Kraft really cares about her students. Her class is by no means easy, but she sends a study guide before every exam and you get two attempts. Her tests are difficult and require a moderate to an obscene amount of studying. Her homework isn't similar to the tests but she makes sure you understand. Expect to work for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kraft expects students to make an effort to learn in her class. However, she is not unapproachable and its clear she cares a great deal about her subject and student sucess. Hands down the best professor of BIOL 313 I could have asked for.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: I cannot recommend Dr. Kraft enough. She is very knowledgeable but makes sure to teach it at the level needed. She gives up a lot of her time to help struggling students. Attendance is mandatory due to quizzes at least once a week unannounced. This is known as one of the most difficult classes. It is definitely not at all easy but she helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor! I had her for 313L and she was amazing. I loved how interactive her lectures were, she liked student participation and group work. She was the one that pushed me to speak at the Yeast Panel and to TA the class next semester! She really cares about all her students

Dr. Kraft truly cares about her students and she wants them to succeed.  She is willing to help students in any way possible so that they can learn the concepts and understand the material. One of my favorite professors at Iowa State, the world needs more professors like her!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Johansen is an okay professor. The class is not extremely hard if you pay attention, but her voice is shrill and hard to listen to. Many problems on the test are recycled from practice exams. Material is interesting if you like the subject but is otherwise rather dry. Seems passionate but unfortunately hard to pay attention to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She rants during lectures about her lab work rather than school material, but going through the material won't change ANYTHING because her exams rarely match lectures, homework's, or practice exams. You have to read the whole textbook and teach yourself to get a decent grade. It's a shame she's a tenured professor, passing her class is very hard.
Don't listen to the other reviews, Dr. Johansen is great! She's passionate and makes cell bio really interesting!

The slides aren't great for taking notes. Her test questions are at a higher level than the book and lecture material, making it hard to perform well on tests. I have never struggled this much in a class, and if you are not a fan of reading the textbook multiple times to understand the material, I would not recommend taking this class with her.

She employs a style of online exams through the testing center. Will not be able to see which answers you got right/wrong. When I emailed her she said that basically because I had asked, she would think about removing the second attempt available for the exams. Then proceeds to say there's lots of students who have complained, but won't change it.

She is kind but that is it. I am a 4.00 student and I got easy As in phys ochem and biochem 4040 compared to this class. I could only manage a A- in this class so I dropped it. She grades nearly entirely based on exams and her exam questions are TOUGH!!! her lecture slides are useless and she just yaps abt her research instead of teaching.

The professor doesn't know how to prepare her students for the midterm exams; the class averages can support this. I'm surprised that this professor is not on academic probation. The only way you could pass this class is by reading the entire textbook; the practice exams are useless. If you can, find another professor to teach you this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She seems nice as a person. However, she consistently rants about topics we don't need to know about. Practice questions for the exams are given however few problems will be on the actual exam. If you don't memorize the textbook you will struggle in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor herself is very nice, but she doesn't actually teach what you need to know. I tried very hard for this class, and it still wasn't enough because you basically have to teach yourself if you want even a chance of doing well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures consist of pictures from the textbook that she never explains. Only way to pass is by reading the entire book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very intelligent but doesn't teach material needed for exams. If you don't read the textbook and take extensive notes, you will not do well. Her lectures consist of topics vaguely associated to the material and don't show up on exams. If you're a good student you can do well, it just takes lots of time and effort outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher and very inspiring - passionate about the subject!
She doesn't actually teach what she puts on her exams. The class average is ridiculously low for a bio class and although she says she'll curve at the end of the term she never does.
Will go on tangents and completely to actually teach what we need to know.

The lectures clearly covered all of the content that was on the exams, allowing for you to understand the content well.  She also has practice exams on Canvas that you can do that often include questions from the actual exam, making those relatively easy as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was a very tough class. Dr. Johansen is a nice person, but her teaching style just does not click with me. She does let the final replace one of your tests if you do better on it. I found it very hard to take notes based on her lectures, as her slides are mostly pictures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Johansen is super kind and obviously very smart, however, she makes it super difficult to learn the material in lecture since she is always relaying things off from biochem which she used to teach. We will go in depth on certain slides from lecture and she will say we don't need to know this till biochem, which confuses everyone.

For the love of god just drop this class if you take it with Kristen Johansen. By far the worst teacher/professor I've ever had, including high school. She is obviously passionate about biology but has absolutely no clue how to teach it to people who don't know the basics. Just drop the class and take it during the spring when she doesn't teach it.

Reads directly off the power points which aren't even helpful to begin with. You are better off skipping class and reading the textbook. Exam score averages are about 60% and there is no curve. Insanely smart but cannot teach for the life of her. Grade is entirely based on exams(80%) and quizzes(20%). I am doing better in ochem than this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I got nothing out of this class and it made me want to give up on biology.  I took this class the same semester as o-chem 2, physics, and calc 3.  I got all A's but a D in this class.  Bogus.  It was impossible for me to use any form of logic to get through the course.  It was all memorization which is why I sucked.  Also, exam questions were leake

Great class, applies to medicine and the human body directly. Power points appear boring because the class is highly fact driven. Pay attention in class and binge read the entire chapter(s) before the exam. Johansen is very motivated to teach.

I really liked that she provided extra study material on quizlet and allowed for 2 test attempts. I don't think the lectures are always SUPER helpful unless you do reading ahead of time. She was very understanding when I needed a test extension bc of a string of bad luck. Very passionate abt what she teaches and students. Test average was decent.
Basically, dont expect to learn anything from her lectures and just read the book your much better off
Going to class is not Worth it, boring and her drawing are horrible. Only 4 exam and final, final can count as two if a midterm grade is lower. Although is a hard class but their a trick to get A.

Her lectures have absolutely nothing to do with the test and are kind of all over the place. The test questions are REALLY specific and weirdly worded, so unless you have a photographic memory good luck. I suggest reading and rereading and rereading every single reading assignment on the syllabus and almost be able to quote the book from memory.

She is hands down the worst professor I have had.  Her notes make no sense, they are just pictures, and her explanations are no help.  There is no curve and the exam averages are extremely low.  I attended every class, took notes, read the book, did the questions assigned, and reviewed the practice exams, nothing helped.

I can vouch for the fact there is no curve in this course even though the exam averages are low. 100% of the grade was exams. You get what you get, except the lowest test score was replaced with the final grade if it was higher. Up to 50% of your grade is your final exam, so make sure you prioritize it!

She makes learning cell biology very difficult with the way she lectures even though she is obviously very passionate about what she teaches. The lecture style is all pictures, not much words, which makes it difficult to understand the pictures. Take advantage of the sample exams she gives and the book is super handy to  have.

All in all this class was AWFUL. There are only 4 exams for points, exam averages were D's and I had B averages and received no curve just a B. MUST buy book as her lecture is useless (even though I went first half of class, I stopped after I realized it was pointless) exam is in depth over chapters so read and reread.

As much as most people did not like her I actually found it to be a very interesting class. Yes I attended every class and did not skip but it would have been easy to get through the course without attending. Her subject knowledge I thought was decent and the book was beneficial if you were interested in the subject.
USELESS teacher. Just hope she keeps the online testing and lets you use 3 attempts! I never attended class it was a waste of time...

Her lecture notes are completely worthless. They are full of questions with no information and there is no way to answer the questions. She does not answer them in class and some are not even in the textbook.
She put a lot of effort into creating her lectures and used pictures and animations very well to increase understanding.  I learned a lot from her and found the class to be really interesting.

The most boring and helpless professor I have encountered in my college life.  I cannot believe they arranged her to a 8 AM class for such a difficult subject. I recommend reading the book, according to her practice exams, and pay no attention to her.

The class itself is very hard to follow, as she skips all over the book. She also takes information from lots of other sources without citing, so it's difficult to find more information than what she has in her limited notes. As kind as she is, and as much as she wants you to pass, I recommend taking this in the spring when she does not teach it.

She is very unwilling to help. I was having trouble and she gave me advice of what to study, and nothing she advised me on was even on the test. her voice is downright annoying. She is very confusing, no matter how hard we as a class tried hardly anyone passed this class.

She is really really sweet, and VERY helpful in person. Her lectures are very clear, but it's hard to pay attention because of the high, soft tone of her voice. If you find it hard to pay attention, and can stand to read the text, skip class and rely on the book to get you through. But if you can pay attention, her lectures are very helpful.

For STAT 5/4830, avoid him at all costs. Median grade was 77%. He prides himself on giving us "nightmare" problems on the exams, which, if you did not write them down in their entirety on your notesheet, you will not be able to solve. I did not learn a single thing.

You will also not get to the actually interesting aspects, such as Markov chains.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was his first semester teaching this course, and it showed in some areas, but he was knowledgeable about the topics and explained them well enough. I think that I was more of the issue when it came to comprehension. My main issue was that the practice tests were MUCH easier than the exams, so it was incredibly difficult to know what to study.
Respectful and helpful. Actually good Statistics professor here.

Kris was an excellent 361 professor. The class in general is a lot of work due to the semester going project but Kris make the lab and lecturer go by fast. He is very funny and down to earth but is extremely knowledgable in the course material. Work hard on the lab documents as they are basically the exams. Get a good group prior to the semester.

Kris was awesome. He happened to be very passionate about beer brewing, the topic of 373. When he lectured or taught everything was well-taught. Other people on RMP have said he's hard to understand, but I honestly thought English was his first language when I met him. Great guy, funny, and wants to help/see students succeed.

Favorite professor so far.  IE 361 is a pretty busy class, and Kris understands that.  IE 361 itself should definitely be 4 credits, and most people I've talked to agree that the class itself wasn't super fun, but everyone liked Kris.  He made class engaging and enjoyable.

The professor is readily available and is willing to help you in any way. The group project definitely sneaks up on you, and make sure you come to class to do the labs, which is a part of your grade. The exams make up a good chunk, so remember to study at least a week before.

For this class, he posted his notes beforehand and taught from them. It took me way to long to start printing the notes and taking notes on them, rather than trying to copy everything down. Made this class way easier. Some people are saying that he's hard to understand. I didn't get that at all. Not much homework assigned. Exams weren't hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is the best Statistics professor I have ever had. You definitely need some Calculus base to fully understand all the materials, but even so, Kris will do everything to help you. Ask questions if you get stuck, and make sure you study for this course asap. I can't say how much I like Kris. Take his courses please!!

Kris is excellent at explaining the material,hes not someone who comes in,throws a bunch of mathematical jargon on the board but he actually cares that we get the concepts  right and works hard at helping us grasp the material,having no prior knowledge in the subject, thanks to him i learnt so much in class with ease :) pay attention in class!!!
Can't understand what he is saying. Just like a lot of other professors in math/statistics at large institutions here's another case of, "what did he just say."

Could barely understand half of the words he spoke in this class. He's also just terrible at teaching it. The entire semester I was pretty much struggling because the notes and textbook he provides were not very good at teaching you the material. Do Not Take CS573!

Kris is an excellent teacher and he knows so much about the subject. He explains the material with clarity and motivation it encourages you to work harder and understand more I have never been so much motivated to get out of bed and attend his lectures in the morning. If only I had teachers like him for every class I attended. Such an inspiration.
He is really good

Kris is a great professor. He knows a lot about machine learning and it shows. He is very exciting to listen to and makes class fun. He loves math so he derives a lot of formulas for the concepts learned. He had 5 homeworks (one optional) all of which were very difficult but essential to do. Take this class if you can or want to learn more about ML

Overall, one of my favorite processors here, and her Canvas layout was one of the best I have seen. For the online section there was a discussion and chapter assignments most weeks, and the large assignments (3 total) about once per month. She gave great feedback and was super responsive in emails and truly cared.

reviews.comment: Dr. Stoner is a great professor. She makes jokes during class that are relevant to the course which makes it more enjoyable. Not much homework. Easy grader if she can tell you tried.

She is one of the most amazing professors here at ISU. She takes out the time to write down specific feedbacks for students and she is accessible outside class. She is a fast grader and gives the student enough time to discuss about their grade and to work on their assignments. If you have to take ENGL 314, make sure you take with her.

Had her for a substitute at the beginning of the semester. Very caring and made an effort to converse with students. She made English enjoyable, very much rather had her stay and teach than my current English prof.
Great teacher that made a pretty dull English class into something that you actually look forward to. Also gave the opportunity to revise some assignments after.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Class with her was pretty entertaining with her jokes and comments but the content itself was very dry. Graded on 5 major assignments but all the small assignments in between lead up to the big ones, sometimes it feel like busy work. Lots of writing and little reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: For every assignment Kristin gives, she posts an assignment sheet that tells you exactly how you will be graded. She is always willing to help you both in and out of class. Really funnyinterestingsarcastic in class. The final assignment is not difficult at all. Do the work and you should have no problem.  1010 would recommend.
Greatest prof you could possibly have!
Best English teacher I have had. Definitely recommend her for English.

Best professor I have ever had! She makes class fun and interesting. I have never been more excited to attend an English class day in and day out before. She is very clear on what needs to be done. I was very fortunate to have her for both 150 and 250

Classes are pointless, but attendance is mandatory. Not a lot of homework due for this class. The entire semester is used to write a informative essay. She is very attractive so i recommend her to everyone
hottie
For the class, she was alright; made it bareable...
Easy, but alot of the work felt like busy work, high school english was harder
No Comments
She was great!  She really identified with the class.  And she was pretty cute.

Great teacher I have so far this semester

cute

She was easy going and made class fun.  She could identify with us as students.
Very good English class.  My 104 teacher was stupid but Kristen was great!
Excellent teacher, friendly classroom
great teacher, made class interesting
She was very laid back, which was very cool and made it easy to complete the wor
class is very comfortable and it helps with school work.
she's laid back and awesome!!Great Professor!!!

Dude is legit. Brings a ton of industry experience (Tesla and SolarCity) to the class, so his words have weight behind them. He brought Pat Demers (creator of Ames Ride) on as a guest speaker one of the days. You get out of the class what you put in. Taught me a lot about contributing to a larger, enterprise-level app, and some of the nuances of it
Mouly is a cool guy, you can tell he really cares about students. The class work was a bit confusing but totally manageable.

Probably the only professor who taught SE 339 decently in the last decade. He only taught during Spring/Fall 2022 semesters however if he ever comes back do sign up for his classes as he is very knowledgeable in what he teaches. The lectures were boring however some in class activities helped make it better. Also, you will have lots of papers due.

I have also taken other, higher PHIL courses; none were as difficult as this. The paper guidelines are brief, the grading criteria is unclear, & grading is very harsh. He is not open to criticism, & on more than one occasion, said things to me that were quite rude. I really wanted to like him because his lectures are entertaining & he is funny.

Kupfer is hilarious and super sweet. He is very lecture heavy but keeps you engaged throughout the entire class. It can be an adjustment to get used to his teaching style, but he makes the class great. I love his class and I would definitely take it again. Super kind and caring and old school!

reviews.comment: Readings are mandatory and you must read them prior to the lecture as tests are given after almost every reading. You have to watch movies, they are very old and along with the readings hard to understand. Does not go over the reading to explain it until after the test. Cannot see grade throughout the course, he can give you an "estimate" though.

reviews.comment: Papers have very little guidelines and are harshly graded. He basically forces you to participate by calling on names randomly. Exams are based on lectures so take notes! ALWAYS be ready to be randomly called on. Dont participate too much, he will start calling on you more. Hes funny but won't take any criticism so be careful asking him questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor that I've gotten to take a class with. Very open minded and discussions were always interesting. This class is one that has stuck with me even 3 semesters later. Most of the class was spent discussing art and thinking critically about messaging, meaning, etc. There's a lot of reading, but it was always interesting.

He is a great professor who cares about his student's ability to process the material and build upon the knowledge learned in every lecture. The lectures are interactive and very interesting to listen to. A couple of essays and several exams are all quite easy if you chip away at them over time and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors I have ever had. Makes class very engaging and interesting especially with how difficult the material is. Would recommend to anyone!
funniest prof ever
Great professor! I loved getting to listen to Kupfer and learn about philosophy, take this class with him !
He is a great professor and this class was fun! There is a lot of reading outside of class, but he goes over the readings during his lectures.

reviews.comment: Horrible.
