reviews.comment: Professor Kupfer is an entertaining and awesome teacher. Prepare to read a lot, and he expects participation during lectures. However, he makes class hilarious and thought-provoking. There are many quizzes, a few papers, and a few exams. If you read the material and engage in class, you're likely to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely my favorite professor I've had so far. Incredible lectures. Very hard grader and the exams are definitely difficult but the class is worth it. Even if you hate philosophy, it's still an amazing class. Made me change my minor.

I took this class online so I'm not sure how the class typically works regularly. However, this class is almost entirely papers. You have several quizzes weekly but their weight is only 20% of your grade if I remember correctly, whereas the papers are 50%. READ THE READINGS. Everything is off of the readings. Ask him questions, he's gives feedback.

Loved Dr. Kupfer. Constantly pushed my knowledge and bounds to the limits but in the best way. If you like concrete courses that teach you to conform and memorize rather than think independently and deeply, this course is not for you. Would highly recommend taking a course with him.

Doesn't check tests for errors, there was no rubric given for any of the essays (which aren't even really essays), doesn't appreciate students with differing views, all the papers we read were decades out of date, and he wasn't clear on what the grading scale for the class would be. The grading scale in the syllabus is not how he actually grades.

Didn't give a clear rubric for essays and then when met with during office hours he still wasn't clear with how grading works. Doesn't check grammar on his quizzes and uses outdated readings and terminology. You won't know your grade unless you email him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The material you learn is so irrelevant and old. The quizzes and tests are about the small details of essays that have nothing to do with the point. The essays are graded very harshly and the prompts are so vague. There are so many better philosophy courses to take.
Kupfer is very approachable outside of class and is easy to get a hold of if you have any questions. Criteria for papers can sometimes be confusing but he's very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Kupfer is a great professor! He really enjoys the material he teaches and cares about his students. Just make sure to do the readings, watch the lectures, and do the quizzes.

This is the only class I have taken of his, and it's online. I wouldn't recommend taking a class online with him, especially if you have extenuating circumstances that cause you to miss something. He will not help you or be understanding at all. Overall the class is average, but prof makes assignment due dates confusing and is not very considerate.

Kupfer is really enthusiastic about the content, lectures are short, and the class is overall really enjoyable because HE has such a good time teaching it. Don't fall behind on the readings and do well on the quizzes to keep your grade up.

Kupfer was an awesome professor. He made it easy to engage in class and stay focused. He encouraged deep thinking and promoted sharing your opinion. He seems to be a caring guy. Stay off your phones in class! One thing he hates <<

He's one of my fav professors, but he makes you work. Such funny stories and you can't help but be engaged. Some advice for all his classes: Do the reading! figure out the author's main idea Go to class and discuss, he will be more lenient on grades if you try Take notes on the quizzes and study these for the exams Go to office hours for papers
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is compromised of weekly quizzes over the readings, a few essays based off of movies and two exams. It's not difficult but it does require that you do the readings, but they are short readings. He is a great professor. Super funny and super kind. There are no study guides for the exam so make sure you know the material as its taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Reading is required before each class, but usually no more than 10 pages; enough to skim over and be prepared. Participation in class isn't necessarily required, but it's easy and you will end up wanting to. He builds a very accepting community, and I know the names of everyone in the class.

I absolutely loved Dr. Kupfer. He's very kind and really cares about his students education. Attendance and participation are important, as the class is spent discussing readings. The only thing I didn't like was that he didn't use blackboard, so I didn't know how I was doing in the class (other than by my own estimation) until final grades.

Great professor, really cares about students success and learning. Lots of reading and quizzes can be tricky, but you will learn a lot and he is generous with grades if you work hard.  Grades are mostly based on papers and exams. Go to class for attendance and quizzes. He actually gets to know everyone's names and also looks like Anthony Hopkins

He's a great guy, knows your name, creates discussion well (as a lot of the class is discussion based). As long as you do the readings you're in good shape grade wise, its not horribly difficult. But as a teacher he's awesome, take his class.

The class I had was small (30 students), and by the end of it we knew each others' names and weren't afraid to talk to one another. He makes an effort to get on a personal level with the students. He uses the Socratic method and does not lecture. The entire class is discussion based on readings with quizzes everyday, four essays, and two exams.

Took Phil 230 and absolutely loved it. The books are a must have but they are interesting once you get the hang of how to comprehend them which doesn't take long. He is a great professor, you just have to put in some work for the class.
definitely need the books but a great professor

Kupfer is a great professor. He's clear on what he expects you to know, has set expectations from the start and will help if you don't understand something. His humor can toe the line but he will censor himself if concerns are expressed. He's extremely knowledgeable about his subject and reasonable. He expects you to think critically.
A fantastic, funny professor! You have to do a lot of reading, but it's all interesting topics that you should be educated about!

Overall one of the best teachers I've had in any subject. He's funny and also makes sure that the class understands the topics. He's also easily approachable and can help at anytime. Overall I thought the class was fun and he's a great teacher!

I took this in fall 1982. He was great. (My son also had him within the last few years.)I thought he was tolerant of students' views opposing his own, as long as students understood that they needed to support those views. I thought he did a lot (positively) to lead students to improve the formulation and expression of their own ideas.
Awesome and inspiring. Also very hot.

Good class, interesting subject. Make sure you're able to make it to all/nearly all classes because it'll hurt your grade if you don't. Keep up on the readings and come to class because there are quizzes on the readings most days. There are a few essays and tests, you have to make sure you really understand the material! REALLY don't skip class!!!

Kupfer's humor may be offensive to some people, but it can be really funny because you have to know he's only joking. He is a very knowledgeable professor and teaches by having a conversation with you. You can miss 3 classes per semester, and it is good to come to class because often there is a 10 pt T/F quiz over the reading. Overall a fun class!

Kupfer is a lot of fun. He's gotten better at accepting other points of view for sure. He's very personable, not like some mechanical-sounding professors I've had. I often stay after class to chat with him. I'll miss Phil 340!
This professor is awesome. If you are easily offended though, you should not take this class. If you get into it, you will develop many of your views about morality.

his humor rides the line of offensive at times but once pointed out to him he corrected his humor to fit the class. the class mixed philosophy with modern movies which made it interesting. show up, take notes and do the work and an A is in your future.
Go to this class to learn, rather than an easy A, he can be a jackass of a teacher and if you don't agree with him he may suck, but overall knows a lot about philosophy.
Kupfer was NOT one of my favorite professors. He is very rude and has an offensive sense of humor in my opinion. However, the class itself was fairly easy.

Kupfer was a great teacher. very witty. if you are the type of person who likes to argue, then you probably won't like him as much. if you just do the reading, listen and take down notes on the quizzes then you will do fine.
fun class, test questions are the same as the quiz ones so make sure you copy them down in class

He's a pretty cool professor. My  first qualm is that he will never admit that he is wrong when presenting to the class. Multiple times, students (myself included) has either a) disproved him, or b) come up with an answer that he "doesn't like", and he with a shrug or even not acknowledging it. In addition, he's a bit too preachy (politically).

Class isn't too difficult.Just make sure you do the daily reading (3-10 pages) and if you brief that(like I did 15 minutes before class) you will do fine.3/4 movies were over fun to watch movies so the papers weren't that big of a deal.Watched movie while I did my paper to get the specifics in the paper.Midterm/Final didn't study and Got B in class
Pick your seat wisely on the first day of class. Assigned seating.
best teacher i have ever had.  I took many of his classes even though they didn't contribute to my graduation status.
Kupfer was a good professor to listen to and was interesting.  His biggest downfall was his grading system as well as the pointless readings that were required for tests.
As provincial and stereotypical as they come.  His views on gender equity are right out of Steinem, and they don't weather well.  A stooge for the liberal elite.

Although he is a knowledgable philosophy professor, I feel that he could care a less about the success of his students. He is extremely anal and takes pride in the fact. Strict attendence, seating chart, no closing your eyes, pretty much your mean high school English teacher all over again.

I've never had a professor more full of himself. Instead of trying to actually help you understand anything he spent the entire class trying to be cool and make people like him. And don't ever be tired when you go to his class because if you even let your head fall for a second he'll single you out and treat you like a idiot in front of everyone.

Phil 230 with Kupfer was my favorite class throughout my entire college experience. I think he was a great teacher and he made the material interesting. He is a little set in his ways but what older professor isn't?
No Comments
VERY interesting, I looked forward to class every day. Really got into some great discussions - animal rights, licensing parenting, the morality of friendship, the will to power, etc. Great teacher!

He's not as easy as he sounds. Almost every single class he gave a quiz which was over the assigned reading. Papers (there are 4) are the most heavily weighed but take forever to write! (Tough subjects) and his 2 exams are only worth 10% each. Atendance is mandatory- miss 3 or grade suffers and you'll miss quizzes. He has terrible jokes- very mean!
You learn a lot, but the class is pretty hard.  Attendance is required and there is a seating chart.  Papers are tough and so are the tests.  Take it if you want to learn, not an easy A.
this class sucked.  not really worth my time, and was very boring and anal about many things.
No Comments
Boorish and preachy.  Anal about seating of all things.  I would not reccomend to upperclassmen or the highly intellegent, as he will insult your intellegence.
Aesthetics is a pretty fabulous class. Very laid-back.

Try and avoid this guy if at all possible, thinks way too highly of himself to do any real good.  Expects the whole class to watch a single movie outside of class.. Too bad there are not 200 rental places in ames.  Overall not a bad guy, but a horribly boring class, and the video thing was rediculous.

I really enjoyed his class. Quizzes were not that difficult if you do the readings.  Papers are graded a bit tough, but fairly. He has a passion for the material that is missing from many professors.  He also keeps class interesting and lively.  Attendance policy is brutal. Miss 3 classes & fail.
He's a pretty good prof, but grades extremely hard on his papers, so be prepared to not get the grade you want to.

This guy teaches so incredibly! You get so much out of the class! I highly recommend taking it..yes the papers are graded a little bit heavily..but with the daily quizzes..it's really easy to make up for lost points!

He is a great guy.  Defintely my best and favorite professor so far.  I don't mind coming to class to hear his lectures. Very Interactive class.  Papers can be a little difficult,but Kupfer is very willing to help his students.  He is very witty and intelligent, but able to relate to his students ve

Class is much easier and you get a much better grade if you do the readings. He assigns pretty interesting ones, and leads very helpful discussions. Test questions are sometimes a little bit difficult, but if you go to most of the classes and pay attention, you should get a good grade.
Made the class fun!!
No Comments
Great teacher, he creates great discussion and is very enjoyable to listen to.
Rocks!

I love Kupfer. I have taken two of his classes and was a T.A. for him also. He's a great guy and always helpful. Not hard if you talk to him about problems, and he's very approachable. He's definitely tough on attendance though.

Attendence policy is bogus- Watch Out!! Missed more than 3 classes & failed DESPITE "A" average & reasons for miss were documented family emergencies! Strongly recommend avoiding any class by him unless you can absolutely guarantee yourself neve

This is a great class that will compliment any major, and Kupfer is a great professor.  Awesome sense of humor, interesting lecture, and just reading the material makes it not TOO tough.  I would really like to meet his daughter...he talks about her a lot
fun teacher

I look forward to Kupfer's class every time I have it. He does a great job with explaining the material and he really knows his stuff. He also makes class interesting/funny. The quizzes aren't hard if you just read the assigned material!
He is hilarious, but I don't sometimes I'm not sure what he wants from us.

I dont know what you guys are thinking, he is my favorite professor!! He is hilarious and he relates the material to you in ways that you understand, if you are having trouble with this class it is only because you dont go or dont do the readings.

He is very cocky and only likes to hear what he believes, any counter points will be scoffed at by him. His quizzes are difficult and his book is by far the worst piece of crap I ever had to read, Im definately going to burn it...
This guy rocks. He is pretty funny, gives great lectures. Explains the topic very well. He is a teacher you need to have atleast for one class.

He has a certain animosity toward his students, especially those who contact him outside of class.  His book is horrible; I would use it for toilet paper, but I don't trust it near my ass.  There are much better profs for this class.  Easy though.

I was in 2 classes he taught (230 and 333). I developed an appreciation for his abilities the second time. If you do not do the daily readings and/or not go to class you will not do well at all. I highly recommend 333 (he is the only one who teaches it).
Great class, great guy. Laid back in his class, easy guy to discuss with. He really gets you thinking. He's probably the main reason why I decided to get a Philosophy minor.
Bo this man boooo

I think that Kupfer is a great professor, thus my taking more than one course from him.  He is witty, personal, and very intelligent.  Very well versed.  Take the opportunity to have him for a class, you'll be challenged and will be better because of it.

Some might say he's a mean @$$hole, but I think he does a great job at getting discussion going in class.  He grades kind of tough on papers, but if you understand the material and ask intelligent questions, you'll do just fine!  PS Go to class!

Although he can be a bear to students that do not argue logically; he is willing to listen to any students point of view. He also tries to push all of his students out of their comfort zone (one of the purposes of Philosophy) to reevaluate their beliefs
He's mean, he's a hypocrite, and if you don't agree with him, you won't do well
He requires a crappy book he wrote for the class and charges $30 for it.

Dr. Krier is brilliant. Truly worth your time to take his class. Yes it's lecture heavy, but he references back to prior concepts and connects units it makes it easy to follow. He's energetic, student engaging, and a professor that's worth your time. A fair grader as long as you show effort!

Professor Krier is a blast in the classroom. His lectures are high energy and passionate albeit pretty disorganized. The assignments in this class are very easy and mostly just for attendance, and the exams are also easy as long as you study well. I will say if you have a right wing bias you might not enjoy a lot of what he has to say in this class
He's awesome

Daniel Krier is all over the place and makes a class that is supposed to be easy and makes it insufferable to take. He posts over one hour long lecture videos and makes you watch two per lecture and then discusses nothing in the videos in lecture. He talks way too much about politics and doesn't teach his subject. Class was very infuriating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Krier was easily accessible outside of class and answered emails promptly. The content itself was fascinating, and I have learned so much! The class is a "work at your own pace" class, which can be tricky if you ever run behind on the material. Overall, I would recommend this class with Dr. Krier!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Krier is one of my favorite professors at ISU. He's very caring and understanding. Attendance isn't required, but I go because his material is very interesting. He's hilarious and passionate about his teachings. He records lecture videos so we can watch before class, and they are long, but the concepts are easy to understand.

This man was crazy, he singled out students for religious views and sociological backgrounds. Proudly told us his beliefs on Marxism and political views, then criticized ours. Used phrases like "if you beat the cows, you beat the kids" and said he had never killed a student but had thought about it. Exams and quizzes are harder than they need to be

Krier is a passionate professor who cares deeply about his students. While his lectures can be disorganized, he's eager to help in office hours. Using unstuck study and the free textbook can make the class manageable.

Unfortunately, my experience with this "professor' left much to be desired. Moreover, communication outside of class was practically non-existent. The grading criteria appeared inconsistent and arbitrary. Assignments were returned with minimal feedback. I felt unengaged and unsupported throughout the semester.

I took his class online so maybe it was different in person but I really did not enjoy this class. The class felt like a history class rather than a sociology class. He wasn't organized, constantly bounced around making him hard to follow, didn't use slides. Seems like a sweet guy and would probably be better in person.

I've taken 3 classes with Krier; 2 were online. I find taking notes in his courses difficult and frustrating because he is all over the place during his lectures. He often begins with one idea and then bounces back and forth between ideas, making it difficult to track what info goes under what heading. Otherwise, he's energetic and caring!

Dr. Krier is such a great professor! He had a lot of quizzes, readings, and lectures to watch but you could tell he really cares for teaching. He also had really funny and interesting lectures. He was always generous with tests, like not having a final test for SOC 401 and allowing an extra week for essays in SOC 334. I recommend his classes.
Handwriting is hard to read and lectures can drag on but he is very good with how he trys to explain stuff and does well to help make sure you know whats going on

Thoughtful professor that cares deeply about students and helps them understand class content. Some of the books were interesting and a good read, others were bland and hard to read without falling asleep. If you attend the lectures and watch his recorded videos, you will do fine. If you are interested in the subject, talk to him in office hours!

Such a kind professor and very passionate about what he teaches. He really cares about his students. Only negatives are that he is slightly disorganized and takes a while to respond to email. It's best to just talk to him after class. I recommend going to his office hours, he is extremely helpful.

This class was brilliant. Engaging and thought-provoking. Very discussion heavy but well-led. Hilarious and awesome professor. Very heavy on reading but that is to be expected, and all texts chosen were relevant and well connected to one another. Great course, great professor. 100% would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very passionate about what he teaches. Writes on the whiteboard, talks through the lecture in his unique way but is personalized. Encourages participation and is very easy to talk to. Do not be afraid to go to his office he is friendly and willing to bend over backwards to help your grade and you. Do what he suggests, listen to his lect. recordings

Dr. Krier is a very good researcher and professor. I just think this course is outdated and he doesn't know how to educate in a way where he makes material comprehensive. Also, he does not give you back your scores until the end of the course so you never know where you are at. Also, random quizzes whenever he says.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love him.

THE best professor I have ever had at Iowa State. Truly inspirational, and a professor who really cares about his work and actually uses his brain. I would take his class again in a heartbeat. Best class I ever took

For the online version I watched lectures and did readings. Very easy points. All you have to do is put in the effort. Easy grader, I got full points on all the short assignments and does unit adjustment points which work as extra credit. Loved the material in the class. Useful material that makes you open your eyes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is a wonderful outlook, but be prepared to spend an hour or so a day, especially with the online class, reading the textbook and watching 45 minute - hour long lectures. The lectures can be sped up which is nice, but your grade depends upon reading comprehension of the text book and your ability to pay attention during lecture.

Prof Krier is a really passionate awesome professor. He knows so much about the subject and loves to talk about it, which is present in his lecturing style. I took this class online and it was definitely not a breeze, very self paced and hours of reading+lectures a day. Friendly and easy to get a hold of via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Was a great teacher and really helped with continuing my learning. I didn't receive a great grade based on my own reasons. I would strongly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about what he teaches. I found it refreshing. I was always entertained watching his lectures. I took this class online and found it easy to get good grades as long as I put in the effort to do the readings and watch his lectures. I rarely had to actually study for any exam of his.

Horrible! You buy a book, but he uses his own materials and tests over it. The book is nothing. He uses the class to spread his own beliefs and his beliefs are "right" and everything else is "wrong." Take with another instructor or use dual- or cross enrollment at DMACC. The F I received was my own choice because I couldn't stand his teaching.

Fantastic professor. Very energetic and passionate about what he does. Incredibly intelligent man and is superb at explaining concepts. The class is not a walk in the park but I would highly recommend it if you are interested in learning a lot.

Good guy, very goofy and opinionated. A lot of reading for each tests and quizzes every week. 10 points for attendance randomly throughout the semester. He was not super organized, and his lectures seemed so long and very boring. Would not recommend class. He curves a lot though!
He was a great teacher and always made class fun! There was only 4 papers and 5 exams!

Would really recommend taking this online. The readings (which he wrote himself) are hilarious and made the material much easier to understand. Exams were easy and the quizzes you do at home are a piece of cake.
HIS LECTURES ARE SUPER CONFUSING, AT IT IS HARD TO UNDERSTAND THE MAIN POINT.

He's a good guy but often he gets a little to into his own topic and strays away from tested material making his test tough. Showing up to class is not necessary but will help your grade with clickers. He assigns papers however they are short and easy so no worries.

I wish i would have paid more attention in this class, maybe i would have done better and enjoyed it more. Krier knows what he's talking about but his notes can get pretty messy/ all over the place. If you take notes on laptop, good luck, bc he also uses drawings to explain things. Hes a nice prof, and knows what he's talking about, just pay attn!
He is definitely very concept based and can spend 20 minutes elaborating on a single idea. But if you are willing to attend class, read the textbook, and pay attention to lecture, you'll do well.

Do not skip class. Every clicker quiz is worth ten points. That's ten points every class time. If you miss them you could miss up to 20% of your grading that is easy. The class has required group work in assigned groups but they are very easy and do not require any out of class time. Just show up and pay attention and you will get an A.
Pretty easy class as long as you can deal with his Marxist views on the world. He is very passionate about his stance and if you can put up with it you will do fine.

I took his online class about 3 years ago. Honestly, it was hard (but not difficult) because (1) he often ran across the classroom which made students hard to hear him (2) he got too passionate about whatever topics he was talking about and go off topics. SO DISTRACTING and ANNOYING. In short he is the WORST LEAST EFFECTIVE professor in my 4 yrs

Teaches only based on his opinion. When I asked my friends taking a different Soc 134 class what materials they were learning there was nothing similar to Krier's lectures. Quizzes require a lot of reading.
This was the hardest class I've ever taken. Krier is a really nice guy and is very passionate about what he is teaching, but his teaching style did not correlate with my learning style.

You are basically quizzed on his opinions. Oh, and there are 24 quizzes and 6 exams in a 16 week course. Oh, and you have to read 30-50 pages for every quiz. Do the math. That's around 1000 pages of reading over the course of the semester.

Fantastic teacher, probably the best I have had in the four years at Iowa State. Go to class because he explains everything. He is very understanding and flexible and willing to answer any questions. To do well, participate in class and ask questions. Exams are tough, but he made the information very interesting.
He likes to talk a lot and use his hands to express everything. He doesn't explain everything so as a student could understand. That's why SI sessions are important. He's a goofy guy and respected.
Funny, interesting, engaging.

Very poor, only cared about his own viewpoint. Testing was baddly done and had only a little to do with the course. I took it with a different teacher and had a much better time, beacuse we truly covered the subject not just the teacher rants

This class wasn't hard. Dan got super into his lectures making it easier to listen. The class itself wasn't hard. All of his test questions came right out of his power points and he recorded and posted all the lectures online so it was easy to study for tests.

Waste of time. The man uses the class room as his own personal soap box. The class itself had little or nothing to do with the subject and the testing was over his point of view and the view point of the field. I will never take a class by this man again and would tell anyone considering to do so, to forget about it.

Great teacher! He's very enthusiastic about this class which makes it easy to listen and learn from. He uses relatable examples. Important to go to class on time and stay the whole time because of clicker quizzes. If you get the chance, I would deff recommend having Krier as a professor.
Awesome teacher.  Absolutely loved him.  Definitely take his class.  As long as you pay attention, you'll do great!

I loved this class and him. I had little interest in sociology before this class. I would take every class he offers and I'm not even a sociology major. Read the book and take notes during lecture and you will do fine on the tests.

Go to class every day. The exams are all lecture based and the way a lot of the questions are worded makes it hard to understand what he is asking. He is very enthusiastic when he is lecturing tho and does make the corse interesting.

Krier has a very charismatic and enthusiastic view on education. You really have to open yourself up, or you're going to end up angry and in denial of many things.  It's pretty important to note that while he leans left strongly, he advocates a government where the welfare is a priority... not the authoritarian socialism everyone seems believe.

Enjoyed his class. He gives a disclaimer at the beginning of the semester that you may not like what you hear. I feel his class is very engaging and thought provocative. His class helps shows why the world is as it is. If you can open your mind, this class will help you see differently.
The class is very pro-socialism and very anti-capitalism.  Dr. Krier is a good teacher, and very passionate, but many things like religious beliefs are dismissed as ridiculous.

he's a very very passionate teacher and it seems like he enjoys teaching sociology a lot! he's very funny and interesting....as long as you pay attention in class, take notes and attend SI. you'll do well in class=)

Prof Krier is very passionate about this class and does a good job conveying the message he wants to send. The problem is that the message he sends is a very biased one. He is obviously not a fan of conservatives, people who are religious, or those in the military.

Attendance is mandatory. Tests are almost completely from his lectures. He says if you understand the picture he has in his head, you'll do ok (his tests are completely opinion based, impossible to study.) His slides and lectures are very unorganized. His grading scale is confusing and he didn't help me figure out my grade. Very disappointed.

This professor is responsible for ruining my education.  He set the bar so high for all the other professors that no others have even come close.  I learned SO much in this class and it was nearly effortless.  This was one of my first classes and I was so excited for the rest of college but have found that he is a one of a kind teacher. :(

I know many students hated this class.  He doesn't cater to the conservative / religious minded and makes that pretty apparent early on.  I absolutely loved this class however.  He taught with such amazing enthusiasm that I had absolutely no problem acing his tests because I soaked up every word he said.  I never once studied.  GREAT PROFESSOR!

Terrible teacher, you are tested simply on his opinions. I had a great grade in the class, until the last test. Be aware it is the most opinionated thing you will see all semester and it will end up being 1/4 of your grade. This class is worthless unless you like socialist crap.

I really enjoyed this class. Prof. Krier has a very different teaching style so you have to be willing to break away from the norm for a while. If you pay attention in lecture or go to SI you will do fine in the course.

Very interesting class.  Definitely not a 100 level class.  If you don't pay attenstion in class you will not do great in the tests (based 90% on lecture).  Dr. Krier teaches very differently, his lectures seem more like a seminar than a lecture with bullet points and so on (again, pay attention in lecture).  He records his lectures and SI is good
I enjoyed this class and thought this professor was interesting to listen to and you can tell he really is passionate about Sociology

Wonderful Professor! Originally read reviews about him in August and was slightly afraid, but so long as you try to understand what he says and ask him questions, you'll be fine. One of my best professors this Fall!

Prof Krier is very passionate about Sociology! He can be very entertaining, making the class fun to come to. Concentration and attendance in this class is important (especially for clicker points), though lecture recordings are posted online if you didn't catch something that he said. If you want to like this class, you definitely will!

I really enjoyed this class. I went into it scared after reading these reviews but I have no idea what these people are talking about. Professor Krier would go out of his way to help anybody and if you go to the si sessions you have a pretty much guaranteed A.

I love this class! The tests are difficult but not impossible if you study. It's a super relaxed atmosphere and you can tell Dr. Krier really cares about his work. Don't be afraid to confront him personally to talk about your grade or anything. He's leniant about test dates and reading quizzes often get pushed back. Stick with the material!

If you are not interested in Sociology, you will probably not like taking it from him. He's very passionate but I had an extremely hard time understanding his lectures. His tests are also very difficult. I became uninterested quickly and lost interest which made my grade suffer.

A lot of people find Dr. Krier to be too opinionated and too hard. Yes, his tests are difficult, but if you come into this class with an open head and attend class and listen to what he says, then it isn't difficult to grasp the material. Go for it!

person below is so mean! dont listen to him or her! the tests were hard for me but i learned a lot in that class and like the professor said before this class makes me  about some issues. you will learn alot and u will see importance of studying socio. i am even planning to minor in that field.
Dude... DROP THIS CLASS AS SOON AS POSSIBLE FOR YOUR LIFE. One of most horrible class I ever been in my life.
Socialist, Rude, arrogant, sometimes brilliant but mostly silly. I was annoyed by his lecture rather than finding something helpful. Tests are hard.
he is very in love with his job but he is not good at lecturing and his tests do not resemble the lecture
Prof Krier is very passionate about his work. His lectures are somewhat disorganized but are interesting. I love the subject and think that I will benefit from the class this semester.
Rude prof., strange and disorganized lectures. The tests tend to not represent class material- so you may suffer score wise. Take this class from someone else of possible.

Dull. Arrogant. Rude. Strange and useless lectures. You have to learn the class material on your own time to do well in this class.Beware of being singled out in class, esp. if you are catholic or conservative. Oh- and how did this guy get tenured? Big mistake!
One of the most hostile class environments I've ever been.

Unless you are a left-winger or a socialist, do not take this class. He will berate your beliefs. He will also try to isolate people by asking them their religion or political opinion. He's doing this so that he has someone to mock for the entire class. Also, never ever offer your opinion in class. He will shut you down. Complete jerk.

I've had this Prof twice and for a reason! His mind works differently than most that I have encountered and in a good way. Sometimes there were things I didn't want to hear but that's the whole point that he's trying to get across with his students. Extremely helpful after class and will work with you if you need help. All in all - he kicks ass!

It SUCKS!!!With full of reading, i begin to hate English letters. The lecture is not helpful, the quiz require a lot in textbook which you have to read AFTER class, what he taught is nothing to do with the exam, i HATE him, it's not like a 100+ subject.I spend all day reading textbooks and slides.It makes no sense. Never,Ever choose it !!
You'll be hearing alot of the word ModerNITYYYYYYYYYYYY!!! LOL :-)

This was one of the most thought invoking classes I've had at ISU. He has a different world view than most at ISU. The bozos rating this prof badly simply can't deal with ideas that are contrary to what they want to hear. That said, this class is not taught like a 100 level course. You MUST go to lecture and listen. TAs are unapproachable facists.

Over all this man is very fragmented and makes class just terrible. Has no respect for others opinions or students. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM. The TA's grade as if this is a 400 level class. Just a terrible experience.

One of the most arrogant, biased and selfish people I have ever met/encountered. He doesn't give any of his students respect so don't bother giving your opinion, he'll throw it back in your face. Tests are impossible and his TA's are clueless. Worst class I've ever taken/worst teacher I've ever had. Don't take this class with him as your professor.

Class time used to push his Marxist agenda/to belittle, bully and humiliate his students, whether their opinions agree with his or not. Constantly says things that are contradictory, rapidly shuffles though disorganized powerpoints, and places emphasis on words senselessly (mo-der-ni-tyyyyy). Registered for this class? Get out!

This professor is rude. At the beginning of the class he says he wants to make you angry. And he does. In each and every class you feel depressed and frustrated to the point where you want to walk up the steps and out the door. Oh, and he hates "glowing screens" (cells, laptops, etc.) For the sake of your sanity don't take this class. Beware of TAs
Just read all the rest of the comments you get the idea. UGHHHH
Very unorganized which makes every day in his class incredibly frustrating.

Very disorganized, socialist, confusing. Narcissistic. Rude and disrespectful to other's opinions. Rambles in lectures. Tests are very difficult, and often have little to do with what he's spoken about. Hates capitalism and America for it. TA's are clueless. Don't get test  grades back for 2-3 weeks, essays are worse. This class is just annoying.
This guy is nuts, hard to understand sometimes, but when you do he's absolutely brilliant. He seems to have really conceited TAs though, which know absolutely nothing but think they do.
Bad! Really bad!! It is just 100s class not 400s!!
JUST AWFUL

I've had this prof before in Soc 235 and I still enjoy having him as my professor! He does tend to rush through slides but he makes sure to go into detail about what he's lecturing. I don't see how people have issues with this guy - he's frickin AWESOME! Like he said, if he doesn't make you angry, he's not doing his job. All in all, this guy ROCKS!

He is very enthusiastic. I enjoy going to lecture just because he gets so excited. However, he seems to be pretty rude to differing viewpoints (although I agree with almost all of his viewpoints). DO NOT text message in his class or he will freak out. He is pretty good about getting across the main points and I'm glad I had him as a professor.

I think he is a wonderful teacher. I love how makes his students challenge their view points. He is very passionate about what he is teaching so I never find lecture to be boring. This class isn't too difficult if you make sure to attend lecture since most of the exam material is from this.

Whether you agree or disagree with his political viewpoints (ironically, i actually agree with most of them), any intelligent person will notice his blatant disrespect towards anyone with a different opinion-interrupting, belittling comments, the whole nine yards. It's disgusting. If you get him for sociology SWITCH professors, immediately.

Looking for an easy GenEd? Stop. This is not the class for you. The instructor is fascinating, but has little organizational skill. Rushes to fit in info for tests which cover lecture, long slide series and picky book info not covered in lecture. Essays assigned often, graded difficultly. TAs seem to think of themselves as classroom stormtroopers.

hes passionate but he he speeds through slides so fast you cant understand anything and then rambles...contradicts himself so much its mind boggling...he used to be an accountant and it obvious hes very bitter towards a lot of people from that. class is somewhat fun due to its utter absurdenss but wouldn't call it "learning"

The teacher itself wasn't too bad, it was his way of assigning things which was.  He would mention things and then go off on a tangent, and you wouldn't know what to do.  Most discussed material was on the test, though you did have to read the book to get everything.  If it were test only I would have done much better.
This guy is awesome.  I highly recommend taking his class. If you go to class and listen you'll get an A, it's not overly difficult.
Terrible teacher does not make any sense talks a lot and expect you to write down everything two much information to study and a lot of it probably won't even be on the test

worst teacher I have ever had. terrible, rude, crass. He was disrespectful to students and completely against any type of capitalism governement. The final was 125 questions, single space and completely impossible to understand. Content covered nothing in class.
he isn't very organized and does a lot of hand gestures that distract you

I took this class with him after taking 134 last semester. He is enthusiastic, however, he makes you buy 8 books and doesn't use them. He is socialist and shows it, and enjoys pointing out the faults in America & Capitalism. The final was completely unrepresentative of the semester. I had an extremely bad taste in my mouth after this year's class.

This professor is amazing. He's not your average professor telling you what you want to hear. He says it like he sees it and people who don't like him generally don't like being challenged or faced with another radically different opinion. This class should be required for everyone. He's the reason I changed my major!
Every american student should be required to take this class with this prof.  He is amazing.

Thinks he is god. Also has an extreme dislike to capitalism. He should teach the intro to Sociology class just like it should be, as an intro with all perspectives, not just his own that most people do not agree with.  Horrible teacher, do not take his class.
sometimes he gets wrapped up in his sociology party and goes fast, but he is SUPER interesting, wicked smart and pretty funny.  One of the best I have had at Iowa State

He is my favorite professor here at ISU! I've never had a professor who showed so much passion for his work and can throw sense of humor in class. He is very informative and will answer any questions given to him during or after class. I recommend him for anyone! He is simply amazing and I hope to have him as my professor again someday!

I think he is a great professor! I find myself listening to him during class fascinated and amused. Even though I am not even considering majoring in such a field, he really makes me interested. Though he can be hard to understand, he is very helpful to put in effort to make things clearer for you when given questions. I wish I had him more often.

He thinks he is god's gift to earth.  He has a major supererority complex which is ironic given the course.  He is arrogant and condescending.  Don't bother studying for the tests, you can't.  All he talked about was transvestic fetishism... pointless cartoons and political propaganda comprised the entire class.

Krier is a pretty good professor. it is very clear that he is super passionate about what he teaches and he really just wants to open our eyes to the way the world really is. I think he tries to make the class fair, but his TA's (well at least one) is kind of a joke. they seem to be on a power trip and are super anal about things that shouldnt matt

dr. krier is an alright teacher and guy but his TA's are idiots. they think they are god's gifts to earth and if you even go and talk to krier for 5 minutes you will find out he thinks they ae dumb and full of themselves. this class would be great were it not for these joke of a wannabe teachers assistants
pretty good, as long as you went to class or got the notes and understood it you were good
He is the best teacher that I have seen at ISU! He doesnt mind just stating the plain truth instead of just beating around the bush to be politically correct. He is awesome!

I think he missed his true calling as a minister, because every lecture is a sermon.  I didn't dislike the class, but he had a tendency to get off topic and make up facts to suit his arguments.  But, underneath all of the fluff was some decent information.

i was really excited to take this social problems class. i'm a soc major and am very interested in it. this was more of a history class than anything. he didn't teach anything relevant to the course description except for the last 2 weeks of class when we actually talked a little bit about social problems. will never take a class from him again.

This guy is so passionate about his work.  Don't take his class for granted because you can learn so much more than the straight curriculum.  He relates so well with college students that he will probably be my favorite teacher ever!
Wonderful teacher, made me very interested in Sociology.
Prof. Krier was my best teacher this semester during my first year!  He has so mush enthusiasm for the subject that it's just contagious.  He knows his stuff...and soon you will too!
He should let us use laptops

Krier is awesome! He makes class a fun thing. I'm so excited to go to his class in the morningt. The lectures are great and he can be a very funny and interesting guy. One of my favorite teachers ever.

Got in a lot of arguments with the guy. He's passionate about teaching and wants everybody to succeed. If you considering yourself moderate to conservative you WILL get frustrated. Just go to class, listen up, and do well on the tests. His class is worth taking, just take his lessons with a grain of salt.
Professor Krier is one of the best educators that i have come across!

Krier was very helpful in this class. As long as you attend class, and especially if you make an effort to introduce yourself to Krier, you will get an excellent grade. He offers easy extra credit opportunities to help your grade. Great teacher and great class!

I'm not convinced that everyone who bashes Krier's "narrow" (at face value, sure) politics understand that the discipline of sociology studies the phenomena of social reality in a way that is very much represented by his teachings.  I'm not convinced it's Krier that is their problem, but it is more likely sociology itself.  Call me crazy...

He's a pretty liberal guy who will challenge your views if you're a conservative. That being said, he's extremely helpful and is passionate about teaching. I've talked with him one on one several times and he's really gotten me interested in social problems and sociology in general. Take his 235 class, it's a blast.
Very enthusiastic teacher who made lecture exciting, learned more than I thought I would because the class was so easy
teaches based off of his own writings and slide shows and tests on them. he is very liberal and biased. his tests are extremely wordy. i did not like him, but if you are extremely liberal you may.

Very liberal, which is good and bad. You need to go to class, some test questions are based only on things he talks about in class. You can get away without reading the book. People complain about his slides, but you don't need to take notes in class - DOWNLOAD THE SLIDES OFF WEBCT - just listen to the lecture and study the slides later. Rating: B+

bias, but good. he is very interesting but tests are wordy and in his view not necessarily the text. read slides, a computer in class would help because he doesn't always stay on the slides all the time but he posts them in web ct so you can follow along. go to class, not mandatory but helpful
Class is fun to go to but you have to take notes to do well. A lot of questions on tests are his point of view, so knowing the text doesn't do much good. Tests are worded ridiculously.

He's semi-good-looking for his age.  The best was when he brought his daughter in because his babysitter was sick and she drew on the wall under the whiteboard with a dry-erase marker. He's a really good teacher too!  Enthusiactic and thought-provocking!!

He's a great teacher he is very passionate about what he teaches and makes you get excited about the class. You have to go to class because some assignments only given during class.  Some of the time he is a little unorganized and jumps around with his slides making it a little hard to keep up but overall is a really interesting and easy class.
Good Professor if you hate this guy there is something wrong with you one of the most pasionate teacher i have had in college

not sure what to think about him, very liberal bashes conservative views, grades off his own writings which is tough, sometimes doesn't think about what he's saying, kind of funny, good class but defiently not structured as a 100 level, hard if you don't go to class n take notes (which he spends about 5 seconds on each slide so write quick)
Loved him. Great teacher. Learned a lot and enjoyed class throughly.

The guy is so disorganized it drove me nuts.  He used his powerpoints from Soc 134 and spent maybe 10 seconds on each one.  I enjoyed his passion for the subject, but unfortunately it translated into confusion.  Tests are hard too.  Hes an ok prof, but  if possible I would avoid him or suck up better than I did.

Loved him.  Go to class!  Some assignments are given out only in class and his lectures cover the material you will be tested over - I didn't open my textbook once.  Lectures are pretty interesting and often amusing.
I normally hate power point in the classes but kriers is really good.  really interesting class that I would recommend to anyone  one of the best profs on campus

If you like to listen to the ramblings of a flaming liberal who only represents one side of an argument in a class that promotes looking at things from different points of view then you'll love this class! If you are religious, conservative, or a man I would suggest not taking his class!!!
One of the best profs at ISU.  His class will blow your mind and his powerpoints are hilarious.
GREAT PROFESSOR! I never thought I'd be so interested in his teachings about sociology. He knows his stuff and is really passionate about it. His enthusiasm is what makes the class fun!

I took 235. The class it self is easy but he makes it too hard then it is supose to be. I would his class to people that likes to memorize other then thinking. Bad sociologist. If you want to be the grass in the garden go for i because he doesn't let you think, he can't even find the mistakes in his books because he is stupidly passionate
Best professor at ISU!
damn good, he actually cares about what he's teaching
You have to go to class and listen to him, but he is funny.  If you hate liberals don't go, if you are liberal go it is great.

If you like single minded liberal view, then this is your professor.  If you have a mind of your own stay clear.  Energetic, but doen't like to listen to students views on a subject if it doesn't match his.  Anti-military individual that likes to blaze through ridiculous amount of slides hoping you will remember them all
If you want to go to class and hear how great liberals are and how conservatives are the scum of the earth than this professor is for you, if not don't even try.

He's very enthusiatic and if you actually talk to him he's a great guy. Unfortunately his teaching style sucks. Beware of all the TA's!!! They would rather eat glass than respond to a question with some civility!

Class is pointless.  He spends no more than 25 seconds on each slide, which is FILLED with text.  Instead class is reserved for political rants.  The only thing I've learned in this class is that if you don't know what to do in life, just be a sociologist and you can get paid to complain about stuff.
Very passoniate about the subject and relates the subject to your life.  I would reccomend the class.
MOST BAD ASS PROFESSOR OF ALL TIME!

I have never had a professor so inspired about what he is teaching.It really inspires the student to want to do better, and I didnt even agree with 90% of what he was teaching. He is very liberal, but knows his stuff. Even us good christian republicans can learn something from this guy.
he is an amzing professor. he is energetic, unordinary funny and doesn't take any crap from people. you learn so much it hurts. i absolutely loved his socail issues class! highly recommended!
very passionate about his work and the importance of educating students on it. great resource to seek out for help or ask related questions.
AWEFUL!!!  makes a 100 level course as hard as a 400.  very peppy but very lousy teaching style.  Notes long, confusing and up for aprox. 30 seconds before he takes them down.  RUN AWAY!!!
He is very peppy, he's an ok teacher.

He knows about the liberal agenda and thats about all you hear about during class.  I don't know if he actually teaches sociology.  Very energetic which makes class interesting.  Not very easy to work with.  His TA's were very sweet and made up for him being a jerk when having an issue.

I went in to see him shortly after a friend of mine was in a  really bad accident and I had gotten behind in my studies.  I was told that to screw my head back on, and that maybe I shouldnt be attending ISU.
good, but doesn't convey the material as i would have liked.  tests are very hard if you aren't completely understanding the material.  READ!
Very Passionate, very smart.  A lot of knowledge to pass down.  He definately opened my eyes.  I've been recommending him to all my friends.

One of the worst teachers i've ever had. Passionate but cannot teach it to others. Rambles on and on about the material and in the middle of lecturing loses his place because he is so wrapped up and has to start all over. Seriously, he shouldn't be teaching this class...

Dr. Krier is honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. He is very passionate about what he teaches and his lectures are amazing. Yes, his tests are very difficult, but as long as you go to lecture(he puts a lot of lecture questions on his tests) and keep up with the readings, you should do fine.

Hes passonate about his stuff, but he goes all over the place in lecture, and you dont get very far. His tests are complicated, which is weird because he talks about grades and how they are bad judges of learning. If you dont agree with his opinions hes likely to get a little mad. Loves his Soc but not an effective teacher
His test are very difficult.
hes the man just because hes soo cool in class
No Comments
I think this guy is a great teacher. He has a love for the subject and he knows what he is talking about. If you have a question, he will answer it for you. I would recommend this professor!

for what its worth I think this guy is a GREAT teacher but i dont think his skills as a teacher translate well into this class. when i went to lecture i understood everything completely but when it came exam time the questions weren't very straightforward
No Comments

He is fan-tas-tic!!! I haven't laughed that hard in any class, ever, and his approach to teaching social problems is extraordinary! he actually makes you think about stuff, and learn, too! Outstanding! So much fun!!! Not an easy class, but is worth every minute!

The class is great if you actually go to them(just because he doesn't take attendance doesn't mean you should skip), the book wasn't the best. I loved this class and now I'm going to go for a minor in Soc. Probably the best professor I've had, actually *enjoys* teaching.
he is one of the greatest professors ever.
this guy is a spaz! his tests are impossible, he forgets often that he is teaching a 100 level class

This was his first year at ISU, so give him a break.  Tests were fairly hard, but he was very willing to work with the class to make things fair-curved the tests some and the class in general.  He really wanted to know how students were understanding the material, which is hard in big lectures.
I didn't want to take Soc, but I had to fill a Behaviorial science requirement. He isn't that bad as long as you goto all the classes.
i was excited about the course, but after this one, I don't think I will take any class in soc. He can't explain his things well enough, and the text is not very helpful at all.
I was very interested in taking this soc class, but afterwards i'm not sure if i even want to take one even again!
This guy is pathetic!!! Never ever take a class with him.  He is by far the worst teacher that I have ever had.  Avoid his class at all costs!!!!!
Very Bad.  If you expect help or are interested in this class take another one.  Even the TA's said that he was the worst.
A little shaky at first but he is pretty interesting and helpful.

I don't know why these frowning faces are here. Krier was great! He was enthusiastic about what he was teaching and he taught it in an entertaining way. As long as you go to class, you should get an A.

Most of the time I had no idea what he was talking about in class, (modernity, what???) but he was very enthused so at least he was interesting to watch and listen to. The readings were useless and there were tons of notes to be taken.

i had krier before he went to iowa state (at william and mary), and he was unbelievable.  he goes on tangents often but they are interesting and reflect his passion for teaching.  make an effort to get to know him outside of class and he will be extremely helpful and geniunely interested in you.

Ok I thought Dr. krier was horrible, the book was useless and his notes never matche up to the book. He thinks he is teaching a level 400 class when it is an introduction.  I would never recommend him-switch if you have him!!!
VERY enthused about the subject, very entertaining.  The tests are tough and the reading assignments are just about useless, but the lectures are interesting and there is a lot to learn from them.

Does a good job in the lectures, farily interesting and very motivated about the subject. His first test was difficult, but his second was not. I think he just needed to adjust his testing style because i had him his first semester at ISU from a small private east coast college.
No Comments

He is very excited about what he is teaching, thus making the class much more interesting than the average. He also tries to present things in an applicable manner, and will try to help every student pass if he can.
What in the world is this guy talking about?  How many times will he say modernity in one lecture?  Get ready to be confused by his tangents and crazy long notes you take.

Best professor I've had at Iowa State. Sad to hear he's retiring from the university because I'd recommend taking his classes to anyone. He cares a lot about the success of his students and is always there to help when needed.

Awesome guy who really cares about students as individuals. Sorry to hear he's retiring from ISU, but we all know he'll do amazing things. He is how all teachers should strive to act and teach. Jim for President!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Kurtenbach was one of my favorites! He truly cares about his students' success in & outside of the classroom. Some of the material was hard to understand, but the exams ended up being easier than I thought and he's always willing to help with projects & homework.

At first, this course and professor seemed difficult, but Kurtenbach is actually a really good professor! ACCT 384 is a tough course, but Kurtenbach tries to simplify things and keep his teaching applicable to real life. He was often available outside of class and was very willing to help if asked. He values participation and encourages questions.

Jim is the best professor I have ever had. The class itself was a little difficult, but he made it so easy to understand and often gave time to work on team assignments and ask him questions during class. He tried very hard to make sure everyone did well in the class with generous grading. He also responded to emails quickly.

The concepts for 384 are really hard and the projects/assignments are difficult. However, Kurtenbach always made time for me to come in for office hours and always responded to emails in a timely manner. He did everything he could to make the class easier for everyone. His lectures were usually engaging.

Best teacher I've ever had. The class itself was really hard at first because using the software is a bit challenging. But going to his office hours weekly really helped. He was so accommodating and genuinely cared about us. I would love to take another course of his just to be in his presence. He's also the smartest man I've ever met.

Utilize office hours if you need help. Half group and half individual projects so try to stay on top of those and not do them last minute. The lectures just go over stuff in the book so you don't HAVE to go, but he does give help on the projects assigned in class too, so I'd recommend you go to them. Overall great professor and very down to earth.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at ISU. There's a lot of assignments, but if you talk with him, it's very doable. He is always willing to help & will extend deadlines. Also very clear what is on exams & what's expected of you. Definitely take this class with Jim! He also brought our class donuts. He makes class fun & genuinely prepares you for your future.

Great Professor. All 384 classes are the same no matter the professor, so take it with Kurtenbach. He makes lectures interesting and grades easily, but makes sure you understand what is needed for exams and projects. Lots of projects, both individual and team but very duable. Recommend taking this class with him. You will not regret it.
Jim  is a knowledgable professor. He is approachable and respectful for the students.

Kurtenbach was awesome, he was very informal and preferred to be called jim or kurtenbach instead of doctor kurtenbach. He was kind of scatterbrained at times but he was EXTREMELY approachable and very helpful. I highly recommend taking him if you can

Professor Kurtenbach is a great teacher.  Knows the subject matter very well.  Challenges students to do their best.  I might not get a great grade in the class, but I learned much more than I would have from an average difficulty teacher.
the material covered is not difficult. there is just a lot of stuff you need to know. Great prof. More then willing to meet you to go over things. Best accounting prof thus far!!!
Just didn't do it for me.

Hands down the best accounting professor. 386 presents is a class but professor is very help in and out of class. Makes sure that students understand the material before he moves on. Though he is unorganized he gets the most difficult material covered thoroughly.
No Comments

Dr. Kurtenbach is a nice guy with a lot of interesting stories who cares about his students. He is very disorganized, though, and should spend more time preparing for class, maybe even make up more lecture notes beforehand. He has trouble sticking to an agenda, when questioned goes on tangents or too deeply into stuff covered later in the course.

He is a great professor who is wonderful to talk to in and out of class. He is extremely understanding of everyone and always willing to listen to feedback. Have a problem with him? Just talk to him! The video lectures honestly were not that necessary, you can just skim the powerpoints and be ready for the exam.

Kindest soul, is super understanding and fun. His TA was grading hard for things that weren't clarified by him and so I emailed him to asked for an opportunity to resubmit with changes and he just went in and graded it differently. All he cares about is his students learning. It is clear he loves us all.

He is not the worst professor of this class, but his lectures are also online and they are LONG (and pointless). The class time is spent discussing the lectures vaguely and you will talk about the SAME THING for a month with him. Probably the least interesting part of this class is at the beginning and end (both of which he is responsible for).

The only complaint would be the way he calls out people who are late to his 8 am's, and sometimes the weekly workload was a bit heavy. Super fair grader, interesting lectures, very passionate about teaching. A lot of homework, it's graded fairly though. He said there would be two exams a semester but I took two classes with him and never had one.

Honestly one of the best professors in the ABE department. If you make an honest attempt to do the work (it's not hard, just a lot that can be easily found in the resources he provides), you will do great. His lectures resemble TED Talks, which I personally enjoy; very informative and he makes each topic as interesting as possible.

Dr. Rosentrater genuinely cares about his students. Lot's of homework, although most of is straight forward, if you attend lectures. Very understanding when it comes to work load and Hw deadlines. By far one of the best professors at ISU.

He is my study abroad professor and is honestly one of the most humble guys I have ever met. Hes respectful and always telling jokes and just makes learning fun. He loves France and will most likely miss a lecture or two (yay no class!). Hes really chill, if you have him for ABE your lucky because hes really cool.

A really caring professor. He is passionate about his work too. He will forget about tests if he isn't reminded and will just assign a small project instead. The homework can be challenging, but he is almost always available for help in his office or via email.
Good guy!

Excellent professor in the ABE department. Very honest and caring. Loves to give extremely time consuming assignments, not necessarily difficult. Will make an effort to learn your name, and know when you're slacking or relying on others in the class. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Always willing to help when he's available and in the country
Too much homework and projects! No exam.

Dr. R is amazing, this class is a 400-level one (taken by many Grad students) this being said it's not an easy class. But it's mainly projects and huge assignments, invest time and effort and you'll end up with a good grade
Very supportive professor. Best teacher in department. Always willing to help. Great guy!
No tests. Only projects. Put in the effort you get a good grade. At times a lot of work.

Professor Kumar is a great lecturer. She uses her previous role at Google to provide case studies and examples of how the lecture materials could be used in industry. You will complete a semester long project that could be used as a portfolio piece, and she is a great help if you ask her questions/participate her office hours.

Professor Kumar was great for a different class, but not for this qualitative research class. Not sure if it's because this is what she did for work but she is more opinionated and grades harder in this class. Just wish she was consistent. She gives you the option to work on a project solo... and then pairs you up anyway for lecture activities.

This is for the experimental Qualitative Research course. Very cool learning from an ex-Google Researcher and learning about the field from someone who has actually done it. This course is graded a little more strictly than her other ones. Her TA is not as tactful at giving feedback and inserts a lot of their own opinions when grading.

This was for the Emerging Topics in HCI: Responsible Tech class in Fall 2022. Professor Kumar is an ex-Google UX Researcher and is very knowledgeable about the field. She shares her own real-world experience as she teaches different topics about how to approach the creation of new technologies responsibly. Very heavy on readings and discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Course material was very dull and Kumar did not make it more interesting. Dr. Kumar knows the material well but is not good at teaching. Average course grades are terrible but he puts a huge curve on the class. Labs are useless and contribute nothing to the course. Quizzes are very easy, exams and homework are awful and graded very harshly

If you want to learn anything or get an A forget about it. Everyone will fail everything so he will just curve the class so everyone gets a B and he doesn't look as bad. If you're ok with an easy B then take it because he can't afford to give lower grades.
By far and away the most boring man I've ever attempted to listen to. He would go a few minutes long every class so I had to start leaving while he was talking to make my bus. Worst professor ever

Ok slides but when he lectures he just talks and talks. Very difficult to follow/process derivations on the screen. If you are extremely dedicated to reading the book you will be in mediocre shape. Still, the final was incredibly more difficult than midterms, long, and worth an unfair 30% of the final grade. Everyone cheats so grades are inflated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Speaks in a monotone which makes it extremely difficult to follow him, and he is never accessible outside class. He gives pop quizzes and makes them worth a gruesome 15% of the final grade to force people to attend. First two exams were easy. The final exam screwed everyone over and the average was around 50%, but he curves the class eventually.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Kumar isn't a very exciting instructor, but his course policies are very clear and quite lenient. He shoots down questions on occasion, but he usually works to foster a good learning environment for the class and posts lots of materials online. If it weren't for the pop quizzes, there was little reason to ever go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His 324 class is an easy A if you do the homework and pay attention in lecture. The exams are graded fairly and based on the homework. Always willing to answers any questions and is very polite.
I started off not liking Kumar however he grew on me as the semester when on.  In the end I think he has become my favorite  ISU teacher.  Fair exams (excluding the final but it was graded fair).
Exams are based from homework like problems from the book. Additional problems help for exams. He is always willing to answer questions.

Didn't like him at first, but grew on me by the end of the semester.  If you show that you care about understanding the material throughout the semester he will like you.  I went to his office hours several times, and he will explain the problems until you understand them.
Not great but not awful.

Terrible professor: posts lecture notes written in felt tip pen, extremely hard to read, spends half the class trying to figure out his own example problems.  You're going to have to teach yourself out of the book.

Worst teacher at ISU.  He might know everything there is to know, but the way he explains it is horrible.  I hate EE stuff, but in 442 I had a good teacher who was good at working out examples, not just putting up the same notes he has had for 5 years.  By far my least favorite class ever.
Boring, notes are illegible, test material is more difficult than practice problems, does a bad job working practice problems, good luck!

Easily worst teacher I've ever had. Shows no interest in students, tests unfairly difficult. Very intelligent, yet can't convey even simple ideas. Class made easier because answer key to homework widely available and used as learning aid. Inflated grades. If his 442 class severely maimed my interest in EE, 448 finished it off. Unequivocally  awful.

Boring, no enthusiasm, would have been harder if the whole class didn't have solutions to the homework.  One page of notes for like 3 weeks of class and they look like they're written in pastels.  Have fun with this guy.

Incredibly confusing. Can't answer q's. Didn't teach anything, put me to sleep, I left class every day in a state of depression. Labs pointless. Tests unfairly difficult given his horrific inability to teach. Kumar made appointments, broke them, then blamed student for not trying to get help. Did well despite Kumar, grades significantly inflated.

Not the best teacher, although I thought the class material was very easy.  If you're taking the course, look at the old posts for homework and exam solutions, and remove the extra 'xxx' from the 'whatever.com/hw1.htmlxxx' on the address.
Easy A. Just do as he asks, do the homework, and bring your calculator.
Kumar's was probably the easiest part, although his material was probably the toughest, because it just seemed like he didn't care.  He gave almost everyone I know a 100% on their test too.
Class if very informative but doesnt seem to be helpful with ANY of the homework... good luck!

I think that Dr. Kumar may have changed his ways.  I took EE 324 with him spring 05 and he was very good.  If you did the homeworks, you would go good on tests.  Still took the tests out of 20 points though, which is tough.  A 20 point exam worth 20% of your grade, every point off on a test is 1% off of your overall.
Very Unhelpful.  Very Poor at following through problems in a decent manner during class discussion.  Gives very difficult tests with poor emphasis on course material
This class seriously sucked. Did not follow a plan whatsoever. He put me to sleep in every class. In summary, he is the most unprofessional professor the ECPE department has ever got.
He is the worst professor I have ever had.  His exams is out of 20 points and no partial credit
I dont even know where to start with this guy. Blocked me from coming into his office DURING office hours. Lectures will put you to sleep. Tests are a nightmare. Final even worse. Just glad its over.
Not as bad as everyone says, the class sucks but he doesn't, average is B-, don't have to do that good to get a decent grade in the class
No Comments
Terrible professor, uses a terrible book, and hard to find the application for the items learned in class.  All math, no theory.
worst case ever ... a nighmare class
Very difficult to understand, and impossible to read his notes on the overhead, which gets students lost very quickly.  Exams are unfairly difficult and graded with no partial credit.
Terrible teaching style.  Comes to class with pre-prepared overheads.  You spend the whole hour trying to stay awake, and fighting to understand what he's doing, because he skips so many steps.
Square watermelons are my favorite.
If you want to learn about bullet trains and random Chinese social values for no reason, take this guy. His lectures and TA's are incomprehensible and I learned absolutely nothing.

Don't ever take him, please save yourself. He's horrible, and you won't understand anything he says because of his accent. He's bad at teaching because half the time he doesn't even talk about the course it's about something random. If you have him, switch immediately.

doesn't lecture about anything on the quizzes or exams. just read the textbook and slides. idk why I have to take this class. the ta's are unintelligible. if you have to take econ101, DO NOT take it with choi.
Choi is an awful professor he just rambles and shares his irrelevant stories that have no connection to his presented lecture notes. If choose any other Econ 1010 professor besides Choi Kwan!!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor gives us two quizzes a week and the average grade for quizzes in my class is around 5-6/10. Get ready to learn it all on your own.

Also, make sure you do really well on the group project. As long as you get the average on the exams and get an A in the group project, you should do pretty well in the class.

She cares about your education&every decision she makes is to help you learn the material, not necessarily to help you get a good grade. Study her CanYou ?s on lecture slides to do well on tests! Class is setup to encourage attendance, independent&group learning, & critical thinking. I will frequently refer back to what I learned in Bio212.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Kukday is a hard professor. Her exams very challenging and often very wordy. We did a group project which was informative but didn't seem to make sense with the rest of the class. Lot of team based learning so you will literally fail if you don't go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly just a ridiculous way of grading. I have had difficult classes before, and never have I felt this baffled at how unfair and crazy hard the tests are. If you get this class, good luck!

She's not the best. We have to do a group project, which seems really out of place in a lecture.
