We do enough group activities in the supplemental lab, so I don't understand why we need to do another one for the lecture. She doesn't give feedback at all for the assignments. The content is very boring and dry.

This was by far the most frustrating and difficult class I have taken. I knew Bio 212 would be hard but Professor Kukday exceeded my expectations. She doesn't make study guides for any of her tests. This leaves you with hundreds of lecture notes and txtbook pages to look over. Her tests are impossible and you leave lecture more confused than before
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you are not planning on showing up to lecture, take this class with a different professor. We were assigned seating with a group for a semester long project at the beginning and it was nice to be able to sit with familiar faces every class. If you do your best this class really shouldn't be a problem.

Kukday rocks don't let anyone tell you any different. She literally gives you every single tool you need to get an A in the class. All of her exams are based off of her powerpoints, she has a cap on Top Hat and activity points, and she is very willing to help. Very doable class.

I had heard terrible things about Kukday. There's no doubt that this class can be difficult, but I actually really like her. If you just pay attention in class and then go to her with specific questions you have she is more than happy to help. Also study by answering the "can you" questions she provides and you'll get an A.

She's a pretty good professor, however she is very tough. None of the practice problems/ practice test actually helped with the exam. To be honest, only 4 questions were similar. Also don't expect a "curve", because almost everyone that took it during fall 2016, didn't receive a curved grade.

Dr. Kukday is really good at what she does. People are usually frustrated with her because of her difficult tests, but her tests only make up 40% of the final grade. Another 40% comes from participation class, which you'll get 100% on if you go to class and pay attention. The rest comes from a project that is graded by clear criteria.

Took this class online and liked the pace of it, you were able to space homework and exams out well. Her online lectures and nice and short and succinct, but very very dry, dull, and uninteresting. Most of the MasteringBiology as well as her exams can be found online, so if you really don't care you can use that. Her other assignments are busy work
Go to class because there is a lot of in-class points. Do all the homework and extra credit. If you get all those points and have a B average on the tests you should get an A in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She gives so many in-class opportunities to earn points that it's extremely silly to skip class. Her exam questions make you think but they're not impossible. Overall, she's very helpful and open to discussion/questions.

Dr. Kukday was one of my favorite professors last semester! When material was challenging, I felt like I could go talk to her and ask her questions - she's so nice and she cares about student learning! The group project wasn't my favorite, but I did enjoy the chance to think out loud with my team. I studied best by answering her 'can you' questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's awful. Nothing in the lectures is covered in the tests, nor anything in the homework. Her study guides never cover anything in the test either, it's like you're expected to know it before you take the class. You try to talk to her and she puts you down. In a bad group for the group project worth most of the grade? Out of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Most of the students taking 212 are freshmen & have yet to learn that most biology classes are difficult. While I hate working in groups the atmosphere she tries to create in her classes is very useful in the future. Her main project is similar to one in Biol 313 & you have to develop real study habits to do well. She makes you work for your grade.

Dr Kukday is an very nice person & a great professor. She wants her students to succeed so if you take initiative, go to her with questions, & use the resources she provides, you will do well. Biol 212 is a difficult course but she provides students many opportunities to learn the material with activities & earn tons of points through participation
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Everyone complains about Kukday, but she really does give you all the tools you need to succeed. She includes questions at the end of every powerpoint (all slides posted online) that are pretty similar to the test. However, she is quite rude whenever I have approached her after lecture with questions. Overall, a very doable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are almost impossible to follow and she purposely writes the tests to confuse you, so you don't really learn, you just end up memorizing some of the random facts she says in lecture. She means well, but is not effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is hard. You have to dedicate a lot of time preparing for the exams if you want to do well. TopHat questions saved my grade. The group project is easy, but you have to put in effort. Go to class because she does like to do a lot of random worksheets that can range from 5-20 points.

Dr. Kukday is a tough professor when it comes to tests. The averages were very low, but she used that to curve the class by a lot at the end. You have probably heard horrible things about her, but she turned out to be ok. Just go to each class and pay attention, because there are a lot of easy in-class points that helped balance my bad exam scores.

Class is structured oddly, the groups you are assigned you have to sit with. As long as you go to lecture and get the participation points it should go okay. Make sure you do the Can You.. at the end of each power point since that is what you are tested on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: It is the class itself that I think is poorly designed. Dr. Kukday is very nice and has a great personality, but the class is terrible. She tries to help as much as she can though. The class is graded majorly off of a group project, you also have assigned seats in a huge lecture. Also, in class activities are done often and are a large percentage.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Huge group project worth almost 40% of entire grade. Attendance is mandatory (clicker questions). Homework at least once a week, but only for participation and easy to pass. Her lectures are boring, I could never understand what she was saying, tests have NOTHING to do with material. Not interesting. Only good thing was the 10-15% curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She moves through information quickly without explaining the details, but the details she doesn't cover will be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terrible professor! Should not be allowed to teach undergraduate students!! She doesn't know how to dumb things down for an introductory course and does an unnecessary huge group project that you can easily fail! DON'T take 212 with her if you can help it! I didnt learn a single thing in this class.

Her tests are very tricky and the averages for them tend to be in the C-D range. The group project can either really help or hurt your grade because it's worth so many points. But it's not that hard as long as you work with your group. The clicker points add up but they are fairly easy and the homework is also super easy.

I did not like this prof at all. Half of the questions in her exams are NOT in her powerpoint slides. It was hard to stay focus in class since most of the things she says is hard to understand as a student. I do read the textbook and look over her slides but her exams are still confusing to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Taking this class made me realize why so many people hate learning about science.  She did not make learning fun or engaging at all. She taught the class as if we were all had a PHD in biochemistry like her. She needs to learn how to actually teach students, not just read off of a slide. I learned nothing from this class. 2 thumbs down.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She makes an introductory biology class much more difficult than it needs to be. She tries to have students do group work and group projects in a 300+ lecture class, vague about expectations for projects as well. Had to ASK her to put up example projects bc everyone was receiving poor grades on theirs bc she wasn't clear about what she expected.
Waste of time.  The lectures were boring and didn't make any sense.   Everything she talked about had little to no relevance to her exams.

Her lectures are veryyyyy long. She likes to go over case studies instead of actually covering the material, which would be super cool if any of knew what she was talking about in the first place. On the group projects she wants you to read between the lines so get creative and study all the materials for the exams.

Dr. Kukday actually became one of my favorite teachers over the semester. At first, I didnt like that the lectures were long and often kind of boring, and she does have a slight accent that takes a little getting used to, but she is genuinely passionate about what she knows and will always take time to explain something if needed.
Kukday Tries to be nice and helpful but the way she teaches makes it nearly impossible to get better than a C on the tests. The only good thing is that she curves that class by more than 10%

Honestly she gives hard tests and the class is a lot of work but there was about a 15% curve in my class so it wasn't so bad in the end. Also just showing up to class and doing the in class group assignments is a big grade booster. There was generally 2 homework assignments a week but it was pretty easy to get 100% on those as well.
Clicker questions everyday, long lectures, semester long project!!! Not always clear and  she gives hard tests!

Dr. Kukday has good intentions and WANTS to be a good teacher, but does a poor job of it. You are assigned groups for the semester to work with in and outside of class. Our group once asked her a question in class and she looked at us as if we were dumb and walked away. Avoid taking this class.

The class was online.  All of the tests were open book/ note.  The tests are tough!  Beware of the projects.  The really brought my grade down! She doesn't give any feedback.  We had mastering biology homework all the time! The answers are online though! :)

Kukday likes to speed through the powerpoints as fast as she can speak, which is fairly fast. It was really hard for me to get a whole slide written into my notes so I asked her to slow down, explaining it would help. She not only refused to slow down, but also told me I was wrong and that it would not help me. Felt somewhat offended.

Dr. Kukday gets a pretty bad reputation. It's hard to teach a big lecture class like 212. I got a midterm grade for this class, the way to get it up is to talk to her and ask for help, study hard for the exams (look at the take away questions at the end of her powerpoints!), and do what you can to ace your group project.

Don't be scared away from other reviews on Dr. Kukday. She tries to make Biol 212 as interesting as possible, which is tough, it is a pretty boring class. However, if you do not like group projects I would switch to another professor. The group project is semester long and you are given assigned seats with your group. Overall, it was not hard pass.

This is the hardest class I took my first year at Iowa State. I was failed the first 3 exams and was failing the class. After failing the first 3 I started going in and talking to Dr. Kukday about the class material. If you take the time to talk to her, and show that you are trying, this class won't be as hard as everyone says it is.

This class is definitely tough, but if you read the book and actually put in some time studying you can do well. Most of the people who complain about this class don't read the book and still expect to do well. Her tests are hard, but this is a tough class no matter who the professor is (and she curves it at the end). Overall, not a bad professor.

At the start of the semester I was very excited for this class as I was a biology major. Now that the semester is over I have lost my drive for this subject I once cared for so much. She was by far the worst professor I've had at Iowa State. Also HATED the group assigned seats and projects. Don't take her class if you have a choice.

There's a lot of group work involved, but easy points. The tests are pretty hard and cover barely anything from lecture. Half of the time there is clicker issues and she blames it on the students when it is clearly her. I feel like I have learned nothing all semester. No one ever pays attention because her lectures are very long and boring.

Don't let the other reviews scare you away. No matter what professor you have, this class won't be an easy A. Go to class & get the easy points, do the pre-lecture assignments (they're participation), & use her 'can you' questions at the end of slides to study for the tests. She isn't an unfair teacher &  she genuinely wants to help you. Just ask!

Dr. Kukday has a unique style of teaching and while I applaud her effort and enthusiam, it does make a fairly introductory biology class a little harder than it should be. The emphasis on participation points is little excessive in my opinion. Im sure she will eventually iron out the kinks in her approach. Even professors have a learning curve.

I took BIOL 212 with her and couldn't understand her most of the time. Her tests are way too hard. The average grade was always around 50%. There were assignments due before every lecture that took quite a bit of time. she did curve the class at the end, but I feel like I didn't learn anything to help me in future courses. Avoid taking her.

I was afraid to take this class because everyone said Dr. Kukday is an awful teacher.  In all honesty she really isn't that bad.  I enjoyed having her as a teacher.  Biology 212 is a tough course anyway therefore you can't expect it to be easy.  If you go to class, study the lecture notes, and put real effort into this course you can get an A.

She is horrible. She gives assigned seats in a 300+ lecture. She doesn't explain anything. The tests are horrible and there is no good way to study, she is also no help in pointing you in the correct direction.  She blames the students for poor grades even though everyone is getting them. She is rude and unhelpful. She is a horrible lecturer.

She spends all of lecture talking about hardly related case studies and group work, neither of which prepare you for the ridiculously specific test questions. Be prepared to do group work in a 300 person lecture and thoroughly read the book outside of class to pass the exams. Avoid her if you can.

Though she was not great, she was not as bad as some people make her out to be.  Read the book and go to class! Pay careful attention to her case studies in class and read the book for the rest. She provides past exam ?s before tests. Do these! If you take the time to do all of this you can get an A on a curve. There are worse professors out there.

She is very poor with communication outside of class. I had a terrible time with my proctor receiving the passwords for tests. The testing center recommended I discuss it with her. She made it seem like my fault even though I had confirmation emails to prove I registered my proctor. I received a 0 on the first test due to this problem.

Worst professor I have ever had. Extremely boring  to listen to. All of her notes are over case studies. 90% of her tests are over material not cover in class. A T.A. taught the class for a couple classes and he was 10 times better at teaching than she was. Does not know how to relate to students. I would rather die a virgin than retake her class.

The class is extremely difficult to follow along in. We were given assigned seats and Kukday will not work with you if you can't see very well but are put in the back of the room. Often gives incorrect information, and tests on answers from worksheets you never got feedback for. The only time I learned anything in this class was when a TA taught.

SHE IS AWFUL! Test averages are abysmal: studying or not for them never made a difference on the grade received (I believe I failed 3 of 5 tests and got D's on the other 2). I learned almost nothing, and what I did learn was from my tutor. On the bright side, she such an atrocious teacher that the class was curved to the point I ended with an A.

Worst professor I have ever had.  If you enjoy class averages around 50% she is the professor for you.  Spends a lot of lecture time on case studies that she doesn't explain and treats the class like a high school class with her name tags.  I would recommend looking for other professors as Kukday is horrible.

Worst teacher I've ever had. Tries to do group work in a class of 300+ and makes everyone bring a name tag. Her notes have no words on them, just pictures that she explains in class (little help later). Test scores average 50's, and she blames her students' learning styles. No control over class, everyone is always talking. I hate her.

As another user put, she is very distracting, both with "kay's" and barely relevant case studies. The first exam averaged 57.5/100. A quote after said exam results: "I encourage you to reflect on the exam and think of ways to adapt your learning strategies to fit the context of this class. Memorization will only be of limited help on future exams."

she does everything in groups and uses way too many case studies. every couple words out of her mouth is "kay?" and can be extremely distracting. you do quizzes online for every chapter. can be rude toward students when participation does not occur. rethink taking this class with her unless this is the only time you can take it.

This professor does not follow the material covered in other sections. She does a lot of case studies but doesn't explain any of the material beforehand. She is hard to follow. My class was the first semester is has taught at ISU and we had EXTREMELY low test averages. If you have this professor I suggest you switch out of her section if possible.

He's a very tough teacher to have. As long as you keep up with his class and ask questions all will make sense. I started out disliking him but as the semester came to a close I was able to appreciate his teaching style. Yes of course there are things I would change but he's not as bad as everyone makes him out to be
You will learn nothing. If you choose to try and learn. You will always be wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Man spent an entire class arguing why he doesn't need to teach the content on his exam

Cool and funny, but he cannot teach. No online notes, if you missed a lecture for a legit reason like getting sick; good luck learning what happened that day. Better hope your friend took notes. Lectures were him writing equations on the board, nearly no examples. Do what's required and he'll lecture your class on why that will earn you a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He will definitely try to trick you. If you don't ask questions he will give you a tough quiz.

I rated him nicely on course evaluations, then saw this in my email: "Discussion grades were some hits but a lot of misses, and really poor effort by a number of people, who failed to answer the questions within the prompt at all." He then did not give any feedback, and it tanked my grade to a B. It was plenty easy until he pulled this move.

He takes a very long time to grade. You can never expect your grades back within the month. Second, the quizzes are 5 questions in 5 minutes. Third, a few of the quiz and test questions are often hard to understand. Overall, I was just very frustrated with the grading time mostly. If you are someone who likes to know your grades quick, don't take!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures and hard to grasp. And the quizzes where only timed 5 minute's which were hard to complete and answer fully. On the exam it would be very hard to chose a correct answer because all the choices were very similar making it more difficult.

If you are gonna take his course for credit. Don't do it. He gives no sense of direction for the exams and quizzes. Overall don't take this course if you just need it for credits it's not worth your time.

I go to this class every day and still have a C in it. He gave us a quiz on a lesson we did not learn yet because he was mad no one would volunteer to answer his question. Overall average on the quiz was a 3/10 and he refuses to listen to reason about removing it. Pretty much he makes all his quizzes super hard and it tanks your grade.

I took the online version. It was pretty straight forward. Only 1assignment and rest of the grade was multiple choice quiz/exams. If you read the material and listen to his lecture (which are pretty short for online class), you will do great. His textbook was a good pick - pretty interesting. I would take another class with him.

I took the online section of this course and it was fairly simple. My only complaint would be that he just seems to read out of the textbook and doesn't teach the material. Other than that even if u just watch the lectures he posts and skim the readings you will do fairly well. He gives a good amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very forgiving about make-up exams and he is very understanding.

Due dates for assignments move without notice or pop quizzes appear out of thin air. Exams count for majority of grade, but aren't really based on what is covered in lecture, reading, or writing assignments. Course material is interesting, it just needs someone else teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Burgason is a great professor. In my opinion, he connects with his students very well. There are a few pop quizzes, three reflection papers and three exams, but they are fairly straightforward (show up for exam review). He will also tell you that the easiest way to lose points is to not follow directions, so read directions carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Terrible professor who doesnt seem to grasp the material he teaches. Entire grade comes down to 3 papers and 3 tests. He just reads off his PowerPoint for every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easy A. He posts all notes online, go to class because he does give pop quizzes. One final paper which he isn't a tough grader. The class is about Capital Punishment so it's an overall interesting class. Prior to the exam, he gives everyone very SPECIFIC information on what will be on the exam basically word for word. So no surprises.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He takes forever to explain things and when he does they dont even make sense. He is strict for no reason and also has no idea what he is doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the worst teachers i've ever had. He just stands at his podium and follows his prepared lecture notes, rarely stopping for questions. My opinion of him sank lower when he showed up 50 minutes late for our final but still made us take the whole test. If you struggle at math, find a different teacher
study or get.
A great teacher.
He does his best to teach. Tests  are easy and identical to previous years tests and fair grader :))

I've never been less inspired in my life.  I really wasn't looking for inspiration in a stats class, but really this put me into a coma.  Far too many days hung up on the same lame part of a lesson like we are stupid.  Really, Kyle, we are not morons.

terrible teacher. teaches the same exact problem for at least 2 class periods. i had to teach myself almost everything from the book. however he does post old exams on the website and the new tests are almost identical to them. fairly easy but very annoying.
not very clear while teaching...showed up 45 minutes late for the final.
No Comments

Kyle is very good at explaining statistics in easy to understand ways and steps. He also is funny, talks a lot, often takes too long and rolls homework over to the next class. His tests are all written problems and require calculators.
No Comments
He's a decent teacher. I never dreaded going to class - he explained things clearly and gave cool examples and studies. We got out of class 10 min. early on most days.
good teacher can connect with the class and has uses examples to help teach the material.
Makes the boring material more tolerable. If you go to lecture and pay attention you can easily get an A.
He's ok.  Obvious it's his first time teaching.  Kind of boring, but the course material is interesting.
Uses powerpoints with his lectures
10/10 would take again! Great teacher, easy class!
Great Professor, but a lot of content in the class makes the hw and quizzes long.

Really great professor, makes econ really easy to understand regardless of whether you've had experience with the class before or not. His lectures are well-paced and include top-hat questions that can be done in or out of class, which really help cement the ideas taught while giving a good idea of what exams and quizzes are going to look like.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor and gives you the recourses to succeed like student hours and is open outside of class. Has a relaxing accent. Very passionate about economics. Overall great teacher.
Easy to understand and teaches for non-economic students

Dr. Lagoudakis is an amazing teacher, not because he knows a ton about economics (although he does), but he's able to tie that knowledge into real world examples and is always able to keep the students engaged. Homework can be time consuming, but exams are always easier than homework. Listen and pay attention and you'll do great in Dr.'s class.

Amazing professor and really cares about his students and how they learn. Homework is often Harding then exam context but good for practice. He takes direct questions on the quizzes for exam questions so review those. Overall love the class and professor!

I LOVED this class with Professor Lagoudakis! GO TO OFFICE HOURS, it's so worth the time, and he will answer any question! Study what he tells you to study! He literally gives you the answers to your exams in class! Would 100% take this class again!

Had this professor halfway through the semester, and I couldn't have asked for a better professor. Homework is more difficult than quizzes and exams, but it's manageable. If you do struggle with the material, Lagoudakis is always willing to meet with you to discuss the areas you're having trouble with. Class is overall fun.
Might've been the worst class I have taken at Iowa State, and I'm premed. So disorganized and is so helpless when trying to ask questions about studying for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures just all over the place and her course packet is so long you will go through more than 30 pages in one lecture. Hard to keep track of and just a bad format. She just expects you to remember all of these incredibly specific pieces that she wants in answers.

Explains things way more in depth than what is required to know. All weekly homework and labs were worth 5 points, while exams were worth 100. Exam questions could be very specific and could also be from past exams. Lectures were not particularly engaging, but followed directly along with the book given at the beginning of the semester.

Dr. Ziegler is great, but definitely should've stuck with the course packets. My grade was much better at the beginning of the semester, but she changed up the lectures and it messed a lot of people up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr cox was our substitute lecturer on the first day and I have never been more devasted to see a sub go. Zieglers ok, but being taught by a bot would have similar results.

She's a very caring professor and you can tell she puts in a lot of work behind the scenes. She explains why each formula is constructed a certain way and what each term is actually contributing. She uses datasets from real studies which makes the class more interesting. You can use a note sheet during exams (write down all the "interpretations")

I did get a C in STATS 301, but that was entirely my fault. Professor Ziegler makes it very clear at the beginning of the semester that attendance of lectures is not mandatory, but is easily the most important part of the class. I skip way too many lectures, and if you do too, DO NOT SKIP LECTURES IN THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: BEST Stats teacher. Take her class if you can. Lectures can get boring, but she is very clear about what will be on exams and quizzes and can use notes on both. Also available outside of class if help is needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Ziegler is a really good professor. She cares that you do well and is always willing to help. The most important thing is to put in the effort and you'll do well on the exams. Would definitely recommend Stats 104 over 101 based on what I've heard from people taking 101.

Online class setup is very easy and has options for all types of learners. You can do the lab or choose to skip lab and have HW grade apply to both. Lecture videos are boring but everyones is. If you have a question, she seems to answer faster than the other staff members which is quite annoying because I try not to bother her too much.

Ziegler was pretty good, I liked her. I personally am just bad at any math so it was a slight struggle but I don't think others would have any problems with this class. There were 2 grade options for online; participate in the labs (zoom) or don't and scores would be based what you chose.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Took this class online and is set up extremely well. She posts very good lecture videos and you just fill out the note packet and keep up with homework/labs/exams. Labs are on zoom and you fill out a shared document. Vast majority of the content is very easy to understand. Some homeworks can be quite hard and 1 exam is dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took this class with the idea of it being easy. I reviewed all of the prerecorded lectures online, did the homework during my selected lab time so that I could utilize my professor if needed, and I was still not doing good. I emailed my professor to see what I could do to bring my grade up. The answer I receive was to simply, "try harder".
She was the only one online for stats 104. I wouldn't take her again. You won't learn anything from her.

I took this online and the way she organized it was amazing. I would recommend participating in labs and watching the lectures if you are confused but I usually didn't even watch them. She gives a lot of helpful resources and is always encouraging students to attend her office hours. You are allowed to use a note card on the exams. Overall easy A.

I am in no way a math person, but STAT 104 was perfect for me. I had the option of getting graded on homework and lectures (group work with other classmates) or just the homework. I did with lectures and she was great with providing feedback and clearly explaining what we were confused on. We also got a notecard for exams which is always a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stat 104 is just a pretty boring class, but it is not too terribly difficult. Exams are the majority of the final grade, but you get to use a notecard so that makes them a lot easier. I stopped going to lecture a few weeks in to class and began just watching her lectures online so I could view them at 2x speed and I did very well in the course.

Fairly dry lectures, but the homework and practice exams were very helpful in preparing for exams. Let's you use a page of notes on the exam. Labs are in a group and there is a big group project at the end of the year. Labs are definitely the best way of learning the class. Not rude and seemed to enjoy teaching.

Dr. Ziegler is a good professor, and it is extremely helpful to go to office hours or ask questions in class. There is a lot of group work, which can be frustrating at times. The practice exams, homework, and labs are all helpful in studying for exams. The exams are really easy compared to most of the homework and labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Ziegler is super nice and friendly when discussing coursework or outside matter. He is very strict, however, about deadlines and grading. Her lectures are very long and heavy, so be prepared to take good notes. This class would have been better without Covid.

Dr. Zieglers recorded lectures are extremely helpful, but there are lots of them per week. In some videos, she shows her cats! The TA/grad instructor that she delegates work to is not very good so Id recommend going straight to her if you need help.

Don't take a class with this teacher. She REQUIRES group projects. If you care about your GPA, stay away from this class at all costs. I requested to do work by myself, and she said no. I dropped this class faster than a hot potatoe.
She comes off super rude and half of the class is sleeping the entire class period. Complete waste of my time. I HIGHLY recommend taking ANY other professor. You will thank me in the future.

Prepare to be babied through 301. Don't get me wrong, it's fairly easy to get a good grade, but you will learn along the way too. It can feel patronizing at times, but Dr. Ziegler clearly states why she does what she does. Go to class for tophat attendance, fill out a notecard based on the practice exam. You can do better than me easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Ziegler is a solid professor. The practice exams are reflective of the real exam and her slides are easy to follow, if you actually attend lecture and pay a little bit of attention. She has great examples during her lectures that make statistical concepts much easier to understand. She is an all around great professor and you get what you put in

Dr. Ziegler is awesome! I have never thought I would understand Statistics. However, Dr. Ziegler's lectures were very organized and easy to comprehend. She has Ph.D in Education and her teaching skills are best. She provides a lot of good examples in her lectures that you can download and follow her R codes to practice. It was a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Doctor Ziegler is an excellent professor. I have had her for two different statistics classes and she was great both times. She is highly accessible outside of class and always willing to meet if you are having trouble with the subject matter. She really cares about your understanding of statistics and does her best to teach you well.

Dr. Ziegler is very kind, but can sometimes come off rude. The class is very homework heavy, which is honestly for the best as it is the only was I learned the material. The lectures are extremely dry and honestly not worth your time. Lab is super inefficient, but you must go. Other professors are way more laid back, so if you can switch then do it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Ziegler was a great professor in my opinion. I did not find 301 to be difficult as long as you go to class and pay attention. Her lectures provide all of the information needed to be successful on the exams. A downside to her class is the group project and using jmp for all of the homework. One of my favorite professors at ISU so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Practice exams given are limited and the exam doesnot really reflect the practice. How are you expected to do well without practice to a similar question on exam but then get shocked when something pops up that you haven' seen before nor in lecture or practice exams. 1practice exam for each exam. Hard to understand lecture and power point are blank

Makes you buy the textbook which you only need for a few homeworks (make a friend that has the textbook and don't buy it). Her lectures are extremely hard to take notes on and her slides are full of information she doesn't talk about and you don't get time to write down. It's impossible to keep up and then she only posts blank slides on canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you have to take 104, Dr. Ziegler is your best choice. She actually studied stats AND stats education, so she knows the info and how to teach it. The class itself is a pain with lots of busy work and assignments that are more difficult than the exams. Also, a group project that is plain awful. But Dr. Ziegler is great at explaining content.

Terrible professor. Her slides aren't easy to follow to study from. Her lectures are dry. Very test heavy class and she is very picky in her grading. She makes sly rude comments during lecture or through emails about lecture attendance. The material is easy but she makes it harder then it needs to be.
She is great. Not difficult to get a good grade in if you do the work, but I felt I learned a ton from this class. highly recommend

This was a good class and she did her best to make sure that everyone was comprehending the concepts. Homework is from out of the book, so buying the textbook is required. She was very willing to meet outside of class time. Tests make up a large portion of the grade and there is a group project. I would take a class taught by her again.

The coursework was fine but the lecture was as dryer than I ever thought possible. She failed to differentiate the subjects that she taught and just about everything just blended together so I wasn't sure what I was learning most of the time. She was nice in class but she was very picky in her grading for the exams which made up most of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Doctor Lamm is an excellent professor. She gives good lectures and examples, no tests, and will often do at least one homework problem in lectures. She is very helpful, understanding, and an amazing professor. 2100 has been great with her.

No exams!!! Beyond grateful that I had her for 381, made junior year much more bearable. You have 4 bigger projects in place of exams which are graded somewhat harshly, but getting an A is still very doable as long as you turn in everything in on time. I wish she taught every ChemE class at ISU!

Failed this class with a professor who played tricks on tests and made us gamble points for more time. Retook with Lamm and got an A! She's so kind and supportive and just wants to see kids succeed. She makes material so easy and is always available for extra help. Favorite professor at all of ISU!

I took both 381 and 358 with Dr. Lamm. She had a full understanding of the concepts, and was able to have further discussion in office hours. Dr. Lamms lectures were amazing. She laid out all the material well and explained the concepts. She answered any questions thoroughly. Do the homework! It definitely helped me solidify the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Probably the easiest class in the ChE major, Dr. Lamm does a great job of not making things too difficult, but also making sure you have a solid grasp on everything going on. Go to every class, do ALL the reading, and do the homework. She grades pretty harshly on tests in my opinion, but just study past exams and practice packet and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Rough 1st impression as the 1st email I got from her said this would be the hardest you'd ever had to work in a class. But my goodness if every professor was as helpful as Dr Lamm ISU would be a better place. Goes out of her way to ensure you understand, but you have to meet her halfway and seek help. Students choose grading %s, very clear and fair
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tough material to cover in this class, so you have to put in the work. Dr. Lamm makes it as bearable as it can be. Very lenient with grading as long as you at least have an idea of what to do. Very helpful, always emails back with suggestions and extra help

Dr. Lamm is an amazing teacher. She truly cares about each and every student. Apart from that, she makes sure that you know the content. She's willing to help if you go into her many scheduled office hours. Furthermore, she recognizes the hard work and effort you put in and makes sure you get credit for it. The book is definitely not optional.
Great all around professor. Exam's were challenging but passable.
Amazing professor !!!

Amazing professor! I wish I could have her for all my ChE classes, she makes hard concepts easy.  She really cares about her students and how they're doing in class.  Super helpful during her office hours if you can go I highly recommend it.    If you keep up on readings and do the homework the tests shouldn't be too hard.
Loved the class. I got stuck with a bad group, but the class was still very interesting. Dr. Lamm is really willing to help you both in and out of the classroom. One of my favorite professors so far.
Team based learning style is great if you get a good group. Regardless Dr. Lamm is a great teacher and will help you outside of class if you need it.

Dr. Lamm is an excellent professor. I highly recommend her for any Chemical Engineering course especially ChE 210. The course is more team-based and teach-yourself, but she answers all questions very well. Her tests aren't bad at all because they're open book/notes (even the final). I think the final course grade is curved a little too.

You learn your stuff from her. Super organized and she knows what she is talking about. Try to read the textbook ahead of time or you might get lost. Test may not be easy since she doesn't do the curve thing but if you absorb things from lecture you can score 100%. Definitely try her!
Amazing!  Very interested in students learning.

Dr Lamm is one of the best profs I've ever had.  She's very organized, a tough grader (but fair), very approachable and helpful. I would def take class her again.  Keys to doing well: Attend every class!  Be respectful/no phones, no chit chat. Be prepared and ask questions.
Awesome teacher, really cares about she is teaching and her students.  very helpful and enjoys helping students understand the material.  She wants her students to do well.  Excellent teacher!

Probably the best professor I have ever had. Always willing to help students understand, no matter how difficult the material. She made a very difficult class very tolerable and inspired enthusiasm.  A most excellent teacher.
Very good professor.  She really cares about whether or not you understand.
No Comments
No Comments

I recommend taking any class with Laehn. She is so passionate and extremely well spoken. She clearly knows what she is talking about and has the ability to articulate abstract concepts very well. I will say this class is not an easy A, but it is manageable if you attend class and do the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Laehn is an amazing professor, but the material in this course is very difficult. There are 4 essay exams, a midterm, and a final exam (all of which are on paper). Be ready to show up to every class, otherwise you aren't going to know the material. Also be ready to study, as there is a lot of material needed to know for the exams.

Laehn is one of the best professors I've ever had. She makes POLS very interesting and easy to understand. She's very caring (she brought us donuts!) and is understanding of sick days. However, don't skip since pop quizzes are very crucial to your grade. That being said, I always felt prepared for exams thanks to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite professor so far at ISU. She is extremely intelligent and is extremely involved with the material. All of the 2 exams and 4 in-class essays are on paper and in class (all written). If you are not interested in the constitution, Supreme Court, etc., this is not the class for you. She also doesn't seem to believe in 100% on exams/essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor. In a case like political science, she is so passionate about educating her students. She does do pop quizzes as "attendance" once or twice a week, but they are usually pretty easy, and some she will just give you a 100 for showing up. Exams are not bad. Not a ton of homework either. Absolutely amazing professor.

I loved this class and she was a great professor. Only downside is she writes on the board and it can be a lot to write down. Tests are easy if you study properly. Attendance isn't mandatory but there is weekly pop quizzes, if she notices there aren't a lot of people in class she'll do two that week.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Be ready to read in this class and attend the lectures! This professor was very humorous and very kind when giving us the content in the class, she is very detailed when it comes to the actual content and what it means implicitly. Make sure to read the excerpts given and do good on the essays because there are only so few things graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best political science professor at Iowa State. The fact this class is a 100's level shocks me, it's definitely a hard class. Very much based on the constitution. 3 exams total with about 10 pop quizzes. Study hard for 1st exam as she let our class use that score on our second one. Complete readings as it will help you on pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course material is difficult but her lectures are very helpful and I've learned a lot. There is a lot of difficult reading but her lectures are extremely helpful so while attendance isn't required I would definitely recommend going.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She gives quizzes on assigned readings every now and then instead of taking attendance. Good lecturer and grades tests fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Laehn is an exemplar professor. She is passionate about what she teaches and lecture reflects that. The class is heavy on assigned reading and I would recommend you stay on top of it and engage with the material to do well. Do not use your phone in class, it won't end well if you do. I loved this class.

Susan is an extremely generous and interactive professor. She is lecture-heavy, with no slideshows or textbooks. There are readings assigned out of class, though I wouldn't say they are required to pass with a good grade. Entire grade is based on two exams and two tests, so show up to class. She is upbeat and has a sense of humor, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, informative lectures. You need to go to class to do well on the papers and exams. Cares a lot for students and very willing to help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class has 2 in-class papers, 2 exams, & 1 final. No cheat sheets for exams. Not mandatory, but lectures are great for understanding the material. No homework besides reading for class. Dr. Laehn is a wonderful professor, very interactive w class, all lectures are on whiteboard.

GO TO THE LECTURES. She is an amazing speaker and makes you want to go to class, not required but heavily recommended. There's multiple books to read and 5 quizzes throughout the semester, you're able to drop the lowest scored one. One final exam on the whole semester, she gives great feedback. Awesome TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For this class theres quizzes almost every week done with your group members. As long as you're understanding the quizzes, you'll get 100% on all of them. There's one big research essay for your final and you work on it throughout the entire semester which is pretty much the only thing she truly grades, and she gives great feedback the essay.

This class is horrible. The professor requires you to read excerpts of cases and buy a whole book, except rarely any of it is actually important. Also, the notes she writes down on the board for you to copy are also unimportant as none of it ever graded. The class has 3 exams and 2 essays. Except the exams are also essays. The TAs are unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An amazing professor, and I will 100% take more of her classes. She is fun, interesting to talk to, and engaging to listen to. It is very lecture-heavy, but the lectures are interesting and fun to attend. There are some readings but they are pretty simple to skim and get the summary of. I would highly recommend this teacher!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have learned more in Susan's classes than I have in any other of my classes. She goes in depth about political theory and then dives into constitutional law. It was a hard class but I enjoyed every moment of it. I would 100% recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Laehn goes into depth about court cases that are important in the governmental system and how certain laws came to be. I really enjoyed this class and thought it was very important that she played devils advocate in cases that were heavy in topic. Be sure to go to class and read the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Laehn truly does care for her students. She wants to challenge her students in order for them to grow and be the best they can be- not just as students but as human beings. Make sure to go to every class, as it is lecture heavy. You read a lot but she does a great job of going over the material and explaining it very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting class taught well. Professor Laehn is very interactive with the class and seems to genuinely enjoy her job. There is a lot of reading, so be ready for that. About a dozen pop quizzes, but they're usually very easy if you've done your readings. Don't skip class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her lectures were amazing. As long as you do the readings and pay attention in class, you will do fine. I love her and I would 100% take another class by her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures, although you must go to them if you want a good chance at passing the class. She is very good and passionate about what she teaches, easy to learn if you put in some time.
She has amazing lectures, but they are ones that you have to go to otherwise you will not pass the class.

This class was a fun one. Im not even a poli sci major but I really enjoyed it. its clear she enjoys teaching kids about something she's passionate about and makes it interesting. a lot of pop quizzes but a lot of them are just "put your name on it and you'll get ten points".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
POLS 339

Your only grades in this class are 3 exams and a 1500+ word final paper. You will read A LOT in this class. The exams are short answers followed by an essay written in a blue book.  She will give you a study guide with topics to focus on, but brush up on everything you've read and learned in that section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While there's a good amount of pop-quizzes there not difficult. If you pay attention or know basic information its pretty simple, it is important to study for the exams, an go over assigned-readings as if not there's questions you miss because of it. Does do exams with blue books, but very enjoyable professor whose clearly very smart.

Dr. Laehn is by far my favorite professor at Iowa State. Her lectures are always amazing, I have honestly never checked the clock in one of her classes. There is a bit of reading but she makes an effort for this class to make sure all of the readings are free. She's very considerate of students. Your success is entirely up to you so go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Susan was a excellent professor. As long as you show up to lecture and do the readings there is no excuse for you to get an easy A. I learned so much about this subject because she does so well at explaining all the concepts and almost all the basics of Political Science. If need a political science class I highly recommend taking her class!

Attendance is not required but highly recommended because you can only get the content during lectures. There are pop quizzes through the semester that you can only take in person. Great prof, she tries not to give us too much work

Dr. Laehn is a great professor. Youll have a certain number of pop quizzes throughout the semester and are pretty important to your grade. Theyre only available in-person, so just show up to the lectures and youll do fine. Quite a bit of reading but its nothing too intensive. Overall, shes nice and very knowledgeable on American politics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Larry is one of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures can be hard to follow at times, however they are very rewarding. He cares deeply about his students and pushes everyone to produce the best work possible. He is an amazing professor and a great guy.

I took his class my first semester here, and I still think about his classes. He made lectures entertaining and truly cares about the students. If you attend class and take notes, then you are fine for the exams. You have to do the assigned readings, which are only four, so just do the readings.

McDonnell made this class seem like a breeze. Lectures and readings are highly informative and help out tremendously during the exams. I took this class over the summer and would 100% do it again. McDonnell also seems to genuinely care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor at Iowa State, Larry is awesome and I highly recommend talking his class if you need to fulfill a Gen Ed requirement!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy class but he will talk so much before class about things that seem irrelevant. Class always ends a little late. He cares about the students and is funny in an odd way. He is a really cool guy I would recommend taking him. Gives you the essay questions before the exams and exit tickets for every class. Assignments are fairly easy

Attendance is taken, yet attending lectures is a waste. He goes off on many tangents and falls behind schedule fast. During his tangents he often said very questionable things, ranging from factually wrong to very offensive content. I was genuinely offended by the things he said. Grades are entered late, and tests are made off of textbook content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Larry is the best professor I have ever had. He is insightful, cares about each of his students, and makes class enjoyable. I felt like somebody really cared about my success and encouraged me to be the best I can be. Definitely take one of his classes even if you are not a history major. Awesome guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Larry really cares about his students and his very passionate about the content. The lecture/class was very much discussion focused. No right or wrong answers but wanted to hear what the student had to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have never met a professor who cares so much about his students. He really cared about the students understanding of a topic that he is so passionate about. He is a pretty easy grader. Go to his office hour at least once he is worth getting to know!

Very interesting course! They say to read the textbook, but I got by fine without it. Just go to every lecture, spend time preparing for essay and the two exams, and speak a couple of times in discussion and you should be fine.

I'm not even a history major and I enjoyed this guy. Mr. McDonnell made for a very interesting class experience. He's quirky, but that's what made the class fun. Regardless of his political views, he's a kind person and I totally respect that. Just read the material and show up every day and he'll like you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are done poorly, dont bother volunteering answers to his questions because every single one is a trick question, asks questions irrelevant to the learning, lectures are let out almost 5 minutes late every time, suggesting information rather than firm in educating you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: McDonnell is my favorite professor at Iowa State. There is a lot of reading, but the class is great. Discussion was worth 30% of our final grade, so if you don't talk go to his office hours and tell him why. He really cares about the success of his students. Show up to class, he takes attendance every so often be he knows who is showing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Larry is the best damn professor Ive ever had. Not because of his teaching cause there are better teachers but because no one cares more than him. Larry wants all of his students to succeed not just in his class but in life. He really truly cares and if you take time to talk to him during office hours youll do just fine in any of his classes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: A professor that is different than most. Easy class that you can get by without doing the readings, but barely get by. Study the essay questions for tests and you'll be fine. Felt like he let his opinion about present topics get in the way of his lectures sometime which can be boring at times. Good person who cares about his students however.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Really Funny in a weird way

This guy is brilliant. Literally all you have to do is go to this class and be somewhat prepared (like, just know what the book is vaguely about) and you'll do fine. Get to know him a little and actually come prepared, you'll get an A. Lecture isn't mandatory but you should go, a lot of your grade comes from written discussion questions in class.

Honestly the best teacher I have had at Iowa State University. You have to read a lot but the discussions make it worth it. I am not even a history major and I have taken 4 classes with him. Defiantly would recommend.

This class was very interesting, but hard for me. You need to read all of the books he assigns you, because they are on the test. It's a lot of work, but a very interesting class. Go to lecture because it's worth it, and raise your hand in discussion group otherwise you won't get participation points.

Pretty chill professor. The only time you will run into trouble is if you use your cell phone or obviously, and i mean obviously, don't do the reading. Other than that it's pretty hard for him not to like you. Canadians, man.

McDonnell is a great guy. I love his stories that he tells throughout the semester. He could do with a bit less trash talking of the U.S (he's canadian.) The lecture is huge, so if you want to never attend lecture, you can. However, I recommend going to lecture because the textbook doesn't cover what he lectures on. Just listen to him in class.

Larry is one of the most brilliant professors I have had the honor to have at Iowa State. His class is difficult, but asking for help and getting to know him is key. His lectures are mostly from his brain, and they are detailed and organized. If you love American history, take a class with Larry. You will not regret it!

Ends classes at least 5 minutes late every time. Uninformative lectures, don't bother going. Seems like a nice enough fellow, but not a good lecturer. Recitation is important- 25% of the grade. Tests are fairly easy, multiple choice and an essay - the essay questions are given out before the exam. Exam grading is pretty arbitrary, depends on the TA

One of the most interesting classes that I have ever taken at ISU. His class is based on discussion which means that readings are required. However, the discussions are almost always interesting and he always incorporates humor into them. Word of advice is to speak to him after or before class. He is down to earth and is willing to help you out.

Really liked this professor, lecture was always interesting and he approached the material with a different perspective than most would. The class was a little slow at the start but picked up quick. This was a good class that was not hard and not much extra work.

My only knock on this guy is that he ends class late every time. Interesting readings, with good discussion. Not a typical retelling of the facts, offers a perspective a general survey would not give, thats what makes his classes worthwhile. All concrete grading comes at the end of the class with a big paper and final.

Prof. McDonnell, is in my opinion, one of the most brilliant professors to teach at Iowa State University. His lectures are fun and interesting and his tests are not too hard (just read the darned textbook and you're good to go). He's a very nice guy and opens your mind to the horrors/accomplishments western civilization (Year 1600+) have committed

Don't go to lecture, it is boring and not needed to do well. Attend recitation, its 25% of the grade. Gives out exam essays prior to test so you can write and memorize them. Multiple choice are fairly easy. Some effort is required, but skimming will get you through.
This was the second class I took with him, and I enjoyed him much more as the professor of a smaller class.  Funny, engaging, if I had more semesters left I would take more classes with him!
Lots of work, but you learn as much as you put in!  Fascinating lectures and the discussions are always fun.  Passionate, brilliant guy.

He really likes to dwell on the depth of things. I'm sure he was at the very least a philosophy minor. The information HE gives is less important than what you get from your TA during resitation. You could totally ace this class going only to resitation. Overall, he's just a so-so teacher. Kind of funny, but almost tries too hard.
Usually fairly interesting lectures. Reading the textbook and going to recitation is more important than attending the lectures. Usually pretty funny and sarcastic in his lectures.

Takes about 15 minutes to start lecturing. Goes off on tangents. Usually ends class 4 minutes late. He used occasional humor. Not needed to go to class. Grade depends on TA, but an easy A. I would take him again.

Has fairly interesting lectures but I still ended up doing the Sudoku most of the time.  Grading on assignments and tests is based on whether the TA likes it or not. Fairly easy but I usually had a few points taken off for no reason on tests which dropped my grade to an A-. Punishes people for having cell phones out in class

Just dropped this course after week 2 (I've never dropped a course before ). Comes off as conceited. Grading and assignment structure make no sense. Tries to be funny and relatable but fails miserably. Talks about his political opinions. Lectures are unrelated to course content.

CJ 3400 course, he waits until last minute to put all the grades in towards the end of the semester. Blames it on the fact he is a grad student with no TA. Synthesis's paper grading is very inconsistent.(Keeps top 3 scores) Participation is 17% of your grade, book assign 12%, quizzes 26%, synthesis's 25, final exam and group project are both 10%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: take with different professor. Is not clear at all, grading makes no sense. I've never had a professor at Iowa State grade so bad without reason nor take it so seriously. I had to drop the class because nothing made sense. Legit go with any other professor.

His class is VERY time consuming. The lectures he gives in class DO NOT match with the work and textbook readings we're asked to do outside of class, especially to the synthesis papers we have to write every other week that make up most of your grade. He's a very harsh grader and will not explain to you what you did wrong. Attendance DOES matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you have a chance to take this class with another professor go with them. Expectations are often not clear in this class. Attendance is a LARGE portion of your grade and there is very little you are graded on. Two hard exams with stuff he does not teach and 3 difficult papers that are graded tough. Overall, go with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class consists of 2 (difficult) exams, 4 (hard) papers, and a group presentation. Attendance matters, as a good portion of your grade is attendance. The exams are hard, and the papers require extensive knowledge to get a good grade. This class is passable, as long as you put in quite a bit of effort. Prof Larter can also be snarky at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Communication with the class was often unclear. There were times I was unsure whether class would meet. During finals week, we were told about a group project but not clearly informed about whether there would also be an exam. On the first day, he mentioned he had been assigned to teach the course and did not want to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He picks fav0rites. If he doesn't like you, or doesn't like one of your friends, your experience is 10x harder. He gave me an F for an essay that I afterwards compared with another student's who got a B. They're arguing the same point and had the same length and mostly the same evidence points. When I asked what I did wrong he didn't answer.

The prof was sweet and this class was seemingly simple but became confusing with the lack of online resources, inaccurate syllabus, unknown timeline, and difficult concepts. quizzes happen randomly without warning and are a huge part of your grade. Solo presentation at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests in this class do not correlate with the lectures. This is an online class, and he is not engaged with his students whatsoever. I have commiserated with many students who are also frustrated that he does not answer his emails. The class average for the last two tests were 65%. Good luck .

John definitely is an expert in the field of linguistics. He does not however care about his students at all. Attended office hours just to be told to try harder and not worry so much. Very rude and snippy with the students. Lectures do not relate to what is in the exams or a lot of the readings. I would strongly consider not taking this class.

He was a pretty good teacher until about the end of the semester. Our class is very small, yet my assignments have not been graded since last month. Also, there was a huge project due and we were given no details or guidelines to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: John is a great teacher, really funny, and really intelligent. He knows his stuff. The class is not easy, but if you go to class, do your study guides, and pay attention, you'll be fine
John is brilliant, and this class is excellent for anyone wanting to pursue TESL. The class is tough but John is a fair grader. Definitely recommend this class and any other class taught by John!
A great teacher!  He definately knows what he is talking about.  Lectures relate to the readings.  Tests are difficult, but he is fair.  Very interesting class.

John knows his stuff, but only in his area of specialization. Not very open to international perspectives at all. A good teacher only for mainstream America. Avoid John if you are a minority or international student. Not curious about issues/events abroad. Insensitive toward minorities and international students. A provincial mindset. Narrow views.

Amazing teacher! Very informed and organized. I actually learned something in this class which is more than I can say for most. He took the needs of the students into consideration and adapted the syllabus to fit our interests :) The assignments weren't really assignments... they were more like thinking exercises. I would definately recommend Levis
Excellent instructor, challenging class with lots of homework but always went over it in class. Though he rarely collected it, it really helps to actually do the work.

Very nice guy, seemed to enjoy teaching.  Homework was assigned often but was rarely collected, 4 short papers and one large project required, in addition to midterm and final exams.  Attendance is taken also.  Something like 80% get A's in the class.

Chem 331 - Was a very good professor and was very accessible outside of class. He was always more than willing to go through homework or previous exams to make sure I understood the concepts. He would also give extra credit on the exams related to what we talked about in class. I would take it again!

I had Levi for Chem231, and he is an absolutely fantastic professor. He is so kind and a great teacher, and wants his students to WIN! He is very clear with the content he is asking us to know for the test, basically giving us the exact kind of questions and principles to know. He's great to meet with, and I wish I could have him again. Reccomend!

I did not enjoy this class at all. A majority of the class was not doing well or failing aspects of tests and he would hardly go over it. I felt expected to learn on my own and the tests were challenging. He would tell us that we need to learn things better that he would only skim in class. Unless you are “chemistry minded” this class is very hard.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. Reads the slides word for word then leaves class early. Uses websites to autogenerate all of the homework. Tells you to read every chapter by yourself and do 20-40 practice questions from the book per unit to understand it, covers 3 units per week. Class average exam 1 was a failing grade. Bad attitude!!

Professor Stanley does a great job at teaching difficult material. He is always available after class to answer any lingering questions, and hint at exam material. He cares greatly about students and curves exam grades and the class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: At first, I really disliked Stanley, but it wasn't due to his teaching style; it was mainly because of the class material. He has a good sense of humor and genuinely cares about his students' success. If I had a different professor, I don't think I would have performed as well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was one of the best professors I have had at Iowa State and I do not believe I would have succeeded in class if he wasn't teaching. The class is overall difficult, but his lectures are understandable. He moves quickly sometimes but there is a lot of material to go over, however. Tests are reasonable as well. Overall, great professor!

Stanley is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about your success in ochem. He understands the course is hard and does a great job teaching it most clearly. He doesn't hesitate to answer any questions or slow down in class. He posts online lectures but go to class! He covers everything on the exams and hints as to what will be on them.
I think I would've gotten an A if he was the professor the whole semester.

Dr. Stanley genuinely wants you to succeed in ochem and understands it is a challenging class. He goes through the material thoroughly and is generous when grading exams. Make sure to go to the lecture, as he reviews everything you need to know for exams.
Levi is amazing. Best professor I've had.
I enjoyed his class more than any other chemistry class I've taken. Exams are your whole grade, but you get one drop. Lectures are everything in this class, attend!

I had taken OChem 331 online due to Covid and then I needed to take 332 for vet school. He does not slow down or really take time to answer question before or after class. He just lectures and then class is over. He does not think about the students that had to take OChem 331 online and then we got put into an in-person class to fend for ourselves.

Dr. Stanley is a wonderful professor! His lectures can sometimes be dry, but they are very helpful in understanding all there is to ochem II. You will definitely need to have a good grasp on ochem I concepts (synthesis and mechanisms) because his course is mainly just expanding on those concepts. His exam, though tough, are do-able and have a curve

Excellent lecture slides and does great with explanations. Wiley+ hw is fine. Exams are hard but he sometimes curves them within reason & lowest score dropped. This semester's final exam questions were extremely difficult/complex because for past exams some students posted the questions on Chegg. Brush up on multistep synthesis from ochem I.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: O chem is a notorious class, but I think Dr. Stanley does a good job breaking it down. With any advanced chem course, it is test heavy, so be prepared for frequent exams. If you like Wiley+ the homework will be no problem, but I found it time-consuming and not helpful. Exams are as difficult as expected, but he gives you 3 hours to take them.
Super difficult class. Just reads off the lecture slides so isn't much of a help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Stanley was an okay professor, however, his lectures focused on what his research was about and then was not on the exam. We spent 20 minutes on the creation of sugar free sweeteners and it was not on the exam. I was on average 10% above average on tests, and I still struggled. I went to office hours, I spent over 30 hours a week on this class.

Best prof. I have ever had. His exams are super hard, but I got an A with flying colors. But that took hours of study, going into his office hours, attending lectures regularly etc. He curves the exams as well. Take it with if can get him. His lectures are a bit dry but you learn everything from there. So, don't skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Levi provides you with all the tools to be successful in Ochem II. He provides outlined and annotated notes for each chapter, which makes lectures more about learning and less about note taking. This also makes them easy to reference to. He holds exam reviews sessions and is always willing to accommodate students needs. Makes it easy to do well in

Dr. Stanley is a fantastic professor. He genuinely cares about his students and tries his best to make organic chemistry as entertaining as possible. The tests can be tough (the average on the last two and the final were about 50% before a curve) but he curves to make up for this. Be sure to study a lot or you will not do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Stanley is really good at explaining things in lecture and is one of the best professors I've had at ISU. He curves the class the standard organic chemistry >85% is an A and also an additional curve on top of tests which is super helpful. He also does review sessions before tests which are very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.
