reviews.comment: One of the nicest and most understanding teachers. You can really tell he cares about his students, their wellbeing, and their learning experience. He really pushes you and sometimes it's hard to understand why you're doing an assignment but it's worth it.

Really nice guy, but he doesn't seem to understand that we have other classes to do work for. Even when you bring your concerns to him he blows you off. Terrible at giving instruction and guidance. Sometimes he can lose his temper and be a little unprofessional. Again, he's nice but he's a bad teacher. Studio feels more like a 3-hour lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough grader
Overall, she is a really tough grader, and she sees the flaws in everything.

I took this half-semester course expecting a GPA booster, but the grading felt subjective. Despite following instructions, I received low scores seemingly based on my viewpoints rather than the rubric. Overall, this was one of my most disappointing classes at ISU and I would not recommend it.

This class work wise was really not that bad. Now where I draw the line is being nitpicked on any little mistake I made on discussions that are prompted to you in a very vague way that makes mistakes easy. The criticism is subjective and in no way constructive. I would avoid this gen Ed at all costs and pick something else that is graded less harsh

She grades extremely harshly on the littlest details and it's almost impossible to get a perfect score. Prompts to assignments are extremely vague expects you to read 100+ pages a week along with answer the questions given.  I would recommend to take this course but please take my advise and don't take it with this professor

reviews.comment: Dr. Deininger, like all professors, does not grade assignments but the teaching assistants do. I took the half-semester class and it wasn't terrible but yes you had a discussion post, unit quiz, and book quizzes to do every week and one final project which isn't bad. Just don't fall behind and pay attention to deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have just started this class a few weeks ago and I hate it. TA's are horrible at being consistent. Discussion post are the only thing that matters and they grade wayyyy to harshly. not to mention she wants you to read 100+ pages a week. its so frustrating because a post you make one week could be a 12/12 then but a 5/12 the next week. don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took several courses with Dr. Deininger during my time at Iowa State. I enjoyed every course she taught. I greatly appreciated the wonderful feedback she gave us on our papers and how she challenged us to think critically about contemporary issues facing France. Very knowledgeable and always available and happy to meet outside of class.

This is one of the easiest classes I've taken that's actually enjoyable. No exams, just a weekly quiz and a discussion post with a final project. Because it was a self-lead online course, interaction with Dr. Deininger is minimal, but she's always available to answer questions. Just look over the material she posts to Canvas and read assigned text.

I took the half semester course, and it really wasn't that bad. I don't know why everyone is saying that she is such a terrible professor. Each week there's a discussion post and quiz. The discussions and quizzes are easy. Most of the answers are on quizlet. This class was an easy class and I would recommend it to others.

She was a very difficult teacher that I don't think really cared to be there. You have 2 assignments every week a quiz and discussions. When it comes to the discussions she Is not nice. When it comes to the quizzes most of them are not even found in the textbook or on the internet. Overall try to avoid getting her.

She grades very, very subjectively. You will not get an A no matter what. Use direct quotes, evidence, justification, good diction, etc., and you will still be graded not fairly. RIP your 4.0 if you have one. Also, she is so egotistical with her "Dr." title.

This was a half-semester online class and was hard. A majority of questions were not on quizlet/chegg, and a good amount were wrong. There was A LOT of reading material with hardly any interaction between Deininger and students. The discussion posts were graded VERY difficultly with hardly any feedback. Only 10 assignments, but lowest 3 dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Shes not a good teacher. Just tells you to read stuff that has nothing to do with the exams. Exam questions have multiple correct answers, but only one counts. Doesnt really get her self involved with this class. It doesnt seem like she wants to teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class online, so we both had to adapt to the new learning style, but she put in little effort. Mountains of busywork assignments with little to no meaning, and she makes it very unclear how to do the assignments. Then, when students are confused, she takes out her anger on the class. Easily one of the worst professors at this university
She grades way too harshly for such an easy class. Thanks to her, I'll be getting my first B in a foreign language class because of how unfair her grading is. I would not recommend her at all.

She doesn't communicate well at all, when things are due and how you should do them is always very obscure, as she goes off the syllabus and doesn't tell you what the new plan is. I hope you're organized, cause if you're not, good luck

My experience in this class is sullied a bit by the fact that Deininger was gone for half of it because of a surgery and essentially forced it to be an online class for that period of time.  I missed a lot of deadlines because the line of communication with her was so restricted during that time.  I wish she had had a better backup plan.

Dr. Deininger is nice and her class is easy. She frequently brings in candy and likes to have class outside when possible. She almost never has textbooks for her classes. However do the assigned reading because there is usually a small (3 question) quiz over it and then discussion/participation points too. Good news is there is very little reading.

Dr. Deininger is very helpful to students and is usually forgiving if you do an assignment incorrectly but clearly exhibit that you put forth effort. She is very knowledgeable about French language and culture and offers real insight to those who are also interested in the topic.

Dr. Deininger is a fair professor with a fun and relatable personality. She's willing to listen to students (en français or english) as well as work on dates for assignments if circumstances are severe. She cares and is passionate about French and France. I've loved having her over the last 3 years. NEVER expects textbooks for 300+ classes! :)

Dr. Deininger loves what she teaches and she brings a personal aspect into it. This class is France Today and so she relates a lot of the material back to her experiences, which is great! I loved the class and it was great to learn about the country!
She likes to talk about herself a lot but she's pretty nice. No final which is nice. Class is pretty straight-forward, do the readings and participate in class and you'll do fine.
She's a really consistent teacher and no textbooks! :)
She's a fair teacher and the class was really fun.

Good class, but must have prior French experience to excel. If not proficient with conjugation, spelling, and grammar, you will run into problems. Assignments are not always clear, and it is crucial that you consult the syllabus. Keep in mind, it is a 300 level and you are treated as such. Most papers and assignments must be printed out beforehand.
she is helpful and the class is mostly group work. But it is not clear with the activities that you have to do with homework and exams.

Not a fan of the class, but it was relatively easy. Most of the work was discussion, en francais and the book was annoying and dry to read. But I loved going every day and Melissa is a wonderful teacher and I like her very much! She is wonderful with answering questions and listening to your comments. She gives no extra credit...so be weary.

Expectations on homework assignments were very unclear. Readings were almost always boring and hard to follow. She did not feel very approachable at all. I usually very much enjoy French, but I dreaded and disliked her class. Avoid her if at all possible.

Madame Deininger is an excellent professor. She was very flexible with homework assignments.  She is friendly and easy to get along with.  She brought treats for the class, which was very different from most professors..in a good way. :)  I learned a lot in her class and definitely further developed my french speaking, reading and writing skills.
The class wasn't at all what I thought it was going to be.  Didn't learn anything.
He's very monotone, so good luck paying attention. You don't necessarily need to go to class, but a lot of his slides are just pictures that you have to be in class to understand.

His questions on exams and homework were worded in a way that made the question unclear about what he wanted from us. When I took it, exams were online, and now they are in class. Sometimes, exam questions would have no correct answers because he copied and pasted parts of questions but not all of them. He was very monotoned during lecture.

He seems nice but I couldn't pay attention to the lectures no matter how hard I tried, they were so boring and monotone and unengaging. In recitation he gives you all the answers for the HW so I would go for those but nothing else. It was easy since he gave HW answers and he posts all his notes but the lectures were so incredibly boring

He seems like a nice guy outside of the classroom, but I actually couldn't listen to his lectures.  They were SO boring, and he has the most monotone voice ever.  The content is already not interesting so the lectures were pretty bad.  Everything is available online including the tests which was nice.

Great professor! His lectures were pretty boring, but the material is very accessible outside of class if you don't go. He goes over homework problems weekly and will do all of them during office hours. The exams were online, so they were easy to understand. Very easy to ask questions. Other than the boring lectures, this class was pretty easy!

He seems like a nice guy but his lectures were awful. I didn't learn anything from going to lecture and rarely took notes. All he did was read off his slides and mostly used pictures which weren't helpful.

This class in general is going to be difficult, but he made the class feel simpler to understand. You have to go to almost every lecture to maintain understanding though. He posts all the material on canvas, so assignments and exams are fairly straightforward.

Does a decent job at providing resources if you miss class, however going to class is pointless, i learned more reviewing the materials at home. He does go over homework questions in class weekly that was helpful. This class should honestly be taught online. The tests are difficult and answers are no where to be found in provided material.

BBMB 221 is a tough class, but he was super willing to meet with me outside of his designated office hours (due to another class conflict) to answer questions and help me prepare for the tests. His Canvas page is very well organized and he provides a range of materials for each lecture: the slides, the lecture notes, and review questions!
He is a good professor. He cares about the class content, the students and the grades. He takes difficult material and makes it become really easy.

reviews.comment: Very unorganized. Inexperienced. Often got in the way of projects. Class attendance was mandatory but coming to class was pointless.

He had very unclear expectations that would seem to change often, leading us to kind of be confused on what we were supposed to do.

Tony means well - there were many times I was confused but he gives a lot of clarification for assignments if you ask. I don't think he really understand that not everyone can read his mind but his course was enjoyable. I had a good time learning about all different things.

Hede my warning

Professor Moton is a cool guy and easy to talk to, but his teaching style needs work. His classes mostly consist of him just reading the textbook, and assignments are unclear. Grading is a bit tough without much explanation, and I often left class feeling confused and frustrated. I ended the class feeling like I've learned next to nothing.
Graded pretty easily. He will make class very fun to go to but can also be a little close-minded at times. Sometimes makes decisions that'll make your head turn. Also kind of unreliable at times.

Tony makes promises he can't keep, flat out lies about his plans for the course, and is incredibly overbearing. This is a super hands on course and Tony continued to tell the class that is was “our show” and “up to us” and the second that we had ideas of our own he would immediately take over (with worse ideas). He is often hard to work with.
Didn't show up to classes. Shows favorites in class. Doesn't care about other students. He doesn't let students use their ideas.

Grades hard. The amount of time that is expected in this course is insane. The entire class is group work except for one assignment and the final. You can tell he cares about his students but micromanages projects rather than guiding. He will not teach you how to edit. Cried a lot.

Tony is a great person and mentor, but this course is one of the worst courses I have ever taken. 
Tony constantly changes his mind (due dates, quizzes, etc.)
He does group grading
Has too large of expectations
Grades unfairly
Talks badly of his students behind their back
Makes you do work for other people in the class
Does not teach anything

The class as a whole is easy, he gives 100% on all assignments that are not quizzes. He is not a good lecturer and the stuff he lectured on was never used. The final was awful. It was on stuff that he did not teach us. He gave us a mock exam without an answer key so we didn't know if we were doing it right. Then it was nothing like the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class as a whole was pretty easy because he gives 100% on every project/assignment you do, but there are some quizzes that he does that are nearly impossible to do because of how bad his lectures are. The lectures are brutal and boring, and it is impossible to pay attention during them, but attendance is not mandatory.

Super easy professor. Attendance is taken once per week so I would show up until it was taken each week. Lectures are boring and in my opinion a waste. Exams and homework are extremely easy, just look at the review slides. Basically a free A class.

Professor has extremely dry lectures. 10 percent of the grade can be earned by showing up directly to class. Pop Quizzes for attendance are extremely random. Reads directly off the lecture rather than teaching examples and using student feedback.

Extra credit of 10% given just for showing up to class and doing easy pop quizzes. Lectures were very dry and slow. Never anything different, ever, just PowerPoint presentations. Reads the slides. :/
Exams were hard but they had one extra credit question each. EASY homework and group projects.

Solid lecturer, lectures were very useful for exams. I wonder if this class has been watered down- on exam 2- 3 of 5 questions were straight ripped from HW/recitation. Sometimes Trent struggles with answering complex questions and beats around the bush, and also not the most sociable prof. But I liked him and thought the content was well structured
He gives exams that are almost impossible to pass since they dont cover 90% of the topics of the time

I had this professor for COMS3110, and while his lectures were helpful in studying for the exam, any idea that was confusing was not clarified well. He would not say anything about the exams; they would always have one hard question with very little time to think about it. If you have to take this class just try your best to get through it.

I had Nok as my assigned Professor, but I found myself attending Trent's lectures more. If you're going to take 311 definitely take it with Trent. I definitely wouldn't say he's great but at least better than Nok. Thing I dislike the most from Trent is that he doesn't answer questions directly but will cut around the bushes and not answer it. ever.

Trent is sarcastic and a tough grader. Either your correct or you're so wrong and he'll make that known. He has an inability to answer a question and will just talk his way around it and throw some big words in there. If you answer one of his questions, he almost always says you're wrong and then doesn't answer his own question. Don't recommend!

Good professor. Class can feel slow, but he explains questions well. The department itself makes this class terrible to take. No schedule for assignments, they drop homework a week before it's due. Trent is a good person, but sometimes it feels like he wants to make this class harder than needed. No posted notes, and not too helpful for exam prep.
Actually a great professor overall, would study one of his sessions again (will actually, he's teaching 327 next semester)

The course just sucks, but Muhr doesn't really make it better
Quizzes are easy, 2 attempts + google
HW is garbage, lectures teach easy problems and the slides are poorly handwritten half organized videos
Exams are tough but not impossible, review homework and practice Leet/Geek problems online
The book is tangent related to the homework, 3/10.
Took during summer, was a hard class but Trent is a good professor.

Take the course if you're not working over the Summer. The concepts take a bit of time to understand and you will need that time.
When you do take this course over the summer, take it in the later part of summer. 

In the mean time read:

Introduction to Algorithms (9780262258104)
Ch: 1 - 4, 6, 10, 12, 22 

This covers the first half of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is rather disorganized, and the material is pretty dry. I was often bored in class, but it wasn't entirely the fault of Muhr. Generally, you'll get better practice of the material by completing programming assignments and carefully going through the ZyBooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, this class has a lot of homework, and you must attend lecture as you can get a lot of points from attendence.

I think he overcomplicated the materials sometimes, and the lecture is not very intuitive. He tried his best, and he is very nice and patient if you go ask him a question. 228 is a very important class and will be very useful, just try your best to understand the material. Project 3 is kinda a lot, but the rest of the projects are not too bad.

For reference, I had an A in 227. 228 is a class where you get much less programming practice and the exams have a lot of programming-heavy questions. I wish I would have taken this class more seriously at the start, exam grades killed my overall grade in the class. However, I did enjoy Muhr as a lecturer overall! He is easy to understand.

I think Muhr gets bad feedback because of the difficulty of the classes Trent teaches. Muhr is a generally caring and nice professor that is usually open and available for feedback and questions. He doesn't mind extending deadlines and regrading homework because he seems to genuinely want students to succeed and understand what he teaches.

Graduate student under Georgi Batinov. He tries his best to follow up with questions, but the lectures were very boring to me. If you breezed through CS227, just be careful because this class is harder and much more disorganized. To succeed, try to apply things you learn in lectures and the textbook to your own small program to help with exams.

OMG, Many of students were complaining about this CS311 online course. "I also had a difficult time understanding what was actually being asked. I did ask the TA for clarification and got an answer that I thought I understood. I apparently still didn't (as demonstrated by my received grade on that problem)."(Piazza)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I will start by clarifying, she is an amazing person. She is super sweet and caring. However, avoid her class. she takes forever to grade (months). Lectures/discussions drag on. She is a VERY hard grader and even when you get good feedback, you'll still get a C. She also cancels class nearly weekly, so it feels like any class effort is wasted.
Very fair with grading assignments. Visited her during office hours, and she was so kind. Will tell you what you need to do on the major assignments to do well. There's extra credit as well!

You'd get nothing but good feedback on a paper, yet receive such a low grade. She is so strict and brutal with her grading. The class was organized nicely and she was a very very very nice person and very understanding, but her grading was all or nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking this course with Dr. Murphy, especially if it is online. She is extremely difficult to contact and took +10 days to respond to an email. Not very clear grading criteria, and took 7+ weeks to get first grades back. She did allow for revisions, which were helpful. Very nice person, but not a great professor.

For an online class, this was a mess. She took forever to grade the major assignments (which were graded hard, even tho we barely had any feedback to improve on). She only provided feedback on the first assignment, which was annoying because it was hard to figure out what you did wrong for resubmission. Wouldnt recommend this class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of discussions, quizzes, and other homework assignments every week.  Second half of semester you do a lot of group work.  Relatively easy work, never stressed.  Professor was so caring and was always there to help.  Highly recommend her as an english professor. Many resources provided by the professor.  Communicated very well to students!! :)

I feel like my dislike for this class/professor was primarily because it was online. I generally received really good feedback but really disliked the class overall. Based on other reviews, I would recommend taking this class in-person.

Amy intends to be on a first name basis with all of her students. ISU's English classes can be monotonous and boring, but she will facilitate interesting discussions regardless. She is tough on grades, but allows a revision and gives good critique so there is no excuse for bad grades.
She was an amazing teacher! You are so lucky if you get to have her!

Amy is such a fun, reasonable and understanding person. If you go talk to her she'll help you significantly and she will tell you right away the personality types that work with her teaching style. This ENFP wouldn't have switched for anyone. I loved having Amy for 250. She's a little tough on grading but not too bad. Also extensions possible.

Amy Murphy has been my favorite professor of my entire college career. Incredibly approachable and interested in her students success. Attendance is mandatory, however her lectures are interesting and engaging so there were rare times I didn't want to go. No exams, only papers. Her grading is clear in her rubrics. Willing to work with her students

Amy was the best professor I've had yet. She cares about her students and will help anyone learn if they need it. She loves to make any kind of conversation and is extremely friendly. I would definitely take her classes again. She's a great professor and person in general. She also clarifies the curriculum as well which is super helpful.
Super chill
She's dope. Really funny and goes with the flow. She is really easy to get along with however I did have to read a lot and actually do work.
A great and flexible teacher. Understands that most of her student may not like writing. Very straight forward and clear. Would highly recommend

Amy is a great professor. She gives great feedback and makes sure you know what you're doing. She doesn't really follow the curriculum guidelines and cuts out "busy work" as she calls it which is really nice. She allowed revisions on ALL papers instead of allowing you to do only one like the department says.

A bit more work, but he cares about how you're doing and is very considerate when it comes to outside life and mental health. Extremely educated and you could easily talk with him for hours. His projects are very student led, which could be misunderstood as not giving any instruction by some--but if you take the time to communicate you'll be fine.

Great Professor! Took him for two studios, and definitely loved. He is easy going and lets you have fun with you work. Definitely someone to consider if you love working at your own pace and love to go crazy with your designs.

Mikesch is super devoted and genuinely interested in what he teaches, which is always important. Very eccentric and will sometimes swear, but that's what makes him funny. He personally helped me when my grade was dropping, and offered an insane amount of extra credit. I would take literally any class with him again.
Great!
Mikesch is awesome. He is really funny and will help you so much with your projects. Best teacher I have had in college so far.

He is a funny guy, and sometimes a bit absent minded.  He goes off on tangents all the time and spends too much time on  trivial stuff.  The class was extremely helpful and got better as the semester went on.  The assignments were rather easy and sometimes helpful.  He is a very blunt person, but don't take it personally, he's like that to everyone
No Comments
First name is Mikesch first of all ... very helpful and has great ideas / knows a lot about practicing & past architects ... runs a nice laid-back studio.
I thought she did pretty good. A lot of people complained, but I think that's because English 150 and 250 are seen to be a waste of time, which I might be inclined to agree a little.
Ananda is a quiet, shy, and easy-going teacher. Going to class is not required and there is no reason for you to go. She is extremely picky on her rubric. If you follow the rubric, you will get an A.

There are so many unnecessary assignments that are given that don't enhance learning whatsoever. She makes you buy 3 books and says you will need them for readings but you can easily get away with not reading the books. This class is a waste of time and there is too much busy work that makes me question my sanity. If you can, get another professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Doesn't make sense to have one paper to write per week. Very nitpicky. Acts as if her class is the only class we're taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Must go to class as attendance is mandatory. Have take home exams and also must attend four performances and write reflections about them.

Cason is absolutely amazing. He is genuine and such a kind person. He always has a smile on his face and wants to help out. Cason has interactive and engaging lectures while also not bombarding you with homework. You still have to do your work and put effort in though. I would say Cason is in elite company when it comes to professors at ISU.

Incredibly great lectures. They were engaging, fun, and enjoyable. I can not emphasize enough how good he is at lectures. He is a tough grader on the essays, but the tests are open note with no testing center, and he provides plenty of extra credit opportunities so it wasn't a big deal.

Attendance is mandatory, but they were fun and engaging. The exams were all online and open note. The mid-term and final are both 1000 word "Reaction Papers" about performances you went to. Not super interested in theater but Cason made it fun.

Cason is an amazing professor! He cares about his students, lectures are very enjoyable, class is well organized but not very difficult. Attendance is graded and there were a decent number of assignments but everything was pretty straightforward and also all tests are open note which I really appreciated. I definitely recommend taking this class!
Attendance is graded, but his lectures are fun. Your midterm and finals are reaction papers to any kind of performance. The textbook used was written by him.
Cason is the best!
Super awesome guy :)

Cason is a great professor! He loves teaching and it really shows in his lectures. This class has two papers that you write based on a performance you went to. There is also exams and quizzes, but they are all take-home and open note, multiple attempts, and not timed. Easy class, you will get an A if you do your work and attend! Tophat attendance!

Extremely easy class. My only complaint is that the textbook is required, and you have to buy it for $70. Exams are very easy, reading quizzes are very easy. 2 essays are also graded very easily. Theater is not the most interesting subject for me but there were some bits in the class that I enjoyed.

If you need a gen ed credit, take THTRE 106 with Cason. Even if you don't like theatre, he will find a way to make it fun for you. Just a genuine guy who wants to connect with his students. Definitely my favorite professor of the semester. His lectures are fun and full of memes. The textbook says it's required, but I never got it and I was fine.

Fantastic professor, very professional and caring with his students. Very helpful in the classroom setting if youre looking into theatre. Very passionate about this topic and it shows. The enthusiasm he puts into his lectures (of other classes, this one doesnt really have many) is infectious!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: yes sir yes sir I love cason murphy with my whole being

I absolutely loved this class! I took this class because it was easy, but he really sparked my interest in theatre and made me look forward to attending lectures. Cason is not only an amazing professor but an overall wonderful human being with a big heart. The grade is made up of attendance, 3 reaction papers, 6 online reading tests, and 3 exams

Best professor I've ever had. Cason is also my advisor and he is the most laid back and genuine person. He gives amazing feedback and really cares about each student. Highly recommend taking any class with him.
the best professor ever, not just because it'a an easy course, I really learned lots of things and he always willing to help students, take this course! you will definitely enjoy it.

Cason has been one of my favorite professors to date! He is incredibly real, passionate about theatre, and a master of the subject. My lecture was pretty big, but he knew many of us by name and actually recognized me on campus a semester after I took the class! Lectures are filled with funny anecdotes, videos, and demonstrations. He's the best!!!!

Professor Murphy is genuinely great at what he does! Originally I wasn't very interested in theatre but after taking this course with him, my interest has definitely been sparked. He made our classes enjoyable and highly interactive. He is a wonderful professor and person who was willing to help students. Recommended his class to all of my friends!
Fine but passes off a lot of his workload onto guest lecturers and relies on too many videos. Maybe just lazy? A new prof should show a better work ethic. It's an easy A.

An amazing lecturer, professor, and overall great human being. He appeals to his students' human condition, needs and has made an impact on my first year of college. His assignments and exams are all well put together, he has a burning passion for the topics discussed as well as making them extremely interactive, this is what theatre is all about.
Awesome fun to go to @ 9am, funny, down to earth, understanding, lots of extra credit chances, interesting content, not difficult, gives feedback on papers!

Far too tedious of a workload full of nonsense thought provoking questions that leave you feeling entirely too unaccomplished afterwards. I am a typical straight A student and Rachel Murdocks 15-week speech class has brought me to my knees.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Murdock is awful she spent more time filling out her student page about her various degrees then actually teaching. I was reading other rankings and I am shock people actually thought she was good. From my census of the class I am in almost half the class is failing and the workload I got outweighs my math workload. Keep in mind this is speech.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Eng 302 was an extremely tedious class that basically just taught us all a lot of things that we already know. I really enjoyed it however! Prof Murdock really knew what she was talking about and did a really great job of relating the assignments to potential real life job situations. Really liked her!
Prof Murdock is great. She was very gracious as I was dealing with some things that caused many absences, but she let me do the work regardless. I'd recommend her!

All you have to do is show up and listen. I bought the book and never opened it or did the readings. The material was very common sense and very easy. There were various pop quizzes and case studies but those are done in your assigned group. if you aren't there your group can mark you absent and you get no credit for that assignment. Witty as well.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. She literally reads off the Powerpoint all the time in a monotone and stumbles over her words. She gives random pop quizzes and case studies with no warning, so if you skip you'll lose points. It feels like she's out to trick the students. I will say that she is open to student suggestions to make the class better.
Rachel Murdock is a nice person, but she is not great at teaching. Her lectures are long and dull, plus she gives random quizzes and in class case studies so you always have to attend.
This class ruined my academic confidence. This is the sole class I did not get an A in. Would do anything but every take an online course of his again.

Read before class, DONT MISS LECTURE, print his notes, do the end of chapter exercises and review the lecture notes. The test sample questions didn't help me at all. Understanding the lecture notes and doing the end of chapter exercises is what got me an A. you need to put effort in the course. Memorizing material will not help at all.

Prof. Myers is a bit hard to understand if you don't read ahead. He's doing a better job with the exams by allowing a cheat sheet for amino acids and other items. Class is difficult due to the material, time it needs to be learned in, and the format. - Be warned!
No Comments

His problem sets from the book are of great help, though his train of thought in lectures is sometimes disorganized. If asked a question he will do a good job answering it. It's a hard class if it's your first BBMB class. The practice exams are semi-helpful, but the best bet is reading the book and working on the problems he gives.
He is really boring but the tests are not too bad. You HAVE to read the text which is also horribly uninteresting.

SHE IS THE BEST!! Seminar class, the textbooks are the chapter books or short stories she provides. The class was a lot of work, but a lot of fun. She also changed the assignments up due to corona & gave us time to go into breakout "rooms" to speak about the relevant info & use Spanish. FUN CLASS & I wish we could've met in person :'(

Read lots of short stories and watch movies. Come to class prepared and participate to have a better understanding of the story plots. She is very helpful and teaches each unit differently, so it's never the same. Very enjoyable class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is nice and goes over the material pretty well. However, her grading is a bit harsh

Profe Myers is super nice and really flexible if you talk to her. Her class is fun, but if you skip you will be really confused. There is a lot of reading poetry and short stories, so if that isn't your thing this is no the class for you. If you don't speak Spanish proficiently you will struggle a lot because she does not slow down.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Myers was incredible and my fav professor at Iowa State. It was a seminar class so the level was hard but with Myers it was interesting and I learned so much! Understands students and holds them to their level while challenging them to grow. She has a world view and personal perspective which makes her perfect to teach the class. Recommend her
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Profe. Myers is awesome. She is so sweet and wants everyone to understand the grammar points. The tests are not that hard considering she tells you what's going to be on them; no surprises here. The homework is essentially participation and there are three papers, but this shouldn't be a problem if you're good at writing. Recomdaría!

Profe Myers is the best! She makes class interactive and fun! Sometimes a lot of homework but it's not hard. There are two tests that are hard, but they're a replica of the study guide with different sentences and she prepares you well.  Wrote 2 papers and the final was a research paper. She made class enjoyable to come to, I highly recommend her!!

By far one of the smartest and kindest professors I have ever had. He wants all his students to succeed and provides enough top hat and extra credit to carry your grade if you are a bad test taker. The exams are on the harder side, but don't let that discourage you from taking his class he wants all his students to succeed.
Great professor. Kept class lively and interesting. Clearly very passionate about the topics he teaches. Highly recommend any class he teaches.
Great professor.  His tests can be a bit difficult, but if you attend class regularly and take advantage of his review sessions, you should have no problem pulling off an A or B

He knows what he talks about when it comes to the Psychology of Religion.  He tries to make class fun, and his review sessions for the tests are very helpful.  Not my all time favorite class, but in the top.

This class sucked!!  I don't care how attractive he is.  His assignments are just a lot of busy work, which I could have done without when I was taking 4 other classes.  I changed this class to P/NP because I didn't want to do what was required to get an A.  Also, he doesn't use Web CT.  All my other classes did, just not him.
He's helpful, very clear, fair, and just about every lecture is interesting.  Oh yeah, and he's hot as hell too.
He's a good teacher.  He tries to play it off that his class is really hard in the beginning but it's not.  He is really nice and lectures are pretty interesting. Oh yeah and he's kinda cute.
His essays on his tests are pretty in-depth, but he does a great job of teaching and keeping people interested. He gives out of class assignments that take some time but he grades rather fairly.

He suffers from the new professor syndrome in that he tries to make you do too much work and cover too much material.  He's cute, though, so you forgive him in the end.  He really seems to love the material that he covers, and is always willing to help his students.

He is an awesome professor and a sincere up-beat person. Extremely approachable and very easy going. Is passionate about Psychology and Religion. So if you are interested in either he will talk your leg off.

Hard, but rewarding imo. Attend all lectures, take extra time to study, and you will deeply understand the material. The real explanations happen during lecture. If you don't understand something, you need to understand it: it'll be on the exam. The meanings and applications are more important than the equations.

Oh, you don't have a PhD in kinetics already? Wasn't that one of the prereqs for 314? Sucks to be you then...

Disorganized class, disorganized lectures, disorganized grading, you never know what to expect so you can simply try your best. I suppose he is trying, but after 20 years, not much has changed it seems.
"Dont be a victim" - R.E. Napolitano

He is a really good professor. He gives very specific feedback of the group assignment and quiz. His exam is very easy, just ask questions like some formula variables meanings. But his team assignments are a little bit hard. The most important thing is DO NOT MISSING ANY CLASS. He has no ppt, so you must take notes that is important content in exam
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Napolitano was a great professor to have. Although his tests were hard, he really teaches the material very well. The background that you need for this class is very poorly taught and he makes sure we strengthen the fundamentals. A lot of deep level learning.
Tough tests you can't image!!

His class was pretty harsh. However, I was very luck when I was taking his class. He gave us the online exams with a lot of technology problems. So he gave us two attempts. Sometime, the questions will pop up in your blackboard before you take the exam. That makes the class much easier.
Attending lecture is not helpful. He always assumes you know something. He puts high expectation on you but does a really poor job teaching us in a understandable and organized way.

His powerpoint slides are poorly organized. His explanation does not make sense. The test was hard, and he likes to test on something that he didn't talk about in the class. In the class, he just mumble on and on. The laboratory program is also unorganized and is lack of sufficient guidance. All in all, he doesn't like teaching and not good at it.

Thermo is hard. No doubt about it, and it's going to take a lot of work to do well, but it's possible. He's willing to help if you're willing to put in the work to try and figure out what you don't understand before coming up to him. Very rewarding class in the end, and the better you do here, the easier Kinetics will be.

I think he is not that much into teaching, and kind of irresponsible. I gave the test for him to regrade, and I never got it back. The materials is hard, and he think we understand everything already, but in fact none of us understand the subject.
If you go to him with a question, prepare to feel insulted, belittled, and still not have a clue whats going on.
His class is realistically a 10 credits class worth of work.  So be prepared...
You have to have him, so good luck. (there should be an easy rating below 1.....) Material is OK, but his choice in the book makes it extremely hard.
Try to avoid him but, Dr No is inevitable.

She has potential to be a good educator. Her style of teaching is straight to the point, so straight in fact that I am bored to tears. She is minimally engaging, and lectures are taught as if she is a student reading her own notes rather than educating. Makes frequent mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please do not get discouraged by previous reviews. She is a great professor, and it is not her fault you could not pass Math 1500 because you were on your phone. She really cares for her students and will go out of her way to make sure you understand the topic. She will always answer your questions.

If you're looking for a professor who cares about what they teach, she's a great choice. She presents with slides in her lectures and frequently stops to ensure that what she's teaching is understood. The rest of the curriculum is the same as any other Iowa State math class. I would absolutely recommend her; these reviews do not do justice.
Awful professor. Couldn't really understand her and she did handwritten notes and her handwriting was not legible. I would not recommend her to anyone. I had to self teach.
Very difficult, had to self teach
Her lectures were hard to hear and were quite boring. Her handwriting was not always legible.

This teacher was good at teaching, but I was in the Drawing I class, and he made it feel more like a Design Studio I class. One project was directly from Design Studio I, and another was very similar. He is understanding about absences, though, and wants you to succeed.

Professor Edwards is a fun guy. He's got a unique personality and tends to trail off topic in class. You may not always see eye to eye with the feedback and recommendations he gives for your work but either way the feedback is detailed and informative. There is a lot of work to be done outside of your time in the studio, but it is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice enough as a person but tends to ramble throughout class. When it comes to the assignment, it tells you what to do but not specifically what he was looking for in the assignment. I don't think he is very good at understanding people's different levels of artistry and grades very tough on work that should have been acknowledged better.

He doesn't provide any clear criteria for what he expects or how he grades, which was frustrating, but I really enjoyed having him as a teacher nonetheless. He doesn't seem to grade on improvement or drawing to the best of your ability which is fine for students more advanced at art but sucks for those who are learning.
Nathan Edward's yaps a lot but he's a slay queen eater. Love that carabiner he wears. Period.

Hated everything about this course. His lectures were wordy and rarely helpful. He could not specify what he wanted for a project. He drafted us for the group project, making some feel less. He is so particular. As someone with OCD, this drove me insane; I spent more time on projects than I should've. I changed my major after. Run.

I really liked Professor Edwards and his class. It was my first studio class in college and I found him to be a great introduction. I have accommodations and he was helpful/understanding of my needs in his class. If you ask questions and be sure to look at Canvas, it is not a bad class, but if you don't put in the effort you won't do well.

The man could not articulate what he wants to save his life. His lectures and studio classes are full of buzzwords and yammering but nothing of substance. He grades harshly with zero feedback after giving little to no instruction. Avoid for 102.

Nathan is a very interesting instructor. I took a drawing level 1 course with him as the instructor and I have zero experience in drawing. He only really helps those that are already excelling in the course but if you are falling behind he will not treat you with respect and will intentionally ignore you and your attempts to reach out for help

Nathan is a great professor, he is very clear with his grading and instructions. If you put in the work and ask questions while you are working on projects you will get a good grade. He is very understanding and will work with you on deadlines. He is also the professor for the Friday lectures which is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable. He gives good feedback and supports all of your ideas or gives you ideas to improve. He is very flexible and understanding. He is an awesome professor and he isn't very strict with deadlines. He is also the professor for the Friday Lecture which is very helpful.

DSN S 102 is a great class. It pushes you outside of your comfort zone (in a good way). Nathan understands this and makes sure you go through the entire design process. He is very knowledgeable and helpful if you're stuck without telling you the answer but instead pushing you in the right direction. He is a great professor and loves what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nathan was a good professor and was very helpful in critiques. He is very flexible with projects and if you put in the effort you will receive a good grade. Highly recommend for 102 Studio
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Edwards would be the kind of person to come on here and look at his reviews, haha. He is fun-loving, creative, and a talented artist. I hope I can have classes with him in the future.

I really enjoyed having Nathan as a professor. He really pushed me to think broader and he is an amazing critiquer. I thought he was pretty funny and he gets really passionate about what he is talking about. One thing to note is that he does not give as much time in class time to work on assignments as other 102 professors.

I has Nathan for my Core Year 102 and overall liked him. He's a little odd, which is great, because it pushes the boundaries on what you thought you were capable of doing. Expect to collage frequently... He loves it. His technique and way of teaching has really helped me now that I'm in the Architecture professional program.

He's a nice guy, but as someone else said he's not great at clarifying or articulating what he wants and expects from you. Bad at responding to e-mails also. To make matters worse we didn't get grades for our first project until the day our third (of 4) was due.  Seems to want you to do things the way he does them, which is a specific taste.

As a first year design instructor his job is to push you to think deeper & look farther for inspiration. When you get his opinion it's always going to be with the intent to push you farther; that's what design is about. If you want a pat on the back every day, that's not how it works. Work hard & push your own boundaries and you'll do great.

Nathan (like all the Design Core instructors) is there to push students out of their comfort zone. He is always trying to get you to look past your own self imposed limits on things. It can be frustration at times but you can't get better if you don't push yourself.

Honestly the worst experience having him as a design instructor as a freshman. Has no sense of clarity and constantly takes your ideas and reforms them into his instead of helping you build and develop your own. He rarely give in class work days and is not responsible enough to arrange for professional critiquers.
This professor does not know how to teach or speak. I counted 55 "um"s in less than 5 minutes..

Ruki is the worst design professor I have ever had. Her attendence policy is lax as she seems to take it less seriously than the students, cancelling or moving class online with very little warning for a 7:45 studio. The projects are underexplained, overcomplicated, and restrictive. She took every step not to accomodate my disabilities. Run.

Everyone complained there wasnt enough time given for the capstone project but the first few projects were super helpful is helping me find a direction for my project and presenting myself more confidently. At the Senior Show my classmates had actual purposeful design projects. She also helped me find an internship.
Alumni of the program with deep design expertise. Not what you expect but very industry oriented. Excellent guest speakers. Expects lots of research and sketches. Very helpful during office hours.

Ruki has been the worst design professor I've had. She does not give clear guidelines for assignments online or in person, yet has high expectations. Does not teach you how to use new programs. Does not provide feedback or look over your progress work. She doesn't grade assignments until the end of the semester. Does not reply to emails.

Only gave us six weeks to work on our capstone projects which is dumb because all other sections had 9-12 weeks for theirs. Most of the assignments we had for the first half of the semester were weird and felt like busy work. Very unclear instructions. Only good thing is she graded very easily so far (for me, anyway). Just wish we had more time.

Gave us a lot of assignments at the beginning of the semester that didn't have anything to do with the class, and only gave us 6 weeks for our capstone projects when it is a CAPSTONE CLASS. No rubrics, vague instructions, no critiques, and grading took awhile. Never felt like going to class was helpful or worth my time.

While Ruki is a nice person, this class was awful. She never gave feedback; when she did, it was contradicted by the next student she talked to. She would either talk for an hour during class about nonsense or not speak one word. There is no rubric, and she grades very harsh; also at the very end of the year! However, attendance isn't mandatory.

Not super clear on guidelines and criteria for projects, no rubric or detailed outline. Attendance is not taken but she mainly communicates in class so you don't want to miss it. She has high expectations for a sophomore level class, but gives feedback and checks in. Hard to know what she expects and how to execute things.

The class itself was fine, but the professor gave off the impression that he couldn't be bothered to do his own job; a TA taught the vast majority of the lectures. The professor was also not very organized; on at least three occasions the autograder would incorrectly mark off points on assigments that should receive full credit.

Aer-290A is listed as online class. So my assumption was it was an online class. Instructor decided a last minute in person meeting date and time several times. Nelson is extremely arrogant and condescending. He takes forever to respond to emails. Sending in person meeting announcement a night before is extremely unprofessional & unorganized.

Labs were challenging but doable. Upon completion of these, I usually felt satisfied because I could picture myself doing similar tasks in an actual Aerospace Engineering Job. Lectures at times weren't incredibly helpful, but the assignments and overall layout of the course was very good.

The homeworks for this class were so incredibly long. Between completing the code, uploading it, and completing the LaTeX reports it just always felt like it took 10 hours just to get something so simple done and submitted. I will say that this class really tought me a skill, and Nelson is a great resource. Just wish he would reduce the work load
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: All of your grade is the homework/lab, which makes sense for coding classes. Nelson did a good job introducing and explaining concepts, but has horrible responses to students. Takes him forever to get back to students and is often unhelpful when he finally does.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 361 is probably the worst class of all time. Its coding in C and I'm pretty sure ill never use it so long as I have a career in Aerospace. The labs take forever to complete, but none of this means Nelson is a bad prof. I had him for 161 and 361 and he was always willing to help or to clarify concerns. He's a fair guy, but read the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had him for a section of my aero 160 class and the entirety of this semesters aero 161 class. The lack of planning in this class is awful. Our "syllabus" outlining the semester schedule is "updated" each week to seeming include whatever we had thrust upon us that week, and we were blindsided in our Monday class that our second exam is in 3 days.

I had him as a teacher for m:2:i and it has been the most frustrating experience. They wont show you how to turn in the homework for the Forst half of the semester so you and your peers will be left floundering in a sea of unknowns. They seem to pull grades out of nowhere. The class itself is run unprofessionally and feels ad libed.

I took this class in 2024. Why are we paying her? Cancles class all the time. Unprepared. Lazy. Skips office hours. NEVER IN HER OFFICE. So arrogant about how important her research is all the time. If she thinks her research is so important and she should blow off us students she should stop teaching and get a job as just a research person.
Dr. Neppl is one of the best profs at ISU. She is so good at teaching and connects with students. You can tell she is passionate about her work and I would recommend her to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Neppl was kind and engaging in class. You could tell that she cared about making class worthwhile for the students. I will say that she is not very generous when it comes to extra help outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Neppl was amazing! Not only were her lectures super interesting, but she was amazing at conducting discussions. I was able to get away with not reading her textbook because I went to lectures, but you have to do at least one. She boosts grades off of participation too. There is also a textbook you have to use for group work. Workload was easy.
This professor is amazing. Yes, the class requires that you read the textbook but if you read, it becomes an easy A. Professor is willing to meet outside of class to go over any confusions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was delivered solely online and there were no lectures. We received pdf documents over each topic within the unit but they weren't helpful for the tough exams. There were only 4 exams, 40 points each. According to the canvas grade book not one person earned 40/40 on any of the exams. If it's online, I would wait to take it.
Thee best teacher at ISU. But her tests are hard and doesn't really follow the study guide. It's the take home messages that she bases her questions off of.

I cant say enough good things about Dr. N. Her lectures are engaging and powerful. She has a way of instilling passion in her students. Bring some Kleenex to the abuse and illness class because youre going to see and hear some real tearjerkers, but she does a great job of putting names and faces to statistics and moving students to action.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Neppl is by far my favorite professor here at ISU! She is passionate about her job, and it shows in her lectures. She did an AMAZING job teaching this course, and a learned a lot! I wanted to come to lectures and do homework. I would highly recommend this course and Dr. Neppl!

Dr. Neppl was THE MOST understanding/wonderful professor I had at ISU. Not only is she an amazing teacher who truly cares about her subject material, she truly cares about her students. I was going through a lot while I was taking her class, and she was beyond understanding. She's the only reason I got through that semester. Take her class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Neppl. I think she makes her lectures very interesting. She is a tough grader, but she is very helpful and understanding. She gives up random participation points, so it is important to go to class. She also doesn't put her lectures online, so going to class is essential for getting the notes.
can't understand a word he says. might as well be up there speaking another language.
Even his answers to some class quizzes are wrong, ugh.

I'm an ACCT major and not all that familiar with MIS but he went slow and made sure the material made sense. If you put in effort for your grade, he'll do the same. Little hard to understand time to time but wasn't bad.

As others have stated, really hard to learn Java language from this professor. Work at it, maybe find some friends who can help you understand what is being taught. A breeze if you have experience with Java.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. This should be a relatively easy class. However,he teaches this class in a way where he assumes students already understand the a basic terminology and functions of Java. He is a very boring speaker, doesn't update the grade book until the very end of the semester, and rarely tells you when homework is due.

If you haven't had experience with programming Java before, get ready for a tough class if you have Professor Ngwenya. He uses a lot of vocab that is specific to the class but never ties in how it is relevant to what you are learning or why it even matters. Java programming isn't hard to learn, just don't learn it from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had. Doesn't teach anything and the things he talks about have no relation to the homework and content on the exams. You will have to teach yourself the whole class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are in class assignment everyday so you have to go to class but when you are there he does not teach you anything. He rambles about programming techniques that do not apply to what we should be learning about. The class should be taught as someone having zero programming experience and he does not do this. Had to teach everything to myself.

I found her to be disrespectful and set in her own ways. She thinks that her way is always right and really doesn't listen to her students. I don't think she is a good teacher, when we asked her to clarify things, she only made us more confused. Her instructions and expectations are misleading and confusing. I did not feel valued in her class.

Nice as a person, but not an effective teacher. She gave very mixed signals as to what she wanted from us. Class could have been very interesting but she just uses a powerpoint and talks off of that. The extra credit was the only thing that helped me, but we had to beg her for it all the time. The book is helpful, but I learned more from youtube.

Welp, mixed emotions about Phuong. Nice lady, terrible at teaching. English isn't her first language so she isn't the easiest to understand. She have quite a bit of extra credit which was the only thing that kept my grade up in the class, especially being that I had to teach myself everything outside of class.
She is impossible to understand, and is the hardest paper grader I have ever had. Does not explain assignments at all. Avoid.

This instructor is difficult to understand, as she is originally from a different country. She is the hardest grader that I have ever had, and she says she is correct even when she is wrong. Her grading makes no sense and citation is nearly impossible to perfect with her.

Thanh (Tom but with an N) is a great teacher. He dives into great detail on as many aspects of a problem as he can while still maintaining relevancy to the course expectations and tests. To really make the most of any lecture, I recommend doing the homework for the previous lecture (or at least the one before that) as the next lecture usuallybuilds
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He does a lot of examples with clear steps, as long as you can follow along, there's no problem. The homework helps a lot and is pretty identical to the test. So just find the hardest problem on the homework and that'll most likely be on the test. There's just a lot of equations to memorize. I only really needed the book to do the practice problems

Dr. Nguyen did an awesome job instructing this class and made it fairly easy. No surprises on exams, and he actually gives specific problems from the book that he will base the exam and quiz questions off of, so if you do those, the exams are really easy. Take it with him if you can, I understand everything from the class and my GPA got a boost.

Thanh is a great professor. He extremely caring about his students and their success in the class. The lectures are completely optional, except for pre-announced quiz days. They can be boring, but he goes over helpful examples. His quizzes and tests are straight from the book, making them straight forward.  Successful and easy class with Thanh!

Diff Eq was surprisingly easy with Dr. Nguyen.  His lectures can be boring and pointless at times but overall he does a good job of covering the concepts, the best part is that his quizzes and exams are just like the homework and pretty easy. He is also very helpful if you're struggling

I loved this class. Dr. Nguyen does a pretty job of explaining concepts in lecture and doing problems very similar to the homework. The tests and quizzes were exactly like the homework and the examples he did in class so this class was pretty easy.

Dr. Nguyen is so nice and you can tell he really cares about students.  DiffEq is a tough class, but the problems he puts on quizzes/tests are all fairly straightforward - you're not gonna get something unexpected.
Take differential equations with anyone but him.

I bought the textbook only for the access code. You have to go to class because there are a lot of clicker questions. If you took calculus in high school this class is a cakewalk, if not it is difficult.

HATED, HATED, this class. This guy is pretentious and thinks he can teach better than anyone and will not take suggestions on fixing his teaching styles. Do not take this class as he is an awful Teacher who expects too much from his students who he doesn't teach enough. You're better off learning from a book or online yourself.

Thanh is a nice guy and this class isn't incredibly hard but his teaching kind of sucks at times.  Instead of teaching step by step how to do a problem, he just quickly tells you how to do it once and then has you answer multiple clicker questions about it. If you want to actually LEARN how to do the problem, it is best to just read the textbook.

Skip this class with him if you can. Really bad at teaching and messes up frequently during lecture "demonstrating" the answers. However, he continues to test us on stuff we haven't learned and the practice exams usually differ drastically from the real test unlike he says. Skip this class!

The overall structure of this course is very poor but I feel that is just how the math department runs at Iowa State. Attendance is necessary because you have a weekly quiz in recitation and clicker points for every class lecture. The homework is the most time consuming thing. Overall, the professor explains things pretty well during lecture.

Dr. Nguyen is a very caring instructor who wants you to do well. His accent takes a little to get used to but really isn't a problem at all. Very nice man who makes himself very available to help you. Tough class, but he's a good one to take it with. Knows his stuff.

Thanh is a very kind and intelligent man who wants you to do well. He has an accent which can be hard to understand but what he lacks in clarity there he far makes up for in explaining things and what he expects you to do. Easy grader and will crack a few jokes, also gives some extra credit. Not an easy class but he does what he can. Recommended

Tough class. Starts out easy but gets really abstract and unclear after the first month. If you fall behind at all you're screwed. I think I got 60% or less on every test (around class average), but curved up to a B-. So just try to stay above the curve, cause he curve average to a B-.
If you have no previous calculus knowledge, this is not the class for you. He is super nice and an easy grader, but his accent can make it very hard to learn. There are better professors on campus.
Thanh is very kind, but his accent definitely takes some getting used to. What he says can sometimes be difficult to understand but it's doable. Gives extra credit quite a bit.
Super easy class. Literally just 1 homework assignment a week that sometimes only took 30 mins. He is very helpful and puts out a ton of videos. He will answer questions and is an easy grader.

Stuart is a great guy, he made the example videos for the homework very understanding and if you ever had a question about the homework, he made sure you got your answer. Loved this class even if Revit got a bit tricky to use at the end, and I wish he taught more classes here at Iowa State as he is a great engineer and knows his stuff.

I never got to meet him in-person, but I took CE 170 online with him and it was a decent experience. His grading standards were fair. There is one project a week that usually takes 3-4 hours and he posts videos online. As long as you watch the videos you should be fine. Overall a good experience and he seems like a good guy.

My class with him was online so I didn't get too talk to him much, but he is a really nice and funny professor. He uploaded videos explaining the material and they were always clear and helpful. Whenever I reached out to him through email he was prompt to respond and help out.

Pretty great guy who knows his stuff. His exams are pretty much copy-paste from the old exams. The only negative thing is that he works at the DOT so this is not his main job so he can run behind on entering grades. Other than that hes awesome and I wish he taught more classes. Don't buy a book and he makes this class an easy A.

He is a bridge engineer with the DOT and he's from an engineering family so he knows what he's talking about.  He doesn't give much homework and the exams are easy if you use the study guides he posts.  He allows cheat sheets for the exams.

Lectures bounce around, slides are not organized at all. There is very little clear information to take notes from, things appear on the exam that were covered in a singular picture on the slides. Plays kahoot after every lecture, top 5 get extra credit. He is a really nice guy, just difficult to learn from. Chat GPT explained the concepts better.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super smart and sweet guy. We were scheduled for MWF but fridays were optional if you needed to catch up. He's very forgiving if you mess up or forget an assignment and overall his class is very fun!

Peters is an okay professor. His voice is rough to listen to, but you get used to it. Go to class because you can get extra credit if you do well in the kahoot at the end of class and he sometimes gives extra credit if you just show up. The exams are a little rough, but use the study guides, kahoots, and jeopardy slides to study and you'll be fine.

Dr Peters is the sweetest. You can tell he truly cares about his students and their success. His exams are hard and sometimes much more complex than lecture content, but he tends to provide a lot of extra credit for showing up and participating in Kahoots. It'll be a tough course, but he's so nice!

Peters is a nice guy but not a very good teacher. He seems to expect students to know what he's about to teach before he teaches it. The only things in the grade book are 4 exams, and 4 quizzes, so if you do poorly on something, it's hard to come back from. He does offer EC Kahoots and occasional attendance EC, so look at lectures ahead of class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Peters seems like a nice guy but learning micro from him was very hard. The class is graded by very few things and the tests were really hard. If you go to lecture he will randomly give extra credit which was nice and he did curve the class at the end. But if you have to curve, how well did you teach the material in the first place?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really good professor and does well explaining topics and encourages students to ask questions. The only part of the course I didn't like was you're only graded on exams. So if you do bad on one your grade tanks. He did give extra credit at the end of the course which was nice.

His class is set up to your only grade is what you get on you exams and quizzes. His exams are tough and his questions on his exams are very confusing. He only gives extra credit to those who make it on the top 5 of kahoots.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this professor. I just hated going to the testing center for exams. Also, the exams are not at all like the study guides he sends out, so don't waste your time memorizing answers. He is a cool guy, and the final was not cumulative, which was very nice.

Talks so fast that when I am taking notes I have to erase it because it doesnt make sense.On the next slide before I even can write down a sentence. The homework videos are pointless if you can only watch them once and disappear after the due date. So much information in so little time. Definitely needs a change in the curriculum.

Good professor. Lectures are mandatory unless someone sends you the code for class survey. Wish there were more points opportunities because I am not a good exam taker but had 100% on surveys, homework, and quizzes. Still a great prof, would take again.

Nick was amazing but his tests were hard. You had to go to class because he did class surveys for 5 points. Lectures were interesting if you actually like microbio. I was having a tough semester and Nick was willing to work with me which eased a lot of stress.
He seems pretty caring. Offers quite a bit of extra credit. The tests are hard because of tricks like all of the above, none of the above, and true/false questions where false comes first.

ONE OF THE BEST TEACHERS IN MICRO!! Dr. Peters is so kind and caring. He just wants his students to learn. I have also heard that he is great in his plant path classes. He is so easy to talk to and will always answer your questions. Amazing teacher!

An awesome professor for this class! I took this class over the summer, and he structured it in a way where it felt very self-paced with taking notes for each exam and did not feel overwhelming. He gives a LOT of materials to study with including a Kahoot, Jeopardy, and a pre-made notesheet covering the basics material for each exam.

I really liked this professor! He is easygoing and has very clear expectations. If you review the material and watch the lectures, you will do fine on the tophat, quizzes, and exams. I felt that he cared about the success of his students as he always sent out weekly "to do" lists and made sure we understood the concepts. Great teacher!

Professor Peters is very passionate about microbiology and he shares that with the students. He hosts review sessions, explains topics, and answers insightful questions. Be prepared to use TopHat and study for exams, sometimes they can be difficult but if you study well and take notes you'll be good! He's one of my favorite professors I've had.
Dr. Peters is an awesome professor. Absolutely clear expectations and really goes the extra mile for students to learn and succeed. Definitely top 5 of professors I've had at ISU.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is the best professor for this class! He is very nice and listens to students about what they are finding hard about the unit. His exams and quizzes are straight forward and he always makes a kahoot to study from! He does tophat after every lecture but always gives us the answer before the time runs out. He is a great professor!

Genuine, intelligent guy! Tophat for credit, gives answers during lecture so should go but no attendance. Tests are average/hard but if you study the study guide and his notes you will do well. Class is interesting and he makes it as simple as he can. He wants everyone to pass so he's very nice with the grading scale. One of my fav professors
He is so knowledgeable in microbiology, he sometimes forgets it. Ask him many questions and he will explain it to you, but you will have to ask! Great guy to talk to! Go to class for tophat.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Peters is really good overall, though for a 200 level class it's a bit too much and hard. He did a pretty decent job explaining tougher topics, and reiterating important points. He reviews topics at the beginning of each lecture that students want to go over again. TopHat is used, and get half a point for just answering the question.
This class is WAY too hard for two credits

Overall, he's a super cool person. The first professor I've met that teaches a science that is actually normal, married, and has a life outside of his research. He did a good job making the complex information simpler. He makes great use of Top Hat. Overall, he did a really good job.

Nicks pretty chill, he cares about this topic and wants you to know the big picture ideas. exams 2 and 3 aren't the greatest but just hang in there. The quizzes are pretty easy and you should do them with a study group to make it easier on yourself. Overall, this class wasn't too bad and was kinda interesting learning about the infections and such.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a monotone voice. Lectures are very boring but Top Hat points are very important. You NEED the extra credit by the end of the semester to save your grade. Class is only 2 credits but if more like a 4 credit course difficulty. Way too complicated material. Exams are very difficult. Shoot for 100% on quizzes. DONT forget to do them.
Very good teacher. I hate school and he made his class not that bad to attend. Very nice guy.

Go to class so you can get the extra credit for getting above 90% in Tophat. Usually gives the answers to the tophats as well. Very passionate and smart about what he's teaching. Although, his is monotone and easy to tune out. Go to the review sessions and really memorize the slides, everything on the exam will be taken from the slides.

Apparently, he used to teach at Harvard Med. Not sure what in the world he did to end up at Iowa State, but regardless I am feeling very blessed to have him. I could listen to his soft voice talk about bacterial infections for days. Insider tip: if you ask him about his pet lobster, he'll give you extra credit. A real gem.

Dr. Peters was a phenomenal teacher. His grading criteria was clear cut without any confusion. He did not have the standard curse of knowledge that plagues so many teachers. No matter how complex or simple material was, he would always find a way to make it simpler. Truly a hidden gem of a teacher.
