He has this over ego personality.
Great teacher who is very personable. Gives great advice and really pushes you to do your best. You will get as much out of the class as you put in.
He's very passionate about graphic design but definitely has fun with it. He does hold high expectations, but only to make you a better designer. Very cool, personable guy.

Julian is hilarious. Is from Columbia and has an accent but is very friendly and understandable. I believe this is his first year teaching, but he is very savvy with both technology and design, and can help you with almost anything. My favorite instructor this semester.
Hes a great professor. Just go to class. Dont be a lazy person.

Terrible professor who does not teach what the tests will be over. Classes are pointless but you still need to go because of pop quizzes. His lectures are super boring and goes off on weird tangents. Average test grades were all below 60%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Bartolotti  is obviously very passionate about what he teaches. Has an accent that takes a few classes to get used to. Be prepared for a quiz every other class. Tests are difficult and he makes it known the first day of class that most people will fail the first midterm and want to drop. Hw and quizzes balance this out and boost final grade a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors that I've had! He knows what he is talking about and knows how to give examples with simplify the concept and makes it more intuitive. As long and you attend lectures and study well ahead of time for the test you will do fine. Anyone who does badly just didn't care enough to study hard enough for the tests.
Professor Bartolotti is great! He really cares about students and wants you to do well. He is one of my favorite professors at ISU!

Worst teacher I have ever had. Every test average was below a 55% , but won't tell you what the curve is until grades are due at end of semester. Goes on rants about European schooling, does not answer questions in class, pop quizzes given often. In class slides barely help with homework. DO NOT GET HIM AS A PROFESSOR.

He is hard to understand and fixes his mistakes on questions during the test. His test scores are low and below 55% average. The tests are nearly impossible to score well on. It is confusing to know what grade you have until the end of the semester. I would not recommend if you want higher than a C in the class.
Very hard to understand he goes of on his "tangents" and likes to talk about things that are not relevant to the class material and then tries to cram lectures before exams.

Dr. Bartalotti is a great professor. In my experience, those who have trouble in his class just don't care about the material. However, don't expect to get an easy A as you have to study pretty hard for his exams, but, if you know the material they are very simple.

Otavio is a great guy who really cares about his students. He is always willing to help. The only problem is, he is way too smart to be teaching an introduction class. His tests are nearly impossible, the average was below 60 percent on both midterms and the final. He doesn't give a grading scale so he can adjust them at the end of the semester.

Ruined my GPA. Don't take him for econ 102. his tests are impossible. Average for first test was a 55%, second was a 60, and a 48% for the final. I barely got a B- in this class. Every other professor would be easier. lectures are pointless to go to
This is by far the best professor I have ever had in my life. Tests are incredibly easy and completely like the homework assignments. Drop the mic because this guy is real.
This is by far the worst professor I have ever had in my life. Tests are incredibly hard and nothing like the homework assignments. Drop immediately unless you are up for the challenge.
Interesting character with endless stories which make class exciting. Gives you great feedback on your papers and presents topics and material that are relevant to your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The majority of students in my class hated him, but I thought he was wonderful because we have very similar interests.  Reasons why other students hated him: The class is extremely boring, but easy. The college requires him to grade on a bell curve, so many students received C's, but you can revise assignments to get one grade letter higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Highly recommend. Very sweet teacher that is willing to help you with any questions you may have

Francis was a great professor. He is so passionate about what he is teaching about and it is obvious. Attending class is extremely important due to random attendance points. There is one partner project. The best advice I can give for that is to NOT wait until the last second. Getting it done early is important.

He is exceptional to work with. His knowledge of planning is great given his vast experience, teaching method, and commitment to students. He is one of the best met. I would describe him as a transformational leader, having worked with him closely. He is a great resource to mankind.

Francis is super passionate about the class content and gives really good lectures. He likes to include discussions and relate the material back to current events. He does give out several pop quizzes, so make sure to reread your notes before class. He also has a semester research project that you do with a partner, so find a friend in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was super easy, and if you put in one bit of effort you can easily get an A

Francis treats you like an adult, so long as you show him you are one.  This class is meant to ensure that when you graduate you are fluent in data analysis. His assignments take time but thoroughly teach you how to use computer programs and websites to gather, organize, analyze and present data and information in a very professional manner.

This class (International Planning) is the primary reason Francis is still at Iowa State.  This subject excites him and he definitely shows it in class. I transfers that excitement to you and does a great job portraying both sides of all arguments.  He makes you critically analyze policies and forces you to learn. He treats you like a professional.

Good guy, good professor. Has expectations? Yes, but if you think he is too hard you should think again about being in college - he just expects you to read and learn and write like a grown up, not a high schooler. His accent is fine if you  pay attention. I thought he was fair and polite to students, and treated them professionally.

Yes, he is hard, and he has a thick accent, but you will learn more then you could have imagined in this class. If you have a problem understanding him (because of his accent), he will be happy to try again. He is hard because he wants us to learn, and if you put yourself into it, you will learn. The man is incredibly smart

Mediocre at best. Teaching consists of reading from powerpoints with a few stories in between. Grades extremely hard and is unable to properly explain why when confronted. Never hears anything to the contrary. He is extremely Afrocentric and will pay special attention and grant favors to Black students and those from Africa. Avoid if possible.
He not the best teacher we have in CRP, but hes not bad.  He is very hard to understand, and grades very hard.

This class is supposed to be a sophmore level class,  yeah right.  As a senior, it was one of the worst that I have ever taken.  He puts his notes on his website, which is a good thing because when he gets going there is no way to understand him.  Grades very hard, just not a good class or teacher.
Best teacher we have

ISU is really missing a great guy. He seems intimidating at first, but once you meet him on a personal level, he's a really great guy. He's not going to be the easiest professor to take, but that's because he wants you to learn the resources he teaches. By far, my favorite professor at ISU. He's a 10/10 guy and I would take him whenever possible.

Overstreet is the man. While the class was hard for myself personally I realized I wasn't utilizing my resources. After meeting with him for his office hours, doing the practice quizzes, and having him go over practice quizzes I felt much more prepared. Don't be afraid to go to his office hours and make sure to attend every class if possible.

Overstreet is a phenomenal professor. Truly cares about his students and wants to ensure they learn rather than pounding endless amounts of redundant information into our heads. He is strict but it helps set the tone for the class. He makes this class as simple as possible and is always open for questions without being condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at ISU.

Professor Overstreet is by far the best professor I have had at Iowa State. He may seem tough and strict at first, but as you pass through the semester, you will see he is only looking out for his student's best interests. He provides everything you need to succeed, but you have to put in the work. USE HIS OFFICE HOURS. Especially for the projects.

Professor Overstreet can sound tough at first but took the time to connect with his students and ensure a conducive learning environment. There are designated office hours and he offers practice homework to study. He also gives all the information to attain your Lean Six Sigma Green belt at a discount. He was my favorite professor at Iowa State.

Professor Overstreet has been one of my favorite professors at Iowa State. I took SCM 301 and wanted to take his SCM 424 class. Professor Overstreet makes students want to come each day because he can make lectures fluid and understandable. If you are a supply chain major take Professor Overstreets classes.

Had for SCM301. Favorite professor at ISU, but you have to put in the work. He doesn't allow slacking off. He seems really strict at first, but he's trying to help. He prepares you for what I think the real world is like. Lectures are amazing, makes everything relatable, understands and gets to know everyone. I went to his office hours just to talk

While Professor Overstreet was my toughest professor at ISU, he was also one of my favorites. He has a great passion for learning and wants each student to succeed equally. I did not enjoy my time at first in his class, but that eventually changed once I attended his office hours, which I highly recommend. Plus, he always used real-world examples.

Professor Overstreet was fantastic for SCM 424. He may come off as mean and scary due to his military background and persona. Getting to know him-- he is very knowledgable and wants you to do the best you can in his course. He is always available to talk to if you have problems with homework or group projects, and responds to emails very quickly.
As a senior at Iowa State I would confidently say that Professor Overstreet is the best professor that I have had at Iowa State University.

Difficult with a large workload. 450 was the only SCM class more difficult than this for me. Dr. Overstreet is a practical and real-world professor. Highly recommended for any SCM major.
Helped in securing an internship in CI. Do not underestimate the value this class can provide, especially since it is easy to get a Green Belt in Lean Six Sigma.

Professor Overstreet is probably the best professor I've had so far at ISU. The class is not necessarily easy, but expectations for assignments, attendance, etc are clear and straight forward. There weren't surprises on exams. The content is taught in a manageable way, and he is more than willing to help students if you go to office hours.

Prof. Overstreet is one of my favorite professors i've had at ISU. He gives amazing feedback and is always glad to answer student questions. Super encouraging and great at explaining difficult concepts in an accessible manner. Just show up on time and put some effort in as this class and is super worthwhile. He just wants to see you succeed.

Best professor Ive had! Was really nervous after the 1st class about him being too difficult, but he turned out to be my favorite! Really good at explaining material if you actually listen and super helpful outside of class (emails, office visits). This class is known to be hard, but if you study you wiIl get an A. I wish he taught more classes!!
Best Professor I've had so far in the supply chain department. I wish he taught more courses than he does so I could have him as a professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Overstreet was my favorite professor of all college. He helps you understand the criteria and prepares you for the work-world. Although this is arguably the toughest supply chain course, he teaches it in a way that helps you understand it, and he is definitely willing to give extra help. He is a phenomenal professor for this subject.

Professor Overstreet truly cares about his class and his students. This class is really hard, but he has set up the grading system in such a way that students can succeed if they try. He is always happy to help if you reach out to him, and he takes the time to get to know his students. The group projects were the hardest part of this class for me.

Professor Overstreet is easily one of my favorite professors in the supply chain major. I highly recommend taking this class with him if your schedule allows. Professor Overstreet cares about each of one his students and makes the hard class, enjoyable. He pushes students, helps students, and has a passion for what he does. Outstanding professor.

Professor Overstreet was easily the best professor I have ever had. He really pushes you to not just understand his class but care about it as well. I would 100% recommend taking 424 with him. If you're reading just the bad reviews, he takes in all of the recommendations that people give and has changed his teaching to benefit students.

Professor Overstreet is an amazing professor! He values the success of his students and takes our feedback to heart. The class is well structured and he even STOMPS to emphasize important material. Some tips to pass- 1) go to class 2)talk to him 3)study and do in-class assignments

Dr. Overstreet is the most quality teacher I have ever had. He cares very much about the success of his students. He makes himself very available to his students for help and is extremely knowledgeable on what he teaches. This class can be difficult and if you're lazy you'll get a lousy grade. Pay attention to his foot stomps, they're test Q's

Didn't enjoy this class at all. Didn't really get the knowledge the prof tries to deliver in class. Would prefer it if the prof writes out the formulas & answers for the questions he's discussing. He's a group prof, but often times, I didn't understand the materials he's trying to teach, which makes it a really tough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I have ever had at Iowa State. The class is tough, but he does his best to make sure you understand and succeed in it. You can't slack off in this class, if you put in the effort and he knows it, then you will be doing fine. 100% recommend taking this class with Dr. Overstreet.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overstreet was a great professor, tough class but he makes the class worth taking with valuable information that will be used later in life. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: BEST PROF AT ISU!!! 424 is decently hard, but he genuinely wants you to do well. Attendance is mandatory, but if you go to class you will do well. Ask questions and go to his office hours and you will do fine in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Overstreet is by far my favorite SCM professor. He's so awesome. He really understands the materials and wants you to do well. If you're struggling, go to his office hours! This class is decently hard and the tests are hard. But if you go to class and study and do well on assignments, you should be fine. TAKE 424 WITH HIM!! Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Rob was great, 424 is a tough class but he was very clear about his expectations for his students and he was very helpful when answering questions. The class itself was an even mix of homework, projects, and tests. You don't need a book but you will have to go to class if you want to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: SCM 424 is easily the most difficult supply chain class at Iowa State, but Overstreet goes out of his way to help you with it. The class is heavy on in class work, group projects, and tests that are both in class and take home. You have to put in the work but if you meet with him and ask for help, youll do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Coming into this class, it is one of the toughest business classes at Iowa State. Taking it with Professor Overstreet was one of the best decisions over other options. He is very good about making sure students understand what he is teaching. He takes attendance everyday so show up and participate. The tests are hard but ask questions beforehand.

I recommend taking SCM 424 with Overstreet instead of Danny Johnson. Overstreet has shown he is empathetic toward his students by understanding scm424 is one of the hardest scm classes to take. He will take the exams to get a better understanding what is on it and then share a study guide based on what topic is on the exam before students take it.

Mr. Kolstad is very helpful outside of classes and is very willing to help you with homework problems and is liberal with extensions if he sees you're working through things. it doesn't seem like he is very knowledgeable with Solidworks however he encourages you to poke around and learn for yourself. lectures are very useful and on the point for HW
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't think Kolstad knows Solidworks very well. He doesn't teach it, period. He can't even point you toward good resources for learning it. He has time in industry, but he didn't come across as super knowledgeable engineer. He struggled teaching basics like GD&T - maybe a reflection of bad teaching rather than a lack of knowledge

Great guy, worked in industry for a while so he knows what he is talking about. Gives great feedback to groups and is willing to work with you. He was a realistic professor and graded fairly. Great choice for Capstone.

Professor Kolstad is awesome! He is extremely helpful and if he doesn't know the answer to a question he will help find you someone who does. He cares a lot about his students, especially if they are putting forth a good effort. I would highly recommend taking this class with him!

Mr. Kolstad was awesome. He's really knowledgeable from his past experience at CAT, he will let you repeatedly know he worked at CAT. He is super nice and easy to get outside of class. He will make everything as easy as possible for you and help you out as much as possible. TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU CAN!
Really caring teacher, best professor I have had here

I really liked Mr. Kolstad. There were times when he was confusing with assignments or didn't understand how to use things on Solidworks, but he was very helpful and accessible by email all the time. He is very caring and gets to know his students. I'd highly recommend him for 170. Class wasn't terribly hard either.
He is fine, not clear enough with SolidWorks and lets you discover it by yourself. However, I think its the best thing to do with SolidWorks is to discover it by yourself.
He is a very helpful professor. If you show up to class, make a good effort, and meet all of your deadlines, you won't have any problems. I learned a ton from him.

Owen is a great professor! The class itself takes a lot of time outside of scheduled lab time, so be prepared to work. If you have any issues,  he is  down to earth and very easy to approach. He also has a lot of experience outside of academia. He worked for John Deere, Oshkosh, and Cat.  If you get him, you are lucky!

Kolstad is a professional engineer with incredible experience who decided to teach after a long career. Luckily, he did. He really encouraged team building among groups and becoming a better public speaker in order to convey your ideas. Overall, a very nice guy who you can tell enjoys sharing his experience and teaching a class. Ask questions!
Loved it! He is extremely intelligent and challenges you to think

His effort was not wasted on me.  I get it.  He's an amazing brain.  I don't know how he can keep all that in his head and reiterate it again and again.  He uses the dialectic to teach, which is very uncommon in the modern academic setting.  It is a lost art.  I wish he hadn't stopped talking to me when I started having trouble with the university.
awful, horrible class. it was boring and stupid and he had a huge god complex. he talked in circles and never made any sense.
Hard to Understand

Owen is an interesting guy.  Knows alot and very opinionated- tries to convince students -not- to teach.  Class was almost always discussion-based. Students were graded on two 5 page papers, a group presentation of a book, and a book report of it. Attendance is not taken.  A HUGE number of books/coursepacks are technically required.  Reccomended.
Owen is a great guy, very smart and with a lot of insight into the future of American education.  Assignments (all 4 of them) are easy, do the reading and come to class and you're good to go.
This class is awesome.  The teacher is so nice and all we do is discuss readings and other stuff that we are interested in.

His class is good. He makes you think but you only have four assignments. The rest is a lot of reading. Sometimes the discussions are a little confusing, but Prof. Owen is a nice guy so don't be afraid to ask if you need help or have questions.
No Comments

I LOVED this class. The material is difficult but if you work, whole worlds open And Dr.Owen is a wonderful teacher who loves the material and who makes you love it too. Some people probably would hate this class with him because it (gasp) really makes you think, but if you want to learn and grow, this is the class and the instructor for you.
Some things I liked, some things I didn't. Over all was good. He is kinda crazy, but he means well and I like that.

Those who rate this prfessor poorly don't understand what he is trying to get you to do.  He never really answers anything but insteads strives for YOU to answer it.  he wants the student to form their own opinions about a topic instead of forcing his on to the class.  If you take the time to listen to what he says you'll get a lot from this class.

This guy is crazy.  He is very opinionated and talks about many things that make no sense.  He tries to make points that in the end have no point.  He talks about Chicago like it is the best place on earth, and apparently living here means that we suck.  Anyway, I really don't enjoy his class.

This teacher is odd. He is very opinionated. His class is very very boring and its easy to just not go. I would recommend going about 1/2 the times tho because he almost grades you on your attendance, he won't learn your name, he just has a paper with everyones picture. DON'T HAVE TOO MUCH FUN!

This is the easiest class in the world.  I never went to class, never read or even purchased half of the books and still came out of the class with an A.   All you have to do to pass the class is read cliff notes on the books (which can be hard to find) and make sure you understand the "main point".

Prof. Owen is very knowledgable, helpful and irritating at times. His classes either force you to shake your head and wonder what the hell or you shake your head and wonder WHY the hell. Although he may seem to have an agenda, at times, what prof doesn't?

I loved this class and I love Prof Owen. He's a cool dude and, yes, he goes on tangents for awhile, but who doesn't. He REALLY cares about people. Also, on the ease of the class- I hardly went, barely read anything and have a SOLID A.

In my opinion, he doesn't have a good grasp on reality.  He told my class to go a head and let our kids try extasy or herion if they wish.  I am liberal, but he is just crazy.  Also there are 9 books for this class, other teachers use one.  Major expense.

I really enjoyed this course.  It was challenging because he forced you beyond the correct answer.  You have to put thought into it and develop your own ideas.  It's really helpful and I think he's a great teacher.
Horrible class.. boring, lots of reading, prof is unclear.  He's a cool guy and genuinely tries to do his best, but for some reason, falls short.  Several papers and a group project.
No Comments

I thought Prof. Owen was an outstanding individual.  Yes, the course is challenging, but that is only because he forces you to think.  You can't just skim the reading assignments and expect to pass.  You must engage in the reading and open your mind.
Man acted like he was a god; if you weren't his favorite, you were nobody

She would cancel 2 minutes before class started. We were lucky when she canceled 20 minutes before, but I had to walk 20 minutes. Iowa is cold. She was absent an alarming amount too. She used medical excuses, but if you're having medical issues, you can cancel class ahead of time. I felt she did not respect our learning. Waste of 1000 + dollars

Decent lectures, copied from the textbook. She's knowledgeable and responds quickly if you ask questions. She cares about her students. Misses class frequently with less than 30 minutes notice (one day shy of 3 weeks missed this semester). Does upload lecture videos to cover missed classes but may be days later. Nice person, but tough to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class asynchronous over the summer, there were recorded lectures every few days and take home exams every week for six weeks, not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Really a fantastic professor. Understanding of the work she is giving, does not assign an unreasonable amount. Goes over material that will actually be on quizzes, tests, etc. Explains the processes and concepts as we work through them. It was easy to learn this way.

 
Show up to lecture, work through problems with her, and you will do very well.

Needs to learn what she is teaching, isn't very helpful when you have a question about your code and how to change it. Also rambles on about some topics that have already been discussed in detail and have been agreed on by the class that we understood.

She is a great professor and cares about her students and their learning. Very accessible outside of class and helpful in answering questions or concerns about the concepts. Made lectures fun by showing videos that help visual learners and walks through the problems so they are easily understood.

It felt like Professor Padalkar needed to learn what she was teaching. She could only help with code by looking at her example, which, if you did not do the same thing, she could not help. She also canceled 8 classes throughout the semester, most of them without reason, then tried to stuff four weeks' worth of material in two 2 weeks.
She cancelled class all the time and barely helped on assignments, just told to read notes and not helpful

She was a very mediocre teacher, she didn't know how to code very well which seems odd for a teacher teaching a coding class, the lectures didn't seem to connect to the assignments very well and she didn't offer much help if you had questions. She also canceled class 25% of the time with no heads up but would expect you to come to class every time.

She was pretty good. She cancelled class a good chunk of the time, but then since we didn't learn a lot of material, we were given take home tests/final, which we had a week to work on. She was fairly assessable and was always present during her office hours. I would recommend her if you don't have to take thermo 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She cancelled classes repeatedly without letting anyone know. We'd make the effort to show and she was a no-show. Doesn't take education seriously. Do Not Recommend.

Professor was off sick for nearly 3 weeks worth of classes across the semester when added up.
Material was added online however no real material was tought outside of copying examples in class.

A pretty mediocre professor overall, would have been a lot better if she actually taught us the Matlab principles we needed to finish our homework. Did a good job teaching the principles of physics, but the information we learned in class wasn't always applied well in assignments. Didn't always have the answers for questions when asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty bad professor. Reads off the slides for the entirety of lecture and grades only by homework and quizzes. Make sure you don't miss anything because you need a 95 to get an A in this class. The one saving grace is you get to make a 'cheat sheet' for quizzes-- but there's so much content to write down and its unclear what will be tested over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst prof I've had at ISU. She consistently makes mistakes and doesn't seem to understand the material.  Her quizzes are just at test of how well you can write her slides down on your crib sheet. Class consisted of her reading her slides verbatim. Cancelled class multiple times with very little notice and was late for the final.  Awful professor.

Professor Padalkar did a good job lecturing and homeworks covered the material well. However, her tests were more about what you were able to write down on your note sheet than what you knew in the class. She would choose obscure diagrams you had to draw and label. She does not take feedback or criticism well and gets quite defensive.

Cancelled class frequently, read off slides in class. This thermo is so different than the other sections, I feel like I won't be prepared for thermo 2. Didn't round up my 89.96% after she canceled class half the time.

I think Dr. Padalkar may have been going through something personal this semester, but fair warning regardless: she cancelled class 5+ times, took forever to grade anything, little to no feedback on HW, was rude and condescending to stdnts in class. Tests are far too long for the time allotted; so, learn to work fast. Grading scale is very generous
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easily the least organized, helpful or caring professor I've ever had in my years at ISU. She'd show up to class late, move homework back 2 weeks or more because she hadn't taught us the needed material yet, and showed no care in the world for her students. She even edited the syllabus grading criteria during finals week. Negatively. AWFUL TEACHER.

Super easy grading scale. She really cares about students performance, and if you show up to class and don't look engaged, she may call you out, so at least pretend to be trying even if you aren't Super easy if you use the lecture slides, however she can be rather disorganized at times. No exams (or final), just "quizzes" which are basically review

Dr. Padalkar has excellent lectures and lecture slides. The first half of this class is essentially a repeat of thermo 1 and 2. She has quizzes, homeworks, and 3 exams. She is very approachable and works through lots of examples. I would definitely recommend taking ME530 with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took thermo 1 with her in the fall of 2018. It was a good experience. Lectures contained adequate information. In-class participation and working through problems together. Amazing grading scale and relatively easy content wise. She went over stuff that actually showed up in thermo 2 which was actually really helpful. Solid choice!

Lectures were a bit disorganized, and sometimes I felt like we were rehashing the same topics multiple lectures in a row. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but she would have quizzes or in-class participation. Exams were a lot more conceptual/trivia than I was anticipating . But like when I had her for thermo 1, the grading scale is very generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She expects class participation, but as long as you follow along you should be good. Her grading criteria are very fair...I think anything above an 85% is an A. She's a little disorganized, but always gives the class enough time to prepare for exams and complete homework. Cares that students grasp material and is a fair professor.

Arguably the least organized professor I have ever had and is not timely with any part of a class. The slides provided rarely match what she presents and many quiz/test questions are "trivia" questions based off of incredibly specific facts. She incredibly defensive when she makes mistakes on examples and is disrespectful in a 1-on-1 setting.

Didn't show to several classes and didn't tell the class why until after the fact. Gave quizzes and exams based off of random details in her lecture slides. Did not follow her syllabus, would tell the class the day homework was due that there was no homework. This class should be an easy A, but she's managed to make that impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Thermo with Padalar was straight forward. Show up to class and you'll do fine. Exams are really hard to finish in 50 minutes, but you get a cheat sheet and there is a big curve. Watch out for quizzes on Thursdays
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Thermo is difficult, but if you attend her lectures and visit office hours regularly you will do well. She is very helpful with the difficult homework. Study hard and write quickly on exams. She also does a built in curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pros: goes through tons of example problems, class curve is generous, great teaching techniques and is a very good lecturer. Cons: I don't feel like I learned much past plugging and chugging. Exams were RIDICULOUSLY paced, waaay too long for 50 minutes. I knew how to do every problem, literally just couldn't work fast enough to finish
One of the best at ISU

Very good professor. Super easy class if you don't mind not learning much of every concept other than knowing how to get an A and solve homework problems. As long as you don't skip class and just show up and write down whatever is discussed in class (usually textbook problems), A is guaranteed. I would not take this class with anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, very motivational, truly cares about students learning the material and her grading system is fair and reasonable. I would not take ME 231 with anybody else in the department.

She works through tons of examples that are really helpful for tests and homework. Lectures can be pretty boring but as long as you're there to do the worked in-class examples you should be fine. Also, her grading scale was ridiculously easy, so that was nice.

Love her class. Really cares for her students and wants them to learn. Attendance is not mandatory but encouraged, because she tells you what the important concepts are and it is always usually in the exams. She also curves the class a lot, so it is relatively easier to get an A in her class. Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing professor

Had a very generous grade scale and balanced exam scores and homework scores well. She is repetitive which helps remember some of the tougher concepts. She won't hand everything to you, but she will give you the help and time needed to get a decent grade. She moves fast sometimes but if you stick with it, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. So helpful, very smart, and attentive to her students and the success of her class.
Great professor
Decent professor. Easy grading scale.

Just go to class, and you will understand what she wants from you. If you miss a class, I recommend emailing her to give you notes, as the course is very dependent on you going to class and taking your own notes. But she is very helpful and gives clear instructions.

Alison truly cares about the students. She is truly understanding of students and their lives, and just wants them to succeed. Her lectures are entertaining and encourages having conversations about the material.

Alison is one of the best professors I've had in my 4 years at Iowa State. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it is important for knowing the content & succeeding in the class. She makes the class very interesting and wants all of her students to succeed. She will work with you to help you succeed and is very flexible. Loved her and the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Phillips was a very polite, friendly face that made me eager to pay attention during this morning lecture. Many say that she was hard to listen to, but if you sit up front, the lectures can seem quite personal. The material was interesting and I know that Dr. Phillips was working hard to make sure we understood it and would succeed.
Really nice and good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Average lecturer, not as entertaining as the first section's professor for the class, but got the job done.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Phillips's lectures weren't as interesting as the other Psych101 professors', but she takes more time to explain different topics. Her section of the class was the easiest for me because she doesn't cover as much material, and explains topics very well.

Her section of Psych 101 is average. Attendance isn't mandatory but you need to show up to lectures to understand what is going on since the test is only based on lectures. Test was not too bad but some of the lectures seemed to drag on for a very long time. Pay close attention because a lot of material is thrown at you in a short amount of time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice woman interesting lectures

Like Meissner, also very arrogant and not very interested in trying to help students understand difficult topics. Instead just blows through topics that are difficult like everyone should understand them with ease. She is a decent lecturer but not well respected so it makes the lectures tough to sit through. You need to go to them and read, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I actually did best in her section of the 3. Extremely clear, and the lectures covered everything on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Extremely disorganized class, was teaching random concepts from the class at random times during the semester. Attending lectures was basically useless, as you can't learn anything from them, also had no recitation or lab to make up for it. Had to rely on hws, previous knowledge to study for exams. One of the nicest professors and won't fail many.
Very knowledgable and can explain most concepts. Connects concepts with each other.
Very helpful professor, although lectures and homeworks were sometimes confusing or tough, he was always there to answer any questions I had. Fair grader and overall cared about his students passing.

Course was asynchronous and the professor had absolutely no idea how to do that successfully. Had about 15-20 different documents and links in each weekly module, and most of them were not even needed or helpful. Lectures jumped around from topic to topic and did not have a concise meaning to each.
His lectures are sometimes hard to follow. Wish he would've gone more in depth with teaching the computational portion of the class. Cool guy! Great in office hours and in review time.
He explains concepts very well in class, and he's very willing to help with homework questions (especially during lab) and he's always cheerful about it.
Almost no feedback on the extremely hard and confusing homework. The lectures are decent but very scattered around. He teaches at a much higher level than a 301 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He wost most helpful during the optional labs and allows you to work with other students on homework. Lectures and projects can get dry and difficult if you're into social science because he uses a lot of biology examples. Good, but not great professor.

His lecture is clear but his notes sometimes not that helpful for exam review. You must have a textbook to go over before exams, homework can be tricky unless you fully understand the learning materials. No recommendation for skipping classes, some key points needed his proper explanations to understand if you are not a great self-learner.

Knows his material very well, but doesn't make an effort to make it easy to understand. We pushed through the material so fast that I don't feel like anything stuck. Little to no help with SAS code. Homework was either right or wrong; no feedback was given. Felt like you were flailing about in the dark on HW and tests. Very disappointed in all.

Does not go into enough detail when it comes to the SAS Code we have to use for assignments--end up having to google a lot. Weekly assignments are way too long. He is extremely helpful and will respond to e-mails fast usually. However, is not always clear in lectures. Excepts too much from what little he gives in lecture/lab
His species ordination class was fantastic.  He's an expert in this field and is a very effective and interesting teacher.
Great teacher, it good to stil have some around
One of the few gems among the teachers in statistics. Actually knows his statistics inside and out. Top notch class.
very clear and insightful

Jones was a fine lecturer however during the course it was clear he had an "I understand this so if you don't then you're clearly not capable of this" attitude. The course was already hard enough despite me personally doing well, so I can't image how crushing some of his comments may have been to someone trying their best yet still struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is confusing at first, the labs are long and tedious, yet they teach you a lot. Long readings for HWs are helpful. Lectures are quite slow, but Jones is helpful during office hours and very nice. Quizzes and exams are multiple choice and simple, and the final project is hard but 100% doable. Put in some effort and you wont regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Jones is decent. His lectues are very dry, but the content is useful. 288 is very reading heavy, and if you do it legit, you will read the Tiva datasheet for hours upon hours, but the labs are fun. I liked that he sent the class multiple emails a week with deadlines. His handwriting is bad and he also showed up 3-5 mins late everyday
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class content overall is okay! He takes a bit of time to get used to, but he does want you to succeed. Homework is good prep for exams, quizzes are simple, and TAs are tough but helpful. Dr. Jones expects you to follow his work ethic, with long readings and time-consuming labs, but that's the only way to understand how a microcontroller works.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Labs difficult, lecture is sort of slow and can be boring at times. Overall not bad if you try.

Prof. Jones did a great job explaining the materials in this class. The class is well-structured. I liked his teaching methodology. You will spend hours reading, but this is the only way to understand how a microcontroller works. Homework assignments are a good resource to review for exams. The exams weren't really bad.

Tests intentionally designed to trip you up. Advice for quiz preparation is vague and quiz answers are never shown or discussed, completely defeating their purpose. Labs are overly complicated and long. Instructor has outdated teaching philosophy and assumes we've been doing embedded systems since birth. Needs to be restructured badly.

The problem with this course is there's way too much documentation thrown in your face from day one. Throwing students into the deep end immediately hinders learning. Everything feels rushed. This class needs to be split into two separate courses and restructured. Homeworks felt unnecessary. Quizzes were overly difficult. Labs were way too long
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Just started the semester with this class, and I can already say that this instructor makes the class a lot harder than it needs to be. I feel like the quizzes and labs and homeworks are enough, and the exams should be done away with altogether. It's just so much material that's thrown at your face.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His lectures are very dry and dull. His homework is insanely long with 20-50 pages of reading to "skim" over. Be ready to spend whole days working on it. His labs are very poorly written and the TAs really don't know what each checkmark is. The labs are also very long, so don't expect to get them done during the two-hour lab time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Labs will take longer than 185 and 281 labs, and you'll spend hours after your lab time working on those so prepare for that. Dr. Jones's lectures are slow and I feel like they didn't help me understand the datasheet material that much. What will really help to understand this stuff is doing labs and HW. Also not a fan of the canvas exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones is really smart and knows his stuff. Lectures can be boring, but are very important. His homeworks were mostly participation, but helped a lot on quizzes. Overall, the class outside of lab is mostly learning how to read a big datasheet. You'll have to do the same thing at your job so it's important to know how to navigate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CprE 288 Embedded Systems at Iowa State is very time consuming. There is an inordinate amount of material crammed into this class. The labs can be extremely challenging, and often times TAs are unable or unwilling to assist, unfortunately. Taking it remotely during COVID likely made it much harder. Start early on everything. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Jones claims that the goal of this course is to learn how to effectively derive valuable information from technical documents. Do this and you should fair well. The difficulty is that he refuses to learn how to use the standard tools of our university such as Canvas. His inconsistency makes the class feel overwhelming online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Jones does a good job making the projects interesting. All of his slides are posted online so not a big deal if you miss class. It is a fair class.

Overall, he did a good job with the class and I'm happy. I'd only complain about the homework's, some of them just felt so "extra". He hosts study sessions and the TA's do a good job with preparing us for exams. You literally cannot fail this class... I put it on the complete back burner and got a C. I did learn a lot though for the minimal effort.

Dr. Jones is a pretty decent professor. He's very knowledgeable about what he teaches, but his lectures can be a bit dry. However, you pay attention you'll learn a lot. The final project that is actually fairly fun. The only bad thing about this class is the labs due to the length and their boring nature. The exams are also difficult.

Jones is very intellgent but not the most effective teacher. Lectures are important for understanding material, however they are not very engaging. Labs can be very time consuming (especially with a bad lab partner) and homework can often be long/tedious, but both do help you learn material. He is a fair grader and offers plenty of extra credit.

Dr. Jones is extremely intelligent, but he has no idea how to relate to students who have no knowledge on embedded systems. He assigns hundreds of pages of reading to "skim" and you should be able to pick up all the important details to understand with no teaching. The grading scale is easy and the content isn't hard. It is extremely time demanding
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pr Jones is my least favorite professor I have had so far at ISU. The way that he taught the class made it so much harder than it should have been to understand the material, and he had next to no organization for assignments. Pr. Jones would finish lab instructions during the first lab period and didn't grade assignments/tests for 2+ months. Avoid

Jones definitely teaches some very useful and applicable stuff in his class, but I feel like the way the class is structured is unorganized. Sure, the content is difficult, and he assigns a lot of reading before quizzes. He is by no means a bad professor, it's just the way the course is structured just makes it frustrating and more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Lecture slides are horrendous. Tests aren't hard. Labs are extremely long but TAs and Jones are always accessible and ready to help. Lots of readings for quizzes but you can just skim through it. Group project depends on your team so it's a hit or miss. Be prepared to put in LOTS of hours into the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Jones made sure I really understood the material that he was teaching. The course was challenging, but he is a passionate teacher and fosters that same passion in his students. Simple guy who loves what he does, would definitely take again. Be ready for a lot of work with labs and projects though!

Professor Jones gives weekly quizzes for 288. He sends out 50-60 pages worth of reading for quizzes two days before the quiz is given. He is incredibly undependable, and often delays the work of the first lab section because he is still writing the labs. He WILL NOT explain the quiz answers after the quiz, and the quiz disappears. Also MUCH more..
Hes more competent and relatable then most the professors in this field, and he will take your questions directly. Always open to talk in office hours

CprE 488 is the hardest class I've taken at Iowa State by far. The labs take a ton of time outside of class and can often be very frustrating. However, I did learn a lot from the class and it does an excellent job teaching students to figure out tough problems on their own.

Dr. Jones is pretty much average in every respect. Nothing stands out as a real drawback, but there's definitely room for improvement. Be prepared for tests that are at least 1.5x as hard as you'd expect (mostly because he doesn't give practice exams). For 288, be sure to truly understand the labs and homework.

Lectures can be long and he tries to engage students but his methods are not the best. Sit up front if you want to stay focused. Hes very smart and don't hesitate to ask him questions. He stresses reading the data sheet early on and I would take that advice, if you wait till the last minute it can make labs, homework, or tests more difficult.
Dr. Jones is a pretty cool guy. He's an expert at micro controllers even if he gets a little confused some times.

Dr. Jones is the man. I don't know what bad rep for. He answers questions even during weekends. He curves two steps while some professors do the opposite. The tests are really tough, but that's just what it is.

I think he's a tough professor but in no way is he a bad one. You definitely need to work for the grade and that's what he wants you to do. Tests are a bit tough though. But in the end, he's a very respectable man.
Great prof. The answers to the class are right in front of you. The key to the whole class is lab and the key to lab is to read the data sheet. If you don't read the sheet you will not do well.

Not a fan of this class. His review sessions provide little of what is on the tests. He basically gives you the code for your labs and you just fill in the blanks. This should probably be an upper level course. If you don't have any knowledge of I/O sensors you find the class difficult.

Very tough class. Lots of memorization and notes-referencing needed. The entire class is centered around the lab, so if you fall behind in the beginning, there's no catching back up. Expect to put a lot of time into this class. This professor just makes it harder than it needs to be.

This class was less about a lab as reinforcement and more about the class as a reinforcement for the lab. The labs are super hard if you don't understand what is going on. The professor is not lenient at all. For Cpre288, I recommend finding another professor. This professor made this class incredibly hard, more so than needed.
Good professor. extremely helpful. Able to learn a lot.

I had to work very hard for the A in this class. Overall, it was extremely interesting. Becraft has a dry sense of humor which made me pay attention in class. I know some other people think he's boring, but the content is very interesting. I hate reading textbooks and I never opened mine. Other people have told me they wouldn't pass without it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He expects a lot from you. Tests have really tricky wording, you really have to pay attention. I had to study like crazy and I still didnt do super great on the tests bc of the dumbest details in the question. The homeworks he sends are also oddly specific after comparing what you just learned in class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is pretty difficult. His exams are set to where you can't go back and change your answer which is extremely annoying. His exams are also very difficult and specific so they would be impossible to do without my notes. This pandemic saved my grade because I would've failed his exam in the center. Take with different professor if you can!

Philip is pretty cool. Honestly, you really have to teach yourself to write extremely fast, the man goes like real fast. Like sometimes I'm just watching Philip smile while he relays information and then the second that I look back at the slides he moved to a completely different topic. Study and read and you can do alright on his exams.

Phil loves biology and puts his heart into the slides and making fancy transitions that he smiles his little heart off at. The exams are rough, and ask very specific questions. Attendance isn't required but he does tophat during class which counts into your grade. The homework isn't too hard.
Tests are hard and extremely specific. Dr. Becraft does know what he's talking about and loves Bio. Keeps talking about a barbecue on Friday's though so that's weird.

If you do the homework, you will get an A on the tests. He is clear in what he expects you to know and understand. He is a fair grader and a good lecturer. He is concise and I enjoyed being in his class. His top hat questions are very representative of the tests.
Extremely intelligent man, it just shows way too much when taking tests as they are extremely difficult. Do your homework and you can get the class average of a 60% on tests and still pass however.

Dr. Becraft gives you a great opportunity to succeed. He had all the important points highlighted on the slides, he posted all the slides online, and there was an obscene amount of extra credit. BIO 212 is not an easy class by any stretch of the imagination, but if you work hard at it and come to the lectures, you should be just fine.
Extremely smart, tests are tough and goes wayyyy too quickly in lecture to even take notes on what the tests are over.
Tough class Hard to here Old Man Knows his stuff though
She's amazing and never made anyone feel bad for not understanding. She takes the time to make sure you get it.

Great professor that cares about you learning the content while also making assignments enjoyable. Always willing to help answer questions about projects or assignments and brings candy to every class.

Very passionate about power plants, connected a lot to research she's done. Carries over to her teaching and makes it very easy to engage in the content. In-person verbal only final seems intimidating, but she is lenient and guides you if you get lost or confused. Very personable in office hours and on field trips, really wants students to succeed.

Super great professor. She only wants to make sure her students learn the content well and she will help you and give you the feedback so you do well in her class. Go to office hours and attempt the practice problems and this class will be a rewarding experience and an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No busy work, and very good lectures! If you do at least some of the practice before quizzes and tests you'll pass!

Amazing person and professor. Excels at making sure students understand the material. Exams and quizzes she checks your work when you turn it in and gives you the opportunity to correct it to ensure you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's rare to find a professor that can be an easy grader while also making sure to actually teach you the material, but Paola is one of those rare few. Fantastic lectures, exams are difficult problems but if you take your time and know where things are in the slides and books it is easy to get a good grade. Just make sure to ask her for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Pittoni is a great teacher who genuinely cares about her students' success. Her lectures are clear, and she goes above and beyond in office hours to ensure you understand. She's fair in grading, approachable, and brings positivity to every class. While group work can be time-consuming, she fosters collaboration, making ME160 a great experience.
For a math based class she does no almost no examples and when she does, she does them in the most con fusing, convoluted order possible so that you can't follow her work
Problems are not easy, but if you DO THE HW you can bring your work and the quizzes are similar. Also answered a Teams question after she was in bed. That just shows her dedication.

Dr. Pittoni is a great professor for this course. She is very caring, understanding, and fair in the grading of students. Her content is difficult, but she provides great resources to learn and is available/willing to help you. One of the best professors I've had.
Best teacher to have! Heat transfer should be hard but she will guide you through that. Utilizing her slide and especially her HW/practice problem solution is my advice.

She was one of the best professors I have ever had. Very helpful. Work hard and go to office hours! She is very accessible outside of class. Go to class and you will get very helpful insight on the exams/quizzes. Be prepared to work hard but you will learn a ton! She genuinely cares about you and your learning. 10/10 take her class
Attendance not mandatory, but it is easy to fall behind if you don't pay attention in class.

I cannot begin to explain how amazing of a professor she is. Due to covid, I had minimal interaction with students or professors. She creates an amazing environment, and I love her teaching style. I think it's rare to find a professor who cares this much.
By far the best professor I've ever had. She's more than a professor, she was like a mom to me. Truly a passionate and inspiring person.
So far she's been the best professor I had at ISU.
Absolutely great professor! I learned a lot and had a great time in her course!

LITERALLY THE BEST TEACHER EVER. She cares about you understanding the material and wants you to do well in the class. Hopefully you get a good group, so they're easy to work with and it can be time consuming outside of class. Other than that, the class was easy going.

Pittoni is very intelligent and helpful. Her lectures are great, but in the chance you need extra explaining, she is very helpful at office hours. She is a lovely human and always brightens your day. She grades fairly and you learn a lot. I definitely recommend taking ME170 with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Best professor at Iowa State. The other profs are not even close. She cares about each student, tells you what will be on the quizzes and exams, and provides tons of resources to study. Heat Transfer should be horribly hard, but she is such a great prof that I had no trouble getting a perfect on the midterm with some effort. Take her class!
She was the best professor I have ever had.
She's very energetic and enthusiastic when she teaches. Be ready to work hard for the projects.

Fantastic professor. She really knows her stuff, and her only goal for the semester is to help you understand the material. If you attend class, she clearly tells you EVERYTHING that is on the quizzes and exams, and you definitely won't fall asleep listening to the broccoli vs ice cream lectures.

Technically you dont have to come to class because she posts her notes online but I highly suggest it because her guidance and teaching is really helpful. Shes funny and honestly super caring about her students and their grades. She told us first day of class you can google the book and find the pdf. Dont waste your money. Easy to get an A or B
In class activities are graded so show up. She really cares about the students learning and is very available and willing to help outside of class.
A nice teacher that clearly knows what she is doing. She cares for all her students and actively displays it. She gets people to participate.

She has a light accent, but she is quite easy to understand. There is an assignment worth 1-2% of your entire grade each day, so dont skip class. That being said there were no tests for my class, only a final worth only 3% There are two group projects worth most of your grade, difficulty will be determined by the competency of your group. Recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Good professor, helps you learn everything that you need.
Hands down the best professor I ever had throughout my ME degree. She sincerely cares for her students and is really passionate about what she teaches.

She is a really great professor, very helpful in office hours, and cares a lot about her students. Every class has an in class assignment so don't skip. Not many exams so make sure you take projects seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Pittoni was great.. I hate going to lectures but her class was entertaining and very well done. She put complex concepts into terms that college students can understand which helps a ton. She didn't dive deep into proofs or complex mathematical problem solving and focused on the big picture and the conceptual side of it (thankgod). She's awesome.
I had to do most of the work by myself. Lectures were not that useful.

She clearly tells you what to expect for quizzes, the midterm, and the final. Yes all of her problems take a significant amount of time and typing into your calculator but they're not too difficult. She really wants you to learn in lecture and she also is available in her office for whatever questions you have. She's one of the best professors!
She really cares!

Paola is awesome and cares about all of her students. She is super helpful in and outside of class and was a fairly easy grader. However, group projects are graded heavily in the class so make sure to keep everyone accountable and get things done on time or your grade could really suffer. Other than that, it was an awesome class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super helpful during office hours. Very nice woman. Would definitely take another class with her
She is a very helpful teacher, if you ask she WILL help you big time.  Plus go to her office hours she really does her best to get you to understand everything.
She's a really cool person and makes class interesting. Highly recommend taking Heat Transfer with her. Quizzes are straight from the homework and she only has a midterm and a final.

She's Italian, so she can be hard to understand at first, but by the third or fourth lecture, you'll have no trouble. Make sure you bring your textbook and do the homework. Its not collected, but your quizzes are a problem from the assigned homework.

Class content is challenging but lectures clearly explain the procedures to complete the assignments.  The assignments were done in groups and the tests were well written and fair.  She is easily contacted and ready to help if you have any questions. She also cares about her students grades and will be fair in grading and assigning homework.
Paola was an awesome teacher. She was always helpful and really showed interest in helping students learn. She was very passionate about the topic and made the class engaging and relatable.
really hard class and her method of teaching is not one of the best.

Took ENG 2500 with him; he is the best English professor! After each project, he gives you a week off from class to hold grading conferences to help you improve your draft. He grades very fairly and has a decent amount of "free points" assignments. Just do the work and show up, and you'll get an A.
Caring, lots of extra credit, fair amount of time to get assignments done.
He is very easy on grading; he cares more about your effort than anything. He's funny and very real with the students; he doesn't "act" like a professor, he acts like a normal person.

solidly my favorite english teacher ive ever had. 
his teaching style is so fun and interesting, he manage to get my C average in english butt to pay attention and be interested in what he was talking about.
nothing but good things to say about him.
hes a fair grader with everything that you do and always willing to help out if you need it.he great

Sam is such a down to earth and chill professor. You'll have occasional reading outside of class but nothing beyond that besides the essays. The feedback he gives on papers is so helpful and makes sure you're where you need to be! Overall, really funny dude and makes class super enjoyable.

this class is a gen ed and should be treated as such. he is a harsh grader and had me stressing over English, the class that should have been the least of my worries. He was a nice guy and very easy to reach, and maybe I just don't like English, but this class was painful and felt like it never ended.

Very easy-going! He was funny and down-to-earth, making the class more personal and casual. The grading on assignments was fair, but be prepared for the grade to reflect the amount of work you put in. His instruction was casual and entertaining, and work time was allotted in class. He was helpful in answering questions and always provided feedback.
Always willing to respond to questions and a very caring professor! Reach out and he will ensure that you have the resources to succeed!

Piccone has the most fun classes I've taken so far. Super engaging lectures and is pretty chill. He's a pretty tough grader comparatively to other 150 teachers but he gives thorough feedback and will make sure you get the grade you deserve if you put in the effort.

Professor Piccone is a very honest professor, who does NOT have a professional approach to his lectures, which contain around 20 students. Piccone made his students work for their grades, but if you participate in classes...which is all group work, he recognizes your efforts and WILL give you those points as a buffer in your larger assignments.

The biggest fault of this professor was him trying to turn this course into something it's not. He will want his papers written like poetry. He is a complete poetry nerd and will imbue that into how he grades this course. You could follow the rubric, to the letter, but will still get a B or a C on the paper. Do yourself a favor. Pick another prof.

No slides were ever presented the whole time we just broke out into small groups and read the textbook.  There are 6 "pop reflections" and you don't know when they are, and if you miss one your grade drops significantly. Easy class overall, but not enjoyable.

reviews.comment: Class is easy but not enjoyable. Attendance 6 times/semester if you miss one your grade will drop a lot, no makeups or excuses accepted. Class was pointless to go to because I had already learned concepts. We would just talk to our groups and read from the textbook the whole class and do in class activities that we got no credit for.

Take MKT 363X (Creative tools) if you actually want to learn how to work in digital marketing. Literally, the only class I've taken at ISU that taught me something valuable for after graduation. You learn how to make a website, take professional photos, etc. Attendance is mandatory only M&W. Silas gives great feedback to help increase your grade.

Silas is a great professor, but his structure for 362 is not great. The whole semester you work on a group project where if you have group members that suck, you basically get stuck doing the whole project. He also makes attendance mandatory. The final exam was hard and included content I don't remember learning about. Still an easier class.

You have one, 5-question quiz due every week, and your other assignment is a slide from your final project due at the end of the semester. He is super engaging in class but doesn't make it mandatory to go.
Awesome professor would highly recommend to anyone who needs a marketing credit. He was an awesome professor and active in his field
Silas makes lectures extremely engaging and if you participate you will definitely learn more. He grades pretty easily and is straight forward with everything. 115% take his classes he's amazing.

Silas is Awesome. He's very thorough with the content and tries to incorporate humor into his lectures to make class overall more enjoyable. Class is very dependant on the group, so if you get a bad group or bad group member, it can make or break your grade. Weekly easy quizzes help with that though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is very enthusiastic in class and wants to make his students laugh, you can tell he loves his job. Gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit and wants students to pass. Has a Tophat question everyday for attendance related to the lectures. Makes office hours a lot of fun, would easily have him as a professor again.

Cary Pint is so far my favorite teacher I've had for lecture so far this year. He is very enthusiastic and gives great in detail lectures on all the subjects. He is very kind to the students and seems to love his job. 10/10 prof and would love to take the class again. It wasn't very hard with the extra credit if you just attend class.

Honestly, Cary is the best professor that I have had at ISU, he is super passionate during lectures and you can tell he cares about what he is teaching. He is always very helpful in help hours, and overall a great guy.
Cary is very a nice and caring professor. Great choice to have him as a professor for any class.

Cary is great, by dynamics isn't! He teaches the course well, cares for his students, wants them to succeed, and provides as many partial credit points on exams as possible. However, the individual project was graded harsh and the rubric is super broad, so spend TIME on it. 1st exam is a physics, so if you do bad, don't worry, there's 3 more tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Pint is one of the greatest professors of all time. His enthusiasm for the course's contents and endless dynamics puns made lectures fun to attend. Best dynamics professor by far. Be prepared for corny jokes and dynamics puns. Grades his own tests so he gives lots of partial credit. Dynamics as a class is just difficult so be prepared to study.

Overall Prof. Pint is an amazing professor to take ME 345 with. He puts in the effort to make sure everyone is doing great, gives great feedback, and is always accessible. If you're struggling in the class feel free to ask, he will always help you out. I enjoyed showing up to lecture, he makes lecture very fun and you can tell he is passionate.
Professor Pint grades all exams himself, which is very dynamic.

reviews.comment: Dr. Pint showed me how great a professor could be for a core engineering course. I loved having Pint, lots of puns and a great mentor for dynamics and life. VERY talkative, beware. ME345 is intense but Pint had a lot of examples every class which were very helpful for hw and exams. He also gives A LOT of partial credit which is a life saver. He rambles on a lot but is great, will help you out anytime and boost your grade

The amount of time spent on homework for this class rivaled STATICS, and the directions for statics was far more clear than the directions for this class.

Insane amount of work for pre lab and post lab. These labs take about 6 hours to complete just to do it again the next week. Never saw her once. Definitely avoid this class, I knew the ratings were bad but wow. Please if possible find anyone else. This class is one credit and takes me way more time than any of my STEM classes.
Took this fall of 2023 and I am still traumatized by her labs.
Attending Dr. Pistolesi's lab was one of my LEAST favorite things to look forward to during the week. Usually, labs tend to be fun, have clear instue

She doesn't respond to emails, no reactions to concerns about TAs, and coursework is crazy for a 1 credit lab. does not respond to emails and whats nothing to do with you and all the TAs are booty cheeks

Some post-labs are more analysis-heavy, but shouldn't take longer than 1-2 hr. Lecture teaches the necessary content for analysis, but don't be afraid to look stuff up! TAs might grade differently, but an A is not impossible.

I have never seen her in my 2 semesters of taking her labs. The TAs she had graded so differently among sections. The labs were also inaccurate and did not give us the correct result, even after we followed the lab manual very carefully. I have never liked her labs and I never will.

Ask your TAs questions and use the help center to your advantage. Choose project partner wisely.

While the lab itself is fairly easy if you have a TA who is helpful, if not, good luck. Pistolesi will not step in and help, or even respond if something is going on. Grading won't be clear, because half the time it will depend on the TA.

Show up and do every assignment and you should get a decent grade. Pick your lab partners wisely and STUDY HARD for practicals.

I only saw her once the whole semester. She came in, never introduced herself then left. The class was a lot of busy work, and the ELNs were not graded the same. You have no clue what the practicals are about, and most of the time, you still have a 3-hour lab to complete after a practical. Most of the time, the lab never related to the class.

Way too much busy work for a 1 credit class. I never saw the professor once this year, having taken 177 and 178, luckily I had decent TAs or I would've been in trouble. The post-lab quizzes were unreasonably difficult and worth like 30% of your grade

Dr. Pistolesi is the professor for all the gen chem labs. Thousands of students per semester! And still replies to emails and visits labs. The structure with prelabs took a bit to get used to but the class is fine. Some differences by TA but everyone has the same assignments.

I cannot tell which was worse; the poorly-written lab instructions, or the horrendously designed lab practical's. Get ready for 3+ hours of work outside of lab for only 1 credit!

THE WORST. I do not understand how she even has a job. She writes the labs, and they're filled with mistakes and confusing wordings. Horrible class and NEGATIVE points for wrong answers on homework with no solutions posted

NOPE! The lab manual had a lot of typos, very little clarity, and was hard to follow. This often left me to do the experiments wrong because the manual was not thorough with explanations. All she does is write the labs, nothing else. Everything is done by the TA. I have a HORRIBLE TA, crazy how she got hired. The labs make no sense and are 2 weeks ahead of lecture. I honestly wouldn't know how Sara is as a professor because i've never seen her a day in my life only the TA for the class.
