She also constantly asks if you have questions, so if you're lost you can ask at any point. The team based learnings are also directly off the slides, so if you were paying attention you can get all the right answers.

Personally, I never went to class and just looked over the notes on my own time. My only downfall is that I missed a lot of points due to missed tophats. Overall going to class isn't that important if u do the hw on time. I looked up those answers as I was taking the exams so take this information as you wish. Dr. Renu is super helpful.

Dr. Srivastava was one of my favorite professors I've had at Iowa State! She is passionate about biology and she offers online review sessions every week to help kids understand. Her tests are complex but they were open note and if you study, you'll do great. She is friendly and willing to answer any questions or guide student learning. Good prof!

The tests are poorly written ( typo's, grammar issues, and bad phrasing) which can make some questions annoying and difficult to understand. Lecture requires tophat use every day which is a big portion of grades so if you don't show up or answer the questions during lecture your grade will suffer. You can take all tests twice. Easy enoguh to pass.
Very caring and good instructions
This was one of the most disorganized and poorly run class I have taken full stop! I won't take a class with him again!

Awful Professor. Assigns thousands of homework and tasks without considering the students' needs. Will be unavailable most of the time and will pop back 4 hours or a day before the class, and will assign a 1-week task whose deadline will be in 4 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is usually under prepared for class. Many times he prepares an example to demonstrate in class, only to encounter errors. Later, he has to send out an announcement correcting the example and explaining the right approach. He is a nice person, but unfortunately not the best professor.

He was absolutely never prepared for class, slide deck was ripped from another professor and half the time he didn't even know what he was presenting himself (probably because its his first time seeing the slide deck). Watching him try and code was funny and 9 times out of 10 someone in class had to help him fix his errors in his code.

Mike is hilarious! He tries to play songs before every class, tells amazing stories and is very clear in his grading. Make sure you completely fill out every question, otherwise you will miss points. If you take this class, put in a little effort and you will do well.
An inspiration to his peers and students, while also holding up a banner of progression and learning. While I don't know exactly who I want to be, I hope I am like this man.

Mike is best professor I have had at ISU. He is disorganized, does not stick to his schedule, and can be forgetful, but he is the most inspiring, kindest, and most invested in his class of any professor I have taken. Mammology is a TOUGH class-- he expects us to know A LOT, but the lectures are so engaging and fun, it did not feel that difficult.

He's a great guy to chat with, but very disorganized and overall just not a great professor sadly. Assignments will be returned (hopefully) weeks to months late with feedback that contradicts the advice you were given among many other issues. Avoid if possible.

Great guy, super funny, and tells lots of stories about the content in the class. I always found myself in engaged in his lectures.  I will say he can be disorganized and not always provide clear explanations so make sure you can take notes and teach yourself at times.  I recommend taking his courses!
Funny guy, lots of dad jokes. Hard exams, but co-taught with Jennifer Schieltz. No filter so swearing is there. Good guy.

LOVED Professor Rentz. Always had a good time when he held his lectures and always had a fun way to begin class. Was a very passionate and entertaining professor who loved to have some fun when teaching. Great guy!

I have taken almost every single class Mike teaches and he's easily my favorite instructor at ISU. His lectures are always fun to listen to and he'll answer as many questions as confidently as he can. He does formulate some really tough exams, BUT he crafts each exam based on what he was able to cover in lecture to be fair. Overall a great person

He had a few group projects that were very easy to complete. He liked trying to make the class laugh, so get ready for dad jokes. He was very engaging as a prof. If swearing bothers you, brace yourself because he's got no filter lol.

Very fun and likable. Makes the lectures more fun by adding jokes. He co-teached with Jennifer Schieltz and was mostly there on fridays, so I am not sure how much grading and exams were done by him. Overall the class was fairly easy if you go to class and pay attention.
Rentz is an amazing professor who makes the class lectures interesting and involved. His exam questions are hard and often comprehensive so those are rough but he is a great professor.
The class was okay. He is not very kind.

Mike is a wonderful person and he sincerely cares for his students. His exams are very difficult, but if you study you will do well on them. He does have frequent pop quizzes, so you must be there. If you are a person who needs organization from your professors, AVOID HIM AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE! He is the most disorganized professor I've had at ISU.

This review is for the capstone course for Animal Ecology wildlife option, but I have had 5 courses with Rentz during my time at Iowa State. I just don't think he is a good professor. 350 characters are not enough to explain my experiences. If there were more options for professors for wildlife students, I would have chosen others.

Mike gives great lectures that keep you really interested. I also had him for NREM 120 and lab in A ECL 365. Come to class or you may miss important information not on the lecture slides. There are also pop quizzes.

Lectures were largely unuseful and provided little clarity on subjects that he expected us to know. He would always go on tangents about personal experiences that people really didn't need to know. I managed to do okay in his class because I study quite hard. While he seems like a nice enough person, I just wouldn't recommend his class.

Mike's my favorite professor at Iowa State. He can be a little sporadic at times but his classes are never boring and he genuinely cares about providing a good learning experience for his students. Would definitely recommend taking any class taught by him.

Took this online because of COVID. There were 5 tests, like 10 assignments (writing a couple of paragraphs) and online participation quizzes. Pretty easy overall and Mike was always fun to listen to. I also had him for BIOL 365 Lab and he was great there too.

Dr. Rentz is the best professor I've had. With classes going online he's been very understanding and has looked out for his students constantly checking in. He's hilarious and you can tell he cares about what he's teaching. Definitely recommend for any class at ISU.
Seriously one of the best professors Ive ever had. He is so passionate about what he does and is a very interesting lecturer. The exams are easy as long as you study.

Awesome class. Mike is one of my favorite professors. He is an incredibly engaging lecturer and really a great professor all around. His open relaxed approach and open door policy has helped me through a lot of personal hiccups as well as academic. Awesome human, awesome educator. Would take another class with him for sure.

Mike is great! I had his class Freshman year and he gave lectures that kept me entertained and engaged the whole time. He likes to start off class with classic rock songs and he rocks out in front of a lecture hall of 300 students. His lectures are easy to follow and he makes sure to throw in his own flare while presenting (i.e. cursing).

I enjoyed the lab portion of vertebrate biology. We worked on a section of the lab manual once a week and had a quiz every 3-4 weeks. The first few weeks are a bit dry because it is just memorization of vertebrate classes but it gets better. There are also 3 papers regarding vertebrate biology topics in the news but it is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I thought this class would be easy. It is purposefully NOT. It's one of the most boring classes. Professor is nice but the exams are hard. Professor uses even the last second of class time to lecture which makes it unbearable. Tophat is not just participation but you actually have to get the answer right which is not fair when it's a new lecture

Mike is the best professor I have had in all my years at ISU. He genuinely cares for students and has reached out to me outside of class many times for my well-being. Deadlines are soft and he often doesn't doc you for turning things in late. If you do all of the papers/reflections (there are quite a few but they aren't hard) you will get an A.

Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had. I went out of my way to take his mammalogy class and I would take it again if I could. Lectures are entertaining and he's generally just a super nice guy. Tests are not difficult if you show up, pay attention, and study. Easy to work with and cares about you as a student, 11/10.

Mike is soooo much fun! I'm not in his dept. but there's days I wish I was! Class was super easy, only 4 simple tests all semester. Makes class really fun, lectures well, and makes you want to go to class. Very easy to contact if issues every come up and definitely cares about his students. For sure trying to take him again!
Rentz is absolutely amazing. He's hilarious and makes it fun to learn in class. I'm going to go out of my way to have him as a professor again.

Mike is a great professor. He is a little unusual in that he is very casual, while still being professional. He really cares about his students and wants them to learn new skills, rather than just memorize facts. He is very encouraging and welcoming. His lectures are fun, and the lab provides many opportunities for hands-on experience.
I loved the way Mike taught. He was very enthusiastic and you can tell he loves what he does. I probably learned the most I've learned in any class so far, and I never had to stress out too much.

Mike is a wonderful professor.  Although sometimes he can be disorganized, he the only professor I have had yet who truly cares how I do in school and where I end up in life.  He wants all his students to succeed and be the best that they can.
Mike is AWESOME! He is hilarious and makes class enjoyable, but most importantly he like learning new things with the students he teaches. He is by far one of the best teachers I have ever had!

Mike was just hired on to the NREM department to create new classes for the influx of students entering the department. 365L was his first assigned class to take over while he works on formulating new courses and he did a great job. Quirky and enthusiastic, he loves what he does and makes the class enjoyable to not only attend, but learn.

*MAE2200W at Mizzou* This content in this class is pretty straightforward and has daily quizzes that help with the material. However, the writing (which takes up most of the grade) is graded tough while having no defined criteria. Even papers with opinion based topics or ones that involve information about new content are graded harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had professor Montazami for MAE 2200W and is a good professor and has good lectures. The biggest thing is you need to attend class because there are quizzes almost every day and exam questions are in class examples. He wants you to succeed, and is easy to talk to but the writing assignments he grades pretty harshly.
A good teacher for a fairly easy course, tests have a lot of weight but they're all take-home and very similar to homework. Good at answering questions regarding homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tough course

Excellent professor. Exam problems are mostly examples done in class, so attend class as he doesn't post the work done in class online. There are some recorded lectures from a few years ago that he posts online but going to class and learning how to do the examples are the best way to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A passionate and engaging professor. I was worried with my grade on the first exam but he gave another exam and summed up the two grades; beyond that point I was able to maintain a good grade. Very helpful during office hours and after class if you approach him. The programming part was the better half of the course.

He cares a lot about his students. On the engineering half of the course he does many many samples problems in class and you will be fine with Elyse exams if you understand the examples. On the programming half we did one or two short codes per lectures. He goes over the answer code step by step and makes sure everyone understand the functions. Thx

The first half of the semester was used to cover engineering concepts and the second for programming. Dr. Reza is a seasoned, knowledgeable, and caring professor. He explains in detail and with examples. You need to make an appointment for office hours but he is most helpful and walks you through the solution. Grading is fine. He curves the final

Professor Montazami grades on a whim. Show work or suffer, but you wont know what is enough work til you fail something thinking you had enough work. I had to email him several times about grades and his canvas grade book was never accurate.

Great guy, writes very clear, color coordinated, notes on the board. He has his own version of a "textbook" which is free to download and he basically teaches straight from it. He had pop quizzes until the whole COVD thing, but if you pay attention to the smaller details in lectures you'll be fine. Exams weren't easy unless you actually studied.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: The class was not very hard for me. As long as you go to class and work with your classmates on projects and ask them for help, you will do well. However, if you don't do well on any assignment it will tank your grade. Just make sure you keep up with the work and try to get everything done and you will be ok

Overall great professor, and a good grade is attainable if you're willing to put in some work. The class is broken up into coding in MatLab, and problem solving physics problems. Be ready for in class quizzes over MatLab and try your best not to miss these (need a 70% in the coding category of the class to pass). Exams questions come from homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of bonus points. Even if it is obvious that you got wrong on project and exams, if you ask him for extra points for trying hard and how other parts are done well, he gives 80% of the full point on that part.( not the whole bonus point, for that part). His grading criteria changes at the end of the semester. he has bad pronunciation.

He is an amazing professor. I know because I have a had pretty bad ones from this school. He is a great listener; his explanation is very firm and his grasp on concepts is just marvelous. I admire his a subject matter expert and as an individual. Courteous and caring; he treats students like people and not like just a student number.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor and I just love the way he taught this course. More attention was paid on learning then assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Midterm too hard(Although I think its fine :),  and the average is around 50+. So he made a second test, as extra credit, where the score will be add to the midterm, and the extra points will be added to the finals. Easy pop quiz, easy homework.

Dr. M was really passionate about the subject. He does many problems on blackboard and explains every step clearly.  HW was graded for completion only but  quizzes are graded. attending the review sessions help with the exams. Also, very helpful during office hours. Differently recommend him!

Professor Montazami went through many example problems which was very helpful. After each problem, he asks if everyone understood the problem, which is nice and helpful.  His exams are very similar to in class sample problems but he is  a harsh grader.  He is very helpful and flexible with office hours.
Just Finish ME 160 with him and received an A-. Exam guidelines are clear, he gives extra credit points toward the end of the semester. Very helpful in class and at office hours.

This class isn't the hardest, but you will have to work for it. Professor Montazami's lectures can be incredibly boring. He isn't the nicest guy in class, but if you talk to him during office hours he is very kind and willing to help. He stated doing random in class extra credit in class assignments towards the end of the year.
The topic was really made easy; homework was reasonable and grading was fair. Thanks

Professor Montazami, is gaining experience as a professor, and it shows. I found the class to be easy, as he curved the test and gave a lot of easy points. He also focuses less on the programming and more on the math, while other professors do the opposite.

Not clear, hard to understand, takes forever to do nothing, if no prior experience in the subject this teacher is difficult, late to class in morning, instructions are unclear for tests and projects, seems generally very last minute and seems like he has had NO experience teaching because he has not had any experience.

Always late to class. Hard to understand what he says. Talks quiet.  Bad at writing tests (does not use proper grammar).  Makes class very boring.  Does not use time well in class to teach. Unexperienced professor.
Incredible Prof!

I took this class Fall 2015. Dr. Waldman was very friendly and gave interesting lectures. She included lots of pictures and occasional videos to further explain topics and keep students interested. This was one of my favorite classes.

Class participation is a large part of the grade, she gives online quizzes during class and lots of clicker points. She's a great lecturer, made an introductory bio course fairly interesting. The first half of the semester is a lot of memorization, but she communicates well with her SI instructor so the exam reviews are very helpful.

Gives long lectures, but breaks them up with clicker questions and videos. There are a lot of tests and if you do bad on a few of them your grade will suffer. There is a lot of info on the exams so you'll need to study. Overall a pretty decent class.

She was an amazing lecturer. She made class interesting, she had good notes on slides, and we had 6 exams, which was much more helpful than 3 big ones because there is so much information to cover. I definitely would recommend taking BIOL 211 with her!

Dr. Waldman taught this class for the first time this semester; her SI TA was really helpful (and you could probably get the old SI notes with a google search). Be ready to study for her tests; they aren't necessarily hard, but there is a lot of information to cover.

I really enjoyed this class.  There was a lot of information to learn but it wasn't hard.  If you utilize the SI worksheets and practice exams, you will do well in this class.  Dr. Waldman was always available if you needed her.
She puts all of the info on the slides and they're all online, explains things very well and still makes it fun. If I could take this class again I would.

Okay, so she is pretty bad. Her powerpoints and SO long and not very interesting, she just reads powerpoints. All the tests are cumulative (none of the other professors do this) and very difficult. You NEED to go to class, read and probably do SI in order to do alright. Very bad class, I wish I had taken it next semester with a different prof.

This is her first semester teaching and I get that, but there is such a thing as unrealistic expectations. I literally despise this class and her teaching style. Reading me PowerPoint slides does not count as teaching. Tests are ridiculously hard and worded really weird making them hard to understand.

Rhonda is wonderful. While the 302 research project can be a scary prospect, she knows exactly how to help everyone through it. Classes are small so you get to know the people who are critiquing or collaborating on your work. Very helpful experience for future research writing.
Great teacher.  If you go to class and do the work its an easy A. She's really helpful if you every have any questions

Her open mindedness for different research project topics results in an Ivy League quality experience at a large, public university. Personally did not feel however that she was "difficult". If you understand the material, the quizzes are free points.

Rhonda is a very sweet lady and a great teacher. I had her for PSYCH 302 last spring. Though writing the research papers could be difficult, she made them more manageable by assigning things section by section, so it was easier to tackle. She's very helpful and considerate- loved being in her class :)

This is my 3rd year at Iowa State and she is my favorite teacher yet. She has an incredible way of making you feel really comfortable. She recognized that the course is very intimdating, but consistently reminded us that we'd be "experts" by the end of the semester. It was a lot of work but my most meaninful experience at Iowa State so far. :)

She's very nice, & the class isn't difficult. However, we had to write research papers, and rather than have her correct our drafts, we had to exchange them with other students. The thing is, how can you trust them to correct your paper when they don't know any more than you do? Always get her to look at your papers (which she'll gladly do).
Loved her!

She was a very nice and approachable prof which is unusual :). She also made SPSS assignments seem harder than they had to be by explaining them awkwardly. She didn't have her TA give much time for reviewing our tests which made it really hard to fit into schedules. She calls you by name which can be somewhat annoying if no one is volunteering.

She's a really nice person, and will go out of her way to help anyone. She admits to not knowing everything about SPSS, but she always made sure to connect you with someone who could answer your questions. Overall she's a good teacher.

Horrible. The only reason people think she is a good  teacher is that she is a nice person. She gets confused by her own lecture, forgets to tell us important info for assignments, and confused me on a lot of stuff that I already did well on in other classes. I wish I could take it with someone else

She is a very nice person and seems to really enjoy what she does. However, sometimes she would confuse me on concepts I already understood. But she is more than willing to help anyone with a question.

She was friendly and very willing to help outside of class. But she had a hard time explaining things in lecture, especially when questions were asked. The only psych course I've taken and not aced (still a good grade though).

She has been very helpful in explaining these tough concepts that most of us have not learned yet about writing a technical paper.  She is also very approachable and is just a nice person all around, I also had her for Psych 440.
Yue Ren is a great professor. Lectures are easy to follow and he is more than willing to help you understand a topic more. I would definitely take another class with him as my professor.

Reny is the best professor! His class is not challenging and doesn't add much to your workload. He does a few attendance checks because the lectures are empty near the end (poor guy). He will reopen quizzes if you miss them and gives extra credit opportunities. He's not super tech-savvy, so be patient. He has an accent, but it is understandable.

Reny is an awesome professor! He implemented an attendance grade because he felt that not enough people made it to class, but he usually tells you when the next attendance check will be (usually Wednesdays). He offers extra credit for participating in class, though I feel it would be nearly impossible not to get an A in this course.

Dr. Ren is a very knowledgeable professor who cares about his students. His lectures are funny and interesting. Weekly discussions are compulsory but he is flexible for late submissions. Random attendance checks. A final research paper on any topic related to this class.

Reny is a very kind professor; he wouldn't grade you if he didn't have to. He's always willing to be flexible with students and answer questions. His grading criteria are very broad, but he gives specific feedback after grading. 10 random attendance checks, 10 class discussions, 5 model international conferences, 1 quiz, and 1 final paper.

Reny is kind and hilarious, and the class is easy, but I didn't learn anything. He gives extra credit if you answer questions in class, so you're all set if you participate. The quizzes are open notes, so you never need to study. He's a lovely person with interesting stories though!

5 random attendance checks, three open note at home quizzes and final is at home online along with a three part group project. He doesn't grade difficult and posts his notes. I would go to class to just listen and use his notes for the quizzes which always got me a good score. Offers extra credit for raising your hand even if you get it wrong!

POL 121 is a great course if you need to meet the International Perspectives Requirement. Three group projects, three quizzes, and one final. All tests are online & open note. Reny is a great professor who emphasizes in-class participation but still gives students access to his lecture slides. He also does random attendance checks for points.

I LOVE RENY. Actually the best professor I've had at this school. He randomly throws out extra credit points, and you don't even have to be right. He will still give them to you. He is very kind and sincere. It is clear that he truly cares about his students. I am taking a course that I don't need to have him again.

Mr Ren was hands down the best professor I had this semester. When I informed him about some mental health struggles, he was more than willing to accommodate and help me get the best grade I could possibly get.

All Dr. Ren cares about is that you also care. If he didn't have to give exams, I don't believe he would. Show up, be engaged, and you will be more than fine in this class. Doesn't require much time at all outside of class besides one project during the entire semester. He is a little difficult to understand at first, but is awesome afterward.

Professor Ren is a great professor, he cares about his students, makes the lectures and debates fun and enjoyable, and gives out extra credit for in-class participation. The tests are open-note, so if you pay attention in class to what he talks about and the main points of the slides you won't have any problems.
This Professor is amazing it is really easy to get extra credit as long as you participate in his class. He is very flexible and understanding.

Reny is the best! The class is super easy. He often calls students out for easy questions and gives extra credit for answering (he always helps if you don't know the answer). I reached out to him multiple times, and he's always willing to help raise grades. Very approachable, caring, and kind.

Very smart and funny. Wish hed just write a book instead of teaching classes because of the way information just flows out of him instead of follow a curriculum. Very easy and he will always work and make time for students even if he isnt super close with them.
Renny was a great prof, the class was quite easy. The tests were open book and if you took notes in class - easy A. He was super nice and understanding.

Yue Ren is such a caring professor and is often very funny. Show up to lectures and listen/take notes and you will do just fine. Had occasional test but they were open note/internet (although they were kind of tricky). Would highly recommend any political science course he teaches!

INST 235 with Reny was a perfect gen Ed. Everyone is given extra credit points for in class discussion. Reny cares for his students and can be quite funny some times. The class is also super easy, just show up and participate.
Exams are worth 15 points, Participating in class can get you 5 points of extra credit. Show up, be enraged, and you are going to pass with an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Cares about his students success. Has an accent but still is easy to understand. Class is all about just showing up and participating in lectures.

Reny is the best professor I have had at my time here at Iowa State. He will do everything in his power to help you succeed in his course. I have never met another professor who cares so deeply about their students like he does. If you have the chance to take this course with him I HIGHLY recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Reny was my favorite professor this semester. He is extremely caring and kind to his students, he cracks lots of jokes in his lectures, and he loves class discussions. Lectures are live webex calls, but lecture info is posted on canvas. 2 quizzes, 1 Model UN presentation, and 1 final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Yue Ren is amazing! He has an accent but is a very caring and his class is not difficult at all. Would reccomend taking POL S 241 if you need to do a world perspective elective.
Very enthusiastic!

Reny is an amazing professor that cares so much about his students. This class is super easy if you just show up and put forth an effort. This class has A LOT of extra credit as well. The grade is made up of 3 quizzes, a final, and random attendance checks. No homework. Review session before every quiz- Tells you EXACTLY what's on the quiz.

Ren is awesome. He loves what he talks about in class and makes it interesting. Overall took as an elective and its as a very easy class. Lots of extra credit and genuinely cares about class. Just 3 quizzes and a final with no homework. Random attendance points though.

Dr. ren is very kind and always is understanding you do have random attendance checks and he will allow extra credit to those who he knows is always in class. He always makes sure he does not offend anyone and lays information like it is. He is an awesome professor and made the international studies class very interesting.

Very intelligent and a great guy. Whether you're a poly sci major or are just trying to meet an elective requirement, this is a perfect class and professor. It's an easy A because you can memorize quizlets and his review sessions, but if you actually listen to his lectures he makes them very interesting. Random attendance 5 times thats 15% of grade

Incredibly easy class, learned almost nothing though. Lectures are boring but attendance definitely helps your grade. Even though the class was a waste of time, Ren is an incredibly nice guy and it seems like he is a lot more intelligent than the content he is teaching requires him to be. Show up for attendance checks and quiz reviews... easy A.

Dr. Ren is extremely caring and really does want you to succeed in his class. His quizzes are extremely easy, he even does review sessions before every quiz with the class. He also offers extra credit for those who need it.

Great Professor and fun lectures. Is very discussion focused so be prepared to talk and up-to-date on issues the course covered. If you are participating and willing to put in the work this is an easy A. Would recommend to any Political Science undergrad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good Professor, cares about students, gets students engaged.

Dr. Ren was by far the best professor I had this semester and quite possibly the best professor I've ever had. He is very fair in his grading and the quizzes/exams are super easy. You just have to show up to class and you can pretty much pass no problem. He does everything he can to help the students. Very very great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Reny is awesome. He is the most caring professor that I have ever had. He understands that students have a lot going on and doesn't assume that his class is the only important one. I learned a lot from the class, and it's a good class to take if you need to fill your international perspectives requirement.
interesting class. a quick and efficient way to learn Chinese foreign policy.

Reny is the best professor I have had at Iowa State. He uses the diverse background of his students to make the class very interactive and personal. He works to make every student succeed if they communicate with him. I have heard he teaches an amazing Chinese Law/Foreign Policy class for those interested!

Reny is a great guy and seems to want everyone to succeed. He goes over test questions before the tests. He does attendance checks every so often so just try to make it to those days of class. Overall very good professor.

Reny is by far one of the best professors I've had at Iowa State. His class was very easy but he cares more about discussion and learning than tests. His lectures were interesting, he has a lot of amazing stories, and he cares about all of his students. I would definitely recommend his classes because he is an awesome guy.

literally played age of empires every day in class, and the quizzes he goes over all the questions with the class before taking it and the final, so as long as you can memorize true and false and multiple choice questions for like 20-30 minutes, or cheat if you feel like it, than you will get an A.
Don't bother going to class. Its worth just about nothing.  Show up for the quizzes and the final and cheat on all of them. A+

One of the most caring Professors there is in the department. Rather than take tests and write papers, he has you debate and discuss lecture material. In the long run I've learned more from him than most other professors at Iowa State.

Reny is honestly one of the nicest professors I've had at Iowa State, though he can be difficult to understand at times. Easy A as long as you pay attention during the quiz reviews. Final was all multiple choice with most questions coming from the 3 quizzes given during the semester.  2 "random" attendance checks during the semester.

He is slightly hard to understand, but he makes sure you are able to comprehend everything. He cares very much about his students understanding the information. The classes are pretty much 100% lecture and you wont  miss much if you don't go to every class.
Enjoyed his class. There is a definite accent, but he knows how to teach. He will ask discussion questions often so do be sure to pay attention when in class or he will catch you off guard.

Great professor that really loves what he is doing and cares for the students. He can at times be quite blunt with you which is never a bad thing, and at other times can give little direction, but isn't that part of learning? A unique dude and I think our section had some of the btter work just because of how much he allowed us to do our own way.

I thought Patrick was very helpful. He is fairly new to the design program at Iowa State and I think he is doing well. He is always willing to meet outside of class, and goes out of his way to make this class fun and interesting. He goes out of his way to know his students and genuinely wants you to achieve your goals.

The worst professor you can be stuck with for 102. I counted the number of times until the end of the semester when i wouldn't have to put up with him anymore. Totally disrespectful of you and your efforts, do everything you can to not be in his class.

Tina is very nice and is willing to work with you through anything. However, she has problems with articulating exactly what she wants out of a project. My class had many misunderstandings with her rubrics, since what she explained in class contradicted what was on Canvas or the module wasn't updated.
This class was a pretty easy A, but the class felt all around very unorganized, and I did not learn much at all.

This class had very interesting course material for graphic designers, but her lectures were all over the place and she talked very fast. There are no exams, just weekly 'Case Study' assignments, with required readings, as well as in-class activities and two projects. Don't make the mistake I did; attend class regularly, attendance is graded.

I took 377, 388 was the only option to choose from. I am taking 388 next semester with Tina, though!
She's an amazing teacher! She's funny, caring, respectful, and very nice. It is a MWF class, but you don't have class every Friday. Classes are lectures, but they're great, and she goes through them fast. Studies and activities are really easy!
Shes great! Very flexible when it comes to her teaching style. Lectures were fantastic! Readings could be a bit boring. Tests were open book!

Her lectures felt like she didn't know what we already knew or didn't. She would go incredibly slow through the basics of Python, and then she sped through the physics part of the class. She was also unnecessarily strict in her lab.
Just attend and do good in the lab and your fine
I loved every second of this class; professor riedel is the reason i'm excited to be an aerspace engineer. the lectures were enganging and the homework was easy if you attended class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really great professor! She super nice and really good with python. If you have a problem with python, she'll know exactly what it is. She makes the material and workout problems easy to understand. She also draws diagrams with colors.

Dr. Riedel is a great introductory professor for AERE. There are many topics to move through in a short amount of time for this class, but she is always available and willing to help, not to mention extremely knowledgeable in her subject areas. I came in with 0 coding experience and struggled, but she was always there to help when I had questions.

This class is supposed to be an introductory course, but that's not the case. As someone who had limited knowledge on coding, this class really sucked. Besides the class, Carolyn is a tough grader. She is also unfair sometimes. She made the final cumulative just because the class did poorly on the midterm. Are poor exam grades entirely our fault?

Professor Riedel is a great professor who wants her students to do well. Yes, there is a lot of information covered in the lectures, but as long as you take notes, the homework should not take too long. I found the labs to be very fun when it came to the LTA's, but you need to put time and effort into it, and she doesn't mess around with safety.

Lectures were long and tough but the labs were fun and interactive. This class covers a large amount of information so it is very difficult to cover all that in the given time. Carolyn does a decent job making sure its all covered but the midterms and finals are comprehensive so it seems like an insane amount of information to remember.

She is very knowledgeable and very nice person. I enjoyed her positive attitude throughout the year. She is very easygoing with grading, but not with safety. With her lecture she moves very fast. She teaches the class assuming that you have a lot of prior knowledge (especially with coding and physics) and moves very fast. BesidesthatGood Professor!

The midterm had 4 questions that were difficult and the average was around a D. The labs involve knowledge of programming and knowing how to actually build an aircraft and figure out the dimensions and make it from scratch. This is impossible to do as a beginner. Not an introductory course. This was the course i disliked the most.
Fun Class, covers a wide range of topics, all introduction to aerospace engineering.

Aere 1600 is NOT an intro course. You are expected to know so much and keep in mind the midterm mean was a 66% and no one got perfect score, there was only 4 problems. She is not great at managing this course but she is a good person.

Carolyn is a great professor for the intro to aerospace engineering course. She is passionate about the content and clearly lays out all expectations for you to succeed. She can get serious when people talk during her lectures, but is super nice all around and will gladly help you if you are stuck on anything. Ask her about her carillon playing!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Carolyn always is willing to help students with a problem if necessary. She is nice to talk to and tries to make class and lab as enjoyable as possible. AER E 160 is a really easy class if you put in the work.

Class wasn't very difficult, only had three homework assignments over the course of the semester, midterm was done online with open notes. Final was straightforward, 5 questions within 2 hour period. Main time sink was the LTA project and labs.
A good professor, forgiving

Great lab tech. Intimidating at first but you warm up to her. Do all the work you are assigned in lab. It's possible if you just plug in with no distractions and get it done. You work with the same team the entire semester so just be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She has helped out a lot in my lab classes especially when it came to programming .
She's a great prof. She has high expectations but really wants you to succeed.
New to engineering, but Carolyn is super nice and really helped out this semester.
Carolyn was a good lecturer, and she was very helpful with answering questions. Just follow the assignment instructions and you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Carolyn is not the main lecturer of AERE 160 but instead is the coordinator for the lab portion of the class. She is strict and can come off as sharp but can be cool when talked to one on one. Make sure when doing any homework or  projects that you follow all guidelines and do all homework exactly as she says or you will be docked points.

There is a lot of reading in HIST 2220. Her grading is semi-difficult, but she is an amazing lecturer. She cares about everyone, and if you show up to class, you will benefit from the info and get to meet her. A+ professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As a professor, she is caring and knowledgeable. I really enjoyed her lectures about the history of food as it relates to society in different time periods. There are a lot of papers. She expects quality structure, a clear thesis, and knowledge in one's writing. Participate and attend on discussion days. Take good notes to refer back to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Riney-Kehrberg is by far one of my favorite professors. She cares deeply about each of her students and takes time to get to know them personally. I would recommend taking any classes with her or her husband!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While I found the class difficult, I absolutely loved having Riney-Kehrberg. She was helpful with any questions, accessible and cared about students. She made everyone feel welcome. The class content was so interesting. Would highly recommend for any history or sociology majors!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was a really good lecturer and even though she doesn't give a whole lot of things on her slides, you know exactly what to write. She give study guides that are close to her tests so if you thoroughly practice you know what her tests will be on.

She does her best to make the class interesting. It's basically one long narrative with no outline of important points, so taking notes is difficult. She does provide study guides for exams, but they're essay exams so it's only semi-helpful. Weekly reading journals can make or break your grade. Very helpful when asked & not an overly tough grader.

She does a great job of teaching the material.  The material is boring, dry, and lacks enthusiasm. If you try to discuss opinions she will never agree or will dock points on exams. Weekly readings and journals, 3 exams, and a final large project which was a paper. This is history from 1900-1945, there are many interesting topics that aren't covered

Pamela doesn't normally teach History 495 (capstone research project) but compared to other professors I've heard about, Pamela is one of the best. Throughout the semester, she has held us accountable for weekly journals that kept track of our progress during our projects, which made the process easier. Answered all my of questions when I had them.
Comments on papers can be very insulting and if your not a history major or grad student can make you feel as if she doesn't have the time to talk to you. Wouldn't take unless you have too!!

Great Teacher! There was no textbook but the material she handed out was easy to read and do assignments on. Essays were somewhat difficult, but if you pay attention in class you should have no problem

Easy assignments, easy tests, easy papers. Although if you are actually interested in history she does a mediocre job and often weighs insignificant things greater than important events. The TA usually did her 2 lectures in 15 minutes and more clearly. Class should be renamed U.S. History 1900-1945 with an emphasis on women's studies.
This class was a lot of work, but very interesting.
Very good class
Very good class.  Fair amount of reading, but it was usually interesting.

She is an awesome teacher, but her lack of notes makes it necessary to go to class.  And sometimes it's hard to decide what to write down and keep up with her lectures since she has no outlines or anything.
Very interesting class, lecture was worth attending. Big paper and 8-page midterm/final, so be prepared. Other than the massive amounts of writing in a short period, the class was fun.

Comments on returned paperwork were often insulting as if the student did not know how to write a paper, verbal directions on paperwork are often misleading or not explained well. However, she tends not to grade as hard as her comments would sometimes suggest. Lectures and book work tend not to be of much use but can come back on a take home test.
Class was more fun than you'd expect.  Good lecturer.
Very good class.  Lectures are interesting and most of the readings are actually fun.  I really enjoyed it.
this woman is extremely Annoying, does a very poor job describing critical details in some Historical events, and chooses to preach about what she thinks is important.. typical ISU professor
Good Class!  Lectures and readings are interesting.
Interesting class.  Good lectures.  Essay exams but not too tough.
Brilliant lecturer, good discussion leader, but too attractive to make concentration easy.
Good story teller, knows everything. Easy tests but they are essay.
If I wanted to learn by reading a book I'd go to the library, How about some useful lecture time, I can lead a discussion for god's sake

Very good prof, she makes you work hard but you learn a lot. Her lectures are very intersting and organized well. Lots of novels to read and papers to write. Tests are papers only. She is very helpful if you ask and knows a lot about the subject.

She is a wonderful professor. She is makes you work hard but if you try your best you get a good grade. She is knows and lot about the topics and is good at teaching it. Keeps the history intersting. She is one of the best professors I have ever had.
Very good class if you are interested in History.  Don't take if you want an easy A.  I have a history minor and loved this class.  She keeps it interesting.
No Comments
This was a very easy class, but I am a History major. That may have something to do with it. In my opinion it all depends on the TA that you get.

Dick Williams is such a funny guy. This class is needed for the Environmental Science major. It is an extremely easy class about things that you should know about Iowa State and also about resources that are offered. There is no homework or exams. If you show up you get a pass. A lot of people just work on other work during the class.

Williams knows a lot of information about seemingly everything. If you have a question, he can probably answer it. This class was pretty boring, but it's required, and it provides some good information.
Professor Williams is one of the nicest professors at ISU. He is very funny and is so easy to talk to. If you have any questions, it is very likely that he has the answer.

He has a very mellow, reserved personality that threw me for quite the loop, but this is absolutely not a bad thing- just something to know ahead of time. He answers all of the questions you ask during meetings and classes, and explains things to you rather than just telling you "here's how it is, go with it." He can also be really funny!!
The best adviser at Iowa State. Super helpful and clear. When you register for classes he'll walk you through everything and makes it super easy.
Richard is the greatest guy in the world.  He is the adviser for environmental science and is a life-saver. He is super helpful and will help you with whatever questions you have.

Dr. Richie is super knowledgable about language development & super nice too! You got two chances on exams so it is very easy to get a good grade- she is more concerned about you learning: not stressing out about a grade. She gets cool guest speakers to answer questions. The final is a group project which I am not a fan of, but it wasn't miserable.

It is an easy class, but the lecture is mandatory due to tophat questions being a large part of your grade. Exams and quizzes are all online. Richie is a great professor. She is passionate about the topics she speaks about and is extremely understanding to students.
Richie was a good professor for a hard class. I HATE research but this class was doable.

She was ok. She expects you to know a lot and doesn't teach much. She guides you in directions and shows you a rubric. All semester leads up to a giant project (research paper and 10-min presentation).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love love love Dr. Richie. So kind and made the writing aspect of research methods super practical. Made this class so fun and helps you really do an experiment on something you are passionate about. Simple writing assignments and gives you class time to work on them. Must show up for data collection and oral presentations though! One of the best!

She really cares about her students. I asked her so many questions, and she had nothing but amazing feedback for me. This course was very easy and a lot of fun. If you can take it with her, definitely do!

Dr. Richie is an amazing woman. She is kind and clearly cares about what she teaches and about her students. As far as 413 goes, get the book and at least skim it, it is very helpful. If you don't want to read the book, go to class. She cares a lot about class attendance, but you will love what you're learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: You can tell that Dr. Richie loves this class. She's so passionate about the concepts and she gets excited while covering it. This can lead to getting off-topic, but I learned new and interesting things every day. The textbook didn't really add anything, so going to class and understanding her lectures was the most important thing. She's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Richie is the sweetest person. She cares so much about her students and does whatever she can to help everyone succeed. Doing the reading is important, but it's more important to go to class and make sure you understand the material she covers there. She is willing to explain anything you don't understand, and she reviews concepts every class.

Dr. Richie is extremely sweet. She is very fair with her policies. Attendance isnt mandatory, but coming to class really makes a difference and helps you do well. She does review of the previous class every lecture, which is great. She is very open to feedback and questions. The only grades in the class are the 4 exams, no busy work. Loved 312!

Dr. Richie is amazing, first of all. She cares deeply about her students' success and is willing to study with you to help you be successful. The entire grade rides on 4 exams, though, so studying and reading the book is mandatory. She is such a lovely, caring person and I am grateful to have had a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class itself is kind of boring but it's a learning community, so I guess that's just how it goes. She's a really great professor though. She genuinely cares about each and every one of us and she's always willing to help students who need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Richie is really sweet and wants you to do your best in her class. She is always there to help you if you need it. It is important to go to class to get the notes to study for the exams. It is also important to read, unlike a lot of other courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: My favorite class and probably the best IE teacher I have had! his lectures are interesting and he offers quite a bit of extra credit, but to obtain it you must go to lecture. His office hours were late but if you went he always asked how you were doing. A very personable and likeable person.

Half of his assignments you have to have an outside job site that will allow you to interrupt their work to preform studies on and the other half of his assignments he doesn't actually teach how to do the content he asks for.

Dr. Stone was extremely knowledgeable about the topic of safety.  His lectures were excellent, though not necessary to attend to pass the class.  There are a lot of labs and work involved, but if you do them well, you will easily get an A.

Professor Stone was great. Graded by few things tho - some homework assignments, a final group project, and two exams. As long as you do your best he will give you a good grade. Do NOT cram for the exams, be sure to study weeks before!
Extremely difficult midterm and final exam. The material during the class was entirely not related to the real world.

Professor Stone really cares about his class and about his students. He teaches a ton in his class so the stress level is pretty high trying to keep up. The midterm will be brutal, even if you study for weeks. If you show him you are putting in effort you will most likely end up with an A, but he will make sure you nearly die to get it.

He is knowledgable and does a good job making dry content pretty interesting, although the class had a death by powerpoint feel every now and then. Most of the class grade is made up of the two exams and final project. The midterm was the most grueling exam I've ever taken, 77 short answer questions in 3 hours. Be ready to memorize powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Hardest most extensive exams I've ever received in my life. It's impossible for the average person to memorize all of the content on this very very very lengthy midterm and final. So much stress. Do not take this class if you don't have to.

His course was very lecture heavy and the lectures would be dull and uninspired. The entire final grade for this course was based on 2 large tests (from lecture material) and 1 final group project. Very easy to fail.

Be prepared to have an intense, but caring man with a deep voice lecture you. He has great lectures and is sort of a tough grader at times. He's also the busiest person I've met, so try to coordinate times to speak with him as early as possible.

Stone is an awesome professor. A lot of his exam questions are based on homework problems, some of which are optional, so be sure to practice them. Don't miss class on days where lab groups are assigned because he will recall if you were gone. Overall, he was very good about answering questions and made the class interesting.
Skip this teacher, terrible grading structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Richard M Stone was single handedly the most Amazing teacher anyone will come across at Iowa State University. His class was able to Inspire me to become a more enthusiastic engineer! I would highly recommend taking IE 271 with Rich. His majestic Biceps alone makes this class worth it in the end. The course itself was challenging, but rewarding!

Stone is a lively character that appreciates teaching and learning. His tests are definitely based on the slides and you need to know exact definitions. I never purchased a textbook and he only mentioned 1 table in it ever. He's fun to listen to, but the material is specific and there's a lot of it.

I really enjoyed his class. He really tries to assert his dominance as a professor in the beginning of the semester. DO NOT text in class. He will call you out and possibly make you leave class. I really learned a lot and he is extremely knowledgeable about anything Ergonomics related.  The exams are about 2/3 memorization and 1/3 application

Looks are decieving. He may come off as super strict and unaprochable, but he is really a great guy! The class is not impossible, but it requires effort. Go to class! The exams are heavy on memorization so take good notes since the online powerpoints are not always updated. Just stay focused and you will enjoy the class.

You must attend class to get homework, in class worksheets, and his fully filled out lecture slides. He also gives pop quizzes if there arnt enough people in class. For the exams, make sure to memorize his slides. In addition, he does give extra credit that can boost your overall grade by 5% at the end of the class which really helps

Dr. Stone is a great instructor, but is AWFUL at responding to emails. I have emailed him 4 times this semester, and I have received no responses. It's a bit frustrating. His responsiveness to emails is the only thing that is bad about his teaching. He knows his stuff extremely well. Tests are difficult and hard to study for.
Made IE271 extremely fun! Grade is made up of 2 test, a final, and homework(there are only 6 assignments); so don't miss anything. Besides that, fantastic class!

I absolutely loved taking IE 271 with Dr Stone! He is kind of intimidating but I went to his office hours and he was so helpful! He makes the class extremely interesting and uses tons of real life application. I also found him hilarious and loved class. You have to work hard to do well. Don't skip class or then your screwed. Write down everything.

There is only 2 tests and a final in this class. So be very careful when studying for the first two, they are very important. The homework is generally very self explanatory and easy to get B's or higher on. Study the math, but you're an engineer if you're in this class. What you need to watch out for is vocab vocab vocab, and listsconcepts

He is a passionate teacher. I was unclear about a couple things but I went to his office hours and he tries to help you as much as he can. If you go to him with specific questions, he will explain it for you. His tests are primarily based on the big homeworks. If you know those you'll have almost all the test. Other test Q's are random memorization

He is very interesting to listen to and you should definitely go to lecture if you want to get a good grade.  His tests are very specific and require a lot of memorization.  Not a hard class if you put the effort in.

Very unreasonable and nit-picky. Does not grade on a curve. So, if you mess up one of the exams, you are pretty much done for the semester. Not a bad professor but he is very uptight. Class is interesting but the grading is harsh and unreasonable.

This guy is very entertaining to say the least. Not a big fan of his personality BUT I can't say he is a bad teacher. His tests usually suck, very harsh grading but he wants you to learn the material. Dr Stone is a character.

Honestly if you go to class and listen, you should get at least a B.  This class was fairly straight forward and the tests were pretty easy.  I haven't missed a class and I study for the tests, and if anyone else does the same they should pass fairly easily.  Also it's a very interesting class!
Seriously, memorize everything he says. Exams are ridiculously thorough and nit-picky. He's really bad at responding to emails.
Good. Very engaged with lectures. Tests are alright as long as you go to class.

Dr. Stone is an engaging lecturer with impeccable domain knowledge. However, come prepared to memorize everything...literally. If you have difficulties with rote memorization, you might consider an alternative course selection.
Not the easiest class in the world, but he is extremely helpful so go to his office hours!!  DO NOT surf the web in class, unless you want to drop kicked out of class.  Just kidding, but seriously.
He is a really good teacher but a challenging one. You will learn a lot!

Taking this class was one of the worst I have taken. It is really hard and extremely time consuming. It will be the only class you can focus on versus your other classes. Time management is really hard with this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had chuck for 131 studio/lecture. He is a good professor in and out of studio. Lecture was fun and tests were easy. The studio course load is HEAVY, but its super rewarding to end the semester with so much art to show for it. He is also a super easy grader if you're good at realism. He isn't afraid to give you 100% on projects if you deserve it.

Chuck is a great professor in the studio. I grew a lot over this course and he really wants everyone to grow. Expect a lot of studio time outside of class if you want a good grade. The lecture is redundant when you have his studio but you can use that time to sketch!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall, good teacher. Since I had an alternate studio teacher ( Streeter), it was nice to go to his lectures and hear him hammer in different points. Plus, after class he is very accessible and willing to answer any questions. Tests were not that hard as long as you knew the material before and read the stuff 30 minutes before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: hes a nice guy, sure. but lecture is useless. i have a different professor (pappenheimer) for studio, and neither teach from textbook whatsoever. when asked about what to study for tests, he says he cant answer due to "fairness." in reality, this just lead to not knowing what to study, confusion, and ultimately bad grades on tests due to this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chuck is the best professor I've ever had. I would highly recommend him, I couldn't say enough great things about him. If you are willing to put the time and the work in you will do just fine in his class. You just have to work hard, which pays off in the end. Best professor for 131, guarantee.
Tough class, great professor.
Best professor I've had at Iowa state. He is very inspirational! I loved his class!!!

I had him for 131 Lecture. His lectures were completely useless and not helpful at all. All he is interested in doing is promoting himself and his own work. That's all he ever seemed to talk about. Never met someone as self promoting as this guy!
Really great. Extremely helpful and knowledgeable. Learned a lot in his class.
He was my professor for the lecture part of 131. He was amazing! He met with me outside of class to talk about my studio work, and I'm not even in his studio! Great guy and teacher!
he knows his**** and has been around the block. very interesting; very helpful if you apply his teachings.
lecture is a bit boring but know the book for the tests and you'll be fine; in studio is very helpful but a tough grader--take his suggestions and apply them to your work and you should do fine.
very interesting

This class wasn't all that bad because it was only 8 weeks long. Other than that, it was pretty boring and taught me the same things my studio professor taught me the class before. Pretty pointless, study 30 minutes before the quizzes and you should do decent.
He is hard on you if you dont have too much previous drawing skill.

I learned a lot from the text he chose for the class but the lecture was pretty pointless.  He likes to talk about himself and his own artwork a lot.  Maybe that's helpful to some, but I didn't think it was.
Awesome lecturer. Very talented artist, makes the subject very interesting. Encourages drawing during class and is very helpful in understanding new techniques.
The BEST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD!  Chuck knows drawing, and also loves to teach.  He practices what he teaches and shows his work in progress to his students.  Highly recommend.

Chuck Richards is the most boring lecturer that i've ever had to sit through. it is not possible to get around it, just a warning... he was the worst to sit through. his tests were easy but it was painful to get there!
Wonderful
I learned more from him than any other professor thus far in my college career. He's very talented and very helpful. Awesome.
No Comments
Extremely professional professor and person. ISU is lucky to emply such an artist.  If I took anything away from the CoD it was Chucks talent and ability to help you become better.  Thanks Chuck!
Chuck is always more than willing to help you in any way that he can.  I learned so much from him.
One of the best teachers that I ever had.  He is an incredible artist and professor
She is always ready to help you out if you ask.
Dr. Rosati is very passionate about physics. As someone who knows nothing about physics this class was pretty difficult, but she was always there to help if I needed it. I like her accent too

Dr. Rosati is very lenient with deadlines and gives you extra time for lab reports if you have a good excuse (like a valid sickness, as in my case). Answers email questions genuinely and tries to explain thoroughly but doesn't quite hit the mark all the time with her explanations. Her lab manuals are outdated and incorrect more often than not.
Just a whole lot of work. Grading criteria isn't explained well and a lot of the concepts must be self taught

Rosati is a decent lab instructor. She grades fairly, sometimes even rather lightly. She explains the labs decently and is willing to help if there are issues. She is also very forgiving for personal issues.

Worst experience I have had at Iowa State with a Professor.  She is absolutely atrocious at teaching.  Uses strictly power point to teach.  Doesn't matter if you attend class, won't learn anything anyways.  Luckily I found the solutions to her hw and taught myself well enough to pass.  Otherwise I would have failed.
I had a great experience in this class. She was quite helpful, although a little difficult to hear, but was more than willing to help.
DO NOT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE, TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR.  350 characters aren't enough to desrcibe the frustration, anger, and every cuss word I'd like to type about my physics experience.
She's really nice but her English is very hard to understand.  Making the class difficult if you don't already have a good grasp on physics.

I don't even know what was going on in her class. She randomly gave examples and didn't explain what they were for. She also yelled a lot at people. She almost cried when no one was answering the questions she asked, but I don't think that anyone understood the questions she was asking.
Willing to help with lab analysis, and any problems you may have with the lab.
She does not give enough time for tests.  70% of your grade is on the tests when you have to put a lot of work on many other things in this class: lab, quizzes, and homework every week.
No more recitation quizzes on Fridays it screws up bar time on Thurs. nights!!!
Professor Rowling is amazing! His lectures are so interesting and he's always willing to answer questions! One of the best classes I've ever taken.
Extremely kind, asked us what he could do better, made an extremely boring subject as fun as he could.
Love this professor! His lectures can be boring but the exams and course material are easy. He gives out lots of extra credit. Attendance is also for extra credit. Would recommend him to anyone!

Class was well taught, which made it easy to get a good grade in the class. The class grade is based on exams and SmartBook assignments. He was very flexible and changed the time for smartbooks mid-way through the semester. He is funny and actually cares about what he teaches. He also made some extra credit smartbooks towards the end of the class.

Matt makes class fun and engaging with great stories and is so funny. Makes you not want to miss class. He explains content well and relates it to real life, though you may need YouTube to learn info since he draws a lot. He's down-to-earth, helpful, and really wants students to succeed. One of the best professors I've had—highly recommend!

I enjoyed Prof. Rowling a lot, him as a person was funny as hell and made class fun sometimes. But the topics being taught were difficult. He writes a lot of stuff on the board that is hard to follow, and I honestly ended up teaching myself rather than him most of the time.

His teaching style is weird because he just draws out stuff and it is very hard to understand The exams are hard and you have no idea what to study, he has study guides but he tells us that its not useful. Also whenever its exam review he wants us to ask questions and its hard to ask because when he is teaching it's really confusing.

He helped me progressive overload my learning, leading to hypertrophication of my brain. He is actually incredibly funny as well, prolly one of the more GOATED professors out there ngl twin. Grading was easy and exams felt like high school. I would walk up to him during an exam and he would walk me through the questions. 5 big booms 1000/10.

Matt is a great professor! This is a very easy class if you engage in lectures. Matt is a very personable and funny guy, and makes hard concepts seem super easy. He also provides extra credit points if you fill out exam study guides before each exam. Exams are worth a lot, but graded very easily. This guy is great.

I did not enjoy Food Science as I learned at the start of the semester, so it was my last priority. Prof Rowling understood that some students don't need this class like others, and he made it fair for both kinds of students. He was a nice guy, and the lectures were chill, although I skipped a lot.

Matt is my favorite professor I've had so far at ISU. He is so kind and down to earth and really wants to connect with his students. His lectures are clear and he recorded his webex lectures so we could go back and view them again. The material is easy to follow and he loves when people ask questions. If you can have him at some point you should!

Dr. Rowling did a great job of simplifying nutrition in a way that is understandable even for students who don't major in the field. His lectures would get off-topic sometimes, but he never wanted to waste our time and kept the course on track. He also gets to personally know you if you bother to come to class and ask questions.

by far the best professor I've had at ISU. He makes tough concepts so graspable and draws a lot on the board which is helpful when going through metabolism. He cares about students. Definitely a cool guy. Went to office hours to talk about my exam and ended up chatting about life.

Rowling is awesome - he's not big on busy work! stay on top of packback posts and you'll be good. I'd recommend going to lecture because test material comes from class (not always in notes), but notes are posted to canvas. he likes to crack jokes and makes class relaxed and enjoyable - yes, even at 8am
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Can we just appreciate this guy for a moment? He is a wonderful professor. This guy has been one of the best professors I have had in my 5 years at ISU. Even during the pandemic and the confusion and turmoil due to that, he is always accessible and still tries to have class like a normal lecture. He is empathetic and really knowledgeable.

By far one of the best professors Ive ever had. Hes a very personal guy, making it easy to enjoy the lecture and the information. This class made me apply the information in my own life. Hes always available to talk to students outside of class. Theres no homework but most of the exam material is written on a white board so you need to attend.

The short answers on the tests are from the lecture notes but are still difficult. He wouldnt be in his office during office hours so it was hard to find him outside of class. Overall the class was ok. Not sure if I would take another class with him.
Many Exam questions are taken from lectures, so make sure you go/watch them. Tests mainly over the overall picture but do need to know some specifics.

Makes his lectures available online in case you miss class which is very considerate. Easy to talk to, down to earth and understanding. Is knowledgeable in what he's teaching. Can be unclear in grading on exams, just talk to him about it if you disagree with something. Go to class because his short answers are from lecture. Textbook helps a little.
Dr. Rowling loves to teach and wants his students to learn and do well. Very approachable. His lectures really helped me learn and I never wanted to miss class.
Matt is an amazing professor. He makes the class enjoyable

Best professor I have had.  He makes learning what I believe to be slightly challenging material both easy and very enjoyable.  Super super easy to talk to, so I would for sure take advantage of that if you have any sort of questions or concerns.
Great professor who cares about how the students do. You'll learn a lot in his lectures if you pay attention.
Great professor.
Dr. Rowling is an overall caring, funny, and passionate guy. He makes learning about tough subjects fun and do-able.

He explains topics very conceptually in an easy-to-understand manner instead of reading off of a slide, which is super helpful. Lectures are great honestly, I never wanted to skip. He may be a great teacher but his tests are not easy by any means, you DO need to study for them. Definitely my fave prof so far, dude is rad.

Dr. Rowling is a great teacher. He really wants to make sure his student understand the material and is always willing to try and clarify topic in or out of class. His lectures are posted but a bunch of his questions of exams come from things he says in class, so don't skip. Easy to listen to in class and overall I would recommend him as a teacher.

I loved this class. Matt is a great lecturer. His lectures are easy to understand and follow along with, and they are also very interesting. There are only four tests (including the final), but you get to drop your lowest grade. If you attend every lecture and pay attention you shouldn't have any problems with the tests.

Does a good job making some dry material more interesting with personal stories.  He kept the level of the class appropriate realizing we'll have chances to get a lot more in depth in later courses.  He does everything he can to help you get a good grade.  The lecture slides cover what's on the tests so the book is really optional.

Dr. Rowling was one of my favorites I have had so far.  Not only does he know what he is teaching about very well, but he answers questions clearly and will do every thing he can to make sure you are as prepared as possible for the tests.

Nice guy, not so nice class. I found that the best way to study was to just read the textbook. I am not a fan of trick questions or wording questions in confusing ways on purpose. I felt like I knew the material, but it would be a simple mistake of not choosing the "best" answer. He was really accommodating though about rescheduling quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a Junior this is the worst professor i've ever had at this university. Weekly quizzes in the testing center, no study guides, and no practice exams. One of our current assignments is to make our own study guide and turn it in for him to grade. He doesn't give you an idea of what could be in the exam but only posts 60-100 page lecture slides.

Almost 50% of your grade is quizzes based solely on the textbook (the powerpoints are unrelated) and even if you do know the concept, the questions are worded poorly. You learn nothing, just read mildly related stories about whatever. Class average is 60% and prof just shrugs. As a 4.0 student, do not take this class it has no upsides.

This is genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. 
We have weekly quizzes that MUST be taken in the Testing Center, even though this is an online class. 
These quizzes are full of trick questions. The class average for these quizzes is less than 60%. He WILL NOT curve this grade no matter how poor the class did. 
DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!!

NOT GOOD. An example of a typical test question would be one about a location we never learned about, and that is not in the textbook. He tries to teach you how to study and get an A, but no one knew what to study in the first place. Worst class I've ever taken.

Professor Rudolph is a great teacher for this class and understands the topic very well. He often makes jokes in his lectures to keep us engaged, as it is a very information-heavy course. There are chapter exams each week with 15 multiple-choice questions. Read the chapter in the textbook and you'll do fine. The course is hard, not his fault.

Genuinely a great guy and very engaging with students (when they choose to be engaging back).
