His class is tough and his quizzes consist of 15, 5 word multiple choice questions that often contain little trick questions and answers to throw you off. Every quiz must be taken at the testing center and there is one every week.
weekly quizzes at testing center based on the chapter textbook. no study guides, 70 slides of the key points in the chapter and its basically memorizing every little thing based on textbook.
He gives out weekly quizzes with no study guide. The exam has no study guide as well. He will just give you a couple hundred slides to read through and hope you know what is on the exam.

Professor Rudolph was very open to working with his students during this online summer course. He was able to cater to needs and showed attention to his students. However, the quizzes are proctored, and it can be difficult to find a proctor. I had to pay at my local library to take the test in this course. It is not easy either must study.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IN THE SUMMER. I am taking this class as a summer class, and it makes me want to rip my hair out. There are two quizzes a week that need to be procotred, and if you are not on the iSU campus, it is going to cost you hundreds of dollars. He is a horrible teacher and doesnt want to do his job or help you out an any way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you show up and make sure your projects are meeting all the requirements before submission, this is an easy A, and you will learn a lot in the process. Just be ready to spend a lot of time on projects.

Lectures are painfully boring. Long pauses for participation never work because no one's engaged. He docks 15+ points for using outside code, slides don't help, and exams are way too long (2 days!). Random TopHat attendance and too much talking. Everyone has a B, but no one's learning.

Class is incredibly boring with lectures often only covering 2 or 3 slides at a time. We were a whole 2 chapters behind the syllabus plan because of how long it takes, and he punishes reading ahead in the textbook by docking points for anything you put in the homework that was never covered in class. Probably the worst teacher I've had. Do not take

Grades very harsh and gives no curve to help with his students routinely low exams scores. Also seems to put material on the exam that doesn't seem necessary and is put there simply to trip students up and get the question wrong. Lastly lectures are extremely boring and gives random attendance checks to make sure people are showing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have never written any reviews on this so me writing this is making it clear just how bad this course was. The mid term and final the averages were devastating low and not curved. Attendance is mandatory and lectures will put you to sleep. The questions on exams are a joke and mostly fun facts that somehow you're expected to know. DO NOT TAKE.

Class averages on exams where below 60% but still refused to curve. Ridiculously strict attendance policy for how boring and useless the lectures were. Attendance is taken at random and for each missed class it is 2% off your final grade. Do not take this professor!!!

Exams barely reflected class material and covered many chapters we never discussed but were on exams because they were on the reading schedule. Lab and project grading lacked clarity, with no rubrics or sometimes no feedback for point deductions. Overall, unclear expectations made success unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class itself was not very bad but the professor was terrible. The class was structured to be lab heavy with a group project a midterm and a final. The two exams did not cover a single thing we learned in class. Most classes we would just go over a couple slides and hardly cover any material. Attendance is mandatory and worth a lot.

Terrible course, but nice guy. Attendance policy is harsh, with each absence dropping your grade by 2%. Classes are very dry and boring. I learned much more about technology and databases in the google data analytics course than this class. Nice guy but the curriculum and way of teaching is not the greatest.
Okay, professor. I would recommend taking another instructor, though.

Brian is really nice guy and clearly knows his stuff! But I had a few issues with his class. For projects, there wasn't a concrete rubric. This made it difficult to pinpoint exactly what he expected out of the projects and led to some gray areas of confusion. Other than that, it's not terrible. Do the readings and participate.

Awful. Average on midterm and final was 55% no curve. Only saving quality of the class is individual projects and group projects are not too difficult and easy A to add fluff to your grade. But gives boring lectures that aren't engaging boring weird and not worth time. Only went to class due to top hat attendance

Lectures are often boring and dry. Attendance also makes up a lot of your grade He does not give you a study guide for the exam so you "make your own study guide" for a 80 question exams based off of 500 slides which is absurd. Exams are mostly trick questions and "fun facts" of random not important information. Good guy just not a good class.

Professor Rudolph has a huge working background in MIS, so he provides plenty of real-world insight. He isn't the typical lecturer who purely sticks to the book. His lectures are always interesting and responds to emails very quickly.

Professor Rudolph is a great teacher as far as lecturing goes. Each unexcused Top Hat attendance is 2% off your final grade. The assignments are fairly difficult, but if you go to class it's fine. Exams averages are consistently lower than 60% often times lower. Questions feel more like an english test with a lot of trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad i dont like this class

Rudolph was a hilarious lecturer, but the class itself is just so poor. The content, book, and slides are terribly dry and people just have to take it as a required class. Rudolph was great, the class isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rudolph was a really great professor who aspires for a bright future for all of his students. He wants his students to learn and ensures that by following up on tests and going over how to solve problems that many students struggled on. His class is not an easy A but I would recommend anyone to take it with him as you will learn more because of it.

Ruoyu Wu is the greatest professor to ever step foot on Iowa State University. He genuinely cares about his students and their success and could literally not be more respectful. Also, this class is despicably easy, the practice exams are literally the exact same as the regular exams just different numbers.
I enjoyed Prof. Wu pace of teaching, I think the reason most people who do not do well in the class is because more than 75% of the class doesn't show up. Do the homework and you will get an A.
Extremely intelligent and passionate, but not a great lecturer. Lecture videos from other professors posted in canvas are more helpful

He is so sweet but knows so much about math that he does not fully explain the problems. The tests are with the other calc classes; they are over nothing you learn in class or the practice quizzes you do. It is a weed-out class, so be prepared to do terribly on the tests and only be saved by the curve.

Not very engaging so if you don't like math it's hard to pay attention. Be sure to go to supplemental instruction or watch the Butler videos as they were honestly more helpful than the lectures. He's a chill professor though

He's a nice guy who knows his math but doesn't explain it well. He has a slight accent, but he's understandable. He often starts problems he won't finish, leaving them as "practice," which makes the lesson confusing. You will rely on the curve to pass this class. Would not recommend taking his class if you want to learn.

He's a middle of the road professor. He is a bit hard to understand at times but that's not something he can control. My biggest pet peeve with him is that sometimes he'll just stop and move on to the next question in the middle of solving the problem because "you know how to do this already", which is incredibly frustrating when I don't know.
hard to understand but still love Uncle Roy 10/10 wouldn't recommend.
The curve saves you
Dr. Wu is a good teacher, and I felt like it was beneficial to go to the lecture. My only complaint is that sometimes he is hard to understand, but I understand that's not his fault.
Class is fine, not very hard. However, for creative assignments, he grades difficulty without giving a reason. Docked points without a proper explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AMAZING MAN. I struggled a lot during the semester I took his course, and he was very flexible and accommodating for me. Without his help, I probably would have failed the class. As sad as it is to say, he knows that his class isn't one everyone is in because of a passion, so he is very good about keeping the work light and being understanding.
Hard on the grading, whether it's on your bug collection or exams. Get ready to feel like you're going to fail.
Dr. Jurenka is a decent professor but, theres little to no information giving on the lectures slides. You have to really listen to what he's saying in order to get all the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While his lectures are a bit monotone, dude is a really awesome person and cares about what you learn in his class. Start collecting insects immediately as the insect collections were by far the hardest part of the class. Tests are relatively easy and graded kindly. Tophat is used in class for extra credit. Loved this class!!!

Not the most exuberant speaker, but once you get past that hes a WONDERFUL and kind professor/person. It's obvious that he truly cares about helping his students succeed and gives every last chance to do your best. Often comes in to lab to assist our TA and assist students. I would take another course with him in a heartbeat.

Dr. Rutenberg has to be one of my favorite professors here at ISU. She clearly loves what she's doing and knows how to teach history very well. She is very considerate and understanding. I encourage you to talk to her at least once. She was AMAZING!

Dr. Rutenberg was amazing and her class was incredibly organized and informative. This class had a very obvious theme: she built an argument supporting the whole semester and changed how I view the world. My one critique is that it's a LOT of reading and writing. Sometimes, Dr. Rutenberg can also seem a bit unapproachable, but it's mostly just RBF.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Rutenberg is bar none one of the most underrated and underappreciated professors in the midwest as far as I'm concerned. She truly, TRULY, cares about the well-being of her students and understands that life doesn't stop when you're in college. She is inspiring and exudes a positive energy that pushes her students to reach their full potential

Dr. Rutenberg is an extremely knowledgeable professor, and she cares more about students learning the material than testing them arbitrarily. Her classes are refreshing because they focus on understanding the material through creative projects and group discussions. She is adaptable with her schedule and fair in her grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amy is an amazing teacher. This class is cross posted as history and gender studies. Coming from a history background, she made it easier to understand a gender studies-historical view of the past.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Weaver is very kind and very invested in his class. The class is mostly lectures with a few group projects. The content is simple, and his exams are very similar to the homeworks that are assigned each week. Overall, this class was fairly easy and very interesting. The lab is so much fun, as you simply get to go birding each week!
I've never had a professor less passionate about a subject as he is about physiology. Read the textbook and don't go to class.

He clearly doesn't know what he's doing or understand what he's teaching. It's a fairly easy class, but the difficulty comes from his bad explanations and using the textbook questions for exams which don't align with what we talked about in class, so then he gives points back after the fact to compensate.

Dr. Weaver gave boring lectures and covered many topics in one lecture. The exams were literally quiz questions and part 2 of the exams was graded harshly but got easier. He does take attendance points through Kahoot whether you get them wrong or right. Overall, he's an okay professor but I wouldn't voluntarily take his class again.

Great professor for 315. His lectures were well put together. He provided quizzes that directly reflected the exam. His exams were straightforward, without many curveballs. All over, great professor. Would recommend!

Dr. Weaver is readily available outside of class and office hours. Quizzes for each section make up a big part of your grade and are great ways to study for the test. If you attend lectures, practice the quizzes, and ask him questions, you will get a good grade. His mastery of the subject and desire to teach effectively is evident in his lectures.
Kind and engaging in lecture, helps keep things lighthearted
TAKE AT A COMMUNITY COLLEGE. Martin is mostly fine, although not the best. The problem is the tests are just overly difficult.

If you have a question or concern that has to do with university policies that involves Professor Martin, it may be a mistake to approach him alone. Protect yourself and find someone outside the math department (with at least as much authority as he does) than can help you talk to him, and fact-check everything he says.
Very approachable and witty. Clearly knows his subject matter and does a good job at explaining things. Best math professor I've had at Iowa State, by far.
Very sarcastic and knowledgable. Decent teacher who cares about his students. He made a difficult class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very personable and is obviously knowledgeable about the subject
Very clear about the subject matter and what he expects out of the students. Talked really loud--which was good since it kept me awake at 8 in the morning.

Dr. Martin is very knowledgeable about many topics in mathematics, and that shows in the classroom. Dr. Martin is very approachable, and willing to help during office hours. Some 30% of the grade was dedicated to attendance, and the projects don't require too much effort to be decent. The class seemed scary on paper, but Dr. Martin made it a snap.
Dr. Martian and the TAs were super helpful. He always did an awesome job explaining things the first time in lecture.

Decent amount of questions on math lab plus,  but not nearly as many as I hear other professors assign. Quizzes every week in recitation, but are fairly easy if you pay attention in class. Exams are defiantly way harder though.
His lectures are usually easy to follow, and he has a good sense of humor that occasionally provides some much needed comic relief. The quizzes are very easy, whereas the exams are very challenging.

He is not a very good teacher. Sucks at lecture and literally can not get through an example without messing up. He is a rude guy and has no idea how to teach to people who do not understand Calculus.

This is my second time taking the class. The first time around I had Dr. Jenkins.. needless to say their teaching styles vary greatly. Martin goes through the problems very slowly when you first learn them and is always eager to help. Bottom line, if you are actually trying hard in his class and respect him, he will respect and help you in any way.
Amazing man, he is absolutely awesome. Smartest professor that I have ever had. He is arrogant, cocky, and brilliant. He makes learning calc easy and interesting. 10/10 would love to have him again
Martin was not the best lecturer. He was also very sarcastic and wasn't that helpful outside of class. I suggest getting a tutor if you have him or go meet with the TA for help.
He was definitely not the nicest professor I've had.  The recitations and hw were the only parts that prepared me for the test, not his lectures. Tests were ROUGH.

Very good professor. Draws on his iPad for lectures, which was a little strange at first, but still easy to read. He skips over the easy/review parts of problems, which is good if you know what you're doing, because there's no time wasted. He comes thoroughly prepared and tells you only what you need to know.
Dr Martin was a great calc teacher.  does a lot of good examples in class.
Really knows what he is talking about. Doesn't try to make you learn pointless info. Arrogant and yet very funny. Not easy by any means.

I thought Martin was a pretty good professor! Calc II is not an easy subject, and he did a good job of going over everything that needed to be covered in an understandable way. The pace was quick simply because of the amount of material that needed to be covered.  There were no surprises on exams, we learned everything on them.
I thought he was a good teacher. kind of funny. Also, he is very willing to help outside of class.  Just remember calc II is hard in general so get SI help if you need it.
the lectures are worthless, no study material or any exam pre guide line. Very unhelpful in the beginning. recitation is much important than the lecture itself.

He is okay, very sarcastic and has a different sense of humor. I didnt find his notes to be helpful. The online homework was how i learned the topics right before the tests. He sometimes doesnt put curves on tests with an average of 60 because he gives extra credit, i think thats dumb.

I thought he communicated efficiently. He's not a NICE teacher, but he can show by example how to do math very well. He's not a hand holder. You have to try on the homework and look at examples to do well.

Overall he is an ok teacher not great by any respect but decent. The key to this entire class is SI! Martin will give you a pretty good foundation of the concepts(with A LOT of notes, I filled an entire 5 subject notebook)but SI shows you how you would actually apply the concepts and solve problems that would be on tests. Got an A(mostly b/c of SI)

I really don't like this professor. He is very arrogant and doesn't care about students. He doesn't provide any practice problems or old exams other than the broad homework assignments he gives you and expects you to just learn everything on your own. The tests are all written specifically to challenge engineering students and have many tricks
I really don't like this professor at all. He is very arrogant and doesn't care about students.

All the examples he writes are from the book, except the book does it better, all the derivations he does are from the book, except the book does it better. He is arrogant and he does not explain the material in a comprehensive way.

This was a retake for me, so maybe it's just because I already somewhat knew the material, but I thought he was one of the better math profs I've had. Sometimes came across a little condescending, but I don't blame him - this is usually a freshman course and he got a few dumb questions, which he did a decent job answering. I got an A.

He does not have a good delivery style for the information. He starts new problems without finishing old ones and does not understand why students have problems with the material. He is arrogant and does not like student involvement in classes.

Ryan was very good at teaching Combinatorics.  He knew the subject really well and it showed in his lectures.  His homework and test approach was very refreshing.  I learned a great deal in the course.  Not th easiest, but if you can do the work you will do well.

Martin was the worst professor I have ever had.  I had taken Math 165 at a community college and passed with a B.  I decided to take it again at ISU in hopes of getting an A.  All Martin did was teach you the basics then expect you to know everything on the final.  It says a lot when 69% of the class failed the final and the average was a 45%.

All Ryan Martin does it teach over your head and then screw you over on the test.  He will teach you decently but when it comes down to the test he will throw in tricks that you did not go over in class.  Altogether he is a mediocre professor at best and I advise that he be your last option for this class.
No Comments

Decent teaching ability. He doesn't seem to care about students or their concerns. Gets all fussy when people want to know "crazy" things such as class averages on tests, which were ridiculously hard (57% was average on them). As stated before, very arrogant. You will have virtually no idea where you're grade is at until you get your transcript.

Terrible professor.  Very arrogant and doesn't care about his students.  He would only give us grade updates when the entire class emailed him.  Students asked him questions during lecture and he responded "save that for recitation."  I will never take a class from this man again.  Possibly the most unhelpful professor I've had here.

He makes a course with extremely dry material a entertaining class to be at. Really livens up the class and really gets his point across in his teaching. A very clear professor who can visualize what he is teaching extremely well.

He'll come off as arogant, but he knows the subject and he teaches it well.  He'll tell you exactly what you need to do for his tests, but he's not going to give you practice problems for them.  Learn the theorems and you'll be great.  That's the only way to make the tests easy on yourself.
I think he's a considerate guy. Easy to work with and lots of extra credit.
He is very helpful outside of class.  He is always willing to answer questions, and encourages class participation.  His tests weren't too bad.

He is very boring, and unhelpful. He skips all around and leaves you confused. His quizzes and tests are fairly hard, but he will give you tons of partial credit! It's not hard to pull of a B; it's just putting up with him in the process.

Saxon is pretty great and funny, sometimes can be passive-aggressive if you mess up. Tests are all online (Quizlet), and the labs are not too long either. Mastercam homework does take a while, each assignment you get 2 weeks to complete, just don't procrastinate and you'll be fine. Don't go to lecture, you'll be fine reviewing slides on your own.

This guy is good. Lectures are good, homework is hard, and labs are long. But tests are online. Saxon once made a joke during a review session for our midterm that if we didn't know a question to google it, which I thought was funny. We had to write a paper once, and all he asked was to not ChatGPT "all" of it. Good guy, good class.
amazing 10/10 would take again. good material, actually learned something but wasn't drowning in work.
Saxon was very fun to have for class and always made little jokes and had fun with teaching. Show up to class, and ask questions when you are confused, and you will be just fine!
Great professor. Taught with passion and was very knowledgeable. Talked to you as a person
Took fluid power with him. Homework and reports kind of sucked, but he did a great job teaching. The labs were very hands-on and he explained things great.

Professor Van Ryswyk is such an amazing professor! She is so kind, relaxed, knowledgeable, approachable, and welcoming! I love her lectures, she is so interactive and educational while keeping the class light-hearted and enjoyable. I always love running into her on campus as well because she makes all of her students feel important and valued!

Jen is amazing! She really connects with the students. There were a lot of paper assignments with your chosen partner(s), but they were all very easy. She gives out in class assignments so make sure you come to class! Shes super understanding and genuinely cares for her students.

Jen is amazing. She makes the class fun and makes sure you understand. She is also good at giving examples so you better understand the concept. She also prepares you for the test and gives you multiple chances on assignments!

Jen was a great professor. She works as the administrator of the lab school, but does the lecture for this class. She is always willing to help and answer any questions and is extremely relatable. She is hilariously sarcastic (not to students but about funny situations) and is very down to earth. Definitely a great class.

Professor Smith is amazing! His lectures were fun and interesting, and you can tell he really has a passion for teaching. You definitely need to be prepared to study for his exams, but so long as you put in the effort in his classes, you'll get a lot out of them. Can't recommend him enough!
His lectures are well-paced in delivery and the content isn't all over the place; it's well organized. Also, he's a really nice and understanding, supportive individual.

LOVED his class! My fav. class at Iowa State! The tests have a lot of essays, but he gives you questions of the day every lecture and the essays correspond with those. Tophat questions during class. His lectures are so interesting I would recommend him! He is willing to help outside of class, and has review sessions.
Really interesting class and a great professor! Attendance wasn't required, but it was a really important component to understanding material.

He's too passionate about Calculus, and this could be a good thing, but he is quite obnoxious in recitation and makes it hard to focus. I guess it's good that he's passionate, but I don't personally enjoy his teaching style.

Good luck taking anything meaningful away from his lectures. Goes on tangents with topics irrelevant to the course material, skips steps in problems that leave the students puzzled, and poor time management of lectures. Broken record here but watch the butler videos instead or attend his lectures.

If I could go back in time and choose any other professor for calc 1, I would. The way that he lectures does not fit with how students can learn. After not even a month of lectures I would say attendance dropped roughly 60-70%. Of the 30-40% left in the class, I would say 3/4 of them were watching Steve Butler videos. Would not recommend.

Avoid this professor if you are wanting to take calc 1. He gets off topic during lectures, moves too fast faced, and will start a practice problem with only 2 minutes left of class. Many students in my lecture (including me) had to resort to watching Butler videos during class to understand the lesson.

Nice guy, but you're not going to learn much attending lectures. I haven't gone to a class past the third week of school and still have an A just from watching Steve Butler videos and doing the homework.
Professor Roettger can be hard to follow, but engaging with the class and using resources like Unstuck ai for study prep can really help. Attending lectures is a must to succeed.

After exam 1, I think my experience with roettger ends here. Lectures are confusing, he doesn't do a very good job of explaining the concepts. He goes off on tangents about things he claims are interesting but have no bearing on what you'll actually be doing in the class. He doesn't use class time very well. Go to Butler's lectures instead.
If you are in his lecture or recitation, just know you're cooked.

Super kind and caring guy, could tell he wanted everyone to succeed. Attending class is not mandatory but you will most likely get lost if you miss a day or two. Luckily he does post everything on Canvas and offers you opportunities to help improve your grade. Honestly a great and funny guy but paying close attention every class is a must.
Fanastic teacher, always went above and beyond expectations. cares a lot about his job!

Very irrelevant notes and lectures. Little was learned going to class and the notes didn't make sense so it wasn't worth going to class. Very few examples were given and homework answers were always a guess. He cares about his students but it was hard to succeed, had to study a lot for tests and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was an unnecessarily hard class. Took it thinking it would be a somewhat easy A. It was not. It lowered my GPA. I showed up to every lecture and did all the homework and at the end of the day I have no idea what I learned in this class. It was very disorganized and the examples on the test felt random and sometimes only vaguely related to lecture.

This professor can be hard to understand while he is going through the material for the lecture. You will have to pay attention very well. He is there to help with questions and makes sure to ask for understanding. I found some of the topics to be interesting but other a little confusing and unrelatable to the material on the test and homework.

I'm unsure if it's just my learning style being different than him, but this is the only math course I've had trouble understanding the concepts in class. He will explain something simple and somehow make it complex. My saving grace was honestly watching youtube teachers explain concepts. I got a good grade, but imho, it was harder than needed.

Organized course and super kindhearted. However, the topics discussed don't relate to the textbook. It's super confusing, make sure to show up to lectures and attend all SI sessions offered if possible. Tests aren't very long, but the questions are hard and sometimes don't relate to the textbook. A lot of the time, just examples he makes up.

Professor Roettger has been the worst professor I have had so far at ISU. He comes to lecture unprepared. He puts a blank sheet of paper underneath the projector and writes irrelevant notes taken directly from the textbook and sometimes only does 1 actual example per class. His writing is hard to read, and his accent makes him hard to understand.

While this professor is a funny guy and very knowledgeable, the lectures are obsolete to what is happening with the tests and homework. Nearly everything he covers seems random and doesn't follow any plan. Nor does he break down the steps of anything he does on the projector. TA's were the only way I got any decent grades, AVOID THIS CLASS.

This professor was not good. He promised he would write a final review guide, and then the Friday before the final changed his mind and did not give us one. He also teaches random concepts that are confusing to grasp and do not seem like he is following any sort of curriculum. Stay away from this class if you can!

As someone who has taken calculus, organic chemistry, and biochemistry, this class is horrible. Not hard concepts, but he manages to ask the most confusing and mind-boggling questions. If you are looking for a math credit to graduate and care about your GPA, I would advise you to avoid this class at all costs. Nice man and will help if you need tho

Professor Roettger is a good professor. His class is not difficult if you show up, most of the material is elementary math with a few added concepts. If you need help, he will go out of his way to explain concepts and to help you understand. He also takes any of these questions in class.

Professor Roettger is a great professor. I have him for my Math 104 class and he is a very caring person. If you are struggling in class he always makes sure that you can email him or go to his office during hours. He has bad handwriting so it can be hard to read but you can always ask him to clarify and he is happy to do so!

His class is easy concept wise you just have to pay attention. You will never do any more math than basic addition, subtraction, division, and multiplication in this class. He has sloppy hand writing and that does make it hard to take notes sometimes.
He was hard to understand and didnt seem like he even understood what he was teaching. He would get confused by his own notes and would get irritated anytime you asked for clarification

If there is anything you can do to avoid having Roettger, do it. It will save you many tears and frustrations. If you ask any questions he will just act like you do not know anything as well as barely explain on how he had gotten from point A to B. The only thing he will do to "help" your grade is dropping the two lowest homework grades.
Was not very good at explaining the material.

Thick accent, hard to understand,homework assignments not much time.Hard to follow lectures, doesn't explain how he gets from point A to B, get lost in the process.Handwriting is literally chicken scratch. Barely anyone shows up until it comes to test day. A lot was based on games like poker. To do good on tests, you need to know how to play those.
He gets super frustrated if you ask a question and he doesnt know how to answer it. His cover a lot of past lectures so If you dont understand a topic youre most likely gonna be lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In my opinion, he should not be a professor. His notes are taken like a 12 year old boy. They are not eligible and make no sense. He gives 0 feedback. I set up office hours with him because I was lost on the homework, and he picked fun at me when I was not able to answer his questions. He blames the grades on the student and takes no accountability

He is a nice guy, but cannot teach probability. It doesn't help that I can barely understand his accent, but he goes through the lecture way too fast, takes notes in chicken scratch, grades harshly, and gives no feedback. I do not recommend this professor. This class was supposed to be my "easy A" class, and it was my worst grade.

Prof Roettgers lectures sometimes feel like they were created last minute, and occasionally the lectures can get confusing. Hes otherwise a pretty solid prof. People saying the material was difficult or confusing probably shouldve spent less time talking throughout lecture. My class had a bunch of idiots that acted like they were still in HS

Professor Roettger seems like a genuinely nice guy. He is a terrible lecturer. He can't explain any of the class material and frequently makes mistakes and frantically jumps between topics. He'll forget several words while writing his barely readable notes out during lecture, making his sentences illegible. Luckily, participation was not required.

I really do think that Christian cares about his students and wants to help them. However, he is awful at explaining even the simplest of concepts and ends up making content way harder than it is. He hand writes everything and it is really hard to read. Be ready to learn how to do the math on your own. The class itself really isnt hard content.

He does not teach well. In math, you need to teach the content and not just provide students with examples and explain it in that sense. His English is not the best but it is understandable if you turn your ears on and it gets easier as the year goes on. Concepts are difficult but interesting.

Roettger is a great guy, but have him explain probability to you and youll be left even more confused. This class is easy IF youve learned probability in high school. Even then get ready to teach yourself. His wording on questions can be confusing, but if you follow the textbook you should be fine.

You can tell he cares a lot about his students and wants everyone in his class to succeed, but lectures are often confusing and difficult to follow. It was easier to learn the material in recitation rather than in lectures. Quizzes and exams make up most of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He genuinely cares about his students. He kinda just acts like a dad. I do feel bad sometimes because at the end of class he'll be talking still and people will be disrespectful and loud because they want to leave. Like, talking over him isn't required when you're packing your stuff up.

Get ready to teach yourself. He means well, but he seems like his level of education is too high for being able to clearly explain topics in this basic-level math class. He doesn't do well with having to explain problems in ways different than his original approach. There's homework once a week and the tests are a big percentage of your grade.

Professor Roettger means well&I think he's truly a nice guy. He's just not a great teacher. I had a really hard time understanding the lectures, and when he was asked to explain in a different way, he would get frustrated and tell us it was in the book or notes instead of helping in a different way. If ur up for teaching urself, this class is for u
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Just kind of rude how he addresses students with questions and over explains. His accent can also be hard to understand.
He means well, but he struggles explaining topics and often rambles.

Has a fairly thick accent that makes him hard to understand. Likes to use the chalkboard in class instead of more modern techniques. Does a descent job of explaining stuff, but you will still need to read in order to fully understand all of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Roettger means well, but he's just a bad teacher. Doesn't do a good job explaining topics and when you ask questions or go to office hours he goes off on lengthy tangents about things that have nothing to do with what you are asking him to clarify. Avoid at all costs even if it means taking an 8am. I got a B+ in calc 2 if that says anything...

I had Dr. Roettger for Calc III. It took about a week to get used to his accent, but once I had it down I had no difficulties understanding him. He can ramble at times, and be a bit unclear, but if you're unsure and you ask a question he'll usually clear it right up. He is always willing to make time for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: What a guy. He is an ok teacher but a genuine guy and he wants you to succeed. if you switch out of his class because of his rating SHAME on YOU.

I had Roettger for my Math 165 class and after reading some of these reviews, I was slightly worried going into the semester. He may not be the best at teaching the material, but if you stay on top of the HW and are prepared for tests, he makes it really easy to succeed in his class. Overall, Roettger is a really nice guy and his class is easy.

If you're great at calculus feel free to take Calc 1 with him. He's nice, but it's nearly impossible to learn from him if calculus isn't your strong point. He isn't clear in explaining and often leaves examples unfinished before moving on to some other topic you might not get. I passed only because the homework was really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Professor Roettger is a really nice guy who doesn't deserve such a low rating. He cares about his students and genuinely wants them to do well and get good grades. He is hilarious in class, and all the homework is online and helpful. The only downside is he sometimes explains things in an odd way.

Chris tries his best to teach this class. It isn't that he doesn't care, maybe his style just wasn't for me. Anyways, Calc III is essentially Calc II in 3D but easier. You've really got to try in this one but if you're coming from Calc II, it should be manageable. He shows you this cool tool for drawing the models online but I didn't try it at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Roettger is very, very intelligent. He knows what you're doing, and he's pretty good at giving real-world applications. I honestly thought I was going to get a B- in the class and ended up with an A so that was cool. It's difficult, but doable. Go to his office hours!! He loves it, and I'm pretty sure I got that A because he knew who I was!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class was very homework heavy. It's okay in the beginning when it's 25 problems on vector addition, but when you're expected to do 15 surface integral equations, you tend to start abusing MyMathLabs system. As for the rest of the class, tests aren't tough if you study the book, neither are quizzes. He is a nice guy and will root for you.

He can't explain a lot of concepts taught in class and just teaches from the book. Be prepared for him to not be able to answer your questions. Exams are challenging and you really have to work for your grade. He is nice as an individual, just not good with this class.
He does not know what he is teaching. His tests are nothing like the study guides. I wish someone would have told me.

Here's the thing. Christian is a really nice guy, but he isn't good at teaching Calc II. He will certainly help you to the best of his ability, but get ready to teach Calc II to yourself from the textbook and online resources. Unfortunately, he is simply not an effective teacher; but he is a very kind, very understanding guy.

This guy is a joke, avoid at all costs. He' by far the worst instructor I've had in 5 years of college. You can't understand a word he says. His writing on the chalkboard is anything but legible. On our first exam, 20% of the exam covefed material that was only taught in ONE of his THREE sections. He consistently has epicly offensive body odor.
He's the best grader you could ever get for a course. Like for the finals I was expecting a 70% instead I got a 89%. He's super nice and he really cares about us.

Nice guy, but lectures are pretty pointless. Recitation weekly is mandatory due to quizzes. The final study guide and the actual final didn't overlap in the slightest. TA's are the only thing that make the class even remotely bearable.

At Iowa State, Professor Roettger is the best math professor I have had so far. He is passionate about teaching Calculus III and he is great at finding REAL WORLD APPLICATIONS! Plus he made multiple Harry Potter references in class, which I greatly appreciated. Also he is the only calculus teacher I've found whose tests are reasonable!

This was THE best math class I have ever taken. Not only did the prof. try to make the class fun, he also tried to give real-life applications to the things we were learning, as can often be difficult to see on one's own when learning something like calculus.

I had never taken calculus before so I really hated this class. The professor is not clear and chooses poor examples. My TA was good and was the only reason I got good test scores. All the test averages were in the 50-60%. The material wasn't too difficult until the last couple chapters.

The problem is Roettger is that he's too smart and doesn't know how to communicate to freshmen learning calc for the first time. Seriously. Class is beyond easy if you took calculus in high school. Never went to lecture, but recitation is required, where you have a weekly quiz. Online homework is annoying, but helpful.

Professor Roettger is a terrible lecturer and is near impossible to understand. Luckily 151 is not a rather challenging course to begin with so if you end up with a reasonably good TA for recitation you will be fine. Don't bother attending lectures. Show up to recitation and keep with your homework and you will do fine.

Worst professor I have ever worked with. Entered in a test grade wrong and would not change it! Wouldn't even listen to me and try to help. Never take a class with him, hopefully he gets canned sooner rather then later!
He's the worst pro I have met ever, he had no idea what he was teaching on the class. Get out asap.

People complained because math is hard for them, and they blame it on the professor. Compared to the other math teachers, Roettger was far superior. His passion and humor inspired me. He is very helpful and understanding if a test was hard/you had trouble with the homework. Overall, a great prof!

Terrible. Writes on the chalkboard like a kindergartener, very disorganized, and makes mistakes while doing example problems on a routinely basis.  He also gets antsy and irate when someone asks a question.  I'm thankful we only had him for the first half of the semester.

Very friendly, albeit frazzled and eccentric. Uses examples from the book but spends time solving them on the board without referring to his notes. Weekly quizzes are straight off the homework. His tests are quite a bit harder than those of other professors, so you will have to actually learn the material to get an A. Make use of his office hours!
Horrible at being prepared for class.  Reads directly from book and gets confused even then.
Worst professor I've ever had. Gets confused on the examples he gets from the book. He reads the book like its a script. No point in going to class. Get a tutor or get out.

You can do well in the class even if you don't attend lecture. However, he has a generous grading scale, and he curves the exams as well. Be sure to do the online homework and do the practice problems in the book.
Roettger rarely teaches for tests and is difficult to understand at times. Prepare to teach yourself the material for big tests.

He has know idea what he is doing half the time.  He tries to do examples, but he always messes something up and he hardly ever finds what he did.  He doesn't do enough examples, and his finals are worth 40% of the grade!  Get out if you can.
Horrible professor! You will have a hard time with calculus three if you take it with him.

He seems to know his stuff very well, but he cannot relay that information to his students. I taught myself the class and did fine, his tests were not too bad. Definitely buy the textbook and try toughing out the first ten minutes of every lecture to get a feel where you should be.

Calling him a professor is probably not recommended. Does not write on board well. Also seems to be a little scrambled when it comes to thoughts and exlpainations. A good TA or SI leader will negate the need for him, not real reason for going to class. I don't recommend having him by any means. AVOID!
Try asking for help, he goes ballistic.rely on TA's and math help room

TERRIBLE! Seriously AVOID AVOID AVOID! He shows up to class 10 mins late every day. He took 40 mins to do 1 problem. We stopped going to lecture because he can't communicate what he is trying to teach. Also write on the board like a small child, so that's not helpful at all. TAKE THIS CLASS AT DMACC OR WITH ANY OTHER TEACHER....you've been warned!

Allllrighty. I'm sure he's an absolute genius, but he could NOT communicate calculus to my class full of business majors, nonetheless get us to care enough about it to want to understand.  He threw things at us that were way over our heads.  He had good TA's that made the class bearable, and learnable.  But he on his own did not.
He is sometimes hard to understand.  He writes on the board like a 5-7 year old would and I generally hated his class.  Try to find another professor, if it's the last thing you do!

Tests and quizzes were of adequate difficulty and reflected class material, he proved a lot of theorems that were not going to show up in homework or on tests, drew a lot of pictures to help visualize concepts, makes interesting sound effects to drive the points home, very fair grader and was open to hear any rebuttal a student had

Switch sections if you possibly can.  He says things like "I have a useful example but it's boring so we'll skip that."  Got a good grade, but the departmental final was hard cause he taught us so little.

I honestly liked his teaching style a lot. Just come to class and you'll learn, do the practice exams and you'll pass. He does seem to get off topic occasionally but he usually has a point. I passed and enjoyed this class even though my math skills are sometimes lacking.

I don't know why people don't like him, he is very knowledgeable and a good teacher. His exams are completely based on the lectures and they are fairly curved based on the performance of the class. You just need to do the homework to study for the class.

... Ugh! Get out while you can!! I am GREAT at Math, but this class made me feel like a failure. Don't get me wrong, he is extremely smart and seems to know what he is talking about. However, he has NO IDEA how to explain it to students!!!! His accent/ character is interesting but that's about it. Bail out, get  help, or hold on 2 yur sweet ass!
get out of this class if you can.
He's a little weird but super funny. His teaching style is different than most which is why some people have trouble understanding him. I loved him as a teacher though.

Very difficult to understand. He often goes on wild tangents and tests you on obscure theories. Attend SI and maybe get a tutor if you actually want to do well in this course. upside: his sound affects while teaching almost make class bearable

He is a very strange guy. Confuses himself A LOT. His test are completely different than what he teaches in class. Class is pointless to go to. He just rambles on and reads from his slides. He post homework whenever he gets around to doing it. If you have him I would recommend switching or plan on getting a tutor before you start his class.
He is a horrible professor and has very hard exams. Good news, he curves his class so much you'll pass with below a 50

The man can't explain why he does the things he does in class. I think his trouble is he expects calc to come naturally to everyone just because it comes naturally to him. I would avoid taking his sections if possible.

I liked him - his curve was very generous, and he worked hard after class every day to help me understand some tricky elements of DifEQ.  Lots of people didn't 'get' him, but basically he's got a lot of imagination and loves what he does.  Math geniuses are just quirky sometimes.
He knows his stuff, he's just terrible at explaining, lectures are useless

IF YOU HAVE THIS PROFESSOR, SWITCH SECTIONS. I am an honors student who was good at math but he made everything extremely confusing. He goes on about stuff you don't need to know and does not prepare you for tests at all. My SI leader even told us he makes up numbers for his answers when he cannot figure it out. NEVER TAKE CALCULUS WITH ROETTGER.
Smart man. Has no idea how to teach.

He knows what he is trying to teach but he just doesn't know how to teach. He is sometimes funny in class, especially when you point out a mistake he made while trying to teach something(happens A LOT!) Lecture doesn't help you to understand but the people in the class will explain it in a much better way that is easier to understand

Although he may know what he is talking about, he is HORRIBLE at explaining it. 9 out of 10 times you have no idea what this guy is saying. His tests are nearly impossible to do well on because the material is almost completely different from what he taught (or tried to teach). If you have him, GOOD LUCK! your going to need a lot of outside help.

I love a challenge, and, honestly, he delivered one.  Despite that there were no tests just quizzes, the homework was not graded, and attendance was not mandatory the material covered proved itself the devil. The secret to its exorcism are the SI sessions. Lectures did not help; reading the book did.  He also is quite funny in class.

I easily aced calc 1. 4 years later I retook it with this guy as a refresher before calc 2. I did everything a good student should do (attendance, homework, practice tests). Nothing prepared me for his exams. He tests beyond the scope of the class and has to apply insane curves so anyone can pass. Avoid this guy. You won't learn what you need to.
So confusing. Questions on his quizzes and exams do not reflect anything he teaches you in class. I would avoid getting him as a professor if you can.

I would definitely avoid getting him as a teacher. Going to class is pointless because he goes off on tangents that you can't understand. In general, he is hard to understand and always makes mistakes. He is smart, but has no idea how to teach a class. I don't recommend taking his class unless you're ok with teaching yourself the class on your own

I don't know what everybody is complaining about. He's really not a bad teacher. Calculus is a pretty damn confusing subject for a lot of people. If you don't ask questions, go to class, or talk to the professor during office hours, you can NOT expect to get a good grade. I took calc 3 with Professor Roettger and got an A- with a lot of studying.

I totally agree with what everyone has said. He is definetly out in his own little world and constantly makes mistakes on the homework and examples he does in class. The only plus about having him is the noises he makes when drawing graphs. YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED

Difficult to understand, Frequently goes off on tangents. Tests are extremely difficult, The class average was always in the D or F range. Does not explain concepts well.Definitely try to avoid getting him

I can not stress enough how everyone on here is right.  This guy is a very bad teacher.  He isn't clear in class, tests are hard, and he makes the weirdest noises that I have ever heard.  I do believe he is smart,  what I can not understand is why he is still teaching
Had to teach myself everything. if you are stuck with him check out the khan academy on youtube. that stuff is amazing

Half the questions on the exam are hard but legitimate -the other half are totally unexpected surprise extremely difficult and makes you want to pound your head on the table.  Hard to keep attention to him during lecture because he skips steps in his head while doing work, so it doesn't make sense to the average student.
everything that needs to be said has been said.  be prepared to be confused and be prepared to cry.  but just do the work, do your best and hope for an enormous curve!

By far the hardest class I have ever taken. Class average for the final was 36 percent. He is very smart, but terrible at teaching it. DO WHATEVER YOU CAN TO NOT TAKE HIM. He does not teach to the test at all. He skips steps and makes mistakes constantly. YOU DON'T LEARN ANYTHING. I have NEVER commented on a prof before but you need to be warned!!!

Professor Roettger knows how to do math; there's no question about it. However, he could not explain it to students to save his life. I feel like I actually unlearned math in his class, and did better when I didn't attend class.

If you don't go to class and keep quiet when you don't understand something he says, you're obviously going to get screwed in the tests. He covers in class exactly what you need to know and assigns homework in the same manner. But you need to study and go to class. His tests are no joke, but definitely doable with study. Plus there's a nice curve.

I have no doubt that Prof. Roettger knows his stuff when it comes to calculus, but he cannot convey it well to students.  There was little student involvment or interaction in his classroom: not a "hands-on" learning environment.

Awful. Absolutely one of the worst teachers I have ever had. I normally understand math with out question. He was very unhelpful when I had a question and generally confused me more. He is very eccentric and tends to get off task frequently.

He's impossible to understand. There's no reason to even go to class if you do you're wasting your time since he does almost every example wrong. I learned nothing in his class and should have switched. His tests are also way harder than any department midterm or final, good luck.
going to class is pointless, if anything just confuses you more.

This teacher is by far the worst I have ever had to date.  His exams are nothing like his assigned homework problems - if they are, he twists them and words them differently and will throw in the most complicated problems ever, so that you merely confuse yourself with what you once thought was correct.  He has a horrible tardiness problem.

My experience is that he comes into class and makes up a textbook from scratch. Very hard to follow along- often times during class an informal class survey showed that no one knew what was going on. Test were very hard and practice exams were unlike the real one.

Awful teacher. Very thick accent and hard to understand. He is constantly messing up on his own examples which causes great confusion. I would not recommend him to anyone. My class started out full and by mid semester 14 people would show up. He does not do a good job preparing you for material on tests either.

The class is easy, but only if you teach yourself the material. If you use the book and not pay attention in class you'll do better in the class. He can answer an occasional question, but gets flustered when we don't understand what he is saying. Has a very strong accent so can be hard to understand him. If you can try to get a different teacher.
Easy class, but he can't teach it that well.  If you have common sense then this is the easiest class, but he will confuse you the way he explains it. Read the book, and you will get an A.
No Comments

He is the worst teacher i have ever had, the class average on the final exam was 42% on a curve.  He gave practice exams that were totally different then the exam. He sucks at life. Get out of the class while you still can.

This guy can't be understood and he constantly makes mistakes on the examples that HE filled out. Students constantly correct him and class averages on tests were below %65 on a good day. Best advice, if you get a CD guide with your textbook, use that and don't pay attention to him.

I remember in the first test we took, out of about 220 students, 80 got a D or better. The next day about half the people dropped the class. As for lectures, extremely boring and his weird accent doesnt help. Tests are extremely hard. DO NOT TAKE CLASS WITH THIS GUY.

His intentions are good and he really wants you to learn, but he just isn't very good at being clear about what he is talking about.  He is nice and tries to be helpful but cannot always explain things in a meaningful way.  You would think that elementary math would be easy, but it was not.

This class absolutely blows.  He makes easy trigonometry impossibly hard.  You MUST avoid this proff.  He makes practice exams for the tests and they are COMPLETELY different.  He once made a test so hard that the class average (about 100 ppl) was a 47% and he even recieved an e-mail from his teaching assistant saying that prob. #17 wasn't workable

He is a horrible teacher,basically he doesn't teach, yet he is teaching americas teachers how to.  You do better in the class by just reading the book, not by going to class.  The tests are a joke.  Nothing like the homework!!
No Comments
No Comments
This guy is a joke... Terrible  If it was up to the professors in this math department the majority of us would fail our math requirements!
horrible, just horrible
HE TEACHES MATH ON POWERPOINT!! PISS POOR TEACHER FIND SOMEONE ELSE!! DIDN'T LEARN MUCH
No Comments
No Comments
If you get him DROP the class right away! I got better test scores when i skipped lecture for 3 weeks than when i accually went to lecture. Makes no sense in lecture and can't teach.

I think im the only person that laughs during lecture at his constant graph sound effects. Comedy aside this guy need to find out what hes doing wrong and fix it. One test averaged a 30%. Can't teach, about half the class goes to lecture. Don't take his classes, find ANYONE else. Go to SI it rocks!
very unclear in lecture
he sucks

Ohh my god.  I never seen a teacher who could actualy make you learn less that what you did before.  It is better to go to friends and peers to get help and to teach you the subject.  The only thing that I learned from the class was how to use to word ZWOOP.  The good thing is you get a g  oood nap.

horrible horrible teacher. can't understand what he's saying, homeworks problems are the hardest in the book but still not as hard as the ones on his tests. he said in class that the test is the only time he can reward creative thought, so you get screwed hard on the test. 10 questions worth 100 pts
Not good at all.  Bad speaking, poor teaching, period.

Makes his real test about 10 times harder than homework and the practice tests. So you think you know the material and when the test comes you don't. If you can't get a different teacher, just hope you do good on the mid term and the final because you probably won't go good on his tests.
Roetager cfan't speak very good english so you find yourself struggling to understand what he is saying and not what he is teaching.

Professor Roettger is a nice guy, but he has trouble teaching and making clear what he is trying to get across in class. Also the tests were much harder than any of the homework or example problems discussed in class. Unless you've had calculus before you might want to look for a different teacher.
No Comments

He's very excited about graph theory.  He has a good grasp on his subject, and gives good feedback.  Sometimes when he's lecturing he can stumble a little.  I can imagine that he would have some trouble with a large class.
Bad teacher

Picky professor, flies through lecture slides. Attendance is 140 points of your grade, if you miss class he does not post any notes. Requires you to come to class on Friday's for labs when they can be done easily outside of class. Very stuck in his way for him to a younger professor. Passes out activity sheets like we're 5 years old.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An interesting class into development and globalization. Professor Mindes made the class interesting with assignments that were thought provoking and original. Week to week assignments were fairly easy. Be prepared for A LOT of reading and time sensitive exams that are somewhat difficult, as well as detailed papers every unit. Overall great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took SOC 310 and SOC 302 with him! He's funny, sarcastic, and very smart. Buy textbooks because the questions on the quizzes are directly from the reading, quizzes are timed, so don't mess around. Tests are open note/book but are hardish. Go to class! All the important stuff is said during his lectures, and he grades on attendance.

Actually took SOC 302 but it wasn't listed here? Anyways Dr. Mindes is great he makes boring material fun and engaging. Lots of in-class activities, used Pokemon to teach sampling methods. Tests and quizzes are open book/note but kinda tough. Assignments were easy. Actually takes the time to get to know his students, knew everyone's name by week 2.

He's funny and sarcastic, which makes him personable. He can be a tough grader on certain things so make sure you aren't giving half the effort. This class needs a textbook because all the reading quizzes are from textbook info but I found an online PDF version so you don't need to buy one! No exams, just a TON of group work.

Professor Mindes was a very experienced teacher for this course. He has lots of knowledge on the topics covered. Lecture attendance was mandatory and the actual lecture portion was easy to understand if you are interested in the topics. Be sure to study for the exams tho!

Really awesome professor thats super personable and really respects his students. His lectures are not the most interesting but he really tries to keep students involved and throughs in some humor here and there which is really cool. Overall, one of the best professors at Iowa State just due to the face that he is super relatable and cool.

I question why we pay to take this class all she does is tell us to read the book. If you ask her a question she tells you to look at the book. In the first 8 classes we had she taught for 2 of them, the other 6 were quizzes on the book. She has taught for 25% of lectures. Very disappointed with the IE department and that they think this is okay

Ryan struggles to a explain a concept when you already understand it and know the answer. She manages to confuse herself as she speaks about statistics and can hardly convey what she means to a lecture, if she even gets it herself. One of the worst lecturers I've had.

Dr. Ryan is a nice prof and she really understands those things. Her lectures are kind of simple and content is pretty hard. But after that, you will find you gained a lot. Work hard and harvest a lot
Dr. Ryan was a great professor! I think a lot of people give her a hard time because they simply did not deserve to pass their stat course and they find out very quickly why in this course.

Dr. Ryan is a fine professor. Her slides are extremely concise (you are saving a lot of trees by taking her class) and, even though she doesn't explain the material very well, she is extremely accessible. If you know basic stats, you will get an A. Simple as that.

This class is hard in general. Make sure you do the assigned homework and practice exams and attend lecture in order to do well on the Quizzes and Exams. On the bright side, you do get to make a sheet of notes to take into exams and the class has a very nice curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If you get Dr. Ryan for IE 413, RUN. The class is tough, because it is a 400 level class, but the way it is taught and the structure of the class is awful. Several kids will not graduate in December 2017 or May 2018, because they have to wait until fall of 2018 to retake the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr Ryan's IE 413 class at 8 am is a good place to take a nap before you go to your 9 am class. 6 more weeks until finals and I don't think I have a good grasp of what this class is even about and why should I care.
Barely listen to what she talks about lectures.
Very sweet, genuinely cares about helping students
Great Professor!

Why take Ambien when you can listen to a Sarah Ryan lecture? I was hoping for Sly (good teacher) and got Ryan. Still had high hopes for learning but those were crushed after realizing she had no idea how to teach. If you want to learn engineering economics read Yahoo Finance on a daily basis. Don't waste money paying for what you'll teach yourself.

Sarah Ryan (Dr. Ryan as she calls herself)is more interested in what scarf she will wear to class than she is in teaching. Maybe this is because she knows nothing about the subject or she just sucks at teaching in general.  She has the most monotone voice ever. She would be better off teaching a class about proper scarf wearing techniques. Awful.

Lectures are fairly dry, but that is probably due to the subject (it's hard to make Engineering Economics exciting).  She acts put out when you ask for help outside of class.  The class is hard simply due to the harsh grading.

Not that difficult of a teacher.  Kind of annoying and boring which is probably the reason for most of the complaints.  Stay on top of the homework and the tests will be cake.  Fall behind or slack...well, that's a different story.

She does treat students like its a elementry class. Dont try and leave early!  BUT the material was not too hard. Most of it common sense. Lectures were boring but useful later when I could print them out and study.

not a extremely hard class if you do the homework and attend.  worthwhile for any engineer to learn about the other side of business.  to anyone who thinks otherwise: enjoy doing the same job in front of your computer for the rest of your life!

I was hoping on getting the other prof for this class, but ended up getting this ding-bat.  Reminds me of elementary school.  She looks like an elemenatary teacher, dresses like one, and treats the class like it is 2nd grad.  Couldn't stand her.
fine for first 3 months, then really hard for 3 weeks

Material is easy if you can go to class/read the book or anything related to it with out jamming a pen in your eye. It is the most boring thing I have ever done in my life!!! Very hard to study or even concentrate on anything for this class just out of plain lack of interest and boringness.

Dr. Ryan runs lecture like a kindergarten class.  She insists on using every last precious second of class time even if she has no material to cover- so we sit there watching her START an example problem that nobody cares about, which she never actually SOLVES.  Her lectures are just plain awful.
One of the worst teacher I have had at ISU.  The material isn't too bad but her lectures are extremely booring!!!

Lectures are dull, but "pop" in-class exercises mean u need to go.  Material's pretty easy, there's a project that's a pain in the butt, but as an engineer this class definately takes a back seat to more important ones.  TAs are really helpful.

I had Shelby for MATH 1960, and she was great! The course is a bit more difficult than 1950, but it is definitely manageable, especially if you stay on top of homework. Shelby does a great job at explaining each topic and keeping everything organized. She is very kind and willing to help if you are confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: MATH 1960! Shelby is GREAT! She is really great at answering questions and explaining things in multiple different ways if you don't understand.  Sometimes things can get a little slow because they are things you have done in the past.  It is quite a bit of homework but pretty manageable I think. Attendance is mandatory and you do get points for it
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was very enjoyable! Shelby makes each lesson easy to understand and is very easy to reach outside of class. There is homework every class, but it is very doable and is hardly ever busy work. The practice exams for each test were very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shelby is such a good math professor. Her style of teaching is VERY helpful, and most students will not need to study very hard outside of class. The information sticks with you, and she makes math enjoyable!

Shelby is very accessible outside of classes, and I would recommend going to study hours the day of a quiz or exam to go over more material. She explains all of the course work really well and as long as you do your best to meet with her you will succeed.

She is the best professor I've had yet. Extremely caring and willing to work with you outside of class if needed. In class, she gives great explanations and makes what could be difficult easy to understand. Math 195 isn't hard if you show up and actually try. The study material (practice tests) is really helpful, so be sure to take advantage of it

You'd think that elementary math would be easy, but it's much more complex than one would think. Shelby assigns a lot of work nightly, and it's often graded based on accuracy rather than completion. There are 3-night exams that are mandatory and make up over half of your final grade. Attendance is crucial for this class.

reviews.comment: Shelby explains the criteria very well, going in I thought it would be an easy class and it turned out to be pretty complex. Study and pay attention. reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Shelby is such an amazing professor. The class starts of easy but the topics gradually get more complex. Go to class and do the homework otherwise you will be lost, but she is extremely accommodating when the circumstances present itself.

I took this class online but there are weekly Zooms. There are 3 major exams which can be difficult but doing homework and taking weekly quizzes really helps you understand the material. There were Zoom classes on M/W and then Friday was a video lecture and 1 point quiz (which could be done anytime Wednesday-Sunday each week).

This has been one of the only math classes I have actually understood and enjoyed. She really cares about your learning and understanding of the material and will work outside of class time with you. One of the best math teachers I have ever had.

Shelby. Is. AMAZING! I am an education major and took Math 195 with Professor Shelby Schmidt. She makes things make SO MUCH SENSE! I feel pretty confident in math, but even those who didnt feel confident loved her and we ALL learned so much. Shelby utilizes all learning types well. Shes very thoughtful about how she words things. You WILL LEARN!

Shelby has made my math experience a great one, and I highly recommend taking MATH 195 with her. It's clear she's eager to help you succeed. She thoroughly explains problems, assigns homework that directly relates to the content of the class, and always talks about how wiling she is to meet during her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: There is a lot of busy work and homework every night for this class, but if you show up and do the homework and in class activities you will be fine. Shelby is so sweet and kind and really tries to make the class enjoyable. She puts a lot of time and effort into helping you succeed! Also she always had tests graded by the next day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great Prof, once you get to know her and her style/ grading style, you'll respect her even more. She definitely wants her students to succeed. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor.  At first she was a little difficult to read but once you get to know her you will find that she is very caring and easy to work with. Christopher Sean Scott is a very structured, direct, and provides a lot of in-class work time. His Typography II class allows good room for creativity, and he checks in with you every class to see if you have any questions or need feedback.
Amazing teacher, talks a lot but if you listen to him he gives great advise and amazing ideas for you to explore in you're work. Super kind and understanding.
Chris was a very good professor for my class he was very easy to talk to and explained every assignment in depth. I got a 100% in his class he graded very easy. Good guy

He lectures for an hour in almost every studio and repeats what he says thrice. He has not graded a single assignment but has strict due dates. He seems to lack basic software skills and is very egotistical. Personally, I would never take him again.

While it was tough at the beginning of the semester, he seemed to learn along the way and got a lot better towards the end of the semester. His lectures are long but he always cares about the work you show him and seemed to care about each student individually. 
Definitely don't listen to the negativity and form your own opinion instead.

His class makes me actually want to kms

reviews.comment: Do not take any course of his. Incredibly large ego, does not teach, doesn't believe in giving A's, and just generally frustrating. The workload is intense but also pointless.

She's ok. EVS 120 is just not very good at signaling what you need to know for the exam, studying is a lot of guesswork. Assignments and quizzes are fairly easy, but the exams are what can really screw you over.
This class is pretty simple, however the tests get a lot harder as they go on. Make sure you review some of the seemingly random details for the second half of the course.

So sweet and loves teaching! The exams are very easy, and the content is incredibly interesting. The class covers all aspects of ecology and addresses a lot of global issues that I found fascinating. There a few homeworks with a few in class group assignments, and several exams.
I wonder how someone like her has a phd
One of the worst lecturers in the whole world
So difficult and boring

she's the worst doctor in ISU
