reviews.comment: One of the worst lecturer in ISU. I wish if they thought carefully before they hired her.

This lecturer is so disrespectful. It's a shame that ISU has someone like her as a faculty member. 
Her lectures are boring and she doesn't know how to explain the materials.

Highly recommend Dr.Schieltz! Very knowledgeable and teaches in a clear direct way.  Loved hearing her opinions and stories about the content.  The class has lots of lectures but some slides are very specific statistics, graphics, and photos that will randomly appear on the tests.  It is very difficult to study for this course, she is great thou.
Dr. Schieltz is good at explaining difficult things. I learned a lot.

Very good professor, she is good at explaining things so you can fully understand them. My only criticism is that the tests were very specific so if you did not write down all the specific percents listed in lecture you could end up missing points on the test. Overall there are few assignments outside of class so it was not too intensive.

Some assignments in class, so show up even though attendance isn't mandatory. Easy points if you pay attention and participate. Schieltz is engaging and entertaining, so just show up and be ready to learn and should be easy enough to pass.

Professor Schieltz has fantastic lectures and really knows what she is talking about and can answer most if not all questions you ask her about the class. Very caring and understanding, so if you show up to class and pay attention, you should have no problem passing, as well as enjoying her classes
This class is super easy. She is super nice and knowledgeable. The class is set up well. The homework assignments aren't difficult but you definitely do learn a lot. very fun

She was very clear in lectures and had some class participation, but not anything too much or annoying. The slide shows she taught with were nicely laid out and always made available either before or right after class. Only 2 or 3 group projects, but they were very simple.

She was very nice and would make a few jokes here and there.The exams are fairly easy if you pay attention in class and do the lecture quizzes. You do have to take a few days to study because a lot of information is thrown at you and anything can be on the test. She does tell you when something is important to know for the test though.

Dr. Schieltz is an okay lecturer. Knows the material pretty well. Doesn't budge on extending due dates though, so don't expect any leniency. She isn't as fun as the other professor, Mike. She also adamantly prefers to be referred to as "Dr. Schieltz", so do not refer to her as anything else. Might take again. Not my favorite, not the worst.

Lecture quiz for each lecture, 3 questions each. One assignment a week, some in-class and some out of class, unless there's an exam. Work in groups for some in-class assignments. Exams are around 150 points, once or twice a month. A few extra credit opportunities. About everything is available on Canvas. She's very knowledgeable and nice.

I really enjoyed this class! There were regular homework assignments but the consistency was really nice, especially for an online class. I would recommend this class to a friend- my only regret is that it wasn't in person. I think I would have enjoyed the face-to-face interaction a lot more, but that is completely out of anybody's control!

Jennifer is one of the best professors Ive ever had. She is so caring and passionate about what she teaches. I loved every second of her course. The exams are really easy, but you need to take notes and write down the side points, as those are always on the exam. I would take every class Jennifer teaches if I could.

I thought this class would be easy. It is purposefully NOT. It's one of the most boring classes. Professor is nice but the exams are hard. Professor uses even the last second of class time to lecture which makes it unbearable. Tophat is not just participation but you actually have to get the answer right which is not fair when it's a new lecture

I would totally take a class with Jennifer again. When I had a personal circumstance come up that interfered with the class, she was more than willing to work around it with me and help find a solution to fit my needs. Class was not too hard if you just do the work. Has an interesting perspective to share as well in class

Jennifer is not quite as fun as her counterpart Mike, but I still had a good time taking class with her. She makes an effort to make the content understandable and relevant to our lives. It is easy to tell she is passionate about nat. resources. Beware tho, she does love TopHat, so be prepared to show up to class.

Pretty good lecturer, really knows what he's talking about. Exams were essay tests, and a couple of the questions were difficult to determine what he wanted. Seems tough to get an A, he says this himself, so if you're thinking of taking this to fulfil a culture credit or whatever you might want to take an easier class.
Braun obviously cares about his studies, but did nothing to help, respond to emails, or provide any sort of instruction on assignments.

Dr. Sebastian Braun is one of the best and most knowledgeable professors I have had during my time in school!
His lectures, while long, are incredibly informative and thought-provoking. Also, his accent is very fun!! Be ready to leave his lectures contemplating your place and purpose in the world(in a good way).

Dr. Braun exemplifies what it means to be a collegiate level professor. The style of the class can be confusing, but once you complete an assignment and discuss in class, the criteria for success become evident. One of the benefits of this class structure is the discussion format which allows a deeper understanding than otherwise would be achieved.

Finals and paper are worth more than 50% of the grades. Didn't give me any feedback for my finals or paper. Criteria is not explained well. He doesn't post notes so you have to go to every lecture. A LOT OF READING. 60 pages a week on average and 100 pages to read some weeks. I would not take this class again ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grades harshly and gives extremely vague instructions on every assignment. Gave about 3 guidelines for our final, a 15-20 page research paper. Don't expect a response if you email him, even multiple times. From experience, expect to be reading and writing about 5x more than you would for a class like English 250. Always has HW due over the weekend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and passionate about his content area. You must go to every lecture and take good notes to get a good grade. He is a very tough grader and his criteria are fairly unclear, but you should be fine as long as you take good notes and write good essays. Great guy.

Dr. Braun's teaching style depends on you being at the lecture and taking notes on what he's saying. He doesn't have lecture slides for you to take notes on. He is very unclear about what he wants and it harms a lot of students. Suggest going in during office hours to discuss what he expects and do it early in the semester. Also attend the lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All we did in this class all semester was hold discussions that were vaguely about what we were reading - we read 5 books this semester :( - I feel like I didn't learn anything about anthropology other than how to write to meet Dr. Braun's mysterious standards that were never fully explained to us. Really not a fan of this class.

If you are interested in Native Americans he is very knowledge and his 2 hour lectures go by extremely fast. Super nice and fun guy. However, do not expect to get a good grade. He wrecked my 4.0 GPA (a STEM major) as his final and exams are out of 15-20 points and questions are EXTREMELY confusing. If you don't care about your grade, take the class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Braun's passion for American Indian studies comes through in his lectures. There are weekly readings with a response on a discussion board. He shared facts, and gave context for what occurred without making political or social commentary. Think critically about what you've learned. The tests were quite simple if you paid attention in class.

I thought this professor was great... At first. Then we get to the exams, and as someone who gets 100 percent on every assignment. I get an F on BOTH exams. Which are worth 50% of his grade in some insane world. This screams to me, professor grades completion on assignments and decides he cares on exams just to fail the students he failed to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Braun was one of the most respectful, dedicated professors I ever had. His knowledge on the Native American culture, and his drive to teach us students everything that he could about their culture/relationship to land, was incredible. This class has heavy reading and writing (4 books, two essays and weekly discussion). Not an easy A class.

Boy let me tell you, as someone who doesn't read alot, I think I've made of for it because of this class. I've never had to read so many boring books before in my life. I have no idea what is going on or what is getting graded, but we were taught in the first week that science isn't real. All i'm saying is if you don't have to take this class don't
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

This class really makes you think and it's overall very interesting.

Do not take a class with Professor Braun! I cannot stress that more as he is not only incapable of teaching but also incapable of talking to students in a respectful manner. RUN AWAY

What should have been an easy introductory class turned into a nightmare. Lectures do not cover any relevant materials and the textbooks are useless. Probably one of the best professors out there! Loved his lectures.
Didnt seem very open to disagreement. You do well if you agree with him

Great professor, very highly respected. However, the class is very reading heavy and there are quizzes almost everyday. You HAVE TO attend class. I am an Elementary Education student and I think this class is more geared toward English majors. Would not recommend if you are El Ed but overall a great English class if you are willing to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is a great prof and makes ealry american lit so much more fun to learn! He has great humor and is very reasonable about his test/quiz structure! Great proffessor!! one of the best ive had in the engl department

reviews.comment: Professor Sivils is a really funny guy, even during 8 am's. He makes English classes interesting. Show up, read, and the rest is easy. There are plenty of pop quizzes, but they are over very short readings. He will help you immensely with papers--just bring them in beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is one of the best classes i've taken here at ISU. He's hilarious and explains the material very well. His test are easy if you take the time to prep for them because he gives you time to look over the test a week before. You only get 3 absences and the 4th one he drops your grade 10%, so show up. His class is interesting so it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This was an okay class with a TON of reading. Class discussions were good some days and pointless others; several films were shown which felt like a waste of my time. Grading policies were unclear and quizzes were 60% of the grade; however, quizzes were not regular and were pass fail which makes it hard to gauge your progress as a student.

Be ready to read is an understatement. Daily quizzes, but questions are just pulling obvious details from the readings. Tries hard to get discussions going and doesn't call on just the same people all the time. If youre struggling he WILL help you. Participation is mandatory to a point he understands people are shy. If he sees you trying youre good
There was a lot of reading which means long essay tests but he was great! Always made me laugh and very approachable if you had a problem!
I took English 201 and it was all about crime novels, every book was interesting and it made it easy to read and keep up in class.
Great professor. Very willing to help any student or discuss any questions further. Down to earth and clear. Tries to relate material to modern day. Recommend to anyone needing an English class.
He's a good guy that cares about his students and wants them to do well. Really good guy to have if you are writing a dissertation. Highly published and respected.

This class was challenging, as he actually expected us to work! I learned so much about writing and literature from this class and he made it entertaining. It was a hard class for me, but I am so grateful I took it.

This was a survey of Early American Lit. He was incredibly knowledgeable, but absolutely terrible at keeping class interesting. We read the works and he talks at us about them. He does not supply rubrics or any indication of what he requires on assignments and/or presentations and grades them incredibly hard.
Please give this man an award. Encouraging, affable, and an expert in his field. I keep feeling like I'm learning something, even though he's often not explicitly teaching. Fantastic professor.

There are instructors who are overly pedantic to feed their own ego and then there are instructors who can be humble and explain concepts on your level. Dr. Selim falls into that category. Super likeable, personable guy who's super easy to get a hold of outside of class. Doesn't talk down to students and is straight forward with course expectations

This is a man who you can tell from day one loves what he does more than anything. He loves engaging with his students and is generally fair with exam questions. Lectures are easy to understand and fairly straightforward although I had a lot of prior knowledge going into his class so I can't speak for new comers.
Go to class. HW takes a little. Labs are fine not too difficult. Selim is a fair guy at the end of the day but it takes some work.

Make sure to go to your labs as this is worth a lot of your grade and it helps you understand the implementation of the course. Start thinking of a final project idea early as you have to design your own project.

Professor Selim is a very gifted lecturer. Every class was well put together and engaging, and he frequently stopped for questions or audience participation. Everything was explained very well -- new topics were easy to understand, and even if you were familiar with the concept you'd learn some new interesting facts about it.
One of the best profs @ ISU. He is very knowledgeable! Highly recommended.

His lectures were clear and made sure alot of us understood the concepts during lecture. If we didnt, he was easily accessible after class for understanding. The labs to me were challenging but fun to me! The only issue is I wish the instructions for certain things were more clear but other than that Selim is a good professor and fun class.

This is for CPRE 437 but I didn't find it on the list so I chose the nearest course (431). This was the 1st time to be offered but so far Selim went above and beyond. I gained the needed experience in wireless and the important security protocols in these networks. The lectures were heavy but he cares about helping students understand the material.

You must take CPR E 281 with this guy. He handles this huge course (4 credits) well and is so clear. He genuinely cares that every student understands each slide! he is quick to respond to emails and gives many resources to help you complete your work without giving you direct answers to HW questions. Overall, I would take a class with him again.

CPRE 281 is one of the hardest classes however Dr. Selim is one of the best lecturers and was able to go through lots of material patiently and in the easiest way possible. He is also good at answering questions and is available outside the lecture time. TAs were also very helpful during labs especially Nazar who taught the recitations v. well.

This is my second course with Selim. He knows how to grab our attention during an online lecture by asking multiple questions during the lecture. His exams are difficult if you don't study, otherwise, you will find them easy. He encourages us to ask questions & dedicate enough time outside the lecture to answer any remaining questions. RECOMMENDED!

Selim is the best. He is very caring and always is very patient in answering students' questions. His lectures are amazing. He's very good at explaining. I took his class online, and it always feels like he is teaching from a war zone. You can hear baby crying, car honks, and people yelling from his Zoom background noise. Pretty funny.

Great lectures for the online class that allows you to learn the basics of information system security. Excellent TA for fall 2021 semester, very knowledgeable and willing to help. Projects are interesting and you get to choose your own topic which is cool. Willing to accommodate for students as well. Great class and great professor.

I would say Selim is the best professor at ISU. He always cares that every student understands everything in his slides. He stops from time to time to wait for questions, in addition, he dedicates 20 minutes after each lecture for questions only (an hour per week in addition to his regular office hours). I strongly recommend any class he teaches.

Selim is one of the best professors at Iowa State. He teaches the class very well, encouraging questions and making sure everyone understands before moving on. He is also easy to communicate with and offers lots of extra credit opportunities.

Selim is probably the best professor at iowa state. He explains topics very thoroughly and give lots of examples. He is very willing to answer questions and even saves time after lecture dedicated to only questions. He also gives lots of extra credit and is a nice guy in general

I like to refer to him as Goatlim because he is such a good prof. You can tell he's passionate about the topic and that makes his teaching so good. He always answers questions and tries his best to make the learning environment the best I can possibly be.
Passionate about computer engineering and great sense of humor. Show up. Pay attention. He picks great TAs as well so if he can't help you one of them surely can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I just wanted to thank Dr. Selim for the time and efforts he put into making this course smoother. I honestly enjoyed this class and I learned quite a lot. The TA's were beneficial as well. I would recommend to anyone to take this course with Dr. Selim he is a really very good instructor. I like him using Discord for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was a great professor and cared about the topic. Was very willing to teach and was always answering any questions, no matter how simple or complicated. Typed out the code in class and went over it making sure we understood the material. Only issue was the tests were a little hard.

I enjoyed taking this class with Dr. Selim. We have to read before each class but Zybook is a nice interactive book to read from. Also, the group assignments and projects were fun and beneficial. Recorded lectures are a big plus and organized in a nice way. Discord server made it easy for us to interact with him and the TAs. I highly recommend this
Selim was an amazing teacher, while his tests were hard he taught everything very well. Team-based projects worked very.

I really enjoyed taking this class with Dr. Selim. He was very understanding of difficult situations and graded assignments, tests, and labs within a week and the projects within 2-3. His lectures were engaging to watch since I really enjoyed the material in them.

Dr. Selim used Zoom for lecturing and he was engaging us by asking questions every few slides and asking us to reply via Zoom chat. This kept me engaged in every single lecture. In addition, he stays around 30 minutes after each lecture until answering all students' questions. His exams are not easy not hard (just right). Best online class!

This is the senior design course so Dr. Selim and Dr. Maruf were mainly managing around 60 projects. Both Dr. Selim and Dr. Maruf were very flexible and available. Dr. Selim really cares about his students and very responsive via email. I already took 3 courses with him until now and would advise everyone to take whatever courses he teaches.

Selim was the instructor for the senior design course. Although there is no teaching in this course, Selim managed the class very professionally especially after the migration of the course to online instructions due to COVID-19. I would like to thank him for curving the IRP grades and also for the bonus assignment at the end of the semester.

I'm writing now because I saw a bad review and want to put my 2 cents in. Selim is a very good professor and he cares about the students. Some students don't like team based learning, others are not collaborative which can affect their team's perforamnce. I enjoyed the class and the amount of programming practice that we did all over the semester.

I still didn't receive my final grade but until now I have A-. Selim gives a lot of bonus points that compansate any points lost in exams (two midterms and one fonal). There is a group final project by the end of the semester which is relatively hard. He was the best professor to deal with the online migration compared to my other classes

This class is taught in Team based learning which is awful. You're expected to teach each other which does not work. The class is fine, but just dont take it with this professor. If you take it with this professor there is no dropped exam, an extra lab, Team-based learning, and a final project.

I took this class in its first round of Team Based Learning. Selim tried his best and that was obvious, but the material was just too much for 50 minute class periods, always beginning with a 5 question team quiz and ending with not enough time for an "application activity" with a group. I changed my major after taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I did the TBL version of this class. It was run well, and the class was structured in a way so that learning was at the forefront. However, if you got a bad group, good luck trying to learn well. It's possible, just hard. Mohamed was very receptive to feedback and made the students know he cared about their learning. Overall, a good experience.

Selim was a good instructor. This class was taught as team-based learning, as long as you get decent team members it's very beneficial to discuss. There are weekly reading and a lab so you'll definitely have to commit a chunk of time to the class. There were often errors/typos in quizzes and assignments but gave you full points if pointed it out.

He's a nice guy and his slides are good, but his exams are memorizing 600+ slides. He refuses to give practice problems or reviews because this is a 400+ level course so we shouldn't need any help. If you spend a week studying to memorize every nook and cranny of the slides you'll be fine. The homework is easy enough.

Dr. Selim is clearly passionate and knowledgeable on the subject. He is always welcoming us to ask questions. Unfortunately, it was difficult for me to stay engaged in lecture due to the nature of the content (it was very easy to just read the slides before homework, quizzes and exams). Further, the average on the one midterm exam was a 90%. Crazy

Selim is a great professor. Compared to my other classes, his class was the best. He is running team-based learning but at the same time, he is putting a lot of effort to make sure that everyone is understanding the material. I definitely will take his other classes. He told me he is also teaching CPRE 281 and CPRE 431.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: SE185 is a team-based learning course, which is just a terrible idea for an entry-level coding class. But that may not be Mo's choice. But he still isn't good. He very obviously uses code for graded problems that he doesn't prepare himself, and it is full of errors and typos. The online homework is really nice and is probably the only you'll learn.

A great professor, hes genuinely interested in teaching students and enthusiastic about what he teaches. Online homework twice a week and mini group projects each lecture class, but if you have a good group youll be okay.

Selim is a great teacher. Informative and effective in lectures. Sometimes he goes a little long, not giving enough time for groups to finish the in class assignment but usually graded accordingly. The class is formatted in team-based learning, so there a lot of group assignments in class, as well as multiple assignments each week online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really great guy, he's a very caring teacher and does pretty well with the short time he has to lecture. The homework is difficult and I had to work outside of class with a tutor, but there's just a ton of material to cover in this class and it's not easy. Professor Selim does what he can and I def. would look forward to another class from him.

There's a lot of homework. It has almost zero weight and usually doesn't take too much time, but making a habit of doing it well is really important. I've seen many people try to get around some of the homework by guessing/skipping multiple choice homework assignments, but those were a valuable tool for me to really learn the content of the class.

Lectures are clear and the professor is great at explaining intricacies of coding in C. He addresses common misconceptions/mistakes in C, why certain techniques are necessary, gives context of real life applications. The labs and exams are designed well/can be difficult - will truly test if you know the material and have problem-solving skills.
He does not know the labguage. He uses code prepared by previous professors and TA.

Selim seems like he cares, but this was his very first time teaching the course. I spent over 10 hours every week on the weekly homework and about 5 hours on each lab. Unfortunately the homework and lab work did not seem to help me learn anything as I failed every exam and untimately the class with a 58% Note: There was absolutely no curve
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you don't have much programming experience this class may be difficult for you. I struggled with this class only because the labs were a lot harder than what they should've been and I had no prior programming experience. Just pay attention in class and you should do good, most people did.

His lectures can be a bit boring at times, but that's understandable when you consider the amount of material that has to be covered in CPRE281. The homework's are challenging, but are good practice for the exams. The labs are all relatively easy which gives you a false sense of security going into the time consuming final project.

Selim is not as funny as Stoychev but his lectures are very simple and understandable. Go to class and the labs and tests should be easy. Homework and Project are another story, but just make sure you spend enough time on them and its managable.

Hell of a guy. He was my lecturer for 281; he uses Stoytchev's slides but does a great job of going into detail. Weekly assignments are challenging but fair, same goes for tests. Final project is time consuming so dont put it off. I felt like Selim really cared for how we did in the course and did everything he could to prepare us.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Mohamed was my recitation TA when I took the class. His hour recitation would suffice to sum up the previous week's material. He's very accessible and is always willing to further simplify ideas if I'm still struggling with it. They class picks up when it introduces sequential circuits, but having Mohamed's help definitely made things easier.

Mohamed was my recitation TA for CPR E 281. I believe that he is either working towards getting his doctorate or already has one, regardless, he is very effective at teaching the material. I learned more in the weekly hour with him than I did in the 3 hours of weekly class time. Stand-up guy.
She is an incredibly caring and knowledgeable professor. She cares about all of the students in her class, and will greet us all by name every class. 10/10 would take her class again

Sinem is my favorite professor in the entire world and she can do no wrong. Makes a boring subject really interesting and is so caring and amazing in all ways. Highly recommend any of her classes to anymore.

She provided lots of help to ensure that all content was understood, gave specific assignment instructions, printed us worksheets/study guides, reviewed notes as a class, walked around helping us all individually, offered help outside of class, and knew each classmate's name personally. She's a great teacher of content and makes you feel seen!

Sinem is one of the best professor. She makes sure to visit with each and every student before class just to see how they are doing. She genuinely cares about you. I 100% recommender her if you take ENGL 219.
She was amazing. One of my favorite professors at ISU. Would recommend this class over and over!
She was the best English teacher I've ever ever had Iowa State.
Required attendnace but never benefited from going to class. Easy course.

Dr. Sonsaat Hegelheimer is my fav professor I've had at Iowa State. She cares about your individualized education and is always MORE than willing to help re-explain things. Very respectful of your time and ensures a safe learning environment. She is one of the more attentive professors here so take advantage of office hours and one on one time!

Sinem is one of my favorite professors at ISU. I'd take more classes with her in a heartbeat

We had 3 classes we could skip before it effected our grade. ENGL219 was pretty easy, especially because she will answer any questions that you come up with. Sometimes her answer is a little confusing, but she will reword it if you still don't understand.
Awsome professor

Professor Cordery is amazing! Super energietic and caring. I truly can't express how great he is. His class can be a little boring, Sports History, but he makes it engaging. You have one quiz every week and a big final exam. We read two books in this class and had to participate in the discussion for points. One group project as well.
Very funny and entertaining professor and made the class fun. Mostly lectures with a few papers and quizzes.

You will need to show up to his lectures to do well in the course, but he makes them enjoyable. The exam structure was not my favorite as you had to write a 750 word essay and 2 paragraphs all by hand in 50 minutes, but you have access to the essay prompt ahead of time. The grading on the essays; however, was very fair. Great Course.

Dr. Cordery is a very good lecturer. Class is extremely interesting and he makes it clear that he expects students to ask questions. Class is very note heavy and he has a couple odd policies about electronics, but not much to worry about. Tests can be difficult to finish in the 50 min time frame. Try to take this class or others from Dr Cordery.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cordery was a great professor for History 202. His lectures are intresting, not to fast or long, and he answers questions very well. He uses quick power points with pictures that are easy to remember but contain a lot of information. Solid professor all around and a fun dude to talk too. Never felt lost in his class.

Professor Cordery is such an interesting teacher. Lectures are basically all notes, but he doesn't make it boring. Unless there's a test you don't really need to show up to the lectures, only the recitations. Yet, I have yet to miss one.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Cordery is my favorite professor at Iowa State. He is funny and genuinely cares about the success of his students. He makes learning easy. He also made a great choice in TA, who was also very helpful.

The History 195 class was a weird class since we only met once a week. He was always cheery and cracked quite a few jokes. If you show that youre serious about the class and maybe crack a few jokes, he wont be as intimidating anymore. Every time I see him he always stop and chat with me. Hes very passionate about his job and students.

Dr. Cordery is absolutely fantastic at lecturing. They are well organized, just enough information on the slides so that you can copy down some but have to listen for more. The only times I found myself drifting away were days I was really tired, and that's saying something. Very knowledgeable on Western Civ, always has answers to questions.

While this class was a dumpster fire (they just restructured it, will be better next semester), Dr. Cordery tried his best to make it easy for us. He can be somewhat intimidating, but if you can make him laugh or show you care about history, you won't have any problems. In-class assignments were very easy, and final presentation was very easy too.

He taught HIST 195 and it was so much busy work. The guidelines for the final presentation were so vague and he kept adding more and more things during dead week for us to add to the presentation. When he taught HIST 202 it was fine. I expected the level of work we received but not in 195. If you have the option, don't take him for 195
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A power-tripping virtue-signaling millennial. I took his playwrighting course. A 3000-level course, and we spent the first two weeks reviewing the same plot structures we already know. Then, when he runs out of material, he overlectures and tries to get people to discuss things they've already juiced dry. I'm on the left, and I think he's too woke.

Performative. Genuinely hostile to students in the most saccharine way possible and actively discourages open and honest discussions, thoughts, or questions. I have never seen someone give off more "I couldn't make it as a writer so now I teach" energy in my entire life.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely performative theatre kid, extends lecture when he runs out of things to say by making students do meaningless activities such as chanting one another's name while mimicking body movements. Completely nonunderstanding that student's have other courses. I have not had a course before where the first day the professor would not work for me.
Theatre kid professor

ENGL 3120 - Taylor was a great instructor and I enjoyed his class a lot! There was a group project at the middle/end of the semester but it was very fun to work on. Overall, I would recommend this class to anyone interested in improving their writing and oral skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy for an English class ( I just suck at writing) He splits the class into harry potter type houses and each house can earn points. I honestly had a lot of fun in his lectures. Would recommend him over other English professors.
I really enjoyed his lectures (and this was a non-lecture class). I hope I have him as a professor again.

I thoroughly enjoyed listening to his lectures, and I also found this professor to be very kind and patient, and even occasionally funny.

I would 100% take another one of his classes in the future, and hope I have the opportunity to.

Lectures for this class were a waste of time. Mitra is nice and probably would be a good prof if in a different class, but I dunno why we are forced to attend lecture and he expects us to listen instead of work on the app. The TA you have is way more important than him as a prof. My TA was great.

Good professor, friendly and always available through office hours or Discord. Willing to solve students' problems with their app. Lecutres could be a little more relevant to the work, but still informative. This class requires a lot of work, but the work isn't exactly difficult. The difficulty is largely dependent on your group and TA.
The lectures weren't really all that important since all of your time and energy for this class goes to the app. What TA you have is more important. He was funny though.

309 was a good class, except for the canvas and lectures. I felt my time in lectures could have been spent better by working with my team on our project. Sometimes important topics that were supposed to be covered in lecture only happened after we needed them.

Professor Mitra's class was the worse I've ever taken. The lectures are not applicable to what you need for the app. He tried running examples this semester for frontend and none of them worked. I would recommend taking it with another professor, since Mitra made my semester miserable.

Professor Mitra's class was an incredibly valuable experience. I'd strongly recommend visiting his office hours at Atanasoff Hall, where he fixed all the errors in 30 seconds and gave me good advice for the app. Whether it was debugging code or understanding project requirements, his support made all the difference.

Mitra is great outside of class for 1 on 1 help, but he sucks in lecture. The content was always delivered several weeks after it should have been, meaning we were. often covering stuff I had already taught myself. Most people weren't paying attention and were just working on their projects. The class is a great intro to software development though
One of the most disorganized classes I have ever taken. If you can, don't take 309 with this professor.

Lectures weren't as applicable to our project. I spent most of my time debugging with a stack overflow or asking my TA for help. Help hours weren't that helpful because I waited a long time only to figure out the answer myself. Your grade in this class mostly depends on your TA and your group mates and of course your own contribution to the project

His class provides real-world-applicable experience (for Backend) with Springboot, Maven, ORM, databases, testing, REST APIs, and Scrum. I think it's a great class to help build your resume and gain knowledge in general. At the same time, his class is incredibly disorganized (see other comments). Lectures are really a side-quest from the project.

No offense to him, but think his lectures are pretty useless. 75% of the class is working on their project and now actually paying attention. I think having 1 day per week to work on your project in class would be great. The work itself isn't too hard, but getting everything in your IDE set up is(at least for frontend). Though he's a solid prof

Must have a group of 4 to take the class. Lectures were informative. Professor actually cares about class understanding, offers individual & group help. Always want's to know what he can do better/ change up. Has high expectations (doesn't like giving out 100%, got several 97.92%).

Not the greatest of lecturers, but is a good person. Much of what he discussed in class did not feel relevant to the project and most of the class did not understand or pay attention to lectures. Very accessible outside of class and open to answering questions.

If more professors were like Mitra, the world would be a better place. 309 has honestly made me consider the switch from engineering to computer science. While the class could perhaps be a little more organized, I think Mitra himself is a very kind, funny, respectful person who has gotten me much more interested in the field of software development

I took COMS 227 over the summer and professor Mitra was overall a good professor. Lecture videos were quite clear and exams really tested your knowledge on Java and the fundamentals of objected-oriented programming.  Homework assignments were quite lengthy, hard, and time consuming though. He is great to reach out for help with anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Absent teacher, purposefully avoids answering basic questions about the course, commends students who make it impossible for him not to answer for not giving up. Wildly disorganized and unprepared every day, the homework assignments are a mess. Don't recommend ever taking.

Mitra is awesome. Had him for 309, dont think I talked to him once back when I was taking that. Decided to do independent study with him because I liked the content he teached tho. Hes kind of a hard arse, but if you prove your diligent hes very understanding. He just wants everyone to do their work. 309 is an important class for being a developer.
Grading criteria is the most opaque I've ever seen, class learning was setup almost backwards. Cannot recommend to take voluntarily.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is one of the best in the COM S department at ISU. Some individuals don't like him due to his teaching style, but he is by far one of the only professors that have taught something relevant in the career world after university.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Required attendance wasn't my favorite but he's a good lecturer and you can tell he cares about his students. I can't say I always paid attention but lectures definitely contained useful info in regards to the project. Also was very accessible outside of lectures. Class was a ton of fun too

For Com S 309, it felt like the lectures were mostly only relevant for backend coders. If attendance weren't required, I wouldn't have gone. That being said, he seemed like a really nice professor who cared a lot about the class.
Wow, very good. Ask for help

Lectures are required but do little more than explain assignments.

Not available during scheduled office hours. Does not keep appointments; left me waiting over an hour more than once.

Does not listen when you explain the problem you need help with, but constantly misinterprets and goes off on tangents without allowing you to speak.

I think Mitra was pretty helpful and reasonable with the grading. Although there is not much you can learn from the lectures, you have to find out everything by yourself. This class can also be a total nightmare if you have incompetent team members, so be very very careful.

Need a good group to have this class go well for you. Lectures are useless, have to learn everything on your own. Nothing was clear in the class and you cannot get 100% on the assignments, they purposely make it so you can't get enough points for full credit, because "Nobody is perfect"

Most unclear grading criteria for a software development class I have ever experienced so far. I did the rubrics criteria, and then got praise from the TA and a good grade but then got taken down by professor for not meeting criteria not on the rubrics which are our only resource to see what grade we get. I wish I could leave a lengthier review.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Clearly cares very much for his students and wants them to succeed.

He's simply the best, and really care about his students progress. Easy A because it really depends on how much effort you put in. Project management is important especially when you start working, and some students dismiss his lectures as not related, but they're important because they expose you to things like Agile and SCRUM frameworks

I made this account just to leave this review. The class was not that hard but as a professor, he isn't great. I learned nothing in class and the quizzes seemed to have nothing to do with the actual material. I enjoyed the project but that's because of my team, not the actual course. Buckle up. This class has a lot of highs and lows.

Mitra was an okay professor. The class material didn't really make any sense, but then again, the class wasn't really about the lecture material. This class is all about learning how to teach yourself a new software and creating something new with it. As long as you keep up with the class, most people will get a lot out of it.

309 is generally more about your ability to teach yourself rather than what you learn in class. That being said, Mitra is one of the most dedicated professors when it comes to answering questions and helping you with your project. I spent many Saturdays with him over the semester fixing things. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class was completely pointless, they should just tell us the required software to be used throughout the entire semester and never hold class again. Professor wasn't anything special. He was funny for sure but it didn't seem like he had your best interest in mind. I'd take him again but I can't and won't take him seriously.

I get the sense that Mitra does not care very much what his students get out of his class and that he doesn't want to be there. He wasn't bad, but I didn't learn anything from him, 309 is all about the project, the group of people you work with, and how hard your TA grades you.

Mitra is definitely passionate about software development, but lecture seems very pointless and everything can be studied outside of class. They can be confusing/pointless at times. However, the TAs and him are very helpful if you ask for assistance on your group project. Just get the group project done and pass the exams and you'll be fine

Took him for 309. Lectures are boring and squeaky because of his microphone. Ended up leaving because of it multiple times. Class is very "throw you in the sharktank" like. You either learn by yourself or sink. My TA was helpful, but Mitra always was very short and unhelpful with answers. Gives you review questions for exams, but no answers.

I'm torn on Professor Mitra. He does a good job helping students on their projects and getting them the help they need if he can't answer your question. His lectures aren't great. 25% of the grade is exams, but the study materials are a bit lacking. He provides review questions but not answers. Also the slides are not the most helpful or incomplete

Awesome professor, cares about his students and tries to help each of them in their projects. - The class he teaches is about a semester long project so self teaching and teamwork are what determines your grade, not only lectures. - He will talk about easy project management topics to use in the teams and if you take notes exams are easy.
In lecture we learn how to count from 1 to 10, but the assignment of this class expect us to solve implicit differentiation of multi-variable functions. Google is your real instructor in COMS309.

He's a bit scattered during lectures, but overall if you take good notes and consult him outside of class, the material isn't hard to learn. He tries to give everyone as good an opportunity to succeed as possible and he really helped my 309 group get our act together and become more successful.
Horrible teacher, rambles on about nothing during lecture, generally does not seem to know what he is talking about. Class is a waste of time besides doing the project.

COMS 309 is a big project class - one big one to be exact, but I will focus on the professor here. Simanta seems to care a lot about everything he teaches and is incredibly available, having office hours for 8 hours a week and on weekends. His organization of course material could be improved as his website is not well thought out.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very, VERY unorganized -- probably the most out of any professor I've ever had. He'll routinely make changes to the schedule while telling no one, adding a ton of stress to an already intensive course. That said, he does care about the students and the grade you receive, and is easy to reach outside of class.

Mitra is extremely unorganized. He always changes his grading scales and his deadlines so you are never exactly sure what is going on. You usually have to teach yourself the topics, but nothing is too hard to learn. All of that aside, Mitra is extremely caring and is always helpful with your questions and concerns. Really a top-notch guy.
Best professor I had at ISU. He really cares about what people learn.

When you meet with him ask him questions, he cares a lot about everyone learning through their project and will give you good advice and organizational tips. Lectures not very important outside of random attendence.

probably the most unorganized class i have ever taken. due dates always being moved around and the grading criteria for most of the projects are really not clear at all. content of the class wasn't bad- just the organizational part was terrible
Fun profesor. pretty laidback, as long as you do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Super nice and approachable professor. He is rare in that he understands how students are doing and ENGAGES!! He'll stop the class to take polls and make sure everyone is getting what he's teaching. Not many CS profs go the distance he does to connect with students. He was very enthusiastic too and there were NO SURPRISES ON ANY EXAM period. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is smart,  good at explaining things .  He emphasizes on how you prove the correctness of an algorithm.  A lot of ACM problems are given,  so be prepared for all-night coding.  The class focuses on how well you understand algorithm and manipulate it in your coding.  Also,  Mitra is the Coach of Iowa State team in ACM competition.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Respected by students

reviews.comment: this professor is very unclear and does not explain assignments or expectations. All of the learning comes from the book and his powerpoints and quizzes are riddled with errors. He does not seem to understand the Blackboard learn software.

His grading criterion is not clear because he cares about students performance than perfection. He is always willing to talk and help you. He makes you write detailed reports which are extremely helpful in professional environment. Easily the best and most understanding professor. Keenness to learn earns an A. No book required.

Mitra taught a tough subject really well.  He wants his students to do well, but doesn't make it easy by nay means.  You need to work hard to get a good grade in the class.  Chegg helps with homework, but doesn't take the test for you. Problem solving class in its finest. Sadly all the mistakes make sense. Great teacher of a difficult class.
He is really good at what he does. He seems like he cares about your academic well being.
Easy Grader

Honestly, he should not teach algorithms. I say this because this lecturer seems to have extremely weak background in ComS especially programming. He teaches this class in Summer and because he doesn't seem to be confident about his own ComS skills,he makes the class easy. But he is smart :He hides his weakness by organizing ACM for students

Mitra provided no clear grading policy, wasted time in lecture by reading off slides, and made us memorize those slides for the midterm. 85% of the class walked out with an A, but i doubt 85% of the class learned anything from Mitra himself. If you could choose to have another professor, then please do yourself a favor.
Best Computer Science Course

Mitra cares a lot about software development which is great. The unfortunate thing is that the class tries to do too much. I feel it could do more by trimming down on requirements. The class has a handful of assignments, tests/quizzes, as well as a semester long project. It's just too much stuff to make it all meaningful. Less is more.
Going to class is a must to keep up and make sure to show that your working in the class because if he knows your working he will bump your grade up at the end of the class
Mitra seems like a nice enough, well intentioned guy, but this class is just awful.  Homework is busy work, organized terribly lectures are pointless etc.  Avoid if possible
Not bad.

One of the best in the department. Really enjoyed having him as a teacher for 311. Expect to read the book or you won't learn. The class is structured like a lab to do hands on work and see where you need help. Holds your interest this way instead of hearing someone drone on. Cares about your learning very much.

Assigns and expects students to read the section before explaining it. Does a very good job of teaching specifics and details. If you don't do the reading, don't expect to learn much during his lecture (your fault for not reading - it was assigned). Learned quite a lot from him. Very easy going and helpful when explaining things in detail.
I didn't learn much in class, but the homeworks taught me a lot. Mitra was helpful in office hours, but tended to ramble on in tangents during class.
HE's Amazing! very helpful

Not sure what all these people are complaining about.  Mitra was awesome about helping, was ALWAYS on time with email responses even after midnight!  GO TO OFFICE HOURS, this guy will teach you amazingly one on one if you need it.  Too bad more people don't TRY to learn from Mitra, my favorite ISU prof.

Very poor with explanations - lectures are pointless and make absolutely no sense. Over half the class has dropped and several of those who are left are not passing the course. Grading is unfair, not learning much from the course. Also hard to reach....does not respond to emails soon or answer questions on the discussion board.

It's hard to understand him because he didn't explain many materials very clearly. It ate our times much to do homework because homework instructions were not clearly and hard to understand. Sometimes some of his information were unimportant.

Hard to understand him at times.  Really wants students to do well, but he isn't very good at explaining the material.  Know the vocabulary, he changes it up a lot making his directions hard to understand for assignments and exams at times.
Lots of pointless tangents in lecture; didn't give enough examples or practical application; wanted students to succeed though and answered questions well.

Mitra is probably my favorite coms professor. Yes, now and then he does teach something he hasn't adequately learned himself. But he is far better than many of the other professors in this department at teaching.  His labs are particularly well designed and fun.  If you are ready to ask questions and assert yourself, you can learn a lot from Mitra.

He failed miserably at adequately explaining any of the proper documentation procedures - and the ones he did explain were out of date by IEEE standards.  Horrible at teaching anything - he spent most of the class on tangents about topics that had no relevance to what we were trying to accomplish for the class.  309 had such potential, he ruined it

Dr. Mitra is a great professor, and just wants students to do their best on the exams. The tests and homework are the only graded material in the course, attendance is optional, but is suggested, heez has some good jokes to keep you awake.

Graded on a belt system.  You had to prove what skill level you were at on the tests and homeworks and then that was compared to the rest of the class.  Kind of a strange grading scale but really works in the students favor.  Don't save the homeworks til the last minute, they are lengthy.

Very helpful professor, fair minded and interested in helping students do their best.  On the other hand he lets some things slide that are detrimental like many students regularly coming in 15 minutes late and not being penalized.  309 is not an easy class to teach, but the information he gives is valuable for the future job market.

I personally found him to be a good teacher. As the content of the class is based more on methods of software development, it is hard to be completely definitive and discrete. I actually used what I learned from this class in a software development internship. I look forward to taking another class with him.
Terrible.

Terrible class, idiotic content, stupid assignments, everyone in group fails if one person farks off, completely unrealistic cirriculum.  This guy is teaching because he couldn't survive in the startup world - BS he teachers isn't used in the real world.

Mitra needs to consider what he's trying to teach in this course.  The class was a mix of ideas not well explained.  Assignments are busy work; poor organization made the project painful.  Attendance and book quizes are not appreciated.  If students can get an A without coming to class, let them.  Draw them in with interesting material, not points.
Mitra is a great guy.  He will always be there to help you if you go to his office hours.
Well intentioned, and not too boring. Generally worthwhile. Main weakness is in organization and consistency, especially when assigning projects.

Awsome Teacher!  Very helpful and knowledgeable. Also very busy, so for the students that posted above....go see him in his office for immediate assistance.  If you take time out for him, he will do what he can to help you.  Probably one of ISUs best Com Sci instructors.  People who dont like him don't go do class, he is unfavorable to slackers
I enjoyed this class, learned alot about software development and java, introduces a lot of new concepts that are useful in software design/development, and am using them in other classes
The worst teacher I've ever had in 4+ years at Iowa State. The worst grading scale I've ever seen. Does not respond to emails or questions.

Horrible teacher. Totally disorganized, way to in love with worthless concepts which he spends way too much class time on. On the plus side, you can basically coast with little to no effort and get an A. Just don't expect to learn anything in the process. And god help you if you don't already know version control before you start the semester.
He's a nice guy. Willing to help if you're willing to ask. He's not always clear on things but if you ask he tries to make it easier to understand.

His heart's in the right place, but he's just not a good professor.  Lots of busywork, and very disorganized.  Most of the class consisted of a group project, but due to organization problems, the design docs weren't due until a week before the project.  Very bad for a software engineering class that's supposed to teach good design skills.
Tries hard but just isnt a good teacher. very book oriented, not a clear explainer, and a terrible grader. Half the class of 80 dropped or failed. Willing to bend some rules though.
poor teacher, average class
Pathetic attempt at teaching.  Go back to industry.
Nice guy. Retakes are a plus.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Gives a lot of busy work.  It's a struggle to stay awake in his classes.  He watches class attendance.
His lecture weren't extremely clear but he was very willing to give my group more time for our project.
No Comments
Taught software engineering with no textbook; allows you to re-take exams!

The class was very interesting. However, there are so many online lecture videos it is overwhelming. Homework is not too bad. There are group projects and as long as you communicate it is not painful. The exams are not great, it is timed 60 minutes for 61 questions I felt rushed. The documentaries are actually really cool and emotional to watch.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Skrynnikova is a great online instructor. NREM120 was a perfect addition to my schedule and was able to be completed without stress. She is easy to contact through email and has online office hours if ever needed. Assignments and quizzes aren't super difficult. A handful of group projects! I didn't use the textbook though!

This class is easy, and you do not need the textbook to pass. There are a lot of lecture videos which makes the class very boring. There are 3 or 4 test, 10ish quizzes, some discussions, and group projects. Would recommend if you need a low stress class.

I took this class completely online so I didn't have a lot of communication with the professor. There are quizzes and tests but they aren't too difficult. There are several group projects that account for quite a bit of your grade. She was very responsive with any questions over email and replied quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: This was probably one of the best honors seminars I've taken so far. I loved the reading and documentaries she had us watch and I feel that she adapted the course to its online structure very well. I would love to take another one of her seminars!

Linda is great. Took this as an online course and it was fairly easy to do with a good sized schedule. A lot of the quizzes are on Quizlet but the farther you get the less you find. Discussion is easy and there are 2 exams and 1 final, all not at the testing center. Find a friend and do the weekly things together
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You wouldn't think that an online class would have a group project, but you do. Tough grader on the homework but quizzes are all on Quizlet. Exams are a little tougher though.

Lidia, was great.  I took the class online over the summer and it was very easy.  The online class is made up of quizzes, discussion topics, and tests.  The tests you can take online at any time, which is nice.  She would send out recaps over our discussions in class.  Seems like she really cares about the students .  Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lidia was great. Good feedback and easy to contact. Class wasn't terribly hard. There was a textbook but since it was online it wasn't super necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor

She's a great professor and teacher. Class consisted of readings which were really long, but could easily be skimmed for content and lectures which were slow but easy to follow. Weekly discussion posts and short essays (1.5 pages tops) account for most of your grade, with quizzes that are very straightforward and taken directly from lectures. 10/10

Lidia is literally the best professor I have ever had. She saved my semester and besides that is a great teacher. She is very flexible with assignments. The assignments can be hard, but she isn't a strict grader. She is one of those professors that wants you to do as well as possible. I would love to take another class with her.

Speech with Dr. Rinker was very easy as long as you put in the effort. We gave a total of 4 presentations throughout the semester and he was a fairly easy grader. Between the assignments and extra credit you should be fine however I've heard he may not be teaching 311 anymore but if you get him for other courses stay in his section.

This class is pretty much all group work which can be good and bad. 450 is the best class to take at ISU for real-life farming applications. However, it is not as hands-on as they say it is at the beginning of the semester. Skyler isn't very good at replying to emails, but is overall a good professor. He wants you to learn and connect with students
Class is set up a little weird, in my opinion, but overall he's a cool guy who knows a lot about farm management. Class can seem very disorganized but as long as you're chill, it's cool.

Kostya is a superb professor. Though calc 2 is one of most difficult classes at ISU, he made the lecture environment very easy-going, while still teaching material well. If you use an iPad for class, he uploads all slides prior to lecture and they are extremely digital note friendly. Show up and put in the work, you will succeed in his lecture.

Great lecturer, follows roughly the same style of teaching as Butler videos. Has good humor and spirit and makes resources for blank and filled slides available usually before class. Good feedback when you need to ask questions and lots of practice problems.
Good sense of humor and clear explanations. Make sure you show up to class, but even if you don't he uploads his lecture slides. Excellent professor.

Slutsky is a great guy and although Calc 2 is a difficult course, he made it much more enjoyable with his humor. I loved the jokes he would make and it honestly kept the energy in the room going. The course is very difficult but I think he does a great job to teach the material as he goes very deep into the reasoning for the material.

I really enjoyed Skaars' class as a whole. If you take the time to study for the two exams in the semester, you'll be just fine, especially as he adds on points to make up for a curve. It's very information heavy, but the labs included in the class make it fun. He does start 4 pt pop quizzes towards the end of the semester, so show up.
Came in knowing pretty much everything. If you are a farm kid its all review, if not its a lot of facts to learn and know. Lots of vocab.

I love Skaar. He is so passionate about beef. I struggled in this class because I didn't come from a cattle background, but I met with him before and after class, and he was very willing to lead me to the right answer; he does this during exams, too. I would talk to him about so many other things, and he is very sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very picky grader when it comes to homework, quizzes and exams. Each exam took me well over an hour and the final took me over two hours . If you don't use the exact wording he wants he will mark it wrong.  When you take the final you can either have it replace your whole grade,drop it or have it added into your grade.

Fun older man, great in conversation. Labs are required but I missed three and still got an A in the class. You will get stuck on hour long tangents but he clearly cares and loves to answer questions. Holds "office" hours for an hour before and after class right in the room as well as will make time to meet with you whenever. Overall pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He wasn't the greatest teacher, but it's evident how much he loves animals. He's just a cute old man with a calming voice. Except when he makes you sit outside on a tractor in 5° F weather for almost 2 hours while he talks about beef cattle. But I enjoyed him.
Great professor. He is easy to work with and very understanding. Fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: All the homework very heavily relies on being present at the labs, so have transportation to get to the off-campus labs.
Have good transportation off campus, because lab is very rarely on campus.

Suppose you don't have an Ag background, good luck! The lectures typically do not correlate much with the tests, which account for 70% of your grade. If you do ask him a question, be prepared for the best answer ever or a condescending tone. The exams typically consist of 120 questions, so study frequently and create a Quizlet to review every day.

Relies heavily on two tests. Takes a lot of study time if you have no background in animal ag. You have to go to labs, or you'll be clueless. Lectures are interesting and provide a good background, but they don't directly correlate with the tests. Study ahead and understand all the terminology.

If you miss a lab or aren't good at exams good luck. Two exams make up 70 percent of the grade. Dr. Skaar is a nice guy though, I really enjoyed getting to know him. Make Quizlets and review notes and you will probably be fine.

Skaar is a great and personable professor. For this class, he brings in a wide variety of speakers from across the industry. While the time for this class is not the most convenient, it is just once a week. Worksheets were easy if you properly read the question, and the big project is just all opinion. Also, the exam was at a brewery.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about what he does, and his lectures can be very interesting. Labs are essential to go to; pretty much everything in the lab is on the exams. One thing about him is that he doesn't get back to your emails, so just talk to him in person if you can. Exams are pretty easy if you study and actually learn the material.

Absolutely love Dr. Skaar! He is a silly dude, and is super passionate about animals (especially beef). I do not have a farming background, and I still found the class super easy, I studied about 1 hour total for the whole semester. The exams are most of your grade, but minimal effort should get you an A if you show up and pay attention.

Professor Skaar is a knowledgeable instructor, but the grading heavily depends on the exams. While the material can be challenging without a farm background, engaging with the lectures and using tools like Unstuck ai can help prepare for the assessments.
I hated this professor so much. Made me hate my major.
Fun guy and super fun to listen to during lectures. However, we never finish the slides and you are expected to go over them on your own.

Doing the HW was almost impossible without going through the whole thing with him. Also, the exams are exclusively short answer, and he is looking for VERY specific answers. You can tell he cares about the students and he is very enthusiastic about answering any questions, but the HW and exam are just unnecessarily difficult.

Skaar was overall a great professor, but the homework and exams were pretty tricky. If you do not write it exactly how he said it, it will likely be counted wrong. Besides that, he answers any questions and is a very helpful professor. He also offers extra credit through in-class quizzes and other opportunities throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a fantastic prof but the tests determine how you do. The first test isn't until right after spring break, so it's over everything from the beginning of the year to then. The labs are essential for the second exam. Study a lot for the exams because it's hard to bounce back.
He loves his field of study and is a great guy in general. The homework can be a bit tricky, but he will help you a lot just by asking questions.

Very nice and easy going. This class has one lecture section and one lab section. the lectures aren't mandatory but the labs are if you want your daily lab points. The exams are roughly 100 questions long and can be a little tough if you don't study enough. A lot of information you have to know.

Professor Skaar is a great person. I believe he truly cares about his students. He is sometimes unorganized, and his canvas was kind of hard to maneuver. There are 2 exams worth 75% of your grade, so definitely study. I didn't come from a farm background, so much of the material was hard to memorize, but it's manageable.

I had him for Intro to animal science. He talks as though you should already know everything. He talks as though everyone in the class is a farmer and should understand his lingo. As someone who grew up in the city, I never had any idea what he was talking about. But great guy.

Followed all of their random formatting requirements and still didn't do well on the final paper. The class is relatively easy to pass if you go to every class but both he and Olsen are very conservative and let it show in this class. All of the speakers were conservative and mostly uninteresting. Didn't have this issue with Skaar freshman year.

411 is required but it is such a joke. Sherry Olsen and Skaar teach it together and I feel like I am just being forced to watch fox news but more of a waste of time. Olsen needs to stop teaching and Skaar needs to get with the times.

I took ANS 426 and ANS 411. He is unclear with his instructions constantly, he doesn't care to make content interesting, and he surrounds himself and our class with conservative white men. It makes no logical sense and all his instructions fir every assignment are a very large paragraph of tangents. You do not get much out of these classes

To do any good on homework or test you have to write exactly what he wants to see or don't bother. The exams are very lengthy and all word problems. He grades all homework and exams by hand so just keep that in mind. Way more difficult than the other 200-level ans courses. Personally would avoid taking his classes unless you have to.

Overall animal science 101 with Dr. Skaar was very enjoyable, but the major downfall of the class is that the 2 exams are 75% of your grade. I have a farm background so the class was fairly easy for me but if you don't have that background good luck charlie. I recommend studying a lot if you don't have prior knowledge of livestock.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really like Dr. Skaar and think he tries really hard to make his classes fun. 411 was a super easy class as your only graded on Packback, reflection sheets, and a final project. This class had no tests or homework unless you didn't get something done in class. Pretty simple, he wants you to succeed and be successful after college.

Skaar really enjoys teaching this course to his students. He always has entertaining stories and is able to answer questions accurately. Definitely passionate about animal science and agriculture. Be aware though the 2 big exams for this course are over 100 questions are is weighted extremely heavy. Be prepared to study!

Caring professor but if he needs to flunk you he will. Grades heavy, but answers your questions. Basically, doesn't care if students fail or are doing badly. Treats every course as its 400/500 levels and expects every student to think like he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'll make it simple, this professor made me hate my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have had in my college career. This class nowhere near matches the workload of the other ansci 200-levels. Grades extremely hard and wants specific answers that no one knows.

Dr. Skaar a caring professor that honestly wants you to do well. However, his tests are long and difficult. His homework assignments are very wordy and are hard to navigate through at times. If you ask questions though, he will help you out and walk you through everything. Overall, I would take classes with him again.

Dr. Skaar was incredibly helpful during COVID. He was willing to answer any questions on the homework and quizzes, which meant those were easy As. He would also help you on tests if you just asked. I really wish we could have been in person, but he was very helpful and his lectures were very enjoyable!

It takes him until two days before final grades are out for you to know your grade for the first time since the mid-term grades were released. His Canvas is an absolute disaster. he abbreviates everything making it extremely difficult to know what to do and what not to do. He is a nice person, just can't use technology... It's 2020 figure it out.

Two exams count for 75% of your grade. Labs will last full two hours during the farm tours. Needs very specific terms on homeworks, tests, etc. Be aware that grading is not always the same based on what TA grades your assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There's a quiz every lecture period. Labs are usually on the farms as just a walking tour so it's not super exciting. However, Skaar is a very entertaining lecturer and is very knowledgeable on the subjects he teaches. The only downside was his TA's that graded some of the papers with different answers than what his lecture notes say.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will not like this if you have a very anthropomorphic stance on animals. This class made me a vegan :)

Amazing lecturer, and wonderful to talk to if you are unsure about your major. If you have an ag background, this class is fairly easy. There are assignments that have to be turned in in paper, which can be easy to forget about. Very protective/strict about attendance. There are good quizlets for exam studying, I got As on the exams using them.
Homework is not hard at all. Do your work and you will be good!
He knows what he talking about the labs were fun and I loved every second of him will take another class of his soon! :)

I loved taking this class with Skaar. I did have to work for my grade, but I enjoyed the lectures and labs. Exams were all multiple choice and true or false, making them easy if you pay attention and study. Skaar is very knowledgeable and I feel that he cares about the success of his students. I would recommend taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Skaar is an amazing teacher, in recent years he has moved to multiple choice on exams and he owns up to mistakes. He is very picky about attendance but he is accommodating. He is very respectful and fun too. I would recommend taking this class!
Too much homework for it to only be 25 percent of your grade. He lied about what was to be expected on the first exam. A little lazy as well. Not a terrible guy, just not a good professor.

Dr. Skaar is a guy you want in your corner. However, he is the most difficult grader I've encountered. If you do not word it EXACTLY like he does, it's probably wrong. Go talk to him, that is the best way to pass. He truly does care, but he has an odd way of showing it by criticizing young people and our poor wording at least once a week in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most fun classes I have taken at Iowa State! Does a good job of making sure you understand the material even if you didn't come from a livestock background.
