reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Class is one that you have to work for. Lots of material thrown at you, but it's not impossible. He's is very passionate about animals, especially the beef industry, and wants you to learn about it as much as possible. Things are very detailed and can be quite specific, but it's for a good reason. Show up for class, otherwise you wont understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really amazing professor. Works really hard to help you, especially if you go to him with questions. He's always more than happy to explain material more in-depth or in a different way so that you can understand. Take good notes and review them! Exams are a bit difficult, but if you're well prepared they're quite easy.

He's a great professor and he is pretty passionate in his lectures. The lectures are very detailed so take good notes. The labs are crucial. Quizzes in the beginning of lecture so make sure to review material from the previous week for easy points. He answers questions well too. File assignments/notes effectively, heavy review for exams needed.

Skaar was one of the best professors Ive had for a lecture. He allowed students to ask questions during lecture and answered them kindheartedly. Unfortunately, there was a large amount of homework. Each class has a quiz. Each lab has a worksheet. And after lab you have another assignment that must be turned in, in paper, outside class hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Awful teacher takes as many points as possible. loves to see people fail. If you can't quote him word for word you won't do well.

He can be a tough grader and his grading criteria isnt that clear. Hes a really nice guy that gives amazing lectures! He really knows what hes talking about. The tests are difficult and you really need to study for them.

He's okay, a little old school so kind of stuck in his ways. Grading kinda unfair, depends on the TA you get for the section you're put in. Tests are big--STUDY. Material isn't hard, just lots of memorizing. Lectures are okay, he can fly a bit without giving lots of substantial material, but don't skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Skaar wasn't too bad of a teacher. Seemed knowledgable about the industry, the powerpoint notes could have been put together better. An easy quiz in class and wks in lab once a week. Homework wasn't to bad either, it was sometimes long. Study hard for the tests as they are fill in the blank and multiple choice. Farm tours were fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Skaar is an alright professor. Just do your homework but he can be rude to students. He doesn't allow collaboration on Tophat quizzes. You only have two exams so studying is really important. Just show up to labs and you will get credit.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A fantastic lecturer. Has lots of stories and comments that you can only get in class. Fun labs at the ISU farms. Lots of study material if you complete the worksheets. Beware of the TAs!

This class is impossible if you are unwilling to regurgitate word-for-word what Skaar says in lectures. If you have even a slight background in beef you will struggle because objectively right answers are wrong because they aren't exactly what Skaar was looking for. The pop quizzes are extra credit and the lectures are long/pointless.

Loved ANS 101! He tries to make sure everyone understands the material. Labs are fun and tests are relatively easy (but lengthy). Very helpful for people who do not have a farming background. Just make sure to keep up with the homework and prepare for the in class quizzes.
He's way better than Jodi, so I can't complain

Always willing to clarify things you don't understand, and is willing to fix things to make them right as well. Really nice and funny guy. He also tries to get to know individuals, not just a class as a whole.
He's a little spacey, but his class is fun! He curves his exams up so at least some people get a 100%. You'll know exactly what you have to study and as long as you memorize it all you'll be good.

Dr. Skaar really cared about students and if you were struggling he did his best to help. I had him for animal science 101 and i don't come from a farming background and still did well. He had lots of homework, one due every week and a quiz in class every week for 5 points but it was manageable. Tests were easy if you listened and did the work.
He's the best professor I have ever had in my life. He's so funny, easy lecture, and fun class overall. Recommend this 100%.

I absolutely HATE this professor. I lost points on my exam because I used the word "is" instead of "was" and when I asked him about it he told me that I had all the right answers but they weren't worded the right way. I am a beef producer in this  class and he makes me hate working with cattle.

I enjoyed Dr. Skaar's teaching method. He is laid-back, funny, and informative. Your grade comes from only two tests, so be sure to study for them if you want to do well.  Super easy class if you take the time to study and/or have a farm background at all. Fill out the study guide, study them, memorize the breeds, and you will do well.
He is very passionate about what he teaches. The tests are a little bit difficult if you don't study for them.
Skaar is hilarious and great at explaining things. He's always willing to talk if you have any questions or comments. He'll love you if you tell him animal related puns and ask questions .
He's very helpful with any questions that you have! Even though there's homework every week it's very do able and straightforward!
This class is a great intro to Animal Science. Dr. Skaar is very friendly and welcoming, and is eager to teach students all about animals.

Super interesting lectures, and very nice.  Only has two tests all semester, so they cover a lot of information.  That doesn't make them hard, the hard part is answering questions exactly how he wants it answered.  Your answer may be right, but not exactly what he wants.  That is the only thing that bothered me.

Dr. Skaar was a great prof for 101, not for beef science. If you don't have a beef background don't take this class. It is really confusing. He goes on long tangents about things that aren't relevant, and will grade a correct answer as wrong if the answer isn't exactly "what he was looking for". Use the practice exam to study, and review with him!

Dr. Skaar does a great job of going over every possible aspect a bovine farmer would run into. His homework and tests can have difficult wording, but if you ask him to elaborate, he is VERY helpful. So do the homework in advance. He also has a practice exam. USE IT TO STUDY. Most of the concepts, if not all of them, are on his exams as well.

Skaar is my favorite professor. His lectures are incredibly clear and straightforward. There is an easy 5-point quiz every week over the past week's materials, so if you don't go to class you won't be able to make up those points. Labs are sometimes difficult because they are off campus at different farms. Overall, it was a really enjoyable class!

101 Is great. His TA's are tough graders, have to be exact with wording. The labs can be a pain because it's at the hansen center which is behind the towers. Later into the semester you start taking farm tours, which is really fun. Homework can be very long and only worth 10 points. Lecture also has quizzes every week worth 5 points plus a bonus ?
Prof Skaar is fun. Just go to class and turn in your homework! Easy A if you try. I got a D but it was my own fault lol
I really enjoyed having Skaar as a teacher. He was good at what he does and make things clear and easy to understand. I would take another class with him.

Skaar is my advisor and he is always willing to help people with material. Coming from a beef background,  I learned a lot from taking this class. Tedious homework assignments, but he wants you to draw conclusions from the material. Tests are challenging if you don't truly understand the material, but go to class, do the homework and you'll be fine
He has a lot of assignments. He test are really hard sometimes and there are times he will dock you points if he didn't like how you worded something even if its right.

Dr. Skaar is super friendly and makes his classes accessible to all students. I took both his 101 class and his beef science class. They both had quite a bit of homework and the tests could be challenging, but everything was very fair and I learned a lot. 101 was my favorite ISU class!!!
Really enjoyed him.

Dr. Skaar is a great professor. He is very passionate about what he is talking about. Class isn't required but without going it would be hard to do well on the tests, which are very long but pretty easy. He can be kind of scatter brained during lecture, but it keeps it interesting and fun. The labs are hands on and you can learn a lot.

Great to listen to in lectures. Taking notes in class really helps, but the slideshows he uses are usually all online. Labs take a long time and are usually a lot of work.  Only real complaint is his aide which is a 20 something 'know it all' type woman who thinks she HAS to add her comment to whatever he says, which usually just the same thing.
Who doesn't love Skaar! You have to work at it, but in the end if you worked hard, you will get a good grade.

This crazy guy.....likes to ramble and laugh at a whole lot of nothing, but was an incredible teacher when he is focused. Many times he would bring in a high expert if he didn't know information (Super nice for keeping things interesting) and always answered questions and tried to work with you on anything
He likes to ramble in class, which makes it distracting and hard to pay attention. Homework is hard, he will dock points over nothing! Tests are over many subjects, hard and long. STUDY for them!
Homework/quizes are easy. More difficult for people who have no history in domestic animals (cattle, sheep, pigs, ect). Tests are difficult.

Dr. Skaar is very passionate about this class. He keeps it exciting. If you go to class and the labs, it is not hard to get a good grade. He is willing to help any time if you go to him. Overall great professor who makes the class fun.

Great professor.  Doesn't spoon feed you/makes you work hard for your grade which is refreshing.  A lot of students not used to that hated the class because they actually had to pay attention, learn, study, and try hard to pass.  Plenty of homework, but it helps when studying for the exams, which can be a challenge.  I enjoyed the class.
Class was interesting but lectures were sometimes unorganized. Slides had a lot of information and go by fast. Homework can take a long time. Friendly teachers though and fun. Loved labs.

Study for the exams as much as possible, they have a lot of information on them and they are half of your graded. The other half is from in class quizzes, homework and labs. There are  no make up points for any of theses, if you miss class you get a zero for them.

Fun for 101, but more serious for 226, especially if you don't have a beef background. I like AnS 101 with him a lot, but he didn't explain things very well in beef, he assumed everyone knew what he was talking about and there was no textbook to refer to.
Decent Prof..hard tests!

He's very helpful and is just a goofy guy -- likes to go off on stories. He makes the learning atmosphere very relaxing, bringing coffee to tests in case you need it. He teaches well and thorough enough BUT he thinks everyone has a common knowledge (or thinks its common sense) of all things beef and if you don't know, he'll treat you like an idiot.
Very helpful at times and other just an ass. very unorganized lost homework 3 different times and wouldn't admit it was him also tried cheating me out of many points.
Skaar is the man!

I thought this class was really unorganized, but the material itself was pretty easy. Still, the tests are really hard to study for as a result of this courses' unorganized teaching style. Just make sure to come to class everyday and do the homework! Only way to pass.
Awesome!

Photo-Copy EVERYTHING you turn into him! He loses stuff easily and then wont give you even partial credit when its his fault! He won't email you back - don't even bother. He takes off points for the tiniest things and unless you have a VERY strong background in cattle don't take this class it will just make your schedule suck.
You have to be nuts not to love Skaar as a professor!
I love animal science!!!

I owe so much to Brad Skaar, he is by far the best advisor that I have met. (he isn't even mine and I use him) He treats you like an adult and has many life experiances, very smart and my role model, I can't say enough good things about this guy.

Awesome teacher and class! Going to class helps...get points just for being there. Study using hw, quizzes, and daily sheets for the exams...they really help. Exams aren't too difficult. Learned alot in this class!

This class is pointless. It's a requirement so grin and bear it. Skaar spends most of the time flapping his jaws about nothing related to the class. He's highly personable, but I don't feel is a good teacher.
Great guy, lots of fun!

****. Biased against anyone not from a farm background. Dislikes anyone who's opinion doesn't match his own. Uninformed/doesn't care about animal welfare. Impossible to get a hold of. Unwilling to make accommodations. Grading is biased and very dependent on his mood at the time of grading. Attitude is very fake.
Extremely disorganized and is rarely in class...hope for good TA's because they're the only ones there to help you. Easy class overall
If you are AnSci, Skaar is by far the best advisor you can get. He's very helpful and honestly cares about how you're doing. Treats you like an intelligent student, unlike most people with freshman.
Fun teacher that is enthusiastic about teaching. Weekly quizes are easy. Take notes and do the homework. Study notes, homework, quizes and daily worksheets for tests.

Take his class!! He's a lot of fun and makes things very interesting. You'll do well if you attend every lecture and lab (easy quizes every lecture and daily points every lab) and do the homework. The tests aren't bad if you study the material, there's usually nothing surprising on the tests. Everything is gone over pretty well. Overall- excellent!

Skaar rocks my socks. Great teacher, very enthusiastic, but he can be disorganized and is usually the first to admit it. Look over the old test and study sheet and the class will be a breeze. Don't forget to do your homework.

Really nice teacher, I'm a Dairy Science major, so the subject matter is in my interests anyway, but we did some neat tours. Show up for class, do the homework, and study for the tests. Tests aren't hard but he puts stuff in that wasn't necessarily covered in class but might have been on the hw. Not a hard class to get through.

Really nice guy and will try to help you out with anything.  But probably the most disorganized man alive.  A lot of class time is spent trying to figure out what to do next and there is a lot of confusion with directions on assignments and class work.
Very fun teacher! Class was interesting and fun! Enjoyed getting to know him.
My favorite class. ever. He is an awesome teacher...keeps class interesting and fun
A good teacher he knows how to interact well with the students and can make them laugh too.
His class is disorganized and half the time he is sitting in the back observing.
He's nice and interesting but he doesn't really know what is going on this semester becuase the admin changed lab so hes not really all that helpful.
He saved my life. And adding to that, he is such a great person. I feel as if he actually CARES about you, as an individual. And he likes country music!
Dr. Skaar is great- loved the class, it was fun and interesting.  He is obviously excited to be teaching, and really gets to know his students.
Good teacher
A great teacher!
Dr. Skaar rocks!

At the beginning he comes off kind of confusing like.  But after awhile you get use to him and his sillyness and everything just makes sense.  Real easy going guy and he cares how you are doing.  Fun guy!
This guy is great, i wish he would teach all my classes.  He really cares about what he's doing. :)
Skaar is a great guy and not to mention hilarious! Lab was always a blast despite the fact it was fri afternoon!
One of the nicest guys you'll ever want to meet.  Will jump through fire to get you what you need.
No Comments

Dr. Slagell is knowledgeable and very passionate about the subject. She helps put the speeches into context which is useful. Most class periods start with a brief 10-15 minute lecture followed by directed group discussion on the reading(S). The exams are relatively easy but projects require significant effort.I strongly recommend this class!

Easy A. Take attendance in Lab. Given 5 quizzes in lecture but it's in the schedule so you know when to go. I couldn't stand the way she talked. It was annoying. However, the material is easy and just common sense so it doesn't matter who is teaching it.

Dr. Slagell is an amazing professor.  The class itself is challening but only if you don't invest the time.  Most of the complaints I heard from other students were not valid, they seemed upset they had to do work.  I think most assume this is an easy class and are surprised when it turns out they can't just sling crap together and call it gold.
Attending class is pointless. There is no structure, I don't even know what is going on in the class when I am there. She grades tough, and assigns a lot of busy work.
Always excited about this subject. Sometimes too happy for some people in the class.

Very nice woman that is very knowledgeable on subject, with well-designed, fair exams on material taken from books, and a VERY forgiving grading system with plenty of extra credit. Lectures with Slagell herself are usually pointless, however; the material is all on WebCT and in the textbook, so lecture is at most watching clips of amateur speakers.
Very nice and enthusiastic. Passionate about her work, makes you care about the subject. Shes helpful when you ask, class is fun.
Very interesting subject. I enjoyed the group work and the opportunities to learn about history and disect its rhetoric. Final project was rather hard but graded fairly.

The Professor was excited about the subject which is rare, and for a speech professor she demonstrates very well how a presenter should present when teaching. Great use of powerpoint. She will give you the grade you earn.
VERY VERY BORING...guaranteed to put you in deep sleep..............
one word...BORING...
Boring lecture that was not helpful at all.  The class itself is not hard, but she writes tricky multiple choice tests.

She is the most boring teacher I have ever had. The material is fairly stupid as well. The busy work is not necessary and only serves to solidify the feeling that she does not know what she is talking about.
Totally cool class. Dr. Slagell is funny and digs the speeches. BUT there is tons of reading and writing papers.  Don't take the class if you don't like to read or write.  Lots of history stuff too.

The lecture for this class was extremely boring!!!  Most of the class is in the lab where you are with about 20-some people, it's a pretty easy class but a lot of busy work... I felt like I was in high school again.
definitely not cool. she needs to take her own class and learn how to capture the audience's attention. for a speech teacher, not a great speaker. the class is a ton of busy work as well.
No Comments

Dr. Sly is an excellent Capstone professor.  He has TONS of industry experience and could answer any questions we asked about our project.  He understands the difficulties with these kinds of projects and was the best professor for the job.

Dr. Sly has been around the block. He knows what works and what doesn't. Sometimes it was frustrating to have to fight him on things, but I think he still wants the best for his students. If you have logic and reason behind something, he's fine to work with. But he is a tough grader.

Did you know he restores old Porsche's? Even if you do, he's still going to tell you. Senior design really is not difficult but he constantly fights you and the company you work with. He is the engineer everyone on the shop floor hates. No room for common sense, time studies for everything, numbers this, all talk and no walk.

I won't recommend sly for any class. His homework and exams take four times whatever he thinks it should take you, so do them early enough. Tough exams overall, and we barely got to finish them and sometimes not. TA and his office hours are helpful, but again understand the homework carefully they are a significant portion of the exams.
Perfect professor for senior design lecture is useless but attendance is mandatory

The professor does not use any of the formulas mentioned in the powerpoint slides. Instead uses excel to solve every problem. The lecture are not self sufficient and the homework, lectures and exams are completely unrelated. This course can be aced only if you study on your own. The prof doesn't help at all. Ridiculous experience.

Actually, the content of this class is very easy for me. However, I still wanna give a very low score for him because his homework is really foolish. You can not imagine that the questions always miss some important words or state confusedly. Due to this, you can always get low points. I try to ask him but there are too many questions like this.

This is a very difficult class. It feels easy at the beginning, after few chapters, the quality of powerpoint straightly goes down, NO EXAMPLE QUESTION, ONLY THEOREM, NO EQUATIONS. Sometimes the HW questions and solutions have lots of errors(not explained clearly). Tricky exam(long and hard with short time), the average is usually between  65% to 75%.

He doesn't announce when quizzes will be very well. He just assigns them on blackboard and it could be a weekend and you wouldn't bother looking till Monday so don't be lazy about checking blackboard often. The group project was confusing. Exams are tough, but read the book and watch lectures and you will be fine.

Worst teacher ever! exams are tough, only gives 15  minutes to spend quizzes online, tons of homework. Paid not for online class but ended up exactly the same as online class. I don't have any words to describe anymore!
Great Prof!
He is awesome. Knows a lot about the market, the world and I like his overall point of view

With out any prior knowledge of programming this class was really hard. My advice is make friends with people who understand the material to help you get through. He is a cool guy but does not know how to teach very well.

He is a genius. That said, he expects a lot. The class starts of slow, but the middle of the semester is hell. 20 hours a week at points...on one program. He gives out way too hard of homework and labs compared to his easy examples. A lot of self-teaching. However, I admit I did learn the most from this class. Stick with it. Half our class dropped.

great prof, really knows the materials, the lectures are good. he is a successful businessman so his perspective on many things things that are going on in the real world is very worth listening.  The course is actually not hard, maybe because i learned java before, but i truely enjoy the class and learn a lot of things.

He is a very intelligent guy, but when it  comes to teaching he could make it a little clearer. Pay attention in class and don't wait till the night before to start the homework. Many of the assignments are quite difficult but if you do them and try to understand the tests and quizzes aren't that bad.

His examples are simply amazing. They make sense and are relevant to the present economic scenario. I'd rather call this class "Wealth Management for engineers". He gives personal examples of his own experiences with investments and how made a ton of money.
BA, take this class! Easy A just for doing the work, tests are easy and so are the projects.

Does not go over HW or lab. Assumes too much. Is ALWAYS too busy with his other "job" to really care about students. Does even really know how to program himself. If you are new to programming and taking this course... Pray...

His lectures are very long and drawn out.  The man loves to hear himself talk.  I would definitely suggest taking Engr 160 instead.  You would be better off.  His tests are graded very hard, and assignments were sometimes impossible to figure out.  Save yourself hours in the lab and try to switch.
He just simply read through the slides. Kinda boring in class. But not hard to get an A. Exams computation questions are very similar to the homework and in class quizzes.
Real world examples were simply awesome. I had this class right after lunch and he made a good job most of the time in keeping people awake.

This professor is by far one of my favorite yet.  The content of the class itself (the way the book teaches it) is fairly boring, but the REAL WORLD situations that the professor uses to compare are amazing.  I really, really like this guy!
He is a great guy with a great story, but he teaches way too fast.  It is really not as much Sly as it is IE 148.  AVOID THIS CLASS ...unless it is required for you.
Teacher does not like answering questions

He's an awesome teacher. Having a two hour lecture at 8 AM was definitely not easy but if you go to class you shouldn't have trouble with the homework but if you do the homework and labs early and run into a problem, he's happy to help. Tests aren't too bad, if everyone doesn't do well he's usually willing to curve them.
tests too hard
Learned more about real-life stuff then about the class. I'm okay with that because I use the stuff I learned a lot.
average difficulty class. homework is very strictly graded. his teaching can be confusing sometimes.

Bad, Bad, Bad... Spends half the class talking about himself and the other half reading word for word of the book provided slides.  Test are easy if you have a buddy that has taken him since he is too lazy to change the questions. TA's do all the work including all WebCT questions.  Projects and homework takes 5 times too long-lack of orgainization
good
david sly can't teach. be prepared to be a good friend with textbook and have a study group for homeworks.

also had him for TLOG360, so EASY as a prof. His delivery sucks and he basically just reads the slides off for an hour a day, but the classes aren't really that hard and he has good side stories about racing porsche's and buying airplanes, etc.
A good guy to get to know and is helpful outside of class, but lecture and and the book material are kinda confusing in what to study for on tests, but otherwise a pretty good class

Very smart self made millionare.  That right there made him interesting to me.  He may not have lectured on the subject all the time but he made the classes interesting by relating the "real world" which it was apparent he knew about.  Tests were slightly above average on the difficulty level, but very bareable if you go over the slides he tells u2
He is the worst teacher ever.  His cell phone not only went off during our first exam but he went into the hallway to talk.  I am sure that it was one of his many Pro Planner calls.

I am shocked by the positive ratings here.  Everyone complained about him the entire semester.  He was not prepared for class at all.  The lecture was usually made up as class went on.  He spent way more time running his business than running his class on ISU's dime.  The class was based on VB.net and we didn't have the software until midterms
A Professor who is incredibly smart, but just does not devote a lot of his time to his students and making sure they understand what is going on.

The guy was a great teacher.  Honestly i learned alot in this class because of him.  He understands the students and when the class doesnt understand it he doesnt just say screw it and hopes for the best but instead he goes back and makes sure he teaches everything.  Easy to follow and just an all around good guy.

Sly actually listens to students. He put together practice tests for our last 2 (out of 3) exams because we asked. He also seems very willing to help in any way he can, and he really knows his stuff. The class is tough, but working in groups really helps. He did pile a lot of work on us at once, but he pushed most of it back by our request.

Let's be honest - this guy always knows what he's talking about.  He relates well to students, and is MORE than fair when it comes to grading.  That's not to say that class wasn't tough - he's not the best teacher.  Even so, with a little work you'll succeed.  Recommend to student who prefer learning something to obsessing over their GPA.

Dave is quite possibly one of the best teachers I have had while at ISU.  He actually made me money through his in class investment advice.  Very application oriented and can give real personal advice and guidance on a host of different topics.
very hard, avoid him
Great teacher, willing to help when asked and enjoys doing it.

Dave Sly is the biggest **** Iowa State has ever seen!  He's a genius and still makes time for the lowly freshmen, helping them understand how to program in VBA.  During our class he'd not only help us out, he was also sealing deals on his cell phone making millions of dollars.  Sly=**** City!
very boring lecture, not very enthusiastic about teaching this class.
Dr. Sly is a nice guy, but not the best teacher.  The material is not that difficult, which is good because you will end up teaching yourself.

Sly is a fun guy to have as a teacher, however, he seems to have some trouble explaining some concepts. He teaches you real world stuff as well as required book material. Great class, great professor, glad I took it.

He is very knowledgeable about his industry and has had many real life experiences so uses that to make the classes interesting.  I have a hard time keeping up or understanding some parts of his classes because he assumes we know more than we do.  Otherwise, a very concerned and focused teacher.
Very unorganized but a good professor.  Waits til last minute to post lecture notes.  Very smart but has trouble explaining concepts sometimes.

his classes are really easy, power point style. not particularly interesting, but he is rich, never worked for a company in his whole life; so maybe he has the right ideas. incredibly smart, unless you are a dumb business major.
Very hard to understand.  Knows way to much and is very smart, but doesnt know how to relate to freshman who have never been around to this kind of work.  Has a hard time explaining things.
Does his best to make the material interesting and teach things that will be useful down the road.  I really enjoyed the class.
...what can i say? he sucks at teaching
Really enjoyed his class.  Fun teacher and knew what he was talking about!

Alls you can say is what a knowledgable helpful,and yes i must say it, stud. He had a great project that we did that really helped to learn the material. Very easy to talk to and was destined to be doing what he is doing. Thanks Dr. Sly
Very smart. Maybe too smart?
good guy, willing to help, loves his job (he's gotta, he's a millionair)
No Comments
Very boring.  Not a good idea to take over the summer.
No Comments

I am impressed by his ability! Especially for being a grad student. He has had a lot of experience. But, I wonder how he could have gotten all of that experience in the 15 years he has been out in the real world because I swear he has been everywhere!

ENVS3420 - You get 2 weeks to do the module which is some reading and then 4 quizzes each 10 questions long and one discussion post. The class is incredibly easy. No exams or anything just the quizzes and discussion post every other week. The content is interesting, but I don't really feel like I learned anything.

Her TAs grade everything and take forever to grade it. The material was very easy. TA does not provide any feedback and takes off 1/2 a point, and just says good job on papers. Just took this class to reach full-time status, and it is a really easy class to get through. Two weeks are given to do each module and you could do everything at any point.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very easy online class. 4 quizzes, 1 discussion post, and 1 writing assignment due biweekly. Dr. Andrews and her TA gave good feedback on assignments and things were graded quickly. The topics covered are interesting and thought-provoking. Good variety of reading, videos, and lecture videos to keep things fresh.

Super easy 300 level course,discussions and larger assignments were pretty easy to get through and pretty interesting. A couple of the larger assignments were really tedious to do but arent a massive impact on your grade if you dont do one or two of them. Definitely focused more on learning/creating interest rather than being picky about specifics.

Taken as a 300+ just to get credits and it was actually a really enjoyable class. Professor Andrews is great and really understands that her students have lives/work/other classes outside of her own. The material is interesting and the coursework is very manageable. Would take again/take another one of her classes.

Dr. Andrews is an awesome professor and is very understanding. She made lectures and homework assignments fun, interesting, and usually pretty easy. No exams, but a few quizzes due and an essay/some other kind of assignment due weekly. Great option to fill a 300+ level course requirement.

AGRON 342 was a fun class. I took it online and passed with ease. There are bi-weekly quizzes and like 2 or 3 papers throughout the semester. The class made me think, but was in no way hard. Dr. Andrews just wants her students to make the best out of the class.

Great teacher! Actually cares about what she teaches and puts effort into it. You get more out of the class the more you put in. Offers extra credit at the end, very easy to get an a if you try. All quiz questions come from powerpoints.
She never encourages students to share their opinions. She only believes what she thoughts. Take another section if you want to learn something

World Food Issues is one of the easiest classes I have taken at Iowa State. We had 2 paper for the whole semester, both which were super easy. The bi-weekly quizzes are also so easy and she'll help you if you need (during the quiz). There is attendance points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class was just kind of boring. There weren't a lot of assignments, which can be interpreted as a good thing, it's just that even missing just a few assignments can mess with your grade. This class could have been like a few weeks long and it wouldn't have made much of a difference. Overall pretty easy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy in terms of assignments. There is reading reviews, some have a lot of concepts but if you do them all at once you don't have to worry. Lectures can be incredibly boring at times, and you're graded heavy on attendance. The best part was the health fair. Unit plan is a lot of work but easy to complete.

I loved this professor! Most of your grade comes from attendance. There were weekly chapter reviews online but you could easily look them up. You have to make a tiny health lesson and present it in front of elementary students at a health fair. This was fun. There is also a Unit plan that takes a while to make but she is very helpful.
Only reason I didn't give her a 1 is because it's an orientation class.

I had a negative interaction with this professor during class. She is dismissive and strict. She has major issues with any phone use, even if you have stuff going on at home. In a class I had with her, she forced me to take an exam the day after my car accident, and I had a concussion. I wouldn't recommend her unless necessary.

I have had Dr. Smiley for 252, 372, and 472, and I can't recommend her enough. Her classes are tough but rewarding, and she truly cares about her students and is passionate about what she teaches. 472 was especially beneficial for those considering graduate school- it is a difficult class and requires hard work, but it is worth it!

Dr. Smiley is an incredible professor - one of the best I've had in my time at ISU. This class is her passion; she cares that students understand the material, and she assesses this with regular DQ's, quizzes, exams, and papers. Be prepared for a lot of very challenging course material, but don't be discouraged - this class is incredibly rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Smiley is an incredible professor. Her classes are difficult, but if you do the necessary work to learn the material and engage in class, you will succeed. She is remarkably caring and attentive to her students. The content is interesting but challenging. Be prepared for 100-Q T/F exams as well as team-based learning.

Dr. Smiley is so knowledgeable and has a method for the way that she teaches and tests! It may appear tough but its her way of making sure that you fully understand the material, which if you go onto grad school is much needed! Will forever be grateful for everything she taught me!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teaching methods were unusual and just overall not the greatest.

Had the trio 252/372/472, challenging upper-level classes, but they prepare you for graduate level coursework. Lots of papers but they tied into everything learned in class so they weren't hard. Dr. Smiley is a wonderful professor and she enjoys the smaller class. Put in the effort, it's rewarding, don't assume you can get by with minimal effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Smiley was an incredibly condescending instructor. She consistently acted rude towards her co-professor as well as other students. Her course (KIN 252) was by far the most pointless class I've taken so far at Iowa State. For KIN 252 in particular her instruction was fine, But I will be sure not to have her for any other important class.
Moved at such a slow pace. I was so bored.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She kind of thinks she knows everything and is kind of condescending. Does not give much encouragment. Lots of work that seems like busy work or unimportant. The class was easy though. You also have to pay to print a poster assignment at the end of the semester that is about $50 per group.

KIN 372 is the worst class, taught by the worst professor. Unclear grading guidelines and lectures do not make any sense with the material she is attempting to provide. Prepare to do a lot of team-based learning during class. There is a lot of homework, with several assignments due per week. Avoid Dr. Smiley like the plague.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is the type of professor to think that her class is the only one that matters. You are given 3-4 homework assignments a week along with long chapter readings. On top of this, you are given in class questions that are the same weight as the tests and are not graded uniformly at all. Plus exams are 100 questions T/F in 50 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Smiley is great and all, but she's extremely rude. She often got snippy with her associate professor when things didn't go her way. She can be rude when in class and when you talk to her. Attendance is mandatory, and you will fail if you don't attend class, which is hard since it's 8 am on the other side of campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Smiley co-teaches this course with Lisa Dukes. This class is a combo of guest lectures and a big group project. You must attend class because attendance is graded even though the class is only offered at 8 am. Many little assignments lead up to the course project, so stay on top of those. Also, you read a lot of research articles for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Definitely a tough teacher but she is doing it in our best interests. If you are taking an upper-level KIN class that you CHOSE to take, it will be challenging. She pushes you to understand the material for the tests. Notes are confusing, but she answers questions great. One of my hardest but most rewarding classes at ISU w Smiley.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is not bad at lecturing by any means, but the structure of the course was quite ridiculous in my opinion. The vast majority of the grade was determined by one group project and presentation. The numerous quizzes students do for the first couple weeks hold very little value. The project that determines your grade has poor structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found this professor to be unorganized and rude at times. A lot of assignments were tedious and unnecessarily hard. There were a total of 3 exams, all of which were lengthy. Class attendance matters a lot, and the 6-week project really determines whether you pass or not. If you need help I highly suggest reaching out to the TA, not the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Group work, group work, and more group work. Half the semester was just group work and it made it hard due to covid. She was pretty snippy towards her associate professor and I felt like the class was scared of her. I liked the thought of the class but I think the change of the class structure due to covid made her a little angry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A TON of group work and homework. Project that is a huge chunk of grade. Expected to learn on your own outside of class and discuss topics in class. Team discussion really helps and topics are easy to understand. Overall class is unorganized and there is way to much outside work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is very tough! However, if you put in the work, go to class, read the book, study you will do great and will LEARN a lot. Dr. Smiley challenges you and if you rise to the occasion you will do fine in the class. You can tell she really enjoys teaching.

Class used a group learning with iRATs and TRATs which helped us prepare for the test. In class points were awarded for group questions during class. While the juggling project was lengthy and annoying, it definitely cemented concepts in my brain and helped my learning quite a bit. Class is hard, but Dr. Smiley wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Smiley is phenomenal. She expects a lot but is fair and fun. Put in the work and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: All you need to know: 1. Lots, I mean lots of HW 2. Lots of reading (to do the every other day quizzes and HW) 3. Tough exams/quizzes. Not because the material is hard but because of her inability to specify a question's setting ex.,asks you if putting a golf ball is more closed skill than batting a baseball but doesn't tell u if ball was pitched.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Smiley-Oyen was the easily the best professor I had in the  Kinesiology department! She challenges you so nothing comes easy, but you actually feel like she cares and wants you to do well.  Kin 472 is a smaller class, the text and readings are mandatory. A lot of the class was spent on discussion of the assigned readings.

Dr. Smiley was a tricky professor but is super knowledgeable and made the concepts really interesting to learn. You do have to do all of the readings and attend lecture to do well - it's definitely not a class that you can float by in. If you put in the work, it's really interesting and rewarding when you get the grade! My favorite Kin course yet!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Smiley's class is definitely one you have to work for, but she presents the material well and has very clear expectations. She is obviously knowledgeable and very easy to talk to. If you put in the work (reading the book, doing the pre-class questions, etc.) you will do just fine. She's a really neat person to get to know too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Smiley-Oyen at first seems tough and cold, but go to her office hours and you will discover she just wants students to learn in a way that is applicable to life. She doesn't spoon feed you answers, but neither will your boss. If you pay attention, attend lecture, study the slides, and fill out the study guides you should not have a problem.

She knows the content but she is terrible at teaching it to students. I personally think that she should not be teaching. Disorganized. Doesn't let you know of assignment expectations. She won't help you out with assignments or anything really. You work in groups but none of it helps with learning. I would not take this class unless it's required.

Anything graded is hypocritical, she'll tell you not to read into her questions, but then you have to infer a lot of information for the next question and then back again. Does a horrible job of clarifying tricky or similar information. Gets very defensive if you find any inconsistency or mistake with grades.

Dr. Smiley was an awesome professor. Many people thought she was confusing or unclear but if you ACTIVELY pay attention, she really teaches the material well. She always made class exciting and is a really fun and goofy teacher.

She is smart, but doesn't pass that on well to students. She's unclear about expectations and how detailed she expects the in class stuff to be.  You work in groups which is fine, if you're willing to participate and contribute to your group. Her tests are very tricky, so read carefully.

She is very knowledgeable but when it comes to relaying that to students she has a lot of difficulty. She is unorganized and describes things very general. When asked for clarity on issues she gets very defensive and still doesn?t clarify (Ex: how do you want us to explain this ? logically, how many examples do you want- a reasonable number).  Even

This is her first semester teaching the class instead of just teaching the lab. She's all over the place. Class is extremely disorganized and questions are vague and poorly worded. She will eventually get better, but a little rough around the edges right now. She seems a bit jittery.

The test are 70-80 questions and are challenging questions, but she does a great teaching the material and making you understand it so you can do well. It isn't required to go to class but you would be lost if you didn't. She is very nice and willing to answer questions. She wants you to do well.

He has an attendance policy in class where if you miss more than three classes, you automatically fail his class. You could have a 100% A+ and still fail regardless. This logic makes zero sense; things happen in college that you can't predict: Funeral, family emergency, car won't start etc. On top of that, he's a hardass that shows zero sympathy.

I have never seen a professor whine more about the "wrong-doings" of students in his class. He complains or even completely ignores your emails if you address him by the wrong name or are not 100% professional. Group projects are a nightmare. He doesn't teach the class material, he just says, "This is on the test," and moves on. Awful experience.

I can not believe Eric Smith is still employed at Iowa State; he is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He constantly brings up all his past success at Hy-Vee, which is mostly irrelevant to the class. He also brings up his goat farm, I swear he is more passionate about that than actually teaching the class. Almost made me change my major.

Non traditional way of lectures where he mostly talks about his experience and his goat farm. Used to be high up in corporate, carries the same mentality to class. Brutal lectures to sit through, but on exam review days , he tells exactly what to expect on exams.

Very unorganized and confusing class. He makes it feel like he is the dictator ruling over his class and does not take into account students opinion. He teaches solely off of his own work experience and his own business which is fine if you want to trade beef or own a goat farm. Does not hold himself to the same standard he expects of his students.

Showing up to class is mandatory and you have to be prepared to answer questions o the fly or else you lose lots of points. Homework assignments you have to teach yourself how to do. The overall class environment is very disorganized, there seems to be no process of how he teaches. To add to this he's not a very nice professor either.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors ever. He is the most unfair when it comes to grading. I have spent hours and hours working on projects and vague homework assignments and he still graded everyone really harshly. People always had to tell him how to do his job since he would often make mistakes in grading. He is rude and arrogant to say the least. AVOID.

He's a little crazy! Beware if you like super clear directions, don't want to come to every class, and don't like speaking up. He cold calls on everyone for participation, really struggles to present things in a timely manner (ask him clarifying questions), and doesn't really have a filter. He's a pretty nice guy though and has a lot of experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I have had at Iowa state.

I always enjoyed going to class, he would always talk about his experience working in corporate procurement. He teaches you how to succeed in a business setting and what is actually important than focusing on course content. Some of the projects were difficult because he wasn't straight forward to what he wanted. However, grades fairly.

His class really does take up a lot of time. For some reason I still enjoy it more that the other SCM classes with less work. I honestly feel like he actively taught us something, rather than just repeating the same things and expecting us to get it. He does this for fun, you can tell.

Go to class everyday it is a huge part of your grade. The weekly quizzes come straight from the book and go directly on the test word for word. If you need advice he is the guy to go to. I cannot say enough good things about him.

I really don't like her. She is so bad! She graded assignments very lately which makes really difficult to improve the grade. Her instruction, feedback and lectures everything was so bad that you can't really even learning anything. Even, she couldn't reply students email.
It took a while to grade our assignments: I don't know what I got on an essay from October and its finals week.

Where do I begin.  Why are there only 15 assignments across 4 months, and why does the professor not grade stuff 2 months passed the submission date.  If you can't do well on exams, which aren't easy, good luck.  The country project sucked, poorly managed.  This classed used to be at the 240ish range, now its 125. Would never consider taking again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith gave helpful feedback on how to improve essays when grading. We did have many technical difficulties during the semester that weren't necessarily solved quickly. If you have a heavy courseload, beware that during the final week of each module, you will have a 3 page paper due early Friday evening and a 60 question exam due Sunday night.

Yes, this course was disorganized, as modules were posted late every week, things didn't get graded, and communication was rough. BUT, it's a 125 course that everyone is taking to meet another Degree Audit requirement. The essays were easy, the exams were open notes, and it's a chilled class where I learned a lot about politics, so it's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is not the greatest with communication and didn't notice a major exam flaw until 2 days after the due date. Her lectures are great & you can use on exams. There are also papers and discussion posts about a country you pick at the beginning of the first week of class; make sure you are ready to write 5 papers about that country's government.

The most disorganized professor I've ever come across! Not only did I have to constantly email her to correct the readings (page numbers didn't align between the syllabus and the text), but she forgot to publish modules almost every week. Lectures are chaotic and all over the place and busy work is of her upmost priority. Easy A, though.

I actually had her for PolS 383, but that wasn't listed as an option since it's her first semester teaching the class. 

This class has been my least favorite that I've taken though Iowa State, largely because of the teaching style. There was little to no reliable structure, you didn't actually learn anything if you attended class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer. Shouts so much and complicates the topic! she is disorganized and she never finishes a topic in the allocated time. she pretends to be nice and helpful but she is prejudiced towards a certain demography. she pokes holes in assignments and points of view of people of color and gives ears to white students.

Make sure to keep up on the professor as she tends to forget to grade things. This class stressed me out because nothing was ever in the grade book. The professor gives extra credit but you have to keep up on her to get the details. The tests are open book and they are still super difficult. There is also a group final presentation.
she's the most disorganized person. She gives no feedback what so ever on the tests and the lectures bored the hell out of me. Did I learn anything in this class? I don't even know.

I took the online version of PolS 241. It was the usual online stuff and wasn't extremely difficult. You'll actually need to read your textbooks to get by in the exams so know your stuff before you take it. The hardest thing was doing an online and coordinating the group project between members; it was definitely hard to communicate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is very nice person and clearly means well. If you go to her office you'll get a long conversation with a lot of personal questions. But she is soooo disorganized. It takes her forever to say anything, and when she does she'll repeat herself four times. This makes her fall way behind on the syllabus, and everything gets even more disorganized.
Dr. Smith is very easy to talk to and is knowledgeable.
Great Professor, well designed class. Readings were organized to make a point and lead into each other.

Professor Smith is not very organized or articulate, so she sometimes takes forever to say something obvious. She also does not accept it if you disagree with her. The class was usually pretty willing to have a good discussion, though, and she did not get in the way too often.

Knows the subject material really well, and the class is really interesting, and she is always willing to talk after class about current events. The problem is that there is never enough time to discuss everything in class so we are always rushed. It would be nice if we got an extra half hour. We could have some kind of class discussion.

This professor will amaze you at how disorganized and confused she can get. She is one of the most scatterbrained and awkward professors I have ever encountered. Way to many different assignmentsprojects going on that she even had trouble keeping up with. Not a hard class  but, she just puts way more on everyone's plate than is necessary.

There were a lot of class discussions among students on top of her PowerPoint lectures. PowerPoints & Exam Reviews (with the topics of MC questions and essay prompts given) are published to BlackBoard. You also have to write 6 country profile responses throughout the semester (can use Wikipedia). Class attendance is mandatory, miss 4+ = drop class.
Pretty easy class, but she will drive you crazy with how disorganized she is. Mandatory attendance!
Not a bad class, but she goes off targets sometimes. She needs more experiences to teach, but she also helps her students a lot.

Very nice lady.  She makes an effort to make the lectures interesting but for someone who is only taking the class for a required elective the class is a bore.  She goes off on tangents sometimes, but overall, not a bad professor. I recommend for someone interested in political science, rather than a software engineer.
Homework is easy with participation. Very encouraging teaching.
This guy is the real deal. If you want information on what the world of business looks like outside of college, he is your man. No nonsense. Put in the effort, and you will be rewarded greatly.

Professor Snook is one of my favorite professors at Iowa State. He is very funny and his lectures are always intriguing. There are two groups projects, two exams, and a couple individual projects. He is always willing to help and gives great feedback. I highly recommend taking MIS 301 with Snook.

I had Julie in Spring 2017 for an online course. The course was laid out well, assignments were easy to understand, and her online discussions were relevant to real-ife things. The reason I gave her a 4 is that she was a really slow grader, but she did give good solid feedback on papers and on discussion posts.

I was shocked to see Dr. J's low scores. This is the second class that I have had with her and thought she was awesome. The content was very engaging and she provided context into various views of leadership and how diversity is central to this. The team based learning environment was a great way to develop a comfort level to discuss hard issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took this class as part of the leadership program. If you go to class, participate, and pay attention you'll do great. There is a lot of reading but it's on par with a 300 level class. Teacher is incredibly friendly and always available to meet with you to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Julie clearly cares about her students. She gives good feedback on papers that you write and also tells you about new leadership and job opportunities around campus!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Unclear deadlines, tons of reading tons, of homework, lots of pain. I took the class to fill a hole in my schedule, I seriously  regret taking it.  Your grade is based on five papers based of the readings from a 240 page book, she is extremely harsh grader and will take off tons of points for minor errors in spelling or grammar .
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Very kind and means well. Unclear in presenting assignments. Syllabus says one thing, Blackboard says another, and she says something entirely different. Takes very long to post grades and to answer emails. Readings are boring and there are loads of them. Claims to require participation in class discussions, but does nothing to enforce this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Julie was a great teacher. I was nervous on a public speaking class but she did a great job. This class was at the University of Utah and was her first time teaching it but did great. Super easy. Asks you to read but says she won't penalize you if you don't because she doesn't read it herself. I highly recommend taking her public speaking class.

I never did a single reading in the class and waited to do the Portfolio project 5 hours before it was due and got a all the points. Class was to easy from the get go and all the students knew it and took advantage of it. Sadly the class was women and leadership and neither the  professor or the TA had any leadership qualities at all!

Class was 100% paper based.  No need to read assigned PDFs unless you want to participate in class discussion.  About half the readings were really interesting, the others were repetitive.  She was a bit unclear about paper/project requirements so READ ASSIGNMENT SHEETS CAREFULLY!

Took the class b/c it sounded interesting but it was the exact opposite.  Very boring text readings and forced discussion while in class.  She is very unclear with what she wants in work.  Very scatterbrained prof.  Paper requirement are VERY long, 10-15 pages.
Dante was an amazing TA! He was able to explain concepts for DiffEq in a way that actually made sense. He is extremely enthusiastic about DiffEq and engaging as well!

He was an amazing TA for DiffEq. He was able to explain complex problems better than anywhere else. His office hours, and the review before quizzes were part of why I did as well as I did. He is really helpful, and you can do well on the quizzes if you review the quiz banks, go to office hours, and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the toughest professors I had at Iowa State, One thing that he does that lowers his teaching score is unfair grading. He zeroed my participation points from 90% to a whole 0%, which is wrong because I attended most of the classes, and he intentionally lower my grade using his professor power. Highly Not Recommended.

Eric was the best professor I've ever had. He's blunt and direct, but you can tell he genuinely cares in a way other professors don't. His classes are more like business meetings, and are very big on discussion. When you do something right, he makes sure to tell you you're doing a good job. Very rewarding and positive class experience (:

Awesome instructor. I found class to be very engaging and most days it flew by. The group projects are extremely tough if your group does not work well together. The grading is very tough and can be hard to know exactly what you need to do to get an A. Wish I could have done better, but I learned a lot from this class.

Don't take this class with Eric: he somehow expects you to do well on projects with extremely vague directions and then will be disappointed and show the class examples of good projects AFTER the due date. Talks about Hy-Vee a little too much and gets distracted- forgetting to talk about material relevant to the exam, which then surprises you
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors ever. He is the most unfair when it comes to grading. I have spent hours and hours working on projects and vague homework assignments and he still graded everyone really harshly. People always had to tell him how to do his job since he would often make mistakes in grading. He is rude and arrogant to say the least. AVOID.

Not a fan of Eric. He's abrasive and subjective. Plays favorites and calls you out if your not one. Grades tough, demand attendance, not a friendly guy in class. However, if you attend office hours and ask for 1-on-1 help he can be pretty supportive! Unfortunately, not all students have time to coddle his ego.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was a Hyvee Exec and gives excellent life examples of when he was in purchasing. I definitely got a lot out of this class that I will use in my future career. There are three big projects and it sucks if you have a bad group. The tests are easy if you study. People say he can be tough but he's preparing you for the real world. Take it with him.

He treats his students like they are 12 years old. Didn't give guidelines for a paper and then when the low average came back he gave examples just making fun of what people put in the paper because no one had any idea what he wanted. The dudes a joke, but you're guaranteed to get a decent grade.

Eric's class is the only class I actually look forward to going to. He teaches different than the typical professor which is great, he doesn't lecture much. He has no tolerance for electronics during class which initially I thought was BS but the class is only 50 minutes long and he's entertaining the whole time so the time flies by.

Eric was overall a great teacher. His previous professional background before Iowa State is very helpful and at times he seems very hard on grading and expectations but if you work hard toward his expectations it will help you a lot in the long run. Through his class participation it helped me a lot with critical thinking and decision making.
He's a cool guy, great stories and he is real funny. HE IS SO DIFFICULT THOUGH. He makes material harder than it needs to be, and he seems to enjoy it or something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Eric Smith is by far the best professor I've had at ISU in my 4 years here. He is an ex-executive for Hy-Vee so he brings a ton of real world knowledge into his classes and is very passionate about the topics. He makes lecture on a potentially boring topic (purchasing) very interesting. 10/10 would take again.

Eric Smith is by far the best professor I have had at Iowa State.  Being an ex-exec at a large company, he has fantastic real world experience that teaches valuable life lessons and helps prepare his students for the real business world. Learned more in this class than my last 20 classes combined.  Absolutely take this class if you have the chance

The most arrogant SOB I've ever met in my life. He cares more about telling stupid stories than teaching. Literally screams at people who look away from him talking for two seconds. Being in a room with him was the most dreadful two hours of my week, every week. People only like him because he's easy, everything else about him is awful.

There lots of group projects, but if you put in a good effort, it will pay off in the end. The exams are 60% memorization, 40% of topics gone over in class. Participation is crucial; he takes attendance every day. Bases his teaching on his real professional experiences.

All around awesome instructor. He has tons of interesting stories from his experience in purchasing which makes it much easier to understand some of the cocepts in the class. It's obvious that he genuinely cares about his students and he helps you out as much he he can.  Here's a chili pepper (:
Treats students very well and is interested in what they are doing. However, classes move pretty slow, not much material is covered. His stories are good, but class content isn't the best.

Eric is by far and away my favorite teacher I've had at ISU so far! I'm absolutely awful at math and he somehow made stats make enough sense I got a C+ in the class. He makes everything relateable and is definitely someone I'd take a class with again.

Great guy and professor. The subject matter was difficult for me but he made sure to answer all questions. Comes across very real and personal. Tries to get to know everyone even though there were around 95 students in the class.

He is the best professor I have ever had! I have never paid so much attention or learned so much out of a class. He keeps the class engaged. He also connects the class to real life experiences. The tests are not too bad, especially because he tells you exactly what you need to know. The quizzes are a pain, but not too challenging. HW is helpful.

Best professor I've ever had. Turns a boring topic into one that I enjoyed attending twice a week. Takes attendance every day so I would recommend going. The tests are difficult but he gives you all the tools to be successful. Homework and weekly quizzes are about what youd expect. If you attend class they are pretty easy.

This class is awesome and taught by one of the best professors the SCM department and ISU has to offer. He has tons of experiences and teaches you business life lessons along with purchasing. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!!!

Eric is one of the best instructors that I have had at ISU. He does a great job of bridging the gap between real world application and academia. Also, extremely lighthearted and makes his class enjoyable
Hands down the best professor at Iowa State. Take any and every class you can with him!!!
BEST INSTRUCTOR EVER. AWESOME GUY!!

Eric Smith is the best professor at Iowa State. I have taken Stat 226, MIS 330, and SCM 301 with him and he was an outstanding teacher for all of them. He likes to talk a lot about his experience in the business field but you learn a lot about real world experience. He makes Stat interesting which is literally impossible. Get Eric for any class.
He is just a Lecturer fo this class, he does not write the tests fo this class. He gives you alot of real world but the tests are conceptual based.

Eric is one of the greatest professors I have had at ISU! He is incredibly personable and truly cares about his students. He made a super boring class fun and I actually learned a lot. Seriously, if you have the chance- take his class because you won't regret it.

Favorite professor at ISU! Extremely personable and you can go to him for any questions about the class or life in general. Wants students to actually learn, and become better people in the process. So much respect for Eric.

Missy Springsteen is a very relaxed professor, but definitely one to respect. She is very straightforward about what she teaches, very open and honest about how the course has changed as the laws dictating what can be taught change. No homework, and the midterm and final are open note and extremely easy.

You can tell she truly cares about what she teaches! The tests were easy if you attended class and listened to the lectures. I could find every question from each exam in my notes. One of my favorite classes!

Dr. Missy is seriously the best! She is understanding, blunt, and willing to help. Her "final" is a meeting with her to see how you grew over the semester, which really points out the positives. She is a great source if you need a letter of recommendation, advice, or just support. She does not sugarcoat the education world, which is so nice to hear

Dr. Springsteen was amazing to have. She reminds me a lot of my high school English teacher who I loved. As someone who has always been interested in the history of education, this class was very easy for me.

Dr. Missy is an AMAZING professor. She was understanding and helpful when I was managing a couple family losses. She gives great tips and really helps you grow as an educator. She also is a very fun and entertaining lecturer. I would highly encourage people to take a class with Dr. Missy!

Dr. Springsteen is phenomenal. She's fun, she's relatable, and she brings necessary real-life experience into her lectures. She cares about knowing her students and wants us to succeed. I can't say enough about how great she is.
Best prof at Iowa State, hands down!

Dr. Springsteen is amazing. She has so much experience being a teacher veteran. She implements her personal experiences into EDUC 204, which really helps give perspective. She is also such a cool person overall. She was very accommodating and cares about her students.
Love her! She has a good sense of humor and her lectures are entertaining. Be careful to not ask questions that already have the answer on Canvas!
She was such a hoot! You can tell she has a passion for education but isn't going to sugar coat it to make you stay. Would recommend her class.

Missy is THE BEST! She organizes this class in a very digestible way. She's so flexible and genuinely supports you. Attendance is graded, but you can attend other sections if you miss your own. You have to acknowledge your biases as a future educator in order to grow, but it's not "difficult", it just requires an open mind & genuine reflection.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Springsteen was super nice. She is very unique, but that made the class so much better. There is a lot of reading you have to do and she doesn't force you to do it, but you are just hurting yourself if you don't. She did a great job providing examples of a lot of situations we discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can't say enough good things about Professor Haupt!!! She really wants everyone to learn and grow as future educators. She brings in a lot of stories from her time as a teacher and understands that we have other obligations outside of class. 100% would take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a great person. I enjoyed going to her classes, but she's a very tough grader. She doesn't give clear criteria and will not hesitate to dock points over small things. She's very fun and friendly, but it's not easy.
Amazing professor. If you are going into secondary ed you will have to have her.

Prof. SH is so funny and caring. She is passionate about her work at ISU and provides personal examples from her prior middle school teaching career. She is personable and gives valuable feedback. As long as you are proficient in writing and willing to put in effort, this class is an easy A.

Take this course if you want to spend a semester learning about rocks and gems! Be prepared what you're signing up for. All lectures have information that will be on 4 tests that will hugely determine your grade in the class. There are also surprise POP quizzes. If you put in work and effort you will see results, if not, be prepared for poor grades
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Spry was a joy to listen to, and I loved his lectures. I wasn't very happy with the grading curve as it seemed pointless to try in this class bc your grade is not based on what you do; it's based on chance and how the rest of the class does. As someone who often gets sick, it sucked that I was forced to go to class out of fear of missing a quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I decided to take GEOL 105 for a needed natural science credit. You can tell right away Professor Spry is extremely passionate about gems and even brings some to class for you to look at! There are 3 quizzes and 2 exams you NEED to show up for in class. Review the lecture slides and go to class and you should be set up to get a decent grade.

Did not enjoy this class. He only grades on 4 things and offers no extra credit, so if you do bad on any of these exams, you're screwed. He seems like a nice guy who is clearly passionate, but the format of his class was not it. It was hard for me to memorize all of the jargon and he didn't provide any study guides. Not as easy as my advisor said.

reviews.comment: You can tell he is very passionate about his material and he is a nice guy but he goes through material very fast and his quizzes and exams are very detailed and very hard. You are expected to memorize a lot or be a very good guesser to get an A. No homework or any outside work required which was very nice!

A good guy and very well respected by everyone. In the class itself there are few opportunities for class points. Your grade is decided by the Midterm and Final. You learn, what you take out of class. Take this class very seriously and save ALL of your lab scores. You must use these to study for the 2 tests in class.
