reviews.comment: Really helpful, maybe not the most exciting lecturer, but knows his stuff and is super nice! Decent about of work, optical mineralogy takes a while before you feel even decently comfortable with it.
Perfect, the best
perfect
Awesome professor and appreciated intelligence, he really has a spark for this class and gemstones, he is nice and truly seems to care. Also he isn't too bad on the eyes or the ears ;)
Great teacher and very knowledgeable! He's very nice and is more than happy to talk with you about the subject!
He is a really great teacher and has a cool Austrailan accent. He never gets mad about attendance but you have two pop quizes so you should go to class and its easy.
For a class that no one takes seriously, he is quite a good teacher. It has to be horribly frustrating to teach drop outs and stupid students.
Does a good job teaching stupid students.
Shes an amazing person and really tries to work 1 on 1 to get students where they need to be. Iowa State could not have a hired a more passionate and caring person.

She was one of my favorite TA's/Professors I have had at Iowa State. She is so caring and devoted to anatomy that it makes it so easy to be engaged! She is also very easy to talk to and reminds me of my grandma (in the best way). Very great TA!

Anatomy lab is so much fun and she makes it really interactive and easy to understand. She is also really cute and happy all the time which makes learning easier. She really cares about her students doing well.

Anatomy lab is the hardest one i have ever taken. you must SPELL every word that may be in minitest--look at models and write the name of structure, 20 points per time. although she is a tough grader, she is nice and willing to help student. i am an international student, and she is italian, she knows how difficult the things are and give me hints.
Pasta Cooking Class.... AMAZING!!!!! She is a wonderful teacher and person.  Would love to take more classes with her! :)

Way too excited about Bio and it's funny.  Lab completely sucks because there is so much you have to do in the three hours.  Would be cool if it wasn't so cramed with info.  She is very smart and helpful, attend class, listen, and look interested and she'll like you

Field Botany=Easiest 2 science credits in history. If you are a Humanities or LAS Major, take this class for an easy A. You get to go outside and classes usually get out an hour to an hour and a half early.
I had her for Biology 265 (Field Botany, formerly Botany 202) and she's freakin' amazing!
AVOID.  hated this class due to her she is so unclear, and once docked me points for having things in a papper that she didnt think i knew.

I had a really hard time with her, didn't understand her lectures, didn't understand her explanations when I asked questions.  Felt like the class was very biased towards botany, and that she wasn't as familiar with the animal labs.  But, she is really enthusiastic, and she plays good music during labs.

I was fortunate to have this professor as my lab teaching assistant.  She has a Spanish accent, but it makes biological words so much more interesting. Very excited about lab work that is being discovered which makes us enthusiatic! Answers any questions you may have and goes over lab thoroughly.

This is an awesome class to just get away from the boring sit down of regular classes. You get to go outside and learn while having some fun. It's a very easy class and the teacher is very interesting. You get to go on some field trips and learn to recognize plants. Overall excellent class.

His critiques during class are vague and unhelpful, leading you to believe you are doing well in class. If you ask for more help during office hours, he will tell you no and that he is uninterested in having those conversations. He gives out the assignment details late, allowing you less than a week to complete it. Extremely arrogant.
Mitchell Squire blew me away with his interesting approach to design. He can be hard at times, but he really just wants you to make your best work. Loved learning from him!
He was the BEST prof. I have ever met. If you work for it you will have the best project of your time at Iowa State. You read articles and write to make the architecture meaningful
Simply mind blowing and life changing.
His arrogance exceeds his ability to teach. A semester with him makes me hate the artistic world. I have never been more disappointed with a professor in my college experience.

I had Mitchell for a independent study studio my 5th year. I received little to no feedback and a general "cold-shoulder" from him. The entire semester he acted above the class and like he despised us. He wouldn't come to class. If we needed advice we would have to come to him. WORST TEACHER IN MY UNDERGRADUATE EXPERIENCE.
Mitchell exhibited favoritism towards females too much in classroom environment.
the most blissful ass kicking i've had.  incredible insight when you can understand what he's saying.
ALL AROUND GREAT TEACHER.  HE'LL PROBABLY BECOME THE EDITOR OF ONE OF THOSE COLLECTIONS OF ARCH CRITIC ESSAY BOOKS WE ALL WASTED MONEY ON WHILE IN SCHOOL. COOL GUY.
No Comments

How this guy has a job... i dont know. Absolutely the worst professor I have had in my entire life. Impossibly hard grader, impossibly hard quizzes and exams, and his lectures are BORING and usually not even covering course material. DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HIM! The only people with passing grades on our finals cheated... that tells you everything

He is so unorganized that we have to have 3 quizzes (2 during the same class period) and an exam back-to-back within a week. Don't even bother studying for the quizzes, you're going to fail anyway. The syllabus says the quizzes will be on Canvas, but they have all been in-person (shocker). For the sake of your sanity, DO NOT TAKE.

He is not following the syllabus dates; our midterm is for some reason in the middle of November. The group project is also a mess, and makes no sense, as he keeps changing the requirements

You absolutely cannot follow his lectures and if you fall behind he moves on. He doesn't seem to know what he's talking about and makes long pauses frequently. I would not take any of his classes if you want to actually learn

A group project is a big part of your grade, but he does not conduct peer reviews at the end, so make sure you get a good group or you will be stuck doing all of the work.

SO HARD! So much statistics for this class. He is soft spoken, hard to understand, and boring. Very hard material and tests are very difficult. You don't get individual grades, you only ever get a cumulative grade update 2 times in the semester. Will say something is not on the test then it will be.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: It was a pleasure to take Professor Ramaswami's class.  Lectures were thoughtful, insightful, and interesting.  We sets high expectations for projects, presentations and the final exam, and though not easy, it was worthwhile and fulfilling.

Very knowledgeable professor and truly cares about his students.  Would recommend taking a class with him.  The only down side(s) are his lectures can be boring and he assigns weekly homework where you have to research a topic and then right a "paragraph" about it.  Some people found his test hard, but he does curve.

Professor Ramaswami is one of the smartest and most caring professors at Iowa State.  His class is hard but you just need to take it seriously and ask questions.  He is very helpful and loves when you come to his office hours.  Get to know the guy and attend class and take notes.  Also very beneficial to read the text book.

I've literally had to meet with the head of the marketing department about how this guy treated me whenever I asked a question in his class. "Ask a friend for the notes, I'm sorry you don't understand what I'm teaching;" "The book and powerpoint won't help you for the test" but makes you read it for the quizzes. Absolutely awful-Avoid avoid avoid.

Dr. Ramaswami knows a lot about marketing research, and is an expert in the field. Despite this, he struggles to communicate and teach this material to his class. He gets rather hostile when you ask him questions or ask for clarification, and is frequently unclear or disorganized regarding testsquizzesgroup projectshomework. Very frustrating.

He is hard to listen to, especially as a night class. He speaks very quietly and is extremely unclear with expectations. All of his assignments are very vague and he seems to think that they are easy to understand. Tests are very difficult. Has a really good curve though.  Sometimes gives extra credit for attendance.

Hard to understand due to quiet demeanor. Not a hard class, but not easy either. Talks about all test questions in class if your paying attention - which is hard! Book is not necessary. Tests are hard, but puts a curve on the class if needed.  Overall, a very knowledgeable professor.
Would avoid taking it with him if possible.  Tests are near impossible.  Expectations are not clear at all.

He is willing to help but he rushes his teaching and doesn't take time to explain things in class.  The class is not to hard but it is not easy by any means.  The content can be difficult, as he doesn't take the time to explain to the students.
He was an alright teacher. He likes to talk about himself a lot but he is an easy grader and very willing to help outside of class with anything. Very knowledgeable guy and very nice.
Really boring class. Thinks his advice is the most important thing you will ever hear. Gives fill in the blank tests. Would recommend avoiding him if possible.

The whole class was extremely lost on all of the short answer tests but he realized that and was very easy on the grading.....I highly recommend him as a teacher for the simple fact that he is an easy grader!!

This professor has been the best I've had at ISU! He's extremely knowledgable and very willing to help you not only in class but to build your resume. The project is probably the most relevant project I've done, if you are at all thinking of a career in brand management it will for sure differentiate you from others. Highly recommend the class!

Very interesting class, especially if you have had an internship in the past. Applicable examples, and up to date concepts. Project is a huge part, start early. Tests are difficult, but he is reasonable. I recommend this course.
The classes were really boring, but the book helped to clarify concepts a lot. Relatively easy class.
Really interesting class and he does a great job of teaching it. Project is a big part of grade make sure you have a good group.
I really like him. He is probably the smartest man I have ever met! Very helpful, but the class got harder at the end of the semester. Gives a fun project.

Good teacher. He makes concepts really simple so you can understand them. The only problem could be is if you want to slack and not pay attention, you probably won't understand what is going on in the class.

Class coursework itself was easy, used a textbook that he wrote that had quizzes and discussion posts. Attendance/participation was graded yet not mentioned when going over the syllabus. DOES NOT reply to emails, replied to one email and none after that even if it was for something important. Lectures consisted of him just talking about nothing.

- There are no exams
- Late submissions get 0 credit
- Doesn't reply to emails
- Rambles about POINTLESS things
- Doesn't know how to answer the most basic questions
- Doesn't know how to use technology

- Says one thing, does another
- Random attendance check ins
Save yourself. DO NOT take his class.

MIS professor that cannot use Canvas. Be fully prepared to have your grades lowered right before the end of semester because that is "the way the system is set up" according to him. Lectures are haphazardly put together, most of ours were just him going through the book. 

On the positive end, he does allow you to resubmit the project portions.
Do not take his class you will learn more about his flute than any mis material. His book is nonsense and does not help with the quizzes or hmw. It was a total waste of time and lazy teaching.

Do not take this class from Sree. He rambles about pointless things that have nothing to do with the content. Talks quietly and doesn't make sense half the time. Goes back on his word; told me something would not be graded, then gave everyone 24 hours to complete said lengthy assignment - just to end up giving everyone a 0 even though we did it.

One of the worst professors I have had at ISU, lectures are just rambling without much meaning, exams and group project were a joke but easy to get good grades on, skipped class for 2 months and didn't miss a thing or have anything due during that period. Very easy class, awful quality if you expect to learn something. Lucky 310 is similar material

Good guy, very bland lectures. Not a lot of people would go. We pretty much went through the book and he talked about it. Not a lot of homework and only two exams, which weren't bad. There was a group project too, and as long as you attempted to do it well he gave a good grade. Again, good guy, knows his stuff, but not great lectures.

Sree is a great guy but not a great professor you will not learn much about MIS in this class. It is however a class where tests are taken online and there is no need to study. If the tests are moved back into centers the Tests will be very difficult.

Sree is a nice guy, but not a very good professor. Seems to have no direction or plan for the class. I am not sure what I learned/was supposed to learn in this class. Quite easy, but if you are at all interested in MIS I would not recommend

He's a good guy, but not a great professor. Would definitely recommend this course to someone who isn't really interested in MIS. There are two tests a a handful of projects/assignments, but no group work. I would take again, but I also am not interested in MIS.

I have been recommending him to everyone! If you are not interested in taking an MIS class, this is perfect. The homework and exams are super easy and require minimal effort. Super sweet guy who cares about what he does, but probably do not take if you are actually interested in MIS.
Never responds to emails, very vague about his assignments and what he's looking for. He has no idea what he is doing and I don't understand how he is still even teaching.
Sree is clueless. Doesn't respond to any emails. Questions from months ago haven't been answered on discussion board. All around terrible professor.

Class was pretty easy with only two exams and a couple easy assignments and group projects. Don't really need to go to class because he just reads off the slides and everything is posted to canvas. He also is bad at responding to emails and canvas messages- he never replied or did anything when I asked him about my grade on an exam.

Worst teacher I have ever had. NO clue how to run a class. Never responds to emails. Doesn't teach. Doesn't label assignments as assignments so you will miss them if you are not careful. Doesn't grade things. Assignment descriptions are so vague you will be so confused. Does not know how to run a class or teach. I've never had such an awful teacher
This guy has no clue what he's doing. Does not respond to any emails. Very boring. No clue how he's still teaching.

Going into week 5 of classes now, Sree still hasn't even told us the definition of MIS. He does not respond to emails or his course discussion board. he lectures heavy mostly about life and tries to relate to MIS. his exams are very similar to his pre exams or practically the same. group project is super easy. very unorganized and can't read his handwriting at all so it can get confusing just do the homework and get good grades. easy class to skip. does not grade until the end of semester

hes boring the class will not catch your attention or be interesting to you. hes very nice but boring, I had a midterm next week and I honestly feel like i really havent learned anything. not much homework so far though.

Not worth taking his class; late for grading, lectures on and on. Positive is that he doesn't give a lot of tests, but quizzes randomly.

He is very unorganized and a bit selfish I feel . He does not respond to emails on time , does not come prepared to class and he reads from the book . Very boring lectures , more often than not you will find yourself sleeping
Sree was one of the most unorganized professors I have had at Iowa State. Grades were never in, assignments weren't explained, and he never went out of his way to help his students.

I do not recommend Nilakanta. His lectures are so boring and you go over the same material the entire week. Class has no direction, he'll just talk about whatever he wants to. Project is very ambiguous and he provides very little feedback. Subjectively grades HW with no feedback. Two tests, 5 HW assignments, and a group project.

WORST TEACHER! He rambles the entire class and you can not even understand what he is saying.  He does not care about his students and his tests are nearly impossible.  If you can get another teacher do so, as this is the worst one I have had at Iowa State. You will learn nothing about the class, and I have no idea what it is even about.
He is so boring and I have no idea what he taught is related to the class or not. Read the book and skip all classes you. And retake it next semester.  Nothing can learn from him.
He is an awful teacher. Half the time you can not understand what he is saying. He rambles in class and half of the stuff he talks about is not even related to the class.

You want boring? Attend this class.  You want grades? Read the book THOROUGHLY (it's all he tests on)and do the project.  You want to understand data modeling at the end of this course?  Good Luck! Unorganized, throw your syllabus away, we are currently 3 weeks behind with three weeks to go, and trust me, it will all be on the final. What teaching?

I liked him as a person.  Hes pretty laid back and understanding.  His teaching could use some work.  He seemed a little unorganized at times and the class didnt seem to have structure or direction.  I never had a good sense of where we were going or what I was learning although I was getting good grades.

Horrible teacher. Rambles on in class about stuff that is irrelevant to the course, homework and tests. Doesn't have any structure for notes. Never responds to emails, and his English isn't the greatest. Doesn't use a textbook so you have no idea what to study for the exams. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Awful. Class required in MIS program. Nilakanta barely taught at all. Class run by grad student. Whole class was a joke. We had to learn a brand new programming language on our own (Ruby on Rails). We basically were supposed to replicate WebCT except make it better (all in 1 semester). Class time is a waste. They don't use a normal grading system.

MIS538 is a class for the self guided student.  If you need to be spoonfed, you should seek other classes.  The class includes a lot of reading, including Ph.D. level works.  A great class for those who are willing to put in the extra time to truly understand the material.  Not a great class for a typical MBA (you will face M.S. in IS students).

Sree is a cool guy. Very laid back and always willing to help out.  His tests are pretty tough because they're over the book, and he doesn't cover it much in class.  Projects and homeworks are easy because they're same as ComS 207 basically.
Knows his stuff, good guy, challenging material

Ok, the class was simple...he is a very cool guy and would allow the class to have some interesting conversations (not on topic), but the only thing I gained from this class was how to use Oracle (or break it), he really didn't teach at all the last half of the semester, just did oracle demos.
Cool Guy.  Very interesting when not lecturing.  Constantly Fell asleep, but very knoledge able.  Always willing to help.

He has no instructions for the projects or homework he gives out.  Never really mentions the book, or whats on the tests or anything.  Lectures are really boring, week of midterms he might of have spent 4 days talking about the class, rest of the time he just lectures about random stuff.  Very unhappy...

The professor teaches you everything you need to know about Hadoop. The labs are a lot of work, but if you are interested in big data, they are valuable introductions to the different technologies. He also cares a lot about the students and tries to help them.
the only guidance you can get is from the TAs and it is sometimes not on time.
Best instructor! Intelligent, clear and always make students involved

Dr. Srikanta is one of the most gentle professors i've come across at ISU. His CPRE419 benefitted me a lot, the course was much involved with lot of interesting labs, the professor did a great job on delivering excellent content on Large Scale Data analysis tools, a field of Big Data that is till evolving  by the day. Great class i would recommend.
Best instructor I have had at IAState. Clear, concise explanations. Involved homework.
Definitely the best lecturer I have had at ISU. He kept us involved with questions, and presented the material very clearly.
Need to be in his class and pay attention. Otherwise it is tough. Makes us work for the grade.

great teacher

good teacher. teaches in easy to understand way.

You can tell he enjoys the subject and knows a lot about it.  His enthusiasm is contagious.  Very helpful, good balance of algorithms and programming work
The best prof I've had here at ISU.
Best prof ever!  He can even lecture without notes.

Linda is absolutely adorable, but her lectures are extremely boring and you could just read them on your own and get the same ,if not more, out of it. She focuses on large pictures during class but tests over weird little details. She makes this class much harder than it needs to be.

Linda is adorable but this class is way harder than it needs to be. Often specific details are tested for on the exams so the learning is not conceptual. Do not underestimate this course, you will need to study for the exams and quizzes if you want an A. She goes through powerpoints very fast. It is a hard class to make interesting.

Overall, it was a fun class with the lab.  There's a lot of science behind cooking and you'll get into a lot of it.  There was a fair amount of memorization in some sections but if you thought of the material in context, the answer could often be reasoned through.

My only complaint with Linda was that she goes through here powerpoints very quickly.  However her tests are very straightforward and as long as you go through them once or twice on your own you will find them very easy.

Great class and good professor! Information from lectures is super clear. I did not take the lab though and tests include a lot of lab material, so it is difficult to get that material. If you ask though she will definitely help you. A lot of memorization.
the best class i have ever expetienced!!

So unhelpful! I hated going to class because it was totally unnecessary. She was plenty nice but not helpful when it came to questions. She knows what she's talking about but she just wasn't a good teacher over all. She also has no points other than the test which she makes way harder than necessary for a 111 class.
She is an awesome teacher!!  She is very easy to ask questions too and she makes class fly by.  Lab is the best part of this class and the food rocks!!

Linda is an awesome lab TA.  She is very nice and helpful.  She's willing to answer any questions and spends time going over things when students don't understand them.  This lab is a blast!  You get to taste all kinds of foods.  Make sure you know what problems can arise in preparing the food and remedies for them - that's a big part of the tests!

This class was a blast, and Linda is the nicest person. You get to taste a ton of good food. Make sure you go to every lab bc you get points for going. Also, make sure you know the defects and what causes them in products.

Overall an easy class. There's a discussion post and lecture videos w/ questions due weekly. Not hard, but definitely time consuming. Two tests, both four long essay questions, and two current event papers. Once again not hard, but majorly time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Globe 320 is a very easy and helpful course before travelling on an internship. This course only has a few assignments, but they are all due around the same time. The assignments are not that difficult, but they just require a bit of research and time. Professor Swoboda is very helpful if there is anything you need for these assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Swoboda is a great professor. She is very caring for her students and really wants them to succeed. She grades very easily and supplies students with great feedback on assignments. 211 is also an easy course that requires a bit of work outside of class, but is overall very easy.

Over-passionate, over-loving, and over-educated are 3 phrases I'd used to describe Mr.  Swartwood.  His clashing outfits and decadent taste leave you coming back most Mondays and some Wednesdays.  His teaching style is uniquely his, and this will not be like any class you've taken before.  Be prepared to learn on your own and think freely.
Just loves to ramble.

Basically agreeing with everyone else. Super unprofessional relationships with students. 
Yes, he is funny and at times the class is entertaining. However, really horrible in every other way. Has you working on a project all semester and then gives you the guidelines two days before it's due. So much time wasted on unnecessary things

Most unorganized class I've ever taken. Assignment reqs and due dates change all the time,you never really know what's gonna happen in class,& instructions are almost always unclear. You also get just a few minutes for a 10 pt quiz each week. Class could be interesting if he wasn't so all over the place. His disorganization makes class much harder.

Prof. Swartwood, doesn't know how to stay on topic. There is no clear direction of the class and the syllabus is subject to change at any moment. He also will just do random things such as bring in a guest speaker when it's supposed to be work time for projects.

Guy does not have an organized bone in his body. No clear time on when assignmentsare due and changes the assignments multiple times leading up to the due date. This is the most unorganized class I have ever taken and did not know when any assignments are due. He also changed the final two days before it was due!!!

Good professor. Clearly explains all concepts and encourages students to share their ideas and questions. Tells you exactly what is going to be on the quizzes and tests and will have it on canvas (not even in a testing center) if the class agrees on that.

Dawn is a quirky person but her personality fits the class. She cares a lot about her students and their success. Open note quizzes and super easy exams with only a few readings with simple response questions. Doesn't always take attendance but will on occasion.

Acts in an aggressive manner. she wants to encourage us as students to ask questions and participate, but when we do she barates and makes fun of you and says you're wrong. she does t like to teach clearly because she acts like she doesn't want to be there. and if she doesn't like you get bad grade.

She typically answers your question with another question and then looks at you stupidly and argues with you if you disagree on anything she believes.  Assigns massive projects near the same time with little to no time to work on them.

Wasn't very clear on assignments.  If you ask questions, she makes you feel stupid.  Participate and user her office hours and she will like you.  Try hard and you will receive a good grade. Gets very angry when people talk.
Sweet rules! This is one of the easiest ComSt classes I've taken all because Dawn is so helpful. Not only was it easy, but I learned more in this class then most.

She was very nice and the class was easy for the most part. There were a few things that were hard to wrap your mind around, but she was always coming around to help. I like that she tried to relate to us by talking about TV shows she likes before class started. Be prompt and ready to learn though! She doesn't like tardiness.

Thought she was a very good teacher. The class is a lot of work, but its all explained very clearly. She is VERY nice, and takes time to make everyone understands. I would highly reccomdend her class. I'm taking another with her next semester!

She was very calm with our class, extended due dates, and took it really slow, almost to slow.  The material was pretty easy, so I could see why she got frustrated when people didn't do good on the quizes, but she never got overally upset.  From what I heard, she has calmed down alot, and I thought she was very approachable.
She gets really moody, takes it out on the class. Makes it clear she in not a fan of ISU. Not understanding if you have to miss do to very reasonable reasons

She is a rather tough grader and is not very approachable. When you go to talk to her she acts like you're wasting her time and she is not very helpful at all. She also likes to give you multiple projects at one time. She likes you to talk a lot, but debates and argues everything you say!
I learned LP and NLP optimization for supply chains really well. Lecture videos and weekly RATs were super helpful.

This class was super helpful because of all the in-class practice problems. Working through examples with the professor and in groups made the material way easier to understand. Posted videos and walkthroughs were great for reviewing later, and the professor was always available to help. Overall, the hands-on approach really made everything click.

reviews.comment: Not the best SCM 460 professor. Uses Team Based Learning and online lectures instead of actually teaching. She rambles on about unimportant things like she is trying to prove that she knows a lot about them. However, this class is required for the first year of any design major so you just gotta learn to deal with her pointless ramblings and projects.
Awful at grading tests

Often rambles about irrelevant things.  At first the class is interesting, however she quickly begins getting into depth about topics that are not important to the class.  She has an odd sense of humor, and the tests are nothing like the material on the so called study guide.  Tests are all short answer basically and she has ridiculous assignments.

If you can drop the class, I recommend it, or any class she teaches. Worst professor in the CRP dept. hands down. There isn't a CRP undergrad who doesn't have a story to tell about Bradbury. Truly has a liberal agenda towards planning.
overall great prof! you learn a lot!  shes easy going and has a nice personality!  i enjoyed her class.
I took her class nearly 3 years ago and still hold a grudge. She is useless, whiny, arrogant, and taught incredibly irrelevant information. One of the worst professors of my college career
tries to bombard you with useless information, then tests over irrelevant material.

Good teacher, kind of a hard grader.  Readings were very long, but you can get by pretty without reading if you go to the class and pay attention.  Interesting topics, actually quite helpful in the real world! Not that hard to get an A if you try

Unlike the whiny freshmen, I think she is a great teacher.  Very fair with the amount of assignments she gives but a little heavy on the reading.  I enjoyed her class a lot, perhaps one of the best teachers in the CRP department.

somewhat decent lectures, but she has an annoying, almost distracting voice. and she's REALLY obnoxious. the class itself is pretty pointless, but not unreasonably hard. and don't bother buying the text, we used it for 2 days
Just awful.

The kind of designer I hope I never become: cold, whiny and arrogant.  I'm sure she's good at whatever she does, but it's not teaching 183. I'm retaking the class with a different professor and it's going a million times better.
the way she talks is distracting. Shes an "um" and "ok" teacher
I swear she hates me

I'll agree SL's section was challenging, but you're at college to learn, no. There were two A's in her fall section. I had one of them, but I did have to work my ass off. I thought her topics were interesting, but she is a disjointed lecturer.
I hated this class. i barely got a C and it was required for my major which sucked
Provides adequate level of challenge to raise the bar for demanding students. Provides knowledge through practice. A great professor for students who want to learn.
I failed the stupid class.  The grading and tests sucked.  The teaching didnt really do anything.  I never missed the class or slept, and i still didnt learn anything.
she's crazy
No Comments
No Comments

The theory taught by the professor was one-sided, if not too much to read aloud from the textbook, and examples were very scarce. The assignments were easy; you could finish them by looking at the book. The exams were particularly difficult, as we were required to complete over 20 pages in 2 hours. Please bypass this professor's course.

Very difficult stat theory concepts in the class, but he explained well during lectures, and showed how to do them in R. Also posted notes in readable and concise way on his github, labs were also set up well. But the exams didn't relate much to the class material, tested over very difficult calc concepts and were way too long, also barely curved.

Dr. Syring, although seemingly kind, was quite rude. His homework assignments didn't represent the topics learned in class. His exams were ridiculously hard and nearly impossible to finish. He also did NOT curve the class even though nobody finished above 90%. He clearly values research more than teaching and doesn't respect undergraduate students.

Lectures are just proofs being derived with no explanation or intuitive reasoning. Material is flown over and maybe 30% of it is explained. Exams are impossible and have failing class averages. Notable quotes: "I don't understand why you guys did so bad on the exam but were fine on HW" and "Do you guys even know calculus?" Syring is out of touch
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Professor Syring gave 9 homework assignments and 3 exams during the semester I took his course.  

The homework assignments were heavy.

The exams were possibly the worst part of the course.  Exam 1 had an easy 1st 3 questions and a 4th question that required advanced calculus with no preparatory review.  Exam 2 was 26 pages.

Would not recommend.

She expects her students to read her mind and is very rude when students come to help- she talks about herself so much and wastes students class time, then expects several office hour meetings and ALL work done out of class. Big waste of time.

Very knowledgeable but likes to name drop about who she knows and has worked with.  Quite self promoting for her children's work. Didn't really provide information for someone trying to get started in this area.
Best teacher I have ever had.

Terrible professor. She may be good at working with children's choirs, but she does not relate well to older students and future teachers. Used nepotism in her favor to require a student teacher to do MORE student teaching after graduation.

She was probably the worst prof. I've had. Everything other people has said is completely true.  I love music but I still hated her class.  She was terrible...just terrible...I could talk forever about how bad it was but they only give me 500 words...I know there is someone else who teaches this class so DON'T take it from Munson!!!!

This teacher never returns papers,or return's e-mails.  Took 2 weeks to get a response to an e-mail.  She requires you to go watch HER choir and write a paper about it. Very rude, and un-organized.  Office is a HUGE mess. (That's an understatement) She has favorites- and expects we read her mind.
I agree totally!

Doesn't care about her students especially non music majors. Tends to ridicule students that she doesn't favor. Doesn't listen to questions, and assumes we should just know everything. She thinks she has a passion for music, really she makes it a chore.

Rodrigo is very forgetful. He likes to jump around his slides. He is a very strict grader; he wants you to be specific in your answers, but you still get them wrong for not being specific enough. Even though the class isn't mandatory, he still likes to write on the board once and have that on the exam. Choose a different professor if possible!!

He will say to not be specific on a test and then take you down points for not being specific. Will also take off points for having slightly incorrect spelling and yet will misspell words like "hot dog". Says to "look at the big picture" and then will turn around and ask for specifics. Honestly, never again.

I actually took ANS3730A with him. In 2 days he presented over 200 slides worth of material. His voice put me to sleep and his slides are poorly organized and way over filled. His exam was extremely hard with misspellings, incorrect answers, and focused on little details he briefly mentioned on slides he told us not to worry about. WORST professor.

Good professor for a difficult class. I really enjoy the content and you can tell that Tarte cares for his students and the subject. That being said, you will get the most out of the class if you show up, participate, and ask questions. Tarte is very knowledgeable and just wants everyone to learn. Overall, one of my favorite classes.

This is by far the WORST class I have ever taken. I study 8 hours for each exam and get an average of a C. He spells things wrong on his slides then when you spell it that way on exams he gets mad. Answer keys are wrong. He doesn't respond to emails. He doesn't provide extra credit. He doesn't curve exams. He is SUPER picky on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is no extra credit or curving of anything. The entire class grade is based on 3 exams, 6 quizzes, and 6 homeworks. You only get to use your notes on homework assignments and he picks exam and quiz questions from one line in the lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you read all of the slides!! If you don't, you won't do well in class. In my opinion, he does explain things well if you ask him questions. Very kind overall.

If you attend the lecture and pay attention and youll be fine. If you don't understand then talk to him, he'll answer any questions. Pay attention in lecture because the quizzes and tests are from the slides sort of. Lots of extra credit.
Hard to understand and doesnt test over lecture focus points spelling is a must even if he spells it wrong the whole semester on his slides
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Be prepared to memorize a lot of slides word for word if you want to pass a quiz or test. No homework to boost your grade. Tests cover both lecture and lab material. There is no such thing as multiple choice. Has to be the correct answer with the the correct words or it is wrong, even when you would think its close enough.

This was his first semester lecturing. His quiz's and exams are very hard, he takes them straight out of his slides however, he is very picky on the answers that he wants and spelling. I doubt more than 5 people got an A in his class. You do not need to go to class he posts all his lectures online and doesn't take attendance.

This is his first semester teaching. He cares about his students but his quizzes and exams are very hard! There is a lot of information covered and we rushed through information the entire semester. Overall you learn a lot and the lab portion is defiantly worth taking this class. I would not take this class unless you are interested in meat science

She's an academic advisor who is very active and respected among the students. I felt she can be helpful at times and you really have to be on her goodie goodie list of people if you want her respect.

She really isn't that good with communicating. She used to be more proactive early on when I was in Itec but after a few semesters, she started to go downhill. She doesn't respond to emails in a timely manner and will go days before getting back to you. There are better advisors at Iowa State.

Tamara is the academic adviser for the Industrial Technologies program. They genuinely take the ITEC program from being a good program to an incredible one. If every adviser were as good as Tamara, the entire college would thrive at the highest level, and every student would have the support and guidance they need to reach their fullest potential.

Tamara is a truly caring person. She loves loves loves loves to talk, so bring your listening ears. But she also loves to listen so try your best to strike up conversations with her. She is also a big fan of sending emails so expect to get a lot of news about fairs and job listings. She's a great resource for everything and loves Pedro Pascal.
She is awful. She is disorganized and doesn't respond to emails in a timely manner.

TSM 111 is a great opportunity to learn more about industry in AST and ITech. Tamara is the ultimate tour guide of the department. If you show up and give a good effort you will pass with an A easily.

She is always approachable and willing to help when you need her. TSM 111 introductory course to the Industrial Technology major its fairly easy and just requires attendance and completion of the short reflections due each week. I enjoyed Tamara and TSM 111 and went back to be a peer mentor and have greatly enjoyed the class and Tamara herself.

Really good professor with a fantastic structure of lectures/readings. Lectures reflect the reading by giving practice problems similar to exams + actually talking about what we are learning in the readings. If you have never coded before, I highly recommend taking Tancreti's lecture. Really easy to reach out to him in person or on piazza
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite professor at Iowa State. Lectures genuinely made concepts so easy to understand. I loved how he actually walked through coding examples during class time and provided various ways to solve problems instead of just reading off slides. Make sure you start homework early, though. I wish he taught 228 too :/

His lectures were clear and informative, and his slides were easy to follow and reflected what would be on the exams. Exams were just like the practice exams, and lots of study material was given. HOWEVER, his coding assignments were notoriously tough and had multiple mistakes in the specs. Set aside lots of time for those

Great professor. His lecture style is fantastic. He teaches by engaging with the class. He proposes a concept or problem and asks for feedback from students on how to solve it. He explains concepts well. I truly wish he taught 228.

Professor Matt is a great professor. I honestly think he is everything a student could ask for in a professor. His lectures are content-rich and well-made--He takes time for the students and is more patient and kind than I would be. The provided readings and projects are good. He is knowledgeable and seems to actually care for his students.
Class was graded very leniently and didn't seem to be too challenging. Tancreti is a solid professor who gives clear, albeit dry, lectures.
Tancreti is awesome! Always helpful and lectures are decent, although you can probably complete the work without them. Homework isn't too difficult, and tests are similar to the practice exam.

I didn't have him for lecture, but he ran all the assignments for the class. There were 4 assignments, one of which was overly tough. The rest were fine and well written. Pay attention and do Zybooks and you will be fine. Take advantage of the practice exams posted to get ready for exams.

Honestly, I didn't really enjoy his lectures that much. I only came because attendance was part of our grade and I also am paying to be there. However, I learned most of the concepts from the zybooks or labs, just because I couldn't really focus in class. Tancreti is a great guy, and the class wasn't too hard so I can't complain to much.
Amazing professor. Just go to his office hours, and you'll get fantastic feedback on our work. Overall easy to understand and well structured course
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tancreti has great lectures that get the point across.  He also cares about his students and will help teach the concepts in any way he can.  COM S 227 is one of the most failed classes, but he is a professor that will help you succeed.
Very nice guy, had 2 classes with him in the same semester. Very regular homework / test intervals, with plenty of time to prep and access to note sheets.

Prof. Tancreti's 227 class was enjoyable. Engaging lectures made complex concepts clear. Assignments strike a balanced difficulty, challenging students while managing workload. This fosters a deeper understanding, but exams can be time-consuming.
Very engaging lectures.
Easy course and lenient grader, lectures are a bit boring.

He's a great professor, very intelligent. He might seem a little reserved, but if you ask a question he is willing to help. He asks questions to the class during lecture so you're not lost. You'll know exactly what to expect on tests. The labs are helpful in walking you through how to apply the content. hw assignments can be a little time consuming

He kind of scared me on the first day when he explained that about 1/3 of the people last semester didn't get a high enough grade to move on to 228, but I really didn't struggle in this class. He gives way more than enough time to finish the major homework assignments as long as you start them early. Worst part was all the exams were on paper.
Amazing teacher, as long as you attend lectures and pay attention to class you will pass.

THE GOAT COM S professor. Incredibly smart guy. Attendance is not required but I highly recommend going to every lecture. I learned more from his lectures than from the textbook. I recommend following along with him in Eclipse to learn the most. When solving problems in class, he often asks the class for ideas and will re-explain concepts if needed

The lecture topics' pacing is slow and does not match the homework topics. Doesn't go into the detail required to be successful in the assignments. I took his Intro to Java course and for someone who taught myself basic Java prior to this sem, he doesn't explain the core topics in a beginner-friendly way for someone who's never coded before.

Prepare to spend a lot of time on the major assignments. Also prepare for the sheer amount of resources that this professor gives you throughout the semester. Professor Tancreti is an amazing professor, always quick to answer emails and give helpful feedback both one-on-one and via Piazza. I would love to be able to take a class with him again.

Probably the best professor I have taken to date. Do not skip his lectures. He is extremely good at just teaching what you need to know. He doesn't show any slides or anything he just goes right in to doing work and encourages you to follow along with him. Com S 227 is really not hard at all unless you just go to his lectures.
Tancreti > everyone else. Period.

Professor Tancreti makes the class manageable; there are only 2 exams and 2 projects although the projects might come in 2-3 parts. Gives more than enough time on the projects, but also isn't stingy on extensions if you ask him. Homework and attendance is not graded but the exams consist of purely lecture and homework materials.

You should attend all lectures, as he explains difficult concepts in a simple way. Makes illustrations on the board that make it clear. Very helpful and  reasonable in going over homework and test grades. But as with a lot of the COMS department here, they make their classes and grading as "out to get you" to try to reduce the number of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I came into 227 as my second coding class with no prior knowledge about coding. Professor Tan Creti often asks students for ideas on how to solve the examples on board this keeps the class engaging. If you ever don't understand anything he takes the time to explain the concept and make sure you actually understand it.

After hearing some bad things about Tancreti from a peer, I had low expectations. I was surprised to find that he is actually an excellent teacher. He has a really good grasp on the concepts we learn- he answers student questions really well during lecture, and his lectures are methodical and easy to follow.

Matthew Tan Creti is hands-down one of the best professors in Com Sci. He is very approachable and will answer all questions that are asked. Assigned readings were due before class. During class, he would go over example problems on whatever the topic for said reading was which helped me reinforce many coding concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at ISU. He breaks down the content very well and teaches it smoothly. His passion for the subject comes through in the lectures which makes listening and taking notes easy. The class only had 2 projects and 2 exams, the weekly homeworks were ungraded which was so nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, Tan Creti is a good teacher. Sometimes his lectures are boring, especially if you did the reading. If questions are asked in the lecture, he responds really well. Most of the time he understands the question that was asked, and I think asking questions is the best way to learn in this class. He answers questions after class if you stay
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: They were an excellent professor. Very caring and had engaging activities to ensure you understood the material and was always open to answer any questions.

Tara is a little odd in some of the little assignments she had us do throughout the course, but she is a really great professor that cares about how you're doing in her course. She's really easy to get ahold of outside of class times, as well as giving great feedback on papers.
They were a very good professor. Gave lots of good feedback and created a good classroom environment. I would take this class again; it's not hard if you show up and complete your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was easy, but I constantly had to defend myself because the teacher kept accusing me of using AI for my essays. It was frustrating, especially when I wrote a discussion post using the assigned article and still got accused. Not everything is AI, some of us actually read and write our own work! Grade the work, not your feelings.

Tara Labovich is an amazing professor. They are kind, approachable, and helpful throughout the course. Most importantly, they give students a ton of freedom when writing; students are encouraged to choose topics of interest to them, which helps them engage more meaningfully with the topics being taught, and enjoy becoming better writers. 100000/10.
JP is a great guy and wants his students to do well.
JP is freakin awesome. Very caring and knowledgeable.

JP is a great prof, you can tell that he knows his stuff. There is homework due every week, but it is not insanely difficult like some ChE courses. He has well-organized lectures and is helpful during office hours. We had exams with a range of difficulties, so definitely study and prepare as best you can. The textbook is a great resource.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Tessonnier was an awesome professor this semester. He was always helpful in office hours and wanted us to do well. If you have the chance take 381 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Tessonnier was a superb professor for ChE 381. His lectures were clear and definitely not boring. The tests were not bad at all if you did all of the homework and practice exams and made sure you understood it. He curves them too. Overall a great professor and an interesting (I thought) class.

Dr. Tchaprazov Is the kind of professor that requires luck to pass. There seems to be no rhyme or reason for his grading style. He gives very vague feedback, sometimes even unrelated to your assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He REALLY wants people to participate and answer questions. I thought he was a little scary as he would interrupt me to explain just how wrong I was. He also told me that irony isn't a figure of speech, and then later said imagery wasn't either. This confused me as I'm pretty damn sure they are. He's a tough grader and will not go easy on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the toughest graders I have ever had. He gives no useful feedback and insults you with annotations on assignments that should not nearly receive the attention they get.

Overall a great class subject matter wise but having to do a group consulting report online is the worst idea someone could have had for this class. Honestly doing the group projects by my self would had been less work. VERY TOUGH GRADER!!! Felt like I was putting a ton of effort in and wasn't see the results. Doesn't offer curves or extra credit.

Good professor! A lot of times he will lecture the whole class period, but he is very funny so it goes by quickly. The only downside to this class was the tests. They are mainly multiple choice, true or false, & fill in the blanks, but they are super specific lines in the stories that you may not remember. Listen to the lectures to get the answers!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Grading was never clear and wasn't sure what was needed for projects. Rubrics were confusing but otherwise class wasn't too bad for an online format.

Always ready to accommodate students and dedicated to student success. A rather traditional English teacher, but in the good way. No BS, just material. Grades relative to the rest of the class and owns to his mistakes. Very respectable, kind, and funny as well.

Worst professor ever. I emailed him for feedback to improve on my papers since it was an online course and he refused to respond to me numerous times. He changes the rubric within his announcements the day before the assignment is due so you have to redo it. Final half of semester is a group paper which he is extremely unclear about. Horrible man.

There is reading for every lecture, so beware of that. The discussions and pop quizzes relate to the readings, and I felt stupid every time I didn't do the reading. Pay attention in class, and the tests will be fairly easy. I loved his lectures, as they gave some life advice too. He is very understanding and a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: You do have to actually read the material, as he does occasionally give out pop quizzes, but they are easy and short. Exams are easy if you attend lectures, he also frequently gives 1 freebie. Engages and leads great discussions that are both interesting and make exams super easy. On the one harder exam he allows a cheat sheet. Term paper is short.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. His "critiques" for papers are very negative and he never gives constructive criticism. Nothing will ever be good enough for him. His grading is very inconsistent and not helpful when trying to learn what you did wrong.

Lot of reading but it's all skim-able and very manageable for an English course. He explains things very well in lecture. Easy grader, and easy exams if you look over the slides beforehand. He was flexible when I had to take an exam early, reachable outside of class, and definitely entertaining! Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell Tchaprazov wants you to succeed and he's an interesting guy to listen to. You have quizzes after a few topics based partially on lecture, but mostly on the reading, which he goes over in detail in class, and the readings are all stories or poems so it's not bad. You have a paper on the end, but he's a really fair grader!

Very interesting class to fulfill elective requirements. Textbook is used and must be read to get full participation points and for the exams. 2 quizzes, 2 exams, and a final. Lectures are worth attending and cover topics for the exams/quizzes. A good amount of reading outside of class, but not unmanageable. Professor is wonderful and helpful

I am in the process of taking one of his classes and so far so good. He is very caring and reachable outside of class. He wants us to succeed and will do whatever he can do to help make that possible. The class is very paper heavy but you should expect that in an English course. He is very clear as to what he is expecting on papers. Meet with him.

The class is discussion heavy and he will try to make quieter students participate. If there was ever an issue with the class or a question came up, he was easy to reach outside of class. The class covers a lot of topics and he goes into detail on various aspects of the readings, which makes class fast paced and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Grade is solely based on exams and pop quizzes. He will dock your grade after three absences from the class. Tons of reading but the exams and pop quizzes aren't too difficult as long as you do the readings and pay attention during class. Exams get easier through the semester as you go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Grades are solely exams and pop quizzes. Docks grade after so many absences. Tons of reading for the class. Exams aren't too difficult if you do the readings and pay attention at least halfway during class. Homework is easy and sparse.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He wants you to write to his level of knowledge and understanding. Write what he's looking for and you'll do fine. Need to show up to class and have everything ready for the day. Expect 3 papers and 2 presentations and 1 quiz. Looks strict but is pretty chill once you get comfortable with him. Very mild accent too, easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever taken. Contradicts most of what he says which makes writing any essay hard when you don't know exactly what he wants you to do. Always finds something to nitpick on, downgrades just because he doesn't like the way you worded something, even though your way isn't wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor. Very knowledgeable. I took Engl250 short semester with him and it wasn't pretty. Have to admit despite him being nice, his also a tough grader. Very strict when it comes to homework submission. He also has a sense of caring. I would only recommend to take his class if you are looking for a challenge. If not don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bulgarian. Likes to quote Madonna. Has an app on his phone that lets him take care of kittens and sometimes you hear his phone meow. Cool dude, easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He cares deeply about literature and is always available for his students. His teaching style is amazing because everyone talks in class. It was very enjoyable to go to class and the readings were not heavy at all. This class is definitely worth it, but you can't slack off and get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: English 201 is a literature survey course, so it's no surprise that there is an exceptional amount of reading. Overall, this professor was fair if you made effort in the classroom. This was not an easy A, but I found that this class was very enjoyable and worth it! Very interetsing professor and no lectures really-lots of class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I took the half semester option for this class. He is an interesting and nice guy, but different when it comes to grading. He is very inconsistent and tends to take away major points if your paper isn't exactly the way he would have written it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a good guy but I did not enjoy his teaching style. His instructions were clear but grading style was inconsistent. I would ask for one on one time with him to improve my papers throughout the semester. He would give feedback, but it was more negativity than constructive criticism. Nice guy, but an average professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took ENG 250 as a half semester course, so it was a lot of work in a little amount of time, but he made it easy as it was possible to be, I think. Make sure you do the assigned readings and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gave no one in the class an A.

At first he may seem a little rough around the edges, but if you participate or at least pay attention, you'll do fine. He like when kids talk to him one-on-one and will help you if you need it. He hates late work, so always be on time. I did pretty well in this class because I listened to his instructions, as to what he wanted in a paper.

I took the half-semester version, so I had a 3 hour lecture twice a week from him. He gave a good break and I never got tired of him. He is Romany so he has an accent but it's ok to understand 99% of the time. He loves students who participate and ask questions. His office hours are helpful and he will go over a paper with you no problem at all!

Worst. Teacher. Ever. I tell everyone to report her if they can. She is the rudest teacher I've ever had, she's made me cry and said I couldn't take her class solely because I asked her to send my ONLY grade for the class and she got annoyed at me about it???? She's just plain rude and its blatant, she doesn't respect her students at all. DONT TAKE

Took her class during spring of 2021 online. Teresa is a tough professor and a hard grader. She will push you to do better. Cons: Very little critiquing before grades, graded mostly on the quality of the skills you already possessed Pros: Very clear class structure (due dates, criteria etc.) She's obviously very knowledgeable and skilled
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very unclear and rude comments. Grades harshly even for good work that you only had a short period of time to do.
This was an excellent class and Teresa is a world class artist and instructor Iowa State is lucky to have an artist of this caliber on staff.
Teresa is a helpful and personable instructor.  There are guidelines for the student to follow and if you do, you will get a good grade.
Definitely does not seem to care about her students much at all. Easy grader if you do a lot of extra work on the side

She seemed a little moody (freaked out for strange reasons).  Process work was wasn't ever discussed until the end.. when it was too late.. and you'd get a bad grade for it.  Some of her comments seemed a little ****.  I did learn a lot (she knows her stuff)
Definitely a Fruit Loop but very helpful and really wants her students to learn!
She is very **** and doesn't seem to care about her students.

Teresa is a fun loving person.  Shes helpful when she can be and if she doesnt know, she'll find out.  Shes kind of a fruit loop but shes loads of fun and I wish there were more classes I could take with her!  Shes very encouraging!

Attend class & DO THE ASSIGNED READINGS or you will fail the pop quizzes. Everything on the test is directly from the book. She HATES when people are late to class and will seriously stop a lecture to shame someone and/or tell them to LEAVE for being late! The way she pronounced the countries: "Kenya" and "Niger" is something I will never forget.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her class was super hard, because she was never clear on how to study for exams and what would be on them.

Rudest Prof ever. I was in her class for a week and didn't understand the classical readings that were required and she basically told me i was an idiot, because i was a college student who couldnt understand the readings. She also told me to have a nice life when i had her sign my drop slip. DO NOT RECOMMEND

Very interesting material, but extremely hard class. Dr. Besser lectures with PowerPoints, but does not allow laptop use nor does she post complete PowerPoints to Blackboards. The TAs are helpful. On-line homework is ridiculous; textbook doesn't help for homework, just for test preparation. The on-line tests are very difficult, but the curve helps.

SOC 134 with Dr. Besser was my worst class of the semester. The TA's did not respond to emails and were rude when you needed a grade they messed up fixed. Dr. Besser was sometimes polite in email responses, and other times quite rude. I have been trying to get my grade corrected for this class for a month, but it still has not been fixed.

I loved this professor. She was a very lenient grader. She curved all tests, homework, and our final grade. She made adjustments to assignments and tests that she made mistakes on. It is necessary that you read every chapter in order to do well. If you do that, you will do great. The people giving her a poor rating probably didn't do the homework.
Very very intelligent teacher. She is very interesting to listen to and is always very clear in her explanations. She explains expectations well and grades very very fairly.

worst teacher I've ever had. Impossible test and confusing course work. Test not even related to what we learned in class. Doesn't help with any questions; she always directs you to her TA's. If i were you, get a different teacher before she ruins your GPA.
Notes unorganized, tests awful. If you have to take sociology, I would recommend another teacher.
Terrible teacher, went in to talk to her to try to get help and was helpless. Very frustrated to pay so much for a class and get little to no help. Get a different teacher.

Pretty tough class. If I had to write one more paper for Mr. Besser this semester, I would have just dropped out with 9 credits left until graduation. Seriously. My head hurts. However, I did learn a lot.

Such a terrible teacher. She ruined my interest in sociology and I probably will never take a sociology class again. If you have the choice with another teacher go with the other teacher and not Besser. The tests were nothing that she taught and her notes are extremely disorganized.
Tests are very difficult. So many notes and book readings
Tests are impossible, doesnt give study guides. I would not recommend taking this class with her.
Too many papers!
You learn the material well
No more words. Worst that I've ever taken any class :(
Lots of cool info in this course. I went to class, I listened, I did well. The book is unnecessary if you don't mind missing a few points.

Tough but fair. Requires a moderate amount of reading and frequently assigns papers. Does not allow laptops in class. Is pretty clear about what she expects from written assignments, and if you make the necessary changes, your grade on papers will improve.
Never went to class and I paid the price. Fail the class; hard exams, lots of reading and studying. She is tough and expects a lot. GO TO CLASS.
This was my only 100 level class I took this semester and easily the hardest. Tests are hard and nearly impossible to stud for. If I could go back I would not take this course.
Good Professor who knows a lot about the subject. Tried hard to make all of the subject matter interesting.

Extremely hard exams. She expects a lot out of you. You have to read the material in the book for half of the exam. She only covers maybe 3/4 of the material on the exam and then you need to read the other half. She does understand what she is talking about but has a hard time explaining it to others.
The EXAMS is the HARDEST!!! Difficulties: Level 100= Level 300.

Besser is very knowledgeable of Sociology but her teaching methods are in need of improvement. She is obviously very passionate and the material is interesting, but the powerpoint slides are hard to focus on especially in such a big class. It is hard to get help and studying for the exams is impossible. Thank god for the curve.

She knows the material inside and out. But when it comes to teaching it to students, she's horrible. The material is beyond interesting but the exams are impossible to study for. She will never help students prepare for exams which are about 80% of your grade. If it wasn't for the curve grading scale. 90% would fail. I don't recommend this class.

She is obviously very good at what she does, but comes across as very stereotypical. I dropped this class because I was not doing well and needed  to keep my GPA up. It's interesting material, but the professor is terrible.

Literally could not understand her tests. No point in studying for them. She straight up said to the class teaching an undergraduate class was a "waste of her time" and would rather focus on upper-level courses. The only thing I got out of this class was a lower GPA. If you want to do well find someone who had the class before and saved notes.

One of the hardest classes I have taken at ISU. Do not take it if you want an easy A. The tests are so hard you will laugh and fill in the dots. Exam two taken had an average of 55%. There is 150 kids that received a bad grade. Is it the teacher or the poor studying? I think your smart enough to figure that question out.

Worst thing: TA'S SUCK & they do all of the grading. "Reaction points" only lower your grade, even though she claims it will help. Tests are extremely difficult; must attend lectures, take detailed notes as well as read/understand the textbook (100's of pages) is nearly impossible. Don't take this class if you want an easy A. You won't get one.

Prof. Besser is a great sociology teacher!  I really liked attending her lectures; and it got me interested in possibly taking another soc class.  The response questions were a little annoying, but if you showed up to class, skimmed the book before tests, and actually turned a research assignment in, you were fine.  I'd want her as a teacher again.
Good instructor. The topics that she discussed were interesting. She know her stuff when it comes to Sociology. As long as you show up and take notes you should do well.

She is a terrible teacher and the TAs are horrible. They don't help or respond to help if you need it. And she has these stupid reaction points after some of the lectures that are supposed to be "easy" five points and all they do is slowly lower you're grade because she doesn't give you a good grade unless you have the same opinion and ideas as her

Boring lecture, easy subjects, easy tests, CONFUSING COURSEWORK. Having students pick options from this contract thing with mismatched due dates and vague requirements guaranteed the confusion of everyone in the class. Got a horrible grade on my paper, and I consider myself a great paper writer. HORRIBLE TAs.

This class isn't the funnest but Dr. Besser tries to have fun with mid-class breaks. Exams are somewhat hard, you leave feeling like an A and come out with a B+. In terms of getting help your on your own, the TA's wouldnt respond or help. Do the extra credit! go to class!
Exams are not very clear, she is very opinionated. If you are looking for a easy class...this isn't it.
I am a straight A student, but struggling to get a B in this class. I don't think she reads over her tests to check for clarity.

Incomprehensible. Professor Besser is very  opinionated and tends to teach more of what she seems interested in rather than anything relative to sociology. Lecture is useless, might as well read the notes online. Did not learn anything.
Very Good Teacher, Found class to be interesting, and easy enough as long as you acutally attend class and do the readings
Good teacher, though lecture is a little boring. Liven it up!
I did not like this like at all. Teacher was very unclear and runs through notes so print them off before and she makes up random words to try and confuse you.

Besser makes certain material seem important and other just to be random facts. Such as class polls about how religious the class is and on their average house income.  In stead of studying useful material for the test you have to make sure you study and memorize all of the useless in class polls and memorize the percentages. Dry lecture. Dry class

There are 3 5-7 page papers due before each test which seems a little much for an introductory class.  The tests are very long also and multiple choice which can either make or break your grade so good luck!

Besser didn't explain the matirial well at all.  She goes really fast through the slides so write fast or print off the pp before class.  Tests are hard. Memorize class statistics.. there's questions on the tests about them. I studied at least 5 hours a week for this class and more before tests and let's just say this class definitly lowered my GPA

Not the most exciting class.  The material is dry and not always clear.  Instructor seems enthusiastic about Sociology but at the same time doesn't provide much help.  Don't argue with her about test questions because she won't budge even if the question is poorly written and/or misleading. But would take her over the other instructor for this clas
Test questions can be unclear and complicated even if you study and attend class.  Lectures are fairly interesting.

Besser is a great professor. She's extremely prompt with emails or any questions you may have. Lecture can be kind of boring, but if you pay attention/take notes and study the notes and read the book chapters, the tests aren't bad at all. Recitation is a total waste of time. I just don't think it's needed for a Sociology class.

A few sophopmores told me they didn't like her, but I have no idea what they were talking about. As long as you attend lecture, take notes, and review them you should do fine. Liked this class a lot! Recitation was pointless, though...

Loved this class! It was easy. Just got to class and recitation. Take good notes. Read the chapters..it will help you in class and some questions on the test are taken from readings. You need to go to class because she randomly gives very EASY reaction points where you have to write a short essay about a topic you just talked about. EASY!

Entry level class not that difficult. You do have to make an effort like showing up for class and maybe looking over the book before the test but the book was very interesting. Not that difficult people. Attendence makes your grade with in class points. Don't show up, don't expect an A.

I don't know what all of these complaints about 134 are about! The class was very easy! My TA was exceptional. The readings were important but easy to understand and only took like an hour a week! All of her lectures are powerpoints and she puts them on webCT. So just go to class to earn the class points. This class was too easy..

Always talks about herself. Sometimes relates it back to sociology. Getting a good TA is key since she can go through slides fast and make the class a little more boring than sociology really is. Easy class overall if you just memorize the vocabulary before every test and go to most classes. She takes attendance somedays.
Not all that bad as an educator.  The tests were much harder than anticipated.

This professor was very weak.  Her performance was slow and labored making it hard to follow along without becoming bored.  The amount of reading was great for the few questions asked over the text.  Very lousy.

Whoever said she was a good teacher is simply wrong. She makes up words and tries to sound intelligent. She is rude to people who come in late, and her tests are specific according to class statistics. Need to pay attention in lecture & pretty much need to go to get 'reaction points' and full notes. I only did well because of my high school class.
Very nice, easy to understand.

This class is a complete waste of time. Questions on the test are worded wierd and half the time they don't make sense. Lecture is also a waste. The only reason to go is for in class points. Tests are difficult and her lectures confuse you more than help you. She doesn't explain the subject well. I did not like the class or her teaching style.
I constantly feel that besser in lecture is up on a soap box. Her tests are very difficult, and the TA I have is worthless. Honestly, in a 100 level class this one is too hard.
this is a boring class that i would never have gone too if not for the fact that besser is a complete babe!!  If she was 10 years younger I would totally do her.

I was told this class would be easy. It wasn't it was just BORING! So I didn't go and she has inclass quizes for participation and she leaves notes off her slides. The tests are really specific and she words questions in a weird way. Overall did NOT like this class.
Not bad but on the monotonous side which can get long and tiresome.  Has fun jokes but too late in the class to be funny usually.

This class is way easier than people make it out to be.  Here's a hint: do the reading.  There are some pretty stupid questions on the tests, but they're not overly difficult.  Recitation extra credit can help make up for a poor test score.

I would suggest taking this class with a different prof. Dr. Besser covers a lot of material at once and her tests are very difficult.  Her TAs are also not very helpful.  I did, however, learn A LOT from her!
