Unorganized and not a very good lecturer. Very random and notes are hard to follow. She has a hard time finding descent TAs too. Overall though, the best of a lot of bad choices.
Type of class your glad to get out of the way. Teacher isnt mean or anything just slightly difficult. I had a bad TA as well. If you go to class and study you will get a B for sure.
she is one of those teacher you don't want unless you really want to go to every class and really pay attention. If you don't go you will fail.

She's alright.  But I think the tests were a lot harder than they should have.  I knew the material real well and got a B+.  She words the things wrong.  Hope to god you get in a recitation with a bunch of dumb people because your curve is based off of the people in your recitation.  Not the others.

I had her for soc. 134 and she is a lot harder in this class. She challenges you to under a lot about complex organizations. Don't: get behind in the readings, procrastinate the 15-20 page paper, or sluff off on the tests.
by far the worst teacher i have ever had
Class is pretty interesting. Tests are very difficult.

Terry Besser is a nice lady but it seems like she expects the world from her students.  Her Complex Organiztions class is very difficult.  Don't take it unless you have a lot of time to keep up with the readings she assigns...it's not easy.
I thought she was a great! She truly cares about her students and is very willing to help anyone. She made an effort to connect with students.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
I heard that about 1/2 of the students that have to take this course have to retake it, including me.  She's hard and doesn't seem the nicest.
Her examples are very interesting and she is a great lecturer!

Besser was pretty interesting professor.  Very political especially before the election.  She definitely was a Kerry supporter to the core!  Her lectures were well organized and fairly interesting but her assistants were not.  She's not the end of the world, but she's not ideal by any means!
I also agree that she sucks. She didn't do a very good job explaining assignments and class would put you to sleep everytime.
I agree, she sucks
Pay attention and you'll do fine just don't get to frustrated.  It is a harder sociology class.
She sucks

She doesn't give much help, just pushes you off on her TA's. Like someone already said she teaches like we want to major in sociology. It is a nearly impossible 100 course and thats not the way it should be. It's intro to sociology for a reason.

This is a 100 level course but she teaches it like you want to major in Sociology! I wouldn't recommend her to anyone, she is very unclear about what she will cover on the exams and covers 7 chapters at a time.
I did not enjoy this class, and felt that for a one hundred level class it was way hard.
The class wasn't too hard, it was the tests.  I love lecture (only skipped 2), but the tests were difficult to understand, making the theories difficult to grasp.

An overall interesting class, although slow at first. If you read the book, you don't have to attend class all the time to get an A (although you should get the notes). Besser tells fun stories to illustrate important points.
No Comments
The questions on her test were hard and didn't make sense.  It doesn't really help studying your notes before the test because her questions are so unclear!

She is probably the most boring person ever... but she can teach well... except when making the test she must forget everything. I enjoyed listening to her sometimes, but she definatly doesnt teach the test-at ALL!

Alot of people (approx 40%) dropped the class after one exam.  This is not meant to be a hard class but i think it is made hard.  I have done well in sociology at advanced level in high school but in this class i am average!!!
You couldn't pay me to take this class again. If you have any interest in the subject, prepare for it to be decimated.

There is a reason this class is infamous. It is very hard. However, purely looking at lectures, Nok is pretty good. She gives good explanations that are overly theoretical at times, but I was able to follow along most of the time and not be bored. Really wish that this course would just give more study material for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nok is a decent professor. She lays concepts out pretty well and clearly wants students to do well. That being said, this is a very hard class. A lot of the difficulty comes from not being able to practice. There is no test practice outside of recitations, and 80% of the grade comes from exams. Despite this, Nok tries her best to prepare you.

Her class has vague expectations and an uncertainty of what is gonna appear on exams, which are 80% of your overall grade in the end. Exams were the most difficult component of the class. Recitations, homework and lecture examples are all way easier than some questions appeared on her exams. No curves to exams even when the average is in mid-60s.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a genius and the best prof for this class. Gives a lot of examples in class, but often feels more like an info dump on the whiteboard than explanations. This class is very hard, but passable- makes sense it's the 3rd most failed/dropped class here.

She's like an algorithm machine and knows them all by heart. It's honestly kinda wild watching a professor just walk up to the board, no notes, and start writing everything for the whole class. Either she's a genius or a total robot!

Only halfway thru the semester and I've already learned more from her than in 3 yrs of college. Her class is no joke, she really squeezes everything out of you. Don't take her class if you want an easy ride. But if you actually want to learn stuff, she's the real deal.

Lectures were fast-paced and not very good for learning; most of my understanding came from studying outside of class(Leetcode!). She focused mostly on theoretical proofs, making topics harder to understand than if taught practically. Exams were hard, most weight fell on the last couple questions that required applying knowledge in unfamiliar ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rather than actually teaching or explaining concepts, she tends to copy directly from reference materials without clarification. There's little to no actual instruction, yet students are still expected to learn and perform. I strongly advise future students to avoid taking a course with her if possible.

Although the notes can be found online, it wasn't that much of a help. She expects you to understand the very core of a concept/algorithm, thus, she usually throws in a surprise question on every exam, particularly the very last number. Wouldn't recommend her if you want someone who can explain something thoroughly, as she teaches really fast
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I didn't directly have as a lecturer but she led the CS311 class. While extremely smart, she expects you to know everything and perform well on the exams she writes. This is despite not clarifying a lot of the content and just brushing over many of the topics. Be prepared to spend a lot of out of class time trying to understand what is going on.

Luckily I passed this class with a B but had I not got a tutor, I would've failed. This professor is very lecture heavy and will write 10 pages of notes per class. I found myself attending Trent Muhr's lectures more often (even though he wasn't great either), and I could at least understand. 1/10, don't recommend  with Nok. ISU's most failed class.

This course was ruthless, and it was made that way by Nok. The TA team and she are unforgiving on homework submissions and formatting, and aren't afraid to give zeroes for even the most subtle violations of their "requirements." The exams all consisted of one final problem, with 5-6 parts, and were unsolvable for the average student.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at ISU. Exams are always structured in a way that only covers 1/5 of the things she said we should review. Not only that but she also likes to put an extremely hard question that is worth 50% of the grade on the exam. Do not recommend.

311 is not that bad
Nok is a solid professor. She has well paced lectures and grades VERY leniently on exams. So far, exams have been similar enough to practice problems provided during recitation and homeworks. She is helpful during office hours and can be reached easily via email. Overall, she is kind and willing to help you succeed in the class.

The content isn't the most difficult thing you'll study. But, the course is structured poorly. Lecture notes aren't posted. So if you missed your class, you won't know what you missed unless you have a friend. The professors refused to help you solve homework problems. The SI session was also not helpful. Exams = 70%, Homework = 30%

Get ready to read and write. And I mean, a lot! This class is very difficult and I see why it is 3rd most failed class in ISU. I recommend not taking this class during her semester(Spring) because the papers are quite difficult. They are very leetcode heavy. Get ready for medium to hard difficult leetcode questions on exams. Exams are 70%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not good at being a professor. Rambles thru concepts. Slides missing key concepts needed for HW. Unengaging lectures. Tells students to "try harder" when most of the class does not perform well on the exam question over the topic we talked about for 15 minutes one time.Cannot stay on time/schedule. Treats every new concept as if it is review for us

Professor Chiou is not the best lecturer. His lectures are often confusing and difficult to stay focused on, because sometimes it feels like rambling. However, he is very lenient when grading exams. You can get a good understanding of all the topics by rereading the lecture slides. He does do in-class exercises that can improve your grade a lot.

Worst professor I have ever had. Avoid at all costs. Does not release course grades, and is multiple months behind on assignments. Berates students to their faces in office hours and in class when they are just asking for help. Says students know nothing. Lectures into the wall and has millions of slides that are all equation jumble. DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He doesn't give us any practice problems besides the one example in lecture, and he's super rude in class. He acts like we're supposed to learn everything instantly and keeps saying things are ‘too easy' or to just ‘burn it into your brain.'”

His lectures are very derivation heavy, and he laughs at us when we don't understand his "simple" theoretical examples. He rarely does any actual numerical examples, claiming that we already know this stuff. He is hard to understand in his ramblings and his homeworks and exams are incredibly time consuming.

I'm sure he has good intentions, but his lectures are genuinely so difficult to gain knowledge from. Lots of heavy derivations and the homework is much harder than what is covered in class and what is given to other sections. The material has been quite confusing lately and the lecture slides do not always give enough info to do the homework well.
Borderline demeaning to his students, does not explain things well, and homeworks are vastly more difficult than other sections.
Attend the lectures and you will do good on the pre-labs, even if they can take some time. The labs themselves were enjoyable and the workload wasn't unreasonable.

Attendance is mandatory, and says there is no acceptable reason to miss or leave early, yet gives pop quizzes that take 45 minutes 5 minutes before the end of class meaning you have to stay well past the scheduled time to finish. Many times the lecture for the corresponding lab was taught after the lab had been completed. Poorly ran course overall

The class is a lab class so prelabs and lab reports are expected. The professor adds homework and in lecture quizzes just to make the class harder. The homework is unrelated to the labs done and quizzes test oddly specific parts of lectures/labs from the previous month or so. Hes really full of himself and doesnt explain whats needed to do labs
Boring. A crap ton of work for a 2 credit class. Cant avoid so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tracy is very kind and helpful professor! She gives great feedback on all of your assignments, especially lesson plans. She also has pretty good advice based off her experience.

She is very kind and for sure shows that she is passionate about teaching and the education world. The only thing I find challenging is that she often doesn't seem to have a clear plan for the day, and assignments can be unclear.
Tracy is the best teacher and literally so kind and helpful!

Tracy was amazing! 2050 was my favorite class this year. If history isn't your thing you might not love the course but Tracy provides a collaborative environment and makes sure you aren't just hearing another lecture. You can tell she is passionate and qualified about what she teaches. I really enjoyed having her- she is kind and so helpful!
Professor is very kind and teaches well. Lectures are interactive and interesting.
She is amazing and the best teacher I have ever had. Grades very well. She is so smart and has taught me a ton. She really made me want to be a teacher.
Your attendance will greatly impact your grade but if you just go to class you'll be good. She genuinely cares about how are are doing!
Absolutely loved her!! Literally just show up to class. It's so easy. Not a lot of work at all, she'll probably even give you extra credit if you show up on a day where not many people show up.
She is awesome
Tracy was very engaging with her students. You can tell she has a passion for teaching. I love her. 10/10.

The class is all lectures with no content. Felt like I learned nothing from this class. I will give her some grace as she follows how the other professor teaches this (the other professor is even worse). There is no hope for Block 1 Social Studies as long as Tracy or Diana Figuerdo teach it. School of Ed, please do better!

Lectures are pointless. Rabbles on about mandatory attendance but i highly recommend doing Top Hat questions from your bed.
All he does is about his personal life for 20 minutes, doing some random code that has almost nothing to do with labs The only necessities of this class are zybooks, labs, and the practice exams. FADE LECTURE!!!!

Talks the whole class about random things and then you go to lab and it says "use what you learned in lecture to do this problem" but the only thing you learned from lecture was that back in the day they didn't have as good of computers as we do now. You learn nothing in lecture but need to answer Top Hat. Would change majors from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, he was a good professor. Lecture was boring and not helpful, online textbook was easy, exams were even easier, only hard parts were some of the labs. My class also had a bunch of ego-lords which made the lecture infuriating to be present in, listening to people trying to teach the professor. His higher-level classes are likely much better.

Bad lectures and barely teaches anything. All he does is blab about his achievements, and if you dont attend then thats 1/5th of your grade gone. The exams are also way harder than the practice exams that he gives. Hes also barely reachable outside of class hours and he doesnt respond to emails. He is a chill guy besides his classes, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are incredibly off topic and disorganized. He will teach things in the lectures that the homework and labs went over weeks ago. His communication with the TA's is abysmal. The labs are either incredibly easy or overly complex and often require students to use bad programming practices. 20% of your grade is through TopHats.

You can never reach him outside of class. He doesn't respond to his emails. AWFUL communication between him and the TAs. The lab instructions he made are atrociously bad. He does TopHat (attendance) in the first 1 or 2 minutes of lecture. Might as well skip if you're late. TopHat is a significant part of the grade. The lectures are useless.

I simply cannot believe he is still at Iowa State University, or at any high level academia at all. The class was simple, but its the fact that I paid multiple thousands of dollars to learn C from an online textbook (free at W3 schools, by the way), and had to suffer his terribly condescending attitude and lack of communication seems unacceptable.

He's a very easy-going teacher and doesn't care too much about what you do in class. However, 10% of your grade is based on attendance, and his class is usually at 8 a.m., so be mindful of that. He's an easy grader, and you get cheat sheets for every exam as well as one exam drop.
Requires a proctored hand written final for a masters class. Does not provide notes or slides, does not indicate what should be studied, final is 30% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For having little experience in C programming, he does an excellent job of helping students understand it in a logical way. The examples presented in the lectures are well thought out and explained thoroughly if you pay attention. Labs can be tricky sometimes, and help is sometimes needed but overall helped me learn a lot of useful stuff.

He does not fully explain his code which makes it hard to understand if you're a beginner at coding. It is vital that you spend time teaching yourself outside class because he only goes through about half of the course content in his lectures. The lecture and homework pacing is very disconnected. He is a great guy to talk to though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniels is clearly knowledgeable in the field. My issue with the course was mainly the pacing. The online textbook covers all the concepts in a fairly intuitive way, but the labs expect you to extrapolate these concepts to the extremes and throw you into the deep end pretty quickly. There's also little resources available to prepare for tests

Classes are a waste of time, he spends 2 full lectures explaining the problem instead of the actual code. The labs are too you have to write those reports as if you are going to publish them. If you see comments saying he is hardworking, that's completely false. He never updates the Canvas and the TAs have to do all his work for him (TA told me).

Some people like his rough way of doing things, and others don't. If you look past this and attend the lectures, you will do really well, and if you don't then you may do fine, but not quite as good as those who went to class. For the most part, it's more important to have prior coding practice than going to lecture.

I had never coded prior to this class. I did all of the readings and asked questions to my TAs outside of lecture. I really succeeded in this class but many others taking it did not. He tends to curve tests by about 10 points (out of 100-150). Sometimes lectures are pointless but sometimes there are very important lectures. (Lecture ex. on test)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof daniels is really kind and really helpful when it comes to certain things that some students feel are difficult. He even upped the grading scale for people who had Fs in order for them to atleast receive a D- he is truly a caring and hardworking professor
Not a good professor, full of himself and thinks that freshman college students will be up at 8 am ready to understand code that they haven't fully learned yet.

Lectures were mostly watching him code real examples, which I prefer over other professors just reading lecture slides. The class is learning about the very basics of programming, so you wont have to create anything more than a single file. Make sure to read the textbook and complete the lab.

The class is very informative. I recommend to anyone wanting a security background, however, Daniels is the worst professor they could possibly find. The class, to him, is a joke. Grades mean nothing. He grades tests with extreme harshness and such avg was 30% in one test. He takes pride in his teaching, while he has no skills at that. Such a shame
Class is good if you enjoy looking at some dude writing some code you wont understand and has nothing to do with labs at 8 am.
Good at teaching first-years. Havent had him for anything besides 185

His lectures mainly composed of you watching him code something that you don't understand after you felt like you wasted an hour. You think to yourself I don't want to go to the next lecture at 8 am, but you miss easy points through tophat. Lab is were most of the points come from, and were you actually learn how to code. Don't forget the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Most of your learning will be done through reading then applying those topics in lab. Reading assignments aren't that bad, though. You can go into the course without much programming experience and come out with a good grade if you work for it. Not going to lecture will hurt your grade a little as Top Hat scores will be a part of your grade.

I had experience coding in high school, so a lot of the fundamental concepts he taught were just refreshers for me. If you have no coding experience PLEASE seek out practice in the C language before taking his class. His class goes very fast, and I saw a lot of my peers truly struggle from having no experience at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The lectures were interesting, but you won't learn a lot from them. All the learning is done in lab. Make sure you do all of the readings and know what they mean.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: We were told we would be graded for 'programming practice', which was never assigned. Thus, outside of participation through tophat and reading checks, we were only graded through tests and labs. That being said, tests were easy, and labs were tough but mostly participation based. Rarely went to lecture, learned all through (good) textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniels was a good teacher. The online interactive textbook is very helpful in understanding everything. His lectures were basically watching him solve problems through programming and understanding his logic behind it. They were somewhat helpful go to. The tests were not too difficult but the labs can be challenging at times, but very doable.

Dr. D is a cool guy. His assigned online interactive reading (Zybooks) really helped me learn C and basic programming techniques. The way the course is set up, if you do okay on the exams (more than a 70% on each one), do all of the labs, and do all of the readings, you will do well. He isn't good at responding to emails, though.

The only reason you should take Dr. Daniels class is if youve programmed before. If youre new to programming, dont take this class. In lecture, all he does is program things well be doing our junior/senior year. And in the labs, the TAs are a saving grace because he makes the labs super hard and they dont go along with the book or lecture.

The class is easy but the tests are pretty hard. Dr. D is really cool, but his lectures only account for 5% of your grade, and they aren't very informal. It is required to take this class for CPRE, but you probably just need to focus on the labs and readings, because you will learn much more from them than in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a person Dr. D is a great guy. But his lectures are basically "Here, watch me write this cool program". It gets boring at times, but he's still willing to answer questions. The tests are challenging, and don't rely too much on notes to help you out. The labs are probably the most important part of the class, so focus more on those.
Make sure you show up the week of Halloween to see his costume. He is a cool teacher and the class isn't too hard, but the labs can be difficult.

Dr. D is alright. His 185 class is mainly just watching him write programs and understand the logic behind them. Most of your learning will be through zybooks and during labs with the TAs. The labs get progressively more difficult throughout the semester, so get ready to work. This class really tests if you wanna stay in CprE or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Daniels is a pretty good professor. He's got a huge history with programming and is passionate for the topics as well. The class is mostly projects but do NOT forget the readings as I did. You're lucky if you have him in the fall as you'll get to see his Halloween costume ;)

A really nice and helpful guy. His best quality is that he's very easy going. The course covered a large number of topics, but it wasn't that difficult to keep track of. All in all it was a good course, and he has a standard teaching style
Very fun guy. He does a good job, but was pretty hands off. Just lectured in class. Would take again.
Fun, smart, will explain almost anything. Demonstrates cool projects during class.
Didnt know what he is doing. He de-motivated me and I hated programming.

Daniels is a well-rounded individual who is respected by most students. His lectures are always interesting and help explore the intricate details and real life applications of coding. He really helped me understand C language and how applicable it could be in the future as an electrical engineer.

This class is easy if you pay attention in lecture. Try not to get distracted by his sexy belly and his tasty looking diet coke.   Hes a brilliant guy and will occasionally get off topic in lecture which can be pretty funny. You will pass the class if you finish every lab and make a good cheat sheet for every exam. Also go to the exam reviews.

Dr. D is the most laid back cool instructor I've had. Show up to class, follow along (actually follow along), write & compile the code from class on your laptop as he is doing it and you will get an A. Expectations are clear for exams, drops the lowest exam. If you do it right, no Final. Don't know how anyone couldn't like him. Coolest hobbies too

He has a rather spontaneous teaching style that may not suit everyone. For me, having programmed before, it was great. He would come into class and ask if we wanted to learn to make fractals or do some encryption, and put the concepts we learned to use. But his grading scale is a bit odd, as it changes every semester. Current TAs are excellent.

He's pretty cool. He really enjoys teaching this class. The only work we had to do in the class was what we did in lab and weekly programming practice (where you program whatever you want in C for 45 minutes). I found it easy, though I've programmed before.
He is not helpful, besides, condesceding to you when you are trying to figure something out with him. More important, his TAs both are very indifferent to students in the lab!

If you have any prior programming experience, this will be the easiest class you have ever taken. If not, there is an abundance of resources available to you. Anyone not receiving a good grade in this class can only blame themselves. Daniels is very helpful. If you go to his office hours, you will walk out knowing whatever you were unsure about.

He comes of as having a big ego (which I would say he probably does).  His material doesn't really drill down into any particular category too deeply, but its covered in depth more than some other security classes.  I had trouble paying attention to him cause he gets on my nerves a bit, but a lot of students seem to like him.  He drops lowest test.
He is a wonderful teacher, and I can't wait to have him again in the future.
wow... take it with stoytchev, even those who have not programmed before, i promise you, you will learn better with stoytchev.
wow... just wow...

Class was a joke. He seems rather arrogant. He does indeed sigh a lot and definitely doesn't seem like he wants to be there. Class was interesting, lecture was pointless. He dropped a test grade (including the final). I don't blame him for not wanting to be there; the class was a joke. Take it with Doctor Stoytchev if you can.
Other than being rather disorganized, he's an awesome prof who is very smart, enthusiastic about his subject and cares about his students.

This professor acts like he is forced to teach the class and doesn't really get into it.  The class itself is very easy, and if you have questions he will occasionally get off of his pedestal and answer them for you.

This professor seems to rant more than teach.  It's more or so ranting on how his life (and research) is then teaching students what they need to know for their Labs.  The TA that I had was clueless on what had to be done and seemed clueless to help.  If you are looking for independent study this professor would be ideal.

About the most worthless teacher ISU has to offer (next to Tian).  randomly talks about whatever he wants (mostly irrelevant), <sighs> alot and gets annoying, doesn't know 1/2 of what he talks about, goes over class time because he rambles on about "extreme senarios"......basically, you may as well skip class and learn everything on your own.
Very easy class, however the TA expects you to read his mind.  Its kinda odd but it feels like the TA and proff don't communicate over what the HW should be over.
Expects you to put in the work to know the material.  If you read the textbook and take decent notes, you can ace the exams.

He seems rather unorganized at times and his handwriting is horrible, but he's more than willing to clarify if you have any questions.  He's very approachable, if you get past the PhD ego.  He expects you to be competent.
No Comments

While he is a very caring person, the class was extremely difficult. When asking questions, I could never get a clear answer, we always ran out of time in class to go over the workbook. Everything is very harshly graded. No matter how much you study for the exams, it will never be enough.

This professor and class were honestly the bane of my existence this semester. He teaches in a flipped classroom, and as far as teaching goes is a bit of a stretch. I spent countless hours studying for exams, but I have never scored higher than a 58%. If your answer is not exactly what he is looking for, good luck.

Dr. Thompson is an excellent professor. He uses a flipped classroom that works very well for learning O Chem. He gives great feedback and is accessible to answer questions. He allowed me to actually learn the content and do good in the course. He "requires" the textbook but I did just fine without it. I easily got 4% extra credit in the course.

A flipped classroom style means that most learning has to be done out of class. He gives students a lot of resources to be successful. The lectures are pretty boring but important. Don't buy the textbook, you have readings but can get away with just using the study guide. You have to buy the study guide/ course packet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is a really great in-depth look at soil chemistry. Highly recommend this course.

Dr. Thompson has the lectures pre-recorded, so class time can be spent actually working through the practice problems & answering questions. The course is not terribly difficult, & can be passed with modest effort. He is very helpful & accommodating. Participation matters. Go to class. The homework/practice is very similar to the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory, he grades it. The class averages on test were very low, i mean 50%. He does not curve grades or tests. Tests are not like hw or practice. He acts like he cares but really doesn't. The one person that added that good review, is not honest. Find another professor and not the mathurs either, they work together

reviews.comment: Dont take this class.

reviews.comment: Dr. Thompson is a fantastic professor. He is very caring and wants his students to succeed. Dr. Thompson is very accessible and goes the extra mile to provide additional support to learn the material. Highly recommend his class.

reviews.comment: Lazy way of teaching, calls it "flipped classroom". Basically teaching yourself. Wont provide answers to hw questions or study guides. Seems like after covid, he doesnt like to do his job.

reviews.comment: This class is very easy if you show up. Attendance is not required, but he has the class set up so you can earn a ton of extra credit just by answering questions or participating in class. The assignments are easy to do and understand, and you get to go on a class trip as well.

I like the way this class is set up. You just read the chapter, watch a lecture video, and then get two attempts on the quiz each week. It's online so it's at your own pace and the material is very easy to understand.

Ok, so I would say it's an easy A, but god, the lectures are boring if you go to them. The quizzes are online and so easy to get 2 tries. I would say if you're trying to learn anything about theme parks, it's super outdated, and a good yt video will get you more info but it is easy if you need to boost your GPA and kinda like theme parks.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Okay aside from the fact that I simply couldnt stand the sound of his voice this class was poorly put together. Not to mention theres 0 study materials.

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A if you show up and do your work on time. He is a great professor and grades fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Go to class and get your participation points early in the semester. Lectures are a bit boring if you already have hotel experience.
Very easy going.
Very helpful and caring.
Not good at giving advice or general direction. Better come with specific questions to ask.
No Comments

Absent all semester and made us rely on long, off-topic video lectures. Weekly quizzes were full of typos, wrong answers, and repeated mistakes from past semesters. Communication was terrible, he didn't know how to use Canvas, and Exam 1 covered chapters we never learned. Completely unprofessional and disorganized. Avoid this class at all costs.
Easiest class ive taken at ISU.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tony is legit the goat. He gives a bank of all potential exam/quiz questions on the first day of class. If you communicate with him, he is very accommodating about due dates and makeups. Chill professor that understands you have classes other than his. Very little outside work and lectures are often finished early. Would recommend taking it w/ him.

Tony is a great teacher and his lectures are very interesting and helpful if you choose to listen. The class itself is fairly easy if you commit time to study the question bank for quizzes and if you show up for tests. Very interesting professor and has a lot of fun stories. I wish he had more classes!

Townsend? More like GOATsend. This man is like Kobe in his prime #RIP24. He is hilarious and spends a lot of class telling a lot of stories about his life and personal experiences. He likes cigars, energy drinks and having a good time. The quizzes and test are relatively easy and I would highly recommend taking his class if he is available.
Nice guy who is funny but his lectures are worthless.

Professor Townsend is one of my favorite professors at Iowa State. Not only does he have study guides for his exams, you know exactly what will be on the exams. He is caring for his students and really wants to get to know the class. He is also helpful outside of class, and gives great advice. His lectures are very funny.

Prof Townsend is one of my favorite professors I have had at Iowa State University! Show up to class because he takes attendance every day, however, he will give you attendance credit if you email him a valid reason for missing. His lectures are never boring, he has great stories/real world examples, and what he teaches is what he tests. Great guy!

For a guy that teaches project management this guys classes are the worst managed in the Business College. Professor Townsend was late to his own final, handed out 6 or 7 exams before realizing that he didn't have enough. He then disappeared for like 30 minutes and left those 6-7 people who had the final alone with no supervision. Easy A for them.

This guy rambles so much that he borders on incoherent. Sometimes his rants have some very minor connection to the material, but it's not often. He's a fun guy but don't expect to learn much from his lectures. He started taking attendance due to so many people skipping his lectures.

Schedules and Agendas were not followed. Extremely Lecture heavy and lectures consisted of lots of rambling, some roughly related to the topics at hand, and others were random stories from his personal life.
thumbs up
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He really knows his stuff, but it can be tough to glean the important parts from his tangents and rambling. I would recommend taking his section if only for the fact that he doesn't take himself too seriously. He cares about his students and negotiated due dates with the class a few times. Subject matter is dry but Townsend made it memorable.

"study hour for credit" is just about right. The lectures aren't great, but the slides can be helpful when studying for the 2 tests. Not many points in the class but it's fairly easy to do well. Tests aren't a breeze but study the terms (as he suggests) and look up the rest in the slides and you'll be fine (he gives a study guide).

Class itself wasn't difficult. Townsend was consistently late to class and went off on a lot of tangents, but that adds to the low level of difficulty of the class. He thinks he's funnier than he actually is, but you don't have to pay attention in lecture which is nice. Try to not think too hard about the offensive stuff he will inevitably say.

Dr. Townsend's lectures felt more like storytime than anything else. He definitely thinks he's funnier than he really is. He was generally happy to accommodate student requests, but this could be because he didn't have a rigid structure in the first place. He genuinely cares about his students, but you have to keep him on track.

reviews.comment: Great class, great conversation.
This class is basically a study hour for credit. Learned nothing in lecture but got to sit at a computer for an hour and a half twice a week and it was an easy pass.

reviews.comment: Tony Townsend often goes off on tangents. When this happens, it catches your attention for about thirty seconds before you continue to not pay attention. Thanks Tony. Here's to more years of lecturing about this horrible class.
Excellent Instructor
really boring class

I took Organizational and Social Implications of Human Computer Interaction with Dr. Townsend.  He is a charismatic fellow with very random pieces of info.As for the course, it's relatively easy and I did not req the book (off campus student). There was a project that was due (8pg paper double spaced) and two mini exams.lectures were loooong.

Professor Townsend selects interesting readings which definitely encouraged me to think about the topic from more than one perspective. I appreciated the fact that he challenged conventional thinking.

Townsend is crazy! He makes going to class fun, but I doubt you will learn much because of his random stories. His tests are based on the vocab from the textbook and he lets you know what to expect. If you are looking for a GPA booster, this it. The guy acts like Denny Crane from Boston Legal. Nice Guy and knows his stuff, but not the best teacher.
funny guy and knows how to hold short class sessions when needed
easy class if you understand computers already, the only way you'd screw up is if you get cocky and don't look at the vocab.  true, class is usually worthless, but his stories would make up for it
Super teacher

Don't go to lectures, he reads from slides. Study the vocab he puts on webct, read the book, easy A. His life stories are hilarious though. Very bubble personality, easy to talk too, and his TA is awesome, very helpful.

LOL-This guy is really interesting. His lectures are POINTLESS to go to, everything you need is the book and the vocab words that he posts before tests. Make sure to study the entire page that the vocab word is on cause that's how he gets his ?'s for tests. Quizzes supereasy, do the experiment 4 E. Credit. He reads from slides-don't go to lecture

How can you complain about this professor? He's funny, interesting, and easy!  Sure his lectures have nothing to do with the tests, but who cares?! Study the vocab. words that he gives out before the tests and you've got an A.  He's awesome

MIS330: An INTRO class. He makes it bearable through his knowledge and good examples. Didn't read the book? Don't expect an A. That's life. MIS435: Telecomm is hard to scope. Given real-world problems, undergrads fall down and suffer (we saw it). Overall: Door is always open; he's always helpful.

Townsend didn't lecture, he read from the slides which he later told us not to use to study...  I didn't learn anything.  Very unstructured, no syllabus on the first day and would only tell us about a test like 2 weeks prior.  He is a pretty nice guy though, I doubt he wanted to teach this class.

Townsend's lectures are so worthless that I don't see how he could be a tenured university professor. I got an A in the class and didn't learn anything. Obviously doesn't care about his students, just himself.
Lead in class disucssion fantastically.  And hey, I gave you a pepper.

Horrible prof as lecture covers no material and just tells worthless stories and jokes. Always late to class, obviously not prepared, doesn't answer emails. Tests are hard to do good on unless you read the book several times, although its an easy class to get a C in.
Not clear on class expectations, but funny and easy to get a decent grade.  Didn't learn a lot, but didn't care to.  Take this prof, he's way better than the other MIS one.
Full of knowledge, interesting lectures.  You have to read the book to get a good grade on the exams.  No complaints here.
Awesome teacher. Had a great time in his class. Very funny guy. You learn about a lot of other stuff outside of the tested book material. Well worth the time to take it.
Very interesting lecturer, vague about requirements. Tends to get off-track too easily in lecture and in-person, leaving problems unresolved.

Class is worthless b/c he spends all his time on research and thinking about how great he is.  I wanted to learn something, but came away with an A and nothing to show for it.  There's no way I could get a job with anything to do w/ telecomm.

Well if you looking to learn anything from this professor...good luck. Funny and entertaining class on subject matter not related to telecomm/networking. Seems way to preoccupied with research and the class suffers from it.
Super easy, class was a complete joke.  He rewrote the last half of the final after the TA screwed it up.
Jokes, Jokes and Jokes - you will for sure get an A in this class - that's all about this guy!
Good professor, funny guy.
Good

This class can be pretty dry for a lot of people, but terry makes it 100 times more interesting than anyone else. His handwriting is god awful, but so are the other Econ teachers. He admits it, can make a good joke out of it, and still presents his material in a clear, concise manner. I would literally die for this man.

Dr. Alexander is a great lecturer and cares for his students. He encourages participation, but his lectures are a must so don't plan on skipping very many. If you show up, participate, and utilize him as a resource, you will do very well.

Terry was a fantastic Econ102 professor. While there isn't much homework (5 assignments all semester), he really dives in and makes you understand the concepts and how they apply to real life. Tests are made to be difficult, and while I was stressed towards the end of the semester because of the final, the course was overall really good.

reviews.comment: I'm not sure if I can speak for everyone else, but Terry made econ MUCH, much more difficult than it needed to be. If you need help, get it, because he expects you to know everything inside out ten times through.

reviews.comment: Do not do it. Just dont. He means well but makes the class one billion times harder than it needs to be. Tests are all handwritten where other Econ professors do multiple choice. I worked my life away just to get a B.

reviews.comment: He cares a lot about his students. You have to go to class to get notes but he is always if his office if you have questions. Exams are similar to the practice test.

reviews.comment: Very Fair with grading and fairly understanding. If you go to the lectures and study for the test you will most likely get an A. The way he teaches is also very good!!!

I loved having him as a professor! I had him for longer Econ 101 lectures for 1.5 hours twice a week and he would usually try to lighten up class with fun stories and jokes to makes class go by quicker. He also held review sessions, and the online practice exams were similar to what the actual exams. I would take his class again!

reviews.comment: He is an amazing teacher if you are willing to work for it. You HAVE to go to class to pass. If you go to lectures, you will do great on the exams. Pop quizzes are a thing, but they are quite easy. Overall amazing teacher and made me fall in love with Econ!

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher 1 on 1 but in lecture his teaching method could be a little more concise.

reviews.comment: Terry Alexander is an awesome professor if you meet with him one on one. He takes the time and effort to answer your questions in a way that is easy to understands. His biggest downfall is that he tries to teach the whole lecture hall like that and it detracts from his teaching.

reviews.comment: This professor was one of the best professors I have had. He made the class engaging and will tell funny stories in between the information. He talks to people and will hold random conversations in class. His class is easy to follow and he posts notes and lecture videos on blackboard each week. I highly recommend him as a professor.

I found Terry to be a hilarious guy who interacts a lot with the students and genuinely tries to get to know us and makes a huge lecture seem more personal. Econ is not my area at all so I found the content to be hard and all tests are short answer/essay/graphing. Everyday is the same routine with him lecturing just writing notes out on the board.

Terry does things his own way. He's an odd duck but a wonderful duck. His tests aren't a cakewalk since there is no Multiple Choice and even the T/F requires explanation.  As for lecture, he introduces something. and then does it again. and then goes over it again. and then in the next class goes over it again. He makes sure you get it.

reviews.comment: Homework is completely useless. Nothing like the tests or what he teaches in class. The tests are extremely hard, and does an awful job in lecture doing problems like them to prepare students.
I Love this prof.

He's an amazing teacher who cares. He makes sure you get the material even if you struggle. He's very personable. All his lecture notes are up online. Make sure you try your best on the in-class quizzes, which are only available in class. Got to class and try to understand, and you'll do well
