reviews.comment: Easy A for finance student !  took this class last semester. But be sure to go for class and Prof Sapp Is very friendly and easy grader. MUST TAKE CLASS !
One of the best professors. From day one, his expectations from students are very clear. I took as many as four courses with him and I wish I could take more.

Dr. Sapp is one of the smartest professors in the college of business. His course is challenging but you will leave it with a great deal of knowledge. Expect to prepare for tests & quizzes far in advance because there is a lot of material throughout the course. Overall, I would highly recommend Dr. Sapp's class.

Dr. Sapp is very knowledgeable of investment concepts. However, his class his very rigorous. The lecture notes are fairly identical between his undergraduate and graduate course. He only gives a midterm and final exam along with 4 quizzes. They require memorization and application. There are also a few group assignments. Lectures and notes are long

The homework and group projects are a lot of work so start early on them. He is kind of hard to listen to in lecture, and isn't super specific on what he wants all of the time. Don't miss the homework/group project walkthrough days, they are extremely important.

Sapp is an incredibly intelligent man and his class is fairly interesting. You will not need a book for this class, his lecture notes are great. Make sure you attend class to fill in lecture notes. If you memorize the material the tests are straight forward. I recommend taking this class with Dr. Sapp.

Sapp is extremely knowledgeable however can belittle you in his office.  You don't need the book, and he curves the class about 10%. The exams were tricky, but the quizzes were what really got people tripped up. Make sure you stay on top of the excel assignments (There's 3) and take good notes and go to class and you will do fine.

Not a terrible teacher. Kind of hard to listen to with a monotone voice. The class is curved which helps A LOT. Is fair when grading quizzes, but midterm is tough as are the assignments. Goes SUPER fast when going over assignments so take notes. Don't buy the book.

Sapp is a great teacher, but you have to pay attention. If you have a short attention span or aren't interested in finance, take this with someone else. He gets students involved hands on, and presents material in a very clean and easy to understand way. I highly suggest taking 320 with him.

Dr. Sapp is an excellent professor.  His course is challenging.  You will learn and comprehend significant investment analysis and methods. Dr. Sapp does an excellent job of integrating Excel applications into the course work and projects.  A passing or better grade will be very difficult to achieve without attending class. He is very helpful.

This class isn't an easy or guaranteed A, but it is definitely attainable if you attend class and study due to the large curve. Sapp is extremely intelligent and very helpful. Take good notes on how to do assignments and you'll do well.

Great Professor. He is a bit more challenging than others who teach this class I'm sure, but you get a lot more out of it as a result. He is a very accomplished guy that knows his stuff. I would still read the textbook, although he presents the material in a much easier to understand way.

Great professor. Is an expert in the field of finance, but is able to get information across to students in an easy to understand way. Is very clear of expectations and is always willing to work with you and help you as needed.

Pretty hard class but it's pretty interesting as well. He's kind of monotone so you need to make sure you're paying attention but he knows what he's talking about and overall I enjoyed his lectures. Make sure you review well for the test and take his practice exams. They give you a good idea of how much you have it down
A great professor from any angle. Dear Travis thank you very much!! It is such professors who arm their students with knowledge, which help them navigate in their professional lives.
One of the best professors I have come across. Knows what he is teaching very well.

Don't need the textbook, his tests come from his notes packet that he sends you at the beginning of the semester. Some of the material is pretty tough, but the class overall isn't too bad. Not the most exciting to listen to, but coming to class helps a lot!!!!
Lots of reading, but interesting if you like PE, VC, and M&A. Always very helpfull. If you don't like to come, don't take it.
Wonderful Professor! I'm a non-traditional student.  He explained everything very clearly and and with the right speed. Problems on tests were taught in class with great clarity!

Great summer class, he explained everything very clearly. Basically applied algebra. Even though he has a monotone voice, he can be funny, so stay awake. Grade was based on 2 tests, and 2 quizzes. So study!!!

Not the most exciting man to listen to, but he sure knows his stuff.  Attending class is a must, especially when he goes over the problem sets.  Exams are very fair, problems exactly like those on problem sets and notes.  Gives 3 large assignments, but he walks you through them step by step if you go to class.  Absolutely 100% do not buy the book.

Don't buy the textbook; I never used it. Not an exciting professor, but gives clear explanations. Stocktrak trading project was fairly easy, and tests weren't too bad. Quizzes weren't bad, but you need to study. Excel assignments are difficult, but if you go to class he basically walks you through all of them before they are due.

Great professor. He does fantastic job explaining by showing many examples. He doesn't trick you on exams. If you paid attention in his lectures, his exams are fair game. His facial expression kinda remind of Peter character from the movie Office Space :).
Fantastic professor!  Great summer class in Finance 301.  Had to work hard, but well worth it.
Sapp is very boring but seems to know his stuff. There is noone better than him for fin 320..unfortunately

Pretty good professor. Pretty easy, explains things very well. However, very very very boring to listen to. The class is pretty easy though, and he curves the class pretty well. Don't buy the textbook though because he has a course packet that has everything you need.

Very clear about how he teaches, but yes, pretty boring. Book has very limited use, course packet comes with everything you need.  Pretty big curve at the end. Pretty good overall if you can stand a pretty bland and routine class.
Very friendly & professional professor. Yes, he does have a monotone voice, but he knows his stuff, and tells you exactly what to expect on the exam. Unbelievably HUGE curve.
His class sooooooooo nice..If you concentrate his class..It's not boring. and test is also not difficult. good!!!
Can't believe of bad reviews here. His exams are not that hard all if you PAY ATTENTION in lecture! One of few genuinely nice professor I had at ISU. Look for the Simpsons reference on his exam.
very boring class. sometimes i think he is a wax figure...

Not the most exiting guy to listen to, but he eplains the material well.  Make sure you know how to do all of his example problems before the quizzes and tests.  Easy class if youre good at math.  HUGE curve.

Worst class I've ever taken.  He is so boring and knows the information too well to actually get across what you need to do and skips important steps cus he forget that the class doesn't know this stuff
super boring lecture, monotone voice.  examples in class are easy but tests are very difficult

Worst professor that I have had at ISU. He will give you the easiest form of a problem during lecture and practice exams; only to ask you the most difficult version of a question on a test. I would not recommend this professor to anyone! The other instructors in the department make this class much easier to understand.
Teaches at a great pace.  Expains problems throughly.  Will definetly recommended.  He has a great curve.  Very passable class.
This guy is a pretty big nerd.  He knows his stuff and teaches it pretty good but the class is easy and is required.  He isn't the worst I have had.
Good teacher.  Had him for 2 classes now.  I dont really mind him.  I would take more classes with him also.
BORING beyond belief, if you have to take this class take it in the summer! Get it over with as quickly as possible. Nice guy, just sooooo boring. Tests are ok if you study somewhat.

This class is so easy.  The guy is actuall interesting if you can stay awake.  But I have slept in every class I have ever took so naturally I slept most of the time, but when I did listen he was interesting.  SO EASY.

Be there to do the example problems, but if you miss he posts the solutions. Tests aren't terrible if you have the notes and examples. Staying awake in class is the bigger issue. Very monotone, but nice. Curve is HUGE!

Possibly THE most boring professor on earth.  His monotone voice and verbatim powerpoint presentations do nothing to help you learn.  Grading over just a couple of components doesn't help either.  By far the worst finance professor I've had (had several).

EXTREMELY boring class, and Sapp is an extremely boring guy with a terribly monotone voice.  I can't imagine Finance being an exciting subject in any way shape or form, but I think this guy makes it more boring.  Not necessarily a bad teacher, though...
This class sucks and it is very, very boring....
SOOOO boring, and tests are ridiculously hard.  When 78% is an A with the curve, the class is obviously ridiculous.  I beleive ACTION Sapp is the worst teacher i've ever had.

This guy is the worst teacher I've ever had in my entire life.  Granted he is teaching some boring stuff anyway, but this guy really takes the cake.  His monotone voice, not to mention the fact that this guy has no personality.  Sapp Sucks!!!
Very good instructor if you come to class.  Whole grade based on just a few exams, if you mess up one, you're screwed!
The class was hard, but he made it somewhat easier.. His tone might get you to sleep, but he's a good professor..
I didn't think this class was that easy.  I do think that Prof Sapp is an excellent instructor and very helpful.  I liked him alot.
VERY VERY boring, and monotone. Stay away from this guy or you'll fall asleep!  Easy class overall though!

If you fail this professor Adeleke's classes, I think it is your own fault. If you do the readings and pay attention in the class, you will do fine. He only grades a few things, but if you apply things in class and stuff from the readings you will get a good grade. He can be short sometimes, but he will respond if you contact him outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am an A student and this is the first D I have gotten . The class consist of 100 point for the semester and the final is 35 points. Professor Adeleke wants a certain writing style but does not specify what that is. He does not include rubrics for anything and he does not answer emails. He said his class should be easy but that was NOT the case.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: amazing man, would 100% recommend

Dr. Adeleke is a wonderful speaker with lots of knowledge to share with his students. However, there were only 3 tests and they were all essay, with no information provided about what the essay questions would be. There's SO MUCH READING and it's required because the tests are not based solely upon his lectures. No other assignments, very scary.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures arent the best. Hes more of a story teller. The book is more helpful than the professor. He's a bit intimidating and gets angry easily although he means well. There's also a large group project without a rubric. I would not take this class if you want an easy gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A wonderful professor who really knows his material. One of the most interesting classes I have taken at Iowa State. To some, he may a sign a hefty amount of reading, but every reading is extremely interesting and important to learn. Also, you are given plenty of time to complete the readings. I would take any class taught by Dr. Adeleke.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: After reading the comment s written by previous  by previous students, I would have to say that I have to disagree. Yes, the readings are long but they aren't mandatory, only for the first weeks of class they are but then it is a breeze. All you have to do is show up pay attention and listen for the test topics when he goes over them in class.

Dr. Adeleke is a hard professor, he is also one of the best I've ever had. If you have questions, go to his office hours. Read all of the material he requires, get familiar with his speech patterns a he has a thick Nigerian accent. I have taken many classes from him and I have learned a lot! He may be misunderstood, but do not overlook this gem.

Do yourself a favor and do not take this class.  You will be required to read hundreds of pages throughout the semester but the tests will consist of ten questions. There is good chance you will be yelled at in class. Lectures are very unclear and tests are difficult.

not helpful at all. if you go to him during office hours to ask questions, he will yell at you and say you haven't read. calls students out on faults instead of talking to them privately. too much reading. waste of a class

The first day of class he clarifies that his purpose is to not make you feel sorry if you're white. He does expect students to do the work he assigns and only lazy students don't succeed. If you go to class and read small parts of what he tells you, you will do fine. He GIVES you the questions for the exam so you don't even have to figure that out
Switch Classes!! I highly recommend not taking this class with him. There are many other U.S Diversity classes that are much easier.

He is very hard. The test answers have to be from the text book if  not you receive a very low grade. If he tells you the answers in class and you write that on the essay exam you will get it wrong because it was not from the readings.  He makes an introductory course way harder than it should be and is very bad grading.
Don't take this class with him. I enjoy anything, but he makes the class way too hard.
While he is very knowledgeable and has a lot of first hand experience, attending class is often painful as you discuss the same things for weeks at a time without adding on to previous discussions.

At all costs, avoid this course.   He is a complete failure to the academic world.  Like the comment below, to get a good grade you have to agree with him on everything, feel sorry for being white, brown-nose, and teach yourself.  His lectures are completely impromptu and fyi- you don't need to do any readings until he tells you what exams are over

Self centered and grades harsh. Talks with an extreme accent. Likes class discussions, but doesn't like when they venture away from his thoughts. To get an A, agree with everything he says, worship the ground he walks on, and feel sorry for being white.

Dr. Adeleke is an outstanding scholar, director, and professor.  He is the best of the best.  Does he have high expectations?  Yes, but he challenges his students to rise to the occasion.  He is a master instructor and leader who is focused on making a true difference.

Good professor. Always interesting, if not helpful. Don't expect him to hold your hand. Tests are all essays, attendance and participation are mandatory. But he's a good teacher with a lot of knowledge to give.
No Comments

HAD FOR AF AM 201.  Has a heavy accent, speaks kind of fast and mumbles a lot.  Uses 4-5 major textbooks plus about 30 readings on reserve at Parks Library.  Very hard for an intro course.  Wouldn't take it again.  Wants specific answers on tests--dates, names, times... hard to pack in so much information in so little time.

Professor Poon's teaching style doesn't work for a lot of people. He goes through problems very quickly and doesn't explain concepts super in-depth. 

That being said, there are so many ways to get additional help for this course. I can't recommend enough going to supplemental instruction sessions and help hours. They can help tremendously.

I took this course because even though I took calculus in high school, and I wanted to make sure I understood the parts that I didn't get very well the first time\ After taking this class, I can confidently say that it did not work. Poon spends way too long on easy stuff and not enough time on complex topics. Plus, his accent is hard to understand.
he is not from the US so his accent is a bit hard to understand and he doesn't cover a ton of stuff thats on the test.
Goes so fast and I don't understand his thinking process, he over complicates things so much

At first, It seemed like Poon would go through too many problems too quickly without much explaining but now that I'm in calc 3 and have a professor that gets through 3 problems an hour I truly miss the fast pace of Prof Poon's lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You might as well accept an F for the semester already if you have this guy for Calc 2. TERRIBLE. His lectures are very fast paced and hard to follow, then he scratched his head when EVERYONE FAILS the exam. Do not, for the love of God, take a Calculus class with this man.

He is really hard to understand, not really his fault, but it just makes class a lot harder. The class was graded on a generous curve but only because the exams were so hard. He assigned a ton of homework for this particular class.
Absolutely horrendous - I mean almost unimaginably bad.

This man has zero respect for any of his students. He flies through lecture while skipping over many steps to difficult calculus problems. last semester, during his last lecture before the final, I asked him a question about a problem he was doing on the board. He responded to me saying "You should know this already" and proceeded to ignore me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Poon was difficult to understand most of the time and spent all class time doing example problems without explaining the concepts. I watched a lot of Khan Academy and other videos for this class, wouldn't have done well without doing that. He is very smart and caring when you go to his office hours, but the lectures were rough. Tests aren't bad
This guy was awful. I didn't learn a thing in lecture, just thank god for my TA. I taught myself basically everything. He can't even pronounce half the terms!
Long story short, do your self a favor and switch out of his class as soon as your read this... I wish I had any other teacher in the world

His lectures are super boring and hard to follow. Honestly spent most of the time on my phone when I went to class.  Eventually I stopped going.  I consider myself  smart math guy (usually get A's except for Bolles in 166) so I was able to just teach myself everything.  His tests are super laid out and not challenging if you have some math knowledg
Extremely hard to understand.  Very tough grader. Would not recommend.

Take the American's lecture if you can because after 1 week of listening to Poon's voice struggle to say the word "vectors" I wanted to blow my brains out. The quizzes are 20% of your grade and most everyone does terrible because they have little to do with what you went over in class that week.
His lectures were helpful to a degree because he goes through a lot of examples and explains them thoroughly. Also the tests aren't too difficult if you do the review guide.

Dr. Poon is the worst professor I've ever had. There are 3 homework assignments a week, a quiz every week, and his lectures are reading straight from a powerpoint which is straight from the book. Change into a different section if you get him.
Everyone falls asleep.  Boring lecture, broken english, and teaching straight off a powerpoint.  Brutal class
He isn't a good teacher. His lectures are all powerpoint mostly from the book. Students fall asleep all over, even in the front row.

He starts the class early, before everyone gets in. His grading is very bad - cuts off 40% mark just for rounding error. Grading scale is not clear - he doesn't give any way to know peers' performance. Curve is not helpful at all. Sticks to his notes, and jumps from here to there. Does not explain the problem, very hard to keep track of.  BAD!

Decent teacher, but his English is a little spotty. I had to teach myself a bit from the textbook. Passable class, but tough to get an A as the tests are fairly difficult and the curve was not very helpful.

Dr. Poon is an awful lecturer and he makes his T.A.'s grade quizzes and tests very,  very strictly. He starts class early every time, speaks awful english, and writes illegibly. The homework takes up to 10 hours every week, but you can usually get 100% on it. Getting an A in the class is nearly impossible, even if you attend every lecture.

Terrible lecturer. Hard to understand wherever you sit in the room, very small, sloppy writing on the chalkboard which is sometimes illegible. Never puts notes online and it's impossible to catch half the things he says in lecture. Assigns homework on both Friday and Sunday which makes no sense as well as over spring break. Overall, not a fan.

Every class he first gives a very in depth explanation of all theoriesformulas used and how they were derived. He then proceeds to solve many examples to show how to apply the theoriesformulas. Very helpful if you pay attention.
Poon is a professor who likes to make both the tests and assignments hard as hell.
He is a very harsh grader and gives out many difficult assignments

Hard to understand due to a heavy accent. Writing on board is hard to read no matter where you sit. Poon also doesn't read the questions that he writes on the board and will often start solving them without explaining why he's doing what he does. He will also start class 5 min early, before everyone has a chance to get there from their prior class.

Poon gives out more homework than any other professor I have had at Iowa State. I was so buried in homework that I had a hard time finding time for other classes. In doing all this homework you would think I would have a clear understanding of the material, but Poon covers so much material you never know whats coming on the next quiztest.
Easiest Math class I've ever taken at Iowa State. Got an easy A and I'm not even good at Math. Would recommend taking with this professor.

He was the worst professor I have ever had, avoid at all costs.  Unless your want to teach yourself, I imagine he would be great for that. He flies through as much material as he can as quickly as he can, which may sound good, but in practice you learn nothing.

dude is a stunna, doing math like its his job!!!  but in all seriousness Dr. Poon's class was very enjoyable for me.  I would recommend sitting near the front of the room as he has a strong accent.  after he released his notes on blackboard it became much easier.  book homework is free points and my math lab helps you learn!! would take again!!!!!!

Difficult to understand at first, but after a few weeks I didn't struggle to understand him.  Brilliant professor, knows the subject very well and shows class how to do problems efficiently.  If you pay attention in lecture the material is not difficult to comprehend.

Decent professor but pretty hard to understand. The tests covered a large volume of material which is what made them hard. If you search on isu's website for other professor's web pages you can find their old exams which are pretty useful. The "practice exams" he gives you on mathlab aren't very helpful, but do get you extra points on the test.
I am glad I took this class with him, I've learned a lot!
Terrible accent and very difficult to understand till you get used to him.  Tests are somewhat easy but still need to study plenty because of the volume of material covered.
sticks strictly to his notes, but was knowledgable. Somewhat hard to understand..but the course is geared for individual learning, and its not too hard at all. Recitation is worthless

Poon would teach even if no one was in the room. He is a short Asian man with a medium accent and cannot say parabola. His lectures are not helpful in learning the material (unless he writes on the blackboard) and the recitations are not much more helpful. Be prepared to teach yourself in this course.
He is awful because he is hard to understand and has poor teaching methods.  His homework is put online late and his notes aren't very helpful.

He has alot of difficulty with speaking English. He sounds like a broken record when he speaks and he has only one way to explain things due to his limited English skills. But his redeeming quality is the notes he posts online. Overall, his crappy English negates all his knowledge. He does get props for his name: Pronounced You-Tongue-Poon.

Absolutely hilarious! Funniest prof ever even though he doesn't try to be. He will repeat the same sentence 3 or 4 times before moving on to the next one. Tests are very easy. Hard not to get an A. Don't talk during lecture or he will stop mid sentence and stare at you.
Terrible teacher. Easy tests.
Going to lecture is useless.  Speaks very broken English.  I learn everything from my rececitation and the textbook.

One of the worst math teacher I've ever had.  Uses very complicated problems for examples and does a poor job explaining things in general.  His tests are really easy though and rarely cover the hardest material.

If you go to class, take notes, and DO THE HOMEWORK, the class isn't too bad. His grading system can be confusing and hard to get an A, but he really teaches the material which helps in later math classes. Also, a TI-89 is a life saver. Ask questions in recitation, not in lecture, because he'll take a half hour to answer it.
A useless prof in all ways

Poon is a nice guy and gets to business as soon as he enters the class room. He knows his stuff, but assigns too little homework and no odd problems. If you follow his advice word for word regarding tests and attend the lectures, you can pass the course without your head exploding.
Lectures are very clear with many examples.  Expect any quizzes to cover the most difficult material from lecture.

Ok he knows his stuff, but he has an inability to teach. I think he gets confused sometimes if you ask a question, which isn't good for Calc III. He also get upset easily, so try not to screw around in class!

The largest gripe I had about this class is the fact that Poon has absolutely no classroom control. Students made fun of him, were disrespectful, and walked across the front of the room while lecture was going on. It made for a very hard enviroment to learn in. He knows his stuff but I was not happy with this class.
No Comments

One of the hardest classes I have taken. I'm not really sure what I got out of it. Tests are pointless to study for, but go to review sessions for EC. Not clear on the syllabus and changes it so rack up points early on for the best outcome. Nice curve because of the syllabus issue. HWs are graded hard, sometimes has EC. Good guy that is too smart.

Dr. Tuggle is too smart to teach undergraduate students. But he realizes that his class is hard and gives a very generous curve. Final is super easy. Go to review sessions and pay attention in class you will be just fine!

Dr. Tuggle teaches this class as if the undergrads are graduate students.  PowerPoints are useless to study off of and tests were confusing.  I managed a C-D on every test and failed the final and still got a B so the curve helps a lot.  Overall don't take if you don't have to
Dr. Tuggle prides himself on making his class VERY difficult. It honestly seems like he tries to make his class as confusing as possible.

While he was undoubtedly made lectures worthwhile, his grading criteria was a joke. Randomly takes points off on essays with no explanation, changed the format for each exam. Provided solid study guides.
In my opinion he was a pretty good teacher and the grade was mainly based off of three test and one essay. But overall he made the lectures pretty interesting and enjoyable.

An amazing professor. He is a ton of fun and has a lot of personality that seeps into his lectures. He's very passionate about history and the world in general and it shows. He changed our whole last two lectures the day before because of some world events that he thought took precedent, which was really cool.

Lectures are loaded with content, but his power points have the info you need. Gives a standard history test with matching, recognize and define, and an essay section. First two tests he has given the topics you can discuss on the essay before the test so you have time to prepare. He also sprinkles swearing into his lectures, so beware.
Dr. Tynan is very organized. This was not a hard class at all.
Prof Tynan is hilarious, understanding, and grades fairly
He was really great! I made otherwise boring and tedious lectures rather interesting and the class was very lowkey.

I've taken 301 as well as Social Psych with Prof. Tynan. He's a genuinely good dude and probably the best psychology professor I've had at ISU. I would highly recommend taking a class with him in addition to 301 if you get the chance.

Dr. Tynan's class was very boring, but he is a kind, caring professor. His class was very lecture-heavy, with in-class quizzes at the end of class occasionally. He seemed to be interested in the topic, but it was relatively boring. There are online exams and weekly assignments. Very easy class, but the class itself is boring!
Class is kinda boring but I was able to get an A in the class. Online exams and quizzes. You do have in class quizzes that he gives the codes for in class so you have to show up.

Professor Tynan gives great lectures and makes class enjoyable with his humor. He's easy to communicate with, grades fast, and the exams were pretty manageable. Sometimes he moves a bit quickly through slides, but overall, a solid and engaging professor.

You can tell Dr. Tynan really cares about his students and loves when students are engaged. Can be tricky to pay attention since the lectures can be a bit boring and tedious, but understandable in a research class. He does simple participation quizzes at the end of each class- easy points. Exams can be hard though.
He generally teaches well with good humor and has a great section on gender/sex differences.

Class is very tedious if you're not interested in research. There are in classes quizzes that are graded for attendance at the end of every class. No discussions or papers- its all online quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took psych 280 with this professor and I would definitely take a course with him again. His lectures were very interesting and he did an amazing job making it relatable for students. He made time for questions each lecture and encouraged participation in a chill environment. Tests were really easy and the lecture before an exam was always review.

I've taken Tynan before, and I love how he teaches. It just clicks with me. This class has a lot of discussion boards and a semester paper that he grades pretty harshly. He also had some weird discussion questions that I didn't feel comfortable doing, but other than that, it was a very interesting and fun class!
Great prof. Engaged with the class often and could tell he cared. Do his study guides before exams and you're golden
Not amazing, not awful

He made a intro class very entertaining and engaging. He was understanding about any issues people may have, as well as very clear about what his expectations were. Definitely will try to take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend taking a class with Stacey. Her teaching is unorganized, with frequent tangents and videos that don't feel relevant. Group work doesn't connect to the material, and you'll likely need to teach yourself to do well on the in-person midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She overall is a nice person. My only issue is that she is very much unprepared for everything. The final and midterm are in person and are very difficult considering its 50 multiple choice and 6 essays. No one finished in time and failed the exams. The final project on top of the final exam a lot. I would avoid 314&317 for your stress alone.
This was one of the hardest classes for me to attend. This class is extremely boring and hard to follow. I would recommend taking other classes with other professors for com st credit.

Tye-Williams is caring, personable, and funny.  Although I love her, I was not a fan of the class.  Two big exams, many journals, & papers that seemed like busy work.  Class wasn't necessarily mandatory but got extra credit if you went regularly.  Participation matters a good amount.  Lecture heavy but slides weren't made that well imo.

Dr. Tye-Williams is friendly and responds to emails well. However, she's very unorganized and her courses lack structure and preparation. Her guidelines lack clear grading criteria which makes it difficult to complete assignments. I'd recommend taking courses with a different instructor (like Dr. Coffelt or Fornoff).

Group project for a non-profit organization that lasts the whole semester.  Many group activities that were actually very fun.  A good amount of papers, but not enough to be tiring.  Only two exams that were fairly easy if you studied!  Love the professor, seemed interested in supporting her work and yours as well!!  Treats you with respect.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures often felt unnecessary as she spent most of the time showing an excessive amount of videos and giving us "group activities." You really teach yourself most of the material for the tests, which are short answer heavy. Personally, she was my least favorite professor and I did not love her style of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance kind of matters, lose 5 points per class after 2 freebies. Lectures often felt unnecessary, never really read the book. You'll need to cram a little for the tests if you don't read, but she still graded my essays pretty generously. She's nice, class was pretty easy.

Stacy is a great teacher! Her lectures are always very clear and straight forward.  The topics were not always interesting but she applied them well to help understanding.  Tests are difficult, but she is a fair grader and does not try to trick you.  Very nice and approachable.

Stacy is a wonderful teacher. Her tests are a bit difficult but she is fair. If you approach her with questions she is very easy to talk with. She does refer to the book a lot and attendance is expected because you miss a bit when you skip. Overall very fair and understanding!
Wonderful teacher.  Creative lectures even though some topics were boring.  Easy going!  Taking class from her again.

I've also taken 314 with Stacy. She's a nice, helpful teacher, but her classes require a lot of reading and a lot of paper writing. She's a really fair grader though. Her tests can be kind of tricky, especially when it comes to her matching section. Overall she's a good teacher and I've been able to get good grades in her classes.

While the class itself is not super difficult, you have to teach yourself all the material. He does not give you any lecture videos, just notes, but office hours are helpful. He does not post assignments or quizzes on time, you are always crammed up to the deadlines. You also never know how you're doing because nothing is graded in a timely manner.
never povided enough info for class, no lecture online during pendemic
We never know where we stand in the class. It sucks to not know where you stand in the class in terms of marks. I didnt enjoy this professor a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: At least two quizzes per week, so must attend class. Doesn't post any grades online just hands back papers and posts grades online at end. It is difficult to know where you stand in the class. Does a good job keeping class entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Expect homework due on Friday to be posted on Wednesday with multiple mistakes in them, even when he says he will post it Monday. Don't expect grades to be posted as he doesn't use canvas. He will stop teaching in order to stare at people who walk in late(even though he is also always late). He makes you feel like an idiot when asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tuttle believes that you should try the same amount, your hardest, for any class regardless of grades. No regard for time management for other classes and uses this as an excuse not to post any grades. If you go to ask him a question he will answer it, but he makes sure you feel like an idiot. He is a good lecturer and teacher overall though.

Oh Tuttle... - Amazing at lectures, his material is gold - He is nitpicky about attendance, don't be late - Homework is not an easy 100%, it is a lot and it is challenging, double check your answers, this will either pull up or down your grade - He will get caught up in the math, go too theorical and become dull sometimes

He's probably the best professor that I have ever had in terms of how well and clearly he explained things. There are quizzes almost every lecture but it helps with the understanding of the material. That being said he does have some issues with returning grades in a timely fashion.

Dr Tuttle is the best professor i've had, and i'm not even a EE. His lectures were extremely helpful, and his notes were also great. You are expected to work, but his way of teaching, and the way his class is organized really makes you learn his stuff. Also extremely helpful during his office hours. Favorite professor I've had.

The quizzes weren't too bad, but often the homeworks were a slog in the mud; you'd go for help to his office hours and half the time he completely missed them. Will interrupt lecture and loudly remark if one person walks in late or talks to somebody else.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tuttle is a great teacher and explains things very well in lecture. He does not require a textbook, and I did not use it the whole semester, as his slides posted online are very thorough. Quizzes Monday and Wednesday. Reasonably challenging homework due Friday. He is respected and has a dry sense of humor which was entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a really cool teacher with good lectures that I liked going to. If you have hime you can aleays go into office hours or shoot him an email and get help.

If you show up late for class, he stops presenting and stares at you until you sit down, then loudly comments on your lateness. Mon/Wed  pop quiz; Friday HW is due. HW questions are much more difficult than lecture notes. Lab is extremely long. He has a tendency to present rather than teach. His exams are extremely easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers at Iowa State. He makes high quality lecture slides that have good content. If you learn from him and his lecture slides, you will have the knowledge to land a good job once you graduate. I honestly think he should start teaching other professors on how they can be more effective. I never did get my homework back though....
He is a very nice teacher, but the hw are hard though
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: There was a quiz every monday and wednesday but the quizzes were fairly easy. They were very helpful for staying caught up in the class. He is a really good lecturer and will call out students who disrespect him or the class. If you are here to learn, take Tuttle.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The professor explains concepts very clearly.  To help us fully understand concepts, we had two quizzes every week along with a weekly homework.  His sarcasm makes every lecture fun to attend.

He doesn't take disrespect from anyone. You are there to learn so if you are bothering the class he will call you out. Keeps class light with jokes and is very straight forward in what you need to accomplish to pass the class.
Great Professor!
GT is the best professor I have ever had. He recently stated that next year (2017) will be his last year at Iowa State. Get him while you still can.
One of the best instructors I've had. Clear, helpful, fair, while still making you learn a lot and put in effort. Very knowledgeable about semiconductors.

GT is the man - you really want to take EE230 with him. He is the reason I understand basics, theory, and applications for diodes/transistors/amplifiers/etc. Don't let someone persuade you otherwise, his classes are extremely useful in the real world. He is really involved with the curriculum board and making sure everyone is on the same page.

GT is easily my favorite ECpE professor and always will be. After taken 201, 230, and now 333X with him - there isn't anyone better. He teaches the material at a level you can understand it, which is great for the introductory courses when things are new. The weekly quizzes are awesome because it forces you to learn and retain material for exams.
Pfft. You don't need your homework back. Tuttle is loved.

Tuttle truly cares about the material he teaches and the technical development of his students. I have used him multiple times as a resource for help in both 201 and some of my other classes. He even has a couple of clubs outside of class. His classes aren't a breeze but if you utilize all the help he gives, they're not bad at all.

One of the best professors i have ever had. He genuinely cares for his students. Goes out of his way to try to start clubs and help his students. Provides relevant uses for circuits being used in class andor gives us useful circuits as part of lectures.

Gary Tuttle is the best professor I've had in my 4 semesters of college. He genuinely cares and his lectures are enjoyable.  His power points were the best I've seen of any class and I will be using his 230 notes for my 230 class. 1010 would take again.

Naturally, an introduction to circuits class consists of a lot of dry material; however, Dr. Tuttle did very well at  providing interesting applications of principles learned in class. He structured the class in a way that forced you to learn and work hard, even if it was a lot of work for him. Motivates you to become a great engineer.
Professor Tuttle is personable, knowledgeable, friendly, and more than willing to help anyone in need.
Great lectures, he's clear with his material and humorous at times. He really is there to help you. One of the few professors at Iowa State that actually cares about the quality of your material.
My favorite lecturer ever and has a great sense of humor. Really knows his stuff. Don't talk in his class though he  hates that.
Great Lectures and if you do the homework and labs like he asks ur good

GT has the best notes about EE on the internet. His lectures are a bit dry, but pretty helpful. The homework is hard and hard, and usually comes out Monday night, due Friday. He's a laid back guy (unless you talk in class) and is helpful and accommodating.  He explains hard concepts clearly. Quizzes are frequent; assignments are slowly returned.

Very Slow Grader. Turned in homework and would get it back ... MONTHS later. This class is very easy, he curves it a ridiculous amount. He says they're online notes but doesn't post them. Also if homework is due wednesday, don't expect to see it posted before monday morning and correction to be posted tuesday at like 9 pm when he works through them

Overall a great professor. Very clear lecturer, gives good examples. Homework was definitely increasingly difficult as semester went on. Plan on setting aside a LOT of time for the homework. Labs can be tricky. Exams also tripped me up, but most people did fine. He's a nice guy and will answer questions. Don't make him mad by talking in lecture.

Overall a very good lecturer, does a great job of explaining the material and is very helpful if you have questions.  Only complaint is that he does not return graded homework, tests, or quizzes in a timely manner.  Outside of that he is one of the better electrical engineering teachers at Iowa State.
Awesome prof, explains topics clearly, knows his stuff, genuinely wants to see you succeed.  Has tons of office hours and always helps me work through problems.

Tuttle is a pretty good EE professor. He has really good ways of explaining certain topics and prepares you for the tests. Sure he might be rather dry and the material is pretty easy, but that's partly because he isn't trying to overly complicate or confuse everyone like some other professors.His grading DOES take FOREVER so don't expect promptness

Horrible prof. Boring material, but he's easy so you'll still get an A. Laziest guy on Earth. Don't expect to get grades for anything back, ever. He puts homework up two days before it's due. Forgets to put up practice tests. The solutions to the quizzes he puts up are frequently wrong. TAs are even more worthless.
Easy professor.  Makes things interesting and his dry sense of humor is hilarious.

One of the best professors I have had at Iowa State.  His randomness and dry sense of humor keep the lectures interesting.  The last half of the class is challenging, but any effort outside of class and you will do fine.  He is very helpful outside of class as well.
I had this guy for three semesters in a row.  My favorite proffessor at Iowa State.  Pretty much taught me everything I needed for electrical engineering, and helped me get a job.  Thanks Gary!
Tuttle is the man, not easy/interesting material but he made it beraable, and of course tried to make lectures interesting, everyone should have Tuttle for at least one class.
Greatest guy on Iowa State's faculty list

Good teacher.  Effective lectures when he actually prepares one, however, often he didn't have anything prepared because he chose to work on his car all night instead.  Comes to class about 10 minutes late every day.  Grades fairly, but takes long time to get exams back. Often late to office hours.

Great Professor!  He made coming to class at 8AM worth it.  Very funny and he make E E 203 concept easy to understand.  However, his exams are tough, which took my grade down one letter grade.  Tuttle is one professor you should have at least one class with if you are a EE/CprE.
A good teacher, tests are kinda tricky though, but an all-around decent guy

The book was worthless, but Gary helped out a lot by teaching the material very well.  Overall, he was a good professor when it came to teaching, but when it came to grading and returning work, he has a hard time getting things back to students at all.
"I don't like giving homework and you don't like doing it."  Great prof, though is slightly strange when he doesn't look at you when answering a question.
Had for both 333 and 332, Awesome teacher

"Let the confusion begin!" - Class motto as stated by Dr. Tuttle.  Awesome class, easy to grasp concepts if you are interested in the material.  Notes help MUCH better than the book, so take good notes!
Great, energetic lectures.  Has a sense of humor.  Even poked fun at Limp Bizkit fans in one of the lab descriptions.  Rather slow at returning work, but he's a great professor other than that.

His lectures are great!!! Homeworks are hard but make you think,,,which is a good thing!!! He gives quizes so often which i didnt like because my perception for quizes is different than with exams. He grades fairly.
Great Prof.  Tries to make lecture interesting.
Overall great guy.  His lectures are not always the best, but he seems to love to teach and will take as much time as necessary to answer any question.
Awesome teacher, very easy to talk to.
No Comments
Fair grader and easy to talk to
Awesome teacher
No Comments

Prof Jensen was a good instructor for this class. Grading was straightforward. There were a few "live" quizzes where you would need to zoom with him and talk through some homework problems, but it was pretty low pressure. Puts you in groups with people who have similar schedules as yours, which is nice. Very helpful if you ever have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Easy class, very to the point. Opens all the assignments up, you can do all of them in 1 day. 
Used lockdown browser.

Jensen was fair, but exams/quizzes are most of your grade. His conceptuals are awful and unlike anything he teaches. Quantitatives were off of a practice set with changed names and numbers. Big curve, and he was very willing to answer questions when asked. Exam review sessions were very helpful. 3 quizzes, 2 exams, 4 HWs, and a smartbook/chapter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Would definitely take Finance 301 with Tyler. Only two exams, and they are both online. He does reviews the night before exams which help a lot. He's a great professor that I would take again.

Lecture videos are so boring I want to tear my eyeballs out. I stopped watching them after a week like 4. One smartbook each week and 4 homework the whole semester. The homework is McGraw Hill and he keeps the hint videos on. Then 4 quizzes, I don't remember but each quiz is split into 2. 2 exams, and the final is cumulative. Easier than in person.
Professor Jensen was able to make the general concepts in this course very applicable and the examples he used made it so easy to understand.

Tyler was a good professor. He knew what he was talking about and is very smart. His class was difficult and it took a lot of studying to do well on the exams. He made sure you knew exactly what was going to be on the exams and if you put in the work, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tyler is a great professor for example, when nearly the entire class got 50% on the first quiz he dedicated a whole lecture to how he could improve. He added a review session the night before any exam/test, and answers to his testable question bank. Overall, as long as you go over the testable questions twice and know what you're talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tyler is an approachable guy who always wants to help. He can be a very boring lecturer but is very good at teaching and explaining finance concepts from multiple angles. The class is all about understanding conceptual problems through examples on Top Hat, and knowing how to do problem set, math questions. If you can do both of these, you'll be set
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most boring classes I've ever taken and I love finance. There is no soul in his lectures at all, basically just collecting a paycheck forcing students to watch 5-year-old lectures in an extremely monotone unpassionate way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tough class, the tests are difficult but he gives you a question bank at the start of the semester with questions that will be on the test. As long as you study you'll be fine. Decent curve at the end of the semester, went from a D+ to a C+. Class is overall very test heavy.

The professor is fine and helpful if you have any questions. We had weekly lectures and then homework's. The exams had content we practiced, so as long as you study and know what is going on, the class is fine.

Professor Jensen is a good professor I just never liked how the class is structured. For my finance class, a weekly assignment would be worth 20 points and the larger ones were worth 200. However, the exams are worth much more for example the final was worth around 600 points. He's a good prof but he's very no-nonsense and is test-heavy.

Professor Jensen is a solid choice for this class. He understands the material and is very willing to help students outside of class. He helped simplify the concepts, although I would definitely consider his voice hard to listen to in class (may have fallen asleep). Also, without going to class and paying attention, good luck passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Jensen was a solid choice for 301. This is the only class he teaches, so he knows the material well. He is also nice and willings to explain or do examples. You have all the problems for the exams beforehand, but a lot of them are very difficult and require a lot of help from an outside resource. It is easy to slack off in class, so don't!

FIN301 with Jensen is definitely not as easy and smooth as I imagined it would be at the start of the semester. This is a very difficult class. Daily classes are just lectures where he will read off slides and occasionally give an example if asked. Quizzes and Exams were VERY difficult. Required a lot of out of class time studying and preparing.

Jensen is a nice guy but his whole class is mainly based on Tests/Quizzes. He doesn't use a microphone in lecture and writes on the whiteboard, so if you sit in the back you will have a tough time. The grading scale isn't very forgiving so I'd recommend the Help Labs as there are very little tutors available

Professor Jensen is one of the few professors in the COB who is a truly good lecturer. He does an excellent job of simplifying the concepts and teaching them. The quizzes and exams are not easy, but if you pay attention in class and do the practice problems you will have no issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jensen is a fine professor and teaches well, but his exams are nitpicky and grade on minor details, so even if you've mastered a topic it's still easy to miss problems by misinterpretation and wording. Easy B, very difficult A.

Explained the concept very clear and easy to understand. If you need extra examples he have office hours or you can email him to stop by he's a very nice guy. People who do bad in this course pay attention to their phone more than the class lecture I've noticed. He have help lab that are very helpful. The student in help lab is very nice !

He have help lab which students in that help room are very friendly and helpful. If you want an A in the class I would do the packet he give you right from the beginning and go to help room and his office hours for help. Those that fail or get a bad grade is not because he's bad, is b/c they didn't use the resources that was provided.

Fantastic teacher. All quiz questions come from lecture (don't buy the book) or from the problem set that you are given the first week. His grading is clear, and he is very fair. When I visited him outside of class for questions, he was extremely helpful. Honestly, he's my favorite professor I've had at ISU so far
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you're looking for a great FIN 301 experience, Tyler Jensen is the professor for you! He gives every possible question that will be on the quizzes, so there is no way you should be surprised on what shows up. His conceptual questions can be a bit tough, but the answers are in the slides. 2 of the quizzes are take-home, but they're a bit tougher.

Jensen simplifies finance and engages the class. He's a cool guy that has a passion for his discipline, while also caring for students. All of the math problems come from a problem set given at the beginning of the semester. I found the material easy, even though all of your grade is tests/quizzes. I would definitely take with Jensen if possible.

He really cares about his students, to the point where he took time out of his lectures to memorize every single name by the second week, then use them throughout the semester. Really smart guy and very respected

I really love his class. He explains very clearly. His test are the same as the problem sets that he gives out in class so make sure you do it. The class was a bit hard but had extra credits which was really helpful. If you REALLY wanna learn Finance, then you should take this class with him. or if you just want an easy A, find another one.
Tyler cares about his students. You aren't going to find an easy Finance 301 class at ISU, but he is by far the best professor for the course and is extremely helpful compared to the rest

Prof. Jensen was great! He takes a lot of time to explain things and answer questions if you have them. Go to his office for help with the problem sets, he will explain everything and is super helpful. Has  few opportunities for extra credit and the quizzes he gives are not bad if you go to class. Highly recommend him. DONT GET THE BOOK, never used

He is a very helpful professor, and also one of my favorite professors. He likes to put hashtags in the beginning of lectures and it makes everyone laugh. The material is not necessarily difficult, but he makes it seem like a piece of cake. NO assignments, only 5 quizzes, a midterm and final. He has a curve, but if you go to class, you will do fine
this teacher is horrible. she cannot teach a single lesson correctly and the tests have nothing to do with the "material" which we teach on our own. never take her class if you want to pass.

She was a terrible teacher! Lectures were heavy on content and doesn't know how to do one thing, "TEACH!" I had her years ago in 2015, I rather go to military school than to sit in one of her lectures. Exams were not easy and that was a huge percentage of our grade. I wonder if she still teaches, but if she does... then god bless you soul good luck
I really liked her and she really knew her information

I was originally excited to take this class; however, my excitement soon stopped. Both the online lectures and the labs were unorganized and a waste of time. Lab at 8am was awful especially when it would only last 10-15 minutes and never got you in shape. Both the instructor and TA's were unorganized and unhelpful. Tests were unnecessarily hard.

You go to two labs per week and the lecture works is all online. Her online lectures are poorly scraped together and and extremely boring. She makes the assignments way harder than they need to be and offers no help. Tests are difficult and you're never sure what will be on them. Unfortunately this class is required for all Kin majors.

terrible at lecturing. all she does is make power points word for word from the textbook and just read it to us. then her tests were nothing at all like what we learned in class no matter how much I studied I never did well on tests.
She is very unclear about what will be on tests. Also, she makes material that should be relatively easy to comprehend confusing. She makes the class harder than it needs to be.

Professor Jones is real easy going. She is funny, polite, and really attempts to get her students engaged. I do think the tests are bit hard considering there are no hints of what will be on the exam. However, she is always willing to help if you look for it.

Her lectures have nothing on the test. You have to go to class because she takes attendance. I honestly think she shouldn't be teaching this at a university. She misspells things on the slides and test. Find the PDF form of the book online. Also do not take the lab with her!! Take lab with a TA.
Talks for the entire class about textbook material and none of it is useful for her tests...

As a disclaimer, Tyanez had never taught this course before and she was thrown in it in a rather confusing way. However, with that being said as a prof. at a university I would expect her to be able to teach this course  little better than she did. She tried. It was just unfortunate for the students because she was as confused as we were
She makes this class so much harder than it needs to be. She dosent seem to know what shes taking about.

This teacher is awful. She teaches the second half of H S 350 and she makes it way more difficult than it needs to be. She doesn't ever clarify anything. She doesn't even seem like she knows what she is talking about in class, she is constantly looking at her notes. She ruined human diseases for me after she took over.
Pretty difficult to understand what she expects. Was really confused on a lot of things. Tests were pretty easy, just ask her to clarify things a lot.

Simply put, she is awful. There is no direction to the class and her tests are completely unfair. I was looking forward to this class and her lack of care and utter ignorance to fostering learning in the class ruined the experience for me. If every Kinesiology major is required to take this, it should be worthwhile. No direction to the class.

Her test a pretty hard just because some of the questions seem like trick questions. She gives you and opportunity to do extra credit which helps your grade. I wouldn't panic if you don't do well on the test because the lab will probably raise you a whole letter grade. Just attend class for clicker points and lab for participation points
Took an honors seminar with him! Such a nice guy and so engaging. Loved when he would tell stories or talk about his research
Pretty easy class and intersting
Great professor. He's always willing to help you or work with you if you have conflicts. His tests aren't hard if you study his notes.
No Comments
figures grades 3 different ways and gives you the best one so even if you test badly or mess up the quizzes, you can still do really well
Easy to get answers, tests not overly hard.  Funny, and super excited about his nutrition.  Makes the material sorta interesting.

Tyler Morgan inspired me to major in Supply Chain Management. He is, by far, one of my favorite professors at Iowa State University. His lectures are filled with important supply chain processes and information that a Supply Chain major will use in their career and even for those just entering a manufacturing industry.
Morgan is a really good professor but the class itself is pretty difficult in my opinion. Practice, practice, practice. Do well on the 3 homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Morgan is a pretty solid teacher. He has plenty of teaching and industry experience and gives very good, real life examples. He explains things well and gives plenty of opportunities to practice what he teaches. Very responsive to what his students desire to get out of his class. Gives very good study guides so you know exactly what is on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: He is very intelligent when it comes to supply chain. His lectures are interesting because he relates the subject to real world problems. The tests can be difficult due to the amount of information needed to memorize. Take your time on the homework because they are only 3 of them each 10% of the class. You also must go to class he will give quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This instructor does a great job of covering the material and is very willing to explain things a different way, many times, until you understand. He is very helpful and caring. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I had a good time in his class, test are somewhat difficult but homework isn't.  As long as you stay focused in class and go in when you need help you'll be alright.  Also read over your notes because there are quizzes

Great teacher. Very helpful, wants his students to succeed. His homework and tests aren't the easiest but not the most difficult. Go to class, go in for help, he's more than willing to work with you. Enjoyed his lectures, he keeps it interesting and explains the material VERY well and clearly. Wish he taught more supply chain classes!
For a new professor he did a good job teaching this class. There is a ton if info so be in class

Dr. B gets a bad rep, but she is a generally very nice and funny professor that just does not communicate her expectations to students. My biggest issue with this class was the fact that she would always tell us she wanted a paper done one way in class, and then she would totally switch up her grading criteria after we submitted.

This class and professor are easily both my worst class/professor experiences since coming to Iowa State. So many unclear expectations, yet she grades you to the highest-utmost-unrealistic standards. There is also just SO much unnecessary work - please don't take this course with this professor if you don't have to!

AWFUL!! We had an awful group project where you did all the work if one of your teammates didn't work. She is super unclear. Always states to look in the book, yet she contradicts it. She is not flexible, can be verbally insulting, and is quick to anger. Honestly, the only good parts were when it was one on one with her. Just don't take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tyrrell was easily one of the most difficult professors I have come across at Iowa State. She practically stated at the beginning of the course that the "rubric was the bare minimum" and would proceed to place her unrealistic expectations on all of the assignments. I would suggest looking for a new professor if you can.

This is easily the worst professor I have had at Iowa State. She puts up the wrong assignments and will frequently give vague instructions. She will then blame everyone but herself by saying, "I don't understand how this could have been misunderstood." I wouldn't even trust her to teach kindergarten

She made English a nightmare. I can't stress enough how she wore me down as the semester progressed. She's not consistent. she favors students she likes. Extremely narrow-minded but likes to act like she isn't. Extremely stressful to deal with how she grades because she marks you down for taking her advice. She never gives useful feedback.

Not accommodating. Talked to her outside of class; she would clarify my questions but she would grade me down for taking her own advice. she discusses "examples" in class that are NOT A-papers so you won't know what she wants anyway. No one in the class knew what she expected.
Ask too many questions and she will dislike you.

reviews.comment: whoever's reading this i think a bitter student must have decided to review bomb this rmp page. dr. tyrrell expected students to come to class and do the work correctly. if you did you were fine. i actually felt like she pushed me to do better and i actually learned something

Just awful, she is the worst teacher I have ever had. The toughest grader and is very snippy to students when she's asked questions so just don't even bother asking. Terrible at emails, this class was very detrimental to my mental health and I should've dropped it. I truly hate english now and sincerely hope that the university shows her the door.

reviews.comment: She is the hardest grader I have had in any course and it amazed me and my classmates how hard she graded. If you asked a question during class she would not really answer it how you wanted. On the other hand, outside of class she is one of the nicest professors ever. I would not recommend taking her class unless you want a lot of homework to do.

she is terrible and i hope she gets cut from this program. she complains about having 4 class and cant keep track of them... BRENDA WE HAVE 5 OR MORE. she is incompetent and a terrible grader. drop her class do not take english with her because you will suffer. she has made my mental health terrible and i have cried multiple times because of her

drop this teacher at all costs! She is terrible she docked me points for having covid because i couldn't be in class for an in class assignment. She will tell you something sounds good tell you how to fix it so you use what she said word for word and then she grades your assignment and says that it is wrong and that you did the whole paper wrong...
There are huge budget cuts coming to LAS. I hope the English department doesn't get rid of good professors and keep her around.
I truly hope this woman is exploited for her behavior.

Rude. She is rude and has a tone issue. Makes students feel stupid when asking questions, and often complains about having to grade the VERY complex assignments. WELL GUESS WHAT BRENDA? WE. ARE. PAYING. YOU. This woman has some serious power complexes, and thinks that my class is simply disrespectful so we deserve all of her negativity. Expose her.

Took the class far too seriously. Was incredibly nitpicky on papers, far more than the other instructors friends had this semester. Spent a lot of class complaining about (lack of) attendance to those of us who were still coming in. Don't make the entire class involve online work and activities if you want us to see any use to coming in person.

This woman is a straight heathen, I cannot believe she got hired at a university the way she teaches. She is an extremely harsh grader and so passive aggressive. She is rude, mean, pretentious, and so much worse. If you get her, transfer out IMMEDIATELY.

reviews.comment: If you find yourself enrolled in ENGL 250 with this woman, change out of it as soon as possible. She expects you to treat her class like it's your only class. reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had by far. Extremely tough grader, she will do anything to give you the lowest score possible. Even if you have an extenuating circumstance, she still gets mad at you for not being in class.

Professor Tyrell had an insane amount of papers and assignments due with minimal time to work on them and no respect for the fact that her students had other classes as well. reviews.comment: Someone seems to be trolling her RMP page. I had this professor this semester. She was certainly tough, but the rubrics make it clear how you could do better. She has a very chill and carefree attitude in class, which makes her more approachable than some of my others profs.

reviews.comment: in the nicest way possible, she really shouldn't have a teaching license

if you get this teacher drop! if you miss one day you will get a zero on an assignment even if you gave her a heads up or had an emergency. her notes on your papers will make no sense and she gets upset if you ask to many questions. says she is so busy because she has 5 classes and gets confused but doesn't care that we take that many classes too!

reviews.comment: Brenda treats this class like it's worth 12 credits. I regularly spend 8-10 hours per week on this class, when I spend 5 on my other credits. She overloads the students then acts like she's a saint for giving us an extra 2 days to work on it. Absolutely do not take, I hope no other student has to go through this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you get Dr. Tyrell, for your own sake drop the class or change teachers. I have never had a professor who was worse at explaining assignment criteria. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I thought I hated AP Lang, but Dr. B takes my hatred to another level. I am frequently frustrated with her grading and comments on papers. Her expectation for our writing is outrageous as we are not English majors who know how to write perfectly. When students ask simple questions, she gets snippy if she thinks the answers are blatantly obvious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is the worst English class I have ever taken. I would rate her a 0 but that is not an option. She frequently snaps at students when asking simple questions about coursework. The prompts for essays are very lengthy and so specific it is hard to understand what she wants. She grades very slowly and feedback on papers is pretty bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She assigns homework for almost every night and will not give you the points for them so you will never know your actual grade. Her rubrics for projects say that if you do everything she tells you..... you will get a C. She has gone on many rants about why English should have the lowest averages for classes instead of STEM because English is harder

She says that if you fulfill all of the requirements for a paper you will get a C. Her instructions are unclear and must be explained several times. Then when you do ask a question she either rephrases the question and asks it back to you or laughs and says she already answered it. The average score for papers is 20 points lower than other classes.

She is always too busy to help out students, and if you do meet with her, she will tell you to fix certain things and still give you a D. Along with being condescending about your intelligence throughout the paper by making false claims of plagiarism. If you get this professor, immediately get out of the class.

She grades incredibly harshly. The first day of class she explained that we would only pass the class with an A if we went above and beyond. On papers, she takes forever to grade and when you are finally passing the class, she gives you a terrible grade on paper that was supposed to be graded a month ago, and your grade drops 2 letter grades.

Rude and condescending in class. Feedback on drafts is unhelpful and often only viewable after the final has already been submitted. Refuses to take any student feedback, devotes a sizable chunk of class time complaining (to people who showed up) about attendance issues. Expectations are unclear and change day to day. Take this with anyone else.

if you told me she was not actually a professor rather than a random person who showed up and spewed nonsense i wouldnt be surprised, most assignments take months to grade and lectures are almost detrimental to the material

Do NOT take this class with her. Literally the worst professor I have ever had. I think of myself as an A student and I have never struggled so hard to get a B.  Highest grade for the positive-informative assignment was 100/125. That is a B-. Lectures are boring so try to take it online, but in-class might be helpful for the group work.

the average grade for each essay was 35 points lower (out of 150) than the other professor in English 250. Awful Grader grades months after you submit and does not give you feedback on your drafts. She claims she is too busy to give feedback on our drafts yet she is one of the toughest grading this useless class. Don't take with her at all costs.

AWFUL! She never gives you the same instructions twice. she gets mad if you ask a question about the work and say she told you already when she hasn't. Do not bother asking questions after class she will not give you an answer and will say to email her instead. I did not know how to do a paper and she was no help at all. Transfer out of her class!!
