reviews.comment: The class of ENGL 250 is kind of a boring class, but Dr. Tyrrell made it less miserable than it would normally be. She would often have "mental health days" where she would cancel class and just have us turn in the assignment for that day which was always very nice. Also had a good amount of extra credit for redoing stuff or doing fun stuff outside

She definitely knows her stuff when it comes to English, but teaching is not her strong suit. With every essay she explains the requirements differently about 3 times per paper. The differences are so extreme that I have to go back and change what I have already written.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's just an okay teacher. She was more preoccupied with her own work to help with ours. Did not give feedback to help improve writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory, you can only miss a few days until it impacts your grade. She gives out a few pop quizzes to make sure you are reading. The assignments aren't bad and is also a pretty easy grader, pay attention in class and use examples she provides in your essay and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: All assignments are almost 2 times longer than any other english professor I've heard of.  Other professors give out 500-700 word papers, this one gives 4 or 5 pagers.  Extra credit options are available but the amount of work is much more than any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Cheri is simply amazing. She pushes you and makes you work for it but it is well worth it. You will leave the class with great portfolio pieces.

Prepare to work for your grade. I had Cheri for Art 108, Art 109, and multiple Art GR courses including Rome. Cheri doesn't take off the cuff critiques. She is critical and tough because she wants YOU to EXCEL in the real world. Graphic design is a tough, fast-paced profession. Take it from me... 12 years since graduation. No handouts.

She gives great advice when you ask. She is easy to understand if you ask the right questions. At times it can be hard to please her with any designs, but that happens with all design classes. She emails back almost immediately when you have questions with you're design. I wish I had her for other classes!

Cheri Ure is a wonderful professor, I don't know why so many people gave bad reviews. I love her and I try to get in her sections as often as possible. She is nice to students, and gives beneficial & constructive criticism. She almost always responds to questions (including email) quickly. Amazing professor!

Probably the most misunderstood and one of the most passionate instructors in the program. She will let you do what you want and be "creative" if you show you're capable of being a quality designer. She never approaches me in class unless I first ask, and we'll have an amazing conceptual conversation. Because she trusts me, even though we disagree.
Cheri is a great teacher. She may be confusing to understand at first but she has a lot of great feedback and experience to share.
She's a nice lady, however she will tear your work apart and no matter how excited you were about it walking into class, she will make you want to crawl in a hole by the end of class.

Cheri is the best. She is honest, funny and knows what she's talking about. She always tries to push your ideas to be conceptually and visually stronger. The other students obviously don't know what they're talking about. In 270, everyone sucks. I would be frustrated teaching new designers too.

Everyone else on this site has given Cheri bad reviews, but I loved having her as an instructor.  Sometimes her ideas to "help" with a student's project are unclear and hard to visualize when she describes them, but she does genuinely care and can give you some very helpful advice if you're open minded.

I'm so relieved to find that I wasn't the only person who found Cheri to be unbelievably hard to work with. Praise one day, and then you get blasted to pieces the next. Some of the other comments:"living through her students" and "belittling other classmates" are scarily accurate. These reviews are dead on summaries of my experience.

I'm pretty confident with my abilities but, for the entirety of the class cheri did nothing but laugh when i referred to having a style, belittled my classmates and i, and make vague remarks that were supposed to be translated into substance. she is a sad, negative, pathetic, old lady with a closed mind to new ideas and creativity. im being nice

Impossible to understand..it seems the only way she can teach is to just say what you did wrong rather than what would improve your work, so unfortunately a lot of us ended up having to redo  projects...She made me revise a grid FIVE TIMES because she never explained to me what exactly she wanted out of it--extremely frustrating..wouldnt recommend

Having Cheri in Rome was the worst experience I've had.. not only did she make me uncomfortable, but at one point she told me she, "wanted to live through me" by doing my project for me... which shortly after she told me step by step what I should do to get the grade.. WRONG. Don't do it.. she took away my confidence and creative freedom.
unfortunately the woman talks in riddles. You think she is trying to help, and then realize none of it makes any sense. She is nice, but I didn't get much out our discussions of my work.
worst teacher I ever had
Agree with the previous post.  She has a lot of theory involved with her teaching, but not much practicality.  She can push you in the right direction, but not me!
No Comments
Unsympathetic teacher who expects you to spend tons of money on her projects and then gives you a hard time when you cant afford it.

Very knowledgable on all of the subjects covered in the course. Very accommodative and aware of student's understanding of the topics. Made himself available often and was very good at providing resources and office hours to make sure students understood the topics.

Being one of his first classes he's ever taught, you have to understand hes not a perfect teacher yet. Do all the the homework to the best ability, study hard for  the exams, and always go in for help. He is a very nice guy but kind of shy so you have to approach him first. Once you know him he is there to help and will always do anything to help.

He is very confusing and his lectures are long and boring. He also gave us homework that did our TA (a senior in Chemical Engineering) did not know how to do. He is understanding and willing to push back homework to give us more time and he is great one to one with students, but he confusing during lectures and goes to fast on new topics.

Uz is very nice and very intelligent, but he is not the best teacher. Often he drones on and offers no opportunities for class participation, which personally helps me learn and keeps me engaged. His tests often have material that isn't covered in class or in homework. However, he is very helpful and patient 1 on 1.  Overall I would not recommend.
Doesn't grade fairly, good at 1 on 1 teaching but not good at all in classroom. Be expected to know more than what he will put on study guide for exams.

Uz is new and the first few weeks were really rocky. Nobody had any clue what was going on in the class. Luckily Uz knew that  and was understanding. He pushed back due dates and helped on quizzes if he felt he did a poor job preparing people, which was often the case, especially at the beginning of the semester. Great 1 on 1 .
The two hour lectures get REALLY long. He is great at explaining things one-on-one but nothing makes sense when he tries to explain it to the whole class.
Dr. VanLoocke is very engaging, lectures very well, supports students, and is easy to find and get a hold of. He really knows what he is talking about.

Easiest class I've ever taken. Some topics were interesting, although this class might as well be called "Climate Change 101." Dr. VanLoocke is nice, and a decent lecturer. I was just super bored in class all the time because it was super surface level and straightforward content.

As others have said, he's super nice, funny, and overall does his best to help students. He has some extra credit. HOWEVER he's pretty disorganized in both the in-person lecture and the online organization of the student portal. He has lots of office hours so that's great!

Dr. Vanloocke was very enthusiastic about his class and took time to ensure that students actually understood the material. He was very friendly and open, always willing to re-explain or elaborate on material. I also found that Dr. Vanloocke's lectures were also pretty entertaining. By studying, reviewing, and clarifying hard topics, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I honestly did not go to this class much but when I did I really enjoyed him. He definitely knows what he's talking about and very helpful answering questions.

Dr. V is passionate in what he teaches and has some really great dad humor. Towards the end of the year his notes are mainly graphs/pictures so its important to show up in order to understand what the notes mean. Class is interesting as a whole but a little scattered in material. Gives plenty of extra credit. Enjoyed the class overall!!

Can't say enough about this guy. Best professor I've encountered at Iowa State. He cares about the topics, his students, and his ability to teach effectively. Very easy to do well in class if you just ask him questions when you're confused and put in a little effort on the assignments. This class is the reason I'm an Agronomy major.

Dr. V is one of the best professors I've encountered at Iowa State. He genuinely cares and works hard to teach well. If you go to his office hours he will be super helpful and answer lots of questions. Lots of people have said his class was hard but if you show up and pay attention in class he makes it extremely easy. Just put in a little effort.

really friendly person but talks a little bit fast during lecture, so I would recommend printing out the lecture notes if you can (he posts them online for you to use). Gives weekly 20 question homework assignments; they aren't that bad if you work with a group. His lectures are a little dull and sometimes it's confusing how everything connects.
Excellent professor for a great class. Too bad he does not teach more courses.

Brett is a phenomenal instructor. I received a B- in 331, and this was because of a lack of interest in the subject. Brett completely changed my attitude about this subject with his easy, 5-10-minute flipped lectures. Spending the entire lecture doing a worksheet in groups is spectacular. I wish that all of my classes did this.
him and Mason Koretiz are the best profs in the chem department in my opinion

Lectures are actually group work, the content is taught via prerecorded videos you're expected to watch before class. Puts in good energy and effort to lectures so they aren't boring (as can easily be the case with O Chem). Exams make up the majority of your grade, so beware!
Dr. VanVeller is a really amazing teacher who truly cares about the students. He is always quick to reply to email and really makes the learning easy if you put in the time.

VanVeller's lectures are really interesting, and he uses cute examples and stories to make the concepts memorable. Before every test, he has a review day, which helps a lot. The class is graded mostly on tests, so it's a good idea to make sure you do well on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. VanVeller is an okay lecturer but teaches with the assumption that you have already read the section or chapter. I strongly recommend going to office hours as he is very approachable and office hours are in a group setting. His tests are lenient and practice makes perfect.

I was nervous going into this class as organic chemistry is a difficult subject. However, VanVeller made Ochem very enjoyable and he is a super funny guy! This was his first semester teaching, but he was a better professor than some that have taught for years. His exams are hard, but i felt like I learned a lot from this class. Great professor!

I gave a 3 on helpfulness, but I never asked for help so I don't know. One time he did adjust my exam grade after arguing for points.  Brett is a funny guy who makes class fun to go to. Pretty clear on what to expect on exams. However, he sometimes abbreviates or skips parts of mechanisms which can leave you confused or guessing. Overall, Good guy.

There are so many guest speakers that Laura does nothing in the class besides telling you what you will do during work time. Be aware that Laura's boyfriend will attend the online class lecture and help Laura grade your final. This class is very disorganized. When we asked for an outline for the final, we received it three days before we presented.

Laura does not demonstrate teaching practices that our other professors teach us. Everything she does- giving you feedback or creating an assignment- is from ChatGPT or MagicSchoolAI. We are given the final portfolio with 1 week left and 18 long assignments without direction. And your entire grade depends on the final project. Avoid at all costs!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was extremely disorganized, and Laura's communication was poor throughout the semester. Expectations were unclear, and it was difficult to get proper feedback or understand what was expected of us. The lack of structure made it hard to succeed in the course. She gives terrible feedback and is super harsh on grading students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Laura during class is awful. She is very sporadic and disorganized. She will assign something then forget she assigned it the next class period. She is horrible with grading  you're all smart, etc., then tear you to shreds with feedback. However, outside of class she is extremely helpful. She was so great and helpful and then in class I'm scared.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I know many negative reviews here, and I had an extremely difficult semester. I was turning things in months late, but the whole time, I met with Laura and talked to her about what I was going through and what I needed to do to catch up. She is so kind and understanding, and she works so hard to support her students. If you need help, just ask her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Laura is late to many of our practicums. She can never finish a thought/instruction before assigning work. She will take your personal computer out of your hands and has deleted tabs. The lesson plans you have to make are extensive. Every other professor has said it's too much and when we give the plans to future admin they will be overwhelmed.

This class is taught for 3 hours on Zoom every week and the first hour or two is a guest speaker. Laura does not provide clear instructions or tell us what we are supposed to do for assignments. The final project is done with groups and is unclear. The ProStart competition is mandatory and forces you to skip your classes that day. Worst professor.

Laura is truly awful. She tells us that we don't have to reinvent the wheel regarding lesson plans, but then says our lesson plans aren't good enough because they've been done before. She has zero organizational skills and cannot remember what she is trying to teach. Good luck if you have to miss class or leave early, she will use it against you.

Be aware she is the worst professor I have had. FCS students are stuck with her all 4 years. She does not grade anything, she doesn't answer emails; she will go into your student account to get your phone number to text over a weekend about something. Her assignments never relate to the course material and are time-consuming with no instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a very hard grader, but also horrible at communication. Very disorganized so the bad grade comes from her teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. As long as you attend class regularly and participate it is a fun/interesting class, and easy to get a good grade in.

Best professor I have had, she actually cares about you. She genuinely wants you to do well and succeed. She is very understanding and flexible with deadlines which is really nice for times your stressed and overwhelmed. If you have a positive mindset truly want to have a career in FCS you will love Laura and her class.

By far the worse teacher I have had the pleasure to experience. Has no organizational skills and doesn't have a clue how to run a class as assignments that were originally brought up are dropped and new ones randomly show up. Cancels classes at a moments notice multiple times. She is single handedly destroying the FCS department at ISU.

I love Laura but this semester was tough. We had an emergency TA come in because our assignments weren't being graded. There was a loss of communication. A majority of us were confused I love how passionate Laura is about spreading the word about FCS but I think she needs to focus more on her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 206 had *lots* of readings. If you don't get behind on those and fill out the reflections she has you do, it'll be a pretty straight forward class until the awful final project. There was no guidance on it. We had to get an emergency TA because of the disorganization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Laura is honestly such a genuine person, but as a professor she is really not great. Almost every class consisted of a random guest speaker that never really had that much to do with FCS. I don't think I actually learned a single thing in this class, and I hope there is more structure added in the future.

Laura is very caring and personable but should NOT be a professor. I have not learned anything in this class and never know what to expect when I walk in the door. Half the time, the class has a guest speaker or something thrown together the day of. There is no structure in this class, good luck.
Most of the time the assignments in class seem last minute or unplanned. The final was thrown together and last minute and she doesn't respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Laura is a fun and personable professor, but her turnaround time on grading assignments is absurd. Lots of guest speakers and you submit notes for points, so attendance is mandatory. Lots of 10 point assignments and 3 50+ point assignments that can majorly impact your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is an amazing person and professor! She does group projects and brings in many wonderful guest speakers! She cares about you and wants you to do your best! Textbook is used sometimes but you need to buy it.
Showed up late to multiple classes. Tons of mistakes in slides. Worst professor I've had

Namrata Vaswani is one of ISU's worst professors and I don't say that lightly. She yells at students. The grading scheme was completely broken with 80% of the grade based on 4 exams. Tests are exponentially more difficult than homework. She basically incited a revolution with her tyrannical teaching methods this semester. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is an okay professor who is clearly very intelligent struggles to teach. Has a really thick accent which makes it extremely difficult to follow along in lectures. She went over quite a few examples in class which was helpful. Overall, grading was fairly lenient, but you should expect to put in a lot of effort to understand everything.

Professor Vaswani rarely finished a problem in class. On more than one occasion students found mistakes with her work so instead of correcting herself she changes the problem or moves onto something else. She does not explain material and is vague in the explanation that she does give.
She is a good grader. Her quizzes are not too hard, she usually explains the quiz before she gives it to you. Her homework is also not so bad.

She is very difficult to understand, but grades rather kindly. First test was absurdly easy, second was about normal difficulty. She's very accommodating if you have questions or conflicts (I rescheduled a test twice). Not a great teacher, notes not entirely useful, but goes over useful examples in class, if you manage to stay awake.

Does not have a clue as to how to teach. Basically just reads from lecture slides. Mumbles a lot. Very thick foreign accent is difficult to understand. Nervous movements during lectures are extremely annoying. The textbook was absolutely horrible. If she ends up being your instructor, drop the course.
Did not teach much.  All content was learned off wikipedia.

She was and is terrible.  If you have her don't expect to do well or learn anything from lecture.  If you have never had probobility you should wait until the spring that guy is better.  Never yet learned a single thing in lecture.

I had her as a TA for lab in EE 224.  All I can say is, 'Would you like to show up?'  She would come hours late to lab.  Don't ask her for help in lab, she'll just utter something in arabic.  I don't think she grades the lab reports either.  You are better off to do the labs on your own time.  She likes the lab room as hot as possible too.

LOTS OF MATH IN AGRON 180!!!! The equations were crazy complicated but were provided on quizzes/tests. VanLooke is a nice guy though and a pretty good lecturer. The TA's were really helpful if you had questions about the quizzes. The HW was manageable: one quiz per week open note. Very application based class, but it was interesting.

LOTS OF MATH IN THIS CLASS!!! The equations are really overwhelming for an agronomy course. Tophats in every class. Dr. VanLooke is very nice though and the TA's were really helpful if you had questions. HW was manageable it was a quiz every week and you can use your notes. Overall, pretty interesting course!

I would not suggest this course to anyone. He is truly one of the worst professors that I have had at Iowa State. The course is nothing like the syllabus. Be prepared to learn nothing about "Global Agriculture" and be ready for him to shove his climate change agenda down your throat. Make sure you bring a calculator, there is plenty of math.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very enjoyable and it shows he is passionate about what he does. He moves a bit fast but if you ask him to slow down a bit he will and also wants to make sure his students are understanding the material. The exams are very heavy but there are study guides and they are open note.
Dr. VanLooke is a great teacher. He truly loves what he does and it shows. He is always trying to make class fun and exciting.
The exams are very stressful and huge in size. Make sure to study a lot, otherwise a good class overall.

Get ready to cry! The worst prof. He does not care nor listen. No assignment rubric or sheet to explain what he is looking for but, will be incredibly difficult when it comes to grading. He can't even use Blackboard to properly get feedback out to you, but that's your problem! Not all assignments are in the syllabus and they take HOURS. total BS!

If you are not in lecture, you will not be able to fill in the blanks on the lecture slides. With that being said, Dr. V does a great job at highlighting the important information on the slides so that you have a very good idea of what to study. He is very helpful and very passionate about exercise physiology! 10/10 would take again.

Dr. Valentine is great. He's funny when he shows his true personality. His class is very lecture heavy, but I always thought they were interesting. His tests are tough, but not ridiculously tough. I enjoyed his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terrible Instructor. Rudy at time forgets deadlines for assignments, as well as he goes fast in his lectures. He doesn't explain the material as well to help you understand the overall concept. The note slides are filled with tons of information of which became hard to understand. His exams are also written much harder than what they need to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Valentine. He's honest, funny, and straight forward. He doesn't make it harder than it has to be, and tries to be relatable. I'm taking another class with him because I took this class first.

This was the best required class out of the 3 El Ed has to take. Class was fun most of the time, you have to participate and you play a music-related game every class. Homework is easy, if you miss a few points she lets you resubmit for full credit. You're allowed 4 free absences unless it's a performance day. Overall she's a really sweet professor

I loved Dr. VerSteegt! She was incredible at what she does and I would 100% recommended her class. She actively worked hard to get to know her students and I could tell she genuinely cared. You don't have to have any musical talent to do well in her class.
This was my favorite class at ISU! Easiest class there is. The professor was super fun and entertaining. Participation greatly matters! The assignments are few and not hard at all.

I LOVE HER!!! She talks to us like her students to help us and I don't think that's a bad thing at all. Sometimes you want to feel like a little kid again, anyway. While this is a required class to El Ed majors, she made the class fun and engaging. I don't understand how she gets bad scoring; she is an amazing person and teacher.

Speaks to class like we are in elementary school, which isn't horrible. It's just annoying because I would like to be treated like an adult. Ukes are kinda embarrassing to carry to class lol but it was fun to learn how to play. Easy grader too.

Super fun and nice professor. The class may seem a little silly, but it's fun and easy. She is very considerate and understanding. She does a great job of always providing ways to incorporate music to the gen ed classroom. Overall, great professor and class!

She talks to students like they are her elementary music kids and you do a lot of similar activities to what you would do in an elementary school music class. She teaches you a few songs on the ukulele throughout the class.

Dr. VerSteegt is an amazing professor. She gives great feedback on assignments and tells you how to fix them to become better educators. She is entertaining and passionate and that helps, especially if you have the later section. Advice- participate 100% in the activities, they are fun.
Super helpful. I hate music but I loved this class because of her.
She gave us 5 days we didn't have to go to class. She was kind, reasonable, and I actually learned so much from her. I would definetly take a class with her again.
I loved her! She made me want to show up to a night class. I recommend her to anyone who is taking this class!

Mrs. VerSteegt is PHENOMINAL! I took Music for Elementary Teachers with her and every class was tons of fun. It is an easy class as long as you show up and participate. Prepare for learning how to play the recorder, sing and dance. She is an easy grader- if you try and do your best, you'll do just fine.

I thought I would hate this class but I LOVED it! Kris is so uplifting and positive that she made me want to go to class just to hear her sing. She truly cares about each of her students. I couldn't speak more highly of her.

Took his thermodynamics 1 class at MSOE. Nice guy but hours of homework each week. Makes the material in class straightforward but the homework's are way harder than in class examples. If you want to get perfect scores on homework each week that can easily take over 5 hours. Tests easier than homework but by no means easy.

He's a good teacher but his homeworks are crazy long. He acts nice and acts like he cares about you, but then ruins you GPA and it seems like he enjoys it. Makes the class 10 times harder than it has to be and doesn't care about whether or not you pass.

Had to spend nearly 10 hours a week on HW alone inspite of working in a group of 5 students. Exams were extremely challenging and long , mot students struggled to finish exam on time(including me). In the end all the hard work paid off with an A grade. If you work hard in his class, you will be rewarded, but his class is a time gobbler!
Extremely hard course with a minimum of 12 hours per week on homework. Professor acts nice but kills your grade for fun.

This is by far the best class I have taken in order to prepare to become a teacher. There aren't many things that get graded, for the things that do, she makes sure to explain exactly how to get full points and will allow you to resubmit until you get that. Come to class, enjoy, and get an amazing grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kristina is super nice. The class is really easy. You get up to 4 misses, before it drops your grade. You never have to preform by yourself musically. You have very few assignments. You do almost all assignments in class. You can show up to another class time if you can't make it to your own that day.

As an EL ED major I had to take her music class for my degree even though I have zero plans to ever teach music, and I enjoyed it thoroughly. She is very inspirational and there was never a class/lecture that I wasn't fully engaged in what we were doing. You do not have to be a musical mastermind to pass the class with an A. Effort is what matters!

Kristina is an AMAZING professor. She understands that not everyone wants to be a music teacher, so she has a lot of assignments where you can incorporate music into the general education classroom, and backs it up with evidence of why we should do so. She is funny, sweet, and I've never not enjoyed one of her classes, even if I was unmotivated.

Dr. VanVeller is the very best professor I have ever had, the material is difficult but he does everything to make it less daunting he explains things in depth and clearly while also being entertaining. He expects us to work hard but also makes ochem fun
Dr Van veller is a great professor. The class might seem hard at the beginning but towards the latter half, it becomes easy. He is the best organic chemistry professor at Iowa State.

Van Veller is a great teacher and an even better person. He is very enthusiastic and funny, which makes class actually worthwhile and enjoyable. Unlike the other Organic Chemistry professors, Van Veller is very understanding and accommodating with his students.  He's always looking to help his students out and does a great job letting then succeed.

A really funny guy. This is a difficult subject, but he explains it well and if you pay attention in class, you can have a good idea of what's on the test. Ask questions if you get confused. I'm also not a big textbook person, and I didn't open it once this semester. His PowerPoints and my notes were more than enough.

Orgo 2 is a difficult subject, which is why I'm sure some reviews (mine included) can be a bit biased. However, VanVeller is a great guy and a decent teacher. Every time I've gone into his office hours, he has given me lots of points back and been very helpful. He drops big test hints in lecture. Best advice: study your mechanisms and read a lot.

Dr. Van Veller is very good at explaining difficult concepts of Organic Chemistry in a clear and simple way. He also will give big hints as to what will be important to know for the exam during lecture.
The sweetest man. His class is easy to get through and he's such a sweet man!
Easy and a great review for education majors.

Long, very droning lectures. Exams were extremely specific and were not based on study guides given. 3 exams, including the final and 3 assignments based on chapters. Attendance was taken but it was unclear if it was for a grade or not
He has no interest in his students who take an interest in their grades. He is awful at working with students. Should not be a professor.

This professor frustrated me. His exams, which we had to take online, were noticeably inconsistent with lecture material. It was too easy to lose points based on technicalities even if one had done his homework and knew the material. He assigns easy homework assignments, but I would recommend doing a lot of extra in-depth studying before exams.
Expects you to know specifics for exams, make sure to do all the reading. Responds quickly when you need help.

Giri's lectures aren't the most interesting but you'll learn a lot in one semester. He expects you to know specifics on exams so do the readings and listen! However, if you have any issues in the class he is always willing to help and is an overall nice guy. He also has an awesome offbeat sense of humor.
Nice teacher and really helpful. Class is really interesting and quite easy.

Although the material was difficult, I really did end up enjoying it. The professor made it interesting and was always willing to take questions and tried to keep students interacting throughout lessons. Awesome guy!

Go to class and listen! He's a great guy and very knowledgeable about this stuff. It can be easy to skip or space off, but if you listen in class you don't have to read much of the book. He gives a great study guide and if you go in to his office hours he'll help you fill it out. Also go to class b/c he gives extra credit but doesn't tell you when!

Very clear about signs for sign language. Unlike what was said in a previous review, ASL is taught in this course; however, Signed Enlish is taught first, and then Signed Pidgin English is used as a stepping stone to ASL.

The class isn't terrible.  I took it over the summer and it moved quickly, which is to be expected.  You do NOT learn ASL, you learn a variation of it.  You have to practice and go over the words frequently.  His example sentences sounds like he is arguing with his wife or something.  He is passionate, and is willing to help you out.

Vleck was terrible.  He gets impatient if you ask questions.  I couldn't attend lecture without falling asleep.  His voice is monotone and dull. Very boring. Didn't know what he was talking about. Just read the textbook--it explains it a lot better than he does. Asks some ridiculous clicker questions that are super detailed. Long pauses in class to "search for a word" that he was thinking of.

I think he's really good looking. Pretty boring, but he knows his stuff. Very difficult to get a good grade in, but if you try really hard, you'll succeed. Very monotonous voice. Does not make learning fun or exciting.

He's a very amusing professor, made the 9am not too bad. Difficult to motivate self if not super into anthropology. Good story teller. If you do the homework, take the quizzes, participate in recitation, and mostly pay attention in class you will be fine.

Viatori is almost too good at his job. He really ought to have his own talk show or something. He makes a lot of super complicated material very easy to understand.  He is also super kind and patient and its fun to listen to his lectures. Good man good professor. Got a lot out of  his class
Great guy, the tests are easy and class is funny if you have an intelligent sense of humor. He answers any questions you might have and everything is in the notes.

Overall average teacher, lectures are boring making the 50min seem like a million. Always tried to cracked jokes (mostly about millennials -_-) which fell flat most of the time. Good.

Moody and uninteresting. Would only take his class if necessary.
Really knows his stuff and knows how to teach it. A lot of information covered, but if you study and pay attention you will do fine. A great class, very interesting, and definitely reccommended.

the tests are tough but its easy to pay attention when looking at max.  The T.A.'s are pretty friendly and helpful.

Dr. Viatori wasn't always clear on what he wanted us to write down for notes, but lecture was usually stimulating. The TAs are a bit picky in grading, but that's no big deal... not flexible or helpful would not recomend at ALL

very nice guy, also can be funny at times.

I took him in the summer, and he admits that he has a closer relationship with students in the summer because the class size is smaller.
Generally awesome instructor. I thought some of the books would be horribly boring, but they turned out to be really entertaining and rather easy to read. He is helpful, approachable, and personable.

AWFUL. With perfect attendance, I learned nothing. Viatori is patronizing and doesn't answer any questions. We never used the textbooks. Lab was fun, but that's only because the prof wasn't there. I would NOT recommend this course!

Funny, smart, hot, awesome in every way! He was a very interesting professor. He made the subject much more interesting than I thought it could be. And put humor into everything. Projects weren't terribly difficult, just a lot of reading.
Good Prof.
young and cute. He will be a better professor with a few more years of experience.
He brings himself to the students level and makes jokes to keep us awake on a subject that isnt very intertaining
Very good prof.  He makes sure you know the material before he gives you tests and there are no surprises on said tests.  Easy classes, even the upper level one.
Definately a HOT teacher, but also good. Very funny, interactive, and can pretty much make you feel comfortable coming for help or just  yelling out stupid questions during lecture.

I would tend to think that "girls giggling and sighing and trying to attract his attention" is a problem of the students, not the professor.  I found it refreshing to have a professor who wasn't stuck in his twenty-year teaching groove.  He is extremely  knowledgeable in the areas that we studied, and he is also in on what is 'cutting edge'.

HE is not so bad. He is young and just learning how to teach.I was one of his biggest critics at first, but he is getting better. Also he is willing to explain things to you, know matter how simple the idea seems to everyone else.

Just because an instructor is good-looking doesn't mean they don't have to teach. Most of class time is spent with girls giggling and sighing and trying to attract his attention, so nothing gets accomplished.  I doubt he'd accomplish anything, anyway, because he has no idea what he's doing. For the record, I'm a girl, so this isn't "sour grapes."

I took Rus101 and Rus102 with Professor Vorozhbit and I loved them both. Prof Vorozhbit is the sweetest lady and really cares about her students. She makes sure everyone understands the material and is very helpful with reminding students about the tutor she has available if you are struggling. Very generous grader and giving person.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall an easy class, but the lectures and reading/documentaries for each unit take forever to finish. Definitely don't save all the work for the end, but it'll be fairly easy to get an A/B with minimal effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class was okay overall. She takes months to get homework assignments graded, so it is difficult to prepare for chapter tests without knowing what you did wrong and what you need to work on. She is accessible and a kind grader, I just don't know if I got as much from this class in terms of language development.

Great professor and a very generous grader. I took Russian 101 and 102 with her and got A's in both. Attendance is required. If you miss more than 3 times then your grade will suffer. She cares about her students and it shows. Highly recommend if you want to learn a difficult language without risking your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Simply put, Mrs. Vorozhbit is an awesome professor. She is a great person, and on top of that can teach Russian very well. She is willing to work with you to enhance your learning and go over material outside of class. Easily one of the best professors I have had at Iowa State, I would not hesitate to take a class with her again.

All Online. Very easy class, but there is a lot of articles to read and videos to watch. Quizzes are super easy though. Weekly discussions and a journal with 5 entries on a topic of your choosing. If you don't get a 100, she will tell you why and give you some more discussion points to look up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Maria is a very good professor. She is quite skilled at teaching languages, and uses a variety of approaches for all types of learners. She is very caring. Sometimes she says things in Russian that I don't quite understand because it is fast - but the classes are small and you should ask questions if you can't quite understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Wonderful women. She is so kind hearted and really strives to spark an interest in Russian culture in her students. The workbook homework is annoying but make the quizzes easier. Quizes are every other week, a lot of the answers can be found somewhere in the quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Only speaks in Russian, does not always give the English translation and is very hard to understand. She is very caring, and accessible outside of class but does not know how to teach Russian in an effective manner for language learners. You will need to spend a lot of time outside of class studying on your own.
Relatively easy 300-level, half-semester course that's easy to do from home.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Maria Vorozhbit is a real gem. She teaches in English, because Russian is a very difficult language for english speakers to pick up easily. Tests are every two weeks which require you to turn in your workbook exercises before you can take the test. These exercises are kind of annoying, theyre 20 pages. But besides that there is no homework. EASY A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: + She is an amazing professor, very kind, and loves Russia and teaching. + Do the workbook long before its due, and the tests are almost identical to the in class stuff you do.  The day before the test review is almost a copy of the test. + Ask questions about Russia, she loves to talk about Russia and has very interesting stories.

Maria is fantastic and probably one of the kindest people I've ever met. Really cares about the students; super kind grader; and every once in a while brings yummy Russian treats to class (!) Couldn't have asked for a better introduction to the Russian language! Ochen horosho!!!!!
Maria is a superb professor, I very much enjoyed it.

She is a great professor. She tries to make the lectures a little entertaining usually besides the constant drilling over new information. Attend class, and don't save the workbook for the day before the test because It takes awhile to do.

Great class, she was enthusiastic about the subject, while a little bit nervous at times was still a good teacher. I also really appreciated the essay style exams as they are so much easier than multiple choice.
she is very nice but sometimes she is not capable telling us what she wants in the test, so it was confusing. Over all it was an interesting class, medium hard the test are long writting
oops

Had her for Biol336x. I loved that class, and yes it was hard. In class group discussion questions from the end of book chapters, all hand written essay tests and does mostly ppts to base her tests on. Work hard and go to class you'll do well in her classes. She's very pleasant overall.
Very helpful, very approachable, and always positive.

I really liked the prof., he is a very nice lady.  Her tests are EXTREMELY hard.  Total of 9 people in class, so it is very "close knit" type of class.  I am not doing very well, but I think if you put effort in to the class she will reward you.  Books not needed.  VERY TOUGH CLASS = BIO 434 Endocrinology

This class was extremely interesting. My only complaint is that exams were full of nitty-gritty details and were thus hard to prepare for. By the same token, they didn't count for very much in the class so they couldn't hurt you that much.
Much better than the other prof who taught the class.  Actually further explained the lecture and didn't just read off the slides.  Higher level class # = more respect for students.
No Comments
Boring.  Avoid this class at all costs.  The Vleck's have absolutely no idea how to teach.

WHAT A JOKE!  Take some more teaching classes and learn how to teach!  Also, take some technology classes so that we don't have to watch you dink around with the intercom for 20 minutes and then call your husbend in to help because you can't figure it out.  Use the knowledge you have!

So this was on the first study guide (a.k.a. a list of over 200 terms): The following are vocabulary words from lecture you should be familiar with for the first exam in Zool 155. There are additional lists of key terms at the end of your reading chapters as well...ENOUGH SAID.

Possibly one of the least helpful teachers I've had. Her lectures incredibly boring and didnt feel she always knew a lot about the material. Offered poor study guides and expected way to much out of students on the tests. I wouldn't reccommend this professor or her spouse to anyone.

This was a very frustrating class to upperclassmen, so it was mortifying for us freshmen! ONe of my friends had a different professor last year (03-04) and said it was an easy A. I feel bad for them but the Vlecks are horrible professors.

I was interested in zoology as a major but after this class I need a break. I'm not sure if they understand the capacity of the average student. I stopped studying after the 2nd exam b/c I figured I would always get a low c no matter what I did and my theory held true throughout the semester.
She was a lot easier on the ear than her husband and she explained thing clearly.
No Comments

this teaching couple is the worst! run for the hills - FAST! they are idiots, are boring as heck, and can't teach themselves out of a wet paper bag, waste of time and money for the serious student - heck even for the one looking for an easy out....they SUCK!

This was a first sem class for me my freshman yr and I did horrible.  Do whatever you can to get another professor.  He doesn't take all the answers from his notes and the questions are confusing to read on the tests

This class is way to hard for an Intro. clas.  If you have to take a science class for requirements, I wouldn't recommend this one. The test are hard, and nothing makes sense that either of the teachers say in class.

Doesn't know her subject- For my class, it was Mr/Mrs teaching, and I seriously think he writes her notes and she just reads them. Can't pronounce long words or **** or labia. Can't operate her little microphone; can't operate the computer projector thingy. Makes my brain ache of misinformation.

This professor has made me HATE public relations. I dropped PR as my major after taking this class. Rambles the whole class period about everything that will be on the final and seems to not care at all about his students opinions. Get ready to be graded based on your teams work as well because your portion barely matters

I went to class and it wasn't all that bad if you tried to take notes and paid attention. He leaves a lot of the work up to you and kind of forces you to work with your teammates. The whole semester you have one giant group project. He's kind of fun if you work hard and he knows it, but also doesn't always explains stuff the best.

Didn't know what was going on most of the time in the class. He is very outdated and seems to not really care about teaching. I opened my laptop to take notes and he thought I was "online shopping" and shut my computer. Goes through the slides super fast and barely explains them, and then states that its all important and going to be on the final.
Awful. Disorganized. It is apparent he didn't put much thought into the class.

Really great teacher. Cares about the students. Has a very soft friendly voice that makes you feel very comfortable. Book use isn't required, but it helps. Grade is based off: A) 3 Exams and a Final B) One paper about the approaches (4-5 pgs) C) Weekly papers about your life Does an amazing pre-test study session that really helps with the test.
Nice guy, tries to be clear, fair.  Has a very soft, effeminate voice that has a nasty habit of lulling you to sleep...
No Comments
nice man, good teacher. He cares about his students.
Good teacher, a nice guy. He speaks a little softly so have you pay attention. He gives good examples and made the class enjoyable.
extra credit oppurtunities are GREAT!! is nice in trying to help students -- speaks a little too softly perhaps
Good speaker, will provide help if you ask for it. Extra credit opportunities, tests aren't that horrendous.

Half the semester is lecture based, then becomes team projects as the class is based off of how to effectively communicate in teams. This class is about what you put into it. Read directions very carefully for assignments, very tough grader! Easier class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sweet little elderly lady. I have taken classes with her before. This class is very relaxed - a little bit of lecture at the beginning half. One exam, then group projects/papers/presentations. Would take this class again, its an easier class just has busy work. The topic (Professional Communication) is easy if you feel good about communication
Does not give any kind of structure to any assignment. Tells you when things are due but then grades them terribly because there is no kind of structure or rubric to follow.
so much reading out of the text book, and its very confusing. quizes all the time, little extra credit.

She spends the majority of the semester lecturing. Sometimes it seemed like she would find random connections to the content to talk about to take up class time. She doesn't have a rubric for her grading so if you do poorly it's very hard to understand why. You'll need the textbook for open book and note texts. Take good notes on lectures.
Her class is NOT hard, she is really nice and sweet, she is clear BUT watch out for her quizzes. They cover what you learn but she does not write the best quizzes.

Dr. Vrchota is a pretty nice lady. She sometimes gets words mixed up but she grades very easy. Took this as a summer course, 8 papers and a group project. 7 of the papers are 2 pages in length and the final paper can be anywhere from 3-5. I would recommend taking this class.
She is very nice.  Will answer any questions you have.  Only assignments are 3 papers and 2 exams.  No homework though attendance is required.
Wastes time in class, counts to 10 when asking questions, treats most students like children
Great!
Great!
She is a little weird, but that makes things interesting...  She is a really nice lady. She is also very understanding.  Her classes are fairly easy, but may be a little boring.

This class is a lot of fun. She does a lot of different activities to keep you interested. You need to go to class but it is worth it, she makes the classes go very fast. She is always there to help in any way that she can. I love this class. She is one of my favorite professors I have ever had!
She was pretty straightforward and was there to answer questions all the time. She cares about her students and is down to earth. She grades easily if you know your stuff.
The lady is quite the bat but she does know what she is talking about, well most times.  And beware, she will clap to get the class to quiet down.
Took his class over winter break, and you were not able to work ahead on any assignments. And you had scheduled exams, and if you couldn't take it at the time provided, you'd get deducted 10%.
Very vague instructions and rubrics. Time limits on exams and quizzes felt unreasonable.

Easy enough class to pass, but the structure is terrible. The study guide was not relevant to the exam. The class encourages cheating because your notes cannot be concise enough to be useful on the tests, due to the extensive material covered on the tests. No study of actual leaders, only theories and models of professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is pretty boring. It is also fortunately really easy if you just try a bit. Exams are open note and can be typed so I just wrote everything and got one of the highest grades in the class. One thing is that he graded my final paper less than 10 minutes after I submission. I think that he probably graded it using ai.

This professor talks all the way through class without taking a breath but yet doesn't teach you much. it is his way or no way. exams are ridiculous. you haven't learned anything and then you are asked phd level questions on the material that you didn't learn. It useless, take it from me, it is not my objective to be sitting here writing, beware.
As long as you pay attention in lectures you will be all good. He gives you all of the resources you need and more. If you use what he gives to you, you cant fail with him.

The grade was based on quizzes, two exams, a short and a long paper. The material was easy, and the class was straightforward. The professor graded writing harshly, saying I needed to be more specific or in-depth, taking points. Exams were 40 multiple-choice and two essay q's, and quizzes were simple. Passing is easy; higher grades take effort.

John was an alright instructor, although his grading and exams were odd. I took full notes directly from what we learned and fully went through the review guides along with reading the supporting texts, just to find many areas on the exams were not stated in the review at all. Anything written will be judged to a heavily unneeded level, Good Luck!

He is a decent professor. He gets back to you fast. You only have weekly timed quizzes in the lockdown browser, but they're not too hard. You only have a midterm and a final, and they are somewhat challenging with how much information you have to have. They are also in lockdown browser, but you can take them anywhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Watt is a nice enough guy, but his lectures are some of the roughest lectures I have ever had to sit through. The lectures are long and have no volume to his voice, it makes the lectures drag on and with nothing but lecture slides to go along with it. Very exam heavy with little time given to complete them with essay questions at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! He does have a pretty quiet tone when teaching but his lectures are understandable and applicable to weekly quizzes. His blunt sense of humor makes the class enjoyable as well. Extra credit is offered in this course and if you prepare for the midterm/final according to the syllabus you can for sure get an A.

Professor Watt was a knowledgeable professor, albeit a little soft-spoken. There were only two exams in the class (7 chapters per exam), and everything had the same grade weight. Even with excellent handwritten notes (which were used on exams) and not missing a class, my grade suffered due to inability to go back and check my work on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Watt for both MGMT 371 and 372 and loved him both times. His dry sense of humor makes for entertaining lectures on otherwise very bland topics. Wish I could take him for all of my dumb business core classes.

Professor Watt requires attendance in class, but he usually tries to have engaging conversations in each class. He's personable and tries to treat you like a friend more than a student. He is understanding about any mistakes or mishaps on assignments as well. Strongly recommend, one of the coolest professors at ISU.

For a mgmt teacher, he manages and runs the class poorly. Boring lectures, but attendance is required. Take notes bc you get to bring them into the exam. Exam is not too hard if you have notes and understand everything he has taught. You dont get to see what you missed on quizzes/exams and you have to answer the questions before going to theNextOne

Only thing I disliked about taking MGMT 371 with Watt was the group project that is required by the curriculum. Professor Watt is a straightforward lecture giver and often inserts his own quips and dry humor into lessons. Very easygoing and gets back to you quickly over email.

Prof. Watt's lectures are informative dense & follow the textbook reasonably. Weekly tests are a breeze if you skim the textbook rather than notes/lecture power-points. The two exams were a bit challenging, but he allows physical notes, book included if you bought the physical copy. Otherwise, provides what he is looking for with written essay q's.

Took him online over winter break, really wasn't too bad. I skipped his recorded lectures and just read the book and I ended with a 92%, and his online courses only required writing 2 papers which were quickly done. Not too bad of a prof but with being online he wasn't very involved.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Studying the text book you are forced to buy is pointless. He only accepts answers from his lecture notes that will differ from the text. Only business class I ever dropped. One of those people that exploits the little bit of power he has. Sad individual.

Very strict on grades but is usually good with communication. If you don't put your heart and soul into a one-page essay, you'll fail which is really dumb imo. Only went to one in-person lecture and couldn't stand his negative tone and uncaring attitude, and in the COVID-affected 2021 semester, not having online classes and instead just recording?

This professor is not too difficult. Honestly I rarely read or even paid much attention to lectures and was able to do really well in the class. It is mostly common sense stuff. The professor is very friendly and responsive to concerns

John is EASILY the worst professor I have ever had at Iowa State. He is so unenthusiastic during all of his lectures and constantly in a negative mood. When grading exams he is so specific that is near impossible to achieve an A. The feedback he gives on papers is unhelpful and just plain rude.

Overall, he is the worst professor I have had at Iowa State. His lectures are him reading out of a textbook, or pop quizzes. The organization of his class is very confusing and unorthodox. His biggest pet peeve is when students don't memorize and check the 21-page syllabus before every class. Choose a different professor otherwise, there are more.

John is the worst professor I have had at Iowa State. His lectures are him reading out of the textbook for 50 minutes. The class is never engaged due to this, his solution is pop quizzes. His biggest pet peeve is having a student ask a question that has an answer on his 21-page syllabus. He understands the material but he is a terrible instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: John is a nice guy, but the class itself is incredibly boring. Your grade is based heavily on the exams, so be sure to study early on because basically everything is included. There are also a lot of writing assignments that are very repetitive and seemingly unnecessary. Overall, I would recommend taking this class with a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: John is always willing to help you if you meet him half way of course. He enjoys seeing his students succeed. The class is content heavy so attending lecture is beneficial. Most of the things on the exam are talked about in class. Really helpful when he gives specific essays that will be on the exam. Would recommend John!

Ppl on here complaining bout tests & study guides are only telling half truths. Ya, tests will suck if you dont do the study guides & the study guides can look long. He says at the beginning to start study guides early. Study guides covers everything & gives you all the essay questions that could be on tests. Ppl are just lazy & dont listen to him.

Watt is okay. Teaches material well, but the class is ridiculously boring. You have to write two long essays with little to go on. Watt seems like a nice guy, but also academically tough. I would look to find a different professor since Watt won't give you an A unless you master the material. Tests are very difficult, no curve. Pop quizzes as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's not too bad. Pretty funny dude, but lectures are kind of difficult to sit through. Attendance appears to be pretty lenient. Tests are the most difficult aspect of the class. Prepare your study guides instead of taking notes during class (this will help in the end). He also seems helpful in office hours, especially for exam prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: John is a nice dude, so I wouldn't worry about him as a professor. The class is not very easy though. You would think a philosophy type class would be easy but not really. There is 485 points you can get in the class. 300 of which come from 3 tests. The others are from papers (one of which is 6 pages single spaced) grades written part of test hard
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was John Watt's first semester teaching at Iowa State and it kind of showed. There is no incentive to show up to class and all he does is lecture and usually get off topic. Expects you to read a bunch of articles before class and assigns 6 papers to write. His exams are doable if you do the study guide, but the study guides take 8+ hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: he is super understanding, wants you to learn, and is very educated on the subject. i would highly recommend
Dr. Wanamaker is a great professor and great guy. I learned so much taking his class and he encourages participation. Wish I could've taken more from him.
Dr. Wanamaker was a great professor and really valued his students and their success! 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is wonderful! Such a smart guy and knows what's he's talking about. Participation and attendance are very important for this class!
Dr. Wanamaker was so helpful in ENSCI 382 and made it an enjoyable class. He is also just a nice guy who wants his students to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Wanamaker is tha best professor ever!

I took this class just to get some natural science credits out of the way, and I feared the worst. Much to my surprise, however, I ended up loving the class. Professor Wanamaker gives great lectures and is very helpful. Participation can kill your grade, though, so read the book and attend the lectures.

He really loves teaching this class.  His lectures are interesting (if you're into it) and he does easy groups activities that break up the longer classes.  He's great about listening to student feedback and answering questions.  When it comes to material, the lecture powerpoints and study guides cover it well. One of my favorite courses!

Dr. Wanamaker was awesome. He was really excited to talk about the things that we were learning and really wanted students to have the same enthusiasm. The class can be difficult if you don't read, but if you attend lecture, you should be golden. There are always review sessions before tests, so it is easy to get questions answered.

I really liked this class because he was really enthusiastic about his class and he cared about whether people understand the material or not. He is really funny as well like when he talks about waves he actually dances around and makes the class really interesting.
Lots of group work
Marlee was a solid professor, just brought down by her boring lectures. The labs were good due to the hands on learning. Overall a easy A (engineering wise)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think all the negative reviews are from her lectures, which are an absolute snooze fest. Reads directly from the posted lecture slides and has multiple tophat questions during each lecture. The first couple of labs are actually fun. it is just math for the whole semester where you reference formulas and trigonometry rules.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class can be boring, but if you pay attention to her lectures and labs you'll do great. Her examples help very much on the homework as do her lab overviews, so pay attention or you'll be lost! Choose a good lab group who knows what they're doing as the lab reports can get a bit long. Overall, she's a nice and helpful professor who always helps.

Class was easy. Just do the homework which is given every other week, and you will ace the exams. Labs are tedious and lab reports are annoying to do. Ask questions during lab if you have them Marlee will help you.
Very knowledgeable and willing to help if you ask. Labs are well thought out and give you opportunities for hands on with equipment.
Professor Walton let's you know what she expects. She responds quickly to emails and is willing to help. The labs are kind of fun. Lectures are lectures.

Marlee is a fine professor. She doesn't require lecture attendance but will put some pop quizzes into lectures. Labs are where every bit of knowledge in surveying is provided, but lectures help supplement the concepts pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is very monotone so the lectures can get boring. She gives lots of information before labs that is sometimes unnecessary but helps. Showing up to class might not seem super helpful but I suggest going because you miss quite a lot. I asked for some extra help and she was very open to accommodate my requests.

Marlees lectures are incredibly boring. Additionally, her lectures were given many times after the homework and lab on that topic had been turned in. The class was very confusing, and I learned little from lecture and lab. If youre struggling, I HIGHLY recommend reading the textbook.

Her lectures are extremely dry and repetitive. There are online lectures/quizzes every Friday and I only ever payed attention to those since the Monday lecture was a complete repeat of that. She only shows up to the labs a few times and the rest of the time it is the TA. If you have a good group for the lab then the work isn't bad.
Labs are graded hard. Shes a sweetheart though. I dont see how anyone could dislike her. Shes kinda cute and definitely knows everything there is to know about surveying.

She shows up half of the time, the other half is the teaching assistants. Lab groups are essential, be in a good group as you will be spending a lot of time with this group during lab and outside of lab to finish lab reports.

Professor appeared for maybe a quarter of the classes. Otherwise, she left TAs with notes that they seemed to have trouble understanding. Lab often covers material that won't be covered for weeks in lecture. Fridays are all online video lectures, some of which matter and some of which were complete wastes of time.

She's alright. Very dry. Do the homework. The tests are always reflective of the material from the homework and labs. The multiple choice portions of the exams are the only difficult part of the exams, as they mainly come from the Friday online lectures. Take notes on the video lecture slides. Helpful in office hours and when you have questions.

This class was extremely boring and her grading criteria for the lab reports are ridiculous. She barely teaches you anything in lecture then expects you to know all the material by the time you do your lab. I honestly hated this class more than calculus 2 or physics 1.
She is very clear with her concepts and teaches well but is very very strict about deadlines. doesn't give any extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was a waste of time, and it almost made me drop out of CE.  She is incredibly dry and her lectures are not helpful, so I found myself teaching myself from the book almost weekly. Also her graders were really bad my semester so getting an A was almost impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DO NOT GET THE TEXTBOOK! She advises you read it but this class is a relatively easy one and I did well without ever even opening it. Waste of money.   Lectures on Fridays are canceled and will be replaced by online video lectures and a short quiz. It can be done on your own time and I would say its better than a Friday afternoon lecture.

She was a pretty good teacher overall.  Very knowledgeable about surveying.  Lectures were pretty boring but if you go you will know what to do on the homework and in labs.  Tests aren't extremely difficult, but she puts a lot on them, making them time crunched.
Easy class and interesting labs. Lectures can get a bit boring/mundane at times, but generally the information is very useful for civil engineers, which is all that matters.

Professor Walton was always willing to help me whenever I had questions.  She took time to explain things when I asked and responded quickly to e-mails. The labs were kind of fun when you get to work with the equipment.
Professor Walton was helpful whenever I had questions or concerns.  She did try to explain expectations of the labs and go over what would be on the exams.

Good prof. You don't have to do so well on labs, just do it get mostly As a little Bs and maybe 2 Cs and your good. Exams are easy because its similar to her review which is great. She teaches the material, take notes and look over them and you'll be fine on exams. She's a nice lady!
