reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Wibowo was by far my favorite professor yet. He really cares about how his students do and will do anything to help you succeed. Saying that, he makes you work for it. The homework is hard, but prepares you very well for the exam. Take this course serious as the material is hard and comes at you fast.

My favorite Profesor I have had so far at Iowa State. I have never had a Profesor that cares more about his students. He puts in so much time outside of class to help students out. He has a great personality and is very funny. Even though I was in a sizable lecture, he gets to know the students and likes to walk around and short talk before class.
I respect the man but not the method.

If this teacher taught the entire semester and not just half, 90% of the students would have failed. The average for his first test was an F. He would not go over statics or mechanics, he didn't post grades online, he assigned homework that took hours upon hours to complete, and he never posted solutions or notes online. I recommend anyone else.

Taking a class with Hartanto means 2 things: you will hate yourself but you will pass and be prepared for anything that comes at you. The expectations are high and the course is difficult, but he prepares you best for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Horrible at putting testable materials into lectures. Homework was nothing like in class examples or problems. Lectures did not help at all. Homework was very long and not taught prior to being assigned. Exams were extremely hard. Made us buy a $100 textbook we never used then had to buy a $120 code book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Statics can be difficult, but he made it easy, seriously. Just come to class and pay attention to his examples and explanations. I also did the homework, which prepared me for the exams. At the end, I could say that I was very pleased with the grade I got. And as he said it, if you didn't do the homework yourself, you'd be struggling in the exams.

Learned the most in college from this class, made me realized other structures classes didn't really prepare me for my career as a structural engineer. Do the homework, pay attention in class, and you will be fine. He doesn't spoon feed and wants you to work to understand, but it is worth it. And he is almost always in his office if you need him.

Some of these positive reviews leave me very skeptical. This teacher does not give step by step solutions, he only gave 1 hour of availability a week (he wasn't there two times I stopped by) and doesn't post grades online. The average for his test was an F. Smart dude but stubborn and not a good teacher. Expects students to understand material ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Statics 3x and when I took it with Dr. W I could see myself passing the class. He explains things clearly and gives a lot of examples. Do the homework and go to his office hours if you have questions, it helps. He cares about his students. Definitely better compared to my past Statics profs. A lot of material, but he didn't set the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Imagine you are a child learning to swim. On the edge of the pool, an accomplished lifeguard repeatedly blows his whistle and shrieks, "Swim! SWIM! Why aren't you swimming??" This process goes on for the length of an entire semester. This is how Dr. Hart teaches.

Professor Wibowo is probably the best professor I have had so far at ISU. Is very friendly and gives out ALOT of extra credit. The examples he does in class closely resemble what you see on an exam so going to class was a good idea.

Dr. Wibowo is one of the best teachers at isu . While I had to work my butt off, I was encouraged to work hard and learn the material in detail. This was great and I feel that I know the material so much better now than compared to my other classes. My suggestion for success, work hard and ask questions (he is always available for questions).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While this teacher definitely knows what he's talking about, he goes over the bare minimum in class, then gives much harder problems for homework. The homework takes 6 to 8 hours, and is given weekly! He doesn't post examples nor helpful notes online, and the tests are ALL trick questions. Also he refuses to go over subjects from 332 and mechanics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great material, great class, worth taking! Prestressed is not the easiest thing to learn, but he made the class interesting and he could explain everything in great detail. I enjoyed taking the class and learned a lot. Homework could be long, but he wanted you to learn, unlike most professors in CE.

Hart is one of my favorite professors in CE. He taught a tough class well. He is readily available outside of office hours. He is always willing to help students who are willing to try. His homework assignments are long, but they help you understand the material very well. He does a great job teaching a lot of material in a short time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Skills: Excel, programming language, algebra. There is statics, if you did high school physics, you good. If you know the stuff from the power point, you don't have to go to class, however classwork and homework are given in class, and you choose your group. Harsh grading, but you get points back if you ask. Helpful b/c he wants you to succeed ^_^

Unfair grader, takes way to long to grade anything, lectures are boring and uneventful, expects you to understand everything from the first time teaching you, and can be rude at times. Pick someone else.

Definitely not an "easy A" class, but man he's amazing! He will make you learn a lot, whether you like it or not. I respect this guy. He'll explain the concepts so you can understand the material better. I wish he taught other classes. ISU has a lot of "easy A" instructors but you don't really learn anything from those structures classes.

Hart is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are full of examples and he explains concepts along with equations so you get a well rounded idea of what's going on. He is always available to help and answers emails at essentially any time of day/night. He also gives you great review material before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor will teach you if you want to sincerely learn. Make sure that you have a properly formulated question before going to him, once you have a clear questions he will help you readily.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Took the class last summer and so far he is the best teacher I have ever had at ISU. He explained everything clearly and he made you understand the material from the very fundamental basics. The quizzes and exams were fair. And he made you think and really understand the concepts, not only using equations.

Dr. Wolff is one of the most caring professors I've had. Her class was straightforward, and I appreciated being able to work at my own pace since there was so much content and memorization involved. My first few exams were slightly rough, but she helped me go through the tests and explain the math questions I got wrong step by step. She is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Shes the nicest and extremely understanding. Awesome grader, everything in her courses shes taught me have been straightforward. Youre lucky if you get her!

Professor Wolff is a great Professor. I have had her for a number of classes such as FSHN 167, FSHN 361, and FSHN 367. She is pretty easy going and is extremely helpful if you ask for assistance. She helped me actually learn the information and the foundation for FSHN 167 by not forcing material, but instead reinforcing it. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He dropped the LearnSmart assignments after the 3rd week, which are a core part of your grade. Inaccessible outside of class, and his office hours were wrong on the syllabus. There was a lot of extra credit offered because of the sudden drop in assignments to buffer exams, but hardly any of it was added. He is a great guy, but very disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a very good professor and really cared about this course and his students. Very nice guy and felt bad that more people didn't attend his lectures. Barely had any assignments in this course so the grade relied mostly on exams which were tough at times. Overall, he was a good professor and made this course fun.

Not many people went to my class, he rambles a lot. Nice guy, doesn't respond to emails. He only assigned a few homeworks, but tests you're kind of on your own. There were a few opportunities for extra credit as well.

Whenever I went to this class I regretted it. He goes on a tangent during class and does not address the important topics that are coming in homework or tests in detail, so I would just wind up reading the book on my own. Exams and homework are not hard as long as you read the book. Enroll in the online section instead!

He's a nice guy, but his lectures go on for way longer than they need to. Honestly, I spent most of the time tuning him out and doing work for other classes. He'll just rehash what's in the book and then add on one thing you need to know for the exam. I thought the TA was better than the professor. He's not horrible, just very, very boring.

Barely anyone shows up to class because he rambles about irrelevant topics that are often not useful or related to course content. With my experience, Mr. Wong does not respond to emails. Assignments can be unclear. The research participation system that he used for extra points was an absolute mess that caused widespread confusion.

John Wong likes to waste everyone's time. The class is really just one big group project with no guidelines. We're talking about writing multiple pages about a 'fictitious' company. I'm a senior in college, and I'm spending my time writing the background for a company that doesn't exist. Really?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Wong is a very insightful person but doesn't do anything to actually help you in the class. The whole class is just one giant group project and he gives you no actual guidelines for what this project should be or look like. I got a good grade but wouldn't recommend doing it again or telling anyone to take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is so caring and he really wants students to do well. He also shares a lot of life wisdom throughout class so make sure you're paying attention.

Do not hesitate to have John Wong as your professor. Yes, 343 is a challenging class, but he is so passionate about his students and wants so badly for them to succeed. He is not afraid to push everyone, but for the most part everyone is successful. The CAT project is really time consuming and hard, but very beneficial- even if you don't like sales
Dr. Wong is really passionate about teaching and it really reflects. The class was exceptional and is highly recommended.
Best professor I've ever had!

Professor Wong was excellent.  Given the short time constraints, I found he hit all of the major points of the course in stride.  His lectures were insightful, inspiring, and full of well supported information.  You can tell he loves to teach, and I loved to learn from him.  He is easy to reach outside of class - I will keep in touch in the future.

John Wong is one of the best professor's and assests ISU has in the marketing department. He stays long hours to ensure he students are doing well. If you don't get an A, it's due to the fact in you didn't put in the time. You'll leave this class a better person.

John really wants you to succeed, but you have to work for it. The group project is long and you will need to put in a lot of work. But, the class is an easy A as long as you put in the effort. He has weekly quizzes, and papers due at the end of the semester. All around he's a great guy, but the class is hard work.
Awesome class, Dr. Wong is very passionate about what he teaches, and gives life lessons rather than just sales lessons. Very beneficial class, definitely recommend to any student.

Dr. Wong is the best! I have no idea what the course would be without the CAT project. I thought marketing at ISU was a joke until I took this course. You prepare the whole semester for a 20 minute role play; try to sell a piece of CAT equipment to your customer(ZieglerCAT sales team). You learn course material with real life experiences.

While this class is generally thought of as "easy", it is one of the classes that I have learned the most about sales and how business is conducted in my time at Iowa State. Listening to Dr. Wong about things that he has done is very informative, and honestly, pretty amazing. I would recommend this class to any business student at Iowa State.

MKT 343, also known as the CAT class. At first it is really intimidating, but if you stick it out and put in the work it can be one of the most beneficial classes you will ever take. The midterm is easy if you read the required articles and show up to class.  The project is intimidating but Dr. Wong is willing to help you if you are willing to work

Honestly most of the class material seemed pretty self-explanatory so it made for kind of boring lectures. He expects a lot out of students. He wants you to read the textbook, weekly articles and separate book (The Culture Code). Not really necessary to buy the textbook. Tests are all essay and can be difficult. He is very passionate about sales.

Amazing professor! Pretty easy to understand. The CAT project is most of the semester, it's a lot of work, but you will get a lot out of it. He is willing to bend over backwards to help you. Attendance isn't mandatory, but highly encouraged. He keeps lecture interesting and fun. Highly recommend!
Dr. Wong is an AMAZING professor. Take his class if you get the chance. You will learn a lot about selling and you get to work with Caterpillar. You get get a real world experience in a classroom.
My favorite professor at Iowa State. He likes to lecture but makes them meaningful and relates to the students well. HIGHLY recommend taking him.
Professor Wong is BY FAR the best professor I've ever had at Iowa State. He wants the absolute best for his students, and he is extremely accommodating. You'll love the guy
I am so glad that I took this class. Learned a lot from the project. This class helped me doing my internship.

TAKE THIS CLASS! He is hands down the greatest professor I have had at Iowa State. He truly cares about students and wants you to learn. Go to class and learn everything you can from the guy. The project is a lot of work but definitely a beneficial experience worth having.
One of the best professors I've had at ISU! Not a marketing major and took the class as an elective, and loved it! Dr. Wong is very kind and helpful. I would recommend any class taught by him!
Such an amazing professor! I have never met someone more passionate about teaching. VERY HARD but one of the best classes I have taken. Makes everything you talk about in class so interesting.

Best teacher I've ever had at ISU!  You have to be willing to put in effort to get a good grade- but it is 100% worth it.  Class can be challenging, but if you do your readings and participate you are guaranteed to pass.  He truly cares about his student's success and their future.  TAKE HIS CLASS!

Great professor! Truly cares about each of his student's success. Will go above and beyond to help you, if you ask for help. Always finds a way to make class fun, crack a joke, or tell one of his infamous "Wong-isms."
Class seems a little overwhelming in the beginning, just stick with it.  One of the most beneficial classes I have ever taken.

Best prof i have ever had at ISU. He will push you to your limits and will be the hardest prof you'll have, but you will be better for it. If you give a crap about you're education this is hte man to call.

I loved Dr. Wong. He was a great guy, he made his lectures entertaining and clever. We were in a small room for 343 so I never had an issue hearing him. Our end of the year project was a lot of work but it was one of the most useful projects I have done in my time at ISU. He was also very willing to meet with students and give us extra help.
Takes forever to grade tests. Does not respond to student emails.

Worst professor I've ever had at ISU. He's a nice guy, bad at teaching. Doesn't fulfill the teacher responsibilities. Didn't have enough exams once. Two times he gave me zeros for course work. One of them was for a test. And not only did he do that, he took forever to fix it. Doesn't respond to any emails either. Avoid, interest isnt in students.
soo hot
He is horrble. Avoid at all costs. He can barely speak english, and even when he does, you dont wanna hear it anyway.

Showed up about 50% of the time, got a good nap in most days, read the material the day before the test, came out with a B+. Pretty easy class. Wong's a nice guy, just clueless on tech and don't sit in the back-- you won't be able to hear him.

Probably the worst teacher i've had at ISU.  Not only does he NOT talk about what's on the test, he does it in a very boring and hard to follow way.  This makes him twice as bad as most teachers.  He also has a very poor class attendance.
Not interesting in the least and his notes are just scribbles if you can avoid this teacher do it

He's a pretty good professor. He likes to go off on tangeants, but he keeps things interesting. He is a little late in getting grades to you. However, tests aren't that hard. Everything you need to know for the tests will be out of the textbook.
Not a big fan of his teaching.

He takes two weeks to give you a your test grades back!!!! and they are scantron.  Its just laziness on his part.  Class is so boring, thank god for crosswords.  Tests are not easy at all. His accent is a little entertaining.  "Maaaaketting, i's Cooo!"
Took Mkt 343 and Mkt 340 with Dr. Wong. He tries his best to deliver the subject to his students. He tries to keep up with current events and give his all to his students. Great professor!

He is definitely a professor that will challenge you, but he's a wonderful guy. Consumer Behavior was a little confusing at times, but the tests and the final project were decent and interesting to partake in.
I dropped because he just is not clear. The tests are over 9 Chapters at a time.
I hated this class.  It was sooo boring, part because of material, part because of Wong.  If you have a chance take it with someone else!

He likes chatting, but doesn't like teaching.  His heart was not in the course.  Self-conscious, unorganized, habitually tardy.  Called in sick for class one day, I still don't think he was sick.  Easy grader, poor class.

Very helpful guy. Tests are too bad, but you absolutely need to read the book to have a good grade on tests.  Studying is much needed in class, but real-life application in lecture help make this class very interesting

This professor is horrible. His TA is much better. The TA covers the information in more depth. Mr. Wong likes to trail off about nothing. Most of what he talks about in class is not on the test, the majority comes out of the book so plan on doing a lot of reading. His notes are very dis-organized and unprofessional. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!
This class was supper easy!! All you have to do is go to class and follow the review sheets before the tests and you will at least get an A- Definatly take this calss from him!!!
No Comments
Great guy... very interesting... this class was soo friggin easy

He drones on and on and on every class. I could not stand to sit through his classes! The TA was a much better teacher. The informaton was fairly easy. He goes through notes to fast so you can't write everything down. Not the worst I've had, but try to find another pro if possible.

He is hard to understand when he talks. Talks about unrealted topics from 3/4 of the time then rushes throught the notes and you don't get a chance to write any of them down.  The class is not to hard, if you can make yourself sit through his lectures....

He's traveled a lot and his familis his world, so he goes off on little stories about them and his trips. He's a good guy that means well.  He wants everyone to do well, so he gives a lot of info for exam reviews.  Read the book and the handouts and you will do fine.

i skipped a good amount of class and got a B in the class. always go to class the week b4 tests for the review sheet.  Going to class helps out a ton. saves you time from finding your own info in the book to study for tests
Not bad, seems to get a little more emotional about customer satisfaction than he should.

He is a good guy...very nice.  The class is pretty easy to get through without a lot of teaching so I think that helped him out a bit.  I have had better and much worse professors so I'd see hes about avg.

This professor will test over material that is not covered in class or in the book. He expects you to extrapolate info. This would okay if you had any background in marketing, but 340 is supposed to be an introductory course. Nice guy -poor instructor. Does offer extra credit due to low test scores.

Homework isn't mandatory, but if you do all of them, your grade will go up by half a grade at the end of the semester. Periodically offers extra credit throughout the course or on quizzes. Also, if you play the final for the class then you will receive extra credit. I recommend doing the homework to do well on the quizzes. Hardest was ear training!

I don't have enough room to tell of how awesome of a teacher George is. He cares about student success above all and isn't afraid of adjusting the syllabus to accommodate the learning rate of his students. He is hilariously awkward at times (in a good way). Definitely have him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: George is one of the best music instructors I've ever had in my 16 years of playing. As a nonmajor, it can be difficult to find time to practice multiple days a week, but he's really understanding of that. However, he has pushed my cello playing to levels I didn't know I could reach in such a short amount of time. Excellent player and instructor.

One of the best profs at ISU. He understands that students have personal lives and so he's easy to talk to.  He actually cares about his students mastering the material. As long as you show up to class and listen, you will pass. No exams just weekly quizzes that are very doable for someone with no music background. More profs should be like him.

Such an easy class! I've had music experience before, but even for those first starting out, Dr. Work is impeccable with describing new concepts and teaching beginners. It's basically a music theory class exploring triads, scales, rhythm, note names, etc. Highly recommend for a fun "easy" A
Cello Lessons, He is a really good guy, easy to understand, and knows how to push you to make you sound good. He isn't incredibly strict about practicing, but is very helpful in lessons.

Work is a really nice guy, very understanding if you have to miss class or make up a quiz or something. One of the most laid back profs I've ever had. This class was easy and basically a catch up for a ll the basic music knowledge I had when I was younger. I'm sure 221 will be 10 times worse than this.
good
Fantastic instructor and very likable guy. It is damn hard to find a private bass of cello instructor better than him!
Mr. Work is an AWESOME prof!

Excellent musician.  As a teacher, he can be very patient, yet he's always working to bring the student's level up to the highest degree, exponentially.  He does an excellent job of reinforcing good technique and inspiring excellent musicianship.  Even as a cellist, he makes a great bass instructor!
Top notch class act. Very good ability, very agreeable and a good guy.
Very excellent cello instructor. Knows what he's talking about when it comes to music. Easygoing guy but gets you to want to work.
World class technical and artistic instruction.  Super!!!
bad bad bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His only redeeming factor is that he sometimes tries to be a nice guy. However, he is a horrendous teacher and does not put time into his class. HW & Exams questions were unclear, and he doesn't bothering finishing his examples. He also made the class more confused when he tried to answer questions. Probably better off learning from the textbook.

Actually terrible. Run. Quizzes/Homeworks are full of errors. Expect to be driven insane not knowing who's at fault for errors. He devoted 30 minutes to this class a week, tops. Doesn't put in the effort to make good assignments, lectures, example problems, or in answering questions. It's Finals week and I still don't know how this class is graded.

So, taking him online is a big mistake. Only has homework and Quizzes. Two big problems is that you can not see what you do wrong every assignment, and his quizzes are too long with not enough time. This professor is lazy. He will never answer any questions about the quizzes or homework. His office hours are useless. Does not even work the problem.

Dr. Wright is a nice guy and this class is very easy by graduate engineering standards. There is still a fair amount of work, but it's not overly difficult and grading is relaxed. The quality of the lectures was lacking at times and quiz content usually just came directly off a posted PDF. Quizzes weren't written well. Pretty interesting content.

Lectures are not bad all, go to class. It's not bad and you get a lot from it. Mark grades really generously and doesn't give a lot of homework either. The homework we got was only just a completion grade. Very chill dude and you won't regret taking Thermo II with him.
This class was a joke. He curves the class like crazy. I got 40 something percent of the two exams and a 70 on the final which was super easy. All exams are open note. I finished with a B+

Really easy grading in the class. His lectures are good, but I didn't feel like I learned much from the class at all. Homeworks took a while but were graded on completion. We also only had 7 assignments throughout the semester. The exam grading was also extremely generous. In one of the exam I got 30% but it ended up being like a B or B-.

I took this course online, it was very manageable. A short quiz, discussion, and a few other short assignments each week. Assigned group project that starts around mid-semester. Be sure to get familiar with your group so that you do not get behind. Otherwise, a great class to take!
Great professor and always willing to help. If you get your work done, you will be fine. Try to find a good group as the class is very group project-heavy. Overall great teacher. Really liked her.

Prof Wright was AWESOME!! I loved this class! The material was easy, the work was flexible, and there was one group project at the end of the semester. The exams were a little difficult, but they weren't worth much of your grade. If you don't do well in this class, you absolutely deserve it! Wonderful responder!

Ann was one of the best professors I have ever had. I took MGMT 470 with her online. The class is very easy to follow and assignments are due every Sunday. She cares deeply about her students and wants everyone to succeed. The final for the class was a group project. I highly recommend this professor!
Anne might be the best professor I've ever had at Iowa State. She's very approachable and provides great insight and material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
- responds fast to emails
- always there for students
- no exams / only weekly quizzes (2 attempts allowed) 
- assignments listed in the syllabus already 
- grades work / not necessary accuracy
- 10/10 :)

Ann Wright is a phenomenal professor. She cares about her student and teaches with real life examples. There is a lot of group work associated with her classes, but as long as you submit all your assignments on time there is no reason you shouldn't finish the semester with an A .

Anne does a phenomenal job in making this class easy. The group project has 4 reports and a short 7-10 min presentation. Lots of YouTube and you can use the book for your reflection paper. Quiz is easy too since its at home.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Probably the sweetest and most caring professor I have ever had. She made the class super easy and simple for the online format. You have weekly discussions, chapter reflections, and one final group presentation project. She is a simple grader. Complete the assignments and you'll get an A. Wright is easy going and willing to help anyone, anytime.

As many of the previous reviews have stated, Mrs. Wright is a great teacher and cares about her student's success. She will answer questions pertaining to the class as well as question unrelated to class. I would highly recommend taking her as a teacher if you have the option to do so!

Professor Wright is a real gem. She is extremely kind and caring. Her class is really easy, and if you pay attention, you will get an A. For the majority of the class you will be working with your teams. Fun class to meet new people at ISU

She is genuine and caring. The class is fairly easy, just make sure that you study the quizzes before taking the exams. The CAPSIM group project can be tricky. I was lucky that my teammate figured it all out. Lectures are boring, but you'll want to show up for group work days and in-class assignments. Final is optional.

She's a really good professor and genuinely wants you to do well. The Capsim simulation is kinda confusing at first but she's always willing to ask questions. She's an extremely positive person and the class was pretty easy, but it's easy to get lost during the lectures. Tests are easy if you study the power point presentations.

Professor Wright is genuinely very willing to help and listen to students. Material of the class isn't terribly difficult, even though the exams are quite annoying. (A lot of multiple-choice vocabulary with usually two plausible answers.) Either way, just show up to class, pay attention, do the prescribed activities, and you will get a good grade.

Ann Wright is amazing. She is really nice. This class might at first seem intimidating but it really is not a difficult class. The professor cares about students learning something from this class greatly.
Seriously the best professor ever! She is so caring and helpful. Very easy homework and tests are online. Need to go to class most days for attendance or in-class assignments.

Anne is a very nice teacher and she cares about her students. She sticks to her syllabus and won't surprise you with any homework. Attendance is required but her lectures usually have videos and she is a lenient grader. Do the work and you'll get an A. She cares about her students success :)
Very good teacher, I like how personable she is. I still studied for the exams but other than that this class wasn't out-of-class work heavy.

She cares about your grades and your learning experience a lot. There are times when I was sick and missed some in-class activities; she allows me to do it at home and submit it online. All the in-class assignments and schedules are clearly listed in the syllabus so you'll know when not to miss the class.

Great Teacher. If taking her class she will go over the tests before you take it. Make sure you right down everything she talks about and study it. and you will pass with an easy A and won't have to take the final..

Anne was a great professor. She was so caring of her students to the point it hurt! The class was simple: Show up for nearly every class, do the outside work (easy), contribute in your assigned team projects/exercises (easy). Do those things and you'll receive an A.

For all business majors who have to take this course, please try to take it with Anne. She is the sweetest, and doesn't make anything difficult. Nothing is weighted, and she is straight forward with how the class is set up. Nothing difficult if you just do your work.
Tests are easy if you go to reviews, she is easy going if you forgot something. Cares about your grade

She is a very nice person and is passionate about student success! The class is mostly discussion based, but the tests are based on the readings from the book. She is kind of a tough grader on assignments, but they are pretty simple. The majority of this course is a group project simulation, and she is very helpful with the groups.

I stopped attending lectures after the first half of the course. Dr. Wu is not very clear in his work and tends to derive equations rather than showing how to use them. I switched to watching Steve Butler's lecture videos and they are much more helpful. The quizzes in this course are extremely difficult, and were my main source of stress.

Professor Wu is very approachable and takes the time to answer questions. However, he teaches using pen, and his handwriting makes it hard to follow. Due to time constraints, he occasionally skims over some content. Because of these challenges, I stopped attending lectures after the first half of the course.

Be ready to live translate the material because his Z's look like 3's and thetas and phi's are identical. But he has a fun class period with starting class off with practice problems and makes fun of some people if you get it completely wrong. If you want to accel watch the butler video before class. Also, Sphere is pronounced schphere.

Taken fall 2024. Lectures were useful since he provided examples to follow along with and work out problems at the start of most lectures. He always stuck around after lecture for questions and provided useful feedback most of the time. Sometimes what he says or writes isn't clear; use supplemental content. Stay on track with the course schedule!!
Reads off slides and doesn't explain examples very well. I found myself skipping lectures and teaching myself because the lectures were so unhelpful. Can be hard to understand.

It's Calc 3, get ready to put your time in. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you skip a few lectures, catching up will be tough. His lectures were mostly clear and a lot of examples were given, although sometimes his explanations didn't work for me / weren't in-depth enough.

I liked Wu's lectures, he was clear and to the point. If you follow the steps he gives, then you'll be just fine. The quizzes could be difficult, but the quiz questions are typically more difficult than the test questions so you should be fine.

Wu is not awesome at teaching content. In the year of COVID he read off the slides and didn't work through any problems. If you are an auditory learner you will be fine, but I cannot visualize math orally, so I taught myself all of the content. There were also section where he didn't give us the formulas we needed to complete homework
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are easy because he teaches how to solve questions in classes. He didn't really go thru why we need to use eqs n stuff (makes me lack understanding). So, did pretty bad in the final especially those prob solving as all I did is remember solutions.

Only 10% of his class was graded on anything besides exams, which is a tad scary. He is VERY willing to give points back on exams and push back homework deadlines, one of the kindest people I have met. His classes vary a lot in difficulty, but he always curves it quite high so you will do well no matter the overall difficulty.

Tests are easy as long as u do the practice tests before hand. He discusses arbitrary science topics 10 min at the start of every lectures coz he cares more about knowledge than the grade, assume his students are not smart which leads him to explain the details of his working steps (can be boring to smart student). I like him!

Dr. Wu is easily the worst teacher I've had in my life. He forgot to teach some material, he made so many mistakes, his lectures were VERY scrambled and boring, and he overall lowered my interest in math. Attention math majors like me out there: Take charge of your education and do NOT have him teach your class, even if it's for the math majors.

90% of our grade was based on 3 exams, so be sure to study hard for those. He's a passionate and funny guy, albeit a bit hard to understand. You can tell he really loves his job, though, and I really enjoyed spending a tiny bit of time at the start of each class to discuss a science article because he absolutely just loves science.
I love this professor. He truly cares about his students. His lectures are boring and you don't need to go to learn the material but his exams are just like the practice exam.

Reads straight off the slides instead of working through problems on a board, which I found hard to follow at times. Takes too much time in class going over the basics & small steps in problems. Homework is frustratingly more difficult than exams -- make use of recitation & TA's. Exams are very similar to practice exams.

Dr. Wu's lectures will work for some, but not the many. This semester, he has read the slides word for word. This is not the professor you want if you're a visual learner like myself. Nevertheless, the content can be easily learned outside of class, and the practice exam is a great resource to prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are useless, spends time on things that we should know such as he spent an entire class on partial fractions and nearly 2 classes on how springs go up and down which required 20 mins. Over all useless lectures, easy tests would not recommend if you want to actually understand the content. Book is useless exams are same as practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wu is a great teacher for the calc. The class itself is difficult but he does a good job of goin through the material and getting you acquainted with concepts. He is sort of quiet and hard to listen to if you take it in the morning, just saying.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is a great professor. He explains all the problems very clearly, answers questions completely and he gives practice exams that are just like the real exam. Only downside is that he waits until the end of the semester to curve grades, so you dont really know what your grade will be.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: I had a very hard time learning anything that professor Wu tried to teach us. He flies through material and he never asks the class questions at all.
Very pleased with this guy. Open to all questions, very clear when explaining the concepts, and shows out all steps when working out a problem. Grades tough, but the exams have no surprises on them.
The best math professor I ever met!!
It's easy to fall asleep during lecture, but there wont' be any surprises on the exams and he's eager to help during office hours.
Great teacher...Explain well the materials and easy to understand.

Very soft spoken and sympathetic towards students.  Picks reasonable problems for quizzes and exams and is honestly more concerned with students learning the material than grades.  Probably the first Math professor I've had at Iowa State I've liked.  Wish I had teachers like this all the way through school, I would be much better off!

Great professor, just the way he taught the class made it really easy to understand, and if I had any questions at all he was always really good at explaining everything, even if it took 3 times to explain the same thing.

Dr. Wu is an amazing professor! I genuinely enjoyed his class and learned so much. He truly cares about his students, both their performance and whether they actually understand the material. He's incredibly kind, approachable, and supportive. Just a really great human and professor overall. I would definitely recommend taking any class with him!

After many classes went online this semester, Dr. Wu has been my one saving grace. While the class is fairly difficult, and the lectures a little dry, this guy really cares about the mental health of his students and has made a significant effort to help us through this weird semester (eliminating time limits on exams, extending deadlines, etc.).

Dr. Wu genuinely wants you to learn and do well (get a good grade). He was especially helpful during the transition to remote learning (thanks COVID). You will need the textbook as exams are open-textbook (not open-note). We also had a pretty easy final group project and no final exam. Minimal homework throughout the semester.

Wu's lectures can be a bit boring but he tells you everything you need to know to do well on quizzes and exams. He is also very willing to help if you are struggling with the concepts. He listens well to feedback and makes adjustments based on what the class tells him. Overall he is a great guy and a bit of a jokster.

This review is "very simple actually." Perhaps the worst class I have ever taken. He didn't even teach and just talked about his research that had nothing to do with class. Additionally, the final project was full of mistakes and he told everyone different things. Additionally, the grader was incompetent and didn't know what they were doing.

Nice guy, but not a good lecturer. Scheduled office hrs on Friday nights. Slides are straight from book and often contain unimportant information. Lectures are boring and pointless (when quizzes weren't given). Quizzes are big part of your grade, but warned ahead of time. Recommend a chegg account for hw. Avoid if possible

It is really hard to understand is accent which makes the material bit hard to understand. A very knowledgeable person and a kind person when you seek for help. If you are looking for an easy A in the class take him but if you looking forward to learn don't take him. Exams are super easy and straight from the homework (or similar to practice prob.

After 30 pages of solutions for each of the six homework assignments, I realized I hadn't learned a thing. He was gone several times and just walked out to take a phone call during one of the tests and never came back. The class was easy, but all he really said was, "it's very simple actually" after he posts a 20-page nonsensical solution.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you do your homework and pay attention in class you should have no problems. Tests are very similar to homeworks and quizzes so study them and you'll be fine.

Wu was a horrible lecturer. He basically will read you the slides for lectures, then give you ridiculous homework and quizzes to check to see if you learned the material he never really taught well enough. He is usually fair with the tests though.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Super easy class, minus the homeworks. You know EXACTLY what's going to be on the tests before hand. Homeworks are tough though, but not impossible if started on time.  Also, he was there a good half of the lectures so become really acquainted with the TA.

He cares a lot about his students. Very understanding. Posts all materials online, and gives access to past exams which is very helpful for preparation. Lots of office hours to get your doubts cleared.

I had Dr. Wu for STAT 471 (was not an option for me to select). He was very kind and clearly cared about his students. Previous exams are provided to prepare for tests, and they are very helpful. The final is a bit more difficult than the other exams, so make sure to pay extra attention at the end. Overall a great class and professor, I recommend!
you have to read his note when preparing the exam. the exam is pretty pretty similar with his sample. do homework by yourself, you will have A at the end.

Professor Wu is very understanding and grades relatively easy. He writes his own notes based off of the book and goes through them in class. All the tests were open note and open book. However, they are very lengthy. For the final, which was two hours long, only about five people completely finished. The final was also 45%. Overall, I recommend.

Lectures can be boring at times. He offers his notes online so you can always reference them when needed. He is very helpful when you struggle with HW although they are straightforward for the most part. Posts practice exams that are exactly like the ones given to current students so study those. Enthusiastic about stats in  his office hours

A wonderful professor. He posts all notes online, posts past quizzes, and is very understanding. The quizzes and exams are remarkably similar to those from years past. The homework is tedious and time consuming, but it is straightforward. Use the JMP software as often as you can on the homework; it will save you loads of time.
Easy class if you study the old exams before the tests
Decent class, hw easy graded, tests similar to practice exams.
No Comments

Sang Kim is a thoughtful, helpful, knowledgeable professor. He is more willing to listen to and act on student feedback than most professors in ISU's ECpE department. I was surprised by not receiving an "A" grade that I thought I deserved through consistent above-average grades, and the curve applied at the end of the course was not transparent.
He's the worst professor I've ever encountered in my entire life.
He explained the really difficult topics step by step and in detail so it is not that hard if you are focusing on the class. Class is not that busy and grading is really generous and understandable.

Kim is very rude person. working with him was one of my worst experiences. not very helpful. i would not recommend this course to anybody. and he's not very technically strong. often gets stuck in the middle of a lecture. always seems unprepared.
Not a hard class. Homework, quizzes and tests are reasonable. Research and simulink project at the end.

He is good teacher and also realizes that giving impossible tests doesn't really make a person learn.  Tests are not hard and homework isn't bad either.  Only had 3 quizzes.  Not sure if he prepares us enough for EE422 and EE423 but I enjoyed him.
No Comments

Good lecturer, but a bit dry. Passionate and extremely knowledgeable about his subject. Always available for questions, even gives you cell number. Homework can be difficult at times, but its pretty reasonable. Fair grader. Take good notes, pay attention, read the book once and awhile and youll do fine.
May be a good researcher, but not a good professor

Wu was a pretty good teacher.  I thought he was a bit unclear a few times, but he still did very good.  The homework was harder than the exams, and the exams made up 80% of the grade.  Wu is a very nice guy, and he really wants you to do well.  The concepts are interesting, and the class was pretty good. Probably my favorite meteorology professor.

Wu was a great teacher. The class wasn't easy at all, but he was helpful enough that made it not that bad. His exams are a lot easier then the homework he assigns. He wants everyone to continue in meteorology. He has a great sense of humor. Plus, last semesters midterm exam was exactly the same as the previous year.

get a basic understanding on a very wide range of topics without being overwhelmed with unnecessary load or complexity. I feel like I was given the opportunity to actively participate in my learning and be very creative. The lectures were also pretty good.

Professor Wymore is knowledgeable about what he teaches. His biggest weakness is that he does not have a commanding voice which causes a distracting learning environment, and his lectures can be sometimes monotone. He is most helpful in office hours, and it is definitely easier to take EE285 if you have prior programming experience.

Mat is nice and knows what he is doing but he speaks quietly during lectures and it can be very hard to hear him when he's trying to teach. If you don't understand code make sure you ask him or TAs because it will build up and labs are the most important for your grade in this class

He knows what he's teaching and how to answer students' questions. Prior experience in programming and circuitry is helpful and will allow you to breeze through this class. For those touching programming for the first time, ASK for help from peers and TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. Provides all necessary information in lecture, easy to get a hold of, easy to work with. I have enjoyed this course. The labs are fairly difficult, but doable with help.

Probably the best professor in the department for your learning. He's willing to talk about anything and is really knowledgeable about operating systems which helps. Great class, you get to learn about an important and evolving topic in the field. Labs help you learn and allow for experimentation. Excellent professor, and always willing to help.

Mat is probably the most laid-back professor I've had. His courses are not perfect, but he is easy to understand and work with. Don't expect to get an A by just showing up to class. But if he sees you're putting in the effort, he will be willing to compromise grade things leniently.

Extremely laid back and easy going. It always seemed like he was moving back due dates for labs and hw. The course itself is in no way difficult and it seemed like he recognized that. While not entirely mandatory, his lectures were pretty interesting and informative.

Mat was a very caring professor! Definitely cared about each student and was very accommodating given the circumstances. Made lecture content easy to understand, even if it was just the basics of C. Overall made an environment that was easy to learn in!

Mat was a great professor. Due to the whole class being remote, he was very accommodating and would constantly let students have extensions on assignments if they needed them. He did a good job of giving us the resources we needed to be able to complete our labs and projects. This class did a good job of covering Android topics.
Best CPR E professor I had during college. Projects aren't overly difficult, but you will learn a lot from them. Lectures are straightforward and easy to understand.

Dr. Wymore is hilarious in lectures and always had good talking points. He knows a lot about operating systems and CPR E in general and was a good resource to ask questions to. He's also EXTREMELY kind when it comes to grading and accommodations for students, something I really appreciated during the COVID-19 pandemic.

I am a honor student and ready to start my phd at top 3 ivys, so this is not about grading. 

Honestly, it is not about difficulty either, it is about his attitude towards students. He might be very smart, but he is kind of condescending in his teaching.  

Good luck with his next position, very much good luck with his next batch of students.

Very knowledgable on the material and explains it very well. You learn so much about R coding for statistics and data science in a short amount of time, sets you up very well for a future job. Only problem is that he isn't very available to help outside of class and his TA was terrible with grading and help on homework.

Prof. Dai made this class 10x harder than it needed to be. He expected far too much from his students. Homework assignments were ridiculously hard and took HOURS. Each assignment took nearly 8-10 hours each week. FIND A FRIEND! Also, his lectures were exceptionally boring. Had this class had any other professor, I would have greatly enjoyed it.

Although this course is relatively easy, I don't like him to teach even though I hope he does not teach this course. The reason is: 1. The test time is fixed and can only be in-class time and cannot be freely chosen on a certain day. 2. What you haven't done will force you to admit it. I once received an email asking if I did certain things, even t

The grading in this class starts out very easy and then gets harder and harder and I mean unnecessarily harder. I would get docked points on labs and home-works for not valid reasons it was like they were looking for ways to take away points and find things wrong. The lectures are very boring the format of the class if basically like DS201 but in r

Dr. Dai is pretty dry as a lecturer but it seems like he wants to get better. He doesn't really inspire you and I stopped paying attention halfway through the semester. There were parts of the homework that involved using R to simulate that we're "required but not graded" so I didn't do that part and suffered no repercussions.

Going to lectures are not mandatory but it will help somewhat, but he has trouble keeping a good pace so what we finish all the material, the end of lecture is pretty rushed because he covers so much content each time. He assigns readings and I would highly recommend reading them and going to recitation to be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly the tests did not match the lectures and it was difficult to do well since it was material we were not familiar with. It is also exam heavy and the weekly quizzes do not really reflect your grade that much you can ace all of them and do bad on one exam and your grade will tank a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests were hard I attended every lecture and it would be something so irrelevant no coordination to previous lectures. He is generous lets us take our personalized formula sheet to the tests. He also will just read the lecture slide to you so you really only need to go for tophat.

Dr. Wang is very pleasant to listen to in lecture and clearly loves physics. He is easy to understand and is clear on what is expected of us for test/quizzes. He is also very approachable and happy to help clarify something that you don't understand. Exams and the final are worth a lot. Just have a good formula sheet and you will be fine.
i agree that he is using stupid criteria
Stupid criteria
No Comments

We did Top Hat questions that 90% of the class got incorrect, and he STILL graded Top Hat points on accuracy. He never reexplained the subjects that nobody understood. Class averages never reached above 70% on exams. If you have the option to change professors, do it for your own good. This class was actual rage-bait.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He forgets this is an elementary organic chemistry course, and talks over our heads for the entire lecture without explanation.He is not easy to get ahold of. Homework was to be 14% of our grade, got moved down to 4%, and the remaining 10% got added onto the exam percentage. He does grade on a 70% class average curve-- aka the only way we passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: doesn't give indepth explanations

This class was horrible. We had homework that accounted for a significant number of points. He decided to take away ALL of the homework assignments we already completed, when it wouldn't work for only a few people. He told me personally to drop the class with a C. The average grade was 40-50% on a curve. Friend retook 3 times with the same prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zhao has plenty of knowledge but doesn't listen to students about what topic they need reviewed again. He speeds through slides and changed nothing even after all 5 exam averages were 40-50% each time. You can't ask questions in lecture so just prepare to ask Youtube. Take the regular O Chem 1, not Elementary O Chem 1. It sounds harder... it's not.

This is the worst class I have EVER taken. He grades on a 70% curve. Without the curve, I would've absolutely failed the entire class. And he's in such denial too, constantly claiming that a class average of 50% on an exam is normal. If you have to take this class like I did, pick a section with a different professor unless you want to die.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would rather change my major 15x than take this class. Took away homework after people complained the program wasn't working. Doesn't put in the tophat or 'designated' homework points til end of the semester. Doesn't elaborate, expects to know the material; and the lecture is a review. Tests are a joke; be prepared to cry while drawing hexagons.

Zhao takes his lecture slides directly from the textbook, but steps may be skipped. Get ready to read the textbook and definitely do the practice problems! The exams are not easy but his practice exam format is almost exactly what is on the exams, same concept in the same spot and the same number of questions about it - focus on those topics most!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really liked Zhao for ochem, he is very caring and wants everyone to do well. He explains things in detail and does practice problems in class. Ochem is a hard course so if you want to do well you have to study, but he provides everything you need to succeed and curves his exams a lot. He is overall a very nice guy and makes it more enjoyable.

Yan Zhao knows what he's talking about and is passionate about it. He makes lectures interesting a connects them to real world examples. The class itself is moderately difficult, but he does an awesome job at explaining things and provides plenty of practice problems. I highly recommend!

To pass this class you really need to study and prepare for the tests because the tests had some really difficult questions. I like him as a person, but I don't really like his teaching style as he would drone on and on. The best advice I have is to do ALL the practice questions and always assume the test will be more difficult than you think.

He was AWFUL! He didn't show his face at all during virtual office hours, his lectures weren't helpful at all. He wasn't helpful when asked questions about the content discussed in the course, for example, he actually said "If you don't know something, you never will and I can't help you." To be honest, I learned more from my tutor than from him.

Dr. Zhao is a great professor! He spends so much time helping students understand the foundational concepts of organic chemistry which is super helpful. I took this class online, which allowed me to take really good notes from the lecture videos. Exam questions come from lecture content. Don't use the book - it's confusing and takes forever to read

Not a good lecturer. His powerpoints are unclear, unhelpful, and hard to look at. His exam questions were very unfair and their difficulty level did not reflect what was covered in lectures. I think hes a nice guy, but he seems offended when you ask questions. His lectures are essentially useless, go to SI/tutoring. Textbook wont help
Put graduate level questions on undergraduate exams. Does not explain concepts very well to people just starting in organic chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I don't get most of the reviews posted here. Zhao spent a lot of time on the really important concepts and only briefly covered what he deemed unimportant, AKA pacing was excellent. The slides were beautiful and were my #1 resource. There was probably too much homework, though. Zhao was very passionate and I felt lucky to have him

Zhao was difficult in the way that his lectures were not paced well and the slides were taken directly from the textbook slides. The homework was difficult and I basically taught myself the material all semester. Exams aren't awfully hard and he will curve if average is below 70%. Only take if you're willing to work hard for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr Zhao clearly knows a lot about organic chemistry, but good luck following his 100 mile/minute lectures. They were the most dry lectures I have every attended, and it is impossible to take notes while in class. The book is your best bet for learning the material. There is so much homework that is impossible to do without looking on chegg.
He is a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I think with the material he had to teach, he did a good job. He covered things pretty quickly. There was also a lot of homework! For organic chemistry, it wasn't that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Zhao was an alright teacher. He moved pretty fast through lectures but was always available for extra help and the exams were pretty much the same as the practice exams with a few examples from lecture. It's a difficult class but just pay attention, do the work, and get a tutor and you'll be fine. Also he laughs at his own jokes A LOT
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hes not good at teaching students. Bad chem teacher. But hes good in his chemistry.
I absolutely loved him for Organic Chemistry 1. I thought he was a fantastic professor and his teaching style worked really well for me. Just as good as Dr. Winters, if not better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Organic Chemistry 1 is hard enough as it is, but typically he helped the smarter students succeed rather than those of us who were struggling. Yes, the tests were basically the book but he also often used direct examples from his slides. He was very understanding when there was a grading mistake on the tests (saved my grade.)

Zhao knows Ochem very well, but he's bad at relating it in a simple way. He talks in the beginning of the class about how he doesn't want to force you to memorize anything, but he makes you do it anyway. His tests were twice as hard as what I saw in Winters' class, reading the book, SI, and practice exams are your best bet. Wish I had Winters
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is very monotoned so it is very hard to listen to his lectures. He basically outlines every chapter in his lecture slides so it's honestly easier to just read the book yourself. Get ahead early, once you get even 1 chapter behind it is hard to catch up. Take with Winter, do NOT take with Zhao. Good curve but not prepared for 332.

This class was hard. His lectures seemed kind of incomplete, so I had to read the book and work all the problems to supplement his lectures. Exams were hard, look at past exams for tips. Go to his review before each exam, he drops hints about what will be on them. I did well on the first 4 exams, but the final destroyed me. Expect a hard final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I cannot stress enough that if you want to do well in this class, you MUST attend SI sessions before exam to obtain a practice exam and get an idea what the actual exam is. Homework is difficult unless you buy chegg account since it's online and requires exact look of a structure. If you do these two things, you should do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The textbook is essential, READ IT. He makes his own tests, and they are HARD. Go to the SI sessions and ask a lot of questions about mechanisms and reactants as soon as he starts teaching them about halfway through the semester. This class. Hard.

Professor is very helpful and willing to clarify or answer questions. He wants you to understand, not memorize. Print his provided partial notes and fill them in during class. Use the practice tests to study for exams. The exams seem hard, but there are a lot of easy and freebie points.

Dont miss class and take the notes. Read the chapter prior to lecture and do the homework. He is VERY HELPFUL and will take his time to explain any questions you have. The material isn't that hard; keep motivated and you'll do fine!

Always go to class, read the book and review your notes. he is VERY helpful and always willing to clarify your questions. The class is not an easy one - or the material itself. But attending classes, reading chapters and reviewing your notes - you should be fine.

An overall pretty good professor, and is very easy to understand.  I would recommend attending class because you can only get the notes from the lectures.  Also go to the SI sessions, because they can clarify points that you didn't quite understand in the lecture.  I didn't think I would get an A in this class, but I pulled it off!
Attending class and reviewing past exams will get you an easy A. The class isn't hard. He's very helpful in preparing students for tests and finals. A good teacher if a little boring.
Just attend lecture and look over old exams and this class will be a breeze. People that think this class was hard must not have attended lecture or payed attention.
Going to lecture is pretty much a waste of time. I learned everything from the book and from SI. Old exams posted online are VERY helpful.

Attendance not recommended. Class is extremely boring and you will most likely get nothing out of it. Notes are very long and overly complicated. I found studying the night before the exam for a couple hours to put me WELL above the average. Old exams posted online are VERY helpful. Memorize SN/E processes and nomenclature and you will get an A!

I thought Zhao was a really good professor. He must have changed his style, because the tests reflected what he taught. I could always understand what he said, but class could get a little dry at times. I would recommend him for 231.
I attended his class a couple of years ago. He is very knowledgeable and helpful.

It appears that Zhao co-taught Chem 231, and it appears that he cannot handle 331 on his own either. You will learn little to nothing in class, and exams are so difficult, you'll want to laugh.  The average score of all 5 exams this semester was a 60%.  Take another prof (K. Trahanovsky), and you will probably do better.
No Comments

Anyone who says what he does in class doesn't relate to the tests obviously hasn't been paying much attention.  Many examples he gives in class appear on the tests.  He speaks English very well, and is very intelligent.
im not going to lie, this is a tough class, but an A is totally possible if you just do the practice problems and study the practice tests

What he teaches in class doesn't really reflect what he puts on the tests, so if you take his class make sure you understand everything on his tests from the year before.  Go to the help sessions with the grad studentss, that helped a LOT.
No idea what he said all semester, couldn't explain anything to save his life.  He can't explain any concepts and there is no help for people who don't understand chemistry.

She is knowledgeable in her teaching, but she teaches this course assuming you already know all the material. She is very difficult to understand and is extremely unclear on what she expects for assignments. Coding is expected on almost every homework she assigns, but she does not teach coding at all. Good luck.

I had her as a TA, and I'll be the first to point out that the reason she's a TA and no longer a professor is because of how bad a professor she is. Hearing her try to pathetically teach the material makes it even more confusing, and when she grades tests, she'll dock points with absolutely no explanation. She doesn't even deserve to be a TA.

Dr. Yan spends half the class reviewing what we did the previous lecture, and spends half the lecture doing meaningless algebra. She is very unorganized and improvises a lot of policies, homework, and quizzes. However, I can tell she is extremely passionate about numerical analysis, and she is knowledgeable and kind.

She is a nice person but its hard to follow her teaching style. I have taken calc 1, 2, and 3 with different profs and Calc 1 with this professor was my lowest grade. She doesn't do handwritten problems or notes during class, she only reads off a slideshow. She goes through the slides quickly and its sometimes difficult to write everything down.
If you take her, best of luck understanding what she says.

She can't speak english, so I recommend going to Barloon's lecture. He's good. Her slides are confusing and it doesn't help that you can't understand what she is saying. Make sure you do all of the recitation practice quizzes b/c it's good practice and you'll be questioned over the same questions on the quizzes. Study hard for tests. You'll be ok!

Had trouble understanding her accent. Just watch Steve Butler's videos. Same content, but more informative and engaging. ISU's math department is no joke. Took calc I in high school, A grade the whole year. I put 12-15 hours per week into calc I this semester and couldn't get an A. They make it harder than it needs to be. Definitely a weeder class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Content was hard but she was good. She was funny and had humor. She was very knowledgeable and always helps
Students understand

Yan is a very kind professor and is very focused on making sure students understand the content. If you take her 481, make sure you have a baseline coding ability and remember your basics from calc 3. You don't need to be great at 266 or 267 to do well in this class. The final was a take-home project and there was one midterm exam.

Very hard to understand with lectures, I had a better time watching Professor Butler's videos and reading the textbook rather than going to lectures. Class was difficult, expect to spend 10-15 hours a week outside of class working on problems. Quizzes were given based off of a 10 problem bank and exams were 7 questions and 75 minutes long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures seem very unorganized, almost like she didn't really know the material. She would get behind compared to other classes, making us even worse for the quizzes. Would much watch the videos posted online such as Steve Butler.

Had her for Intro to Partial Differential Equations. The class was graded mostly on homework, which helped me improve over time in the class. The exams were (mostly) pretty easy as long as you'd done all the homework. The only drawback is that you will most likely be reviewing your notes after lectures a little more than you'd like.
Not a very good teacher

I waited to write this review a year later so I wasn't upset. I had her for diffeq, she was plain and simple no good. I went in multiple times for some extra help she didn't care or help. Our test averages were approx 30% lower than Andreotti's, I went to his lectures after ex1 and then my exam score went up drastically. I only passed because Covid

She was hard to understand and rushed through her notes. For the first test, the average for my section with her was 64% and my friend in another section with a different professor had an average of 84%... on the exact same test

Jue Yan was fine for MATH 207. MATH 207 isn't that hard of a class. If you have trouble just watch YouTube videos. There's tons of tutorials. Overall, if you visit office hours she gives you one extra credit point per visit. You can end up with 6% added onto your grade at the end PLUS you GET the CURVE. Really good person to take this course with!

Dr. Yan really cares about her students but I learned nothing from this class. There were two homework assignments and two presentations that were super easy to do and if you completed them you should get an A. Other than that there's not much else to say about this class becuase I still don't know it's purpose.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: What I got from her. 1. Study section/examples before class. Makes night day difference grasp the lectures. 2. Solve blank paper not looking solutions, over and over. Again night day difference speed confidence exams. 3. Go office/ta ask help in the beginning don't wait. 4. She genuinely doesn't like her student do bad most prof don't care less.
I could never find interest in her lectures. I learned the content from YouTube and practicing homework problems. Only went to lecture for weekly quizzes.

Her lectures are spontaneous and unorganized. She does not explain the point of her every lecture well enough for me to be able apply and solve other problems. However, her homework grading is pretty easy, and I think she always tries her best to help her students getting good score on their exams

Her lectures were often more confusing than helpful. She would often explain somewhat simple concepts in a way that made them seem very complex and hard to understand. I went to class most of the time but still relied heavily on online lectures to actually learn the material.

"Skip class? You won't pass"? More like "Skip class? You'll do better". She's kind of a meme. If I wanted to learn calc 3 again I would not take it, but she's so funny. She calls everything "this guy", she writes with an accent, she tells us things like "do better or drop the class, otherwise you will fail", she yells for no reason some times.

Jue had an obvious language barrier, but I think she did a great job overcoming it and I found it quite easy to follow her during lecture (language wise). As far as content during lecture, she tended to be all over the place and I found the book to be a lot more helpful. HOWEVER, she has an amazing grading policy and I got a B with a 75%.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Terrible class as a freshman to be in...
Thick Chinese accent A little boring and hard to follow Not very much homework for a math class Easy grader on tests

Professor Jue is a good professor. She arrived at exactly 10 every day. We had homework about once a week, and five exams plus the final. The original grading scale had an 85% as the cutoff for an A-, but she still curved the class in the end. Goes over a lot of examples in class.

Smart person, great researcher, horrible professor! She is very confusing, hard to understand and makes even the simplest things totally complicated. Tests are hard, harsh grader but she grades on a curve. First day of class, we had 35 people, now, less than 10 people still go to lectures regularly. You have been warned!

She goes through a lot of examples in class which definitely helps. If you actually DO the homework, than you should have no problem on the exams or quizzes because she  models them after the hw. Overall she was a fine professor for linear algebra, but for a harder class, I might have a harder time following her.

She is a terrible professor. Blows through lecture without teaching anything in depth. Has a very limited vocabulary and is very difficult to understand and is not accommodating with class conflicts. Adds content covered on exams and quizzes the day of the exam. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.
Lectures were clear and easy to understand.  Her notes for each class were posted online after lecture was over.  Approachable and helpful during office hours.
Clear explanations, HW and tests are pretty reasonable. A book would have been nice though
She has passion for teaching. She explains the example well so I don't need to spend much time after class.She is very helpful.
professor Jue is very nice, she is always ready to answer our questions and help us to improve, both the homework and exam are not difficult to deal with.

I would say the lectures are a weak point. There's other resources out there. (see Strang on MIT OCW 18.085) The strong points is that a lot of material is covered due to her style and the fast pace keeps your attention. Also she is very willing and capable to help you if you ask during OH.

I would say the lectures are a weak point. There's other resources out there. (see Strang on MIT OCW 18.085) The strong points is that a lot of material is covered due to her style and the fast pace keeps your attention. Also she is very willing and capable to help you if you ask during OH.  Note: this was for math 481. RMP is glitchy.

At first she seemed terrible because she spoke limited English, but if you attend class and pay close attention, she really is a great teacher. Her tests and quizzes were taken directly from the homework problems. She was interesting to listen to and was always helpful in answering questions.

Terrible.  Her limited English and extremely fast talking make it impossible to comprehend what is going on.  Plus she writes faster than you can, so the entire class is spent just writing, no time for comprehension.  Office hours are minimal and she isn't helpful in explaining things when you go.  Toughest grading policy I've seen in 4 years.
Dr Yan likes teaching numerical analysis. If you can get her for a topic that she is passionate about, the class is pretty good

hard to understand. I have taken a simular course before taking this oen and if i had not i would have been totally lost. Whenever i did ask a question in class she usually did not explain the answer very well.
Her limited vocabulary hinders teaching effectiveness. I feel like she doesn't even know enough English to understand questions that are asked. Without SI, I would've of been lost in this class.
Repeats examples over and over, and over
No Comments

Asks about pacing during lecture, which is helpful if things are going too fast. Good at explaining slides rather than just reading off of them. Good at answering questions both within and outside the scope of the material. Liked her enthusiasm.

Dr. Yandeau-Nelson was a great professor. She's very knowledgeable and engaging. She genuinely wants all of her students to do well.
